Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are dem names, by dem villages, and by dem encampments: twelve princes, according to dem nations.
These are the years of the life of Ishmael: one hundred thirty-seven years. He give up his spirit and died, and was gathered to his people.
Dem lived from Havilah to Shur that is before Egypt, as you go toward Assyria. He lived opposite all his relatives.
This is the history of the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son. Abraham became the father of Isaac.
Isaac was forty years old when he take Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Paddan Aram, the sister of Laban the Syrian, to be his wife.
Isaac entreated Baba God for his wife, because she was barren. Baba God was entreated by him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
The pikin dem struggled together within her. She talk say, “If it is so, why do I live?” She go to inquire of Baba God.
Baba God talk say to her, “Two nations are in una womb. Two peoples Go be separated from una body. The one people Go be stronger than the other people. The elder will serve the younger.”
When her days to be delivered were fulfilled, see am, there were twins in her womb.
The first come out red all over, like a hairy garment. Dem named him Esau.
After that, his brother come out, and his hand had hold on Esau’s heel. He was named Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when she bore dem.
The boys grew. Esau was a skillful hunter, a man of the field. Jacob was a quiet man, living in tents.
Now Isaac love Esau, because he ate his venison. Rebekah love Jacob.
Jacob boiled stew. Esau come in from the field, and he was famished.
Esau talk say to Jacob, “Please feed me with that same red stew, for I be famished.” So his name was call Edom.
Jacob talk say, “First, sell me una birthright.”
Esau talk say, “See am, I be about to die. What good is the birthright to me?”
Jacob talk say, “Swear to me first.” He swore to him. He sold his birthright to Jacob.
Jacob give Esau bread and stew of lentils. He ate and drank, rose up, and go his way. So Esau despised his birthright.
There was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. Isaac go to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
Baba God appeared to him, and talk say, “No go down into Egypt. Live in the land I go tell you about.
Live in this land, and I go be with you, and will bless you. For I go give to you, and to una offspring, all these lands, and I go establish the oath which I swore to Abraham una father.
I go multiply una offspring as the stars of the sky, and will give all these lands to una offspring. In una offspring will all the nations of the earth be blessed,
because Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my requirements, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.”
Isaac lived in Gerar.

The men of the place ask him about his wife. He talk say, “She is my sister,” for he was afraid to say, “My wife”, lest, he thought, “the men of the place might kill me for Rebekah, because she is beautiful to look at.”
When he Bin dey there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and see, and, see am, Isaac was caressing Rebekah, his wife.
Abimelech call Isaac, and talk say, “See am, surely she is una wife. Why did you say, ‘She is my sister?’” Isaac talk say to him, “Because I talk say, ‘Lest I die because of her.’”
Abimelech talk say, “Wetin be this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with una wife, and you would have bring guilt on us!”
Abimelech commanded all the people, saying, “Person wey touches this man or his wife will surely be put to death.”
Isaac sowed in that land, and reaped in the same year one hundred times what he planted. Baba God blessed him.
The man grew great, and grew more and more until he became plenty well-well.
He had possessions of flocks, possessions of herds, and a great household. The Philistines envied him.
Now all the wells which his father’s workers had dug in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped, and filled with earth.
Abimelech talk say to Isaac, “Go from us, for You be much mightier than we.”
Isaac comot from there, encamped in the valley of Gerar, and lived there.

Isaac dug again the wells of water, which dem had dug in the days of Abraham his father. For the Philistines had stopped dem after the death of Abraham. He call dem names after the names by which his father had call dem.
Isaac’s workers dug in the valley, and find there a well of springing water.
The herdsmen of Gerar argued with Isaac’s herdsmen, saying, “The water is ours.” He call the name of the well Esek, because dem contended with him.
Dem dug another well, and dem argued over that, also. He call its name Sitnah.
He left that place, and dug another well. Dem didn’t argue over that one. He call it Rehoboth. He talk say, “For now Baba God has made room for us, and We go be fruitful in the land.”
He go up from there to Beersheba.
Baba God appeared to him the same night, and talk say, “I be the God of Abraham una father. No fear, for I be with you, and will bless you, and multiply una offspring for my worker Abraham’s sake.”
He built an altar there, and call on Baba God’s name, and pitched his tent there. There Isaac’s workers dug a well.
Then Abimelech go to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath his friend, and Phicol the captain of his army.
Isaac talk say to dem, “Why have you come to me, since you hate me, and have sent me away from you?”
Dem talk say, “We see plainly that Baba God was with you. We talk say, ‘Let there now be an oath between us, even between us and you, and Make we make a covenant with you,
that You go do us no harm, as we have not touched you, and as we have done to you nothing but good, and have sent you away in peace.’ You be now the blessed of Baba God.”
He made dem a feast, and dem ate and drank.
Dem rose up some time in the morning, and swore to each other. Isaac sent dem away, and dem comot from him in peace.
The same day, Isaac’s workers come, and told him concerning the well which dem had dug, and talk say to him, “We have find water.”
He call it Shibah. So the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.
When Esau was forty years old, he take as wife Judith, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, the daughter of Elon the Hittite.
Dem grieved Isaac’s and Rebekah’s spirits.
When Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he call Esau his elder son, and talk say to him, “My son?” E tell am say, “Here I be.”
He talk say, “See now, I be old. I no know the day of my death.
Now so, please take una weapons, una quiver and una bow, and go out to the field, and take me venison.
Make me savory chop, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat, and that my soul may bless you before I die.”
Rebekah heard when Isaac spoke to Esau his son. Esau go to the field to hunt for venison, and to bring it.
Rebekah spoke to Jacob her son, saying, “See am, I heard una father speak to Esau una brother, saying,
‘Bring me venison, and make me savory chop, that I may eat, and bless you before Baba God before my death.’
Now so, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command you.
Go now to the flock, and get me from there two good young goats. I go make dem savory chop for una father, such as he loves.
You shall bring it to una father, that he may eat, so that he may bless you before his death.”
Jacob talk say to Rebekah his mother, “See am, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I be a smooth man.
What if my father touches me? I go seem to him as a deceiver, and I would bring a curse on myself, and not a blessing.”
His mother talk say to him, “Let una curse be on me, my son. Only obey my voice, and go get dem for me.”
He go, and got dem, and bring dem to his mother. His mother made savory chop, such as his father love.
Rebekah take the good clothes of Esau, her elder son, which were with her in the house, and put dem on Jacob, her younger son.
She put the skins of the young goats on his hands, and on the smooth of his neck.
She give the savory chop and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob.
He come to his father, and talk say, “My father?” He talk say, “Here I be. Wey be you, my son?”
Jacob talk say to his father, “I be Esau una firstborn. I have done Wetin you ask me to do. Please arise, sit and eat of my venison, that una soul may bless me.”
Isaac talk say to his son, “How is it that you have find it so sharp-sharp, my son?” He talk say, “Because Baba God una God give me success.”
Isaac talk say to Jacob, “Please come near, that I may feel you, my son, whether You be really my son Esau or not.”
Jacob go near to Isaac his father. He felt him, and talk say, “The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”
He didn’t recognize him, because his hands were hairy, like his brother, Esau’s hands. So he blessed him.
He talk say, “Are you really my son Esau?” He talk say, “I be.”
He talk say, “Bring it near to me, and I go eat of my son’s venison, that my soul may bless you.” He bring it near to him, and he ate. He bring him wine, and he drank.
His father Isaac talk say to him, “Come near now, and kiss me, my son.”
He come near, and kissed him. He smelled the smell of his clothing, and blessed him, and talk say, “See am, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which Baba God has blessed.
God give you of the dew of the sky, of the fatness of the earth, and plenty of grain and new wine.
Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you. Be lord over una brothers. Let una mother’s sons bow down to you. Cursed be Everybody wey curses you. Blessed be Everybody wey blesses you.”
As soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, and Jacob had just gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, Esau his brother come in from his hunting.
He also made savory chop, and bring it to his father. He talk say to his father, “Let my father arise, and eat of his son’s venison, that una soul may bless me.”
Isaac his father talk say to him, “Wey be you?” He talk say, “I be una son, una firstborn, Esau.”
Isaac trembled violently, and talk say, “Who, then, is person wey has taken venison, and bring it me, and I have eaten of all before you come, and have blessed him? Yes, he Go be blessed.”
When Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with an exceeding great and bitter cry, and talk say to his father, “Bless me, even me also, my father.”
He talk say, “Una brother come with deceit, and has taken away una blessing.”

He talk say, “No be he rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these two times. He take away my birthright. See, now he has taken away my blessing.” He talk say, “Haven’t you reserved a blessing for me?”
Isaac answer Esau, “See am, I have made him una lord, and all his brothers I have given to him for workers. I have sustained him with grain and new wine. What then will I do for you, my son?”
Esau talk say to his father, “Have you but one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me also, my father.” Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.
Isaac his father answer him, “See am, of the fatness of the earth Go be una dwelling, and of the dew of the sky from above.
By una sword will you live, and You go serve una brother. It will happen, when You go break loose, that you shall shake his yoke from off una neck.”
Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father blessed him. Esau talk say in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand. Then I go kill my brother Jacob.”
The words of Esau, her elder son, were told to Rebekah. She sent and call Jacob, her younger son, and talk say to him, “See am, una brother Esau comforts imself about you by planning to kill you.
Now so, my son, obey my voice. Arise, flee to Laban, my brother, in Haran.
Stay with him a few days, until una brother’s fury turns away;
until una brother’s anger turn away from you, and he forgets Wetin you have done to him. Then I go send, and get you from there. Why should I be bereaved of you both in one day?”

Rebekah talk say to Isaac, “I be weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these, of the daughters of the land, what good will my life do me?”
Isaac call Jacob, blessed him, and commanded him, “You no go take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.
Arise, go to Paddan Aram, to the house of Bethuel una mother’s father. Take a wife from there from the daughters of Laban, una mother’s brother.
May God Almighty bless you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, that you may be a company of peoples,
and give you the blessing of Abraham, to you, and to una offspring with you, that you may inherit the land where you travel, which God give to Abraham.”
Isaac sent Jacob away. He go to Paddan Aram to Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, Rebekah’s brother, Jacob’s and Esau’s mother.

Now Esau see that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Paddan Aram, to take him a wife from there, and that as he blessed him he give him a command, saying, “You no go take a wife of the daughters of Canaan,”
and that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Paddan Aram.
Esau see that the daughters of Canaan didn’t please Isaac, his father.
Esau go to Ishmael, and take, besides the wives that he had, Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebaioth, to be his wife.
Jacob go out from Beersheba, and go toward Haran.
He come to a certain place, and stayed there all night, because the sun had set. He take one of the stones of the place, and put it under his head, and lay down in that place to sleep.
He dreamed. See am, a stairway set upon the earth, and its top reached to heaven. See am, the angels of God ascending and descending on it.
See am, Baba God stood above it, and talk say, “I be Baba God, the God of Abraham una father, and the God of Isaac. The land whereon you lie, to You go I give it, and to una offspring.

Una offspring Go be as the dust of the earth, and You go spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south. In you and in una offspring will all the families of the earth be blessed.
See am, I be with you, and will keep you, Anywhere wey you go, and will bring you again into this land. For I go not leave you, until I have done that which I have spoken of to you.”
Jacob awakened out of his sleep, and he talk say, “Surely Baba God is in this place, and I didn’t know it.”
He was afraid, and talk say, “How dreadful is this place! This is none other than God’s house, and this is the gate of heaven.”
Jacob rose up early in the morning, and take the stone that he had put under his head, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil on its top.
He call the name of that place Bethel, but the name of the city was Luz at the first.
Jacob vowed a vow, saying, “If God Go be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and clothing to put on,
so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, and Baba God Go be my God,
then this stone, which I have set up for a pillar, Go be God’s house. Of all that You go give me I go surely give a tenth to you.”
Then Jacob go on his journey, and come to the land of the pikin dem of the east.
He looked, and see am, a well in the field, and, see am, three flocks of sheep lying there by it. For out of that well dem watered the flocks. The stone on the well’s mouth was large.
There all the flocks were gathered. Dem rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the sheep, and put the stone again on the well’s mouth in its place.
Jacob talk say to dem, “My relatives, where are you from?” Dem talk say, “We be from Haran.”
E tell dem say, “Do you know Laban, the son of Nahor?” Dem talk say, “We know him.”
E tell dem say, “Is it well with him?” Dem talk say, “It is well. See, Rachel, his daughter, is coming with the sheep.”
He talk say, “See am, it is still the middle of the day, not time to gather the livestock together. Water the sheep, and go and feed dem.”
Dem talk say, “We no fit, until all the flocks are gathered together, and dem roll the stone from the well’s mouth. Then we water the sheep.”
While he was yet speaking with dem, Rachel come with her father’s sheep, for she kept dem.

When Jacob see Rachel the daughter of Laban, his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban, his mother’s brother, Jacob go near, and rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother’s brother.
Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept.
Jacob told Rachel that he was her father’s brother, and that he was Rebekah’s son. She ran and told her father.
When Laban heard the news of Jacob, his sister’s son, he ran to meet Jacob, and embraced him, and kissed him, and bring him to his house. Jacob told Laban all these things.
Laban talk say to him, “Surely You be my bone and my flesh.” He lived with him for a month.
Laban talk say to Jacob, “Because You be my brother, should you so serve me for nothing? Tell me, what will una wages be?”
Laban had two daughters. The name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
Leah’s eyes were weak, but Rachel was beautiful in form and attractive.
Jacob love Rachel. He talk say, “I go serve you seven years for Rachel, una younger daughter.”
Laban talk say, “It is better that I give her to you, than that I should give her to another man. Stay with me.”
Jacob served seven years for Rachel. Dem seemed to him but a few days, for the love he had for her.
Jacob talk say to Laban, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in to her.”
Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.
In the evening, he take Leah his daughter, and bring her to him. He go in to her.
Laban give Zilpah his worker to his daughter Leah for a worker.
In the morning, see am, it was Leah. He talk say to Laban, “Wetin be this you have done to me? Didn’t I serve with you for Rachel? Why then have you deceived me?”
Laban talk say, “It No be done so in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn.
Fulfill the week of this one, and We go give you the other also for the service which You go serve with me yet seven other years.”
Jacob did so, and fulfilled her week. He give him Rachel his daughter as wife.
Laban give to Rachel his daughter Bilhah, his worker, to be her worker.
He go in also to Rachel, and he love also Rachel more than Leah, and served with him yet seven other years.
Baba God see that Leah was hated, and he opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.
Leah conceived, and bore a son, and she named him Reuben. For she talk say, “Because Baba God has looked at my suffering. For now my husband will love me.”
She conceived again, and bore a son, and talk say, “Because Baba God has heard that I be hated, he has so given me this son also.” She named him Simeon.
She conceived again, and bore a son. Talk say, “Now this time will my husband be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons.” So his name was call Levi.
She conceived again, and bore a son. She talk say, “This time will I praise Baba God.” So she named him Judah. Then she stopped bearing.
When Rachel see that she bore Jacob no pikin dem, Rachel envied her sister. She talk say to Jacob, “Give me pikin dem, or else I go die.”
Jacob’s anger burned against Rachel, and he talk say, “Am I in God’s place, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?”
She talk say, “See am, my maid Bilhah. Go in to her, that she may bear on my knees, and I also may obtain pikin dem by her.”
She give him Bilhah her worker as wife, and Jacob go in to her.
Bilhah conceived, and bore Jacob a son.
Rachel talk say, “God has judged me, and has also heard my voice, and has given me a son.” So call she his name Dan.
Bilhah, Rachel’s worker, conceived again, and bore Jacob a second son.
Rachel talk say, “I have wrestled with my sister with mighty wrestlings, and have prevailed.” She named him Naphtali.
When Leah see that she had finished bearing, she take Zilpah, her worker, and give her to Jacob as a wife.
Zilpah, Leah’s worker, bore Jacob a son.
Leah talk say, “How fortunate!” She named him Gad.
Zilpah, Leah’s worker, bore Jacob a second son.
Leah talk say, “Happy am I, for the daughters will call me happy.” She named him Asher.
Reuben go in the days of wheat harvest, and find mandrakes in the field, and bring dem to his mother, Leah. Then Rachel talk say to Leah, “Please give me some of una son’s mandrakes.”

She talk say to her, “Is it a small matter that you have taken away my husband? Would you take away my son’s mandrakes, also?” Rachel talk say, “So he will lie with you tonight for una son’s mandrakes.”
Jacob come from the field in the evening, and Leah go out to meet him, and talk say, “You must come in to me; for I have surely hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” He lay with her that night.
God listened to Leah, and she conceived, and bore Jacob a fifth son.
Leah talk say, “God has given me my hire, because I give my worker to my husband.” She named him Issachar.
Leah conceived again, and bore a sixth son to Jacob.
Leah talk say, “God has endowed me with a good dowry. Now my husband will live with me, because I have borne him six sons.” She named him Zebulun.
Afterwards, she bore a daughter, and named her Dinah.
God remember Rachel, and God listened to her, and opened her womb.
She conceived, bore a son, and talk say, “God has taken away my reproach.”
She named him Joseph, saying, “May Baba God add another son to me.”
When Rachel had borne Joseph, Jacob talk say to Laban, “Send me away, that I may go to my own place, and to my country.
Give me my wives and my pikin dem for whom I have served you, and let me go; for you know my service with which I have served you.”
Laban talk say to him, “If now I have find favor in una eyes, stay here, for I have divined that Baba God has blessed me for una sake.”
He talk say, “Appoint me una wages, and I go give it.”
E tell am say, “You know how I have served you, and how una livestock have fared with me.
For it was little which you had before I come, and it has increased to a plenty people. Baba God has blessed you Anywhere wey I turned. Now when will I provide for my own house also?”
He talk say, “What shall I give you?” Jacob talk say, “You no go give me anything. If You go do this thing for me, I go again feed una flock and keep it.
I go pass through all una flock today, removing from there every speckled and spotted one, and every black one among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats. This Go be my hire.

So my righteousness will answer for me hereafter, when you come concerning my hire that is before you. Every one that No be speckled and spotted among the goats, and black among the sheep, that might be with me, Go be considered stolen.”
Laban talk say, “See am, let it be according to una word.”

That day, he removed the male goats that were streaked and spotted, and all the female goats that were speckled and spotted, every one that had white in it, and all the black ones among the sheep, and give dem into the hand of his sons.
He set three days’ journey between imself and Jacob, and Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.
Jacob take to imself rods of fresh poplar, almond, plane tree, peeled white streaks in dem, and made the white appear which was in the rods.
He set the rods which he had peeled opposite the flocks in the gutters in the watering-troughs where the flocks come to drink. Dem conceived when dem come to drink.
The flocks conceived before the rods, and the flocks produced streaked, speckled, and spotted.
Jacob separated the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks toward the streaked and all the black in the flock of Laban: and he put his own droves apart, and didn’t put dem into Laban’s flock.
Whenever the stronger of the flock conceived, Jacob laid the rods in front of the eyes of the flock in the gutters, that dem might conceive among the rods;
but when the flock were feeble, he didn’t put dem in. So the feebler were Laban’s, and the stronger Jacob’s.
The man increased exceedingly, and had large flocks, female workers and male workers, and camels and donkeys.
He heard the words of Laban’s sons, saying, “Jacob has taken away all that was our father’s. From that which was our father’s, has he gotten all this wealth.”
Jacob see the expression on Laban’s face, and, see am, it No be toward him as before.
Baba God talk say to Jacob, “Return to the land of una fathers, and to una relatives, and I go be with you.”
Jacob sent and call Rachel and Leah to the field to his flock,
and talk say to dem, “I see the expression on una father’s face, that it No be toward me as before; but the God of my father Don dey with me.
You know that I have served una father with all of my strength.
Una father has deceived me, and changed my wages ten times, but God didn’t allow him to hurt me.
If he talk say this, ‘The speckled Go be una wages,’ then all the flock bore speckled. If he talk say this, ‘The streaked Go be una wages,’ then all the flock bore streaked.
Thus God has taken away una father’s livestock, and given dem to me.
During mating season, I lifted up my eyes, and see in a dream, and see am, the male goats which leaped on the flock were streaked, speckled, and grizzled.
The angel of God talk say to me in the dream, ‘Jacob,’ and I talk say, ‘Here I be.’
He talk say, ‘Now lift up una eyes, and see am, all the male goats which leap on the flock are streaked, speckled, and grizzled, for I have seen all that Laban does to you.
I be the God of Bethel, where you anointed a pillar, where you vowed a vow to me. Now arise, get out from this land, and return to the land of una birth.’”
Rachel and Leah answer him, “Is there yet any portion or inheritance for us in our father’s house?
No be we accounted by him as foreigners? For he has sold us, and has also quite devoured our money.
For all the riches which God has taken away from our father, that is ours and our pikin dem’s. Now then, Anything wey God has talk say to you, do.”
Then Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his wives on the camels,
and he take away all his livestock, and all his possessions which he had gathered, including the livestock which he had gained in Paddan Aram, to go to Isaac his father, to the land of Canaan.
Now Laban had gone to shear his sheep: and Rachel stole the teraphim that were her father’s.
Jacob deceived Laban the Syrian, in that he didn’t tell him that he was running away.
So he fled with all that he had. He rose up, passed over the River, and set his face toward the mountain of Gilead.
Laban was told on the third day that Jacob had fled.
He take his relatives with him, and pursued him seven days’ journey. He overtook him in the mountain of Gilead.
God come to Laban, the Syrian, in a dream of the night, and talk say to him, “Be careful that you no speak to Jacob either good or bad.”
Laban caught up with Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain, and Laban with his relatives encamped in the mountain of Gilead.
Laban talk say to Jacob, “What have you done, that you have deceived me, and carried away my daughters like captives of the sword?
Why did you flee secretly, and deceive me, and didn’t tell me, that I might have sent you away with mirth and with songs, with tambourine and with harp;
and didn’t allow me to kiss my sons and my daughters? Now have you done foolishly.
It is in the power of my hand to hurt you, but the God of una father spoke to me last night, saying, ‘Be careful that you no speak to Jacob either good or bad.’
Now, you want to be gone, because you greatly longed for una father’s house, but why have you stolen my gods?”
Jacob answer Laban, “Because I was afraid, for I talk say, ‘Lest you should take una daughters from me by force.’
Anyone you find una gods with no go live. Before our relatives, discern Wetin be yours with me, and take it.” For Jacob didn’t know that Rachel had stolen dem.
Laban go into Jacob’s tent, into Leah’s tent, and into the tent of the two female workers; but he didn’t find dem. He go out of Leah’s tent, and entered into Rachel’s tent.
Now Rachel had taken the teraphim, put dem in the camel’s saddle, and sat on dem. Laban felt around all the tent, but didn’t find dem.
She talk say to her father, “No let my lord be angry that I no fit rise up before you; for I’m having my period.” He searched, but didn’t find the teraphim.
Jacob was angry, and argued with Laban. Jacob answer Laban, “Wetin be my trespass? Wetin be my sin, that you have hotly pursued me?
Now that you have felt around in all my stuff, what have you find of all una household stuff? Set it here before my relatives and una relatives, that dem may judge between us two.
“These twenty years I Don dey with you. Una ewes and una female goats have not throw dem young, and I haven’t eaten the rams of una flocks.
That which was torn of animals, I didn’t bring to you. I bore its loss. Of my hand you required it, whether stolen by day or stolen by night.
This was my situation: in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep fled from my eyes.
These twenty years I Don dey in una house. I served you fourteen years for una two daughters, and six years for una flock, and you have changed my wages ten times.

Unless the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac, Bin dey with me, surely now you would have sent me away empty. God has seen my suffering and the labor of my hands, and rebuked you last night.”

Laban answer Jacob, “The daughters are my daughters, the pikin dem are my pikin dem, the flocks are my flocks, and all that you see is mine: and what can I do today to these my daughters, or to dem pikin dem whom dem have borne?
Now come, Make we make a covenant, you and I; and let it be for a witness between me and you.”
Jacob take a stone, and set it up for a pillar.
Jacob talk say to his relatives, “Gather stones.” Dem take stones, and made a heap. Dem ate there by the heap.
Laban call it Jegar Sahadutha, but Jacob call it Galeed.
Laban talk say, “This heap is witness between me and you today.” So it was named Galeed
and Mizpah, for he talk say, “Baba God watch between me and you, when We be absent one from another.
If you afflict my daughters, or if you take wives besides my daughters, no man is with us; see am, God is witness between me and you.”
Laban talk say to Jacob, “See this heap, and see the pillar, which I have set between me and you.
May this heap be a witness, and the pillar be a witness, that I go not pass over this heap to you, and that You go not pass over this heap and this pillar to me, for harm.
The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of dem father, judge between us.” Then Jacob swore by the fear of his father, Isaac.
Jacob offered a sacrifice in the mountain, and call his relatives to eat bread. Dem ate bread, and stayed all night in the mountain.
Early in the morning, Laban rose up, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed dem. Laban comot and come back to his place.
Jacob go on his way, and the angels of God met him.
When he see dem, Jacob talk say, “This is God’s army.” He call the name of that place Mahanaim.
Jacob sent messengers in front of him to Esau, his brother, to the land of Seir, the field of Edom.
He commanded dem, saying, “This is Wetin you shall tell my lord, Esau: ‘This is what una worker, Jacob, says. I have lived as a foreigner with Laban, and stayed until now.
I have cattle, donkeys, flocks, male workers, and female workers. I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find favor in una sight.’”
The messengers come back to Jacob, saying, “We come to una brother Esau. Not only that, but he comes to meet you, and four hundred men with him.”
Then Jacob was greatly afraid and was distressed. He divided the people who were with him, and the flocks, and the herds, and the camels, into two companies;
and he talk say, “If Esau comes to the one company, and strikes it, then the company which is left will escape.”
Jacob talk say, “God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, Baba God, who talk say to me, ‘Return to una country, and to una relatives, and I go do you good,’

I be not worthy of the least of all the loving kindnesses, and of all the truth, which you have shown to una worker; for with just my staff I crossed over this Jordan; and now I have become two companies.
Please deliver me from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I fear him, lest he come and strike me, and the mothers with the pikin dem.
You talk say, ‘I go surely do you good, and make una offspring as the sand of the sea, which no fit be counted because E get so many.’”
He stayed there that night, and take from that which he had with him, a present for Esau, his brother:
two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,
thirty milk camels and dem colts, forty cows, ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten foals.
He delivered dem into the hands of his workers, every herd by itself, and talk say to his workers, “Pass over before me, and put a space between herd and herd.”
He commanded the foremost, saying, “When Esau, my brother, meets you, and asks you, saying, ‘Whose are you? Where are you going? Whose are these before you?’
Then you shall say, ‘Dem be una worker, Jacob’s. It is a present sent to my lord, Esau. See am, he also is behind us.’”
He commanded also the second, and the third, and all that follow the herds, saying, “This is how you shall speak to Esau, when you find him.

You shall say, ‘Not only that, but see am, una worker, Jacob, is behind us.’” For, he talk say, “I go appease him with the present that goes before me, and afterward I go see his face. Perhaps he will accept me.”
So the present passed over before him, and he imself stayed that night in the camp.
He rose up that night, and take his two wives, and his two workers, and his eleven sons, and crossed over the ford of the Jabbok.
He take dem, and sent dem over the stream, and sent over that which he had.
Jacob was left alone, and wrestled with a man there until the breaking of the day.
When he see that he didn’t prevail against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh, and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was strained, as he wrestled.
The man talk say, “Let me go, for the day breaks.” Jacob talk say, “I no go let you go, unless you bless me.”
E tell am say, “Wetin be una name?” He talk say, “Jacob”.
He talk say, “Una name will no longer be call Jacob, but Israel; for you have fought with God and with men, and have prevailed.”
Jacob ask him, “Please tell me una name.” He talk say, “Why is it that you ask what my name is?” He blessed him there.
Jacob call the name of the place Peniel: for, he talk say, “I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.”
The sun rose on him as he passed over Peniel, and he limped because of his thigh.
So the pikin dem of Israel no eat the sinew of the hip, which is on the hollow of the thigh, to this day, because he touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh in the sinew of the hip.
Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, see am, Esau was coming, and with him four hundred men. He divided the pikin dem between Leah, Rachel, and the two workers.
He put the workers and dem pikin dem in front, Leah and her pikin dem after, and Rachel and Joseph at the rear.
He imself passed over in front of dem, and bowed imself to the ground seven times, until he come near to his brother.
Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, fell on his neck, kissed him, and dem wept.
He lifted up his eyes, and see the women and the pikin dem; and talk say, “Wey be these with you?” He talk say, “The pikin dem whom God has graciously given una worker.”
Then the workers come near with dem pikin dem, and dem bowed themselves.
Leah also and her pikin dem come near, and bowed themselves. After dem, Joseph come near with Rachel, and dem bowed themselves.
Esau talk say, “What do you mean by all this company which I met?” Jacob talk say, “To find favor in the sight of my lord.”
Esau talk say, “I have enough, my brother; let that which you have be yours.”
Jacob talk say, “Please, no, if I have now find favor in una sight, then receive my present at my hand, because I have seen una face, as one sees the face of God, and you were pleased with me.
Please take the gift that I bring to you, because God has dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough.” He urged him, and he take it.
Esau talk say, “Make we take our journey, and Make we go, and I go go before you.”
Jacob talk say to him, “My lord knows that the pikin dem are tender, and that the flocks and herds with me have dem young, and if dem overdrive dem one day, all the flocks will die.

Please let my lord pass over before his worker, and I go lead on gently, according to the pace of the livestock that are before me and according to the pace of the pikin dem, until I come to my lord to Seir.”
Esau talk say, “Let me now leave with you some of the folk Wey be with me.” He talk say, “Why? Let me find favor in the sight of my lord.”
So Esau come back that day on his way to Seir.
Jacob traveled to Succoth, built imself a house, and made shelters for his livestock. So the name of the place is call Succoth.
Jacob come in peace to the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he come from Paddan Aram; and encamped before the city.
He bought the parcel of ground where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the pikin dem of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for one hundred pieces of money.
He erected an altar there, and call it El Elohe Israel.
Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob, go out to see the daughters of the land.
Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, see her. He take her, lay with her, and humbled her.
His soul joined to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, and he love the young lady, and spoke kindly to the young lady.
Shechem spoke to his father, Hamor, saying, “Get me this young lady as a wife.”
Now Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah, his daughter; and his sons were with his livestock in the field. Jacob held his peace until dem come.
Hamor the father of Shechem go out to Jacob to talk with him.

The sons of Jacob come in from the field when dem heard it. The men were grieved, and dem were very angry, because he had done folly in Israel in lying with Jacob’s daughter; a thing ought not to be done.
Hamor talked with dem, saying, “The soul of my son, Shechem, longs for una daughter. Please give her to him as a wife.
Make marriages with us. Give una daughters to us, and take our daughters for unaself.
You shall live with us, and the land Go be before you. Live and trade in it, and get possessions in it.”
Shechem talk say to her father and to her brothers, “Let me find favor in una eyes, and Anything wey You go tell me I go give.
Ask me a great amount for a dowry, and I go give Anything wey you ask of me, but give me the young lady as a wife.”
The sons of Jacob answer Shechem and Hamor his father with deceit, and spoke, because he had defiled Dinah dem sister,
and talk say to dem, “We no fit do this thing, to give our sister to one Wey be uncircumcised; for that is a reproach to us.
Only on this condition will we consent to you. If You go be as We be, that every male of you be circumcised;
then will we give our daughters to you, and We go take una daughters to us, and We go live with you, and We go become one people.
But if You go not listen to us, to be circumcised, then We go take our sister, and We go be gone.”
Dem words pleased Hamor and Shechem, Hamor’s son.
The young man didn’t wait to do this thing, because he had delight in Jacob’s daughter, and he was honored above all the house of his father.
Hamor and Shechem, his son, come to the gate of dem city, and talked with the men of dem city, saying,

“These men are peaceful with us. So Make dem live in the land and trade in it. For see am, the land is large enough for dem. Make we take dem daughters to us for wives, and Make we give dem our daughters.
Only on this condition will the men consent to us to live with us, to become one people, if every male among us is circumcised, as Dem be circumcised.
No go dem livestock and dem possessions and all dem animals be ours? Only Make we give our consent to dem, and Dem go live with us.”
All who go out of the gate of his city listened to Hamor, and to Shechem his son; and every male was circumcised, all who go out of the gate of his city.
On the third day, when dem were sore, two of Jacob’s sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each take his sword, come upon the unsuspecting city, and killed all the males.
Dem killed Hamor and Shechem, his son, with the edge of the sword, and take Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and go away.
Jacob’s sons come on the dead, and plundered the city, because dem had defiled dem sister.
Dem take dem flocks, dem herds, dem donkeys, that which was in the city, that which was in the field,
and all dem wealth. Dem take captive all dem little ones and dem wives, and take as plunder everything that was in the house.

Jacob talk say to Simeon and Levi, “You have troubled me, to make me odious to the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites. I be few in number. Dem go gather themselves together against me and strike me, and I go be destroyed, I and my house.”
Dem talk say, “Should he deal with our sister as with a prostitute?”
God talk say to Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel, and live there. Make there an altar to God, who appeared to you when you fled from the face of Esau una brother.”
Then Jacob talk say to his household, and to all who were with him, “Put away the foreign gods that are among you, purify unaself, change una garments.
Make we arise, and go up to Bethel. I go make there an altar to God, who answer me in the day of my distress, and was with me on the way which I go.”
Dem give to Jacob all the foreign gods which were in dem hands, and the rings which were in dem ears; and Jacob hid dem under the oak which was by Shechem.
Dem traveled, and a terror of God was on the cities that were around dem, and dem didn’t pursue the sons of Jacob.
So Jacob come to Luz (that is, Bethel), which is in the land of Canaan, he and all the people who were with him.
He built an altar there, and call the place El Beth El; because there God was revealed to him, when he fled from the face of his brother.
Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died, and she was buried below Bethel under the oak; and its name was call Allon Bacuth.
God appeared to Jacob again, when he come from Paddan Aram, and blessed him.
God talk say to him, “Una name is Jacob. Una name no go be Jacob any more, but una name Go be Israel.” He named him Israel.
God talk say to him, “I be God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation and a company of nations Go be from you, and kings will come out of una body.
The land which I give to Abraham and Isaac, I go give it to you, and to una offspring after You go I give the land.”
God go up from him in the place where he spoke with him.
Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he spoke with him, a pillar of stone. He poured out a drink offering on it, and poured oil on it.
Jacob call the name of the place where God spoke with him “Bethel”.
Dem traveled from Bethel. There was still some distance to come to Ephrath, and Rachel travailed. She had hard labor.
When she was in hard labor, the midwife talk say to her, “No fear, for now You go have another son.”
As her soul was departing (for she died), she named him Benoni, but his father named him Benjamin.
Rachel died, and was buried on the way to Ephrath (also call Bethlehem).
Jacob set up a pillar on her grave. The same is the Pillar of Rachel’s grave to this day.
Israel traveled, and spread his tent beyond the tower of Eder.
While Israel lived in that land, Reuben go and lay with Bilhah, his father’s concubine, and Israel heard of it. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve.
The sons of Leah: Reuben (Jacob’s firstborn), Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
The sons of Bilhah (Rachel’s worker): Dan and Naphtali.
The sons of Zilpah (Leah’s worker): Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob, who were born to him in Paddan Aram.
Jacob come to Isaac his father, to Mamre, to Kiriath Arba (which is Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac lived as foreigners.
The days of Isaac were one hundred eighty years.
Isaac give up the spirit, and died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days. Esau and Jacob, his sons, buried him.
Now this is the history of the generations of Esau (that is, Edom).
Esau take his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah the daughter of Elon, the Hittite; and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, the Hivite;
and Basemath, Ishmael’s daughter, sister of Nebaioth.
Adah bore to Esau Eliphaz. Basemath bore Reuel.
Oholibamah bore Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These are the sons of Esau, who were born to him in the land of Canaan.

Esau take his wives, his sons, his daughters, and all the members of his household, with his livestock, all his animals, and all his possessions, which he had gathered in the land of Canaan, and go into a land away from his brother Jacob.
For dem substance was too great for dem to live together, and the land of dem travels no fit bear dem because of dem livestock.
Esau lived in the hill country of Seir. Esau is Edom.
This is the history of the generations of Esau the father of the Edomites in the hill country of Seir:
these are the names of Esau’s sons: Eliphaz, the son of Adah, the wife of Esau; and Reuel, the son of Basemath, the wife of Esau.
The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz.
Timna was concubine to Eliphaz, Esau’s son; and she bore to Eliphaz Amalek. These are the sons of Adah, Esau’s wife.
These are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the sons of Basemath, Esau’s wife.
These were the sons of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, Esau’s wife: she bore to Esau Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau: the sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,
chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek: these are the chiefs who come of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Adah.

These are the sons of Reuel, Esau’s son: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah: these are the chiefs who come of Reuel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basemath, Esau’s wife.
These are the sons of Oholibamah, Esau’s wife: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, chief Korah: these are the chiefs who come of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, Esau’s wife.
These are the sons of Esau (that is, Edom), and these are dem chiefs.
These are the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These are the chiefs who come of the Horites, the pikin dem of Seir in the land of Edom.
The pikin dem of Lotan were Hori and Heman. Lotan’s sister was Timna.
These are the pikin dem of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
These are the pikin dem of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. This is Anah who find the hot springs in the wilderness, as he fed the donkeys of Zibeon his father.
These are the pikin dem of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah.
These are the pikin dem of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
These are the pikin dem of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
These are the pikin dem of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
These are the chiefs who come of the Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,
chief Dishon, chief Ezer, and chief Dishan: these are the chiefs who come of the Horites, according to dem chiefs in the land of Seir.
These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom, before any king reigned over the pikin dem of Israel.
Bela, the son of Beor, reigned in Edom. The name of his city was Dinhabah.
Bela died, and Jobab, the son of Zerah of Bozrah, reigned in his place.
Jobab died, and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
Husham died, and Hadad, the son of Bedad, who struck Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place. The name of his city was Avith.
Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.
Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the river, reigned in his place.
Shaul died, and Baal Hanan, the son of Achbor reigned in his place.
Baal Hanan the son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his place. The name of his city was Pau. His wife’s name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.
These are the names of the chiefs who come from Esau, according to dem families, after dem places, and by dem names: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,
chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
chief Magdiel, and chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom, according to dem habitations in the land of dem possession. This is Esau, the father of the Edomites.
Jacob lived in the land of his father’s travels, in the land of Canaan.

This is the history of the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brothers. He was a boy with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s wives. Joseph bring an evil report of dem to dem father.
Now Israel love Joseph more than all his pikin dem, because he was the son of his old age, and he made him a coat of many colors.
His brothers see that dem father love him more than all his brothers, and dem hated him, and no fit speak peaceably to him.
Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brothers, and dem hated him all the more.
E tell dem say, “Please hear this dream which I have dreamed:
for see am, we were binding sheaves in the field, and see am, my sheaf arose and also stood upright; and see am, una sheaves come around, and bowed down to my sheaf.”
His brothers talk say to him, “Will you indeed reign over us? Or will you indeed have dominion over us?” Dem hated him all the more for his dreams and for his words.
He dreamed yet another dream, and told it to his brothers, and talk say, “See am, I have dreamed yet another dream: and see am, the sun and the moon and eleven stars bowed down to me.”

He told it to his father and to his brothers. His father rebuked him, and talk say to him, “Wetin be this dream that you have dreamed? Will I and una mother and una brothers indeed come to bow ourselves down to you to the earth?”
His brothers envied him, but his father kept this saying in mind.
His brothers go to feed dem father’s flock in Shechem.
Israel talk say to Joseph, “No be una brothers feeding the flock in Shechem? Come, and I go send you to dem.” E tell am say, “Here I be.”
E tell am say, “Go now, see whether it is well with una brothers, and well with the flock; and bring me word again.” So he sent him out of the valley of Hebron, and he come to Shechem.
A certain man find him, and see am, he was wandering in the field. The man ask him, “Wetin be you looking for?”
He talk say, “I be looking for my brothers. Tell me, please, where Dem be feeding the flock.”
The man talk say, “Dem have left here, for I heard dem say, ‘Make we go to Dothan.’” Joseph go after his brothers, and find dem in Dothan.
Dem see him far away off, and before he come near to dem, dem conspired against him to kill him.
Dem talk say to each other, “See am, this dreamer comes.
Come now so, and let’s kill him, and throw him into one of the pits, and We go say, ‘An evil animal has devoured him.’ We go see what will become of his dreams.”
Reuben heard it, and delivered him out of dem hand, and talk say, “Let’s not take his life.”
Reuben talk say to dem, “Shed no blood. Throw him into this pit that is in the wilderness, but lay no hand on him” — that he might deliver him out of dem hand, to restore him to his father.
When Joseph come to his brothers, dem stripped Joseph of his coat, the coat of many colors that was on him;
and dem take him, and threw him into the pit. The pit was empty. There was no water in it.

Dem sat down to eat bread, and dem lifted up dem eyes and looked, and see a caravan of Ishmaelites was coming from Gilead, with dem camels bearing spices and balm and myrrh, going to carry it down to Egypt.
Judah talk say to his brothers, “What profit is it if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?
Come, and let’s sell him to the Ishmaelites, and not let our hand be on him; for he is our brother, our flesh.” His brothers listened to him.
Midianites who were merchants passed by, and dem drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. Dem bring Joseph into Egypt.
Reuben come back to the pit; and see that Joseph no be in the pit; and he tore his clothes.
He come back to his brothers, and talk say, “The pikin is no more; and I, where will I go?”
Dem take Joseph’s coat, and killed a male goat, and dipped the coat in the blood.
Dem take the coat of many colors, and dem bring it to dem father, and talk say, “We have find this. Examine it, now, whether it is una son’s coat or not.”
He recognized it, and talk say, “It is my son’s coat. An evil animal has devoured him. Joseph is without doubt torn in pieces.”
Jacob tore his clothes, and put sackcloth on his waist, and mourned for his son many days.
All his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. He talk say, “For I go go down to Sheol to my son mourning.” His father wept for him.
The Midianites sold him into Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh’s, the captain of the guard.
At that time, Judah go down from his brothers, and visited a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah.
Judah see there a daughter of a certain Canaanite whose name was Shua. He take her, and go in to her.
She conceived, and bore a son; and he named him Er.
She conceived again, and bore a son; and she named him Onan.
She yet again bore a son, and named him Shelah: and he was at Chezib, when she bore him.
Judah take a wife for Er, his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in Baba God’s sight. Baba God killed him.
Judah talk say to Onan, “Go in to una brother’s wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother to her, and raise up offspring for una brother.”
Onan know that the offspring wouldn’t be his; and when he go in to his brother’s wife, he spilled it on the ground, lest he should give offspring to his brother.
The thing which he did was evil in Baba God’s sight, and he killed him also.

Then Judah talk say to Tamar, his daughter-in-law, “Remain a widow in una father’s house, until Shelah, my son, is grown up”; for he talk say, “Lest he also die, like his brothers.” Tamar go and lived in her father’s house.
After many days, Shua’s daughter, the wife of Judah, died. Judah was comforted, and go up to his sheep shearers to Timnah, he and his friend Hirah, the Adullamite.
Tamar was told, “See am, una father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.”

She take off of her the garments of her widowhood, and covered sheself with her veil, and wrapped sheself, and sat in the gate of Enaim, which is by the way to Timnah; for she see that Shelah was grown up, and she no be given to him as a wife.
When Judah see her, he thought that she was a prostitute, for she had covered her face.

He turned to her by the way, and talk say, “Please come, let me come in to you,” for he didn’t know that she was his daughter-in-law. She talk say, “What will you give me, that you may come in to me?”
He talk say, “I go send you a young goat from the flock.” She talk say, “Will you give me a pledge, until you send it?”
He talk say, “What pledge will I give you?” She talk say, “Una signet and una cord, and una staff that is in una hand.” He give dem to her, and come in to her, and she conceived by him.
She arose, and go away, and put off her veil from her, and put on the garments of her widowhood.
Judah sent the young goat by the hand of his friend, the Adullamite, to receive the pledge from the woman’s hand, but he didn’t find her.
Then he ask the men of her place, saying, “Where is the prostitute, that was at Enaim by the road?” Dem talk say, “There Don dey no prostitute here.”
He come back to Judah, and talk say, “I haven’t find her; and also the men of the place talk say, ‘There Don dey no prostitute here.’”
Judah talk say, “Make she keep it, lest we be shamed. See am, I sent this young goat, and you haven’t find her.”

About three months later, Judah was told, “Tamar, una daughter-in-law, has played the prostitute. Moreover, see am, she is with pikin by prostitution.” Judah talk say, “Bring her out, and Make she be burned.”

When she was bring out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, “By the man, whose these are, I be with pikin.” She also talk say, “Please discern whose are these — the signet, and the cords, and the staff.”
Judah acknowledged dem, and talk say, “She is more righteous than I, because I didn’t give her to Shelah, my son.” He know her again no more.
In the time of her travail, see am, twins were in her womb.
When she travailed, one put out a hand, and the midwife take and tied a scarlet thread on his hand, saying, “This come out first.”
As he drew back his hand, see am, his brother come out, and she talk say, “Why have you made a breach for yourself?” So his name was call Perez.
Afterward his brother come out, that had the scarlet thread on his hand, and his name was call Zerah.
Joseph was bring down to Egypt. Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh’s, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him from the hand of the Ishmaelites that had bring him down there.
Baba God was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man. He was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
His master see that Baba God was with him, and that Baba God made all that he did prosper in his hand.
Joseph find favor in his sight. He ministered to him, and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.

From the time that he made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, Baba God blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake. Baba God’s blessing was on all that he had, in the house and in the field.
He left all that he had in Joseph’s hand. He didn’t concern imself with anything, except for the chop which he ate. Joseph was well-built and handsome.
After these things, his master’s wife set her eyes on Joseph; and she talk say, “Lie with me.”
But he refused, and talk say to his master’s wife, “See am, my master no dey know Wetin be with me in the house, and he has put all that he has into my hand.
Nobody is greater in this house than I be, and he has not kept back anything from me but you, because You be his wife. How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?”
As she spoke to Joseph day by day, he didn’t listen to her, to lie by her, or to be with her.
About this time, he go into the house to do his work, and there were none of the men of the house inside.
She caught him by his garment, saying, “Lie with me!” He left his garment in her hand, and ran outside.
When she see that he had left his garment in her hand, and had run outside,
she call to the men of her house, and spoke to dem, saying, “See am, he has bring in a Hebrew to us to mock us. He come in to me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice.
When he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garment by me, and ran outside.”
She laid up his garment by her, until his master come home.
She spoke to him according to these words, saying, “The Hebrew worker, whom you have bring to us, come in to me to mock me,
and as I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garment by me, and ran outside.”
When his master heard the words of his wife, which she spoke to him, saying, “This is what una worker did to me,” his serious anger was kindled.
Joseph’s master take him, and put him into the prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were bound, and he was there in custody.
But Baba God was with Joseph, and showed kindness to him, and give him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
The keeper of the prison committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners who were in the prison. Anything wey dem did there, he was responsible for it.
The keeper of the prison didn’t look after anything that was under his hand, because Baba God was with him; and that which he did, Baba God made it prosper.
After these things, the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker offended dem lord, the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief cup bearer and the chief baker.
He put dem in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Joseph was bound.
The captain of the guard assigned dem to Joseph, and he take care of dem. Dem stayed in prison many days.
Dem both dreamed a dream, each man his dream, in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the cup bearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were bound in the prison.
Joseph come in to dem in the morning, and see dem, and see that dem were sad.
He ask Pharaoh’s officers who were with him in custody in his master’s house, saying, “Why do you look so sad today?”
Dem tell am say, “We have dreamed a dream, and E get Nobody who can interpret it.” Joseph talk say to dem, “No interpretations belong to God? Please tell it to me.”
The chief cup bearer told his dream to Joseph, and talk say to him, “In my dream, see am, a vine was in front of me,
and in the vine were three branches. It was as though it budded, it blossomed, and its clusters produced ripe grapes.
Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand; and I take the grapes, and pressed dem into Pharaoh’s cup, and I give the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.”
Joseph talk say to him, “This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.
Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up una head, and restore you to una office. You go give Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, the way you did when you were his cup bearer.
But remember me when it Go be well with you, and please show kindness to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.
For indeed, I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews, and here also I have done nothing that dem should put me into the dungeon.”
When the chief baker see that the interpretation was good, he talk say to Joseph, “I also was in my dream, and see am, three baskets of white bread were on my head.
In the uppermost basket there were all kinds of baked chop for Pharaoh, and the birds ate dem out of the basket on my head.”
Joseph answer, “This is its interpretation. The three baskets are three days.
Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up una head from off you, and will hang you on a tree; and the birds will eat una flesh from off you.”
On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he made a feast for all his workers, and he lifted up the head of the chief cup bearer and the head of the chief baker among his workers.
He restored the chief cup bearer to his position again, and he give the cup into Pharaoh’s hand;
but he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted to dem.
Yet the chief cup bearer didn’t remember Joseph, but forgot him.
At the end of two full years, Pharaoh dreamed: and see am, he stood by the river.
See am, there come up out of the river seven cattle, sleek and fat, and dem fed in the marsh grass.
See am, seven other cattle come up after dem out of the river, ugly and thin, and stood by the other cattle on the brink of the river.
The ugly and thin cattle ate up the seven sleek and fat cattle. So Pharaoh awoke.
He slept and dreamed a second time: and see am, seven heads of grain come up on one stalk, healthy and good.
See am, seven heads of grain, thin and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after dem.
The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven healthy and full ears. Pharaoh awoke, and see am, it was a dream.
In the morning, his spirit was troubled, and he sent and call for all of Egypt’s magicians and wise men. Pharaoh told dem his dreams, but there was Nobody who could interpret dem to Pharaoh.
Then the chief cup bearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, “I remember my faults today.
Pharaoh was angry with his workers, and put me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, me and the chief baker.
We dreamed a dream in one night, I and he. We dreamed each man according to the interpretation of his dream.
There was with us there a young man, a Hebrew, worker to the captain of the guard, and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams. To each man according to his dream he interpreted.
As he interpreted to us, so it was. He restored me to my office, and he hanged him.”
Then Pharaoh sent and call Joseph, and dem bring him hastily out of the dungeon. He shaved imself, changed his clothing, and come in to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh talk say to Joseph, “I have dreamed a dream, and E get Nobody who can interpret it. I have heard it talk say of you, that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.”
Joseph answer Pharaoh, saying, “It no be in me. God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.”
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, “In my dream, see am, I stood on the brink of the river:
and see am, there come up out of the river seven cattle, fat and sleek. Dem fed in the marsh grass,
and see am, seven other cattle come up after dem, poor and very ugly and thin, such as I never see in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.
The thin and ugly cattle ate up the first seven fat cattle,
and when dem had eaten dem up, it no fit be known that dem had eaten dem, but dem were still ugly, as at the beginning. So I awoke.
I see in my dream, and see am, seven heads of grain come up on one stalk, full and good:
and see am, seven heads of grain, withered, thin, and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after dem.
The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven good heads of grain. I told it to the magicians, but there was Nobody who could explain it to me.”
Joseph talk say to Pharaoh, “The dream of Pharaoh is one. What God is about to do he has declared to Pharaoh.
The seven good cattle are seven years; and the seven good heads of grain are seven years. The dream is one.
The seven thin and ugly cattle that come up after dem are seven years, and also the seven empty heads of grain blasted with the east wind; Dem go be seven years of famine.
That is the thing which I spoke to Pharaoh. What God is about to do he has shown to Pharaoh.
See am, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt.
There will arise after dem seven years of famine, and all the plenty Go be forgotten in the land of Egypt. The famine will consume the land,
and the plenty No go be known in the land by reason of that famine which follows; for it Go be very grievous.
The dream was doubled to Pharaoh, because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.
“Now so let Pharaoh look for a discreet and wise man, and set him over the land of Egypt.
Let Pharaoh do this, and Make e appoint overseers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt’s produce in the seven plenteous years.
Make dem gather all the chop of these good years that come, and lay up grain under the hand of Pharaoh for chop in the cities, and Make dem keep it.
The chop Go be for a store to the land against the seven years of famine, which Go be in the land of Egypt; that the land not perish through the famine.”
The thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his workers.
Pharaoh talk say to his workers, “Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom is the Spirit of God?”
Pharaoh talk say to Joseph, “Because God has shown you all of this, E get Nobody so discreet and wise as you.
You go be over my house, and according to una word will all my people be ruled. Only in the throne I go be greater than you.”
Pharaoh talk say to Joseph, “See am, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.”
Pharaoh take off his signet ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck,
and he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had. Dem cried before him, “Bow the knee!” He set him over all the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh talk say to Joseph, “I be Pharaoh, and without you shall no man lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.”
Pharaoh call Joseph’s name Zaphenath-Paneah; and he give him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On as a wife. Joseph go out over the land of Egypt.
Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. Joseph go out from the presence of Pharaoh, and go throughout all the land of Egypt.
In the seven plenteous years the earth produced abundantly.
He gathered up all the chop of the seven years which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the chop in the cities: the chop of the field, which was around every city, he laid up in the same.
Joseph laid up grain as the sand of the sea, well-well, until he stopped counting, for it was without number.
To Joseph were born two sons before the year of famine come, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On, bore to him.
Joseph call the name of the firstborn Manasseh, “For”, he talk say, “God has made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.”
The name of the second, he call Ephraim: “For God has made me fruitful in the land of my suffering.”
The seven years of plenty, that were in the land of Egypt, come to an end.
The seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had talk say. There was famine in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
When all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread, and Pharaoh talk say to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do.”
The famine was over all the surface of the earth. Joseph opened all the store houses, and sold to the Egyptians. The famine was severe in the land of Egypt.
All countries come into Egypt, to Joseph, to buy grain, because the famine was severe in all the earth.
Now Jacob see that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob talk say to his sons, “Why do you look at each other?”
He talk say, “See am, I have heard that E get grain in Egypt. Go down there, and buy for us from there, so that we may live, and not die.”
Joseph’s ten brothers go down to buy grain from Egypt.
But Jacob didn’t send Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, with his brothers; for he talk say, “Lest perhaps harm happen to him.”
The sons of Israel come to buy among people wey come, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
Joseph was the governor over the land. It was person wey sold to all the people of the land. Joseph’s brothers come, and bowed themselves down to him with dem faces to the earth.

Joseph see his brothers, and he recognized dem, but acted like a stranger to dem, and spoke roughly with dem. E tell dem say, “Where did you come from?” Dem talk say, “From the land of Canaan to buy chop.”
Joseph recognized his brothers, but dem didn’t recognize him.
Joseph remember the dreams which he dreamed about dem, and talk say to dem, “You be spies! You have come to see the nakedness of the land.”
Dem tell am say, “No, my lord, but una workers have come to buy chop.
We be all one man’s sons; We be honest men. Una workers No be spies.”
E tell dem say, “No, but you have come to see the nakedness of the land!”
Dem talk say, “We, una workers, are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and see am, the youngest is today with our father, and one is no more.”
Joseph talk say to dem, “It is like I told you, saying, ‘You be spies!’
By this you go be tested. By the life of Pharaoh, you no go go out from here, unless una youngest brother comes here.
Send one of you, and Make e get una brother, and you go be bound, that una words may be tested, whether E get truth in you, or else by the life of Pharaoh surely You be spies.”
He put dem all together into custody for three days.
Joseph talk say to dem the third day, “Do this, and live, for I fear God.
If You be honest men, then let one of una brothers be bound in una prison; but you go, carry grain for the famine of una houses.
Bring una youngest brother to me; so will una words be verified, and you no go die.” Dem did so.
Dem talk say to each other, “We be certainly guilty concerning our brother, in that we see the distress of his soul, when he begged us, and we wouldn’t listen. So this distress has come upon us.”
Reuben answer dem, saying, “Didn’t I tell una, saying, ‘No sin against the pikin,’ and you wouldn’t listen? So also, see am, his blood is required.”
Dem didn’t know that Joseph understand dem; for there was an interpreter between dem.
He turned imself away from dem, and wept. Then he come back to dem, and spoke to dem, and take Simeon from among dem, and bound him before dem eyes.
Then Joseph give a command to fill dem bags with grain, and to restore each man’s money into his sack, and to give dem chop for the way. So it was done to dem.
Dem loaded dem donkeys with dem grain, and comot from there.
As one of dem opened his sack to give his donkey chop in the lodging place, he see his money. See am, it was in the mouth of his sack.
He talk say to his brothers, “My money is restored! See am, it is in my sack!” Dem hearts failed dem, and dem turned trembling to each other, saying, “Wetin be this that God has done to us?”
Dem come to Jacob dem father, to the land of Canaan, and told him all that had happened to dem, saying,
“The man, the lord of the land, spoke roughly with us, and take us for spies of the country.
We talk say to him, ‘We be honest men. We be no spies.
We be twelve brothers, sons of our father; one is no more, and the youngest is today with our father in the land of Canaan.’
The man, the lord of the land, talk say to us, ‘By this I go know that You be honest men: leave one of una brothers with me, and take grain for the famine of una houses, and go una way.
Bring una youngest brother to me. Then I go know that you No be spies, but that You be honest men. So I go deliver una brother to you, and you shall trade in the land.’”
As dem emptied dem sacks, see am, each man’s bundle of money was in his sack. When dem and dem father see dem bundles of money, dem were afraid.
Jacob, dem father, talk say to dem, “You have bereaved me of my pikin dem! Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and you want to take Benjamin away. All these things are against me.”
Reuben spoke to his father, saying, “Kill my two sons, if I no bring him to you. Entrust him to my care, and I go bring him to you again.”

He talk say, “My son no go go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he only is left. If harm happens to him along the way in which you go, then You go bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.”
The famine was severe in the land.
When dem had eaten up the grain which dem had bring out of Egypt, dem father talk say to dem, “Go again, buy us a little more chop.”
Judah spoke to him, saying, “The man solemnly warned us, saying, ‘You no go see my face, unless una brother is with you.’
If you’ll send our brother with us, we’ll go down and buy you chop,
but if you’ll not send him, we’ll not go down, for the man talk say to us, ‘You no go see my face, unless una brother is with you.’”
Israel talk say, “Why did you treat me so badly, telling the man that you had another brother?”

Dem talk say, “The man ask directly concerning ourselves, and concerning our relatives, saying, ‘Is una father still alive? Have you another brother?’ We just answer his questions. Is there any way we could know that he would say, ‘Bring una brother down?’”
Judah talk say to Israel, his father, “Send the boy with me, and we’ll get up and go, so that we may live, and not die, both we, and you, and also our little ones.
I’ll be collateral for him. From my hand will you require him. If I no bring him to you, and set him before you, then let me bear the blame forever,
for if we hadn’t delayed, surely we would have come back a second time by now.”

Dem father, Israel, talk say to dem, “If it must be so, then do this. Take from the choice fruits of the land in una bags, and carry down a present for the man, a little balm, a little honey, spices and myrrh, nuts, and almonds;
and take double money in una hand, and take back the money that was come back in the mouth of una sacks. Perhaps it was an oversight.
Take una brother also, get up, and return to the man.
May God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may release to you una other brother and Benjamin. If I be bereaved of my pikin dem, I be bereaved.”
The men take that present, and dem take double money in dem hand, and Benjamin; and got up, go down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
When Joseph see Benjamin with dem, he talk say to the steward of his house, “Bring the men into the house, and butcher an animal, and prepare; for the men will dine with me at noon.”
The man did as Joseph commanded, and the man bring the men to Joseph’s house.

The men were afraid, because dem were bring to Joseph’s house; and dem talk say, “Because of the money that was come back in our sacks at the first time, we’re bring in; that he may seek occasion against us, attack us, and seize us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”
Dem come near to the steward of Joseph’s house, and dem spoke to him at the door of the house,
and talk say, “Oh, my lord, we indeed come down the first time to buy chop.
When we come to the lodging place, we opened our sacks, and see am, each man’s money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight. We have bring it back in our hand.
We have bring down other money in our hand to buy chop. We no know who put our money in our sacks.”
He talk say, “Peace be to you. No fear. Una God, and the God of una father, has given you treasure in una sacks. I received una money.” He bring Simeon out to dem.
The man bring the men into Joseph’s house, and give dem water, and dem washed dem feet. He give dem donkeys fodder.
Dem prepared the present for Joseph’s coming at noon, for dem heard that dem should eat bread there.
When Joseph come home, dem bring him the present which was in dem hand into the house, and bowed themselves down to him to the earth.
He ask dem of dem welfare, and talk say, “Is una father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he yet alive?”
Dem talk say, “Una worker, our father, is well. He is still alive.” Dem bowed down humbly.
He lifted up his eyes, and see Benjamin, his brother, his mother’s son, and talk say, “Is this una youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?” He talk say, “God be gracious to you, my son.”
Joseph hurried, for his heart yearned over his brother; and he sought a place to weep. He entered into his room, and wept there.
He washed his face, and come out. He controlled imself, and talk say, “Serve the meal.”
Dem served him by imself, and dem by themselves, and the Egyptians, that ate with him, by themselves, because the Egyptians no eat bread with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to the Egyptians.
Dem sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth, and the men surprise well-well one with another.
He sent portions to dem from before him, but Benjamin’s portion was five times as much as any of dem own. Dem drank, and were merry with him.
He commanded the steward of his house, saying, “Fill the men’s sacks with chop, as much as dem can carry, and put each man’s money in his sack’s mouth.
Put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, with his grain money.” He did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, dem and dem donkeys.
When dem had gone out of the city, and No be yet far off, Joseph talk say to his steward, “Up, follow after the men. When you overtake dem, ask dem, ‘Why have you rewarded evil for good?
