No be this that from which my lord drinks, and by which he indeed divines? You have done evil in so doing.’”
He overtook dem, and he spoke these words to dem.
Dem tell am say, “Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from una workers that dem should do such a thing!
See am, the money, which we find in our sacks’ mouths, we bring again to you out of the land of Canaan. How then should we steal silver or gold out of una lord’s house?
With whomever of una workers it is find, Make e die, and we also Go be my lord’s slaves.”
He talk say, “Now also let it be according to una words: he with whom it is find Go be my slave; and You go be blameless.”
Then dem hurried, and each man take his sack down to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
He searched, beginning with the oldest, and ending at the youngest. The cup was find in Benjamin’s sack.
Then dem tore dem clothes, and each man loaded his donkey, and come back to the city.
Judah and his brothers come to Joseph’s house, and he was still there. Dem fell on the ground before him.
Joseph talk say to dem, “What deed is this that you have done? No you know that such a man as I can indeed divine?”

Judah talk say, “What will we tell my lord? What will we speak? Or how will we clear ourselves? God has find out the wickedness of una workers. See am, We be my lord’s slaves, both we, and he also in whose hand the cup is find.”
He talk say, “Far be it from me that I should do so. The man in whose hand the cup is find, he Go be my slave; but as for you, go up in peace to una father.”
Then Judah come near to him, and talk say, “Oh, my lord, please let una worker speak a word in my lord’s ears, and no let una anger burn against una worker; for You be even as Pharaoh.
My lord ask his workers, saying, ‘Have you a father, or a brother?’
We talk say to my lord, ‘We have a father, an old man, and a pikin of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother; and his father loves him.’
You talk say to una workers, ‘Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes on him.’
We talk say to my lord, ‘The boy no fit leave his father: for if he should leave his father, his father would die.’
You talk say to una workers, ‘Unless una youngest brother comes down with you, You go see my face no more.’
When we come up to una worker my father, we told him the words of my lord.
Our father talk say, ‘Go again, buy us a little chop.’
We talk say, ‘We no fit go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then We go go down: for we may not see the man’s face, unless our youngest brother is with us.’
Una worker, my father, talk say to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons:
and the one go out from me, and I talk say, “Surely he is torn in pieces”; and I haven’t seen him since.
If you take this one also from me, and harm happens to him, You go bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.’
Now so when I come to una worker my father, and the boy No be with us; since his life is bound up in the boy’s life;
it will happen, when he sees that the boy is no more, that he will die. Una workers will bring down the gray hairs of una worker, our father, with sorrow to Sheol.
For una worker became collateral for the boy to my father, saying, ‘If I no bring him to you, then I go bear the blame to my father forever.’
Now so, please let una worker stay instead of the boy, my lord’s slave; and let the boy go up with his brothers.
For how will I go up to my father, if the boy no be with me? — lest I see the evil that will come on my father.”
Then Joseph no fit control imself before all people wey stood before him, and he cried, “Cause everyone to go out from me!” Nobody else stood with him, while Joseph made imself known to his brothers.
He wept aloud. The Egyptians heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.
Joseph talk say to his brothers, “I be Joseph! Does my father still live?” His brothers no fit answer him; for dem were terrified at his presence.
Joseph talk say to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.” Dem come near. “He talk say, I be Joseph, una brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
Now no be grieved, nor angry with unaself, that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.
For these two years the famine Don dey in the land, and E get yet five years, in which there Go be no plowing and no harvest.
God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant in the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance.
So now it no be you who sent me here, but God, and he has made me a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
Hurry, and go up to my father, and tell him, ‘This is what una son Joseph says, “God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me. No wait.
You shall live in the land of Goshen, and You go be near to me, you, una pikin dem, una pikin dem’s pikin dem, una flocks, una herds, and all that you have.
There I go nourish you; for E get yet five years of famine; lest you come to poverty, you, and una household, and all that you have.”’
See am, una eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.
You shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that you have seen. You shall hurry and bring my father down here.”
He fell on his brother Benjamin’s neck, and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
He kissed all his brothers, and wept on dem. After that his brothers talked with him.
The report of it was heard in Pharaoh’s house, saying, “Joseph’s brothers have come.” It pleased Pharaoh well, and his workers.
Pharaoh talk say to Joseph, “Tell una brothers, ‘Do this. Load una animals, and go, travel to the land of Canaan.
Take una father and una households, and come to me, and I go give you the good of the land of Egypt, and You go eat the fat of the land.’
Now You be commanded: do this. Take wagons out of the land of Egypt for una little ones, and for una wives, and bring una father, and come.
Also, no concern unaself about una belongings, for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.”
The sons of Israel did so. Joseph give dem wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and give dem provision for the way.
He give each one of dem changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he give three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.
He sent the following to his father: ten donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provision for his father by the way.
So he sent his brothers away, and dem comot. E tell dem say, “See that you no quarrel on the way.”
Dem go up out of Egypt, and come into the land of Canaan, to Jacob dem father.
Dem told him, saying, “Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.” His heart fainted, for he didn’t believe dem.
Dem told him all the words of Joseph, which he had talk say to dem. When he see the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob, dem father, revived.
Israel talk say, “It is enough. Joseph my son is still alive. I go go and see him before I die.”
Israel traveled with all that he had, and come to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father, Isaac.
God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night, and talk say, “Jacob, Jacob!” He talk say, “Here I be.”
He talk say, “I be God, the God of una father. No fear to go down into Egypt, for there I go make of you a great nation.
I go go down with you into Egypt. I go also surely bring you up again. Joseph will close una eyes.”
Jacob rose up from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried Jacob, dem father, dem little ones, and dem wives, in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
Dem take dem livestock, and dem goods, which dem had gotten in the land of Canaan, and come into Egypt — Jacob, and all his offspring with him,
his sons, and his sons’ sons with him, his daughters, and his sons’ daughters, and he bring all his offspring with him into Egypt.
These are the names of the pikin dem of Israel, who come into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn.
The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman.
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Iob, and Shimron.
The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan Aram, with his daughter Dinah. All the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty-three.
The sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and Serah dem sister. The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban give to Leah, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob, even sixteen souls.
The sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife: Joseph and Benjamin.
To Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him.
The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
These are the sons of Rachel, who were born to Jacob: all the souls were fourteen.
The son of Dan: Hushim.
The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban give to Rachel, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob: all the souls were seven.
All the souls who come with Jacob into Egypt, who were his direct offspring, besides Jacob’s sons’ wives, all the souls were sixty-six.
The sons of Joseph, who were born to him in Egypt, were two souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob, who come into Egypt, were seventy.
He sent Judah before him to Joseph, to show the way before him to Goshen, and dem come into the land of Goshen.
Joseph prepared his chariot, and go up to meet Israel, his father, in Goshen. He presented imself to him, and fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.
Israel talk say to Joseph, “Now let me die, since I have seen una face, that You be still alive.”

Joseph talk say to his brothers, and to his father’s house, “I go go up, and speak with Pharaoh, and will tell him, ‘My brothers, and my father’s house, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.
These men are shepherds, for dem Don dey keepers of livestock, and dem have bring dem flocks, and dem herds, and all that dem have.’
It will happen, when Pharaoh summons you, and will say, ‘Wetin be una occupation?’

that you shall say, ‘Una workers Don dey keepers of livestock from our youth even until now, both we, and our fathers:’ that you may live in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians.”

Then Joseph go in and told Pharaoh, and talk say, “My father and my brothers, with dem flocks, dem herds, and all that dem own, have come out of the land of Canaan; and see am, Dem be in the land of Goshen.”
From among his brothers he take five men, and presented dem to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh talk say to his brothers, “Wetin be una occupation?” Dem talk say to Pharaoh, “Una workers are shepherds, both we, and our fathers.”

Dem talk say to Pharaoh, “We have come to live as foreigners in the land, for E get no pasture for una workers’ flocks. For the famine is severe in the land of Canaan. Now so, please let una workers live in the land of Goshen.”
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, “Una father and una brothers have come to you.

The land of Egypt is before you. Make una father and una brothers live in the best of the land. Make dem live in the land of Goshen. If you know any able men among dem, then put dem in charge of my livestock.”
Joseph bring in Jacob, his father, and set him before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
Pharaoh talk say to Jacob, “How many are the days of the years of una life?”

Jacob talk say to Pharaoh, “The days of the years of my pilgrimage are one hundred thirty years. Few and evil Don dey the days of the years of my life, and dem have not attained to the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of dem pilgrimage.”
Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and go out from the presence of Pharaoh.
Joseph placed his father and his brothers, and give dem a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
Joseph nourished his father, his brothers, and all of his father’s household, with bread, according to dem families.
There was no bread in all the land; for the famine was very severe, so that the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan fainted by reason of the famine.
Joseph gathered up all the money that was find in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the grain which dem bought: and Joseph bring the money into Pharaoh’s house.

When the money was all spent in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians come to Joseph, and talk say, “Give us bread, for why should we die in una presence? For our money fails.”
Joseph talk say, “Give me una livestock; and I go give you chop for una livestock, if una money is gone.”

Dem bring dem livestock to Joseph, and Joseph give dem bread in exchange for the horses, and for the flocks, and for the herds, and for the donkeys: and he fed dem with bread in exchange for all dem livestock for that year.

When that year was ended, dem come to him the second year, and talk say to him, “We go not hide from my lord how our money is all spent, and the herds of livestock are my lord’s. E get nothing left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands.

Why should we die before una eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land Go be workers to Pharaoh. Give us seed, that we may live, and not die, and that the land no go be desolate.”
So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, for every man of the Egyptians sold his field, because the famine was severe on dem, and the land became Pharaoh’s.
As for the people, he moved dem to the cities from one end of the border of Egypt even to the other end of it.
Only he didn’t buy the land of the priests, for the priests had a portion from Pharaoh, and ate dem portion which Pharaoh give dem. That is why dem didn’t sell dem land.
Then Joseph talk say to the people, “See am, I have bought you and una land today for Pharaoh. See am, here is seed for you, and you shall sow the land.

It will happen at the harvests, that you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four parts Go be una own, for seed of the field, for una chop, for dem of una households, and for chop for una little ones.”
Dem talk say, “You have saved our lives! Make we find favor in the sight of my lord, and We go be Pharaoh’s workers.”
Joseph made it a statute concerning the land of Egypt to this day, that Pharaoh should have the fifth. Only the land of the priests alone didn’t become Pharaoh’s.
Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; and dem got themselves possessions inside am, and were fruitful, and multiplied exceedingly.
Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years. So the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were one hundred forty-seven years.

The time come near that Israel must die, and he call his son Joseph, and talk say to him, “If now I have find favor in una sight, please put una hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly with me. Please no bury me in Egypt,
but when I sleep with my fathers, you shall carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in dem burying place.” He talk say, “I go do as you have talk say.”
He talk say, “Swear to me,” and he swore to him. Israel bowed imself on the bed’s head.
After these things, someone talk say to Joseph, “See am, una father is sick.” He take with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
Someone told Jacob, and talk say, “See am, una son Joseph comes to you,” and Israel strengthened imself, and sat on the bed.
Jacob talk say to Joseph, “God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,
and talk say to me, ‘See am, I go make you fruitful, and multiply you, and I go make of you a company of peoples, and will give this land to una offspring after you for an everlasting possession.’
Now una two sons, who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I come to you into Egypt, are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh, even as Reuben and Simeon, Go be mine.
Una issue, whom you become the father of after dem, Go be yours. Dem go be call after the name of dem brothers in dem inheritance.

As for me, when I come from Paddan, Rachel died by me in the land of Canaan on the way, when there was still some distance to come to Ephrath, and I buried her there on the way to Ephrath (also call Bethlehem).”
Israel see Joseph’s sons, and talk say, “Wey be these?”
Joseph talk say to his father, “Dem be my sons, whom God has given me here.” He talk say, “Please bring dem to me, and I go bless dem.”
Now the eyes of Israel were dim for age, so that he no fit see. He bring dem near to him; and he kissed dem, and embraced dem.
Israel talk say to Joseph, “I didn’t think I would see una face, and see am, God has let me see una offspring also.”
Joseph bring dem out from between his knees, and he bowed imself with his face to the earth.
Joseph take dem both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel’s right hand, and bring dem near to him.
Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it on Ephraim’s head, who was the younger, and his left hand on Manasseh’s head, guiding his hands knowingly, for Manasseh was the firstborn.
He blessed Joseph, and talk say, “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has fed me all my life long to this day,
the angel who has redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads, and let my name be named on dem, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac. Make dem grow into a plenty people upon the earth.”
When Joseph see that his father laid his right hand on the head of Ephraim, it displeased him. He held up his father’s hand, to remove it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s head.
Joseph talk say to his father, “Not so, my father; for this is the firstborn; put una right hand on his head.”

His father refused, and talk say, “I know, my son, I know. He also will become a people, and he also Go be great. However, his younger brother Go be greater than he, and his offspring will become a plenty people of nations.”
He blessed dem that day, saying, “In You go Israel bless, saying, ‘God make you as Ephraim and as Manasseh’” He set Ephraim before Manasseh.
Israel talk say to Joseph, “See am, I be dying, but God Go be with you, and bring you again to the land of una fathers.
Moreover I have given to you one portion above una brothers, which I take out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.”
Jacob call to his sons, and talk say: “Gather unaself together, that I may tell you that which will happen to you in the days to come.
Assemble unaself, and hear, you sons of Jacob. Listen to Israel, una father.
“Reuben, You be my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength; excelling in dignity, and excelling in power.
Boiling over like water, you no go excel; because you go up to una father’s bed, then defiled it. He go up to my couch.
“Simeon and Levi are brothers. Dem swords are weapons of violence.
My soul, no come into dem council. My glory, no be united to dem assembly; for in dem anger dem killed men. In dem self-will dem hamstrung cattle.
Cursed be dem anger, for it was fierce; and dem serious anger, for it was cruel. I go divide dem in Jacob, and scatter dem in Israel.
“Judah, una brothers will praise you. Una hand Go be on the neck of una enemies. Una father’s sons will bow down before you.
Judah is a lion’s cub. From the prey, my son, you have gone up. He stooped down, he crouched as a lion, as a lioness. Who will rouse him up?
The scepter No go depart from Judah, nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet, until he comes to whom it belongs. To him will the obedience of the peoples be.
Binding his foal to the vine, his donkey’s colt to the choice vine; he has washed his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.
His eyes Go be red with wine, his teeth white with milk.
“Zebulun will live at the haven of the sea. He Go be for a haven of ships. His border Go be on Sidon.
“Issachar is a strong donkey, lying down between the saddlebags.
He see a resting place, that it was good, the land, that it was pleasant. He bows his shoulder to the burden, and becomes a worker doing forced labor.
“Dan will judge his people, as one of the tribes of Israel.
Dan Go be a serpent on the trail, an adder in the path, That bites the horse’s heels, so that his rider falls backward.
I have waited for una salvation, Baba God.
“A troop will press on Gad, but he will press on dem heel.
“Asher’s chop Go be rich. He will produce royal dainties.
“Naphtali is a doe set free, who bears beautiful fawns.
“Joseph is a fruitful vine, a fruitful vine by a spring. His branches run over the wall.
The archers have severely grieved him, shot at him, and persecute him:
But his bow remain strong. The arms of his hands were made strong, by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, (from E get the shepherd, the stone of Israel),

even by the God of una father, who will help you; by the Almighty, who will bless you, with blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that lies below, blessings of the breasts, and of the womb.

The blessings of una father have prevailed above the blessings of una ancestors, above the boundaries of the ancient hills. Dem go be on the head of Joseph, on the crown of the head of him Wey be separated from his brothers.
“Benjamin is a ravenous wolf. In the morning he will devour the prey. At evening he will divide the plunder.”
All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what dem father spoke to dem and blessed dem. He blessed everyone according to his blessing.
He instructed dem, and talk say to dem, “I be to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
in the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, which is before Mamre, in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought with the field from Ephron the Hittite as a burial place.
There dem buried Abraham and Sarah, his wife. There dem buried Isaac and Rebekah, his wife, and there I buried Leah:
the field and the cave that is inside am, which was purchased from the pikin dem of Heth.”
When Jacob finished charging his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the spirit, and was gathered to his people.
Joseph fell on his father’s face, wept on him, and kissed him.
Joseph commanded his workers, the physicians, to embalm his father; and the physicians embalmed Israel.
Forty days were fulfilled for him, for that is how many the days it takes to embalm. The Egyptians wept for him for seventy days.
When the days of weeping for him were past, Joseph spoke to the house of Pharaoh, saying, “If now I have find favor in una eyes, please speak in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,
‘My father made me swear, saying, “See am, I be dying. Bury me in my grave which I have dug for myself in the land of Canaan.” Now so, please let me go up and bury my father, and I go come again.’”
Pharaoh talk say, “Go up, and bury una father, just like he made you swear.”
Joseph go up to bury his father; and with him go up all the workers of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, all the elders of the land of Egypt,
All the house of Joseph, his brothers, and his father’s house. Only dem little ones, dem flocks, and dem herds, dem left in the land of Goshen.
There go up with him both chariots and horsemen. It was a plenty well-well company.
Dem come to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and there dem lamented with a plenty well-well and severe lamentation. He mourned for his father seven days.

When the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, see the mourning in the floor of Atad, dem talk say, “This is a grievous mourning by the Egyptians.” So its name was call Abel Mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan.
His sons did to him just as he commanded dem,

for his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field, for a possession of a burial site, from Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.
Joseph come back into Egypt — he, and his brothers, and all that go up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.
When Joseph’s brothers see that dem father was dead, dem talk say, “It may be that Joseph will hate us, and will fully pay us back for all the evil which we did to him.”
Dem sent a message to Joseph, saying, “Una father commanded before he died, saying,

‘You shall tell Joseph, “Now please forgive the disobedience of una brothers, and dem sin, because dem did evil to you.”’ Now, please forgive the disobedience of the workers of the God of una father.” Joseph wept when dem spoke to him.
His brothers also go and fell down before his face; and dem talk say, “See am, We be una workers.”
Joseph talk say to dem, “No fear, for am I in the place of God?
As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring to pass, as it is today, to save many people alive.
Now so No fear. I go nourish you and una little ones.” He comforted dem, and spoke kindly to dem.
Joseph lived in Egypt, he, and his father’s house. Joseph lived one hundred ten years.
Joseph see Ephraim’s pikin dem to the third generation. The pikin dem also of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born on Joseph’s knees.
Joseph talk say to his brothers, “I be dying, but God will surely visit you, and bring you up out of this land to the land which he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.”
Joseph take an oath of the pikin dem of Israel, saying, “God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here.”
So Joseph died, being one hundred ten years old, and dem embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.
Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who come into Egypt (every man and his household come with Jacob):
Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,
Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,
Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
All the souls who come out of Jacob’s body were seventy souls, and Joseph was in Egypt already.
Joseph died, as did all his brothers, and all that generation.
The pikin dem of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and grew exceedingly mighty; and the land was filled with dem.
Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who didn’t know Joseph.
He talk say to his people, “See am, the people of the pikin dem of Israel are more and mightier than we.
Come, Make we deal wisely with dem, lest dem multiply, and it happen that when any war breaks out, dem also join themselves to our enemies, and fight against us, and escape out of the land.”
So dem set taskmasters over dem to afflict dem with dem burdens. Dem built storage cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Raamses.
But the more dem afflicted dem, the more dem multiplied and the more dem spread out. Dem were grieved because of the pikin dem of Israel.
The Egyptians ruthlessly made the pikin dem of Israel serve,
and dem made dem lives bitter with hard service, in mortar and in brick, and in all kinds of service in the field, all dem service, in which dem ruthlessly made dem serve.
The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah,
and he talk say, “When you perform the duty of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see dem on the birth stool; if it is a son, then you shall kill him; but if it is a daughter, then she shall live.”
But the midwives feared God, and didn’t do what the king of Egypt commanded dem, but saved the baby boys alive.
The king of Egypt call for the midwives, and talk say to dem, “Why have you done this thing, and have saved the boys alive?”
The midwives talk say to Pharaoh, “Because the Hebrew women no be like the Egyptian women; for Dem be vigorous, and give birth before the midwife comes to dem.”
God dealt well with the midwives, and the people multiplied, and grew very mighty.
Because the midwives feared God, he give dem families.
Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, “You shall throw every son Wey be born into the river, and every daughter you shall save alive.”
A man of the house of Levi go and take a daughter of Levi as his wife.
The woman conceived, and bore a son. When she see that he was a fine pikin, she hid him three months.
When she could no longer hide him, she take a papyrus basket for him, and coated it with tar and with pitch. She put the pikin in it, and laid it in the reeds by the river’s bank.
His sister stood far off, to see what would be done to him.
Pharaoh’s daughter come down to bathe at the river. Her maidens walked along by the riverside. She see the basket among the reeds, and sent her worker to get it.
She opened it, and see the pikin, and see am, the baby cried. She had compassion on him, and talk say, “This is one of the Hebrews’ pikin dem.”
Then his sister talk say to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Should I go and call a nurse for you from the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the pikin for you?”
Pharaoh’s daughter talk say to her, “Go.” The maiden go and call the pikin’s mother.
Pharaoh’s daughter talk say to her, “Take this pikin away, and nurse him for me, and I go give you una wages.” The woman take the pikin, and nursed it.
The pikin grew, and she bring him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, and talk say, “Because I drew him out of the water.”
In those days, when Moses had grown up, he go out to his brothers, and looked at dem burdens. He see an Egyptian striking a Hebrew, one of his brothers.
He looked this way and that way, and when he see that there was Nobody, he killed the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
He go out the second day, and see am, two men of the Hebrews were fighting with each other. E tell am say who did the wrong, “Why do you strike una fellow?”
He talk say, “Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Do you plan to kill me, as you killed the Egyptian?” Moses was afraid, and talk say, “Surely this thing is known.”
Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and lived in the land of Midian, and he sat down by a well.
Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters. Dem come and drew water, and filled the troughs to water dem father’s flock.
The shepherds come and drove dem away; but Moses stood up and helped dem, and watered dem flock.
When dem come to Reuel, dem father, he talk say, “How is it that you have come back so early today?”
Dem talk say, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and moreover he drew water for us, and watered the flock.”
He talk say to his daughters, “Where is he? Why is it that you have left the man? Call him, that he may eat bread.”
Moses was content to live with the man. He give Moses Zipporah, his daughter.
She bore a son, and he named him Gershom, for he talk say, “I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign land.”
In the course of those many days, the king of Egypt died, and the pikin dem of Israel sighed because of the bondage, and dem cried, and dem cry come up to God because of the bondage.
God heard dem groaning, and God remember his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
God see the pikin dem of Israel, and God was concerned about dem.
Now Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro, his father-in-law, the priest of Midian, and he led the flock to the back of the wilderness, and come to God’s mountain, to Horeb.
Baba God’s angel appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the middle of a bush. He looked, and see am, the bush burned with fire, and the bush No be consumed.
Moses talk say, “I go turn aside now, and see this great sight, why the bush No be burned.”
When Baba God see that he turned aside to see, God call to him out of the middle of the bush, and talk say, “Moses! Moses!” He talk say, “Here I be.”
He talk say, “No come close. Take una sandals off of una feet, for the place You be standing on is holy ground.”
Moreover he talk say, “I be the God of una father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look at God.
Baba God talk say, “I have surely seen the suffering of my people Wey be in Egypt, and have heard dem cry because of dem taskmasters, for I know dem sorrows.

I have come down to deliver dem out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring dem up out of that land to a good and large land, to a land flowing with milk and honey; to the place of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
Now, see am, the cry of the pikin dem of Israel has come to me. Moreover I have seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress dem.
Come now so, and I go send you to Pharaoh, that you may bring my people, the pikin dem of Israel, out of Egypt.”
Moses talk say to God, “Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring the pikin dem of Israel out of Egypt?”
He talk say, “Certainly I go be with you. This Go be the token to you, that I have sent you: when you have bring the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God on this mountain.”
Moses talk say to God, “See am, when I come to the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem, ‘The God of una fathers has sent me to you;’ and dem ask me, ‘Wetin be his name?’ What should I tell dem?”
God talk say to Moses, “I be WHO I be,” and he talk say, “You shall tell the pikin dem of Israel this: ‘I be has sent me to you.’”

God talk say moreover to Moses, “You shall tell the pikin dem of Israel this, ‘Baba God, the God of una fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.’ This is my name forever, and this is my memorial to all generations.

Go, and gather the elders of Israel together, and tell dem, ‘Baba God, the God of una fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, has appeared to me, saying, “I have surely visited you, and seen that which is done to you in Egypt;

and I have talk say, I go bring you up out of the suffering of Egypt to the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, to a land flowing with milk and honey.”’

Dem go listen to una voice, and you shall come, you and the elders of Israel, to the king of Egypt, and you shall tell him, ‘Baba God, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. Now please Make we go three days’ journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to Baba God, our God.’
I know that the king of Egypt no go give you permission to go, no, not by a mighty hand.
I go reach out my hand and strike Egypt with all my wonders which I go do among dem, and after that he will let you go.
I go give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, and it will happen that when you go, you no go go empty-handed.

But every woman shall ask of her neighbor, and of her who visits her house, jewels of silver, jewels of gold, and clothing; and you shall put dem on una sons, and on una daughters. You shall plunder the Egyptians.”
Moses answer, “But, see am, Dem go not believe me, nor listen to my voice; for Dem go say, ‘Baba God has not appeared to you.’”
Baba God talk say to him, “Wetin be that in una hand?” He talk say, “A rod.”
He talk say, “Throw it on the ground.” He threw it on the ground, and it became a snake; and Moses ran away from it.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Stretch out una hand, and take it by the tail.” He stretched out his hand, and take hold of it, and it became a rod in his hand.
“That dem may believe that Baba God, the God of dem fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you.”
Baba God talk say furthermore to him, “Now put una hand inside una cloak.” He put his hand inside his cloak, and when he take it out, see am, his hand was leprous, as white as snow.
He talk say, “Put una hand inside una cloak again.” He put his hand inside his cloak again, and when he take it out of his cloak, see am, it had turned again as his other flesh.
“It will happen, if Dem go not believe you or listen to the voice of the first sign, that Dem go believe the voice of the latter sign.

It will happen, if Dem go not believe even these two signs or listen to una voice, that you shall take of the water of the river, and pour it on the dry land. The water which you take out of the river will become blood on the dry land.”
Moses talk say to Baba God, “O Lord, I be not eloquent, neither before now, nor since you have spoken to una worker; for I be slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.”
Baba God talk say to him, “Who made man’s mouth? Or who makes one mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? No be it I, Baba God?
Now so go, and I go be with una mouth, and teach you Wetin you shall speak.”
He talk say, “Oh, Lord, please send someone else.”

Baba God’s anger burned against Moses, and he talk say, “What about Aaron, una brother, the Levite? I know that he can speak well. Also, see am, he comes out to meet you. When he sees you, he Go be glad in his heart.
You shall speak to him, and put the words in his mouth. I go be with una mouth, and with his mouth, and will teach you Wetin you shall do.
He Go be una spokesman to the people; and it will happen, that he Go be to you a mouth, and You go be to him as God.
You shall take this rod in una hand, with which you shall do the signs.”

Moses go and come back to Jethro his father-in-law, and talk say to him, “Please let me go and return to my brothers Wey be in Egypt, and see whether Dem be still alive.” Jethro talk say to Moses, “Go in peace.”
Baba God talk say to Moses in Midian, “Go, return into Egypt; for all the men who sought una life are dead.”
Moses take his wife and his sons, and set dem on a donkey, and he come back to the land of Egypt. Moses take God’s rod in his hand.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “When you go back into Egypt, see that you do before Pharaoh all the wonders which I have put in una hand, but I go harden his heart and he No go let the people go.
You shall tell Pharaoh, ‘Baba God says, Israel is my son, my firstborn,
and I have talk say to you, “Let my son go, that he may serve me”; and you have refused to Make e go. See am, I go kill una son, una firstborn.’”
On the way at a lodging place, Baba God met Moses and want to kill him.
Then Zipporah take a flint, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and throw it at his feet; and she talk say, “Surely You be a bridegroom of blood to me.”
So he Make e alone. Then she talk say, “You be a bridegroom of blood,” because of the circumcision.
Baba God talk say to Aaron, “Go into the wilderness to meet Moses.” He go, and met him on God’s mountain, and kissed him.
Moses told Aaron all Baba God’s words with which he had sent him, and all the signs with which he had instructed him.
Moses and Aaron go and gathered together all the elders of the pikin dem of Israel.
Aaron spoke all the words which Baba God had spoken to Moses, and did the signs in the sight of the people.
The people believe, and when dem heard that Baba God had visited the pikin dem of Israel, and that he had seen dem suffering, then dem bowed dem heads and worshiped.
Afterward Moses and Aaron come, and talk say to Pharaoh, “This is what Baba God, the God of Israel, says, ‘Let my people go, that dem may hold a feast to me in the wilderness.’”
Pharaoh talk say, “Wey be Baba God, that I should listen to his voice to let Israel go? I no know Baba God, and moreover I go not let Israel go.”

Dem talk say, “The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Please Make we go three days’ journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to Baba God, our God, lest he fall on us with pestilence, or with the sword.”
The king of Egypt talk say to dem, “Why do you, Moses and Aaron, take the people from dem work? Get back to una burdens!”
Pharaoh talk say, “See am, the people of the land are now many, and you make dem rest from dem burdens.”
The same day Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people, and dem officers, saying,
“You shall no longer give the people straw to make brick, as before. Make dem go and gather straw for themselves.
The number of the bricks, which dem made before, you require from dem. You no go diminish anything of it, for Dem be idle; so dem cry, saying, ‘Make we go and sacrifice to our God.’
Let heavier work be laid on the men, that dem may labor inside am; and no Make dem pay any attention to lying words.”
The taskmasters of the people go out, and dem officers, and dem spoke to the people, saying, “This is what Pharaoh says: ‘I go not give you straw.
Go unaself, get straw where you can find it, for nothing of una work go be diminished.’”
So the people were scattered abroad throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
The taskmasters were urgent saying, “Fulfill una work quota daily, as when there was straw!”

The officers of the pikin dem of Israel, whom Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over dem, were beaten, and demanded, “Why haven’t you fulfilled una quota both yesterday and today, in making brick as before?”
Then the officers of the pikin dem of Israel come and cried to Pharaoh, saying, “Why do you deal this way with una workers?
No straw is given to una workers, and dem tell us, ‘Make brick!’ and see am, una workers are beaten; but the fault is in una own people.”
But he talk say, “You be idle! You be idle! So you say, ‘Make we go and sacrifice to Baba God.’
Go so now, and work, for no straw go be given to you, yet you shall deliver the same number of bricks!”
The officers of the pikin dem of Israel see that dem were in trouble, when it was talk say, “You no go diminish anything from una daily quota of bricks!”
Dem met Moses and Aaron, who stood in the way, as dem come out from Pharaoh:

and Dem tell dem say, “May Baba God look at you, and judge, because you have made us a stench to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his workers, to put a sword in dem hand to kill us.”
Moses come back to Baba God, and talk say, “Lord, why have you bring trouble on this people? Why is it that you have sent me?
For since I come to Pharaoh to speak in una name, he has bring trouble on this people; and you have not rescued una people at all.”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Now you shall see what I go do to Pharaoh, for by a strong hand he shall Make dem go, and by a strong hand he shall drive dem out of his land.”
God spoke to Moses, and talk say to him, “I be Baba God;
and I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, as God Almighty; but by my name Baba God I No be known to dem.
I have also established my covenant with dem, to give dem the land of Canaan, the land of dem travels, in which dem lived as aliens.
Moreover I have heard the groaning of the pikin dem of Israel, whom the Egyptians keep in bondage, and I have remember my covenant.

So tell the pikin dem of Israel, ‘I be Baba God, and I go bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I go rid you out of dem bondage, and I go redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with great judgments:
and I go take you to me for a people, and I go be to you a God; and you shall know that I be Baba God una God, who brings you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.
I go bring you into the land which I swore to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I go give it to you for a heritage: I be Baba God.’”
Moses spoke so to the pikin dem of Israel, but dem didn’t listen to Moses for anguish of spirit, and for cruel bondage.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Go in, speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, that he let the pikin dem of Israel go out of his land.”
Moses spoke before Baba God, saying, “See am, the pikin dem of Israel haven’t listened to me. How then shall Pharaoh listen to me, who am of uncircumcised lips?”
Baba God spoke to Moses and to Aaron, and give dem a command to the pikin dem of Israel, and to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the pikin dem of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
These are the heads of dem fathers’ houses. The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, and Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi; these are the families of Reuben.
The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman; these are the families of Simeon.
These are the names of the sons of Levi according to dem generations: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari; and the years of the life of Levi were one hundred thirty-seven years.
The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, according to dem families.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel; and the years of the life of Kohath were one hundred thirty-three years.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to dem generations.
Amram take Jochebed his father’s sister to imself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram were a hundred and thirty-seven years.
The sons of Izhar: Korah, and Nepheg, and Zichri.
The sons of Uzziel: Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Sithri.
Aaron take Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon, as his wife; and she bore him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
The sons of Korah: Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph; these are the families of the Korahites.
Eleazar Aaron’s son take one of the daughters of Putiel as his wife; and she bore him Phinehas. These are the heads of the fathers’ houses of the Levites according to dem families.
These are that Aaron and Moses, to whom Baba God talk say, “Bring out the pikin dem of Israel from the land of Egypt according to dem armies.”
These are people wey spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the pikin dem of Israel from Egypt. These are that Moses and Aaron.
On the day when Baba God spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying, “I be Baba God. Speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I speak to you.”
Moses talk say before Baba God, “See am, I be of uncircumcised lips, and how shall Pharaoh listen to me?”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “See am, I have made you as God to Pharaoh; and Aaron una brother go be una prophet.
You shall speak all that I command you; and Aaron una brother shall speak to Pharaoh, that he let the pikin dem of Israel go out of his land.
I go harden Pharaoh’s heart, and multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.
But Pharaoh No go listen to you, and I go lay my hand on Egypt, and bring out my armies, my people the pikin dem of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.
The Egyptians shall know that I be Baba God, when I stretch out my hand on Egypt, and bring out the pikin dem of Israel from among dem.”
Moses and Aaron did so. As Baba God commanded dem, so dem did.
Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when dem spoke to Pharaoh.
Baba God spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
“When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, ‘Perform a miracle!’ then you shall tell Aaron, ‘Take una rod, and throw it down before Pharaoh, that it become a serpent.’”
Moses and Aaron go in to Pharaoh, and dem did so, as Baba God had commanded: and Aaron throw down his rod before Pharaoh and before his workers, and it became a serpent.
Then Pharaoh also call for the wise men and the sorcerers. Dem also, the magicians of Egypt, did the same thing with dem enchantments.
For dem each throw down dem rods, and dem became serpents: but Aaron’s rod swallowed up dem rods.
Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he didn’t listen to dem; as Baba God had spoken.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Pharaoh’s heart is stubborn. He refuses to let the people go.
Go to Pharaoh in the morning. See am, he goes out to the water; and you shall stand by the river’s bank to meet him; and the rod which was turned to a serpent you shall take in una hand.
You shall tell him, ‘Baba God, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying, “Let my people go, that dem may serve me in the wilderness:” and see am, until now you haven’t listened.
Baba God says, “In this you shall know that I be Baba God. See am, I go strike with the rod that is in my hand on the waters which are in the river, and dem go be turned to blood.
The fish that are in the river shall die, and the river shall become foul; and the Egyptians shall loathe to drink water from the river.”’”

Baba God talk say to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Take una rod, and stretch out una hand over the waters of Egypt, over dem rivers, over dem streams, and over dem pools, and over all dem ponds of water, that dem may become blood; and there go be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood and in vessels of stone.’”

Moses and Aaron did so, as Baba God commanded; and he lifted up the rod, and struck the waters that were in the river, in the sight of Pharaoh, and in the sight of his workers; and all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood.
The fish that were in the river died; and the river became foul, and the Egyptians no fit drink water from the river; and the blood was throughout all the land of Egypt.
The magicians of Egypt did the same thing with dem enchantments; and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he didn’t listen to dem; as Baba God had spoken.
Pharaoh turned and go into his house, and he didn’t even take this to heart.
All the Egyptians dug around the river for water to drink; for dem no fit drink the river water.
Seven days were fulfilled, after Baba God had struck the river.
Baba God spoke to Moses, Go in to Pharaoh, and tell him, “This is what Baba God says, ‘Let my people go, that dem may serve me.
If you refuse to Make dem go, see am, I go plague all una borders with frogs:

and the river shall swarm with frogs, which shall go up and come into una house, and into una bedroom, and on una bed, and into the house of una workers, and on una people, and into una ovens, and into una kneading troughs:
and the frogs shall come up both on you, and on una people, and on all una workers.’”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out una hand with una rod over the rivers, over the streams, and over the pools, and cause frogs to come up on the land of Egypt.’”
Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt; and the frogs come up, and covered the land of Egypt.
The magicians did the same thing with dem enchantments, and bring up frogs on the land of Egypt.
Then Pharaoh call for Moses and Aaron, and talk say, “Entreat Baba God, that he take away the frogs from me, and from my people; and I go let the people go, that dem may sacrifice to Baba God.”

Moses talk say to Pharaoh, “I give you the honor of setting the time that I should pray for you, and for una workers, and for una people, that the frogs be destroyed from you and una houses, and remain in the river only.”
He talk say, “Tomorrow.” He talk say, “Be it according to una word, that you may know that E get Nobody like Baba God our God.
The frogs shall depart from you, and from una houses, and from una workers, and from una people. Dem shall remain in the river only.”
Moses and Aaron go out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried to Baba God concerning the frogs which he had bring on Pharaoh.
Baba God did according to the word of Moses, and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the courts, and out of the fields.
Dem gathered dem together in heaps, and the land stank.
But when Pharaoh see that there was a respite, he hardened his heart, and didn’t listen to dem, as Baba God had spoken.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out una rod, and strike the dust of the earth, that it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.’”

Dem did so; and Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod, and struck the dust of the earth, and there were lice on man, and on animal; all the dust of the earth became lice throughout all the land of Egypt.
The magicians tried with dem enchantments to produce lice, but dem no fit. There were lice on man, and on animal.
Then the magicians talk say to Pharaoh, “This is God’s finger:” and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he didn’t listen to dem; as Baba God had spoken.

Baba God talk say to Moses, “Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh; see am, he comes out to the water; and tell him, ‘This is what Baba God says, “Let my people go, that dem may serve me.

Else, if You go not let my people go, see am, I go send swarms of flies on you, and on una workers, and on una people, and into una houses: and the houses of the Egyptians go be full of swarms of flies, and also the ground whereon Dem be.
I go set apart in that day the land of Goshen, in which my people live, that no swarms of flies go be there; to the end you may know that I be Baba God on the earth.
I go put a division between my people and una people: by tomorrow shall this sign be.”’”
Baba God did so; and there come grievous swarms of flies into the house of Pharaoh, and into his workers’ houses: and in all the land of Egypt the land was corrupted by reason of the swarms of flies.
Pharaoh call for Moses and for Aaron, and talk say, “Go, sacrifice to una God in the land!”

Moses talk say, “It no be appropriate to do so; for we shall sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians to Baba God our God. See am, shall we sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before dem eyes, and no go dem stone us?
We go go three days’ journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to Baba God our God, as he shall command us.”
Pharaoh talk say, “I go let you go, that you may sacrifice to Baba God una God in the wilderness, only you no go go very far away. Pray for me.”

Moses talk say, “See am, I go out from you, and I go pray to Baba God that the swarms of flies may depart from Pharaoh, from his workers, and from his people, tomorrow; only no let Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more in not letting the people go to sacrifice to Baba God.”
Moses go out from Pharaoh, and prayed to Baba God.
Baba God did according to the word of Moses, and he removed the swarms of flies from Pharaoh, from his workers, and from his people. There remain not one.
Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also, and he didn’t let the people go.
Then Baba God talk say to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, and tell him, ‘This is what Baba God, the God of the Hebrews, says: “Let my people go, that dem may serve me.
For if you refuse to Make dem go, and hold dem still,
see am, Baba God’s hand is on una livestock which are in the field, on the horses, on the donkeys, on the camels, on the herds, and on the flocks with a very grievous pestilence.
Baba God will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt; and nothing shall die of all that belongs to the pikin dem of Israel.”’”
Baba God appointed a set time, saying, “Tomorrow Baba God shall do this thing in the land.”
Baba God did that thing on the next day; and all the livestock of Egypt died, but of the livestock of the pikin dem of Israel, not one died.
Pharaoh sent, and, see am, there No be so much as one of the livestock of the Israelites dead. But the heart of Pharaoh was stubborn, and he didn’t let the people go.
Baba God talk say to Moses and to Aaron, “Take to you handfuls of ashes of the furnace, and let Moses sprinkle it toward the sky in the sight of Pharaoh.
It shall become small dust over all the land of Egypt, and go be a boil breaking out with boils on man and on animal, throughout all the land of Egypt.”
Dem take ashes of the furnace, and stood before Pharaoh; and Moses sprinkled it up toward the sky; and it became a boil breaking out with boils on man and on animal.
The magicians no fit stand before Moses because of the boils; for the boils were on the magicians, and on all the Egyptians.
Baba God hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he didn’t listen to dem, as Baba God had spoken to Moses.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh, and tell him, ‘This is what Baba God, the God of the Hebrews, says: “Let my people go, that dem may serve me.
For this time I go send all my plagues against una heart, against una officials, and against una people; that you may know that E get Nobody like me in all the earth.
For now I would have stretched out my hand, and struck you and una people with pestilence, and you would Don dey cut off from the earth;
but indeed for this cause I have made you stand: to show you my power, and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth;
as you still exalt yourself against my people, that you no go Make dem go.
See am, tomorrow about this time I go cause it to rain a very grievous hail, such as has not been in Egypt since the day it was founded even until now.

Now so command that all of una livestock and all that you have in the field be bring into shelter. Every man and animal that is find in the field, and no be bring home, the hail shall come down on dem, and dem shall die.”’”
People wey feared Baba God’s word among the workers of Pharaoh made dem workers and dem livestock flee into the houses.
Anybody wey didn’t respect Baba God’s word left his workers and his livestock in the field.

Baba God talk say to Moses, “Stretch out una hand toward the sky, that there may be hail in all the land of Egypt, on man, and on animal, and on every herb of the field, throughout the land of Egypt.”
Moses stretched out his rod toward the heavens, and Baba God sent thunder, hail, and lightning flashed down to the earth. Baba God rained hail on the land of Egypt.
So there was very severe hail, and lightning mixed with the hail, such as had not been in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.
The hail struck throughout all the land of Egypt all that was in the field, both man and animal; and the hail struck every herb of the field, and broke every tree of the field.
Only in the land of Goshen, where the pikin dem of Israel were, there was no hail.
Pharaoh sent, and call for Moses and Aaron, and talk say to dem, “I have sinned this time. Baba God is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.
Pray to Baba God; for there Don dey enough of mighty thunderings and hail. I go let you go, and you shall stay no longer.”

Moses talk say to him, “As soon as I have gone out of the city, I go spread abroad my hands to Baba God. The thunders shall cease, and there No go be any more hail; that you may know that the earth is Baba God’s.
But as for you and una workers, I know that you no yet fear Baba God.”
The flax and the barley were struck, for the barley was in the ear, and the flax was in bloom.
But the wheat and the spelt No be struck, for dem had not grown up.
Moses go out of the city from Pharaoh, and spread abroad his hands to Baba God; and the thunders and hail ceased, and the rain No be poured on the earth.
When Pharaoh see that the rain and the hail and the thunders had ceased, he sinned yet more, and hardened his heart, he and his workers.
The heart of Pharaoh was hardened, and he didn’t let the pikin dem of Israel go, just as Baba God had spoken through Moses.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his workers, that I may show these my signs among dem,
and that you may tell in the hearing of una son, and of una son’s son, what things I have done to Egypt, and my signs which I have done among dem; that you may know that I be Baba God.”

Moses and Aaron go in to Pharaoh, and talk say to him, “This is what Baba God, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go, that dem may serve me.
Or else, if you refuse to let my people go, see am, tomorrow I go bring locusts into una country,

and dem shall cover the surface of the earth, so that one no go be able to see the earth. Dem shall eat the residue of that which has escaped, which remains to you from the hail, and shall eat every tree which grows for you out of the field.

Una houses go be filled, and the houses of all una workers, and the houses of all the Egyptians; as neither una fathers nor una fathers’ fathers have seen, since the day that dem were on the earth to this day.’” He turned, and go out from Pharaoh.
Pharaoh’s workers talk say to him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the men go, that dem may serve Baba God, dem God. No you yet know that Egypt is destroyed?”
Moses and Aaron were bring again to Pharaoh, and E tell dem say, “Go, serve Baba God una God; but Wey be people wey will go?”
Moses talk say, “We go go with our young and with our old; with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds will we go; for we must hold a feast to Baba God.”
E tell dem say, “Baba God be with you if I go let you go with una little ones! See, evil is clearly before una faces.
Not so! Go now you Wey be men, and serve Baba God; for that is Wetin you desire!” Dem were driven out from Pharaoh’s presence.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Stretch out una hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that dem may come up on the land of Egypt, and eat every herb of the land, even all that the hail has left.”
Moses stretched out his rod over the land of Egypt, and Baba God bring an east wind on the land all that day, and all night; and when it was morning, the east wind bring the locusts.
The locusts go up over all the land of Egypt, and rested in all the borders of Egypt. Dem were very grievous. Before dem there were no such locusts as dem, nor will there ever be again.

For dem covered the surface of the whole earth, so that the land was darkened, and dem ate every herb of the land, and all the fruit of the trees which the hail had left. There remain nothing green, either tree or herb of the field, through all the land of Egypt.
Then Pharaoh call for Moses and Aaron in haste, and he talk say, “I have sinned against Baba God una God, and against you.
Now so please forgive my sin again, and pray to Baba God una God, that he may also take away from me this death.”
He go out from Pharaoh, and prayed to Baba God.
Baba God turned an exceeding strong west wind, which take up the locusts, and drove dem into the Red Sea. There remain not one locust in all the borders of Egypt.
But Baba God hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he didn’t let the pikin dem of Israel go.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Stretch out una hand toward the sky, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt.”
Moses stretched out his hand toward the sky, and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt for three days.
Dem didn’t see each other, and nobody rose from his place for three days; but all the pikin dem of Israel had light in dem dwellings.
Pharaoh call to Moses, and talk say, “Go, serve Baba God. Only let una flocks and una herds stay behind. Let una little ones also go with you.”
Moses talk say, “You must also give into our hand sacrifices and burnt offerings, that we may sacrifice to Baba God our God.
Our livestock also shall go with us. Not a hoof go be left behind, for of it we must take to serve Baba God our God; and we no know with what we must serve Baba God, until we come there.”
But Baba God hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he wouldn’t Make dem go.
Pharaoh talk say to him, “Get away from me! Be careful to see my face no more; for in the day you see my face you shall die!”
Moses talk say, “You have spoken well. I go see una face again no more.”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Yet one plague more will I bring on Pharaoh, and on Egypt; afterwards he will let you go. When he lets you go, he will surely thrust you out altogether.
Speak now in the ears of the people, and let every man ask of his neighbor, and every woman of her neighbor, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold.”
Baba God give the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians. Moreover the man Moses was plenty well-well in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh’s workers, and in the sight of the people.
Moses talk say, “This is what Baba God says: ‘About midnight I go go out into the middle of Egypt,

and all the firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne, even to the firstborn of the female worker Wey be behind the mill; and all the firstborn of livestock.
There go be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as there has not been, nor go be any more.
But against any of the pikin dem of Israel a dog no go even bark or move its tongue, against man or animal; that you may know that Baba God makes a distinction between the Egyptians and Israel.

All these workers of yours will come down to me, and bow down themselves to me, saying, “Get out, with all the people who follow you”; and after that I go go out.’” He go out from Pharaoh in hot anger.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Pharaoh no go listen to you, that my wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.”
Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh, and Baba God hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he didn’t let the pikin dem of Israel go out of his land.
Baba God spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
“This month go be to you the beginning of months. It go be the first month of the year to you.
Speak to all the congregation of Israel, saying, ‘On the tenth day of this month, dem shall take to dem every man a lamb, according to dem fathers’ houses, a lamb for a household;

and if the household is too little for a lamb, then he and his neighbor next to his house shall take one according to the number of the souls; according to what everyone can eat you shall make una count for the lamb.
Una lamb go be without defect, a male a year old. You shall take it from the sheep, or from the goats:
and you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of the same month; and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it at evening.
Dem shall take some of the blood, and put it on the two door posts and on the lintel, on the houses in which dem shall eat it.
Dem shall eat the meat in that night, roasted with fire, and unleavened bread. Dem shall eat it with bitter herbs.
No eat it raw, nor boiled at all with water, but roasted with fire; with its head, its legs and its inner parts.
You shall let nothing of it remain until the morning; but that which remains of it until the morning you shall burn with fire.
This is how you shall eat it: with una belt on una waist, una shoes on una feet, and una staff in una hand; and you shall eat it in haste: it is Baba God’s Passover.
For I go go through the land of Egypt in that night, and will strike all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and animal. Against all the gods of Egypt I go execute judgments: I be Baba God.
The blood go be to you for a token on the houses where You be: and when I see the blood, I go pass over you, and there shall no plague be on you to destroy you, when I strike the land of Egypt.
This day go be to you for a memorial, and you shall keep it a feast to Baba God: throughout una generations you shall keep it a feast by an ordinance forever.

“‘Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread; even the first day you shall put away yeast out of una houses, for Anybody wey eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul go be cut off from Israel.

In the first day there go be to you a holy convocation, and in the seventh day a holy convocation; no kind of work go be done in dem, except that which every man must eat, that only may be done by you.

You shall observe the feast of unleavened bread; for in this same day I have bring una armies out of the land of Egypt: so you shall observe this day throughout una generations by an ordinance forever.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, you shall eat unleavened bread, until the twenty first day of the month at evening.

There go be no yeast find in una houses for seven days, for Anybody wey eats that which is leavened, that soul go be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether he is a foreigner, or one Wey be born in the land.
You shall eat nothing leavened. In all una habitations you shall eat unleavened bread.’”
Then Moses call for all the elders of Israel, and talk say to dem, “Draw out, and take lambs according to una families, and kill the Passover.

You shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and strike the lintel and the two door posts with the blood that is in the basin; and none of you shall go out of the door of his house until the morning.

For Baba God will pass through to strike the Egyptians; and when he sees the blood on the lintel, and on the two door posts, Baba God will pass over the door, and No go allow the destroyer to come in to una houses to strike you.
You shall observe this thing for an ordinance to you and to una sons forever.
It shall happen when you have come to the land which Baba God will give you, according as he has promised, that you shall keep this service.
It will happen, when una pikin dem ask you, ‘What do you mean by this service?’

that you shall say, ‘It is the sacrifice of Baba God’s Passover, who passed over the houses of the pikin dem of Israel in Egypt, when he struck the Egyptians, and spared our houses.’” The people bowed dem heads and worshiped.
The pikin dem of Israel go and did so; as Baba God had commanded Moses and Aaron, so dem did.

At midnight, Baba God struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of livestock.
Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his workers, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there No be a house where there No be one dead.
He call for Moses and Aaron by night, and talk say, “Rise up, get out from among my people, both you and the pikin dem of Israel; and go, serve Baba God, as you have talk say!
Take both una flocks and una herds, as you have talk say, and be gone; and bless me also!”
The Egyptians were urgent with the people, to send dem out of the land in haste, for dem talk say, “We be all dead men.”
The people take dem dough before it was leavened, dem kneading troughs being bound up in dem clothes on dem shoulders.
The pikin dem of Israel did according to the word of Moses; and dem ask of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and clothing.
Baba God give the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, so that dem Make dem have Wetin dem ask. Dem plundered the Egyptians.
The pikin dem of Israel traveled from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot who were men, besides pikin dem.
A mixed plenty people go up also with dem, with flocks, herds, and even well-well livestock.
Dem baked unleavened cakes of the dough which dem bring out of Egypt; for it no be leavened, because dem were thrust out of Egypt, and no fit wait, and dem had not prepared any chop for themselves.
Now the time that the pikin dem of Israel lived in Egypt was four hundred thirty years.
At the end of four hundred thirty years, to the day, all of Baba God’s armies go out from the land of Egypt.

It is a night to be much observed to Baba God for bringing dem out from the land of Egypt. This is that night of Baba God, to be much observed of all the pikin dem of Israel throughout dem generations.
Baba God talk say to Moses and Aaron, “This is the ordinance of the Passover. No foreigner shall eat of it,
but every man’s worker Wey be bought for money, when you have circumcised him, then shall he eat of it.
A foreigner and a hired worker no go eat of it.
It must be eaten In one house. You no go carry any of the meat outside of the house. No break any of its bones.
All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.

When a stranger shall live as a foreigner with you, and will keep the Passover to Baba God, let all his males be circumcised, and then Make e come near and keep it; and he go be as one Wey be born in the land: but no uncircumcised person shall eat of it.
One law go be to him Wey be born at home, and to the stranger who lives as a foreigner among you.”
All the pikin dem of Israel did so. As Baba God commanded Moses and Aaron, so dem did.
That same day, Baba God bring the pikin dem of Israel out of the land of Egypt by dem armies.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Sanctify to me all the firstborn, Anything wey opens the womb among the pikin dem of Israel, both of man and of animal. It is mine.”

Moses talk say to the people, “Remember this day, in which you come out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand Baba God bring you out from this place. No leavened bread go be eaten.
Today you go out in the month Abib.

It go be, when Baba God shall bring you into the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, which he swore to una fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you shall keep this service in this month.
Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and in the seventh day go be a feast to Baba God.
Unleavened bread go be eaten throughout the seven days; and no leavened bread go be seen with you. No yeast go be seen with you, within all una borders.
You shall tell una son in that day, saying, ‘It is because of that which Baba God did for me when I come out of Egypt.’
It go be for a sign to you on una hand, and for a memorial between una eyes, that Baba God’s law may be in una mouth; for with a strong hand Baba God has bring you out of Egypt.
You shall so keep this ordinance in its season from year to year.
“It go be, when Baba God shall bring you into the land of the Canaanite, as he swore to you and to una fathers, and shall give it you,
that you shall set apart to Baba God all that opens the womb, and every firstborn which you have that comes from an animal. The males go be Baba God’s.
Every firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb; and if You go not redeem it, then you shall break its neck; and you shall redeem all the firstborn of man among una sons.
It go be, when una son asks you in time to come, saying, ‘Wetin be this?’ that you shall tell him, ‘By strength of hand Baba God bring us out from Egypt, from the house of bondage.

When Pharaoh stubbornly refused to Make we go, Baba God killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of animal. So I sacrifice to Baba God all that opens the womb, being males; but all the firstborn of my sons I redeem.’
It go be for a sign on una hand, and for symbols between una eyes: for by strength of hand Baba God bring us out of Egypt.”

When Pharaoh had let the people go, God didn’t lead dem by the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God talk say, “Lest perhaps the people change dem minds when dem see war, and dem return to Egypt”;
but God led the people around by the way of the wilderness by the Red Sea; and the pikin dem of Israel go up armed out of the land of Egypt.
Moses take the bones of Joseph with him, for he had made the pikin dem of Israel swear, saying, “God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones away from here with you.”
Dem take dem journey from Succoth, and encamped in Etham, in the edge of the wilderness.
Baba God go before dem by day in a pillar of cloud, to lead dem on dem way, and by night in a pillar of fire, to give dem light, that dem might go by day and by night:
the pillar of cloud by day, and the pillar of fire by night, didn’t depart from before the people.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, that dem turn back and encamp before Pihahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal Zephon. You shall encamp opposite it by the sea.
Pharaoh will say of the pikin dem of Israel, ‘Dem be entangled in the land. The wilderness has shut dem in.’
I go harden Pharaoh’s heart, and he will follow after dem; and I go get honor over Pharaoh, and over all his armies; and the Egyptians shall know that I be Baba God.” Dem did so.

The king of Egypt was told that the people had fled; and the heart of Pharaoh and of his workers was changed towards the people, and dem talk say, “Wetin be this we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?”
He prepared his chariot, and take his army with him;
and he take six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt, and captains over all of dem.
Baba God hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued the pikin dem of Israel; for the pikin dem of Israel go out with a high hand.
The Egyptians pursued dem. All the horses and chariots of Pharaoh, his horsemen, and his army overtook dem encamping by the sea, beside Pihahiroth, before Baal Zephon.
When Pharaoh come near, the pikin dem of Israel lifted up dem eyes, and see am, the Egyptians were marching after dem; and dem were very afraid. The pikin dem of Israel cried out to Baba God.
Dem talk say to Moses, “Because there were no graves in Egypt, have you taken us away to die in the wilderness? Why have you treated us this way, to bring us out of Egypt?
No be this the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, ‘Leave us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians?’ For it would Don dey better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.”
Moses talk say to the people, “No fear. Stand still, and see the salvation of Baba God, which he will work for you today: for the Egyptians whom you have seen today, you shall never see dem again.
Baba God will fight for you, and you go be still.”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Why do you cry to me? Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, that dem go forward.
Lift up una rod, and stretch out una hand over the sea, and divide it: and the pikin dem of Israel shall go into the middle of the sea on dry ground.
See am, I myself will harden the hearts of the Egyptians, and dem shall go in after dem: and I go get myself honor over Pharaoh, and over all his armies, over his chariots, and over his horsemen.
The Egyptians shall know that I be Baba God, when I have gotten myself honor over Pharaoh, over his chariots, and over his horsemen.”
The angel of God, who go before the camp of Israel, moved and go behind dem; and the pillar of cloud moved from before dem, and stood behind dem.
It come between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel; and there was the cloud and the darkness, yet give it light by night: and one didn’t come near the other all night.
Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and Baba God caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.
The pikin dem of Israel go into the middle of the sea on the dry ground, and the waters were a wall to dem on dem right hand, and on dem left.
The Egyptians pursued, and go in after dem into the middle of the sea: all of Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen.
In the morning watch, Baba God looked out on the Egyptian army through the pillar of fire and of cloud, and confused the Egyptian army.
He take off dem chariot wheels, and dem drove dem heavily; so that the Egyptians talk say, “Let’s flee from the face of Israel, for Baba God fights for dem against the Egyptians!”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Stretch out una hand over the sea, that the waters may come again on the Egyptians, on dem chariots, and on dem horsemen.”

Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea come back to its strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it. Baba God overthrew the Egyptians in the middle of the sea.
The waters come back, and covered the chariots and the horsemen, even all Pharaoh’s army that go in after dem into the sea. There remain not so much as one of dem.
But the pikin dem of Israel walked on dry land in the middle of the sea, and the waters were a wall to dem on dem right hand, and on dem left.
