Thus Baba God saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Israel see the Egyptians dead on the seashore.
Israel see the great work which Baba God did to the Egyptians, and the people feared Baba God; and dem believe in Baba God, and in his worker Moses.
Then Moses and the pikin dem of Israel sang this song to Baba God, and talk say, “I go sing to Baba God, for he has triumphed gloriously. The horse and his rider he has thrown into the sea.
Yah is my strength and song. He has become my salvation. This is my God, and I go praise him; my father’s God, and I go exalt him.
Baba God is a man of war. Baba God is his name.
He has throw Pharaoh’s chariots and his army into the sea. His chosen captains are sunk in the Red Sea.
The deeps cover dem. Dem go down into the depths like a stone.
Una right hand, Baba God, is glorious in power. Una right hand, Baba God, dashes the enemy in pieces.
In the greatness of una excellency, you overthrow people wey rise up against you. You send out una serious anger. It consumes dem as stubble.
With the blast of una nostrils, the waters were piled up. The floods stood upright as a heap. The deeps were congealed in the heart of the sea.
The enemy talk say, ‘I go pursue. I go overtake. I go divide the plunder. My desire go be satisfied on dem. I go draw my sword, my hand shall destroy dem.’
You blew with una wind. The sea covered dem. Dem sank like lead in the mighty waters.
Wey be like you, Baba God, among the gods? Wey be like you, glorious in holiness, fearful in praises, doing wonders?
You stretched out una right hand. The earth swallowed dem.
“You, in una loving kindness, have led the people that you have redeemed. You have guided dem in una strength to una holy habitation.
The peoples have heard. Dem tremble. Pangs have taken hold on the inhabitants of Philistia.
Then the chiefs of Edom were dismayed. Trembling takes hold of the mighty men of Moab. All the inhabitants of Canaan have melted away.
Terror and dread falls on dem. By the greatness of una arm Dem be as still as a stone — until una people pass over, Baba God, until the people pass over who you have purchased.
You shall bring dem in, and plant dem in the mountain of una inheritance, the place, Baba God, which you have made for yourself to live in; the sanctuary, Lord, which una hands have established.
Baba God shall reign forever and ever.”

For the horses of Pharaoh go in with his chariots and with his horsemen into the sea, and Baba God bring back the waters of the sea on dem; but the pikin dem of Israel walked on dry land in the middle of the sea.
Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, take a tambourine in her hand; and all the women go out after her with tambourines and with dances.
Miriam answer dem, “Sing to Baba God, for he has triumphed gloriously. The horse and his rider he has thrown into the sea.”
Moses led Israel onward from the Red Sea, and dem go out into the wilderness of Shur; and dem go three days in the wilderness, and find no water.
When dem come to Marah, dem no fit drink from the waters of Marah, for dem were bitter. So its name was call Marah.
The people murmured against Moses, saying, “What shall we drink?”
Then he cried to Baba God. Baba God showed him a tree, and he threw it into the waters, and the waters were made sweet. There he made a statute and an ordinance for dem, and there he tested dem;

and he talk say, “If You go diligently listen to Baba God una God’s voice, and will do that which is right in his eyes, and will pay attention to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I go put none of the diseases on you, which I have put on the Egyptians; for I be Baba God who heals you.”
Dem come to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water, and seventy palm trees: and dem encamped there by the waters.

Dem take dem journey from Elim, and all the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel come to the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after dem departing out of the land of Egypt.
The whole congregation of the pikin dem of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness;

and the pikin dem of Israel talk say to dem, “We wish that we had died by Baba God’s hand in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the meat pots, when we ate our fill of bread, for you have bring us out into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.”

Then Baba God talk say to Moses, “See am, I go rain bread from the sky for you, and the people shall go out and gather a day’s portion every day, that I may test dem, whether Dem go walk in my law, or not.
It shall come to pass on the sixth day, that dem shall prepare that which dem bring in, and it go be twice as much as dem gather daily.”
Moses and Aaron talk say to all the pikin dem of Israel, “At evening, then you shall know that Baba God has bring you out from the land of Egypt;
and in the morning, then you shall see Baba God’s glory; because he hears una murmurings against Baba God. Wey be we, that you murmur against us?”

Moses talk say, “Now Baba God shall give you meat to eat in the evening, and in the morning bread to satisfy you; because Baba God hears una murmurings which you murmur against him. And Wey be we? Una murmurings No be against us, but against Baba God.”
Moses talk say to Aaron, “Tell all the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel, ‘Come near before Baba God, for he has heard una murmurings.’”
As Aaron spoke to the whole congregation of the pikin dem of Israel, dem looked toward the wilderness, and see am, Baba God’s glory appeared in the cloud.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,

“I have heard the murmurings of the pikin dem of Israel. Speak to dem, saying, ‘At evening you shall eat meat, and in the morning you go be filled with bread: and you shall know that I be Baba God una God.’”
In the evening, quail come up and covered the camp; and in the morning the dew lay around the camp.
When the dew that lay had gone, see am, on the surface of the wilderness was a small round thing, small as the frost on the ground.
When the pikin dem of Israel see it, dem talk say to each other, “Wetin be it?” For dem didn’t know what it was. Moses talk say to dem, “It is the bread which Baba God has given you to eat.”

This is the thing which Baba God has commanded: “Gather of it everyone according to his eating; an omer a head, according to the number of una persons, you shall take it, every man for people Wey in his tent.”
The pikin dem of Israel did so, and gathered some more, some less.
When dem measured it with an omer, person wey gathered much had nothing over, and person wey gathered little had no lack. Dem gathered every man according to his eating.
Moses talk say to dem, “Let Nobody leave of it until the morning.”
Notwithstanding dem didn’t listen to Moses, but some of dem left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and became foul: and Moses was angry with dem.
Dem gathered it morning by morning, everyone according to his eating. When the sun grew hot, it melted.
On the sixth day, dem gathered twice as much bread, two omers for each one, and all the rulers of the congregation come and told Moses.

E tell dem say, “This is that which Baba God has spoken, ‘Tomorrow is a solemn rest, a holy Sabbath to Baba God. Bake that which you want to bake, and boil that which you want to boil; and all that remains over lay up for unaself to be kept until the morning.’”
Dem laid it up until the morning, as Moses ask, and it didn’t become foul, and there were no worms in it.
Moses talk say, “Eat that today, for today is a Sabbath to Baba God. Today you no go find it in the field.
Six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day is the Sabbath. In it there go be none.”
On the seventh day, some of the people go out to gather, and dem find none.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “How long do you refuse to keep my commandments and my laws?
See am, because Baba God has given you the Sabbath, so he gives you on the sixth day the bread of two days. Everyone stay in his place. Let Nobody go out of his place on the seventh day.”
So the people rested on the seventh day.
The house of Israel call its name Manna, and it was like coriander seed, white; and its taste was like wafers with honey.

Moses talk say, “This is the thing which Baba God has commanded, ‘Let an omer-full of it be kept throughout una generations, that dem may see the bread with which I fed you in the wilderness, when I bring you out of the land of Egypt.’”
Moses talk say to Aaron, “Take a pot, and put an omer-full of manna in it, and lay it up before Baba God, to be kept throughout una generations.”
As Baba God commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony, to be kept.
The pikin dem of Israel ate the manna forty years, until dem come to an inhabited land. Dem ate the manna until dem come to the borders of the land of Canaan.
Now an omer is one tenth of an ephah.

All the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel traveled from the wilderness of Sin, by dem journeys, according to Baba God’s commandment, and encamped in Rephidim; but there was no water for the people to drink.
So the people quarreled with Moses, and talk say, “Give us water to drink.” Moses talk say to dem, “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test Baba God?”
The people were thirsty for water there; and the people murmured against Moses, and talk say, “Why have you bring us up out of Egypt, to kill us, our pikin dem, and our livestock with thirst?”
Moses cried to Baba God, saying, “What shall I do with these people? Dem be almost ready to stone me.”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Walk on before the people, and take the elders of Israel with you, and take the rod in una hand with which you struck the Nile, and go.
See am, I go stand before you there on the rock in Horeb. You shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it, that the people may drink.” Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
He call the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because the pikin dem of Israel quarreled, and because dem tested Baba God, saying, “Is Baba God among us, or not?”
Then Amalek come and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
Moses talk say to Joshua, “Choose men for us, and go out, fight with Amalek. Tomorrow I go stand on the top of the hill with God’s rod in my hand.”
So Joshua did as Moses had told him, and fought with Amalek; and Moses, Aaron, and Hur go up to the top of the hill.
When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed. When he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.

But Moses’ hands were heavy; and dem take a stone, and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side. His hands were steady until sunset.
Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: that I go utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under the sky.”
Moses built an altar, and call its name Baba God our Banner.
He talk say, “Yah has sworn: ‘Baba God Go get war with Amalek from generation to generation.’”
Now Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses’ father-in-law, heard of all that God had done for Moses, and for Israel his people, how that Baba God had bring Israel out of Egypt.
Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, received Zipporah, Moses’ wife, after he had sent her away,
and her two sons. The name of one son was Gershom, for Moses talk say, “I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign land”.
The name of the other was Eliezer, for he talk say, “My father’s God was my help and delivered me from Pharaoh’s sword.”
Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, come with his sons and his wife to Moses into the wilderness where he was encamped, at the Mountain of God.
He talk say to Moses, “I, una father-in-law Jethro, have come to you with una wife, and her two sons with her.”
Moses go out to meet his father-in-law, and bowed and kissed him. Dem ask each other of dem welfare, and dem come into the tent.
Moses told his father-in-law all that Baba God had done to Pharaoh and to the Egyptians for Israel’s sake, all the hardships that had come on dem on the way, and how Baba God delivered dem.
Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness which Baba God had done to Israel, in that he had delivered dem out of the hand of the Egyptians.
Jethro talk say, “Blessed be Baba God, who has delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh; who has delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians.
Now I know that Baba God is greater than all gods because of the thing in which dem dealt arrogantly against dem.”
Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, take a burnt offering and sacrifices for God. Aaron come with all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God.
On the next day, Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood around Moses from the morning to the evening.

When Moses’ father-in-law see all that he did to the people, he talk say, “Wetin be this thing that you do for the people? Why do you sit alone, and all the people stand around you from morning to evening?”
Moses talk say to his father-in-law, “Because the people come to me to inquire of God.
When dem have a matter, dem come to me, and I judge between a man and his neighbor, and I make dem know the statutes of God, and his laws.”
Moses’ father-in-law talk say to him, “The thing that you do No be good.
You go surely wear away, both you, and this people that is with you; for the thing is too heavy for you. You No be able to perform it yourself alone.
Listen now to my voice. I go give you counsel, and God be with you. You represent the people before God, and bring the causes to God.
You shall teach dem the statutes and the laws, and shall show dem the way in which dem must walk, and the work that dem must do.

Moreover you shall provide out of all the people able men which fear God: men of truth, hating unjust gain; and place such over dem, to be rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.

Make dem judge the people at all times. It go be that every great matter dem shall bring to you, but every small matter dem shall judge themselves. So shall it be easier for you, and dem shall share the load with you.
If You go do this thing, and God commands you so, then You go be able to endure, and all these people also will go to dem place in peace.”
So Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law, and did all that he had talk say.
Moses chose able men out of all Israel, and made dem heads over the people, rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
Dem judged the people at all times. Dem bring the hard causes to Moses, but every small matter dem judged themselves.
Moses let his father-in-law depart, and he go his way into his own land.
In the third month after the pikin dem of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt, on that same day dem come into the wilderness of Sinai.
When dem had comot from Rephidim, and had come to the wilderness of Sinai, dem encamped in the wilderness; and there Israel encamped before the mountain.
Moses go up to God, and Baba God call to him out of the mountain, saying, “This is Wetin you shall tell the house of Jacob, and tell the pikin dem of Israel:
‘You have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles’ wings, and bring you to myself.
Now so, if You go indeed obey my voice, and keep my covenant, then you go be my own possession from among all peoples; for all the earth is mine;
and you go be to me a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the pikin dem of Israel.”
Moses come and call for the elders of the people, and set before dem all these words which Baba God commanded him.
All the people answer together, and talk say, “All that Baba God has spoken We go do.” Moses reported the words of the people to Baba God.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “See am, I come to you in a thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may also believe you forever.” Moses told the words of the people to Baba God.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Go to the people, and sanctify dem today and tomorrow, and Make dem wash dem garments,
and be ready against the third day; for on the third day Baba God will come down in the sight of all the people on Mount Sinai.
You shall set bounds to the people all around, saying, ‘Be careful that you no go up onto the mountain, or touch its border. Anybody wey touches the mountain go be surely put to death.
No hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or shot through; whether it is animal or man, he no go live.’ When the trumpet sounds long, dem shall come up to the mountain.”
Moses go down from the mountain to the people, and sanctified the people; and dem washed dem clothes.
He talk say to the people, “Be ready by the third day. No have sexual relations with a woman.”

On the third day, when it was morning, there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain, and the sound of an exceedingly loud trumpet; and all the people who were in the camp trembled.
Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God; and dem stood at the lower part of the mountain.
All of Mount Sinai smoked, because Baba God descended on it in fire; and its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked greatly.
When the sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder, Moses spoke, and God answer him by a voice.
Baba God come down on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain. Baba God call Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses go up.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Go down, warn the people, lest dem break through to Baba God to gaze, and many of dem perish.
Let the priests also, who come near to Baba God, sanctify themselves, lest Baba God break out on dem.”
Moses talk say to Baba God, “The people no fit come up to Mount Sinai, for you warned us, saying, ‘Set bounds around the mountain, and sanctify it.’”
Baba God talk say to him, “Go down! You shall bring Aaron up with you, but no let the priests and the people break through to come up to Baba God, lest he break out against dem.”
So Moses go down to the people, and told dem.
God spoke all these words, saying,
“I be Baba God una God, who bring you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
“You go get no other gods before me.
“You no go make for unaself an idol, nor any image of anything that is in the heavens above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:

you no go bow yourself down to dem, nor serve dem, for I, Baba God una God, am a jealous God, visiting the wickedness of the fathers on the pikin dem, on the third and on the fourth generation of people wey hate me,
and showing loving kindness to thousands of people wey love me and keep my commandments.
“You no go take the name of Baba God una God in vain, for Baba God No go hold him guiltless who takes his name in vain.
“Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
You shall labor six days, and do all una work,

but the seventh day is a Sabbath to Baba God una God. You no go do any work in it, you, nor una son, nor una daughter, una male worker, nor una female worker, nor una livestock, nor una stranger Wey be within una gates;
for in six days Baba God made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in dem, and rested the seventh day; so Baba God blessed the Sabbath day, and made it holy.
“Honor una father and una mother, that una days may be long in the land which Baba God una God gives you.
“You no go murder.
“You no go commit adultery.
“You no go steal.
“You no go give false testimony against una neighbor.
“You no go covet una neighbor’s house. You no go covet una neighbor’s wife, nor his male worker, nor his female worker, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is una neighbor’s.”
All the people perceived the thunderings, the lightnings, the sound of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking. When the people see it, dem trembled, and stayed at a distance.
Dem talk say to Moses, “Speak with us yourself, and We go listen; but no let God speak with us, lest we die.”
Moses talk say to the people, “No fear, for God has come to test you, and that his fear may be before you, that you no go sin.”
The people stayed at a distance, and Moses come near to the thick darkness where God was.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “This is Wetin you shall tell the pikin dem of Israel: ‘You unaself have seen that I have talked with you from heaven.
You shall most certainly not make alongside of me gods of silver, or gods of gold for unaself.

You shall make an altar of earth for me, and shall sacrifice on it una burnt offerings and una peace offerings, una sheep and una cattle. In every place where I record my name I go come to you and I go bless you.
If you make me an altar of stone, you no go build it of cut stones; for if you lift up una tool on it, you have polluted it.
You no go go up by steps to my altar, that una nakedness may not be exposed to it.’
“Now these are the ordinances which you shall set before dem.
“If you buy a Hebrew worker, he shall serve six years and in the seventh he shall go out free without paying anything.
If he comes in by imself, he shall go out by imself. If he is married, then his wife shall go out with him.
If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her pikin dem go be her master’s, and he shall go out by imself.
But if the worker shall plainly say, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my pikin dem. I go not go out free;’
then his master shall bring him to God, and shall bring him to the door or to the doorpost, and his master shall bore his ear through with an awl, and he shall serve him for ever.
“If a man sells his daughter to be a female worker, she no go go out as the male workers do.
If she no dey please her master, who has married her to imself, then he shall Make she be redeemed. He go get no right to sell her to a foreign people, since he has dealt deceitfully with her.
If he marries her to his son, he shall deal with her as a daughter.
If he takes another wife to imself, he no go diminish her chop, her clothing, and her marital rights.
If he no dey do these three things for her, she may go free without paying any money.
“One who strikes a man so that he dies shall surely be put to death,
but not if it is unintentional, but God allows it to happen: then I go appoint you a place where he shall flee.
If a man schemes and comes presumptuously on his neighbor to kill him, you shall take him from my altar, that he may die.
“Anybody wey attacks his father or his mother go be surely put to death.
“Anybody wey kidnaps someone and sells him, or if he is find in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.
“Anybody wey curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
“If men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone, or with his fist, and he no dey die, but is confined to bed;

if he rises again and walks around with his staff, then person wey struck him go be cleared: only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall provide for his healing until he is thoroughly healed.
“If a man strikes his worker or his maid with a rod, and he dies under his hand, he shall surely be punished.
Notwithstanding, if he gets up after a day or two, he no go be punished, for he is his property.
“If men fight and hurt a pregnant woman so that she gives birth prematurely, and yet no harm follows, he go be surely fined as much as the woman’s husband demands and the judges allow.
But if any harm follows, then you must take life for life,
eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
burning for burning, wound for wound, and bruise for bruise.
“If a man strikes his worker’s eye, or his maid’s eye, and destroys it, he shall Make e go free for his eye’s sake.
If he strikes out his male worker’s tooth, or his female worker’s tooth, he shall Make e go free for his tooth’s sake.
“If a bull gores a man or a woman to death, the bull shall surely be stoned, and its meat no go be eaten; but the owner of the bull no go be held responsible.

But if the bull had a habit of goring in the past, and it Don dey testified to its owner, and he has not kept it in, but it has killed a man or a woman, the bull go be stoned, and its owner shall also be put to death.
If a ransom is laid on him, then he shall give for the redemption of his life Anything wey is laid on him.
Whether it has gored a son or has gored a daughter, according to this judgment it go be done to him.
If the bull gores a male worker or a female worker, thirty shekels of silver go be given to dem master, and the ox go be stoned.
“If a man opens a pit, or if a man digs a pit and no dey cover it, and a bull or a donkey falls into it,
the owner of the pit shall make it good. He shall give money to its owner, and the dead animal go be his.
“If one man’s bull injures another’s, so that it dies, then dem shall sell the live bull, and divide its price; and dem shall also divide the dead animal.
Or if it is known that the bull was in the habit of goring in the past, and its owner has not kept it in, he shall surely pay bull for bull, and the dead animal go be his own.
“If a man steals an ox or a sheep, and kills it, or sells it; he shall pay five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.
If the thief is find breaking in, and is struck so that he dies, there go be no guilt of bloodshed for him.
If the sun has risen on him, guilt of bloodshed go be for him; he shall make restitution. If he has nothing, then he go be sold for his theft.
If the stolen property is find in his hand alive, whether it is ox, donkey, or sheep, he shall pay double.

“If a man causes a field or vineyard to be eaten, and lets his animal loose, and it grazes in another man’s field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field, and from the best of his own vineyard.
“If fire breaks out, and catches in thorns so that the shocks of grain, or the standing grain, or the field are consumed; person wey kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.
“If a man delivers to his neighbor money or stuff to keep, and it is stolen out of the man’s house; if the thief is find, he shall pay double.
If the thief no be find, then the master of the house shall come near to God, to find out if he hasn’t put his hand to his neighbor’s goods.

For every matter of trespass, whether it is for ox, for donkey, for sheep, for clothing, or for any kind of lost thing, about which one says, ‘This is mine,’ the cause of both parties shall come before God. He whom God condemns shall pay double to his neighbor.
“If a man delivers to his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal to keep, and it dies or is injured, or driven away, no man seeing it;
the oath of Baba God go be between dem both, whether he hasn’t put his hand to his neighbor’s goods; and its owner shall accept it, and he no go make restitution.
But if it is stolen from him, he shall make restitution to its owner.
If it is torn in pieces, Make e bring it for evidence. He no go make good that which was torn.
“If a man borrows anything of his neighbor’s, and it is injured, or dies, its owner not being with it, he shall surely make restitution.
If its owner is with it, he no go make it good. If it is a leased thing, it come for its lease.
“If a man entices a virgin who no be pledged to be married, and lies with her, he shall surely pay a dowry for her to be his wife.
If her father utterly refuses to give her to him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.
“You no go allow a sorceress to live.
“Anybody wey has sex with an animal shall surely be put to death.
“Person wey sacrifices to any god, except to Baba God only, go be utterly destroyed.
“You no go wrong an alien or oppress him, for you were aliens in the land of Egypt.
“You no go take advantage of any widow or fatherless pikin.
If you take advantage of dem at all, and dem cry at all to me, I go surely hear dem cry;
and my serious anger will grow hot, and I go kill you with the sword; and una wives go be widows, and una pikin dem fatherless.
“If you lend money to any of my people with you Wey be poor, you no go be to him as a creditor. You no go charge him interest.
If you take una neighbor’s garment as collateral, you shall restore it to him before the sun goes down,
for that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin. What would he sleep in? It will happen, when he cries to me, that I go hear, for I be gracious.
“You no go blaspheme God, nor curse a ruler of una people.
“You no go delay to offer from una harvest and from the outflow of una presses. “You shall give the firstborn of una sons to me.
You shall do likewise with una cattle and with una sheep. Seven days it go be with its mother, then on the eighth day you shall give it to me.
“You go be holy men to me, so you no go eat any meat that is torn by animals in the field. You shall throw it to the dogs.
“You no go spread a false report. No join una hand with the wicked to be a malicious witness.
“You no go follow a crowd to do evil. You no go testify in court to side with a plenty people to pervert justice.
You no go favor a poor man in his cause.
“If you meet una enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray, you shall surely bring it back to him again.
If you see the donkey of him who hates you fallen down under his burden, no leave him, you shall surely help him with it.
“You no go deny justice to una poor people in dem lawsuits.
“Keep far from a false charge, and no kill the innocent and righteous: for I go not justify the wicked.
“You shall take no bribe, for a bribe blinds people wey have sight and perverts the words of the righteous.
“You no go oppress an alien, for you know the heart of an alien, since you were aliens in the land of Egypt.
“For six years you shall sow una land, and shall gather in its increase,

but the seventh year you shall let it rest and lie fallow, that the poor of una people may eat; and Wetin dem leave the animal of the field shall eat. In the same way, you shall deal with una vineyard and with una olive grove.
“Six days you shall do una work, and on the seventh day you shall rest, that una ox and una donkey may have rest, and the son of una worker, and the alien may be refreshed.
“Be careful to do all things that I have talk say to you; and no invoke the name of other gods or even Make dem be heard out of una mouth.
“You shall observe a feast to me three times a year.

You shall observe the feast of unleavened bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the time appointed in the month Abib (for in it you come out of Egypt), and Nobody shall appear before me empty.
And the feast of harvest, the first fruits of una labors, which you sow in the field; and the feast of ingathering, at the end of the year, when you gather in una labors out of the field.
Three times in the year all una males shall appear before the Lord Baba God.
“You no go offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread. The fat of my feast no go remain all night until the morning.
The first of the first fruits of una ground you shall bring into the house of Baba God una God. “You no go boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.
“See am, I send an angel before you, to keep you by the way, and to bring you into the place which I have prepared.
Pay attention to him, and listen to his voice. No provoke him, for he No go pardon una disobedience, for my name is in him.
But if you indeed listen to his voice, and do all that I speak, then I go be an enemy to una enemies, and an adversary to una adversaries.
For my angel shall go before you, and bring you in to the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite; and I go cut dem off.
You no go bow down to dem gods, nor serve dem, nor follow dem practices, but you shall utterly overthrow dem and demolish dem pillars.
You shall serve Baba God una God, and he will bless una bread and una water, and I go take sickness away from among you.
Nobody will miscarry or be barren in una land. I go fulfill the number of una days.
I go send my terror before you, and will confuse all the people to whom you come, and I go make all una enemies turn dem backs to you.
I go send the hornet before you, which will drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before you.
I go not drive dem out from before you in one year, lest the land become desolate, and the animals of the field multiply against you.
Little by little I go drive dem out from before you, until you have increased and inherit the land.

I go set una border from the Red Sea even to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River; for I go deliver the inhabitants of the land into una hand, and you shall drive dem out before you.
You shall make no covenant with dem, nor with dem gods.
Dem no go live in una land, lest dem make you sin against me, for if you serve dem gods, it will surely be a snare to you.”
He talk say to Moses, “Come up to Baba God, you, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel; and worship from a distance.
Moses alone shall come near to Baba God, but dem no go come near. The people no go go up with him.”
Moses come and told the people all Baba God’s words, and all the ordinances; and all the people answer with one voice, and talk say, “All the words which Baba God has spoken will we do.”
Moses wrote all Baba God’s words, and rose up early in the morning, and built an altar under the mountain, and twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
He sent young men of the pikin dem of Israel, who offered burnt offerings and sacrificed peace offerings of cattle to Baba God.
Moses take half of the blood and put it in basins, and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar.
He take the book of the covenant and read it in the hearing of the people, and dem talk say, “All that Baba God has spoken will we do, and be obedient.”
Moses take the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and talk say, “Look, this is the blood of the covenant, which Baba God has made with you concerning all these words.”
Then Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel go up.
Dem see the God of Israel. Under his feet was like a paved work of sapphire stone, like the skies for clearness.
He didn’t lay his hand on the nobles of the pikin dem of Israel. Dem see God, and ate and drank.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain, and stay here, and I go give you the stone tablets with the law and the commands that I have written, that you may teach dem.”
Moses rose up with Joshua, his worker, and Moses go up onto God’s Mountain.
He talk say to the elders, “Wait here for us, until we come again to you. See am, Aaron and Hur are with you. Anybody wey is involved in a dispute can go to dem.”
Moses go up on the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
Baba God’s glory settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days. The seventh day he call to Moses out of the middle of the cloud.
The appearance of Baba God’s glory was like devouring fire on the top of the mountain in the eyes of the pikin dem of Israel.
Moses entered into the middle of the cloud, and go up on the mountain; and Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, that dem take an offering for me. From everyone whose heart makes him willing you shall take my offering.
This is the offering which you shall take from dem: gold, silver, brass,
blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats’ hair,
rams’ skins dyed red, sea cow hides, acacia wood,
oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet incense,
onyx stones, and stones to be set for the ephod and for the breastplate.
Make dem make me a sanctuary, that I may live among dem.
According to all that I show you, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all of its furniture, even so you shall make it.
“Dem shall make an ark of acacia wood. Its length go be two and a half cubits, its width a cubit and a half, and a cubit and a half its height.
You shall overlay it with pure gold. You shall overlay it inside and outside, and you shall make a gold molding around it.
You shall throw four rings of gold for it, and put dem in its four feet. Two rings go be on the one side of it, and two rings on the other side of it.
You shall make poles of acacia wood, and overlay dem with gold.
You shall put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry the ark.
The poles go be in the rings of the ark. Dem no go be taken from it.
You shall put the testimony which I shall give you into the ark.
You shall make a mercy seat of pure gold. Two and a half cubits go be its length, and a cubit and a half its width.
You shall make two cherubim of hammered gold. You shall make dem at the two ends of the mercy seat.
Make one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end. You shall make the cherubim on its two ends of one piece with the mercy seat.
The cherubim shall spread out dem wings upward, covering the mercy seat with dem wings, with dem faces toward each other. The faces of the cherubim go be toward the mercy seat.
You shall put the mercy seat on top of the ark, and in the ark you shall put the testimony that I go give you.
There I go meet with you, and I go tell you from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim which are on the ark of the testimony, all that I command you for the pikin dem of Israel.
“You shall make a table of acacia wood. Two cubits go be its length, and a cubit its width, and one and a half cubits its height.
You shall overlay it with pure gold, and make a gold molding around it.
You shall make a rim of a hand width around it. You shall make a golden molding on its rim around it.
You shall make four rings of gold for it, and put the rings in the four corners that are on its four feet.
the rings go be close to the rim, for places for the poles to carry the table.
You shall make the poles of acacia wood, and overlay dem with gold, that the table may be carried with dem.
You shall make its dishes, its spoons, its ladles, and its bowls to pour out offerings with. You shall make dem of pure gold.
You shall set bread of the presence on the table before me always.
“You shall make a lamp stand of pure gold. Of hammered work shall the lamp stand be made, even its base, its shaft, its cups, its buds, and its flowers, go be of one piece with it.
There go be six branches going out of its sides: three branches of the lamp stand out of its one side, and three branches of the lamp stand out of its other side;

three cups made like almond blossoms in one branch, a bud and a flower; and three cups made like almond blossoms in the other branch, a bud and a flower, so for the six branches going out of the lamp stand;
and in the lamp stand four cups made like almond blossoms, its buds and its flowers;

and a bud under two branches of one piece with it, and a bud under two branches of one piece with it, and a bud under two branches of one piece with it, for the six branches going out of the lamp stand.
Dem buds and dem branches go be of one piece with it, all of it one beaten work of pure gold.
You shall make its lamps seven, and dem shall light its lamps to give light to the space in front of it.
Its snuffers and its snuff dishes go be of pure gold.
It go be made of a talent of pure gold, with all these accessories.
See that you make dem after dem pattern, which Don dey shown to you on the mountain.
“Moreover you shall make the tabernacle with ten curtains; of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, with cherubim. The work of the skillful workman you shall make dem.
The length of each curtain go be twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits: all the curtains go get one measure.
Five curtains go be coupled together to each other; and the other five curtains go be coupled to each other.
You shall make loops of blue on the edge of the one curtain from the edge in the coupling; and likewise you shall make in the edge of the curtain that is outermost in the second coupling.
You shall make fifty loops in the one curtain, and you shall make fifty loops in the edge of the curtain that is in the second coupling. The loops go be opposite to each other.
You shall make fifty clasps of gold, and couple the curtains to each other with the clasps: and the tabernacle go be a unit.
“You shall make curtains of goats’ hair for a covering over the tabernacle. You shall make dem eleven curtains.
The length of each curtain go be thirty cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits: the eleven curtains go get one measure.
You shall couple five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves, and shall double over the sixth curtain in the forefront of the tent.
You shall make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain that is outermost in the coupling, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain which is outermost in the second coupling.
You shall make fifty clasps of brass, and put the clasps into the loops, and couple the tent together, that it may be one.
The overhanging part that remains of the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that remains, shall hang over the back of the tabernacle.

The cubit on the one side, and the cubit on the other side, of that which remains in the length of the curtains of the tent, shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle on this side and on that side, to cover it.
You shall make a covering for the tent of rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering of sea cow hides above.
“You shall make the boards for the tabernacle of acacia wood, standing up.
Ten cubits go be the length of a board, and one and a half cubits the width of each board.
There go be two tenons in each board, joined to each other: thus you shall make for all the boards of the tabernacle.
You shall make the boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards for the south side southward.
You shall make forty sockets of silver under the twenty boards; two sockets under one board for its two tenons, and two sockets under another board for its two tenons.
For the second side of the tabernacle, on the north side, twenty boards,
and dem forty sockets of silver; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.
For the far part of the tabernacle westward you shall make six boards.
You shall make two boards for the corners of the tabernacle in the far part.
Dem go be double beneath, and in the same way dem go be whole to its top to one ring: thus shall it be for dem both; dem go be for the two corners.
There go be eight boards, and dem sockets of silver, sixteen sockets; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.
“You shall make bars of acacia wood: five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
and five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the side of the tabernacle, for the far part westward.
The middle bar in the middle of the boards shall pass through from end to end.
You shall overlay the boards with gold, and make dem rings of gold for places for the bars: and you shall overlay the bars with gold.
You shall set up the tabernacle according to the way that it was shown to you on the mountain.
“You shall make a veil of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, with cherubim. The work of the skillful workman shall it be made.
You shall hang it on four pillars of acacia overlaid with gold; dem hooks go be of gold, on four sockets of silver.
You shall hang up the veil under the clasps, and shall bring the ark of the testimony in there within the veil: and the veil shall separate the holy place from the most holy for you.
You shall put the mercy seat on the ark of the testimony in the most holy place.
You shall set the table outside the veil, and the lamp stand over against the table on the side of the tabernacle toward the south: and you shall put the table on the north side.
“You shall make a screen for the door of the Tent, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of the embroiderer.
You shall make for the screen five pillars of acacia, and overlay dem with gold: dem hooks go be of gold: and you shall throw five sockets of brass for dem.
“You shall make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long, and five cubits wide; the altar go be square: and its height go be three cubits.
You shall make its horns on its four corners; its horns go be of one piece with it; and you shall overlay it with brass.
You shall make its pots to take away its ashes, its shovels, its basins, its meat hooks, and its fire pans: all its vessels you shall make of brass.
You shall make a grating for it of network of brass: and on the net you shall make four bronze rings in its four corners.
You shall put it under the ledge around the altar beneath, that the net may reach halfway up the altar.
You shall make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay dem with brass.
Its poles go be put into the rings, and the poles go be on the two sides of the altar, when carrying it.
You shall make it with hollow planks. Dem shall make it as it Don dey shown you on the mountain.
“You shall make the court of the tabernacle: for the south side southward there go be hangings for the court of fine twined linen one hundred cubits long for one side:
and its pillars go be twenty, and dem sockets twenty, of brass; the hooks of the pillars and dem fillets go be of silver.
Likewise for the north side in length there go be hangings one hundred cubits long, and its pillars twenty, and dem sockets twenty, of brass; the hooks of the pillars, and dem fillets, of silver.
For the width of the court on the west side go be hangings of fifty cubits; dem pillars ten, and dem sockets ten.
The width of the court on the east side eastward go be fifty cubits.
The hangings for the one side of the gate go be fifteen cubits; dem pillars three, and dem sockets three.
For the other side go be hangings of fifteen cubits; dem pillars three, and dem sockets three.
For the gate of the court go be a screen of twenty cubits, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of the embroiderer; dem pillars four, and dem sockets four.
All the pillars of the court around go be filleted with silver; dem hooks of silver, and dem sockets of brass.
The length of the court go be one hundred cubits, and the width fifty every where, and the height five cubits, of fine twined linen, and dem sockets of brass.
All the instruments of the tabernacle in all its service, and all its pins, and all the pins of the court, go be of brass.
“You shall command the pikin dem of Israel, that dem bring to you pure olive oil beaten for the light, to cause a lamp to burn continually.

In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil which is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall keep it in order from evening to morning before Baba God: it go be a statute forever throughout dem generations on the behalf of the pikin dem of Israel.

“Bring Aaron una brother, and his sons with him, near to you from among the pikin dem of Israel, that he may minister to me in the priest’s office, even Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s sons.
You shall make holy garments for Aaron una brother, for glory and for beauty.
You shall speak to all Wey be wise-hearted, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom, that dem make Aaron’s garments to sanctify him, that he may minister to me in the priest’s office.

These are the garments which dem shall make: a breastplate, and an ephod, and a robe, and a coat of checker work, a turban, and a sash: and dem shall make holy garments for Aaron una brother, and his sons, that he may minister to me in the priest’s office.
Dem shall take the gold, and the blue, and the purple, and the scarlet, and the fine linen.
“Dem shall make the ephod of gold, of blue, and purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of the skillful workman.
It go get two shoulder straps joined to the two ends of it, that it may be joined together.
The skillfully woven band, which is on it, that is on him, go be like its work and of the same piece; of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen.
You shall take two onyx stones, and engrave on dem the names of the pikin dem of Israel:
six of dem names on the one stone, and the names of the six that remain on the other stone, in the order of dem birth.

With the work of an engraver in stone, like the engravings of a signet, you shall engrave the two stones, according to the names of the pikin dem of Israel: you shall make dem to be enclosed in settings of gold.

You shall put the two stones on the shoulder straps of the ephod, to be stones of memorial for the pikin dem of Israel: and Aaron shall bear dem names before Baba God on his two shoulders for a memorial.
You shall make settings of gold,
and two chains of pure gold; you shall make dem like cords of braided work: and you shall put the braided chains on the settings.

“You shall make a breastplate of judgment, the work of the skillful workman; like the work of the ephod you shall make it; of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, you shall make it.
It go be square and folded double; a span go be its length of it, and a span its width.
You shall set in it settings of stones, four rows of stones: a row of ruby, topaz, and beryl go be the first row;
and the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald;
and the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
and the fourth row a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper: dem go be enclosed in gold in dem settings.
The stones go be according to the names of the pikin dem of Israel, twelve, according to dem names; like the engravings of a signet, everyone according to his name, dem go be for the twelve tribes.
You shall make on the breastplate chains like cords, of braided work of pure gold.
You shall make on the breastplate two rings of gold, and shall put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.
You shall put the two braided chains of gold in the two rings at the ends of the breastplate.
The other two ends of the two braided chains you shall put on the two settings, and put dem on the shoulder straps of the ephod in its forepart.
You shall make two rings of gold, and you shall put dem on the two ends of the breastplate, on its edge, which is toward the side of the ephod inward.
You shall make two rings of gold, and shall put dem on the two shoulder straps of the ephod underneath, in its forepart, close by its coupling, above the skillfully woven band of the ephod.

Dem shall bind the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it may be on the skillfully woven band of the ephod, and that the breastplate may not swing out from the ephod.
Aaron shall bear the names of the pikin dem of Israel in the breastplate of judgment on his heart, when he goes in to the holy place, for a memorial before Baba God continually.

You shall put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim; and dem go be on Aaron’s heart, when he goes in before Baba God: and Aaron shall bear the judgment of the pikin dem of Israel on his heart before Baba God continually.
“You shall make the robe of the ephod all of blue.
It go get a hole for the head in the middle of it. It go get a binding of woven work around its hole, as it were the hole of a coat of mail, that it not be torn.
On its hem you shall make pomegranates of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, around its hem; and bells of gold between and around dem:
a golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, around the hem of the robe.
It go be on Aaron to minister: and its sound go be heard when he goes in to the holy place before Baba God, and when he comes out, that he not die.
“You shall make a plate of pure gold, and engrave on it, like the engravings of a signet, ‘HOLY TO Baba God.’
You shall put it on a lace of blue, and it go be on the sash; on the front of the sash it go be.

It go be on Aaron’s forehead, and Aaron shall bear the wickedness of the holy things, which the pikin dem of Israel shall make holy in all dem holy gifts; and it go be always on his forehead, that dem may be accepted before Baba God.
You shall weave the coat in checker work of fine linen, and you shall make a turban of fine linen, and you shall make a sash, the work of the embroiderer.
“You shall make coats for Aaron’s sons, and you shall make sashes for dem and you shall make headbands for dem, for glory and for beauty.
You shall put dem on Aaron una brother, and on his sons with him, and shall anoint dem, and consecrate dem, and sanctify dem, that dem may minister to me in the priest’s office.
You shall make dem linen breeches to cover the flesh of dem nakedness; from the waist even to the thighs dem shall reach:

Dem go be on Aaron, and on his sons, when dem go in to the Tent of Meeting, or when dem come near to the altar to minister in the holy place; that dem no bear wickedness, and die: it go be a statute forever to him and to his offspring after him.
“This is the thing that you shall do to dem to make dem holy, to minister to me in the priest’s office: take one young bull and two rams without defect,
unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil: you shall make dem of fine wheat flour.
You shall put dem into one basket, and bring dem in the basket, with the bull and the two rams.
You shall bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and shall wash dem with water.
You shall take the garments, and put on Aaron the coat, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastplate, and clothe him with the skillfully woven band of the ephod;
and you shall set the turban on his head, and put the holy crown on the turban.
Then you shall take the anointing oil, and pour it on his head, and anoint him.
You shall bring his sons, and put coats on dem.
You shall clothe dem with belts, Aaron and his sons, and bind headbands on dem: and dem go get the priesthood by a perpetual statute: and you shall consecrate Aaron and his sons.
“You shall bring the bull before the Tent of Meeting: and Aaron and his sons shall lay dem hands on the head of the bull.
You shall kill the bull before Baba God, at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
You shall take of the blood of the bull, and put it on the horns of the altar with una finger; and you shall pour out all the blood at the base of the altar.
You shall take all the fat that covers the innards, the cover of the liver, the two kidneys, and the fat that is on dem, and burn dem on the altar.
But the meat of the bull, and its skin, and its dung, you shall burn with fire outside of the camp: it is a sin offering.
“You shall also take the one ram; and Aaron and his sons shall lay dem hands on the head of the ram.
You shall kill the ram, and you shall take its blood, and sprinkle it around on the altar.
You shall cut the ram into its pieces, and wash its innards, and its legs, and put dem with its pieces, and with its head.
You shall burn the whole ram on the altar: it is a burnt offering to Baba God; it is a pleasant aroma, an offering made by fire to Baba God.
“You shall take the other ram; and Aaron and his sons shall lay dem hands on the head of the ram.

Then you shall kill the ram, and take some of its blood, and put it on the tip of the right ear of Aaron, and on the tip of the right ear of his sons, and on the thumb of dem right hand, and on the big toe of dem right foot, and sprinkle the blood around on the altar.

You shall take of the blood that is on the altar, and of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aaron, and on his garments, and on his sons, and on the garments of his sons with him: and he go be made holy, and his garments, and his sons, and his sons’ garments with him.

Also you shall take some of the ram’s fat, the fat tail, the fat that covers the innards, the cover of the liver, the two kidneys, the fat that is on dem, and the right thigh (for it is a ram of consecration),
and one loaf of bread, one cake of oiled bread, and one wafer out of the basket of unleavened bread that is before Baba God.
You shall put all of this in Aaron’s hands, and in his sons’ hands, and shall wave dem for a wave offering before Baba God.
You shall take dem from dem hands, and burn dem on the altar on the burnt offering, for a pleasant aroma before Baba God: it is an offering made by fire to Baba God.
“You shall take the breast of Aaron’s ram of consecration, and wave it for a wave offering before Baba God: and it go be una portion.

You shall sanctify the breast of the wave offering, and the thigh of the wave offering, which is waved, and which is heaved up, of the ram of consecration, even of that which is for Aaron, and of that which is for his sons:

and it go be for Aaron and his sons as dem portion forever from the pikin dem of Israel; for it is a wave offering: and it go be a wave offering from the pikin dem of Israel of the sacrifices of dem peace offerings, even dem wave offering to Baba God.
“The holy garments of Aaron go be for his sons after him, to be anointed in dem, and to be consecrated in dem.
Seven days shall the son Wey be priest in his place put dem on, when he comes into the Tent of Meeting to minister in the holy place.
“You shall take the ram of consecration, and boil its meat in a holy place.
Aaron and his sons shall eat the meat of the ram, and the bread that is in the basket, at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
Dem shall eat those things with which atonement was made, to consecrate and sanctify dem: but a stranger no go eat of it, because Dem be holy.
If anything of the meat of the consecration, or of the bread, remains to the morning, then you shall burn the remainder with fire: it no go be eaten, because it is holy.
“You shall do so to Aaron, and to his sons, according to all that I have commanded you. You shall consecrate dem seven days.
Every day you shall offer the bull of sin offering for atonement: and you shall cleanse the altar, when you make atonement for it; and you shall anoint it, to sanctify it.
Seven days you shall make atonement for the altar, and sanctify it: and the altar go be most holy; Anything wey touches the altar go be holy.
“Now this is that which you shall offer on the altar: two lambs a year old day by day continually.
The one lamb you shall offer in the morning; and the other lamb you shall offer at evening:
and with the one lamb a tenth part of an ephah of fine flour mixed with the fourth part of a hin of beaten oil, and the fourth part of a hin of wine for a drink offering.

The other lamb you shall offer at evening, and shall do to it according to the meal offering of the morning, and according to its drink offering, for a pleasant aroma, an offering made by fire to Baba God.
It go be a continual burnt offering throughout una generations at the door of the Tent of Meeting before Baba God, where I go meet with you, to speak there to you.
There I go meet with the pikin dem of Israel; and the place go be sanctified by my glory.
I go sanctify the Tent of Meeting and the altar: Aaron also and his sons I go sanctify, to minister to me in the priest’s office.
I go live among the pikin dem of Israel, and Go be dem God.
Dem shall know that I be Baba God dem God, who bring dem out of the land of Egypt, that I might live among dem: I be Baba God dem God.
“You shall make an altar to burn incense on. You shall make it of acacia wood.
Its length go be a cubit, and its width a cubit. It go be square, and its height go be two cubits. Its horns go be of one piece with it.
You shall overlay it with pure gold, its top, its sides around it, and its horns; and you shall make a gold molding around it.
You shall make two golden rings for it under its molding; on its two ribs, on its two sides you shall make dem; and dem go be for places for poles with which to bear it.
You shall make the poles of acacia wood, and overlay dem with gold.
You shall put it before the veil that is by the ark of the testimony, before the mercy seat that is over the testimony, where I go meet with you.
Aaron shall burn incense of sweet spices on it every morning. When he tends the lamps, he shall burn it.
When Aaron lights the lamps at evening, he shall burn it, a perpetual incense before Baba God throughout una generations.
You shall offer no strange incense on it, nor burnt offering, nor meal offering; and you shall pour no drink offering on it.

Aaron shall make atonement on its horns once in the year; with the blood of the sin offering of atonement once in the year he shall make atonement for it throughout una generations. It is most holy to Baba God.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,

“When you take a census of the pikin dem of Israel, according to people Wey counted among dem, then each man shall give a ransom for his soul to Baba God, when you count dem; that there be no plague among dem when you count dem.
Dem shall give this, Everybody wey passes over to people Wey counted, half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary (the shekel is twenty gerahs ); half a shekel for an offering to Baba God.
Everybody wey passes over to people Wey counted, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the offering to Baba God.
The rich no go give more, and the poor no go give less, than the half shekel, when dem give the offering of Baba God, to make atonement for una souls.

You shall take the atonement money from the pikin dem of Israel, and shall appoint it for the service of the Tent of Meeting; that it may be a memorial for the pikin dem of Israel before Baba God, to make atonement for una souls.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“You shall also make a basin of brass, and its base of brass, in which to wash. You shall put it between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and you shall put water in it.
Aaron and his sons shall wash dem hands and dem feet in it.
When dem go into the Tent of Meeting, dem shall wash with water, that dem not die; or when dem come near to the altar to minister, to burn an offering made by fire to Baba God.
So dem shall wash dem hands and dem feet, that dem not die: and it go be a statute forever to dem, even to him and to his descendants throughout dem generations.”
Moreover Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Also take fine spices: of liquid myrrh, five hundred shekels; and of fragrant cinnamon half as much, even two hundred and fifty; and of fragrant cane, two hundred and fifty;
and of cassia five hundred, after the shekel of the sanctuary; and a hin of olive oil.
You shall make it a holy anointing oil, a perfume compounded after the art of the perfumer: it go be a holy anointing oil.
You shall use it to anoint the Tent of Meeting, the ark of the testimony,
the table and all its articles, the lamp stand and its accessories, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the basin with its base.
You shall sanctify dem, that dem may be most holy. Anything wey touches dem go be holy.
You shall anoint Aaron and his sons, and sanctify dem, that dem may minister to me in the priest’s office.
You shall speak to the pikin dem of Israel, saying, ‘This go be a holy anointing oil to me throughout una generations.
It no go be poured on man’s flesh, and No make any like it, according to its composition. It is holy. It go be holy to you.
Anybody wey compounds any like it, or Anybody wey puts any of it on a stranger, he go be cut off from his people.’”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Take to yourself sweet spices, gum resin, and onycha, and galbanum; sweet spices with pure frankincense: there go be an equal weight of each;
and you shall make incense of it, a perfume after the art of the perfumer, seasoned with salt, pure and holy:
and you shall beat some of it very small, and put some of it before the testimony in the Tent of Meeting, where I go meet with you. It go be to you most holy.
The incense which you shall make, according to its composition you no go make for unaself: it go be to you holy for Baba God.
Anybody wey shall make any like that, to smell of it, he go be cut off from his people.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“See am, I have call by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah:
and I have filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all kinds of workmanship,
to devise skillful works, to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass,
and in cutting of stones for setting, and in carving of wood, to work in all kinds of workmanship.

See am, I myself have appointed with him Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; and in the heart of all Wey be wise-hearted I have put wisdom, that dem may make all that I have commanded you:
the Tent of Meeting, the ark of the testimony, the mercy seat that is on it, all the furniture of the Tent,
the table and its vessels, the pure lamp stand with all its vessels, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering with all its vessels, the basin and its base,
the finely worked garments — the holy garments for Aaron the priest — the garments of his sons to minister in the priest’s office,
the anointing oil, and the incense of sweet spices for the holy place: according to all that I have commanded you dem shall do.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,

“Speak also to the pikin dem of Israel, saying, ‘Most certainly you shall keep my Sabbaths: for it is a sign between me and you throughout una generations; that you may know that I be Baba God who sanctifies you.
You shall keep the Sabbath so; for it is holy to you. Everybody wey profanes it shall surely be put to death; for Anybody wey does any work inside am, that soul go be cut off from among his people.
Six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day is a Sabbath of solemn rest, holy to Baba God. Anybody wey does any work on the Sabbath day shall surely be put to death.
So the pikin dem of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, to observe the Sabbath throughout dem generations, for a perpetual covenant.
It is a sign between me and the pikin dem of Israel forever; for in six days Baba God made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed.’”
He give to Moses, when he finished speaking with him on Mount Sinai, the two tablets of the testimony, stone tablets, written with God’s finger.

When the people see that Moses delayed to come down from the mountain, the people gathered themselves together to Aaron, and talk say to him, “Come, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man who bring us up out of the land of Egypt, we no know what has become of him.”
Aaron talk say to dem, “Take off the golden rings, which are in the ears of una wives, of una sons, and of una daughters, and bring dem to me.”
All the people take off the golden rings which were in dem ears, and bring dem to Aaron.
He received Wetin dem handed him, and fashioned it with an engraving tool, and made it a molten calf; and dem talk say, “These are una gods, Israel, which bring you up out of the land of Egypt.”
When Aaron see this, he built an altar before it; and Aaron made a proclamation, and talk say, “Tomorrow go be a feast to Baba God.”
Dem rose up early on the next day, and offered burnt offerings, and bring peace offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.
Baba God spoke to Moses, “Go, get down; for una people, who you bring up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves!

Dem have turned aside sharp-sharp out of the way which I commanded dem. Dem have made themselves a molten calf, and have worshiped it, and have sacrificed to it, and talk say, ‘These are una gods, Israel, which bring you up out of the land of Egypt.’”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “I have seen these people, and see am, Dem be a stiff-necked people.
Now so leave me alone, that my serious anger may burn hot against dem, and that I may consume dem; and I go make of you a great nation.”
Moses begged Baba God his God, and talk say, “Baba God, why does una serious anger burn hot against una people, that you have bring out of the land of Egypt with great power and with a mighty hand?

Why should the Egyptians speak, saying, ‘He bring dem out for evil, to kill dem in the mountains, and to consume dem from the surface of the earth?’ Turn from una fierce serious anger, and repent of this evil against una people.

Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, una workers, to whom you swore by una own self, and talk say to dem, ‘I go multiply una offspring as the stars of the sky, and all this land that I have spoken of I go give to una offspring, and dem shall inherit it forever.’”
Baba God repented of the evil which he talk say he would do to his people.
Moses turned, and go down from the mountain, with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand; tablets that were written on both dem sides; on the one side and on the other dem were written.
The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.
When Joshua heard the noise of the people as dem shouted, he talk say to Moses, “E get the noise of war in the camp.”
He talk say, “It no be the voice of people wey shout for victory. It No be the voice of people wey cry for being overcome; but the noise of people wey sing that I hear.”
As soon as he come near to the camp, he see the calf and the dancing. Then Moses’ anger grew hot, and he threw the tablets out of his hands, and broke dem beneath the mountain.
He take the calf which dem had made, and burned it with fire, ground it to powder, and scattered it on the water, and made the pikin dem of Israel drink of it.
Moses talk say to Aaron, “What did these people do to you, that you have bring a great sin on dem?”
Aaron talk say, “No let the anger of my lord grow hot. You know the people, that Dem be set on evil.
For dem talk say to me, ‘Make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man who bring us up out of the land of Egypt, we no know what has become of him.’
I talk say to dem, ‘Anybody wey has any gold, Make dem take it off:’ so dem give it to me; and I threw it into the fire, and out come this calf.”
When Moses see that the people had broken loose, (for Aaron had Make dem loose for a derision among dem enemies),
then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and talk say, “Anybody wey is on Baba God’s side, come to me!” All the sons of Levi gathered themselves together to him.

E tell dem say, “Baba God says, the God of Israel, ‘Every man put his sword on his thigh, and go back and forth from gate to gate throughout the camp, and every man kill his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbor.’”
The sons of Levi did according to the word of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men.
Moses talk say, “Consecrate unaself today to Baba God, yes, every man against his son, and against his brother; that he may give you a blessing today.”
On the next day, Moses talk say to the people, “You have sinned a great sin. Now I go go up to Baba God. Perhaps I shall make atonement for una sin.”
Moses come back to Baba God, and talk say, “Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made themselves gods of gold.
Yet now, if You go, forgive dem sin — and if not, please blot me out of una book which you have written.”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Anybody wey has sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.
Now go, lead the people to the place of which I have spoken to you. See am, my angel shall go before you. Nevertheless in the day when I punish, I go punish dem for dem sin.”
Baba God struck the people, because dem made the calf, which Aaron made.

Baba God spoke to Moses, “Depart, go up from here, you and the people that you have bring up out of the land of Egypt, to the land of which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, ‘I go give it to una offspring. ’
I go send an angel before you; and I go drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite:
to a land flowing with milk and honey: for I go not go up among you, for You be a stiff-necked people, lest I consume you on the way.”
When the people heard this evil news, dem mourned: and Nobody put on his jewelry.

Baba God talk say to Moses, “Tell the pikin dem of Israel, ‘You be a stiff-necked people. If I were to go up into the middle of you for one moment, I would consume you. So now take off una jewelry from you, that I may know what to do to you.’”
The pikin dem of Israel stripped themselves of dem jewelry from Mount Horeb onward.

Now Moses used to take the tent and to pitch it outside the camp, far away from the camp, and he call it “The Tent of Meeting.” Everybody wey sought Baba God go out to the Tent of Meeting, which was outside the camp.
When Moses go out to the Tent, that all the people rose up, and stood, everyone at dem tent door, and watched Moses, until he had gone into the Tent.
When Moses entered into the Tent, the pillar of cloud descended, stood at the door of the Tent, and spoke with Moses.
All the people see the pillar of cloud stand at the door of the Tent, and all the people rose up and worshiped, everyone at dem tent door.
Baba God spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. He turned again into the camp, but his worker Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, didn’t depart from the Tent.

Moses talk say to Baba God, “See am, you tell me, ‘Bring up this people:’ and you haven’t let me know whom You go send with me. Yet you have talk say, ‘I know you by name, and you have also find favor in my sight.’
Now so, if I have find favor in una sight, please show me now una way, that I may know you, so that I may find favor in una sight: and consider that this nation is una people.”
He talk say, “My presence will go with you, and I go give you rest.”
E tell am say, “If una presence no dey go with me, no carry us up from here.

For how would people know that I have find favor in una sight, I and una people? No be it that you go with us, so that We be separated, I and una people, from all the people Wey be on the surface of the earth?”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “I go do this thing also that you have spoken; for you have find favor in my sight, and I know you by name.”
He talk say, “Please show me una glory.”
He talk say, “I go make all my goodness pass before you, and will proclaim Baba God’s name before you. I go be gracious to whom I go be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I go show mercy.”
He talk say, “You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.”
Baba God also talk say, “See am, E get a place by me, and you shall stand on the rock.
It will happen, while my glory passes by, that I go put you in a cleft of the rock, and will cover you with my hand until I have passed by;
then I go take away my hand, and You go see my back; but my face no go be seen.”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Chisel two stone tablets like the first: and I go write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.
Be ready by the morning, and come up in the morning to Mount Sinai, and present yourself there to me on the top of the mountain.
Nobody shall come up with you or be seen anywhere on the mountain. No let the flocks or herds graze in front of that mountain.”
He chiseled two tablets of stone like the first; and Moses rose up early in the morning, and go up to Mount Sinai, as Baba God had commanded him, and take in his hand two stone tablets.
Baba God descended in the cloud, and stood with him there, and proclaimed Baba God’s name.
Baba God passed by before him, and proclaimed, “Baba God! Baba God, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth,

keeping loving kindness for thousands, forgiving wickedness and disobedience and sin; and that will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the wickedness of the fathers on the pikin dem, and on the pikin dem’s pikin dem, on the third and on the fourth generation.”
Moses hurried and bowed his head toward the earth, and worshiped.

He talk say, “If now I have find favor in una sight, Lord, please let the Lord go among us; although this is a stiff-necked people; pardon our wickedness and our sin, and take us for una inheritance.”

He talk say, “See am, I make a covenant: before all una people I go do marvels, such as have not been worked in all the earth, nor in any nation; and all the people among which You be shall see the work of Baba God; for it is an awesome thing that I do with you.
Observe that which I command you today. See am, I drive out before you the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
Be careful, lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land where You be going, lest it be for a snare in the middle of you:
but you shall break down dem altars, and dash in pieces dem pillars, and you shall cut down dem Asherah poles;
for you shall worship no other god: for Baba God, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.
“No make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, lest dem play the prostitute after dem gods, and sacrifice to dem gods, and one call you and you eat of his sacrifice;
and you take of dem daughters to una sons, and dem daughters play the prostitute after dem gods, and make una sons play the prostitute after dem gods.
“You shall make no throw idols for unaself.
“You shall keep the feast of unleavened bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the time appointed in the month Abib; for in the month Abib you come out of Egypt.
“All that opens the womb is mine; and all una livestock that is male, the firstborn of cow and sheep.
You shall redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb. If You go not redeem it, then you shall break its neck. You shall redeem all the firstborn of una sons. Nobody shall appear before me empty.
“Six days you shall work, but on the seventh day you shall rest: in plowing time and in harvest you shall rest.
“You shall observe the feast of weeks with the first fruits of wheat harvest, and the feast of harvest at the year’s end.
Three times in the year all una males shall appear before the Lord Baba God, the God of Israel.
For I go drive out nations before you and enlarge una borders; neither shall any man desire una land when you go up to appear before Baba God, una God, three times in the year.
“You no go offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread. The sacrifice of the feast of the Passover no go be left to the morning.
“You shall bring the first of the first fruits of una ground to the house of Baba God una God. “You no go boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Write you these words: for in accordance with these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.”
He was there with Baba God forty days and forty nights; he neither ate bread, nor drank water. He wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten commandments.

When Moses come down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the testimony in Moses’ hand, when he come down from the mountain, Moses didn’t know that the skin of his face shone by reason of his speaking with him.
When Aaron and all the pikin dem of Israel see Moses, see am, the skin of his face shone; and dem were afraid to come near him.
Moses call to dem, and Aaron and all the rulers of the congregation come back to him; and Moses spoke to dem.
Afterward all the pikin dem of Israel come near, and he give dem all the commandments that Baba God had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.
When Moses was done speaking with dem, he put a veil on his face.
