But when Moses go in before Baba God to speak with him, he take the veil off, until he come out; and he come out, and spoke to the pikin dem of Israel that which he was commanded.
The pikin dem of Israel see Moses’ face, that the skin of Moses’ face shone: and Moses put the veil on his face again, until he go in to speak with him.
Moses assembled all the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel, and talk say to dem, “These are the words which Baba God has commanded, that you should do dem.
‘Six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day there go be a holy day for you, a Sabbath of solemn rest to Baba God: Anybody wey does any work in it go be put to death.
You shall kindle no fire throughout una habitations on the Sabbath day.’”
Moses spoke to all the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel, saying, “This is the thing which Baba God commanded, saying,
‘Take from among you an offering to Baba God. Anybody wey is of a willing heart, Make e bring it, Baba God’s offering: gold, silver, brass,
blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats’ hair,
rams’ skins dyed red, sea cow hides, acacia wood,
oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet incense,
onyx stones, and stones to be set for the ephod and for the breastplate.
“‘Let every wise-hearted man among you come, and make all that Baba God has commanded:
the tabernacle, its outer covering, its roof, its clasps, its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets;
the ark, and its poles, the mercy seat, the veil of the screen;
the table with its poles and all its vessels, and the show bread;
the lamp stand also for the light, with its vessels, its lamps, and the oil for the light;
and the altar of incense with its poles, the anointing oil, the sweet incense, the screen for the door, at the door of the tabernacle;
the altar of burnt offering, with its grating of brass, it poles, and all its vessels, the basin and its base;
the hangings of the court, its pillars, dem sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court;
the pins of the tabernacle, the pins of the court, and dem cords;
the finely worked garments, for ministering in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest’s office.’”
All the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel comot from the presence of Moses.

Dem come, everyone whose heart stirred him up, and everyone whom his spirit made willing, and bring Baba God’s offering, for the work of the Tent of Meeting, and for all of its service, and for the holy garments.
Dem come, both men and women, as many as were willing-hearted, and bring brooches, earrings, signet rings, and armlets, all jewels of gold; even every man who offered an offering of gold to Baba God.
Everyone, with whom was find blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats’ hair, rams’ skins dyed red, and sea cow hides, bring dem.
Everybody wey offered an offering of silver and brass bring Baba God’s offering; and everyone, with whom was find acacia wood for any work of the service, bring it.
All the women who were wise-hearted spun with dem hands, and bring that which dem had spun, the blue, the purple, the scarlet, and the fine linen.
All the women whose heart stirred dem up in wisdom spun the goats’ hair.
The rulers bring the onyx stones, and the stones to be set, for the ephod and for the breastplate;
and the spice, and the oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the sweet incense.
The pikin dem of Israel bring a freewill offering to Baba God; every man and woman, whose heart made dem willing to bring for all the work, which Baba God had commanded to be made by Moses.
Moses talk say to the pikin dem of Israel, “See am, Baba God has call by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
He has filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all kinds of workmanship;
and to make skillful works, to work in gold, in silver, in brass,
in cutting of stones for setting, and in carving of wood, to work in all kinds of skillful workmanship.
He has put in his heart that he may teach, both he, and Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

He has filled dem with wisdom of heart, to work all kinds of workmanship, of the engraver, of the skillful workman, and of the embroiderer, in blue, in purple, in scarlet, and in fine linen, and of the weaver, even of people wey do any workmanship, and of people wey make skillful works.

“Bezalel and Oholiab shall work with every wise-hearted man, in whom Baba God has put wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work for the service of the sanctuary, according to all that Baba God has commanded.”
Moses call Bezalel and Oholiab, and every wise-hearted man, in whose heart Baba God had put wisdom, even everyone whose heart stirred him up to come to the work to do it:

and dem received from Moses all the offering which the pikin dem of Israel had bring for the work of the service of the sanctuary, with which to make it. Dem bring yet to him freewill offerings every morning.
All the wise men, who performed all the work of the sanctuary, each come from his work which dem did.
Dem spoke to Moses, saying, “The people bring much more than enough for the service of the work which Baba God commanded to make.”

Moses give commandment, and dem caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp, saying, “Let neither man nor woman make anything else for the offering for the sanctuary.” So the people were restrained from bringing.
For the stuff dem had was sufficient for all the work to make it, and too much.

All the wise-hearted men among people wey did the work made the tabernacle with ten curtains; of fine twined linen, blue, purple, and scarlet, with cherubim, the work of the skillful workman, dem made dem.
The length of each curtain was twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits. All the curtains had one measure.
He coupled five curtains to each other, and the other five curtains he coupled to each other.
He made loops of blue on the edge of the one curtain from the edge in the coupling. Likewise he made in the edge of the curtain that was outermost in the second coupling.
He made fifty loops in the one curtain, and he made fifty loops in the edge of the curtain that was in the second coupling. The loops were opposite to each other.
He made fifty clasps of gold, and coupled the curtains to each other with the clasps: so the tabernacle was a unit.
He made curtains of goats’ hair for a covering over the tabernacle. He made dem eleven curtains.
The length of each curtain was thirty cubits, and four cubits the width of each curtain. The eleven curtains had one measure.
He coupled five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves.
He made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that was outermost in the coupling, and he made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain which was outermost in the second coupling.
He made fifty clasps of brass to couple the tent together, that it might be a unit.
He made a covering for the tent of rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering of sea cow hides above.
He made the boards for the tabernacle of acacia wood, standing up.
Ten cubits was the length of a board, and a cubit and a half the width of each board.
Each board had two tenons, joined to each other. He made all the boards of the tabernacle this way.
He made the boards for the tabernacle: twenty boards for the south side southward.
He made forty sockets of silver under the twenty boards; two sockets under one board for its two tenons, and two sockets under another board for its two tenons.
For the second side of the tabernacle, on the north side, he made twenty boards,
and dem forty sockets of silver; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.
For the far part of the tabernacle westward he made six boards.
He made two boards for the corners of the tabernacle in the far part.
Dem were double beneath, and in the same way dem were all the way to its top to one ring. He did this to both of dem in the two corners.
There were eight boards, and dem sockets of silver, sixteen sockets; under every board two sockets.
He made bars of acacia wood; five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
and five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle for the hinder part westward.
He made the middle bar to pass through in the middle of the boards from the one end to the other.
He overlaid the boards with gold, and made dem rings of gold for places for the bars, and overlaid the bars with gold.
He made the veil of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen: with cherubim. He made it the work of a skillful workman.
He made four pillars of acacia for it, and overlaid dem with gold. Dem hooks were of gold. He throw four sockets of silver for dem.
He made a screen for the door of the tent, of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of an embroiderer;
and the five pillars of it with dem hooks. He overlaid dem capitals and dem fillets with gold, and dem five sockets were of brass.
Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood. Its length was two and a half cubits, and its width a cubit and a half, and a cubit and a half its height.
He overlaid it with pure gold inside and outside, and made a molding of gold for it around it.
He throw four rings of gold for it, in its four feet; even two rings on its one side, and two rings on its other side.
He made poles of acacia wood, and overlaid dem with gold.
He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to bear the ark.
He made a mercy seat of pure gold. Its length was two and a half cubits, and a cubit and a half its width.
He made two cherubim of gold. He made dem of beaten work, at the two ends of the mercy seat;
one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end. He made the cherubim of one piece with the mercy seat at its two ends.
The cherubim spread out dem wings on high, covering the mercy seat with dem wings, with dem faces toward each other. The faces of the cherubim were toward the mercy seat.
He made the table of acacia wood. Its length was two cubits, and its width was a cubit, and its height was a cubit and a half.
He overlaid it with pure gold, and made a gold molding around it.
He made a border of a hand width around it, and made a golden molding on its border around it.
He throw four rings of gold for it, and put the rings in the four corners that were on its four feet.
The rings were close by the border, the places for the poles to carry the table.
He made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid dem with gold, to carry the table.
He made the vessels which were on the table, its dishes, its spoons, its bowls, and its pitchers with which to pour out, of pure gold.
He made the lamp stand of pure gold. He made the lamp stand of beaten work. Its base, its shaft, its cups, its buds, and its flowers were of one piece with it.
There were six branches going out of its sides: three branches of the lamp stand out of its one side, and three branches of the lamp stand out of its other side:

three cups made like almond blossoms in one branch, a bud and a flower, and three cups made like almond blossoms in the other branch, a bud and a flower: so for the six branches going out of the lamp stand.
In the lamp stand were four cups made like almond blossoms, its buds and its flowers;
and a bud under two branches of one piece with it, and a bud under two branches of one piece with it, and a bud under two branches of one piece with it, for the six branches going out of it.
Dem buds and dem branches were of one piece with it. The whole thing was one beaten work of pure gold.
He made its seven lamps, and its snuffers, and its snuff dishes, of pure gold.
He made it of a talent of pure gold, with all its vessels.
He made the altar of incense of acacia wood. It was square: its length was a cubit, and its width a cubit. Its height was two cubits. Its horns were of one piece with it.
He overlaid it with pure gold, its top, its sides around it, and its horns. He made a gold molding around it.
He made two golden rings for it under its molding crown, on its two ribs, on its two sides, for places for poles with which to carry it.
He made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid dem with gold.
He made the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of sweet spices, after the art of the perfumer.
He made the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood. It was square. Its length was five cubits, its width was five cubits, and its height was three cubits.
He made its horns on its four corners. Its horns were of one piece with it, and he overlaid it with brass.
He made all the vessels of the altar, the pots, the shovels, the basins, the forks, and the fire pans. He made all its vessels of brass.
He made for the altar a grating of a network of brass, under the ledge around it beneath, reaching halfway up.
He throw four rings for the four ends of brass grating, to be places for the poles.
He made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid dem with brass.
He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, with which to carry it. He made it hollow with planks.
He made the basin of brass, and its base of brass, out of the mirrors of the ministering women who ministered at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
He made the court: for the south side southward the hangings of the court were of fine twined linen, one hundred cubits;
dem pillars were twenty, and dem sockets twenty, of brass; the hooks of the pillars and dem fillets were of silver.
For the north side one hundred cubits, dem pillars twenty, and dem sockets twenty, of brass; the hooks of the pillars, and dem fillets, of silver.
For the west side were hangings of fifty cubits, dem pillars ten, and dem sockets ten; the hooks of the pillars, and dem fillets, of silver.
For the east side eastward fifty cubits.
The hangings for the one side were fifteen cubits; dem pillars three, and dem sockets three;
and so for the other side: on this hand and that hand by the gate of the court were hangings of fifteen cubits; dem pillars three, and dem sockets three.
All the hangings around the court were of fine twined linen.

The sockets for the pillars were of brass. The hooks of the pillars and dem fillets were of silver; and the overlaying of dem capitals, of silver; and all the pillars of the court were filleted with silver.

The screen for the gate of the court was the work of the embroiderer, of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen. Twenty cubits was the length, and the height in the width was five cubits, like to the hangings of the court.
Dem pillars were four, and dem sockets four, of brass; dem hooks of silver, and the overlaying of dem capitals, and dem fillets, of silver.
All the pins of the tabernacle, and around the court, were of brass.

This is the amount of material used for the tabernacle, even the Tabernacle of the Testimony, as dem were counted, according to the commandment of Moses, for the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that Baba God commanded Moses.
With him was Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver, and a skillful workman, and an embroiderer in blue, in purple, in scarlet, and in fine linen.
All the gold that was used for the work in all the work of the sanctuary, even the gold of the offering, was twenty-nine talents, and seven hundred thirty shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary.
The silver of people wey were counted of the congregation was one hundred talents, and one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary:

a beka a head, that is, half a shekel, after the shekel of the sanctuary, for Everybody wey passed over to people wey were counted, from twenty years old and upward, for six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty men.
The one hundred talents of silver were for casting the sockets of the sanctuary, and the sockets of the veil; one hundred sockets for the one hundred talents, a talent for a socket.
Of the one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels he made hooks for the pillars, overlaid dem capitals, and made fillets for dem.
The brass of the offering was seventy talents, and two thousand four hundred shekels.
With this he made the sockets to the door of the Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar, the bronze grating for it, all the vessels of the altar,
the sockets around the court, the sockets of the gate of the court, all the pins of the tabernacle, and all the pins around the court.
Of the blue, purple, and scarlet, dem made finely worked garments, for ministering in the holy place, and made the holy garments for Aaron; as Baba God commanded Moses.
He made the ephod of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen.
Dem beat the gold into thin plates, and cut it into wires, to work it in the blue, in the purple, in the scarlet, and in the fine linen, the work of the skillful workman.
Dem made shoulder straps for it, joined together. At the two ends it was joined together.
The skillfully woven band that was on it, with which to fasten it on, was of the same piece, like its work; of gold, of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen; as Baba God commanded Moses.
Dem worked the onyx stones, enclosed in settings of gold, engraved with the engravings of a signet, according to the names of the pikin dem of Israel.
He put dem on the shoulder straps of the ephod, to be stones of memorial for the pikin dem of Israel, as Baba God commanded Moses.
He made the breastplate, the work of a skillful workman, like the work of the ephod; of gold, of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen.
It was square. Dem made the breastplate double. Its length was a span, and its width a span, being double.
Dem set in it four rows of stones. A row of ruby, topaz, and beryl was the first row;
and the second row, a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald;
and the third row, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
and the fourth row, a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper. Dem were enclosed in gold settings.
The stones were according to the names of the pikin dem of Israel, twelve, according to dem names; like the engravings of a signet, everyone according to his name, for the twelve tribes.
Dem made on the breastplate chains like cords, of braided work of pure gold.
Dem made two settings of gold, and two gold rings, and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.
Dem put the two braided chains of gold in the two rings at the ends of the breastplate.
The other two ends of the two braided chains dem put on the two settings, and put dem on the shoulder straps of the ephod, in its front.
Dem made two rings of gold, and put dem on the two ends of the breastplate, on its edge, which was toward the side of the ephod inward.
Dem made two rings of gold, and put dem on the two shoulder straps of the ephod underneath, in its front, close by its coupling, above the skillfully woven band of the ephod.

Dem bound the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it might be on the skillfully woven band of the ephod, and that the breastplate might not come loose from the ephod, as Baba God commanded Moses.
He made the robe of the ephod of woven work, all of blue.
The opening of the robe in the middle of it was like the opening of a coat of mail, with a binding around its opening, that it no suppose be torn.
Dem made on the skirts of the robe pomegranates of blue, purple, scarlet, and twined linen.
Dem made bells of pure gold, and put the bells between the pomegranates around the skirts of the robe, between the pomegranates;
a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, around the skirts of the robe, to minister in, as Baba God commanded Moses.
Dem made the coats of fine linen of woven work for Aaron, and for his sons,
and the turban of fine linen, and the linen headbands of fine linen, and the linen breeches of fine twined linen,
and the sash of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, the work of the embroiderer, as Baba God commanded Moses.
Dem made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, and wrote on it a writing, like the engravings of a signet: “HOLY TO Baba God”.
Dem tied to it a lace of blue, to fasten it on the turban above, as Baba God commanded Moses.
Thus all the work of the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting was finished. The pikin dem of Israel did according to all that Baba God commanded Moses; so dem did.
Dem bring the tabernacle to Moses, the tent, with all its furniture, its clasps, its boards, its bars, its pillars, its sockets,
the covering of rams’ skins dyed red, the covering of sea cow hides, the veil of the screen,
the ark of the testimony with its poles, the mercy seat,
the table, all its vessels, the show bread,
the pure lamp stand, its lamps, even the lamps to be set in order, all its vessels, the oil for the light,
the golden altar, the anointing oil, the sweet incense, the screen for the door of the Tent,
the bronze altar, its grating of brass, its poles, all of its vessels, the basin and its base,
the hangings of the court, its pillars, its sockets, the screen for the gate of the court, its cords, its pins, all the instruments of the service of the tabernacle, for the Tent of Meeting,
the finely worked garments for ministering in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest’s office.
According to all that Baba God commanded Moses, so the pikin dem of Israel did all the work.
Moses see all the work, and see am, dem had done it as Baba God had commanded, even so had dem done it: and Moses blessed dem.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“On the first day of the first month you shall raise up the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting.
You shall put the ark of the testimony in it, and you shall screen the ark with the veil.
You shall bring in the table, and set in order the things that are on it. You shall bring in the lamp stand, and light its lamps.
You shall set the golden altar for incense before the ark of the testimony, and put the screen of the door to the tabernacle.
“You shall set the altar of burnt offering before the door of the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting.
You shall set the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and shall put water inside am.
You shall set up the court around it, and hang up the screen of the gate of the court.
“You shall take the anointing oil, and anoint the tabernacle, and all that is in it, and shall make it holy, and all its furniture: and it Go be holy.
You shall anoint the altar of burnt offering, with all its vessels, and sanctify the altar: and the altar Go be most holy.
You shall anoint the basin and its base, and sanctify it.
“You shall bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and shall wash dem with water.
You shall put on Aaron the holy garments; and you shall anoint him, and sanctify him, that he may minister to me in the priest’s office.
You shall bring his sons, and put coats on dem.
You shall anoint dem, as you anointed dem father, that dem may minister to me in the priest’s office. Dem anointing go be to dem for an everlasting priesthood throughout dem generations.”
Moses did so. According to all that Baba God commanded him, so he did.
In the first month in the second year, on the first day of the month, the tabernacle was raised up.
Moses raised up the tabernacle, and laid its sockets, and set up its boards, and put in its bars, and raised up its pillars.
He spread the covering over the tent, and put the roof of the tabernacle above on it, as Baba God commanded Moses.
He take and put the testimony into the ark, and set the poles on the ark, and put the mercy seat above on the ark.
He bring the ark into the tabernacle, and set up the veil of the screen, and screened the ark of the testimony, as Baba God commanded Moses.
He put the table in the Tent of Meeting, on the side of the tabernacle northward, outside of the veil.
He set the bread in order on it before Baba God, as Baba God commanded Moses.
He put the lamp stand in the Tent of Meeting, opposite the table, on the side of the tabernacle southward.
He lit the lamps before Baba God, as Baba God commanded Moses.
He put the golden altar in the Tent of Meeting before the veil;
and he burned incense of sweet spices on it, as Baba God commanded Moses.
He put up the screen of the door to the tabernacle.
He set the altar of burnt offering at the door of the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting, and offered on it the burnt offering and the meal offering, as Baba God commanded Moses.
He set the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put water inside am, with which to wash.
Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed dem hands and dem feet there.
When dem go into the Tent of Meeting, and when dem come near to the altar, dem washed, as Baba God commanded Moses.
He raised up the court around the tabernacle and the altar, and set up the screen of the gate of the court. So Moses finished the work.
Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and Baba God’s glory filled the tabernacle.
Moses no be able to enter into the Tent of Meeting, because the cloud stayed on it, and Baba God’s glory filled the tabernacle.
When the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the pikin dem of Israel go onward, throughout all dem journeys;
but if the cloud no be taken up, then dem didn’t travel until the day that it was taken up.
For the cloud of Baba God was on the tabernacle by day, and there was fire in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all dem journeys.
Baba God call to Moses, and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem, ‘When anyone of you offers an offering to Baba God, you shall offer una offering of the livestock, from the herd and from the flock.
“‘If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he shall offer a male without defect. He shall offer it at the door of the Tent of Meeting, that he may be accepted before Baba God.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it go be accepted for him to make atonement for him.
He shall kill the bull before Baba God. Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall present the blood and sprinkle the blood around on the altar that is at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
He shall flay the burnt offering, and cut it into pieces.
The sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire on the altar, and lay wood in order on the fire;
and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall lay the pieces, the head, and the fat in order on the wood that is on the fire which is on the altar;
but its innards and its legs he shall wash with water. The priest shall burn all of it on the altar, for a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Baba God.
“‘If his offering is from the flock, from the sheep, or from the goats, for a burnt offering, he shall offer a male without defect.
He shall kill it on the north side of the altar before Baba God. Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall sprinkle its blood around on the altar.
He shall cut it into its pieces, with its head and its fat. The priest shall lay dem in order on the wood that is on the fire which is on the altar,
but the innards and the legs he shall wash with water. The priest shall offer the whole, and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Baba God.
“‘If his offering to Baba God is a burnt offering of birds, then he shall offer his offering of turtledoves or of young pigeons.
The priest shall bring it to the altar, and wring off its head, and burn it on the altar; and its blood go be drained out on the side of the altar;
and he shall take away its crop with its filth, and throw it beside the altar on the east part, in the place of the ashes.

He shall tear it by its wings, but no go divide it apart. The priest shall burn it on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Baba God.
“‘When anyone offers an offering of a meal offering to Baba God, his offering go be of fine flour. He shall pour oil on it, and put frankincense on it.

He shall bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests; and he shall take his handful of its fine flour, and of its oil, with all its frankincense; and the priest shall burn its memorial on the altar, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Baba God.
That which is left of the meal offering go be Aaron’s and his sons’. It is a most holy thing of the offerings of Baba God made by fire.
“‘When you offer an offering of a meal offering baked in the oven, it go be unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers anointed with oil.
If una offering is a meal offering of the griddle, it go be of unleavened fine flour, mixed with oil.
You shall cut it in pieces, and pour oil on it. It is a meal offering.
If una offering is a meal offering of the pan, it go be made of fine flour with oil.
You shall bring the meal offering that is made of these things to Baba God: and it go be presented to the priest, and he shall bring it to the altar.
The priest shall take from the meal offering its memorial, and shall burn it on the altar, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Baba God.
That which is left of the meal offering go be Aaron’s and his sons’. It is a thing most holy of the offerings of Baba God made by fire.
“‘No meal offering, which you shall offer to Baba God, go be made with yeast; for you shall burn no yeast, nor any honey, as an offering made by fire to Baba God.
As an offering of first fruits you shall offer dem to Baba God: but dem no go rise up for a pleasant aroma on the altar.
Every offering of una meal offering you shall season with salt. You no go allow the salt of the covenant of una God to be lacking from una meal offering. With all una offerings you shall offer salt.
“‘If you offer a meal offering of first fruits to Baba God, you shall offer for the meal offering of una first fruits grain in the ear parched with fire, bruised grain of the fresh ear.
You shall put oil on it, and lay frankincense on it: it is a meal offering.
The priest shall burn as its memorial, part of its bruised grain, and part of its oil, along with all its frankincense: it is an offering made by fire to Baba God.
“‘If his offering is a sacrifice of peace offerings; if he offers it from the herd, whether male or female, he shall offer it without defect before Baba God.
He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and kill it at the door of the Tent of Meeting: and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall sprinkle the blood around on the altar.
He shall offer of the sacrifice of peace offerings an offering made by fire to Baba God; the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,
and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on dem, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kidneys, he shall take away.
Aaron’s sons shall burn it on the altar on the burnt offering, which is on the wood that is on the fire: it is an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Baba God.
“‘If his offering for a sacrifice of peace offerings to Baba God is from the flock; male or female, he shall offer it without defect.
If he offers a lamb for his offering, then he shall offer it before Baba God;
and he shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and kill it before the Tent of Meeting: and Aaron’s sons shall sprinkle its blood around on the altar.

He shall offer from the sacrifice of peace offerings an offering made by fire to Baba God; its fat, the entire tail fat, he shall take away close to the backbone; and the fat that covers the inwards, and all the fat that is on the inwards,
and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on dem, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kidneys, he shall take away.
The priest shall burn it on the altar: it is the chop of the offering made by fire to Baba God.
“‘If his offering is a goat, then he shall offer it before Baba God:
and he shall lay his hand on its head, and kill it before the Tent of Meeting; and the sons of Aaron shall sprinkle its blood around on the altar.
He shall offer from it as his offering, an offering made by fire to Baba God; the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,
and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on dem, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kidneys, he shall take away.
The priest shall burn dem on the altar: it is the chop of the offering made by fire, for a pleasant aroma; all the fat is Baba God’s.
“‘It go be a perpetual statute throughout una generations in all una dwellings, that you shall eat neither fat nor blood.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, saying, ‘If anyone sins unintentionally, in any of the things which Baba God has commanded not to be done, and does any one of dem:
if the anointed priest sins so as to bring guilt on the people, then Make e offer for his sin, which he has sinned, a young bull without defect to Baba God for a sin offering.
He shall bring the bull to the door of the Tent of Meeting before Baba God; and he shall lay his hand on the head of the bull, and kill the bull before Baba God.
The anointed priest shall take some of the blood of the bull, and bring it to the Tent of Meeting.
The priest shall dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of the blood seven times before Baba God, before the veil of the sanctuary.

The priest shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of sweet incense before Baba God, which is in the Tent of Meeting; and he shall pour out all of rest of the blood of the bull at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
He shall take all the fat of the bull of the sin offering off of it; the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,
and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on dem, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kidneys, he shall take away,
as it is taken off of the bull of the sacrifice of peace offerings. The priest shall burn dem on the altar of burnt offering.
The bull’s skin, all its meat, with its head, and with its legs, its innards, and its dung,
he shall carry the whole bull outside of the camp to a clean place, where the ashes are poured out, and burn it on wood with fire. Where the ashes are poured out, it go be burned.
“‘If the whole congregation of Israel sins, and the thing is hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and dem have done any of the things which Baba God has commanded not to be done, and are guilty;
when the sin in which dem have sinned is known, then the assembly shall offer a young bull for a sin offering, and bring it before the Tent of Meeting.
The elders of the congregation shall lay dem hands on the head of the bull before Baba God; and the bull go be killed before Baba God.
The anointed priest shall bring of the blood of the bull to the Tent of Meeting:
and the priest shall dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle it seven times before Baba God, before the veil.

He shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar which is before Baba God, that is in the Tent of Meeting; and the rest of the blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
All its fat he shall take from it, and burn it on the altar.
Thus shall he do with the bull; as he did with the bull of the sin offering, so shall he do with this; and the priest shall make atonement for dem, and dem go be forgiven.
He shall carry the bull outside the camp, and burn it as he burned the first bull. It is the sin offering for the assembly.
“‘When a ruler sins, and unwittingly does any one of all the things which Baba God his God has commanded not to be done, and is guilty;
if his sin, in which he has sinned, is made known to him, he shall bring as his offering a goat, a male without defect.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the goat, and kill it in the place where dem kill the burnt offering before Baba God. It is a sin offering.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He shall pour out the rest of its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.
All its fat he shall burn on the altar, like the fat of the sacrifice of peace offerings; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin, and he Go be forgiven.
“‘If anyone of the common people sins unwittingly, in doing any of the things which Baba God has commanded not to be done, and is guilty;
if his sin, which he has sinned, is made known to him, then he shall bring for his offering a goat, a female without defect, for his sin which he has sinned.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and kill the sin offering in the place of burnt offering.
The priest shall take some of its blood with his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering; and the rest of its blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar.

All its fat he shall take away, like the fat is taken away from off of the sacrifice of peace offerings; and the priest shall burn it on the altar for a pleasant aroma to Baba God; and the priest shall make atonement for him, and he Go be forgiven.
“‘If he brings a lamb as his offering for a sin offering, he shall bring a female without defect.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and kill it for a sin offering in the place where dem kill the burnt offering.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering; and all the rest of its blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar.

All its fat he shall take away, like the fat of the lamb is taken away from the sacrifice of peace offerings; and the priest shall burn dem on the altar, on the offerings of Baba God made by fire; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin that he has sinned, and he Go be forgiven.
“‘If anyone sins, in that he hears the voice of adjuration, he being a witness, whether he has seen or known, if he no dey report it, then he shall bear his wickedness.

“‘Or if anyone touches any unclean thing, whether it is the carcass of an unclean animal, or the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of unclean creeping things, and it is hidden from him, and he is unclean, then he go be guilty.
“‘Or if he touches the uncleanness of man, Anything wey his uncleanness is with which he is unclean, and it is hidden from him; when he knows of it, then he go be guilty.

“‘Or if anyone swears rashly with his lips to do evil, or to do good, Anything wey it is that a man might utter rashly with an oath, and it is hidden from him; when he knows of it, then he go be guilty of one of these.
It go be, when he is guilty of one of these, he shall confess that in which he has sinned:

and he shall bring his trespass offering to Baba God for his sin which he has sinned, a female from the flock, a lamb or a goat, for a sin offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin.

“‘If he no fit afford a lamb, then he shall bring his trespass offering for that in which he has sinned, two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, to Baba God; one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering.
He shall bring dem to the priest, who shall first offer the one which is for the sin offering, and wring off its head from its neck, but no go sever it completely.
He shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar; and the rest of the blood go be drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
He shall offer the second for a burnt offering, according to the ordinance; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin which he has sinned, and he go be forgiven.

“‘But if he no fit afford two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, then he shall bring his offering for that in which he has sinned, one tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering. He shall put no oil on it, and he no go put any frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.
He shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take his handful of it as the memorial portion, and burn it on the altar, on the offerings of Baba God made by fire. It is a sin offering.
The priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin that he has sinned in any of these things, and he Go be forgiven; and the rest go be the priest’s, as the meal offering.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,

“If anyone commits a trespass, and sins unwittingly, in the holy things of Baba God; then he shall bring his trespass offering to Baba God, a ram without defect from the flock, according to una estimation in silver by shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary, for a trespass offering.

He shall make restitution for that which he has done wrong in the holy thing, and shall add a fifth part to it, and give it to the priest; and the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the trespass offering, and he Go be forgiven.
“If anyone sins, and does any of the things which Baba God has commanded not to be done; though he didn’t know it, yet he is guilty, and shall bear his wickedness.

He shall bring a ram without defect from of the flock, according to una estimation, for a trespass offering, to the priest; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning the thing in which he sinned and didn’t know it, and he Go be forgiven.
It is a trespass offering. He is certainly guilty before Baba God.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“If anyone sins, and commits a trespass against Baba God, and deals falsely with his neighbor in a matter of deposit, or of bargain, or of robbery, or has oppressed his neighbor,
or has find that which was lost, and dealt falsely inside am, and swearing to a lie; in any of these things that a man does, sinning inside am;

then it go be, if he has sinned, and is guilty, he shall restore that which he take by robbery, or the thing which he has gotten by oppression, or the deposit which was committed to him, or the lost thing which he find,

or any thing about which he has sworn falsely; he shall restore it even in full, and shall add a fifth part more to it. To him to whom it belongs he shall give it, in the day of his being find guilty.
He shall bring his trespass offering to Baba God, a ram without defect from the flock, according to una estimation, for a trespass offering, to the priest.
The priest shall make atonement for him before Baba God, and he Go be forgiven concerning Anything wey he does to become guilty.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,

“Command Aaron and his sons, saying, ‘This is the law of the burnt offering: the burnt offering go be on the hearth on the altar all night until the morning; and the fire of the altar go be kept burning on it.

The priest shall put on his linen garment, and he shall put on his linen breeches upon his body; and he shall remove the ashes from where the fire has consumed the burnt offering on the altar, and he shall put dem beside the altar.
He shall take off his garments, and put on other garments, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.

The fire on the altar go be kept burning on it, it no go go out; and the priest shall burn wood on it every morning: and he shall lay the burnt offering in order upon it, and shall burn on it the fat of the peace offerings.
Fire go be kept burning on the altar continually; it no go go out.
“‘This is the law of the meal offering: the sons of Aaron shall offer it before Baba God, before the altar.

He shall take from there his handful of the fine flour of the meal offering, and of its oil, and all the frankincense which is on the meal offering, and shall burn it on the altar for a pleasant aroma, as its memorial, to Baba God.
That which is left of it Aaron and his sons shall eat. It go be eaten without yeast in a holy place. Dem shall eat it in the court of the Tent of Meeting.
It no go be baked with yeast. I have given it as dem portion of my offerings made by fire. It is most holy, as the sin offering, and as the trespass offering.
Every male among the pikin dem of Aaron shall eat of it, as dem portion forever throughout una generations, from the offerings of Baba God made by fire. Anybody wey touches dem go be holy.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,

“This is the offering of Aaron and of his sons, which dem shall offer to Baba God in the day when he is anointed: one tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a meal offering perpetually, half of it in the morning, and half of it in the evening.
It go be made with oil in a griddle. When it is soaked, you shall bring it in. You shall offer the meal offering in baked pieces for a pleasant aroma to Baba God.
The anointed priest that Go be in his place from among his sons shall offer it. By a statute forever, it go be wholly burned to Baba God.
Every meal offering of a priest go be wholly burned. It no go be eaten.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying, ‘This is the law of the sin offering: in the place where the burnt offering is killed, the sin offering go be killed before Baba God. It is most holy.
The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it. It go be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the Tent of Meeting.
Anything wey shall touch its flesh go be holy. When E get any of its blood sprinkled on a garment, you shall wash that on which it was sprinkled in a holy place.
But the earthen vessel in which it is boiled go be broken; and if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, it go be scoured, and rinsed in water.
Every male among the priests shall eat of it: it is most holy.
No sin offering, of which any of the blood is bring into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place, go be eaten: it go be burned with fire.
“‘This is the law of the trespass offering. It is most holy.
In the place where dem kill the burnt offering, he shall kill the trespass offering; and its blood he shall sprinkle around on the altar.
He shall offer all of its fat: the fat tail, and the fat that covers the innards,
and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on dem, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kidneys, shall he take away;
and the priest shall burn dem on the altar for an offering made by fire to Baba God: it is a trespass offering.
Every male among the priests may eat of it. It go be eaten in a holy place. It is most holy.
“‘As is the sin offering, so is the trespass offering; E get one law for dem. The priest who makes atonement with dem go get it.
The priest who offers any man’s burnt offering, even the priest go get for imself the skin of the burnt offering which he has offered.
Every meal offering that is baked in the oven, and all that is dressed in the pan, and on the griddle, go be the priest’s who offers it.
Every meal offering, mixed with oil or dry, belongs to all the sons of Aaron, one as well as another.
“‘This is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings, which one shall offer to Baba God.
If he offers it for a thanksgiving, then he shall offer with the sacrifice of thanksgiving unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and cakes mixed with oil.
With cakes of leavened bread he shall offer his offering with the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving.
Of it he shall offer one out of each offering for a heave offering to Baba God. It go be the priest’s who sprinkles the blood of the peace offerings.
The flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving go be eaten on the day of his offering. He no go leave any of it until the morning.
“‘But if the sacrifice of his offering is a vow, or a freewill offering, it go be eaten on the day that he offers his sacrifice; and on the next day what remains of it go be eaten:
but what remains of the meat of the sacrifice on the third day go be burned with fire.

If any of the meat of the sacrifice of his peace offerings is eaten on the third day, it No go be accepted, and it no go be credited to him who offers it. It Go be an abomination, and the soul who eats any of it will bear his wickedness.
“‘The meat that touches any unclean thing no go be eaten. It go be burned with fire. As for the meat, everyone Wey be clean may eat it;
but the soul who eats of the meat of the sacrifice of peace offerings, that belongs to Baba God, having his uncleanness on him, that soul go be cut off from his people.

When anyone touches any unclean thing, the uncleanness of man, or an unclean animal, or any unclean abomination, and eats some of the meat of the sacrifice of peace offerings, which belong to Baba God, that soul go be cut off from his people.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, saying, ‘You shall eat no fat, of bull, or sheep, or goat.
The fat of that which dies of itself, and the fat of that which is torn of animals, may be used for any other service, but you shall in no way eat of it.
For Anybody wey eats the fat of the animal, of which men offer an offering made by fire to Baba God, even the soul who eats it go be cut off from his people.
You no go eat any blood, whether it is of bird or of animal, in any of una dwellings.
Anybody wey it is who eats any blood, that soul go be cut off from his people.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, saying, ‘Person wey offers the sacrifice of his peace offerings to Baba God shall bring his offering to Baba God out of the sacrifice of his peace offerings.
With his own hands he shall bring the offerings of Baba God made by fire. He shall bring the fat with the breast, that the breast may be waved for a wave offering before Baba God.
The priest shall burn the fat on the altar, but the breast go be Aaron’s and his sons’.
The right thigh you shall give to the priest for a heave offering out of the sacrifices of una peace offerings.
He among the sons of Aaron who offers the blood of the peace offerings, and the fat, go get the right thigh for a portion.

For the waved breast and the heaved thigh I have taken from the pikin dem of Israel out of the sacrifices of dem peace offerings, and have given dem to Aaron the priest and to his sons as dem portion forever from the pikin dem of Israel.’”

This is the anointing portion of Aaron, and the anointing portion of his sons, out of the offerings of Baba God made by fire, in the day when he presented dem to minister to Baba God in the priest’s office;
which Baba God commanded to be given dem of the pikin dem of Israel, in the day that he anointed dem. It is dem portion forever throughout dem generations.
This is the law of the burnt offering, of the meal offering, and of the sin offering, and of the trespass offering, and of the consecration, and of the sacrifice of peace offerings;
which Baba God commanded Moses in Mount Sinai, in the day that he commanded the pikin dem of Israel to offer dem offerings to Baba God, in the wilderness of Sinai.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Take Aaron and his sons with him, and the garments, and the anointing oil, and the bull of the sin offering, and the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread;
and assemble all the congregation at the door of the Tent of Meeting.”
Moses did as Baba God commanded him; and the congregation was assembled at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
Moses talk say to the congregation, “This is the thing which Baba God has commanded to be done.”
Moses bring Aaron and his sons, and washed dem with water.
He put the coat on him, tied the sash on him, clothed him with the robe, put the ephod on him, and he tied the skillfully woven band of the ephod on him, and fastened it to him with it.
He placed the breastplate on him; and in the breastplate he put the Urim and the Thummim.
He set the turban on his head; and on the turban, in front, he set the golden plate, the holy crown; as Baba God commanded Moses.
Moses take the anointing oil, and anointed the tabernacle and all that was in it, and sanctified dem.
He sprinkled it on the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all its vessels, and the basin and its base, to sanctify dem.
He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, and anointed him, to sanctify him.
Moses bring Aaron’s sons, and clothed dem with coats, and tied sashes on dem, and put headbands on dem; as Baba God commanded Moses.
He bring the bull of the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid dem hands on the head of the bull of the sin offering.

He killed it; and Moses take the blood, and put it around on the horns of the altar with his finger, and purified the altar, and poured out the blood at the base of the altar, and sanctified it, to make atonement for it.
He take all the fat that was on the innards, and the cover of the liver, and the two kidneys, and dem fat; and Moses burned it on the altar.
But the bull, and its skin, and its meat, and its dung, he burned with fire outside the camp; as Baba God commanded Moses.
He presented the ram of the burnt offering: and Aaron and his sons laid dem hands on the head of the ram.
He killed it; and Moses sprinkled the blood around on the altar.
He cut the ram into its pieces; and Moses burned the head, and the pieces, and the fat.

He washed the innards and the legs with water; and Moses burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering for a pleasant aroma. It was an offering made by fire to Baba God; as Baba God commanded Moses.
He presented the other ram, the ram of consecration: and Aaron and his sons laid dem hands on the head of the ram.
He killed it; and Moses take some of its blood, and put it on the tip of Aaron’s right ear, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the great toe of his right foot.

He bring Aaron’s sons; and Moses put some of the blood on the tip of dem right ear, and on the thumb of dem right hand, and on the great toe of dem right foot; and Moses sprinkled the blood around on the altar.
He take the fat, and the fat tail, and all the fat that was on the innards, and the cover of the liver, and the two kidneys, and dem fat, and the right thigh;
and out of the basket of unleavened bread, that was before Baba God, he take one unleavened cake, and one cake of oiled bread, and one wafer, and placed dem on the fat, and on the right thigh.
He put all these in Aaron’s hands and in his sons’ hands, and waved dem for a wave offering before Baba God.
Moses take dem from dem hands, and burned dem on the altar on the burnt offering. Dem were a consecration for a pleasant aroma. It was an offering made by fire to Baba God.
Moses take the breast, and waved it for a wave offering before Baba God. It was Moses’ portion of the ram of consecration, as Baba God commanded Moses.

Moses take some of the anointing oil, and some of the blood which was on the altar, and sprinkled it on Aaron, on his garments, and on his sons, and on his sons’ garments with him, and sanctified Aaron, his garments, and his sons, and his sons’ garments with him.

Moses talk say to Aaron and to his sons, “Boil the meat at the door of the Tent of Meeting, and there eat it and the bread that is in the basket of consecration, as I commanded, saying, ‘Aaron and his sons shall eat it.’
What remains of the meat and of the bread you shall burn with fire.
You no go go out from the door of the Tent of Meeting seven days, until the days of una consecration are fulfilled: for he shall consecrate you seven days.
What Don dey done today, so Baba God has commanded to do, to make atonement for you.
You shall stay at the door of the Tent of Meeting day and night seven days, and keep Baba God’s command, that you no die: for so I be commanded.”
Aaron and his sons did all the things which Baba God commanded by Moses.
On the eighth day, Moses call Aaron and his sons, and the elders of Israel;
and he talk say to Aaron, “Take a calf from the herd for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering, without defect, and offer dem before Baba God.
You shall speak to the pikin dem of Israel, saying, ‘Take a male goat for a sin offering; and a calf and a lamb, both a year old, without defect, for a burnt offering;
and a bull and a ram for peace offerings, to sacrifice before Baba God; and a meal offering mixed with oil: for today Baba God appears to you.’”
Dem bring what Moses commanded before the Tent of Meeting: and all the congregation come near and stood before Baba God.
Moses talk say, “This is the thing which Baba God commanded that you should do: and Baba God’s glory shall appear to you.”

Moses talk say to Aaron, “Draw near to the altar, and offer una sin offering, and una burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself, and for the people; and offer the offering of the people, and make atonement for dem; as Baba God commanded.”
So Aaron come near to the altar, and killed the calf of the sin offering, which was for imself.
The sons of Aaron presented the blood to him; and he dipped his finger in the blood, and put it on the horns of the altar, and poured out the blood at the base of the altar:
but the fat, and the kidneys, and the cover from the liver of the sin offering, he burned upon the altar; as Baba God commanded Moses.
The meat and the skin he burned with fire outside the camp.
He killed the burnt offering; and Aaron’s sons delivered the blood to him, and he sprinkled it around on the altar.
Dem delivered the burnt offering to him, piece by piece, and the head: and he burned dem upon the altar.
He washed the innards and the legs, and burned dem on the burnt offering on the altar.
He presented the people’s offering, and take the goat of the sin offering which was for the people, and killed it, and offered it for sin, like the first.
He presented the burnt offering, and offered it according to the ordinance.
He presented the meal offering, and filled his hand from there, and burned it upon the altar, besides the burnt offering of the morning.
He also killed the bull and the ram, the sacrifice of peace offerings, which was for the people: and Aaron’s sons delivered to him the blood, which he sprinkled around on the altar,
and the fat of the bull and of the ram, the fat tail, and that which covers the innards, and the kidneys, and the cover of the liver:
and dem put the fat upon the breasts, and he burned the fat on the altar:
and the breasts and the right thigh Aaron waved for a wave offering before Baba God, as Moses commanded.
Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people, and blessed dem; and he come down from offering the sin offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings.
Moses and Aaron go into the Tent of Meeting, and come out, and blessed the people: and Baba God’s glory appeared to all the people.
Fire come out from before Baba God, and consumed the burnt offering and the fat upon the altar. When all the people see it, dem shouted, and fell on dem faces.
Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, each take his censer, and put fire in it, and laid incense on it, and offered strange fire before Baba God, which he had not commanded dem.
Fire come out from before Baba God, and devoured dem, and dem died before Baba God.
Then Moses talk say to Aaron, “This is what Baba God spoke of, saying, ‘I go show myself holy to people wey come near me, and before all the people I go be glorified.’” Aaron held his peace.
Moses call Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron, and talk say to dem, “Draw near, carry una brothers from before the sanctuary out of the camp.”
So dem come near, and carried dem in dem coats out of the camp, as Moses had talk say.

Moses talk say to Aaron, and to Eleazar and to Ithamar, his sons, “No let the hair of una heads go loose, and no tear una clothes; so that you no die, and so that he not be angry with all the congregation; but let una brothers, the whole house of Israel, bewail the burning which Baba God has kindled.
You no go go out from the door of the Tent of Meeting, lest you die; for the anointing oil of Baba God is on you.” Dem did according to the word of Moses.
Then Baba God talk say to Aaron,
“You and una sons No be to drink wine or strong drink whenever you go into the Tent of Meeting, or You go die. This go be a statute forever throughout una generations.
You be to make a distinction between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean.
You be to teach the pikin dem of Israel all the statutes which Baba God has spoken to dem by Moses.”

Moses spoke to Aaron, and to Eleazar and to Ithamar, his sons who were left, “Take the meal offering that remains of the offerings of Baba God made by fire, and eat it without yeast beside the altar; for it is most holy;
and you shall eat it in a holy place, because it is una portion, and una sons’ portion, of the offerings of Baba God made by fire: for so I be commanded.

The waved breast and the heaved thigh you shall eat in a clean place, you, and una sons, and una daughters with you: for Dem be given as una portion, and una sons’ portion, out of the sacrifices of the peace offerings of the pikin dem of Israel.

The heaved thigh and the waved breast dem shall bring with the offerings made by fire of the fat, to wave it for a wave offering before Baba God: and it go be yours, and una sons’ with you, as a portion forever; as Baba God has commanded.”
Moses diligently inquired about the goat of the sin offering, and, see am, it was burned: and he was angry with Eleazar and with Ithamar, the sons of Aaron who were left, saying,

“Why haven’t you eaten the sin offering in the place of the sanctuary, since it is most holy, and he has given it you to bear the wickedness of the congregation, to make atonement for dem before Baba God?
See am, its blood No be bring into the inner part of the sanctuary: you certainly should have eaten it in the sanctuary, as I commanded.”

Aaron spoke to Moses, “See am, today dem have offered dem sin offering and dem burnt offering before Baba God; and such things as these have happened to me. If I had eaten the sin offering today, would it Don dey pleasing in Baba God’s sight?”
When Moses heard that, it was pleasing in his sight.
Baba God spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying to dem,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, saying, ‘These are the living things which you may eat among all the animals that are on the earth.
Anything wey parts the hoof, and is cloven-footed, and chews the cud among the animals, that you may eat.
“‘Nevertheless these you no go eat of those that chew the cud, or of people wey part the hoof: the camel, because he chews the cud but no dey have a parted hoof, he is unclean to you.
The cony, because he chews the cud but no dey have a parted hoof, he is unclean to you.
The hare, because she chews the cud but no dey part the hoof, she is unclean to you.
The pig, because he has a split hoof, and is cloven-footed, but no dey chew the cud, he is unclean to you.
Of dem meat you no go eat, and dem carcasses you no go touch; Dem be unclean to you.
“‘These you may eat of all that are in the waters: Anything wey has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas, and in the rivers, that you may eat.
All that no have fins and scales in the seas, and in the rivers, of all that move in the waters, and of all the living creatures that are in the waters, Dem be an abomination to you,
and you detest dem. You no go eat of dem meat, and you shall detest dem carcasses.
Anything wey has no fins nor scales in the waters, that is an abomination to you.
“‘These you shall detest among the birds; dem no go be eaten, Dem be an abomination: the eagle, and the vulture, and the black vulture,
and the red kite, any kind of black kite,
any kind of raven,
the horned owl, the screech owl, and the gull, any kind of hawk,
the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
“‘All flying insects that walk on all fours are an abomination to you.
Yet you may eat these: of all winged creeping things that go on all fours, which have legs above dem feet, with which to hop on the earth.
Even of these you may eat: any kind of locust, any kind of katydid, any kind of cricket, and any kind of grasshopper.
But all winged creeping things which have four feet, are an abomination to you.
“‘By these You go become unclean: Anybody wey touches dem carcass go be unclean until the evening.
Anybody wey carries any part of dem carcass shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening.
“‘Every animal which parts the hoof, and No be cloven-footed, nor chews the cud, is unclean to you. Everybody wey touches dem go be unclean.
Anything wey goes on its paws, among all animals that go on all fours, Dem be unclean to you. Anybody wey touches dem carcass go be unclean until the evening.
Person wey carries dem carcass shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening. Dem be unclean to you.
“‘These are dem which are unclean to you among the creeping things that creep on the earth: the weasel, the rat, any kind of great lizard,
the gecko, and the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
These are dem which are unclean to you among all that creep. Anybody wey touches dem when Dem be dead, go be unclean until the evening.

On Anything wey any of dem falls when Dem be dead, it go be unclean; whether it is any vessel of wood, or clothing, or skin, or sack, Anything wey vessel it is, with which any work is done, it must be put into water, and it go be unclean until the evening; then it Go be clean.
Every earthen vessel, into which any of dem falls, all that is in it go be unclean, and you shall break it.
All chop which may be eaten, that on which water comes, go be unclean; and all drink that may be drunk in every such vessel go be unclean.
Everything whereupon part of dem carcass falls go be unclean; whether oven, or range for pots, it go be broken in pieces: Dem be unclean, and go be unclean to you.
Nevertheless a spring or a cistern in which water is gathered go be clean: but that which touches dem carcass go be unclean.
If part of dem carcass falls on any sowing seed which is to be sown, it is clean.
But if water is put on the seed, and part of dem carcass falls on it, it is unclean to you.
“‘If any animal, of which you may eat, dies; person wey touches its carcass go be unclean until the evening.
Person wey eats of its carcass shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening. He also who carries its carcass shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening.
“‘Every creeping thing that creeps on the earth is an abomination. It no go be eaten.
Anything wey goes on its belly, and Anything wey goes on all fours, or Anything wey has many feet, even all creeping things that creep on the earth, dem you no go eat; for Dem be an abomination.
You no go make unaself abominable with any creeping thing that creeps. You no go make unaself unclean with dem, that you should be defiled through am.
For I be Baba God una God. Sanctify unaself so, and be holy; for I be holy. You no go defile unaself with any kind of creeping thing that moves on the earth.
For I be Baba God who bring you up out of the land of Egypt, to be una God. You shall so be holy, for I be holy.
“‘This is the law of the animal, and of the bird, and of every living creature that moves in the waters, and of every creature that creeps on the earth,
to make a distinction between the unclean and the clean, and between the living thing that may be eaten and the living thing that may not be eaten.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, saying, ‘If a woman conceives, and bears a male pikin, then she go be unclean seven days; as in the days of her monthly period she go be unclean.
In the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin go be circumcised.
She shall continue in the blood of purification thirty-three days. She no go touch any holy thing, nor come into the sanctuary, until the days of her purifying are completed.
But if she bears a female pikin, then she go be unclean two weeks, as in her period; and she shall continue in the blood of purification sixty-six days.

“‘When the days of her purification are completed, for a son, or for a daughter, she shall bring to the priest at the door of the Tent of Meeting, a year old lamb for a burnt offering, and a young pigeon, or a turtledove, for a sin offering:
and he shall offer it before Baba God, and make atonement for her; and she go be cleansed from the fountain of her blood. “‘This is the law for her who bears, whether a male or a female.

If she cannot afford a lamb, then she shall take two turtledoves, or two young pigeons; the one for a burnt offering, and the other for a sin offering: and the priest shall make atonement for her, and she go be clean.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

“When a man go get a rising in his body’s skin, or a scab, or a bright spot, and it becomes in the skin of his body the plague of leprosy, then he go be bring to Aaron the priest, or to one of his sons, the priests:

and the priest shall examine the plague in the skin of the body: and if the hair in the plague has turned white, and the appearance of the plague is deeper than the body’s skin, it is the plague of leprosy; and the priest shall examine him, and pronounce him unclean.
If the bright spot is white in the skin of his body, and its appearance no be deeper than the skin, and its hair hasn’t turned white, then the priest shall isolate the infected person for seven days.
The priest shall examine him on the seventh day, and, see am, if in his eyes the plague is arrested, and the plague hasn’t spread in the skin, then the priest shall isolate him for seven more days.

The priest shall examine him again on the seventh day; and see am, if the plague has faded, and the plague hasn’t spread in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him clean. It is a scab. He shall wash his clothes, and be clean.
But if the scab spreads on the skin, after he has shown imself to the priest for his cleansing, he shall show imself to the priest again.
The priest shall examine him; and see am, if the scab has spread on the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is leprosy.
“When the plague of leprosy is in a man, then he go be bring to the priest;
and the priest shall examine him. See am, if E get a white rising in the skin, and it has turned the hair white, and E get raw flesh in the rising,
it is a chronic leprosy in the skin of his body, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean. He no go isolate him, for he is already unclean.
“If the leprosy breaks out all over the skin, and the leprosy covers all the skin of the infected person from his head even to his feet, as far as it appears to the priest;
then the priest shall examine him; and, see am, if the leprosy has covered all his flesh, he shall pronounce him clean of the plague. It has all turned white: he is clean.
But whenever raw flesh appears in him, he go be unclean.
The priest shall examine the raw flesh, and pronounce him unclean: the raw flesh is unclean. It is leprosy.
Or if the raw flesh turns again, and is changed to white, then he shall come to the priest;
and the priest shall examine him; and, see am, if the plague has turned white, then the priest shall pronounce him clean of the plague. He is clean.
“When the body has a boil on its skin, and it has healed,
and in the place of the boil E get a white rising, or a bright spot, reddish-white, then it go be shown to the priest;

and the priest shall examine it; and see am, if its appearance is lower than the skin, and its hair has turned white, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is the plague of leprosy. It has broken out in the boil.
But if the priest examines it, and see am, E get no white hairs in it, and it no be deeper than the skin, but is dim, then the priest shall isolate him seven days.
If it spreads in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is a plague.
But if the bright spot stays in its place, and hasn’t spread, it is the scar from the boil; and the priest shall pronounce him clean.
“Or when the body has a burn from fire on its skin, and the raw flesh of the burn becomes a bright spot, reddish-white, or white,

then the priest shall examine it; and see am, if the hair in the bright spot has turned white, and its appearance is deeper than the skin; it is leprosy. It has broken out in the burning, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is the plague of leprosy.
But if the priest examines it, and see am, E get no white hair in the bright spot, and it no be lower than the skin, but is faded; then the priest shall isolate him seven days.
The priest shall examine him on the seventh day. If it has spread in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is the plague of leprosy.
If the bright spot stays in its place, and hasn’t spread in the skin, but is faded, it is the swelling from the burn, and the priest shall pronounce him clean; for it is the scar from the burn.
“When a man or woman has a plague on the head or on the beard,

then the priest shall examine the plague; and see am, if its appearance is deeper than the skin, and the hair in it is yellow and thin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is an itch, it is leprosy of the head or of the beard.

If the priest examines the plague of itching, and see am, its appearance no be deeper than the skin, and E get no black hair in it, then the priest shall isolate the person infected with itching seven days.
On the seventh day the priest shall examine the plague; and see am, if the itch hasn’t spread, and E get no yellow hair in it, and the appearance of the itch no be deeper than the skin,
then he go be shaved, but he no go shave the itch; and the priest shall shut him up who has the itch seven more days.

On the seventh day, the priest shall examine the itch; and see am, if the itch hasn’t spread in the skin, and its appearance no be deeper than the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him clean. He shall wash his clothes, and be clean.
But if the itch spreads in the skin after his cleansing,
then the priest shall examine him; and see am, if the itch has spread in the skin, the priest no go look for the yellow hair; he is unclean.
But if in his eyes the itch is arrested, and black hair has grown in it; the itch is healed, he is clean. The priest shall pronounce him clean.
“When a man or a woman has bright spots in the skin of the body, even white bright spots;
then the priest shall examine dem; and see am, if the bright spots on the skin of dem body are a dull white, it is a harmless rash, it has broken out in the skin; he is clean.
“If a man’s hair has fallen from his head, he is bald. He is clean.
If his hair has fallen off from the front part of his head, he is forehead bald. He is clean.
But if E get in the bald head, or the bald forehead, a reddish-white plague; it is leprosy breaking out in his bald head, or his bald forehead.
Then the priest shall examine him; and, see am, if the rising of the plague is reddish-white in his bald head, or in his bald forehead, like the appearance of leprosy in the skin of the flesh,
he is a leprous man. He is unclean. The priest shall surely pronounce him unclean. His plague is on his head.
“The leper in whom the plague is shall wear torn clothes, and the hair of his head shall hang loose. He shall cover his upper lip, and shall cry, ‘Unclean! Unclean!’
All the days in which the plague is in him he go be unclean. He is unclean. He shall live alone. Outside of the camp go be his dwelling.
“The garment also that the plague of leprosy is in, whether it is a woolen garment, or a linen garment;
whether it is in warp, or woof; of linen, or of wool; whether in a skin, or in anything made of skin;
if the plague is greenish or reddish in the garment, or in the skin, or in the warp, or in the woof, or in anything made of skin; it is the plague of leprosy, and go be shown to the priest.
The priest shall examine the plague, and isolate the plague seven days.

He shall examine the plague on the seventh day. If the plague has spread in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in the skin, Anything wey use the skin is used for, the plague is a destructive mildew. It is unclean.
He shall burn the garment, whether the warp or the woof, in wool or in linen, or anything of skin, in which the plague is: for it is a destructive mildew. It go be burned in the fire.
“If the priest examines it, and see am, the plague hasn’t spread in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in anything of skin;
then the priest shall command that dem wash the thing in which the plague is, and he shall isolate it seven more days.

Then the priest shall examine it, after the plague is washed; and see am, if the plague hasn’t changed its color, and the plague hasn’t spread, it is unclean; you shall burn it in the fire. It is a mildewed spot, whether the bareness is inside or outside.
If the priest looks, and see am, the plague has faded after it is washed, then he shall tear it out of the garment, or out of the skin, or out of the warp, or out of the woof:
and if it appears again in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in anything of skin, it is spreading. You shall burn with fire that in which the plague is.
The garment, either the warp, or the woof, or Anything wey thing of skin it is, which you shall wash, if the plague has comot from dem, then it go be washed the second time, and it Go be clean.”
This is the law of the plague of mildew in a garment of wool or linen, either in the warp, or the woof, or in anything of skin, to pronounce it clean, or to pronounce it unclean.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“This go be the law of the leper in the day of his cleansing. He go be bring to the priest,
and the priest shall go out of the camp. The priest shall examine him, and see am, if the plague of leprosy is healed in the leper,
then the priest shall command dem to take for him Wey be to be cleansed two living clean birds, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop.
The priest shall command dem to kill one of the birds in an earthen vessel over running water.
As for the living bird, he shall take it, and the cedar wood, and the scarlet, and the hyssop, and shall dip dem and the living bird in the blood of the bird that was killed over the running water.
He shall sprinkle on him Wey be to be cleansed from the leprosy seven times, and shall pronounce him clean, and shall let the living bird go into the open field.

“Person Wey to be cleansed shall wash his clothes, and shave off all his hair, and bathe imself in water; and he go be clean. After that he shall come into the camp, but shall live outside his tent seven days.

It go be on the seventh day, that he shall shave all his hair off his head and his beard and his eyebrows, even all his hair he shall shave off. He shall wash his clothes, and he shall bathe his body in water, then he go be clean.

“On the eighth day he shall take two male lambs without defect, and one ewe lamb a year old without defect, and three tenths of an ephah of fine flour for a meal offering, mingled with oil, and one log of oil.
The priest who cleanses him shall set the man Wey be to be cleansed, and those things, before Baba God, at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
“The priest shall take one of the male lambs, and offer him for a trespass offering, with the log of oil, and wave dem for a wave offering before Baba God.
