He shall kill the male lamb in the place where dem kill the sin offering and the burnt offering, in the place of the sanctuary; for as the sin offering is the priest’s, so is the trespass offering. It is most holy.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the trespass offering, and the priest shall put it on the tip of the right ear of him Wey be to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall take some of the log of oil, and pour it into the palm of his own left hand.
The priest shall dip his right finger in the oil that is in his left hand, and shall sprinkle some of the oil with his finger seven times before Baba God.

The priest shall put some of the rest of the oil that is in his hand on the tip of the right ear of him Wey be to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, upon the blood of the trespass offering.
The rest of the oil that is in the priest’s hand he shall put on the head of him Wey be to be cleansed, and the priest shall make atonement for him before Baba God.
“The priest shall offer the sin offering, and make atonement for him Wey be to be cleansed because of his uncleanness: and afterward he shall kill the burnt offering;
and the priest shall offer the burnt offering and the meal offering on the altar. The priest shall make atonement for him, and he go be clean.

“If he is poor, and no fit afford so much, then he shall take one male lamb for a trespass offering to be waved, to make atonement for him, and one tenth of an ephah of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal offering, and a log of oil;
and two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, such as he is able to afford; and the one go be a sin offering, and the other a burnt offering.
“On the eighth day he shall bring dem for his cleansing to the priest, to the door of the Tent of Meeting, before Baba God.
The priest shall take the lamb of the trespass offering, and the log of oil, and the priest shall wave dem for a wave offering before Baba God.

He shall kill the lamb of the trespass offering. The priest shall take some of the blood of the trespass offering and put it on the tip of the right ear of him Wey be to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall pour some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand;
and the priest shall sprinkle with his right finger some of the oil that is in his left hand seven times before Baba God.

Then the priest shall put some of the oil that is in his hand on the tip of the right ear of him Wey be to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on the place of the blood of the trespass offering.
The rest of the oil that is in the priest’s hand he shall put on the head of him Wey be to be cleansed, to make atonement for him before Baba God.
He shall offer one of the turtledoves, or of the young pigeons, such as he is able to afford,

even such as he is able to afford, the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering, with the meal offering. The priest shall make atonement for him Wey be to be cleansed before Baba God.”
This is the law for him in whom is the plague of leprosy, Wey be not able to afford the sacrifice for his cleansing.
Baba God spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
“When you have come into the land of Canaan, which I give to you for a possession, and I put a spreading mildew in a house in the land of una possession,
then person wey owns the house shall come and tell the priest, saying, ‘There seems to me to be some sort of plague in the house.’

The priest shall command that dem empty the house, before the priest goes in to examine the plague, that all that is in the house not be made unclean. Afterward the priest shall go in to inspect the house.
He shall examine the plague; and see am, if the plague is in the walls of the house with hollow streaks, greenish or reddish, and it appears to be deeper than the wall;
then the priest shall go out of the house to the door of the house, and shut up the house seven days.
The priest shall come again on the seventh day, and look. If the plague has spread in the walls of the house,
then the priest shall command that dem take out the stones in which is the plague, and throw dem into an unclean place outside of the city:
and he shall cause the inside of the house to be scraped all over, and dem shall pour out the mortar, that dem scraped off, outside of the city into an unclean place.
Dem shall take other stones, and put dem in the place of those stones; and he shall take other mortar, and shall plaster the house.
“If the plague comes again, and breaks out in the house, after he has taken out the stones, and after he has scraped the house, and after it was plastered;
then the priest shall come in and look; and see am, if the plague has spread in the house, it is a destructive mildew in the house. It is unclean.
He shall break down the house, its stones, and its timber, and all the house’s mortar. He shall carry dem out of the city into an unclean place.
“Moreover person wey goes into the house while it is shut up go be unclean until the evening.
Person wey lies down in the house shall wash his clothes; and person wey eats in the house shall wash his clothes.

“If the priest shall come in, and examine it, and see am, the plague hasn’t spread in the house, after the house was plastered, then the priest shall pronounce the house clean, because the plague is healed.
To cleanse the house he shall take two birds, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop.
He shall kill one of the birds in an earthen vessel over running water.
He shall take the cedar wood, and the hyssop, and the scarlet, and the living bird, and dip dem in the blood of the slain bird, and in the running water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
He shall cleanse the house with the blood of the bird, and with the running water, with the living bird, with the cedar wood, with the hyssop, and with the scarlet;
but he shall let the living bird go out of the city into the open field. So shall he make atonement for the house; and it go be clean.”
This is the law for any plague of leprosy, and for an itch,
and for the destructive mildew of a garment, and for a house,
and for a rising, and for a scab, and for a bright spot;
to teach when it is unclean, and when it is clean. This is the law of leprosy.
Baba God spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem, ‘When any man has a discharge from his body, because of his discharge he is unclean.
This go be his uncleanness in his discharge: whether his body runs with his discharge, or his body has stopped from his discharge, it is his uncleanness.
“‘Every bed whereon person wey has the discharge lies go be unclean; and everything he sits on go be unclean.
Anybody wey touches his bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe imself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
Person wey sits on anything whereon the man who has the discharge sat shall wash his clothes, and bathe imself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
“‘Person wey touches the body of him who has the discharge shall wash his clothes, and bathe imself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
“‘If person wey has the discharge spits on him Wey be clean, then he shall wash his clothes, and bathe imself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
“‘Anything wey saddle person wey has the discharge rides on go be unclean.
Anybody wey touches anything that was under him go be unclean until the evening. Person wey carries those things shall wash his clothes, and bathe imself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
“‘Anybody wey person wey has the discharge touches, without having rinsed his hands in water, he shall wash his clothes, and bathe imself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
“‘The earthen vessel, which person wey has the discharge touches, go be broken; and every vessel of wood go be rinsed in water.

“‘When person wey has a discharge is cleansed of his discharge, then he shall count to imself seven days for his cleansing, and wash his clothes; and he shall bathe his flesh in running water, and go be clean.
“‘On the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, and come before Baba God to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and give dem to the priest:
and the priest shall offer dem, the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him before Baba God for his discharge.
“‘If any man has an emission of semen, then he shall bathe all his flesh in water, and be unclean until the evening.
Every garment, and every skin, whereon the semen is, go be washed with water, and be unclean until the evening.
If a man lies with a woman and E get an emission of semen, dem shall both bathe themselves in water, and be unclean until the evening.
“‘If a woman has a discharge, and her discharge in her flesh is blood, she go be in her impurity seven days: and Anybody wey touches her go be unclean until the evening.
“‘Everything that she lies on in her impurity go be unclean. Everything also that she sits on go be unclean.
Anybody wey touches her bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe imself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
Anybody wey touches anything that she sits on shall wash his clothes, and bathe imself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
If it is on the bed, or on anything whereon she sits, when he touches it, he go be unclean until the evening.
“‘If any man lies with her, and her monthly flow is on him, he go be unclean seven days; and every bed whereon he lies go be unclean.

“‘If a woman has a discharge of her blood many days not in the time of her period, or if she has a discharge beyond the time of her period; all the days of the discharge of her uncleanness go be as in the days of her period: she is unclean.
Every bed whereon she lies all the days of her discharge go be to her as the bed of her period: and everything whereon she sits go be unclean, as the uncleanness of her period.
Anybody wey touches these things go be unclean, and shall wash his clothes, and bathe imself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
“‘But if she is cleansed of her discharge, then she shall count to sheself seven days, and after that she go be clean.
On the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, and bring dem to the priest, to the door of the Tent of Meeting.
The priest shall offer the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering; and the priest shall make atonement for her before Baba God for the uncleanness of her discharge.
“‘Thus you shall separate the pikin dem of Israel from dem uncleanness, so Dem go not die in dem uncleanness, when dem defile my tabernacle that is among dem.’”
This is the law of him who has a discharge, and of him who has an emission of semen, so that he is unclean through am;
and of her who has her period, and of a man or woman who has a discharge, and of him who lies with her Wey be unclean.
Baba God spoke to Moses, after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when dem come near before Baba God, and died;

and Baba God talk say to Moses, “Tell Aaron una brother, not to come at all times into the Most Holy Place within the veil, before the mercy seat which is on the ark; lest he die: for I go appear in the cloud on the mercy seat.
“Aaron shall come into the sanctuary with a young bull for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering.

He shall put on the holy linen coat. He go get the linen breeches on his body, and shall put on the linen sash, and he go be clothed with the linen turban. Dem be the holy garments. He shall bathe his body in water, and put dem on.
He shall take from the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel two male goats for a sin offering, and one ram for a burnt offering.
“Aaron shall offer the bull of the sin offering, which is for imself, and make atonement for imself and for his house.
He shall take the two goats, and set dem before Baba God at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
Aaron shall throw lots for the two goats; one lot for Baba God, and the other lot for the scapegoat.
Aaron shall present the goat on which the lot fell for Baba God, and offer him for a sin offering.
But the goat, on which the lot fell for the scapegoat, go be presented alive before Baba God, to make atonement for him, to send him away for the scapegoat into the wilderness.
“Aaron shall present the bull of the sin offering, which is for imself, and shall make atonement for imself and for his house, and shall kill the bull of the sin offering which is for imself.
He shall take a censer full of coals of fire from off the altar before Baba God, and two handfuls of sweet incense beaten small, and bring it within the veil:
and he shall put the incense on the fire before Baba God, that the cloud of the incense may cover the mercy seat that is on the testimony, so that he No go die.
He shall take some of the blood of the bull, and sprinkle it with his finger on the mercy seat on the east; and before the mercy seat he shall sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times.

“Then he shall kill the goat of the sin offering, that is for the people, and bring his blood within the veil, and do with his blood as he did with the blood of the bull, and sprinkle it on the mercy seat, and before the mercy seat.

He shall make atonement for the Holy Place, because of the uncleanness of the pikin dem of Israel, and because of dem wrongdoings, even all dem sins; and so he shall do for the Tent of Meeting, that dwells with dem in the middle of dem uncleanness.

Nobody go be in the Tent of Meeting when he enters to make atonement in the Holy Place, until he comes out, and has made atonement for imself and for his household, and for all the assembly of Israel.
“He shall go out to the altar that is before Baba God and make atonement for it, and shall take some of the bull’s blood, and some of the goat’s blood, and put it around on the horns of the altar.
He shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it, and make it holy from the uncleanness of the pikin dem of Israel.
“When he has finished atoning for the Holy Place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, he shall present the live goat.

Aaron shall lay both his hands on the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the pikin dem of Israel, and all dem wrongdoings, even all dem sins; and he shall put dem on the head of the goat, and shall send him away into the wilderness by the hand of a man Wey be in readiness.
The goat shall carry all dem iniquities on imself to a solitary land, and he shall let the goat go in the wilderness.
“Aaron shall come into the Tent of Meeting, and shall take off the linen garments, which he put on when he go into the Holy Place, and shall leave dem there.

Then he shall bathe imself in water in a holy place, and put on his garments, and come out and offer his burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people, and make atonement for imself and for the people.
The fat of the sin offering he shall burn on the altar.
“Person wey lets the goat go for the scapegoat shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp.

The bull for the sin offering, and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was bring in to make atonement in the Holy Place, go be carried outside the camp; and dem shall burn dem skins, dem flesh, and dem dung with fire.
Person wey burns dem shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp.

“It go be a statute to you forever: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall afflict una souls, and shall do no kind of work, the native-born, or the stranger who lives as a foreigner among you:
for on this day shall atonement be made for you, to cleanse you; from all una sins you go be clean before Baba God.
It is a Sabbath of solemn rest to you, and you shall afflict una souls. It is a statute forever.
The priest, Wey be anointed and Wey be consecrated to be priest in his father’s place, shall make the atonement, and shall put on the linen garments, even the holy garments.

Then he shall make atonement for the Holy Sanctuary; and he shall make atonement for the Tent of Meeting and for the altar; and he shall make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
“This go be an everlasting statute for you, to make atonement for the pikin dem of Israel once in the year because of all dem sins.” It was done as Baba God commanded Moses.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to Aaron, and to his sons, and to all the pikin dem of Israel, and say to dem: ‘This is the thing which Baba God has commanded,
Anything wey man E get of the house of Israel, who kills a bull, or lamb, or goat, in the camp, or who kills it outside the camp,

and hasn’t bring it to the door of the Tent of Meeting, to offer it as an offering to Baba God before Baba God’s tabernacle: blood go be imputed to that man. He has shed blood; and that man go be cut off from among his people.

This is to the end that the pikin dem of Israel may bring dem sacrifices, which dem sacrifice in the open field, that dem may bring dem to Baba God, to the door of the Tent of Meeting, to the priest, and sacrifice dem for sacrifices of peace offerings to Baba God.
The priest shall sprinkle the blood on Baba God’s altar at the door of the Tent of Meeting, and burn the fat for a pleasant aroma to Baba God.
Dem shall no more sacrifice dem sacrifices to the goat idols, after which dem play the prostitute. This go be a statute forever to dem throughout dem generations.’
“You shall say to dem, ‘Any man E get of the house of Israel, or of the strangers who live as foreigners among dem, who offers a burnt offering or sacrifice,
and no dey bring it to the door of the Tent of Meeting, to sacrifice it to Baba God; that man go be cut off from his people.

“‘Any man of the house of Israel, or of the strangers who live as foreigners among dem, who eats any kind of blood, I go set my face against that soul who eats blood, and will cut him off from among his people.
For the life of the flesh is in the blood; and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for una souls: for it is the blood that makes atonement by reason of the life.
So I have talk say to the pikin dem of Israel, “No person among you may eat blood, nor may any stranger who lives as a foreigner among you eat blood.”

“‘Anything wey man E get of the pikin dem of Israel, or of the strangers who live as foreigners among dem, who takes in hunting any animal or bird that may be eaten; he shall pour out its blood, and cover it with dust.

For as to the life of all flesh, its blood is with its life: so I talk say to the pikin dem of Israel, “You no go eat the blood of any kind of flesh; for the life of all flesh is its blood. Anybody wey eats it go be cut off.”

“‘Every person that eats what dies of itself, or that which is torn by animals, whether he is native-born or a foreigner, he shall wash his clothes, and bathe imself in water, and be unclean until the evening: then he go be clean.
But if he no dey wash dem, or bathe his flesh, then he shall bear his wickedness.’”
Baba God talk say to Moses,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and say to dem, ‘I be Baba God una God.
You no go do as dem do in the land of Egypt, where you lived: and you no go do as dem do in the land of Canaan, where I be bringing you. You no go follow dem statutes.
You shall do my ordinances, and you shall keep my statutes, and walk in dem: I be Baba God una God.
You shall so keep my statutes and my ordinances; which if a man does, he shall live in dem. I be Baba God.
“‘None of you shall approach anyone Wey be his close relatives, to uncover dem nakedness: I be Baba God.
“‘You no go uncover the nakedness of una father, nor the nakedness of una mother: she is una mother. You no go uncover her nakedness.
“‘You no go uncover the nakedness of una father’s wife. It is una father’s nakedness.
“‘You no go uncover the nakedness of una sister, the daughter of una father, or the daughter of una mother, whether born at home, or born abroad.
“‘You no go uncover the nakedness of una son’s daughter, or of una daughter’s daughter, even dem nakedness: for dem own is una own nakedness.
“‘You no go uncover the nakedness of una father’s wife’s daughter, conceived by una father, since she is una sister.
“‘You no go uncover the nakedness of una father’s sister: she is una father’s near kinswoman.
“‘You no go uncover the nakedness of una mother’s sister: for she is una mother’s near kinswoman.
“‘You no go uncover the nakedness of una father’s brother, you no go approach his wife. She is una aunt.
“‘You no go uncover the nakedness of una daughter-in-law: she is una son’s wife. You no go uncover her nakedness.
“‘You no go uncover the nakedness of una brother’s wife. It is una brother’s nakedness.
“‘You no go uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. You no go take her son’s daughter, or her daughter’s daughter, to uncover her nakedness; Dem be near kinswomen: it is wickedness.
“‘You no go take a wife to her sister, to be a rival, to uncover her nakedness, while her sister is yet alive.
“‘You no go approach a woman to uncover her nakedness, as long as she is impure by her uncleanness.
“‘You no go lie carnally with una neighbor’s wife, and defile yourself with her.
“‘You no go give any of una pikin dem to sacrifice to Molech. You no go profane the name of una God. I be Baba God.
“‘You no go lie with a man, as with a woman. That is detestable.
“‘You no go lie with any animal to defile yourself with it. No woman may give sheself to an animal, to lie down with it: it is a perversion.
“‘No defile unaself in any of these things: for in all these the nations which I be casting out before you were defiled.
The land was defiled: so I punished its wickedness, and the land vomited out her inhabitants.
You so shall keep my statutes and my ordinances, and no go do any of these abominations; neither the native-born, nor the stranger who lives as a foreigner among you;
(for the men of the land that were before you had done all these abominations, and the land became defiled);
that the land not vomit you out also, when you defile it, as it vomited out the nation that was before you.
“‘For Anybody wey shall do any of these abominations, even the souls that do dem go be cut off from among dem people.
So you shall keep my requirements, that you No practice any of these abominable customs, which were practiced before you, and that you No defile unaself with dem. I be Baba God una God.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to all the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem, ‘You go be holy; for I, Baba God una God, am holy.
“‘Each one of you shall respect his mother and his father. You shall keep my Sabbaths. I be Baba God una God.
“‘No turn to idols, nor make molten gods for unaself. I be Baba God una God.
“‘When you offer a sacrifice of peace offerings to Baba God, you shall offer it so that you may be accepted.
It go be eaten the same day you offer it, and on the next day: and if anything remains until the third day, it go be burned with fire.
If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is an abomination. It No go be accepted;
but Everybody wey eats it shall bear his wickedness, because he has profaned the holy thing of Baba God, and that soul go be cut off from his people.
“‘When you reap the harvest of una land, you no go wholly reap the corners of una field, neither shall you gather the gleanings of una harvest.
You no go glean una vineyard, neither shall you gather the fallen grapes of una vineyard. You shall leave dem for the poor and for the foreigner. I be Baba God una God.
“‘You no go steal. “‘You no go lie. “‘You no go deceive each other.
“‘You no go swear by my name falsely, and profane the name of una God. I be Baba God.
“‘You no go oppress una neighbor, nor rob him. “‘The wages of a hired worker no go remain with you all night until the morning.
“‘You no go curse the deaf, nor put a stumbling block before the blind; but you shall fear una God. I be Baba God.
“‘You shall do no injustice in judgment. You no go be partial to the poor, nor show favoritism to the great; but you shall judge una neighbor in righteousness.
“‘You no go go up and down as a slanderer among una people. “‘You no go endanger the life of una neighbor. I be Baba God.
“‘You no go hate una brother in una heart. You shall surely rebuke una neighbor, and not bear sin because of him.
“‘You no go take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the pikin dem of una people; but you shall love una neighbor as yourself. I be Baba God.
“‘You shall keep my statutes. “‘You no go cross-breed different kinds of animals. “‘You no go sow una field with two kinds of seed; “‘No wear a garment made of two kinds of material.

“‘If a man lies carnally with a woman Wey be a slave girl, pledged to be married to another man, and not ransomed, or given her freedom; dem go be punished. Dem no go be put to death, because she No be free.
He shall bring his trespass offering to Baba God, to the door of the Tent of Meeting, even a ram for a trespass offering.
The priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the trespass offering before Baba God for his sin which he has committed: and the sin which he has committed go be forgiven him.
“‘When you come into the land, and have planted all kinds of trees for chop, then you shall count dem fruit as forbidden. Three years dem go be forbidden to you. It no go be eaten.
But in the fourth year all its fruit go be holy, for giving praise to Baba God.
In the fifth year you shall eat its fruit, that it may yield its increase to you. I be Baba God una God.
“‘You no go eat any meat with the blood still in it. You no go use enchantments, nor practice sorcery.
“‘You no go cut the hair on the sides of una head or clip off the edge of una beard.
“‘You no go make any cuttings in una flesh for the dead, nor tattoo any marks on you. I be Baba God.
“‘No profane una daughter, to make her a prostitute; lest the land fall to prostitution, and the land become full of wickedness.
“‘You shall keep my Sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuary; I be Baba God.
“‘No turn to people Wey mediums, nor to the wizards. No seek dem out, to be defiled by dem. I be Baba God una God.
“‘You shall rise up before the gray head, and honor the face of an old man, and you shall fear una God. I be Baba God.
“‘If a stranger lives as a foreigner with you in una land, you no go do him wrong.
The stranger who lives as a foreigner with you go be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt. I be Baba God una God.
“‘You shall do no unrighteousness in judgment, in measures of length, of weight, or of quantity.
You go get just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin. I be Baba God una God, who bring you out of the land of Egypt.
“‘You shall observe all my statutes, and all my ordinances, and do dem. I be Baba God.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,

“Moreover, you shall tell the pikin dem of Israel, ‘Anyone of the pikin dem of Israel, or of the strangers who live as foreigners in Israel, wey dey give any of his offspring to Molech; he shall surely be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him with stones.
I also will set my face against that person, and will cut him off from among his people because he has given of his offspring to Molech, to defile my sanctuary, and to profane my holy name.
If the people of the land all hide dem eyes from that person, when he gives of his offspring to Molech, and no put him to death;
then I go set my face against that man, and against his family, and will cut him off, and all who play the prostitute after him, to play the prostitute with Molech, from among dem people.
“‘The person that turns to people Wey mediums, and to the wizards, to play the prostitute after dem, I go even set my face against that person, and will cut him off from among his people.
“‘Sanctify unaself so, and be holy; for I be Baba God una God.
You shall keep my statutes, and do dem. I be Baba God who sanctifies you.
“‘For Everybody wey curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death: he has cursed his father or his mother; his blood go be upon him.
“‘The man who commits adultery with another man’s wife, even person wey commits adultery with his neighbor’s wife, the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.
“‘The man who lies with his father’s wife has uncovered his father’s nakedness: both of dem shall surely be put to death; dem blood go be upon dem.
“‘If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both of dem shall surely be put to death: dem have committed a perversion; dem blood go be upon dem.
“‘If a man lies with a male, as with a woman, both of dem have committed an abomination: dem shall surely be put to death; dem blood go be upon dem.
“‘If a man takes a wife and her mother, it is wickedness: dem go be burned with fire, both he and dem; that there may be no wickedness among you.
“‘If a man lies with an animal, he shall surely be put to death; and you shall kill the animal.
“‘If a woman approaches any animal, and lies down with it, you shall kill the woman and the animal. Dem shall surely be put to death. Dem blood go be upon dem.

“‘If a man takes his sister, his father’s daughter, or his mother’s daughter, and sees her nakedness, and she sees his nakedness; it is a shameful thing. Dem go be cut off in the sight of the pikin dem of dem people. He has uncovered his sister’s nakedness. He shall bear his wickedness.

“‘If a man lies with a woman having her monthly period, and uncovers her nakedness; he has made naked her fountain, and she has uncovered the fountain of her blood. Both of dem go be cut off from among dem people.
“‘You no go uncover the nakedness of una mother’s sister, nor of una father’s sister; for he has made his close relative naked. Dem shall bear dem wickedness.
If a man lies with his uncle’s wife, he has uncovered his uncle’s nakedness. Dem shall bear dem sin. Dem shall die childless.
“‘If a man takes his brother’s wife, it is an impurity. He has uncovered his brother’s nakedness. Dem go be childless.
“‘You shall so keep all my statutes, and all my ordinances, and do dem; that the land, where I be bringing you to live, may not vomit you out.
You no go walk in the customs of the nation, which I be casting out before you: for dem did all these things, and so I abhorred dem.
But I have talk say to you, “You shall inherit dem land, and I go give it to you to possess it, a land flowing with milk and honey.” I be Baba God una God, who has separated you from the peoples.

“‘You shall so make a distinction between the clean animal and the unclean, and between the unclean fowl and the clean: and you no go make unaself abominable by animal, or by bird, or by anything with which the ground teems, which I have separated from you as unclean for you.
You go be holy to me; for I, Baba God, am holy, and have set you apart from the peoples, that you should be mine.
“‘A man or a woman that is a medium, or is a wizard, shall surely be put to death: dem shall stone dem with stones. Dem blood go be upon dem.’”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to dem, ‘A priest no go defile imself for the dead among his people;
except for his relatives that are near to him: for his mother, for his father, for his son, for his daughter, for his brother,
and for his virgin sister Wey be near to him, who has had no husband; for her he may defile imself.
He no go defile imself, being a chief man among his people, to profane imself.
“‘Dem no go shave dem heads or shave off the corners of dem beards or make any cuttings in dem flesh.
Dem go be holy to dem God, and not profane the name of dem God; for dem offer the offerings of Baba God made by fire, the bread of dem God; so dem go be holy.
“‘Dem no go marry a woman Wey be a prostitute, or profane. Dem no go marry a woman divorced from her husband; for he is holy to his God.
You shall sanctify him so; for he offers the bread of una God. He go be holy to you; for I Baba God, who sanctify you, am holy.
“‘The daughter of any priest, if she profanes sheself by playing the prostitute, she profanes her father. She go be burned with fire.

“‘Person Wey the high priest among his brothers, upon whose head the anointing oil is poured, and that is consecrated to put on the garments, no go let the hair of his head hang loose, or tear his clothes.
He must not go in to any dead body, or defile imself for his father, or for his mother.
He no go go out of the sanctuary, nor profane the sanctuary of his God; for the crown of the anointing oil of his God is upon him. I be Baba God.
“‘He shall take a wife in her virginity.
A widow, or one divorced, or a woman who Don dey defiled, or a prostitute, these he no go marry: but a virgin of his own people shall he take as a wife.
He no go profane his offspring among his people, for I be Baba God who sanctifies him.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Say to Aaron, ‘None of una offspring throughout dem generations who has a defect may approach to offer the bread of his God.
For Anything wey man he is that has a defect, he no go draw near: a blind man, or a lame, or person wey has a flat nose, or any deformity,
or a man who has an injured foot, or an injured hand,
or hunchbacked, or a dwarf, or one who has a defect in his eye, or an itching disease, or scabs, or who has damaged testicles.
No man of the offspring of Aaron the priest who has a defect shall come near to offer the offerings of Baba God made by fire. Since he has a defect, he no go come near to offer the bread of his God.
He shall eat the bread of his God, both of the most holy, and of the holy.
He no go come near to the veil, nor come near to the altar, because he has a defect; that he may not profane my sanctuaries, for I be Baba God who sanctifies dem.’”
So Moses spoke to Aaron, and to his sons, and to all the pikin dem of Israel.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Tell Aaron and his sons to separate themselves from the holy things of the pikin dem of Israel, which dem make holy to me, and that dem not profane my holy name. I be Baba God.

“Tell dem, ‘If anyone of all una offspring throughout una generations approaches the holy things, which the pikin dem of Israel make holy to Baba God, having his uncleanness on him, that soul go be cut off from before me. I be Baba God.

“‘Anybody wey of the offspring of Aaron is a leper or has an issue; he no go eat of the holy things, until he is clean. Anybody wey touches anything that is unclean by the dead, or a man whose offspring goes from him;
or Anybody wey touches any creeping thing, wey make he may be made unclean, or a man of whom he may take uncleanness, Anything wey uncleanness he has;
the person that touches any such go be unclean until the evening, and no go eat of the holy things, unless he bathe his body in water.
When the sun is down, he go be clean; and afterward he shall eat of the holy things, because it is his bread.
That which dies of itself, or is torn by animals, he no go eat, defiling imself by it. I be Baba God.
“‘Dem shall so follow my requirements, lest dem bear sin for it, and die inside am, if dem profane it. I be Baba God who sanctifies dem.
“‘No stranger shall eat of the holy thing: a foreigner living with the priests, or a hired worker, no go eat of the holy thing.
But if a priest buys a slave, purchased by his money, he shall eat of it; and such as are born in his house, dem shall eat of his bread.
If a priest’s daughter is married to an outsider, she no go eat of the heave offering of the holy things.
But if a priest’s daughter is a widow, or divorced, and has no pikin, and has come back to her father’s house, as in her youth, she may eat of her father’s bread: but no stranger shall eat any of it.
“‘If a man eats something holy unwittingly, then he shall add the fifth part of its value to it, and shall give the holy thing to the priest.
The priests no go profane the holy things of the pikin dem of Israel, which dem offer to Baba God,
and so cause dem to bear the wickedness that brings guilt, when dem eat dem holy things; for I be Baba God who sanctifies dem.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,

“Speak to Aaron, and to his sons, and to all the pikin dem of Israel, and say to dem, ‘Anybody wey is of the house of Israel, or of the foreigners in Israel, who offers his offering, whether it is any of dem vows, or any of dem freewill offerings, which dem offer to Baba God for a burnt offering;
that you may be accepted, you shall offer a male without defect, of the bulls, of the sheep, or of the goats.
But Anything wey has a defect, that you no go offer; for it no go be acceptable for you.
Anybody wey offers a sacrifice of peace offerings to Baba God to accomplish a vow, or for a freewill offering, of the herd or of the flock, it go be perfect to be accepted. It go get no defect.
Blind, injured, maimed, having a wart, festering, or having a running sore: you no go offer these to Baba God, nor make an offering by fire of dem on the altar to Baba God.
Either a bull or a lamb that has any deformity or lacking in his parts, that you may offer for a freewill offering; but for a vow it no go be accepted.
You must not offer to Baba God that which has its testicles bruised, crushed, broken, or cut. You must not do this in una land.
You must not offer the bread of una God from the hand of a foreigner as any of these; because dem corruption is in dem. E get a defect in dem. Dem no go be accepted for you.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,

“When a bull, or a sheep, or a goat, is born, then it shall remain seven days with its mother; and from the eighth day and thenceforth it go be accepted for the offering of an offering made by fire to Baba God.
Whether it is a cow or ewe, you no go kill it and its young both in one day.
“When you sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving to Baba God, you shall sacrifice it so that you may be accepted.
It go be eaten on the same day; you shall leave none of it until the morning. I be Baba God.
“So you shall keep my commandments, and do dem. I be Baba God.
You no go profane my holy name, but I go be made holy among the pikin dem of Israel. I be Baba God who makes you holy,
who bring you out of the land of Egypt, to be una God. I be Baba God.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem, ‘The set feasts of Baba God, which you shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my set feasts.
“‘Six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day is a Sabbath of solemn rest, a holy convocation; you shall do no kind of work. It is a Sabbath to Baba God in all una dwellings.
“‘These are the set feasts of Baba God, even holy convocations, which you shall proclaim in dem appointed season.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month in the evening, is Baba God’s Passover.
On the fifteenth day of the same month is the feast of unleavened bread to Baba God. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
In the first day you go get a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work.
But you shall offer an offering made by fire to Baba God seven days. In the seventh day is a holy convocation: you shall do no regular work.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,

“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem, ‘When you have come into the land which I give to you, and shall reap its harvest, then you shall bring the sheaf of the first fruits of una harvest to the priest:
and he shall wave the sheaf before Baba God, to be accepted for you. On the next day after the Sabbath the priest shall wave it.
On the day when you wave the sheaf, you shall offer a male lamb without defect a year old for a burnt offering to Baba God.

The meal offering with it go be two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mingled with oil, an offering made by fire to Baba God for a pleasant aroma; and the drink offering with it go be of wine, the fourth part of a hin.
You must not eat bread, or roasted grain, or fresh grain, until this same day, until you have bring the offering of una God. This is a statute forever throughout una generations in all una dwellings.
“‘You shall count from the next day after the Sabbath, from the day that you bring the sheaf of the wave offering; seven Sabbaths go be completed:
even to the next day after the seventh Sabbath you shall count fifty days; and you shall offer a new meal offering to Baba God.
You shall bring out of una habitations two loaves of bread for a wave offering made of two tenths of an ephah of fine flour. Dem go be baked with yeast, for first fruits to Baba God.

You shall present with the bread seven lambs without defect a year old, one young bull, and two rams. Dem go be a burnt offering to Baba God, with dem meal offering, and dem drink offerings, even an offering made by fire, of a sweet aroma to Baba God.
You shall offer one male goat for a sin offering, and two male lambs a year old for a sacrifice of peace offerings.
The priest shall wave dem with the bread of the first fruits for a wave offering before Baba God, with the two lambs. Dem go be holy to Baba God for the priest.
You shall make proclamation on the same day: there go be a holy convocation to you; you shall do no regular work. This is a statute forever in all una dwellings throughout una generations.

“‘When you reap the harvest of una land, you must not wholly reap into the corners of una field, and you must not gather the gleanings of una harvest. You must leave dem for the poor, and for the foreigner. I be Baba God una God.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, saying, ‘In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, go be a solemn rest to you, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, a holy convocation.
You shall do no regular work; and you shall offer an offering made by fire to Baba God.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“However on the tenth day of this seventh month is the day of atonement: it go be a holy convocation to you, and you shall afflict unaself; and you shall offer an offering made by fire to Baba God.
You shall do no kind of work in that same day; for it is a day of atonement, to make atonement for you before Baba God una God.
For Anybody wey it is who no go deny imself in that same day; go be cut off from his people.
Anybody wey it is wey do any kind of work in that same day, that person I go destroy from among his people.
You shall do no kind of work: it is a statute forever throughout una generations in all una dwellings.
It go be a Sabbath of solemn rest for you, and you shall deny unaself. In the ninth day of the month at evening, from evening to evening, you shall keep una Sabbath.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and say, ‘On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the feast of tents for seven days to Baba God.
On the first day go be a holy convocation: you shall do no regular work.

Seven days you shall offer an offering made by fire to Baba God. On the eighth day go be a holy convocation to you; and you shall offer an offering made by fire to Baba God. It is a solemn assembly; you shall do no regular work.

“‘These are the appointed feasts of Baba God, which you shall proclaim to be holy convocations, to offer an offering made by fire to Baba God, a burnt offering, and a meal offering, a sacrifice, and drink offerings, each on its own day;
besides the Sabbaths of Baba God, and besides una gifts, and besides all una vows, and besides all una freewill offerings, which you give to Baba God.

“‘So on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the fruits of the land, you shall keep the feast of Baba God seven days: on the first day go be a solemn rest, and on the eighth day go be a solemn rest.

You shall take on the first day the fruit of goodly trees, branches of palm trees, and boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook; and you shall glad well-well before Baba God una God seven days.
You shall keep it a feast to Baba God seven days in the year. It is a statute forever throughout una generations. You shall keep it in the seventh month.
You shall live in temporary shelters seven days. All Wey be native-born in Israel shall live in temporary shelters,
that una generations may know that I made the pikin dem of Israel to live in temporary shelters, when I bring dem out of the land of Egypt. I be Baba God una God.’”
Moses declared to the pikin dem of Israel the appointed feasts of Baba God.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Command the pikin dem of Israel, that dem bring to you pure olive oil beaten for the light, to cause a lamp to burn continually.
Outside of the veil of the Testimony, in the Tent of Meeting, shall Aaron keep it in order from evening to morning before Baba God continually: it go be a statute forever throughout una generations.
He shall keep in order the lamps on the pure gold lamp stand before Baba God continually.
“You shall take fine flour, and bake twelve cakes of it: two tenths of an ephah go be in one cake.
You shall set dem in two rows, six on a row, on the pure gold table before Baba God.
You shall put pure frankincense on each row, that it may be to the bread for a memorial, even an offering made by fire to Baba God.
Every Sabbath day he shall set it in order before Baba God continually. It is on the behalf of the pikin dem of Israel an everlasting covenant.
It go be for Aaron and his sons; and dem shall eat it in a holy place: for it is most holy to him of the offerings of Baba God made by fire by a perpetual statute.”
The son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian, go out among the pikin dem of Israel; and the son of the Israelite woman and a man of Israel strove together in the camp.
The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name, and cursed; and dem bring him to Moses. His mother’s name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
Dem put him in custody, until Baba God’s will should be declared to dem.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Bring out of the camp him who cursed; and let all who heard him lay dem hands on his head, and let all the congregation stone him.
You shall speak to the pikin dem of Israel, saying, ‘Anybody wey curses his God shall bear his sin.

Person wey blasphemes Baba God’s name, he shall surely be put to death. All the congregation shall certainly stone him. The foreigner as well as the native-born, when he blasphemes the Name, go be put to death.
“‘Person wey strikes any man mortally shall surely be put to death.
Person wey strikes an animal mortally shall make it good, life for life.
If anyone injures his neighbor; as he has done, so shall it be done to him:
fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; as he has injured someone, so shall it be done to him.
Person wey kills an animal shall make it good; and person wey kills a man go be put to death.
You go get one kind of law for the foreigner as well as the native-born; for I be Baba God una God.’”
Moses spoke to the pikin dem of Israel; and dem bring out him who had cursed out of the camp, and stoned him with stones. The pikin dem of Israel did as Baba God commanded Moses.
Baba God talk say to Moses in Mount Sinai,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem, ‘When you come into the land which I give you, then the land shall keep a Sabbath to Baba God.
You shall sow una field six years, and you shall prune una vineyard six years, and gather in its fruits;
but in the seventh year there go be a Sabbath of solemn rest for the land, a Sabbath to Baba God. You no go sow una field or prune una vineyard.
What grows of itself in una harvest you no go reap, and you no go gather the grapes of una undressed vine. It go be a year of solemn rest for the land.
The Sabbath of the land go be for chop for you; for yourself, for una worker, for una maid, for una hired worker, and for una stranger, who lives as a foreigner with you.
For una livestock also, and for the animals that are in una land, shall all its increase be for chop.
“‘You shall count off seven Sabbaths of years, seven times seven years; and there go be to you the days of seven Sabbaths of years, even forty-nine years.
Then you shall sound the loud trumpet on the tenth day of the seventh month. On the Day of Atonement you shall sound the trumpet throughout all una land.

You shall make the fiftieth year holy, and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It go be a jubilee to you; and each of you shall return to his own property, and each of you shall return to his family.
That fiftieth year go be a jubilee to you. In it you no go sow, neither reap that which grows of itself, nor gather from the undressed vines.
For it is a jubilee; it go be holy to you. You shall eat of its increase out of the field.
“‘In this Year of Jubilee each of you shall return to his property.
“‘If you sell anything to una neighbor, or buy from una neighbor, you no go wrong each other.
According to the number of years after the Jubilee you shall buy from una neighbor. According to the number of years of the crops he shall sell to you.
According to the length of the years you shall increase its price, and according to the shortness of the years you shall diminish its price; for he is selling the number of the crops to you.
You no go wrong each other; but you shall fear una God: for I be Baba God una God.
“‘So you shall do my statutes, and keep my ordinances and do dem; and you shall live in the land in safety.
The land shall yield its fruit, and you shall eat una fill, and live inside am in safety.
If you talk say, “What shall we eat the seventh year? See am, we no go sow, nor gather in our increase”;
then I go command my blessing on you in the sixth year, and it shall bear fruit for the three years.
You shall sow the eighth year, and eat of the fruits, the old store; until the ninth year, until its fruits come in, you shall eat the old store.
“‘The land no go be sold in perpetuity, for the land is mine; for You be strangers and live as foreigners with me.
In all the land of una possession you shall grant a redemption for the land.
“‘If una brother becomes poor, and sells some of his possessions, then his kinsman Wey be next to him shall come, and redeem that which his brother has sold.
If a man has Nobody to redeem it, and he becomes prosperous and finds sufficient means to redeem it;
then Make e reckon the years since its sale, and restore the surplus to the man to whom he sold it; and he shall return to his property.

But if he no be able to get it back for imself, then what he has sold shall remain in the hand of him who has bought it until the Year of Jubilee: and in the Jubilee it go be released, and he shall return to his property.
“‘If a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, then he may redeem it within a whole year after it Don dey sold. For a full year he go get the right of redemption.

If it no be redeemed within the space of a full year, then the house that is in the walled city go be made sure in perpetuity to him who bought it, throughout his generations. It no go be released in the Jubilee.
But the houses of the villages which have no wall around dem go be accounted for with the fields of the country: dem may be redeemed, and dem go be released in the Jubilee.
“‘Nevertheless the cities of the Levites, the houses in the cities of dem possession, the Levites may redeem at any time.

The Levites may redeem the house that was sold, and the city of his possession, and it go be released in the Jubilee; for the houses of the cities of the Levites are dem possession among the pikin dem of Israel.
But the field of the suburbs of dem cities may not be sold; for it is dem perpetual possession.
“‘If una brother has become poor, and his hand no fit support imself among you; then you shall uphold him. He shall live with you like an alien and a temporary resident.
Take no interest from him or profit, but fear una God; that una brother may live among you.
You no go lend him una money at interest, nor give him una chop for profit.
I be Baba God una God, who bring you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, and to be una God.
“‘If una brother has grown poor among you, and sells imself to you; you no go make him to serve as a slave.
As a hired worker, and as a temporary resident, he go be with you; he shall serve with you until the Year of Jubilee:
then he shall go out from you, he and his pikin dem with him, and shall return to his own family, and to the possession of his fathers.
For Dem be my workers, whom I bring out of the land of Egypt. Dem no go be sold as slaves.
You no go rule over him with harshness, but shall fear una God.
“‘As for una male and una female slaves, whom you may have; of the nations that are around you, from dem you may buy male and female slaves.
Moreover of the pikin dem of the aliens who live among you, of dem you may buy, and of dem families Wey be with you, which dem have conceived in una land; and Dem go be una property.

You may make dem an inheritance for una pikin dem after you, to hold for a possession; of dem may you take una slaves forever; but over una brothers the pikin dem of Israel you no go rule, one over another, with harshness.

“‘If an alien or temporary resident with you becomes rich, and una brother beside him has grown poor, and sells imself to the stranger or foreigner living among you, or to a member of the stranger’s family;
after he is sold he may be redeemed. One of his brothers may redeem him;
or his uncle, or his uncle’s son, may redeem him, or any Wey be a close relative to him of his family may redeem him; or if he has grown rich, he may redeem imself.

He shall reckon with him who bought him from the year that he sold imself to him to the Year of Jubilee. The price of his sale go be according to the number of years; he go be with him according to the time of a hired worker.
If E get yet many years, according to dem he shall give back the price of his redemption out of the money that he was bought for.
If there remain but a few years to the year of jubilee, then he shall reckon with him; according to his years of service he shall give back the price of his redemption.
As a worker hired year by year shall he be with him. He no go rule with harshness over him in una sight.
If he no be redeemed by these means, then he go be released in the Year of Jubilee, he, and his pikin dem with him.
For to me the pikin dem of Israel are workers; Dem be my workers whom I bring out of the land of Egypt. I be Baba God una God.
“‘You shall make for unaself no idols, and you no go raise up an engraved image or a pillar, and you no go place any figured stone in una land, to bow down to it; for I be Baba God una God.
“‘You shall keep my Sabbaths, and have reverence for my sanctuary. I be Baba God.
“‘If you walk in my statutes, and keep my commandments, and do dem;
then I go give you una rains in dem season, and the land shall yield its increase, and the trees of the field shall yield dem fruit.
Una threshing shall reach to the vintage, and the vintage shall reach to the sowing time. You shall eat una bread to the full, and live in una land safely.
“‘I go give peace in the land, and you shall lie down, and Nobody will make you afraid. I go remove evil animals out of the land, neither shall the sword go through una land.
You shall chase una enemies, and dem shall fall before you by the sword.
Five of you shall chase a hundred, and a hundred of you shall chase ten thousand; and una enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
“‘I go have respect for you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, and will establish my covenant with you.
You shall eat old store long kept, and you shall move out the old because of the new.
I go set my tent among you, and my soul no go abhor you.
I go walk among you, and Go be una God, and You go be my people.
I be Baba God una God, who bring you out of the land of Egypt, that you no suppose be dem slaves. I have broken the bars of una yoke, and made you go upright.
“‘But if You go not listen to me, and No go do all these commandments;
and if you shall reject my statutes, and if una soul abhors my ordinances, so that You go not do all my commandments, but break my covenant;

I also will do this to you: I go appoint terror over you, even consumption and fever, that shall consume the eyes, and make the soul to pine away. You go sow una seed in vain, for una enemies will eat it.
I go set my face against you, and You go be struck before una enemies. People wey hate You go rule over you; and You go flee when Nobody pursues you.
“‘If you in spite of these things No go listen to me, then I go chastise you seven times more for una sins.
I go break the pride of una power, and I go make una sky like iron, and una soil like brass.
Una strength Go be spent in vain; for una land no go yield its increase, neither will the trees of the land yield dem fruit.
“‘If you walk contrary to me, and no go listen to me, then I go bring seven times more plagues on you according to una sins.
I go send the wild animals among you, which will rob you of una pikin dem, destroy una livestock, and make you few in number. Una roads will become desolate.
“‘If by these things you no go be reformed to me, but will walk contrary to me;
then I go also walk contrary to you; and I go strike you, even I, seven times for una sins.

I go bring a sword upon you that will execute the vengeance of the covenant. You go be gathered together within una cities, and I go send the pestilence among you. You go be delivered into the hand of the enemy.
When I break una staff of bread, ten women shall bake una bread in one oven, and dem shall deliver una bread again by weight. You shall eat, and not be satisfied.
“‘If you in spite of this no go listen to me, but walk contrary to me;
then I go walk contrary to you in serious anger. I go also chastise you seven times for una sins.
You go eat the flesh of una sons, and You go eat the flesh of una daughters.
I go destroy una high places, and cut down una incense altars, and throw una dead bodies upon the bodies of una idols; and my soul will abhor you.
I go lay una cities waste, and will bring una sanctuaries to desolation. I go not take delight in the sweet fragrance of una offerings.
I go bring the land into desolation; and una enemies that live inside am Go be astonished at it.
I go scatter you among the nations, and I go draw out the sword after you. Una land Go be a desolation, and una cities go be a waste.
Then the land will enjoy its Sabbaths as long as it lies desolate and You be in una enemies’ land. Even then the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
As long as it lies desolate it go get rest, even the rest which it didn’t have in una Sabbaths, when you lived on it.

“‘As for those of you Wey be left, I go send a faintness into dem hearts in the lands of dem enemies. The sound of a driven leaf will put dem to flight; and dem shall flee, as one flees from the sword. Dem go fall when Nobody pursues.
Dem go stumble over each other, as it were before the sword, when Nobody pursues. You go have no power to stand before una enemies.
You go perish among the nations. The land of una enemies will eat you up.
Those of you Wey be left will pine away in dem wickedness in una enemies’ lands; and also in the iniquities of dem fathers dem shall pine away with dem.
“‘If dem confess dem wickedness, and the wickedness of dem fathers, in dem trespass which dem trespassed against me, and also that, because dem walked contrary to me,
I also walked contrary to dem, and bring dem into the land of dem enemies; if then dem uncircumcised heart is humbled, and dem then accept the punishment of dem wickedness;
then I go remember my covenant with Jacob; and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham; and I go remember the land.

The land also Go be left by dem, and will enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies desolate without dem: and Dem go accept the punishment of dem wickedness; because, even because dem rejected my ordinances, and dem soul abhorred my statutes.
Yet for all that, when Dem be in the land of dem enemies, I go not reject dem, neither will I abhor dem, to destroy dem utterly, and to break my covenant with dem; for I be Baba God dem God;
but I go for dem sake remember the covenant of dem ancestors, whom I bring out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be dem God. I be Baba God.’”
These are the statutes, ordinances and laws, which Baba God made between him and the pikin dem of Israel in Mount Sinai by Moses.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and say to dem, ‘When a man consecrates a person to Baba God in a vow, according to una valuation,
una valuation of a male from twenty years old even to sixty years old go be fifty shekels of silver, after the shekel of the sanctuary.
If she is a female, then una valuation go be thirty shekels.
If the person is from five years old even to twenty years old, then una valuation go be for a male twenty shekels, and for a female ten shekels.
If the person is from a month old even to five years old, then una valuation go be for a male five shekels of silver, and for a female una valuation go be three shekels of silver.
If the person is from sixty years old and upward; if he is a male, then una valuation go be fifteen shekels, and for a female ten shekels.
But if he is poorer than una valuation, then he go be set before the priest, and the priest shall assign a value to him. The priest shall assign a value according to his ability to pay.
“‘If it is an animal, of which men offer an offering to Baba God, all that any man gives of such to Baba God becomes holy.
He no go alter it, nor change it, a good for a bad, or a bad for a good: and if he shall at all change animal for animal, then both it and that for which it is changed go be holy.
If it is any unclean animal, of which dem No offer as an offering to Baba God, then he shall set the animal before the priest;
and the priest shall value it, whether it is good or bad. As you the priest values it, so shall it be.
But if he will indeed redeem it, then he shall add the fifth part of it to its valuation.
“‘When a man dedicates his house to be holy to Baba God, then the priest shall evaluate it, whether it is good or bad: as the priest shall evaluate it, so shall it stand.
If person wey dedicates it will redeem his house, then he shall add the fifth part of the money of una valuation to it, and it go be his.
“‘If a man dedicates to Baba God part of the field of his possession, then una valuation go be according to the seed for it. The sowing of a homer of barley go be valued at fifty shekels of silver.
If he dedicates his field from the Year of Jubilee, according to una valuation it shall stand.

But if he dedicates his field after the Jubilee, then the priest shall reckon to him the money according to the years that remain to the Year of Jubilee; and an abatement go be made from una valuation.
If person wey dedicated the field will indeed redeem it, then he shall add the fifth part of the money of una valuation to it, and it shall remain his.
If he No go redeem the field, or if he has sold the field to another man, it no go be redeemed any more;
but the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, go be holy to Baba God, as a devoted field. It go be owned by the priests.
“‘If he dedicates a field to Baba God which he has bought, which No be of the field of his possession,
then the priest shall reckon to him the worth of una valuation up to the Year of Jubilee; and he shall give una valuation on that day, as a holy thing to Baba God.
In the Year of Jubilee the field shall return to him from whom it was bought, even to him to whom the possession of the land belongs.
All una valuations go be according to the shekel of the sanctuary: twenty gerahs to the shekel.
“‘Only the firstborn among animals, which is made a firstborn to Baba God, no man may dedicate it; whether an ox or sheep. It is Baba God’s.
If it is an unclean animal, then he shall buy it back according to una valuation, and shall add to it the fifth part of it; or if it no be redeemed, then it go be sold according to una valuation.

“‘Notwithstanding, no devoted thing, that a man shall devote to Baba God of all that he has, whether of man or animal, or of the field of his possession, go be sold or redeemed: every devoted thing is most holy to Baba God.
“‘Nobody devoted, who go be devoted from among men, go be ransomed; he shall surely be put to death.
“‘All the tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land or of the fruit of the trees, is Baba God’s. It is holy to Baba God.
If a man redeems anything of his tithe, he shall add a fifth part to it.
All the tithe of the herds or the flocks, Anything wey passes under the rod, the tenth go be holy to Baba God.
He no go search whether it is good or bad, neither shall he change it. If he changes it at all, then both it and that for which it is changed go be holy. It no go be redeemed.’”
These are the commandments which Baba God commanded Moses for the pikin dem of Israel on Mount Sinai.
Baba God spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the Tent of Meeting, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after dem had come out of the land of Egypt, saying,
“Take a census of all the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, every male, one by one;
from twenty years old and upward, all Wey be able to go out to war in Israel. You and Aaron shall count dem by dem divisions.
With you there go be a man of every tribe; everyone head of his fathers’ house.
These are the names of the men who shall stand with you: Of Reuben: Elizur the son of Shedeur.
Of Simeon: Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.
Of Judah: Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
Of Issachar: Nethanel the son of Zuar.
Of Zebulun: Eliab the son of Helon.
Of the pikin dem of Joseph: Of Ephraim: Elishama the son of Ammihud. Of Manasseh: Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.
Of Benjamin: Abidan the son of Gideoni.
Of Dan: Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.
Of Asher: Pagiel the son of Ochran.
Of Gad: Eliasaph the son of Deuel.
Of Naphtali: Ahira the son of Enan.”
These are people wey were call of the congregation, the princes of the tribes of dem fathers; dem were the heads of the thousands of Israel.
Moses and Aaron take these men Wey be mentioned by name.

Dem assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second month; and dem declared dem ancestry by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, one by one.
As Baba God commanded Moses, so he counted dem in the wilderness of Sinai.

The pikin dem of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn, dem generations, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, one by one, every male from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war;
people wey were counted of dem, of the tribe of Reuben, were forty-six thousand five hundred.

Of the pikin dem of Simeon, dem generations, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses, people wey were counted of it, according to the number of the names, one by one, every male from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war;
people wey were counted of dem, of the tribe of Simeon, were fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
Of the pikin dem of Gad, dem generations, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war;
people wey were counted of dem, of the tribe of Gad, were forty-five thousand six hundred fifty.
Of the pikin dem of Judah, dem generations, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war;
people wey were counted of dem, of the tribe of Judah, were seventy-four thousand six hundred.
Of the pikin dem of Issachar, dem generations, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war;
people wey were counted of dem, of the tribe of Issachar, were fifty-four thousand four hundred.
Of the pikin dem of Zebulun, dem generations, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war;
people wey were counted of dem, of the tribe of Zebulun, were fifty-seven thousand four hundred.

Of the pikin dem of Joseph, of the pikin dem of Ephraim, dem generations, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war;
people wey were counted of dem, of the tribe of Ephraim, were forty thousand five hundred.
Of the pikin dem of Manasseh, dem generations, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war;
people wey were counted of dem, of the tribe of Manasseh, were thirty-two thousand two hundred.
Of the pikin dem of Benjamin, dem generations, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war;
people wey were counted of dem, of the tribe of Benjamin, were thirty-five thousand four hundred.
Of the pikin dem of Dan, dem generations, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war;
people wey were counted of dem, of the tribe of Dan, were sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
Of the pikin dem of Asher, dem generations, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war;
people wey were counted of dem, of the tribe of Asher, were forty-one thousand five hundred.
Of the pikin dem of Naphtali, dem generations, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war;
people wey were counted of dem, of the tribe of Naphtali, were fifty-three thousand four hundred.
These are people wey were counted, whom Moses and Aaron counted, and the princes of Israel, being twelve men: dem were each one for his fathers’ house.
So all people wey were counted of the pikin dem of Israel by dem fathers’ houses, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war in Israel;
even all people wey were counted were six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty.
But the Levites after the tribe of dem fathers No be counted among dem.
For Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Only the tribe of Levi you no go count, neither shall you take a census of dem among the pikin dem of Israel;

but appoint the Levites over the Tabernacle of the Testimony, and over all its furnishings, and over all that belongs to it. Dem shall carry the tabernacle, and all its furnishings; and dem shall take care of it, and shall encamp around it.
When the tabernacle is to move, the Levites shall take it down; and when the tabernacle is to be set up, the Levites shall set it up. The stranger who comes near go be put to death.
The pikin dem of Israel shall pitch dem tents, every man by his own camp, and every man by his own standard, according to dem divisions.

But the Levites shall encamp around the Tabernacle of the Testimony, that there may be no serious anger on the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel: and the Levites go be responsible for the Tabernacle of the Testimony.”
Thus the pikin dem of Israel did. According to all that Baba God commanded Moses, so dem did.
Baba God spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
“The pikin dem of Israel shall encamp every man by his own standard, with the banners of dem fathers’ houses: at a distance from the Tent of Meeting shall dem encamp around it.”

People wey encamp on the east side toward the sunrise go be of the standard of the camp of Judah, according to dem divisions: and the prince of the pikin dem of Judah go be Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
His division, and people wey were counted of dem, were seventy-four thousand six hundred.
People wey encamp next to him go be the tribe of Issachar: and the prince of the pikin dem of Issachar go be Nethanel the son of Zuar.
His division, and people wey were counted of it, were fifty-four thousand four hundred.
The tribe of Zebulun: and the prince of the pikin dem of Zebulun go be Eliab the son of Helon.
His division, and people wey were counted of it, were fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
All who were counted of the camp of Judah were one hundred eighty-six thousand four hundred, according to dem divisions. Dem shall set out first.
“On the south side go be the standard of the camp of Reuben according to dem divisions. The prince of the pikin dem of Reuben go be Elizur the son of Shedeur.
His division, and people wey were counted of it, were forty-six thousand five hundred.
“People wey encamp next to him go be the tribe of Simeon. The prince of the pikin dem of Simeon go be Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.
His division, and people wey were counted of dem, were fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
“The tribe of Gad: and the prince of the pikin dem of Gad go be Eliasaph the son of Reuel.
His division, and people wey were counted of dem, were forty-five thousand six hundred fifty.
“All who were counted of the camp of Reuben were one hundred fifty-one thousand four hundred fifty, according to dem armies. Dem shall set out second.
“Then the Tent of Meeting shall set out, with the camp of the Levites in the middle of the camps. As dem encamp, so shall dem set out, every man in his place, by dem standards.
“On the west side go be the standard of the camp of Ephraim according to dem divisions: and the prince of the pikin dem of Ephraim go be Elishama the son of Ammihud.
His division, and people wey were counted of dem, were forty thousand five hundred.
“Next to him go be the tribe of Manasseh: and the prince of the pikin dem of Manasseh go be Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.
His division, and people wey were counted of dem, were thirty-two thousand two hundred.
“The tribe of Benjamin: and the prince of the pikin dem of Benjamin go be Abidan the son of Gideoni.
His army, and people wey were counted of dem, were thirty-five thousand four hundred.
“All who were counted of the camp of Ephraim were one hundred eight thousand one hundred, according to dem divisions. Dem shall set out third.
“On the north side go be the standard of the camp of Dan according to dem divisions: and the prince of the pikin dem of Dan go be Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.
His division, and people wey were counted of dem, were sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
“People wey encamp next to him go be the tribe of Asher: and the prince of the pikin dem of Asher go be Pagiel the son of Ochran.
His division, and people wey were counted of dem, were forty-one thousand and five hundred.
“The tribe of Naphtali: and the prince of the pikin dem of Naphtali go be Ahira the son of Enan.
His division, and people wey were counted of dem, were fifty-three thousand four hundred.
“All who were counted of the camp of Dan were one hundred fifty-seven thousand six hundred. Dem shall set out last by dem standards.”
These are people wey were counted of the pikin dem of Israel by dem fathers’ houses. All who were counted of the camps according to dem armies were six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty.
But the Levites No be counted among the pikin dem of Israel; as Baba God commanded Moses.
Thus the pikin dem of Israel did. According to all that Baba God commanded Moses, so dem encamped by dem standards, and so dem set out, everyone by dem families, according to dem fathers’ houses.
Now this is the history of the generations of Aaron and Moses in the day that Baba God spoke with Moses in Mount Sinai.
These are the names of the sons of Aaron: Nadab the firstborn, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the priests who were anointed, whom he consecrated to minister in the priest’s office.

Nadab and Abihu died before Baba God, when dem offered strange fire before Baba God, in the wilderness of Sinai, and dem had no pikin dem. Eleazar and Ithamar ministered in the priest’s office in the presence of Aaron dem father.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Bring the tribe of Levi near, and set dem before Aaron the priest, that dem may minister to him.
Dem shall keep his requirements, and the requirements of the whole congregation before the Tent of Meeting, to do the service of the tabernacle.
Dem shall keep all the furnishings of the Tent of Meeting, and the obligations of the pikin dem of Israel, to do the service of the tabernacle.
You shall give the Levites to Aaron and to his sons. Dem be wholly given to him on the behalf of the pikin dem of Israel.
You shall appoint Aaron and his sons, and dem shall keep dem priesthood. The stranger who comes near go be put to death.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“See am, I have taken the Levites from among the pikin dem of Israel instead of all the firstborn who open the womb among the pikin dem of Israel; and the Levites go be mine:

for all the firstborn are mine. On the day that I struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt I made holy to me all the firstborn in Israel, both man and animal. Dem go be mine. I be Baba God.”
Baba God spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying,
“Count the pikin dem of Levi by dem fathers’ houses, by dem families. You shall count every male from a month old and upward.”
Moses counted dem according to Baba God’s word, as he was commanded.
These were the sons of Levi by dem names: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari.
These are the names of the sons of Gershon by dem families: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath by dem families: Amram, and Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari by dem families: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to dem fathers’ houses.
Of Gershon was the family of the Libnites, and the family of the Shimeites: these are the families of the Gershonites.
People wey were counted of dem, according to the number of all the males, from a month old and upward, even people wey were counted of dem were seven thousand five hundred.
The families of the Gershonites shall encamp behind the tabernacle westward.
The prince of the fathers’ house of the Gershonites go be Eliasaph the son of Lael.
The duty of the sons of Gershon in the Tent of Meeting go be the tabernacle, and the tent, its covering, and the screen for the door of the Tent of Meeting,
and the hangings of the court, and the screen for the door of the court, which is by the tabernacle, and around the altar, and its cords for all of its service.
Of Kohath was the family of the Amramites, and the family of the Izharites, and the family of the Hebronites, and the family of the Uzzielites: these are the families of the Kohathites.
According to the number of all the males, from a month old and upward, there were eight thousand six hundred, keeping the requirements of the sanctuary.
The families of the sons of Kohath shall encamp on the south side of the tabernacle.
