The prince of the fathers’ house of the families of the Kohathites go be Elizaphan the son of Uzziel.
Dem duty go be the ark, the table, the lamp stand, the altars, the vessels of the sanctuary with which dem minister, and the screen, and all its service.
Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest go be prince of the princes of the Levites, with the oversight of people wey keep the requirements of the sanctuary.
Of Merari was the family of the Mahlites, and the family of the Mushites. These are the families of Merari.
People wey were counted of dem, according to the number of all the males, from a month old and upward, were six thousand two hundred.
The prince of the fathers’ house of the families of Merari was Zuriel the son of Abihail. Dem shall encamp on the north side of the tabernacle.
The appointed duty of the sons of Merari go be the tabernacle’s boards, its bars, its pillars, its sockets, all its instruments, all its service,
the pillars of the court around it, dem sockets, dem pins, and dem cords.

People wey encamp before the tabernacle eastward, in front of the Tent of Meeting toward the sunrise, go be Moses, and Aaron and his sons, keeping the requirements of the sanctuary for the duty of the pikin dem of Israel. The stranger who comes near go be put to death.
All who were counted of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the commandment of Baba God, by dem families, all the males from a month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Count all the firstborn males of the pikin dem of Israel from a month old and upward, and take the number of dem names.

You shall take the Levites for me (I be Baba God) instead of all the firstborn among the pikin dem of Israel; and the livestock of the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the livestock of the pikin dem of Israel.”
Moses counted, as Baba God commanded him, all the firstborn among the pikin dem of Israel.
All the firstborn males according to the number of names, from a month old and upward, of people wey were counted of dem, were twenty-two thousand two hundred seventy-three.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the pikin dem of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites instead of dem livestock; and the Levites go be mine. I be Baba God.
For the redemption of the two hundred seventy-three of the firstborn of the pikin dem of Israel, who exceed the number of the Levites,
you shall take five shekels apiece for each one; after the shekel of the sanctuary you shall take dem (the shekel is twenty gerahs ):
and you shall give the money, with which dem remainder is redeemed, to Aaron and to his sons.”
Moses take the redemption money from people wey exceeded the number of people wey were redeemed by the Levites;
from the firstborn of the pikin dem of Israel he take the money, one thousand three hundred sixty-five shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary:
and Moses give the redemption money to Aaron and to his sons, according to Baba God’s word, as Baba God commanded Moses.
Baba God spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
“Take a census of the sons of Kohath from among the sons of Levi, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses,
from thirty years old and upward even until fifty years old, all who enter into the service, to do the work in the Tent of Meeting.
“This is the service of the sons of Kohath in the Tent of Meeting, the most holy things.
When the camp moves forward, Aaron shall go in, and his sons, and dem shall take down the veil of the screen, and cover the ark of the Testimony with it,
and shall put a covering of sealskin on it, and shall spread over it a cloth all of blue, and shall put in its poles.
“On the table of show bread dem shall spread a blue cloth, and put on it the dishes, the spoons, the bowls, and the cups with which to pour out; and the continual bread go be on it.
Dem shall spread on dem a scarlet cloth, and cover the same with a covering of sealskin, and shall put in its poles.
“Dem shall take a blue cloth, and cover the lamp stand of the light, and its lamps, and its snuffers, and its snuff dishes, and all its oil vessels, with which dem minister to it.
Dem shall put it and all its vessels within a covering of sealskin, and shall put it on the frame.
“On the golden altar dem shall spread a blue cloth, and cover it with a covering of sealskin, and shall put in its poles.
“Dem shall take all the vessels of ministry, with which dem minister in the sanctuary, and put dem in a blue cloth, and cover dem with a covering of sealskin, and shall put dem on the frame.
“Dem shall take away the ashes from the altar, and spread a purple cloth on it.

Dem shall put on it all its vessels, with which dem minister about it, the fire pans, the meat hooks, the shovels, and the basins; all the vessels of the altar; and dem shall spread on it a covering of sealskin, and put in its poles.

“When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the sanctuary, and all the furniture of the sanctuary, as the camp moves forward; after that, the sons of Kohath shall come to carry it: but dem no go touch the sanctuary, lest dem die. These things are the burden of the sons of Kohath in the Tent of Meeting.

“The duty of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest go be the oil for the light, the sweet incense, the continual meal offering, and the anointing oil, the requirements of all the tabernacle, and of all that is in it, the sanctuary, and its furnishings.”
Baba God spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
“No cut off the tribe of the families of the Kohathites from among the Levites;
but thus do to dem, that dem may live, and not die, when dem approach to the most holy things: Aaron and his sons shall go in, and appoint dem everyone to his service and to his burden;
but dem no go go in to see the sanctuary even for a moment, lest dem die.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Take a census of the sons of Gershon also, by dem fathers’ houses, by dem families;
you shall count dem from thirty years old and upward until fifty years old; all who enter in to wait on the service, to do the work in the Tent of Meeting.
“This is the service of the families of the Gershonites, in serving and in bearing burdens:
dem shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle, and the Tent of Meeting, its covering, and the covering of sealskin that is above on it, and the screen for the door of the Tent of Meeting,

and the hangings of the court, and the screen for the door of the gate of the court, which is by the tabernacle and around the altar, and dem cords, and all the instruments of dem service, and Anything wey go be done with dem. Dem shall serve in there.

At the commandment of Aaron and his sons go be all the service of the sons of the Gershonites, in all dem burden, and in all dem service; and you shall appoint dem duty to dem in all dem responsibilities.
This is the service of the families of the sons of the Gershonites in the Tent of Meeting: and dem duty go be under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.
“As for the sons of Merari, you shall count dem by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses;
you shall count dem from thirty years old and upward even to fifty years old, Everybody wey enters on the service, to do the work of the Tent of Meeting.
This is the duty of dem burden, according to all dem service in the Tent of Meeting: the tabernacle’s boards, its bars, its pillars, its sockets,

and the pillars of the court around it, and dem sockets, and dem pins, and dem cords, with all dem instruments, and with all dem service: and by name you shall appoint the instruments of the duty of dem burden.
This is the service of the families of the sons of Merari, according to all dem service, in the Tent of Meeting, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.”
Moses and Aaron and the princes of the congregation counted the sons of the Kohathites by dem families, and by dem fathers’ houses,
from thirty years old and upward even to fifty years old, Everybody wey entered into the service, for work in the Tent of Meeting.
People wey were counted of dem by dem families were two thousand seven hundred fifty.
These are people wey were counted of the families of the Kohathites, all who served in the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the commandment of Baba God by Moses.
People wey were counted of the sons of Gershon, dem families, and by dem fathers’ houses,
from thirty years old and upward even to fifty years old, Everybody wey entered into the service, for work in the Tent of Meeting,
even people wey were counted of dem, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses, were two thousand six hundred thirty.
These are people wey were counted of the families of the sons of Gershon, all who served in the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the commandment of Baba God.
People wey were counted of the families of the sons of Merari, by dem families, by dem fathers’ houses,
from thirty years old and upward even to fifty years old, Everybody wey entered into the service, for work in the Tent of Meeting,
even people wey were counted of dem by dem families, were three thousand two hundred.
These are people wey were counted of the families of the sons of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the commandment of Baba God by Moses.
All people wey were counted of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron and the princes of Israel counted, by dem families, and by dem fathers’ houses,
from thirty years old and upward even to fifty years old, Everybody wey entered in to do the work of service, and the work of bearing burdens in the Tent of Meeting,
even people wey were counted of dem, were eight thousand five hundred eighty.
According to the commandment of Baba God dem were counted by Moses, everyone according to his service, and according to his burden. Thus were dem counted by him, as Baba God commanded Moses.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Command the pikin dem of Israel that dem put out of the camp every leper, and Everybody wey has an issue, and Anybody wey is unclean by the dead.
Both you shall put male and female outside of the camp; that dem not defile dem camp, in the middle of which I live.”
The pikin dem of Israel did so, and put dem outside of the camp; as Baba God spoke to Moses, so did the pikin dem of Israel.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel: ‘When a man or woman commits any sin that men commit, so as to trespass against Baba God, and that soul is guilty;
then he shall confess his sin which he has done, and he shall make restitution for his guilt in full, and add to it the fifth part of it, and give it to him in respect of whom he Don dey guilty.

But if the man has no kinsman to whom restitution may be made for the guilt, the restitution for guilt which is made to Baba God go be the priest’s; besides the ram of the atonement, by which atonement go be made for him.
Every heave offering of all the holy things of the pikin dem of Israel, which dem present to the priest, go be his.
Every man’s holy things go be his: Anything wey any man gives the priest, it go be his.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem: ‘If any man’s wife goes astray, and is unfaithful to him,
and a man lies with her carnally, and it is hidden from the eyes of her husband, and is kept close, and she is defiled, and E get no witness against her, and she no be taken in the act;
and the spirit of jealousy comes on him, and he is jealous of his wife, and she is defiled: or if the spirit of jealousy comes on him, and he is jealous of his wife, and she no be defiled:

then the man shall bring his wife to the priest, and shall bring her offering for her: one tenth of an ephah of barley meal. He shall pour no oil on it, nor put frankincense on it, for it is a meal offering of jealousy, a meal offering of memorial, bringing wickedness to memory.
The priest shall bring her near, and set her before Baba God;
and the priest shall take holy water in an earthen vessel; and of the dust that is on the floor of the tabernacle the priest shall take, and put it into the water.

The priest shall set the woman before Baba God, and let the hair of the woman’s head go loose, and put the meal offering of memorial in her hands, which is the meal offering of jealousy. The priest go get in his hand the water of bitterness that brings a curse.

The priest shall cause her to swear, and shall tell the woman, “If no man has lain with you, and if you haven’t gone aside to uncleanness, being under una husband, be free from this water of bitterness that brings a curse.
But if you have gone astray, being under una husband, and if You be defiled, and some man has lain with you besides una husband:”

then the priest shall cause the woman to swear with the oath of cursing, and the priest shall tell the woman, “Baba God make you a curse and an oath among una people, when Baba God allows una thigh to fall away, and una body to swell;
and this water that brings a curse will go into una bowels, and make una body swell, and una thigh fall away.” The woman shall say, “Amen, Amen.”
“‘The priest shall write these curses in a book, and he shall blot dem out into the water of bitterness.
He shall make the woman drink the water of bitterness that causes the curse; and the water that causes the curse shall enter into her and become bitter.
The priest shall take the meal offering of jealousy out of the woman’s hand, and shall wave the meal offering before Baba God, and bring it to the altar.
The priest shall take a handful of the meal offering, as its memorial, and burn it on the altar, and afterward shall make the woman drink the water.

When he has made her drink the water, then it shall happen, if she is defiled, and has committed a trespass against her husband, that the water that causes the curse will enter into her and become bitter, and her body will swell, and her thigh will fall away: and the woman Go be a curse among her people.
If the woman no be defiled, but is clean; then she go be free, and shall conceive offspring.
“‘This is the law of jealousy, when a wife, being under her husband, goes astray, and is defiled;
or when the spirit of jealousy comes on a man, and he is jealous of his wife; then he shall set the woman before Baba God, and the priest shall execute on her all this law.
The man go be free from wickedness, and that woman shall bear her wickedness.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem: ‘When either man or woman shall make a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to separate imself to Baba God,
he shall separate imself from wine and strong drink. He shall drink no vinegar of wine, or vinegar of fermented drink, neither shall he drink any juice of grapes, nor eat fresh grapes or dried.
All the days of his separation he shall eat nothing that is made of the grapevine, from the seeds even to the skins.

“‘All the days of his vow of separation no razor shall come on his head, until the days are fulfilled, in which he separates imself to Baba God. He go be holy. He shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow long.
“‘All the days that he separates imself to Baba God he no go go near a dead body.
He no go make imself unclean for his father, or for his mother, for his brother, or for his sister, when dem die; because his separation to God is on his head.
All the days of his separation he is holy to Baba God.
“‘If any man dies very suddenly beside him, and he defiles the head of his separation; then he shall shave his head in the day of his cleansing. On the seventh day he shall shave it.
On the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest, to the door of the Tent of Meeting.
The priest shall offer one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering, and make atonement for him, because he sinned by reason of the dead, and shall make his head holy that same day.
He shall separate to Baba God the days of his separation, and shall bring a male lamb a year old for a trespass offering; but the former days go be void, because his separation was defiled.
“‘This is the law of the Nazirite: when the days of his separation are fulfilled, he go be bring to the door of the Tent of Meeting,

and he shall offer his offering to Baba God, one male lamb a year old without defect for a burnt offering, and one ewe lamb a year old without defect for a sin offering, and one ram without defect for peace offerings,
and a basket of unleavened bread, cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and dem meal offering, and dem drink offerings.
The priest shall present dem before Baba God, and shall offer his sin offering, and his burnt offering.
He shall offer the ram for a sacrifice of peace offerings to Baba God, with the basket of unleavened bread. The priest shall offer also its meal offering, and its drink offering.

The Nazirite shall shave the head of his separation at the door of the Tent of Meeting, and shall take the hair of the head of his separation, and put it on the fire which is under the sacrifice of peace offerings.

The priest shall take the boiled shoulder of the ram, and one unleavened cake out of the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and shall put dem on the hands of the Nazirite, after he has shaved the head of his separation;

and the priest shall wave dem for a wave offering before Baba God. This is holy for the priest, together with the breast that is waved and the thigh that is offered. After that the Nazirite may drink wine.

“‘This is the law of the Nazirite who vows, and of his offering to Baba God for his separation, besides that which he is able to get. According to his vow which he vows, so he must do after the law of his separation.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying, ‘This is how you shall bless the pikin dem of Israel.’ You shall tell dem,
‘Baba God bless you, and keep you.
Baba God make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you.
Baba God lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’
“So dem shall put my name on the pikin dem of Israel; and I go bless dem.”
On the day that Moses had finished setting up the tabernacle, and had anointed it and sanctified it, with all its furniture, and the altar with all its vessels, and had anointed and sanctified dem;
the princes of Israel, the heads of dem fathers’ houses, offered. These were the princes of the tribes. These are dem who were over people wey were counted:
and dem bring dem offering before Baba God, six covered wagons, and twelve oxen; a wagon for every two of the princes, and for each one an ox: and dem presented dem before the tabernacle.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Accept these from dem, that dem may be used in doing the service of the Tent of Meeting; and you shall give dem to the Levites, to every man according to his service.”
Moses take the wagons and the oxen, and give dem to the Levites.
He give two wagons and four oxen to the sons of Gershon, according to dem service:
and he give four wagons and eight oxen to the sons of Merari, according to dem service, under the direction of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.
But to the sons of Kohath he give none, because the service of the sanctuary belonged to dem; dem carried it on dem shoulders.
The princes give offerings for the dedication of the altar in the day that it was anointed, even the princes give dem offerings before the altar.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Dem shall offer dem offering, each prince on his day, for the dedication of the altar.”
Person wey offered his offering the first day was Nahshon the son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah,

and his offering was: one silver platter, the weight of which was one hundred thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of dem full of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering;
one golden ladle of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
On the second day Nethanel the son of Zuar, prince of Issachar, give his offering.

He offered for his offering: one silver platter, the weight of which was one hundred thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of dem full of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering;
one golden ladle of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nethanel the son of Zuar.
On the third day Eliab the son of Helon, prince of the pikin dem of Zebulun

give his offering: one silver platter, the weight of which was a hundred and thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of dem full of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering;
one golden ladle of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Eliab the son of Helon.
On the fourth day Elizur the son of Shedeur, prince of the pikin dem of Reuben

give his offering: one silver platter, the weight of which was one hundred thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of dem full of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering;
one golden ladle of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Elizur the son of Shedeur.
On the fifth day Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai, prince of the pikin dem of Simeon

give his offering: one silver platter, the weight of which was one hundred thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of dem full of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering;
one golden ladle of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old: this was the offering of Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.
On the sixth day, Eliasaph the son of Deuel, prince of the pikin dem of Gad

give his offering: one silver platter, the weight of which was one hundred thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of dem full of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering;
one golden ladle of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Eliasaph the son of Deuel.
On the seventh day Elishama the son of Ammihud, prince of the pikin dem of Ephraim

give his offering: one silver platter, the weight of which was one hundred thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of dem full of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering;
one golden ladle of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Elishama the son of Ammihud.
On the eighth day Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur, prince of the pikin dem of Manasseh

give his offering: one silver platter, the weight of which was one hundred thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of dem full of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering;
one golden ladle of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.
On the ninth day Abidan the son of Gideoni, prince of the pikin dem of Benjamin

give his offering: one silver platter, the weight of which was one hundred thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of dem full of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering;
one golden ladle of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Abidan the son of Gideoni.
On the tenth day Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai, prince of the pikin dem of Dan

give his offering: one silver platter, the weight of which was one hundred thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of dem full of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering;
one golden ladle of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.
On the eleventh day Pagiel the son of Ochran, prince of the pikin dem of Asher

give his offering: one silver platter, the weight of which was one hundred thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of dem full of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering;
one golden ladle of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Pagiel the son of Ochran.
On the twelfth day Ahira the son of Enan, prince of the pikin dem of Naphtali

give his offering: one silver platter, the weight of which was one hundred thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of dem full of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering;
one golden spoon of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Ahira the son of Enan.
This was the dedication of the altar, on the day when it was anointed, by the princes of Israel: twelve silver platters, twelve silver bowls, twelve golden ladles;
each silver platter weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and each bowl seventy; all the silver of the vessels two thousand four hundred shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary;
the twelve golden ladles, full of incense, weighing ten shekels apiece, after the shekel of the sanctuary; all the gold of the ladles weighed one hundred twenty shekels;
all the cattle for the burnt offering twelve bulls, the rams twelve, the male lambs a year old twelve, and dem meal offering; and the male goats for a sin offering twelve;

and all the cattle for the sacrifice of peace offerings twenty-four bulls, the rams sixty, the male goats sixty, the male lambs a year old sixty. This was the dedication of the altar, after it was anointed.

When Moses go into the Tent of Meeting to speak with Baba God, he heard his voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat that was on the ark of the Testimony, from between the two cherubim: and he spoke to him.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to Aaron, and tell him, ‘When you light the lamps, the seven lamps shall give light in front of the lamp stand.’”
Aaron did so. He lit its lamps to light the area in front of the lamp stand, as Baba God commanded Moses.
This was the workmanship of the lamp stand, beaten work of gold. From its base to its flowers, it was beaten work: according to the pattern which Baba God had shown Moses, so he made the lamp stand.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Take the Levites from among the pikin dem of Israel, and cleanse dem.
You shall do this to dem, to cleanse dem: sprinkle the water of cleansing on dem, Make dem shave dem whole bodies with a razor, and Make dem wash dem clothes, and cleanse themselves.
Then Make dem take a young bull, and its meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil; and another young bull you shall take for a sin offering.
You shall present the Levites before the Tent of Meeting. You shall assemble the whole congregation of the pikin dem of Israel.
You shall present the Levites before Baba God. The pikin dem of Israel shall lay dem hands on the Levites,
and Aaron shall offer the Levites before Baba God for a wave offering, on the behalf of the pikin dem of Israel, that it may be dem own to do the service of Baba God.
“The Levites shall lay dem hands on the heads of the bulls, and you shall offer the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering to Baba God, to make atonement for the Levites.
You shall set the Levites before Aaron, and before his sons, and offer dem as a wave offering to Baba God.
Thus you shall separate the Levites from among the pikin dem of Israel, and the Levites go be mine.
“After that, the Levites shall go in to do the service of the Tent of Meeting: and you shall cleanse dem, and offer dem as a wave offering.
For Dem be wholly given to me from among the pikin dem of Israel; instead of all who open the womb, even the firstborn of all the pikin dem of Israel, I have taken dem to me.
For all the firstborn among the pikin dem of Israel are mine, both man and animal. On the day that I struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I sanctified dem for myself.
I have taken the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the pikin dem of Israel.

I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and to his sons from among the pikin dem of Israel, to do the service of the pikin dem of Israel in the Tent of Meeting, and to make atonement for the pikin dem of Israel; that there be no plague among the pikin dem of Israel, when the pikin dem of Israel come near to the sanctuary.”

Moses, and Aaron, and all the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel did so to the Levites. According to all that Baba God commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so the pikin dem of Israel did to dem.
The Levites purified themselves from sin, and dem washed dem clothes; and Aaron offered dem for a wave offering before Baba God; and Aaron made atonement for dem to cleanse dem.
After that, the Levites go in to do dem service in the Tent of Meeting before Aaron, and before his sons: as Baba God had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so dem did to dem.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“This is that which belongs to the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward dem shall go in to wait on the service in the work of the Tent of Meeting;
and from the age of fifty years dem shall cease waiting on the work, and shall serve no more,
but shall minister with dem brothers in the Tent of Meeting, to perform the duty, and shall do no service. You shall do thus to the Levites concerning dem duties.”
Baba God spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after dem had come out of the land of Egypt, saying,
“Moreover let the pikin dem of Israel keep the Passover in its appointed season.
On the fourteenth day of this month, at evening, you shall keep it in its appointed season — according to all its statutes, and according to all its ordinances, you shall keep it.”
Moses spoke to the pikin dem of Israel, that dem should keep the Passover.
Dem kept the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, at evening, in the wilderness of Sinai. According to all that Baba God commanded Moses, so the pikin dem of Israel did.
There were certain men, who were unclean because of the dead body of a man, so that dem could not keep the Passover on that day, and dem come before Moses and before Aaron on that day.

Those men talk say to him, “We be unclean because of the dead body of a man. Why are we kept back, that we may not offer the offering of Baba God in its appointed season among the pikin dem of Israel?”
Moses answer dem, “Wait, that I may hear what Baba God will command concerning you.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Say to the pikin dem of Israel, ‘If any man of you or of una generations is unclean by reason of a dead body, or is on a journey far away, he shall still keep the Passover to Baba God.
In the second month, on the fourteenth day at evening dem shall keep it; dem shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
Dem shall leave none of it until the morning, nor break a bone of it. According to all the statute of the Passover dem shall keep it.

But the man Wey be clean, and No be on a journey, and fails to keep the Passover, that soul go be cut off from his people. Because he didn’t offer the offering of Baba God in its appointed season, that man shall bear his sin.

“‘If a foreigner lives among you, and desires to keep the Passover to Baba God; according to the statute of the Passover, and according to its ordinance, so shall he do. You go get one statute, both for the foreigner, and for him Wey be born in the land.’”

On the day that the tabernacle was raised up, the cloud covered the tabernacle, even the Tent of the Testimony: and at evening it was over the tabernacle as it were the appearance of fire, until morning.
So it was continually. The cloud covered it, and the appearance of fire by night.
Whenever the cloud was taken up from over the Tent, then after that the pikin dem of Israel traveled; and in the place where the cloud remain, there the pikin dem of Israel encamped.
At the commandment of Baba God, the pikin dem of Israel traveled, and at the commandment of Baba God dem encamped. As long as the cloud remain on the tabernacle dem remain encamped.
When the cloud stayed on the tabernacle many days, then the pikin dem of Israel kept Baba God’s command, and didn’t travel.
Sometimes the cloud was a few days on the tabernacle; then according to the commandment of Baba God dem remain encamped, and according to the commandment of Baba God dem traveled.
Sometimes the cloud was from evening until morning; and when the cloud was taken up in the morning, dem traveled: or by day and by night, when the cloud was taken up, dem traveled.

Whether it was two days, or a month, or a year that the cloud stayed on the tabernacle, remaining on it, the pikin dem of Israel remain encamped, and didn’t travel; but when it was taken up, dem traveled.
At the commandment of Baba God dem encamped, and at the commandment of Baba God dem traveled. Dem kept Baba God’s command, at the commandment of Baba God by Moses.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Make two trumpets of silver. You shall make dem of beaten work. You shall use dem for the calling of the congregation, and for the journeying of the camps.
When dem blow dem, all the congregation shall gather themselves to you at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
If dem blow just one, then the princes, the heads of the thousands of Israel, shall gather themselves to you.
When you blow an alarm, the camps that lie on the east side shall go forward.
When you blow an alarm the second time, the camps that lie on the south side shall go forward. Dem shall blow an alarm for dem journeys.
But when the assembly is to be gathered together, you shall blow, but you no go sound an alarm.
“The sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets. This go be to you for a statute forever throughout una generations.

When you go to war in una land against the adversary who oppresses you, then you shall sound an alarm with the trumpets. Then You go be remember before Baba God una God, and You go be saved from una enemies.

“Also in the day of una gladness, and in una set feasts, and in the beginnings of una months, you shall blow the trumpets over una burnt offerings, and over the sacrifices of una peace offerings; and dem go be to you for a memorial before una God. I be Baba God una God.”
In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle of the testimony.
The pikin dem of Israel go forward according to dem journeys out of the wilderness of Sinai; and the cloud stayed in the wilderness of Paran.
Dem first go forward according to the commandment of Baba God by Moses.
First, the standard of the camp of the pikin dem of Judah go forward according to dem armies. Nahshon the son of Amminadab was over his army.
Nethanel the son of Zuar was over the army of the tribe of the pikin dem of Issachar.
Eliab the son of Helon was over the army of the tribe of the pikin dem of Zebulun.
The tabernacle was taken down; and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, who bore the tabernacle, go forward.
The standard of the camp of Reuben go forward according to dem armies. Elizur the son of Shedeur was over his army.
Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai was over the army of the tribe of the pikin dem of Simeon.
Eliasaph the son of Deuel was over the army of the tribe of the pikin dem of Gad.
The Kohathites set forward, bearing the sanctuary. The others set up the tabernacle before dem arrived.
The standard of the camp of the pikin dem of Ephraim set forward according to dem armies. Elishama the son of Ammihud was over his army.
Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur was over the army of the tribe of the pikin dem of Manasseh.
Abidan the son of Gideoni was over the army of the tribe of the pikin dem of Benjamin.
The standard of the camp of the pikin dem of Dan, which was the rear guard of all the camps, set forward according to dem armies. Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai was over his army.
Pagiel the son of Ochran was over the army of the tribe of the pikin dem of Asher.
Ahira the son of Enan was over the army of the tribe of the pikin dem of Naphtali.
Thus were the travels of the pikin dem of Israel according to dem armies; and dem go forward.

Moses talk say to Hobab, the son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We be journeying to the place of which Baba God talk say, ‘I go give it to you.’ Come with us, and We go treat you well; for Baba God has spoken good concerning Israel.”
E tell am say, “I go not go; but I go depart to my own land, and to my relatives.”
He talk say, “No leave us, please; because you know how We be to encamp in the wilderness, and you can be our eyes.
It go be, if you go with us, yes, it go be, that Anything wey good Baba God does to us, We go do the same to you.”
Dem set forward from the Mount of Baba God three days’ journey. The ark of Baba God’s covenant go before dem three days’ journey, to seek out a resting place for dem.
The cloud of Baba God was over dem by day, when dem set forward from the camp.
When the ark go forward, Moses talk say, “Rise up, Baba God, and let una enemies be scattered! Let people wey hate you flee before you!”
When it rested, he talk say, “Return, Baba God, to the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel.”
The people were complaining in the ears of Baba God. When Baba God heard it, his anger burned; and Baba God’s fire burned among dem, and consumed some of the outskirts of the camp.
The people cried to Moses; and Moses prayed to Baba God, and the fire abated.
The name of that place was call Taberah, because Baba God’s fire burned among dem.
The mixed plenty people that was among dem lusted exceedingly: and the pikin dem of Israel also wept again, and talk say, “Who will give us meat to eat?
We remember the fish, which we ate in Egypt for nothing; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic;
but now we have lost our appetite. E get nothing at all except this manna to look at.”
The manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance like the appearance of bdellium.
The people go around, gathered it, and ground it in mills, or beat it in mortars, and boiled it in pots, and made cakes of it. Its taste was like the taste of fresh oil.
When the dew fell on the camp in the night, the manna fell on it.
Moses heard the people weeping throughout dem families, every man at the door of his tent; and Baba God’s anger burned greatly; and Moses was displeased.
Moses talk say to Baba God, “Why have you treated with una worker so badly? Why haven’t I find favor in una sight, that you lay the burden of all this people on me?
Have I conceived all this people? Have I bring dem out, that you should tell me, ‘Carry dem in una bosom, as a nurse carries a nursing infant, to the land which you swore to dem fathers?’
Where could I get meat to give to all this people? For dem weep to me, saying, ‘Give us meat, that we may eat.’
I be not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me.
If you treat me this way, please kill me right now, if I have find favor in una sight; and no let me see my wretchedness.”

Baba God talk say to Moses, “Gather to me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom you know to be the elders of the people, and officers over dem; and bring dem to the Tent of Meeting, that dem may stand there with you.
I go come down and talk with you there. I go take of the Spirit which is on you, and will put it on dem; and dem shall bear the burden of the people with you, that you not bear it yourself alone.

“Say to the people, ‘Sanctify unaself in preparation for tomorrow, and You go eat meat; for you have wept in the ears of Baba God, saying, “Who will give us meat to eat? For it was well with us in Egypt.” So Baba God will give you meat, and You go eat.
You go not eat one day, nor two days, nor five days, neither ten days, nor twenty days,

but a whole month, until it comes out at una nostrils, and it is loathsome to you; because you have rejected Baba God Wey be among you, and have wept before him, saying, “Why did we come out of Egypt?”’”
Moses talk say, “The people, among whom I be, are six hundred thousand men on foot; and you have talk say, ‘I go give dem meat, that dem may eat a whole month.’
Shall flocks and herds be slaughtered for dem, to be sufficient for dem? Shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together for dem, to be sufficient for dem?”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Has Baba God’s hand grown short? Now You go see whether my word will happen to you or not.”
Moses go out, and told the people Baba God’s words; and he gathered seventy men of the elders of the people, and set dem around the Tent.
Baba God come down in the cloud, and spoke to him, and take of the Spirit that was on him, and put it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit rested on dem, dem prophesied, but dem did so no more.

But two men remain in the camp. The name of one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the Spirit rested on dem; and dem were of people wey were written, but had not gone out to the Tent; and dem prophesied in the camp.
A young man ran, and told Moses, and talk say, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!”
Joshua the son of Nun, the worker of Moses, one of his chosen men, answer, “My lord Moses, forbid dem!”
Moses talk say to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all Baba God’s people were prophets, that Baba God would put his Spirit on dem!”
Moses go into the camp, he and the elders of Israel.

A wind from Baba God go out and bring quails from the sea, and Make dem fall by the camp, about a day’s journey on this side, and a day’s journey on the other side, around the camp, and about two cubits above the surface of the earth.

The people rose up all that day, and all of that night, and all the next day, and gathered the quails. Person wey gathered least gathered ten homers; and dem spread dem all out for themselves around the camp.
While the meat was still between dem teeth, before it was chewed, Baba God’s anger burned against the people, and Baba God struck the people with a plenty well-well plague.
The name of that place was call Kibroth Hattaavah, because there dem buried the people who lusted.
From Kibroth Hattaavah the people traveled to Hazeroth; and dem stayed at Hazeroth.
Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman whom he had married; for he had married a Cushite woman.
Dem talk say, “Has Baba God indeed spoken only with Moses? Hasn’t he spoken also with us?” And Baba God heard it.
Now the man Moses was very humble, more than all the men who were on the surface of the earth.
Baba God spoke suddenly to Moses, to Aaron, and to Miriam, “You three come out to the Tent of Meeting!” The three of dem come out.
Baba God come down in a pillar of cloud, and stood at the door of the Tent, and call Aaron and Miriam; and dem both come forward.
He talk say, “Now hear my words. If E get a prophet among you, I, Baba God, will make myself known to him in a vision. I go speak with him in a dream.
My worker Moses No be so. He is faithful in all my house.
With him, I go speak mouth to mouth, even plainly, and not in riddles; and he shall see Baba God’s form. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my worker, against Moses?”
Baba God’s anger burned against dem; and he comot.
The cloud comot from over the Tent; and see am, Miriam was leprous, as white as snow. Aaron looked at Miriam, and see am, she was leprous.
Aaron talk say to Moses, “Oh, my lord, please no count this sin against us, in which we have done foolishly, and in which we have sinned.
Make she not, I pray, be as one dead, of whom the flesh is half consumed when he comes out of his mother’s womb.”
Moses cried to Baba God, saying, “Heal her, God, I beg you!”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “If her father had but spit in her face, shouldn’t she be ashamed seven days? Make she be shut up outside of the camp seven days, and after that she go be bring in again.”
Miriam was shut up outside of the camp seven days, and the people didn’t travel until Miriam was bring in again.
Afterward the people traveled from Hazeroth, and encamped in the wilderness of Paran.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Send men, that dem may spy out the land of Canaan, which I give to the pikin dem of Israel. Of every tribe of dem fathers, you shall send a man, every one a prince among dem.”
Moses sent dem from the wilderness of Paran according to the commandment of Baba God. All dem were men who were heads of the pikin dem of Israel.
These were dem names: Of the tribe of Reuben, Shammua the son of Zaccur.
Of the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat the son of Hori.
Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
Of the tribe of Issachar, Igal the son of Joseph.
Of the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Nun.
Of the tribe of Benjamin, Palti the son of Raphu.
Of the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel the son of Sodi.
Of the tribe of Joseph, of the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi the son of Susi.
Of the tribe of Dan, Ammiel the son of Gemalli.
Of the tribe of Asher, Sethur the son of Michael.
Of the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi the son of Vophsi.
Of the tribe of Gad, Geuel the son of Machi.
These are the names of the men who Moses sent to spy out the land. Moses call Hoshea the son of Nun Joshua.
Moses sent dem to spy out the land of Canaan, and talk say to dem, “Go up this way by the South, and go up into the hill country.
See the land, what it is; and the people who live inside am, whether Dem be strong or weak, whether Dem be few or many;
and what the land is that dem live in, whether it is good or bad; and what cities Dem be that dem live in, whether in camps, or in strongholds;
and what the land is, whether it is fat or lean, whether E get wood inside am, or not. Be courageous, and bring some of the fruit of the land.” Now the time was the time of the first-ripe grapes.
So dem go up, and spied out the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, to the entrance of Hamath.
Dem go up by the South, and come to Hebron; and Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the pikin dem of Anak, were there. (Now Hebron was built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.)
Dem come to the valley of Eshcol, and cut down from there a branch with one cluster of grapes, and dem bore it on a staff between two. Dem also bring some of the pomegranates and figs.
That place was call the valley of Eshcol, because of the cluster which the pikin dem of Israel cut down from there.
Dem come back from spying out the land at the end of forty days.

Dem go and come to Moses, to Aaron, and to all the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel, to the wilderness of Paran, to Kadesh; and bring back word to dem and to all the congregation. Dem showed dem the fruit of the land.
Dem told him, and talk say, “We come to the land where you sent us. Surely it flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
However the people who live in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified and very large. Moreover, we see the pikin dem of Anak there.
Amalek dwells in the land of the South. The Hittite, the Jebusite, and the Amorite live in the hill country. The Canaanite dwells by the sea, and along the side of the Jordan.”
Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and talk say, “Make we go up at once, and possess it; for We be well able to overcome it!”
But the men who go up with him talk say, “We no be able to go up against the people; for Dem be stronger than we.”

Dem bring up an evil report of the land which dem had spied out to the pikin dem of Israel, saying, “The land, through which we have gone to spy it out, is a land that eats up its inhabitants; and all the people who we see in it are men of great stature.
There we see the Nephilim, the sons of Anak, who come from the Nephilim. We were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in dem sight.”
All the congregation lifted up dem voice, and cried; and the people wept that night.
All the pikin dem of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron. The whole congregation talk say to dem, “We wish that we had died in the land of Egypt, or that we had died in this wilderness!
Why does Baba God bring us to this land, to fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones Go be captured or killed! Wouldn’t it be better for us to return into Egypt?”
Dem talk say to each other, “Make we make a captain, and Make we return into Egypt.”
Then Moses and Aaron fell on dem faces before all the assembly of the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel.
Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, who were of people wey spied out the land, tore dem clothes.
Dem spoke to all the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel, saying, “The land, which we passed through to spy it out, is an exceeding good land.
If Baba God delights in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it to us; a land which flows with milk and honey.
Only no rebel against Baba God, neither fear the people of the land; for Dem be bread for us. Dem defense is removed from over dem, and Baba God is with us. No fear dem.”
But all the congregation threatened to stone dem with stones. Baba God’s glory appeared in the Tent of Meeting to all the pikin dem of Israel.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “How long will this people despise me? and how long will dem not believe in me, for all the signs which I have worked among dem?
I go strike dem with the pestilence, and disinherit dem, and will make of you a nation greater and mightier than dem.”
Moses talk say to Baba God, “Then the Egyptians will hear it; for you bring up this people in una might from among dem.

Dem go tell it to the inhabitants of this land. Dem have heard that you Baba God are in the middle of this people; for you Baba God are seen face to face, and una cloud stands over dem, and you go before dem, in a pillar of cloud by day, and in a pillar of fire by night.
Now if you killed this people as one man, then the nations which have heard the fame of You go speak, saying,
‘Because Baba God No be able to bring this people into the land which he swore to dem, so he has slain dem in the wilderness.’
Now please let the power of the Lord be great, according as you have spoken, saying,

‘Baba God is slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, forgiving wickedness and disobedience; and that will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the wickedness of the fathers on the pikin dem, on the third and on the fourth generation.’
Please pardon the wickedness of this people according to the greatness of una loving kindness, and according as you have forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now.”
Baba God talk say, “I have pardoned according to una word:
but in very deed, as I live, and as all the earth go be filled with Baba God’s glory;
because all those men who have seen my glory, and my signs, which I worked in Egypt and in the wilderness, yet have tempted me these ten times, and have not listened to my voice;
surely dem no go see the land which I swore to dem fathers, neither shall any of people wey despised me see it.
But my worker Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and has follow me fully, him I go bring into the land into which he go. His offspring shall possess it.
Since the Amalekite and the Canaanite live in the valley, tomorrow turn, and go into the wilderness by the way to the Red Sea.”
Baba God spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
“How long shall I bear with this evil congregation, that murmur against me? I have heard the murmurings of the pikin dem of Israel, which dem murmur against me.
Tell dem, ‘As I live, says Baba God, surely as you have spoken in my ears, so will I do to you.
Una dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness; and all who were counted of you, according to una whole number, from twenty years old and upward, who have murmured against me,
surely you no go come into the land, concerning which I swore that I would make you live inside am, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.
But una little ones, that you talk say should be captured or killed, dem I go bring in, and dem shall know the land which you have rejected.
But as for you, una dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness.
Una pikin dem go be wanderers in the wilderness forty years, and shall bear una prostitution, until una dead bodies are consumed in the wilderness.
After the number of the days in which you spied out the land, even forty days, for every day a year, You go bear una iniquities, even forty years, and You go know my alienation.’
I, Baba God, have spoken. I go surely do this to all this evil congregation, Wey be gathered together against me. In this wilderness dem go be consumed, and there dem shall die.”
The men, whom Moses sent to spy out the land, who come back, and made all the congregation to murmur against him, by bringing up an evil report against the land,
even those men who bring up an evil report of the land, died by the plague before Baba God.
But Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, remain alive of those men who go to spy out the land.
Moses told these words to all the pikin dem of Israel, and the people mourned greatly.
Dem rose up early in the morning, and go up to the top of the mountain, saying, “See am, We be here, and will go up to the place which Baba God has promised: for we have sinned.”
Moses talk say, “Why now do you disobey the commandment of Baba God, since it no go prosper?
No go up, for Baba God no be among you; that you not be struck down before una enemies.
For there the Amalekite and the Canaanite are before you, and you shall fall by the sword, because you turned back from following Baba God, so Baba God No go be with you.”
But dem presumed to go up to the top of the mountain. Nevertheless, the ark of Baba God’s covenant and Moses didn’t depart out of the camp.
Then the Amalekites come down, and the Canaanites who lived in that mountain, and struck dem and beat dem down, even to Hormah.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem, ‘When you have come into the land of una habitations, which I give to you,

and will make an offering by fire to Baba God, a burnt offering, or a sacrifice, to accomplish a vow, or as a freewill offering, or in una set feasts, to make a pleasant aroma to Baba God, of the herd, or of the flock;
then person wey offers his offering shall offer to Baba God a meal offering of one tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with the fourth part of a hin of oil.
You shall prepare wine for the drink offering, the fourth part of a hin, with the burnt offering, or for the sacrifice, for each lamb.
“‘Or for a ram, you shall prepare for a meal offering two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with the third part of a hin of oil;
and for the drink offering you shall offer the third part of a hin of wine, of a pleasant aroma to Baba God.
When you prepare a bull for a burnt offering, or for a sacrifice, to accomplish a vow, or for peace offerings to Baba God;
then shall he offer with the bull a meal offering of three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil:
and you shall offer for the drink offering half a hin of wine, for an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Baba God.
Thus shall it be done for each bull, or for each ram, or for each of the male lambs, or of the young goats.
According to the number that you shall prepare, so you shall do to everyone according to dem number.
“‘All Wey be native-born shall do these things in this way, in offering an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Baba God.

If a stranger lives as a foreigner with you, or Anybody wey may be among you throughout una generations, and will offer an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Baba God; as you do, so he shall do.
For the assembly, there go be one statute for you and for the stranger who lives as a foreigner, a statute forever throughout una generations. As You be, so shall the foreigner be before Baba God.
One law and one ordinance go be for you, and for the stranger who lives as a foreigner with you.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem, ‘When you come into the land where I bring you,
then it go be that when you eat of the bread of the land, you shall offer up a wave offering to Baba God.
Of the first of una dough you shall offer up a cake for a wave offering. As the wave offering of the threshing floor, so you shall heave it.
Of the first of una dough, you shall give to Baba God a wave offering throughout una generations.
“‘When you err, and no observe all these commandments, which Baba God has spoken to Moses,
even all that Baba God has commanded you by Moses, from the day that Baba God give commandment, and onward throughout una generations;

then it go be, if it was done unwittingly, without the knowledge of the congregation, that all the congregation shall offer one young bull for a burnt offering, for a pleasant aroma to Baba God, with its meal offering, and its drink offering, according to the ordinance, and one male goat for a sin offering.

The priest shall make atonement for all the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel, and dem go be forgiven; for it was an error, and dem have bring dem offering, an offering made by fire to Baba God, and dem sin offering before Baba God, for dem error.
All the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel go be forgiven, as well as the stranger who lives as a foreigner among dem; for with regard to all the people, it was done unwittingly.
“‘If one person sins unwittingly, then he shall offer a female goat a year old for a sin offering.
The priest shall make atonement for the soul who errs, when he sins unwittingly before Baba God, to make atonement for him; and he go be forgiven.
You go get one law for him wey do anything unwittingly, for him Wey be native-born among the pikin dem of Israel, and for the stranger who lives as a foreigner among dem.
“‘But the soul wey do anything with a high hand, whether he is native-born or a foreigner, the same blasphemes Baba God. That soul go be cut off from among his people.
Because he has despised Baba God’s word, and has broken his commandment, that soul shall utterly be cut off. His wickedness go be on him.’”
While the pikin dem of Israel were in the wilderness, dem find a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath day.
People wey find him gathering sticks bring him to Moses and Aaron, and to all the congregation.
Dem put him in custody, because it had not been declared what should be done to him.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “The man shall surely be put to death. All the congregation shall stone him with stones outside of the camp.”
All the congregation bring him outside of the camp, and stoned him to death with stones, as Baba God commanded Moses.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,

“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem that dem should make themselves fringes in the borders of dem garments throughout dem generations, and that dem put on the fringe of each border a cord of blue:

and it go be to you for a fringe, that you may look on it, and remember all Baba God’s commandments, and do dem; and that you not follow after una own heart and una own eyes, after which you use to play the prostitute;
that you may remember and do all my commandments, and be holy to una God.
I be Baba God una God, who bring you out of the land of Egypt, to be una God: I be Baba God una God.”
Now Korah, the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On, the son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, take some men.
Dem rose up before Moses, with some of the pikin dem of Israel, two hundred fifty princes of the congregation, call to the assembly, men of renown.

Dem assembled themselves together against Moses and against Aaron, and talk say to dem, “You take too much on yourself, since all the congregation are holy, everyone of dem, and Baba God is among dem! Why do you lift unaself up above Baba God’s assembly?”
When Moses heard it, he fell on his face.

He talk say to Korah and to all his company, “In the morning, Baba God will show Wey be his, and Wey be holy, and will cause him to come near to him. Even him whom he shall choose, he will cause to come near to him.
Do this: take censers, Korah, and all his company;
and put fire in dem, and put incense on dem before Baba God tomorrow. It go be that the man whom Baba God chooses, he go be holy. You have gone too far, you sons of Levi!”
Moses talk say to Korah, “Hear now, you sons of Levi!

Is it a small thing to you, that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to imself, to do the service of Baba God’s tabernacle, and to stand before the congregation to minister to dem;
and that he has bring you near, and all una brothers the sons of Levi with you? Do you seek the priesthood also?
So you and all una company have gathered together against Baba God! Wetin be Aaron that you murmur against him?”
Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab; and dem talk say, “We no go come up!
Is it a small thing that you have bring us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, but you must also make yourself a prince over us?
Moreover you haven’t bring us into a land flowing with milk and honey, nor given us inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you put out the eyes of these men? We no go come up.”
Moses was very angry, and talk say to Baba God, “No respect dem offering. I have not taken one donkey from dem, neither have I hurt one of dem.”
Moses talk say to Korah, “You and all una company go before Baba God, you, and dem, and Aaron, tomorrow.
Each man take his censer, and put incense on dem, and each man bring before Baba God his censer, two hundred fifty censers; you also, and Aaron, each his censer.”
Dem each take his censer, and put fire in dem, and laid incense on it, and stood at the door of the Tent of Meeting with Moses and Aaron.
Korah assembled all the congregation opposite dem to the door of the Tent of Meeting. Baba God’s glory appeared to all the congregation.
Baba God spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
“Separate unaself from among this congregation, that I may consume dem in a moment!”
Dem fell on dem faces, and talk say, “God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and will you be angry with all the congregation?”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the congregation, saying, ‘Get away from around the tent of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram!’”
Moses rose up and go to Dathan and Abiram; and the elders of Israel follow him.
He spoke to the congregation, saying, “Depart, please, from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of dem own, lest you be consumed in all dem sins!”
So dem go away from the tent of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, on every side. Dathan and Abiram come out, and stood at the door of dem tents, with dem wives, dem sons, and dem little ones.
Moses talk say, “Hereby you shall know that Baba God has sent me to do all these works; for dem No be from my own mind.
If these men die the common death of all men, or if dem experience what all men experience, then Baba God hasn’t sent me.

But if Baba God makes a new thing, and the ground opens its mouth, and swallows dem up, with all that belong to dem, and dem go down alive into Sheol; then you shall understand that these men have despised Baba God.”
As he finished speaking all these words, the ground that was under dem split apart.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed dem up, with dem households, all of Korah’s men, and all dem goods.
So dem, and all that belonged to dem go down alive into Sheol. The earth closed on dem, and dem perished from among the assembly.
All Israel that were around dem fled at dem cry; for dem talk say, “Lest the earth swallow us up!”
Fire come out from Baba God, and devoured the two hundred fifty men who offered the incense.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, that he take up the censers out of the burning, and scatter the fire away from the camp; for Dem be holy,

even the censers of these sinners against dem own lives. Make dem be made beaten plates for a covering of the altar, for dem offered dem before Baba God. So Dem be holy. Dem go be a sign to the pikin dem of Israel.”
Eleazar the priest take the bronze censers, which people wey were burned had offered; and dem beat dem out for a covering of the altar,

to be a memorial to the pikin dem of Israel, to the end that no stranger, who no be of the offspring of Aaron, would come near to burn incense before Baba God, that he not be as Korah, and as his company; as Baba God spoke to him by Moses.
But on the next day all the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron, saying, “You have killed Baba God’s people!”
When the congregation was assembled against Moses and against Aaron, Dem looked toward the Tent of Meeting. See am, the cloud covered it, and Baba God’s glory appeared.
Moses and Aaron come to the front of the Tent of Meeting.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Get away from among this congregation, that I may consume dem in a moment!” Dem fell on dem faces.

Moses talk say to Aaron, “Take una censer, and put fire from off the altar in it, and lay incense on it, and carry it sharp-sharp to the congregation, and make atonement for dem; for serious anger has gone out from Baba God! The plague has begun.”
Aaron did as Moses talk say, and ran into the middle of the assembly. See am, the plague has begun among the people. He put on the incense, and made atonement for the people.
He stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.
Now people wey died by the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, besides people wey died about the matter of Korah.
Aaron come back to Moses to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and the plague was stopped.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and take rods from dem, one for each fathers’ house, of all dem princes according to dem fathers’ houses, twelve rods. Write each man’s name on his rod.
You shall write Aaron’s name on the rod of Levi; for there go be one rod for each head of dem fathers’ houses.
You shall lay dem up in the Tent of Meeting before the testimony, where I meet with you.
It shall happen, that the rod of the man whom I shall choose shall bud. I go make the murmurings of the pikin dem of Israel, which dem murmur against you, cease from me.”
Moses spoke to the pikin dem of Israel; and all dem princes give him rods, for each prince one, according to dem fathers’ houses, even twelve rods. Aaron’s rod was among dem rods.
Moses laid up the rods before Baba God in the Tent of the Testimony.
On the next day, Moses go into the Tent of the Testimony; and see am, Aaron’s rod for the house of Levi had sprouted, budded, produced blossoms, and bore ripe almonds.
Moses bring out all the rods from before Baba God to all the pikin dem of Israel. Dem looked, and each man take his rod.

Baba God talk say to Moses, “Put back the rod of Aaron before the testimony, to be kept for a token against the pikin dem of rebellion; that you may make an end of dem murmurings against me, that dem not die.”
Moses did so. As Baba God commanded him, so he did.
The pikin dem of Israel spoke to Moses, saying, “See am, we perish! We be undone! We be all undone!
Everybody wey keeps approaching Baba God’s tabernacle, dies! Will we all perish?”
Baba God talk say to Aaron, “You and una sons and una fathers’ house with you shall bear the wickedness of the sanctuary; and you and una sons with you shall bear the wickedness of una priesthood.

Bring una brothers also, the tribe of Levi, the tribe of una father, near with you, that dem may be joined to you, and minister to you; but you and una sons with you go be before the Tent of the Testimony.
Dem shall keep una commands, and the duty of the whole Tent; only dem no go come near to the vessels of the sanctuary and to the altar, that dem not die, neither dem, nor you.
Dem go be joined to you, and keep the responsibility of the Tent of Meeting, for all the service of the Tent. A stranger no go come near to you.
“You shall perform the duty of the sanctuary and the duty of the altar, that there be no more serious anger on the pikin dem of Israel.
See am, I myself have taken una brothers the Levites from among the pikin dem of Israel. Dem be a gift to you, dedicated to Baba God, to do the service of the Tent of Meeting.

You and una sons with you shall keep una priesthood for everything of the altar, and for that within the veil. You shall serve. I give you the service of the priesthood as a gift. The stranger who comes near go be put to death.”

Baba God spoke to Aaron, “See am, I myself have given you the command of my wave offerings, even all the holy things of the pikin dem of Israel. I have given dem to you by reason of the anointing, and to una sons, as a portion forever.

This go be yours of the most holy things from the fire: every offering of dem own, even every meal offering of dem own, and every sin offering of dem own, and every trespass offering of dem own, which dem shall render to me, go be most holy for you and for una sons.
You shall eat of it like the most holy things. Every male shall eat of it. It go be holy to you.

“This is yours, too: the wave offering of dem gift, even all the wave offerings of the pikin dem of Israel. I have given dem to you, and to una sons and to una daughters with you, as a portion forever. Everyone Wey be clean in una house shall eat of it.
“I have given to you all the best of the oil, and all the best of the vintage, and of the grain, the first fruits of dem which dem give to Baba God.
The first-ripe fruits of all that is in dem land, which dem bring to Baba God, go be yours. Everyone Wey be clean in una house shall eat of it.
“Everything devoted in Israel go be yours.

Everything that opens the womb, of all flesh which dem offer to Baba God, both of man and animal go be yours. Nevertheless, you shall surely redeem the firstborn of man, and you shall redeem the firstborn of unclean animals.
You shall redeem people Wey to be redeemed of dem from a month old, according to una estimation, for five shekels of money, after the shekel of the sanctuary, which weighs twenty gerahs.

“But you no go redeem the firstborn of a cow, or the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat. Dem be holy. You shall sprinkle dem blood on the altar, and shall burn dem fat for an offering made by fire, for a pleasant aroma to Baba God.
Dem meat go be yours, as the wave offering breast and as the right thigh, it go be yours.

All the wave offerings of the holy things, which the pikin dem of Israel offer to Baba God, I have given you, and una sons and una daughters with you, as a portion forever. It is a covenant of salt forever before Baba God to you and to una offspring with you.”
Baba God talk say to Aaron, “You go get no inheritance in dem land, neither shall you have any portion among dem. I be una portion and una inheritance among the pikin dem of Israel.
“To the pikin dem of Levi, see am, I have given all the tithe in Israel for an inheritance, in return for dem service which dem serve, even the service of the Tent of Meeting.
From now the pikin dem of Israel no go come near the Tent of Meeting, lest dem bear sin, and die.

But the Levites shall do the service of the Tent of Meeting, and dem shall bear dem wickedness. It go be a statute forever throughout una generations. Among the pikin dem of Israel, dem go get no inheritance.

For the tithe of the pikin dem of Israel, which dem offer as a wave offering to Baba God, I have given to the Levites for an inheritance. So I have talk say to dem, ‘Among the pikin dem of Israel dem go get no inheritance.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,

“Moreover you shall speak to the Levites, and tell dem, ‘When you take of the pikin dem of Israel the tithe which I have given you from dem for una inheritance, then you shall offer up a wave offering of it for Baba God, a tithe of the tithe.
Una wave offering go be credited to you, as though it were the grain of the threshing floor, and as the fullness of the wine press.
Thus you also shall offer a wave offering to Baba God of all una tithes, which you receive of the pikin dem of Israel; and of it you shall give Baba God’s wave offering to Aaron the priest.
Out of all una gifts, you shall offer every wave offering of Baba God, of all its best, even the holy part of it out of it.’
“So you shall tell dem, ‘When you heave its best from it, then it go be credited to the Levites as the increase of the threshing floor, and as the increase of the wine press.
You may eat it anywhere, you and una households, for it is una reward in return for una service in the Tent of Meeting.
You shall bear no sin by reason of it, when you have heaved from it its best. You no go profane the holy things of the pikin dem of Israel, that you not die.’”
Baba God spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
“This is the statute of the law which Baba God has commanded. Tell the pikin dem of Israel to bring you a red heifer without spot, in which is no defect, and which was never yoked.
You shall give her to Eleazar the priest, and he shall bring her outside of the camp, and one shall kill her before his face.
Eleazar the priest shall take some of her blood with his finger, and sprinkle her blood toward the front of the Tent of Meeting seven times.
One shall burn the heifer in his sight; her skin, and her meat, and her blood, with her dung, shall he burn.
The priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet, and throw it into the middle of the burning of the heifer.
Then the priest shall wash his clothes, and he shall bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp, and the priest go be unclean until the evening.
Person wey burns her shall wash his clothes in water, and bathe his flesh in water, and go be unclean until the evening.

“A man Wey be clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and lay dem up outside of the camp in a clean place; and it go be kept for the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel for a water for impurity. It is a sin offering.

Person wey gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening. It go be to the pikin dem of Israel, and to the stranger who lives as a foreigner among dem, for a statute forever.
“Person wey touches the dead body of any man go be unclean seven days.
He shall purify imself with water on the third day, and on the seventh day he go be clean; but if he no dey purify imself the third day, then the seventh day he no go be clean.

Anybody wey touches a dead person, the body of a man who has died, and no dey purify imself, defiles Baba God’s tabernacle; and that soul go be cut off from Israel; because the water for impurity No be sprinkled on him, he go be unclean. His uncleanness is yet on him.
“This is the law when a man dies in a tent: Everybody wey comes into the tent, and everyone Wey be in the tent, go be unclean seven days.
Every open vessel, which has no covering bound on it, is unclean.
“Anybody wey in the open field touches one Wey be slain with a sword, or a dead body, or a bone of a man, or a grave, go be unclean seven days.
“For the unclean, dem shall take of the ashes of the burning of the sin offering; and running water go be poured into a vessel.

A clean person shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, on all the vessels, on the persons who were there, and on him who touched the bone, or the slain, or the dead, or the grave.

The clean person shall sprinkle on the unclean on the third day, and on the seventh day. On the seventh day, he shall purify him. He shall wash his clothes and bathe imself in water, and go be clean at evening.

But the man who go be unclean, and no go purify imself, that soul go be cut off from the middle of the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of Baba God. The water for impurity has not been sprinkled on him. He is unclean.
It go be a perpetual statute to dem. Person wey sprinkles the water for impurity shall wash his clothes, and person wey touches the water for impurity go be unclean until evening.
“Anything wey the unclean person touches go be unclean; and the soul that touches it go be unclean until evening.”
The pikin dem of Israel, even the whole congregation, come into the wilderness of Zin in the first month. The people stayed in Kadesh. Miriam died there, and was buried there.
There was no water for the congregation; and dem assembled themselves together against Moses and against Aaron.
The people quarreled with Moses, and spoke, saying, “We wish that we had died when our brothers died before Baba God!
Why have you bring Baba God’s assembly into this wilderness, that we should die there, we and our animals?
Why have you made us to come up out of Egypt, to bring us in to this evil place? It is no place of seed, or of figs, or of vines, or of pomegranates; neither is there any water to drink.”
