Moses and Aaron go from the presence of the assembly to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and fell on dem faces. Baba God’s glory appeared to dem.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,

“Take the rod, and assemble the congregation, you, and Aaron una brother, and speak to the rock before dem eyes, that it pour out its water. You shall bring water to dem out of the rock; so you shall give the congregation and dem livestock drink.”
Moses take the rod from before Baba God, as he commanded him.
Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly together before the rock, and E tell dem say, “Hear now, you rebels! Shall we bring water out of this rock for you?”
Moses lifted up his hand, and struck the rock with his rod twice, and water come out abundantly. The congregation and dem livestock drank.
Baba God talk say to Moses and Aaron, “Because you didn’t believe in me, to sanctify me in the eyes of the pikin dem of Israel, so you no go bring this assembly into the land which I have given dem.”
These are the waters of Meribah; because the pikin dem of Israel strove with Baba God, and he was sanctified in dem.
Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom, saying: “Thus says una brother Israel: You know all the travail that has happened to us;
how our fathers go down into Egypt, and we lived in Egypt a long time. The Egyptians mistreated us and our fathers.
When we cried to Baba God, he heard our voice, sent an angel, and bring us out of Egypt. See am, We be in Kadesh, a city in the edge of una border.

“Please Make we pass through una land. We go not pass through field or through vineyard, neither will we drink from the water of the wells. We go go along the king’s highway. We go not turn aside to the right hand nor to the left, until we have passed una border.”
Edom talk say to him, “You no go pass through me, lest I come out with the sword against you.”

The pikin dem of Israel talk say to him, “We go go up by the highway; and if we drink una water, I and my livestock, then I go give its price. Only let me, without doing anything else, pass through on my feet.”
He talk say, “You no go pass through.” Edom come out against him with many people, and with a strong hand.
Thus Edom refused to give Israel passage through his border, so Israel turned away from him.
Dem traveled from Kadesh: and the pikin dem of Israel, even the whole congregation, come to Mount Hor.
Baba God spoke to Moses and Aaron in Mount Hor, by the border of the land of Edom, saying,
“Aaron go be gathered to his people; for he no go enter into the land which I have given to the pikin dem of Israel, because you rebelled against my word at the waters of Meribah.
Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring dem up to Mount Hor;
and strip Aaron of his garments, and put dem on Eleazar his son. Aaron go be taken, and shall die there.”
Moses did as Baba God commanded. Dem go up into Mount Hor in the sight of all the congregation.
Moses stripped Aaron of his garments, and put dem on Eleazar his son. Aaron died there on the top of the mountain, and Moses and Eleazar come down from the mountain.
When all the congregation see that Aaron was dead, dem wept for Aaron thirty days, even all the house of Israel.
The Canaanite, the king of Arad, who lived in the South, heard that Israel come by the way of Atharim. He fought against Israel, and take some of dem captive.
Israel vowed a vow to Baba God, and talk say, “If You go indeed deliver this people into my hand, then I go utterly destroy dem cities.”
Baba God listened to the voice of Israel, and delivered up the Canaanites; and dem utterly destroyed dem and dem cities. The name of the place was call Hormah.
Dem traveled from Mount Hor by the way to the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom The soul of the people was very discouraged because of the journey.
The people spoke against God, and against Moses, “Why have you bring us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? For E get no bread, and E get no water; and our soul loathes this light bread.”
Baba God sent venomous snakes among the people, and dem bit the people. Many people of Israel died.

The people come to Moses, and talk say, “We have sinned, because we have spoken against Baba God, and against you. Pray to Baba God, that he take away the serpents from us.” Moses prayed for the people.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Make a venomous snake, and set it on a pole. It shall happen, that everyone Wey be bitten, when he sees it, shall live.”
Moses made a serpent of brass, and set it on the pole. If a serpent had bitten any man, when he looked at the serpent of brass, he lived.
The pikin dem of Israel traveled, and encamped in Oboth.
Dem traveled from Oboth, and encamped at Iyeabarim, in the wilderness which is before Moab, toward the sunrise.
From there dem traveled, and encamped in the valley of Zered.

From there dem traveled, and encamped on the other side of the Arnon, which is in the wilderness, that comes out of the border of the Amorites: for the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
So it is talk say in the book of the Wars of Baba God, “Vaheb in Suphah, the valleys of the Arnon,
the slope of the valleys that incline toward the dwelling of Ar, leans on the border of Moab.”
From there dem traveled to Beer; that is the well of which Baba God talk say to Moses, “Gather the people together, and I go give dem water.”
Then Israel sang this song: “Spring up, well! Sing to it,
the well, which the princes dug, which the nobles of the people dug, with the scepter, and with dem poles.” From the wilderness dem traveled to Mattanah;
and from Mattanah to Nahaliel; and from Nahaliel to Bamoth;
and from Bamoth to the valley that is in the field of Moab, to the top of Pisgah, which looks down on the desert.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,
“Let me pass through una land. We go not turn aside into field, or into vineyard. We go not drink of the water of the wells. We go go by the king’s highway, until we have passed una border.”
Sihon would not allow Israel to pass through his border, but Sihon gathered all his people together, and go out against Israel into the wilderness, and come to Jahaz. He fought against Israel.
Israel struck him with the edge of the sword, and possessed his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, even to the pikin dem of Ammon; for the border of the pikin dem of Ammon was strong.
Israel take all these cities. Israel lived in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon, and in all its villages.
For Heshbon was the city of Sihon the king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab, and taken all his land out of his hand, even to the Arnon.
So people wey speak in proverbs say, “Come to Heshbon. Let the city of Sihon be built and established;
for a fire has gone out of Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon. It has devoured Ar of Moab, The lords of the high places of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Moab! You be undone, people of Chemosh! He has given his sons as fugitives, and his daughters into captivity, to Sihon king of the Amorites.
We have shot at dem. Heshbon has perished even to Dibon. We have laid waste even to Nophah, Which reaches to Medeba.”
Thus Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent to spy out Jazer. Dem take its villages, and drove out the Amorites who were there.
Dem turned and go up by the way of Bashan. Og the king of Bashan go out against dem, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.

Baba God talk say to Moses, “No fear him, for I have delivered him into una hand, with all his people, and his land. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon.”
So dem struck him, with his sons and all his people, until there were no survivors; and dem possessed his land.
The pikin dem of Israel traveled, and encamped in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan at Jericho.
Balak the son of Zippor see all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
Moab was very afraid of the people, because dem were many. Moab was distressed because of the pikin dem of Israel.
Moab talk say to the elders of Midian, “Now this plenty people will lick up all that is around us, as the ox licks up the grass of the field.” Balak the son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

He sent messengers to Balaam the son of Beor, to Pethor, which is by the River, to the land of the pikin dem of his people, to call him, saying, “See am, E get a people who come out of Egypt. See am, dem cover the surface of the earth, and Dem be staying opposite me.

Please come now so curse me this people; for Dem be too mighty for me. Perhaps I shall prevail, that we may strike dem, and that I may drive dem out of the land; for I know that he whom you bless is blessed, and he whom you curse is cursed.”
The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian comot with the rewards of divination in dem hand. Dem come to Balaam, and spoke to him the words of Balak.
E tell dem say, “Lodge here this night, and I go bring you word again, as Baba God shall speak to me.” The princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.
God come to Balaam, and talk say, “Wey be these men with you?”
Balaam talk say to God, “Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, has talk say to me,
‘See am, the people that has come out of Egypt covers the surface of the earth. Now, come curse me dem. Perhaps I go be able to fight against dem, and shall drive dem out.’”
God talk say to Balaam, “You no go go with dem. You no go curse the people; for Dem be blessed.”
Balaam rose up in the morning, and talk say to the princes of Balak, “Go to una land; for Baba God refuses to permit me to go with you.”
The princes of Moab rose up, and dem go to Balak, and talk say, “Balaam refuses to come with us.”
Balak again sent princes, more, and more honorable than dem.
Dem come to Balaam, and talk say to him, “Thus says Balak the son of Zippor, ‘Please let nothing hinder you from coming to me,
for I go promote you to plenty well-well honor, and Anything wey you say to me I go do. Please come so, and curse this people for me.’”
Balaam answer the workers of Balak, “If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I no fit go beyond the word of Baba God my God, to do less or more.
Now so, please wait also here this night, that I may know what Baba God will speak to me more.”
God come to Balaam at night, and talk say to him, “If the men have come to call you, rise up, go with dem; but only the word which I speak to you, that you shall do.”
Balaam rose up in the morning, and saddled his donkey, and go with the princes of Moab.
God’s anger burned because he go; and Baba God’s angel placed imself in the way for an adversary against him. Now he was riding on his donkey, and his two workers were with him.

The donkey see Baba God’s angel standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand; and the donkey turned aside out of the way, and go into the field. Balaam struck the donkey, to turn her into the way.
Then Baba God’s angel stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, a wall being on this side, and a wall on that side.
The donkey see Baba God’s angel, and she thrust sheself to the wall, and crushed Balaam’s foot against the wall. He struck her again.
Baba God’s angel go further, and stood in a narrow place, where there was no way to turn either to the right hand or to the left.
The donkey see Baba God’s angel, and she lay down under Balaam. Balaam’s anger burned, and he struck the donkey with his staff.
Baba God opened the mouth of the donkey, and she talk say to Balaam, “What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?”
Balaam talk say to the donkey, “Because you have mocked me, I wish there were a sword in my hand, for now I would have killed you.”
The donkey talk say to Balaam, “Am I not una donkey, on which you have ridden all una life long until today? Was I ever in the habit of doing so to you?” He talk say, “No.”
Then Baba God opened the eyes of Balaam, and he see Baba God’s angel standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand; and he bowed his head, and fell on his face.
Baba God’s angel talk say to him, “Why have you struck una donkey these three times? See am, I have come out as an adversary, because una way is perverse before me.
The donkey see me, and turned aside before me these three times. Unless she had turned aside from me, surely now I would have killed you, and saved her alive.”
Balaam talk say to Baba God’s angel, “I have sinned; for I didn’t know that you stood in the way against me. Now so, if it displeases you, I go go back again.”
Baba God’s angel talk say to Balaam, “Go with the men; but only the word that I shall speak to you, that you shall speak.” So Balaam go with the princes of Balak.
When Balak heard that Balaam had come, he go out to meet him to the City of Moab, which is on the border of the Arnon, which is in the utmost part of the border.
Balak talk say to Balaam, “Didn’t I earnestly send to you to call you? Why didn’t you come to me? Am I not able indeed to promote you to honor?”
Balaam talk say to Balak, “See am, I have come to you. Have I now any power at all to speak anything? The word that God puts in my mouth, that shall I speak.”
Balaam go with Balak, and dem come to Kiriath Huzoth.
Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep, and sent to Balaam, and to the princes who were with him.
In the morning, Balak take Balaam, and bring him up into the high places of Baal; and he see from there part of the people.
Balaam talk say to Balak, “Build here seven altars for me, and prepare here seven bulls and seven rams for me.”
Balak did as Balaam had spoken; and Balak and Balaam offered on every altar a bull and a ram.
Balaam talk say to Balak, “Stand by una burnt offering, and I go go. Perhaps Baba God will come to meet me. Anything wey he shows me I go tell you.” He go to a bare height.
God met Balaam, and E tell am say, “I have prepared the seven altars, and I have offered up a bull and a ram on every altar.”
Baba God put a word in Balaam’s mouth, and talk say, “Return to Balak, and thus you shall speak.”
He come back to him, and see am, he was standing by his burnt offering, he, and all the princes of Moab.
He take up his parable, and talk say, “From Aram has Balak bring me, the king of Moab from the mountains of the East. Come, curse Jacob for me. Come, defy Israel.
How shall I curse whom God has not cursed? How shall I defy whom Baba God has not defied?
For from the top of the rocks I see him. From the hills I see him. See am, it is a people that dwells alone, and no go be listed among the nations.
Who can count the dust of Jacob, or count the fourth part of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous! Let my last end be like his!”
Balak talk say to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I take you to curse my enemies, and see am, you have blessed dem altogether.”
He answer and talk say, “Must I not take heed to speak that which Baba God puts in my mouth?”
Balak talk say to him, “Please come with me to another place, where you may see dem. You shall see just part of dem, and no go see dem all. Curse dem from there for me.”
He take him into the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars, and offered up a bull and a ram on every altar.
He talk say to Balak, “Stand here by una burnt offering, while I meet over there.”
Baba God met Balaam, and put a word in his mouth, and talk say, “Return to Balak, and say this.”
He come to him, and see am, he was standing by his burnt offering, and the princes of Moab with him. Balak talk say to him, “What has Baba God spoken?”
He take up his parable, and talk say, “Rise up, Balak, and hear! Listen to me, you son of Zippor.
God No be a man, that he should lie, nor the Son of Man, that he should repent. Has he talk say, and will he not do it? Or has he spoken, and will he not make it good?
See am, I have received a command to bless. He has blessed, and I no fit reverse it.
He has not seen wickedness in Jacob. Neither has he seen perverseness in Israel. Baba God his God is with him. The shout of a king is among dem.
God brings dem out of Egypt. He has as it were the strength of the wild ox.
Surely E get no enchantment with Jacob; Neither is there any divination with Israel. Now it go be talk say of Jacob and of Israel, ‘What has God done!’
See am, the people rises up as a lioness. As a lion he lifts imself up. He no go lie down until he eats of the prey, and drinks the blood of the slain.”
Balak talk say to Balaam, “Neither curse dem at all, nor bless dem at all.”
But Balaam answer Balak, “Didn’t I tell una, saying, ‘All that Baba God speaks, that I must do?’”
Balak talk say to Balaam, “Come now, I go take you to another place; perhaps it will please God that you may curse dem for me from there.”
Balak take Balaam to the top of Peor, that looks down on the desert.
Balaam talk say to Balak, “Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
Balak did as Balaam had talk say, and offered up a bull and a ram on every altar.
When Balaam see that it pleased Baba God to bless Israel, he didn’t go, as at the other times, to meet with enchantments, but he set his face toward the wilderness.
Balaam lifted up his eyes, and he see Israel dwelling according to dem tribes; and the Spirit of God come on him.
He take up his parable, and talk say, “Balaam the son of Beor says, the man whose eyes are open says;
he says, wey hear the words of God, wey see the vision of the Almighty, falling down, and having his eyes open:
How goodly are una tents, Jacob, and una tents, Israel!
As valleys Dem be spread out, as gardens by the riverside, as aloes which Baba God has planted, as cedar trees beside the waters.
Water shall flow from his buckets. His seed go be in many waters. His king go be higher than Agag. His kingdom go be exalted.
God brings him out of Egypt. He has as it were the strength of the wild ox. He shall eat up the nations his adversaries, shall break dem bones in pieces, and pierce dem with his arrows.
He couched, he lay down as a lion, as a lioness; who shall rouse him up? Everybody wey blesses you is blessed. Everybody wey curses you is cursed.”
Balak’s anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together. Balak talk say to Balaam, “I call you to curse my enemies, and, see am, you have altogether blessed dem these three times.
So now flee you to una place! I thought to promote you to great honor; but, see am, Baba God has kept you back from honor.”
Balaam talk say to Balak, “Didn’t I also tell una messengers who you sent to me, saying,
‘If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I no fit go beyond Baba God’s word, to do either good or bad of my own mind. I go say what Baba God says’?
Now, see am, I go to my people. Come, I go inform you what this people shall do to una people in the latter days.”
He take up his parable, and talk say, “Balaam the son of Beor says, the man whose eyes are open says;
he says, wey hear the words of God, knows the knowledge of the Most High, and wey see the vision of the Almighty, Falling down, and having his eyes open:
I see him, but not now. I see him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob. A scepter will rise out of Israel, and shall strike through the corners of Moab, and break down all the sons of Sheth.
Edom go be a possession. Seir, his enemies, also go be a possession, while Israel does valiantly.
Out of Jacob shall one have dominion, and shall destroy the remnant from the city.”
He looked at Amalek, and take up his parable, and talk say, “Amalek was the first of the nations, But his latter end shall come to destruction.”
He looked at the Kenite, and take up his parable, and talk say, “Una dwelling place is strong. Una nest is set in the rock.
Nevertheless Kain go be wasted, until Asshur carries you away captive.”
He take up his parable, and talk say, “Alas, who shall live when God does this?
But ships shall come from the coast of Kittim. Dem shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber. He also shall come to destruction.”
Balaam rose up, and go and come back to his place; and Balak also go his way.
Israel stayed in Shittim; and the people began to play the prostitute with the daughters of Moab;
for dem call the people to the sacrifices of dem gods. The people ate and bowed down to dem gods.
Israel joined imself to Baal Peor. Baba God’s anger burned against Israel.
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Take all the chiefs of the people, and hang dem up to Baba God before the sun, that the fierce anger of Baba God may turn away from Israel.”
Moses talk say to the judges of Israel, “Everyone kill his men who have joined themselves to Baal Peor.”

See am, one of the pikin dem of Israel come and bring to his brothers a Midianite woman in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel, while dem were weeping at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
When Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, see it, he rose up from the middle of the congregation, and take a spear in his hand.
He go after the man of Israel into the pavilion, and thrust both of dem through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her body. So the plague was stayed from the pikin dem of Israel.
People wey died by the plague were twenty-four thousand.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,

“Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned my serious anger away from the pikin dem of Israel, in that he was jealous with my jealousy among dem, so that I didn’t consume the pikin dem of Israel in my jealousy.
So say, ‘See am, I give to him my covenant of peace.
It go be to him, and to his offspring after him, the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he was jealous for his God, and made atonement for the pikin dem of Israel.’”
Now the name of the man of Israel that was slain, who was slain with the Midianite woman, was Zimri, the son of Salu, a prince of a fathers’ house among the Simeonites.
The name of the Midianite woman who was slain was Cozbi, the daughter of Zur. He was head of the people of a fathers’ house in Midian.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Harass the Midianites, and strike dem,

for dem harassed you with dem wiles, with which dem have deceived you in the matter of Peor, and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of the prince of Midian, dem sister, who was slain on the day of the plague in the matter of Peor.”
After the plague, Baba God spoke to Moses and to Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, saying,
“Take a census of all the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel, from twenty years old and upward, by dem fathers’ houses, all Wey be able to go out to war in Israel.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with dem in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
“Take a census, from twenty years old and upward; as Baba God commanded Moses and the pikin dem of Israel.” These are those that come out of the land of Egypt.
Reuben, the firstborn of Israel; the sons of Reuben: of Hanoch, the family of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the family of the Palluites;
of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites; of Carmi, the family of the Carmites.
These are the families of the Reubenites; and people wey were counted of dem were forty-three thousand seven hundred thirty.
The sons of Pallu: Eliab.

The sons of Eliab: Nemuel, and Dathan, and Abiram. These are that Dathan and Abiram, who were call by the congregation, who rebelled against Moses and against Aaron in the company of Korah, when dem rebelled against Baba God,
and the earth opened its mouth, and swallowed dem up together with Korah, when that company died; at the time the fire devoured two hundred fifty men, and dem became a sign.
Notwithstanding, the sons of Korah didn’t die.
The sons of Simeon after dem families: of Nemuel, the family of the Nemuelites; of Jamin, the family of the Jaminites; of Jachin, the family of the Jachinites;
of Zerah, the family of the Zerahites; of Shaul, the family of the Shaulites.
These are the families of the Simeonites, twenty-two thousand two hundred.
The sons of Gad after dem families: of Zephon, the family of the Zephonites; of Haggi, the family of the Haggites; of Shuni, the family of the Shunites;
of Ozni, the family of the Oznites; of Eri, the family of the Erites;
of Arod, the family of the Arodites; of Areli, the family of the Arelites.
These are the families of the sons of Gad according to people wey were counted of dem, forty thousand and five hundred.
The sons of Judah: Er and Onan. Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
The sons of Judah after dem families were: of Shelah, the family of the Shelanites; of Perez, the family of the Perezites; of Zerah, the family of the Zerahites.
The sons of Perez were: of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites; of Hamul, the family of the Hamulites.
These are the families of Judah according to people wey were counted of dem, seventy-six thousand five hundred.
The sons of Issachar after dem families: of Tola, the family of the Tolaites; of Puvah, the family of the Punites;
of Jashub, the family of the Jashubites; of Shimron, the family of the Shimronites.
These are the families of Issachar according to people wey were counted of dem, sixty-four thousand three hundred.
The sons of Zebulun after dem families: of Sered, the family of the Seredites; of Elon, the family of the Elonites; of Jahleel, the family of the Jahleelites.
These are the families of the Zebulunites according to people wey were counted of dem, sixty thousand five hundred.
The sons of Joseph after dem families: Manasseh and Ephraim.
The sons of Manasseh: of Machir, the family of the Machirites; and Machir became the father of Gilead; of Gilead, the family of the Gileadites.
These are the sons of Gilead: of Iezer, the family of the Iezerites; of Helek, the family of the Helekites;
and Asriel, the family of the Asrielites; and Shechem, the family of the Shechemites;
and Shemida, the family of the Shemidaites; and Hepher, the family of the Hepherites.
Zelophehad the son of Hepher had no sons, but daughters: and the names of the daughters of Zelophehad were Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These are the families of Manasseh. People wey were counted of dem were fifty-two thousand seven hundred.
These are the sons of Ephraim after dem families: of Shuthelah, the family of the Shuthelahites; of Becher, the family of the Becherites; of Tahan, the family of the Tahanites.
These are the sons of Shuthelah: of Eran, the family of the Eranites.
These are the families of the sons of Ephraim according to people wey were counted of dem, thirty-two thousand five hundred. These are the sons of Joseph after dem families.
The sons of Benjamin after dem families: of Bela, the family of the Belaites; of Ashbel, the family of the Ashbelites; of Ahiram, the family of the Ahiramites;
of Shephupham, the family of the Shuphamites; of Hupham, the family of the Huphamites.
The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: the family of the Ardites; of Naaman, the family of the Naamites.
These are the sons of Benjamin after dem families; and people wey were counted of dem were forty-five thousand six hundred.
These are the sons of Dan after dem families: of Shuham, the family of the Shuhamites. These are the families of Dan after dem families.
All the families of the Shuhamites, according to people wey were counted of dem, were sixty-four thousand four hundred.
The sons of Asher after dem families: of Imnah, the family of the Imnites; of Ishvi, the family of the Ishvites; of Beriah, the family of the Berites.
Of the sons of Beriah: of Heber, the family of the Heberites; of Malchiel, the family of the Malchielites.
The name of the daughter of Asher was Serah.
These are the families of the sons of Asher according to people wey were counted of dem, fifty-three thousand and four hundred.
The sons of Naphtali after dem families: of Jahzeel, the family of the Jahzeelites; of Guni, the family of the Gunites;
of Jezer, the family of the Jezerites; of Shillem, the family of the Shillemites.
These are the families of Naphtali according to dem families; and people wey were counted of dem were forty-five thousand four hundred.
These are people wey were counted of the pikin dem of Israel, six hundred one thousand seven hundred thirty.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“To these the land go be divided for an inheritance according to the number of names.
To the more you shall give the more inheritance, and to the fewer you shall give the less inheritance. To everyone according to people wey were counted of him shall his inheritance be given.
Notwithstanding, the land go be divided by lot. According to the names of the tribes of dem fathers dem shall inherit.
According to the lot shall dem inheritance be divided between the more and the fewer.”
These are people wey were counted of the Levites after dem families: of Gershon, the family of the Gershonites; of Kohath, the family of the Kohathites; of Merari, the family of the Merarites.

These are the families of Levi: the family of the Libnites, the family of the Hebronites, the family of the Mahlites, the family of the Mushites, the family of the Korahites. Kohath became the father of Amram.
The name of Amram’s wife was Jochebed, the daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt. She bore to Amram Aaron and Moses, and Miriam dem sister.
To Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died when dem offered strange fire before Baba God.

People wey were counted of dem were twenty-three thousand, every male from a month old and upward; for dem No be counted among the pikin dem of Israel, because there was no inheritance given dem among the pikin dem of Israel.
These are people wey were counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who counted the pikin dem of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
But among these there No be a man of dem who were counted by Moses and Aaron the priest, who counted the pikin dem of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai.
For Baba God had talk say of dem, “Dem shall surely die in the wilderness.” There No be a man left of dem, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.

Then the daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of Manasseh the son of Joseph come near. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah.
Dem stood before Moses, and before Eleazar the priest, and before the princes and all the congregation, at the door of the Tent of Meeting, saying,
“Our father died in the wilderness. He No be among the company of people wey gathered themselves together against Baba God in the company of Korah, but he died in his own sin. He had no sons.
Why should the name of our father be taken away from among his family, because he had no son? Give to us a possession among the brothers of our father.”
Moses bring dem cause before Baba God.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“The daughters of Zelophehad speak right. You shall surely give dem a possession of an inheritance among dem father’s brothers. You shall cause the inheritance of dem father to pass to dem.
You shall speak to the pikin dem of Israel, saying, ‘If a man dies, and has no son, then you shall cause his inheritance to pass to his daughter.
If he has no daughter, then you shall give his inheritance to his brothers.
If he has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to his father’s brothers.

If his father has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to his kinsman Wey be next to him of his family, and he shall possess it. This go be a statute and ordinance for the pikin dem of Israel, as Baba God commanded Moses.’”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Go up into this mountain of Abarim, and see the land which I have given to the pikin dem of Israel.
When you have seen it, you also go be gathered to una people, as Aaron una brother was gathered;

because in the strife of the congregation, you rebelled against my word in the wilderness of Zin, to honor me as holy at the waters before dem eyes.” (These are the waters of Meribah of Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.)
Moses spoke to Baba God, saying,
“Let Baba God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation,
who may go out before dem, and who may come in before dem, and who may lead dem out, and who may bring dem in; that the congregation of Baba God not be as sheep which have no shepherd.”
Baba God talk say to Moses, “Take Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay una hand on him.
Set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation; and commission him in dem sight.
You shall give authority to him, that all the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel may obey.

He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall inquire for him by the judgment of the Urim before Baba God. At his word dem shall go out, and at his word dem shall come in, both he, and all the pikin dem of Israel with him, even all the congregation.”
Moses did as Baba God commanded him. He take Joshua, and set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation.
He laid his hands on him, and commissioned him, as Baba God spoke by Moses.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Command the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem, ‘See that you present my offering, my chop for my offerings made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to me, in dem due season.’
You shall tell dem, ‘This is the offering made by fire which you shall offer to Baba God: male lambs a year old without defect, two day by day, for a continual burnt offering.
You shall offer the one lamb in the morning, and you shall offer the other lamb at evening;
with one tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a meal offering, mixed with the fourth part of a hin of beaten oil.
It is a continual burnt offering, which was ordained in Mount Sinai for a pleasant aroma, an offering made by fire to Baba God.
Its drink offering go be the fourth part of a hin for the one lamb. You shall pour out a drink offering of strong drink to Baba God in the holy place.
The other lamb you shall offer at evening. As the meal offering of the morning, and as its drink offering, you shall offer it, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Baba God.
“‘On the Sabbath day, two male lambs a year old without defect, and two tenths of an ephah of fine flour for a meal offering, mixed with oil, and its drink offering:
this is the burnt offering of every Sabbath, besides the continual burnt offering, and its drink offering.
“‘In the beginnings of una months, you shall offer a burnt offering to Baba God: two young bulls, and one ram, seven male lambs a year old without defect;
and three tenths of an ephah of fine flour for a meal offering, mixed with oil, for each bull; and two tenth parts of fine flour for a meal offering, mixed with oil, for the one ram;
and one tenth part of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering to every lamb; for a burnt offering of a pleasant aroma, an offering made by fire to Baba God.

Dem drink offerings go be half a hin of wine for a bull, and the third part of a hin for the ram, and the fourth part of a hin for a lamb. This is the burnt offering of every month throughout the months of the year.
One male goat for a sin offering to Baba God; it go be offered besides the continual burnt offering, and its drink offering.
“‘In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is Baba God’s Passover.
On the fifteenth day of this month go be a feast. Unleavened bread go be eaten for seven days.
In the first day go be a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work;
but you shall offer an offering made by fire, a burnt offering to Baba God: two young bulls, and one ram, and seven male lambs a year old; dem go be to you without defect;
and dem meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil. You shall offer three tenths for a bull, and two tenths for the ram.
You shall offer one tenth for every lamb of the seven lambs;
and one male goat for a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
You shall offer these besides the burnt offering of the morning, which is for a continual burnt offering.

In this way you shall offer daily, for seven days, the chop of the offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Baba God. It go be offered in addition to the continual burnt offering, and its drink offering.
On the seventh day you go get a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work.
“‘Also in the day of the first fruits, when you offer a new meal offering to Baba God in una feast of weeks, you go get a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work;
but you shall offer a burnt offering for a pleasant aroma to Baba God: two young bulls, one ram, seven male lambs a year old;
and dem meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil, three tenths for each bull, two tenths for the one ram,
one tenth for every lamb of the seven lambs;
one male goat, to make atonement for you.
Besides the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, you shall offer dem and dem drink offerings. See that Dem be without defect.
“‘In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you go get a holy convocation; you shall do no regular work: it is a day of blowing of trumpets to you.
You shall offer a burnt offering for a pleasant aroma to Baba God: one young bull, one ram, seven male lambs a year old without defect;
and dem meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil, three tenths for the bull, two tenths for the ram,
and one tenth for every lamb of the seven lambs;
and one male goat for a sin offering, to make atonement for you;

besides the burnt offering of the new moon, and its meal offering, and the continual burnt offering and its meal offering, and dem drink offerings, according to dem ordinance, for a pleasant aroma, an offering made by fire to Baba God.
“‘On the tenth day of this seventh month you go get a holy convocation. You shall afflict una souls. You shall do no kind of work;
but you shall offer a burnt offering to Baba God for a pleasant aroma: one young bull, one ram, seven male lambs a year old; all without defect;
and dem meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil, three tenths for the bull, two tenths for the one ram,
one tenth for every lamb of the seven lambs:
one male goat for a sin offering; besides the sin offering of atonement, and the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, and dem drink offerings.
“‘On the fifteenth day of the seventh month you go get a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work. You shall keep a feast to Baba God seven days.
You shall offer a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Baba God: thirteen young bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old; all without defect;
and dem meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil, three tenths for every bull of the thirteen bulls, two tenths for each ram of the two rams,
and one tenth for every lamb of the fourteen lambs;
and one male goat for a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering, its meal offering, and its drink offering.
“‘On the second day you shall offer twelve young bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without defect;
and dem meal offering and dem drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to dem number, after the ordinance;
and one male goat for a sin offering; besides the continual burnt offering, with its meal offering and dem drink offerings.
“‘On the third day eleven bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without defect;
and dem meal offering and dem drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to dem number, after the ordinance;
and one male goat for a sin offering; besides the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, and its drink offering.
“‘On the fourth day ten bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without defect;
dem meal offering and dem drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to dem number, after the ordinance;
and one male goat for a sin offering; besides the continual burnt offering, its meal offering, and its drink offering.
“‘On the fifth day nine bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without defect;
and dem meal offering and dem drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to dem number, after the ordinance;
and one male goat for a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, and its drink offering.
“‘On the sixth day eight bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without defect;
and dem meal offering and dem drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to dem number, after the ordinance;
and one male goat for a sin offering; besides the continual burnt offering, its meal offering, and the drink offerings of it.
“‘On the seventh day seven bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without defect;
and dem meal offering and dem drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to dem number, after the ordinance;
and one male goat for a sin offering; besides the continual burnt offering, its meal offering, and its drink offering.
“‘On the eighth day you go get a solemn assembly: you shall do no regular work;
but you shall offer a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Baba God: one bull, one ram, seven male lambs a year old without defect;
dem meal offering and dem drink offerings for the bull, for the ram, and for the lambs, go be according to dem number, after the ordinance:
and one male goat for a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering, with its meal offering, and its drink offering.

“‘You shall offer these to Baba God in una set feasts, besides una vows, and una freewill offerings, for una burnt offerings, and for una meal offerings, and for una drink offerings, and for una peace offerings.’”
Moses told the pikin dem of Israel according to all that Baba God commanded Moses.
Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the pikin dem of Israel, saying, “This is the thing which Baba God has commanded.
When a man vows a vow to Baba God, or swears an oath to bind his soul with a bond, he no go break his word. He shall do according to all that proceeds out of his mouth.
“Also when a woman vows a vow to Baba God, and binds sheself by a bond, being in her father’s house, in her youth,

and her father hears her vow, and her bond with which she has bound her soul, and her father holds his peace at her; then all her vows shall stand, and every bond with which she has bound her soul shall stand.

But if her father forbids her in the day that he hears, none of her vows, or of her bonds with which she has bound her soul, shall stand. Baba God will forgive her, because her father has forbidden her.
“If she has a husband, while her vows are on her, or the rash utterance of her lips, with which she has bound her soul,
and her husband hears it, and hold his peace at her in the day that he hears it; then her vows shall stand, and her bonds with which she has bound her soul shall stand.

But if her husband forbids her in the day that he hears it, then he shall make void her vow which is on her, and the rash utterance of her lips, with which she has bound her soul. Baba God will forgive her.
“But the vow of a widow, or of her Wey be divorced, everything with which she has bound her soul, shall stand against her.
“If she vowed in her husband’s house, or bound her soul by a bond with an oath,
and her husband heard it, and held his peace at her, and didn’t disallow her; then all her vows shall stand, and every bond with which she bound her soul shall stand.

But if her husband made dem null and void in the day that he heard dem, then Anything wey proceeded out of her lips concerning her vows, or concerning the bond of her soul, no go stand. Her husband has made dem void. Baba God will forgive her.
Every vow, and every binding oath to afflict the soul, her husband may establish it, or her husband may make it void.

But if her husband altogether hold his peace at her from day to day, then he establishes all her vows, or all her bonds, which are on her. He has established dem, because he held his peace at her in the day that he heard dem.
But if he shall make dem null and void after that he has heard dem, then he shall bear her wickedness.”
These are the statutes which Baba God commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, between a father and his daughter, being in her youth, in her father’s house.
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Avenge the pikin dem of Israel for the Midianites. Afterward you go be gathered to una people.”
Moses spoke to the people, saying, “Arm men from among you for the war, that dem may go against Midian, to execute Baba God’s vengeance on Midian.
Of every tribe one thousand, throughout all the tribes of Israel, you shall send to the war.”
So there were delivered, out of the thousands of Israel, a thousand of every tribe, twelve thousand armed for war.
Moses sent dem, one thousand of every tribe, to the war, dem and Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, to the war, with the vessels of the sanctuary and the trumpets for the alarm in his hand.
Dem fought against Midian, as Baba God commanded Moses. Dem killed every male.
Dem killed the kings of Midian with the rest of dem slain: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian. Dem also killed Balaam the son of Beor with the sword.
The pikin dem of Israel take the women of Midian captive with dem little ones; and all dem livestock, all dem flocks, and all dem goods, dem take as plunder.
All dem cities in the places in which dem lived, and all dem encampments, dem burned with fire.
Dem take all the captives, and all the plunder, both of man and of animal.

Dem bring the captives, and the prey, and the plunder, to Moses, and to Eleazar the priest, and to the congregation of the pikin dem of Israel, to the camp at the plains of Moab, which are by the Jordan at Jericho.
Moses, and Eleazar the priest, and all the princes of the congregation, go out to meet dem outside of the camp.
Moses was angry with the officers of the army, the captains of thousands and the captains of hundreds, who come from the service of the war.
Moses talk say to dem, “Have you saved all the women alive?
See am, these caused the pikin dem of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against Baba God in the matter of Peor, and so the plague was among the congregation of Baba God.
Now so kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman who has known man by lying with him.
But all the girls, who have not known man by lying with him, keep alive for unaself.
“Encamp outside of the camp seven days. Anybody wey has killed any person, and Anybody wey has touched any slain, purify unaself on the third day and on the seventh day, you and una captives.
As to every garment, and all that is made of skin, and all work of goats’ hair, and all things made of wood, you shall purify unaself.”
Eleazar the priest talk say to the men of war who go to the battle, “This is the statute of the law which Baba God has commanded Moses:
however the gold, and the silver, the brass, the iron, the tin, and the lead,

everything that may withstand the fire, you shall make to go through the fire, and it go be clean; nevertheless it go be purified with the water for impurity. All that no dey withstand the fire you shall make to go through the water.
You shall wash una clothes on the seventh day, and you go be clean. Afterward you shall come into the camp.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Count the plunder that was taken, both of man and of animal, you, and Eleazar the priest, and the heads of the fathers’ households of the congregation;
and divide the plunder into two parts: between the men skilled in war, who go out to battle, and all the congregation.
Levy a tribute to Baba God of the men of war who go out to battle: one soul of five hundred; of the persons, of the cattle, of the donkeys, and of the flocks.
Take it from dem half, and give it to Eleazar the priest, for Baba God’s wave offering.

Of the pikin dem of Israel’s half, you shall take one drawn out of every fifty, of the persons, of the cattle, of the donkeys, and of the flocks, of all the livestock, and give dem to the Levites, who perform the duty of Baba God’s tabernacle.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest did as Baba God commanded Moses.
Now the plunder, over and above the booty which the men of war take, was six hundred seventy-five thousand sheep,
and seventy-two thousand head of cattle,
and sixty-one thousand donkeys,
and thirty-two thousand persons in all, of the women who had not known man by lying with him.
The half, which was the portion of people wey go out to war, was in number three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep:
and Baba God’s tribute of the sheep was six hundred seventy-five.
The cattle were thirty-six thousand; of which Baba God’s tribute was seventy-two.
The donkeys were thirty thousand five hundred; of which Baba God’s tribute was sixty-one.
The persons were sixteen thousand; of whom Baba God’s tribute was thirty-two persons.
Moses give the tribute, which was Baba God’s wave offering, to Eleazar the priest, as Baba God commanded Moses.
Of the pikin dem of Israel’s half, which Moses divided off from the men who fought
(now the congregation’s half was three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,
and thirty-six thousand head of cattle,
and thirty thousand five hundred donkeys,
and sixteen thousand persons),

even of the pikin dem of Israel’s half, Moses take one drawn out of every fifty, both of man and of animal, and give dem to the Levites, who performed the duty of Baba God’s tabernacle; as Baba God commanded Moses.
The officers who were over the thousands of the army, the captains of thousands, and the captains of hundreds, come near to Moses.
Dem talk say to Moses, “Una workers have taken the sum of the men of war Wey be under our command, and there lacks not one man of us.
We have bring Baba God’s offering, what every man has gotten, of jewels of gold, armlets, and bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and necklaces, to make atonement for our souls before Baba God.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest take dem gold, even all worked jewels.
All the gold of the wave offering that dem offered up to Baba God, of the captains of thousands, and of the captains of hundreds, was sixteen thousand seven hundred fifty shekels.
The men of war had taken booty, every man for imself.
Moses and Eleazar the priest take the gold of the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and bring it into the Tent of Meeting, for a memorial for the pikin dem of Israel before Baba God.

Now the pikin dem of Reuben and the pikin dem of Gad had a plenty well-well plenty people of livestock. When dem see the land of Jazer, and the land of Gilead, that see am, the place was a place for livestock;
the pikin dem of Gad and the pikin dem of Reuben come and spoke to Moses, and to Eleazar the priest, and to the princes of the congregation, saying,
“Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon,
the land which Baba God struck before the congregation of Israel, is a land for livestock; and una workers have livestock.”
Dem talk say, “If we have find favor in una sight, let this land be given to una workers for a possession. No bring us over the Jordan.”
Moses talk say to the pikin dem of Gad, and to the pikin dem of Reuben, “Shall una brothers go to the war, and shall you sit here?
Why do you discourage the heart of the pikin dem of Israel from going over into the land which Baba God has given dem?
Una fathers did so when I sent dem from Kadesh Barnea to see the land.
For when dem go up to the valley of Eshcol, and see the land, dem discouraged the heart of the pikin dem of Israel, that dem no suppose go into the land which Baba God had given dem.
Baba God’s anger burned in that day, and he swore, saying,
‘Surely none of the men who come up out of Egypt, from twenty years old and upward, shall see the land which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; because dem have not wholly follow me,
except Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, and Joshua the son of Nun; because dem have follow Baba God completely.’
Baba God’s anger burned against Israel, and he made dem wander back and forth in the wilderness forty years, until all the generation, who had done evil in Baba God’s sight, was consumed.
“See am, you have risen up in una fathers’ place, an increase of sinful men, to increase the fierce anger of Baba God toward Israel.
For if you turn away from after him, he will yet again leave dem in the wilderness; and You go destroy all these people.”
Dem come near to him, and talk say, “We go build sheepfolds here for our livestock, and cities for our little ones;

but we ourselves Go be ready armed to go before the pikin dem of Israel, until we have bring dem to dem place. Our little ones shall live in the fortified cities because of the inhabitants of the land.
We go not return to our houses, until the pikin dem of Israel have each inherited dem inheritance.
For We go not inherit with dem on the other side of the Jordan, and forward; because our inheritance has come to us on this side of the Jordan eastward.”
Moses talk say to dem, “If You go do this thing, if You go arm unaself to go before Baba God to the war,
and every armed man of You go pass over the Jordan before Baba God, until he has driven out his enemies from before him,
and the land is subdued before Baba God; then afterward you shall return, and be guiltless towards Baba God, and towards Israel; and this land go be to you for a possession before Baba God.
“But if You go not do so, see am, you have sinned against Baba God; and be sure una sin will find you out.
Build cities for una little ones, and folds for una sheep; and do that which has proceeded out of una mouth.”
The pikin dem of Gad and the pikin dem of Reuben spoke to Moses, saying, “Una workers will do as my lord commands.
Our little ones, our wives, our flocks, and all our livestock, go be there in the cities of Gilead;
but una workers will pass over, every man Wey be armed for war, before Baba God to battle, as my lord says.”
So Moses commanded concerning dem to Eleazar the priest, and to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the heads of the fathers’ households of the tribes of the pikin dem of Israel.

Moses talk say to dem, “If the pikin dem of Gad and the pikin dem of Reuben will pass with you over the Jordan, every man Wey be armed to battle, before Baba God, and the land is subdued before you, then you shall give dem the land of Gilead for a possession;
but if Dem go not pass over with you armed, dem go get possessions among you in the land of Canaan.”
The pikin dem of Gad and the pikin dem of Reuben answer, saying, “As Baba God has talk say to una workers, so will we do.
We go pass over armed before Baba God into the land of Canaan, and the possession of our inheritance shall remain with us beyond the Jordan.”

Moses give to dem, even to the pikin dem of Gad, and to the pikin dem of Reuben, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh the son of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land, according to its cities and borders, even the cities of the surrounding land.
The pikin dem of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
Atrothshophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
Beth Nimrah, and Beth Haran: fortified cities, and folds for sheep.
The pikin dem of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
Nebo, and Baal Meon, (dem names being changed), and Sibmah. Dem give other names to the cities which dem built.
The pikin dem of Machir the son of Manasseh go to Gilead, take it, and dispossessed the Amorites who were inside am.
Moses give Gilead to Machir the son of Manasseh; and he lived inside am.
Jair the son of Manasseh go and take its villages, and call dem Havvoth Jair.
Nobah go and take Kenath, and its villages, and call it Nobah, after his own name.
These are the journeys of the pikin dem of Israel, when dem go out of the land of Egypt by dem armies under the hand of Moses and Aaron.
Moses wrote dem goings out according to dem journeys by the commandment of Baba God. These are dem journeys according to dem goings out.

Dem traveled from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the next day after the Passover, the pikin dem of Israel go out with a high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians,
while the Egyptians were burying all dem firstborn, whom Baba God had struck among dem. Baba God also executed judgments on dem gods.
The pikin dem of Israel traveled from Rameses, and encamped in Succoth.
Dem traveled from Succoth, and encamped in Etham, which is in the edge of the wilderness.
Dem traveled from Etham, and turned back to Pihahiroth, which is before Baal Zephon: and dem encamped before Migdol.
Dem traveled from before Hahiroth, and crossed through the middle of the sea into the wilderness. Dem go three days’ journey in the wilderness of Etham, and encamped in Marah.
Dem traveled from Marah, and come to Elim. In Elim, there were twelve springs of water, and seventy palm trees; and dem encamped there.
Dem traveled from Elim, and encamped by the Red Sea.
Dem traveled from the Red Sea, and encamped in the wilderness of Sin.
Dem traveled from the wilderness of Sin, and encamped in Dophkah.
Dem traveled from Dophkah, and encamped in Alush.
Dem traveled from Alush, and encamped in Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
Dem traveled from Rephidim, and encamped in the wilderness of Sinai.
Dem traveled from the wilderness of Sinai, and encamped in Kibroth Hattaavah.
Dem traveled from Kibroth Hattaavah, and encamped in Hazeroth.
Dem traveled from Hazeroth, and encamped in Rithmah.
Dem traveled from Rithmah, and encamped in Rimmon Perez.
Dem traveled from Rimmon Perez, and encamped in Libnah.
Dem traveled from Libnah, and encamped in Rissah.
Dem traveled from Rissah, and encamped in Kehelathah.
Dem traveled from Kehelathah, and encamped in Mount Shepher.
Dem traveled from Mount Shepher, and encamped in Haradah.
Dem traveled from Haradah, and encamped in Makheloth.
Dem traveled from Makheloth, and encamped in Tahath.
Dem traveled from Tahath, and encamped in Terah.
Dem traveled from Terah, and encamped in Mithkah.
Dem traveled from Mithkah, and encamped in Hashmonah.
Dem traveled from Hashmonah, and encamped in Moseroth.
Dem traveled from Moseroth, and encamped in Bene Jaakan.
Dem traveled from Bene Jaakan, and encamped in Hor Haggidgad.
Dem traveled from Hor Haggidgad, and encamped in Jotbathah.
Dem traveled from Jotbathah, and encamped in Abronah.
Dem traveled from Abronah, and encamped in Ezion Geber.
Dem traveled from Ezion Geber, and encamped at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.
Dem traveled from Kadesh, and encamped in Mount Hor, in the edge of the land of Edom.

Aaron the priest go up into Mount Hor at the commandment of Baba God, and died there, in the fortieth year after the pikin dem of Israel had come out of the land of Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month.
Aaron was one hundred twenty-three years old when he died in Mount Hor.
The Canaanite, the king of Arad, who lived in the South in the land of Canaan, heard of the coming of the pikin dem of Israel.
Dem traveled from Mount Hor, and encamped in Zalmonah.
Dem traveled from Zalmonah, and encamped in Punon.
Dem traveled from Punon, and encamped in Oboth.
Dem traveled from Oboth, and encamped in Iye Abarim, in the border of Moab.
Dem traveled from Iyim, and encamped in Dibon Gad.
Dem traveled from Dibon Gad, and encamped in Almon Diblathaim.
Dem traveled from Almon Diblathaim, and encamped in the mountains of Abarim, before Nebo.
Dem traveled from the mountains of Abarim, and encamped in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
Dem encamped by the Jordan, from Beth Jeshimoth even to Abel Shittim in the plains of Moab.
Baba God spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem, “When you pass over the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
then you shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, destroy all dem stone idols, destroy all dem molten images, and demolish all dem high places.
You shall take possession of the land, and live inside am; for I have given the land to you to possess it.

You shall inherit the land by lot according to una families; to the more you shall give the more inheritance, and to the fewer you shall give the less inheritance. Anywhere wey the lot falls to any man, that go be his. You shall inherit according to the tribes of una fathers.

“But if you No drive out the inhabitants of the land from before you, then those you let remain of dem Go be as pricks in una eyes and as thorns in una sides, and Dem go harass you in the land in which you live.
It shall happen that as I thought to do to dem, so will I do to you.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Command the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem, ‘When you come into the land of Canaan (this is the land that shall fall to you for an inheritance, even the land of Canaan according to its borders),
then una south quarter go be from the wilderness of Zin along by the side of Edom, and una south border go be from the end of the Salt Sea eastward.

Una border shall turn about southward of the ascent of Akrabbim, and pass along to Zin; and it shall pass southward of Kadesh Barnea; and it shall go from there to Hazar Addar, and pass along to Azmon.
The border shall turn about from Azmon to the brook of Egypt, and it shall end at the sea.
“‘For the western border, you go get the great sea and its border. This go be una west border.
“‘This go be una north border: from the great sea you shall mark out for unaself Mount Hor.
From Mount Hor you shall mark out to the entrance of Hamath; and the border shall pass by Zedad.
Then the border shall go to Ziphron, and it shall end at Hazar Enan. This go be una north border.
“‘You shall mark out una east border from Hazar Enan to Shepham.
The border shall go down from Shepham to Riblah, on the east side of Ain. The border shall go down, and shall reach to the side of the sea of Chinnereth eastward.
The border shall go down to the Jordan, and end at the Salt Sea. This go be una land according to its borders around it.’”
Moses commanded the pikin dem of Israel, saying, “This is the land which you shall inherit by lot, which Baba God has commanded to give to the nine tribes, and to the half-tribe;

for the tribe of the pikin dem of Reuben according to dem fathers’ houses, and the tribe of the pikin dem of Gad according to dem fathers’ houses, have received, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received, dem inheritance.
The two tribes and the half-tribe have received dem inheritance beyond the Jordan at Jericho eastward, toward the sunrise.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“These are the names of the men who shall divide the land to you for inheritance: Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun.
You shall take one prince of every tribe, to divide the land for inheritance.
These are the names of the men: Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
Of the tribe of the pikin dem of Simeon, Shemuel the son of Ammihud.
Of the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad the son of Chislon.
Of the tribe of the pikin dem of Dan a prince, Bukki the son of Jogli.
Of the pikin dem of Joseph: of the tribe of the pikin dem of Manasseh a prince, Hanniel the son of Ephod.
Of the tribe of the pikin dem of Ephraim a prince, Kemuel the son of Shiphtan.
Of the tribe of the pikin dem of Zebulun a prince, Elizaphan the son of Parnach.
Of the tribe of the pikin dem of Issachar a prince, Paltiel the son of Azzan.
Of the tribe of the pikin dem of Asher a prince, Ahihud the son of Shelomi.
Of the tribe of the pikin dem of Naphtali a prince, Pedahel the son of Ammihud.”
These are dem whom Baba God commanded to divide the inheritance to the pikin dem of Israel in the land of Canaan.
Baba God spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
“Command the pikin dem of Israel to give to the Levites of the inheritance of dem possession cities to live in. You shall give suburbs for the cities around dem to the Levites.
Dem go get the cities to live in. Dem suburbs go be for dem livestock, and for dem possessions, and for all dem animals.
“The suburbs of the cities, which you shall give to the Levites, go be from the wall of the city and outward one thousand cubits around it.

You shall measure outside of the city for the east side two thousand cubits, and for the south side two thousand cubits, and for the west side two thousand cubits, and for the north side two thousand cubits, the city being in the middle. This go be the suburbs of dem cities.
“The cities which you shall give to the Levites, dem go be the six cities of refuge, which you shall give for the man slayer to flee to. Besides dem you shall give forty-two cities.
All the cities which you shall give to the Levites go be forty-eight cities together with dem suburbs.

Concerning the cities which you shall give of the possession of the pikin dem of Israel, from the many you shall take many; and from the few you shall take few. Everyone according to his inheritance which he inherits shall give some of his cities to the Levites.”
Baba God spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, and tell dem, ‘When you pass over the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
then you shall appoint for unaself cities to be cities of refuge for you, that the man slayer who kills any person unwittingly may flee there.
The cities go be to you for refuge from the avenger, that the man slayer not die, until he stands before the congregation for judgment.
The cities which you shall give go be for you six cities of refuge.
You shall give three cities beyond the Jordan, and you shall give three cities in the land of Canaan. Dem go be cities of refuge.
For the pikin dem of Israel, and for the stranger and for the foreigner living among dem, shall these six cities be for refuge; that Everybody wey kills any person unwittingly may flee there.
“‘But if he struck him with an instrument of iron, so that he died, he is a murderer. The murderer shall surely be put to death.
If he struck him with a stone in the hand, by which a man may die, and he died, he is a murderer. The murderer shall surely be put to death.
Or if he struck him with a weapon of wood in the hand, by which a man may die, and he died, he is a murderer. The murderer shall surely be put to death.
The avenger of blood shall imself put the murderer to death. When he meets him, he shall put him to death.
If he shoved him out of hatred, or hurled at him, lying in wait, so that he died,

or in hostility struck him with his hand, so that he died, person wey struck him shall surely be put to death. He is a murderer. The avenger of blood shall put the murderer to death, when he meets him.
“‘But if he shoved him suddenly without hostility, or hurled on him anything without lying in wait,
or with any stone, by which a man may die, not seeing him, and throw it on him, so that he died, and he No be his enemy, neither sought his harm;
then the congregation shall judge between the striker and the avenger of blood according to these ordinances.

The congregation shall deliver the man slayer out of the hand of the avenger of blood, and the congregation shall restore him to his city of refuge, where he had fled. He shall live inside am until the death of the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil.
“‘But if the man slayer shall at any time go beyond the border of his city of refuge, where he flees,
and the avenger of blood finds him outside of the border of his city of refuge, and the avenger of blood kills the man slayer; he no go be guilty of blood,
because he should have remain in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest. But after the death of the high priest, the man slayer shall return into the land of his possession.
“‘These things go be for a statute and ordinance to you throughout una generations in all una dwellings.
“‘Anybody wey kills any person, the murderer go be slain at the mouth of witnesses; but one witness no go testify against any person that he die.
“‘Moreover you shall take no ransom for the life of a murderer Wey be guilty of death; but he shall surely be put to death.
“‘You shall take no ransom for him Wey be fled to his city of refuge, that he may come again to live in the land, until the death of the priest.
“‘So you no go pollute the land in which You be; for blood pollutes the land. No atonement can be made for the land for the blood that is shed in it, but by the blood of him who shed it.
You no go defile the land which you inhabit, in the middle of which I live; for I, Baba God, live in the middle of the pikin dem of Israel.’”

The heads of the fathers’ households of the family of the pikin dem of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of the sons of Joseph, come near, and spoke before Moses, and before the princes, the heads of the fathers’ households of the pikin dem of Israel.

Dem talk say, “Baba God commanded my lord to give the land for inheritance by lot to the pikin dem of Israel. My lord was commanded by Baba God to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters.

If Dem be married to any of the sons of the other tribes of the pikin dem of Israel, then will dem inheritance be taken away from the inheritance of our fathers, and Go be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which dem shall belong. So will it be taken away from the lot of our inheritance.

When the jubilee of the pikin dem of Israel go be, then will dem inheritance be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which dem shall belong. So dem inheritance Go be taken away from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers.”
Moses commanded the pikin dem of Israel according to Baba God’s word, saying, “The tribe of the sons of Joseph speaks right.

This is the thing which Baba God does command concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, ‘Make dem be married to whom dem think best; only dem shall marry into the family of the tribe of dem father.
So shall no inheritance of the pikin dem of Israel move from tribe to tribe; for the pikin dem of Israel shall all keep the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.

Every daughter who possesses an inheritance in any tribe of the pikin dem of Israel go be wife to one of the family of the tribe of her father, that the pikin dem of Israel may each possess the inheritance of his fathers.
So shall no inheritance move from one tribe to another tribe; for the tribes of the pikin dem of Israel shall each keep his own inheritance.’”
The daughters of Zelophehad did as Baba God commanded Moses:
for Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, were married to dem father’s brothers’ sons.
Dem were married into the families of the sons of Manasseh the son of Joseph. Dem inheritance remain in the tribe of the family of dem father.
These are the commandments and the ordinances which Baba God commanded by Moses to the pikin dem of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
These are the words which Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan in the wilderness, in the Arabah over against Suf, between Paran, Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
It is eleven days’ journey from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir to Kadesh Barnea.
In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Moses spoke to the pikin dem of Israel, according to all that Baba God had given him in commandment to dem;
after he had struck Sihon the king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, at Edrei.
Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to declare this law, saying,
“Baba God our God spoke to us in Horeb, saying, ‘You have lived long enough at this mountain.

Turn, and take una journey, and go to the hill country of the Amorites, and to all the places near there, in the Arabah, in the hill country, and in the lowland, and in the South, and by the seashore, the land of the Canaanites, and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the river Euphrates.
See am, I have set the land before you. Go in and possess the land which Baba God swore to una fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give to dem and to dem offspring after dem.’”
I spoke to you at that time, saying, “I be not able to bear you myself alone.
Baba God una God has multiplied you, and see am, You be today as the stars of the sky for plenty people.
Baba God, the God of una fathers, make you a thousand times as many as You be, and bless you, as he has promised you!
How can I myself alone bear una problems, una burdens, and una strife?
Take wise men of understanding and well known according to una tribes, and I go make dem heads over you.”
You answer me, and talk say, “The thing which you have spoken is good to do.”

So I take the heads of una tribes, wise men, and known, and made dem heads over you, captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds, and captains of fifties, and captains of tens, and officers, according to una tribes.
I commanded una judges at that time, saying, “Hear cases between una brothers, and judge righteously between a man and his brother, and the foreigner Wey be living with him.

You no go show partiality in judgment; you shall hear the small and the great alike. You no go be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God’s. The case that is too hard for you, you shall bring to me, and I go hear it.”
I commanded you at that time all the things which you should do.

We traveled from Horeb, and go through all that great and terrible wilderness which you see, by the way to the hill country of the Amorites, as Baba God our God commanded us; and we come to Kadesh Barnea.
I talk say to you, “You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which Baba God our God gives to us.
See am, Baba God una God has set the land before you. Go up, take possession, as Baba God, the God of una fathers, has spoken to you. No fear, neither be dismayed.”

You come near to me, everyone of you, and talk say, “Make we send men before us, that dem may search the land for us, and bring us word again of the way by which we must go up, and the cities to which we shall come.”
The thing pleased me well. I take twelve men of you, one man for every tribe.
Dem turned and go up into the hill country, and come to the valley of Eshcol, and spied it out.
Dem take some of the fruit of the land in dem hands, and bring it down to us, and bring us word again, and talk say, “It is a good land which Baba God our God gives to us.”
Yet you wouldn’t go up, but rebelled against the commandment of Baba God una God.
You murmured in una tents, and talk say, “Because Baba God hated us, he has bring us out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us.

Where are we going up? Our brothers have made our heart melt, saying, ‘The people are greater and taller than we. The cities are great and fortified up to the sky. Moreover we have seen the sons of the Anakim there!’”
Then I talk say to you, “No dread, neither be afraid of dem.
Baba God una God who goes before you, he will fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Egypt before una eyes,
and in the wilderness, where you have seen how that Baba God una God bore you, as a man does bear his son, in all the way that you go, until you come to this place.”
Yet in this thing you didn’t believe Baba God una God,
who go before you on the way, to seek out a place for you to pitch una tents in, in fire by night, to show you by what way you should go, and in the cloud by day.
Baba God heard the voice of una words, and was angry, and swore, saying,
“Surely not one of these men of this evil generation shall see the good land, which I swore to give to una fathers,
except Caleb the son of Jephunneh. He shall see it. I go give the land that he has trodden on to him, and to his pikin dem, because he has wholly follow Baba God.”
Also Baba God was angry with me for una sakes, saying, “You also no go go in there.
Joshua the son of Nun, who stands before you, shall go in there. Encourage him, for he shall cause Israel to inherit it.

Moreover una little ones, whom you talk say should be captured or killed, and una pikin dem, who today have no knowledge of good or evil, dem shall go in there, and I go give it to dem, and dem shall possess it.
But as for you, turn, and take una journey into the wilderness by the way to the Red Sea.”

Then you answer and talk say to me, “We have sinned against Baba God, We go go up and fight, according to all that Baba God our God commanded us.” Every man of you put on his weapons of war, and presumed to go up into the hill country.
Baba God talk say to me, “Tell dem, ‘No go up, neither fight; for I be not among you; lest you be struck before una enemies.’”
So I spoke to you, and you didn’t listen; but you rebelled against the commandment of Baba God, and were presumptuous, and go up into the hill country.
The Amorites, who lived in that hill country, come out against you, and chased you, as bees do, and beat you down in Seir, even to Hormah.
You come back and wept before Baba God; but Baba God didn’t listen to una voice, nor turn his ear to you.
So you stayed in Kadesh many days, according to the days that you remain.
Then we turned, and take our journey into the wilderness by the way to the Red Sea, as Baba God spoke to me; and we encircled Mount Seir many days.
Baba God spoke to me, saying,
“You have encircled this mountain long enough. Turn northward.
Command the people, saying, ‘You be to pass through the border of una brothers the pikin dem of Esau, who live in Seir; and Dem go be afraid of you. So be careful.
No contend with dem; for I go not give you any of dem land, no, not so much as for the sole of the foot to tread on; because I have given Mount Seir to Esau for a possession.
You shall purchase chop from dem for money, that you may eat. You shall also buy water from dem for money, that you may drink.’”

For Baba God una God has blessed you in all the work of una hand. He has known una walking through this great wilderness. These forty years, Baba God una God Don dey with you. You have lacked nothing.
So we passed by from our brothers the pikin dem of Esau, who live in Seir, from the way of the Arabah from Elath and from Ezion Geber. We turned and passed by the way of the wilderness of Moab.

Baba God talk say to me, “No bother Moab, neither contend with dem in battle; for I go not give you any of his land for a possession; because I have given Ar to the pikin dem of Lot for a possession.”
(The Emim lived inside am before, a people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakim.
These also are considered to be Rephaim, as the Anakim; but the Moabites call dem Emim.

The Horites also lived in Seir before, but the pikin dem of Esau succeeded dem. Dem destroyed dem from before dem, and lived in dem place; as Israel did to the land of his possession, which Baba God give to dem.)
“Now rise up, and cross over the brook Zered.” We go over the brook Zered.

The days in which we come from Kadesh Barnea, until we had come over the brook Zered, were thirty-eight years; until all the generation of the men of war were consumed from the middle of the camp, as Baba God swore to dem.
Moreover Baba God’s hand was against dem, to destroy dem from the middle of the camp, until dem were consumed.
So, when all the men of war were consumed and dead from among the people,
Baba God spoke to me, saying,
“You be to pass over Ar, the border of Moab, today.
