then the man who lay with her shall give to the lady’s father fifty shekels of silver. She go be his wife, because he has humbled her. He may not put her away all his days.
A man no go take his father’s wife, and no go uncover his father’s skirt.
Person Wey emasculated by crushing or cutting no go enter into Baba God’s assembly.
A person born of a forbidden union no go enter into Baba God’s assembly; even to the tenth generation shall Nobody of his enter into Baba God’s assembly.
An Ammonite or a Moabite no go enter into Baba God’s assembly; even to the tenth generation shall Nobody belonging to dem enter into Baba God’s assembly forever;
because dem didn’t meet you with bread and with water on the way, when you come out of Egypt, and because dem hired against you Balaam the son of Beor from Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse you.
Nevertheless Baba God una God wouldn’t listen to Balaam; but Baba God una God turned the curse into a blessing to you, because Baba God una God love you.
You no go seek dem peace nor dem prosperity all una days forever.
You no go abhor an Edomite; for he is una brother. You no go abhor an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land.
The pikin dem of the third generation Wey be born to dem may enter into Baba God’s assembly.
When you go out and camp against una enemies, then you shall keep unaself from every evil thing.
If E get among you any man Wey be not clean by reason of that which happens him by night, then shall he go outside of the camp. He no go come within the camp;
but it go be, when evening comes, he shall bathe imself in water. When the sun is down, he shall come within the camp.
You go get a place also outside of the camp where you go relieve yourself.
You go get a trowel among una weapons. It go be, when you relieve yourself, you shall dig with it, and shall turn back and cover una excrement;

for Baba God una God walks in the middle of una camp, to deliver you, and to give up una enemies before you. So una camp go be holy, that he may not see an unclean thing in you, and turn away from you.
You no go deliver to his master a worker who has escaped from his master to you.
He shall live with you, among you, in the place which he shall choose within one of una gates, where it pleases him best. You no go oppress him.
There go be no prostitute of the daughters of Israel, neither shall there be a sodomite of the sons of Israel.
You no go bring the hire of a prostitute, or the wages of a male prostitute, into the house of Baba God una God for any vow; for both of these are an abomination to Baba God una God.
You no go lend on interest to una brother; interest of money, interest of chop, interest of anything that is lent on interest.
You may lend on interest to a foreigner; but to una brother you no go lend on interest, that Baba God una God may bless you in all that you put una hand to, in the land where you go in to possess it.
When you vow a vow to Baba God una God, you no go be slack to pay it; for Baba God una God will surely require it of you; and it would be sin in you.
But if you refrain from making a vow, it go be no sin in you.
You shall observe and do that which has gone out of una lips. Anything wey you have vowed to Baba God una God as a freewill offering, which you have promised with una mouth, you must do.
When you come into una neighbor’s vineyard, then you may eat of grapes una fill at una own pleasure; but you no go put any in una container.
When you come into una neighbor’s standing grain, then you may pluck the ears with una hand; but you no go move a sickle to una neighbor’s standing grain.

When a man takes a wife and marries her, then it go be, if she finds no favor in his eyes, because he has find some unseemly thing in her, that he shall write her a bill of divorce, and put it in her hand, and send her out of his house.
When she has comot out of his house, she may go and be another man’s wife.
If the latter husband hates her, and write her a bill of divorce, and puts it in her hand, and sends her out of his house; or if the latter husband die, who take her to be his wife;

her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after that she is defiled; for that is abomination before Baba God. You no go cause the land to sin, which Baba God una God gives you for an inheritance.
When a man takes a new wife, he no go go out in the army, neither shall he be assigned any business. He go be free at home one year, and shall cheer his wife whom he has taken.
No man shall take the mill or the upper millstone as a pledge; for he takes a life in pledge.
If a man is find stealing any of his brothers of the pikin dem of Israel, and he deals with him as a slave, or sells him; then that thief shall die. So you shall remove the evil from among you.
Be careful in the plague of leprosy, that you observe diligently, and do according to all that the priests the Levites teach you. As I commanded dem, so you shall observe to do.
Remember what Baba God una God did to Miriam, by the way as you come out of Egypt.
When you lend una neighbor any kind of loan, you no go go into his house to get his pledge.
You shall stand outside, and the man to whom you lend shall bring the pledge outside to you.
If he is a poor man, you no go sleep with his pledge.
You shall surely restore to him the pledge when the sun goes down, that he may sleep in his garment, and bless you. It go be righteousness to you before Baba God una God.
You no go oppress a hired worker Wey be poor and needy, whether he is one of una brothers, or one of the foreigners Wey be in una land within una gates.
In his day you shall give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down on it; for he is poor, and sets his heart on it; lest he cry against you to Baba God, and it be sin to you.
The fathers no go be put to death for the pikin dem, neither shall the pikin dem be put to death for the fathers. Every man go be put to death for his own sin.
You no go deprive the foreigner or the fatherless of justice, nor take a widow’s clothing in pledge;
but you shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and Baba God una God redeemed you there. So I command you to do this thing.

When you reap una harvest in una field, and have forgotten a sheaf in the field, you no go go again to get it. It go be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow; that Baba God una God may bless you in all the work of una hands.
When you beat una olive tree, you no go go over the boughs again. It go be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
When you harvest una vineyard, you no go glean it after unaself. It go be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
You shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt. So I command you to do this thing.
If E get a controversy between men, and dem come to judgment, and the judges judge dem; then dem shall justify the righteous, and condemn the wicked.
It go be, if the wicked man is worthy to be beaten, that the judge shall cause him to lie down, and to be beaten before his face, according to his wickedness, by number.
He may sentence him to no more than forty stripes. He no go give more; lest, if he should give more, and beat him more than that many stripes, then una brother Go be degraded in una sight.
You no go muzzle the ox when he treads out the grain.

If brothers live together, and one of dem dies, and has no son, the wife of the dead no go be married outside to a stranger. Her husband’s brother shall go in to her, and take her as his wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother to her.
It go be that the firstborn whom she bears shall succeed in the name of his brother Wey be dead, that his name not be blotted out of Israel.

If the man no dey want to take his brother’s wife, then his brother’s wife shall go up to the gate to the elders, and say, “My husband’s brother refuses to raise up to his brother a name in Israel. He No go perform the duty of a husband’s brother to me.”
Then the elders of his city shall call him, and speak to him: and if he stands and says, “I no want to take her”;

then his brother’s wife shall come to him in the presence of the elders, and loose his shoe from off his foot, and spit in his face. She shall answer and say, “So shall it be done to the man wey No build up his brother’s house.”
His name go be call in Israel, “The house of him who had his shoe removed.”
When men strive against each other, and the wife of one draws near to deliver her husband out of the hand of him who strikes him, and puts out her hand, and takes him by his private parts,
then you shall cut off her hand. Una eye go get no pity.
You no go have in una bag diverse weights, one heavy and one light.
You no go have in una house diverse measures, one large and one small.
You go get a perfect and just weight. You go get a perfect and just measure, that una days may be long in the land which Baba God una God gives you.
For all who do such things, all who do unrighteously, are an abomination to Baba God una God.
Remember what Amalek did to you by the way as you come out of Egypt;
how he met you by the way, and struck the rearmost of you, all who were feeble behind you, when you were faint and weary; and he didn’t fear God.

So it go be, when Baba God una God has given you rest from all una enemies all around, in the land which Baba God una God gives you for an inheritance to possess it, that you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under the sky. You no go forget.
It go be, when you have come in to the land which Baba God una God gives you for an inheritance, possess it, and live in it,

that you shall take some of the first of all the fruit of the ground, which you shall bring in from una land that Baba God una God gives you. You shall put it in a basket, and shall go to the place which Baba God una God shall choose, to cause his name to live there.
You shall come to the priest who go be in those days, and tell him, “I profess today to Baba God una God, that I have come to the land which Baba God swore to our fathers to give us.”
The priest shall take the basket out of una hand, and set it down before Baba God una God’s altar.
You shall answer and say before Baba God una God, “My father was a Syrian ready to perish. He go down into Egypt, and lived there, few in number. There he became a great, mighty, and populous nation.
The Egyptians mistreated us, afflicted us, and imposed hard labor on us.
Then we cried to Baba God, the God of our fathers. Baba God heard our voice, and see our suffering, our toil, and our oppression.
Baba God bring us out of Egypt with a mighty hand, with an outstretched arm, with great terror, with signs, and with wonders;
and he has bring us into this place, and has given us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Now, see am, I have bring the first of the fruit of the ground, which you, Baba God, have given me.” You shall set it down before Baba God una God, and worship before Baba God una God.
You shall glad well-well in all the good which Baba God una God has given to you, and to una house, you, and the Levite, and the foreigner Wey be among you.

When you have finished tithing all the tithe of una increase in the third year, which is the year of tithing, then you shall give it to the Levite, to the foreigner, to the fatherless, and to the widow, that dem may eat within una gates, and be filled.

You shall say before Baba God una God, “I have put away the holy things out of my house, and also have given dem to the Levite, to the foreigner, to the fatherless, and to the widow, according to all una commandment which you have commanded me. I have not transgressed any of una commandments, neither have I forgotten dem.

I have not eaten of it in my mourning, neither have I removed any of it while I was unclean, nor given of it for the dead. I have listened to Baba God my God’s voice. I have done according to all that you have commanded me.
Look down from una holy habitation, from heaven, and bless una people Israel, and the ground which you have given us, as you swore to our fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.”
Today Baba God una God commands you to do these statutes and ordinances. You shall so keep and do dem with all una heart and with all una soul.
You have declared today that Baba God is una God, and that you would walk in his ways, and keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his ordinances, and listen to his voice.
Baba God has declared today that You be a people for his own possession, as he has promised you, and that you should keep all his commandments.
He will make you high above people for everywhere that he has made, in praise, in name, and in honor; and that you may be a holy people to Baba God una God, as he has spoken.
Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, saying, “Keep all the commandment which I command you today.
It go be on the day when you shall pass over the Jordan to the land which Baba God una God gives you, that you shall set yourself up great stones, and coat dem with plaster.

You shall write on dem all the words of this law, when you have passed over; that you may go in to the land which Baba God una God gives you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as Baba God, the God of una fathers, has promised you.
It go be, when you have crossed over the Jordan, that you shall set up these stones, which I command you today, on Mount Ebal, and you shall coat dem with plaster.
There you shall build an altar to Baba God una God, an altar of stones. You no go use any iron tool on dem.
You shall build Baba God una God’s altar of uncut stones. You shall offer burnt offerings on it to Baba God una God.
You shall sacrifice peace offerings, and shall eat there. You shall glad well-well before Baba God una God.
You shall write on the stones all the words of this law very plainly.”
Moses and the priests the Levites spoke to all Israel, saying, “Be silence, and listen, Israel! Today you have become the people of Baba God una God.
You shall so obey Baba God una God’s voice, and do his commandments and his statutes, which I command you today.”
Moses commanded the people the same day, saying,
“These shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people, when you have crossed over the Jordan: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
These shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
With a loud voice, the Levites shall say to all the men of Israel,
‘Cursed is the man who makes an engraved or molten image, an abomination to Baba God, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and sets it up in secret.’ All the people shall answer and say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is person wey dishonors his father or his mother.’ All the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is person wey removes his neighbor’s landmark.’ All the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is person wey leads the blind astray on the road.’ All the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is person wey withholds justice from the foreigner, fatherless, and widow.’ All the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is person wey lies with his father’s wife, because he dishonors his father’s bed.’ All the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is person wey lies with any kind of animal.’ All the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is person wey lies with his sister, his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter.’ All the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is person wey lies with his mother-in-law.’ All the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is person wey secretly kills his neighbor.’ All the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is person wey takes a bribe to kill an innocent person.’ All the people shall say, ‘Amen.’
‘Cursed is person wey no dey uphold the words of this law by doing dem.’ All the people shall say, ‘Amen.’”

It shall happen, if you shall listen diligently to Baba God una God’s voice, to observe to do all his commandments which I command you today, that Baba God una God will set you high above all the nations of the earth.
All these blessings will come upon you, and overtake you, if you listen to Baba God una God’s voice.
You go be blessed in the city, and you go be blessed in the field.
You go be blessed in the fruit of una body, the fruit of una ground, the fruit of una animals, the increase of una livestock, and the young of una flock.
Una basket and una kneading trough go be blessed.
You go be blessed when you come in, and you go be blessed when you go out.
Baba God will cause una enemies who rise up against you to be struck before you. Dem go come out against you one way, and will flee before you seven ways.
Baba God will command the blessing on you in una barns, and in all that you put una hand to. He will bless you in the land which Baba God una God gives you.
Baba God will establish you for a holy people to imself, as he has sworn to you, if you shall keep the commandments of Baba God una God, and walk in his ways.
All the peoples of the earth shall see that You be call by Baba God’s name, and Dem go be afraid of you.
Baba God will grant you abundant prosperity, in the fruit of una body, in the fruit of una livestock, and in the fruit of una ground, in the land which Baba God swore to una fathers to give you.
Baba God will open to you his good treasure in the sky, to give the rain of una land in its season, and to bless all the work of una hand. You go lend to many nations, and You go not borrow.

Baba God will make you the head, and not the tail. You go be above only, and You go not be beneath; if you listen to the commandments of Baba God una God, which I command you today, to observe and to do,
and no go turn aside from any of the words which I command you today, to the right hand, or to the left, to go after other gods to serve dem.

But it shall come to pass, if You go not listen to Baba God una God’s voice, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command you today, that all these curses will come on you, and overtake you.
You go be cursed in the city, and You go be cursed in the field.
Una basket and una kneading trough Go be cursed.
The fruit of una body, the fruit of una ground, the increase of una livestock, and the young of una flock Go be cursed.
You go be cursed when you come in, and You go be cursed when you go out.

Baba God will send on you cursing, confusion, and rebuke, in all that you put una hand to do, until You be destroyed, and until you perish sharp-sharp; because of the evil of una doings, by which you have forsaken me.
Baba God will make the pestilence cling to you, until he has consumed you from off the land, where you go in to possess it.
Baba God will strike you with consumption, with fever, with inflammation, with fiery heat, with the sword, with blight, and with mildew. Dem go pursue you until you perish.
Una sky that is over una head Go be brass, and the earth that is under You go be iron.
Baba God will make the rain of una land powder and dust. It will come down on you from the sky, until You be destroyed.
Baba God will cause you to be struck before una enemies. You go go out one way against dem, and will flee seven ways before dem. You go be tossed back and forth among all the kingdoms of the earth.
Una dead body Go be chop to all birds of the sky, and to the animals of the earth; and there Go be Nobody to frighten dem away.
Baba God will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with the tumors, with the scurvy, and with the itch, of which you can not be healed.
Baba God will strike you with madness, with blindness, and with astonishment of heart.
You go grope at noonday, as the blind gropes in darkness, and you no go prosper in una ways. You go only be oppressed and robbed always, and there Go be Nobody to save you.
You go betroth a wife, and another man shall lie with her. You go build a house, and you no go live in it. You go plant a vineyard, and not use its fruit.

Una ox Go be slain before una eyes, and You go not eat any of it. Una donkey Go be violently taken away from before una face, and No go be restored to you. Una sheep Go be given to una enemies, and You go have Nobody to save you.
Una sons and una daughters Go be given to another people. Una eyes will look, and fail with longing for dem all day long. There Go be no power in una hand.
A nation which you no know eat the fruit of una ground and all of una work. You go only be oppressed and crushed always;
so that the sights that you see with una eyes will drive you mad.
Baba God will strike you in the knees and in the legs with a sore boil, of which you can not be healed, from the sole of una foot to the crown of una head.
Baba God will bring you, and una king whom You go set over unaself, to a nation that you have not known, you nor una fathers. There You go serve other gods of wood and stone.
You go become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword among all the peoples where Baba God will lead you away.
You go carry much seed out into the field, and will gather little in; for the locust will consume it.
You go plant vineyards and dress dem, but You go neither drink of the wine, nor harvest, because worms will eat dem.
You go have olive trees throughout all una borders, but you no go anoint yourself with the oil; for una olives will drop off.
You go father sons and daughters, but Dem go not be yours; for Dem go go into captivity.
Locusts will consume all of una trees and the fruit of una ground.
The foreigner Wey be among You go mount up above you higher and higher, and You go come down lower and lower.
He will lend to you, and you no go lend to him. He Go be the head, and You go be the tail.

All these curses will come on you, and will pursue you, and overtake you, until You be destroyed; because you didn’t listen to Baba God una God’s voice, to keep his commandments and his statutes which he commanded you.
Dem go be for a sign and for a wonder to you and to una offspring forever.
Because you didn’t serve Baba God una God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, by reason of the abundance of all things;
so You go serve una enemies whom Baba God sends against you, in hunger, in thirst, in nakedness, and in lack of all things. He will put an iron yoke on una neck, until he has destroyed you.
Baba God will bring a nation against you from far, from the end of the earth, as the eagle flies; a nation whose language You go not understand;
a nation of fierce facial expressions, that no dey respect the elderly, nor show favor to the young,

and Dem go eat the fruit of una livestock, and the fruit of una ground, until You be destroyed. Dem also no go leave you grain, new wine, or oil, the increase of una livestock, or the young of una flock, until dem have caused you to perish.

Dem go besiege you in all una gates, until una high and fortified walls come down, in which you trusted, throughout all una land. Dem go besiege you in all una gates throughout all una land, which Baba God una God has given you.
You go eat the fruit of una own body, the flesh of una sons and of una daughters, whom Baba God una God has given you, in the siege and in the distress with which una enemies will distress you.
The man Wey be tender among you, and very delicate, his eye Go be evil toward his brother, toward the wife whom he loves, and toward the remnant of his pikin dem whom he has remaining;

so that he No go give to any of dem of the flesh of his pikin dem whom he will eat, because he has nothing left to him, in the siege and in the distress with which una enemy will distress you in all una gates.

The tender and delicate woman among you, who would not venture to set the sole of her foot on the ground for delicateness and tenderness, her eye Go be evil toward the husband that she loves, toward her son, toward her daughter,

toward her young one who comes out from between her feet, and toward her pikin dem whom she bears; for she will eat dem secretly for lack of all things, in the siege and in the distress with which una enemy will distress you in una gates.
If You go not observe to do all the words of this law that are written in this book, that you may fear this glorious and fearful name, Baba God Una GOD;
then Baba God will make una plagues fearful, and the plagues of una offspring, even great plagues, and of long duration, and severe sicknesses, and of long duration.
He will bring on you again all the diseases of Egypt, which you were afraid of; and Dem go cling to you.
Also every sickness and every plague, which No be written in the book of this law, Baba God will bring dem on you, until You be destroyed.
You go be left few in number, even though you were as the stars of the sky for plenty people; because you didn’t listen to Baba God una God’s voice.

It will happen that as Baba God rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you, so Baba God will glad well-well over you to cause you to perish, and to destroy you. You go be plucked from off of the land where you go in to possess it.

Baba God will scatter you among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth. There You go serve other gods, which you have not known, you nor una fathers, even wood and stone.
Among these nations You go find no ease, and there Go be no rest for the sole of una foot; but Baba God will give you there a trembling heart, failing of eyes, and pining of soul.
Una life will hang in doubt before you. You go be afraid night and day, and Go get no assurance of una life.
In the morning You go say, “I wish it were evening!” and at evening You go say, “I wish it were morning!” for the fear of una heart which You go fear, and for the sights which una eyes will see.

Baba God will bring you into Egypt again with ships, by the way of which I told to you that you would never see it again. There You go sell unaself to una enemies for male and female slaves, and nobody will buy you.
These are the words of the covenant which Baba God commanded Moses to make with the pikin dem of Israel in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant which he made with dem in Horeb.
Moses call to all Israel, and talk say to dem: Una eyes have seen all that Baba God did in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, and to all his workers, and to all his land;
the great trials which una eyes see, the signs, and those great wonders.
But Baba God has not given you a heart to know, eyes to see, and ears to hear, to this day.
I have led you forty years in the wilderness. Una clothes have not grown old on you, and una shoes have not grown old on una feet.
You have not eaten bread, neither have you drunk wine or strong drink; that you may know that I be Baba God una God.
When you come to this place, Sihon the king of Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, come out against us to battle, and we struck dem.
We take dem land, and give it for an inheritance to the Reubenites, and to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of the Manassites.
So keep the words of this covenant and do dem, that you may prosper in all that you do.
All of you stand today in the presence of Baba God una God; una heads, una tribes, una elders, and una officers, even all the men of Israel,
una little ones, una wives, and the foreigners Wey be in the middle of una camps, from the one who cuts una wood to the one who draws una water;
that you may enter into the covenant of Baba God una God, and into his oath, which Baba God una God makes with you today;
that he may establish you today as his people, and that he may be una God, as he spoke to you, and as he swore to una fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
Neither do I make this covenant and this oath with you only,
but with people wey stand here with us today before Baba God our God, and also with people Wey not here with us today
(for you know how we lived in the land of Egypt, and how we come through the middle of the nations through which you passed;
and you have seen dem abominations, and dem idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which were among dem);

lest there should be among you man, woman, family, or tribe whose heart turns away today from Baba God our God, to go to serve the gods of those nations; lest there should be among you a root that produces bitter poison;
and it happen, when he hears the words of this curse, that he bless imself in his heart, saying, “I go get peace, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart, to destroy the moist with the dry.”

Baba God No go pardon him, but then Baba God’s anger and his jealousy will smoke against that man, and all the curse that is written in this book will fall on him, and Baba God will blot out his name from under the sky.
Baba God will set him apart for evil out of all the tribes of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant that is written in this book of the law.

The generation to come, una pikin dem who will rise up after you, and the foreigner who will come from a far land, will say, when dem see the plagues of that land, and the sicknesses with which Baba God has made it sick;

and that all of its land is sulfur, salt, and burning, that it No be sown, no dey produce, nor does any grass grow in it, like the overthrow of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, which Baba God overthrew in his anger, and in his serious anger;
even all the nations will say, “Why has Baba God done thus to this land? What does the heat of this great anger mean?”
Then men will say, “Because dem abandoned the covenant of Baba God, the God of dem fathers, which he made with dem when he bring dem out of the land of Egypt,
and go and served other gods, and worshiped dem, gods that dem didn’t know, and that he had not given to dem.
So Baba God’s anger burned against this land, to bring on it all the curses that are written in this book.
Baba God rooted dem out of dem land in anger, in serious anger, and in great indignation, and thrust dem into another land, as it is today.”
The secret things belong to Baba God our God; but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our pikin dem forever, that we may do all the words of this law.

It shall happen, when all these things have come on you, the blessing and the curse, which I have set before you, and you shall call dem to mind among all the nations, where Baba God una God has driven you,
and return to Baba God una God, and obey his voice according to all that I command you today, you and una pikin dem, with all una heart, and with all una soul;
that then Baba God una God will release you from captivity, have compassion on you, and will return and gather you from all the peoples where Baba God una God has scattered you.
If una outcasts are in the uttermost parts of the heavens, from there Baba God una God will gather you, and from there he will bring you back.
Baba God una God will bring you into the land which una fathers possessed, and You go possess it. He will do you good, and increase una numbers more than una fathers.
Baba God una God will circumcise una heart, and the heart of una offspring, to love Baba God una God with all una heart, and with all una soul, that you may live.
Baba God una God will put all these curses on una enemies, and on people wey hate you, who persecuted you.
You shall return and obey Baba God’s voice, and do all his commandments which I command you today.

Baba God una God will make you plenteous in all the work of una hand, in the fruit of una body, in the fruit of una livestock, and in the fruit of una ground, for good; for Baba God will again glad well-well over you for good, as he rejoiced over una fathers;

if You go obey Baba God una God’s voice, to keep his commandments and his statutes which are written in this book of the law; if you turn to Baba God una God with all una heart, and with all una soul.
For this commandment which I command you today No be too hard for you or too distant.
It No be in heaven, that you should say, “Who will go up for us to heaven, and bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that we may do it?”
Neither is it beyond the sea, that you should say, “Who will go over the sea for us, and bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that we may do it?”
But the word is very near to you, in una mouth and in una heart, that you may do it.
See am, I have set before you today life and prosperity, and death and evil.

For I command you today to love Baba God una God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his ordinances, that you may live and multiply, and that Baba God una God may bless you in the land where you go in to possess it.
But if una heart turns away, and You go not hear, but are drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve dem;
I denounce to you today, that You go surely perish. You go not prolong una days in the land where you pass over the Jordan to go in to possess it.
I call heaven and earth to witness against you today, that I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. So choose life, that you may live, you and una descendants;

to love Baba God una God, to obey his voice, and to cling to him; for he is una life, and the length of una days; that you may live in the land which Baba God swore to una fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give dem.
Moses go and spoke these words to all Israel.
E tell dem say, “I be one hundred twenty years old today. I can no more go out and come in. Baba God has talk say to me, ‘You no go go over this Jordan.’
Baba God una God imself will go over before you. He will destroy these nations from before you, and you shall dispossess dem. Joshua will go over before you, as Baba God has spoken.
Baba God will do to dem as he did to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to dem land; whom he destroyed.
Baba God will deliver dem up before you, and you shall do to dem according to all the commandment which I have commanded you.
Be strong and courageous. No fear or scared of dem; for Baba God una God imself is who goes with you. He No go fail you nor forsake you.”

Moses call to Joshua, and talk say to him in the sight of all Israel, “Be strong and courageous, for you shall go with this people into the land which Baba God has sworn to dem fathers to give dem; and you shall cause dem to inherit it.
Baba God imself is who goes before you. He Go be with you. He No go fail you nor forsake you. No fear. No be discouraged.”
Moses wrote this law, and delivered it to the priests the sons of Levi, who bore the ark of Baba God’s covenant, and to all the elders of Israel.
Moses commanded dem, saying, “At the end of every seven years, in the set time of the year of release, in the feast of tents,
when all Israel has come to appear before Baba God una God in the place which he will choose, you shall read this law before all Israel in dem hearing.

Assemble the people, the men and the women and the little ones, and the foreigners Wey be within una gates, that dem may hear, and that dem may learn, and fear Baba God una God, and observe to do all the words of this law;
and that dem pikin dem, who have not known, may hear, and learn to fear Baba God una God, as long as you live in the land where you go over the Jordan to possess it.”

Baba God talk say to Moses, “See am, una days approach that you must die. Call Joshua, and present unaself in the Tent of Meeting, that I may commission him.” Moses and Joshua go, and presented themselves in the Tent of Meeting.
Baba God appeared in the Tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood over the Tent’s door.

Baba God talk say to Moses, “See am, you shall sleep with una fathers. This people will rise up, and play the prostitute after the strange gods of the land, where dem go to be among dem, and will forsake me, and break my covenant which I have made with dem.

Then my anger go be kindled against dem in that day, and I go forsake dem, and I go hide my face from dem, and dem go be devoured, and many evils and troubles shall come on dem; so that Dem go say in that day, ‘Haven’t these evils come on us because our God No be among us?’
I go surely hide my face in that day for all the evil which dem have done, in that dem have turned to other gods.
“Now so write this song for unaself, and teach it to the pikin dem of Israel. Put it in dem mouths, that this song may be a witness for me against the pikin dem of Israel.

For when I have bring dem into the land which I swore to dem fathers, flowing with milk and honey, and dem have eaten and filled themselves, and grown fat; then Dem go turn to other gods, and serve dem, and despise me, and break my covenant.

It will happen, when many evils and troubles have come on dem, that this song will testify before dem as a witness; for it No go be forgotten out of the mouths of dem descendants; for I know dem ways and Wetin dem are doing today, before I have bring dem into the land which I swore.”
So Moses wrote this song the same day, and taught it the pikin dem of Israel.
He commissioned Joshua the son of Nun, and talk say, “Be strong and courageous; for you shall bring the pikin dem of Israel into the land which I swore to dem. I go be with you.”
When Moses had finished writing the words of this law in a book, until dem were finished,
Moses commanded the Levites, who bore the ark of Baba God’s covenant, saying,
“Take this book of the law, and put it by the side of the ark of Baba God’s covenant una God, that it may be there for a witness against you.
For I know una rebellion, and una stiff neck. See am, while I be yet alive with you today, you Don dey rebellious against Baba God. How much more after my death?
Assemble to me all the elders of una tribes, and una officers, that I may speak these words in dem ears, and call heaven and earth to witness against dem.

For I know that after my death You go utterly corrupt unaself, and turn aside from the way which I have commanded you; and evil will happen to you in the latter days; because You go do that which is evil in Baba God’s sight, to provoke him to anger through the work of una hands.”
Moses spoke in the ears of all the assembly of Israel the words of this song, until dem were finished.
Give ear, you heavens, and I go speak. Let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
My doctrine will drop as the rain. My speech will condense as the dew, as the misty rain on the tender grass, as the showers on the herb.
For I go proclaim Baba God’s name. Ascribe greatness to our God!
The Rock, his work is perfect, for all his ways are just. A God of faithfulness wey do no wrong, just and right is he.
Dem have dealt corruptly with him. Dem No be his pikin dem, because of dem defect. Dem be a perverse and crooked generation.
Is this the way you repay Baba God, foolish and unwise people? No be he una father who has bought you? He has made you and established you.
Remember the days of old. Consider the years of many generations. Ask una father, and he will show you; una elders, and Dem go tell you.
When the Most High give to the nations dem inheritance, when he separated the pikin dem of men, he set the bounds of the peoples according to the number of the pikin dem of Israel.
For Baba God’s portion is his people. Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.
He find him in a desert land, in the waste howling wilderness. He surrounded him. He cared for him. He kept him as the apple of his eye.
As an eagle that stirs up her nest, that flutters over her young, he spread abroad his wings, he take dem, he bore dem on his feathers.
Baba God alone led him. There was no foreign god with him.
He made him ride on the high places of the earth. He ate the increase of the field. He caused him to suck honey out of the rock, oil out of the flinty rock;
butter from the herd, and milk from the flock, with fat of lambs, rams of the breed of Bashan, and goats, with the finest of the wheat. From the blood of the grape, you drank wine.
But Jeshurun grew fat, and kicked. You have grown fat. You have grown thick. You have become sleek. Then he abandoned God who made him, and rejected the Rock of his salvation.
Dem moved him to jealousy with strange gods. Dem provoked him to anger with abominations.
Dem sacrificed to demons, not God, to gods that dem didn’t know, to new gods that come up recently, which una fathers didn’t dread.
Of the Rock who became una father, You be unmindful, and have forgotten God who give you birth.
Baba God see and abhorred, because of the provocation of his sons and his daughters.
He talk say, “I go hide my face from dem. I go see what dem end Go be; for Dem be a very perverse generation, pikin dem in whom is no faithfulness.

Dem have moved me to jealousy with that which No be God. Dem have provoked me to anger with dem vanities. I go move dem to jealousy with people Wey not a people. I go provoke dem to anger with a foolish nation.
For a fire is kindled in my anger, that burns to the lowest Sheol, devours the earth with its increase, and sets the foundations of the mountains on fire.
“I go heap evils on dem. I go spend my arrows on dem.
Dem go be wasted with hunger, and devoured with burning heat and bitter destruction. I go send the teeth of animals on dem, with the venom of vipers that glide in the dust.
Outside the sword will bereave, and in the rooms, terror; on both young man and virgin, the nursing infant with the gray-haired man.
I talk say that I would scatter dem far away. I would make dem memory to cease from among men;
were it not that I feared the provocation of the enemy, lest dem adversaries should judge wrongly, lest dem should say, ‘Our hand is exalted, Baba God has not done all this.’”
For Dem be a nation void of counsel. E get no understanding in dem.
Oh that dem were wise, that dem understand this, that dem would consider dem latter end!
How could one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, unless dem Rock had sold dem, and Baba God had delivered dem up?
For dem rock is No be like our Rock, even our enemies themselves concede.
For dem vine is of the vine of Sodom, of the fields of Gomorrah. Dem grapes are poison grapes. Dem clusters are bitter.
Dem wine is the poison of serpents, the cruel venom of asps.
“No be this laid up in store with me, sealed up among my treasures?
Vengeance is mine, and recompense, at the time when dem foot slides; for the day of dem calamity is at hand. Dem doom rushes at dem.”
For Baba God will judge his people, and have compassion on his workers, when he sees that dem power is gone; that E get Nobody remaining, shut up or left at large.
He will say, “Where are dem gods, the rock in which dem take refuge;
which ate the fat of dem sacrifices, and drank the wine of dem drink offering? Make dem rise up and help you! Make dem be una protection.
“See now that I myself am he. E get no god with me. I kill and I make alive. I wound and I heal. E get Nobody who can deliver out of my hand.
For I lift up my hand to heaven and declare, as I live forever,
if I sharpen my glittering sword, my hand grasps it in judgment; I go take vengeance on my adversaries, and will repay people wey hate me.
I go make my arrows drunk with blood. My sword shall devour flesh with the blood of the slain and the captives, from the head of the leaders of the enemy.”
Glad well-well, you nations, with his people, for he will avenge the blood of his workers. He will take vengeance on his adversaries, and will make atonement for his land and for his people.
Moses come and spoke all the words of this song in the ears of the people, he and Joshua the son of Nun.
Moses finished reciting all these words to all Israel.
E tell dem say, “Set una heart to all the words which I testify to you today, which you shall command una pikin dem to observe to do, all the words of this law.
For it is no vain thing for you; because it is una life, and through this thing you shall prolong una days in the land, where you go over the Jordan to possess it.”
Baba God spoke to Moses that same day, saying,
“Go up into this mountain of Abarim, to Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, that is across from Jericho; and see the land of Canaan, which I give to the pikin dem of Israel for a possession.
Die on the mountain where you go up, and be gathered to una people, as Aaron una brother died on Mount Hor, and was gathered to his people;
because you trespassed against me among the pikin dem of Israel at the waters of Meribah of Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin; because you didn’t uphold my holiness among the pikin dem of Israel.
For you shall see the land from a distance; but you no go go there into the land which I give the pikin dem of Israel.”
This is the blessing with which Moses the man of God blessed the pikin dem of Israel before his death.
He talk say, “Baba God come from Sinai, and rose from Seir to dem. He shone from Mount Paran. He come from the ten thousands of holy ones. At his right hand was a fiery law for dem.
Yes, he loves the people. All his saints are in una hand. Dem sat down at una feet. Each receives una words.
Moses commanded us a law, an inheritance for the assembly of Jacob.
He was king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people were gathered, all the tribes of Israel together.
“Let Reuben live, and not die; Nor let his men be few.”
This is for Judah. He talk say, “Hear, Baba God, the voice of Judah. Bring him in to his people. With his hands he contended for imself. You go be a help against his adversaries.”
About Levi he talk say, “Una Thummim and una Urim are with una godly one, whom you proved at Massah, with whom you contended at the waters of Meribah.
He talk say of his father, and of his mother, ‘I have not seen him.’ He didn’t acknowledge his brothers, nor did he know his own pikin dem; for dem have observed una word, and keep una covenant.
Dem shall teach Jacob una ordinances, and Israel una law. Dem shall put incense before you, and whole burnt offering on una altar.
Baba God, bless his skills. Accept the work of his hands. Strike through the hips of people wey rise up against him, of people wey hate him, that dem not rise again.”
About Benjamin he talk say, “The beloved of Baba God will live in safety by him. He covers him all day long. He dwells between his shoulders.”
About Joseph he talk say, “His land is blessed by Baba God, for the precious things of the heavens, for the dew, for the deep that couches beneath,
for the precious things of the fruits of the sun, for the precious things that the moon can yield,
for the best things of the ancient mountains, for the precious things of the everlasting hills,

for the precious things of the earth and its fullness, the good will of him who lived in the bush. Let this come on the head of Joseph, on the crown of the head of him who was separated from his brothers.

The firstborn of his herd, majesty is his. His horns are the horns of the wild ox. With dem he will push all the peoples, to every corner of the world. Dem be the ten thousands of Ephraim. Dem be the thousands of Manasseh.”
About Zebulun he talk say, “Glad well-well, Zebulun, in una going out; and Issachar, in una tents.
Dem go call the peoples to the mountain. There Dem go offer sacrifices of righteousness, for Dem go draw out the abundance of the seas, the hidden treasures of the sand.”
About Gad he talk say, “Person wey enlarges Gad is blessed. He dwells as a lioness, and tears the arm, yes, the crown of the head.

He provided the first part for imself, for the lawgiver’s portion reserved was reserved for him. He come with the heads of the people. He executed the righteousness of Baba God, His ordinances with Israel.”
About Dan he talk say, “Dan is a lion’s cub that leaps out of Bashan.”
About Naphtali he talk say, “Naphtali, satisfied with favor, full of Baba God’s blessing, Possess the west and the south.”
About Asher he talk say, “Asher is blessed with pikin dem. Make e be acceptable to his brothers. Make e dip his foot in oil.
Una bars Go be iron and brass. As una days, so una strength Go be.
“E get Nobody like God, Jeshurun, who rides on the heavens for una help, in his excellency on the skies.
The eternal God is una dwelling place. Underneath are the everlasting arms. He thrust out the enemy from before you, and talk say, ‘Destroy!’
Israel dwells in safety; the fountain of Jacob alone, In a land of grain and new wine. Yes, his heavens drop down dew.
You be happy, Israel! Wey be like you, a people saved by Baba God, the shield of una help, the sword of una excellency? Una enemies will submit themselves to you. You go tread on dem high places.”
Moses go up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is over against Jericho. Baba God showed him all the land of Gilead, to Dan,
and all Naphtali, and the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah, to the western sea,
and the south, and the Plain of the valley of Jericho the city of palm trees, to Zoar.

Baba God talk say to him, “This is the land which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, ‘I go give it to una offspring. ’ I have caused you to see it with una eyes, but you no go go over there.”
So Moses the worker of Baba God died there in the land of Moab, according to Baba God’s word.
He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab opposite Beth Peor, but no man knows where his tomb is to this day.
Moses was one hundred twenty years old when he died. His eye No be dim, nor his strength gone.
The pikin dem of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days, until the days of weeping in the mourning for Moses were ended.
Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands on him. The pikin dem of Israel listened to him, and did as Baba God commanded Moses.
Since then, there has not arisen a prophet in Israel like Moses, whom Baba God know face to face,
in all the signs and the wonders, which Baba God sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh, and to all his workers, and to all his land,
and in all the mighty hand, and in all the awesome deeds, which Moses did in the sight of all Israel.
Now after the death of Moses the worker of Baba God, Baba God spoke to Joshua the son of Nun, Moses’ worker, saying,
“Moses my worker is dead. Now so arise, go across this Jordan, you, and all these people, to the land which I be giving to dem, even to the pikin dem of Israel.
I have given you every place that the sole of una foot will tread on, as I told Moses.
From the wilderness, and this Lebanon, even to the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and to the great sea toward the going down of the sun, go be una border.
No man Go be able to stand before you all the days of una life. As I was with Moses, so I go be with you. I go not fail you nor forsake you.
“Be strong and courageous; for you shall cause this people to inherit the land which I swore to dem fathers to give dem.

Only be strong and very courageous. Be careful to observe to do according to all the law, which Moses my worker commanded you. No turn from it to the right hand or to the left, that you may have good success Anywhere wey you go.

This book of the law no go depart from una mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make una way prosperous, and then you go get good success.
Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. No fear. No be dismayed, for Baba God una God is with you Anywhere wey you go.”
Then Joshua commanded the officers of the people, saying,

“Pass through the middle of the camp, and command the people, saying, ‘Prepare chop; for within three days You be to pass over this Jordan, to go in to possess the land, which Baba God una God gives you to possess it.’”
Joshua spoke to the Reubenites, and to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, saying,
“Remember the word which Moses the worker of Baba God commanded you, saying, ‘Baba God una God gives you rest, and will give you this land.

Una wives, una little ones, and una livestock, shall live in the land which Moses give you beyond the Jordan; but you shall pass over before una brothers armed, all the mighty men of valor, and shall help dem

until Baba God has given una brothers rest, as he has given you, and dem have also possessed the land which Baba God una God gives dem. Then you shall return to the land of una possession, and possess it, which Moses the worker of Baba God give you beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise.’”
Dem answer Joshua, saying, “All that you have commanded us We go do, and Anywhere wey you send us We go go.
Just as we listened to Moses in all things, so will we listen to you. Only may Baba God una God be with you, as he was with Moses.
Anybody wey rebels against una commandment, and no dey listen to una words in all that you command him shall imself be put to death. Only be strong and courageous.”

Joshua the son of Nun secretly sent two men out of Shittim as spies, saying, “Go, view the land, including Jericho.” Dem go and come into the house of a prostitute whose name was Rahab, and slept there.
The king of Jericho was told, “See am, men of the pikin dem of Israel come in here tonight to spy out the land.”
Jericho’s king sent to Rahab, saying, “Bring out the men who have come to you, who have entered into una house; for dem have come to spy out all the land.”
The woman take the two men and hid dem. Then she talk say, “Yes, the men come to me, but I didn’t know where dem come from.
About the time of the shutting of the gate, when it was dark, the men go out. Where the men go, I no know. Pursue dem sharp-sharp. You may catch up with dem.”
But she had bring dem up to the roof, and hidden dem under the stalks of flax which she had laid in order on the roof.
The men pursued dem along the way to the fords of the Jordan River. As soon as people wey pursued dem had gone out, dem shut the gate.
Before dem had lain down, she come up to dem on the roof.
She talk say to the men, “I know that Baba God has given you the land, and that the fear of you has fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land melt away before you.

For we have heard how Baba God dried up the water of the Red Sea before you, when you come out of Egypt; and Wetin you did to the two kings of the Amorites, who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon and to Og, whom you utterly destroyed.
As soon as we had heard it, our hearts melted, and there no be any more spirit in any man, because of you: for Baba God una God, he is God in heaven above, and on earth beneath.
Now so, please swear to me by Baba God, since I have dealt kindly with you, that you also will deal kindly with my father’s house, and give me a true sign;
and that You go save alive my father, my mother, my brothers, and my sisters, and all that dem have, and will deliver our lives from death.”
The men talk say to her, “Our life for yours, if you no talk about this business of ours; and it go be, when Baba God gives us the land, that We go deal kindly and truly with you.”
Then she Make dem down by a cord through the window; for her house was on the side of the wall, and she lived on the wall.
She tell dem say, “Go to the mountain, lest the pursuers find you. Hide unaself there three days, until the pursuers have come back. Afterward, you may go una way.”
The men talk say to her, “We go be guiltless of this una oath which you’ve made us to swear.

See am, when we come into the land, tie this line of scarlet thread in the window which you used to Make we down. Gather to yourself into the house una father, una mother, una brothers, and all una father’s household.

It go be that Anybody wey goes out of the doors of una house into the street, his blood Go be on his head, and We go be guiltless. Anybody wey is with you in the house, his blood go be on our head, if any hand is on him.
But if you talk about this business of ours, then we go be guiltless of una oath which you’ve made us to swear.”
She talk say, “Let it be as you have talk say.” She sent dem away, and dem comot. Then she tied the scarlet line in the window.
Dem go, and come to the mountain, and stayed there three days, until the pursuers had come back. The pursuers sought dem all along the way, but didn’t find dem.
Then the two men come back, descended from the mountain, crossed the river, and come to Joshua the son of Nun. Dem told him all that had happened to dem.
Dem talk say to Joshua, “Truly Baba God has delivered all the land into our hands. Moreover, all the inhabitants of the land melt away before us.”
Joshua got up early in the morning; and dem moved from Shittim, and come to the Jordan, he and all the pikin dem of Israel. Dem camped there before dem crossed over.
After three days, the officers go through the middle of the camp;
and dem commanded the people, saying, “When you see the ark of Baba God una God’s covenant, and the priests the Levites bearing it, then leave una place, and follow it.
Yet there go be a space between you and it of about two thousand cubits by measure — no come closer to it — that you may know the way by which you must go; for you have not passed this way before.”
Joshua talk say to the people, “Sanctify unaself; for tomorrow Baba God will do wonders among you.”
Joshua spoke to the priests, saying, “Take up the ark of the covenant, and cross over before the people.” Dem take up the ark of the covenant, and go before the people.
Baba God talk say to Joshua, “Today I go begin to magnify you in the sight of all Israel, that dem may know that as I was with Moses, so I go be with you.
You shall command the priests who bear the ark of the covenant, saying, ‘When you come to the brink of the waters of the Jordan, you shall stand still in the Jordan.’”
Joshua talk say to the pikin dem of Israel, “Come here, and hear the words of Baba God una God.”

Joshua talk say, “By this you shall know that the living God is among you, and that he will without fail drive the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Hivite, and the Perizzite, and the Girgashite, and the Amorite, and the Jebusite out from before you.
See am, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth passes over before you into the Jordan.
Now so take twelve men out of the tribes of Israel, for every tribe a man.

It go be that when the soles of the feet of the priests who bear the ark of Baba God, the Lord of all the earth, rest in the waters of the Jordan, that the waters of the Jordan Go be cut off. The waters that come down from above shall stand in one heap.”
When the people moved from dem tents to pass over the Jordan, the priests who bore the ark of the covenant being before the people,

and when people wey bore the ark had come to the Jordan, and the feet of the priests who bore the ark had dipped in the edge of the water (for the Jordan overflows all its banks all the time of harvest),

the waters which come down from above stood, and rose up in one heap, a great way off, at Adam, the city that is beside Zarethan; and those that go down toward the sea of the Arabah, even the Salt Sea, were wholly cut off. Then the people passed over near Jericho.

The priests who bore the ark of Baba God’s covenant stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan; and all Israel crossed over on dry ground, until all the nation had passed completely over the Jordan.
When all the nation had completely crossed over the Jordan, Baba God spoke to Joshua, saying,
“Take twelve men out of the people, a man out of every tribe,

and command dem, saying, ‘Take from out of the middle of the Jordan, out of the place where the priests’ feet stood firm, twelve stones, and carry dem over with you, and lay dem down in the place where you’ll camp tonight.’”
Then Joshua call the twelve men, whom he had prepared of the pikin dem of Israel, a man out of every tribe.

Joshua talk say to dem, “Cross before the ark of Baba God una God into the middle of the Jordan, and each of you pick up a stone and put it on una shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the pikin dem of Israel;
that this may be a sign among you, that when una pikin dem ask in the future, saying, ‘What do you mean by these stones?’

then you shall tell dem, ‘Because the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of Baba God’s covenant. When it crossed over the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. These stones go be for a memorial to the pikin dem of Israel forever.’”

The pikin dem of Israel did as Joshua commanded, and take up twelve stones out of the middle of the Jordan, as Baba God spoke to Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the pikin dem of Israel. Dem carried dem over with dem to the place where dem camped, and laid dem down there.
Joshua set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests who bore the ark of the covenant stood; and Dem be there to this day.

For the priests who bore the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan, until everything was finished that Baba God commanded Joshua to speak to the people, according to all that Moses commanded Joshua; and the people hurried and passed over.
When all the people had completely crossed over, Baba God’s ark crossed over, with the priests, in the presence of the people.
The pikin dem of Reuben, and the pikin dem of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, crossed over armed before the pikin dem of Israel, as Moses spoke to dem.
About forty thousand men, ready and armed for war passed over before Baba God to battle, to the plains of Jericho.
On that day, Baba God magnified Joshua in the sight of all Israel; and dem feared him, as dem feared Moses, all the days of his life.
Baba God spoke to Joshua, saying,
“Command the priests who bear the ark of the testimony, that dem come up out of the Jordan.”
Joshua so commanded the priests, saying, “Come up out of the Jordan!”

When the priests who bore the ark of Baba God’s covenant had come up out of the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of the priests’ feet Bin dey lifted up to the dry ground, the waters of the Jordan come back to dem place, and go over all its banks, as before.
The people come up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and encamped in Gilgal, on the east border of Jericho.
Joshua set up those twelve stones, which dem take out of the Jordan, in Gilgal.
He spoke to the pikin dem of Israel, saying, “When una pikin dem ask dem fathers in time to come, saying, ‘What do these stones mean?’
Then you shall let una pikin dem know, saying, ‘Israel come over this Jordan on dry land.

For Baba God una God dried up the waters of the Jordan from before you, until you had crossed over, as Baba God una God did to the Red Sea, which he dried up from before us, until we had crossed over;
that all the peoples of the earth may know that Baba God’s hand is mighty; that you may fear Baba God una God forever.’”

When all the kings of the Amorites, who were beyond the Jordan westward, and all the kings of the Canaanites, who were by the sea, heard how Baba God had dried up the waters of the Jordan from before the pikin dem of Israel, until we had crossed over, dem heart melted, and there was no more spirit in dem, because of the pikin dem of Israel.
At that time, Baba God talk say to Joshua, “Make flint knives, and circumcise again the sons of Israel the second time.”
Joshua made imself flint knives, and circumcised the sons of Israel at the hill of the foreskins.
This is the reason Joshua circumcised dem: all the people who come out of Egypt, who were males, even all the men of war, died in the wilderness along the way, after dem come out of Egypt.
For all the people who come out were circumcised; but all the people who were born in the wilderness along the way as dem come out of Egypt had not been circumcised.

For the pikin dem of Israel walked forty years in the wilderness, until all the nation, even the men of war who come out of Egypt, were consumed, because dem didn’t listen to Baba God’s voice. Baba God swore to dem that he wouldn’t Make dem see the land which Baba God swore to dem fathers that he would give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Dem pikin dem, whom he raised up in dem place, were circumcised by Joshua; for dem were uncircumcised, because dem had not circumcised dem on the way.
When dem were done circumcising the whole nation, dem stayed in dem places in the camp until dem were healed.
Baba God talk say to Joshua, “Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt off of you.” So the name of that place was call Gilgal, to this day.
The pikin dem of Israel encamped in Gilgal. Dem kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month at evening in the plains of Jericho.
Dem ate unleavened cakes and parched grain of the produce of the land on the next day after the Passover, in the same day.
The manna ceased on the next day, after dem had eaten of the produce of the land. The pikin dem of Israel didn’t have manna any more; but dem ate of the fruit of the land of Canaan that year.

When Joshua was by Jericho, he lifted up his eyes and looked, and see am, a man stood in front of him with his sword drawn in his hand. Joshua go to him and talk say to him, “Are you for us, or for our enemies?”
He talk say, “No; but I have come now as commander of Baba God’s army.” Joshua fell on his face to the earth, and worshiped, and ask him, “What does my lord say to his worker?”
The prince of Baba God’s army talk say to Joshua, “Take una shoes off of una feet; for the place on which you stand is holy.” Joshua did so.
Now Jericho was tightly shut up because of the pikin dem of Israel. Nobody go out, and Nobody come in.
Baba God talk say to Joshua, “See am, I have given Jericho into una hand, with its king and the mighty men of valor.
All of una men of war shall march around the city, going around the city once. You shall do this six days.
Seven priests shall bear seven trumpets of rams’ horns before the ark. On the seventh day, you shall march around the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the trumpets.

It go be that when dem make a long blast with the ram’s horn, and when you hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people shall shout with a great shout; and the city wall shall fall down flat, and the people shall go up, every man straight in front of him.”
Joshua the son of Nun call the priests, and talk say to dem, “Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests bear seven trumpets of rams’ horns before Baba God’s ark.”
Dem talk say to the people, “Advance! March around the city, and let the armed men pass on before Baba God’s ark.”

It was so, that when Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests bearing the seven trumpets of rams’ horns before Baba God advanced and blew the trumpets, and the ark of Baba God’s covenant follow dem.
The armed men go before the priests who blew the trumpets, and the ark go after dem. The trumpets sounded as dem go.
Joshua commanded the people, saying, “You no go shout, nor let una voice be heard, neither shall any word proceed out of una mouth, until the day I tell una to shout. Then you shall shout.”
So he caused Baba God’s ark to go around the city, going about it once. Then dem come into the camp, and stayed in the camp.
Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests take up Baba God’s ark.

The seven priests bearing the seven trumpets of rams’ horns in front of Baba God’s ark go on continually, and blew the trumpets. The armed men go in front of dem. The rear guard come after Baba God’s ark. The trumpets sounded as dem go.
The second day dem marched around the city once, and come back into the camp. Dem did this six days.
On the seventh day, dem rose early at the dawning of the day, and marched around the city in the same way seven times. Only on this day dem marched around the city seven times.
At the seventh time, when the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua talk say to the people, “Shout, for Baba God has given you the city!
The city go be devoted, even it and all that is in it, to Baba God. Only Rahab the prostitute shall live, she and all Wey be with her in the house, because she hid the messengers that we sent.
But as for you, only keep unaself from Wetin be devoted to destruction, lest when you have devoted it, you take of the devoted thing; so you would make the camp of Israel accursed, and trouble it.
But all the silver, gold, and vessels of brass and iron, are holy to Baba God. Dem shall come into Baba God’s treasury.”

So the people shouted and the priests blew the trumpets. When the people heard the sound of the trumpet, the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell down flat, so that the people go up into the city, every man straight in front of him, and dem take the city.
Dem utterly destroyed all that was in the city, both man and woman, both young and old, and ox, sheep, and donkey, with the edge of the sword.
Joshua talk say to the two men who had spied out the land, “Go into the prostitute’s house, and bring the woman and all that she has out from there, as you swore to her.”

The young men who were spies go in, and bring out Rahab with her father, her mother, her brothers, and all that she had. Dem also bring out all of her relatives, and dem set dem outside of the camp of Israel.
Dem burned the city with fire, and all that was in it. Only dem put the silver, the gold, and the vessels of brass and of iron into the treasury of Baba God’s house.

But Rahab the prostitute, her father’s household, and all that she had, Joshua saved alive. She lives in the middle of Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers, whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

Joshua commanded dem with an oath at that time, saying, “Cursed is the man before Baba God, who rises up and builds this city Jericho. With the loss of his firstborn he will lay its foundation, and with the loss of his youngest son he will set up its gates.”
So Baba God was with Joshua; and his fame was in all the land.

But the pikin dem of Israel committed a trespass in the devoted things; for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, take some of the devoted things. So Baba God’s anger burned against the pikin dem of Israel.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Beth Aven, on the east side of Bethel, and spoke to dem, saying, “Go up and spy out the land.” The men go up and spied out Ai.

Dem come back to Joshua, and talk say to him, “No let all the people go up; but let about two or three thousand men go up and strike Ai. No make all the people to toil there, for E get only a few of dem.”
So about three thousand men of the people go up there, and dem fled before the men of Ai.
The men of Ai struck about thirty-six men of dem, and dem chased dem from before the gate even to Shebarim, and struck dem at the descent. The hearts of the people melted, and became like water.
Joshua tore his clothes, and fell to the earth on his face before Baba God’s ark until the evening, he and the elders of Israel; and dem put dust on dem heads.

Joshua talk say, “Alas, Lord Baba God, why have you bring this people over the Jordan at all, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to cause us to perish? I wish that we Bin dey content and lived beyond the Jordan!
Oh, Lord, what shall I say, after Israel has turned dem backs before dem enemies!
For the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear of it, and will surround us, and cut off our name from the earth. What will you do for una great name?”
Baba God talk say to Joshua, “Get up! Why have you fallen on una face like that?

Israel has sinned. Yes, dem have even transgressed my covenant which I commanded dem. Yes, dem have even taken some of the devoted things, and have also stolen, and also deceived. Dem have even put it among dem own stuff.

So the pikin dem of Israel no fit stand before dem enemies. Dem turn dem backs before dem enemies, because dem have become devoted for destruction. I go not be with you any more, unless you destroy the devoted things from among you.

“Get up! Sanctify the people, and say, ‘Sanctify unaself for tomorrow, for Baba God, the God of Israel, says, “E get a devoted thing among you, Israel. You cannot stand before una enemies until you take away the devoted thing from among you.”

“‘In the morning so you go be bring near by una tribes. It go be that the tribe which Baba God selects shall come near by families. The family which Baba God selects shall come near by households. The household which Baba God selects shall come near man by man.

It go be, that person Wey taken with the devoted thing go be burned with fire, he and all that he has, because he has transgressed Baba God’s covenant, and because he has done a disgraceful thing in Israel.’”
So Joshua rose up early in the morning and bring Israel near by dem tribes. The tribe of Judah was selected.
He bring near the family of Judah; and he selected the family of the Zerahites. He bring near the family of the Zerahites man by man, and Zabdi was selected.
He bring near his household man by man, and Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was selected.
Joshua talk say to Achan, “My son, please give glory to Baba God, the God of Israel, and make confession to him. Tell me now Wetin you have done! No hide it from me!”
Achan answer Joshua, and talk say, “I have truly sinned against Baba God, the God of Israel, and this is what I have done.

When I see among the plunder a beautiful Babylonian robe, two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold weighing fifty shekels, then I coveted dem and take dem. See am, Dem be hidden in the ground in the middle of my tent, with the silver under it.”
So Joshua sent messengers, and dem ran to the tent. See am, it was hidden in his tent, with the silver under it.
Dem take dem from the middle of the tent, and bring dem to Joshua and to all the pikin dem of Israel. Dem laid dem down before Baba God.

Joshua, and all Israel with him, take Achan the son of Zerah, the silver, the robe, the wedge of gold, his sons, his daughters, his cattle, his donkeys, his sheep, his tent, and all that he had; and dem bring dem up to the valley of Achor.
Joshua talk say, “Why have you troubled us? Baba God will trouble you today.” All Israel stoned him with stones, and dem burned dem with fire and stoned dem with stones.
Dem raised over him a great heap of stones that remains to this day. Baba God turned from the fierceness of his anger. So the name of that place was call “The valley of Achor” to this day.

Baba God talk say to Joshua, “No fear, and no be dismayed. Take all the warriors with you, and arise, go up to Ai. See am, I have given into una hand the king of Ai, with his people, his city, and his land.
You shall do to Ai and her king as you did to Jericho and her king, except you shall take its goods and its livestock for unaself. Set an ambush for the city behind it.”
So Joshua arose, with all the warriors, to go up to Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand men, the mighty men of valor, and sent dem out by night.
He commanded dem, saying, “See am, you shall lie in ambush against the city, behind the city. No go very far from the city, but all of you be ready.
I and all the people Wey be with me will approach to the city. It shall happen, when dem come out against us, as at the first, that We go flee before dem.
Dem go come out after us, until we have drawn dem away from the city; for Dem go say, ‘Dem flee before us, like the first time.’ So We go flee before dem,
and you shall rise up from the ambush, and take possession of the city; for Baba God una God will deliver it into una hand.
It go be, when you have seized the city, that you shall set the city on fire. You shall do this according to Baba God’s word. See am, I have commanded you.”
Joshua sent dem out; and dem go to set up the ambush, and stayed between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of Ai; but Joshua stayed among the people that night.
Joshua rose up early in the morning, mustered the people, and go up, he and the elders of Israel, before the people to Ai.
All the people, even the men of war who were with him, go up, and come near, and come before the city, and encamped on the north side of Ai. Now there was a valley between him and Ai.
He take about five thousand men, and set dem in ambush between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of the city.
So dem set the people, even all the army who was on the north of the city, and dem ambush on the west of the city; and Joshua go that night into the middle of the valley.

When the king of Ai see it, dem hurried and rose up early, and the men of the city go out against Israel to battle, he and all his people, at the time appointed, before the Arabah; but he didn’t know that there was an ambush against him behind the city.
Joshua and all Israel made as if dem were beaten before dem, and fled by the way of the wilderness.
All the people who were in the city were call together to pursue after dem. Dem pursued Joshua, and were drawn away from the city.
There No be a man left in Ai or Beth El who didn’t go out after Israel. Dem left the city open, and pursued Israel.
Baba God talk say to Joshua, “Stretch out the javelin that is in una hand toward Ai, for I go give it into una hand.” Joshua stretched out the javelin that was in his hand toward the city.
The ambush arose sharp-sharp out of dem place, and dem ran as soon as he had stretched out his hand, and entered into the city, and take it. Dem hurried and set the city on fire.

When the men of Ai looked behind dem, dem see, and see am, the smoke of the city ascended up to heaven, and dem had no power to flee this way or that way. The people who fled to the wilderness turned back on the pursuers.
When Joshua and all Israel see that the ambush had taken the city, and that the smoke of the city ascended, then dem turned again, and killed the men of Ai.
The others come out of the city against dem, so dem were in the middle of Israel, some on this side, and some on that side. Dem struck dem, so that dem let none of dem remain or escape.
Dem captured the king of Ai alive, and bring him to Joshua.

When Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness in which dem pursued dem, and dem had all fallen by the edge of the sword, until dem were consumed, all Israel come back to Ai, and struck it with the edge of the sword.
All that fell that day, both of men and women, were twelve thousand, even all the men of Ai.
For Joshua didn’t draw back his hand, with which he stretched out the javelin, until he had utterly destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai.
Israel take for themselves only the livestock and the goods of that city, according to Baba God’s word which he commanded Joshua.
So Joshua burned Ai, and made it a heap forever, even a desolation, to this day.

He hanged the king of Ai on a tree until the evening, and at sundown Joshua commanded, and dem take his body down from the tree, and threw it at the entrance of the gate of the city, and raised a great heap of stones on it that remains to this day.
Then Joshua built an altar to Baba God, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,

as Moses the worker of Baba God commanded the pikin dem of Israel, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses, an altar of uncut stones, on which Nobody had lifted up any iron. Dem offered burnt offerings on it to Baba God and sacrificed peace offerings.
He wrote there on the stones a copy of Moses’ law, which he wrote in the presence of the pikin dem of Israel.

All Israel, dem elders and officers, and dem judges, stood on both sides of the ark before the priests the Levites, who carried the ark of Baba God’s covenant, the foreigner as well as the native; half of dem in front of Mount Gerizim, and half of dem in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the worker of Baba God had commanded at the first, that dem should bless the people of Israel.
