Afterward he read all the words of the law, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the book of the law.
There No be a word of all that Moses commanded, which Joshua didn’t read before all the assembly of Israel, with the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who were among dem.

When all the kings who were beyond the Jordan, in the hill country, and in the lowland, and on all the shore of the great sea in front of Lebanon, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, heard of it
dem gathered themselves together to fight with Joshua and with Israel, with one accord.
But when the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and to Ai,
dem also resorted to a ruse, and go and made as if dem Bin dey ambassadors, and take old sacks on dem donkeys, and old, torn-up and bound up wine skins,
and old and patched shoes on dem feet, and wore old garments. All the bread of dem chop supply was dry and moldy.
Dem go to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal, and talk say to him and to the men of Israel, “We have come from a far country. Now so make a covenant with us.”
The men of Israel talk say to the Hivites, “What if you live among us. How could we make a covenant with you?”
Dem talk say to Joshua, “We be una workers.” Joshua talk say to dem, “Wey be you? Where do you come from?”
Dem tell am say, “Una workers have come from a very far country because of the name of Baba God una God; for we have heard of his fame, all that he did in Egypt,
and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon and to Og king of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth.
Our elders and all the inhabitants of our country spoke to us, saying, ‘Take supplies in una hand for the journey, and go to meet dem. Tell dem, “We be una workers. Now make a covenant with us.”’
This our bread we take hot for our supplies out of our houses on the day we go out to go to you; but now, see am, it is dry, and has become moldy.
These wine skins, which we filled, were new; and see am, Dem be torn. These our garments and our shoes have become old because of the very long journey.”
The men sampled dem provisions, and didn’t ask counsel from Baba God’s mouth.
Joshua made peace with dem, and made a covenant with dem, to Make dem live. The princes of the congregation swore to dem.
At the end of three days after dem had made a covenant with dem, dem heard that dem were dem neighbors, and that dem lived among dem.
The pikin dem of Israel traveled and come to dem cities on the third day. Now dem cities were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath Jearim.
The pikin dem of Israel didn’t strike dem, because the princes of the congregation had sworn to dem by Baba God, the God of Israel. All the congregation murmured against the princes.
But all the princes talk say to all the congregation, “We have sworn to dem by Baba God, the God of Israel. Now so we may not touch dem.
We go do this to dem, and Make dem live; lest serious anger be on us, because of the oath which we swore to dem.”
The princes talk say to dem, “Make dem live, so dem became wood cutters and drawers of water for all the congregation, as the princes had spoken to dem.”
Joshua call for dem, and he spoke to dem, saying, “Why have you deceived us, saying, ‘We be very far from you,’ when you live among us?
Now so You be cursed, and some of You go never fail to be slaves, both wood cutters and drawers of water for the house of my God.”

Dem answer Joshua, and talk say, “Because una workers were certainly told how Baba God una God commanded his worker Moses to give you all the land, and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land from before you. So we were very afraid for our lives because of you, and have done this thing.
Now, see am, We be in una hand. Do to us as it seems good and right to you to do.”
He did so to dem, and delivered dem out of the hand of the pikin dem of Israel, so that dem didn’t kill dem.
That day Joshua made dem wood cutters and drawers of water for the congregation and for Baba God’s altar to this day, in the place which he should choose.

Now when Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem heard how Joshua had taken Ai. and had utterly destroyed it; as he had done to Jericho and her king, so he had done to Ai and her king; and how the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel, and were among dem.
Dem were very afraid, because Gibeon was a great city, as one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai, and all its men were mighty.
So Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem sent to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon, saying,
“Come up to me and help me. Make we strike Gibeon; for dem have made peace with Joshua and with the pikin dem of Israel.”

So the five kings of the Amorites, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon, gathered themselves together and go up, dem and all dem armies, and encamped against Gibeon, and made war against it.

The men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal, saying, “No abandon una workers! Come up to us sharp-sharp and save us! Help us; for all the kings of the Amorites that live in the hill country have gathered together against us.”
So Joshua go up from Gilgal, he, and the whole army with him, including all the mighty men of valor.
Baba God talk say to Joshua, “No fear dem, for I have delivered dem into una hands. Not a man of dem will stand before you.”
Joshua so come to dem suddenly. He marched from Gilgal all night.
Baba God confused dem before Israel. He killed dem with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chased dem by the way of the ascent of Beth Horon, and struck dem to Azekah and to Makkedah.

As dem fled from before Israel, while dem were at the descent of Beth Horon, Baba God hurled down great stones from the sky on dem to Azekah, and dem died. There were more who died from the hailstones than those whom the pikin dem of Israel killed with the sword.

Then Joshua spoke to Baba God in the day when Baba God delivered up the Amorites before the pikin dem of Israel. He talk say in the sight of Israel, “Sun, stand still on Gibeon! You, moon, stop in the valley of Aijalon!”

The sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the nation had avenged themselves of dem enemies. No be this written in the book of Jashar? The sun stayed in the middle of the sky, and didn’t hurry to go down about a whole day.
There was no day like that before it or after it, that Baba God listened to the voice of a man; for Baba God fought for Israel.
Joshua come back, and all Israel with him, to the camp to Gilgal.
These five kings fled, and hid themselves in the cave at Makkedah.
Joshua was told, saying, “The five kings Don dey find, hidden in the cave at Makkedah.”
Joshua talk say, “Roll large stones to cover the cave’s entrance, and set men by it to guard dem;
but no stay there. Pursue una enemies, and attack dem from the rear. No allow dem to enter into dem cities; for Baba God una God has delivered dem into una hand.”
When Joshua and the pikin dem of Israel had finished killing dem with a plenty well-well slaughter until dem were consumed, and the remnant which remain of dem had entered into the fortified cities,
all the people come back to the camp to Joshua at Makkedah in peace. None moved his tongue against any of the pikin dem of Israel.
Then Joshua talk say, “Open the cave entrance, and bring those five kings out of the cave to me.”
Dem did so, and bring those five kings out of the cave to him: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.

When dem bring those kings out to Joshua, Joshua call for all the men of Israel, and talk say to the chiefs of the men of war who go with him, “Come near. Put una feet on the necks of these kings.” Dem come near, and put dem feet on dem necks.
Joshua talk say to dem, “No fear, nor be dismayed. Be strong and courageous, for Baba God will do this to all una enemies against whom you fight.”
Afterward Joshua struck dem, put dem to death, and hanged dem on five trees. Dem were hanging on the trees until the evening.

At the time of the going down of the sun, Joshua commanded, and dem take dem down off the trees, and threw dem into the cave in which dem had hidden themselves, and laid great stones on the mouth of the cave, which remain to this very day.

Joshua take Makkedah on that day, and struck it with the edge of the sword, with its king. He utterly destroyed it and all the souls who were in it. He left Nobody remaining. He did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua passed from Makkedah, and all Israel with him, to Libnah, and fought against Libnah.

Baba God delivered it also, with its king, into the hand of Israel. He struck it with the edge of the sword, and all the souls who were in it. He left Nobody remaining in it. He did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua passed from Libnah, and all Israel with him, to Lachish, and encamped against it, and fought against it.

Baba God delivered Lachish into the hand of Israel. He take it on the second day, and struck it with the edge of the sword, with all the souls who were in it, according to all that he had done to Libnah.
Then Horam king of Gezer come up to help Lachish; and Joshua struck him and his people, until he had left him Nobody remaining.
Joshua passed from Lachish, and all Israel with him, to Eglon; and dem encamped against it fought against it.
Dem take it on that day, and struck it with the edge of the sword. He utterly destroyed all the souls who were in it that day, according to all that he had done to Lachish.
Joshua go up from Eglon, and all Israel with him, to Hebron; and dem fought against it.

Dem take it, and struck it with the edge of the sword, with its king and all its cities, and all the souls who were in it. He left Nobody remaining, according to all that he had done to Eglon; but he utterly destroyed it, and all the souls who were in it.
Joshua come back, and all Israel with him, to Debir, and fought against it.

He take it, with its king and all its cities. Dem struck dem with the edge of the sword, and utterly destroyed all the souls who were in it. He left Nobody remaining. As he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir, and to its king; as he had done also to Libnah, and to its king.

So Joshua struck all the land, the hill country, the South, the lowland, the slopes, and all dem kings. He left Nobody remaining, but he utterly destroyed all that breathed, as Baba God, the God of Israel, commanded.
Joshua struck dem from Kadesh Barnea even to Gaza, and all the country of Goshen, even to Gibeon.
Joshua take all these kings and dem land at one time, because Baba God, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.
Joshua come back, and all Israel with him, to the camp to Gilgal.
When Jabin king of Hazor heard of it, he sent to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, to the king of Achshaph,
and to the kings who were on the north, in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, in the lowland, and in the heights of Dor on the west,
to the Canaanite on the east and on the west, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite in the hill country, and the Hivite under Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
Dem go out, dem and all dem armies with dem, many people, even as the sand that is on the seashore in plenty people, with very many horses and chariots.
All these kings met together; and dem come and encamped together at the waters of Merom, to fight with Israel.
Baba God talk say to Joshua, “No fear because of dem; for tomorrow at this time, I go deliver dem up all slain before Israel. You shall hamstring dem horses and burn dem chariots with fire.”
So Joshua come suddenly, with all the warriors, against dem by the waters of Merom, and attacked dem.

Baba God delivered dem into the hand of Israel, and dem struck dem, and chased dem to great Sidon, and to Misrephoth Maim, and to the valley of Mizpah eastward. Dem struck dem until dem left dem Nobody remaining.
Joshua did to dem as Baba God told him. He hamstrung dem horses and burned dem chariots with fire.
Joshua turned back at that time, and take Hazor, and struck its king with the sword: for Hazor used to be the head of all those kingdoms.
Dem struck all the souls who were in it with the edge of the sword, utterly destroying dem. There was Nobody left who breathed. He burned Hazor with fire.
Joshua captured all the cities of those kings, with dem kings, and he struck dem with the edge of the sword, and utterly destroyed dem; as Moses the worker of Baba God commanded.
But as for the cities that stood on dem mounds, Israel burned none of dem, except Hazor only. Joshua burned that.

The pikin dem of Israel take all the plunder of these cities, with the livestock, as plunder for themselves; but every man dem struck with the edge of the sword, until dem had destroyed dem. Dem didn’t leave any who breathed.
As Baba God commanded Moses his worker, so Moses commanded Joshua. Joshua did so. He left nothing undone of all that Baba God commanded Moses.
So Joshua captured all that land, the hill country, all the South, all the land of Goshen, the lowland, the Arabah, the hill country of Israel, and the lowland of the same;
from Mount Halak, that goes up to Seir, even to Baal Gad in the valley of Lebanon under Mount Hermon. He take all dem kings, struck dem, and put dem to death.
Joshua made war a long time with all those kings.
There No be a city that made peace with the pikin dem of Israel, except the Hivites, the inhabitants of Gibeon. Dem take all in battle.

For it was of Baba God to harden dem hearts, to come against Israel in battle, that he might utterly destroy dem, that dem might have no favor, but that he might destroy dem, as Baba God commanded Moses.

Joshua come at that time, and cut off the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah, and from all the hill country of Israel: Joshua utterly destroyed dem with dem cities.
There were none of the Anakim left in the land of the pikin dem of Israel. Only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod, did some remain.
So Joshua take the whole land, according to all that Baba God spoke to Moses; and Joshua give it for an inheritance to Israel according to dem divisions by dem tribes. The land had rest from war.

Now these are the kings of the land, whom the pikin dem of Israel struck, and possessed dem land beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise, from the valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon, and all the Arabah eastward:

Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and ruled from Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the middle of the valley, and half Gilead, even to the river Jabbok, the border of the pikin dem of Ammon;
and the Arabah to the sea of Chinneroth, eastward, and to the sea of the Arabah, even the Salt Sea, eastward, the way to Beth Jeshimoth; and on the south, under the slopes of Pisgah:
and the border of Og king of Bashan, of the remnant of the Rephaim, who lived at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,
and ruled in Mount Hermon, and in Salecah, and in all Bashan, to the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and half Gilead, the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses the worker of Baba God and the pikin dem of Israel struck dem. Moses the worker of Baba God give it for a possession to the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the pikin dem of Israel struck beyond the Jordan westward, from Baal Gad in the valley of Lebanon even to Mount Halak, that goes up to Seir. Joshua give it to the tribes of Israel for a possession according to dem divisions;

in the hill country, and in the lowland, and in the Arabah, and in the slopes, and in the wilderness, and in the South; the Hittite, the Amorite, and the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite:
the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;
the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lassharon, one;
the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
the king of Shimron Meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;
the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
the king of Dor in the height of Dor, one; the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;
the king of Tirzah, one: all the kings thirty-one.
Now Joshua was old and well advanced in years. Baba God talk say to him, “You be old and advanced in years, and there remains yet well-well land to be possessed.
“This is the land that still remains: all the regions of the Philistines, and all the Geshurites;

from the Shihor, which is before Egypt, even to the border of Ekron northward, which is counted as Canaanite; the five lords of the Philistines; the Gazites, and the Ashdodites, the Ashkelonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites; also the Avvim,
on the south; all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah that belongs to the Sidonians, to Aphek, to the border of the Amorites;
and the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon, toward the sunrise, from Baal Gad under Mount Hermon to the entrance of Hamath;

all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth Maim, even all the Sidonians. I go drive dem out from before the pikin dem of Israel. Just allocate it to Israel for an inheritance, as I have commanded you.
Now so divide this land for an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.”
With him the Reubenites and the Gadites received dem inheritance, which Moses give dem, beyond the Jordan eastward, even as Moses the worker of Baba God give dem:
from Aroer, that is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the plain of Medeba to Dibon;
and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, to the border of the pikin dem of Ammon;
and Gilead, and the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan to Salecah;
all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei (the same was left of the remnant of the Rephaim); for Moses attacked these, and drove dem out.
Nevertheless the pikin dem of Israel didn’t drive out the Geshurites, nor the Maacathites: but Geshur and Maacath live within Israel to this day.
Only he give no inheritance to the tribe of Levi. The offerings of Baba God, the God of Israel, made by fire are his inheritance, as he spoke to him.
Moses give to the tribe of the pikin dem of Reuben according to dem families.
Dem border was from Aroer, that is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the plain by Medeba;
Heshbon, and all its cities that are in the plain; Dibon, Bamoth Baal, Beth Baal Meon,
Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath,
Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth Shahar in the mount of the valley,
Beth Peor, the slopes of Pisgah, Beth Jeshimoth,

all the cities of the plain, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck with the chiefs of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the princes of Sihon, who lived in the land.
The pikin dem of Israel also killed Balaam the son of Beor, the soothsayer, with the sword, among the rest of dem slain.
The border of the pikin dem of Reuben was the bank of the Jordan. This was the inheritance of the pikin dem of Reuben according to dem families, the cities and its villages.
Moses give to the tribe of Gad, to the pikin dem of Gad, according to dem families.
Dem border was Jazer, and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the pikin dem of Ammon, to Aroer that is near Rabbah;
and from Heshbon to Ramath Mizpeh, and Betonim; and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir;

and in the valley, Beth Haram, Beth Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, the Jordan’s bank, to the uttermost part of the sea of Chinnereth beyond the Jordan eastward.
This is the inheritance of the pikin dem of Gad according to dem families, the cities and its villages.
Moses give an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh. It was for the half-tribe of the pikin dem of Manasseh according to dem families.
Dem border was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair, which are in Bashan, sixty cities.

Half Gilead, Ashtaroth, and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, were for the pikin dem of Machir the son of Manasseh, even for the half of the pikin dem of Machir according to dem families.
These are the inheritances which Moses distributed in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan at Jericho, eastward.
But Moses give no inheritance to the tribe of Levi. Baba God, the God of Israel, is dem inheritance, as he spoke to dem.

These are the inheritances which the pikin dem of Israel take in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the tribes of the pikin dem of Israel, distributed to dem,
by the lot of dem inheritance, as Baba God commanded by Moses, for the nine tribes, and for the half-tribe.
For Moses had given the inheritance of the two tribes and the half-tribe beyond the Jordan; but to the Levites he give no inheritance among dem.
For the pikin dem of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. Dem give no portion to the Levites in the land, except cities to live in, with dem suburbs for dem livestock and for dem property.
The pikin dem of Israel did as Baba God commanded Moses, and dem divided the land.

Then the pikin dem of Judah come near to Joshua in Gilgal. Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite talk say to him, “You know the thing that Baba God spoke to Moses the man of God concerning me and concerning you in Kadesh Barnea.
I was forty years old when Moses the worker of Baba God sent me from Kadesh Barnea to spy out the land. I bring him word again as it was in my heart.
Nevertheless, my brothers who go up with me made the heart of the people melt; but I wholly follow Baba God my God.
Moses swore on that day, saying, ‘Surely the land where you walked go be an inheritance to you and to una pikin dem forever, because you have wholly follow Baba God my God.’

“Now, see am, Baba God has kept me alive, as he spoke, these forty-five years, from the time that Baba God spoke this word to Moses, while Israel walked in the wilderness. Now, see am, I be eighty-five years old, today.
As yet I be as strong today as I was in the day that Moses sent me. As my strength was then, even so is my strength now for war, to go out and to come in.

Now so give me this hill country, of which Baba God spoke in that day; for you heard in that day how the Anakim were there, and great and fortified cities. It may be that Baba God Go be with me, and I shall drive dem out, as Baba God talk say.”
Joshua blessed him; and he give Hebron to Caleb the son of Jephunneh for an inheritance.
So Hebron became the inheritance of Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite to this day, because he follow Baba God, the God of Israel wholeheartedly.
Now the name of Hebron before was Kiriath Arba, after the greatest man among the Anakim. Then the land had rest from war.
The lot for the tribe of the pikin dem of Judah according to dem families was to the border of Edom, even to the wilderness of Zin southward, at the uttermost part of the south.
Dem south border was from the uttermost part of the Salt Sea, from the bay that looks southward;
and it go out southward of the ascent of Akrabbim, and passed along to Zin, and go up by the south of Kadesh Barnea, and passed along by Hezron, go up to Addar, and turned towards Karka;
and it passed along to Azmon, go out at the brook of Egypt; and the border ended at the sea. This go be una south border.
The east border was the Salt Sea, even to the end of the Jordan. The border of the north quarter was from the bay of the sea at the end of the Jordan.
The border go up to Beth Hoglah, and passed along by the north of Beth Arabah; and the border go up to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben.

The border go up to Debir from the valley of Achor, and so northward, looking toward Gilgal, that faces the ascent of Adummim, which is on the south side of the river. The border passed along to the waters of En Shemesh, and ended at En Rogel.

The border go up by the valley of the son of Hinnom to the side of the Jebusite (also call Jerusalem) southward; and the border go up to the top of the mountain that lies before the valley of Hinnom westward, which is at the farthest part of the valley of Rephaim northward.
The border extended from the top of the mountain to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, and go out to the cities of Mount Ephron; and the border extended to Baalah (also call Kiriath Jearim);

and the border turned about from Baalah westward to Mount Seir, and passed along to the side of Mount Jearim (also call Chesalon) on the north, and go down to Beth Shemesh, and passed along by Timnah;
and the border go out to the side of Ekron northward; and the border extended to Shikkeron, and passed along to Mount Baalah, and go out at Jabneel; and the goings out of the border were at the sea.
The west border was to the shore of the great sea. This is the border of the pikin dem of Judah according to dem families.
He give to Caleb the son of Jephunneh a portion among the pikin dem of Judah, according to the commandment of Baba God to Joshua, even Kiriath Arba, named after the father of Anak (also call Hebron).
Caleb drove out the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the pikin dem of Anak.
He go up against the inhabitants of Debir: now the name of Debir before was Kiriath Sepher.
Caleb talk say, “Person wey strikes Kiriath Sepher, and takes it, to him I go give Achsah my daughter as wife.”
Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, take it: and he give him Achsah his daughter as wife.
When she come, she had him ask her father for a field. She got off of her donkey, and Caleb talk say, “What do you want?”
She talk say, “Give me a blessing. Because you have set me in the land of the South, give me also springs of water.” So he give her the upper springs and the lower springs.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the pikin dem of Judah according to dem families.
The farthest cities of the tribe of the pikin dem of Judah toward the border of Edom in the South were Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur,
Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah,
Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan,
Ziph, Telem, Bealoth,
Hazor Hadattah, Kerioth Hezron (also call Hazor),
Amam, Shema, Moladah,
Hazar Gaddah, Heshmon, Beth Pelet,
Hazar Shual, Beersheba, Biziothiah,
Baalah, Iim, Ezem,
Eltolad, Chesil, Hormah,
Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah,
Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon. All the cities are twenty-nine, with dem villages.
In the lowland, Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah,
Zanoah, En Gannim, Tappuah, Enam,
Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah,
Shaaraim, Adithaim and Gederah (or Gederothaim); fourteen cities with dem villages.
Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal Gad,
Dilean, Mizpah, Joktheel,
Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon,
Cabbon, Lahmam, Chitlish,
Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah; sixteen cities with dem villages.
Libnah, Ether, Ashan,
Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib,
Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah; nine cities with dem villages.
Ekron, with its towns and its villages;
from Ekron even to the sea, all that were by the side of Ashdod, with dem villages.
Ashdod, its towns and its villages; Gaza, its towns and its villages; to the brook of Egypt, and the great sea with its coastline.
In the hill country, Shamir, Jattir, Socoh,
Dannah, Kiriath Sannah (which is Debir),
Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim,
Goshen, Holon, and Giloh; eleven cities with dem villages.
Arab, Dumah, Eshan,
Janim, Beth Tappuah, Aphekah,
Humtah, Kiriath Arba (also call Hebron), and Zior; nine cities with dem villages.
Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Jutah,
Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah,
Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah; ten cities with dem villages.
Halhul, Beth Zur, Gedor,
Maarath, Beth Anoth, and Eltekon; six cities with dem villages.
Kiriath Baal (also call Kiriath Jearim), and Rabbah; two cities with dem villages.
In the wilderness, Beth Arabah, Middin, Secacah,
Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi; six cities with dem villages.
As for the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the pikin dem of Judah no fit drive dem out; but the Jebusites live with the pikin dem of Judah at Jerusalem to this day.
The lot come out for the pikin dem of Joseph from the Jordan at Jericho, at the waters of Jericho on the east, even the wilderness, going up from Jericho through the hill country to Bethel.
It go out from Bethel to Luz, and passed along to the border of the Archites to Ataroth;
and it go down westward to the border of the Japhletites, to the border of Beth Horon the lower, and on to Gezer; and ended at the sea.
The pikin dem of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, take dem inheritance.
This was the border of the pikin dem of Ephraim according to dem families. The border of dem inheritance eastward was Ataroth Addar, to Beth Horon the upper.
The border go out westward at Michmethath on the north. The border turned about eastward to Taanath Shiloh, and passed along it on the east of Janoah.
It go down from Janoah to Ataroth, to Naarah, reached to Jericho, and go out at the Jordan.
From Tappuah the border go along westward to the brook of Kanah; and ended at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the pikin dem of Ephraim according to dem families;
together with the cities which were set apart for the pikin dem of Ephraim in the middle of the inheritance of the pikin dem of Manasseh, all the cities with dem villages.
Dem didn’t drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer; but the Canaanites live in the territory of Ephraim to this day, and have become workers to do forced labor.

This was the lot for the tribe of Manasseh, for he was the firstborn of Joseph. As for Machir the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead, because he was a man of war, so he had Gilead and Bashan.

So this was for the rest of the pikin dem of Manasseh according to dem families: for the pikin dem of Abiezer, for the pikin dem of Helek, for the pikin dem of Asriel, for the pikin dem of Shechem, for the pikin dem of Hepher, and for the pikin dem of Shemida. These were the male pikin dem of Manasseh the son of Joseph according to dem families.

But Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, but daughters. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

Dem come to Eleazar the priest, and to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the princes, saying, “Baba God commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers.” So according to the commandment of Baba God he give dem an inheritance among the brothers of dem father.
Ten parts fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan, which is beyond the Jordan;
because the daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons. The land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the sons of Manasseh.
The border of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethath, which is before Shechem. The border go along to the right hand, to the inhabitants of En Tappuah.
The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh; but Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the pikin dem of Ephraim.

The border go down to the brook of Kanah, southward of the brook. These cities belonged to Ephraim among the cities of Manasseh. The border of Manasseh was on the north side of the brook, and ended at the sea.
Southward it was Ephraim’s, and northward it was Manasseh’s, and the sea was his border. Dem reached to Asher on the north, and to Issachar on the east.

Manasseh had three heights in Issachar, in Asher Beth Shean and its towns, and Ibleam and its towns, and the inhabitants of Dor and its towns, and the inhabitants of Endor and its towns, and the inhabitants of Taanach and its towns, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its towns.
Yet the pikin dem of Manasseh no fit drive out the inhabitants of those cities; but the Canaanites would live in that land.
When the pikin dem of Israel had grown strong, dem put the Canaanites to forced labor, and didn’t utterly drive dem out.
The pikin dem of Joseph spoke to Joshua, saying, “Why have you given me just one lot and one part for an inheritance, since We be a numerous people, because Baba God has blessed us so far?”

Joshua talk say to dem, “If You be a numerous people, go up to the forest, and clear land for yourself there in the land of the Perizzites and of the Rephaim; since the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you.”

The pikin dem of Joseph talk say, “The hill country No be enough for us. All the Canaanites who live in the land of the valley have chariots of iron, both people Wey in Beth Shean and its towns, and people Wey in the valley of Jezreel.”
Joshua spoke to the house of Joseph, that is, to Ephraim and to Manasseh, saying, “You be a numerous people, and have great power. You no go have one lot only;

but the hill country go be yours. Although it is a forest, you shall cut it down, and it’s farthest extent go be yours; for you shall drive out the Canaanites, though dem have chariots of iron, and though Dem be strong.”
The whole congregation of the pikin dem of Israel assembled themselves together at Shiloh, and set up the Tent of Meeting there. The land was subdued before dem.
Seven tribes remain among the pikin dem of Israel, which had not yet divided dem inheritance.
Joshua talk say to the pikin dem of Israel, “How long will you neglect to go in to possess the land, which Baba God, the God of una fathers, has given you?
Appoint for unaself three men from each tribe. I go send dem, and dem shall arise, walk through the land, and describe it according to dem inheritance; and dem shall come to me.
Dem shall divide it into seven portions. Judah shall live in his borders on the south, and the house of Joseph shall live in dem borders on the north.
You shall survey the land into seven parts, and bring the description here to me; and I go throw lots for you here before Baba God our God.

However, the Levites have no portion among you; for the priesthood of Baba God is dem inheritance. Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received dem inheritance east of the Jordan, which Moses the worker of Baba God give dem.”
The men arose and go. Joshua commanded people wey go to survey the land, saying, “Go walk through the land, survey it, and come again to me. I go throw lots for you here before Baba God in Shiloh.”
The men go and passed through the land, and surveyed it by cities into seven portions in a book. Dem come to Joshua to the camp at Shiloh.
Joshua throw lots for dem in Shiloh before Baba God. There Joshua divided the land to the pikin dem of Israel according to dem divisions.
The lot of the tribe of the pikin dem of Benjamin come up according to dem families. The border of dem lot go out between the pikin dem of Judah and the pikin dem of Joseph.
Dem border on the north quarter was from the Jordan. The border go up to the side of Jericho on the north, and go up through the hill country westward. It ended at the wilderness of Beth Aven.
The border passed along from there to Luz, to the side of Luz (also call Bethel), southward. The border go down to Ataroth Addar, by the mountain that lies on the south of Beth Horon the lower.

The border extended, and turned around on the west quarter southward, from the mountain that lies before Beth Horon southward; and ended at Kiriath Baal (also call Kiriath Jearim), a city of the pikin dem of Judah. This was the west quarter.
The south quarter was from the farthest part of Kiriath Jearim. The border go out westward, and go out to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.

The border go down to the farthest part of the mountain that lies before the valley of the son of Hinnom, which is in the valley of Rephaim northward. It go down to the valley of Hinnom, to the side of the Jebusite southward, and go down to En Rogel.
It extended northward, go out at En Shemesh, and go out to Geliloth, which is over against the ascent of Adummim. It go down to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben.
It passed along to the side over against the Arabah northward, and go down to the Arabah.
The border passed along to the side of Beth Hoglah northward; and the border ended at the north bay of the Salt Sea, at the south end of the Jordan. This was the south border.
The Jordan was its border on the east quarter. This was the inheritance of the pikin dem of Benjamin, by the borders around it, according to dem families.
Now the cities of the tribe of the pikin dem of Benjamin according to dem families were Jericho, Beth Hoglah, Emek Keziz,
Beth Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel,
Avvim, Parah, Ophrah,
Chephar Ammoni, Ophni, and Geba; twelve cities with dem villages.
Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth,
Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah,
Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah,
Zelah, Eleph, the Jebusite (also call Jerusalem), Gibeath, and Kiriath; fourteen cities with dem villages. This is the inheritance of the pikin dem of Benjamin according to dem families.
The second lot come out for Simeon, even for the tribe of the pikin dem of Simeon according to dem families. Dem inheritance was in the middle of the inheritance of the pikin dem of Judah.
Dem had for dem inheritance Beersheba (or Sheba), Moladah,
Hazar Shual, Balah, Ezem,
Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,
Ziklag, Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susah,
Beth Lebaoth, and Sharuhen; thirteen cities with dem villages;
Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan; four cities with dem villages;
and all the villages that were around these cities to Baalath Beer, Ramah of the South. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the pikin dem of Simeon according to dem families.

Out of the part of the pikin dem of Judah was the inheritance of the pikin dem of Simeon; for the portion of the pikin dem of Judah was too much for dem. So the pikin dem of Simeon had inheritance in the middle of dem inheritance.
The third lot come up for the pikin dem of Zebulun according to dem families. The border of dem inheritance was to Sarid.
Dem border go up westward, even to Maralah, and reached to Dabbesheth. It reached to the brook that is before Jokneam.
It turned from Sarid eastward toward the sunrise to the border of Chisloth Tabor. It go out to Daberath, and go up to Japhia.
From there it passed along eastward to Gath Hepher, to Ethkazin; and it go out at Rimmon which stretches to Neah.
The border turned around it on the north to Hannathon; and it ended at the valley of Iphtah El;
Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem: twelve cities with dem villages.
This is the inheritance of the pikin dem of Zebulun according to dem families, these cities with dem villages.
The fourth lot come out for Issachar, even for the pikin dem of Issachar according to dem families.
Dem border was to Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem,
Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath,
Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez,
Remeth, Engannim, En Haddah, and Beth Pazzez.
The border reached to Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth Shemesh. Dem border ended at the Jordan: sixteen cities with dem villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the pikin dem of Issachar according to dem families, the cities with dem villages.
The fifth lot come out for the tribe of the pikin dem of Asher according to dem families.
Dem border was Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph,
Allammelech, Amad, Mishal. It reached to Carmel westward, and to Shihorlibnath.
It turned toward the sunrise to Beth Dagon, and reached to Zebulun, and to the valley of Iphtah El northward to Beth Emek and Neiel. It go out to Cabul on the left hand,
and Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, even to great Sidon.
The border turned to Ramah, to the fortified city of Tyre; and the border turned to Hosah. It ended at the sea by the region of Achzib;
Ummah also, and Aphek, and Rehob: twenty-two cities with dem villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the pikin dem of Asher according to dem families, these cities with dem villages.
The sixth lot come out for the pikin dem of Naphtali, even for the pikin dem of Naphtali according to dem families.
Dem border was from Heleph, from the oak in Zaanannim, Adami-nekeb, and Jabneel, to Lakkum. It ended at the Jordan.
The border turned westward to Aznoth Tabor, and go out from there to Hukkok. It reached to Zebulun on the south, and reached to Asher on the west, and to Judah at the Jordan toward the sunrise.
The fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Chinnereth,
Adamah, Ramah, Hazor,
Kedesh, Edrei, En Hazor,
Iron, Migdal El, Horem, Beth Anath, and Beth Shemesh; nineteen cities with dem villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the pikin dem of Naphtali according to dem families, the cities with dem villages.
The seventh lot come out for the tribe of the pikin dem of Dan according to dem families.
The border of dem inheritance was Zorah, Eshtaol, Irshemesh,
Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah,
Elon, Timnah, Ekron,
Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath,
Jehud, Bene Berak, Gath Rimmon,
Me Jarkon, and Rakkon, with the border over against Joppa.

The border of the pikin dem of Dan go out beyond dem; for the pikin dem of Dan go up and fought against Leshem, and take it, and struck it with the edge of the sword, and possessed it, and lived inside am, and call Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan dem forefather.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the pikin dem of Dan according to dem families, these cities with dem villages.
So dem finished distributing the land for inheritance by its borders. The pikin dem of Israel give an inheritance to Joshua the son of Nun among dem.
According to Baba God’s commandment, dem give him the city which he ask, even Timnathserah in the hill country of Ephraim; and he built the city, and lived there.

These are the inheritances, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the tribes of the pikin dem of Israel, distributed for inheritance by lot in Shiloh before Baba God, at the door of the Tent of Meeting. So dem finished dividing the land.
Baba God spoke to Joshua, saying,
“Speak to the pikin dem of Israel, saying, ‘Assign the cities of refuge, of which I spoke to you by Moses,
that the man slayer who kills any person accidentally or unintentionally may flee there. Dem go be to you for a refuge from the avenger of blood.

He shall flee to one of those cities, and shall stand at the entrance of the gate of the city, and declare his case in the ears of the elders of that city. Dem shall take him into the city with dem, and give him a place, that he may live among dem.
If the avenger of blood pursues him, then dem no go deliver up the man slayer into his hand; because he struck his neighbor unintentionally, and didn’t hate him before.

He shall live in that city until he stands before the congregation for judgment, until the death of the high priest that go be in those days. Then the man slayer shall return, and come to his own city, and to his own house, to the city he fled from.’”
Dem set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath Arba (also call Hebron) in the hill country of Judah.

Beyond the Jordan at Jericho eastward, dem assigned Bezer in the wilderness in the plain out of the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh.

These were the appointed cities for all the pikin dem of Israel, and for the alien who lives among dem, that Anybody wey kills any person unintentionally might flee there, and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stands trial before the congregation.
Then the heads of fathers’ houses of the Levites come near to Eleazar the priest, and to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the heads of fathers’ houses of the tribes of the pikin dem of Israel.
Dem spoke to dem at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, “Baba God commanded through Moses to give us cities to live in, with dem suburbs for our livestock.”
The pikin dem of Israel give to the Levites out of dem inheritance, according to the commandment of Baba God, these cities with dem suburbs.

The lot come out for the families of the Kohathites. The pikin dem of Aaron the priest, who were of the Levites, had thirteen cities by lot out of the tribe of Judah, out of the tribe of the Simeonites, and out of the tribe of Benjamin.
The rest of the pikin dem of Kohath had ten cities by lot out of the families of the tribe of Ephraim, out of the tribe of Dan, and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh.

The pikin dem of Gershon had thirteen cities by lot out of the families of the tribe of Issachar, out of the tribe of Asher, out of the tribe of Naphtali, and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
The pikin dem of Merari according to dem families had twelve cities out of the tribe of Reuben, out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun.
The pikin dem of Israel give these cities with dem suburbs by lot to the Levites, as Baba God commanded by Moses.
Dem give out of the tribe of the pikin dem of Judah, and out of the tribe of the pikin dem of Simeon, these cities which are mentioned by name:
and dem were for the pikin dem of Aaron, of the families of the Kohathites, who were of the pikin dem of Levi; for dem own was the first lot.
Dem give dem Kiriath Arba, named after the father of Anak (also call Hebron), in the hill country of Judah, with its suburbs around it.
But dem give the fields of the city and its villages to Caleb the son of Jephunneh for his possession.
To the pikin dem of Aaron the priest dem give Hebron with its suburbs, the city of refuge for the man slayer, Libnah with its suburbs,
Jattir with its suburbs, Eshtemoa with its suburbs,
Holon with its suburbs, Debir with its suburbs,
Ain with its suburbs, Juttah with its suburbs, and Beth Shemesh with its suburbs: nine cities out of those two tribes.
Out of the tribe of Benjamin, Gibeon with its suburbs, Geba with its suburbs,
Anathoth with its suburbs, and Almon with its suburbs: four cities.
All the cities of the pikin dem of Aaron, the priests, were thirteen cities with dem suburbs.
The families of the pikin dem of Kohath, the Levites, even the rest of the pikin dem of Kohath, had the cities of dem lot out of the tribe of Ephraim.
Dem give dem Shechem with its suburbs in the hill country of Ephraim, the city of refuge for the man slayer, and Gezer with its suburbs,
Kibzaim with its suburbs, and Beth Horon with its suburbs: four cities.
Out of the tribe of Dan, Elteke with its suburbs, Gibbethon with its suburbs,
Aijalon with its suburbs, Gath Rimmon with its suburbs: four cities.
Out of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Taanach with its suburbs, and Gath Rimmon with its suburbs: two cities.
All the cities of the families of the rest of the pikin dem of Kohath were ten with dem suburbs.

Dem give to the pikin dem of Gershon, of the families of the Levites, out of the half-tribe of Manasseh Golan in Bashan with its suburbs, the city of refuge for the man slayer, and Be Eshterah with its suburbs: two cities.
Out of the tribe of Issachar, Kishion with its suburbs, Daberath with its suburbs,
Jarmuth with its suburbs, En Gannim with its suburbs: four cities.
Out of the tribe of Asher, Mishal with its suburbs, Abdon with its suburbs,
Helkath with its suburbs, and Rehob with its suburbs: four cities.
Out of the tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee with its suburbs, the city of refuge for the man slayer, Hammothdor with its suburbs, and Kartan with its suburbs: three cities.
All the cities of the Gershonites according to dem families were thirteen cities with dem suburbs.
To the families of the pikin dem of Merari, the rest of the Levites, out of the tribe of Zebulun, Jokneam with its suburbs, Kartah with its suburbs,
Dimnah with its suburbs, and Nahalal with its suburbs: four cities.
Out of the tribe of Reuben, Bezer with its suburbs, Jahaz with its suburbs,
Kedemoth with its suburbs, and Mephaath with its suburbs: four cities.
Out of the tribe of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead with its suburbs, the city of refuge for the man slayer, and Mahanaim with its suburbs,
Heshbon with its suburbs, Jazer with its suburbs: four cities in all.
All these were the cities of the pikin dem of Merari according to dem families, even the rest of the families of the Levites. Dem lot was twelve cities.
All the cities of the Levites among the possessions of the pikin dem of Israel were forty-eight cities with dem suburbs.
Each of these cities included dem suburbs around dem. It was this way with all these cities.
So Baba God give to Israel all the land which he swore to give to dem fathers. Dem possessed it, and lived in it.
Baba God give dem rest all around, according to all that he swore to dem fathers. Not a man of all dem enemies stood before dem. Baba God delivered all dem enemies into dem hand.
Nothing failed of any good thing which Baba God had spoken to the house of Israel. All come to pass.
Then Joshua call the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh,
and talk say to dem, “You have kept all that Moses the worker of Baba God commanded you, and have listened to my voice in all that I commanded you.
You have not left una brothers these many days to this day, but have performed the duty of the commandment of Baba God una God.

Now Baba God una God has given rest to una brothers, as he spoke to dem. So now return and go to una tents, to the land of una possession, which Moses the worker of Baba God give you beyond the Jordan.

Only take diligent heed to do the commandment and the law which Moses the worker of Baba God commanded you, to love Baba God una God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to Hold am tight to him, and to serve him with all una heart and with all una soul.”
So Joshua blessed dem, and sent dem away; and dem go to dem tents.

Now to the one half-tribe of Manasseh Moses had given inheritance in Bashan; but to the other half give Joshua among dem brothers beyond the Jordan westward. Moreover when Joshua sent dem away to dem tents, he blessed dem,

and spoke to dem, saying, “Return with much wealth to una tents, with well-well livestock, with silver, with gold, with brass, with iron, and with well-well clothing. Divide the plunder of una enemies with una brothers.”

The pikin dem of Reuben and the pikin dem of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh come back, and comot from the pikin dem of Israel out of Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan, to go to the land of Gilead, to the land of dem possession, which dem owned, according to the commandment of Baba God by Moses.

When dem come to the region about the Jordan, that is in the land of Canaan, the pikin dem of Reuben and the pikin dem of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh built there an altar by the Jordan, a great altar to look at.

The pikin dem of Israel heard this, “See am, the pikin dem of Reuben and the pikin dem of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built an altar in the border of the land of Canaan, in the region around the Jordan, on the side that belongs to the pikin dem of Israel.”
When the pikin dem of Israel heard of it, the whole congregation of the pikin dem of Israel gathered themselves together at Shiloh, to go up against dem to war.
The pikin dem of Israel sent to the pikin dem of Reuben, and to the pikin dem of Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, into the land of Gilead, Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest.
With him were ten princes, one prince of a fathers’ house for each of the tribes of Israel; and dem were each head of dem fathers’ houses among the thousands of Israel.
Dem come to the pikin dem of Reuben, and to the pikin dem of Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, to the land of Gilead, and dem spoke with dem, saying,

“Thus says the whole congregation of Baba God, ‘What trespass is this that you have committed against the God of Israel, to turn away today from following Baba God, in that you have built unaself an altar, to rebel today against Baba God?
Is the wickedness of Peor too little for us, from which we have not cleansed ourselves to this day, although there come a plague on the congregation of Baba God,
that you must turn away today from following Baba God? It Go be, since you rebel today against Baba God, that tomorrow he Go be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.

However, if the land of una possession is unclean, then pass over to the land of the possession of Baba God, in which Baba God’s tabernacle dwells, and take possession among us; but no rebel against Baba God, nor rebel against us, in building an altar other than Baba God our God’s altar.
Didn’t Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the devoted thing, and serious anger fell on all the congregation of Israel? That man didn’t perish alone in his wickedness.’”
Then the pikin dem of Reuben and the pikin dem of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh answer, and spoke to the heads of the thousands of Israel,
“The Mighty One, God, Baba God, the Mighty One, God, Baba God, he knows; and Israel shall know: if it was in rebellion, or if in trespass against Baba God (no save us today),
that we have built us an altar to turn away from following Baba God; or if to offer burnt offering or meal offering, or if to offer sacrifices of peace offerings, let Baba God imself require it.
“If we have not out of concern done this, and for a reason, saying, ‘In time to come una pikin dem might speak to our pikin dem, saying, “What have you to do with Baba God, the God of Israel?

For Baba God has made the Jordan a border between us and you, you pikin dem of Reuben and pikin dem of Gad. You have no portion in Baba God.”’ So una pikin dem might make our pikin dem cease from fearing Baba God.
“So we talk say, ‘Let’s now prepare to build ourselves an altar, not for burnt offering, nor for sacrifice;

but it Go be a witness between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we may perform the service of Baba God before him with our burnt offerings, with our sacrifices, and with our peace offerings;’ that una pikin dem may not tell our pikin dem in time to come, ‘You have no portion in Baba God.’

“So we talk say, ‘It go be, when dem tell us or our generations this in time to come, that we shall say, “See am the pattern of Baba God’s altar, which our fathers made, not for burnt offering, nor for sacrifice; but it is a witness between us and you.”’

“Far be it from us that we should rebel against Baba God, and turn away today from following Baba God, to build an altar for burnt offering, for meal offering, or for sacrifice, besides Baba God our God’s altar that is before his tabernacle!”

When Phinehas the priest, and the princes of the congregation, even the heads of the thousands of Israel that were with him, heard the words that the pikin dem of Reuben and the pikin dem of Gad and the pikin dem of Manasseh spoke, it pleased dem well.

Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest talk say to the pikin dem of Reuben, to the pikin dem of Gad, and to the pikin dem of Manasseh, “Today we know that Baba God is among us, because you have not committed this trespass against Baba God. Now you have delivered the pikin dem of Israel out of Baba God’s hand.”

Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, and the princes, come back from the pikin dem of Reuben, and from the pikin dem of Gad, out of the land of Gilead, to the land of Canaan, to the pikin dem of Israel, and bring dem word again.

The thing pleased the pikin dem of Israel; and the pikin dem of Israel blessed God, and spoke no more of going up against dem to war, to destroy the land in which the pikin dem of Reuben and the pikin dem of Gad lived.
The pikin dem of Reuben and the pikin dem of Gad named the altar “A Witness Between Us that Baba God is God.”
After many days, when Baba God had given rest to Israel from dem enemies all around, and Joshua was old and well advanced in years,
Joshua call for all Israel, for dem elders and for dem heads, and for dem judges and for dem officers, and talk say to dem, “I be old and well advanced in years.
You have seen all that Baba God una God has done to all these nations because of you; for it is Baba God una God who has fought for you.

See am, I have allotted to you these nations that remain, to be an inheritance for una tribes, from the Jordan, with all the nations that I have cut off, even to the great sea toward the going down of the sun.
Baba God una God will thrust dem out from before you, and drive dem from out of una sight. You shall possess dem land, as Baba God una God spoke to you.
“So be very courageous to keep and to do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, that you not turn aside from it to the right hand or to the left;
that you not come among these nations, these that remain among you; neither make mention of the name of dem gods, nor cause to swear by dem, neither serve dem, nor bow down unaself to dem;
but Hold am tight to Baba God una God, as you have done to this day.
“For Baba God has driven great and strong nations out from before you. But as for you, no man has stood before you to this day.
One man of you shall chase a thousand; for it is Baba God una God who fights for you, as he spoke to you.
Take good heed so to unaself, that you love Baba God una God.
“But if you do at all go back, and Hold am tight to the remnant of these nations, even these who remain among you, and make marriages with dem, and go in to dem, and dem to you;

know for a certainty that Baba God una God will no longer drive these nations from out of una sight; but dem go be a snare and a trap to you, a scourge in una sides, and thorns in una eyes, until you perish from off this good land which Baba God una God has given you.

“See am, today I be going the way of all the earth. You know in all una hearts and in all una souls that not one thing has failed of all the good things which Baba God una God spoke concerning you. All have happened to you. Not one thing has failed of it.

It shall happen that as all the good things have come on you of which Baba God una God spoke to you, so Baba God will bring on you all the evil things, until he has destroyed you from off this good land which Baba God una God has given you,

when you disobey the covenant of Baba God una God, which he commanded you, and go and serve other gods, and bow down unaself to dem. Then Baba God’s anger Go be kindled against you, and You go perish sharp-sharp from off the good land which he has given to you.”
Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, and call for the elders of Israel, for dem heads, for dem judges, and for dem officers; and dem presented themselves before God.

Joshua talk say to all the people, “Baba God says, the God of Israel, ‘Una fathers lived of old time beyond the River, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nahor: and dem served other gods.
I take una father Abraham from beyond the River, and led him throughout all the land of Canaan, and multiplied his offspring, and give him Isaac.
I give to Isaac Jacob and Esau: and I give to Esau Mount Seir, to possess it. Jacob and his pikin dem go down into Egypt.
“‘I sent Moses and Aaron, and I plagued Egypt, according to that which I did among dem: and afterward I bring you out.
I bring una fathers out of Egypt: and you come to the sea. The Egyptians pursued una fathers with chariots and with horsemen to the Red Sea.
When dem cried out to Baba God, he put darkness between you and the Egyptians, and bring the sea on dem, and covered dem; and una eyes see what I did in Egypt. You lived in the wilderness many days.
“‘I bring you into the land of the Amorites, that lived beyond the Jordan. Dem fought with you, and I give dem into una hand. You possessed dem land, and I destroyed dem from before you.
Then Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel. He sent and call Balaam the son of Beor to curse you,
but I would not listen to Balaam; so he blessed you still. So I delivered you out of his hand.

“‘You go over the Jordan, and come to Jericho. The men of Jericho fought against you, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Girgashite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite; and I delivered dem into una hand.
I sent the hornet before you, which drove dem out from before you, even the two kings of the Amorites; not with una sword, nor with una bow.
I give you a land whereon you had not labored, and cities which you didn’t build, and you live in dem. You eat of vineyards and olive groves which you didn’t plant.’
“Now so fear Baba God, and serve him in sincerity and in truth. Put away the gods which una fathers served beyond the River, in Egypt; and serve Baba God.

If it seems evil to you to serve Baba God, choose today whom You go serve; whether the gods which una fathers served that were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you live; but as for me and my house, We go serve Baba God.”
The people answer, “Far be it from us that we should forsake Baba God, to serve other gods;

for it is Baba God our God who bring us and our fathers up out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage, and who did those great signs in our sight, and preserved us in all the way in which we go, and among all the peoples through the middle of whom we passed.
Baba God drove out from before us all the peoples, even the Amorites who lived in the land. So we also will serve Baba God; for he is our God.”
Joshua talk say to the people, “You no fit serve Baba God, for he is a holy God. He is a jealous God. He No go forgive una disobedience nor una sins.
If you forsake Baba God, and serve foreign gods, then he will turn and do you evil, and consume you, after he has done you good.”
The people talk say to Joshua, “No, but We go serve Baba God.”
Joshua talk say to the people, “You be witnesses against unaself that you have chosen Baba God unaself, to serve him.” Dem talk say, “We be witnesses.”
“Now so put away the foreign gods which are among you, and incline una heart to Baba God, the God of Israel.”
The people talk say to Joshua, “We go serve Baba God our God, and We go listen to his voice.”
So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and made for dem a statute and an ordinance in Shechem.
Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God; and he take a great stone, and set it up there under the oak that was by the sanctuary of Baba God.

Joshua talk say to all the people, “See am, this stone go be a witness against us, for it has heard all Baba God’s words which he spoke to us. It go be so a witness against you, lest you deny una God.”
So Joshua sent the people away, each to his own inheritance.
After these things, Joshua the son of Nun, the worker of Baba God, died, being one hundred ten years old.
Dem buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnathserah, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, on the north of the mountain of Gaash.
Israel served Baba God all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua, and had known all the work of Baba God, that he had worked for Israel.

Dem buried the bones of Joseph, which the pikin dem of Israel bring up out of Egypt, in Shechem, in the parcel of ground which Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred pieces of silver. Dem became the inheritance of the pikin dem of Joseph.
Eleazar the son of Aaron died. Dem buried him in the hill of Phinehas his son, which was given him in the hill country of Ephraim.
After the death of Joshua, the pikin dem of Israel ask of Baba God, saying, “Who should go up for us first against the Canaanites, to fight against dem?”
Baba God talk say, “Judah shall go up. See am, I have delivered the land into his hand.”
Judah talk say to Simeon his brother, “Come up with me into my lot, that we may fight against the Canaanites; and I likewise will go with you into una lot.” So Simeon go with him.
Judah go up, and Baba God delivered the Canaanites and the Perizzites into dem hand. Dem struck ten thousand men in Bezek.
Dem find Adoni-Bezek in Bezek, and dem fought against him. Dem struck the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
But Adoni-Bezek fled. Dem pursued him, caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his big toes.
Adoni-Bezek talk say, “Seventy kings, having dem thumbs and dem big toes cut off, scavenged under my table. As I have done, so God has done to me.” Dem bring him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
The pikin dem of Judah fought against Jerusalem, take it, struck it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire.
After that, the pikin dem of Judah go down to fight against the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, and in the South, and in the lowland.
Judah go against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron. (The name of Hebron before that was Kiriath Arba.) Dem struck Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
From there he go against the inhabitants of Debir. (The name of Debir before that was Kiriath Sepher.)
Caleb talk say, “I go give Achsah my daughter as wife to the man who strikes Kiriath Sepher, and takes it.”
Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, take it, so he give him Achsah his daughter as his wife.
When she come, she got him to ask her father for a field. She dismounted from off of her donkey; and Caleb talk say to her, “What would you like?”
She talk say to him, “Give me a blessing; because you have set me in the land of the South, give me also springs of water.” Then Caleb give her the upper springs and the lower springs.

The pikin dem of the Kenite, Moses’ brother-in-law, go up out of the city of palm trees with the pikin dem of Judah into the wilderness of Judah, which is in the south of Arad; and dem go and lived with the people.
Judah go with Simeon his brother, and dem struck the Canaanites who inhabited Zephath, and utterly destroyed it. The name of the city was call Hormah.
Also Judah take Gaza with its border, and Ashkelon with its border, and Ekron with its border.
Baba God was with Judah; and drove out the inhabitants of the hill country; for he could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because dem had chariots of iron.
Dem give Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had talk say, and he drove the three sons of Anak out of there.
The pikin dem of Benjamin No drive out the Jebusites who inhabited Jerusalem, but the Jebusites live with the pikin dem of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
The house of Joseph also go up against Bethel, and Baba God was with dem.
The house of Joseph sent to spy out Bethel. (The name of the city before that was Luz.)
The watchers see a man come out of the city, and Dem tell am say, “Please show us the entrance into the city, and We go deal kindly with you.”
He showed dem the entrance into the city, and dem struck the city with the edge of the sword; but dem let the man and all his family go.
The man go into the land of the Hittites, built a city, and call its name Luz, which is its name to this day.

Manasseh No drive out the inhabitants of Beth Shean and its towns, nor Taanach and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Dor and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Ibleam and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Megiddo and its towns; but the Canaanites would live in that land.
When Israel had grown strong, dem put the Canaanites to forced labor, and No utterly drive dem out.
Ephraim didn’t drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, but the Canaanites lived in Gezer among dem.
Zebulun didn’t drive out the inhabitants of Kitron, nor the inhabitants of Nahalol; but the Canaanites lived among dem, and became subject to forced labor.
Asher didn’t drive out the inhabitants of Acco, nor the inhabitants of Sidon, nor of Ahlab, nor of Achzib, nor of Helbah, nor of Aphik, nor of Rehob;
but the Asherites lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land; for dem No drive dem out.

Naphtali didn’t drive out the inhabitants of Beth Shemesh, nor the inhabitants of Beth Anath; but he lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land. Nevertheless the inhabitants of Beth Shemesh and of Beth Anath became subject to forced labor.
The Amorites forced the pikin dem of Dan into the hill country, for dem would not allow dem to come down to the valley;
but the Amorites would live in Mount Heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim. Yet the hand of the house of Joseph prevailed, so that dem became subject to forced labor.
The border of the Amorites was from the ascent of Akrabbim, from the rock, and upward.

Baba God’s angel come up from Gilgal to Bochim. He talk say, “I bring you out of Egypt, and have bring you to the land which I swore to give una fathers. I talk say, ‘I go never break my covenant with you.
You shall make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land. You shall break down dem altars.’ But you have not listened to my voice. Why have you done this?
So I also talk say, ‘I go not drive dem out from before you; but dem go be in una sides, and dem gods Go be a snare to you.’”
When Baba God’s angel spoke these words to all the pikin dem of Israel, the people lifted up dem voice, and wept.
Dem call the name of that place Bochim, and dem sacrificed there to Baba God.
Now when Joshua had sent the people away, the pikin dem of Israel each go to his inheritance to possess the land.
The people served Baba God all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great work of Baba God that he had worked for Israel.
Joshua the son of Nun, the worker of Baba God, died, being one hundred ten years old.
Dem buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnath Heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, on the north of the mountain of Gaash.
After all that generation were gathered to dem fathers, another generation arose after dem, who didn’t know Baba God, nor the work which he had done for Israel.
The pikin dem of Israel did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, and served the Baals.

Dem abandoned Baba God, the God of dem fathers, who bring dem out of the land of Egypt, and follow other gods, of the gods of the peoples who were around dem, and bowed themselves down to dem; and dem provoked Baba God to anger.
Dem abandoned Baba God, and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.

Baba God’s anger burned against Israel, and he delivered dem into the hands of raiders who plundered dem. He sold dem into the hands of dem enemies all around, so that dem could no longer stand before dem enemies.
Anywhere wey dem go out, Baba God’s hand was against dem for evil, as Baba God had spoken, and as Baba God had sworn to dem; and dem were very distressed.
Baba God raised up judges, who saved dem out of the hand of people wey plundered dem.

Yet dem didn’t listen to dem judges; for dem prostituted themselves to other gods, and bowed themselves down to dem. Dem turned aside sharp-sharp out of the way in which dem fathers walked, obeying Baba God’s commandments. Dem didn’t do so.

When Baba God raised up judges for dem, then Baba God was with the judge, and saved dem out of the hand of dem enemies all the days of the judge; for it grieved Baba God because of dem groaning by reason of people wey oppressed dem and troubled dem.

But when the judge was dead, dem turned back, and dealt more corruptly than dem fathers in following other gods to serve dem, and to bow down to dem. Dem didn’t cease Wetin dem were doing, or give up dem stubborn ways.
Baba God’s anger burned against Israel; and he talk say, “Because this nation transgressed my covenant which I commanded dem fathers, and has not listened to my voice,
I also will no longer drive out any of the nations that Joshua left when he died from before dem;
that by dem I may test Israel, to see if Dem go keep the Baba God’s way to walk inside am, as dem fathers kept it, or not.”
So Baba God left those nations, without driving dem out hastily. He didn’t deliver dem into Joshua’s hand.
Now these are the nations which Baba God left, to test Israel by dem, even as many as had not known all the wars of Canaan;
only that the generations of the pikin dem of Israel might know, to teach dem war, at least people wey know nothing of it before:
the five lords of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived on Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal Hermon to the entrance of Hamath.
Dem were left to test Israel by dem, to know whether dem would listen to Baba God’s commandments, which he commanded dem fathers by Moses.
The pikin dem of Israel lived among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
Dem take dem daughters to be dem wives, and give dem own daughters to dem sons and served dem gods.
The pikin dem of Israel did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, and forgot Baba God dem God, and served the Baals and the Asheroth.
So Baba God’s anger burned against Israel, and he sold dem into the hand of Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia; and the pikin dem of Israel served Cushan Rishathaim eight years.
When the pikin dem of Israel cried to Baba God, Baba God raised up a savior to the pikin dem of Israel, who saved dem, even Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.
Baba God’s Spirit come on him, and he judged Israel; and he go out to war, and Baba God delivered Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand. His hand prevailed against Cushan Rishathaim.
The land had rest forty years, then Othniel the son of Kenaz died.

The pikin dem of Israel again did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, and Baba God strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel, because dem had done that which was evil in Baba God’s sight.
He gathered the pikin dem of Ammon and Amalek to imself; and he go and struck Israel, and dem possessed the city of palm trees.
The pikin dem of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.

But when the pikin dem of Israel cried to Baba God, Baba God raised up a savior for dem, Ehud the son of Gera, the Benjamite, a left-handed man. The pikin dem of Israel sent tribute by him to Eglon the king of Moab.
Ehud made imself a sword which had two edges, a cubit in length; and he wore it under his clothing on his right thigh.
He offered the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
When he had finished offering the tribute, he sent away the people who carried the tribute.
But he imself turned back from the stone idols that were by Gilgal, and talk say, “I have a secret message for you, O king.” The king talk say, “Keep silence!” All who stood by him left him.
Ehud come to him; and he was sitting by imself alone in the cool upper room. Ehud talk say, “I have a message from God to you.” He arose out of his seat.
Ehud put out his left hand, and take the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his body:
and the handle also go in after the blade; and the fat closed on the blade, for he didn’t draw the sword out of his body; and it come out behind.
Then Ehud go out onto the porch, and shut the doors of the upper room on him, and locked dem.
After he had gone, his workers come and see that the doors of the upper room were locked. Dem talk say, “Surely he is covering his feet in the upper room.”
Dem waited until dem were ashamed; and see am, he didn’t open the doors of the upper room. So dem take the key and opened dem, and see am, dem lord had fallen down dead on the floor.
Ehud escaped while dem waited, passed beyond the stone idols, and escaped to Seirah.
When he had come, he blew a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim; and the pikin dem of Israel go down with him from the hill country, and he led dem.

E tell dem say, “Follow me; for Baba God has delivered una enemies the Moabites into una hand.” Dem follow him, and take the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites, and didn’t allow any man to pass over.
Dem struck at that time about ten thousand men of Moab, every strong man, and every man of valor. No man escaped.
So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. Then the land had rest eighty years.
After him was Shamgar the son of Anath, who struck six hundred men of the Philistines with an ox goad. He also saved Israel.
The pikin dem of Israel again did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, when Ehud was dead.
Baba God sold dem into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; the captain of whose army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth of the Gentiles.
The pikin dem of Israel cried to Baba God, for he had nine hundred chariots of iron; and he mightily oppressed the pikin dem of Israel for twenty years.
Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, judged Israel at that time.
She lived under Deborah’s palm tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim; and the pikin dem of Israel come up to her for judgment.

She sent and call Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh Naphtali, and talk say to him, “Hasn’t Baba God, the God of Israel, commanded, ‘Go and lead the way to Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men of the pikin dem of Naphtali and of the pikin dem of Zebulun?
I go draw to you, to the river Kishon, Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, with his chariots and his plenty people; and I go deliver him into una hand.’”
Barak talk say to her, “If You go go with me, then I go go; but if You go not go with me, I go not go.”
She talk say, “I go surely go with you. Nevertheless, the journey that you take no go be for una honor; for Baba God will sell Sisera into a woman’s hand.” Deborah arose, and go with Barak to Kedesh.
Barak call Zebulun and Naphtali together to Kedesh; and ten thousand men follow him; and Deborah go up with him.
Now Heber the Kenite had separated imself from the Kenites, even from the pikin dem of Hobab, Moses’ brother-in-law, and had pitched his tent as far as the oak in Zaanannim, which is by Kedesh.
Dem told Sisera that Barak the son of Abinoam was gone up to Mount Tabor.
Sisera gathered together all his chariots, even nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people who were with him, from Harosheth of the Gentiles, to the river Kishon.

Deborah talk say to Barak, “Go; for this is the day in which Baba God has delivered Sisera into una hand. Hasn’t Baba God gone out before you?” So Barak go down from Mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.
Baba God confused Sisera, all his chariots, and all his army, with the edge of the sword before Barak. Sisera abandoned his chariot and fled away on his feet.
But Barak pursued the chariots and the army to Harosheth of the Gentiles; and all the army of Sisera fell by the edge of the sword. There No be a man left.
However Sisera fled away on his feet to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite; for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
Jael go out to meet Sisera, and talk say to him, “Turn in, my lord, turn in to me; No fear.” He come in to her into the tent, and she covered him with a rug.
E tell am say, “Please give me a little water to drink; for I be thirsty.” She opened a bottle of milk, and give him a drink, and covered him.
E tell am say, “Stand in the door of the tent, and if any man comes and inquires of you, and says, ‘Is there any man here?’ you shall say, ‘No.’”
