Then Jael Heber’s wife take a tent peg, and take a hammer in her hand, and go softly to him, and struck the pin into his temples, and it pierced through into the ground; for he was in a deep sleep; so he fainted and died.

See am, as Barak pursued Sisera, Jael come out to meet him, and talk say to him, “Come, and I go show you the man whom you seek.” He come to her; and see am, Sisera lay dead, and the tent peg was in his temples.
So God subdued Jabin the king of Canaan before the pikin dem of Israel on that day.
The hand of the pikin dem of Israel prevailed more and more against Jabin the king of Canaan, until dem had destroyed Jabin king of Canaan.
Then Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam sang on that day, saying,
“Because the leaders take the lead in Israel, because the people offered themselves willingly, be blessed, Baba God!
“Hear, you kings! Give ear, you princes! I, even I, will sing to Baba God. I go sing praise to Baba God, the God of Israel.
“Baba God, when you go out of Seir, when you marched out of the field of Edom, the earth trembled, the sky also dropped. Yes, the clouds dropped water.
The mountains quaked Baba God’s presence, even Sinai at the presence of Baba God, the God of Israel.
“In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were unoccupied. The travelers walked through byways.
The rulers ceased in Israel. Dem ceased until I, Deborah, arose; Until I arose a mother in Israel.
Dem chose new gods. Then war was in the gates. Was there a shield or spear seen among forty thousand in Israel?
My heart is toward the governors of Israel, who offered themselves willingly among the people. Bless Baba God!
“Speak, you who ride on white donkeys, you who sit on rich carpets, and you who walk by the way.
Far from the noise of archers, in the places of drawing water, there Dem go rehearse Baba God’s righteous acts, the righteous acts of his rule in Israel. “Then Baba God’s people go down to the gates.
‘Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, utter a song! Arise, Barak, and lead away una captives, you son of Abinoam.’
“Then a remnant of the nobles and the people come down. Baba God come down for me against the mighty.
Those whose root is in Amalek come out of Ephraim, after you, Benjamin, among una peoples. Governors come down out of Machir. People wey handle the marshal’s staff come out of Zebulun.
The princes of Issachar were with Deborah. As was Issachar, so was Barak. Dem rushed into the valley at his feet. By the watercourses of Reuben, there were great resolves of heart.
Why did you sit among the sheepfolds? To hear the whistling for the flocks? At the watercourses of Reuben, there were great searchings of heart.
Gilead lived beyond the Jordan. Why did Dan remain in ships? Asher sat still at the haven of the sea, and lived by his creeks.
Zebulun was a people that jeopardized dem lives to the death; Naphtali also, on the high places of the field.
“The kings come and fought, then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo. Dem take no plunder of silver.
From the sky the stars fought. From dem courses, dem fought against Sisera.
The river Kishon swept dem away, that ancient river, the river Kishon. My soul, march on with strength.
Then the horse hoofs stamped because of the prancing, the prancing of dem strong ones.
‘Curse Meroz,’ talk say Baba God’s angel. ‘Curse bitterly its inhabitants, because dem didn’t come to help Baba God, to help Baba God against the mighty.’
“Jael go be blessed above women, the wife of Heber the Kenite; blessed shall she be above women in the tent.
He ask for water. She give him milk. She bring him butter in a lordly dish.
She put her hand to the tent peg, and her right hand to the workmen’s hammer. With the hammer she struck Sisera. She struck through his head. Yes, she pierced and struck through his temples.
At her feet he bowed, he fell, he lay. At her feet he bowed, he fell. Where he bowed, there he fell down dead.
“Through the window she looked out, and cried: Sisera’s mother looked through the lattice. ‘Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why do the wheels of his chariots wait?’
Her wise ladies answer her, Yes, she come back answer to sheself,

‘Have dem not find, have dem not divided the plunder? A lady, two ladies to every man; to Sisera a plunder of dyed garments, a plunder of dyed garments embroidered, of dyed garments embroidered on both sides, on the necks of the plunder?’
“So let all una enemies perish, Baba God, but let people wey love him be as the sun when it rises in its strength.” Then the land had rest forty years.
The pikin dem of Israel did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight: and Baba God delivered dem into the hand of Midian seven years.
The hand of Midian prevailed against Israel; and because of Midian the pikin dem of Israel made themselves the dens which are in the mountains, and the caves, and the strongholds.
So it was, when Israel had sown, that the Midianites, the Amalekites, and the pikin dem of the east come up against dem.
Dem encamped against dem, and destroyed the increase of the earth, until you come to Gaza. Dem left no sustenance in Israel, and no sheep, ox, or donkey.
For dem come up with dem livestock and dem tents. Dem come in as locusts for plenty people. Both dem and dem camels were without number; and dem come into the land to destroy it.
Israel was bring very low because of Midian; and the pikin dem of Israel cried to Baba God.
When the pikin dem of Israel cried to Baba God because of Midian,
Baba God sent a prophet to the pikin dem of Israel; and E tell dem say, “Baba God says, the God of Israel, ‘I bring you up from Egypt, and bring you out of the house of bondage.
I delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all who oppressed you, and drove dem out from before you, and give you dem land.
I talk say to you, “I be Baba God una God. You no go fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you live.” But you have not listened to my voice.’”
Baba God’s angel come, and sat under the oak which was in Ophrah, that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite. His son Gideon was beating out wheat in the wine press, to hide it from the Midianites.
Baba God’s angel appeared to him, and talk say to him, “Baba God is with you, you mighty man of valor!”

Gideon talk say to him, “Oh, my lord, if Baba God is with us, why then has all this happened to us? Where are all his wondrous works which our fathers told us of, saying, ‘Didn’t Baba God bring us up from Egypt?’ But now Baba God has throw us off, and delivered us into the hand of Midian.”
Baba God looked at him, and talk say, “Go in this una might, and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Haven’t I sent you?”
E tell am say, “O Lord, how shall I save Israel? See am, my family is the poorest in Manasseh, and I be the least in my father’s house.”
Baba God talk say to him, “Surely I go be with you, and you shall strike the Midianites as one man.”
E tell am say, “If now I have find favor in una sight, then show me a sign that it is you who talk with me.
Please no go away, until I come to you, and bring out my present, and lay it before you.” He talk say, “I go wait until you come back.”
Gideon go in and prepared a young goat and unleavened cakes of an ephah of meal. He put the meat in a basket and he put the broth in a pot, and bring it out to him under the oak, and presented it.
The angel of God talk say to him, “Take the meat and the unleavened cakes, and lay dem on this rock, and pour out the broth.” He did so.

Then Baba God’s angel stretched out the end of the staff that was in his hand, and touched the meat and the unleavened cakes; and fire go up out of the rock, and consumed the meat and the unleavened cakes. Then Baba God’s angel comot out of his sight.
Gideon see that he was Baba God’s angel; and Gideon talk say, “Alas, Lord Baba God! Because I have seen Baba God’s angel face to face!”
Baba God talk say to him, “Peace be to you! No fear. You no go die.”
Then Gideon built an altar there to Baba God, and call it “Baba God is Peace.” To this day it is still in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
That same night, Baba God talk say to him, “Take una father’s bull, even the second bull seven years old, and throw down the altar of Baal that una father has, and cut down the Asherah that is by it.
Then build an altar to Baba God una God on the top of this stronghold, in an orderly way, and take the second bull, and offer a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah which you shall cut down.”
Then Gideon take ten men of his workers, and did as Baba God had spoken to him. Because he feared his father’s household and the men of the city, he could not do it by day, but he did it by night.

When the men of the city arose early in the morning, see am, the altar of Baal was broken down, and the Asherah was cut down that was by it, and the second bull was offered on the altar that was built.
Dem talk say to each other, “Who has done this thing?” When dem inquired and ask, dem talk say, “Gideon the son of Joash has done this thing.”
Then the men of the city talk say to Joash, “Bring out una son, that he may die, because he has broken down the altar of Baal, and because he has cut down the Asherah that was by it.”

Joash talk say to all who stood against him, “Will you contend for Baal? Or will you save him? Person wey will contend for him, Make e be put to death by morning! If he is a god, Make e contend for imself, because someone has broken down his altar!”
So on that day he named him Jerub-Baal, saying, “Let Baal contend against him, because he has broken down his altar.”
Then all the Midianites and the Amalekites and the pikin dem of the east assembled themselves together; and dem passed over, and encamped in the valley of Jezreel.
But Baba God’s Spirit come on Gideon, and he blew a trumpet; and Abiezer was gathered together to follow him.
He sent messengers throughout all Manasseh; and dem also were gathered together to follow him. He sent messengers to Asher, and to Zebulun, and to Naphtali; and dem come up to meet dem.
Gideon talk say to God, “If You go save Israel by my hand, as you have spoken,
see am, I go put a fleece of wool on the threshing floor; if E get dew on the fleece only, and it is dry on all the ground, then shall I know that You go save Israel by my hand, as you have spoken.”
It was so; for he rose up early on the next day, and pressed the fleece together, and wrung the dew out of the fleece, a bowl full of water.

Gideon talk say to God, “No let una anger be kindled against me, and I go speak but this once. Please let me make a trial just this once with the fleece. Let it now be dry only on the fleece, and on all the ground let there be dew.”
God did so that night; for it was dry on the fleece only, and there was dew on all the ground.

Then Jerubbaal, Wey be Gideon, and all the people who were with him, rose up early, and encamped beside the spring of Harod. Midian’s camp was on the north side of dem, by the hill of Moreh, in the valley.
Baba God talk say to Gideon, “The people Wey be with You be too many for me to give the Midianites into dem hand, lest Israel brag against me, saying, ‘My own hand has saved me.’

Now so proclaim in the ears of the people, saying, ‘Anybody wey is fearful and trembling, Make e return and depart from Mount Gilead.’” So twenty-two thousand of the people come back, and ten thousand remain.

Baba God talk say to Gideon, “E get still too many people. Bring dem down to the water, and I go test dem for you there. It go be, that those whom I tell una, ‘This shall go with you,’ the same shall go with you; and Anybody wey I tell una, ‘This no go go with you,’ the same no go go.”

So he bring down the people to the water; and Baba God talk say to Gideon, “Everybody wey laps of the water with his tongue, like a dog laps, you shall set him by imself; likewise Everybody wey bows down on his knees to drink.”
The number of people wey lapped, putting dem hand to dem mouth, was three hundred men; but all the rest of the people bowed down on dem knees to drink water.
Baba God talk say to Gideon, “By the three hundred men who lapped will I save you, and deliver the Midianites into una hand. Let all the other people go, each to his own place.”

So the people take chop in dem hand, and dem trumpets; and he sent all the men of Israel every man to his tent, but retained the three hundred men; and the camp of Midian was beneath him in the valley.
That same night, Baba God talk say to him, “Arise, go down into the camp; for I have delivered it into una hand.
But if You be afraid to go down, go with Purah una worker down to the camp.
You go hear Wetin dem say; and afterward una hands Go be strengthened to go down into the camp.” Then go he down with Purah his worker to the outermost part of the armed men who were in the camp.

The Midianites and the Amalekites and all the pikin dem of the east lay along in the valley like locusts for plenty people; and dem camels were without number, as the sand which is on the seashore for plenty people.

When Gideon had come, see am, there was a man telling a dream to his fellow. He talk say, “See am, I dreamed a dream; and see am, a cake of barley bread tumbled into the camp of Midian, and come to the tent, and struck it so that it fell, and turned it upside down, so that the tent lay flat.”
His fellow answer, “This is nothing other than the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel. God has delivered Midian into his hand, with all the army.”

It was so, when Gideon heard the telling of the dream, and its interpretation, that he worshiped. Then he come back into the camp of Israel, and talk say, “Arise; for Baba God has delivered the army of Midian into una hand!”
He divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put into the hands of all dem trumpets, and empty pitchers, with torches within the pitchers.
E tell dem say, “Watch me, and do likewise. See am, when I come to the outermost part of the camp, it go be that, as I do, so you shall do.
When I blow the trumpet, I and all Wey be with me, then blow the trumpets also on every side of all the camp, and shout, ‘For Baba God and for Gideon!’”

So Gideon, and the hundred men who were with him, come to the outermost part of the camp For the beginning of the middle watch, when dem had but newly set the watch. Then dem blew the trumpets, and broke in pieces the pitchers that were in dem hands.

The three companies blew the trumpets, broke the pitchers, and held the torches in dem left hands, and the trumpets in dem right hands with which to blow; and dem shouted, “The sword of Baba God and of Gideon!”
Dem each stood in his place around the camp; and all the army ran; and dem shouted, and put dem to flight.

Dem blew the three hundred trumpets, and Baba God set every man’s sword against his fellow, and against all the army; and the army fled as far as Beth Shittah toward Zererah, as far as the border of Abel Meholah, by Tabbath.
The men of Israel were gathered together out of Naphtali, and out of Asher, and out of all Manasseh, and pursued Midian.

Gideon sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, “Come down against Midian, and take before dem the waters, as far as Beth Barah, even the Jordan!” So all the men of Ephraim were gathered together, and take the waters as far as Beth Barah, even the Jordan.

Dem take the two princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb. Dem killed Oreb at Oreb’s rock, and Zeeb dem killed at Zeeb’s wine press; and pursued Midian. Then dem bring the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon beyond the Jordan.
The men of Ephraim talk say to him, “Why have you treated us this way, that you didn’t call us when you go to fight with Midian?” Dem rebuked him sharply.
E tell dem say, “What have I now done in comparison with you? No be the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer?
God has delivered into una hand the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb! What was I able to do in comparison with you?” Then dem anger was abated toward him, when he had talk say that.
Gideon come to the Jordan, and passed over, he, and the three hundred men who were with him, faint, yet pursuing.
He talk say to the men of Succoth, “Please give loaves of bread to the people who follow me; for Dem be faint, and I be pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.”
The princes of Succoth talk say, “Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in una hand, that we should give bread to una army?”
Gideon talk say, “So when Baba God has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, then I go tear una flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers.”
He go up there to Penuel, and spoke to dem in the same way; and the men of Penuel answer him as the men of Succoth had answer.
He spoke also to the men of Penuel, saying, “When I come again in peace, I go break down this tower.”

Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, and dem armies with dem, about fifteen thousand men, all who were left of all the army of the pikin dem of the east; for there fell one hundred twenty thousand men who drew sword.
Gideon go up by the way of people wey lived in tents on the east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and struck the army; for the army was secure.
Zebah and Zalmunna fled; and he pursued dem. He take the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and confused all the army.
Gideon the son of Joash come back from the battle from the ascent of Heres.
He caught a young man of the men of Succoth, and inquired of him: and he described for him the princes of Succoth, and its elders, seventy-seven men.

He come to the men of Succoth, and talk say, “See Zebah and Zalmunna, concerning whom you taunted me, saying, ‘Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in una hand, that we should give bread to una men Wey be weary?’”
He take the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with dem he taught the men of Succoth.
He broke down the tower of Penuel, and killed the men of the city.
Then he talk say to Zebah and Zalmunna, “What kind of men were dem whom you killed at Tabor?” Dem answer, “Dem were like you. Each one resembled the pikin dem of a king.”
He talk say, “Dem were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As Baba God lives, if you had saved dem alive, I would not kill you.”
He talk say to Jether his firstborn, “Get up, and kill dem!” But the youth didn’t draw his sword; for he was afraid, because he was yet a youth.
Then Zebah and Zalmunna talk say, “Rise and fall on us; for as the man is, so is his strength.” Gideon arose, and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and take the crescents that were on dem camels’ necks.
Then the men of Israel talk say to Gideon, “Rule over us, both you, and una son, and una son’s son also; for you have saved us out of the hand of Midian.”
Gideon talk say to dem, “I go not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you. Baba God shall rule over you.”
Gideon talk say to dem, “I do have a request, that you would each give me the earrings of his plunder.” (For dem had golden earrings, because dem were Ishmaelites.)
Dem answer, “We go willingly give dem.” Dem spread a garment, and every man threw the earrings of his plunder into it.

The weight of the golden earrings that he requested was one thousand and seven hundred shekels of gold, besides the crescents, and the pendants, and the purple clothing that was on the kings of Midian, and besides the chains that were about dem camels’ necks.
Gideon made an ephod out of it, and put it in Ophrah, his city. Then all Israel played the prostitute with it there; and it became a snare to Gideon, and to his house.
So Midian was subdued before the pikin dem of Israel, and dem lifted up dem heads no more. The land had rest forty years in the days of Gideon.
Jerubbaal the son of Joash go and lived in his own house.
Gideon had seventy sons conceived from his body, for he had many wives.
His concubine who was in Shechem also bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech.
Gideon the son of Joash died in a good old age, and was buried in the tomb of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
As soon as Gideon was dead, the pikin dem of Israel turned again, and played the prostitute following the Baals, and made Baal Berith dem god.
The pikin dem of Israel didn’t remember Baba God dem God, who had delivered dem out of the hand of all dem enemies on every side;
neither did dem show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, according to all the goodness which he had shown to Israel.
Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal go to Shechem to his mother’s brothers, and spoke with dem, and with all the family of the house of his mother’s father, saying,

“Please speak in the ears of all the men of Shechem, ‘Is it better for you that all the sons of Jerubbaal, Wey be seventy persons, rule over you, or that one rule over you?’ Remember also that I be una bone and una flesh.”
His mother’s brothers spoke of him in the ears of all the men of Shechem all these words. Dem hearts inclined to follow Abimelech; for dem talk say, “He is our brother.”
Dem give him seventy pieces of silver out of the house of Baal Berith, with which Abimelech hired vain and light fellows, who follow him.
He go to his father’s house at Ophrah, and killed his brothers the sons of Jerubbaal, being seventy persons, on one stone: but Jotham the youngest son of Jerubbaal was left; for he hid imself.
All the men of Shechem assembled themselves together, and all the house of Millo, and go and made Abimelech king, by the oak of the pillar that was in Shechem.
When dem told it to Jotham, he go and stood on the top of Mount Gerizim, and lifted up his voice, cried out, and talk say to dem, “Listen to me, you men of Shechem, that God may listen to you.
The trees set out to anoint a king over themselves. Dem talk say to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us.’
“But the olive tree talk say to dem, ‘Should I stop producing my oil, with which dem honor God and man by me, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’
“The trees talk say to the fig tree, ‘Come and reign over us.’
“But the fig tree talk say to dem, ‘Should I leave my sweetness, and my good fruit, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’
“The trees talk say to the vine, ‘Come and reign over us.’
“The vine talk say to dem, ‘Should I leave my new wine, which cheers God and man, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’
“Then all the trees talk say to the bramble, ‘Come and reign over us.’
“The bramble talk say to the trees, ‘If in truth you anoint me king over you, then come and take refuge in my shade; and if not, let fire come out of the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon.’

“Now so, if you have dealt truly and righteously, in that you have made Abimelech king, and if you have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house, and have done to him according to the deserving of his hands
(for my father fought for you, and risked his life, and delivered you out of the hand of Midian;

and you have risen up against my father’s house today, and have slain his sons, seventy persons, on one stone, and have made Abimelech, the son of his female worker, king over the men of Shechem, because he is una brother);
if you then have dealt truly and righteously with Jerubbaal and with his house today, then glad well-well in Abimelech, and Make e also glad well-well in you;
but if not, let fire come out from Abimelech, and devour the men of Shechem, and the house of Millo; and let fire come out from the men of Shechem, and from the house of Millo, and devour Abimelech.”
Jotham ran away, and fled, and go to Beer, and lived there, for fear of Abimelech his brother.
Abimelech was prince over Israel three years.
Then God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem; and the men of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech,

that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come, and that dem blood might be laid on Abimelech dem brother, who killed dem, and on the men of Shechem, who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.
The men of Shechem set an ambush for him on the tops of the mountains, and dem robbed all who come along that way by dem, and Abimelech was told about it.
Gaal the son of Ebed come with his brothers, and go over to Shechem; and the men of Shechem put dem trust in him.
Dem go out into the field, harvested dem vineyards, trod the grapes, held festival, and go into the house of dem god, and ate and drank, and cursed Abimelech.

Gaal the son of Ebed talk say, “Wey be Abimelech, and Wey be Shechem, that we should serve him? No be he the son of Jerubbaal? No be Zebul his officer? Serve the men of Hamor the father of Shechem, but why should we serve him?
I wish that this people were under my hand! Then I would remove Abimelech.” He talk say to Abimelech, “Increase una army, and come out!”
When Zebul the ruler of the city heard the words of Gaal the son of Ebed, his anger burned.
He sent messengers to Abimelech craftily, saying, “See am, Gaal the son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem; and see am, dem incite the city against you.
Now so, go up by night, you and the people Wey be with you, and lie in wait in the field.

It go be that in the morning, as soon as the sun is up, you shall rise early, and rush on the city. See am, when he and the people Wey be with him come out against you, then may you do to dem as you shall find occasion.”
Abimelech rose up, and all the people who were with him, by night, and dem laid wait against Shechem in four companies.
Gaal the son of Ebed go out, and stood in the entrance of the gate of the city. Abimelech rose up, and the people who were with him, from the ambush.
When Gaal see the people, he talk say to Zebul, “See am, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains.” Zebul talk say to him, “You see the shadow of the mountains as if dem were men.”
Gaal spoke again and talk say, “See am, people are coming down by the middle of the land, and one company comes by the way of the oak of Meonenim.”

Then Zebul talk say to him, “Now where is una mouth, that you talk say, ‘Wey be Abimelech, that we should serve him?’ No be this the people that you have despised? Please go out now and fight with dem.”
Gaal go out before the men of Shechem, and fought with Abimelech.
Abimelech chased him, and he fled before him, and many fell wounded, even to the entrance of the gate.
Abimelech lived at Arumah; and Zebul drove out Gaal and his brothers, that dem no suppose live in Shechem.
On the next day, the people go out into the field; and dem told Abimelech.
He take the people, and divided dem into three companies, and laid wait in the field; and he looked, and see am, the people come out of the city. So, he rose up against dem, and struck dem.
Abimelech and the companies that were with him rushed forward, and stood in the entrance of the gate of the city; and the two companies rushed on all who were in the field, and struck dem.
Abimelech fought against the city all that day; and he take the city, and killed the people in it. He beat down the city, and sowed it with salt.
When all the men of the tower of Shechem heard of it, dem entered into the stronghold of the house of Elberith.
Abimelech was told that all the men of the tower of Shechem were gathered together.

Abimelech go up to Mount Zalmon, he and all the people who were with him; and Abimelech take an ax in his hand, and cut down a bough from the trees, and take it up, and laid it on his shoulder. Then he talk say to the people who were with him, “Wetin you have seen me do, make haste, and do as I have done!”

All the people likewise each cut down his bough, and follow Abimelech, and put dem at the base of the stronghold, and set the stronghold on fire on dem; so that all the people of the tower of Shechem died also, about a thousand men and women.
Then Abimelech go to Thebez, and encamped against Thebez, and take it.
But there was a strong tower within the city, and all the men and women of the city fled there, and shut themselves in, and go up to the roof of the tower.
Abimelech come to the tower, and fought against it, and come near to the door of the tower to burn it with fire.
A certain woman throw an upper millstone on Abimelech’s head, and broke his skull.

Then he call hastily to the young man his armor bearer, and talk say to him, “Draw una sword, and kill me, that men not say of me, ‘A woman killed him.’ His young man thrust him through, and he died.”
When the men of Israel see that Abimelech was dead, dem each comot to his place.
Thus God repaid the wickedness of Abimelech, which he did to his father, in killing his seventy brothers;
and God repaid all the wickedness of the men of Shechem on dem heads; and the curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal come on dem.
After Abimelech, Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, arose to save Israel. He lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
He judged Israel twenty-three years, and died, and was buried in Shamir.
After him Jair, the Gileadite arose, and he judged Israel twenty-two years.
He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkey colts, and dem had thirty cities, which are call Havvoth Jair to this day, which are in the land of Gilead.
Jair died, and was buried in Kamon.

The pikin dem of Israel again did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, and served the Baals, the Ashtaroth, the gods of Syria, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the pikin dem of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines. Dem abandoned Baba God, and didn’t serve him.
Baba God’s anger burned against Israel, and he sold dem into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the pikin dem of Ammon.

Dem troubled and oppressed the pikin dem of Israel that year. For eighteen years, dem oppressed all the pikin dem of Israel that were beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.
The pikin dem of Ammon passed over the Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, so that Israel was very distressed.
The pikin dem of Israel cried to Baba God, saying, “We have sinned against you, even because we have forsaken our God, and have served the Baals.”
Baba God talk say to the pikin dem of Israel, “Didn’t I save you from the Egyptians, and from the Amorites, from the pikin dem of Ammon, and from the Philistines?
The Sidonians also, and the Amalekites, and the Maonites, oppressed you; and you cried to me, and I saved you out of dem hand.
Yet you have forsaken me, and served other gods. So I go save you no more.
Go and cry to the gods which you have chosen. Make dem save you in the time of una distress!”
The pikin dem of Israel talk say to Baba God, “We have sinned! Do you to us Anything wey seems good to you; only deliver us, please, today.”
Dem put away the foreign gods from among dem, and served Baba God; and his soul was grieved for the misery of Israel.
Then the pikin dem of Ammon were gathered together and encamped in Gilead. The pikin dem of Israel assembled themselves together and encamped in Mizpah.
The people, the princes of Gilead, talk say to each other, “Wey be the man who will begin to fight against the pikin dem of Ammon? He go be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”
Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valor, and he was the son of a prostitute. Gilead became the father of Jephthah.
Gilead’s wife bore him sons. When his wife’s sons grew up, dem drove Jephthah out, and talk say to him, “You go not inherit in our father’s house, for You be the son of another woman.”
Then Jephthah fled from his brothers, and lived in the land of Tob. Outlaws joined up with Jephthah, and dem go out with him.
After a while, the pikin dem of Ammon made war against Israel.
When the pikin dem of Ammon made war against Israel, the elders of Gilead go to get Jephthah out of the land of Tob.
Dem talk say to Jephthah, “Come and be our chief, that we may fight with the pikin dem of Ammon.”
Jephthah talk say to the elders of Gilead, “Didn’t you hate me, and drive me out of my father’s house? Why have you come to me now when You be in distress?”
The elders of Gilead talk say to Jephthah, “So we have turned again to you now, that you may go with us, and fight with the pikin dem of Ammon. You go be our head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”
Jephthah talk say to the elders of Gilead, “If you bring me home again to fight with the pikin dem of Ammon, and Baba God delivers dem before me, will I be una head?”
The elders of Gilead talk say to Jephthah, “Baba God Go be witness between us. Surely We go do Wetin you say.”
Then Jephthah go with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and chief over dem. Jephthah spoke all his words before Baba God in Mizpah.
Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the pikin dem of Ammon, saying, “What have you to do with me, that you have come to me to fight against my land?”

The king of the pikin dem of Ammon answer to the messengers of Jephthah, “Because Israel take away my land, when he come up out of Egypt, from the Arnon even to the Jabbok, and to the Jordan. Now so restore that territory again peaceably.”
Jephthah sent messengers again to the king of the pikin dem of Ammon;
and E tell am say, “Thus says Jephthah: Israel didn’t take away the land of Moab, nor the land of the pikin dem of Ammon,
but when dem come up from Egypt, and Israel go through the wilderness to the Red Sea, and come to Kadesh;

then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, ‘Please let me pass through una land;’ but the king of Edom didn’t listen. In the same way, he sent to the king of Moab; but he would not: and Israel stayed in Kadesh.

Then dem go through the wilderness, and go around the land of Edom, and the land of Moab, and come by the east side of the land of Moab, and dem encamped on the other side of the Arnon; but dem didn’t come within the border of Moab, for the Arnon was the border of Moab.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, the king of Heshbon; and Israel talk say to him, ‘Please Make we pass through una land to my place.’
But Sihon didn’t trust Israel to pass through his border; but Sihon gathered all his people together, and encamped in Jahaz, and fought against Israel.
Baba God, the God of Israel, delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and dem struck dem. So Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, the inhabitants of that country.
Dem possessed all the border of the Amorites, from the Arnon even to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness even to the Jordan.
So now Baba God, the God of Israel, has dispossessed the Amorites from before his people Israel, and should you possess dem?
No go you possess that which Chemosh una god gives you to possess? So Anybody wey Baba God our God has dispossessed from before us, dem will we possess.
Now are you anything better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever strive against Israel, or did he ever fight against dem?

While Israel lived in Heshbon and its towns, and in Aroer and its towns, and in all the cities that are along by the side of the Arnon, three hundred years; why didn’t you recover dem within that time?
I so have not sinned against you, but you do me wrong to war against me. May Baba God the Judge be judge today between the pikin dem of Israel and the pikin dem of Ammon.”
However the king of the pikin dem of Ammon didn’t listen to the words of Jephthah which he sent him.
Then Baba God’s Spirit come on Jephthah, and he passed over Gilead and Manasseh, and passed over Mizpah of Gilead, and from Mizpah of Gilead he passed over to the pikin dem of Ammon.
Jephthah vowed a vow to Baba God, and talk say, “If You go indeed deliver the pikin dem of Ammon into my hand,
then it go be, that Anything wey comes out of the doors of my house to meet me, when I return in peace from the pikin dem of Ammon, it go be Baba God’s, and I go offer it up for a burnt offering.”
So Jephthah passed over to the pikin dem of Ammon to fight against dem; and Baba God delivered dem into his hand.
He struck dem from Aroer until you come to Minnith, even twenty cities, and to Abelcheramim, with a plenty well-well slaughter. So the pikin dem of Ammon were subdued before the pikin dem of Israel.
Jephthah come to Mizpah to his house; and see am, his daughter come out to meet him with tambourines and with dances. She was his only pikin. Besides her he had neither son nor daughter.

When he see her, he tore his clothes, and talk say, “Alas, my daughter! You have bring me very low, and You be one of people wey trouble me; for I have opened my mouth to Baba God, and I no fit go back.”

She talk say to him, “My father, you have opened una mouth to Baba God; do to me according to that which has proceeded out of una mouth, because Baba God has taken vengeance for you on una enemies, even on the pikin dem of Ammon.”
She talk say to her father, “Let this thing be done for me. Leave me alone two months, that I may depart and go down on the mountains, and bewail my virginity, I and my companions.”
He talk say, “Go.” He sent her away for two months: and she comot, she and her companions, and mourned her virginity on the mountains.
At the end of two months, she come back to her father, who did with her according to his vow which he had vowed. She was a virgin. It was a custom in Israel
that the daughters of Israel go yearly to celebrate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in a year.

The men of Ephraim were gathered together, and passed northward; and dem talk say to Jephthah, “Why did you pass over to fight against the pikin dem of Ammon, and didn’t call us to go with you? We go burn una house around you with fire!”
Jephthah talk say to dem, “I and my people were at great strife with the pikin dem of Ammon; and when I call you, you didn’t save me out of dem hand.

When I see that you didn’t save me, I put my life in my hand, and passed over against the pikin dem of Ammon, and Baba God delivered dem into my hand. Why then have you come up to me today, to fight against me?”

Then Jephthah gathered together all the men of Gilead, and fought with Ephraim. The men of Gilead struck Ephraim, because dem talk say, “You be fugitives of Ephraim, you Gileadites, in the middle of Ephraim, and in the middle of Manasseh.”

The Gileadites take the fords of the Jordan against the Ephraimites. When the fugitives of Ephraim talk say, “Let me go over,” the men of Gilead talk say to him, “Are you an Ephraimite?” If he talk say, “No”;

then Dem tell am say, “Now say ‘Shibboleth;’” and he talk say “Sibboleth”; for he no fit manage to pronounce it right: then dem seized him, and killed him at the fords of the Jordan. At that time, forty-two thousand of Ephraim fell.
Jephthah judged Israel six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died, and was buried in the cities of Gilead.
After him Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel.
He had thirty sons; and thirty daughters he sent outside his clan, and thirty daughters he bring in from outside his clan for his sons. He judged Israel seven years.
Ibzan died, and was buried at Bethlehem.
After him Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel; and he judged Israel ten years.
Elon the Zebulunite died, and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
After him Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.
He had forty sons and thirty sons’ sons, who rode on seventy donkey colts. He judged Israel eight years.
Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite died, and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.
The pikin dem of Israel again did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight; and Baba God delivered dem into the hand of the Philistines forty years.
There was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was barren, and childless.
Baba God’s angel appeared to the woman, and talk say to her, “See now, You be barren and childless; but you shall conceive, and bear a son.
Now so please beware and drink no wine nor strong drink, and no eat any unclean thing:

for, see am, you shall conceive, and give birth to a son. No razor shall come on his head; for the pikin go be a Nazirite to God from the womb. He shall begin to save Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.”

Then the woman come and told her husband, saying, “A man of God come to me, and his face was like the face of the angel of God, very awesome. I didn’t ask him where he was from, neither did he tell me his name;

but he talk say to me, ‘See am, you shall conceive, and bear a son; and now drink no wine nor strong drink. No eat any unclean thing; for the pikin go be a Nazirite to God from the womb to the day of his death.’”
Then Manoah entreated Baba God, and talk say, “Oh, Lord, please let the man of God whom you sent come again to us, and teach us what we should do to the pikin who go be born.”
God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God come again to the woman as she sat in the field, but Manoah, her husband, no be with her.
The woman hurried and ran, and told her husband, and talk say to him, “See am, the man who come to me that day has appeared to me,”
Manoah arose, and follow his wife, and come to the man, and talk say to him, “Are you the man who spoke to my wife?” He talk say, “I be.”
Manoah talk say, “Now let una words happen. What shall the pikin’s way of life and mission be?”
Baba God’s angel talk say to Manoah, “Of all that I talk say to the woman Make she beware.
She may not eat of anything that comes of the vine, neither Make she drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing. Make she observe all that I commanded her.”
Manoah talk say to Baba God’s angel, “Please stay with us, that we may make a young goat ready for you.”

Baba God’s angel talk say to Manoah, “Though you detain me, I no go eat una bread. If You go prepare a burnt offering, you must offer it to Baba God.” For Manoah didn’t know that he was Baba God’s angel.
Manoah talk say to Baba God’s angel, “Wetin be una name, that when una words happen, we may honor you?”
Baba God’s angel talk say to him, “Why do you ask about my name, since it is incomprehensible?”
So Manoah take the young goat with the meal offering, and offered it on the rock to Baba God. Then the angel did an amazing thing as Manoah and his wife watched.
For when the flame go up toward the sky from off the altar, Baba God’s angel ascended in the flame of the altar. Manoah and his wife watched; and dem fell on dem faces to the ground.
But Baba God’s angel didn’t appear to Manoah or to his wife any more. Then Manoah know that he was Baba God’s angel.
Manoah talk say to his wife, “We shall surely die, because we have seen God.”

But his wife talk say to him, “If Baba God were pleased to kill us, he wouldn’t have received a burnt offering and a meal offering at our hand, and he wouldn’t he have shown us all these things, nor would he have told us such things as these at this time.”
The woman bore a son, and named him Samson. The pikin grew, and Baba God blessed him.
Baba God’s Spirit began to move him in Mahaneh Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
Samson go down to Timnah, and see a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines.
He come up, and told his father and his mother, and talk say, “I have seen a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines. Now so get her for me as my wife.”

Then his father and his mother talk say to him, “No be there a woman among una brothers’ daughters, or among all my people, that you go to take a wife of the uncircumcised Philistines?” Samson talk say to his father, “Get her for me, for she pleases me well.”
But his father and his mother didn’t know that it was of Baba God; for he sought an occasion against the Philistines. Now at that time the Philistines ruled over Israel.
Then go Samson down with his father and his mother to Timnah, and come to the vineyards of Timnah; and see am, a young lion roared against him.
Baba God’s Spirit come mightily on him, and he tore him as he would have torn a young goat; and he had nothing in his hand, but he didn’t tell his father or his mother what he had done.
He go down, and talked with the woman, and she pleased Samson well.
After a while he come back to take her; and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion; and see am, there was a swarm of bees in the body of the lion, and honey.
He take it into his hands, and go on, eating as he go. He come to his father and mother, and give to dem, and dem ate, but he didn’t tell dem that he had taken the honey out of the lion’s body.
His father go down to the woman; and Samson made a feast there, for the young men used to do so.
When dem see him, dem bring thirty companions to be with him.

Samson talk say to dem, “Let me tell you a riddle now. If you can declare it to me within the seven days of the feast, and find it out, then I go give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing;
but if you no fit declare it to me, then you shall give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing.” Dem tell am say, “Tell us una riddle, that we may hear it.”
E tell dem say, “Out of the eater come out chop. Out of the strong come out sweetness.” Dem no fit in three days declare the riddle.

On the seventh day, dem talk say to Samson’s wife, “Entice una husband, that he may declare to us the riddle, lest we burn you and una father’s house with fire. Have you call us to impoverish us? No be that so?”

Samson’s wife wept before him, and talk say, “You just hate me, and no love me. You’ve told a riddle to the pikin dem of my people, and haven’t told it to me.” E tell am say, “See am, I haven’t told my father or my mother, so why should I tell una?”
She wept before him the seven days, while dem feast lasted; and on the seventh day, he told her, because she pressed him severely; and she told the riddle to the pikin dem of her people.

The men of the city talk say to him on the seventh day before the sun go down, “Wetin be sweeter than honey? Wetin be stronger than a lion?” E tell dem say, “If you hadn’t plowed with my heifer, you wouldn’t have find out my riddle.”

Baba God’s Spirit come mightily on him, and he go down to Ashkelon, and struck thirty men of dem, and take dem plunder, then give the changes of clothing to people wey declared the riddle. His anger burned, and he go up to his father’s house.
But Samson’s wife was given to his companion who Bin dey his friend.
But after a while, in the time of wheat harvest, Samson visited his wife with a young goat. He talk say, “I go go in to my wife’s room.” But her father wouldn’t allow him to go in.
Her father talk say, “I most certainly thought that you utterly hated her; so I give her to una companion. No be her younger sister more beautiful than she? Please take her, instead.”
Samson talk say to dem, “This time I go be blameless in the case of the Philistines, when I harm dem.”
Samson go and caught three hundred foxes, and take torches, and turned tail to tail, and put a torch in the middle between every two tails.
When he had set the torches on fire, he Make dem go into the standing grain of the Philistines, and burned up both the shocks and the standing grain, and also the olive groves.

Then the Philistines talk say, “Who has done this?” Dem talk say, “Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he has taken his wife, and given her to his companion.” The Philistines come up, and burned her and her father with fire.
Samson talk say to dem, “If you behave like this, surely I go take revenge on you, and after that I go cease.”
He struck dem hip and thigh with a great slaughter; and he go down and lived in the cave in Etam’s rock.
Then the Philistines go up, encamped in Judah, and spread themselves in Lehi.
The men of Judah talk say, “Why have you come up against us?” Dem talk say, “We have come up to bind Samson, to do to him as he has done to us.”

Then three thousand men of Judah go down to the cave in Etam’s rock, and talk say to Samson, “No you know that the Philistines are rulers over us? What then is this that you have done to us?” E tell dem say, “As dem did to me, so I have done to dem.”
Dem tell am say, “We have come down to bind you, that we may deliver you into the hand of the Philistines.” Samson talk say to dem, “Swear to me that You go not attack me unaself.”
Dem spoke to him, saying, “No; but We go bind you securely, and deliver you into dem hands; but surely We go not kill you.” Dem bound him with two new ropes, and bring him up from the rock.

When he come to Lehi, the Philistines shouted as dem met him. Then Baba God’s Spirit come mightily on him, and the ropes that were on his arms became as flax that was burned with fire, and his bands dropped from off his hands.
He find a fresh jawbone of a donkey, put out his hand, take it, and struck a thousand men with it.
Samson talk say, “With the jawbone of a donkey, heaps on heaps; with the jawbone of a donkey I have struck a thousand men.”
When he had finished speaking, he threw the jawbone out of his hand; and that place was call Ramath Lehi.

He was very thirsty, and call on Baba God, and talk say, “You have given this great deliverance by the hand of una worker; and now shall I die of thirst, and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?”
But God split the hollow place that is in Lehi, and water come out of it. When he had drunk, his spirit come again, and he revived. So its name was call En Hakkore, which is in Lehi, to this day.
He judged Israel twenty years in the days of the Philistines.
Samson go to Gaza, and see there a prostitute, and go in to her.

The Gazites were told, “Samson is here!” Dem surrounded him, and laid wait for him all night in the gate of the city, and were quiet all the night, saying, “Wait until morning light, then We go kill him.”

Samson lay until midnight, and arose at midnight, and laid hold of the doors of the gate of the city, and the two posts, and plucked dem up, bar and all, and put dem on his shoulders, and carried dem up to the top of the mountain that is before Hebron.
E happen say afterward, that he love a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.

The lords of the Philistines come up to her, and talk say to her, “Entice him, and see in which his great strength lies, and by what means we may prevail against him, that we may bind him to afflict him; and We go each give you eleven hundred pieces of silver.”
Delilah talk say to Samson, “Please tell me where una great strength lies, and Wetin you might be bound to afflict you.”
Samson talk say to her, “If dem bind me with seven green cords that were never dried, then shall I become weak, and be as another man.”
Then the lords of the Philistines bring up to her seven green cords which had not been dried, and she bound him with dem.

Now she had an ambush waiting in the inner room. She talk say to him, “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” He broke the cords, as a string of tow is broken when it touches the fire. So his strength No be known.
Delilah talk say to Samson, “See am, you have mocked me, and told me lies: now please tell me with which you might be bound.”
E tell am say, “If dem only bind me with new ropes with which no work Don dey done, then shall I become weak, and be as another man.”
So Delilah take new ropes, and bound him therewith, and talk say to him, “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” The ambush was waiting in the inner room. He broke dem off his arms like a thread.
Delilah talk say to Samson, “Until now, you have mocked me and told me lies. Tell me with Wetin you might be bound.” E tell am say, “If you weave the seven locks of my head with the web.”
She fastened it with the pin, and talk say to him, “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” He awakened out of his sleep, and plucked away the pin of the beam, and the web.
She talk say to him, “How can you say, ‘I love you,’ when una heart No be with me? You have mocked me these three times, and have not told me where una great strength lies.”
When she pressed him daily with her words, and urged him, his soul was troubled to death.

He told her all his heart, and talk say to her, “No razor has ever come on my head; for I Don dey a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb. If I be shaved, then my strength will go from me, and I go become weak, and be like any other man.”

When Delilah see that he had told her all his heart, she sent and call for the lords of the Philistines, saying, “Come up this once, for he has told me all his heart.” Then the lords of the Philistines come up to her, and bring the money in dem hand.
She made him sleep on her knees; and she call for a man, and shaved off the seven locks of his head; and she began to afflict him, and his strength go from him.

She talk say, “The Philistines are upon you, Samson!” He awoke out of his sleep, and talk say, “I go go out as at other times, and shake myself free.” But he didn’t know that Baba God had comot from him.
The Philistines laid hold on him, and put out his eyes; and dem bring him down to Gaza, and bound him with fetters of brass; and he ground at the mill in the prison.
However the hair of his head began to grow again after he was shaved.
The lords of the Philistines gathered dem together to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon dem god, and to glad well-well; for dem talk say, “Our god has delivered Samson our enemy into our hand.”
When the people see him, dem praised dem god; for dem talk say, “Our god has delivered our enemy and the destroyer of our country, who has slain many of us, into our hand.”
When dem hearts were merry, dem talk say, “Call for Samson, that he may entertain us.” Dem call for Samson out of the prison; and he performed before dem. Dem set him between the pillars;
and Samson talk say to the boy who held him by the hand, “Allow me to feel the pillars whereupon the house rests, that I may lean on dem.”
Now the house was full of men and women; and all the lords of the Philistines were there; and there were on the roof about three thousand men and women, who see while Samson performed.
Samson call to Baba God, and talk say, “Lord Baba God, remember me, please, and strengthen me, please, only this once, God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes.”
Samson take hold of the two middle pillars on which the house rested, and leaned on dem, the one with his right hand, and the other with his left.

Samson talk say, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He bowed imself with all his might; and the house fell on the lords, and on all the people who were inside am. So the dead that he killed at his death were more than people wey he killed in his life.

Then his brothers and all the house of his father come down, and take him, and bring him up, and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the burial site of Manoah his father. He judged Israel twenty years.
There was a man of the hill country of Ephraim, whose name was Micah.

He talk say to his mother, “The eleven hundred pieces of silver that were taken from you, about which you uttered a curse, and also spoke it in my ears, see am, the silver is with me. I take it.” His mother talk say, “May Baba God bless my son!”

He restored the eleven hundred pieces of silver to his mother, then his mother talk say, “I most certainly dedicate the silver to Baba God from my hand for my son, to make an engraved image and a molten image. Now so I go restore it to you.”

When he restored the money to his mother, his mother take two hundred pieces of silver, and give dem to a silversmith, who made an engraved image and a molten image out of it. It was in the house of Micah.
The man Micah had a house of gods, and he made an ephod, and teraphim, and consecrated one of his sons, who became his priest.
In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did that which was right in his own eyes.
There was a young man out of Bethlehem Judah, of the family of Judah, who was a Levite; and he lived there.
The man comot out of the city, out of Bethlehem Judah, to live where he could find a place, and he come to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, as he traveled.
Micah talk say to him, “Where did you come from?” E tell am say, “I be a Levite of Bethlehem Judah, and I be looking for a place to live.”
Micah talk say to him, “Live with me, and be to me a father and a priest, and I go give you ten pieces of silver per year, a suit of clothing, and una chop.” So the Levite go in.
The Levite was content to live with the man; and the young man was to him as one of his sons.
Micah consecrated the Levite, and the young man became his priest, and was in the house of Micah.
Then Micah talk say, “Now know I that Baba God will do good to me, since I have a Levite as my priest.”
In those days there was no king in Israel. In those days the tribe of the Danites sought an inheritance to live in; for to that day, dem inheritance had not fallen to dem among the tribes of Israel.

The pikin dem of Dan sent five men of dem family from dem whole number, men of valor, from Zorah, and from Eshtaol, to spy out the land, and to search it. Dem tell dem say, “Go, explore the land!” Dem come to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and lodged there.

When dem were by the house of Micah, dem know the voice of the young man the Levite; so dem turned aside there, and talk say to him, “Who bring you here? What do you do in this place? What do you have here?”
E tell dem say, “Thus and thus has Micah dealt with me, and he has hired me, and I be become his priest.”
Dem tell am say, “Please ask counsel of God, that we may know whether our way which we go go be prosperous.”
The priest talk say to dem, “Go in peace. Una way in which you go is before Baba God.”

Then the five men comot, and come to Laish, and see the people who were there, how dem lived in safety, in the way of the Sidonians, quiet and secure; for there was Nobody in the land, possessing authority, that might put dem to shame in anything, and dem were far from the Sidonians, and had no dealings with anyone else.
Dem come to dem brothers at Zorah and Eshtaol; and dem brothers ask dem, “What do you say?”
Dem talk say, “Arise, and Make we go up against dem; for we have seen the land, and see am, it is very good. Do you stand still? No be slothful to go and to enter in to possess the land.
When you go, You go come to an unsuspecting people, and the land is large; for God has given it into una hand, a place where E get no lack of anything that is in the earth.”
The family of the Danites set out from Zorah and Eshtaol, with six hundred men armed with weapons of war.
Dem go up and encamped in Kiriath Jearim, in Judah. So dem call that place Mahaneh Dan, to this day. See am, it is behind Kiriath Jearim.
Dem passed from there to the hill country of Ephraim, and come to the house of Micah.

Then the five men who go to spy out the country of Laish answer, and talk say to dem brothers, “Do you know that E get in these houses an ephod, and teraphim, and an engraved image, and a molten image? Now so consider Wetin you have to do.”
Dem turned aside there, and come to the house of the young Levite man, even to the house of Micah, and ask him how he was doing.
The six hundred men armed with dem weapons of war, who were of the pikin dem of Dan, stood by the entrance of the gate.

The five men who go to spy out the land go up, and come in there, and take the engraved image, the ephod, the teraphim, and the molten image; and the priest stood by the entrance of the gate with the six hundred men armed with weapons of war.
When these go into Micah’s house, and take the engraved image, the ephod, the teraphim, and the molten image, the priest talk say to dem, “Wetin be you doing?”

Dem tell am say, “Hold una peace, put una hand on una mouth, and go with us, and be to us a father and a priest. Is it better for you to be priest to the house of one man, or to be priest to a tribe and a family in Israel?”
The priest’s heart was glad, and he take the ephod, the teraphim, and the engraved image, and go with the people.
So dem turned and comot, and put the little ones, the livestock, and the goods before dem.
When dem were a good way from the house of Micah, the men who were in the houses near Micah’s house gathered together and overtook the pikin dem of Dan.
As dem cried to the pikin dem of Dan, dem turned dem faces, and talk say to Micah, “What ails you, that you come with such a company?”
He talk say, “You have taken away my gods which I made, and the priest, and have gone away! What more do I have? How can you ask me, ‘What ails you?’”
The pikin dem of Dan talk say to him, “No let una voice be heard among us, lest angry fellows fall on you, and you lose una life, with the lives of una household.”
The pikin dem of Dan go dem way; and when Micah see that dem were too strong for him, he turned and go back to his house.
Dem take that which Micah had made, and the priest whom he had, and come to Laish, to a people quiet and unsuspecting, and struck dem with the edge of the sword; then dem burned the city with fire.
There was no deliverer, because it was far from Sidon, and dem had no dealings with anyone else; and it was in the valley that lies by Beth Rehob. Dem built the city, and lived in it.
Dem call the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan dem father, who was born to Israel; however the name of the city used to be Laish.

The pikin dem of Dan set up for themselves the engraved image; and Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, and his sons were priests to the tribe of the Danites until the day of the captivity of the land.
So dem set up for themselves Micah’s engraved image which he made, and it remain all the time that God’s house was in Shiloh.
In those days, when there was no king in Israel, there was a certain Levite living on the farther side of the hill country of Ephraim, who take for imself a concubine out of Bethlehem Judah.
His concubine played the prostitute against him, and go away from him to her father’s house to Bethlehem Judah, and was there for four months.

Her husband arose, and go after her, to speak kindly to her, to bring her again, having his worker with him, and a couple of donkeys. She bring him into her father’s house; and when the father of the young lady see him, he rejoiced to meet him.
His father-in-law, the young lady’s father, kept him there; and he stayed with him three days. So dem ate and drank, and stayed there.

On the fourth day, dem got up early in the morning, and he rose up to depart. The young lady’s father talk say to his son-in-law, “Strengthen una heart with a morsel of bread, and afterward you shall go una way.”
So dem sat down, ate, and drank, both of dem together. Then the young lady’s father talk say to the man, “Please be pleased to stay all night, and let una heart be merry.”
The man rose up to depart; but his father-in-law urged him, and he stayed there again.
He arose early in the morning on the fifth day to depart; and the young lady’s father talk say, “Please strengthen una heart and stay until the day declines”; and dem both ate.

When the man rose up to depart, he, and his concubine, and his worker, his father-in-law, the young lady’s father, talk say to him, “See am, now the day draws toward evening, please stay all night. See am, the day is ending. Stay here, that una heart may be merry; and tomorrow go on una way early, that you may go home.”
But the man wouldn’t stay that night, but he rose up and comot, and toward Jebus (also call Jerusalem). With him were a couple of saddled donkeys. His concubine also was with him.
When dem were by Jebus, the day was far spent; and the worker talk say to his master, “Please come and Make we turn aside into this city of the Jebusites, and stay in it.”
His master talk say to him, “We no go turn aside into the city of a foreigner that No be of the pikin dem of Israel; but We go pass over to Gibeah.”
He talk say to his worker, “Come and Make we draw near to one of these places; and We go lodge in Gibeah, or in Ramah.”
So dem passed on and go dem way; and the sun go down on dem near Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin.
Dem turned aside there, to go in to stay in Gibeah. He go in, and sat down in the street of the city; for there was Nobody who take dem into his house to stay.
See am, an old man come from his work out of the field at evening. Now the man was from the hill country of Ephraim, and he lived in Gibeah; but the men of the place were Benjamites.
He lifted up his eyes, and see the wayfaring man in the street of the city; and the old man talk say, “Where are you going? Where did you come from?”

E tell am say, “We be passing from Bethlehem Judah to the farther side of the hill country of Ephraim. I be from there, and I go to Bethlehem Judah. I be going to Baba God’s house; and E get Nobody who has taken me into his house.
Yet E get both straw and feed for our donkeys; and E get bread and wine also for me, and for una worker, and for the young man Wey be with una workers. E get no lack of anything.”
The old man talk say, “Peace be to you; how ever let me supply all una needs. Just no sleep in the street.”
So he bring him into his house, and give the donkeys fodder. Then dem washed dem feet, and ate and drank.

As dem were making dem hearts merry, see am, the men of the city, certain base fellows, surrounded the house, beating at the door; and dem spoke to the master of the house, the old man, saying, “Bring out the man who come into una house, that we can have sex with him!”
The man, the master of the house, go out to dem, and talk say to dem, “No, my brothers, please no act so wickedly; since this man has come into my house, no do this folly.
See am, here is my virgin daughter and his concubine. I go bring dem out now. Humble dem, and do with dem what seems good to you; but to this man no do any such folly.”

But the men wouldn’t listen to him: so the man laid hold of his concubine, and bring her out to dem; and dem had sex with her, and abused her all night until the morning. When the day began to dawn, dem Make she go.
Then the woman come in the dawning of the day, and fell down at the door of the man’s house where her lord was, until it was light.

Her lord rose up in the morning, and opened the doors of the house, and go out to go his way; and see am, the woman his concubine had fallen down at the door of the house, with her hands on the threshold.
E tell am say, “Get up, and Make we be going!” but Nobody answer. Then he take her up on the donkey; and the man rose up, and go to his place.
When he had come into his house, he take a knife, and cut up his concubine, and divided her, limb by limb, into twelve pieces, and sent her throughout all the borders of Israel.

It was so, that all who see it talk say, “Such a deed has not been done or seen from the day that the pikin dem of Israel come up out of the land of Egypt to this day! Consider it, take counsel, and speak.”
Then all the pikin dem of Israel go out, and the congregation was assembled as one man, from Dan even to Beersheba, with the land of Gilead, to Baba God at Mizpah.
The chiefs of all the people, even of all the tribes of Israel, presented themselves in the assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand footmen who drew sword.
(Now the pikin dem of Benjamin heard that the pikin dem of Israel had gone up to Mizpah.) The pikin dem of Israel talk say, “Tell us, how did this wickedness happen?”
The Levite, the husband of the woman who was murdered, answer, “I come into Gibeah that belongs to Benjamin, I and my concubine, to spend the night.
The men of Gibeah rose against me, and surrounded the house by night. Dem intended to kill me, and dem raped my concubine, and she is dead.
I take my concubine, and cut her in pieces, and sent her throughout all the country of the inheritance of Israel; for dem have committed lewdness and folly in Israel.
See am, you pikin dem of Israel, all of you, give here una advice and counsel.”
All the people arose as one man, saying, “None of us will go to his tent, neither will any of us turn to his house.
But now this is the thing which We go do to Gibeah: We go go up against it by lot;

and We go take ten men of one hundred throughout all the tribes of Israel, and one hundred of one thousand, and a thousand out of ten thousand, to get chop for the people, that dem may do, when dem come to Gibeah of Benjamin, according to all the folly that dem have worked in Israel.”
So all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, knit together as one man.
The tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribe of Benjamin, saying, “What wickedness is this that is happen among you?

Now so deliver up the men, the base fellows, Wey be in Gibeah, that we may put dem to death, and put away evil from Israel.” But Benjamin would not listen to the voice of dem brothers the pikin dem of Israel.
The pikin dem of Benjamin gathered themselves together out of the cities to Gibeah, to go out to battle against the pikin dem of Israel.
The pikin dem of Benjamin were counted on that day out of the cities twenty-six thousand men who drew the sword, besides the inhabitants of Gibeah, who were counted seven hundred chosen men.
Among all these soldiers there were seven hundred chosen men who were left-handed. Every one of dem could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.
The men of Israel, besides Benjamin, were counted four hundred thousand men who drew sword. All these were men of war.
The pikin dem of Israel arose, go up to Bethel, and ask counsel of God. Dem ask, “Who shall go up for us first to battle against the pikin dem of Benjamin?” Baba God talk say, “Judah first.”
The pikin dem of Israel rose up in the morning, and encamped against Gibeah.
The men of Israel go out to battle against Benjamin; and the men of Israel set the battle in array against dem at Gibeah.
The pikin dem of Benjamin come out of Gibeah, and on that day destroyed twenty-two thousand of the Israelite men down to the ground.
The people, the men of Israel, encouraged themselves, and set the battle again in array in the place where dem set themselves in array the first day.

The pikin dem of Israel go up and wept before Baba God until evening; and dem ask of Baba God, saying, “Shall I again draw near to battle against the pikin dem of Benjamin my brother?” Baba God talk say, “Go up against him.”
The pikin dem of Israel come near against the pikin dem of Benjamin the second day.
Benjamin go out against dem out of Gibeah the second day, and destroyed down to the ground of the pikin dem of Israel again eighteen thousand men. All these drew the sword.

Then all the pikin dem of Israel, and all the people, go up, and come to Bethel, and wept, and sat there before Baba God, and fasted that day until evening; then dem offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before Baba God.
The pikin dem of Israel ask Baba God (for the ark of the covenant of God was there in those days,

and Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it in those days), saying, “Shall I yet again go out to battle against the pikin dem of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease?” Baba God talk say, “Go up; for tomorrow I go deliver him into una hand.”
Israel set ambushes all around Gibeah.
The pikin dem of Israel go up against the pikin dem of Benjamin on the third day, and set themselves in array against Gibeah, as at other times.

The pikin dem of Benjamin go out against the people, and were drawn away from the city; and dem began to strike and kill of the people, as at other times, in the highways, of which one goes up to Bethel, and the other to Gibeah, in the field, about thirty men of Israel.
The pikin dem of Benjamin talk say, “Dem be struck down before us, as at the first.” But the pikin dem of Israel talk say, “Make we flee, and draw dem away from the city to the highways.”
All the men of Israel rose up out of dem place, and set themselves in array at Baal Tamar. Then the ambushers of Israel broke out of dem place, even out of Maareh Geba.
Ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel come over against Gibeah, and the battle was severe; but dem didn’t know that disaster was close to dem.
Baba God struck Benjamin before Israel; and the pikin dem of Israel destroyed of Benjamin that day twenty-five thousand one hundred men. All these drew the sword.
So the pikin dem of Benjamin see that dem were struck; for the men of Israel yielded to Benjamin, because dem trusted the ambushers whom dem had set against Gibeah.
The ambushers hurried, and rushed on Gibeah; then the ambushers spread out, and struck all the city with the edge of the sword.
Now the appointed sign between the men of Israel and the ambushers was that dem should make a great cloud of smoke rise up out of the city.

The men of Israel turned in the battle, and Benjamin began to strike and kill of the men of Israel about thirty persons; for dem talk say, “Surely Dem be struck down before us, as in the first battle.”
But when the cloud began to arise up out of the city in a pillar of smoke, the Benjamites looked behind dem; and see am, the whole city go up in smoke to the sky.
The men of Israel turned, and the men of Benjamin were dismayed; for dem see that disaster had come on dem.
So dem turned dem backs before the men of Israel to the way of the wilderness; but the battle follow hard after dem; and people wey come out of the cities destroyed dem in the middle of it.
Dem surrounded the Benjamites, chased dem, and trod dem down at dem resting place, as far as near Gibeah toward the sunrise.
Eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell; all these were men of valor.
Dem turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon; and dem gleaned five thousand men of dem in the highways, and follow hard after dem to Gidom, and struck two thousand men of dem.
So that all who fell that day of Benjamin were twenty-five thousand men who drew the sword. All these were men of valor.
But six hundred men turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, and stayed in the rock of Rimmon four months.

The men of Israel turned again on the pikin dem of Benjamin, and struck dem with the edge of the sword, both the entire city, and the livestock, and all that dem find. Moreover all the cities which dem find dem set on fire.
Now the men of Israel had sworn in Mizpah, saying, “None of us will give his daughter to Benjamin as a wife.”
The people come to Bethel, and sat there until evening before God, and lifted up dem voices, and wept severely.
Dem talk say, “Baba God, the God of Israel, why has this happened in Israel, that there should be one tribe lacking in Israel today?”
On the next day, the people rose early, and built an altar there, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

The pikin dem of Israel talk say, “Wey be there among all the tribes of Israel who didn’t come up in the assembly to Baba God?” For dem had made a great oath concerning him who didn’t come up to Baba God to Mizpah, saying, “He shall surely be put to death.”
The pikin dem of Israel grieved for Benjamin dem brother, and talk say, “E get one tribe cut off from Israel today.
How shall we provide wives for people wey remain, since we have sworn by Baba God that We go not give dem of our daughters to wives?”
Dem talk say, “What one is there of the tribes of Israel who didn’t come up to Baba God to Mizpah?” See am, Nobody come from Jabesh Gilead to the camp to the assembly.
For when the people were counted, see am, there were none of the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead there.

The congregation sent twelve thousand of the most valiant men there, and commanded dem, saying, “Go and strike the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead with the edge of the sword, with the women and the little ones.
This is the thing that you shall do: you shall utterly destroy every male, and every woman who has lain with a man.”
Dem find among the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead four hundred young virgins, who had not known man by lying with him; and dem bring dem to the camp to Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.
The whole congregation sent and spoke to the pikin dem of Benjamin who were in the rock of Rimmon, and proclaimed peace to dem.
Benjamin come back at that time; and dem give dem the women whom dem had saved alive of the women of Jabesh Gilead. There still no be enough for dem.
The people grieved for Benjamin, because Baba God had made a breach in the tribes of Israel.
Then the elders of the congregation talk say, “How shall we provide wives for people wey remain, since the women are destroyed out of Benjamin?”
Dem talk say, “There must be an inheritance for people Wey escaped of Benjamin, that a tribe not be blotted out from Israel.
However we may not give dem wives of our daughters, for the pikin dem of Israel had sworn, saying, ‘Cursed is person wey gives a wife to Benjamin.’”

Dem talk say, “See am, E get a feast of Baba God from year to year in Shiloh, which is on the north of Bethel, on the east side of the highway that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and on the south of Lebonah.”
Dem commanded the pikin dem of Benjamin, saying, “Go and lie in wait in the vineyards,

and see, and see am, if the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in the dances, then come out of the vineyards, and each man catch his wife of the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.

It go be, when dem fathers or dem brothers come to complain to us, that We go say to dem, ‘Grant dem graciously to us, because we didn’t take for each man his wife in battle, neither did you give dem to dem, otherwise you would now be guilty.’”

The pikin dem of Benjamin did so, and take wives for themselves, according to dem number, of people wey danced, whom dem carried off. Dem go and come back to dem inheritance, built the cities, and lived in dem.
The pikin dem of Israel comot from there at that time, every man to his tribe and to his family, and dem each go out from there to his own inheritance.
In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did that which was right in his own eyes.
In the days when the judges judged, there was a famine in the land. A certain man of Bethlehem Judah go to live in the country of Moab, he, and his wife, and his two sons.

The name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi. The names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Bethlehem Judah. Dem come into the country of Moab, and lived there.
Elimelech, Naomi’s husband, died; and she was left with her two sons.
Dem take for themselves wives of the women of Moab. The name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other was Ruth. Dem lived there about ten years.
Mahlon and Chilion both died, and the woman was bereaved of her two pikin dem and of her husband.
Then she arose with her daughters-in-law, that she might return from the country of Moab; for she had heard in the country of Moab how Baba God had visited his people in giving dem bread.
She go out of the place where she was, and her two daughters-in-law with her. Dem go on the way to return to the land of Judah.
Naomi talk say to her two daughters-in-law, “Go, return each of you to her mother’s house. May Baba God deal kindly with you, as you have dealt with the dead, and with me.
May Baba God grant you that you may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband.” Then she kissed dem, and dem lifted up dem voices, and wept.
Dem talk say to her, “No, but We go return with you to una people.”
Naomi talk say, “Go back, my daughters. Why do you want to go with me? Do I still have sons in my womb, that dem may be una husbands?
Go back, my daughters, go una way; for I be too old to have a husband. If I should say, ‘I have hope,’ if I should even have a husband tonight, and should also bear sons;
