would you then wait until dem were grown? Would you then refrain from having husbands? No, my daughters, for it grieves me seriously for una sakes, for Baba God’s hand has gone out against me.”
Dem lifted up dem voices, and wept again; then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth joined with her.
She talk say, “See am, una sister-in-law has gone back to her people, and to her god. Follow una sister-in-law.”
Ruth talk say, “No urge me to leave you, and to return from following you, for where you go, I go go; and where you stay, I go stay. Una people Go be my people, and una God my God.
Where you die, I go die, and there I go be buried. May Baba God do so to me, and more also, if anything but death parts you and me.”
When she see that she was determined to go with her, she stopped urging her.
So dem both go until dem come to Bethlehem. When dem had come to Bethlehem, all the city was excited about dem, and dem ask, “Is this Naomi?”
She tell dem say, “No call me Naomi. Call me Mara; for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
I go out full, and Baba God has bring me home again empty. Why do you call me Naomi, since Baba God has testified against me, and the Almighty has afflicted me?”
So Naomi come back, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, with her, who come back out of the country of Moab. Dem come to Bethlehem For the beginning of barley harvest.
Naomi had a relative of her husband’s, a mighty man of wealth, of the family of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.
Ruth the Moabitess talk say to Naomi, “Let me now go to the field, and glean among the ears of grain after him in whose sight I find favor.” She talk say to her, “Go, my daughter.”
She go, and come and gleaned in the field after the reapers; and she happened to come to the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was of the family of Elimelech.
See am, Boaz come from Bethlehem, and talk say to the reapers, “May Baba God be with you.” Dem answer him, “May Baba God bless you.”
Then Boaz talk say to his worker who was set over the reapers, “Whose young lady is this?”
The worker who was set over the reapers answer, “It is the Moabite lady who come back with Naomi out of the country of Moab.
She talk say, ‘Please let me glean and gather after the reapers among the sheaves.’ So she come, and has continued even from the morning until now, except that she rested a little in the house.”
Then Boaz talk say to Ruth, “Listen, my daughter. No go to glean in another field, and no go from here, but stay here close to my maidens.

Let una eyes be on the field that dem reap, and go after dem. Haven’t I commanded the young men not to touch you? When You be thirsty, go to the vessels, and drink from that which the young men have drawn.”
Then she fell on her face, and bowed sheself to the ground, and talk say to him, “Why have I find favor in una sight, that you should take knowledge of me, since I be a foreigner?”

Boaz answer her, “I Don dey fully told about all that you have done to una mother-in-law since the death of una husband, and how you have left una father and una mother, and the land of una birth, and have come to a people that you didn’t know before.
May Baba God repay una work, and a full reward be given to you from Baba God, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.”
Then she talk say, “Let me find favor in una sight, my lord, because you have comforted me, and because you have spoken kindly to una worker, though I be No be like one of una workers.”

At meal time Boaz talk say to her, “Come here, and eat some bread, and dip una morsel in the vinegar.” She sat beside the reapers, and dem passed her parched grain, and she ate, and was satisfied, and left some of it.
When she had risen up to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying, “Make she glean even among the sheaves, and no reproach her.
Also pull out some for her from the bundles, and leave it. Make she glean, and no rebuke her.”
So she gleaned in the field until evening; and she beat out that which she had gleaned, and it was about an ephah of barley.
She take it up, and go into the city. Then her mother-in-law see what she had gleaned; and she bring out and give to her that which she had left after she had enough.

Her mother-in-law talk say to her, “Where have you gleaned today? Where have you worked? Blessed be person wey noticed you.” She told her mother-in-law with whom she had worked, “The man’s name with whom I worked today is Boaz.”

Naomi talk say to her daughter-in-law, “May he be blessed by Baba God, who has not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead.” Naomi talk say to her, “The man is a close relative to us, one of our near family people.”
Ruth the Moabitess talk say, “Yes, he talk say to me, ‘You shall stay close to my young men, until dem have finished all my harvest.’”
Naomi talk say to Ruth her daughter-in-law, “It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his maidens, and that dem not meet you in any other field.”
So she stayed close to the maidens of Boaz, to glean to the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest; and she lived with her mother-in-law.
Naomi her mother-in-law talk say to her, “My daughter, shall I not seek rest for you, that it may be well with you?
Now no be Boaz our kinsman, with whose maidens you were? See am, he Go be winnowing barley tonight on the threshing floor.
So wash yourself, anoint yourself, get dressed, and go down to the threshing floor, but no make yourself known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.
It go be, when he lies down, that you shall note the place where he is lying. Then you shall go in, uncover his feet, and lay down. Then he will tell you what to do.”
She talk say to her, “All that you say, I go do.”
She go down to the threshing floor, and did everything that her mother-in-law told her.
When Boaz had eaten and drunk, and his heart was merry, he go to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. She come softly, uncovered his feet, and laid down.
At midnight, the man was startled and turned imself; and see am, a woman lay at his feet.
He talk say, “Wey be you?” She answer, “I be Ruth una worker. So spread the corner of una garment over una worker; for You be a near kinsman.”
He talk say, “You be blessed by Baba God, my daughter. You have shown more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, because you didn’t follow young men, whether poor or rich.
Now, my daughter, No fear. I go do to you all that you say; for all the city of my people knows that You be a worthy woman.
Now it is true that I be a near kinsman. However, E get a kinsman nearer than I.

Stay this night, and in the morning, if he will perform for you the part of a kinsman, good. Make e do the kinsman’s duty. But if he No go do the duty of a kinsman for you, then I go do the duty of a kinsman for you, as Baba God lives. Lie down until the morning.”
She lay at his feet until the morning, then she rose up before one could discern another. For he talk say, “Let it not be known that the woman come to the threshing floor.”
He talk say, “Bring the mantle that is on you, and hold it.” She held it; and he measured six measures of barley, and laid it on her; then he go into the city.
When she come to her mother-in-law, she talk say, “How did it go, my daughter?” She told her all that the man had done for her.
She talk say, “He give me these six measures of barley; for he talk say, ‘No go empty to una mother-in-law.’”
Then she talk say, “Wait, my daughter, until you know what will happen; for the man No go rest until he has settled this today.”
Now Boaz go up to the gate, and sat down there. See am, the near kinsman of whom Boaz spoke come by. E tell am say, “Come over here, friend, and sit down!” He turned aside, and sat down.
He take ten men of the elders of the city, and talk say, “Sit down here,” and dem sat down.
He talk say to the near kinsman, “Naomi, who has come back out of the country of Moab, is selling the parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s.

I thought I should tell you, saying, ‘Buy it before people wey sit here, and before the elders of my people.’ If You go redeem it, redeem it; but if You go not redeem it, then tell me, that I may know. For E get Nobody to redeem it besides you; and I be after you.” He talk say, “I go redeem it.”
Then Boaz talk say, “On the day you buy the field from the hand of Naomi, you must buy it also from Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance.”
The near kinsman talk say, “I no fit redeem it for myself, lest I endanger my own inheritance. Take my right of redemption for yourself; for I no fit redeem it.”

Now this was the custom in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning exchanging, to confirm all things: a man take off his shoe, and give it to his neighbor; and this was the way of legalizing transactions in Israel.
So the near kinsman talk say to Boaz, “Buy it for yourself,” then he take off his shoe.
Boaz talk say to the elders, and to all the people, “You be witnesses today, that I have bought all that was Elimelech’s, and all that was Chilion’s and Mahlon’s, from the hand of Naomi.

Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, I have purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance, that the name of the dead may not be cut off from among his brothers, and from the gate of his place. You be witnesses today.”

All the people who were in the gate, and the elders, talk say, “We be witnesses. May Baba God make the woman who has come into una house like Rachel and like Leah, which both built the house of Israel; and treat you worthily in Ephrathah, and be famous in Bethlehem.
Let una house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, of the offspring which Baba God will give you by this young woman.”
So Boaz take Ruth, and she became his wife; and he go in to her, and Baba God enabled her to conceive, and she bore a son.
The women talk say to Naomi, “Blessed be Baba God, who has not left you today without a near kinsman. Let his name be famous in Israel.
He go be to you a restorer of life, and sustain you in una old age, for una daughter-in-law, wey love you, Wey be better to you than seven sons, has given birth to him.”
Naomi take the pikin, and laid him in her bosom, and became nurse to it.
The women, her neighbors, give him a name, saying, “A son is born to Naomi”. Dem named him Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
Now this is the history of the generations of Perez: Perez became the father of Hezron,
and Hezron became the father of Ram, and Ram became the father of Amminadab,
and Amminadab became the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon became the father of Salmon,
and Salmon became the father of Boaz, and Boaz became the father of Obed,
and Obed became the father of Jesse, and Jesse became the father of David.
Now there was a certain man of Ramathaim Zophim, of the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.
He had two wives. The name of one was Hannah, and the name of other Peninnah. Peninnah had pikin dem, but Hannah had no pikin dem.
This man go up out of his city from year to year to worship and to sacrifice to Baba God of Armies in Shiloh. The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, priests to Baba God, were there.
When the day come that Elkanah sacrificed, he give to Peninnah his wife, and to all her sons and her daughters, portions;
but to Hannah he give a double portion, for he love Hannah, but Baba God had shut up her womb.
Her rival provoked her severely, to irritate her, because Baba God had shut up her womb.
As he did so year by year, when she go up to Baba God’s house. Her rival provoked her; so she wept, and didn’t eat.
Elkanah her husband talk say to her, “Hannah, why do you weep? Why no you eat? Why is una heart grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?”
So Hannah rose up after dem had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh. Now Eli the priest was sitting on his seat by the doorpost of Baba God’s temple.
She was in bitterness of soul, and prayed to Baba God, weeping bitterly.

She vowed a vow, and talk say, “Baba God of Armies, if You go indeed look at the suffering of una worker, and remember me, and not forget una worker, but will give to una worker a boy, then I go give him to Baba God all the days of his life, and no razor shall come on his head.”
As she continued praying before Baba God, Eli see her mouth.
Now Hannah spoke in her heart. Only her lips moved, but her voice No be heard. So Eli thought she was drunk.
Eli talk say to her, “How long will you be drunk? Get rid of una wine!”
Hannah answer, “No, my lord, I be a woman of a sorrowful spirit. I have not been drinking wine or strong drink, but I poured out my soul before Baba God.
No consider una worker a wicked woman; for I Don dey speaking out of the abundance of my complaint and my provocation.”
Then Eli answer, “Go in peace; and may the God of Israel grant una petition that you have ask of him.”
She talk say, “Let una worker find favor in una sight.” So the woman go her way, and ate; and her facial expression no be sad any more.
Dem rose up in the morning early, and worshiped before Baba God, and come back, and come to dem house to Ramah. Then Elkanah know Hannah his wife; and Baba God remember her.
When the time had come, Hannah conceived, and bore a son; and she named him Samuel, saying, “Because I have ask him of Baba God.”
The man Elkanah, and all his house, go up to offer to Baba God the yearly sacrifice, and his vow.
But Hannah didn’t go up; for she talk say to her husband, “Not until the pikin is weaned; then I go bring him, that he may appear before Baba God, and stay there forever.”
Elkanah her husband talk say to her, “Do what seems good to you. Wait until you have weaned him; only may Baba God establish his word.” So the woman waited and nursed her son, until she weaned him.
When she had weaned him, she take him up with her, with three bulls, and one ephah of meal, and a bottle of wine, and bring him to Baba God’s house in Shiloh. The pikin was young.
Dem killed the bull, and bring the pikin to Eli.
She talk say, “Oh, my lord, as una soul lives, my lord, I be the woman who stood by you here, praying to Baba God.
I prayed for this pikin; and Baba God has given me my petition which I ask of him.
So I have also given him to Baba God. As long as he lives he is given to Baba God.” He worshiped Baba God there.
Hannah prayed, and talk say: “My heart exults in Baba God! My horn is exalted in Baba God. My mouth is enlarged over my enemies, because I glad well-well in una salvation.
E get Nobody as holy as Baba God, For E get Nobody besides you, nor is there any rock like our God.
“No keep talking so exceedingly proudly. No let arrogance come out of una mouth, For Baba God is a God of knowledge. By him actions are weighed.
“The bows of the mighty men are broken. People wey stumbled are armed with strength.
People wey were full have hired themselves out for bread. People wey were hungry are satisfied. Yes, the barren has borne seven. Person wey has many pikin dem languishes.
“Baba God kills, and makes alive. He brings down to Sheol, and brings up.
Baba God makes poor, and makes rich. He brings low, he also lifts up.

He raises up the poor out of the dust. He lifts up the needy from the dunghill, To make dem sit with princes, and inherit the throne of glory. For the pillars of the earth are Baba God’s. He has set the world on dem.
He will keep the feet of his holy ones, but the wicked go be put to silence in darkness; for no man shall prevail by strength.

People wey strive with Baba God go be broken to pieces. He will thunder against dem in the sky. “Baba God will judge every corner of the world. He will give strength to his king, and exalt the horn of his anointed.”
Elkanah go to Ramah to his house. The pikin served Baba God before Eli the priest.
Now the sons of Eli were wicked men. Dem didn’t know Baba God.
The custom of the priests with the people was that when anyone offered a sacrifice, the priest’s worker come while the meat was boiling, with a fork of three teeth in his hand;
and he stabbed it into the pan, or kettle, or cauldron, or pot. The priest take all that the fork bring up for imself. So dem did in Shiloh to all the Israelites who come there.
Yes, before dem burned the fat, the priest’s worker come, and talk say to the man who sacrificed, “Give meat to roast for the priest; for he No go accept boiled meat from you, but raw.”
If the man talk say to him, “Let the fat be burned first, and then take as much as una soul desires”; then he would say, “No, but you shall give it to me now; and if not, I go take it by force.”
The sin of the young men was plenty well-well before Baba God; for the men despised the offering of Baba God.
But Samuel ministered before Baba God, being a pikin, clothed with a linen ephod.
Moreover his mother made him a little robe, and bring it to him from year to year, when she come up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, and talk say, “May Baba God give you offspring from this woman for the petition which was ask of Baba God.” Then dem go to dem own home.
Baba God visited Hannah, and she conceived, and bore three sons and two daughters. The pikin Samuel grew before Baba God.
Now Eli was very old; and he heard all that his sons did to all Israel, and how that dem slept with the women who served at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
E tell dem say, “Why do you do such things? for I hear of una evil dealings from all this people.
No, my sons; for it is no good report that I hear! You make Baba God’s people disobey.

If one man sins against another, God will judge him; but if a man sins against Baba God, who will intercede for him?” Notwithstanding, dem didn’t listen to the voice of dem father, because Baba God intended to kill dem.
The pikin Samuel grew on, and increased in favor both with Baba God, and also with men.
A man of God come to Eli, and talk say to him, “Baba God says, ‘Did I reveal myself to the house of una father, when dem were in Egypt in bondage to Pharaoh’s house?

Didn’t I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to go up to my altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? Didn’t I give to the house of una father all the offerings of the pikin dem of Israel made by fire?
Why do you kick at my sacrifice and at my offering, which I have commanded in my habitation, and honor una sons above me, to make unaself fat with the best of all the offerings of Israel my people?’

“So Baba God, the God of Israel, says, ‘I talk say indeed that una house, and the house of una father, should walk before me forever.’ But now Baba God says, ‘Far be it from me; for people wey honor me I go honor, and people wey despise me Go be lightly esteemed.
See am, the days come, that I go cut off una arm, and the arm of una father’s house, that there No go be an old man in una house.
You go see the suffering of my habitation, in all the wealth which I go give Israel; and there no go be an old man in una house forever.
The man of yours, whom I no cut off from my altar, will consume una eyes and grieve una heart; and all the increase of una house will die in the flower of dem age.
“‘This Go be the sign to you, that will come on una two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas: in one day Dem go both die.
I go raise me up a faithful priest, that will do according to that which is in my heart and in my mind. I go build him a sure house; and he will walk before my anointed forever.

It will happen, that everyone Wey be left in una house will come and bow down to him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread, and will say, “Please put me into one of the priests’ offices, that I may eat a morsel of bread.”’”
The pikin Samuel ministered to Baba God before Eli. Baba God’s word was precious in those days. There visions No be frequent.
At that time, when Eli was laid down in his place (now his eyes had begun to grow dim, so that he could not see),
and God’s lamp hadn’t yet gone out, and Samuel had laid down in Baba God’s temple, where God’s ark was;
Baba God call Samuel; and he talk say, “Here I be.”
He ran to Eli, and talk say, “Here I be; for you call me.” He talk say, “I didn’t call. Lie down again.” He go and lay down.
Baba God call yet again, “Samuel!” Samuel arose and go to Eli, and talk say, “Here I be; for you call me.” He answer, “I didn’t call, my son. Lie down again.”
Now Samuel didn’t yet know Baba God, neither was Baba God’s word yet revealed to him.
Baba God call Samuel again the third time. He arose and go to Eli, and talk say, “Here I be; for you call me.” Eli perceived that Baba God had call the pikin.
So Eli talk say to Samuel, “Go, lie down. It go be, if he calls you, that you shall say, ‘Speak, Baba God; for una worker hears.’” So Samuel go and lay down in his place.
Baba God come, and stood, and call as at other times, “Samuel! Samuel!” Then Samuel talk say, “Speak; for una worker hears.”
Baba God talk say to Samuel, “See am, I go do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of everyone wey hear it will tingle.
In that day I go perform against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, from the beginning even to the end.
For I have told him that I go judge his house forever, for the wickedness which he know, because his sons bring a curse on themselves, and he didn’t restrain dem.
So I have sworn to the house of Eli, that the wickedness of Eli’s house no go be removed with sacrifice or offering forever.”
Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of Baba God’s house. Samuel feared to show Eli the vision.
Then Eli call Samuel, and talk say, “Samuel, my son!” He talk say, “Here I be.”
He talk say, “Wetin be the thing that he has spoken to you? Please no hide it from me. God do so to you, and more also, if you hide anything from me of all the things that he spoke to you.”
Samuel told him every bit, and hid nothing from him. He talk say, “It is Baba God. Make e do what seems good to him.”
Samuel grew, and Baba God was with him, and let none of his words fall to the ground.
All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba know that Samuel was established to be a prophet of Baba God.
Baba God appeared again in Shiloh; for Baba God revealed imself to Samuel in Shiloh by Baba God’s word.
The word of Samuel come to all Israel. Now Israel go out against the Philistines to battle, and encamped beside Ebenezer; and the Philistines encamped in Aphek.
The Philistines put themselves in array against Israel. When dem joined battle, Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who killed about four thousand men of the army in the field.

When the people had come into the camp, the elders of Israel talk say, “Why has Baba God defeated us today before the Philistines? Make we get the ark of Baba God’s covenant out of Shiloh and bring it to us, that it may come among us, and save us out of the hand of our enemies.”

So the people sent to Shiloh; and dem bring from there the ark of the covenant of Baba God of Armies, who sits above the cherubim: and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
When the ark of Baba God’s covenant come into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, so that the earth rang again.
When the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, dem talk say, “What does the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews mean?” Dem understand that Baba God’s ark had come into the camp.
The Philistines were afraid, for dem talk say, “God has come into the camp.” Dem talk say, “Woe to us! For there has not been such a thing before.
Woe to us! Who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods that struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.
Be strong, and behave like men, O you Philistines, that you not be workers to the Hebrews, as dem Don dey to you. Strengthen unaself like men, and fight!”
The Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and each man fled to his tent. There was a plenty well-well slaughter; for thirty thousand footmen of Israel fell.
God’s ark was taken; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain.
A man of Benjamin ran out of the army, and come to Shiloh the same day, with his clothes torn, and with dirt on his head.
When he come, see am, Eli was sitting on his seat by the road watching; for his heart trembled for God’s ark. When the man come into the city and told about it, all the city cried out.
When Eli heard the noise of the crying, he talk say, “What does the noise of this tumult mean?” The man hurried, and come and told Eli.
Now Eli was ninety-eight years old. His eyes were set, so that he could not see.
The man talk say to Eli, “I be person wey come out of the army, and I fled today out of the army.” He talk say, “How did the matter go, my son?”

Person wey bring the news answer, “Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there Don dey also a great slaughter among the people. Una two sons also, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and God’s ark Don dey captured.”
When he made mention of God’s ark, Eli fell from off his seat backward by the side of the gate; and his neck broke, and he died; for he was an old man, and heavy. He had judged Israel forty years.

His daughter-in-law, Phinehas’ wife, was with pikin, near to be delivered. When she heard the news that God’s ark was taken, and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed sheself and give birth; for her pains come on her.
About the time of her death the women who stood by her talk say to her, “No fear; for you have given birth to a son.” But she didn’t answer, neither did she regard it.
She named the pikin Ichabod, saying, “The glory has comot from Israel”; because God’s ark was taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
She talk say, “The glory has comot from Israel; for God’s ark Don dey taken.”
Now the Philistines had taken God’s ark, and dem bring it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
The Philistines take God’s ark, and bring it into the house of Dagon, and set it by Dagon.
When the people of Ashdod arose early on the next day, see am, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before Baba God’s ark. Dem take Dagon, and set him in his place again.

When dem arose early on the following morning, see am, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before Baba God’s ark; and the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands were cut off on the threshold. Only Dagon’s torso was intact.
So neither the priests of Dagon, nor any who come into Dagon’s house, step on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod, to this day.
But Baba God’s hand was heavy on the people of Ashdod, and he destroyed dem, and struck dem with tumors, even Ashdod and its borders.
When the men of Ashdod see that it was so, dem talk say, “The ark of the God of Israel no go stay with us; for his hand is severe on us, and on Dagon our god.”

Dem sent so and gathered together all the lords of the Philistines, and talk say, “What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?” Dem answer, “Let the ark of the God of Israel be carried over to Gath.” Dem carried the ark of the God of Israel there.

It was so, that after dem had carried it there, Baba God’s hand was against the city with a plenty well-well confusion; and he struck the men of the city, both small and great so that tumors broke out on dem.
So dem sent God’s ark to Ekron. As God’s ark come to Ekron, the Ekronites cried out, saying, “Dem have bring about the ark of the God of Israel to us, to kill us and our people.”

Dem sent so and gathered together all the lords of the Philistines, and dem talk say, “Send the ark of the God of Israel away, and let it go again to its own place, that it not kill us and our people.” For there was a deadly confusion throughout all the city. The hand of God was very heavy there.
The men who didn’t die were struck with the tumors; and the cry of the city go up to heaven.
Baba God’s ark was in the country of the Philistines seven months.
The Philistines call for the priests and the diviners, saying, “What shall we do with Baba God’s ark? Show us how we should send it to its place.”

Dem talk say, “If you send away the ark of the God of Israel, no send it empty; but by all means return a trespass offering to him. Then You go be healed, and it Go be known to you why his hand No be removed from you.”

Then dem talk say, “What should the trespass offering be which we shall return to him?” Dem talk say, “Five golden tumors, and five golden mice, for the number of the lords of the Philistines; for one plague was on you all, and on una lords.

So you shall make images of una tumors, and images of una mice that mar the land; and you shall give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps he will release his hand from you, from una gods, and from una land.
Why then do you harden una hearts, as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened dem hearts? When he had worked wonderfully among dem, didn’t dem let the people go, and dem comot?
“Now so take and prepare unaself a new cart, and two milk cows, on which there has come no yoke; and tie the cows to the cart, and bring dem calves home from dem;
and take Baba God’s ark, and lay it on the cart. Put the jewels of gold, which you return him for a trespass offering, in a coffer by its side; and send it away, that it may go.

See am; if it goes up by the way of its own border to Beth Shemesh, then he has done us this great evil; but if not, then we shall know that it No be his hand that struck us. It was a chance that happened to us.”
The men did so, and take two milk cows, and tied dem to the cart, and shut up dem calves at home.
Dem put Baba God’s ark on the cart, and the coffer with the golden mice and the images of dem tumors.

The cows take the straight way by the way to Beth Shemesh. Dem go along the highway, lowing as dem go, and didn’t turn aside to the right hand or to the left; and the lords of the Philistines go after dem to the border of Beth Shemesh.
The people of Beth Shemesh were reaping dem wheat harvest in the valley; and dem lifted up dem eyes, and see the ark, and rejoiced to see it.
The cart come into the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh, and stood there, where there was a great stone. Then dem split the wood of the cart, and offered up the cows for a burnt offering to Baba God.

The Levites take down Baba God’s ark, and the coffer that was with it, in which the jewels of gold were, and put dem on the great stone; and the men of Beth Shemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices the same day to Baba God.
When the five lords of the Philistines had seen it, dem come back to Ekron the same day.
These are the golden tumors which the Philistines come back for a trespass offering to Baba God: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one;

and the golden mice, according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five lords, both of fortified cities and of country villages, even to the great stone, on which dem set down Baba God’s ark. That stone remains to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh.

He struck of the men of Beth Shemesh, because dem had looked into Baba God’s ark, he struck fifty thousand seventy of the men. Then the people mourned, because Baba God had struck the people with a great slaughter.
The men of Beth Shemesh talk say, “Wey be able to stand before Baba God, this holy God? To whom shall he go up from us?”
Dem sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath Jearim, saying, “The Philistines have bring back Baba God’s ark. Come down, and bring it up to unaself.”
The men of Kiriath Jearim come, and take Baba God’s ark, and bring it into Abinadab’s house on the hill, and consecrated Eleazar his son to keep Baba God’s ark.
From the day that the ark stayed in Kiriath Jearim, the time was long; for it was twenty years; and all the house of Israel lamented after Baba God.

Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, “If You be returning to Baba God with all una heart, then put away the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from among you, and direct una hearts to Baba God, and serve him only; and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.”
Then the pikin dem of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and served Baba God only.
Samuel talk say, “Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I go pray to Baba God for you.”

Dem gathered together to Mizpah, and drew water, and poured it out before Baba God, and fasted on that day, and talk say there, “We have sinned against Baba God.” Samuel judged the pikin dem of Israel in Mizpah.

When the Philistines heard that the pikin dem of Israel were gathered together at Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines go up against Israel. When the pikin dem of Israel heard it, dem were afraid of the Philistines.
The pikin dem of Israel talk say to Samuel, “No stop crying to Baba God our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines.”
Samuel take a suckling lamb, and offered it for a whole burnt offering to Baba God. Samuel cried to Baba God for Israel; and Baba God answer him.

As Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines come near to battle against Israel; but Baba God thundered with a great thunder on that day on the Philistines, and confused dem; and dem were struck down before Israel.
The men of Israel go out of Mizpah, and pursued the Philistines, and struck dem, until dem come under Beth Kar.
Then Samuel take a stone, and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and call its name Ebenezer, saying, “Baba God helped us until now.”
So the Philistines were subdued, and dem stopped coming within the border of Israel. Baba God’s hand was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

The cities which the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron even to Gath; and Israel recovered its border out of the hand of the Philistines. There was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
He go from year to year in a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah; and he judged Israel in all those places.
His return was to Ramah, for his house was there; and he judged Israel there; and he built an altar to Baba God there.
When Samuel was old, he made his sons judges over Israel.
Now the name of his firstborn was Joel; and the name of his second, Abijah. Dem were judges in Beersheba.
His sons didn’t walk in his ways, but turned aside after dishonest gain, take bribes, and perverted justice.
Then all the elders of Israel gathered themselves together and come to Samuel to Ramah.
Dem tell am say, “See am, You be old, and una sons no walk in una ways. Now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.”
But the thing displeased Samuel, when dem talk say, “Give us a king to judge us.” Samuel prayed to Baba God.
Baba God talk say to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of the people in all that dem tell you; for dem have not rejected you, but dem have rejected me as the king over dem.
According to all the works which dem have done since the day that I bring dem up out of Egypt even to this day, in that dem have forsaken me, and served other gods, so dem also do to you.
Now so listen to dem voice. However you shall protest solemnly to dem, and shall show dem the way of the king who will reign over dem.”
Samuel told all Baba God’s words to the people who ask him for a king.

He talk say, “This Go be the way of the king who shall reign over you: he will take una sons, and appoint dem as his workers, for his chariots, and to be his horsemen; and Dem go run before his chariots.

He will appoint dem to him for captains of thousands, and captains of fifties; and he will assign some to plow his ground, and to reap his harvest, and to make his instruments of war, and the instruments of his chariots.
He will take una daughters to be perfumers, to be cooks, and to be bakers.
He will take una fields, una vineyards, and una olive groves, even dem best, and give dem to his workers.
He will take one tenth of una seed, and of una vineyards, and give it to his officers, and to his workers.
He will take una male workers, una female workers, una best young men, and una donkeys, and assign dem to his own work.
He will take one tenth of una flocks; and You go be his workers.
You go cry out in that day because of una king whom You go have chosen for unaself; and Baba God No go answer you in that day.”
But the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel; and dem talk say, “No; but We go have a king over us,
that we also may be like all the nations, and that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles.”
Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he rehearsed dem in the ears of Baba God.
Baba God talk say to Samuel, “Listen to dem voice, and make dem a king.” Samuel talk say to the men of Israel, “Everyone go to una own city.”
Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah, the son of a Benjamite, a mighty man of valor.
He had a son, whose name was Saul, an impressive young man; and there No be among the pikin dem of Israel a better person than he. From his shoulders and upward he was taller than any of the people.
The donkeys of Kish, Saul’s father, were lost. Kish talk say to Saul his son, “Take now one of the workers with you, and arise, go look for the donkeys.”

He passed through the hill country of Ephraim, and passed through the land of Shalishah, but dem didn’t find dem. Then dem passed through the land of Shaalim, and there dem no be there. Then he passed through the land of the Benjamites, but dem didn’t find dem.
When dem had come to the land of Zuph, Saul talk say to his worker who was with him, “Come, and Make we return, lest my father stop caring about the donkeys, and be anxious for us.”

The worker talk say to him, “See am now, E get in this city a man of God, and he is a man Wey be held in honor. All that he says surely happens. Now Make we go there. Perhaps he can tell us which way to go.”
Then Saul talk say to his worker, “But, see am, if we go, what should we bring the man? For the bread is spent in our sacks, and there No be a present to bring to the man of God. What do we have?”
The worker answer Saul again, and talk say, “See am, I have in my hand the fourth part of a shekel of silver. I go give that to the man of God, to tell us our way.”
(In earlier times in Israel, when a man go to inquire of God, he talk say, “Come, and Make we go to the seer”; for person Wey now call a prophet was before call a seer.)
Then Saul talk say to his worker, “Well talk say. Come, Make we go.” So dem go to the city where the man of God was.
As dem go up the ascent to the city, dem find young maidens going out to draw water, and talk say to dem, “Is the seer here?”
Dem answer dem, and talk say, “He is. See am, he is before you. Hurry now, for he has come today into the city; for the people have a sacrifice today in the high place.

As soon as you have come into the city, You go sharp-sharp find him, before he goes up to the high place to eat; for the people No go eat until he come, because he blesses the sacrifice. Afterwards people Wey invited eat. Now so go up; for at this time You go find him.”
Dem go up to the city. As dem come within the city, see am, Samuel come out toward dem, to go up to the high place.
Now Baba God had revealed to Samuel a day before Saul come, saying,

“Tomorrow about this time I go send you a man out of the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him to be prince over my people Israel. He will save my people out of the hand of the Philistines; for I have looked upon my people, because dem cry has come to me.”
When Samuel see Saul, Baba God talk say to him, “See am, the man of whom I spoke to you! He Go get authority over my people.”
Then Saul approached Samuel in the gateway, and talk say, “Please tell me where the seer’s house is.”
Samuel answer Saul, and talk say, “I be the seer. Go up before me to the high place, for You be to eat with me today. In the morning I go let you go, and will tell you all that is in una heart.
As for una donkeys who were lost three days ago, no set una mind on dem; for dem Don dey find. For whom is all that is desirable in Israel? Is it not for you, and for all una father’s house?”
Saul answer, “Am I not a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel? And my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? Why then do you speak to me like this?”
Samuel take Saul and his worker, and bring dem into the guest room, and made dem sit in the best place among people wey were invited, who were about thirty persons.
Samuel talk say to the cook, “Bring the portion which I give you, of which I talk say to you, ‘Set it aside.’”

The cook take up the thigh, and that which was on it, and set it before Saul. Samuel talk say, “See am, that which Don dey reserved! Set it before yourself and eat; because for the appointed time has it been kept for you, for I talk say, ‘I have invited the people.’” So Saul ate with Samuel that day.
When dem had come down from the high place into the city, he talked with Saul on the housetop.
Dem arose early; and about daybreak, Samuel call to Saul on the housetop, saying, “Get up, that I may send you away.” Saul arose, and dem both go outside, he and Samuel, together.

As dem were going down at the end of the city, Samuel talk say to Saul, “Tell the worker to go on ahead of us.” He go ahead, then Samuel talk say, “But stand still first, that I may cause you to hear God’s message.”
Then Samuel take the vial of oil, and poured it on his head, and kissed him, and talk say, “Hasn’t Baba God anointed you to be prince over his inheritance?

When you have comot from me today, then You go find two men by Rachel’s tomb, on the border of Benjamin at Zelzah. Dem go tell you, ‘The donkeys which you go to look for Don dey find; and see am, una father has stopped caring about the donkeys, and is anxious for you, saying, “What shall I do for my son?”’

“Then You go go on forward from there, and You go come to the oak of Tabor. Three men will meet you there going up to God to Bethel, one carrying three young goats, and another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a bottle of wine.
Dem go greet you, and give you two loaves of bread, which you shall receive from dem hand.

“After that You go come to the hill of God, where the garrison of the Philistines is; and it will happen, when you have come there to the city, that You go meet a band of prophets coming down from the high place with a lute, a tambourine, a pipe, and a harp before dem; and Dem go be prophesying.
Then Baba God’s Spirit will come mightily on you, and You go prophesy with dem, and Go be turned into another man.
Let it be, when these signs have come to you, that you do Wetin be appropriate for the occasion; for God is with you.

“Go down ahead of me to Gilgal; and see am, I go come down to you, to offer burnt offerings, and to sacrifice sacrifices of peace offerings. Wait seven days, until I come to you, and show you Wetin You be to do.”
It was so, that when he had turned his back to go from Samuel, God give him another heart; and all those signs happened that day.
When dem come there to the hill, see am, a band of prophets met him; and the Spirit of God come mightily on him, and he prophesied among dem.

When all who know him before see that, see am, he prophesied with the prophets, then the people talk say to each other, “Wetin be this that has come to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?”
One of the same place answer, “Wey be dem father?” So it became a proverb, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
When he had finished prophesying, he come to the high place.
Saul’s uncle talk say to him and to his worker, “Where did you go?” He talk say, “To seek the donkeys. When we see that dem No be find, we come to Samuel.”
Saul’s uncle talk say, “Please tell me what Samuel talk say to you.”
Saul talk say to his uncle, “He told us plainly that the donkeys were find.” But concerning the matter of the kingdom, of which Samuel spoke, he didn’t tell him.
Samuel call the people together to Baba God to Mizpah;

and he talk say to the pikin dem of Israel, “Baba God, the God of Israel, says ‘I bring Israel up out of Egypt, and I delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all the kingdoms that oppressed you.’

But you have today rejected una God, who imself saves you out of all una calamities and una distresses; and you have talk say to him, ‘No! Set a king over us.’ Now so present unaself before Baba God by una tribes, and by una thousands.”
So Samuel bring all the tribes of Israel near, and the tribe of Benjamin was chosen.
He bring the tribe of Benjamin near by dem families; and the family of the Matrites was chosen. Then Saul the son of Kish was chosen; but when dem looked for him, he could not be find.
So dem ask of Baba God further, “Is there yet a man to come here?” Baba God answer, “See am, he has hidden imself among the baggage.”
Dem ran and got him there. When he stood among the people, he was higher than any of the people from his shoulders and upward.
Samuel talk say to all the people, “Do you see him whom Baba God has chosen, that E get Nobody like him among all the people?” All the people shouted, and talk say, “Long live the king!”
Then Samuel told the people the regulations of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book, and laid it up before Baba God. Samuel sent all the people away, every man to his house.
Saul also go to his house to Gibeah; and the army go with him, whose hearts God had touched.
But certain worthless fellows talk say, “How could this man save us?” Dem despised him, and bring him no present. But he held his peace.
Then Nahash the Ammonite come up, and encamped against Jabesh Gilead: and all the men of Jabesh talk say to Nahash, “Make a covenant with us, and We go serve you.”
Nahash the Ammonite talk say to dem, “On this condition I go make it with you, that all una right eyes be gouged out. I go make this dishonor all Israel.”
The elders of Jabesh talk say to him, “Give us seven days, that we may send messengers to all the borders of Israel; and then, if E get Nobody to save us, We go come out to you.”
Then the messengers come to Gibeah of Saul, and spoke these words in the ears of the people, then all the people lifted up dem voice, and wept.
See am, Saul come following the oxen out of the field; and Saul talk say, “What ails the people that dem weep?” Dem told him the words of the men of Jabesh.
God’s Spirit come mightily on Saul when he heard those words, and his anger burned hot.

He take a yoke of oxen, and cut dem in pieces, and sent dem throughout all the borders of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, “Anybody wey no dey come out after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen.” The dread of Baba God fell on the people, and dem come out as one man.
He counted dem in Bezek; and the pikin dem of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.
Dem talk say to the messengers who come, “Tell the men of Jabesh Gilead, ‘Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, You go be rescued.’” The messengers come and told the men of Jabesh; and dem were glad.
So the men of Jabesh talk say, “Tomorrow We go come out to you, and you shall do with us all that seems good to you.”

On the next day, Saul put the people in three companies; and dem come into the middle of the camp in the morning watch, and struck the Ammonites until the heat of the day. People wey remain were scattered, so that no two of dem were left together.
The people talk say to Samuel, “Wey be person wey talk say, ‘Shall Saul reign over us?’ Bring those men, that we may put dem to death!”
Saul talk say, “No man go be put to death today; for today Baba God has rescued Israel.”
Then Samuel talk say to the people, “Come, and Make we go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there.”

All the people go to Gilgal; and there dem made Saul king before Baba God in Gilgal. There dem offered sacrifices of peace offerings before Baba God; and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.
Samuel talk say to all Israel, “See am, I have listened to una voice in all that you talk say to me, and have made a king over you.
Now, see am, the king walks before you. I be old and gray-headed. See am, my sons are with you. I have walked before you from my youth to this day.

Here I be. Witness against me before Baba God, and before his anointed. Whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I defrauded? Whom have I oppressed? Of whose hand have I taken a ransom to make me blind my eyes? I go restore it to you.”
Dem talk say, “You have not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither have you taken anything from anyone’s hand.”
E tell dem say, “Baba God is witness against you, and his anointed is witness today, that you have not find anything in my hand.” Dem talk say, “He is witness.”
Samuel talk say to the people, “It is Baba God who appointed Moses and Aaron, and that bring una fathers up out of the land of Egypt.
Now so stand still, that I may plead with you before Baba God concerning all the righteous acts of Baba God, which he did to you and to una fathers.
“When Jacob had come into Egypt, and una fathers cried to Baba God, then Baba God sent Moses and Aaron, who bring una fathers out of Egypt, and made dem to live in this place.

“But dem forgot Baba God dem God; and he sold dem into the hand of Sisera, captain of the army of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab; and dem fought against dem.

Dem cried to Baba God, and talk say, ‘We have sinned, because we have forsaken Baba God, and have served the Baals and the Ashtaroth: but now deliver us out of the hand of our enemies, and We go serve you.’
Baba God sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered you out of the hand of una enemies on every side; and you lived in safety.
“When you see that Nahash the king of the pikin dem of Ammon come against you, you talk say to me, ‘No, but a king shall reign over us;’ when Baba God una God was una king.
Now so see the king whom you have chosen, and whom you have ask for. See am, Baba God has set a king over you.

If You go fear Baba God, and serve him, and listen to his voice, and not rebel against the commandment of Baba God, then both you and also the king who reigns over You be followers of Baba God una God.
But if You go not listen to Baba God’s voice, but rebel against the commandment of Baba God, then Baba God’s hand Go be against you, as it was against una fathers.
“Now so stand still and see this great thing, which Baba God will do before una eyes.

No be it wheat harvest today? I go call to Baba God, that he may send thunder and rain; and You go know and see that una wickedness is great, which you have done in Baba God’s sight, in asking for a king.”
So Samuel call to Baba God; and Baba God sent thunder and rain that day. Then all the people greatly feared Baba God and Samuel.
All the people talk say to Samuel, “Pray for una workers to Baba God una God, that we not die; for we have added to all our sins this evil, to ask for a king.”
Samuel talk say to the people, “No fear. You have indeed done all this evil; yet no turn aside from following Baba God, but serve Baba God with all una heart.
No turn aside to go after vain things which no fit profit or deliver, for Dem be vain.
For Baba God No go forsake his people for his great name’s sake, because it has pleased Baba God to make you a people for imself.
Moreover as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against Baba God in ceasing to pray for you: but I go instruct you in the good and the right way.
Only fear Baba God, and serve him in truth with all una heart; for consider what great things he has done for you.
But if you keep doing evil, You go be consumed, both you and una king.”
Saul was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned over Israel forty-two years.

Saul chose for imself three thousand men of Israel, of which two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in the Mount of Bethel, and one thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. He sent the rest of the people to dem own tents.
Jonathan struck the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, “Let the Hebrews hear!”
All Israel heard that Saul had struck the garrison of the Philistines, and also that Israel was considered an abomination to the Philistines. The people were gathered together after Saul to Gilgal.

The Philistines assembled themselves together to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand which is on the seashore in plenty people. Dem come up and encamped in Michmash, eastward of Beth Aven.
When the men of Israel see that dem were in trouble (for the people were distressed), then the people hid themselves in caves, in thickets, in rocks, in tombs, and in pits.
Now some of the Hebrews had gone over the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead; but as for Saul, he was yet in Gilgal, and all the people follow him trembling.
He stayed seven days, according to the time set by Samuel; but Samuel didn’t come to Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him.
Saul talk say, “Bring the burnt offering to me here, and the peace offerings.” He offered the burnt offering.
E happen say that as soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, see am, Samuel come; and Saul go out to meet him, that he might greet him.

Samuel talk say, “What have you done?” Saul talk say, “Because I see that the people were scattered from me, and that you didn’t come within the days appointed, and that the Philistines assembled themselves together at Michmash;
so I talk say, ‘Now the Philistines will come down on me to Gilgal, and I haven’t entreated the favor of Baba God.’ I forced myself so, and offered the burnt offering.”

Samuel talk say to Saul, “You have done foolishly. You have not kept the commandment of Baba God una God, which he commanded you; for now Baba God would have established una kingdom on Israel forever.

But now una kingdom No go continue. Baba God has sought for imself a man after his own heart, and Baba God has appointed him to be prince over his people, because you have not kept that which Baba God commanded you.”
Samuel arose, and go from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. Saul counted the people who were present with him, about six hundred men.
Saul, and Jonathan his son, and the people who were present with dem, stayed in Geba of Benjamin; but the Philistines encamped in Michmash.
The raiders come out of the camp of the Philistines in three companies: one company turned to the way that leads to Ophrah, to the land of Shual;
another company turned the way to Beth Horon; and another company turned the way of the border that looks down on the valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.
Now there was no blacksmith find throughout all the land of Israel; for the Philistines talk say, “Lest the Hebrews make themselves swords or spears”;
but all the Israelites go down to the Philistines, each man to sharpen his own plowshare, mattock, ax, and sickle.
The price was one payim each to sharpen mattocks, plowshares, pitchforks, axes, and goads.
So E happen say in the day of battle, that neither sword nor spear was find in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan; but Saul and Jonathan his son had dem.
The garrison of the Philistines go out to the pass of Michmash.

Now it fell on a day, that Jonathan the son of Saul talk say to the young man who bore his armor, “Come, and Make we go over to the Philistines’ garrison, that is on the other side.” But he didn’t tell his father.
Saul stayed in the uttermost part of Gibeah under the pomegranate tree which is in Migron: and the people who were with him were about six hundred men;
including Ahijah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod’s brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the priest of Baba God in Shiloh, wearing an ephod. The people didn’t know that Jonathan was gone.

Between the passes, by which Jonathan sought to go over to the Philistines’ garrison, there was a rocky crag on the one side, and a rocky crag on the other side: and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.
The one crag rose up on the north in front of Michmash, and the other on the south in front of Geba.

Jonathan talk say to the young man who bore his armor, “Come, Make we go over to the garrison of these uncircumcised. It may be that Baba God will work for us; for E get no restraint on Baba God to save by many or by few.”
His armor bearer talk say to him, “Do all that is in una heart. Turn and, see am, I be with you according to una heart.”
Then Jonathan talk say, “See am, We go pass over to the men, and We go reveal ourselves to dem.
If dem say thus to us, ‘Wait until we come to you!’ then We go stand still in our place, and No go go up to dem.
But if dem say this, ‘Come up to us!’ then We go go up; for Baba God has delivered dem into our hand. This go be the sign to us.”
Both of dem revealed themselves to the garrison of the Philistines: and the Philistines talk say, “See am, the Hebrews are coming out of the holes where dem had hidden themselves!”

The men of the garrison answer Jonathan and his armor bearer, and talk say, “Come up to us, and We go show you something!” Jonathan talk say to his armor bearer, “Come up after me; for Baba God has delivered dem into the hand of Israel.”
Jonathan climbed up on his hands and on his feet, and his armor bearer after him: and dem fell before Jonathan; and his armor bearer killed dem after him.
That first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armor bearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were half a furrow’s length in an acre of land.
There was a trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people; the garrison, and the raiders, also trembled; and the earth quaked, so there was an exceedingly great trembling.
The watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and see am, the plenty people melted away and scattered.
Then Saul talk say to the people who were with him, “Count now, and see Wey be missing from us.” When dem had counted, see am, Jonathan and his armor bearer No be there.
Saul talk say to Ahijah, “Bring God’s ark here.” For God’s ark was with the pikin dem of Israel at that time.
While Saul talked to the priest, the tumult that was in the camp of the Philistines go on and increased; and Saul talk say to the priest, “Withdraw una hand!”
Saul and all the people who were with him were gathered together, and come to the battle; and see am, dem were all striking each other with dem swords in plenty well-well confusion.
Now the Hebrews who were with the Philistines before, and who go up with dem into the camp, from all around, even dem also turned to be with the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.
Likewise all the men of Israel who had hidden themselves in the hill country of Ephraim, when dem heard that the Philistines fled, even dem also follow hard after dem in the battle.
So Baba God saved Israel that day; and the battle passed over by Beth Aven.

The men of Israel were distressed that day; for Saul had adjured the people, saying, “Cursed is the man who eats any chop until it is evening, and I be avenged of my enemies.” So none of the people tasted chop.
All the people come into the forest; and there was honey on the ground.
When the people had come to the forest, see am, honey was dripping, but Nobody put his hand to his mouth; for the people feared the oath.

But Jonathan didn’t hear when his father commanded the people with the oath. So he put out the end of the rod who was in his hand, and dipped it in the honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes brightened.
Then one of the people answer, and talk say, “Una father directly commanded the people with an oath, saying, ‘Cursed is the man who eats chop today.’” The people were faint.
Then Jonathan talk say, “My father has troubled the land. Please look how my eyes have brightened, because I tasted a little of this honey.
How much more, if perhaps the people had eaten freely today of the plunder of dem enemies which dem find? For now has there been no great slaughter among the Philistines.”
Dem struck the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon. The people were very faint;
and the people pounced on the plunder, and take sheep, cattle, and calves, and killed dem on the ground; and the people ate dem with the blood.
Then dem told Saul, saying, “See am, the people are sinning against Baba God, in that dem eat meat with the blood.” He talk say, “You have dealt treacherously. Roll a large stone to me today!”

Saul talk say, “Disperse unaself among the people, and tell dem, ‘Every man bring me here his ox, and every man his sheep, and kill dem here, and eat; and no sin against Baba God in eating meat with the blood.’” All the people bring every man his ox with him that night, and killed dem there.
Saul built an altar to Baba God. This was the first altar that he built to Baba God.

Saul talk say, “Make we go down after the Philistines by night, and take plunder among dem until the morning light, and Make we not leave a man of dem.” Dem talk say, “Do Anything wey seems good to you.” Then the priest talk say, “Make we draw near here to God.”
Saul ask counsel of God, “Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will you deliver dem into the hand of Israel?” But he didn’t answer him that day.
Saul talk say, “Draw near here, all you chiefs of the people; and know and see in which this sin Don dey today.
For, as Baba God lives, who saves Israel, though it is in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die.” But there No be a man among all the people who answer him.
Then he talk say to all Israel, “You be on one side, and I and Jonathan my son Go be on the other side.” The people talk say to Saul, “Do what seems good to you.”
So Saul talk say to Baba God, the God of Israel, “Show the right.” Jonathan and Saul were chosen, but the people escaped.
Saul talk say, “Throw lots between me and Jonathan my son.” Jonathan was selected.

Then Saul talk say to Jonathan, “Tell me Wetin you have done!” Jonathan told him, and talk say, “I certainly did taste a little honey with the end of the rod that was in my hand; and see am, I must die.”
Saul talk say, “God do so and more also; for you shall surely die, Jonathan.”

The people talk say to Saul, “Shall Jonathan die, who has worked this great salvation in Israel? Far from it! As Baba God lives, there no go one hair of his head fall to the ground; for he has worked with God today!” So the people rescued Jonathan, that he didn’t die.
Then Saul go up from following the Philistines; and the Philistines go to dem own place.

Now when Saul had taken the kingdom over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side, against Moab, and against the pikin dem of Ammon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines. Anywhere wey he turned imself, he defeated dem.
He did valiantly, and struck the Amalekites, and delivered Israel out of the hands of people wey plundered dem.
Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua; and the names of his two daughters were these: the name of the firstborn Merab, and the name of the younger Michal.
The name of Saul’s wife was Ahinoam the daughter of Ahimaaz. The name of the captain of his army was Abner the son of Ner, Saul’s uncle.
Kish was the father of Saul; and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.
There was severe war against the Philistines all the days of Saul; and when Saul see any mighty man, or any valiant man, he take him into his service.
Samuel talk say to Saul, “Baba God sent me to anoint you to be king over his people, over Israel. Now so listen to the voice of Baba God’s words.
Baba God of Armies says, ‘I remember what Amalek did to Israel, how he set imself against him on the way, when he come up out of Egypt.
Now go and strike Amalek, and utterly destroy all that dem have, and no spare dem; but kill both man and woman, infant and nursing baby, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.’”
Saul summoned the people, and counted dem in Telaim, two hundred thousand footmen, and ten thousand men of Judah.
Saul come to the city of Amalek, and set an ambush in the valley.

Saul talk say to the Kenites, “Go, depart, go down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with dem; for you showed kindness to all the pikin dem of Israel, when dem come up out of Egypt.” So the Kenites comot from among the Amalekites.
Saul struck the Amalekites, from Havilah as you go to Shur, that is before Egypt.
He take Agag the king of the Amalekites alive, and utterly destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword.

But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep, of the cattle, and of the fat calves, and the lambs, and all that was good, and No be willing to utterly destroy dem; but everything that was vile and refuse, that dem destroyed utterly.
Then Baba God’s word come to Samuel, saying,
“It grieves me that I have set up Saul to be king; for he has turned back from following me, and has not performed my commandments.” Samuel was angry; and he cried to Baba God all night.
Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning; and Samuel was told, saying, “Saul come to Carmel, and see am, he set up a monument for imself, and turned, and passed on, and go down to Gilgal.”
Samuel come to Saul; and Saul talk say to him, “You be blessed by Baba God! I have performed the commandment of Baba God.”
Samuel talk say, “Then what does this bleating of the sheep in my ears, and the lowing of the cattle which I hear mean?”
Saul talk say, “Dem have bring dem from the Amalekites; for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the cattle, to sacrifice to Baba God una God. We have utterly destroyed the rest.”
Then Samuel talk say to Saul, “Stay, and I go tell you what Baba God talk say to me last night.” E tell am say, “Say on.”
Samuel talk say, “Though you were little in una own sight, no be you made the head of the tribes of Israel? Baba God anointed you king over Israel;
and Baba God sent you on a journey, and talk say, ‘Go, and utterly destroy the sinners the Amalekites, and fight against dem until Dem be consumed.’
Why then didn’t you obey Baba God’s voice, but take the plunder, and did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight?”
Saul talk say to Samuel, “But I have obeyed Baba God’s voice, and have gone the way which Baba God sent me, and have bring Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.
But the people take of the plunder, sheep and cattle, the chief of the devoted things, to sacrifice to Baba God una God in Gilgal.”
Samuel talk say, “Has Baba God as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying Baba God’s voice? See am, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to listen than the fat of rams.
For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as idolatry and teraphim. Because you have rejected Baba God’s word, he has also rejected you from being king.”
Saul talk say to Samuel, “I have sinned; for I have transgressed the commandment of Baba God, and una words, because I feared the people, and obeyed dem voice.
Now so, please pardon my sin, and turn again with me, that I may worship Baba God.”
Samuel talk say to Saul, “I go not return with you; for you have rejected Baba God’s word, and Baba God has rejected you from being king over Israel.”
As Samuel turned around to go away, Saul grabbed the skirt of his robe, and it tore.
Samuel talk say to him, “Baba God has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today, and has given it to a neighbor of yours Wey be better than you.
Also the Strength of Israel No go lie nor repent; for he No be a man, that he should repent.”
Then he talk say, “I have sinned; yet please honor me now before the elders of my people, and before Israel, and come back with me, that I may worship Baba God una God.”
So Samuel go back with Saul; and Saul worshiped Baba God.
Then Samuel talk say, “Bring Agag the king of the Amalekites here to me!” Agag come to him cheerfully. Agag talk say, “Surely the bitterness of death is past.”
Samuel talk say, “As una sword has made women childless, so una mother Go be childless among women!” Then Samuel cut Agag in pieces before Baba God in Gilgal.
Then Samuel go to Ramah; and Saul go up to his house to Gibeah of Saul.
Samuel come no more to see Saul until the day of his death; for Samuel mourned for Saul: and Baba God grieved that he had made Saul king over Israel.

Baba God talk say to Samuel, “How long will you mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him from being king over Israel? Fill una horn with oil, and go. I go send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite; for I have provided a king for myself among his sons.”
Samuel talk say, “How can I go? If Saul hears it, he will kill me.” Baba God talk say, “Take a heifer with you, and say, I have come to sacrifice to Baba God.
Call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I go show you Wetin you shall do. You shall anoint to me him whom I name to you.”
Samuel did that which Baba God spoke, and come to Bethlehem. The elders of the city come to meet him trembling, and talk say, “Do you come peaceably?”
He talk say, “Peaceably; I have come to sacrifice to Baba God. Sanctify unaself, and come with me to the sacrifice.” He sanctified Jesse and his sons, and call dem to the sacrifice.
When dem had come, he looked at Eliab, and talk say, “Surely Baba God’s anointed is before him.”

But Baba God talk say to Samuel, “No look on his face, or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for I no see as man sees. For man looks at the outward appearance, but Baba God looks at the heart.”
Then Jesse call Abinadab, and made him pass before Samuel. He talk say, “Baba God has not chosen this one, either.”
Then Jesse made Shammah to pass by. He talk say, “Baba God has not chosen this one, either.”
Jesse made seven of his sons to pass before Samuel. Samuel talk say to Jesse, “Baba God has not chosen these.”

Samuel talk say to Jesse, “Are all una pikin dem here?” He talk say, “There remains yet the youngest. See am, he is keeping the sheep.” Samuel talk say to Jesse, “Send and get him, for We go not sit down until he comes here.”
He sent, and bring him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. Baba God talk say, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”
Then Samuel take the horn of oil, and anointed him in the middle of his brothers. Then Baba God’s Spirit come mightily on David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up and go to Ramah.
Now Baba God’s Spirit comot from Saul, and an evil spirit from Baba God troubled him.
Saul’s workers talk say to him, “See now, an evil spirit from God troubles you.

Let our lord now command una workers Wey be in front of you to seek out a man Wey be a skillful player on the harp. Then when the evil spirit from God is on you, he will play with his hand, and You go be well.”
Saul talk say to his workers, “Provide me now a man who can play well, and bring him to me.”

Then one of the young men answer, and talk say, “See am, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite Wey be skillful in playing, a mighty man of valor, a man of war, prudent in speech, and a handsome person; and Baba God is with him.”
So Saul sent messengers to Jesse, and talk say, “Send me David una son, Wey be with the sheep.”
Jesse take a donkey loaded with bread, and a bottle of wine, and a young goat, and sent dem by David his son to Saul.
David come to Saul, and stood before him. He love him greatly; and he became his armor bearer.
Saul sent to Jesse, saying, “Please let David stand before me; for he has find favor in my sight.”
When the spirit from God was on Saul, David take the harp, and played with his hand; so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit comot from him.
Now the Philistines gathered together dem armies to battle; and dem were gathered together at Socoh, which belongs to Judah, and encamped between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephesdammim.
Saul and the men of Israel were gathered together, and encamped in the valley of Elah, and set the battle in array against the Philistines.
The Philistines stood on the mountain on the one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other side: and there was a valley between dem.
A champion out of the camp of the Philistines named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span go out.
He had a helmet of brass on his head, and he wore a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of brass.
He had brass shin armor on his legs, and a brass javelin between his shoulders.
The staff of his spear was like a weaver’s beam; and his spear’s head weighed six hundred shekels of iron. His shield bearer go before him.

He stood and cried to the armies of Israel, and talk say to dem, “Why have you come out to set una battle in array? Am I not a Philistine, and you workers to Saul? Choose a man for unaself, and Make e come down to me.
If he is able to fight with me and kill me, then will we be una workers; but if I prevail against him and kill him, then You go be our workers and serve us.”
The Philistine talk say, “I defy the armies of Israel today! Give me a man, that we may fight together!”
When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, dem were dismayed, and greatly afraid.
Now David was the son of that Ephrathite of Bethlehem Judah, whose name was Jesse; and he had eight sons. The man was an elderly old man in the days of Saul.
The three oldest sons of Jesse had gone after Saul to the battle: and the names of his three sons who go to the battle were Eliab the firstborn, and next to him Abinadab, and the third Shammah.
David was the youngest; and the three oldest follow Saul.
Now David go back and forth from Saul to feed his father’s sheep at Bethlehem.
The Philistine come near morning and evening, and presented imself forty days.
Jesse talk say to David his son, “Now take for una brothers an ephah of this parched grain, and these ten loaves, and carry dem sharp-sharp to the camp to una brothers;
and bring these ten cheeses to the captain of dem thousand, and see how una brothers are doing, and bring back news.”
Now Saul, and dem, and all the men of Israel, were in the valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.

David rose up early in the morning, and left the sheep with a keeper, and take and go, as Jesse had commanded him. He come to the place of the wagons, as the army which was going out to the fight shouted for the battle.
Israel and the Philistines put the battle in array, army against army.
David left his baggage in the hand of the keeper of the baggage, and ran to the army, and come and greeted his brothers.
As he talked with dem, see am, the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, come up out of the ranks of the Philistines, and talk say the same words; and David heard dem.
All the men of Israel, when dem see the man, fled from him, and were terrified.

The men of Israel talk say, “Have you seen this man who has come up? He has surely come up to defy Israel. The king will give great riches to the man who kills him, and will give him his daughter, and make his father’s house free in Israel.”

David spoke to the men who stood by him, saying, “What go be done to the man who kills this Philistine, and takes away the reproach from Israel? For Wey be this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?”
The people answer him in this way, saying, “So shall it be done to the man who kills him.”

Eliab his oldest brother heard when he spoke to the men; and Eliab’s anger burned against David, and he talk say, “Why have you come down? With whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know una pride, and the naughtiness of una heart; for you have come down that you might see the battle.”
David talk say, “What have I now done? Is there not a cause?”
He turned away from him toward another, and spoke like that again; and the people answer him again the same way.
When the words were heard which David spoke, dem rehearsed dem before Saul; and he sent for him.
David talk say to Saul, “Let no man’s heart fail because of him. Una worker will go and fight with this Philistine.”
Saul talk say to David, “You No be able to go against this Philistine to fight with him; for You be but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.”
David talk say to Saul, “Una worker was keeping his father’s sheep; and when a lion or a bear come, and take a lamb out of the flock,
I go out after him, and struck him, and rescued it out of his mouth. When he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and struck him, and killed him.
Una worker struck both the lion and the bear. This uncircumcised Philistine go be as one of dem, since he has defied the armies of the living God.”

David talk say, “Baba God who delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.” Saul talk say to David, “Go! Baba God Go be with you.”
Saul dressed David with his clothing. He put a helmet of brass on his head, and he clad him with a coat of mail.
David strapped his sword on his clothing, and he tried to move; for he had not tested it. David talk say to Saul, “I no fit go with these; for I have not tested dem.” Then David take dem off.

He take his staff in his hand, and chose for imself five smooth stones out of the brook, and put dem in the pouch of his shepherd’s bag which he had. His sling was in his hand; and he come near to the Philistine.
The Philistine walked and come near to David; and the man who bore the shield go before him.
When the Philistine looked around, and see David, he disdained him; for he was but a youth, and ruddy, and had a good looking face.
The Philistine talk say to David, “Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?” The Philistine cursed David by his gods.
The Philistine talk say to David, “Come to me, and I go give una flesh to the birds of the sky, and to the animals of the field.”

Then David talk say to the Philistine, “You come to me with a sword, with a spear, and with a javelin; but I come to you in the name of Baba God of Armies, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.

Today, Baba God will deliver you into my hand. I go strike you, and take una head from off you. I go give the dead bodies of the army of the Philistines today to the birds of the sky, and to the wild animals of the earth; that all the earth may know that E get a God in Israel,
and that all this assembly may know that Baba God no dey save with sword and spear; for the battle is Baba God’s, and he will give you into our hand.”
When the Philistine arose, and walked and come near to meet David, David hurried, and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine.
David put his hand in his bag, take a stone, and slung it, and struck the Philistine in his forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the earth.
So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and struck the Philistine, and killed him; but there was no sword in the hand of David.
Then David ran, stood over the Philistine, take his sword, drew it out of its sheath, killed him, and cut off his head with it. When the Philistines see that dem champion was dead, dem fled.

The men of Israel and of Judah arose and shouted, and pursued the Philistines as far as Gai and to the gates of Ekron. The wounded of the Philistines fell down by the way to Shaaraim, even to Gath and to Ekron.
