The pikin dem of Israel come back from chasing after the Philistines and dem plundered dem camp.
David take the head of the Philistine, and bring it to Jerusalem; but he put his armor in his tent.
When Saul see David go out against the Philistine, he talk say to Abner, the captain of the army, “Abner, whose son is this youth?” Abner talk say, “As una soul lives, O king, I no fit tell.”
The king talk say, “Inquire whose son the young man is!”
As David come back from the slaughter of the Philistine, Abner take him and bring him before Saul with the head of the Philistine in his hand.
Saul talk say to him, “Whose son are you, you young man?” David answer, “I be the son of una worker Jesse the Bethlehemite.”
When he had finished speaking to Saul, the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan love him as his own soul.
Saul take him that day, and would Make e go no more home to his father’s house.
Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he love him as his own soul.
Jonathan stripped imself of the robe that was on him, and give it to David, and his clothing, even including his sword, his bow, and his sash.
David go out Anywhere wey Saul sent him, and behaved imself wisely; and Saul set him over the men of war. It was good in the sight of all the people, and also in the sight of Saul’s workers.

As dem come, when David come back from the slaughter of the Philistine, the women come out of all the cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet king Saul, with tambourines, with gladness, and with instruments of music.
The women sang to each other as dem played, and talk say, “Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.”
Saul was very angry, and this saying displeased him. He talk say, “Dem have ascribed to David ten thousands, and to me dem have ascribed only thousands. What can he have more but the kingdom?”
Saul watched David from that day and forward.
On the next day, an evil spirit from God come mightily on Saul, and he prophesied in the middle of the house. David played with his hand, as he did day by day. Saul had his spear in his hand;
and Saul threw the spear, for he talk say, “I go pin David even to the wall!” David escaped from his presence twice.
Saul was afraid of David, because Baba God was with him, and had comot from Saul.
So Saul removed him from his presence, and made him his captain over a thousand; and he go out and come in before the people.
David behaved imself wisely in all his ways; and Baba God was with him.
When Saul see that he behaved imself very wisely, he stood in awe of him.
But all Israel and Judah love David; for he go out and come in before dem.

Saul talk say to David, “See am, my elder daughter Merab, I go give her to you as wife. Only be valiant for me, and fight Baba God’s battles.” For Saul talk say, “No let my hand be on him, but let the hand of the Philistines be on him.”
David talk say to Saul, “Who am I, and Wetin be my life, or my father’s family in Israel, that I should be son-in-law to the king?”
But at the time when Merab, Saul’s daughter, should Don dey given to David, she was given to Adriel the Meholathite as wife.
Michal, Saul’s daughter, love David; and dem told Saul, and the thing pleased him.

Saul talk say, I go give her to him, that she may be a snare to him, and that the hand of the Philistines may be against him. So Saul talk say to David, “You shall today be my son-in-law a second time.”
Saul commanded his workers, “Talk with David secretly, and say, ‘See am, the king has delight in you, and all his workers love you. Now so be the king’s son-in-law.’”
Saul’s workers spoke those words in the ears of David. David talk say, “Does it seem to you a light thing to be the king’s son-in-law, since I be a poor man, and lightly esteemed?”
The workers of Saul told him, saying, “David spoke like this.”

Saul talk say, “Tell David, ‘The king desires no dowry except one hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to be avenged of the king’s enemies.’” Now Saul thought he would make David fall by the hand of the Philistines.
When his workers told David these words, it pleased David well to be the king’s son-in-law. Before the deadline,

David arose and go, he and his men, and killed two hundred men of the Philistines. Then David bring dem foreskins, and dem give dem in full number to the king, that he might be the king’s son-in-law. Then Saul give him Michal his daughter as wife.
Saul see and know that Baba God was with David; and Michal, Saul’s daughter, love him.
Saul was even more afraid of David; and Saul was David’s enemy continually.
Then the princes of the Philistines go out; and as often as dem go out, David behaved imself more wisely than all the workers of Saul, so that his name was highly esteemed.
Saul spoke to Jonathan his son, and to all his workers, that dem should kill David. But Jonathan, Saul’s son, greatly delighted in David.
Jonathan told David, saying, “Saul my father seeks to kill you. Now so, please take care of yourself in the morning, and live in a secret place, and hide yourself.
I go go out and stand beside my father in the field where You be, and I go talk with my father about you; and if I see anything, I go tell you.”

Jonathan spoke good of David to Saul his father, and talk say to him, “No let the king sin against his worker, against David; because he has not sinned against you, and because his works Don dey very good toward you;

for he put his life in his hand, and struck the Philistine, and Baba God worked a great victory for all Israel. You see it, and rejoiced. Why then will you sin against innocent blood, to kill David without a cause?”
Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan: and Saul swore, “As Baba God lives, he no go be put to death.”
Jonathan call David, and Jonathan showed him all those things. Then Jonathan bring David to Saul, and he was in his presence, as before.
There was war again. David go out, and fought with the Philistines, and killed dem with a great slaughter; and dem fled before him.
An evil spirit from Baba God was on Saul, as he sat in his house with his spear in his hand; and David was playing with his hand.
Saul sought to pin David to the wall with the spear; but he slipped away out of Saul’s presence, and he stuck the spear into the wall. David fled, and escaped that night.
Saul sent messengers to David’s house, to watch him, and to kill him in the morning. Michal, David’s wife, told him, saying, “If you no save una life tonight, tomorrow You go be killed.”
So Michal let David down through the window. He go away, fled, and escaped.
Michal take the teraphim, and laid it in the bed, and put a pillow of goats’ hair at its head, and covered it with clothes.
When Saul sent messengers to take David, she talk say, “He is sick.”
Saul sent the messengers to see David, saying, “Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may kill him.”
When the messengers come in, see am, the teraphim was in the bed, with the pillow of goats’ hair at its head.
Saul talk say to Michal, “Why have you deceived me thus, and let my enemy go, so that he is escaped?” Michal answer Saul, “He talk say to me, ‘Let me go! Why should I kill you?’”
Now David fled and escaped, and come to Samuel at Ramah, and told him all that Saul had done to him. He and Samuel go and lived in Naioth.
Saul was told, saying, “See am, David is at Naioth in Ramah.”
Saul sent messengers to seize David: and when dem see the company of the prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing as head over dem, God’s Spirit come on Saul’s messengers, and dem also prophesied.
When Saul was told, he sent other messengers, and dem also prophesied. Saul sent messengers again the third time, and dem also prophesied.
Then he also go to Ramah, and come to the great well that is in Secu: and he ask, “Where are Samuel and David?” One talk say, “See am, Dem be at Naioth in Ramah.”
He go there to Naioth in Ramah. Then God’s Spirit come on him also, and he go on, and prophesied, until he come to Naioth in Ramah.
He also stripped off his clothes, and he also prophesied before Samuel, and lay down naked all that day and all that night. So dem say, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
David fled from Naioth in Ramah, and come and talk say before Jonathan, “What have I done? Wetin be my wickedness? Wetin be my sin before una father, that he seeks my life?”
E tell am say, “Far from it; You go not die. See am, my father does nothing either great or small, but that he discloses it to me. Why would my father hide this thing from me? It No be so.”

David swore moreover, and talk say, “Una father knows well that I have find favor in una eyes; and he says, ‘No let Jonathan know this, lest he be grieved:’ but truly as Baba God lives, and as una soul lives, E get but a step between me and death.”
Then Jonathan talk say to David, “Anything wey una soul desires, I go even do it for you.”
David talk say to Jonathan, “See am, tomorrow is the new moon, and I no suppose fail to dine with the king; but let me go, that I may hide myself in the field to the third day at evening.
If una father misses me at all, then say, ‘David earnestly ask leave of me that he might run to Bethlehem his city; for it is the yearly sacrifice there for all the family.’
If he says, ‘It is well;’ una worker go get peace: but if he is angry, then know that evil is determined by him.
So deal kindly with una worker; for you have bring una worker into a covenant of Baba God with you; but if E get wickedness in me, kill me yourself; for why should you bring me to una father?”
Jonathan talk say, “Far be it from you; for if I should at all know that evil were determined by my father to come on you, then wouldn’t I tell una that?”
Then David talk say to Jonathan, “Who will tell me if perchance una father answers you roughly?”
Jonathan talk say to David, “Come, and Make we go out into the field.” Dem both go out into the field.

Jonathan talk say to David, “By Baba God, the God of Israel, when I have sounded my father about this time tomorrow, or the third day, see am, if E get good toward David, no go I then send to you, and disclose it to you?

Baba God do so to Jonathan, and more also, should it please my father to do you evil, if I no disclose it to you, and send you away, that you may go in peace. May Baba God be with you, as he Don dey with my father.
You no go only while yet I live show me the loving kindness of Baba God, that I not die;
but you shall also not cut off una kindness from my house forever; no, not when Baba God has cut off every one of the enemies of David from the surface of the earth.”
So Jonathan made a covenant with David’s house, saying, “Baba God will require it at the hand of David’s enemies.”
Jonathan caused David to swear again, for the love that he had to him; for he love him as he love his own soul.
Then Jonathan talk say to him, “Tomorrow is the new moon, and You go be missed, because una seat Go be empty.
When you have stayed three days, go down sharp-sharp, and come to the place where you hid yourself when this started, and remain by the stone Ezel.
I go shoot three arrows on its side, as though I shot at a mark.

See am, I go send the boy, saying, ‘Go, find the arrows!’ If I tell the boy, ‘See am, the arrows are on this side of you. Take dem;’ then come; for E get peace to you and no danger, as Baba God lives.
But if I say this to the boy, ‘See am, the arrows are beyond you;’ then go una way; for Baba God has sent you away.
Concerning the matter which you and I have spoken of, see am, Baba God is between you and me forever.”
So David hid imself in the field. When the new moon had come, the king sat imself down to eat chop.
The king sat on his seat, as at other times, even on the seat by the wall; and Jonathan stood up, and Abner sat by Saul’s side, but David’s place was empty.
Nevertheless Saul didn’t say anything that day, for he thought, “Something has happened to him. He No be clean. Surely he No be clean.”
On the next day after the new moon, the second day, David’s place was empty. Saul talk say to Jonathan his son, “Why no dey the son of Jesse come to eat, either yesterday, or today?”
Jonathan answer Saul, “David earnestly ask permission of me to go to Bethlehem.

He talk say, ‘Please let me go, for our family has a sacrifice in the city. My brother has commanded me to be there. Now, if I have find favor in una eyes, please let me go away and see my brothers.’ So he has not come to the king’s table.”

Then Saul’s anger burned against Jonathan, and E tell am say, “You son of a perverse rebellious woman, no I know that you have chosen the son of Jesse to una own shame, and to the shame of una mother’s nakedness?
For as long as the son of Jesse lives on the earth, You go not be established, nor will una kingdom. So now send and bring him to me, for he shall surely die!”
Jonathan answer Saul his father, and talk say to him, “Why should he be put to death? What has he done?”
Saul throw his spear at him to strike him. By this Jonathan know that his father was determined to put David to death.
So Jonathan arose from the table in fierce anger, and ate no chop the second day of the month; for he was grieved for David, because his father had treated him shamefully.
In the morning, Jonathan go out into the field at the time appointed with David, and a little boy with him.
He talk say to his boy, “Run, find now the arrows which I shoot.” As the boy ran, he shot an arrow beyond him.
When the boy had come to the place of the arrow which Jonathan had shot, Jonathan cried after the boy, and talk say, “No be the arrow beyond you?”
Jonathan cried after the boy, “Go fast! Hurry! No delay!” Jonathan’s boy gathered up the arrows, and come to his master.
But the boy didn’t know anything. Only Jonathan and David know the matter.
Jonathan give his weapons to his boy, and talk say to him, “Go, carry dem to the city.”
As soon as the boy was gone, David arose out of the south, and fell on his face to the ground, and bowed imself three times. Dem kissed each other, and wept one with another, and David wept the most.

Jonathan talk say to David, “Go in peace, because we have both sworn in Baba God’s name, saying, ‘Baba God is between me and you, and between my offspring and una offspring, forever.’” He arose and comot; and Jonathan go into the city.
Then David come to Nob to Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech come to meet David trembling, and talk say to him, “Why are you alone, and no man with you?”

David talk say to Ahimelech the priest, “The king has commanded me to do something, and has talk say to me, ‘Let Nobody know anything about the business about which I send you, and what I have commanded you. I have sent the young men to a certain place.’
Now so Wetin be under una hand? Please give me five loaves of bread in my hand, or Anything wey is available.”
The priest answer David, and talk say, “I have no common bread, but E get holy bread; if only the young men have kept themselves from women.”

David answer the priest, and talk say to him, “Truly, women Don dey kept from us as usual these three days. When I come out, the vessels of the young men were holy, though it was only a common journey. How much more then today shall dem vessels be holy?”
So the priest give him holy bread; for there was no bread there but the show bread that was taken from before Baba God, to put hot bread in the day when it was taken away.
Now a certain man of the workers of Saul was there that day, detained before Baba God; and his name was Doeg the Edomite, the best of the herdsmen who belonged to Saul.
David talk say to Ahimelech, “No be there here under una hand spear or sword? For I have neither bring my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king’s business required haste.”

The priest talk say, “See am, the sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the valley of Elah, is here wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you would like to take that, take it; for E get no other except that here.” David talk say, “E get none like that. Give it to me.”
David arose, and fled that day for fear of Saul, and go to Achish the king of Gath.
The workers of Achish talk say to him, “No be this David the king of the land? Didn’t dem sing to each other about him in dances, saying, ‘Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands?’”
David laid up these words in his heart, and was very afraid of Achish the king of Gath.
He changed his behavior before dem, and pretended to be insane in dem hands, and scribbled on the doors of the gate, and let his spittle fall down on his beard.
Then Achish talk say to his workers, “Look, you see the man is insane. Why then have you bring him to me?
Do I lack madmen, that you have bring this fellow to play the madman in my presence? Should this fellow come into my house?”
David so comot from there, and escaped to the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and all his father’s house heard it, dem go down there to him.
Everybody wey was in distress, Everybody wey was in debt, and Everybody wey was discontented, gathered themselves to him; and he became captain over dem. There were with him about four hundred men.
David go from there to Mizpeh of Moab, and he talk say to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and my mother come out with you, until I know what God will do for me.”
He bring dem before the king of Moab; and dem lived with him all the time that David was in the stronghold.
The prophet Gad talk say to David, “No stay in the stronghold. Depart, and go into the land of Judah.” Then David comot, and come into the forest of Hereth.

Saul heard that David was discovered, with the men who were with him. Now Saul was sitting in Gibeah, under the tamarisk tree in Ramah, with his spear in his hand, and all his workers were standing around him.

Saul talk say to his workers who stood around him, “Hear now, you Benjamites! Will the son of Jesse give everyone of you fields and vineyards? Will he make you all captains of thousands and captains of hundreds,

that all of you have conspired against me, and E get Nobody who discloses to me when my son makes a treaty with the son of Jesse, and E get none of you Wey be sorry for me, or discloses to me that my son has stirred up my worker against me, to lie in wait, as it is today?”
Then Doeg the Edomite, who stood by the workers of Saul, answer and talk say, “I see the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
He inquired of Baba God for him, give him chop, and give him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”
Then the king sent to call Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father’s house, the priests who were in Nob; and dem all come to the king.
Saul talk say, “Hear now, you son of Ahitub.” He answer, “Here I be, my lord.”

Saul talk say to him, “Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, in that you have given him bread, and a sword, and have inquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as it is today?”
Then Ahimelech answer the king, and talk say, “Who among all una workers is so faithful as David, Wey be the king’s son-in-law, and is taken into una council, and is honorable in una house?

Have I today begun to inquire of God for him? Be it far from me! No let the king impute anything to his worker, nor to all the house of my father; for una worker knows nothing of all this, less or more.”
The king talk say, “You shall surely die, Ahimelech, you, and all una father’s house.”

The king talk say to the guard who stood about him, “Turn, and kill the priests of Baba God; because dem hand also is with David, and because dem know that he fled, and didn’t disclose it to me.” But the workers of the king wouldn’t put out dem hand to fall on the priests of Baba God.
The king talk say to Doeg, “Turn and attack the priests!” Doeg the Edomite turned, and he attacked the priests, and he killed on that day eighty-five people who wore a linen ephod.
He struck Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword, both men and women, pikin dem and nursing babies, and cattle and donkeys and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
One of the sons of Ahimelech, the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David.
Abiathar told David that Saul had slain Baba God’s priests.
David talk say to Abiathar, “I know on that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul. I be responsible for the death of all the persons of una father’s house.
Stay with me. No fear, for person wey seeks my life seeks una life. For You go be safe with me.”
David was told, “See am, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and are robbing the threshing floors.”
So David inquired of Baba God, saying, “Shall I go and strike these Philistines?” Baba God talk say to David, “Go strike the Philistines, and save Keilah.”
David’s men talk say to him, “See am, We be afraid here in Judah. How much more then if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?”
Then David inquired of Baba God yet again. Baba God answer him, and talk say, “Arise, go down to Keilah; for I go deliver the Philistines into una hand.”
David and his men go to Keilah, and fought with the Philistines, and bring away dem livestock, and killed dem with a great slaughter. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.
When Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David to Keilah, he come down with an ephod in his hand.
Saul was told that David had come to Keilah. Saul talk say, “God has delivered him into my hand; for he is shut in by entering into a town that has gates and bars.”
Saul summoned all the people to war, to go down to Keilah, to besiege David and his men.
David know that Saul was devising mischief against him; and he talk say to Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod here.”
Then David talk say, “O Baba God, the God of Israel, una worker has surely heard that Saul seeks to come to Keilah, to destroy the city for my sake.
Will the men of Keilah deliver me up into his hand? Will Saul come down, as una worker has heard? Baba God, the God of Israel, I beg you, tell una worker.” Baba God talk say, “He will come down.”
Then David talk say, “Will the men of Keilah deliver me and my men into the hand of Saul?” Baba God talk say, “Dem go deliver you up.”
Then David and his men, who were about six hundred, arose and comot out of Keilah, and go Anywhere wey dem could go. Saul was told that David was escaped from Keilah; and he give up going there.
David stayed in the wilderness in the strongholds, and remain in the hill country in the wilderness of Ziph. Saul sought him every day, but God didn’t deliver him into his hand.
David see that Saul had come out to seek his life. David was in the wilderness of Ziph in the wood.
Jonathan, Saul’s son, arose, and go to David into the woods, and strengthened his hand in God.
E tell am say, “No fear; for the hand of Saul my father no go find you; and You go be king over Israel, and I go be next to you; and Saul my father knows that also.”
Dem both made a covenant before Baba God. Then David stayed in the woods, and Jonathan go to his house.
Then the Ziphites come up to Saul to Gibeah, saying, “No dey David hide imself with us in the strongholds in the woods, in the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south of the desert?
Now so, O king, come down. According to all the desire of una soul to come down; and our part Go be to deliver him up into the king’s hand.”
Saul talk say, “You be blessed by Baba God; for you have had compassion on me.
Please go make yet more sure, and know and see his place where his haunt is, and who has seen him there; for I Don dey told that he deals very crafty.

See so, and take knowledge of all the lurking places where he hides imself, and come again to me with certainty, and I go go with you. It shall happen, if he is in the land, that I go search him out among all the thousands of Judah.”
Dem arose, and go to Ziph before Saul: but David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah on the south of the desert.
Saul and his men go to seek him. When David was told, he go down to the rock, and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. When Saul heard that, he pursued David in the wilderness of Maon.

Saul go on this side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the mountain; and David hurried to get away for fear of Saul; for Saul and his men surrounded David and his men to take dem.
But a messenger come to Saul, saying, “Hurry and come; for the Philistines have made a raid on the land!”
So Saul come back from pursuing David, and go against the Philistines. So dem call that place Sela Hammahlekoth.
David go up from there, and lived in the strongholds of En Gedi.
When Saul had come back from following the Philistines, he was told, “See am, David is in the wilderness of En Gedi.”
Then Saul take three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and go to seek David and his men on the rocks of the wild goats.
He come to the sheep pens by the way, where there was a cave; and Saul go in to relieve imself. Now David and his men were staying in the innermost parts of the cave.

David’s men talk say to him, “See am, the day of which Baba God talk say to you, ‘See am, I go deliver una enemy into una hand, and you shall do to him as it shall seem good to you.’” Then David arose, and cut off the skirt of Saul’s robe secretly.
Afterward, David’s heart struck him, because he had cut off Saul’s skirt.
He talk say to his men, “Baba God forbid that I should do this thing to my lord, Baba God’s anointed, to stretch out my hand against him, since he is Baba God’s anointed.”
So David checked his men with these words, and didn’t allow dem to rise against Saul. Saul rose up out of the cave, and go on his way.
David also arose afterward, and go out of the cave, and cried after Saul, saying, “My lord the king!” When Saul looked behind him, David bowed with his face to the earth, and showed respect.
David talk say to Saul, “Why do you listen to men’s words, saying, ‘See am, David seeks to harm you?’

See am, today una eyes have seen how Baba God had delivered you today into my hand in the cave. Some urged me to kill you; but I spared you; and I talk say, I go not stretch out my hand against my lord; for he is Baba God’s anointed.

Moreover, my father, see am, yes, see the skirt of una robe in my hand; for in that I cut off the skirt of una robe, and didn’t kill you, know and see that E get neither evil nor disobedience in my hand, and I have not sinned against you, though you hunt for my life to take it.
May Baba God judge between me and you, and may Baba God avenge me of you; but my hand No go be on you.
As the proverb of the ancients says, ‘Out of the wicked comes wickedness;’ but my hand No go be on you.
Against whom has the king of Israel come out? Whom do you pursue? A dead dog? A flea?
May Baba God so be judge, and give sentence between me and you, and see, and plead my cause, and deliver me out of una hand.”
E happen say, when David had finished speaking these words to Saul, that Saul talk say, “Is that una voice, my son David?” Saul lifted up his voice, and wept.
He talk say to David, “You be more righteous than I; for you have done good to me, whereas I have done evil to you.
You have declared today how you have dealt well with me, because when Baba God had delivered me up into una hand, you didn’t kill me.
For if a man finds his enemy, will he Make e go away unharmed? So may Baba God reward you good for that which you have done to me today.
Now, see am, I know that You go surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel Go be established in una hand.
Swear now so to me by Baba God, that You go not cut off my offspring after me, and that You go not destroy my name out of my father’s house.”
David swore to Saul. Saul go home, but David and his men go up to the stronghold.
Samuel died; and all Israel gathered themselves together, and mourned for him, and buried him at his house at Ramah. Then David arose, and go down to the wilderness of Paran.
There was a man in Maon, whose possessions were in Carmel; and the man was plenty well-well. He had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats; and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.
Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail. This woman was intelligent and had a beautiful face; but the man was surly and evil in his doings. He was of the house of Caleb.
David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep.
David sent ten young men, and David talk say to the young men, “Go up to Carmel, and go to Nabal, and greet him in my name.
Tell him, ‘Long life to you! Peace be to you, and peace be to una house, and peace be to all that you have.
Now I have heard that you have shearers. Una shepherds have now been with us, and we didn’t harm dem, neither was there anything missing from dem, all the while dem were in Carmel.
Ask una young men, and Dem go tell you. So let the young men find favor in una eyes; for we come on a good day. Please give Anything wey comes to una hand, to una workers, and to una son David.’”
When David’s young men come, dem spoke to Nabal all those words in the name of David, and waited.
Nabal answer David’s workers, and talk say, “Wey be David? Wey be the son of Jesse? E get many workers who break away from dem masters these days.
Shall I then take my bread, my water, and my meat that I have killed for my shearers, and give it to men who I no know where dem come from?”
So David’s young men turned on dem way, and go back, and come and told him all these words.
David talk say to his men, “Every man put on his sword!” Every man put on his sword. David also put on his sword. About four hundred men follow David, and two hundred stayed by the baggage.
But one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal’s wife, saying, “See am, David sent messengers out of the wilderness to Greet our master; and he insulted dem.
But the men were very good to us, and we No be harmed, and we didn’t miss anything, as long as we go with dem, when we were in the fields.
Dem were a wall to us both by night and by day, all the while we were with dem keeping the sheep.
Now so know and consider Wetin you go do; for evil is determined against our master, and against all his house; for he is such a worthless fellow that one no fit speak to him.”

Then Abigail hurried and take two hundred loaves of bread, two bottles of wine, five sheep ready dressed, five seahs of parched grain, one hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid dem on donkeys.
She talk say to her young men, “Go on before me. See am, I be coming after you.” But she didn’t tell her husband, Nabal.
As she rode on her donkey, and come down by the covert of the mountain, that see am, David and his men come down toward her, and she met dem.
Now David had talk say, “Surely in vain I have kept all that this fellow has in the wilderness, so that nothing was missed of all that pertained to him. He has come back me evil for good.
God do so to the enemies of David, and more also, if I leave of all that belongs to him by the morning light so much as one who urinates on a wall.”
When Abigail see David, she hurried and got off of her donkey, and fell before David on her face, and bowed sheself to the ground.
She fell at his feet, and talk say, “On me, my lord, on me be the blame! Please let una worker speak in una ears. Hear the words of una worker.

Please no let my lord pay attention to this worthless fellow, Nabal; for as his name is, so is he. Nabal is his name, and folly is with him; but I, una worker, didn’t see my lord’s young men, whom you sent.

Now so, my lord, as Baba God lives, and as una soul lives, since Baba God has withheld you from blood guiltiness, and from avenging yourself with una own hand, now so let una enemies, and people wey seek evil to my lord, be as Nabal.
Now this present which una worker has bring to my lord, let it be given to the young men who follow my lord.
Please forgive the trespass of una worker. For Baba God will certainly make my lord a sure house, because my lord fights Baba God’s battles. Evil No go be find in you all una days.

Though men may rise up to pursue you, and to seek una soul, yet the soul of my lord Go be bound in the bundle of life with Baba God una God. He will sling out the souls of una enemies, as from the hollow of a sling.
It will come to pass, when Baba God has done to my lord according to all the good that he has spoken concerning you, and has appointed you prince over Israel,

that this go be no grief to you, nor offense of heart to my lord, either that you have shed blood without cause, or that my lord has avenged imself. When Baba God has dealt well with my lord, then remember una worker.”
David talk say to Abigail, “Blessed is Baba God, the God of Israel, who sent you today to meet me!
Blessed is una discretion, and blessed are you, who have kept me today from blood guiltiness, and from avenging myself with my own hand.

For indeed, as Baba God, the God of Israel, lives, who has withheld me from harming you, unless you had hurried and come to meet me, surely there wouldn’t Don dey left to Nabal by the morning light so much as one who urinates on a wall.”
So David received from her hand that which she had bring him. Then E tell am say, “Go up in peace to una house. See am, I have listened to una voice, and have granted una request.”
Abigail come to Nabal; and see am, he held a feast in his house, like the feast of a king. Nabal’s heart was merry within him, for he was very drunk. So she told him nothing, until the morning light.
In the morning, when the wine had gone out of Nabal, his wife told him these things, and his heart died within him, and he became as a stone.
About ten days later, Baba God struck Nabal, so that he died.

When David heard that Nabal was dead, he talk say, “Blessed is Baba God, who has pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and has kept back his worker from evil. Baba God has come back the evildoing of Nabal on his own head.” David sent and spoke concerning Abigail, to take her to imself as wife.
When David’s workers had come to Abigail to Carmel, dem spoke to her, saying, “David has sent us to you, to take you to him as wife.”
She arose, and bowed sheself with her face to the earth, and talk say, “See am, una worker is a worker to wash the feet of the workers of my lord.”
Abigail hurried, and arose, and rode on a donkey, with five ladies of hers who follow her; and she go after the messengers of David, and became his wife.
David also take Ahinoam of Jezreel; and dem both became his wives.
Now Saul had given Michal his daughter, David’s wife, to Palti the son of Laish, who was of Gallim.
The Ziphites come to Saul to Gibeah, saying, “No dey David hide imself in the hill of Hachilah, which is before the desert?”
Then Saul arose, and go down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
Saul encamped in the hill of Hachilah, which is before the desert, by the way. But David stayed in the wilderness, and he see that Saul come after him into the wilderness.
David so sent out spies, and understand that Saul had certainly come.

Then David arose, and come to the place where Saul had encamped; and David see the place where Saul lay, with Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his army. Saul lay within the place of the wagons, and the people were encamped around him.

Then David answer and talk say to Ahimelech the Hittite, and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, saying, “Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp?” Abishai talk say, “I go go down with you.”

So David and Abishai come to the people by night: and, see am, Saul lay sleeping within the place of the wagons, with his spear stuck in the ground at his head; and Abner and the people lay around him.

Then Abishai talk say to David, “God has delivered up una enemy into una hand today. Now so please let me strike him with the spear to the earth at one stroke, and I go not strike him the second time.”
David talk say to Abishai, “No destroy him; for who can stretch out his hand against Baba God’s anointed, and be guiltless?”
David talk say, “As Baba God lives, Baba God will strike him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall go down into battle and perish.
Baba God forbid that I should stretch out my hand against Baba God’s anointed; but now please take the spear that is at his head, and the jar of water, and Make we go.”

So David take the spear and the jar of water from Saul’s head; and dem go away: and no man see it, or know it, nor did any awake; for dem were all asleep, because a deep sleep from Baba God was fallen on dem.
Then David go over to the other side, and stood on the top of the mountain far away off; a great space being between dem;
and David cried to the people, and to Abner the son of Ner, saying, “No you answer, Abner?” Then Abner answer, “Wey be you who cries to the king?”
David talk say to Abner, “No be you a man? Wey be like you in Israel? Why then have you not kept watch over una lord, the king? For one of the people come in to destroy the king una lord.

This thing no be good that you have done. As Baba God lives, You be worthy to die, because you have not kept watch over una lord, Baba God’s anointed. Now see where the king’s spear is, and the jar of water that was at his head.”
Saul know David’s voice, and talk say, “Is this una voice, my son David?” David talk say, “It is my voice, my lord, O king.”
He talk say, “Why does my lord pursue his worker? For what have I done? What evil is in my hand?

Now so, please let my lord the king hear the words of his worker. If it is so that Baba God has stirred you up against me, Make e accept an offering. But if it is the pikin dem of men, Dem be cursed before Baba God; for dem have driven me out today that I shouldn’t cling to Baba God’s inheritance, saying, ‘Go, serve other gods!’
Now so, no let my blood fall to the earth away from the presence of Baba God; for the king of Israel has come out to seek a flea, as when one hunts a partridge in the mountains.”
Then Saul talk say, “I have sinned. Return, my son David; for I go no more do you harm, because my life was precious in una eyes today. See am, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.”
David answer, “See am the spear, O king! Then let one of the young men come over and get it.
Baba God will render to every man his righteousness and his faithfulness; because Baba God delivered you into my hand today, and I wouldn’t stretch out my hand against Baba God’s anointed.
See am, as una life was respected today in my eyes, so let my life be respected in Baba God’s eyes, and Make e deliver me out of all oppression.”
Then Saul talk say to David, “You be blessed, my son David. You go both do mightily, and will surely prevail.” So David go his way, and Saul come back to his place.

David talk say in his heart, “I go now perish one day by the hand of Saul. E get nothing better for me than that I should escape into the land of the Philistines; and Saul will despair of me, to seek me any more in all the borders of Israel. So shall I escape out of his hand.”
David arose, and passed over, he and the six hundred men who were with him, to Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath.
David lived with Achish at Gath, he and his men, every man with his household, even David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal’s wife.
Saul was told that David had fled to Gath: and he sought no more again for him.

David talk say to Achish, “If now I have find favor in una eyes, Make dem give me a place in one of the cities in the country, that I may live there. For why should una worker live in the royal city with you?”
Then Achish give him Ziklag that day: so Ziklag belongs to the kings of Judah to this day.
The number of the days that David lived in the country of the Philistines was a full year and four months.
David and his men go up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites; for those were the inhabitants of the land, who were of old, on the way to Shur, even to the land of Egypt.
David struck the land, and saved no man or woman alive, and take away the sheep, the cattle, the donkeys, the camels, and the clothing. Then he come back, and come to Achish.
Achish talk say, “Against whom have you made a raid today?” David talk say, “Against the South of Judah, against the South of the Jerahmeelites, and against the South of the Kenites.”

David saved neither man nor woman alive, to bring dem to Gath, saying, “Lest dem should tell about us, saying, ‘David did this, and this Don dey his way all the time he has lived in the country of the Philistines.’”
Achish believe David, saying, “He has made his people Israel utterly to abhor him. So he Go be my worker forever.”
In those days, the Philistines gathered dem armies together for warfare, to fight with Israel. Achish talk say to David, “Know assuredly that You go go out with me in the army, you and una men.”
David talk say to Achish, “So You go know what una worker can do.” Achish talk say to David, “So I go make you my bodyguard forever.”
Now Samuel was dead, and all Israel had mourned for him, and buried him in Ramah, even in his own city. Saul had put away people wey had familiar spirits the wizards, out of the land.
The Philistines gathered themselves together, and come and encamped in Shunem; and Saul gathered all Israel together, and dem encamped in Gilboa.
When Saul see the army of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly.
When Saul inquired of Baba God, Baba God didn’t answer him by dreams, by Urim, or by prophets.

Then Saul talk say to his workers, “Seek for me a woman who has a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and inquire of her.” His workers talk say to him, “See am, E get a woman who has a familiar spirit at Endor.”

Saul disguised imself and put on other clothing, and go, he and two men with him, and dem come to the woman by night. Then he talk say, “Please consult for me by the familiar spirit, and bring me up whomever I shall name to you.”

The woman talk say to him, “See am, you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off people wey have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land. Why then do you lay a snare for my life, to cause me to die?”
Saul swore to her by Baba God, saying, “As Baba God lives, no punishment will happen to you for this thing.”
Then the woman talk say, “Whom shall I bring up to you?” He talk say, “Bring Samuel up for me.”
When the woman see Samuel, she cried with a loud voice; and the woman spoke to Saul, saying, “Why have you deceived me? For You be Saul!”
The king talk say to her, “No fear! What do you see?” The woman talk say to Saul, “I see a god coming up out of the earth.”

E tell am say, “What does he look like?” She talk say, “An old man comes up. He is covered with a robe.” Saul perceived that it was Samuel, and he bowed with his face to the ground, and showed respect.

Samuel talk say to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me, to bring me up?” Saul answer, “I be very distressed; for the Philistines make war against me, and God has comot from me, and answers me no more, by prophets, or by dreams. So I have call you, that you may make known to me what I shall do.”
Samuel talk say, “Why then do you ask me, since Baba God has comot from you and has become una adversary?
Baba God has done to you as he spoke by me. Baba God has torn the kingdom out of una hand, and given it to una neighbor, even to David.
Because you didn’t obey Baba God’s voice, and didn’t execute his fierce serious anger on Amalek, so Baba God has done this thing to you today.

Moreover Baba God will deliver Israel also with you into the hand of the Philistines; and tomorrow you and una sons Go be with me. Baba God will deliver the army of Israel also into the hand of the Philistines.”
Then Saul fell sharp-sharp his full length on the earth, and was terrified, because of Samuel’s words. There was no strength in him; for he had eaten no bread all day long or all night long.

The woman come to Saul, and see that he was very troubled, and talk say to him, “See am, una worker has listened to una voice, and I have put my life in my hand, and have listened to una words which you spoke to me.
Now so, please listen also to the voice of una worker, and let me set a morsel of bread before you. Eat, that you may have strength, when you go on una way.”
But he refused, and talk say, “I go not eat.” But his workers, together with the woman, constrained him; and he listened to dem voice. So he arose from the earth and sat on the bed.
The woman had a fattened calf in the house. She hurried and killed it; and she take flour, and kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread of it.
She bring it before Saul, and before his workers; and dem ate. Then dem rose up, and go away that night.
Now the Philistines gathered together all dem armies to Aphek; and the Israelites encamped by the spring which is in Jezreel.
The lords of the Philistines passed on by hundreds and by thousands; and David and his men passed on in the rear with Achish.

Then the princes of the Philistines talk say, “What about these Hebrews?” Achish talk say to the princes of the Philistines, “No be this David, the worker of Saul the king of Israel, who Don dey with me these days, or rather these years, and I have find no fault in him since he fell away to today?”

But the princes of the Philistines were angry with him; and the princes of the Philistines talk say to him, “Make the man return, that he may go back to his place where you have appointed him, and Make e not go down with us to battle, lest in the battle he become an adversary to us. For with what should this fellow reconcile imself to his lord? Should it not be with the heads of these men?
No be this David, of whom people sang to each other in dances, saying, ‘Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands?’”

Then Achish call David, and talk say to him, “As Baba God lives, you Don dey upright, and una going out and una coming in with me in the army is good in my sight; for I have not find evil in you since the day of una coming to me to this day. Nevertheless, the lords no favor you.
So now return, and go in peace, that you not displease the lords of the Philistines.”
David talk say to Achish, “But what have I done? What have you find in una worker so long as I Don dey before you to this day, that I may not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?”
Achish answer David, “I know that You be good in my sight, as an angel of God. Notwithstanding the princes of the Philistines have talk say, ‘He no go go up with us to the battle.’
So now rise up early in the morning with the workers of una lord who have come with you; and as soon as You be up early in the morning, and have light, depart.”
So David rose up early, he and his men, to depart in the morning, to return into the land of the Philistines, and the Philistines go up to Jezreel.
When David and his men had come to Ziklag on the third day, the Amalekites had made a raid on the South, and on Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag, and burned it with fire,
and had taken captive the women and all who were in it, both small and great. Dem didn’t kill any, but carried dem off, and go dem way.
When David and his men come to the city, see am, it was burned with fire; and dem wives, dem sons, and dem daughters were taken captive.
Then David and the people who were with him lifted up dem voice and wept until dem had no more power to weep.
David’s two wives were taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

David was greatly distressed; for the people spoke of stoning him, because the souls of all the people were grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters; but David strengthened imself in Baba God his God.
David talk say to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, “Please bring the ephod here to me.” Abiathar bring the ephod to David.
David inquired of Baba God, saying, “If I pursue after this troop, will I overtake dem?” He answer him, “Pursue; for You go surely overtake dem, and will without fail recover all.”
So David go, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and come to the brook Besor, where people wey were left behind stayed.
But David pursued, he and four hundred men; for two hundred stayed behind, who were so faint that dem no fit go over the brook Besor.
Dem find an Egyptian in the field, and bring him to David, and give him bread, and he ate; and dem give him water to drink.
Dem give him a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins. When he had eaten, his spirit come again to him; for he had eaten no bread, and drank no water for three days and three nights.
David ask him, “To whom do you belong? Where are you from?” He talk say, “I be a young man of Egypt, worker to an Amalekite; and my master left me, because three days ago I got sick.
We made a raid on the South of the Cherethites, and on that which belongs to Judah, and on the South of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire.”

David talk say to him, “Will you bring me down to this troop?” He talk say, “Swear to me by God that You go not kill me and not deliver me up into the hands of my master, and I go bring you down to this troop.”

When he had bring him down, see am, dem were spread around over all the ground, eating, drinking, and dancing, because of all the great plunder that dem had taken out of the land of the Philistines, and out of the land of Judah.
David struck dem from the twilight even to the evening of the next day. Not a man of dem escaped from there, except four hundred young men, who rode on camels and fled.
David recovered all that the Amalekites had taken; and David rescued his two wives.
There was nothing lacking to dem, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, neither plunder, nor anything that dem had taken to dem. David bring back all.
David take all the flocks and the herds, which dem drove before those other livestock, and talk say, “This is David’s plunder.”

David come to the two hundred men, who were so faint that dem could not follow David, whom also dem had made to stay at the brook Besor; and dem go out to meet David, and to meet the people who were with him. When David come near to the people, he greeted dem.

Then all the wicked men and base fellows, of people wey go with David, answer and talk say, “Because dem didn’t go with us, We go not give dem anything of the plunder that we have recovered, except to every man his wife and his pikin dem, that he may lead dem away, and depart.”
Then David talk say, “No do so, my brothers, with that which Baba God has given to us, who has preserved us, and delivered the troop that come against us into our hand.
Who will listen to you in this matter? For as his share is who goes down to the battle, so shall his share be who stays with the baggage. Dem shall share alike.”
It was so from that day forward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel to this day.
When David come to Ziklag, he sent some of the plunder to the elders of Judah, even to his friends, saying, “See am, a present for you from the plunder of Baba God’s enemies.”
He sent it to people wey were in Bethel, to people wey were in Ramoth of the South, to people wey were in Jattir,
to people wey were in Aroer, to people wey were in Siphmoth, to people wey were in Eshtemoa,
to people wey were in Racal, to people wey were in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, to people wey were in the cities of the Kenites,
to people wey were in Hormah, to people wey were in Borashan, to people wey were in Athach,
to people wey were in Hebron, and to all the places where David imself and his men used to stay.
Now the Philistines fought against Israel; and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain on Mount Gilboa.
The Philistines overtook Saul and on his sons; and the Philistines killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.
The battle go hard against Saul, and the archers overtook him; and he was greatly distressed by reason of the archers.

Then Saul talk say to his armor bearer, “Draw una sword, and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me!” But his armor bearer would not; for he was terrified. So Saul take his sword, and fell on it.
When his armor bearer see that Saul was dead, he likewise fell on his sword, and died with him.
So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armor bearer, and all his men, that same day together.

When the men of Israel who were on the other side of the valley, and people wey were beyond the Jordan, see that the men of Israel fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, dem abandoned the cities and fled; and the Philistines come and lived in dem.
On the next day, when the Philistines come to strip the slain, dem find Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
Dem cut off his head, stripped off his armor, and sent into the land of the Philistines all around, to carry the news to the house of dem idols, and to the people.
Dem put his armor in the house of the Ashtaroth, and dem fastened his body to the wall of Beth Shan.
When the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,
all the valiant men arose, go all night, and take the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth Shan; and dem come to Jabesh, and burned dem there.
Dem take dem bones and buried dem under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
After the death of Saul, when David had come back from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had stayed two days in Ziklag;
on the third day, see am, a man come out of the camp from Saul, with his clothes torn, and earth on his head. When he come to David, he fell to the earth, and showed respect.
David talk say to him, “Where do you come from?” E tell am say, “I have escaped out of the camp of Israel.”

David talk say to him, “How did it go? Please tell me.” He answer, “The people have fled from the battle, and many of the people also have fallen and are dead. Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.”
David talk say to the young man who told him, “How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?”
The young man who told him talk say, “As I happened by chance on Mount Gilboa, see am, Saul was leaning on his spear; and see am, the chariots and the horsemen follow close behind him.
When he looked behind him, he see me, and call to me. I answer, ‘Here I be.’
He talk say to me, ‘Wey be you?’ I answer him, ‘I be an Amalekite.’
He talk say to me, ‘Please stand beside me, and kill me; for anguish has taken hold of me, because my life lingers in me.’

So I stood beside him and killed him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he had fallen. I take the crown that was on his head and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have bring dem here to my lord.”
Then David take hold on his clothes, and tore dem; and all the men who were with him did likewise.
Dem mourned, wept, and fasted until evening, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of Baba God, and for the house of Israel; because dem had fallen by the sword.
David talk say to the young man who told him, “Where are you from?” He answer, “I be the son of a foreigner, an Amalekite.”
David talk say to him, “Why were you not afraid to stretch out una hand to destroy Baba God’s anointed?”
David call one of the young men, and talk say, “Go near, and cut him down!” He struck him so that he died.
David talk say to him, “Una blood be on una head; for una mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I have slain Baba God’s anointed.’”
David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son
(and he commanded dem to teach the pikin dem of Judah the song of the bow; see am, it is written in the book of Jashar):
“Una glory, Israel, was slain on una high places! How the mighty have fallen!
No tell it in Gath. No publish it in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines glad well-well, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.
You mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew or rain on you, and no fields of offerings; For there the shield of the mighty was defiled and throw away, The shield of Saul No be anointed with oil.
From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, Jonathan’s bow didn’t turn back. Saul’s sword didn’t return empty.
Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in dem lives. In dem death, dem No be divided. Dem were swifter than eagles. Dem were stronger than lions.
You daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you delicately in scarlet, who put ornaments of gold on una clothing.
How the mighty have fallen in the middle of the battle! Jonathan was slain on una high places.
I be distressed for you, my brother Jonathan. You Don dey very pleasant to me. Una love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.
How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!”
After this, David inquired of Baba God, saying, “Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah?” Baba God talk say to him, “Go up.” David talk say, “Where shall I go up?” He talk say, “To Hebron.”
So David go up there with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
David bring up his men who were with him, every man with his household. Dem lived in the cities of Hebron.
The men of Judah come, and there dem anointed David king over the house of Judah. Dem told David, “The men of Jabesh Gilead were people wey buried Saul.”
David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh Gilead, and talk say to dem, “Blessed are you by Baba God, that you have shown this kindness to una lord, even to Saul, and have buried him.
Now may Baba God show loving kindness and truth to you. I also will reward you for this kindness, because you have done this thing.
Now so let una hands be strong, and be valiant; for Saul una lord is dead, and also the house of Judah have anointed me king over dem.”
Now Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul’s army, had taken Ishbosheth the son of Saul, and bring him over to Mahanaim;
and he made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
Ishbosheth, Saul’s son, was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned two years. But the house of Judah follow David.
The time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
Abner the son of Ner, and the workers of Ishbosheth the son of Saul, go out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
Joab the son of Zeruiah and David’s workers go out, and met dem by the pool of Gibeon; and dem sat down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.
Abner talk say to Joab, “Please let the young men arise and play before us!” Joab talk say, “Make dem arise!”
Then dem arose and go over by number: twelve for Benjamin and for Ishbosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of David’s workers.
Dem each caught his opponent by the head, and thrust his sword in his fellow’s side; so dem fell down together: so that place in Gibeon was call Helkath Hazzurim.
The battle was very severe that day; and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, before David’s workers.
The three sons of Zeruiah were there, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel: and Asahel was as light of foot as a wild gazelle.
Asahel pursued Abner; and in going he didn’t turn to the right hand or to the left from following Abner.
Then Abner looked behind him, and talk say, “Is that you, Asahel?” He answer, “It is.”
Abner talk say to him, “Turn aside to una right hand or to una left, and grab one of the young men, and take his armor.” But Asahel would not turn aside from following him.
Abner talk say again to Asahel, “Turn aside from following me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How then could I look Joab una brother in the face?”

However he refused to turn aside. So Abner with the back end of the spear struck him in the body, so that the spear come out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same place. As many as come to the place where Asahel fell down and died stood still.
But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. The sun go down when dem had come to the hill of Ammah, that lies before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.
The pikin dem of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, and became one band, and stood on the top of a hill.

Then Abner call to Joab, and talk say, “Shall the sword devour forever? No you know that it Go be bitterness in the latter end? How long will it be then, before you ask the people to return from following dem brothers?”
Joab talk say, “As God lives, if you had not spoken, surely then in the morning the people would have gone away, and not each follow his brother.”
So Joab blew the trumpet; and all the people stood still, and pursued Israel no more, and dem fought no more.
Abner and his men go all that night through the Arabah; and dem passed over the Jordan, and go through all Bithron, and come to Mahanaim.
Joab come back from following Abner; and when he had gathered all the people together, nineteen men of David’s and Asahel were missing.
But David’s workers had struck Benjamin and of Abner’s men so that three hundred sixty men died.
Dem take up Asahel, and buried him in the tomb of his father, which was in Bethlehem. Joab and his men go all night, and the day broke on dem at Hebron.
Now there was long war between Saul’s house and David’s house. David grew stronger and stronger, but Saul’s house grew weaker and weaker.
Sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;
and his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
and the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;
and the sixth, Ithream, of Eglah, David’s wife. These were born to David in Hebron.
While there was war between Saul’s house and David’s house, Abner made imself strong in Saul’s house.
Now Saul had a concubine, whose name was Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah; and Ishbosheth talk say to Abner, “Why have you gone in to my father’s concubine?”

Then Abner was very angry about Ishbosheth’s words, and talk say, “Am I a dog’s head that belongs to Judah? Today I show kindness to Saul’s house una father, to his brothers, and to his friends, and have not delivered you into the hand of David; and yet you charge me today with a fault concerning this woman!
God do so to Abner, and more also, if, as Baba God has sworn to David, I no do even so to him;
to transfer the kingdom from Saul’s house, and to set up David’s throne over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beersheba.”
He could not answer Abner another word, because he was afraid of him.
Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, “Whose is the land?” and saying, “Make una alliance with me, and see am, my hand Go be with you, to bring all Israel around to you.”
He talk say, “Good. I go make a treaty with you, but one thing I require of you. That is, You go not see my face unless you first bring Michal, Saul’s daughter, when you come to see my face.”
David sent messengers to Ishbosheth, Saul’s son, saying, “Deliver me my wife Michal, whom I was given to marry for one hundred foreskins of the Philistines.”
Ishbosheth sent and take her from her husband, even from Paltiel the son of Laish.
Her husband go with her, weeping as he go, and follow her to Bahurim. Then Abner talk say to him, “Go! Return!” and he come back.
Abner had communication with the elders of Israel, saying, “In times past, you sought for David to be king over you.
Now then do it; for Baba God has spoken of David, saying, ‘By the hand of my worker David, I go save my people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all dem enemies.’”
Abner also spoke in the ears of Benjamin: and Abner go also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel, and to the whole house of Benjamin.
So Abner come to David to Hebron, and twenty men with him. David made Abner and the men who were with him a feast.

Abner talk say to David, “I go arise and go, and will gather all Israel to my lord the king, that dem may make a covenant with you, and that you may reign over all that una soul desires.” David sent Abner away; and he go in peace.
See am, David’s workers and Joab come from a raid, and bring in a great plunder with dem; but Abner No be with David in Hebron; for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.
When Joab and all the army who was with him had come, dem told Joab, “Abner the son of Ner come to the king, and he has sent him away, and he has gone in peace.”
Then Joab come to the king, and talk say, “What have you done? See am, Abner come to you. Why is it that you have sent him away, and he is already gone?
You know Abner the son of Ner. He come to deceive you, and to know una going out and una coming in, and to know all that you do.”
When Joab had come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, and dem bring him back from the well of Sirah; but David didn’t know it.
When Abner was come back to Hebron, Joab take him aside into the middle of the gate to speak with him quietly, and struck him there in the body, so that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.
Afterward, when David heard it, he talk say, “I and my kingdom are guiltless before Baba God forever of the blood of Abner the son of Ner.

Let it fall on the head of Joab, and on all his father’s house. Let there not fail from the house of Joab one who has an issue, or Wey be a leper, or who leans on a staff, or who falls by the sword, or who lacks bread.”
So Joab and Abishai his brother killed Abner, because he had killed dem brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.
David talk say to Joab, and to all the people who were with him, “Tear una clothes, and clothe unaself with sackcloth, and mourn in front of Abner.” King David follow the bier.
Dem buried Abner in Hebron; and the king lifted up his voice, and wept at Abner’s grave; and all the people wept.
The king lamented for Abner, and talk say, “Should Abner die as a fool dies?
Una hands no be bound, and una feet no be put into fetters. As a man falls before the pikin dem of wickedness, so you fell.” All the people wept again over him.
All the people come to urge David to eat bread while it was yet day; but David swore, saying, “God do so to me, and more also, if I taste bread, or anything else, until the sun goes down.”
All the people take notice of it, and it pleased dem; as Anything wey the king did pleased all the people.
So all the people and all Israel understand that day that it No be of the king to kill Abner the son of Ner.
The king talk say to his workers, “No you know that there a prince and a great man has fallen today in Israel?
I be weak today, though anointed king. These men, the sons of Zeruiah are too hard for me. May Baba God reward the evildoer according to his wickedness.”
When Saul’s son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands became feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.

Saul’s son had two men who were captains of raiding bands. The name of one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the pikin dem of Benjamin (for Beeroth also is considered a part of Benjamin:
and the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and have lived as foreigners there until today).

Now Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son who was lame in his feet. He was five years old when the news come about Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel; and his nurse picked him up and fled. As she hurried to flee, he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.
The sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, go and come at about the heat of the day to the house of Ishbosheth, as he take his rest at noon.
Dem come there into the middle of the house, as though dem would have fetched wheat; and dem struck him in the body: and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.
Now when dem come into the house, as he lay on his bed in his bedroom, dem struck him, killed him, beheaded him, and take his head, and go by the way of the Arabah all night.

Dem bring the head of Ishbosheth to David to Hebron, and talk say to the king, “See am, the head of Ishbosheth, the son of Saul, una enemy, who sought una life! Baba God has avenged my lord the king today of Saul, and of his offspring. ”
David answer Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and talk say to dem, “As Baba God lives, who has redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
when someone told me, ‘See am, Saul is dead,’ thinking that he bring better news, I seized him and killed him in Ziklag, which was the reward I give him for his news.
How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house on his bed, should I not now require his blood from una hand, and rid the earth of you?”

David commanded his young men, and dem killed dem, cut off dem hands and dem feet, and hanged dem up beside the pool in Hebron. But dem take the head of Ishbosheth, and buried it in Abner’s grave in Hebron.
Then all the tribes of Israel come to David at Hebron, and spoke, saying, “See am, We be una bone and una flesh.
In times past, when Saul was king over us, it was you who led Israel out and in. Baba God talk say to you, ‘You go be shepherd of my people Israel, and You go be prince over Israel.’”
So all the elders of Israel come to the king to Hebron, and king David made a covenant with dem in Hebron before Baba God; and dem anointed David king over Israel.
David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.
In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months; and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.

The king and his men go to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, who spoke to David, saying, “The blind and the lame will keep you out of here”; thinking, “David no fit come in here.”
Nevertheless David take the stronghold of Zion. This is David’s city.

David talk say on that day, “Anybody wey strikes the Jebusites, Make e go up to the watercourse and strike the lame and the blind, Wey be hated by David’s soul.” So dem say, “The blind and the lame no fit come into the house.”
David lived in the stronghold, and call it David’s city. David built around from Millo and inward.
David grew greater and greater; for Baba God, the God of Armies, was with him.
Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, with cedar trees, carpenters, and masons; and dem built David a house.
David perceived that Baba God had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for his people Israel’s sake.
David take more concubines and wives for imself out of Jerusalem, after he had come from Hebron; and more sons and daughters were born to David.
These are the names of people wey were born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
When the Philistines heard that dem had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines go up to seek David, but David heard about it and go down to the stronghold.
Now the Philistines had come and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.

David inquired of Baba God, saying, “Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you deliver dem into my hand?” Baba God talk say to David, “Go up; for I go certainly deliver the Philistines into una hand.”
David come to Baal Perazim, and David struck dem there. Then he talk say, “Baba God has broken my enemies before me, like the breach of waters.” So he call the name of that place Baal Perazim.
Dem left dem images there; and David and his men take dem away.
The Philistines come up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
When David inquired of Baba God, he talk say, “You no go go up. Circle around behind dem, and attack dem in front of the mulberry trees.
When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry trees, then stir yourself up; for then Baba God has gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.”
David did so, as Baba God commanded him, and struck the Philistines all the way from Geba to Gezer.
David again gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.

David arose, and go with all the people who were with him, from Baale Judah, to bring up from there God’s ark, which is call by the Name, even the name of Baba God of Armies who sits above the cherubim.
Dem set God’s ark on a new cart, and bring it out of Abinadab’s house that was on the hill; and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove the new cart.
Dem bring it out of Abinadab’s house, which was in the hill, with God’s ark; and Ahio go before the ark.
David and all the house of Israel played before Baba God with all kinds of instruments made of cypress wood, with harps, with stringed instruments, with tambourines, with castanets, and with cymbals.
When dem come to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached for God’s ark, and take hold of it; for the cattle stumbled.
Baba God’s anger burned against Uzzah; and God struck him there for his error; and he died there by God’s ark.
David was displeased, because Baba God had broken out against Uzzah; and he call that place Perez Uzzah, to this day.
David was afraid of Baba God that day; and he talk say, “How could Baba God’s ark come to me?”
So David would not move Baba God’s ark to be with him in David’s city; but David carried it aside into Obed-Edom the Gittite’s house.
Baba God’s ark remain in Obed-Edom the Gittite’s house three months; and Baba God blessed Obed-Edom and all his house.

King David was told, “Baba God has blessed the house of Obed-Edom, and all that belongs to him, because of God’s ark.” So David go and bring up God’s ark from the house of Obed-Edom into David’s city with gladness.
When people wey bore Baba God’s ark had gone six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf.
David danced before Baba God with all his might; and David was clothed in a linen ephod.
So David and all the house of Israel bring up Baba God’s ark with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.
As Baba God’s ark come into David’s city, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out through the window, and see king David leaping and dancing before Baba God; and she despised him in her heart.
Dem bring in Baba God’s ark, and set it in its place, in the middle of the tent that David had pitched for it; and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before Baba God.
When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of Baba God of Armies.
He give to all the people, even among the whole plenty people of Israel, both to men and women, to everyone a portion of bread, dates, and raisins. So all the people comot, each to his own house.

Then David come back to bless his household. Michal the daughter of Saul come out to meet David, and talk say, “How glorious the king of Israel was today, who uncovered imself today in the eyes of the workers of his workers, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovers imself!”

David talk say to Michal, “It was before Baba God, who chose me above una father, and above all his house, to appoint me prince over the people of Baba God, over Israel. So I go celebrate before Baba God.
I go be yet more vile than this, and Go be base in my own sight. But of the workers of whom you have spoken, Dem go honor me.”
Michal the daughter of Saul had no pikin to the day of her death.
When the king lived in his house, and Baba God had given him rest from all his enemies all around,
the king talk say to Nathan the prophet, “See now, I live in a house of cedar, but God’s ark dwells within curtains.”
Nathan talk say to the king, “Go, do all that is in una heart; for Baba God is with you.”
That same night, Baba God’s word come to Nathan, saying,
“Go and tell my worker David, ‘Baba God says, “Should you build me a house for me to live in?
For I have not lived in a house since the day that I bring the pikin dem of Israel up out of Egypt, even to this day, but have moved around in a tent and in a tabernacle.

In all places in which I have walked with all the pikin dem of Israel, did I say a word to any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to be shepherd of my people Israel, saying, ‘Why have you not built me a house of cedar?’”’
Now so tell my worker David this, ‘Baba God of Armies says, “I take you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep, to be prince over my people, over Israel.
I Don dey with you Anywhere wey you go, and have cut off all una enemies from before you. I go make you a great name, like the name of the great ones Wey be in the earth.
I go appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant dem, that dem may live in dem own place, and be moved no more. The pikin dem of wickedness No go afflict dem any more, as at the first,
and as from the day that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel. I go cause you to rest from all una enemies. Moreover Baba God tells you that Baba God will make you a house.
When una days are fulfilled, and you sleep with una fathers, I go set up una offspring after you, who will proceed out of una body, and I go establish his kingdom.
He will build a house for my name, and I go establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
I go be his father, and he Go be my son. If he commits wickedness, I go chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the pikin dem of men;
but my loving kindness No go depart from him, as I take it from Saul, whom I put away before you.
Una house and una kingdom Go be made sure forever before you. Una throne Go be established forever.”’”
Nathan spoke to David all these words, and according to all this vision.
Then David the king go in, and sat before Baba God; and he talk say, “Who am I, Lord Baba God, and Wetin be my house, that you have bring me this far?
This was yet a small thing in una eyes, Lord Baba God; but you have spoken also of una worker’s house for a great while to come; and this among men, Lord Baba God!
What more can David say to you? For you know una worker, Lord Baba God.
For una word’s sake, and according to una own heart, you have worked all this greatness, to make una worker know it.
So You be great, Baba God. For E get Nobody like you, neither is there any God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

What one nation in the earth is like una people, even like Israel, whom God go to redeem to imself for a people, and to make imself a name, and to do great things for you, and awesome things for una land, before una people, whom you redeemed to yourself out of Egypt, from the nations and dem gods?
You established for yourself una people Israel to be una people forever; and you, Baba God, became dem God.
Now, Baba God, the word that you have spoken concerning una worker, and concerning his house, confirm it forever, and do as you have spoken.
Let una name be magnified forever, saying, ‘Baba God of Armies is God over Israel; and the house of una worker David Go be established before you.’
For you, Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, have revealed to una worker, saying, ‘I go build you a house.’ So una worker has find in his heart to pray this prayer to you.
“Now, O Lord Baba God, You be God, and una words are truth, and you have promised this good thing to una worker.

Now so let it please you to bless the house of una worker, that it may continue forever before you; for you, Lord Baba God, have spoken it. Let the house of una worker be blessed forever with una blessing.”
