After this, David struck the Philistines and subdued dem; and David take the bridle of the mother city out of the hand of the Philistines.

He struck Moab, and measured dem with the line, making dem to lie down on the ground; and he measured two lines to put to death, and one full line to keep alive. The Moabites became workers to David, and bring tribute.
David struck also Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he go to recover his dominion at the River.
David take from him one thousand seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand footmen. David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but reserved of dem for one hundred chariots.
When the Syrians of Damascus come to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck twenty two thousand men of the Syrians.
Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus; and the Syrians became workers to David, and bring tribute. Baba God give victory to David Anywhere wey he go.
David take the shields of gold that were on the workers of Hadadezer, and bring dem to Jerusalem.
From Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, king David take a great quantity of brass.
When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer,

then Toi sent Joram his son to king David, to greet him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him; for Hadadezer had wars with Toi. Joram bring with him vessels of silver, vessels of gold, and vessels of brass:
King David also dedicated these to Baba God, with the silver and gold that he dedicated of all the nations which he subdued;
of Syria, of Moab, of the pikin dem of Ammon, of the Philistines, of Amalek, and of the plunder of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
David earned a reputation when he come back from striking down eighteen thousand men of the Syrians in the Valley of Salt.
He put garrisons in Edom. Throughout all Edom put he garrisons, and all the Edomites became workers to David. Baba God give victory to David Anywhere wey he go.
David reigned over all Israel; and David executed justice and righteousness for all his people.
Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army, Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder,
Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were priests, Seraiah was scribe,
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites, David’s sons were chief ministers.
David talk say, “Is there yet any Wey be left of Saul’s house, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?”
There was of Saul’s house a worker whose name was Ziba, and dem call him to David; and the king talk say to him, “Are you Ziba?” He talk say, “I be una worker.”
The king talk say, “Is there not yet any of Saul’s house, that I may show the kindness of God to him?” Ziba talk say to the king, “Jonathan still has a son, Wey be lame in his feet.”
The king talk say to him, “Where is he?” Ziba talk say to the king, “See am, he is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, in Lo Debar.”
Then king David sent, and bring him out of the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lo Debar.
Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, come to David, and fell on his face, and showed respect. David talk say, “Mephibosheth.” He answer, “See am, una worker!”

David talk say to him, “No fear of him; for I go surely show you kindness for Jonathan una father’s sake, and will restore to you all the land of Saul una father. You go eat bread at my table continually.”
He bowed down, and talk say, “Wetin be una worker, that you should look at such a dead dog as I be?”
Then the king call to Ziba, Saul’s worker, and talk say to him, “All that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to una master’s son.

Till the land for him, you, una sons, and una workers. Bring in the harvest, that una master’s son may have bread to eat; but Mephibosheth una master’s son will always eat bread at my table.” Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty workers.
Then Ziba talk say to the king, “According to all that my lord the king commands his worker, so una worker will do.” So Mephibosheth ate at the king’s table, like one of the king’s sons.
Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Mica. All that lived in Ziba’s house were workers to Mephibosheth.
So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem; for he ate continually at the king’s table. He was lame in both his feet.
After this, the king of the pikin dem of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.

David talk say, “I go show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent by his workers to comfort him concerning his father. David’s workers come into the land of the pikin dem of Ammon.

But the princes of the pikin dem of Ammon talk say to Hanun dem lord, “Do you think that David honors una father, in that he has sent comforters to you? Hasn’t David sent his workers to you to search the city, to spy it out, and to overthrow it?”
So Hanun take David’s workers, shaved off one half of dem beards, and cut off dem garments in the middle, even to dem buttocks, and sent dem away.
When dem told David this, he sent to meet dem, for the men were greatly ashamed. The king talk say, “Wait at Jericho until una beards have grown, and then return.”

When the pikin dem of Ammon see that dem had become odious to David, the pikin dem of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Beth Rehob, and the Syrians of Zobah, twenty thousand footmen, and the king of Maacah with one thousand men, and the men of Tob twelve thousand men.
When David heard of it, he sent Joab, and all the army of the mighty men.
The pikin dem of Ammon come out, and put the battle in array at the entrance of the gate. The Syrians of Zobah and of Rehob, and the men of Tob and Maacah, were by themselves in the field.
Now when Joab see that the battle was set against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Israel, and put dem in array against the Syrians.
The rest of the people he committed into the hand of Abishai his brother; and he put dem in array against the pikin dem of Ammon.
He talk say, “If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you shall help me; but if the pikin dem of Ammon are too strong for you, then I go come and help you.
Be courageous, and Make we be strong for our people, and for the cities of our God; and may Baba God do what seems good to him.”
So Joab and the people who were with him come near to the battle against the Syrians, and dem fled before him.
When the pikin dem of Ammon see that the Syrians had fled, dem likewise fled before Abishai, and entered into the city. Then Joab come back from the pikin dem of Ammon, and come to Jerusalem.
When the Syrians see that dem were defeated by Israel, dem gathered themselves together.
Hadadezer sent, and bring out the Syrians who were beyond the River: and dem come to Helam, with Shobach the captain of the army of Hadadezer at dem head.
David was told that; and he gathered all Israel together, passed over the Jordan, and come to Helam. The Syrians set themselves in array against David, and fought with him.
The Syrians fled before Israel; and David killed seven hundred charioteers of the Syrians, and forty thousand horsemen, and struck Shobach the captain of dem army, so that he died there.

When all the kings who were workers to Hadadezer see that dem were defeated before Israel, dem made peace with Israel, and served dem. So the Syrians were afraid to help the pikin dem of Ammon any more.

At the return of the year, at the time when kings go out, David sent Joab, and his workers with him, and all Israel; and dem destroyed the pikin dem of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem.
At evening, David arose from his bed and walked on the roof of the king’s house. From the roof, he see a woman bathing, and the woman was very beautiful to look at.
David sent and inquired after the woman. One talk say, “No be this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, Uriah the Hittite’s wife?”
David sent messengers, and take her; and she come in to him, and he lay with her (for she was purified from her uncleanness); and she come back to her house.
The woman conceived; and she sent and told David, and talk say, “I be with pikin.”
David sent to Joab, “Send me Uriah the Hittite.” Joab sent Uriah to David.
When Uriah had come to him, David ask him how Joab did, and how the people fared, and how the war prospered.
David talk say to Uriah, “Go down to una house and wash una feet.” Uriah comot out of the king’s house, and a gift from the king was sent after him.
But Uriah slept at the door of the king’s house with all the workers of his lord, and didn’t go down to his house.
When dem had told David, saying, “Uriah didn’t go down to his house,” David talk say to Uriah, “Haven’t you come from a journey? Why didn’t you go down to una house?”

Uriah talk say to David, “The ark, Israel, and Judah, are staying in tents; and my lord Joab and the workers of my lord, are encamped in the open field. Shall I then go into my house to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? As you live, and as una soul lives, I go not do this thing!”
David talk say to Uriah, “Stay here today also, and tomorrow I go let you depart.” So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day, and the next day.
When David had call him, he ate and drink before him; and he made him drunk. At evening, he go out to lie on his bed with the workers of his lord, but didn’t go down to his house.
In the morning, David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
He wrote in the letter, saying, “Send Uriah to the forefront of the hottest battle, and retreat from him, that he may be struck, and die.”
When Joab kept watch on the city, he assigned Uriah to the place where he know that valiant men were.
The men of the city go out, and fought with Joab. Some of the people fell, even of David’s workers; and Uriah the Hittite died also.
Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;
and he commanded the messenger, saying, “When you have finished telling all the things concerning the war to the king,
it go be that, if the king’s serious anger arise, and he asks you, ‘Why did you go so near to the city to fight? Didn’t you know that dem would shoot from the wall?

Who struck Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? Didn’t a woman throw an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died at Thebez? Why did you go so near the wall?’ then you shall say, ‘Una worker Uriah the Hittite is also dead.’”
So the messenger go, and come and showed David all that Joab had sent him for.
The messenger talk say to David, “The men prevailed against us, and come out to us into the field, and we were on dem even to the entrance of the gate.
The shooters shot at una workers from off the wall; and some of the king’s workers are dead, and una worker Uriah the Hittite is also dead.”

Then David talk say to the messenger, “Tell Joab, ‘No let this thing displease you, for the sword devours one as well as another. Make una battle stronger against the city, and overthrow it.’ Encourage him.”
When Uriah’s wife heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she mourned for her husband.
When the mourning was past, David sent and take her home to his house, and she became his wife, and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased Baba God.
Baba God sent Nathan to David. He come to him, and talk say to him, “There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.
The rich man had very many flocks and herds,

but the poor man had nothing, except one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and raised. It grew up together with him, and with his pikin dem. It ate of his own chop, drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was like a daughter to him.

A traveler come to the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to prepare for the wayfaring man who had come to him, but take the poor man’s lamb, and prepared it for the man who had come to him.”
David’s anger burned hot against the man, and he talk say to Nathan, “As Baba God lives, the man who has done this deserves to die!
He must restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity!”
Nathan talk say to David, “You be the man. This is what Baba God, the God of Israel, says: ‘I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you out of the hand of Saul.

I give you una master’s house, and una master’s wives into una bosom, and give you the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that would Don dey too little, I would have added to you many more such things.

Why have you despised Baba God’s word, to do that which is evil in his sight? You have struck Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and have taken his wife to be una wife, and have slain him with the sword of the pikin dem of Ammon.
Now so the sword will never depart from una house, because you have despised me, and have taken Uriah the Hittite’s wife to be una wife.’

“This is what Baba God says: ‘See am, I go raise up evil against you out of una own house; and I go take una wives before una eyes, and give dem to una neighbor, and he will lie with una wives in the sight of this sun.
For you did this secretly, but I go do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.’”
David talk say to Nathan, “I have sinned against Baba God.” Nathan talk say to David, “Baba God also has put away una sin. You go not die.
However, because by this deed you have given great occasion to Baba God’s enemies to blaspheme, the pikin also Wey be born to You go surely die.”
Nathan comot to his house. Baba God struck the pikin that Uriah’s wife bore to David, and it was very sick.
David so begged God for the pikin; and David fasted, and go in, and lay all night on the ground.
The elders of his house arose beside him, to raise him up from the earth: but he would not, and he didn’t eat bread with dem.

On the seventh day, the pikin died. David’s workers were afraid to tell him that the pikin was dead, for dem talk say, “See am, while the pikin was yet alive, we spoke to him, and he didn’t listen to our voice. How will he then harm imself, if we tell him that the pikin is dead?”
But when David see that his workers were whispering together, David perceived that the pikin was dead; and David talk say to his workers, “Is the pikin dead?” Dem talk say, “He is dead.”

Then David arose from the earth, and washed, and anointed imself, and changed his clothing; and he come into Baba God’s house, and worshiped. Then he come to his own house; and when he requested, dem set bread before him, and he ate.
Then his workers talk say to him, “Wetin be this that you have done? You fasted and wept for the pikin while he was alive, but when the pikin was dead, you rose up and ate bread.”
He talk say, “While the pikin was yet alive, I fasted and wept; for I talk say, ‘Wey know whether Baba God No go be gracious to me, that the pikin may live?’
But now he is dead, why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I go go to him, but he No go return to me.”
David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and go in to her, and lay with her. She bore a son, and he call his name Solomon. Baba God love him;
and he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he named him Jedidiah, for Baba God’s sake.
Now Joab fought against Rabbah of the pikin dem of Ammon, and take the royal city.
Joab sent messengers to David, and talk say, “I have fought against Rabbah. Yes, I have taken the city of waters.
Now so gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city, and take it; lest I take the city, and it be call by my name.”
David gathered all the people together, and go to Rabbah, and fought against it, and take it.

He take the crown of dem king from off his head; and its weight was a talent of gold, and in it were precious stones; and it was set on David’s head. He bring a great quantity of plunder out of the city.

He bring out the people who were in it, and put dem under saws, under iron picks, under axes of iron, and made dem pass through the brick kiln; and he did so to all the cities of the pikin dem of Ammon. Then David and all the people come back to Jerusalem.
After this, Absalom the son of David had a beautiful sister, whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David love her.
Amnon was so troubled that he became sick because of his sister Tamar; for she was a virgin; and it seemed hard to Amnon to do anything to her.
But Amnon had a friend, whose name was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David’s brother; and Jonadab was a very subtle man.
E tell am say, “Why, son of the king, are you so sad from day to day? No go you tell me?” Amnon talk say to him, “I love Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.”

Jonadab talk say to him, “Lay down on una bed, and pretend to be sick. When una father comes to see you, tell him, ‘Please let my sister Tamar come and give me bread to eat, and prepare the chop in my sight, that I may see it, and eat it from her hand.’”

So Amnon lay down and faked being sick. When the king come to see him, Amnon talk say to the king, “Please let my sister Tamar come, and make me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat from her hand.”
Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, “Go now to una brother Amnon’s house, and prepare chop for him.”
So Tamar go to her brother Amnon’s house; and he was lying down. She take dough, and kneaded it, made cakes in his sight, and baked the cakes.
She take the pan, and poured dem out before him; but he refused to eat. Amnon talk say, “Have all men leave me.” Then every man go out from him.
Amnon talk say to Tamar, “Bring the chop into the room, that I may eat from una hand.” Tamar take the cakes which she had made, and bring dem into the room to Amnon her brother.
When she had bring dem near to him to eat, he take hold of her, and talk say to her, “Come, lie with me, my sister!”
She answer him, “No, my brother, No force me! For no such thing ought to be done in Israel. No you do this folly.
As for me, where would I carry my shame? And as for you, You go be as one of the fools in Israel. Now so, please speak to the king; for he No go withhold me from you.”
However he would not listen to her voice; but being stronger than she, he forced her, and lay with her.
Then Amnon hated her with exceedingly great hatred; for the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had love her. Amnon talk say to her, “Arise, be gone!”
She talk say to him, “Not so, because this great wrong in sending me away is worse than the other that you did to me!” But he would not listen to her.
Then he call his worker who ministered to him, and talk say, “Now put this woman out from me, and bolt the door after her.”
She had a garment of various colors on her; for the king’s daughters who were virgins dressed in such robes. Then his worker bring her out and bolted the door after her.
Tamar put ashes on her head, and tore her garment of various colors that was on her; and she laid her hand on her head, and go her way, crying aloud as she go.

Absalom her brother talk say to her, “Has Amnon una brother been with you? But now hold una peace, my sister. He is una brother. No take this thing to heart.” So Tamar remain desolate in her brother Absalom’s house.
But when king David heard of all these things, he was very angry.
Absalom spoke to Amnon neither good nor bad; for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar.
After two full years, Absalom had sheep shearers in Baal Hazor, which is beside Ephraim: and Absalom invited all the king’s sons.
Absalom come to the king, and talk say, “See now, una worker has sheep shearers. Please let the king and his workers go with una worker.”
The king talk say to Absalom, “No, my son, Make we not all go, lest we be burdensome to you.” He pressed him; however he would not go, but blessed him.
Then Absalom talk say, “If not, please let my brother Amnon go with us.” The king talk say to him, “Why should he go with you?”
But Absalom pressed him, and he let Amnon and all the king’s sons go with him.

Absalom commanded his workers, saying, “Mark now, when Amnon’s heart is merry with wine; and when I tell una, ‘Strike Amnon,’ then kill him. No fear. Haven’t I commanded you? Be courageous, and be valiant!”
The workers of Absalom did to Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king’s sons arose, and every man got up on his mule, and fled.
While dem were on the way, the news come to David, saying, “Absalom has slain all the king’s sons, and there No be one of dem left!”
Then the king arose, and tore his garments, and lay on the earth; and all his workers stood by with dem clothes torn.

Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David’s brother, answer, “No let my lord suppose that dem have killed all the young men the king’s sons; for Amnon only is dead; for by the appointment of Absalom this Don dey determined from the day that he forced his sister Tamar.
Now so no let my lord the king take the thing to his heart, to think that all the king’s sons are dead; for only Amnon is dead.”
But Absalom fled. The young man who kept the watch lifted up his eyes, and looked, and see am, many people were coming by way of the hillside behind him.
Jonadab talk say to the king, “See am, the king’s sons are coming! It is as una worker talk say.”
As soon as he had finished speaking, see am, the king’s sons come, and lifted up dem voice, and wept. The king also and all his workers wept bitterly.
But Absalom fled, and go to Talmai the son of Ammihur, king of Geshur. David mourned for his son every day.
So Absalom fled, and go to Geshur, and was there three years.
King David longed to go out to Absalom; for he was comforted concerning Amnon, since he was dead.
Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart was toward Absalom.

Joab sent to Tekoa, and bring a wise woman from there, and talk say to her, “Please act like a mourner, and put on mourning clothing, please, and no anoint yourself with oil, but be as a woman who has mourned a long time for the dead.
Go in to the king, and speak like this to him.” So Joab put the words in her mouth.
When the woman of Tekoa spoke to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, showed respect, and talk say, “Help, O king!”
The king talk say to her, “What ails you?” She answer, “Truly I be a widow, and my husband is dead.
Una worker had two sons, and dem both fought together in the field, and there was Nobody to part dem, but the one struck the other, and killed him.

See am, the whole family has risen against una worker, and dem say, ‘Deliver him who struck his brother, that we may kill him for the life of his brother whom he killed, and so destroy the heir also.’ Thus dem would quench my coal which is left, and would leave to my husband neither name nor remainder on the surface of the earth.”
The king talk say to the woman, “Go to una house, and I go give a command concerning you.”
The woman of Tekoa talk say to the king, “My lord, O king, may the wickedness be on me, and on my father’s house; and may the king and his throne be guiltless.”
The king talk say, “Anybody wey says anything to you, bring him to me, and he No go bother you any more.”

Then she talk say, “Please let the king remember Baba God una God, that the avenger of blood destroy not any more, lest dem destroy my son.” He talk say, “As Baba God lives, not one hair of una son shall fall to the earth.”
Then the woman talk say, “Please let una worker speak a word to my lord the king.” He talk say, “Say on.”

The woman talk say, “Why then have you devised such a thing against the people of God? For in speaking this word the king is as one Wey be guilty, in that the king No dey bring home again his banished one.
For we must die, and are like water spilled on the ground, which no fit be gathered up again; neither does God take away life, but devises means, that person Wey banished not be an outcast from him.

Now so seeing that I have come to speak this word to my lord the king, it is because the people have made me afraid. Una worker talk say, ‘I go now speak to the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his worker.’
For the king will hear, to deliver his worker out of the hand of the man who would destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.
Then una worker talk say, ‘Please let the word of my lord the king bring rest; for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and bad. May Baba God, una God, be with you.’”
Then the king answer the woman, “Please no hide anything from me that I ask you.” The woman talk say, “Let my lord the king now speak.”

The king talk say, “Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?” The woman answer, “As una soul lives, my lord the king, Nobody can turn to the right hand or to the left from anything that my lord the king has spoken; for una worker Joab urged me, and he put all these words in the mouth of una worker;
to change the face of the matter has una worker Joab done this thing. My lord is wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are in the earth.”
The king talk say to Joab, “See am now, I have done this thing. Go so, and bring the young man Absalom back.”

Joab fell to the ground on his face, showed respect, and blessed the king. Joab talk say, “Today una worker knows that I have find favor in una sight, my lord, king, in that the king has performed the request of his worker.”
So Joab arose and go to Geshur, and bring Absalom to Jerusalem.
The king talk say, “Make e return to his own house, but Make e not see my face.” So Absalom come back to his own house, and didn’t see the king’s face.
Now in all Israel there was Nobody to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty. From the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no defect in him.

When he cut the hair of his head (now it was at every year’s end that he cut it; because it was heavy on him, so he cut it); he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels, after the king’s weight.
Three sons were born to Absalom, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar. She was a woman with a beautiful face.
Absalom lived two full years in Jerusalem, and he didn’t see the king’s face.
Then Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king, but he would not come to him. Then he sent again a second time, but he would not come.
So he talk say to his workers, “See am, Joab’s field is near mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire.” So Absalom’s workers set the field on fire.
Then Joab arose, and come to Absalom to his house, and talk say to him, “Why have una workers set my field on fire?”

Absalom answer Joab, “See am, I sent to you, saying, ‘Come here, that I may send you to the king, to say, “Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me to be there still. Now so let me see the king’s face, and if E get wickedness in me, Make e kill me.”’”
So Joab come to the king, and told him; and when he had call for Absalom, he come to the king, and bowed imself on his face to the ground before the king; and the king kissed Absalom.
After this, Absalom prepared a chariot and horses for imself, and fifty men to run before him.

Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate. When any man had a suit which should come to the king for judgment, then Absalom call to him, and talk say, “What city are you from?” He talk say, “Una worker is of one of the tribes of Israel.”
Absalom talk say to him, “See am, una matters are good and right; but E get no man deputized by the king to hear you.”
Absalom talk say moreover, “Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man who has any suit or cause might come to me, and I would do him justice!”
It was so, that when any man come near to do him obeisance, he stretched out his hand, and take hold of him, and kissed him.
Absalom did this sort of thing to all Israel who come to the king for judgment. So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
At the end of forty years, Absalom talk say to the king, “Please let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed to Baba God, in Hebron.
For una worker vowed a vow while I stayed at Geshur in Syria, saying, ‘If Baba God shall indeed bring me again to Jerusalem, then I go serve Baba God.’”
The king talk say to him, “Go in peace.” So he arose, and go to Hebron.
But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, “As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then you shall say, ‘Absalom is king in Hebron!’”
Two hundred men go with Absalom out of Jerusalem, who were invited, and go in dem simplicity; and dem didn’t know anything.

Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, from his city, even from Giloh, while he was offering the sacrifices. The conspiracy was strong; for the people increased continually with Absalom.
A messenger come to David, saying, “The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.”

David talk say to all his workers who were with him at Jerusalem, “Arise, and Make we flee; or else none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry to depart, lest he overtake us sharp-sharp, and bring down evil on us, and strike the city with the edge of the sword.”
The king’s workers talk say to the king, “See am, una workers are ready to do Anything wey my lord the king chooses.”
The king go out, and all his household after him. The king left ten women, who were concubines, to keep the house.
The king go out, and all the people after him; and dem stayed in Beth Merhak.
All his workers passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who come after him from Gath, passed on before the king.
Then the king talk say to Ittai the Gittite, “Why do you also go with us? Return, and stay with the king; for You be a foreigner, and also an exile. Return to una own place.
Whereas you come but yesterday, should I today make you go up and down with us, since I go where I may? Return, and take back una brothers. Mercy and truth be with you.”
Ittai answer the king, and talk say, “As Baba God lives, and as my lord the king lives, surely in what place my lord the king is, whether for death or for life, una worker Go be there also.”
David talk say to Ittai, “Go and pass over.” Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones who were with him.
All the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over. The king also imself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over, toward the way of the wilderness.
See am, Zadok also come, and all the Levites with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God; and dem set down God’s ark; and Abiathar go up, until all the people finished passing out of the city.
The king talk say to Zadok, “Carry God’s ark back into the city. If I find favor in Baba God’s eyes, he will bring me again, and show me both it, and his habitation;
but if he says, ‘I have no delight in you;’ see am, here am I. Make e do to me as seems good to him.”
The king talk say also to Zadok the priest, “No be you a seer? Return into the city in peace, and una two sons with you, Ahimaaz una son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.
See am, I go stay at the fords of the wilderness, until word comes from you to inform me.”
Zadok so and Abiathar carried God’s ark to Jerusalem again; and dem stayed there.

David go up by the ascent of the Mount of Olives, and wept as he go up; and he had his head covered, and go barefoot: and all the people who were with him each covered his head, and dem go up, weeping as dem go up.
Someone told David, saying, “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.” David talk say, “Baba God, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.”
When David had come to the top, where God was worshiped, see am, Hushai the Archite come to meet him with his coat torn, and earth on his head.
David talk say to him, “If you pass on with me, then You go be a burden to me;

but if you return to the city, and tell Absalom, ‘I go be una worker, O king. As I Don dey una father’s worker in time past, so will I now be una worker; then will you defeat for me the counsel of Ahithophel.’
No you have Zadok and Abiathar the priests there with you? So Anything wey you hear out of the king’s house, tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
See am, dem have there with dem dem two sons, Ahimaaz, Zadok’s son, and Jonathan, Abiathar’s son. Send to me everything that you shall hear by dem.”
So Hushai, David’s friend, come into the city; and Absalom come into Jerusalem.

When David was a little past the top, see am, Ziba the worker of Mephibosheth met him with a couple of donkeys saddled, and on dem two hundred loaves of bread, and one hundred clusters of raisins, and one hundred summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.

The king talk say to Ziba, “What do you mean by these?” Ziba talk say, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine, that people Wey faint in the wilderness may drink.”
The king talk say, “Where is una master’s son?” Ziba talk say to the king, “See am, he is staying in Jerusalem; for he talk say, ‘Today the house of Israel will restore me the kingdom of my father.’”
Then the king talk say to Ziba, “See am, all that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours.” Ziba talk say, “I bow down. Let me find favor in una sight, my lord, O king.”
When king David come to Bahurim, see am, a man of the family of Saul’s house come out, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera. He come out and cursed as he come.
He throw stones at David, and at all the workers of king David, and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.
Shimei talk say when he cursed, “Be gone, be gone, you man of blood, and base fellow!

Baba God has come back on you all the blood of Saul’s house, in whose place you have reigned! Baba God has delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom una son! See am, You be caught by una own mischief, because You be a man of blood!”
Then Abishai the son of Zeruiah talk say to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Please let me go over and take off his head.”
The king talk say, “What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? Because he curses, and because Baba God has talk say to him, ‘Curse David;’ who then shall say, ‘Why have you done so?’”

David talk say to Abishai, and to all his workers, “See am, my son, who come out of my bowels, seeks my life. How much more this Benjamite, now? Leave him alone, and Make e curse; for Baba God has invited him.
It may be that Baba God will look on the wrong done to me, and that Baba God will repay me good for the cursing of me today.”
So David and his men go by the way; and Shimei go along on the hillside opposite him, and cursed as he go, threw stones at him, and threw dust.
The king, and all the people who were with him, come weary; and he refreshed imself there.
Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, come to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.
When Hushai the Archite, David’s friend, had come to Absalom, Hushai talk say to Absalom, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
Absalom talk say to Hushai, “Is this una kindness to una friend? Why didn’t you go with una friend?”
Hushai talk say to Absalom, “No; but whomever Baba God, and this people, and all the men of Israel have chosen, his will I be, and with him I go stay.
Again, whom should I serve? Shouldn’t I serve in the presence of his son? As I have served in una father’s presence, so will I be in una presence.”
Then Absalom talk say to Ahithophel, “Give una counsel what we shall do.”

Ahithophel talk say to Absalom, “Go in to una father’s concubines that he has left to keep the house. Then all Israel will hear that You be abhorred by una father. Then the hands of all Wey be with You go be strong.”
So dem spread a tent for Absalom on the top of the house, and Absalom go in to his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
The counsel of Ahithophel, which he give in those days, was as if a man inquired at the inner sanctuary of God. So was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.
Moreover Ahithophel talk say to Absalom, “Let me now choose twelve thousand men, and I go arise and pursue after David tonight.
I go come on him while he is weary and exhausted, and will make him afraid. All the people Wey be with him will flee. I go strike the king only,
and I go bring back all the people to you. The man whom you seek is as if all come back. All the people go be in peace.”
The saying pleased Absalom well, and all the elders of Israel.
Then Absalom talk say, “Now call Hushai the Archite also, and Make we hear likewise what he says.”
When Hushai had come to Absalom, Absalom spoke to him, saying, “Ahithophel has spoken like this. Shall we do what he says? If not, speak up.”
Hushai talk say to Absalom, “The counsel that Ahithophel has given this time No be good.”

Hushai talk say moreover, “You know una father and his men, that Dem be mighty men, and Dem be fierce in dem minds, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the field. Una father is a man of war, and No go lodge with the people.

See am, he is now hidden in some pit, or in some other place. It will happen, when some of dem have fallen at the first, that Anybody wey hears it will say, ‘E get a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom!’
Even person Wey valiant, whose heart is as the heart of a lion, will utterly melt; for all Israel knows that una father is a mighty man, and people Wey with him are valiant men.
But I counsel that all Israel be gathered together to you, from Dan even to Beersheba, as the sand that is by the sea for plenty people; and that you go to battle in una own person.
So shall we come on him in some place where he go be find, and We go light on him as the dew falls on the ground; and of him and of all the men Wey be with him We go not leave so much as one.
Moreover, if he has gone into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city, and We go draw it into the river, until there no be one small stone find there.”

Absalom and all the men of Israel talk say, “The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel.” For Baba God had ordained to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that Baba God might bring evil on Absalom.
Then Hushai talk say to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, “Ahithophel counseled Absalom and the elders of Israel that way; and I have counseled this way.
Now so send sharp-sharp, and tell David, saying, ‘No lodge tonight at the fords of the wilderness, but by all means pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people Wey be with him.’”
Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying by En Rogel; and a female worker used to go and tell dem; and dem go and told king David. For dem might not be seen to come into the city.
But a boy see dem, and told Absalom. Then dem both go away sharp-sharp, and come to the house of a man in Bahurim, who had a well in his court; and dem go down there.
The woman take and spread the covering over the well’s mouth, and spread out bruised grain on it; and nothing was known.

Absalom’s workers come to the woman to the house; and dem talk say, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman talk say to dem, “Dem have gone over the brook of water.” When dem had sought and could not find dem, dem come back to Jerusalem.
After dem had comot, dem come up out of the well, and go and told king David; and dem talk say to David, “Arise and pass sharp-sharp over the water; for thus has Ahithophel counseled against you.”
Then David arose, and all the people who were with him, and dem passed over the Jordan. By the morning light there lacked not one of dem who had not gone over the Jordan.

When Ahithophel see that his counsel No be follow, he saddled his donkey, arose, and go home, to his city, and set his house in order, and hanged imself; and he died, and was buried in the tomb of his father.
Then David come to Mahanaim. Absalom passed over the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.
Absalom set Amasa over the army instead of Joab. Now Amasa was the son of a man whose name was Ithra the Israelite, who go in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah, Joab’s mother.
Israel and Absalom encamped in the land of Gilead.
When David had come to Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the pikin dem of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lodebar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
bring beds, basins, earthen vessels, wheat, barley, meal, parched grain, beans, lentils, roasted grain,
honey, butter, sheep, and cheese of the herd, for David, and for the people who were with him, to eat; for dem talk say, “The people are hungry, and weary, and thirsty in the wilderness.”
David counted the people who were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over dem.

David sent the people out, a third part under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. The king talk say to the people, “I go also surely go out with you myself.”

But the people talk say, “You no go go out; for if we flee away, Dem go not care for us; neither if half of us die, will dem care for us. But You be worth ten thousand of us. So now it is better that You be ready to help us out of the city.”
The king talk say to dem, “I go do what seems best to you.” The king stood beside the gate, and all the people go out by hundreds and by thousands.

The king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, “Deal gently for my sake with the young man, even with Absalom.” All the people heard when the king commanded all the captains concerning Absalom.
So the people go out into the field against Israel; and the battle was in the forest of Ephraim.
The people of Israel were struck there before David’s workers, and there was a great slaughter there that day of twenty thousand men.
For the battle was there spread over the surface of all the country, and the forest devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.

Absalom happened to meet David’s workers. Absalom was riding on his mule, and the mule go under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the sky and earth; and the mule that was under him go on.
A certain man see it, and told Joab, and talk say, “See am, I see Absalom hanging in an oak.”
Joab talk say to the man who told him, “See am, you see it, and why didn’t you strike him there to the ground? I would have given you ten pieces of silver, and a sash.”

The man talk say to Joab, “Though I should receive a thousand pieces of silver in my hand, I still wouldn’t stretch out my hand against the king’s son; for in our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, ‘Beware that Nobody touch the young man Absalom.’
Otherwise if I had dealt falsely against his life (and E get no matter hidden from the king), then you yourself would have set yourself against me.”
Then Joab talk say, “I’m not going to wait like this with you.” He take three darts in his hand, and thrust dem through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in the middle of the oak.
Ten young men who bore Joab’s armor surrounded and struck Absalom, and killed him.
Joab blew the trumpet, and the people come back from pursuing after Israel; for Joab held the people back.
Dem take Absalom and throw him into the great pit in the forest, and raised over him a plenty well-well heap of stones. Then all Israel fled, each to his own tent.

Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for imself the pillar which is in the king’s valley, for he talk say, “I have no son to keep my name in memory.” He call the pillar after his own name. It is call Absalom’s monument, to this day.
Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok talk say, “Let me now run, and carry the king news, how Baba God has avenged him of his enemies.”
Joab talk say to him, “You must not be the bearer of news today, but you must carry news another day. But today you must carry no news, because the king’s son is dead.”
Then Joab talk say to the Cushite, “Go, tell the king Wetin you have seen!” The Cushite bowed imself to Joab, and ran.

Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok talk say yet again to Joab, “But come what may, please let me also run after the Cushite.” Joab talk say, “Why do you want to run, my son, since that You go have no reward for the news?”
“But come what may,” he talk say, “I go run.” E tell am say, “Run!” Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the Plain, and outran the Cushite.
Now David was sitting between the two gates; and the watchman go up to the roof of the gate to the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, see am, a man running alone.
The watchman cried, and told the king. The king talk say, “If he is alone, E get news in his mouth.” He come closer and closer.
The watchman see another man running; and the watchman call to the porter, and talk say, “See am, a man running alone!” The king talk say, “He also brings news.”
The watchman talk say, “I think the running of the first one is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” The king talk say, “He is a good man, and comes with better news.”

Ahimaaz call, and talk say to the king, “All is well.” He bowed imself before the king with his face to the earth, and talk say, “Blessed is Baba God una God, who has delivered up the men who lifted up dem hand against my lord the king!”
The king talk say, “Is it well with the young man Absalom?” Ahimaaz answer, “When Joab sent the king’s worker, even me una worker, I see a great tumult, but I no know what it was.”
The king talk say, “Turn aside, and stand here.” He turned aside, and stood still.
See am, the Cushite come. The Cushite talk say, “News for my lord the king, for Baba God has avenged you today of all people wey rose up against you.”

The king talk say to the Cushite, “Is it well with the young man Absalom?” The Cushite answer, “May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rise up against you to do you harm, be as that young man is.”
The king was much moved, and go up to the room over the gate, and wept. As he go, he talk say, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I had died for you, Absalom, my son, my son!”
Joab was told, “See am, the king weeps and mourns for Absalom.”
The victory that day was turned into mourning among all the people; for the people heard it talk say that day, “The king grieves for his son.”
The people sneaked into the city that day, as people Wey be ashamed steal away when dem flee in battle.
The king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, “My son Absalom, Absalom, my son, my son!”

Joab come into the house to the king, and talk say, “Today you have shamed the faces of all una workers, who today have saved una life, and the lives of una sons and of una daughters, and the lives of una wives, and the lives of una concubines;

in that you love people wey hate you, and hate people wey love you. For you have declared today, that princes and workers are nothing to you. For today I perceive that if Absalom had lived, and all we had died today, then it would have pleased you well.

Now so arise, go out, and speak to comfort una workers; for I swear by Baba God, if you no go out, not a man will stay with you this night. That would be worse to you than all the evil that has happened to you from una youth until now.”

Then the king arose, and sat in the gate. Dem told to all the people, saying, “See am, the king is sitting in the gate.” All the people come before the king. Now Israel had fled every man to his tent.

All the people were at strife throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, “The king delivered us out of the hand of our enemies, and he saved us out of the hand of the Philistines; and now he has fled out of the land from Absalom.
Absalom, whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now so why no you speak a word of bringing the king back?”

King David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, “Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, ‘Why are you the last to bring the king back to his house? Since the speech of all Israel has come to the king, to return him to his house.
You be my brothers. You be my bone and my flesh. Why then are you the last to bring back the king?’
Say to Amasa, ‘No be you my bone and my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if you no be captain of the army before me continually instead of Joab.’”
He bowed the heart of all the men of Judah, even as one man; so that dem sent to the king, saying, “Return, you and all una workers.”
So the king come back, and come to the Jordan. Judah come to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to bring the king over the Jordan.
Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite, who was of Bahurim, hurried and come down with the men of Judah to meet king David.
There were a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the worker of Saul’s house, and his fifteen sons and his twenty workers with him; and dem go through the Jordan in the presence of the king.
A ferry boat go to bring over the king’s household, and to do what he thought good. Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king, when he had come over the Jordan.

He talk say to the king, “No let my lord impute wickedness to me, or remember that which una worker did perversely the day that my lord the king go out of Jerusalem, that the king should take it to his heart.
For una worker knows that I have sinned. So see am, I have come today as the first of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.”
But Abishai the son of Zeruiah answer, “Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed Baba God’s anointed?”

David talk say, “What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah, that you should be adversaries to me today? Shall any man be put to death today in Israel? For no I know that I be king over Israel today?”
The king talk say to Shimei, “You go not die.” The king swore to him.

Mephibosheth the son of Saul come down to meet the king; and he had neither groomed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king comot until the day he come home in peace.
When he had come to Jerusalem to meet the king, the king talk say to him, “Why didn’t you go with me, Mephibosheth?”
He answer, “My lord, O king, my worker deceived me. For una worker talk say, I go saddle me a donkey, that I may ride on it, and go with the king; because una worker is lame.
He has slandered una worker to my lord the king, but my lord the king is as an angel of God. Do so Wetin be good in una eyes.
For all my father’s house were but dead men before my lord the king; yet you set una worker among people wey ate at una own table. What right so have I yet that I should cry any more to the king?”
The king talk say to him, “Why do you speak any more of una matters? I say, you and Ziba divide the land.”
Mephibosheth talk say to the king, “Yes, Make e take all, because my lord the king has come in peace to his own house.”
Barzillai the Gileadite come down from Rogelim; and he go over the Jordan with the king, to conduct him over the Jordan.
Now Barzillai was a very aged man, even eighty years old. He had provided the king with sustenance while he stayed at Mahanaim; for he was a plenty well-well man.
The king talk say to Barzillai, “Come over with me, and I go sustain you with me in Jerusalem.”
Barzillai talk say to the king, “How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?

I be eighty years old, today. Can I discern between good and bad? Can una worker taste what I eat or what I drink? Can I hear the voice of singing men and singing women any more? Why then should una worker be a burden to my lord the king?
Una worker would but just go over the Jordan with the king. Why should the king repay me with such a reward?

Please let una worker turn back again, that I may die in my own city, by the grave of my father and my mother. But see am, una worker Chimham; Make e go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good to you.”
The king answer, “Chimham shall go over with me, and I go do to him that which shall seem good to you. Anything wey you request of me, that I go do for you.”
All the people go over the Jordan, and the king go over. Then the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he come back to his own place.
So the king go over to Gilgal, and Chimham go over with him. All the people of Judah bring the king over, and also half the people of Israel.

See am, all the men of Israel come to the king, and talk say to the king, “Why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen you away, and bring the king, and his household, over the Jordan, and all David’s men with him?”

All the men of Judah answer the men of Israel, “Because the king is a close relative to us. Why then are you angry about this matter? Have we eaten at all at the king’s cost? Or has he given us any gift?”

The men of Israel answer the men of Judah, and talk say, “We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more claim to David than you. Why then did you despise us, that our advice no suppose be first had in bringing back our king?” The words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.

There happened to be there a base fellow, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite; and he blew the trumpet, and talk say, “We have no portion in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse. Every man to his tents, Israel!”
So all the men of Israel go up from following David, and follow Sheba the son of Bichri; but the men of Judah joined with dem king, from the Jordan even to Jerusalem.

David come to his house at Jerusalem; and the king take the ten women his concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put dem in custody, and provided dem with sustenance, but didn’t go in to dem. So dem were shut up to the day of dem death, living in widowhood.
Then the king talk say to Amasa, “Call me the men of Judah together within three days, and be here present.”
So Amasa go to call the men of Judah together; but he stayed longer than the set time which he had appointed him.

David talk say to Abishai, “Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom did. Take una lord’s workers, and pursue after him, lest he get imself fortified cities, and escape out of our sight.”
Joab’s men go out after him, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men; and dem go out of Jerusalem, to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.

When dem were at the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa come to meet dem. Joab was clothed in his apparel of war that he had put on, and on it was a sash with a sword fastened on his waist in its sheath; and as he go along it fell out.
Joab talk say to Amasa, “Is it well with you, my brother?” Joab take Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him.

But Amasa take no heed to the sword that was in Joab’s hand. So he struck him with it in the body, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and didn’t strike him again; and he died. Joab and Abishai his brother pursued Sheba the son of Bichri.
One of Joab’s young men stood by him, and talk say, “Person wey favors Joab, and person Wey for David, Make e follow Joab!”

Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the highway. When the man see that all the people stood still, he carried Amasa out of the highway into the field, and throw a garment over him, when he see that Everybody wey come by him stood still.
When he was removed out of the highway, all the people go on after Joab, to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.
He go through all the tribes of Israel to Abel, and to Beth Maacah, and all the Berites. Dem were gathered together, and go also after him.

Dem come and besieged him in Abel of Beth Maacah, and dem throw up a mound against the city, and it stood against the rampart; and all the people who were with Joab battered the wall, to throw it down.
Then a wise woman cried out of the city, “Hear, hear! Please say to Joab, ‘Come near here, that I may speak with you.’”
He come near to her; and the woman talk say, “Are you Joab?” He answer, “I be.” Then she talk say to him, “Hear the words of una worker.” He answer, “I’m listening.”
Then she spoke, saying, “Dem used to say in old times, ‘Dem shall surely ask counsel at Abel;’ and so dem settled a matter.
I be among people Wey peaceable and faithful in Israel. You seek to destroy a city and a mother in Israel. Why will you swallow up Baba God’s inheritance?”
Joab answer, “Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy.

The matter No be so. But a man of the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, has lifted up his hand against the king, even against David. Just deliver him, and I go depart from the city.” The woman talk say to Joab, “See am, his head Go be thrown to you over the wall.”

Then the woman go to all the people in her wisdom. Dem cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and threw it out to Joab. He blew the trumpet, and dem were dispersed from the city, every man to his tent. Then Joab come back to Jerusalem to the king.
Now Joab was over all the army of Israel, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites,
Adoram was over the men subject to forced labor, Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was the recorder,
Sheva was scribe, and Zadok and Abiathar were priests,
and Ira the Jairite was chief minister to David.

There was a famine in the days of David for three years, year after year; and David sought the face of Baba God. Baba God talk say, “It is for Saul, and for his bloody house, because he put the Gibeonites to death.”

The king call the Gibeonites, and talk say to dem (now the Gibeonites No be of the pikin dem of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites, and the pikin dem of Israel had sworn to dem; and Saul sought to kill dem in his zeal for the pikin dem of Israel and Judah);
and David talk say to the Gibeonites, “What should I do for you? And with what should I make atonement, that you may bless Baba God’s inheritance?”

The Gibeonites talk say to him, “It is no matter of silver or gold between us and Saul, or his house; neither is it for us to put any man to death in Israel.” He talk say, “Anything wey you say, that I go do for you.”
Dem talk say to the king, “The man who consumed us, and who devised against us, that we should be destroyed from remaining in any of the borders of Israel,
let seven men of his sons be delivered to us, and We go hang dem up to Baba God in Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of Baba God.” The king talk say, “I go give dem.”
But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of Baba God’s oath that was between dem, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

But the king take the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bore to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she bore to Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite.

He delivered dem into the hands of the Gibeonites, and dem hanged dem on the mountain before Baba God, and all seven of dem fell together. Dem were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, at the beginning of barley harvest.

Rizpah the daughter of Aiah take sackcloth, and spread it for sheself on the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water poured on dem from the sky. She allowed neither the birds of the sky to rest on dem by day, nor the animals of the field by night.
David was told what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.

So David go and take the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh Gilead, who had stolen dem from the street of Beth Shan, where the Philistines had hanged dem, in the day that the Philistines killed Saul in Gilboa;
and he bring up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son. Dem also gathered the bones of people wey were hanged.

Dem buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the country of Benjamin in Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father: and dem performed all that the king commanded. After that, God answer prayer for the land.
The Philistines had war again with Israel; and David go down, and his workers with him, and fought against the Philistines. David grew faint;
and Ishbibenob, who was of the sons of the giant, the weight of whose spear was three hundred shekels of brass in weight, he being armed with a new sword, thought he would kill David.

But Abishai the son of Zeruiah helped him, and struck the Philistine, and killed him. Then the men of David swore to him, saying, “No go out with us to battle any more, so that you no quench the lamp of Israel.”
After this, that there was again war with the Philistines at Gob. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Saph, who was of the sons of the giant.
There was again war with the Philistines at Gob; and Elhanan the son of Jaare-Oregim the Bethlehemite killed Goliath the Gittite’s brother, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
There was again war at Gath, where there was a man of great stature, who had six fingers on every hand, and six toes on every foot, twenty four in count; and he also was born to the giant.
When he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimei, David’s brother, killed him.
These four were born to the giant in Gath; and dem fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his workers.
David spoke to Baba God the words of this song in the day that Baba God delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul,
and he talk say: “Baba God is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer, even mine;
God is my rock in whom I take refuge; my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower, and my refuge. My savior, you save me from violence.
I call on Baba God, Wey be worthy to be praised; So shall I be saved from my enemies.
For the waves of death surrounded me. The floods of ungodliness made me afraid.
The cords of Sheol were around me. The snares of death caught me.
In my distress, I call on Baba God. Yes, I call to my God. He heard my voice out of his temple. My cry come into his ears.
Then the earth shook and trembled. The foundations of heaven quaked and were shaken, because he was angry.
Smoke go up out of his nostrils. Consuming fire come out of his mouth. Coals were kindled by it.
He bowed the heavens also, and come down. Thick darkness was under his feet.
He rode on a cherub, and flew. Yes, he was seen on the wings of the wind.
He made darkness a shelter around imself: gathering of waters, and thick clouds of the skies.
At the brightness before him, coals of fire were kindled.
Baba God thundered from heaven. The Most High uttered his voice.
He sent out arrows, and scattered dem; lightning, and confused dem.
Then the channels of the sea appeared. The foundations of the world were laid bare by Baba God’s rebuke, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.
He sent from on high and he take me. He drew me out of many waters.
He delivered me from my strong enemy, from people wey hated me, for dem were too mighty for me.
Dem come on me in the day of my calamity, but Baba God was my support.
He also bring me out into a large place. He delivered me, because he delighted in me.
Baba God rewarded me according to my righteousness. He rewarded me according to the cleanness of my hands.
For I have kept Baba God’s ways, and have not wickedly comot from my God.
For all his ordinances were before me. As for his statutes, I No depart from dem.
I was also perfect toward him. I kept myself from my wickedness.
So Baba God has rewarded me according to my righteousness, According to my cleanness in his eyesight.
With the merciful You go show yourself merciful. With the perfect man You go show yourself perfect.
With the pure You go show yourself pure. With the crooked You go show yourself shrewd.
You go save the afflicted people, But una eyes are on the haughty, that you may bring dem down.
For You be my lamp, Baba God. Baba God will light up my darkness.
For by you, I run against a troop. By my God, I leap over a wall.
As for God, his way is perfect. Baba God’s word is tested. He is a shield to all people wey take refuge in him.
For Wey be God, besides Baba God? Wey be a rock, besides our God?
God is my strong fortress. He makes my way perfect.
He makes his feet like hinds’ feet, and sets me on my high places.
He teaches my hands to war, so that my arms bend a bow of brass.
You have also given me the shield of una salvation. Una gentleness has made me great.
You have enlarged my steps under me. My feet have not slipped.
I have pursued my enemies and destroyed dem. I didn’t turn again until dem were consumed.
I have consumed dem, and struck dem through, so that dem no fit arise. Yes, dem have fallen under my feet.
For you have armed me with strength for the battle. You have subdued under me people wey rose up against me.
You have also made my enemies turn dem backs to me, that I might cut off people wey hate me.
Dem looked, but there was Nobody to save; even to Baba God, but he didn’t answer dem.
Then I beat dem as small as the dust of the earth. I crushed dem as the mire of the streets, and spread dem abroad.
You also have delivered me from the strivings of my people. You have kept me to be the head of the nations. A people whom I have not known will serve me.
The foreigners will submit themselves to me. As soon as dem hear of me, Dem go obey me.
The foreigners will fade away, and will come trembling out of dem close places.
Baba God lives! Blessed be my rock! Exalted be God, the rock of my salvation,
even the God who executes vengeance for me, who brings down peoples under me,
who brings me away from my enemies. Yes, you lift me up above people wey rise up against me. You deliver me from the violent man.
So I go Thank God to you, Baba God, among the nations, and will sing praises to una name.
He gives great deliverance to his king, and shows loving kindness to his anointed, to David and to his offspring, forever more.”
Now these are the last words of David. David the son of Jesse says, the man who was raised on high says, the anointed of the God of Jacob, the sweet psalmist of Israel:
“Baba God’s Spirit spoke by me. His word was on my tongue.
The God of Israel talk say, the Rock of Israel spoke to me, ‘One who rules over men righteously, who rules in the fear of God,
go be as the light of the morning, when the sun rises, a morning without clouds, when the tender grass springs out of the earth, through clear shining after rain.’

Most certainly my house No be so with God, yet he has made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure, for it is all my salvation, and all my desire, although he no dey make it grow.
But all the ungodly Go be as thorns to be thrust away, because dem no fit be taken with the hand,
But the man who touches dem must be armed with iron and the staff of a spear. Dem go be utterly burned with fire in dem place.”
These are the names of the mighty men whom David had: Josheb Basshebeth a Tahchemonite, chief of the captains; the same was Adino the Eznite, against eight hundred slain at one time.

After him was Eleazar the son of Dodai the son of an Ahohite, one of the three mighty men with David, when dem defied the Philistines who were there gathered together to battle, and the men of Israel had gone away.
He arose and struck the Philistines until his hand was weary, and his hand froze to the sword; and Baba God worked a great victory that day; and the people come back after him only to take plunder.
After him was Shammah the son of Agee a Hararite. The Philistines had gathered together into a troop, where there was a plot of ground full of lentils; and the people fled from the Philistines.
But he stood in the middle of the plot and defended it, and killed the Philistines; and Baba God worked a great victory.
Three of the thirty chief men go down, and come to David in the harvest time to the cave of Adullam; and the troop of the Philistines was encamped in the valley of Rephaim.
David was then in the stronghold; and the garrison of the Philistines was then in Bethlehem.
David longed, and talk say, “Oh that someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem, which is by the gate!”

The three mighty men broke through the army of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem that was by the gate, and take it and bring it to David; but he would not drink of it, but poured it out to Baba God.
He talk say, “Be it far from me, Baba God, that I should do this! No be this the blood of the men who risked dem lives to go?” So he would not drink it. The three mighty men did these things.
Abishai, the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was chief of the three. He lifted up his spear against three hundred and killed dem, and had a name among the three.
No be he most honorable of the three? so he was made dem captain. However he no be included as one of the three.

Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, who had done mighty deeds, killed the two sons of Ariel of Moab. He also go down and killed a lion in the middle of a pit in a time of snow.
He killed a huge Egyptian, and the Egyptian had a spear in his hand; but he go down to him with a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did these things, and had a name among the three mighty men.
He was more honorable than the thirty, but he didn’t attain to the three. David set him over his guard.
Asahel the brother of Joab was one of the thirty: Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
Helez the Paltite, Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,
Abiezer the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
Heleb the son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the pikin dem of Benjamin,
Benaiah a Pirathonite, Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash.
Abialbon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam the son of Sharar the Ararite,
Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maacathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
Hezro the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,
Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, armor bearers to Joab the son of Zeruiah,
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
and Uriah the Hittite: thirty-seven in all.
Again Baba God’s anger burned against Israel, and he moved David against dem, saying, “Go, count Israel and Judah.”

The king talk say to Joab the captain of the army, who was with him, “Now go back and forth through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beersheba, and count the people, that I may know the sum of the people.”

Joab talk say to the king, “Now may Baba God una God add to the people, however many dem may be, one hundred times; and may the eyes of my lord the king see it. But why does my lord the king delight in this thing?”
Notwithstanding, the king’s word prevailed against Joab, and against the captains of the army. Joab and the captains of the army go out from the presence of the king to count the people of Israel.
Dem passed over the Jordan, and encamped in Aroer, on the right side of the city that is in the middle of the valley of Gad, and to Jazer;
then dem come to Gilead, and to the land of Tahtim Hodshi; and dem come to Dan Jaan, and around to Sidon,
and come to the stronghold of Tyre, and to all the cities of the Hivites, and of the Canaanites; and dem go out to the south of Judah, at Beersheba.
So when dem had gone back and forth through all the land, dem come to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
Joab give up the sum of the counting of the people to the king: and there were in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men who drew the sword; and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.

David’s heart struck him after he had counted the people. David talk say to Baba God, “I have sinned greatly in that which I have done. But now, Baba God, put away, I beg you, the wickedness of una worker; for I have done very foolishly.”
When David rose up in the morning, Baba God’s word come to the prophet Gad, David’s seer, saying,
“Go and speak to David, ‘Baba God says, “I offer you three things. Choose one of dem, that I may do it to you.”’”

So Gad come to David, and told him, and talk say to him, “Shall seven years of famine come to you in una land? Or will you flee three months before una foes while dem pursue you? Or shall there be three days’ pestilence in una land? Now answer, and consider what answer I shall return to him who sent me.”
David talk say to Gad, “I be in distress. Make we fall now into Baba God’s hand; for his mercies are great. Let me not fall into man’s hand.”
So Baba God sent a pestilence on Israel from the morning even to the appointed time; and seventy thousand men died of the people from Dan even to Beersheba.

When the angel stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, Baba God relented of the disaster, and talk say to the angel who destroyed the people, “It is enough. Now withdraw una hand.” Baba God’s angel was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

David spoke to Baba God when he see the angel who struck the people, and talk say, “See am, I have sinned, and I have done perversely; but these sheep, what have dem done? Please let una hand be against me, and against my father’s house.”
Gad come that day to David, and talk say to him, “Go up, build an altar to Baba God on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”
David go up according to the saying of Gad, as Baba God commanded.
Araunah looked out, and see the king and his workers coming on toward him. Then Araunah go out, and bowed imself before the king with his face to the ground.

Araunah talk say, “Why has my lord the king come to his worker?” David talk say, “To buy una threshing floor, to build an altar to Baba God, that the plague may be stopped from afflicting the people.”

Araunah talk say to David, “Let my lord the king take and offer up what seems good to him. See am, the cattle for the burnt offering, and the threshing instruments and the yokes of the oxen for the wood.
All this, O king, does Araunah give to the king.” Araunah talk say to the king, “May Baba God una God accept you.”

The king talk say to Araunah, “No; but I go most certainly buy it from you for a price. I go not offer burnt offerings to Baba God my God which cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
David built an altar to Baba God there, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. So Baba God was entreated for the land, and the plague was removed from Israel.
Now king David was old and advanced in years; and dem covered him with clothes, but he no fit keep warm.

So his workers talk say to him, “Let a young virgin be sought for my lord the king. Make she stand before the king, and cherish him; and Make she lie in una bosom, that my lord the king may keep warm.”
So dem sought for a beautiful young lady throughout all the borders of Israel, and find Abishag the Shunammite, and bring her to the king.
The young lady was very beautiful; and she cherished the king, and served him; but the king didn’t know her intimately.
Then Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted imself, saying, “I go be king.” Then he prepared him chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
His father had not displeased him at any time in saying, “Why have you done so?” and he was also a very handsome man; and he was born after Absalom.
He conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah, and with Abiathar the priest; and dem follow Adonijah and helped him.
But Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and the mighty men who belonged to David, No be with Adonijah.
Adonijah killed sheep, cattle, and fatlings by the stone of Zoheleth, which is beside En Rogel; and he call all his brothers, the king’s sons, and all the men of Judah, the king’s workers;
but he didn’t call Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, and the mighty men, and Solomon his brother.
Then Nathan spoke to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, saying, “Haven’t you heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith reigns, and David our lord no dey know it?
Now so come, please let me give you counsel, that you may save una own life, and una son Solomon’s life.

Go in to king David, and tell him, ‘Didn’t you, my lord, king, swear to una worker, saying, “Assuredly Solomon una son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne?” Why then does Adonijah reign?’
See am, while You be still talking there with the king, I go also come in after you and confirm una words.”
Bathsheba go in to the king in his room. The king was very old; and Abishag the Shunammite was serving the king.
Bathsheba bowed, and showed respect to the king. The king talk say, “What would you like?”
She talk say to him, “My lord, you swore by Baba God una God to una worker, ‘Assuredly Solomon una son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.’
Now, see am, Adonijah reigns; and you, my lord the king, no know it.
He has slain cattle and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and has call all the sons of the king, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the captain of the army; but he hasn’t call Solomon una worker.
You, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, that you should tell dem who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
Otherwise it will happen, when my lord the king sleeps with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon Go be considered criminals.”
See am, while she was still talking with the king, Nathan the prophet come in.
Dem told the king, saying, “See am, Nathan the prophet!” When he had come in before the king, he bowed imself before the king with his face to the ground.
Nathan talk say, “My lord, king, have you talk say, ‘Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne?’

For he has gone down today, and has slain cattle, fatlings, and sheep in abundance, and has call all the king’s sons, the captains of the army, and Abiathar the priest. See am, Dem be eating and drinking before him, and saying, ‘Long live king Adonijah!’
But he hasn’t call me, even me una worker, Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and una worker Solomon.
Was this thing done by my lord the king, and you haven’t shown to una workers who should sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?”
Then king David answer, “Call Bathsheba in to me.” She come into the king’s presence and stood before the king.
The king swore, and talk say, “As Baba God lives, who has redeemed my soul out of all adversity,

most certainly as I swore to you by Baba God, the God of Israel, saying, ‘Assuredly Solomon una son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place;’ I go most certainly do this today.”
Then Bathsheba bowed with her face to the earth, and showed respect to the king, and talk say, “Let my lord king David live forever!”
King David talk say, “Call to me Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada.” Dem come before the king.
The king talk say to dem, “Take with you the workers of una lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.
Let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there king over Israel. Blow the trumpet, and say, ‘Long live king Solomon!’
Then come up after him, and he shall come and sit on my throne; for he go be king in my place. I have appointed him to be prince over Israel and over Judah.”
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada answer the king, and talk say, “Amen. May Baba God, the God of my lord the king, say so.
