As Baba God Don dey with my lord the king, even so may he be with Solomon, and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord king David.”
So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites go down and had Solomon ride on king David’s mule, and bring him to Gihon.
Zadok the priest take the horn of oil from the Tent, and anointed Solomon. Dem blew the trumpet; and all the people talk say, “Long live king Solomon!”
All the people come up after him, and the people piped with pipes, and rejoiced with great gladness, so that the earth shook with dem sound.
Adonijah and all the guests who were with him heard it as dem had finished eating. When Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he talk say, “Why is this noise of the city being in an uproar?”
While he yet spoke, see am, Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest come; and Adonijah talk say, “Come in; for You be a worthy man, and bring better news.”
Jonathan answer Adonijah, “Most certainly our lord king David has made Solomon king.
The king has sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and dem have caused him to ride on the king’s mule.
Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king in Gihon. Dem have come up from there rejoicing, so that the city rang again. This is the noise that you have heard.
Also, Solomon sits on the throne of the kingdom.

Moreover the king’s workers come to bless our lord king David, saying, ‘May una God make the name of Solomon better than una name, and make his throne greater than una throne;’ and the king bowed imself on the bed.
Also thus talk say the king, ‘Blessed be Baba God, the God of Israel, who has given one to sit on my throne today, my eyes even seeing it.’”
All the guests of Adonijah were afraid, and rose up, and each man go his way.
Adonijah was afraid because of Solomon; and he arose, and go, and hung onto the horns of the altar.

Solomon was told, “See am, Adonijah fears king Solomon; for, see am, he is hanging onto the horns of the altar, saying, ‘Let king Solomon swear to me first that he No go kill his worker with the sword.’”
Solomon talk say, “If he shows imself a worthy man, not a hair of his shall fall to the earth; but if wickedness is find in him, he shall die.”
So king Solomon sent, and dem bring him down from the altar. He come and bowed down to king Solomon; and Solomon talk say to him, “Go to una house.”
Now the days of David come near that he should die; and he commanded Solomon his son, saying,
“I be going the way of all the earth. You be strong so, and show yourself a man;

and keep the instruction of Baba God una God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, his commandments, his ordinances, and his testimonies, according to that which is written in the law of Moses, that you may prosper in all that you do, and Anywhere wey you turn yourself.

Then Baba God may establish his word which he spoke concerning me, saying, ‘If una pikin dem are careful of dem way, to walk before me in truth with all dem heart and with all dem soul, there no go fail you,’ he talk say, ‘a man on the throne of Israel.’

“Moreover you know also what Joab the son of Zeruiah did to me, even what he did to the two captains of the armies of Israel, to Abner the son of Ner, and to Amasa the son of Jether, whom he killed, and shed the blood of war in peace, and put the blood of war on his sash that was around his waist, and in his shoes that were on his feet.
Do so according to una wisdom, and no let his gray head go down to Sheol in peace.
But show kindness to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and Make dem be among people wey eat at una table; for so dem come to me when I fled from Absalom una brother.

“See am, E get with you Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite, of Bahurim, who cursed me with a grievous curse in the day when I go to Mahanaim; but he come down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by Baba God, saying, ‘I go not put you to death with the sword.’
Now so no hold him guiltless, for You be a wise man; and You go know Wetin you ought to do to him, and you shall bring his gray head down to Sheol with blood.”
David slept with his fathers, and was buried in David’s city.
The days that David reigned over Israel were forty years; he reigned seven years in Hebron, and he reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
Solomon sat on David his father’s throne; and his kingdom was firmly established.
Then Adonijah the son of Haggith come to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon. She talk say, “Do you come peaceably?” He talk say, “Peaceably.
He talk say moreover, I have something to tell you.” She talk say, “Say on.”

He talk say, “You know that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel set dem faces on me, that I should reign. However the kingdom is turned around, and has become my brother’s; for it was his from Baba God.
Now I ask one petition of you. No deny me.” She talk say to him, “Say on.”
He talk say, “Please speak to Solomon the king (for he No go tell you ‘no’), that he give me Abishag the Shunammite as wife.”
Bathsheba talk say, “Alright. I go speak for you to the king.”

Bathsheba so go to king Solomon, to speak to him for Adonijah. The king rose up to meet her, and bowed imself to her, and sat down on his throne, and caused a throne to be set for the king’s mother; and she sat on his right hand.
Then she talk say, “I ask one small petition of you; no deny me.” The king talk say to her, “Ask on, my mother; for I go not deny you.”
She talk say, “Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah una brother as wife.”

King Solomon answer his mother, “Why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask for him the kingdom also; for he is my elder brother; even for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab the son of Zeruiah.”
Then king Solomon swore by Baba God, saying, “God do so to me, and more also, if Adonijah has not spoken this word against his own life.
Now so as Baba God lives, who has established me, and set me on my father David’s throne, and who has made me a house as he promised, surely Adonijah go be put to death today.”
King Solomon sent Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; and he fell on him, so that he died.

To Abiathar the priest the king talk say, “Go to Anathoth, to una own fields; for You be worthy of death. But I go not at this time put you to death, because you bore the Lord Baba God’s ark before David my father, and because you were afflicted in all in which my father was afflicted.”
So Solomon thrust Abiathar out from being priest to Baba God, that he might fulfill Baba God’s word, which he spoke concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.
This news come to Joab; for Joab had follow Adonijah, although he didn’t follow Absalom. Joab fled to Baba God’s Tent, and held onto the horns of the altar.
King Solomon was told, “Joab has fled to Baba God’s Tent, and see am, he is by the altar.” Then Solomon sent Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, saying, “Go, fall on him.”

Benaiah come to Baba God’s Tent, and talk say to him, “Thus says the king, ‘Come out!’” He talk say, “No; but I go die here.” Benaiah bring the king word again, saying, “Thus talk say Joab, and thus he answer me.”
The king talk say to him, “Do as he has talk say, and fall on him, and bury him; that you may take away the blood, which Joab shed without cause, from me and from my father’s house.

Baba God will return his blood on his own head, because he fell on two men more righteous and better than he, and killed dem with the sword, and my father David didn’t know it: Abner the son of Ner, captain of the army of Israel, and Amasa the son of Jether, captain of the army of Judah.
So dem blood will return on the head of Joab, and on the head of his offspring forever. But for David, for his offspring, for his house, and for his throne, there Go be peace forever from Baba God.”
Then Benaiah the son of Jehoiada go up and fell on him, and killed him; and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.
The king put Benaiah the son of Jehoiada in his place over the army; and the king put Zadok the priest in the place of Abiathar.
The king sent and call for Shimei, and talk say to him, “Build yourself a house in Jerusalem, and live there, and no go anywhere else.
For on the day you go out and pass over the brook Kidron, know for certain that You go surely die. Una blood Go be on una own head.”
Shimei talk say to the king, “Wetin you say is good. As my lord the king has talk say, so will una worker do.” Shimei lived in Jerusalem many days.
At the end of three years, two of Shimei’s slaves ran away to Achish, son of Maacah, king of Gath. Dem told Shimei, saying, “See am, una slaves are in Gath.”
Shimei arose, saddled his donkey, and go to Gath to Achish, to seek his slaves; and Shimei go, and bring his slaves from Gath.
Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath, and had come again.

The king sent and call for Shimei, and talk say to him, “Didn’t I adjure you by Baba God, and warn you, saying, ‘Know for certain, that on the day you go out, and walk anywhere else, you shall surely die?’ You talk say to me, ‘The saying that I have heard is good.’
Why then have you not kept the oath of Baba God, and the commandment that I have instructed you with?”
The king talk say moreover to Shimei, “You know in una heart all the wickedness that you did to David my father. So Baba God will return una wickedness on una own head.
But king Solomon Go be blessed, and David’s throne Go be established before Baba God forever.”
So the king commanded Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; and he go out, and fell on him, so that he died. The kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.

Solomon made an alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt, and take Pharaoh’s daughter, and bring her into David’s city, until he had finished building his own house, Baba God’s house, and the wall around Jerusalem.
However the people sacrificed in the high places, because there No be yet a house built for Baba God’s name.
Solomon love Baba God, walking in the statutes of David his father; except that he sacrificed and burned incense in the high places.
The king go to Gibeon to sacrifice there; for that was the great high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.
In Gibeon, Baba God appeared to Solomon in a dream by night; and God talk say, “Ask for what I should give you.”

Solomon talk say, “You have shown to una worker David my father great loving kindness, because he walked before you in truth, in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with you. You have kept for him this great loving kindness, that you have given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is today.
Now, Baba God my God, you have made una worker king instead of David my father. I be just a little pikin. I no know how to go out or come in.
Una worker is among una people which you have chosen, a great people, that no fit be numbered or counted for plenty people.
Give una worker so an understanding heart to judge una people, that I may discern between good and evil; for Wey be able to judge this great people of yours?”
This request pleased the Lord, that Solomon had ask this thing.

God talk say to him, “Because you have ask this thing, and have not ask for yourself long life, nor have you ask for riches for yourself, nor have you ask for the life of una enemies, but have ask for yourself understanding to discern justice;
see am, I have done according to una word. See am, I have given you a wise and understanding heart; so that there Don dey Nobody like you before you, and after you none will arise like you.
I have also given you that which you have not ask, both riches and honor, so that there No go be any among the kings like you for all una days.
If You go walk in my ways, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as una father David walked, then I go lengthen una days.”

Solomon awoke; and see am, it was a dream. Then he come to Jerusalem, and stood before the ark of Baba God’s covenant, and offered up burnt offerings, offered peace offerings, and made a feast for all his workers.
Then two women who were prostitutes come to the king, and stood before him.
The one woman talk say, “Oh, my lord, I and this woman live in one house. I delivered a pikin with her in the house.
The third day after I delivered, this woman delivered also. We were together. There was no stranger with us in the house, just us two in the house.
This woman’s pikin died in the night, because she lay on it.
She arose at midnight, and take my son from beside me, while una worker slept, and laid it in her bosom, and laid her dead pikin in my bosom.
When I rose in the morning to nurse my pikin, see am, it was dead; but when I had looked at it in the morning, see am, it No be my son, whom I bore.”

The other woman talk say, “No; but the living one is my son, and the dead one is una son.” The first one talk say, “No; but the dead one is una son, and the living one is my son.” Thus dem spoke before the king.
Then the king talk say, “One says, ‘This is my son who lives, and una son is the dead;’ and the other says, ‘No; but una son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.’”
The king talk say, “Get me a sword.” So dem bring a sword before the king.
The king talk say, “Divide the living pikin in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other.”

Then the woman whose the living pikin was spoke to the king, for her heart yearned over her son, and she talk say, “Oh, my lord, give her the living pikin, and in no way kill him!” But the other talk say, “He go be neither mine nor yours. Divide him.”
Then the king answer, “Give her the living pikin, and definitely No kill him. She is his mother.”
All Israel heard of the judgment which the king had judged; and dem feared the king; for dem see that the wisdom of God was in him, to do justice.
King Solomon was king over all Israel.
These were the princes whom he had: Azariah the son of Zadok, the priest;
Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud, the recorder;
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the army; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
Azariah the son of Nathan was over the officers; Zabud the son of Nathan was chief minister, the king’s friend;
Ahishar was over the household; and Adoniram the son of Abda was over the men subject to forced labor.
Solomon had twelve officers over all Israel, who provided chop for the king and his household. Each man had to make provision for a month in the year.
These are dem names: Ben Hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
Ben Deker, in Makaz, in Shaalbim, Beth Shemesh, and Elon Beth Hanan;
Ben Hesed, in Arubboth (Socoh and all the land of Hepher belonged to him);
Ben Abinadab, in all the height of Dor (he had Taphath, Solomon’s daughter, as wife);
Baana the son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo, and all Beth Shean which is beside Zarethan, beneath Jezreel, from Beth Shean to Abel Meholah, as far as beyond Jokmeam;

Ben Geber, in Ramoth Gilead (the towns of Jair the son of Manasseh, which are in Gilead, belonged to him; and the region of Argob, which is in Bashan, sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars, belonged to him);
Ahinadab the son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
Ahimaaz, in Naphtali (he also take Basemath the daughter of Solomon as wife);
Baana the son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
Jehoshaphat the son of Paruah, in Issachar;
Shimei the son of Ela, in Benjamin;
Geber the son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the country of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan; and he was the only officer who was in the land.
Judah and Israel were numerous as the sand which is by the sea in plenty people, eating and drinking and making merry.
Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines, and to the border of Egypt. Dem bring tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.
Solomon’s provision for one day was thirty cors of fine flour, sixty measures of meal,
ten head of fat cattle, twenty head of cattle out of the pastures, and one hundred sheep, besides deer, and gazelles, and roebucks, and fattened fowl.
For he had dominion over all on this side the River, from Tiphsah even to Gaza, over all the kings on this side the River: and he had peace on all sides around him.
Judah and Israel lived safely, every man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan even to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.
Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.
Those officers provided chop for king Solomon, and for all who come to king Solomon’s table, every man in his month. Dem let nothing be lacking.
Dem also bring Barley and straw for the horses and swift steeds to the place where the officers were, each man according to his duty.
God give Solomon abundant wisdom and understanding, and plenty well-well understanding, even as the sand that is on the seashore.
Solomon’s wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the pikin dem of the east and all the wisdom of Egypt.
For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all the nations all around.
He spoke three thousand proverbs; and his songs numbered one thousand five.
He spoke of trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon even to the hyssop that grows out of the wall; he also spoke of animals, of birds, of creeping things, and of fish.
People of people for everywhere come to hear the wisdom of Solomon, sent by all kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.
Hiram king of Tyre sent his workers to Solomon; for he had heard that dem had anointed him king in the place of his father, and Hiram had always love David.
Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,

“You know that David my father could not build a house for the name of Baba God his God because of the wars which were around him on every side, until Baba God put his enemies under the soles of his feet.
But now Baba God my God has given me rest on every side. E get no enemy and no evil occurrence.
See am, I intend to build a house for the name of Baba God my God, as Baba God spoke to David my father, saying, ‘Una son, whom I go set on una throne in una place shall build the house for my name.’

Now so command that cedar trees be cut for me out of Lebanon. My workers Go be with una workers; and I go give you wages for una workers according to all that you say. For you know that E get nobody among us wey know how to cut timber like the Sidonians.”
When Hiram heard the words of Solomon, he rejoiced greatly, and talk say, “Blessed is Baba God today, who has given to David a wise son to rule over this great people.”
Hiram sent to Solomon, saying, “I have heard the message which you have sent to me. I go do all una desire concerning timber of cedar, and concerning cypress timber.

My workers will bring dem down from Lebanon to the sea. I go make dem into rafts to go by sea to the place that you specify to me, and will cause dem to be broken up there, and You go receive dem. You go accomplish my desire, in giving chop for my household.”
So Hiram give Solomon cedar timber and cypress timber according to all his desire.
Solomon give Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat for chop to his household, and twenty cors of pure oil. Solomon give this to Hiram year by year.
Baba God give Solomon wisdom, as he promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of dem made a treaty together.
King Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel; and the levy was thirty thousand men.
He sent dem to Lebanon, ten thousand a month by courses; for a month dem were in Lebanon, and two months at home; and Adoniram was over the men subject to forced labor.
Solomon had seventy thousand who bore burdens, and eighty thousand who were stone cutters in the mountains;
besides Solomon’s chief officers who were over the work, three thousand and three hundred, who ruled over the people who labored in the work.
The king commanded, and dem cut out large stones, costly stones, to lay the foundation of the house with worked stone.
Solomon’s builders and Hiram’s builders and the Gebalites cut dem, and prepared the timber and the stones to build the house.

In the four hundred and eightieth year after the pikin dem of Israel had come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month Ziv, which is the second month, he began to build Baba God’s house.
The house which king Solomon built for Baba God had a length of sixty cubits, and its width twenty, and its height thirty cubits.
The porch in front of the temple of the house had a length of twenty cubits, which was along the width of the house. Ten cubits was its width in front of the house.
He made windows of fixed lattice work for the house.
Against the wall of the house, he built floors all around, against the walls of the house all around, both of the temple and of the inner sanctuary; and he made side rooms all around.

The lowest floor was five cubits wide, and the middle was six cubits wide, and the third was seven cubits wide; for on the outside he made offsets in the wall of the house all around, that the beams no suppose be inserted into the walls of the house.
The house, when it was under construction, was built of stone prepared at the quarry; and no hammer or ax or any tool of iron was heard in the house while it was under construction.
The door for the middle side rooms was in the right side of the house. Dem go up by winding stairs into the middle floor, and out of the middle into the third.
So he built the house, and finished it; and he covered the house with beams and planks of cedar.
He built the floors all along the house, each five cubits high; and dem rested on the house with timber of cedar.
Baba God’s word come to Solomon, saying,

“Concerning this house which You be building, if You go walk in my statutes, and execute my ordinances, and keep all my commandments to walk in dem; then I go establish my word with you, which I spoke to David una father.
I go live among the pikin dem of Israel, and No go forsake my people Israel.”
So Solomon built the house, and finished it.

He built the walls of the house within with boards of cedar: from the floor of the house to the walls of the ceiling, he covered dem on the inside with wood; and he covered the floor of the house with cypress boards.
He built twenty cubits on the back part of the house with boards of cedar from the floor to the ceiling. He built dem for it within, for an inner sanctuary, even for the most holy place.
In front of the temple sanctuary was forty cubits.
There was cedar on the house within, carved with buds and open flowers. All was cedar. No stone was visible.
He prepared an inner sanctuary in the middle of the house within, to set the ark of Baba God’s covenant there.
Within the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in its height; and he overlaid it with pure gold; and he covered the altar with cedar.
So Solomon overlaid the house within with pure gold. He drew chains of gold across before the inner sanctuary, and he overlaid it with gold.
He overlaid the whole house with gold, until all the house was finished. He also overlaid the whole altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary with gold.
In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim of olive wood, each ten cubits high.
Five cubits was the one wing of the cherub, and five cubits the other wing of the cherub. From the tip of one wing to the tip of the other was ten cubits.
The other cherub was ten cubits. Both the cherubim were of one measure and one form.
One cherub was ten cubits high, and so was the other cherub.

He set the cherubim within the inner house. The wings of the cherubim were stretched out, so that the wing of the one touched the one wall, and the wing of the other cherub touched the other wall; and dem wings touched each other in the middle of the house.
He overlaid the cherubim with gold.
He carved all the walls of the house around with carved figures of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, inside and outside.
He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, inside and outside.
For the entrance of the inner sanctuary, he made doors of olive wood. The lintel and door posts were a fifth part of the wall.
So he made two doors of olive wood; and he carved on dem carvings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid dem with gold. He spread the gold on the cherubim and on the palm trees.
He also did so for the entrance of the temple door posts of olive wood, out of a fourth part of the wall;
and two doors of cypress wood. The two leaves of the one door were folding, and the two leaves of the other door were folding.
He carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers; and he overlaid dem with gold fitted on the engraved work.
He built the inner court with three courses of cut stone and a course of cedar beams.
The foundation of Baba God’s house was laid in the fourth year, in the month Ziv.
In the eleventh year, in the month Bul, which is the eighth month, the house was finished throughout all its parts, and according to all its specifications. So he spent seven years building it.
Solomon was building his own house thirteen years, and he finished all his house.

For he built the House of the Forest of Lebanon. Its length was one hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits, on four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams on the pillars.
It was covered with cedar above over the forty-five beams, that were on the pillars, fifteen in a row.
There were beams in three rows, and window was facing window in three ranks.
All the doors and posts were made square with beams: and window was facing window in three ranks.
He made the porch of pillars. Its length was fifty cubits and its width thirty cubits; with a porch before dem, and pillars and a threshold before dem.
He made the porch of the throne where he was to judge, even the porch of judgment; and it was covered with cedar from floor to floor.
His house where he was to live, the other court within the porch, was of the like work. He made also a house for Pharaoh’s daughter (whom Solomon had taken as wife), like this porch.
All these were of costly stones, even of cut stone, according to measure, sawed with saws, inside and outside, even from the foundation to the coping, and so on the outside to the great court.
The foundation was of costly stones, even great stones, stones of ten cubits, and stones of eight cubits.
Above were costly stones, even cut stone, according to measure, and cedar wood.
The great court around had three courses of cut stone, and a course of cedar beams; like the inner court of Baba God’s house and the porch of the house.
King Solomon sent and bring Hiram out of Tyre.

He was the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in brass; and he was filled with wisdom and understanding and skill, to work all works in brass. He come to king Solomon, and performed all his work.
For he fashioned the two pillars of brass, eighteen cubits high apiece; and a line of twelve cubits encircled either of dem.
He made two capitals of molten brass, to set on the tops of the pillars. The height of the one capital was five cubits, and the height of the other capital was five cubits.
There were nets of checker work, and wreaths of chain work, for the capitals which were on the top of the pillars; seven for the one capital, and seven for the other capital.
So he made the pillars; and there were two rows around on the one network, to cover the capitals that were on the top of the pillars: and he did so for the other capital.
The capitals that were on the top of the pillars in the porch were of lily work, four cubits.
There were capitals above also on the two pillars, close by the belly which was beside the network. There were two hundred pomegranates in rows around the other capital.
He set up the pillars at the porch of the temple. He set up the right pillar, and call its name Jachin; and he set up the left pillar, and call its name Boaz.
On the top of the pillars was lily work: so the work of the pillars was finished.
He made the molten sea of ten cubits from brim to brim, round in shape. Its height was five cubits; and a line of thirty cubits encircled it.
Under its brim around there were buds which encircled it for ten cubits, encircling the sea. The buds were in two rows, throw when it was throw.

It stood on twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east; and the sea was set on dem above, and all dem hindquarters were inward.
It was a hand width thick. Its brim was worked like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It held two thousand baths.
He made the ten bases of brass. The length of one base was four cubits, four cubits its width, and three cubits its height.
The work of the bases was like this: dem had panels; and there were panels between the ledges;
and on the panels that were between the ledges were lions, oxen, and cherubim; and on the ledges there was a pedestal above; and beneath the lions and oxen were wreaths of hanging work.
Every base had four bronze wheels, and axles of brass; and the four feet of it had supports. The supports were throw beneath the basin, with wreaths at the side of each.
Its mouth within the capital and above was a cubit. Its mouth was round after the work of a pedestal, a cubit and a half; and also on its mouth were engravings, and dem panels were square, not round.
The four wheels were underneath the panels; and the axles of the wheels were in the base. The height of a wheel was a cubit and half a cubit.
The work of the wheels was like the work of a chariot wheel. Dem axles, and dem rims, and dem spokes, and dem naves, were all of throw metal.
There were four supports at the four corners of each base. Its supports were of the base itself.
In the top of the base there was a round band half a cubit high; and on the top of the base its supports and its panels were of the same.
On the plates of its supports, and on its panels, he engraved cherubim, lions, and palm trees, each in its space, with wreaths all around.
He made the ten bases in this way: all of dem had one casting, one measure, and one form.
He made ten basins of brass. One basin contained forty baths; and every basin was four cubits; and on every one of the ten bases one basin.
He set the bases, five on the right side of the house, and five on the left side of the house. He set the sea on the right side of the house eastward and toward the south.
Hiram made the basins, the shovels, and the basins. So Hiram finished doing all the work that he worked for king Solomon in Baba God’s house:
the two pillars; the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars; the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars;
the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks; two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the pillars;
the ten bases; the ten basins on the bases;
the one sea; the twelve oxen under the sea;
the pots; the shovels; and the basins: even all these vessels, which Hiram made for king Solomon, in Baba God’s house, were of burnished brass.
The king throw dem in the plain of the Jordan, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarethan.
Solomon left all the vessels unweighed, because there were so many of dem. The weight of the brass could not be determined.
Solomon made all the vessels that were in Baba God’s house: the golden altar and the table that the show bread was on, of gold;
and the lamp stands, five on the right side, and five on the left, before the inner sanctuary, of pure gold; and the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs, of gold;

the cups, the snuffers, the basins, the spoons, and the fire pans, of pure gold; and the hinges, both for the doors of the inner house, the most holy place, and for the doors of the house, of the temple, of gold.

Thus all the work that king Solomon did in Baba God’s house was finished. Solomon bring in the things which David his father had dedicated, the silver, the gold, and the vessels, and put dem in the treasuries of Baba God’s house.

Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, with all the heads of the tribes, the princes of the fathers’ households of the pikin dem of Israel, to king Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of Baba God’s covenant out of David’s city, which is Zion.
All the men of Israel assembled themselves to king Solomon at the feast, in the month Ethanim, which is the seventh month.
All the elders of Israel come, and the priests picked up the ark.
Dem bring up Baba God’s ark, the Tent of Meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the Tent. The priests and the Levites bring these up.
King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel, who were assembled to him, were with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle, that could not be counted or numbered for plenty people.
The priests bring in the ark of Baba God’s covenant to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, to the most holy place, even under the cherubim’s wings.
For the cherubim spread dem wings out over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its poles above.
The poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the holy place before the inner sanctuary; but dem No be seen outside. Dem be there to this day.
There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets which Moses put there at Horeb, when Baba God made a covenant with the pikin dem of Israel, when dem come out of the land of Egypt.
E happen say, when the priests had come out of the holy place, that the cloud filled Baba God’s house,
so that the priests could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud; for Baba God’s glory filled Baba God’s house.
Then Solomon talk say, “Baba God has talk say that he would live in the thick darkness.
I have surely built you a house of habitation, a place for you to live in forever.”
The king turned his face around, and blessed all the assembly of Israel; and all the assembly of Israel stood.
He talk say, “Blessed is Baba God, the God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth to David una father, and has with his hand fulfilled it, saying,

‘Since the day that I bring my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel to build a house, that my name might be there; but I chose David to be over my people Israel.’
“Now it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of Baba God, the God of Israel.
But Baba God talk say to David my father, ‘Whereas it was in una heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in una heart.
Nevertheless, you no go build the house; but una son who shall come out of una body, he shall build the house for my name.’

Baba God has established his word that he spoke; for I have risen up in the place of David my father, and I sit on the throne of Israel, as Baba God promised, and have built the house for the name of Baba God, the God of Israel.
There I have set a place for the ark, in which is Baba God’s covenant, which he made with our fathers, when he bring dem out of the land of Egypt.”
Solomon stood before Baba God’s altar in the presence of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward heaven;

and he talk say, “Baba God, the God of Israel, E get no God like you, in heaven above, or on earth beneath; who keeps covenant and loving kindness with una workers, who walk before you with all dem heart;
who has kept with una worker David my father that which you promised him. Yes, you spoke with una mouth, and have fulfilled it with una hand, as it is today.

Now so, may Baba God, the God of Israel, keep with una worker David my father that which you have promised him, saying, ‘There no go fail from you a man in my sight to sit on the throne of Israel, if only una pikin dem take heed to dem way, to walk before me as you have walked before me.’
“Now so, God of Israel, please let una word be verified, which you spoke to una worker David my father.
But will God in very deed live on the earth? See am, heaven and the heaven of heavens no fit contain you; how much less this house that I have built!
Yet have respect for the prayer of una worker, and for his supplication, Baba God my God, to listen to the cry and to the prayer which una worker prays before you today;
that una eyes may be open toward this house night and day, even toward the place of which you have talk say, ‘My name go be there;’ to listen to the prayer which una worker prays toward this place.
Listen to the supplication of una worker, and of una people Israel, when dem pray toward this place. Yes, hear in heaven, una dwelling place; and when you hear, forgive.
“If a man sins against his neighbor, and an oath is laid on him to cause him to swear, and he comes and swears before una altar in this house;
then hear in heaven, and act, and judge una workers, condemning the wicked, to bring his way on his own head, and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.
“When una people Israel are struck down before the enemy, because dem have sinned against you; if dem turn again to you, and confess una name, and pray and make supplication to you in this house;
then hear in heaven, and forgive the sin of una people Israel, and bring dem again to the land which you give to dem fathers.
“When the sky is shut up, and E get no rain, because dem have sinned against you; if dem pray toward this place, and confess una name, and turn from dem sin, when you afflict dem,

then hear in heaven, and forgive the sin of una workers, and of una people Israel, when you teach dem the good way in which dem should walk; and send rain on una land, which you have given to una people for an inheritance.

“If E get famine in the land, if E get pestilence, if E get blight, mildew, locust or caterpillar; if dem enemy besieges dem in the land of dem cities; Anything wey plague, Anything wey sickness E get;
Anything wey prayer and supplication is made by any man, or by all una people Israel, who shall each know the plague of his own heart, and spread out his hands toward this house,

then hear in heaven, una dwelling place, and forgive, and act, and give to every man according to all his ways, whose heart you know; (for you, even you only, know the hearts of all the pikin dem of men;)
that dem may fear you all the days that dem live in the land which you give to our fathers.
“Moreover concerning the foreigner, Wey be not of una people Israel, when he comes out of a far country for una name’s sake
(for dem shall hear of una great name, and of una mighty hand, and of una outstretched arm); when he comes and prays toward this house;

hear in heaven, una dwelling place, and do according to all that the foreigner calls to you for; that all the peoples of the earth may know una name, to fear you, as do una people Israel, and that dem may know that this house which I have built is call by una name.

“If una people go out to battle against dem enemy, by Anything wey way you shall send dem, and dem pray to Baba God toward the city which you have chosen, and toward the house which I have built for una name;
then hear in heaven dem prayer and dem supplication, and maintain dem cause.
If dem sin against you (for E get no man who no dey sin), and You be angry with dem, and deliver dem to the enemy, so that dem carry dem away captive to the land of the enemy, far off or near;

yet if dem repent in the land where Dem be carried captive, and turn again, and make supplication to you in the land of people wey carried dem captive, saying, ‘We have sinned, and have done perversely; we have dealt wickedly;’

if dem return to you with all dem heart and with all dem soul in the land of dem enemies, who carried dem captive, and pray to you toward dem land, which you give to dem fathers, the city which you have chosen, and the house which I have built for una name;
then hear dem prayer and dem supplication in heaven, una dwelling place, and maintain dem cause;

and forgive una people who have sinned against you, and all dem wrongdoings in which dem have transgressed against you; and give dem compassion before people wey carried dem captive, that dem may have compassion on dem
(for Dem be una people, and una inheritance, which you bring out of Egypt, from the middle of the iron furnace);
that una eyes may be open to the supplication of una worker, and to the supplication of una people Israel, to listen to dem whenever dem cry to you.
For you separated dem from among all the peoples of the earth, to be una inheritance, as you spoke by Moses una worker, when you bring our fathers out of Egypt, Lord Baba God.”

It was so, that when Solomon had finished praying all this prayer and supplication to Baba God, he arose from before Baba God’s altar, from kneeling on his knees with his hands spread out toward heaven.
He stood, and blessed all the assembly of Israel with a loud voice, saying,
“Blessed be Baba God, who has given rest to his people Israel, according to all that he promised. There has not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by Moses his worker.
May Baba God our God be with us, as he was with our fathers. Make e not leave us or forsake us;
that he may incline our hearts to him, to walk in all his ways, and to keep his commandments, and his statutes, and his ordinances, which he commanded our fathers.

Let these my words, with which I have made supplication before Baba God, be near to Baba God our God day and night, that he may maintain the cause of his worker, and the cause of his people Israel, as every day requires;
that all the peoples of the earth may know that Baba God imself is God. E get Nobody else.
“Let una heart so be perfect with Baba God our God, to walk in his statutes, and to keep his commandments, as it is today.”
The king, and all Israel with him, offered sacrifice before Baba God.

Solomon offered for the sacrifice of peace offerings, which he offered to Baba God, twenty two thousand head of cattle, and one hundred twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the pikin dem of Israel dedicated Baba God’s house.

The same day the king made the middle of the court holy that was before Baba God’s house; for there he offered the burnt offering, and the meal offering, and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that was before Baba God was too little to receive the burnt offering, the meal offering, and the fat of the peace offerings.

So Solomon held the feast at that time, and all Israel with him, a great assembly, from the entrance of Hamath to the brook of Egypt, before Baba God our God, seven days and seven more days, even fourteen days.

On the eighth day he sent the people away; and dem blessed the king, and go to dem tents joyful and glad in dem hearts for all the goodness that Baba God had shown to David his worker, and to Israel his people.
When Solomon had finished the building of Baba God’s house, the king’s house, and all Solomon’s desire which he was pleased to do,
Baba God appeared to Solomon the second time, as he had appeared to him at Gibeon.

Baba God talk say to him, “I have heard una prayer and una supplication, that you have made before me. I have made this house holy, which you have built, to put my name there forever; and my eyes and my heart go be there perpetually.

As for you, if You go walk before me, as David una father walked, in integrity of heart, and in uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded you, and will keep my statutes and my ordinances;
then I go establish the throne of una kingdom over Israel forever, as I promised to David una father, saying, ‘There no go fail from you a man on the throne of Israel.’
But if you turn away from following me, you or una pikin dem, and not keep my commandments and my statutes which I have set before you, but go and serve other gods, and worship dem;

then I go cut off Israel out of the land which I have given dem; and I go throw this house, which I have made holy for my name, out of my sight; and Israel Go be a proverb and a byword among all peoples.
Though this house is so high, yet Everybody wey passes by it Go be astonished and hiss; and Dem go say, ‘Why has Baba God done this to this land, and to this house?’

and Dem go answer, ‘Because dem abandoned Baba God dem God, who bring dem fathers out of the land of Egypt, and laid hold of other gods, and worshiped dem, and served dem. So Baba God has bring all this evil on dem.’”
At the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the two houses, Baba God’s house and the king’s house
(now Hiram the king of Tyre had furnished Solomon with cedar trees and cypress trees, and with gold, according to all his desire), King Solomon give Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.
Hiram come out of Tyre to see the cities which Solomon had given him; and dem didn’t please him.
He talk say, “What cities are these which you have given me, my brother?” He call dem the land of Cabul to this day.
Hiram sent to the king one hundred twenty talents of gold.
This is the reason of the levy which king Solomon raised, to build Baba God’s house, his own house, Millo, Jerusalem’s wall, Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up, taken Gezer, burned it with fire, killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and given it for a wedding gift to his daughter, Solomon’s wife.
Solomon built in the land Gezer, Beth Horon the lower,
Baalath, Tamar in the wilderness,

all the storage cities that Solomon had, the cities for his chariots, the cities for his horsemen, and that which Solomon desired to build for his pleasure in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.
As for all the people who were left of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who No be of the pikin dem of Israel;
dem pikin dem who were left after dem in the land, whom the pikin dem of Israel No be able utterly to destroy, of dem Solomon raised a levy of bondservants to this day.
But of the pikin dem of Israel Solomon made no bondservants; but dem were the men of war, his workers, his princes, his captains, and rulers of his chariots and of his horsemen.
These were the five hundred fifty chief officers who were over Solomon’s work, who ruled over the people who labored in the work.
But Pharaoh’s daughter come up out of David’s city to her house which Solomon had built for her. Then he built Millo.

Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar which he built to Baba God three times per year, burning incense with dem, on the altar that was before Baba God. So he finished the house.
King Solomon made a fleet of ships in Ezion Geber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red Sea, in the land of Edom.
Hiram sent in the fleet his workers, sailors who had knowledge of the sea, with the workers of Solomon.
Dem come to Ophir, and fetched from there gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and bring it to king Solomon.
When the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning Baba God’s name, she come to test him with hard questions.

She come to Jerusalem with a plenty well-well caravan, with camels that bore spices, well-well gold, and precious stones; and when she had come to Solomon, she talked with him about all that was in her heart.
Solomon answer all her questions. There No be anything hidden from the king which he didn’t tell her.
When the queen of Sheba had seen all the wisdom of Solomon, the house that he had built,

the chop of his table, the sitting of his workers, the attendance of his officials, dem clothing, his cup bearers, and his ascent by which he go up to Baba God’s house; there was no more spirit in her.
She talk say to the king, “It was a true report that I heard in my own land of una acts, and of una wisdom.
However I didn’t believe the words until I come and my eyes had seen it. See am, not even half was told me! Una wisdom and prosperity exceed the fame which I heard.
Happy are una men, happy are these una workers, who stand continually before you, who hear una wisdom.
Blessed is Baba God una God, who delighted in you, to set you on the throne of Israel. Because Baba God love Israel forever, so he made you king, to do justice and righteousness.”

She give the king one hundred twenty talents of gold, and a plenty well-well quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again was there such an abundance of spices as these which the queen of Sheba give to king Solomon.
The fleet of Hiram that bring gold from Ophir, also bring in from Ophir great quantities of almug trees and precious stones.
The king made of the almug trees pillars for Baba God’s house, and for the king’s house, harps also and stringed instruments for the singers; no such almug trees come or were seen, to this day.
King Solomon give to the queen of Sheba all her desire, Anything wey she ask, besides that which Solomon give her of his royal bounty. So she turned and go to her own land, she and her workers.
Now the weight of gold that come to Solomon in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents of gold,
besides that which the traders bring, and the traffic of the merchants, and of all the kings of the mixed people, and of the governors of the country.
King Solomon made two hundred bucklers of beaten gold; six hundred shekels of gold go to one buckler.
he made three hundred shields of beaten gold; three minas of gold go to one shield; and the king put dem in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with the finest gold.
There were six steps to the throne, and the top of the throne was round behind; and there were armrests on either side by the place of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests.
Twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other on the six steps. Nothing like it was made in any kingdom.

All king Solomon’s drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were of pure gold. None were of silver, because it was considered of little value in the days of Solomon.
For the king had a fleet of Tarshish at sea with Hiram’s fleet. Once every three years the fleet of Tarshish come, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.
All the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
Year after year, every man bring his tribute, vessels of silver, vessels of gold, clothing, armor, spices, horses, and mules.
Solomon gathered together chariots and horsemen. He had one thousand four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, that he kept in the chariot cities and with the king at Jerusalem.
The king made silver as common as stones in Jerusalem, and cedars as common as the sycamore trees that are in the lowland.
The horses which Solomon had were bring out of Egypt. The king’s merchants received dem in droves, each drove at a price.

A chariot come up and go out of Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for one hundred fifty shekels; and so dem exported dem to all the kings of the Hittites, and to the kings of Syria.
Now king Solomon love many foreign women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians, and Hittites;

of the nations concerning which Baba God talk say to the pikin dem of Israel, “You no go go among dem, neither shall dem come among you; for surely Dem go turn away una heart after dem gods.” Solomon joined to these in love.
He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines; and his wives turned away his heart.
When Solomon was old, his wives turned away his heart after other gods; and his heart No be perfect with Baba God his God, as the heart of David his father was.
For Solomon go after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
Solomon did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, and didn’t go fully after Baba God, as David his father did.
Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, on the mountain that is before Jerusalem, and for Molech the abomination of the pikin dem of Ammon.
So he did for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to dem gods.
Baba God was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned away from Baba God, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice,
and had commanded him concerning this thing, that he no suppose go after other gods; but he didn’t keep that which Baba God commanded.

So Baba God talk say to Solomon, “Because this is done by you, and you have not kept my covenant and my statutes, which I have commanded you, I go surely tear the kingdom from you, and will give it to una worker.
Nevertheless, I go not do it in una days, for David una father’s sake; but I go tear it out of una son’s hand.
However I go not tear away all the kingdom; but I go give one tribe to una son, for David my worker’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake which I have chosen.”
Baba God raised up an adversary to Solomon: Hadad the Edomite. He was one of the king’s offspring in Edom.
For when David was in Edom, and Joab the captain of the army had gone up to bury the slain, and had struck every male in Edom
(for Joab and all Israel remain there six months, until he had cut off every male in Edom);
Hadad fled, he and certain Edomites of his father’s workers with him, to go into Egypt, when Hadad was still a little pikin.
Dem arose out of Midian, and come to Paran; and dem take men with dem out of Paran, and dem come to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who give him a house, and appointed him chop, and give him land.
Hadad find great favor in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he give him as wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
The sister of Tahpenes bore him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh’s house; and Genubath was in Pharaoh’s house among the sons of Pharaoh.
When Hadad heard in Egypt that David slept with his fathers, and that Joab the captain of the army was dead, Hadad talk say to Pharaoh, “Let me depart, that I may go to my own country.”
Then Pharaoh talk say to him, “But what have you lacked with me, that see am, you seek to go to una own country?” He answer, “Nothing, however only let me depart.”
God raised up an adversary to him, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from his lord Hadadezer king of Zobah.
He gathered men to imself, and became captain over a troop, when David killed dem of Zobah. Dem go to Damascus, and lived there, and reigned in Damascus.
He was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, besides the mischief of Hadad. He abhorred Israel, and reigned over Syria.
Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephraimite of Zeredah, a worker of Solomon, whose mother’s name was Zeruah, a widow, also lifted up his hand against the king.
This was the reason why he lifted up his hand against the king: Solomon built Millo, and repaired the breach of his father David’s city.
The man Jeroboam was a mighty man of valor; and Solomon see the young man that he was industrious, and he put him in charge of all the labor of the house of Joseph.
At that time, when Jeroboam go out of Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite find him on the way; now Ahijah had clad imself with a new garment; and dem two were alone in the field.
Ahijah laid hold of the new garment that was on him, and tore it in twelve pieces.
He talk say to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces; for Baba God, the God of Israel, says, ‘See am, I go tear the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to you
(but he go get one tribe, for my worker David’s sake and for Jerusalem’s sake, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel);

because that dem have forsaken me, and have worshiped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the pikin dem of Ammon. Dem have not walked in my ways, to do that which is right in my eyes, and to keep my statutes and my ordinances, as David his father did.
“‘However I go not take the whole kingdom out of his hand; but I go make him prince all the days of his life, for David my worker’s sake whom I chose, who kept my commandments and my statutes;
but I go take the kingdom out of his son’s hand, and will give it to you, even ten tribes.
To his son will I give one tribe, that David my worker may have a lamp always before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen me to put my name there.
I go take you, and you shall reign according to all that una soul desires, and go be king over Israel.

It go be, if You go listen to all that I command you, and will walk in my ways, and do that which is right in my eyes, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as David my worker did; that I go be with you, and will build you a sure house, as I built for David, and will give Israel to you.
I go afflict the offspring of David for this, but not forever.’”
So Solomon sought to kill Jeroboam; but Jeroboam arose, and fled into Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and was in Egypt until the death of Solomon.
Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, no be dem written in the book of the acts of Solomon?
The time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
Solomon slept with his fathers, and was buried in his father David’s city; and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.
Rehoboam go to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
When Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard of it (for he was yet in Egypt, where he had fled from the presence of king Solomon, and Jeroboam lived in Egypt,
and dem sent and call him), Jeroboam and all the assembly of Israel come, and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
“Una father made our yoke difficult. Now so make the hard service of una father, and his heavy yoke which he put on us, lighter, and We go serve you.”
E tell dem say, “Depart for three days, then come back to me.” The people comot.
King Rehoboam take counsel with the old men, who had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, “What counsel do you give me to answer these people?”
Dem replied, “If You go be a worker to this people today, and will serve dem, and answer dem with good words, then Dem go be una workers forever.”
But he abandoned the counsel of the old men which dem had given him, and take counsel with the young men who had grown up with him, who stood before him.
E tell dem say, “What counsel do you give, that we may answer these people, who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Make the yoke that una father put on us lighter?’”

The young men who had grown up with him talk say to him, “Tell these people who spoke to you, saying, ‘Una father made our yoke heavy, but make it lighter to us;’ tell dem, ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist.
Now my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, but I go add to una yoke. My father chastised you with whips, but I go chastise you with scorpions.’”
So Jeroboam and all the people come to Rehoboam the third day, as the king ask, saying, “Come to me again the third day.”
The king answer the people roughly, and abandoned the counsel of the old men which dem had given him,

and spoke to dem according to the counsel of the young men, saying, “My father made una yoke heavy, but I go add to una yoke. My father chastised you with whips, but I go chastise you with scorpions.”
So the king didn’t listen to the people; for it was a thing bring about from Baba God, that he might establish his word, which Baba God spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

When all Israel see that the king didn’t listen to dem, the people answer the king, saying, “What portion have we in David? We no have an inheritance in the son of Jesse. To una tents, Israel! Now see to una own house, David.” So Israel comot to dem tents.
But as for the pikin dem of Israel who lived in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over dem.

Then king Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the men subject to forced labor; and all Israel stoned him to death with stones. King Rehoboam hurried to get imself up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.
So Israel rebelled against David’s house to this day.

When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had come back, dem sent and call him to the congregation, and made him king over all Israel. There was Nobody who follow David’s house, except for the tribe of Judah only.

When Rehoboam had come to Jerusalem, he assembled all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen men, who were warriors, to fight against the house of Israel, to bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.
But the word of God come to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
“Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people, saying,

‘Baba God says, “You no go go up or fight against una brothers, the pikin dem of Israel. Everyone return to his house; for this thing is from me.”’” So dem listened to Baba God’s word, and come back and go dem way, according to Baba God’s word.
Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and lived in it; and he go out from there, and built Penuel.
Jeroboam talk say in his heart, “Now the kingdom will return to David’s house.

If this people goes up to offer sacrifices in Baba God’s house at Jerusalem, then the heart of this people will turn again to dem lord, even to Rehoboam king of Judah; and Dem go kill me, and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.”

So the king take counsel, and made two calves of gold; and E tell dem say, “It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem. Look and see am una gods, Israel, which bring you up out of the land of Egypt!”
He set the one in Bethel, and the other put he in Dan.
This thing became a sin; for the people go even as far as Dan to worship before the one there.
He made houses of high places, and made priests from among all the people, who No be of the sons of Levi.

Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the feast that is in Judah, and he go up to the altar. He did so in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves that he had made, and he placed in Bethel the priests of the high places that he had made.

He go up to the altar which he had made in Bethel on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, even in the month which he had devised of his own heart; and he ordained a feast for the pikin dem of Israel, and go up to the altar, to burn incense.
See am, a man of God come out of Judah by Baba God’s word to Beth El; and Jeroboam was standing by the altar to burn incense.

He cried against the altar by Baba God’s word, and talk say, “Altar! Altar! Baba God says: ‘See am, a son Go be born to David’s house, Josiah by name. On you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense on you, and Dem go burn men’s bones on you.’”
He give a sign the same day, saying, “This is the sign which Baba God has spoken: See am, the altar Go be split apart, and the ashes that are on it Go be poured out.”

When the king heard the saying of the man of God, which he cried against the altar in Bethel, Jeroboam put out his hand from the altar, saying, “Seize him!” His hand, which he put out against him, dried up, so that he could not draw it back again to imself.
The altar was also split apart, and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God had given by Baba God’s word.

The king answer the man of God, “Now intercede for the favor of Baba God una God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored me again.” The man of God interceded with Baba God, and the king’s hand was restored to him again, and became as it was before.
The king talk say to the man of God, “Come home with me, and refresh yourself, and I go give you a reward.”
The man of God talk say to the king, “Even if you give me half of una house, I would not go in with you, neither would I eat bread nor drink water in this place;
for so was it commanded me by Baba God’s word, saying, ‘You shall eat no bread, drink no water, and no return by the way that you come.’”
So he go another way, and didn’t return by the way that he come to Bethel.

Now an old prophet lived in Bethel, and one of his sons come and told him all the works that the man of God had done that day in Bethel. Dem also told dem father the words which he had spoken to the king.
Dem father talk say to dem, “Which way did he go?” Now his sons had seen which way the man of God go, who come from Judah.
He talk say to his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” So dem saddled the donkey for him; and he rode on it.
He go after the man of God, and find him sitting under an oak. E tell am say, “Are you the man of God who come from Judah?” He talk say, “I be.”
Then E tell am say, “Come home with me, and eat bread.”
He talk say, “I may not return with you, nor go in with you. I go not eat bread or drink water with you in this place.
For it was talk say to me by Baba God’s word, ‘You shall eat no bread or drink water there, and no turn again to go by the way that you come.’”
E tell am say, “I also am a prophet as You be; and an angel spoke to me by Baba God’s word, saying, ‘Bring him back with you into una house, that he may eat bread and drink water.’” He lied to him.
So he go back with him, ate bread in his house, and drank water.
As dem sat at the table, Baba God’s word come to the prophet who bring him back;

and he cried out to the man of God who come from Judah, saying, “Baba God says, ‘Because you Don dey disobedient to Baba God’s mouth, and have not kept the commandment which Baba God una God commanded you,
but come back, and have eaten bread and drank water in the place of which he talk say to you, “Eat no bread, and drink no water”; una body No go come to the tomb of una fathers.’”
After he had eaten bread, and after he drank, he saddled the donkey for the prophet whom he had bring back.
When he had gone, a lion met him by the way and killed him. His body was thrown on the path, and the donkey stood by it. The lion also stood by the body.
See am, men passed by, and see the body thrown on the path, and the lion standing by the body; and dem come and told it in the city where the old prophet lived.

When the prophet who bring him back from the way heard of it, he talk say, “It is the man of God who was disobedient to Baba God’s mouth. So Baba God has delivered him to the lion, which has mauled him and slain him, according to Baba God’s word, which he spoke to him.”
He talk say to his sons, saying, “Saddle the donkey for me,” and dem saddled it.
He go and find his body thrown on the path, and the donkey and the lion standing by the body. The lion had not eaten the body, nor mauled the donkey.
The prophet take up the body of the man of God, and laid it on the donkey, and bring it back. He come to the city of the old prophet to mourn, and to bury him.
He laid his body in his own grave; and dem mourned over him, saying, “Alas, my brother!”
After he had buried him, he spoke to his sons, saying, “When I be dead, bury me in the tomb in which the man of God is buried. Lay my bones beside his bones.
For the saying which he cried by Baba God’s word against the altar in Bethel, and against all the houses of the high places which are in the cities of Samaria, will surely happen.”

After this thing Jeroboam didn’t return from his evil way, but again made priests of the high places from among all the people. Anybody wey want to, he consecrated him, that there might be priests of the high places.
This thing became sin to the house of Jeroboam, even to cut it off, and to destroy it from off the surface of the earth.
At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam became sick.

Jeroboam talk say to his wife, “Please get up and disguise yourself, so that you no go be recognized as Jeroboam’s wife. Go to Shiloh. See am, Ahijah the prophet is there, who talk say that that I would be king over this people.
Take with you ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what will become of the pikin.”
Jeroboam’s wife did so, and arose, and go to Shiloh, and come to Ahijah’s house. Now Ahijah could not see; for his eyes were set by reason of his age.

Baba God talk say to Ahijah, “See am, Jeroboam’s wife is coming to inquire of you concerning her son; for he is sick. Tell her such and such; for it Go be, when she comes in, that she will pretend to be another woman.”
So when Ahijah heard the sound of her feet as she come in at the door, he talk say, “Come in, Jeroboam’s wife! Why do you pretend to be another? For I be sent to you with heavy news.
Go, tell Jeroboam, ‘Baba God, the God of Israel, says: “Because I exalted you from among the people, and made you prince over my people Israel,

and tore the kingdom away from David’s house, and give it you; and yet you have not been as my worker David, who kept my commandments, and who follow me with all his heart, to do that only which was right in my eyes,
but have done evil above all who were before you, and have gone and made for yourself other gods, molten images, to provoke me to anger, and have throw me behind una back;

so, see am, I go bring evil on the house of Jeroboam, and will cut off from Jeroboam Everybody wey urinates on a wall, person Wey shut up and person Wey left at large in Israel, and will utterly sweep away the house of Jeroboam, as a man sweeps away dung, until it is all gone.
The dogs will eat person wey belongs to Jeroboam who dies in the city; and the birds of the sky will eat person wey dies in the field: for Baba God has spoken it.”’
Arise so, and go to una house. When una feet enter into the city, the pikin will die.
All Israel will mourn for him and bury him; for he only of Jeroboam will come to the grave, because in him E get find some good thing toward Baba God, the God of Israel, in the house of Jeroboam.
Moreover Baba God will raise up a king for imself over Israel, who will cut off the house of Jeroboam. This is the day! What? Even now.

For Baba God will strike Israel, as a reed is shaken in the water; and he will root up Israel out of this good land which he give to dem fathers, and will scatter dem beyond the River, because dem have made dem Asherah poles, provoking Baba God to anger.
He will give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam, which he has sinned, and with which he has made Israel to sin.”
Jeroboam’s wife arose and comot, and come to Tirzah. As she come to the threshold of the house, the pikin died.
All Israel buried him and mourned for him, according to Baba God’s word, which he spoke by his worker Ahijah the prophet.
The rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he fought, and how he reigned, see am, Dem be written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
The days which Jeroboam reigned were twenty two years, then he slept with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his place.

Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which Baba God had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonitess.
Judah did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, and dem provoked him to jealousy with dem sins which dem committed, above all that dem fathers had done.
For dem also built for themselves high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.
There were also sodomites in the land. Dem did according to all the abominations of the nations which Baba God drove out before the pikin dem of Israel.
In the fifth year of king Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt come up against Jerusalem,
and he take away the treasures of Baba God’s house, and the treasures of the king’s house. He even take away all of it, including all the gold shields which Solomon had made.
King Rehoboam made shields of brass in dem place, and committed dem to the hands of the captains of the guard, who kept the door of the king’s house.
It was so, that as often as the king go into Baba God’s house, the guard bore dem, and bring dem back into the guard room.
Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all that he did, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in David’s city. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonitess. Abijam his son reigned in his place.
Now in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam the son of Nebat, Abijam began to reign over Judah.
He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
He walked in all the sins of his father, which he had done before him; and his heart No be perfect with Baba God his God, as the heart of David his father.
Nevertheless for David’s sake, Baba God his God give him a lamp in Jerusalem, to set up his son after him, and to establish Jerusalem;
because David did that which was right in Baba God’s eyes, and didn’t turn aside from anything that he commanded him all the days of his life, except only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
Now there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.
The rest of the acts of Abijam, and all that he did, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
Abijam slept with his fathers, and dem buried him in David’s city; and Asa his son reigned in his place.
In the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa began to reign over Judah.
He reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
Asa did that which was right in Baba God’s eyes, as David his father did.
He put away the sodomites out of the land, and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.
He also removed Maacah his mother from being queen, because she had made an abominable image for an Asherah. Asa cut down her image and burned it at the brook Kidron.
But the high places No be taken away. Nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect with Baba God all his days.
He bring into Baba God’s house the things that his father had dedicated, and the things that he imself had dedicated: silver, gold, and utensils.
There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all dem days.
Baasha king of Israel go up against Judah, and built Ramah, that he might not allow anyone to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.

Then Asa take all the silver and the gold that was left in the treasures of Baba God’s house, and the treasures of the king’s house, and delivered it into the hand of his workers. Then King Asa sent dem to Ben Hadad, the son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion, king of Syria, who lived at Damascus, saying,

“E get a treaty between me and you, between my father and una father. See am, I have sent to you a present of silver and gold. Go, break una treaty with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.”
Ben Hadad listened to king Asa, and sent the captains of his armies against the cities of Israel, and struck Ijon, and Dan, and Abel Beth Maacah, and all Chinneroth, with all the land of Naphtali.
When Baasha heard of it, he stopped building Ramah, and lived in Tirzah.

Then king Asa made a proclamation to all Judah. Nobody was exempted. Dem carried away the stones of Ramah, and its timber, with which Baasha had built; and king Asa used it to build Geba of Benjamin, and Mizpah.

Now the rest of all the acts of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities which he built, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? But in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.
Asa slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in his father David’s city; and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.
Nadab the son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah; and he reigned over Israel two years.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, and walked in the way of his father, and in his sin with which he made Israel to sin.
Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him; and Baasha struck him at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines; for Nadab and all Israel were besieging Gibbethon.
Even in the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha killed him, and reigned in his place.

As soon as he was king, he struck all the house of Jeroboam. He didn’t leave to Jeroboam any who breathed, until he had destroyed him; according to the saying of Baba God, which he spoke by his worker Ahijah the Shilonite;
for the sins of Jeroboam which he sinned, and with which he made Israel to sin, because of his provocation with which he provoked Baba God, the God of Israel, to anger.
Now the rest of the acts of Nadab, and all that he did, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all dem days.
In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha the son of Ahijah began to reign over all Israel in Tirzah for twenty-four years.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, and walked in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin with which he made Israel to sin.
Baba God’s word come to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,

“Because I exalted you out of the dust, and made you prince over my people Israel, and you have walked in the way of Jeroboam, and have made my people Israel to sin, to provoke me to anger with dem sins;
see am, I go utterly sweep away Baasha and his house; and I go make una house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
The dogs will eat Baasha’s descendants who die in the city; and person wey dies of his in the field, the birds of the sky will eat.”
Now the rest of the acts of Baasha, and what he did, and his might, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Baasha slept with his fathers, and was buried in Tirzah; and Elah his son reigned in his place.

Moreover Baba God’s word come by the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha and against his house, both because of all the evil that he did in Baba God’s sight, to provoke him to anger with the work of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam, and because he struck him.
In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah the son of Baasha began to reign over Israel in Tirzah for two years.
His worker Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspired against him. Now he was in Tirzah, drinking imself drunk in the house of Arza, who was over the household in Tirzah;
and Zimri go in and struck him, and killed him, in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.
When he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, he attacked all the house of Baasha. He didn’t leave him a single one who urinates on a wall among his relatives or his friends.
Thus Zimri destroyed all the house of Baasha, according to Baba God’s word, which he spoke against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,
for all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, which dem sinned, and with which dem made Israel to sin, to provoke Baba God, the God of Israel, to anger with dem vanities.
Now the rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he did, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
