Jehu sent through all Israel; and all the worshipers of Baal come, so that there No be a man left that didn’t come. Dem come into the house of Baal; and the house of Baal was filled from one end to another.
E tell am say who kept the wardrobe, “Bring out robes for all the worshipers of Baal!” So he bring robes out to dem.

Jehu go with Jehonadab the son of Rechab into the house of Baal. Then he talk say to the worshipers of Baal, “Search, and see that none of the workers of Baba God are here with you, but only the worshipers of Baal.”

So dem go in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had appointed for imself eighty men outside, and talk say, “If any of the men whom I bring into una hands escape, person wey lets him go, his life go be for the life of him.”

As soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, Jehu talk say to the guard and to the captains, “Go in and kill dem! Let Nobody escape.” So dem struck dem with the edge of the sword. The guard and the captains threw the bodies out, and go to the inner shrine of the house of Baal.
Dem bring out the pillars that were in the house of Baal, and burned dem.
Dem broke down the pillar of Baal, and broke down the house of Baal, and made it a latrine, to this day.
Thus Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.
However, Jehu didn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin, the golden calves that were in Bethel and that were in Dan.

Baba God talk say to Jehu, “Because you have done well in executing that which is right in my eyes, and have done to Ahab’s house according to all that was in my heart, una descendants shall sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.”
But Jehu take no heed to walk in the law of Baba God, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He didn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam, with which he made Israel to sin.
In those days Baba God began to cut away parts of Israel; and Hazael struck dem in all the borders of Israel;
from the Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, and the Reubenites, and the Manassites, from Aroer, which is by the valley of the Arnon, even Gilead and Bashan.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehu, and all that he did, and all his might, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Jehu slept with his fathers; and dem buried him in Samaria. Jehoahaz his son reigned in his place.
The time that Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria was twenty-eight years.
Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah see that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring.

But Jehosheba, the daughter of king Joram, sister of Ahaziah, take Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him away from among the king’s sons who were slain, even him and his nurse, and put dem in the bedroom; and dem hid him from Athaliah, so that he No be slain.
He was with her hidden in Baba God’s house six years while Athaliah reigned over the land.

In the seventh year Jehoiada sent and fetched the captains over hundreds of the Carites and of the guard, and bring dem to him into Baba God’s house; and he made a covenant with dem, and made a covenant with dem in Baba God’s house, and showed dem the king’s son.
He commanded dem, saying, “This is Wetin you must do: a third of you, who come in on the Sabbath, go be keepers of the watch of the king’s house;
a third of you go be at the gate Sur; and a third of you at the gate behind the guard. So you shall keep the watch of the house, and be a barrier.
The two companies of you, even all who go out on the Sabbath, shall keep the watch of Baba God’s house around the king.
You shall surround the king, every man with his weapons in his hand; and person wey comes within the ranks, Make e be slain. Be with the king when he goes out, and when he comes in.”

The captains over hundreds did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded; and dem each take his men, people wey were to come in on the Sabbath, with people wey were to go out on the Sabbath, and come to Jehoiada the priest.
The priest delivered to the captains over hundreds the spears and shields that Bin dey king David’s, which were in Baba God’s house.
The guard stood, every man with his weapons in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, along by the altar and the house, around the king.
Then he bring out the king’s son, and put the crown on him, and give him the covenant; and dem made him king, and anointed him; and dem clapped dem hands, and talk say, “Long live the king!”
When Athaliah heard the noise of the guard and of the people, she come to the people into Baba God’s house:

and she looked, and see am, the king stood by the pillar, as the tradition was, with the captains and the trumpets by the king; and all the people of the land rejoiced, and blew trumpets. Then Athaliah tore her clothes, and cried, “Treason! Treason!”

Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of hundreds who were set over the army, and talk say to dem, “Bring her out between the ranks. Kill Anybody wey follows her with the sword.” For the priest talk say, “No Make she be slain in Baba God’s house.”
So dem made way for her; and she go by the way of the horses’ entry to the king’s house, and she was slain there.
Jehoiada made a covenant between Baba God and the king and the people, that dem should be Baba God’s people; also between the king and the people.

All the people of the land go to the house of Baal, and broke it down; his altars and his images broke dem in pieces thoroughly, and killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. The priest appointed officers over Baba God’s house.

He take the captains over hundreds, and the Carites, and the guard, and all the people of the land; and dem bring down the king from Baba God’s house, and come by the way of the gate of the guard to the king’s house. He sat on the throne of the kings.
So all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. Dem had slain Athaliah with the sword at the king’s house.
Jehoash was seven years old when he began to reign.
Jehoash began to reign in the seventh year of Jehu, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zibiah of Beersheba.
Jehoash did that which was right in Baba God’s eyes all his days in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
However the high places No be taken away. The people still sacrificed and burned incense in the high places.

Jehoash talk say to the priests, “All the money of the holy things that is bring into Baba God’s house, in current money, the money of the people for whom each man is evaluated, and all the money that it comes into any man’s heart to bring into Baba God’s house,
let the priests take it to dem, each man from his donor; and dem shall repair the damage to the house, Anywhere wey any damage is find.”
But it was so, that in the twenty-third year of king Jehoash the priests had not repaired the damage to the house.

Then king Jehoash call for Jehoiada the priest, and for the other priests, and talk say to dem, “Why no you repair the damage to the house? Now so take no more money from una treasurers, but deliver it for repair of the damage to the house.”
The priests consented that dem should take no more money from the people, and not repair the damage to the house.

But Jehoiada the priest take a chest, and bored a hole in its lid, and set it beside the altar, on the right side as one comes into Baba God’s house; and the priests who kept the threshold put all the money that was bring into Baba God’s house into it.
When dem see that there was much money in the chest, the king’s scribe and the high priest come up, and dem put it in bags and counted the money that was find in Baba God’s house.

Dem give the money that was weighed out into the hands of people wey did the work, who had the oversight of Baba God’s house; and dem paid it out to the carpenters and the builders, who worked on Baba God’s house,
and to the masons and the stone cutters, and for buying timber and cut stone to repair the damage to Baba God’s house, and for all that was laid out for the house to repair it.
But there No be made for Baba God’s house cups of silver, snuffers, basins, trumpets, any vessels of gold, or vessels of silver, of the money that was bring into Baba God’s house;
for dem give that to people wey did the work, and repaired Baba God’s house with it.
Moreover dem didn’t demand an accounting from the men into whose hand dem delivered the money to give to people wey did the work; for dem dealt faithfully.
The money for the trespass offerings, and the money for the sin offerings No be bring into Baba God’s house. It was the priests’.
Then Hazael king of Syria go up, and fought against Gath, and take it; and Hazael set his face to go up to Jerusalem.

Jehoash king of Judah take all the holy things that Jehoshaphat and Jehoram and Ahaziah, his fathers, kings of Judah, had dedicated, and his own holy things, and all the gold that was find in the treasures of Baba God’s house, and of the king’s house, and sent it to Hazael king of Syria; and he go away from Jerusalem.
Now the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
His workers arose, and made a conspiracy, and struck Joash at the house of Millo, on the way that goes down to Silla.
For Jozacar the son of Shimeath, and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his workers, struck him, and he died; and dem buried him with his fathers in David’s city; and Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
In the twenty-third year of Joash the son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz the son of Jehu began to reign over Israel in Samaria for seventeen years.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, and follow the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin. He didn’t depart from it.
Baba God’s anger burned against Israel, and he delivered dem into the hand of Hazael king of Syria, and into the hand of Benhadad the son of Hazael, continually.
Jehoahaz begged Baba God, and Baba God listened to him; for he see the oppression of Israel, how the king of Syria oppressed dem.
(Baba God give Israel a savior, so that dem go out from under the hand of the Syrians; and the pikin dem of Israel lived in dem tents as before.
Nevertheless dem didn’t depart from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, with which he made Israel to sin, but walked in dem; and the Asherah also remain in Samaria.)
For he didn’t leave to Jehoahaz of the people any more than fifty horsemen, and ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen; for the king of Syria destroyed dem, and made dem like the dust in threshing.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his might, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Jehoahaz slept with his fathers; and dem buried him in Samaria; and Joash his son reigned in his place.
In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz began to reign over Israel in Samaria for sixteen years.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight. He didn’t depart from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin; but he walked in dem.
Now the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, and his might with which he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Joash slept with his fathers; and Jeroboam sat on his throne. Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

Now Elisha became sick with the illness of which he died; and Joash the king of Israel come down to him, and wept over him, and talk say, “My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen!”
Elisha talk say to him, “Take bow and arrows”; and he take bow and arrows for imself.
He talk say to the king of Israel, “Put una hand on the bow”; and he put his hand on it. Elisha laid his hands on the king’s hands.

He talk say, “Open the window eastward”; and he opened it. Then Elisha talk say, “Shoot!” and he shot. He talk say, “Baba God’s arrow of victory, even the arrow of victory over Syria; for You go strike the Syrians in Aphek, until you have consumed dem.”
He talk say, “Take the arrows”; and he take dem. He talk say to the king of Israel, “Strike the ground”; and he struck three times, and stopped.

The man of God was angry with him, and talk say, “You should have struck five or six times. Then you would have struck Syria until you had consumed it; whereas now You go strike Syria just three times.”
Elisha died, and dem buried him. Now the bands of the Moabites invaded the land at the coming in of the year.
As dem were burying a man, see am, dem see a band of raiders; and dem threw the man into Elisha’s tomb. As soon as the man touched Elisha’s bones, he revived, and stood up on his feet.
Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

But Baba God was gracious to dem, and had compassion on dem, and had respect for dem, because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and would not destroy dem, and he didn’t throw dem from his presence as yet.
Hazael king of Syria died; and Benhadad his son reigned in his place.

Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz take again out of the hand of Benhadad the son of Hazael the cities which he had taken out of the hand of Jehoahaz his father by war. Joash struck him three times, and recovered the cities of Israel.
In the second year of Joash son of Joahaz king of Israel Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah began to reign.
He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign; and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jehoaddin of Jerusalem.
He did that which was right in Baba God’s eyes, yet not like David his father. He did according to all that Joash his father had done.
However the high places No be taken away. The people still sacrificed and burned incense in the high places.
As soon as the kingdom was established in his hand, he killed his workers who had slain the king his father,

but the pikin dem of the murderers he didn’t put to death; according to that which is written in the book of the law of Moses, as Baba God commanded, saying, “The fathers no go be put to death for the pikin dem, nor the pikin dem be put to death for the fathers; but every man shall die for his own sin.”
He killed ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt, and take Sela by war, and call its name Joktheel, to this day.
Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash, the son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, “Come, Make we look each other in the face.”

Jehoash the king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, “The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give una daughter to my son as wife. Then a wild animal that was in Lebanon passed by, and trampled down the thistle.
You have indeed struck Edom, and una heart has lifted you up. Enjoy the glory of it, and stay at home; for why should you meddle to una harm, that you fall, even you, and Judah with you?’”
But Amaziah would not listen. So Jehoash king of Israel go up; and he and Amaziah king of Judah looked each other in the face at Beth Shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
Judah was defeated by Israel; and each man fled to his tent.

Jehoash king of Israel take Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Jehoash the son of Ahaziah, at Beth Shemesh, and come to Jerusalem, and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits.
He take all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that were find in Baba God’s house and in the treasures of the king’s house, the hostages also, and come back to Samaria.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehoash which he did, and his might, and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Jehoash slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel; and Jeroboam his son reigned in his place.
Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah lived after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel fifteen years.
Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
Dem made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; but dem sent after him to Lachish, and killed him there.
Dem bring him on horses, and he was buried at Jerusalem with his fathers in David’s city.
All the people of Judah take Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the place of his father Amaziah.
He built Elath, and restored it to Judah. After that the king slept with his fathers.
In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah, Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel began to reign in Samaria for forty-one years.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight. He didn’t depart from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin.

He restored the border of Israel from the entrance of Hamath to the sea of the Arabah, according to Baba God, the God of Israel’s word, which he spoke by his worker Jonah the son of Amittai, the prophet, who was from Gath Hepher.
For Baba God see the suffering of Israel, that it was very bitter; for all, slave and free, and there was no helper for Israel.
Baba God didn’t say that he would blot out the name of Israel from under the sky; but he saved dem by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash.

Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might, how he fought, and how he recovered Damascus, and Hamath, which had belonged to Judah, for Israel, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Jeroboam slept with his fathers, even with the kings of Israel; and Zechariah his son reigned in his place.
In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah began to reign.
He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
He did that which was right in Baba God’s eyes, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
However the high places No be taken away. The people still sacrificed and burned incense in the high places.
Baba God struck the king, so that he was a leper to the day of his death, and lived in a separate house. Jotham, the king’s son was over the household, judging the people of the land.
Now the rest of the acts of Azariah, and all that he did, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
Azariah slept with his fathers; and dem buried him with his fathers in David’s city: and Jotham his son reigned in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah the son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in Samaria six months.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, as his fathers had done. He didn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin.
Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him, and struck him before the people, and killed him, and reigned in his place.
Now the rest of the acts of Zechariah, see am, Dem be written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
This was Baba God’s word which he spoke to Jehu, saying, “Una sons to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.” So E happen say.
Shallum the son of Jabesh began to reign in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned for a month in Samaria.
Menahem the son of Gadi go up from Tirzah, come to Samaria, struck Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria, killed him, and reigned in his place.
Now the rest of the acts of Shallum, and his conspiracy which he made, see am, Dem be written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
Then Menahem attacked Tiphsah, and all who were in it, and its border areas, from Tirzah. He attacked it because dem didn’t open dem gates to him, and he ripped up all dem women who were with pikin.
In the thirty ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem the son of Gadi began to reign over Israel for ten years in Samaria.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight. He didn’t depart all his days from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin.
Pul the king of Assyria come against the land, and Menahem give Pul one thousand talents of silver, that his hand might be with him to confirm the kingdom in his hand.

Menahem exacted the money from Israel, even from all the mighty men of wealth, from each man fifty shekels of silver, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned back, and didn’t stay there in the land.
Now the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Menahem slept with his fathers, and Pekahiah his son reigned in his place.
In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah the son of Menahem began to reign over Israel in Samaria for two years.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight. He didn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin.

Pekah the son of Remaliah, his captain, conspired against him and attacked him in Samaria, in the fortress of the king’s house, with Argob and Arieh; and with him were fifty men of the Gileadites. He killed him, and reigned in his place.
Now the rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and all that he did, see am, Dem be written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah the son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria for twenty years.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight. He didn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin.

In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria come and take Ijon, Abel Beth Maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali; and he carried dem captive to Assyria.
Hoshea the son of Elah made a conspiracy against Pekah the son of Remaliah, attacked him, killed him, and reigned in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham the son of Uzziah.
Now the rest of the acts of Pekah, and all that he did, see am, Dem be written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
In the second year of Pekah the son of Remaliah king of Israel, Jotham the son of Uzziah king of Judah began to reign.
He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jerusha the daughter of Zadok.
He did that which was right in Baba God’s eyes. He did according to all that his father Uzziah had done.
However the high places No be taken away. The people still sacrificed and burned incense in the high places. He built the upper gate of Baba God’s house.
Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all that he did, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
In those days, Baba God began to send Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah against Judah.
Jotham slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in his father David’s city, and Ahaz his son reigned in his place.
In the seventeenth year of Pekah the son of Remaliah, Ahaz the son of Jotham king of Judah began to reign.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He didn’t do that which was right in Baba God his God’s eyes, like David his father.

But he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, yes, and made his son to pass through the fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom Baba God throw out from before the pikin dem of Israel.
He sacrificed and burned incense in the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.
Then Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel come up to Jerusalem to wage war. Dem besieged Ahaz, but could not overcome him.
At that time Rezin king of Syria recovered Elath to Syria, and drove the Jews from Elath; and the Syrians come to Elath, and lived there, to this day.

So Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria, saying, “I be una worker and una son. Come up and save me out of the hand of the king of Syria, and out of the hand of the king of Israel, who rise up against me.”
Ahaz take the silver and gold that was find in Baba God’s house, and in the treasures of the king’s house, and sent it for a present to the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria listened to him; and the king of Assyria go up against Damascus, and take it, and carried its people captive to Kir, and killed Rezin.
King Ahaz go to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria, and see the altar that was at Damascus; and king Ahaz sent to Urijah the priest a drawing of the altar and plans to build it.
Urijah the priest built an altar. According to all that king Ahaz had sent from Damascus, so Urijah the priest made it for the coming of king Ahaz from Damascus.
When the king had come from Damascus, the king see the altar; and the king come near to the altar, and offered on it.
He burned his burnt offering and his meal offering, poured his drink offering, and sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings on the altar.
The bronze altar, which was before Baba God, he bring from the front of the house, from between his altar and Baba God’s house, and put it on the north side of his altar.

King Ahaz commanded Urijah the priest, saying, “On the great altar burn the morning burnt offering, the evening meal offering, the king’s burnt offering, his meal offering, with the burnt offering of all the people of the land, dem meal offering, and dem drink offerings; and sprinkle on it all the blood of the burnt offering, and all the blood of the sacrifice; but the bronze altar Go be for me to inquire by.”
Urijah the priest did so, according to all that king Ahaz commanded.
King Ahaz cut off the panels of the bases, and removed the basin from off dem, and take down the sea from off the bronze oxen that were under it, and put it on a pavement of stone.
He removed the covered way for the Sabbath that dem had built in the house, and the king’s entry outside to Baba God’s house, because of the king of Assyria.
Now the rest of the acts of Ahaz which he did, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
Ahaz slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in David’s city, and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.
In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea the son of Elah began to reign in Samaria over Israel for nine years.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, yet No be like the kings of Israel who were before him.
Shalmaneser king of Assyria come up against him, and Hoshea became his worker, and bring him tribute.

The king of Assyria find conspiracy in Hoshea; for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and offered no tribute to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year. So the king of Assyria seized him, and bound him in prison.
Then the king of Assyria come up throughout all the land, go up to Samaria, and besieged it three years.
In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria take Samaria, and carried Israel away to Assyria, and placed dem in Halah, and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.
It was so because the pikin dem of Israel had sinned against Baba God dem God, who bring dem up out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and had feared other gods,
and walked in the statutes of the nations whom Baba God throw out from before the pikin dem of Israel, and of the kings of Israel, which dem made.

The pikin dem of Israel secretly did things that No be right against Baba God dem God; and dem built high places for themselves in all dem cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fortified city;
and dem set up for themselves pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill, and under every green tree;
and there dem burned incense in all the high places, as the nations whom Baba God carried away before dem did; and dem did wicked things to provoke Baba God to anger;
and dem served idols, of which Baba God had talk say to dem, “You no go do this thing.”

Yet Baba God testified to Israel, and to Judah, by every prophet, and every seer, saying, “Turn from una evil ways, and keep my commandments and my statutes, according to all the law which I commanded una fathers, and which I sent to you by my workers the prophets.”
Notwithstanding, dem would not listen, but hardened dem neck, like the neck of dem fathers, who didn’t believe in Baba God dem God.

Dem rejected his statutes, and his covenant that he made with dem fathers, and his testimonies which he testified to dem; and dem follow vanity, and became vain, and follow the nations that were around dem, concerning whom Baba God had commanded dem that dem no suppose do like dem.
Dem abandoned all the commandments of Baba God dem God, and made molten images for themselves, even two calves, and made an Asherah, and worshiped all the army of the sky, and served Baal.
Dem caused dem sons and dem daughters to pass through the fire, used divination and enchantments, and sold themselves to do that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, to provoke him to anger.
So Baba God was very angry with Israel, and removed dem out of his sight. There was none left but the tribe of Judah only.
Also Judah didn’t keep the commandments of Baba God dem God, but walked in the statutes of Israel which dem made.
Baba God rejected all the offspring of Israel, afflicted dem, and delivered dem into the hands of raiders, until he had throw dem out of his sight.
For he tore Israel from David’s house; and dem made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king; and Jeroboam drove Israel from following Baba God, and made dem sin a great sin.
The pikin dem of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam which he did; dem didn’t depart from dem
until Baba God removed Israel out of his sight, as he talk say by all his workers the prophets. So Israel was carried away out of dem own land to Assyria to this day.

The king of Assyria bring men from Babylon, from Cuthah, from Avva, and from Hamath and Sepharvaim, and placed dem in the cities of Samaria instead of the pikin dem of Israel; and dem possessed Samaria, and lived in its cities.
So it was, at the beginning of dem dwelling there, that dem didn’t fear Baba God. So Baba God sent lions among dem, which killed some of dem.

So dem spoke to the king of Assyria, saying, “The nations which you have carried away and placed in the cities of Samaria no know the law of the god of the land. So he has sent lions among dem, and see am, dem kill dem, because dem no know the law of the god of the land.”
Then the king of Assyria commanded, saying, “Carry there one of the priests whom you bring from there; and Make dem go and live there, and Make e teach dem the law of the god of the land.”
So one of the priests whom dem had carried away from Samaria come and lived in Bethel, and taught dem how dem should fear Baba God.
However every nation made gods of dem own, and put dem in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans had made, every nation in dem cities in which dem lived.
The men of Babylon made Succoth Benoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima,
and the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the Sepharvites burned dem pikin dem in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
So dem feared Baba God, and also made from among themselves priests of the high places for themselves, who sacrificed for dem in the houses of the high places.
Dem feared Baba God, and also served dem own gods, after the ways of the nations from among whom dem Bin dey carried away.

To this day dem do Wetin dem did before. Dem no fear Baba God, and dem No follow the statutes, or the ordinances, or the law, or the commandment which Baba God commanded the pikin dem of Jacob, whom he named Israel;
with whom Baba God had made a covenant, and commanded dem, saying, “You no go fear other gods, nor bow unaself to dem, nor serve dem, nor sacrifice to dem;
but you shall fear Baba God, who bring you up out of the land of Egypt with great power and with an outstretched arm, and you shall bow unaself to him, and you shall sacrifice to him.
The statutes and the ordinances, and the law and the commandment, which he wrote for you, you shall observe to do forever more. You no go fear other gods.
You no go forget the covenant that I have made with you. You no go fear other gods.
But you shall fear Baba God una God, and he will deliver you out of the hand of all una enemies.”
However dem No listen, but dem did Wetin dem did before.
So these nations feared Baba God, and also served dem engraved images. Dem pikin dem likewise, and dem pikin dem’s pikin dem, as dem fathers did, so dem do to this day.
Now in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Hezekiah the son of Ahaz king of Judah began to reign.
He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Abi the daughter of Zechariah.
He did that which was right in Baba God’s eyes, according to all that David his father had done.

He removed the high places, and broke the pillars, and cut down the Asherah. He also broke in pieces the bronze serpent that Moses had made, because in those days the pikin dem of Israel burned incense to it; and he call it Nehushtan.
He trusted in Baba God, the God of Israel; so that after him was Nobody like him among all the kings of Judah, nor among dem that were before him.
For he joined with Baba God. He didn’t depart from following him, but kept his commandments, which Baba God commanded Moses.
Baba God was with him. Anywhere wey he go, he prospered. He rebelled against the king of Assyria, and didn’t serve him.
He struck the Philistines to Gaza and its borders, from the tower of the watchmen to the fortified city.
In the fourth year of king Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria come up against Samaria, and besieged it.
At the end of three years dem take it. In the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was taken.
The king of Assyria carried Israel away to Assyria, and put dem in Halah, and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes,
because dem didn’t obey Baba God dem God’s voice, but transgressed his covenant, even all that Moses the worker of Baba God commanded, and would not hear it or do it.
Now in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria come up against all the fortified cities of Judah, and take dem.

Hezekiah king of Judah sent to the king of Assyria to Lachish, saying, “I have offended you. Return from me. That which you put on me, I go bear.” The king of Assyria appointed to Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
Hezekiah give him all the silver that was find in Baba God’s house, and in the treasures of the king’s house.
At that time, Hezekiah cut off the gold from the doors of Baba God’s temple, and from the pillars which Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and give it to the king of Assyria.

The king of Assyria sent Tartan and Rabsaris and Rabshakeh from Lachish to king Hezekiah with a great army to Jerusalem. Dem go up and come to Jerusalem. When dem had come up, dem come and stood by the conduit of the upper pool, which is in the highway of the fuller’s field.
When dem had call to the king, Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebnah the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph the recorder come out to dem.
Rabshakeh talk say to dem, “Say now to Hezekiah, ‘Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria, “What confidence is this in which you trust?
You say (but Dem be but vain words), ‘E get counsel and strength for war.’ Now on whom do you trust, that you have rebelled against me?
Now, see am, you trust in the staff of this bruised reed, even in Egypt. If a man leans on it, it will go into his hand, and pierce it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust on him.

But if you tell me, ‘We trust in Baba God our God;’ no be that he whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah has taken away, and has talk say to Judah and to Jerusalem, ‘You shall worship before this altar in Jerusalem?’
Now so, please give pledges to my master the king of Assyria, and I go give you two thousand horses, if You be able on una part to set riders on dem.
How then can you turn away the face of one captain of the least of my master’s workers, and put una trust on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?
Have I now come up without Baba God against this place to destroy it? Baba God talk say to me, ‘Go up against this land, and destroy it.’”’”

Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, Shebnah, and Joah, talk say to Rabshakeh, “Please speak to una workers in the Syrian language, for we understand it. No speak with us in the Jews’ language, in the hearing of the people Wey be on the wall.”

But Rabshakeh talk say to dem, “Has my master sent me to una master and to you, to speak these words? Hasn’t he sent me to the men who sit on the wall, to eat dem own dung, and to drink dem own urine with you?”
Then Rabshakeh stood, and cried with a loud voice in the Jews’ language, and spoke, saying, “Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria.
Thus says the king, ‘No let Hezekiah deceive you; for he No go be able to deliver you out of his hand.
No let Hezekiah make you trust in Baba God, saying, “Baba God will surely deliver us, and this city no go be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.”

No listen to Hezekiah.’ For thus says the king of Assyria, ‘Make una peace with me, and come out to me; and everyone of you eat from his own vine, and everyone from his own fig tree, and everyone drink water from his own cistern;

until I come and take you away to a land like una own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees and of honey, that you may live, and not die. No listen to Hezekiah, when he persuades you, saying, “Baba God will deliver us.”
Has any of the gods of the nations ever delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath, and of Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah? Have dem delivered Samaria out of my hand?
Wey be dem among all the gods of the countries, that have delivered dem country out of my hand, that Baba God should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?’”
But the people stayed quiet, and answer him not a word; for the king’s commandment was, “No answer him.”
Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, come with Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph the recorder, to Hezekiah with dem clothes torn, and told him Rabshakeh’s words.
When king Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, covered imself with sackcloth, and go into Baba God’s house.
He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz.
Dem tell am say, “Thus says Hezekiah, ‘Today is a day of trouble, of rebuke, and of rejection; for the pikin dem have come to the point of birth, and E get no strength to deliver dem.

It may be Baba God una God will hear all the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master has sent to defy the living God, and will rebuke the words which Baba God una God has heard. So lift up una prayer for the remnant that is left.’”
So the workers of king Hezekiah come to Isaiah.
Isaiah talk say to dem, “Tell una master this: ‘Baba God says, “No fear of the words that you have heard, with which the workers of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
See am, I go put a spirit in him, and he will hear news, and will return to his own land. I go cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.”’”
So Rabshakeh come back and find the king of Assyria warring against Libnah; for he had heard that he had comot from Lachish.
When he heard it talk say of Tirhakah king of Ethiopia, “See am, he has come out to fight against you, he sent messengers again to Hezekiah, saying,
‘Tell Hezekiah king of Judah this: “No let una God in whom you trust deceive you, saying, Jerusalem No go be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.
See am, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, by destroying dem utterly. Will you be delivered?
Have the gods of the nations delivered dem, which my fathers have destroyed, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the pikin dem of Eden who were in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah?”’”
Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it. Then Hezekiah go up to Baba God’s house, and spread it before Baba God.

Hezekiah prayed before Baba God, and talk say, “Baba God, the God of Israel, who sit above the cherubim, You be the God, even you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth.
Incline una ear, Baba God, and hear. Open una eyes, Baba God, and see. Hear the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to defy the living God.
Truly, Baba God, the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and dem lands,
and have throw dem gods into the fire; for dem were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone. So dem have destroyed dem.
Now so, Baba God our God, save us, I beg you, out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, Baba God, are God alone.”
Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, “Baba God, the God of Israel, says ‘You have prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria, and I have heard you.
This is the word that Baba God has spoken concerning him: ‘The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and ridiculed you. The daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you.
Whom have you defied and blasphemed? Against whom have you exalted una voice and lifted up una eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel!

By una messengers, you have defied the Lord, and have talk say, “With the plenty people of my chariots, I have come up to the height of the mountains, to the innermost parts of Lebanon, and I go cut down its tall cedars and its choice cypress trees; and I go enter into his farthest lodging place, the forest of his fruitful field.
I have dug and drunk strange waters, and with the sole of my feet will I dry up all the rivers of Egypt.”
Haven’t you heard how I have done it long ago, and formed it of ancient times? Now I have bring it to pass, that it should be yours to lay waste fortified cities into ruinous heaps.

So dem inhabitants had little power. Dem were dismayed and confounded. Dem were like the grass of the field, and like the green herb, like the grass on the housetops, and like grain blasted before it has grown up.
But I know una sitting down, una going out, una coming in, and una raging against me.
Because of una raging against me, and because una arrogance has come up into my ears, so I go put my hook in una nose, and my bridle in una lips, and I go turn you back by the way by which you come.’

“This Go be the sign to you: This year, You go eat that which grows of itself, and in the second year that which springs of the same; and in the third year sow, and reap, and plant vineyards, and eat its fruit.
The remnant that has escaped of the house of Judah will again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.
For out of Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and out of Mount Zion people wey shall escape. Baba God’s zeal will perform this.
“So Baba God says concerning the king of Assyria, ‘He No go come to this city, nor shoot an arrow there. He No go come before it with shield, nor throw up a mound against it.
By the way that he come, by the same he will return, and he No go come to this city,’ says Baba God.
‘For I go defend this city to save it, for my own sake, and for my worker David’s sake.’”
That night, Baba God’s angel go out, and struck one hundred eighty-five thousand in the camp of the Assyrians. When men arose early in the morning, see am, these were all dead bodies.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria comot, and go and come back, and lived at Nineveh.
As he was worshiping in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him with the sword; and dem escaped into the land of Ararat. Esar Haddon his son reigned in his place.
In those days Hezekiah was sick and dying. Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz come to him, and talk say to him, “Baba God says, ‘Set una house in order; for You go die, and not live.’”
Then he turned his face to the wall, and prayed to Baba God, saying,
“Remember now, Baba God, I beg you, how I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in una sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Before Isaiah had gone out into the middle part of the city, Baba God’s word come to him, saying,

“Turn back, and tell Hezekiah the prince of my people, ‘Baba God, the God of David una father, says, “I have heard una prayer. I have seen una tears. See am, I go heal you. On the third day, You go go up to Baba God’s house.
I go add to una days fifteen years. I go deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria. I go defend this city for my own sake, and for my worker David’s sake.”’”
Isaiah talk say, “Take a cake of figs.” Dem take and laid it on the boil, and he recovered.
Hezekiah talk say to Isaiah, “What Go be the sign that Baba God will heal me, and that I go go up to Baba God’s house the third day?”
Isaiah talk say, “This Go be the sign to you from Baba God, that Baba God will do the thing that he has spoken: should the shadow go forward ten steps, or go back ten steps?”
Hezekiah answer, “It is a light thing for the shadow to go forward ten steps. No, but let the shadow return backward ten steps.”
Isaiah the prophet cried to Baba God; and he bring the shadow ten steps backward, by which it had gone down on the sundial of Ahaz.
At that time Berodach Baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah; for he had heard that Hezekiah Bin dey sick.

Hezekiah listened to dem, and showed dem all the storehouse of his precious things, the silver, the gold, the spices, and the precious oil, and the house of his armor, and all that was find in his treasures. There was nothing in his house, or in all his dominion, that Hezekiah didn’t show dem.
Then Isaiah the prophet come to king Hezekiah, and talk say to him, “What did these men say? From where did dem come to you?” Hezekiah talk say, “Dem have come from a far country, even from Babylon.”
He talk say, “What have dem seen in una house?” Hezekiah answer, “Dem have seen all that is in my house. E get nothing among my treasures that I have not shown dem.”
Isaiah talk say to Hezekiah, “Hear Baba God’s word.
‘See am, the days come that all that is in una house, and that which una fathers have laid up in store to this day, Go be carried to Babylon. Nothing Go be left,’ says Baba God.
‘Dem go take away some of una sons who will issue from you, whom You go father; and Dem go be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.’”
Then Hezekiah talk say to Isaiah, “Baba God’s word which you have spoken is good.” He talk say moreover, “No be it so, if peace and truth Go be in my days?”

Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and all his might, and how he made the pool, and the conduit, and bring water into the city, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
Hezekiah slept with his fathers, and Manasseh his son reigned in his place.
Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hephzibah.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, after the abominations of the nations whom Baba God throw out before the pikin dem of Israel.

For he built again the high places which Hezekiah his father had destroyed; and he raised up altars for Baal, and made an Asherah, as Ahab king of Israel did, and worshiped all the army of the sky, and served dem.
He built altars in Baba God’s house, of which Baba God talk say, “I go put my name in Jerusalem.”
He built altars for all the army of the sky in the two courts of Baba God’s house.

He made his son to pass through the fire, practiced sorcery, used enchantments, and dealt with people wey had familiar spirits, and with wizards. He did much evil in Baba God’s sight, to provoke him to anger.

He set the engraved image of Asherah that he had made in the house of which Baba God talk say to David and to Solomon his son, “In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, will I put my name forever;

I go not cause the feet of Israel to wander any more out of the land which I give dem fathers, if only Dem go observe to do according to all that I have commanded dem, and according to all the law that my worker Moses commanded dem.”
But dem didn’t listen, and Manasseh seduced dem to do that which is evil more than the nations did whom Baba God destroyed before the pikin dem of Israel.
Baba God spoke by his workers the prophets, saying,
“Because Manasseh king of Judah has done these abominations, and has done wickedly above all that the Amorites did, who were before him, and has also made Judah to sin with his idols;
so Baba God the God of Israel says, ‘See am, I bring such evil on Jerusalem and Judah that Anybody wey hears of it, both his ears will tingle.
I go stretch over Jerusalem the line of Samaria, and the plummet of Ahab’s house; and I go wipe Jerusalem as a man wipes a dish, wiping it and turning it upside down.
I go throw off the remnant of my inheritance, and deliver dem into the hands of dem enemies. Dem go become a prey and a plunder to all dem enemies,
because dem have done that which is evil in my sight, and have provoked me to anger, since the day dem fathers come out of Egypt, even to this day.’”

Moreover Manasseh shed innocent blood well-well, until he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another; besides his sin with which he made Judah to sin, in doing that which was evil in Baba God’s sight.
Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and all that he did, and his sin that he sinned, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
Manasseh slept with his fathers, and was buried in the garden of his own house, in the garden of Uzza; and Amon his son reigned in his place.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he began to reign; and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Meshullemeth the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, as Manasseh his father did.
He walked in all the ways that his father walked in, and served the idols that his father served, and worshiped dem;
and he abandoned Baba God, the God of his fathers, and didn’t walk in the way of Baba God.
The workers of Amon conspired against him, and put the king to death in his own house.
But the people of the land killed all people wey had conspired against king Amon; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.
Now the rest of the acts of Amon which he did, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
He was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and Josiah his son reigned in his place.
Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jedidah the daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath.
He did that which was right in Baba God’s eyes, and walked in all the way of David his father, and didn’t turn aside to the right hand or to the left.
In the eighteenth year of king Josiah, the king sent Shaphan, the son of Azaliah the son of Meshullam, the scribe, to Baba God’s house, saying,
“Go up to Hilkiah the high priest, that he may count the money which is bring into Baba God’s house, which the keepers of the threshold have gathered of the people.
Make dem deliver it into the hand of the workmen who have the oversight of Baba God’s house; and Make dem give it to the workmen Wey be in Baba God’s house, to repair the damage to the house,
to the carpenters, and to the builders, and to the masons, and for buying timber and cut stone to repair the house.
However there was no accounting made with dem of the money that was delivered into dem hand; for dem dealt faithfully.”
Hilkiah the high priest talk say to Shaphan the scribe, “I have find the book of the law in Baba God’s house.” Hilkiah delivered the book to Shaphan, and he read it.

Shaphan the scribe come to the king, and bring the king word again, and talk say, “Una workers have emptied out the money that was find in the house, and have delivered it into the hands of the workmen who have the oversight of Baba God’s house.”
Shaphan the scribe told the king, saying, “Hilkiah the priest has delivered a book to me.” Then Shaphan read it before the king.
When the king had heard the words of the book of the law, he tore his clothes.
The king commanded Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam the son of Shaphan, Achbor the son of Micaiah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king’s worker, saying,

“Go inquire of Baba God for me, and for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that is find; for great is Baba God’s serious anger that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not listened to the words of this book, to do according to all that which is written concerning us.”

So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah, go to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe (now she lived in Jerusalem in the second quarter); and dem talked with her.
She tell dem say, “Baba God the God of Israel says, ‘Tell the man who sent you to me,
“Baba God says, ‘See am, I go bring evil on this place, and on its inhabitants, even all the words of the book which the king of Judah has read.

Because dem have forsaken me, and have burned incense to other gods, that dem might provoke me to anger with all the work of dem hands, so my serious anger go be kindled against this place, and it No go be quenched.’”
But to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of Baba God, tell him, “Baba God the God of Israel says, ‘Concerning the words which you have heard,

because una heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before Baba God, when you heard what I spoke against this place, and against its inhabitants, that dem should become a desolation and a curse, and have torn una clothes, and wept before me; I also have heard you,’ says Baba God.

‘So see am, I go gather you to una fathers, and You go be gathered to una grave in peace. Una eyes No go see all the evil which I go bring on this place.’”’” So dem bring this message back to the king.
The king sent, and dem gathered to him all the elders of Judah and of Jerusalem.

The king go up to Baba God’s house, and all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with him, with the priests, the prophets, and all the people, both small and great; and he read in dem hearing all the words of the book of the covenant which was find in Baba God’s house.

The king stood by the pillar, and made a covenant before Baba God, to walk after Baba God, and to keep his commandments, his testimonies, and his statutes, with all his heart, and all his soul, to confirm the words of this covenant that were written in this book; and all the people agreed to the covenant.

The king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the threshold, to bring out of Baba God’s temple all the vessels that were made for Baal, for the Asherah, and for all the army of the sky, and he burned dem outside of Jerusalem in the fields of the Kidron, and carried dem ashes to Bethel.

He got rid of the idolatrous priests, whom the kings of Judah had ordained to burn incense in the high places in the cities of Judah, and in the places around Jerusalem; those also who burned incense to Baal, to the sun, and to the moon, and to the planets, and to all the army of the sky.

He bring out the Asherah from Baba God’s house, outside of Jerusalem, to the brook Kidron, and burned it at the brook Kidron, and beat it to dust, and throw its dust on the graves of the common people.
He broke down the houses of the male shrine prostitutes that were in Baba God’s house, where the women wove hangings for the Asherah.

He bring all the priests out of the cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba; and he broke down the high places of the gates that were at the entrance of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, which were on a man’s left hand at the gate of the city.
Nevertheless the priests of the high places didn’t come up to Baba God’s altar in Jerusalem, but dem ate unleavened bread among dem brothers.
He defiled Topheth, which is in the valley of the pikin dem of Hinnom, that no man might make his son or his daughter to pass through the fire to Molech.

He take away the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun, at the entrance of Baba God’s house, by the room of Nathan Melech the officer, who was in the court; and he burned the chariots of the sun with fire.

The king broke down the altars that were on the roof of the upper room of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars which Manasseh had made in the two courts of Baba God’s house, and beat dem down from there, and throw dem dust into the brook Kidron.

The king defiled the high places that were before Jerusalem, which were on the right hand of the mountain of corruption, which Solomon the king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Sidonians, and for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, and for Milcom the abomination of the pikin dem of Ammon.
He broke in pieces the pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, and filled dem places with men’s bones.

Moreover the altar that was at Bethel, and the high place which Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, had made, even that altar and the high place he broke down; and he burned the high place and beat it to dust, and burned the Asherah.

As Josiah turned imself, he spied the tombs that were there in the mountain; and he sent, and take the bones out of the tombs, and burned dem on the altar, and defiled it, according to Baba God’s word which the man of God proclaimed, who proclaimed these things.

Then he talk say, “What monument is that which I see?” The men of the city told him, “It is the tomb of the man of God, who come from Judah, and proclaimed these things that you have done against the altar of Bethel.”
He talk say, “Make e be! Let Nobody move his bones.” So dem let his bones alone, with the bones of the prophet who come out of Samaria.

All the houses also of the high places that were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke Baba God to anger, Josiah take away, and did to dem according to all the acts that he had done in Bethel.
He killed all the priests of the high places that were there, on the altars, and burned men’s bones on dem; and he come back to Jerusalem.
The king commanded all the people, saying, “Keep the Passover to Baba God una God, as it is written in this book of the covenant.”
Surely there No be kept such a Passover from the days of the judges who judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel, nor of the kings of Judah;
but in the eighteenth year of king Josiah, this Passover was kept to Baba God in Jerusalem.

Moreover Josiah removed people wey had familiar spirits, the wizards, and the teraphim, and the idols, and all the abominations that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, that he might confirm the words of the law which were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest find in Baba God’s house.

There was no king like him before him, who turned to Baba God with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses; and there was none like him who arose after him.
Notwithstanding, Baba God didn’t turn from the fierceness of his great serious anger, with which his anger burned against Judah, because of all the provocation with which Manasseh had provoked him.

Baba God talk say, “I go also remove Judah out of my sight, as I have removed Israel, and I go throw off this city which I have chosen, even Jerusalem, and the house of which I talk say, ‘My name go be there.’”
Now the rest of the acts of Josiah, and all that he did, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
In his days Pharaoh Necoh king of Egypt go up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates; and king Josiah go against him; and Pharaoh Necoh killed him at Megiddo, when he had seen him.

His workers carried him in a chariot dead from Megiddo, and bring him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own tomb. The people of the land take Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and anointed him, and made him king in his father’s place.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign; and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, according to all that his fathers had done.
Pharaoh Necoh put him in bonds at Riblah in the land of Hamath, that he might not reign in Jerusalem; and put the land to a tribute of one hundred talents of silver, and a talent of gold.
Pharaoh Necoh made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in the place of Josiah his father, and changed his name to Jehoiakim; but he take Jehoahaz away, and he come to Egypt and died there.

Jehoiakim give the silver and the gold to Pharaoh; but he taxed the land to give the money according to the commandment of Pharaoh. He exacted the silver and the gold of the people of the land, from everyone according to his assessment, to give it to Pharaoh Necoh.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zebidah the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, according to all that his fathers had done.
In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon come up, and Jehoiakim became his worker three years. Then he turned and rebelled against him.

Baba God sent against him bands of the Chaldeans, and bands of the Syrians, and bands of the Moabites, and bands of the pikin dem of Ammon, and sent dem against Judah to destroy it, according to Baba God’s word, which he spoke by his workers the prophets.
Surely at the commandment of Baba God this come on Judah, to remove dem out of his sight, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he did,
and also for the innocent blood that he shed; for he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and Baba God would not pardon.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and all that he did, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
So Jehoiakim slept with his fathers, and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.
The king of Egypt didn’t come out of his land any more; for the king of Babylon had taken, from the brook of Egypt to the river Euphrates, all that belonged to the king of Egypt.
Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months. His mother’s name was Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, according to all that his father had done.
At that time the workers of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon come up to Jerusalem, and the city was besieged.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon come to the city while his workers were besieging it,

and Jehoiachin the king of Judah go out to the king of Babylon, he, and his mother, and his workers, and his princes, and his officers; and the king of Babylon captured him in the eighth year of his reign.

He carried out from there all the treasures of Baba God’s house, and the treasures of the king’s house, and cut in pieces all the vessels of gold, which Solomon king of Israel had made in Baba God’s temple, as Baba God had talk say.

He carried away all Jerusalem, and all the princes, and all the mighty men of valor, even ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and the smiths. Nobody remain, except the poorest people of the land.
He carried away Jehoiachin to Babylon, with the king’s mother, the king’s wives, his officers, and the chief men of the land. He carried dem into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.
All the men of might, even seven thousand, and the craftsmen and the smiths one thousand, all of dem strong and fit for war, even dem the king of Babylon bring captive to Babylon.
The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin’s father’s brother, king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
For through the anger of Baba God, this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until he had throw dem out from his presence. Then Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon come, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and encamped against it; and dem built forts against it around it.
So the city was besieged until the eleventh year of king Zedekiah.
On the ninth day of the fourth month, the famine was severe in the city, so that there was no bread for the people of the land.

Then a breach was made in the city, and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king’s garden (now the Chaldeans were against the city around it); and the king go by the way of the Arabah.
But the Chaldean army pursued the king, and overtook him in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.
Then dem captured the king, and carried him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah; and dem passed judgment on him.
Dem killed Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes, then put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him in fetters, and carried him to Babylon.

Now in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, a worker of the king of Babylon, come to Jerusalem.
He burned Baba God’s house, the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, even every great house, he burned with fire.
All the army of the Chaldeans, who were with the captain of the guard, broke down the walls around Jerusalem.

Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive the residue of the people who were left in the city, and people wey fell away, who fell to the king of Babylon, and the residue of the plenty people.
But the captain of the guard left some of the poorest of the land to work the vineyards and fields.
The Chaldeans broke up the pillars of brass that were in Baba God’s house and the bases and the bronze sea that were in Baba God’s house, and carried the brass pieces to Babylon.
Dem take away the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the spoons, and all the vessels of brass with which dem ministered.
The captain of the guard take away the fire pans, the basins, that which was of gold, in gold, and that which was of silver, in silver.
The two pillars, the one sea, and the bases, which Solomon had made for Baba God’s house, the brass of all these vessels No be weighed.

The height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits, and a capital of brass was on it. The height of the capital was three cubits, with network and pomegranates on the capital around it, all of brass; and the second pillar with its network was like these.
The captain of the guard take Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold;

and out of the city he take an officer who was set over the men of war; and five men of people wey see the king’s face, who were find in the city; and the scribe, the captain of the army, who mustered the people of the land; and sixty men of the people of the land, who were find in the city.
Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard take dem, and bring dem to the king of Babylon to Riblah.
The king of Babylon attacked dem, and put dem to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was carried away captive out of his land.
As for the people who were left in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, even over dem he made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor.

Now when all the captains of the forces, dem and dem men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor, dem come to Gedaliah to Mizpah, even Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of the Maacathite, dem and dem men.
Gedaliah swore to dem and to dem men, and talk say to dem, “No fear because of the workers of the Chaldeans. Live in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and it Go be well with you.”

But in the seventh month, Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the royal offspring come, and ten men with him, and struck Gedaliah, so that he died, with the Jews and the Chaldeans that were with him at Mizpah.
All the people, both small and great, and the captains of the forces, arose, and come to Egypt; for dem were afraid of the Chaldeans.

In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, Evilmerodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison;
and he spoke kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings who were with him in Babylon,
and changed his prison garments. Jehoiachin ate bread before him continually all the days of his life;
and for his allowance, there was a continual allowance given him from the king, every day a portion, all the days of his life.
Adam, Seth, Enosh,
Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared,
Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,
Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Diphath, and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
The sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raama, Sabteca. The sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
Cush became the father of Nimrod. He began to be a mighty one in the earth.
Mizraim became the father of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
Pathrusim, Casluhim (where the Philistines come from), and Caphtorim.
Canaan became the father of Sidon his firstborn, Heth,
the Jebusite, and the Amorite, the Girgashite,
the Hivite, the Arkite, the Sinite,
the Arvadite, the Zemarite, and the Hamathite.
The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.
Arpachshad became the father of Shelah, and Shelah became the father of Eber.
To Eber were born two sons: the name of the one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided; and his brother’s name was Joktan.
Joktan became the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Ebal, Abimael, Sheba,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
Shem, Arpachshad, Shelah,
Eber, Peleg, Reu,
Serug, Nahor, Terah,
Abram (also call Abraham).
The sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.
These are dem generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema,
Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These are the sons of Ishmael.
The sons of Keturah, Abraham’s concubine: she bore Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. The sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.
The sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the sons of Keturah.
Abraham became the father of Isaac. The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel.
The sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.
The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
The sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam; and Timna was Lotan’s sister.
The sons of Shobal: Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. The sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah.
The son of Anah: Dishon. The sons of Dishon: Hamran, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. The sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
Now these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom, before any king reigned over the pikin dem of Israel: Bela the son of Beor; and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his place.
Jobab died, and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who struck Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Avith.
Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.
Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the River reigned in his place.
Shaul died, and Baal Hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his place.
Baal Hanan died, and Hadad reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Pai: and his wife’s name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.
Then Hadad died. The chiefs of Edom were: chief Timna, chief Aliah, chief Jetheth,
chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
chief Magdiel, and chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom.
These are the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,
Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, and Shelah; which three were born to him of Shua’s daughter the Canaanitess. Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in Baba God’s sight; and he killed him.
Tamar his daughter-in-law bore him Perez and Zerah. All the sons of Judah were five.
The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara; five of dem in all.
The son of Carmi: Achar, the troubler of Israel, who committed a trespass in the devoted thing.
The son of Ethan: Azariah.
The sons also of Hezron, who were born to him: Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai.
Ram became the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab became the father of Nahshon, prince of the pikin dem of Judah;
and Nahshon became the father of Salma, and Salma became the father of Boaz,
and Boaz became the father of Obed, and Obed became the father of Jesse;
and Jesse became the father of his firstborn Eliab, and Abinadab the second, and Shimea the third,
Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
Ozem the sixth, David the seventh;
and dem sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. The sons of Zeruiah: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, three.
Abigail bore Amasa; and the father of Amasa was Jether the Ishmaelite.
Caleb the son of Hezron became the father of pikin dem of Azubah his wife, and of Jerioth; and these were her sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
Azubah died, and Caleb married Ephrath, who bore him Hur.
Hur became the father of Uri, and Uri became the father of Bezalel.
Afterward Hezron go in to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, whom he take as wife when he was sixty years old; and she bore him Segub.
Segub became the father of Jair, who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.
Geshur and Aram take the towns of Jair from dem, with Kenath, and its villages, even sixty cities. All these were the sons of Machir the father of Gilead.
After Hezron died in Caleb Ephrathah, Abijah Hezron’s wife bore him Ashhur the father of Tekoa.
The sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron were Ram the firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
Jerahmeel had another wife, whose name was Atarah. She was the mother of Onam.
The sons of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
The sons of Onam were Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai: Nadab and Abishur.
The name of the wife of Abishur was Abihail; and she bore him Ahban and Molid.
The sons of Nadab: Seled and Appaim; but Seled died without pikin dem.
The son of Appaim: Ishi. The son of Ishi: Sheshan. The son of Sheshan: Ahlai.
The sons of Jada the brother of Shammai: Jether and Jonathan; and Jether died without pikin dem.
The sons of Jonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These were the sons of Jerahmeel.
Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. Sheshan had a worker, an Egyptian, whose name was Jarha.
Sheshan give his daughter to Jarha his worker as wife; and she bore him Attai.
Attai became the father of Nathan, and Nathan became the father of Zabad,
and Zabad became the father of Ephlal, and Ephlal became the father of Obed,
and Obed became the father of Jehu, and Jehu became the father of Azariah,
and Azariah became the father of Helez, and Helez became the father of Eleasah,
and Eleasah became the father of Sismai, and Sismai became the father of Shallum,
and Shallum became the father of Jekamiah, and Jekamiah became the father of Elishama.
The sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel were Mesha his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph; and the sons of Mareshah the father of Hebron.
The sons of Hebron: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
Shema became the father of Raham, the father of Jorkeam; and Rekem became the father of Shammai.
The son of Shammai was Maon; and Maon was the father of Beth Zur.
Ephah, Caleb’s concubine, bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez; and Haran became the father of Gazez.
The sons of Jahdai: Regem, Jothan, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
Maacah, Caleb’s concubine, bore Sheber and Tirhanah.
She bore also Shaaph the father of Madmannah, Sheva the father of Machbena, and the father of Gibea; and the daughter of Caleb was Achsah.
These were the sons of Caleb, the son of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah: Shobal the father of Kiriath Jearim,
Salma the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph the father of Beth Gader.
Shobal the father of Kiriath Jearim had sons: Haroeh, half of the Menuhoth.
The families of Kiriath Jearim: the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites; from dem come the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites.
The sons of Salma: Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth Beth Joab, and half of the Manahathites, the Zorites.
The families of scribes who lived at Jabez: the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These are the Kenites who come from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.
Now these were the sons of David, who were born to him in Hebron: the firstborn, Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess; the second, Daniel, of Abigail the Carmelitess;
the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith;
the fifth, Shephatiah of Abital; the sixth, Ithream by Eglah his wife:
six were born to him in Hebron; and he reigned there seven years and six months. He reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem;
and these were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon, four, of Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel;
and Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet,
Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet, nine.
All these were the sons of David, besides the sons of the concubines; and Tamar was dem sister.
Solomon’s son was Rehoboam, Abijah his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,
Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,
Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son,
Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,
Amon his son, and Josiah his son.
The sons of Josiah: the firstborn Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, and the fourth Shallum.
