The sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, and Zedekiah his son.
The sons of Jeconiah, the captive: Shealtiel his son,
Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
The sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei. The sons of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah; and Shelomith was dem sister;
and Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab Hesed, five.
The sons of Hananiah: Pelatiah and Jeshaiah; the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, the sons of Shecaniah.
The son of Shecaniah: Shemaiah. The sons of Shemaiah: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat, six.
The sons of Neariah: Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam, three.
The sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani, seven.
The sons of Judah: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
Reaiah the son of Shobal became the father of Jahath; and Jahath became the father of Ahumai and Lahad. These are the families of the Zorathites.
These were the sons of the father of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. The name of dem sister was Hazzelelponi.
Penuel was the father of Gedor and Ezer the father of Hushah. These are the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, the father of Bethlehem.
Ashhur the father of Tekoa had two wives, Helah and Naarah.
Naarah bore him Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari. These were the sons of Naarah.
The sons of Helah were Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan.
Hakkoz became the father of Anub, Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel the son of Harum.
Jabez was more honorable than his brothers. His mother named him Jabez, saying, “Because I bore him with sorrow.”

Jabez call on the God of Israel, saying, “Oh that you would bless me indeed, and enlarge my border! May una hand be with me, and may you keep me from evil, that I may not cause pain!” God granted him that which he requested.
Chelub the brother of Shuhah became the father of Mehir, who was the father of Eshton.
Eshton became the father of Beth Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah the father of Ir Nahash. These are the men of Recah.
The sons of Kenaz: Othniel and Seraiah. The sons of Othniel: Hathath.
Meonothai became the father of Ophrah: and Seraiah became the father of Joab the father of Ge Harashim; for dem were craftsmen.
The sons of Caleb the son of Jephunneh: Iru, Elah, and Naam. The son of Elah: Kenaz.
The sons of Jehallelel: Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
The sons of Ezrah: Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon; and she bore Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa.
His wife the Jewess bore Jered the father of Gedor, Heber the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah. These are the sons of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mered take.
The sons of the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham, were the father of Keilah the Garmite, and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.
The sons of Shimon: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben Hanan, and Tilon. The sons of Ishi: Zoheth, and Ben Zoheth.
The sons of Shelah the son of Judah: Er the father of Lecah, Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the families of the house of people wey worked fine linen, of the house of Ashbea;
and Jokim, and the men of Cozeba, and Joash, and Saraph, who had dominion in Moab, and Jashubilehem. These records are ancient.
These were the potters, and the inhabitants of Netaim and Gederah: dem lived there with the king for his work.
The sons of Simeon: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, Shaul;
Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, and Mishma his son.
The sons of Mishma: Hammuel his son, Zaccur his son, Shimei his son.
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters; but his brothers didn’t have many pikin dem, and all dem family No multiply like the pikin dem of Judah.
Dem lived at Beersheba, Moladah, Hazarshual,
at Bilhah, at Ezem, at Tolad,
at Bethuel, at Hormah, at Ziklag,
at Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susim, at Beth Biri, and at Shaaraim. These were dem cities until David’s reign.
Dem villages were Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan, five cities;
and all dem villages that were around the same cities, to Baal. These were dem settlements, and dem have dem genealogy.
Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah the son of Amaziah,
Joel, Jehu the son of Joshibiah, the son of Seraiah, the son of Asiel,
Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,
and Ziza the son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah —
these mentioned by name were princes in dem families. Dem fathers’ houses increased greatly.
Dem go to the entrance of Gedor, even to the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for dem flocks.
Dem find fat pasture and good, and the land was wide, and quiet, and peaceful; for people wey lived there before were descended from Ham.

These written by name come in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and struck dem tents. The Meunim who were find there, and dem destroyed dem utterly to this day, and lived in dem place; because there was pasture there for dem flocks.
Some of dem, even of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men, go to Mount Seir, having for dem captains Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.
Dem struck the remnant of the Amalekites who escaped, and have lived there to this day.

The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel (for he was the firstborn; but, because he defiled his father’s couch, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph the son of Israel; and the genealogy No be to be listed according to the birthright.
For Judah prevailed above his brothers, and from him come the prince; but the birthright was Joseph’s) —
the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
The sons of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,
Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,
and Beerah his son, whom Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria carried away captive. He was prince of the Reubenites.
His brothers by dem families, when the genealogy of dem generations was listed: the chief, Jeiel, and Zechariah,
and Bela the son of Azaz, the son of Shema, the son of Joel, who lived in Aroer, even to Nebo and Baal Meon;
and he lived eastward even to the entrance of the wilderness from the river Euphrates, because dem livestock were multiplied in the land of Gilead.
In the days of Saul, dem made war with the Hagrites, who fell by dem hand; and dem lived in dem tents throughout all the land east of Gilead.
The sons of Gad lived over against dem, in the land of Bashan to Salecah:
Joel the chief, Shapham the second, Janai, and Shaphat in Bashan.
Dem brothers of dem fathers’ houses: Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber, seven.
These were the sons of Abihail, the son of Huri, the son of Jaroah, the son of Gilead, the son of Michael, the son of Jeshishai, the son of Jahdo, the son of Buz;
Ahi the son of Abdiel, the son of Guni, chief of dem fathers’ houses.
Dem lived in Gilead in Bashan, and in its towns, and in all the suburbs of Sharon, as far as dem borders.
All these were listed by genealogies in the days of Jotham king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.

The sons of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, of valiant men, men able to bear buckler and sword, and to shoot with bow, and skillful in war, were forty-four thousand seven hundred sixty, that were able to go out to war.
Dem made war with the Hagrites, with Jetur, and Naphish, and Nodab.
Dem were helped against dem, and the Hagrites were delivered into dem hand, and all who were with dem; for dem cried to God in the battle, and he was answer dem, because dem put dem trust in him.
Dem take away dem livestock; of dem camels fifty thousand, and of sheep two hundred fifty thousand, and of donkeys two thousand, and of men one hundred thousand.
For many fell slain, because the war was of God. Dem lived in dem place until the captivity.
The pikin dem of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land: dem increased from Bashan to Baal Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.
These were the heads of dem fathers’ houses: even Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel, mighty men of valor, famous men, heads of dem fathers’ houses.
Dem trespassed against the God of dem fathers, and played the prostitute after the gods of the peoples of the land, whom God destroyed before dem.

So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria, and he carried dem away, even the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and bring dem to Halah, Habor, Hara, and to the river of Gozan, to this day.
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel.
The pikin dem of Amram: Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Eleazar became the father of Phinehas, Phinehas became the father of Abishua,
Abishua became the father of Bukki. Bukki became the father of Uzzi.
Uzzi became the father of Zerahiah. Zerahiah became the father of Meraioth.
Meraioth became the father of Amariah. Amariah became the father of Ahitub.
Ahitub became the father of Zadok. Zadok became the father of Ahimaaz.
Ahimaaz became the father of Azariah. Azariah became the father of Johanan.
Johanan became the father of Azariah, who executed the priest’s office in the house that Solomon built in Jerusalem.
Azariah became the father of Amariah. Amariah became the father of Ahitub.
Ahitub became the father of Zadok. Zadok became the father of Shallum.
Shallum became the father of Hilkiah. Hilkiah became the father of Azariah.
Azariah became the father of Seraiah. Seraiah became the father of Jehozadak.
Jehozadak go into captivity, when Baba God carried Judah and Jerusalem away by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.
The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.
These are the names of the sons of Gershom: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to dem fathers’ households.
Of Gershom: Libni his son, Jahath his son, Zimmah his son,
Joah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son, and Jeatherai his son.
The sons of Kohath: Amminadab his son, Korah his son, Assir his son,
Elkanah his son, and Ebiasaph his son, Assir his son,
Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son, and Shaul his son.
The sons of Elkanah: Amasai and Ahimoth.
As for Elkanah, the sons of Elkanah: Zophai his son, Nahath his son,
Eliab his son, Jeroham his son, and Elkanah his son.
The sons of Samuel: the firstborn, Joel, and the second, Abijah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzzah his son,
Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, Asaiah his son.
These are dem whom David set over the service of song in Baba God’s house, after the ark come to rest there.
Dem ministered with song before the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting, until Solomon had built Baba God’s house in Jerusalem. Dem performed the duties of dem office according to dem order.
These are people wey served, and dem sons. Of the sons of the Kohathites: Heman the singer, the son of Joel, the son of Samuel,
the son of Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Eliel, the son of Toah,
the son of Zuph, the son of Elkanah, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai,
the son of Elkanah, the son of Joel, the son of Azariah, the son of Zephaniah,
the son of Tahath, the son of Assir, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah,
the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel.
His brother Asaph, who stood on his right hand, even Asaph the son of Berechiah, the son of Shimea,
the son of Michael, the son of Baaseiah, the son of Malchijah,
the son of Ethni, the son of Zerah, the son of Adaiah,
the son of Ethan, the son of Zimmah, the son of Shimei,
the son of Jahath, the son of Gershom, the son of Levi.
On the left hand dem brothers the sons of Merari: Ethan the son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch,
the son of Hashabiah, the son of Amaziah, the son of Hilkiah,
the son of Amzi, the son of Bani, the son of Shemer,
the son of Mahli, the son of Mushi, the son of Merari, the son of Levi.
Dem brothers the Levites were appointed for all the service of the tabernacle of God’s house.

But Aaron and his sons offered on the altar of burnt offering, and on the altar of incense, for all the work of the most holy place, and to make atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the worker of God had commanded.
These are the sons of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,
Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,
Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,
Zadok his son, and Ahimaaz his son.
Now these are dem dwelling places according to dem encampments in dem borders: to the sons of Aaron, of the families of the Kohathites (for dem own was the first lot),
to dem dem give Hebron in the land of Judah, and its suburbs around it;
but the fields of the city, and its villages, dem give to Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
To the sons of Aaron dem give the cities of refuge, Hebron; Libnah also with its suburbs, Jattir, Eshtemoa with its suburbs,
Hilen with its suburbs, Debir with its suburbs,
Ashan with its suburbs, and Beth Shemesh with its suburbs;
and out of the tribe of Benjamin, Geba with its suburbs, Allemeth with its suburbs, and Anathoth with its suburbs. All dem cities throughout dem families were thirteen cities.
To the rest of the sons of Kohath were given by lot, out of the family of the tribe, out of the half-tribe, the half of Manasseh, ten cities.

To the sons of Gershom, according to dem families, out of the tribe of Issachar, and out of the tribe of Asher, and out of the tribe of Naphtali, and out of the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities.
To the sons of Merari were given by lot, according to dem families, out of the tribe of Reuben, and out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun, twelve cities.
The pikin dem of Israel give to the Levites the cities with dem suburbs.

Dem give by lot out of the tribe of the pikin dem of Judah, and out of the tribe of the pikin dem of Simeon, and out of the tribe of the pikin dem of Benjamin, these cities which are mentioned by name.
Some of the families of the sons of Kohath had cities of dem borders out of the tribe of Ephraim.
Dem give to dem the cities of refuge, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim with its suburbs; Gezer also with its suburbs,
Jokmeam with its suburbs, Beth Horon with its suburbs,
Aijalon with its suburbs, Gath Rimmon with its suburbs;
and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Aner with its suburbs, and Bileam with its suburbs, for the rest of the family of the sons of Kohath.
To the sons of Gershom were given, out of the family of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan with its suburbs, and Ashtaroth with its suburbs;
and out of the tribe of Issachar, Kedesh with its suburbs, Daberath with its suburbs,
Ramoth with its suburbs, and Anem with its suburbs;
and out of the tribe of Asher, Mashal with its suburbs, Abdon with its suburbs,
Hukok with its suburbs, and Rehob with its suburbs;
and out of the tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee with its suburbs, Hammon with its suburbs, and Kiriathaim with its suburbs.
To the rest of the Levites, the sons of Merari, were given, out of the tribe of Zebulun, Rimmono with its suburbs, Tabor with its suburbs;
and beyond the Jordan at Jericho, on the east side of the Jordan, were given dem, out of the tribe of Reuben, Bezer in the wilderness with its suburbs, and Jahzah with its suburbs,
Kedemoth with its suburbs, and Mephaath with its suburbs;
and out of the tribe of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead with its suburbs, Mahanaim with its suburbs,
Heshbon with its suburbs, and Jazer with its suburbs.
Of the sons of Issachar: Tola, and Puah, Jashub, and Shimron, four.

The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel, heads of dem fathers’ houses, of Tola; mighty men of valor in dem generations. Dem number in the days of David was twenty-two thousand six hundred.
The son of Uzzi: Izrahiah. The sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah, five; all of dem chief men.
With dem, by dem generations, after dem fathers’ houses, were bands of the army for war, thirty-six thousand; for dem had many wives and sons.
Dem brothers among all the families of Issachar, mighty men of valor, listed in all by genealogy, were eighty-seven thousand.
The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Jediael, three.
The sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri, five; heads of fathers’ houses, mighty men of valor; and dem were listed by genealogy twenty-two thousand thirty-four.
The sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these were the sons of Becher.
Dem were listed by genealogy, after dem generations, heads of dem fathers’ houses, mighty men of valor, twenty thousand two hundred.
The son of Jediael: Bilhan. The sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
All these were sons of Jediael, according to the heads of dem fathers’ households, mighty men of valor, seventeen thousand two hundred, who were able to go out in the army for war.
So were Shuppim, Huppim, the sons of Ir, Hushim, and the sons of Aher.
The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, Shallum, and the sons of Bilhah.
The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, whom his concubine the Aramitess bore. She bore Machir the father of Gilead.
Machir take a wife of Huppim and Shuppim, whose sister’s name was Maacah. The name of the second was Zelophehad; and Zelophehad had daughters.
Maacah the wife of Machir bore a son, and she named him Peresh. The name of his brother was Sheresh; and his sons were Ulam and Rakem.
The sons of Ulam: Bedan. These were the sons of Gilead the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh.
His sister Hammolecheth bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
The sons of Shemida were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
The sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, Tahath his son,
Zabad his son, Shuthelah his son, Ezer, and Elead, whom the men of Gath who were born in the land killed, because dem come down to take away dem livestock.
Ephraim dem father mourned many days, and his brothers come to comfort him.
He go in to his wife, and she conceived, and bore a son, and he named him Beriah, because there was trouble with his house.
His daughter was Sheerah, who built Beth Horon the lower and the upper, and Uzzen Sheerah.
Rephah was his son, and Resheph, and Telah his son, Tahan his son,
Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,
Nun his son, and Joshua his son.
Dem possessions and settlements were Bethel and its towns, and eastward Naaran, and westward Gezer, with its towns; Shechem also and its towns, to Azzah and its towns;

and by the borders of the pikin dem of Manasseh, Beth Shean and its towns, Taanach and its towns, Megiddo and its towns, and Dor and its towns. The pikin dem of Joseph the son of Israel lived in these.
The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Serah was dem sister.
The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel, who was the father of Birzaith.
Heber became the father of Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and Shua dem sister.
The sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These are the pikin dem of Japhlet.
The sons of Shemer: Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.
The sons of Helem his brother: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
The sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
The sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
The sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.

All these were the pikin dem of Asher, heads of the fathers’ houses, choice and mighty men of valor, chief of the princes. The number of dem listed by genealogy for service in war was twenty-six thousand men.
Benjamin became the father of Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, Aharah the third,
Nohah the fourth, and Rapha the fifth.
Bela had sons: Addar, Gera, Abihud,
Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,
Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.
These are the sons of Ehud. These are the heads of fathers’ households of the inhabitants of Geba, who were carried captive to Manahath:
Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera, who carried dem captive; and he became the father of Uzza and Ahihud.
Shaharaim became the father of pikin dem in the field of Moab, after he had sent dem away. Hushim and Baara were his wives.
By Hodesh his wife, he became the father of Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam,
Jeuz, Shachia, and Mirmah. These were his sons, heads of fathers’ households.
By Hushim, he became the father of Abitub and Elpaal.
The sons of Elpaal: Eber, Misham, and Shemed, who built Ono and Lod, with its towns;
and Beriah, and Shema, who were heads of fathers’ households of the inhabitants of Aijalon, who put to flight the inhabitants of Gath;
and Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth,
Zebadiah, Arad, Eder,
Michael, Ishpah, Joha, the sons of Beriah,
Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,
Ishmerai, Izliah, Jobab, the sons of Elpaal,
Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi,
Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel,
Adaiah, Beraiah, Shimrath, the sons of Shimei,
Ishpan, Eber, Eliel,
Abdon, Zichri, Hanan,
Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah,
Iphdeiah, Penuel, the sons of Shashak,
Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah,
Jaareshiah, Elijah, Zichri, and the sons of Jeroham.
These were heads of fathers’ households throughout dem generations, chief men. These lived in Jerusalem.
The father of Gibeon, whose wife’s name was Maacah, lived in Gibeon,
with his firstborn son Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, and Zecher.
Mikloth became the father of Shimeah. Dem also lived with dem brothers in Jerusalem, near dem brothers.
Ner became the father of Kish. Kish became the father of Saul. Saul became the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
The son of Jonathan was Merib Baal. Merib Baal became the father of Micah.
The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz became the father of Jehoaddah. Jehoaddah became the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri became the father of Moza.
Moza became the father of Binea. Raphah was his son, Eleasah his son, and Azel his son.
Azel had six sons, whose names are these: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. All these were the sons of Azel.
The sons of Eshek his brother: Ulam his firstborn, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third.
The sons of Ulam were mighty men of valor, archers, and had many sons, and sons’ sons, one hundred fifty. All these were of the sons of Benjamin.
So all Israel were listed by genealogies; and see am, Dem be written in the book of the kings of Israel. Judah was carried away captive to Babylon for dem disobedience.
Now the first inhabitants who lived in dem possessions in dem cities were Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the temple workers.
In Jerusalem lived of the pikin dem of Judah, of the pikin dem of Benjamin, and of the pikin dem of Ephraim and Manasseh:
Uthai the son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani, of the pikin dem of Perez the son of Judah.
Of the Shilonites: Asaiah the firstborn, and his sons.
Of the sons of Zerah: Jeuel and dem brothers, six hundred ninety.
Of the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hassenuah,
and Ibneiah the son of Jeroham, and Elah the son of Uzzi, the son of Michri, and Meshullam the son of Shephatiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah;
and dem brothers, according to dem generations, nine hundred fifty-six. All these men were heads of fathers’ households by dem fathers’ houses.
Of the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin,
and Azariah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the ruler of God’s house;
and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah, and Maasai the son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer;
and dem brothers, heads of dem fathers’ houses, one thousand seven hundred sixty; very able men for the work of the service of God’s house.
Of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari;
and Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah the son of Mica, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph,
and Obadiah the son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun, and Berechiah the son of Asa, the son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.
The porters: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and dem brothers (Shallum was the chief),
who previously served in the king’s gate eastward. Dem were the porters for the camp of the pikin dem of Levi.

Shallum the son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his brothers, of his father’s house, the Korahites, were over the work of the service, keepers of the thresholds of the tent. Dem fathers Bin dey over Baba God’s camp, keepers of the entry.
Phinehas the son of Eleazar was ruler over dem in time past, and Baba God was with him.
Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah was porter of the door of the Tent of Meeting.
All these who were chosen to be porters in the thresholds were two hundred twelve. These were listed by genealogy in dem villages, whom David and Samuel the seer ordained in dem office of trust.
So dem and dem pikin dem had the oversight of the gates of Baba God’s house, even the house of the tent, by wards.
On the four sides were the porters, toward the east, west, north, and south.
Dem brothers, in dem villages, were to come in every seven days from time to time to be with dem:
for the four chief porters, who were Levites, were in an office of trust, and were over the rooms and over the treasuries in God’s house.
Dem stayed around God’s house, because that duty was on dem; and to dem duty was its opening morning by morning.
Certain of dem were in charge of the vessels of service; for these were bring in by count, and these were taken out by count.
Some of dem also were appointed over the furniture, and over all the vessels of the sanctuary, over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense, and the spices.
Some of the sons of the priests prepared the mixing of the spices.
Mattithiah, one of the Levites, who was the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, had the office of trust over the things that were baked in pans.
Some of dem brothers, of the sons of the Kohathites, were over the show bread, to prepare it every Sabbath.
These are the singers, heads of fathers’ households of the Levites, who lived in the rooms and were free from other service; for dem were employed in dem work day and night.
These were heads of fathers’ households of the Levites, throughout dem generations, chief men. These lived at Jerusalem.
Jeiel the father of Gibeon, whose wife’s name was Maacah, lived in Gibeon with
his firstborn son Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
Mikloth became the father of Shimeam. Dem also lived with dem brothers in Jerusalem, near dem brothers.
Ner became the father of Kish. Kish became the father of Saul. Saul became the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
The son of Jonathan was Merib Baal. Merib Baal became the father of Micah.
The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz became the father of Jarah. Jarah became the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri became the father of Moza.
Moza became the father of Binea; and Rephaiah his son, Eleasah his son, and Azel his son.
Azel had six sons, whose names are these: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.
Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain on Mount Gilboa.
The Philistines follow hard after Saul and after his sons; and the Philistines killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.
The battle go hard against Saul, and the archers overtook him; and he was distressed by reason of the archers.

Then Saul talk say to his armor bearer, “Draw una sword, and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised come and abuse me.” But his armor bearer would not; for he was terrified. So Saul take his sword, and fell on it.
When his armor bearer see that Saul was dead, he likewise fell on his sword, and died.
So Saul died with his three sons; and all his house died together.
When all the men of Israel who were in the valley see that dem fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, dem abandoned dem cities, and fled; and the Philistines come and lived in dem.
On the next day, when the Philistines come to strip the slain, dem find Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
Dem stripped him, and take his head and his armor, and sent into the land of the Philistines all around, to carry the news to dem idols, and to the people.
Dem put his armor in the house of dem gods, and fastened his head in the house of Dagon.
When all Jabesh Gilead heard all that the Philistines had done to Saul,
all the valiant men arose, and take away the body of Saul, and the bodies of his sons, and bring dem to Jabesh, and buried dem bones under the oak in Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
So Saul died for his trespass which he committed against Baba God, because of Baba God’s word, which he didn’t keep; and also because he ask counsel of one who had a familiar spirit, to inquire,
and didn’t inquire of Baba God. So he killed him, and turned the kingdom over to David the son of Jesse.
Then all Israel gathered themselves to David to Hebron, saying, “See am, We be una bone and una flesh.

In times past, even when Saul was king, it was you who led out and bring in Israel. Baba God una God talk say to you, ‘You go be shepherd of my people Israel, and you go be prince over my people Israel.’”
So all the elders of Israel come to the king to Hebron; and David made a covenant with dem in Hebron before Baba God; and dem anointed David king over Israel, according to Baba God’s word by Samuel.
David and all Israel go to Jerusalem (also call Jebus); and the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, were there.
The inhabitants of Jebus talk say to David, “You go not come in here.” Nevertheless David take the stronghold of Zion. The same is David’s city.
David talk say, “Anybody wey strikes the Jebusites first go be chief and captain.” Joab the son of Zeruiah go up first, and was made chief.
David lived in the stronghold; so dem call it David’s city.
He built the city all around, from Millo even around; and Joab repaired the rest of the city.
David grew greater and greater; for Baba God of Armies was with him.

Now these are the chief of the mighty men whom David had, who showed themselves strong with him in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king, according to Baba God’s word concerning Israel.
This is the number of the mighty men whom David had: Jashobeam, the son of a Hachmonite, the chief of the thirty; he lifted up his spear against three hundred and killed dem at one time.
After him was Eleazar the son of Dodo, the Ahohite, who was one of the three mighty men.
He was with David at Pasdammim, and there the Philistines were gathered together to battle, where there was a plot of ground full of barley; and the people fled from before the Philistines.
Dem stood in the middle of the plot, defended it, and killed the Philistines; and Baba God saved dem by a great victory.
Three of the thirty chief men go down to the rock to David, into the cave of Adullam; and the army of the Philistines were encamped in the valley of Rephaim.
David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was in Bethlehem at that time.
David longed, and talk say, “Oh that one would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem, which is by the gate!”

The three broke through the army of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem, that was by the gate, and take it, and bring it to David; but David would not drink any of it, but poured it out to Baba God,

and talk say, “My God forbid me, that I should do this! Shall I drink the blood of these men who have put dem lives in jeopardy?” For dem risked dem lives to bring it. So he would not drink it. The three mighty men did these things.
Abishai, the brother of Joab, he was chief of the three; for he lifted up his spear against three hundred and killed dem, and had a name among the three.
Of the three, he was more honorable than the two, and was made dem captain; however he no be included in the three.

Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, who had done mighty deeds, killed the two sons of Ariel of Moab. He also go down and killed a lion in the middle of a pit on a snowy day.

He killed an Egyptian, a man of great stature, five cubits high. In the Egyptian’s hand was a spear like a weaver’s beam; and he go down to him with a staff, plucked the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did these things, and had a name among the three mighty men.
See am, he was more honorable than the thirty, but he didn’t attain to the three; and David set him over his guard.
The mighty men of the armies also include Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,
Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, Abiezer the Anathothite,
Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,
Maharai the Netophathite, Heled the son of Baanah the Netophathite,
Ithai the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the pikin dem of Benjamin, Benaiah the Pirathonite,
Hurai of the brooks of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,
Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite,
the sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan the son of Shagee the Hararite,
Ahiam the son of Sacar the Hararite, Eliphal the son of Ur,
Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite,
Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai the son of Ezbai,
Joel the brother of Nathan, Mibhar the son of Hagri,
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite, the armor bearer of Joab the son of Zeruiah,
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
Uriah the Hittite, Zabad the son of Ahlai,
Adina the son of Shiza the Reubenite, a chief of the Reubenites, and thirty with him,
Hanan the son of Maacah, and Joshaphat the Mithnite,
Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham the Aroerite,
Jediael the son of Shimri, and Joha his brother, the Tizite,
Eliel the Mahavite, and Jeribai, and Joshaviah, the sons of Elnaam, and Ithmah the Moabite,
Eliel, and Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.
Now these are people wey come to David to Ziklag, while he was a fugitive from Saul the son of Kish. Dem were among the mighty men, his helpers in war.
Dem were armed with bows, and could use both the right hand and the left in slinging stones and in shooting arrows from the bow. Dem were of Saul’s relatives of the tribe of Benjamin.
The chief was Ahiezer, then Joash, the sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; Jeziel and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth; Beracah; Jehu the Anathothite;
Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the thirty and a leader of the thirty; Jeremiah; Jahaziel; Johanan; Jozabad the Gederathite;
Eluzai; Jerimoth; Bealiah; Shemariah; Shephatiah the Haruphite;
Elkanah, Isshiah Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korahites;
and Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham of Gedor.

Some Gadites joined David in the stronghold in the wilderness, mighty men of valor, men trained for war, who could handle shield and spear; whose faces were like the faces of lions, and dem were as swift as the gazelles on the mountains:
Ezer the chief, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third,
Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,
Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,
Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,
Jeremiah the tenth, and Machbannai the eleventh.
These of the sons of Gad were captains of the army: person wey was least was equal to one hundred, and the greatest to one thousand.
These are people wey go over the Jordan in the first month, when it had overflowed all its banks; and dem put to flight all who lived in the valleys, both toward the east and toward the west.
Some of the pikin dem of Benjamin and Judah come to the stronghold to David.

David go out to meet dem, and answer dem, “If you have come peaceably to me to help me, my heart Go be united with you; but if you have come to betray me to my adversaries, since E get no wrong in my hands, may the God of our fathers see this and rebuke it.”

Then the Spirit come on Amasai, who was chief of the thirty, and he talk say, “We be yours, David, and on una side, you son of Jesse. Peace, peace be to you, and peace be to una helpers; for una God helps you.” Then David received dem, and made dem captains of the band.

Some of Manasseh also joined David, when he come with the Philistines against Saul to battle; but dem didn’t help dem; for the lords of the Philistines sent him away after consultation, saying, “He will desert to his master Saul to the jeopardy of our heads.”
As he go to Ziklag, some from Manasseh joined him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai, captains of thousands who were of Manasseh.
Dem helped David against the band of rovers; for dem were all mighty men of valor, and were captains in the army.
For from day to day men come to David to help him, until there was a great army, like God’s army.
These are the numbers of the heads of people wey were armed for war, who come to David to Hebron, to turn the kingdom of Saul to him, according to Baba God’s word.
The pikin dem of Judah who bore shield and spear were six thousand eight hundred, armed for war.
Of the pikin dem of Simeon, mighty men of valor for the war, seven thousand one hundred.
Of the pikin dem of Levi four thousand six hundred.
Jehoiada was the leader of the household of Aaron; and with him were three thousand seven hundred,
and Zadok, a young man mighty of valor, and of his father’s house twenty-two captains.
Of the pikin dem of Benjamin, Saul’s relatives, three thousand: for until then, the greatest part of dem had kept dem allegiance to Saul’s house.
Of the pikin dem of Ephraim twenty thousand eight hundred, mighty men of valor, famous men in dem fathers’ houses.
Of the half-tribe of Manasseh eighteen thousand, who were mentioned by name, to come and make David king.
Of the pikin dem of Issachar, men who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do, dem heads were two hundred; and all dem brothers were at dem command.
Of Zebulun, such as were able to go out in the army, who could set the battle in array, with all kinds of instruments of war, fifty thousand, and who could command and No be of double heart.
Of Naphtali one thousand captains, and with dem with shield and spear thirty-seven thousand.
Of the Danites who could set the battle in array, twenty-eight thousand six hundred.
Of Asher, such as were able to go out in the army, who could set the battle in array, forty thousand.
On the other side of the Jordan, of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and of the half-tribe of Manasseh, with all kinds of instruments of war for the battle, one hundred twenty thousand.

All these were men of war, who could order the battle array, and come with a perfect heart to Hebron, to make David king over all Israel; and all the rest also of Israel were of one heart to make David king.
Dem were there with David three days, eating and drinking; for dem brothers had supplied provisions for dem.

Moreover people wey were near to dem, as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, bring bread on donkeys, on camels, on mules, and on oxen: supplies of flour, cakes of figs, clusters of raisins, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep in abundance; for there was gladness in Israel.
David consulted with the captains of thousands and of hundreds, even with every leader.

David talk say to all the assembly of Israel, “If it seems good to you, and if it is of Baba God our God, Make we send word everywhere to our brothers Wey be left in all the land of Israel, with whom the priests and Levites are in dem cities that have suburbs, that dem may gather themselves to us.
Also, Make we again bring the ark of our God back to us; for we didn’t seek it in the days of Saul.”
All the assembly talk say that dem would do so; for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.
So David assembled all Israel together, from the Shihor the brook of Egypt even to the entrance of Hamath, to bring God’s ark from Kiriath Jearim.
David go up with all Israel to Baalah, that is, to Kiriath Jearim, which belonged to Judah, to bring up from there Baba God’s ark that sits above the cherubim, that is call by the Name.
Dem carried God’s ark on a new cart, and bring it out of Abinadab’s house; and Uzza and Ahio drove the cart.
David and all Israel played before God with all dem might, even with songs, with harps, with stringed instruments, with tambourines, with cymbals, and with trumpets.
When dem come to Chidon’s threshing floor, Uzza put out his hand to hold the ark; for the oxen stumbled.
Baba God’s anger burned against Uzza, and he struck him, because he put his hand on the ark; and he died there before God.
David was displeased, because Baba God had broken out against Uzza. He call that place Perez Uzza, to this day.
David was afraid of God that day, saying, “How can I bring God’s ark home to me?”
So David didn’t move the ark with him into David’s city, but carried it aside into Obed-Edom the Gittite’s house.
God’s ark remain with the family of Obed-Edom in his house three months; and Baba God blessed Obed-Edom’s house and all that he had.
Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David with cedar trees, masons, and carpenters, to build him a house.
David perceived that Baba God had established him king over Israel; for his kingdom was exalted on high, for his people Israel’s sake.
David take more wives at Jerusalem, and David became the father of more sons and daughters.
These are the names of the pikin dem whom he had in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet,
Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.
When the Philistines heard that David was anointed king over all Israel, all the Philistines go up to seek David; and David heard of it, and go out against dem.
Now the Philistines had come and made a raid in the valley of Rephaim.
David inquired of God, saying, “Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you deliver dem into my hand?” Baba God talk say to him, “Go up; for I go deliver dem into una hand.”
So dem come up to Baal Perazim, and David defeated dem there. David talk say, God has broken my enemies by my hand, like waters breaking out. So dem call the name of that place Baal Perazim.
Dem left dem gods there; and David give a command, and dem were burned with fire.
The Philistines made a another raid in the valley.
David inquired again of God; and God talk say to him, “You no go go up after dem. Turn away from dem, and come on dem opposite the mulberry trees.
When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry trees, then go out to battle; for God has gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.”
David did as God commanded him; and dem attacked the army of the Philistines from Gibeon even to Gezer.
The fame of David go out into all lands; and Baba God bring the fear of him on people for everywhere.
David made imself houses in David’s city; and he prepared a place for God’s ark, and pitched a tent for it.
Then David talk say, “Nobody ought to carry God’s ark but the Levites. For Baba God has chosen dem to carry God’s ark, and to minister to him forever.”
David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem, to bring up Baba God’s ark to its place, which he had prepared for it.
David gathered together the sons of Aaron and the Levites:
of the sons of Kohath, Uriel the chief, and his brothers one hundred twenty;
of the sons of Merari, Asaiah the chief, and his brothers two hundred twenty;
of the sons of Gershom, Joel the chief, and his brothers one hundred thirty;
of the sons of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the chief, and his brothers two hundred;
of the sons of Hebron, Eliel the chief, and his brothers eighty;
of the sons of Uzziel, Amminadab the chief, and his brothers one hundred twelve.
David call for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites, for Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab,

and talk say to dem, “You be the heads of the fathers’ households of the Levites. Sanctify unaself, both you and una brothers, that you may bring the ark of Baba God, the God of Israel, up to the place that I have prepared for it.
For because you didn’t carry it at first, Baba God our God broke out in anger against us, because we didn’t seek him according to the ordinance.”
So the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves to bring up the ark of Baba God, the God of Israel.
The pikin dem of the Levites bore God’s ark on dem shoulders with its poles, as Moses commanded according to Baba God’s word.
David spoke to the chief of the Levites to appoint dem brothers as singers with instruments of music, stringed instruments, harps, and cymbals, sounding aloud and lifting up dem voices with gladness.
So the Levites appointed Heman the son of Joel; and of his brothers, Asaph the son of Berechiah; and of the sons of Merari dem brothers, Ethan the son of Kushaiah;
and with dem dem brothers of the second rank, Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel, the doorkeepers.
So the singers, Heman, Asaph, and Ethan, were given cymbals of brass to sound aloud;
and Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah, with stringed instruments set to Alamoth;
and Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah, with harps tuned to the eight-stringed lyre, to lead.
Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was over the singing. He taught the singers, because he was skillful.
Berechiah and Elkanah were doorkeepers for the ark.
Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer, the priests, blew the trumpets before God’s ark; and Obed-Edom and Jehiah were doorkeepers for the ark.
So David, the elders of Israel, and the captains over thousands, go to bring the ark of Baba God’s covenant up out of the house of Obed-Edom with gladness.
When God helped the Levites who bore the ark of Baba God’s covenant, dem sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
David was clothed with a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who bore the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah the choir master with the singers; and David had an ephod of linen on him.
Thus all Israel bring the ark of Baba God’s covenant up with shouting, with sound of the cornet, with trumpets, and with cymbals, sounding aloud with stringed instruments and harps.
As the ark of Baba God’s covenant come to David’s city, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out at the window, and see king David dancing and playing; and she despised him in her heart.
Dem bring in God’s ark, and set it in the middle of the tent that David had pitched for it; and dem offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in Baba God’s name.
He give to everyone of Israel, both man and woman, to everyone a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins.
He appointed some of the Levites to minister before Baba God’s ark, and to commemorate, to thank, and to praise Baba God, the God of Israel:

Asaph the chief, and second to him Zechariah, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel, with stringed instruments and with harps; and Asaph with cymbals, sounding aloud;
with Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests with trumpets continually, before the ark of the covenant of God.
Then on that day David first ordained to Thank God to Baba God, by the hand of Asaph and his brothers.
Oh Thank God to Baba God. Call on his name. Make what he has done known among the peoples.
Sing to him. Sing praises to him. Tell of all his marvelous works.
Glory in his holy name. Let the heart of people wey seek Baba God glad well-well.
Seek Baba God and his strength. Seek his face forever more.
Remember his marvelous works that he has done, his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth,
you offspring of Israel his worker, you pikin dem of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He is Baba God our God. His judgments are in all the earth.
Remember his covenant forever, the word which he commanded to a thousand generations,
the covenant which he made with Abraham, his oath to Isaac.
He confirmed the same to Jacob for a statute, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant,
saying, “I go give you the land of Canaan, The lot of una inheritance,”
when you were but a few men in number, yes, very few, and foreigners were in it.
Dem go about from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
He allowed no man to do dem wrong. Yes, he reproved kings for dem sakes,
“No touch my anointed ones! Do my prophets no harm!”
Sing to Baba God, all the earth! Display his salvation from day to day.
Declare his glory among the nations, and his marvelous works among all the peoples.
For great is Baba God, and greatly to be praised. He also is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but Baba God made the heavens.
Honor and majesty are before him. Strength and gladness are in his place.
Ascribe to Baba God, you relatives of the peoples, ascribe to Baba God glory and strength!
Ascribe to Baba God the glory due to his name. Bring an offering, and come before him. Worship Baba God in holy array.
Tremble before him, all the earth. The world also is established that it no fit be moved.
Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth glad well-well! Make dem say among the nations, “Baba God reigns!”
Let the sea roar, and its fullness! Let the field exult, and all that is in it!
Then the trees of the forest will sing for gladness before Baba God, for he comes to judge the earth.
Oh Thank God to Baba God, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever.
Say, “Save us, God of our salvation! Gather us together and deliver us from the nations, to Thank God to una holy name, to triumph in una praise.”
Blessed be Baba God, the God of Israel, from everlasting even to everlasting. All the people talk say, “Amen,” and praised Baba God.
So he left Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of Baba God’s covenant, to minister before the ark continually, as every day’s work required;
and Obed-Edom with dem brothers, sixty-eight; Obed-Edom also the son of Jeduthun and Hosah to be doorkeepers;
and Zadok the priest, and his brothers the priests, before Baba God’s tabernacle in the high place that was at Gibeon,
to offer burnt offerings to Baba God on the altar of burnt offering continually morning and evening, even according to all that is written in Baba God’s law, which he commanded to Israel;
and with dem Heman and Jeduthun, and the rest who were chosen, who were mentioned by name, to Thank God to Baba God, because his loving kindness endures forever;
and with dem Heman and Jeduthun with trumpets and cymbals for those that should sound aloud, and with instruments for the songs of God; and the sons of Jeduthun to be at the gate.
All the people comot, each man to his house; and David come back to bless his house.
When David lived in his house, David talk say to Nathan the prophet, “See am, I live in a house of cedar, but the ark of Baba God’s covenant is in a tent.”
Nathan talk say to David, “Do all that is in una heart; for God is with you.”
That same night, the word of God come to Nathan, saying,
“Go and tell David my worker, ‘Baba God says, “You no go build me a house to live in;
for I have not lived in a house since the day that I bring up Israel to this day, but have gone from tent to tent, and from one tent to another.

In all places in which I have walked with all Israel, did I speak a word with any of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to be shepherd of my people, saying, ‘Why have you not built me a house of cedar?’”’
“Now so, you shall tell my worker David, ‘Baba God of Armies says, “I take you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep, to be prince over my people Israel.
I Don dey with you Anywhere wey you have gone, and have cut off all una enemies from before you. I go make you a name, like the name of the great ones Wey be in the earth.
I go appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant dem, that dem may live in dem own place, and be moved no more. The pikin dem of wickedness No go waste dem any more, as at the first,
and from the day that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel. I go subdue all una enemies. Moreover I tell una that Baba God will build you a house.
It will happen, when una days are fulfilled that you must go to be with una fathers, that I go set up una offspring after you, who Go be of una sons; and I go establish his kingdom.
He will build me a house, and I go establish his throne forever.
I go be his father, and he Go be my son. I go not take my loving kindness away from him, as I take it from him that was before you;
but I go settle him in my house and in my kingdom forever. His throne Go be established forever.”’”
According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.
Then David the king go in, and sat before Baba God; and he talk say, “Who am I, Baba God, and Wetin be my house, that you have bring me this far?
This was a small thing in una eyes, God; but you have spoken of una worker’s house for a great while to come, and have respected me according to the standard of a man of high degree, Baba God.
What can David say yet more to you concerning the honor which is done to una worker? For you know una worker.
Baba God, for una worker’s sake, and according to una own heart, you have done all this greatness, to make known all these great things.
Baba God, E get Nobody like you, neither is there any God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

What one nation in the earth is like una people Israel, whom God go to redeem to imself for a people, to make you a name by great and awesome things, in driving out nations from before una people, whom you redeem out of Egypt?
For you made una people Israel una own people forever; and you, Baba God, became dem God.
Now, Baba God, let the word that you have spoken concerning una worker, and concerning his house, be established forever, and do as you have spoken.
Let una name be established and magnified forever, saying, ‘Baba God of Armies is the God of Israel, even a God to Israel. The house of David una worker is established before you.’
For you, my God, have revealed to una worker that You go build him a house. So una worker has find courage to pray before you.
Now, Baba God, You be God, and have promised this good thing to una worker.
Now it has pleased you to bless the house of una worker, that it may continue forever before you; for you, Baba God, have blessed, and it is blessed forever.”
After this, David defeated the Philistines and subdued dem, and take Gath and its towns out of the hand of the Philistines.
He defeated Moab; and the Moabites became workers to David, and bring tribute.
David defeated Hadadezer king of Zobah to Hamath, as he go to establish his dominion by the river Euphrates.
David take from him one thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen; and David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but reserved of dem enough for one hundred chariots.
When the Syrians of Damascus come to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck twenty-two thousand men of the Syrians.
Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus; and the Syrians became workers to David, and bring tribute. Baba God give victory to David Anywhere wey he go.
David take the shields of gold that were on the workers of Hadadezer, and bring dem to Jerusalem.
From Tibhath and from Cun, cities of Hadadezer, David take well-well brass, with which Solomon made the bronze sea, the pillars, and the vessels of brass.
When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,

he sent Hadoram his son to king David, to Greet him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him (for Hadadezer had wars with Tou); and he had with him all kinds of vessels of gold and silver and brass.

King David also dedicated these to Baba God, with the silver and the gold that he carried away from all the nations; from Edom, from Moab, from the pikin dem of Ammon, from the Philistines, and from Amalek.
Moreover Abishai the son of Zeruiah struck eighteen thousand of the Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
He put garrisons in Edom; and all the Edomites became workers to David. Baba God give victory to David Anywhere wey he go.
David reigned over all Israel; and he executed justice and righteousness for all his people.
Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;
Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abimelech the son of Abiathar, were priests; Shavsha was scribe;
and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David were chief officials serving the king.
After this, Nahash the king of the pikin dem of Ammon died, and his son reigned in his place.

David talk say, “I go show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. David’s workers come into the land of the pikin dem of Ammon to Hanun, to comfort him.

But the princes of the pikin dem of Ammon talk say to Hanun, “Do you think that David honors una father, in that he has sent comforters to you? Haven’t his workers come to you to search, to overthrow, and to spy out the land?”
So Hanun take David’s workers, shaved dem, and cut off dem garments in the middle at dem buttocks, and sent dem away.

Then some people go and told David how the men were treated. He sent to meet dem; for the men were greatly humiliated. The king talk say, “Stay at Jericho until una beards have grown, and then return.”

When the pikin dem of Ammon see that dem had made themselves odious to David, Hanun and the pikin dem of Ammon sent one thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen out of Mesopotamia, out of Aram-maacah, and out of Zobah.

So dem hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, and the king of Maacah with his people, who come and encamped near Medeba. The pikin dem of Ammon gathered themselves together from dem cities, and come to battle.
When David heard of it, he sent Joab with all the army of the mighty men.
The pikin dem of Ammon come out, and put the battle in array at the gate of the city; and the kings who had come were by themselves in the field.
Now when Joab see that the battle was set against him before and behind, he chose some of all the choice men of Israel, and put dem in array against the Syrians.
The rest of the people he committed into the hand of Abishai his brother; and dem put themselves in array against the pikin dem of Ammon.
He talk say, “If the Syrians are too strong for me, then You be to help me; but if the pikin dem of Ammon are too strong for you, then I go help you.
Be courageous, and Make we be strong for our people and for the cities of our God. May Baba God do that which seems good to him.”
So Joab and the people who were with him come near to the front of the Syrians to the battle; and dem fled before him.
When the pikin dem of Ammon see that the Syrians had fled, dem likewise fled before Abishai his brother, and entered into the city. Then Joab come to Jerusalem.
When the Syrians see that dem were defeated by Israel, dem sent messengers, and call out the Syrians who were beyond the River, with Shophach the captain of the army of Hadadezer leading dem.

David was told that; so he gathered all Israel together, passed over the Jordan, come to dem, and set the battle in array against dem. So when David had put the battle in array against the Syrians, dem fought with him.
The Syrians fled before Israel; and David killed of the Syrian men seven thousand chariots, and forty thousand footmen, and also killed Shophach the captain of the army.
When the workers of Hadadezer see that dem were defeated by Israel, dem made peace with David, and served him. The Syrians would not help the pikin dem of Ammon any more.

At the time of the return of the year, at the time when kings go out, Joab led out the army, and wasted the country of the pikin dem of Ammon, and come and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem. Joab struck Rabbah, and overthrew it.

David take the crown of dem king from off his head, and find it to weigh a talent of gold, and there were precious stones in it. It was set on David’s head, and he bring well-well plunder out of the city.

He bring out the people who were in it, and had dem cut with saws, with iron picks, and with axes. David did so to all the cities of the pikin dem of Ammon. Then David and all the people come back to Jerusalem.
After this, war arose at Gezer with the Philistines. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Sippai, of the sons of the giant; and dem were subdued.
Again there was war with the Philistines; and Elhanan the son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
There was again war at Gath, where there was a man of great stature, who had twenty-four fingers and toes, six on each hand, and six on each foot; and he also was born to the giant.
When he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimea David’s brother killed him.
These were born to the giant in Gath; and dem fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his workers.
Satan stood up against Israel, and moved David to take a census of Israel.
David talk say to Joab and to the princes of the people, “Go, count Israel from Beersheba even to Dan; and bring me word, that I may know how many E get.”

Joab talk say, “May Baba God make his people a hundred times as many as Dem be. But, my lord the king, no be dem all my lord’s workers? Why does my lord require this thing? Why will he be a cause of guilt to Israel?”
Nevertheless the king’s word prevailed against Joab. So Joab comot, and go throughout all Israel, then come to Jerusalem.

Joab give up the sum of the census of the people to David. All those of Israel were one million one hundred thousand men who drew a sword; and in Judah were four hundred seventy thousand men who drew a sword.
But he didn’t count Levi and Benjamin among dem; for the king’s word was abominable to Joab.
God was displeased with this thing; so he struck Israel.
David talk say to God, “I have sinned greatly, in that I have done this thing. But now put away, I beg you, the wickedness of una worker; for I have done very foolishly.”
Baba God spoke to Gad, David’s seer, saying,
“Go and speak to David, saying, ‘Baba God says, “I offer you three things. Choose one of dem, that I may do it to you.”’”
So Gad come to David, and talk say to him, “Baba God says, ‘Take una choice:

either three years of famine; or three months to be consumed before una foes, while the sword of una enemies overtakes you; or else three days the sword of Baba God, even pestilence in the land, and Baba God’s angel destroying throughout all the borders of Israel. Now so consider what answer I shall return to him who sent me.’”
David talk say to Gad, “I be in distress. Let me fall, I pray, into Baba God’s hand; for his mercies are plenty well-well. No let me fall into man’s hand.”
So Baba God sent a pestilence on Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.

God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it. As he was about to destroy, Baba God see, and he relented of the disaster, and talk say to the destroying angel, “It is enough. Now withdraw una hand.” Baba God’s angel was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

David lifted up his eyes, and see Baba God’s angel standing between earth and the sky, having a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem. Then David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell on dem faces.

David talk say to God, “No be it I who commanded the people to be counted? It is even I who have sinned and done very wickedly; but these sheep, what have dem done? Please let una hand, O Baba God my God, be against me, and against my father’s house; but not against una people, that dem should be plagued.”
Then Baba God’s angel commanded Gad to tell David that David should go up and raise an altar to Baba God on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
David go up at the saying of Gad, which he spoke in Baba God’s name.
Ornan turned back, and see the angel; and his four sons who were with him hid themselves. Now Ornan was threshing wheat.
As David come to Ornan, Ornan looked and see David, and go out of the threshing floor, and bowed imself to David with his face to the ground.

Then David talk say to Ornan, “Give me the place of this threshing floor, that I may build an altar to Baba God on it. You shall sell it to me for the full price, that the plague may be stopped from afflicting the people.”

Ornan talk say to David, “Take it for yourself, and let my lord the king do that which is good in his eyes. See am, I give the oxen for burnt offerings, and the threshing instruments for wood, and the wheat for the meal offering. I give it all.”
King David talk say to Ornan, “No; but I go most certainly buy it for the full price. For I go not take that which is yours for Baba God, nor offer a burnt offering that costs me nothing.”
So David give to Ornan six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the place.
David built an altar to Baba God there, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and call on Baba God; and he answer him from the sky by fire on the altar of burnt offering.
Then Baba God commanded the angel, and he put his sword back into its sheath.
At that time, when David see that Baba God had answer him in the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, then he sacrificed there.
For Baba God’s tabernacle, which Moses made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering, were at that time in the high place at Gibeon.
But David no fit go before it to inquire of God; for he was afraid because of the sword of Baba God’s angel.
Then David talk say, “This is the house of Baba God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”
David give orders to gather together the foreigners who were in the land of Israel; and he set masons to cut dressed stones to build God’s house.
David prepared iron in abundance for the nails for the doors of the gates, and for the couplings; and brass in abundance without weight;
and cedar trees without number, for the Sidonians and the people of Tyre bring cedar trees in abundance to David.

David talk say, “Solomon my son is young and tender, and the house that is to be built for Baba God must be exceedingly magnificent, of fame and of glory throughout all countries. I go so make preparation for it.” So David prepared abundantly before his death.
Then he call for Solomon his son, and commanded him to build a house for Baba God, the God of Israel.
David talk say to Solomon his son, “As for me, it was in my heart to build a house to the name of Baba God my God.
But Baba God’s word come to me, saying, ‘You have shed blood abundantly, and have made great wars. You no go build a house to my name, because you have shed much blood on the earth in my sight.
See am, a son go be born to you, who go be a man of peace. I go give him rest from all his enemies all around; for his name go be Solomon, and I go give peace and quietness to Israel in his days.
He shall build a house for my name; and he Go be my son, and I go be his father; and I go establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel for ever.’
Now, my son, may Baba God be with you and prosper you, and build the house of Baba God una God, as he has spoken concerning you.
May Baba God give you discretion and understanding, and put you in charge of Israel; that so you may keep the law of Baba God una God.
Then You go prosper, if you observe to do the statutes and the ordinances which Baba God give Moses concerning Israel. Be strong and courageous. No fear, and no be dismayed.

Now, see am, in my suffering I have prepared for Baba God’s house one hundred thousand talents of gold, one million talents of silver, and brass and iron without weight; for it is in abundance. I have also prepared timber and stone; and you may add to dem.
E get also workmen with you in abundance, cutters and workers of stone and timber, and all kinds of men Wey be skillful in every kind of work;
of the gold, the silver, the brass, and the iron, E get no number. Arise and be doing, and may Baba God be with you.”
David also commanded all the princes of Israel to help Solomon his son, saying,

“No be Baba God una God with you? Hasn’t he given you rest on every side? For he has delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand; and the land is subdued before Baba God, and before his people.

Now set una heart and una soul to follow Baba God una God. Arise so, and build the sanctuary of Baba God, to bring the ark of Baba God’s covenant and the holy vessels of God into the house that is to be built for Baba God’s name.”
Now David was old and full of days; and he made Solomon his son king over Israel.
He gathered together all the princes of Israel, with the priests and the Levites.
The Levites were counted from thirty years old and upward; and dem number by dem polls, man by man, was thirty-eight thousand.
David talk say, “Of these, twenty-four thousand were to oversee the work of Baba God’s house, six thousand were officers and judges,
four thousand were doorkeepers, and four thousand praised Baba God with the instruments which I made for giving praise.”
David divided dem into divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel, three.
The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran, three. These were the heads of the fathers’ households of Ladan.
The sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These four were the sons of Shimei.
Jahath was the chief, and Zizah the second; but Jeush and Beriah didn’t have many sons; so dem became a fathers’ house in one reckoning.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, four.

The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses; and Aaron was separated, that he should sanctify the most holy things, he and his sons, forever, to burn incense before Baba God, to minister to him, and to bless in his name, forever.
But as for Moses the man of God, his sons were named among the tribe of Levi.
The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.
The sons of Eliezer were: Rehabiah the chief; and Eliezer had no other sons; but the sons of Rehabiah were very many.
The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.
The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief, and Isshiah the second.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died, and had no sons, but daughters only: and dem brothers the sons of Kish take dem as wives.
The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth, three.

These were the sons of Levi after dem fathers’ houses, even the heads of the fathers’ houses of people wey were counted individually, in the number of names by dem polls, who did the work for the service of Baba God’s house, from twenty years old and upward.
For David talk say, “Baba God, the God of Israel, has given rest to his people; and he dwells in Jerusalem forever.
Also the Levites will no longer need to carry the tabernacle and all its vessels for its service.”
For by the last words of David the sons of Levi were counted, from twenty years old and upward.

For dem office was to wait on the sons of Aaron for the service of Baba God’s house, in the courts, and in the rooms, and in the purifying of all holy things, even the work of the service of God’s house;

for the show bread also, and for the fine flour for a meal offering, whether of unleavened wafers, or of that which is baked in the pan, or of that which is soaked, and for all measurements of quantity and size;
and to stand every morning to thank and praise Baba God, and likewise in the evening;
and to offer all burnt offerings to Baba God, on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, and on the set feasts, in number according to the ordinance concerning dem, continually before Baba God;
and that dem should keep the duty of the Tent of Meeting, the duty of the holy place, and the duty of the sons of Aaron dem brothers, for the service of Baba God’s house.
These were the divisions of the sons of Aaron. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
But Nadab and Abihu died before dem father, and had no pikin dem: so Eleazar and Ithamar executed the priest’s office.
David with Zadok of the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar, divided dem according to dem ordering in dem service.

There were more chief men find of the sons of Eleazar than of the sons of Ithamar; and dem were divided like this: of the sons of Eleazar there were sixteen, heads of fathers’ houses; and of the sons of Ithamar, according to dem fathers’ houses, eight.
Thus were dem divided impartially by drawing lots; for there were princes of the sanctuary, and princes of God, both of the sons of Eleazar, and of the sons of Ithamar.

Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the scribe, who was of the Levites, wrote dem in the presence of the king, the princes, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the heads of the fathers’ households of the priests and of the Levites; one fathers’ house being taken for Eleazar, and one taken for Ithamar.
Now the first lot come out to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,
the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim,
the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin,
the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,
the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,
the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,
the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab,
the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,
the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez,
the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,
the twenty-first to Jachin, the twenty-second to Gamul,
the twenty-third to Delaiah, and the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.
This was dem ordering in dem service, to come into Baba God’s house according to the ordinance given to dem by Aaron dem father, as Baba God, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
Of the rest of the sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shubael; of the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
Of Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah the chief.
Of the Izharites, Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
The sons of Hebron: Jeriah, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah; of the sons of Micah, Shamir.
The brother of Micah: Isshiah; of the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The son of Jaaziah: Beno.
The sons of Merari: of Jaaziah, Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
Of Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons.
Of Kish, the son of Kish: Jerahmeel.
The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites after dem fathers’ houses.

These likewise throw lots even as dem brothers the sons of Aaron in the presence of David the king, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the fathers’ households of the priests and of the Levites; the fathers’ households of the chief even as those of his younger brother.

Moreover, David and the captains of the army set apart for the service certain of the sons of Asaph, and of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who were to prophesy with harps, with stringed instruments, and with cymbals. The number of people wey did the work according to dem service was:
of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah. The sons of Asaph were under the hand of Asaph, who prophesied at the order of the king.

Of Jeduthun; the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six, under the hands of dem father Jeduthun, who prophesied in giving thanks and praising Baba God with the harp.
Of Heman; the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
All these were the sons of Heman the king’s seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn. God give to Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

All these were under the hands of dem father for song in Baba God’s house, with cymbals, stringed instruments, and harps, for the service of God’s house; Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman being under the order of the king.
The number of dem, with dem brothers who were instructed in singing to Baba God, even all who were skillful, was two hundred eighty-eight.
Dem throw lots for dem offices, all alike, the small as well as the great, the teacher as well as the student.
Now the first lot come out for Asaph to Joseph; the second to Gedaliah, he and his brothers and sons were twelve;
the third to Zaccur, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the fourth to Izri, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the fifth to Nethaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the sixth to Bukkiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the seventh to Jesharelah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the ninth to Mattaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the tenth to Shimei, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the eleventh to Azarel, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the thirteenth, Shubael, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the fourteenth, Mattithiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the fifteenth to Jeremoth, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the sixteenth to Hananiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the seventeenth to Joshbekashah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the eighteenth to Hanani, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the nineteenth to Mallothi, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the twentieth to Eliathah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the twenty-first to Hothir, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the twenty-second to Giddalti, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the twenty-third to Mahazioth, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the twenty-fourth to Romamti-Ezer, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
For the divisions of the doorkeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah the son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph.
Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, and Eliehoenai the seventh.
Obed-Edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sacar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, and Peullethai the eighth; for God blessed him.
Sons were also born to Shemaiah his son, who ruled over the house of dem father; for dem were mighty men of valor.
The sons of Shemaiah: Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad, whose brothers were valiant men, Elihu, and Semachiah.
All these were of the sons of Obed-Edom: dem and dem sons and dem brothers, able men in strength for the service; sixty-two of Obed-Edom.
Meshelemiah had sons and brothers, valiant men, eighteen.
Also Hosah, of the pikin dem of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief (for though he No be the firstborn, yet his father made him chief),
Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, and Zechariah the fourth: all the sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen.
