Of these were the divisions of the doorkeepers, even of the chief men, having offices like dem brothers, to minister in Baba God’s house.
Dem throw lots, the small as well as the great, according to dem fathers’ houses, for every gate.
The lot eastward fell to Shelemiah. Then for Zechariah his son, a wise counselor, dem throw lots; and his lot come out northward.
To Obed-Edom southward; and to his sons the storehouse.
To Shuppim and Hosah westward, by the gate of Shallecheth, at the causeway that goes up, watchman opposite watchman.
Eastward were six Levites, northward four a day, southward four a day, and for the storehouse two and two.
For Parbar westward, four at the causeway, and two at Parbar.
These were the divisions of the doorkeepers; of the sons of the Korahites, and of the sons of Merari.
Of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of God’s house and over the treasures of the dedicated things.
The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the fathers’ households belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
The sons of Jehieli: Zetham, and Joel his brother, over the treasures of Baba God’s house.
Of the Amramites, of the Izharites, of the Hebronites, of the Uzzielites:
and Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler over the treasures.
His brothers: of Eliezer, Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomoth his son.

This Shelomoth and his brothers were over all the treasures of the dedicated things, which David the king, and the heads of the fathers’ households, the captains over thousands and hundreds, and the captains of the army, had dedicated.
Dem dedicated some of the plunder won in battles to repair Baba God’s house.

All that Samuel the seer, and Saul the son of Kish, and Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah, had dedicated, Anybody wey had dedicated anything, it was under the hand of Shelomoth, and of his brothers.
Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were for the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges.

Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, men of valor, one thousand seven hundred, had the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan westward, for all the business of Baba God, and for the service of the king.

Of the Hebronites was Jerijah the chief, even of the Hebronites, according to dem generations by fathers’ households. Dem were sought for in the fortieth year of the reign of David, and mighty men of valor were find among dem at Jazer of Gilead.

His brothers, men of valor, were two thousand seven hundred, heads of fathers’ households, whom king David made overseers over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter pertaining to God, and for the affairs of the king.

Now the pikin dem of Israel after dem number, the heads of fathers’ households and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and dem officers who served the king, in any matter of the divisions which come in and go out month by month throughout all the months of the year — of every division were twenty-four thousand.
Over the first division for the first month was Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
He was of the pikin dem of Perez, the chief of all the captains of the army for the first month.
Over the division of the second month was Dodai the Ahohite, and his division; and Mikloth the ruler: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The third captain of the army for the third month was Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada the priest, chief: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
This is that Benaiah who was the mighty man of the thirty, and over the thirty: and of his division was Ammizabad his son.
The fourth captain for the fourth month was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The fifth captain for the fifth month was Shamhuth the Izrahite: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The sixth captain for the sixth month was Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The seventh captain for the seventh month was Helez the Pelonite, of the pikin dem of Ephraim: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The eighth captain for the eighth month was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The ninth captain for the ninth month was Abiezer the Anathothite, of the Benjamites: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The tenth captain for the tenth month was Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zerahites: and in his division were Twenty-four thousand.
The eleventh captain for the eleventh month was Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the pikin dem of Ephraim: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The twelfth captain for the twelfth month was Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
Furthermore over the tribes of Israel: of the Reubenites was Eliezer the son of Zichri the ruler; of the Simeonites, Shephatiah the son of Maacah;
of Levi, Hashabiah the son of Kemuel; of Aaron, Zadok;
of Judah, Elihu, one of the brothers of David; of Issachar, Omri the son of Michael;
of Zebulun, Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah; of Naphtali, Jeremoth the son of Azriel;
of the pikin dem of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Azaziah; of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Pedaiah;
of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo the son of Zechariah; of Benjamin, Jaasiel the son of Abner;
of Dan, Azarel the son of Jeroham. These were the captains of the tribes of Israel.
But David didn’t take the number of dem from twenty years old and under, because Baba God had talk say he would increase Israel like the stars of the sky.
Joab the son of Zeruiah began to take a census, but didn’t finish; and serious anger come on Israel for this. The number no be put into the account in the chronicles of king David.
Over the king’s treasures was Azmaveth the son of Adiel: and over the treasures in the fields, in the cities, and in the villages, and in the towers, was Jonathan the son of Uzziah;
Over people wey did the work of the field for tillage of the ground was Ezri the son of Chelub;
and over the vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite; and over the increase of the vineyards for the wine cellars was Zabdi the Shiphmite;
and over the olive trees and the sycamore trees that were in the lowland was Baal Hanan the Gederite; and over the cellars of oil was Joash;
and over the herds that fed in Sharon was Shitrai the Sharonite; and over the herds that were in the valleys was Shaphat the son of Adlai;
and over the camels was Obil the Ishmaelite; and over the donkeys was Jehdeiah the Meronothite; and over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite.
All these were the rulers of the property which was king David’s.
Also Jonathan, David’s uncle, was a counselor, a man of understanding, and a scribe; and Jehiel the son of Hachmoni was with the king’s sons.
Ahithophel was the king’s counselor: and Hushai the Archite was the king’s friend.
After Ahithophel was Jehoiada the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar. Joab was the captain of the king’s army.

David assembled all the princes of Israel, the princes of the tribes, the captains of the companies who served the king by division, the captains of thousands, the captains of hundreds, and the rulers over all the substance and possessions of the king and of his sons, with the officers and the mighty men, even all the mighty men of valor, to Jerusalem.

Then David the king stood up on his feet, and talk say, “Hear me, my brothers, and my people! As for me, it was in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of Baba God’s covenant, and for the footstool of our God; and I had prepared for the building.
But God talk say to me, ‘You no go build a house for my name, because You be a man of war, and have shed blood.’

However Baba God, the God of Israel, chose me out of all the house of my father to be king over Israel forever. For he has chosen Judah to be prince; and in the house of Judah, the house of my father; and among the sons of my father he take pleasure in me to make me king over all Israel.
Of all my sons (for Baba God has given me many sons), he has chosen Solomon my son to sit on the throne of Baba God’s kingdom over Israel.
He talk say to me, ‘Solomon, una son, shall build my house and my courts; for I have chosen him to be my son, and I go be his father.
I go establish his kingdom forever if he continues to do my commandments and my ordinances, as it is today.’

Now so, in the sight of all Israel, Baba God’s assembly, and in the audience of our God, observe and seek out all the commandments of Baba God una God; that you may possess this good land, and leave it for an inheritance to una pikin dem after you forever.

You, Solomon my son, know the God of una father, and serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind; for Baba God searches all hearts, and understands all the imaginations of the thoughts. If you seek him, he Go be find by you; but if you forsake him, he will throw you off forever.
Take heed now; for Baba God has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong, and do it.”
Then David give to Solomon his son the plans for the porch of the temple, for its houses, for its treasuries, for its upper rooms, for its inner rooms, for the place of the mercy seat;
and the plans of all that he had by the Spirit, for the courts of Baba God’s house, for all the surrounding rooms, for the treasuries of God’s house, and for the treasuries of the dedicated things;
also for the divisions of the priests and the Levites, for all the work of the service of Baba God’s house, and for all the vessels of service in Baba God’s house;
of gold by weight for the gold, for all vessels of every kind of service; for all the vessels of silver by weight, for all vessels of every kind of service;

by weight also for the lamp stands of gold, and for its lamps, of gold, by weight for every lamp stand and for its lamps; and for the lamp stands of silver, by weight for every lamp stand and for its lamps, according to the use of every lamp stand;
and the gold by weight for the tables of show bread, for every table; and silver for the tables of silver;
and the forks, the basins, and the cups, of pure gold; and for the golden bowls by weight for every bowl; and for the silver bowls by weight for every bowl;
and for the altar of incense refined gold by weight; and gold for the plans for the chariot, and the cherubim that spread out and cover the ark of Baba God’s covenant.
“All this”, talk say David, “I Don dey made to understand in writing from Baba God’s hand, even all the works of this pattern.”

David talk say to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. No fear, nor be dismayed; for Baba God, even my God, is with you. He No go fail you, nor forsake you, until all the work for the service of Baba God’s house is finished.

See am, E get the divisions of the priests and the Levites, for all the service of God’s house. Every willing man who has skill, for any kind of service, go be with you in all kinds of work. Also the captains and all the people Go be entirely at una command.”
David the king talk say to all the assembly, “Solomon my son, whom alone God has chosen, is yet young and tender, and the work is great; for the palace No be for man, but for Baba God.

Now I have prepared with all my might for the house of my God the gold for the things of gold, the silver for the things of silver, the brass for the things of brass, iron for the things of iron, and wood for the things of wood; also onyx stones, stones to be set, stones for inlaid work, of various colors, all kinds of precious stones, and marble stones in abundance.

In addition, because I have set my affection on the house of my God, since I have a treasure of my own of gold and silver, I give it to the house of my God, over and above all that I have prepared for the holy house,
even three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, with which to overlay the walls of the houses;

of gold for the things of gold, and of silver for the things of silver, and for all kinds of work to be made by the hands of artisans. Who then offers willingly to consecrate imself today to Baba God?”
Then the princes of the fathers’ households, and the princes of the tribes of Israel, and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, with the rulers over the king’s work, offered willingly;

and dem give for the service of God’s house of gold five thousand talents and ten thousand darics, of silver ten thousand talents, of brass eighteen thousand talents, and of iron one hundred thousand talents.
People with whom precious stones were find give dem to the treasure of Baba God’s house, under the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite.
Then the people rejoiced, because dem offered willingly, because with a perfect heart dem offered willingly to Baba God; and David the king also rejoiced with great gladness.
So David blessed Baba God before all the assembly; and David talk say, “You be blessed, Baba God, the God of Israel our father, forever and ever.

Yours, Baba God, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, and the majesty! For all that is in the heavens and in the earth is yours. Yours is the kingdom, Baba God, and You be exalted as head above all.
Both riches and honor come from you, and you rule over all! In una hand is power and might! It is in una hand to make great, and to give strength to all!
Now so, our God, we thank you, and praise una glorious name.
But who am I, and Wetin be my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly as this? For all things come from you, and of una own have we given you.
For We be strangers before you, and foreigners, as all our fathers were. Our days on the earth are as a shadow, and E get no remaining.
Baba God our God, all this store that we have prepared to build you a house for una holy name comes from una hand, and is all una own.

I know also, my God, that you try the heart, and have pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have willingly offered all these things. Now I have seen with gladness una people, Wey be present here, offer willingly to you.
Baba God, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Israel, our fathers, keep this desire forever in the thoughts of the heart of una people, and prepare dem heart for you;
and give to Solomon my son a perfect heart, to keep una commandments, una testimonies, and una statutes, and to do all these things, and to build the palace, for which I have made provision.”

Then David talk say to all the assembly, “Now bless Baba God una God!” All the assembly blessed Baba God, the God of dem fathers, and bowed down dem heads and prostrated themselves before Baba God and the king.

Dem sacrificed sacrifices to Baba God, and offered burnt offerings to Baba God, on the next day after that day, even one thousand bulls, one thousand rams, and one thousand lambs, with dem drink offerings and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel,
and ate and drank before Baba God on that day with great gladness. Dem made Solomon the son of David king the second time, and anointed him before Baba God to be prince, and Zadok to be priest.
Then Solomon sat on the throne of Baba God as king instead of David his father, and prospered; and all Israel obeyed him.
All the princes, the mighty men, and also all of the sons of king David submitted themselves to Solomon the king.
Baba God magnified Solomon exceedingly in the sight of all Israel, and give to him such royal majesty as had not been on any king before him in Israel.
Now David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
The time that he reigned over Israel was forty years; he reigned seven years in Hebron, and he reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
He died at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.
Now the acts of David the king, first and last, see am, Dem be written in the history of Samuel the seer, and in the history of Nathan the prophet, and in the history of Gad the seer,
with all his reign and his might, and the times that go over him, and over Israel, and over all the kingdoms of the countries.
Solomon the son of David was firmly established in his kingdom, and Baba God his God was with him, and made him exceedingly great.
Solomon spoke to all Israel, to the captains of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges, and to every prince in all Israel, the heads of the fathers’ households.
So Solomon, and all the assembly with him, go to the high place that was at Gibeon; for God’s Tent of Meeting was there, which Baba God’s worker Moses had made in the wilderness.
But David had bring God’s ark up from Kiriath Jearim to the place that David had prepared for it; for he had pitched a tent for it at Jerusalem.
Moreover the bronze altar that Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, had made was there before Baba God’s tabernacle; and Solomon and the assembly were seeking counsel there.
Solomon go up there to the bronze altar before Baba God, which was at the Tent of Meeting, and offered one thousand burnt offerings on it.
That night, God appeared to Solomon and talk say to him, “Ask for Wetin you want me to give you.”
Solomon talk say to God, “You have shown great loving kindness to David my father, and have made me king in his place.
Now, Baba God, let una promise to David my father be established; for you have made me king over a people like the dust of the earth in plenty people.
Now give me wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people; for who can judge this great people of yours?”

God talk say to Solomon, “Because this was in una heart, and you have not ask riches, wealth, honor, or the life of people wey hate you, nor yet have you ask for long life; but have ask for wisdom and knowledge for yourself, that you may judge my people, over whom I have made you king,
so wisdom and knowledge is granted to you. I go give you riches, wealth, and honor, such as none of the kings have had who Don dey before you had, and none after You go have.”
So Solomon come from the high place that was at Gibeon, from before the Tent of Meeting, to Jerusalem; and he reigned over Israel.
Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen that he placed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem.
The king made silver and gold to be as common as stones in Jerusalem, and he made cedars to be as common as the sycamore trees that are in the lowland.
The horses which Solomon had were bring out of Egypt and from Kue. The king’s merchants purchased dem from Kue.
Dem bring up and bring out of Egypt a chariot for six hundred pieces of silver, and a horse for one hundred fifty. Dem also exported dem to the Hittite kings and the Syrian kings.
Now Solomon decided to build a house for Baba God’s name, and a house for his kingdom.
Solomon counted out seventy thousand men to bear burdens, eighty thousand men who were stone cutters in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred to oversee dem.
Solomon sent to Huram the king of Tyre, saying, “As you dealt with David my father, and sent him cedars to build him a house in which to live, so deal with me.

See am, I be about to build a house for the name of Baba God my God, to dedicate it to him, to burn before him incense of sweet spices, for the continual show bread, and for the burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, and on the set feasts of Baba God our God. This is an ordinance forever to Israel.
“The house which I be building Go be great; for our God is greater than all gods.
But Wey be able to build him a house, since heaven and the heaven of heavens no fit contain him? Who am I then, that I should build him a house, except just to burn incense before him?

“Now so send me a man skillful to work in gold, in silver, in brass, in iron, and in purple, crimson, and blue, and wey know how to engrave engravings, to be with the skillful men Wey be with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom David my father provided.
“Send me also cedar trees, cypress trees, and algum trees out of Lebanon; for I know that una workers know how to cut timber in Lebanon. See am, my workers Go be with una workers,
even to prepare me timber in abundance; for the house which I be about to build Go be great and wonderful.
See am, I go give to una workers, the cutters who cut timber, twenty thousand cors of beaten wheat, twenty thousand baths of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil.”
Then Huram the king of Tyre answer in writing, which he sent to Solomon, “Because Baba God loves his people, he has made you king over dem.”

Huram continued, “Blessed be Baba God, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who has given to David the king a wise son, endowed with discretion and understanding, who would build a house for Baba God, and a house for his kingdom.
Now I have sent a skillful man, endowed with understanding, of Huram my father’s,

the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan; and his father was a man of Tyre, skillful to work in gold, in silver, in brass, in iron, in stone, in timber, and in purple, in blue, in fine linen, and in crimson, also to engrave any kind of engraving and to devise any device; that there may be a place appointed to him with una skillful men, and with the skillful men of my lord David una father.
“Now so the wheat the barley, the oil and the wine, which my lord has spoken of, Make e send to his workers;
and We go cut wood out of Lebanon, as much as you need. We go bring it to you in floats by sea to Joppa; and you shall carry it up to Jerusalem.”
Solomon counted all the foreigners who were in the land of Israel, after the census with which David his father had counted dem; and dem find one hundred fifty-three thousand six hundred.
He set seventy thousand of dem to bear burdens, eighty thousand who were stone cutters in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred overseers to assign the people dem work.

Then Solomon began to build Baba God’s house at Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where Baba God appeared to David his father, which he prepared in the place that David had appointed, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
He began to build in the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.
Now these are the foundations which Solomon laid for the building of God’s house. The length by cubits after the first measure was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.
The porch that was in front, its length, according to the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and the height one hundred twenty; and he overlaid it within with pure gold.
He made the larger room with a ceiling of cypress wood, which he overlaid with fine gold, and ornamented it with palm trees and chains.
He decorated the house with precious stones for beauty. The gold was gold from Parvaim.
He also overlaid the house, the beams, the thresholds, its walls, and its doors with gold; and engraved cherubim on the walls.
He made the most holy place. Its length, according to the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and its width twenty cubits; and he overlaid it with fine gold, amounting to six hundred talents.
The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper rooms with gold.
In the most holy place he made two cherubim by carving; and dem overlaid dem with gold.

The wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits long: the wing of the one was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house; and the other wing was five cubits, reaching to the wing of the other cherub.
The wing of the other cherub was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house; and the other wing was five cubits, joining to the wing of the other cherub.
The wings of these cherubim spread themselves out twenty cubits. Dem stood on dem feet, and dem faces were toward the house.
He made the veil of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen, and ornamented it with cherubim.
Also he made before the house two pillars of thirty-five cubits height, and the capital that was on the top of each of dem was five cubits.
He made chains in the inner sanctuary, and put dem on the tops of the pillars; and he made one hundred pomegranates, and put dem on the chains.
He set up the pillars before the temple, one on the right hand, and the other on the left; and call the name of that on the right hand Jachin, and the name of that on the left Boaz.
Then he made an altar of brass, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
Also he made the molten sea of ten cubits from brim to brim. It was round, five cubits high, and thirty cubits in circumference.
Under it was the likeness of oxen, which encircled it, for ten cubits, encircling the sea. The oxen were in two rows, throw when it was throw.

It stood on twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east; and the sea was set on dem above, and all dem hindquarters were inward.
It was a handbreadth thick; and its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It received and held three thousand baths.

He also made ten basins, and put five on the right hand, and five on the left, to wash in dem. The things that belonged to the burnt offering were washed in dem; but the sea was for the priests to wash in.
He made the ten lamp stands of gold according to the ordinance concerning dem; and he set dem in the temple, five on the right hand, and five on the left.
He made also ten tables, and placed dem in the temple, five on the right side, and five on the left. He made one hundred basins of gold.
Furthermore he made the court of the priests, the great court, and doors for the court, and overlaid dem doors with brass.
He set the sea on the right side of the house eastward, toward the south.
Huram made the pots, the shovels, and the basins. So Huram finished doing the work that he did for king Solomon in God’s house:
the two pillars, the bowls, the two capitals which were on the top of the pillars, the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars,
and the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks; two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the pillars.
He also made the bases, and he made the basins on the bases;
one sea, and the twelve oxen under it.
Huram his father also made the pots, the shovels, the forks, and all its vessels for king Solomon, for Baba God’s house, of bright brass.
The king throw dem in the plain of the Jordan, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.
Thus Solomon made all these vessels in great abundance; for the weight of the brass could not be determined.
Solomon made all the vessels that were in God’s house, the golden altar also, and the tables with the show bread on dem;
and the lamp stands with dem lamps, to burn according to the ordinance before the inner sanctuary, of pure gold;
and the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs of gold that was perfect gold;

and the snuffers, the basins, the spoons, and the fire pans of pure gold. As for the entry of the house, its inner doors for the most holy place and the doors of the main hall of the temple were of gold.

Thus all the work that Solomon did for Baba God’s house was finished. Solomon bring in the things that David his father had dedicated, even the silver, the gold, and all the vessels, and put dem in the treasuries of God’s house.

Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the princes of the fathers’ households of the pikin dem of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of Baba God’s covenant out of David’s city, which is Zion.
So all the men of Israel assembled themselves to the king at the feast, which was in the seventh month.
All the elders of Israel come. The Levites take up the ark;
and dem bring up the ark, the Tent of Meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the Tent; these the priests the Levites bring up.
King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel, who were assembled to him, were before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle that could not be counted or counted for plenty people.
The priests bring in the ark of Baba God’s covenant to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, to the most holy place, even under the wings of the cherubim.
For the cherubim spread out dem wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its poles above.
The poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the ark in front of the inner sanctuary; but dem No be seen outside; and it is there to this day.
There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets which Moses put at Horeb, when Baba God made a covenant with the pikin dem of Israel, when dem come out of Egypt.
When the priests had come out of the holy place (for all the priests who were present had sanctified themselves, and didn’t keep dem divisions;

also the Levites who were the singers, all of dem, even Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and dem sons and dem brothers, arrayed in fine linen, with cymbals and stringed instruments and harps, stood at the east end of the altar, and with dem one hundred twenty priests sounding with trumpets);

when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking Baba God; and when dem lifted up dem voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praised Baba God, saying, “For he is good; for his loving kindness endures forever!” then the house was filled with a cloud, even Baba God’s house,
so that the priests could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud; for Baba God’s glory filled God’s house.
Then Solomon talk say, “Baba God has talk say that he would live in the thick darkness.
But I have built you a house and home, a place for you to live in forever.”
The king turned his face, and blessed all the assembly of Israel: and all the assembly of Israel stood.
He talk say, “Blessed be Baba God, the God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth to David my father, and has with his hands fulfilled it, saying,

‘Since the day that I bring my people out of the land of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel to build a house in, that my name might be there and I chose no man to be prince over my people Israel;
but now I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name might be there; and I have chosen David to be over my people Israel.’
Now it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of Baba God, the God of Israel.
But Baba God talk say to David my father, ‘Whereas it was in una heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in una heart;
nevertheless you no go build the house; but una son who will come out of una body, he shall build the house for my name.’

“Baba God has performed his word that he spoke; for I have risen up in the place of David my father, and sit on the throne of Israel, as Baba God promised, and have built the house for the name of Baba God, the God of Israel.
There I have set the ark, in which is Baba God’s covenant, which he made with the pikin dem of Israel.”
He stood before Baba God’s altar in the presence of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands

(for Solomon had made a bronze scaffold, five cubits long, and five cubits wide, and three cubits high, and had set it in the middle of the court; and he stood on it, and knelt down on his knees before all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward heaven)
and he talk say, “Baba God, the God of Israel, E get no God like you in heaven or on earth; you who keep covenant and loving kindness with una workers who walk before you with all dem heart;
who have kept with una worker David my father that which you promised him. Yes, you spoke with una mouth, and have fulfilled it with una hand, as it is today.

“Now so, Baba God, the God of Israel, keep with una worker David my father that which you have promised him, saying, ‘There no go fail you a man in my sight to sit on the throne of Israel, if only una pikin dem take heed to dem way, to walk in my law as you have walked before me.’
Now so, Baba God, the God of Israel, let una word be verified, which you spoke to una worker David.
“But will God indeed live with men on the earth? See am, heaven and the heaven of heavens no fit contain you; how much less this house which I have built!
Yet have respect for the prayer of una worker, and to his supplication, Baba God my God, to listen to the cry and to the prayer which una worker prays before you;

that una eyes may be open toward this house day and night, even toward the place where you have talk say that you would put una name; to listen to the prayer which una worker will pray toward this place.
Listen to the petitions of una worker, and of una people Israel, when dem pray toward this place. Yes, hear from una dwelling place, even from heaven; and when you hear, forgive.
“If a man sins against his neighbor, and an oath is laid on him to cause him to swear, and he comes and swears before una altar in this house;
then hear from heaven, act, and judge una workers, bringing retribution to the wicked, to bring his way on his own head; and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.
“If una people Israel are struck down before the enemy because dem have sinned against you, and dem turn again and confess una name, and pray and make supplication before you in this house;
then hear from heaven, and forgive the sin of una people Israel, and bring dem again to the land which you give to dem and to dem fathers.
“When the sky is shut up, and E get no rain, because dem have sinned against you; if dem pray toward this place, and confess una name, and turn from dem sin, when you afflict dem;

then hear in heaven, and forgive the sin of una workers of una people Israel, when you teach dem the good way in which dem should walk; and send rain on una land, which you have given to una people for an inheritance.

“If E get famine in the land, if E get pestilence, if E get blight or mildew, locust or caterpillar; if dem enemies besiege dem in the land of dem cities; Anything wey plague or Anything wey sickness E get;
Anything wey prayer and supplication is made by any man, or by all una people Israel, who will each know his own plague and his own sorrow, and shall spread out his hands toward this house;
then hear from heaven una dwelling place and forgive, and render to every man according to all his ways, whose heart you know (for you, even you only, know the hearts of the pikin dem of men)
that dem may fear you, to walk in una ways, so long as dem live in the land which you give to our fathers.

“Moreover concerning the foreigner, Wey be not of una people Israel, when he comes from a far country for una great name’s sake, and una mighty hand, and una outstretched arm; when dem come and pray toward this house;

then hear from heaven, even from una dwelling place, and do according to all that the foreigner calls to you for; that all the peoples of the earth may know una name and fear you, as do una people Israel, and that dem may know that this house which I have built is call by una name.
“If una people go out to battle against dem enemies, by Anything wey way you send dem, and dem pray to you toward this city which you have chosen, and the house which I have built for una name;
then hear from heaven dem prayer and dem supplication, and maintain dem cause.
“If dem sin against you (for E get no man who no dey sin), and You be angry with dem, and deliver dem to the enemy, so that dem carry dem away captive to a land far off or near;

yet if dem come to dem senses in the land where Dem be carried captive, and turn again, and make supplication to you in the land of dem captivity, saying, ‘We have sinned, we have done perversely, and have dealt wickedly;’

if dem return to you with all dem heart and with all dem soul in the land of dem captivity, where dem have carried dem captive, and pray toward dem land, which you give to dem fathers, and the city which you have chosen, and toward the house which I have built for una name;
then hear from heaven, even from una dwelling place, dem prayer and dem petitions, and maintain dem cause, and forgive una people who have sinned against you.
“Now, my God, let, I beg you, una eyes be open, and let una ears be attentive, to the prayer that is made in this place.
“Now so arise, Baba God, into una resting place, you, and the ark of una strength. Let una priests, Baba God, be clothed with salvation, and let una saints glad well-well in goodness.
“Baba God, no turn away the face of una anointed. Remember una loving kindnesses to David una worker.”
Now when Solomon had finished praying, fire come down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices; and Baba God’s glory filled the house.
The priests could not enter into Baba God’s house, because Baba God’s glory filled Baba God’s house.

All the pikin dem of Israel looked on, when the fire come down, and Baba God’s glory was on the house. Dem bowed themselves with dem faces to the ground on the pavement, worshiped, and Thank God to Baba God, saying, “For he is good; for his loving kindness endures for ever.”
Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before Baba God.
King Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty-two thousand head of cattle and a hundred twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the people dedicated God’s house.

The priests stood, according to dem positions; the Levites also with instruments of music of Baba God, which David the king had made to Thank God to Baba God, when David praised by dem ministry, saying “For his loving kindness endures for ever.” The priests sounded trumpets before dem; and all Israel stood.

Moreover Solomon made the middle of the court that was before Baba God’s house holy; for there he offered the burnt offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar which Solomon had made No be able to receive the burnt offering, the meal offering, and the fat.
So Solomon held the feast at that time for seven days, and all Israel with him, a plenty well-well assembly, from the entrance of Hamath to the brook of Egypt.
On the eighth day, dem held a solemn assembly; for dem kept the dedication of the altar seven days, and the feast seven days.

On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, he sent the people away to dem tents, joyful and glad of heart for the goodness that Baba God had shown to David, and to Solomon, and to Israel his people.
Thus Solomon finished Baba God’s house and the king’s house; and he successfully completed all that come into Solomon’s heart to make in Baba God’s house and in his own house.
Baba God appeared to Solomon by night, and talk say to him, “I have heard una prayer, and have chosen this place for myself for a house of sacrifice.
“If I shut up the sky so that E get no rain, or if I command the locust to devour the land, or if I send pestilence among my people;
if my people, Wey be call by my name, will humble themselves, pray, seek my face, and turn from dem wicked ways; then I go hear from heaven, will forgive dem sin, and will heal dem land.
Now my eyes Go be open my ears attentive to prayer that is made in this place.
For now I have chosen and made this house holy, that my name may be there forever; and my eyes and my heart Go be there perpetually.
“As for you, if You go walk before me as David una father walked, and do according to all that I have commanded you, and will keep my statutes and my ordinances;
then I go establish the throne of una kingdom, according as I covenanted with David una father, saying, ‘There no go fail you a man to be ruler in Israel.’
But if you turn away, and forsake my statutes and my commandments which I have set before you, and shall go and serve other gods, and worship dem;

then I go pluck dem up by the roots out of my land which I have given dem; and this house, which I have made holy for my name, I go throw out of my sight, and I go make it a proverb and a byword among all peoples.
This house, which is so high, Everybody wey passes by it go be astonished, and shall say, ‘Why has Baba God done this to this land and to this house?’

Dem shall answer, ‘Because dem abandoned Baba God, the God of dem fathers, who bring dem out of the land of Egypt, and take other gods, worshiped dem, and served dem. So he has bring all this evil on dem.’”
At the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built Baba God’s house and his own house,
Solomon built the cities which Huram had given to Solomon, and caused the pikin dem of Israel to live there.
Solomon go to Hamath Zobah, and prevailed against it.
He built Tadmor in the wilderness, and all the storage cities, which he built in Hamath.
Also he built Beth Horon the upper and Beth Horon the lower, fortified cities, with walls, gates, and bars;

and Baalath, and all the storage cities that Solomon had, and all the cities for his chariots, the cities for his horsemen, and all that Solomon desired to build for his pleasure in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.
As for all the people who were left of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who No be of Israel;
of dem pikin dem who were left after dem in the land, whom the pikin dem of Israel didn’t consume, of dem Solomon conscripted forced labor to this day.
But of the pikin dem of Israel, Solomon made no workers for his work; but dem were men of war, and chief of his captains, and rulers of his chariots and of his horsemen.
These were the chief officers of king Solomon, even two-hundred fifty, who ruled over the people.

Solomon bring up Pharaoh’s daughter out of David’s city to the house that he had built for her; for he talk say, “My wife no go live in the house of David king of Israel, because the places where Baba God’s ark has come are holy.”
Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to Baba God on Baba God’s altar, which he had built before the porch,

even as the duty of every day required, offering according to the commandment of Moses, on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, and on the set feasts, three times per year, during the feast of unleavened bread, during the feast of weeks, and during the feast of tents.

He appointed, according to the ordinance of David his father, the divisions of the priests to dem service, and the Levites to dem offices, to praise and to minister before the priests, as the duty of every day required; the doorkeepers also by dem divisions at every gate, for David the man of God had so commanded.
Dem didn’t depart from the commandment of the king to the priests and Levites concerning any matter, or concerning the treasures.
Now all the work of Solomon was prepared from the day of the foundation of Baba God’s house until it was finished. So Baba God’s house was completed.
Then Solomon go to Ezion Geber and to Eloth, on the seashore in the land of Edom.

Huram sent him ships and workers who had knowledge of the sea by the hands of his workers; and dem come with the workers of Solomon to Ophir, and bring from there four hundred fifty talents of gold, and bring dem to king Solomon.

When the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she come to test Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a plenty well-well caravan, including camels that bore spices, gold in abundance, and precious stones. When she had come to Solomon, she talked with him about all that was in her heart.
Solomon answer all her questions. There no be anything hidden from Solomon which he didn’t tell her.
When the queen of Sheba had seen the wisdom of Solomon, the house that he had built,

the chop of his table, the seating of his workers, the attendance of his ministers, dem clothing, his cup bearers also, dem clothing, and his ascent by which he go up to Baba God’s house; there was no more spirit in her.
She talk say to the king, “It was a true report that I heard in my own land of una acts and of una wisdom.
However I didn’t believe dem words until I come, and my eyes had seen it; and see am, the half of the greatness of una wisdom No be told me. You exceed the fame that I heard!
Happy are una men, and happy are these una workers, who stand continually before you, and hear una wisdom.

Blessed be Baba God una God, who delighted in you, to set you on his throne, to be king for Baba God una God; because una God love Israel, to establish dem forever. So made he you king over dem, to do justice and righteousness.”
She give the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold, spices in great abundance, and precious stones. There was never before such spice as the queen of Sheba give to king Solomon.
The workers of Huram and the workers of Solomon, who bring gold from Ophir, also bring algum trees and precious stones.

The king used algum tree wood to make terraces for Baba God’s house and for the king’s house, and harps and stringed instruments for the singers. There were none like these seen before in the land of Judah.
King Solomon give to the queen of Sheba all her desire, Anything wey she ask, besides that which she had bring to the king. So she turned, and go to her own land, she and her workers.
Now the weight of gold that come to Solomon in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents of gold,
besides that which the traders and merchants bring. All the kings of Arabia and the governors of the country bring gold and silver to Solomon.
King Solomon made two hundred bucklers of beaten gold. Six hundred shekels of beaten gold go to one buckler.
He made three hundred shields of beaten gold. Three hundred shekels of gold go to one shield. The king put dem in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with pure gold.
There were six steps to the throne, with a footstool of gold, which were fastened to the throne, and armrests on either side by the place of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests.
Twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other on the six steps. There was nothing like it made in any other kingdom.
All king Solomon’s drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were of pure gold. Silver No be considered valuable in the days of Solomon.
For the king had ships that go to Tarshish with Huram’s workers. Once every three years, the ships of Tarshish come bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
All the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
Dem each bring tribute, vessels of silver, vessels of gold, clothing, armor, spices, horses, and mules every year.
Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, that he stationed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem.
He ruled over all the kings from the River even to the land of the Philistines, and to the border of Egypt.
The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedars to be as abundant as the sycamore trees that are in the lowland.
Dem bring horses for Solomon out of Egypt and out of all lands.

Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, no be dem written in the history of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam the son of Nebat?
Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.
Solomon slept with his fathers, and he was buried in his father David’s city: and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.
Rehoboam go to Shechem; for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
When Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard of it (for he was in Egypt, where he had fled from the presence of king Solomon), Jeroboam come back out of Egypt.
Dem sent and call him; and Jeroboam and all Israel come, and dem spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
“Una father made our yoke grievous: now so make the grievous service of una father, and his heavy yoke which he put on us, lighter, and We go serve you.”
E tell dem say, “Come again to me after three days.” So the people comot.
King Rehoboam take counsel with the old men, who had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, “What counsel do you give me about how to answer these people?”
Dem spoke to him, saying, “If You be kind to these people, please dem, and speak good words to dem, then Dem go be una workers forever.”
But he abandoned the counsel of the old men which dem had given him, and take counsel with the young men who had grown up with him, who stood before him.
E tell dem say, “What counsel do you give, that we may give an answer to these people, who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Make the yoke that una father put on us lighter?’”

The young men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, “Thus you shall tell the people who spoke to you, saying, ‘Una father made our yoke heavy, but make it lighter on us;’ thus you shall say to dem, ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist.
Now whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I go add to una yoke. My father chastised you with whips, but I go chastise you with scorpions.’”
So Jeroboam and all the people come to Rehoboam the third day, as the king ask, saying, “Come to me again the third day.”
The king answer dem roughly; and king Rehoboam abandoned the counsel of the old men,
and spoke to dem after the counsel of the young men, saying, “My father made una yoke heavy, but I go add to it. My father chastised you with whips, but I go chastise you with scorpions.”
So the king didn’t listen to the people; for it was bring about by God, that Baba God might establish his word, which he spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

When all Israel see that the king didn’t listen to dem, the people answer the king, saying, “What portion have we in David? We no have an inheritance in the son of Jesse! Every man to una tents, Israel! Now see to una own house, David.” So all Israel comot to dem tents.
But as for the pikin dem of Israel who lived in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over dem.

Then king Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was over the men subject to forced labor; and the pikin dem of Israel stoned him to death with stones. King Rehoboam hurried to get imself up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.
So Israel rebelled against David’s house to this day.

When Rehoboam had come to Jerusalem, he assembled the house of Judah and Benjamin, one hundred eighty thousand chosen men who were warriors, to fight against Israel, to bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam.
But Baba God’s word come to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
“Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin, saying,

‘Baba God says, “You no go go up, nor fight against una brothers! Every man return to his house; for this thing is of me.”’” So dem listened to Baba God’s words, and come back from going against Jeroboam.
Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem, and built cities for defense in Judah.
He built Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,
Beth Zur, Soco, Adullam,
Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,
Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah,
Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron, which are fortified cities in Judah and in Benjamin.
He fortified the strongholds, and put captains in dem, and stores of chop, oil and wine.
He put shields and spears in every city, and made dem exceedingly strong. Judah and Benjamin belonged to him.
The priests and the Levites who were in all Israel stood with him out of all dem territory.
For the Levites left dem suburbs and dem possession, and come to Judah and Jerusalem; for Jeroboam and his sons throw dem off, that dem no suppose execute the priest’s office to Baba God.
He imself appointed priests for the high places, for the male goats, and for the calves which he had made.
After dem, out of all the tribes of Israel, people wey set dem hearts to seek Baba God, the God of Israel, come to Jerusalem to sacrifice to Baba God, the God of dem fathers.
So dem strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and made Rehoboam the son of Solomon strong for three years; for dem walked three years in the way of David and Solomon.
Rehoboam take a wife for imself, Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David and of Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse.
She bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
After her, he take Maacah the daughter of Absalom; and she bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
Rehoboam love Maacah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines; for he take eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and became the father of twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
Rehoboam appointed Abijah the son of Maacah to be chief, the prince among his brothers; for he intended to make him king.
He dealt wisely, and dispersed of all his sons throughout all the lands of Judah and Benjamin, to every fortified city. He give dem chop in abundance and he sought many wives for dem.
When the kingdom of Rehoboam was established and he was strong, he abandoned Baba God’s law, and all Israel with him.
In the fifth year of king Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt come up against Jerusalem, because dem had trespassed against Baba God,
with twelve hundred chariots, and sixty thousand horsemen. The people were without number who come with him out of Egypt: the Lubim, the Sukkiim, and the Ethiopians.
He take the fortified cities which belonged to Judah, and come to Jerusalem.

Now Shemaiah the prophet come to Rehoboam, and to the princes of Judah, who were gathered together to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and talk say to dem, “Baba God says, ‘You have forsaken me, so I have also left you in the hand of Shishak.’”
Then the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves; and dem talk say, “Baba God is righteous.”

When Baba God see that dem humbled themselves, Baba God’s word come to Shemaiah, saying, “Dem have humbled themselves. I go not destroy dem; but I go grant dem some deliverance, and my serious anger no go be poured out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
Nevertheless Dem go be his workers, that dem may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.”

So Shishak king of Egypt come up against Jerusalem and take away the treasures of Baba God’s house and the treasures of the king’s house. He take it all away. He also take away the shields of gold which Solomon had made.
King Rehoboam made shields of brass in dem place, and committed dem to the hands of the captains of the guard, who kept the door of the king’s house.
As often as the king entered into Baba God’s house, the guard come and bore dem, then bring dem back into the guard room.
When he humbled imself, Baba God’s serious anger turned from him, so as not to destroy him altogether. Moreover, there were good things find in Judah.

So king Rehoboam strengthened imself in Jerusalem and reigned; for Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which Baba God had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonitess.
He did that which was evil, because he didn’t set his heart to seek Baba God.

Now the acts of Rehoboam, first and last, no be dem written in the histories of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, in the genealogies? There were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried in David’s city; and Abijah his son reigned in his place.
In the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam, Abijah began to reign over Judah.
He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

Abijah joined battle with an army of valiant men of war, even four hundred thousand chosen men; and Jeroboam set the battle in array against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, who were mighty men of valor.
Abijah stood up on Mount Zemaraim, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and talk say, “Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel:
Ought you not to know that Baba God, the God of Israel, give the kingdom over Israel to David forever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
Yet Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the worker of Solomon the son of David, rose up, and rebelled against his lord.
Worthless men were gathered to him, base fellows who strengthened themselves against Rehoboam the son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and tender hearted, and could not withstand dem.
“Now you intend to withstand the kingdom of Baba God in the hand of the sons of David. You be Plenty people, and the golden calves which Jeroboam made you for gods are with you.

Haven’t you driven out the priests of Baba God, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made priests for unaself according to the ways of the peoples of other lands? Anybody wey comes to consecrate imself with a young bull and seven rams may be a priest of people Wey no gods.
“But as for us, Baba God is our God, and we have not forsaken him. We have priests serving Baba God, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites in dem work;

and dem burn to Baba God every morning and every evening burnt offerings and sweet incense. Dem also set the show bread in order on the pure table; and the lamp stand of gold with its lamps, to burn every evening; for we keep the instruction of Baba God our God, but you have forsaken him.

See am, God is with us at our head, and his priests with the trumpets of alarm to sound an alarm against you. Pikin dem of Israel, no fight against Baba God, the God of una fathers; for You go not prosper.”
But Jeroboam caused an ambush to come about behind dem; so dem were before Judah, and the ambush was behind dem.
When Judah looked back, see am, the battle was before and behind dem; and dem cried to Baba God, and the priests sounded with the trumpets.
Then the men of Judah give a shout. As the men of Judah shouted, God struck Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
The pikin dem of Israel fled before Judah, and God delivered dem into dem hand.
Abijah and his people killed dem with a great slaughter, so five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell down slain.
Thus the pikin dem of Israel were bring under at that time, and the pikin dem of Judah prevailed, because dem relied on Baba God, the God of dem fathers.
Abijah pursued Jeroboam, and take cities from him, Bethel with its villages, Jeshanah with its villages, and Ephron with its villages.
Jeroboam didn’t recover strength again in the days of Abijah. Baba God struck him, and he died.
But Abijah grew mighty, and take for imself fourteen wives, and became the father of twenty-two sons, and sixteen daughters.
The rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways, and his sayings are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo.
So Abijah slept with his fathers, and dem buried him in David’s city; and Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days, the land was quiet ten years.
Asa did that which was good and right in Baba God his God’s eyes;
for he take away the foreign altars and the high places, broke down the pillars, cut down the Asherah poles,
and commanded Judah to seek Baba God, the God of dem fathers, and to obey his law and command.
Also he take away out of all the cities of Judah the high places and the sun images; and the kingdom was quiet before him.
He built fortified cities in Judah; for the land was quiet, and he had no war in those years, because Baba God had given him rest.

For he talk say to Judah, “Make we build these cities, and make walls around dem, with towers, gates, and bars. The land is yet before us, because we have sought Baba God our God. We have sought him, and he has given us rest on every side.” So dem built and prospered.

Asa had an army of three hundred thousand out of Judah who bore bucklers and spears, and two hundred eighty thousand out of Benjamin who bore shields and drew bows. All these were mighty men of valor.
Zerah the Ethiopian come out against dem with an army of a million troops and three hundred chariots, and he come to Mareshah.
Then Asa go out to meet him, and dem set the battle in array in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

Asa cried to Baba God his God, and talk say, “Baba God, E get Nobody besides you to help, between the mighty and him who has no strength. Help us, Baba God our God; for we rely on you, and in una name are we come against this plenty people. Baba God, You be our God. No let man prevail against you.”
So Baba God struck the Ethiopians before Asa and before Judah; and the Ethiopians fled.

Asa and the people who were with him pursued dem to Gerar: and so many of the Ethiopians fell that dem could not recover themselves; for dem were destroyed before Baba God and before his army; and dem carried away well-well booty.
Dem struck all the cities around Gerar; for the fear of Baba God come on dem, and dem plundered all the cities; for there was much plunder in dem.
Dem also struck the tents of livestock, and carried away sheep in abundance, and camels, and come back to Jerusalem.
The Spirit of God come on Azariah the son of Oded:

and he go out to meet Asa, and talk say to him, “Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin! Baba God is with you, while You be with him; and if you seek him, he Go be find by you; but if you forsake him, he will forsake you.
Now for a long time Israel was without the true God, without a teaching priest, and without law.
But when in dem distress dem turned to Baba God, the God of Israel, and sought him, he was find by dem.
In those times there was no peace to him who go out, nor to him who come in; but great troubles were on all the inhabitants of the lands.
Dem were broken in pieces, nation against nation, and city against city; for God troubled dem with all adversity.
But you be strong, and no let una hands be slack; for una work Go be rewarded.”

When Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he take courage, and put away the abominations out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from the hill country of Ephraim; and he renewed Baba God’s altar that was before Baba God’s porch.
He gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and people wey lived with dem out of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon; for dem come to him out of Israel in abundance when dem see that Baba God his God was with him.
So dem gathered themselves together at Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of Asa’s reign.
Dem sacrificed to Baba God in that day, of the plunder which dem had bring, seven hundred head of cattle and seven thousand sheep.
Dem entered into the covenant to seek Baba God, the God of dem fathers, with all dem heart and with all dem soul;
and that Anybody wey would not seek Baba God, the God of Israel, should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman.
Dem swore to Baba God with a loud voice, with shouting, with trumpets, and with cornets.
All Judah rejoiced at the oath, for dem had sworn with all dem heart, and sought him with dem whole desire; and he was find by dem. Then Baba God give dem rest all around.

Also Maacah, the mother of Asa the king, he removed from being queen, because she had made an abominable image for an Asherah; so Asa cut down her image, ground it into dust, and burned it at the brook Kidron.
But the high places No be taken away out of Israel; nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect all his days.
He bring the things that his father had dedicated, and that he imself had dedicated, silver, gold, and vessels into God’s house.
There was no more war to the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.
In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, Baasha king of Israel go up against Judah, and built Ramah, that he might not allow anyone to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
Then Asa bring out silver and gold out of the treasures of Baba God’s house and of the king’s house, and sent to Ben Hadad king of Syria, who lived at Damascus, saying,

“Let there be a treaty between me and you, as there was between my father and una father. See am, I have sent you silver and gold. Go, break una treaty with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.”
Ben Hadad listened to king Asa, and sent the captains of his armies against the cities of Israel; and dem struck Ijon, Dan, Abel Maim, and all the storage cities of Naphtali.
When Baasha heard of it, he stopped building Ramah, and let his work cease.
Then Asa the king take all Judah, and dem carried away the stones of Rama, and its timber, with which Baasha had built; and he built Geba and Mizpah with dem.

At that time Hanani the seer come to Asa king of Judah, and talk say to him, “Because you have relied on the king of Syria, and have not relied on Baba God una God, so the army of the king of Syria has escaped out of una hand.
No be the Ethiopians and the Lubim a huge army, with chariots and horsemen exceeding many? Yet, because you relied on Baba God, he delivered dem into una hand.

For Baba God’s eyes run back and forth throughout the whole earth, to show imself strong in the behalf of dem whose heart is perfect toward him. You have done foolishly in this; for from now on You go have wars.”
Then Asa was angry with the seer, and put him in the prison; for he was in a rage with him because of this thing. Asa oppressed some of the people at the same time.
See am, the acts of Asa, first and last, see am, Dem be written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa was diseased in his feet. His disease was exceedingly great: yet in his disease he didn’t seek Baba God, but just the physicians.
Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the forty-first year of his reign.

Dem buried him in his own tomb, which he had dug out for imself in David’s city, and laid him in the bed which was filled with sweet odors and various kinds of spices prepared by the perfumers’ art; and dem made a plenty well-well fire for him.
Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place, and strengthened imself against Israel.
He placed forces in all the fortified cities of Judah, and set garrisons in the land of Judah, and in the cities of Ephraim, which Asa his father had taken.
Baba God was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the first ways of his father David, and didn’t seek the Baals,
but sought to the God of his father, and walked in his commandments, and not in the ways of Israel.
So Baba God established the kingdom in his hand. All Judah bring tribute to Jehoshaphat, and he had riches and honor in abundance.
His heart was lifted up in the ways of Baba God. Furthermore, he take away the high places and the Asherah poles out of Judah.
Also in the third year of his reign he sent his princes, even Ben Hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah, to teach in the cities of Judah;
and with dem the Levites, even Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tobadonijah, the Levites; and with dem Elishama and Jehoram, the priests.
Dem taught in Judah, having the book of Baba God’s law with dem. Dem go about throughout all the cities of Judah and taught among the people.
The fear of Baba God fell on all the kingdoms of the lands that were around Judah, so that dem made no war against Jehoshaphat.
Some of the Philistines bring Jehoshaphat presents and silver for tribute. The Arabians also bring him flocks, seven thousand seven hundred rams, and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.
Jehoshaphat grew great exceedingly; and he built fortresses and store cities in Judah.
He had many works in the cities of Judah; and men of war, mighty men of valor, in Jerusalem.
This was the numbering of dem according to dem fathers’ houses: From Judah, the captains of thousands: Adnah the captain, and with him three hundred thousand mighty men of valor;
and next to him Jehohanan the captain, and with him two hundred eighty thousand;
and next to him Amasiah the son of Zichri, who willingly offered imself to Baba God, and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of valor.
From Benjamin: Eliada, a mighty man of valor, and with him two hundred thousand armed with bow and shield;
and next to him Jehozabad, and with him one hundred eighty thousand ready and prepared for war.
These were people wey waited on the king, besides those whom the king put in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.
Now Jehoshaphat had riches and honor in abundance; and he allied imself with Ahab.
After some years, he go down to Ahab to Samaria. Ahab killed sheep and cattle for him in abundance, and for the people who were with him, and moved him to go up with him to Ramoth Gilead.
Ahab king of Israel talk say to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, “Will you go with me to Ramoth Gilead?” He answer him, “I be as You be, and my people as una people. We go be with you in the war.”
Jehoshaphat talk say to the king of Israel, “Please inquire first for Baba God’s word.”

Then the king of Israel gathered the prophets together, four hundred men, and talk say to dem, “Shall we go to Ramoth Gilead to battle, or shall I forbear?” Dem talk say, “Go up; for God will deliver it into the hand of the king.”
But Jehoshaphat talk say, “No be there here a prophet of Baba God besides, that we may inquire of him?”

The king of Israel talk say to Jehoshaphat, “E get yet one man by whom we may inquire of Baba God; but I hate him, for he never prophesies good concerning me, but always evil. He is Micaiah the son of Imla.” Jehoshaphat talk say, “No let the king say so.”
Then the king of Israel call an officer, and talk say, “Get Micaiah the son of Imla sharp-sharp.”

Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah each sat on his throne, arrayed in dem robes, and dem were sitting in an open place at the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets were prophesying before dem.
Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made imself horns of iron and talk say, “Baba God says, ‘With these you shall push the Syrians, until Dem be consumed.’”
All the prophets prophesied so, saying, “Go up to Ramoth Gilead, and prosper; for Baba God will deliver it into the hand of the king.”
The messenger who go to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, “See am, the words of the prophets declare good to the king with one mouth. Let una word so, please be like one of dem own, and speak good.”
Micaiah talk say, “As Baba God lives, what my God says, that will I speak.”
When he had come to the king, the king talk say to him, “Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth Gilead to battle, or shall I forbear?” He talk say, “Go up, and prosper. Dem go be delivered into una hand.”
The king talk say to him, “How many times shall I adjure you that you speak to me nothing but the truth in Baba God’s name?”
He talk say, “I see all Israel scattered on the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd. Baba God talk say, ‘These have no master. Make dem each return to his house in peace.’”
The king of Israel talk say to Jehoshaphat, “Didn’t I tell una that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?”
Micaiah talk say, “So hear Baba God’s word: I see Baba God sitting on his throne, and all the army of heaven standing on his right hand and on his left.
Baba God talk say, ‘Who will entice Ahab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth Gilead?’ One spoke saying in this way, and another saying in that way.
A spirit come out, stood before Baba God, and talk say, ‘I go entice him.’ “Baba God talk say to him, ‘How?’
“He talk say, ‘I go go, and Go be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.’ “He talk say, ‘You go entice him, and will prevail also. Go and do so.’
“Now so, see am, Baba God has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these una prophets; and Baba God has spoken evil concerning you.”
Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah come near, and struck Micaiah on the cheek, and talk say, “Which way did Baba God’s Spirit go from me to speak to you?”
Micaiah talk say, “See am, you shall see on that day, when you go into an inner room to hide yourself.”
The king of Israel talk say, “Take Micaiah, and carry him back to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king’s son;
and say, ‘Thus says the king, “Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him with bread of suffering and with water of suffering, until I return in peace.”’”
Micaiah talk say, “If you return at all in peace, Baba God has not spoken by me.” He talk say, “Listen, you people, all of you!”
So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah go up to Ramoth Gilead.
The king of Israel talk say to Jehoshaphat, “I go disguise myself, and go into the battle; but you put on una robes.” So the king of Israel disguised imself; and dem go into the battle.
Now the king of Syria had commanded the captains of his chariots, saying, “No fight with small nor great, except only with the king of Israel.”

When the captains of the chariots see Jehoshaphat, dem talk say, “It is the king of Israel!” So dem turned around to fight against him. But Jehoshaphat cried out, and Baba God helped him; and God moved dem to depart from him.
When the captains of the chariots see that it No be the king of Israel, dem turned back from pursuing him.

A certain man drew his bow at random, and struck the king of Israel between the joints of the armor. So he talk say to the driver of the chariot, “Turn una hand, and carry me out of the army; for I be severely wounded.”
The battle increased that day. However the king of Israel propped imself up in his chariot against the Syrians until the evening; and at about sunset, he died.
Jehoshaphat the king of Judah come back to his house in peace to Jerusalem.

Jehu the son of Hanani the seer go out to meet him, and talk say to king Jehoshaphat, “Should you help the wicked, and love people wey hate Baba God? Because of this, serious anger is on you from before Baba God.
Nevertheless E get good things find in you, in that you have put away the Asheroth out of the land, and have set una heart to seek God.”
Jehoshaphat lived at Jerusalem; and he go out again among the people from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and bring dem back to Baba God, the God of dem fathers.
He set judges in the land throughout all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city,
and talk say to the judges, “Consider Wetin you do, for you no judge for man, but for Baba God; and he is with you in the judgment.
Now so let the fear of Baba God be on you. Take heed and do it; for E get no wickedness with Baba God our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of bribes.”

Moreover in Jerusalem Jehoshaphat appointed Levites and priests, and of the heads of the fathers’ households of Israel, for the judgment of Baba God, and for controversies. Dem come back to Jerusalem.
He commanded dem, saying, “You shall do this in the fear of Baba God, faithfully, and with a perfect heart.

Whenever any controversy comes to you from una brothers who live in dem cities, between blood and blood, between law and commandment, statutes and ordinances, you must warn dem, that dem not be guilty towards Baba God, and so serious anger come on you and on una brothers. Do this, and You go not be guilty.

See am, Amariah the chief priest is over you in all matters of Baba God; and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, in all the king’s matters. Also the Levites go be officers before you. Deal courageously, and may Baba God be with the good.”
After this, the pikin dem of Moab, the pikin dem of Ammon, and with dem some of the Ammonites, come against Jehoshaphat to battle.
Then some come who told Jehoshaphat, saying, “Plenty people is coming against you from beyond the sea from Syria. See am, Dem be in Hazazon Tamar” (that is, En Gedi).
Jehoshaphat was alarmed, and set imself to seek to Baba God. He proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.
Judah gathered themselves together to seek help from Baba God. Dem come out of all the cities of Judah to seek Baba God.
Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in Baba God’s house, before the new court;

and he talk say, “Baba God, the God of our fathers, no be you God in heaven? No be you ruler over all the kingdoms of the nations? Power and might are in una hand, so that Nobody is able to withstand you.
Didn’t you, our God, drive out the inhabitants of this land before una people Israel, and give it to the offspring of Abraham una friend forever?
Dem lived in it, and have built you a sanctuary in it for una name, saying,

‘If evil comes on us — the sword, judgment, pestilence, or famine — We go stand before this house, and before you (for una name is in this house), and cry to you in our suffering, and You go hear and save.’
Now, see am, the pikin dem of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom you would not let Israel invade when dem come out of the land of Egypt, but dem turned aside from dem, and didn’t destroy dem;
see am, how dem reward us, to come to throw us out of una possession, which you have given us to inherit.
Our God, will you not judge dem? For we have no might against this great company that comes against us. We no know what to do, but our eyes are on you.”
All Judah stood before Baba God, with dem little ones, dem wives, and dem pikin dem.
Then Baba God’s Spirit come on Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, the Levite, of the sons of Asaph, in the middle of the assembly;

and he talk say, “Listen, all Judah, and you inhabitants of Jerusalem, and you, king Jehoshaphat. Baba God says to you, ‘No fear, and no be dismayed because of this great plenty people; for the battle No be yours, but God’s.
Tomorrow, go down against dem. See am, Dem be coming up by the ascent of Ziz. You go find dem at the end of the valley, before the wilderness of Jeruel.

You go not need to fight this battle. Set unaself, stand still, and see the salvation of Baba God with you, O Judah and Jerusalem. No fear, nor be dismayed. Go out against dem tomorrow, for Baba God is with you.’”
Jehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground; and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before Baba God, worshiping Baba God.
The Levites, of the pikin dem of the Kohathites and of the pikin dem of the Korahites, stood up to praise Baba God, the God of Israel, with an exceeding loud voice.

Dem rose early in the morning, and go out into the wilderness of Tekoa. As dem go out, Jehoshaphat stood and talk say, “Listen to me, Judah, and you inhabitants of Jerusalem! Believe in Baba God una God, so You go be established! Believe his prophets, so You go prosper.”

When he had taken counsel with the people, he appointed people wey were to sing to Baba God, and give praise in holy array, as dem go out before the army, and say, “Thank God to Baba God; for his loving kindness endures forever.”
When dem began to sing and to praise, Baba God set ambushers against the pikin dem of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, who had come against Judah; and dem were struck.

For the pikin dem of Ammon and Moab stood up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to utterly kill and destroy dem: and when dem had finished the inhabitants of Seir, everyone helped to destroy another.
When Judah come to the place overlooking the wilderness, dem looked at the plenty people; and see am, dem were dead bodies fallen to the earth, and there were none who escaped.
