When Jehoshaphat and his people come to take dem plunder, dem find among dem in abundance both riches and dead bodies, and precious jewels, which dem stripped off for themselves, more than dem could carry away. Dem take plunder for three days, it was so much.
On the fourth day, dem assembled themselves in Beracah Valley, for there dem blessed Baba God. So the name of that place was call “Beracah Valley” to this day.
Then dem come back, every man of Judah and Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat in front of dem, to go again to Jerusalem with gladness; for Baba God had made dem to glad well-well over dem enemies.
Dem come to Jerusalem with stringed instruments, harps, and trumpets to Baba God’s house.
The fear of God was on all the kingdoms of the countries, when dem heard that Baba God fought against the enemies of Israel.
So the realm of Jehoshaphat was quiet, for his God give him rest all around.
Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he began to reign; and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.
He walked in the way of Asa his father, and didn’t turn aside from it, doing that which was right in Baba God’s eyes.
However the high places No be taken away, and the people had still not set dem hearts on the God of dem fathers.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, first and last, see am, Dem be written in the history of Jehu the son of Hanani, which is included in the book of the kings of Israel.
After this, Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined imself with Ahaziah king of Israel. The same did very wickedly.
He joined imself with him to make ships to go to Tarshish. Dem made the ships in Ezion Geber.

Then Eliezer the son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, “Because you have joined yourself with Ahaziah, Baba God has destroyed una works.” The ships were wrecked, so that dem No be able to go to Tarshish.
Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in David’s city, and Jehoram his son reigned in his place.
He had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. All these were the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.
Dem father give dem great gifts of silver, of gold, and of precious things, with fortified cities in Judah; but he give the kingdom to Jehoram, because he was the firstborn.
Now when Jehoram had risen up over the kingdom of his father, and had strengthened imself, he killed all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the princes of Israel.
Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did Ahab’s house; for he had Ahab’s daughter as his wife. He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight.
However Baba God would not destroy David’s house, because of the covenant that he had made with David, and as he promised to give a lamp to him and to his pikin dem always.
In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves.
Then Jehoram go there with his captains and all his chariots with him. He rose up by night and struck the Edomites who surrounded him, along with the captains of the chariots.
So Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah revolted at the same time from under his hand, because he had forsaken Baba God, the God of his fathers.
Moreover he made high places in the mountains of Judah, and made the inhabitants of Jerusalem play the prostitute, and led Judah astray.

A letter come to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, “Baba God, the God of David una father, says, ‘Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat una father, nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah,

but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and have made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to play the prostitute like Ahab’s house did, and also have slain una brothers of una father’s house, who were better than yourself,
see am, Baba God will strike una people with a great plague, including una pikin dem, una wives, and all una posessions;
and You go have great sickness with a disease of una bowels, until una bowels fall out by reason of the sickness, day by day.’”
Baba God stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines, and of the Arabians Wey be beside the Ethiopians;

and dem come up against Judah, broke into it, and carried away all the posessions that were find in the king’s house, including his sons and his wives; so that there was no son left him, except Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.
After all this Baba God struck him in his bowels with an incurable disease.
In process of time, at the end of two years, his bowels fell out by reason of his sickness, and he died of severe diseases. His people made no burning for him, like the burning of his fathers.
He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem eight years. He comot without being missed; and dem buried him in David’s city, but not in the tombs of the kings.

The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, because the band of men who come with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the oldest. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned.
Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Athaliah the daughter of Omri.
He also walked in the ways of Ahab’s house, because his mother was his counselor in acting wickedly.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, as did Ahab’s house, for dem were his counselors after the death of his father, to his destruction.
He also follow dem counsel, and go with Jehoram the son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth Gilead, and the Syrians wounded Joram.

He come back to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds which dem had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah go down to see Jehoram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick.
Now the destruction of Ahaziah was of God, in that he go to Joram; for when he had come, he go out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom Baba God had anointed to cut off Ahab’s house.
When Jehu was executing judgment on Ahab’s house, he find the princes of Judah and the sons of the brothers of Ahaziah, serving Ahaziah, and killed dem.

He sought Ahaziah, and dem caught him (now he was hiding in Samaria), and dem bring him to Jehu, and killed him; and dem buried him, for dem talk say, “He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought Baba God with all his heart.” The house of Ahaziah had no power to hold the kingdom.
Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah see that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring of the house of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath, the king’s daughter, take Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stealthily rescued him from among the king’s sons who were slain, and put him and his nurse in the bedroom. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest (for she was the sister of Ahaziah), hid him from Athaliah, so that she didn’t kill him.
He was with dem hidden in God’s house six years while Athaliah reigned over the land.

In the seventh year, Jehoiada strengthened imself, and take the captains of hundreds, Azariah the son of Jeroham, Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, Azariah the son of Obed, Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri, into a covenant with him.
Dem go around in Judah, and gathered the Levites out of all the cities of Judah, and the heads of fathers’ households of Israel, and dem come to Jerusalem.
All the assembly made a covenant with the king in God’s house. E tell dem say, “See am, the king’s son must reign, as Baba God has spoken concerning the sons of David.
This is the thing that you must do. A third part of you, who come in on the Sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, go be porters of the thresholds.
A third part go be at the king’s house; and a third part at the gate of the foundation. All the people Go be in the courts of Baba God’s house.
But let Nobody come into Baba God’s house, except the priests and people wey minister of the Levites. Dem shall come in, for Dem be holy, but all the people shall follow Baba God’s instructions.
The Levites shall surround the king, every man with his weapons in his hand. Anybody wey comes into the house, Make e be slain. Be with the king when he comes in, and when he goes out.”

So the Levites and all Judah did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded: and dem each take his men, people wey were to come in on the Sabbath; with people wey were to go out on the Sabbath; for Jehoiada the priest didn’t dismiss the shift.
Jehoiada the priest delivered to the captains of hundreds the spears, and bucklers, and shields, that Bin dey king David’s, which were in God’s house.
He set all the people, every man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, near the altar and the house, around the king.
Then dem bring out the king’s son, and put the crown on him, and give him the testimony, and made him king. Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and dem talk say, “Long live the king!”
When Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she come to the people into Baba God’s house.

Then she looked, and, see am, the king stood by his pillar at the entrance, and the captains and the trumpets by the king. All the people of the land rejoiced, and blew trumpets. The singers also played musical instruments, and led the singing of praise. Then Athaliah tore her clothes, and talk say, “Treason! treason!”

Jehoiada the priest bring out the captains of hundreds who were set over the army, and talk say to dem, “Bring her out between the ranks; and Anybody wey follows her, Make e be slain with the sword.” For the priest talk say, “No kill her in Baba God’s house.”
So dem made way for her. She go to the entrance of the horse gate to the king’s house; and dem killed her there.
Jehoiada made a covenant between imself, all the people, and the king, that dem should be Baba God’s people.
All the people go to the house of Baal, broke it down, broke his altars and his images in pieces, and killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars.

Jehoiada appointed the officers of Baba God’s house under the hand of the priests the Levites, whom David had distributed in Baba God’s house, to offer the burnt offerings of Baba God, as it is written in the law of Moses, with rejoicing and with singing, as David had ordered.
He set the porters at the gates of Baba God’s house, that Nobody who was unclean in anything should enter in.

He take the captains of hundreds, the nobles, the governors of the people, and all the people of the land, and bring the king down from Baba God’s house. Dem come through the upper gate to the king’s house, and set the king on the throne of the kingdom.
So all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. Dem had slain Athaliah with the sword.
Joash was seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zibiah, of Beersheba.
Joash did that which was right in Baba God’s eyes all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
Jehoiada take for him two wives, and he became the father of sons and daughters.
After this, Joash intended to restore Baba God’s house.

He gathered together the priests and the Levites, and talk say to dem, “Go out to the cities of Judah, and gather money to repair the house of una God from all Israel from year to year. See that you expedite this matter.” However the Levites didn’t do it right away.

The king call for Jehoiada the chief, and talk say to him, “Why haven’t you required of the Levites to bring in the tax of Moses the worker of Baba God, and of the assembly of Israel, out of Judah and out of Jerusalem, for the Tent of the Testimony?”
For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken up God’s house; and dem also give all the dedicated things of Baba God’s house to the Baals.
So the king commanded, and dem made a chest, and set it outside at the gate of Baba God’s house.
Dem made a proclamation through Judah and Jerusalem, to bring in for Baba God the tax that Moses the worker of God laid on Israel in the wilderness.
All the princes and all the people rejoiced, and bring in, and throw into the chest, until dem had filled it.

Whenever the chest was bring to the king’s officers by the hand of the Levites, and when dem see that there was much money, the king’s scribe and the chief priest’s officer come and emptied the chest, and take it, and carried it to its place again. Thus dem did day by day, and gathered money in abundance.

The king and Jehoiada give it to people wey did the work of the service of Baba God’s house. Dem hired masons and carpenters to restore Baba God’s house, and also people wey worked iron and brass to repair Baba God’s house.
So the workmen worked, and the work of repairing go forward in dem hands. Dem set up God’s house as it was designed, and strengthened it.

When dem had finished, dem bring the rest of the money before the king and Jehoiada, from which were made vessels for Baba God’s house, even vessels with which to minister and to offer, including spoons and vessels of gold and silver. Dem offered burnt offerings in Baba God’s house continually all the days of Jehoiada.
But Jehoiada grew old and was full of days, and he died. He was one hundred thirty years old when he died.
Dem buried him in David’s city among the kings, because he had done good in Israel, and toward God and his house.
Now after the death of Jehoiada, the princes of Judah come, and bowed down to the king. Then the king listened to dem.
Dem abandoned the house of Baba God, the God of dem fathers, and served the Asherah poles and the idols, so serious anger come on Judah and Jerusalem for this dem guiltiness.
Yet he sent prophets to dem, to bring dem again to Baba God, and dem testified against dem; but dem would not listen.

The Spirit of God come on Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest; and he stood above the people, and talk say to dem, “Thus says God, ‘Why do you disobey Baba God’s commandments, so that you no fit prosper? Because you have forsaken Baba God, he has also forsaken you.’”
Dem conspired against him, and stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king in the court of Baba God’s house.
Thus Joash the king didn’t remember the kindness which Jehoiada his father had done to him, but killed his son. When he died, he talk say, “May Baba God look at it, and repay it.”

At the end of the year, the army of the Syrians come up against him: and dem come to Judah and Jerusalem, and destroyed all the princes of the people from among the people, and sent all dem plunder to the king of Damascus.

For the army of the Syrians come with a small company of men; and Baba God delivered a plenty well-well army into dem hand, because dem had forsaken Baba God, the God of dem fathers. So dem executed judgment on Joash.

When dem had comot from him (for dem left him very sick), his own workers conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and killed him on his bed, and he died. Dem buried him in David’s city, but dem didn’t bury him in the tombs of the kings.
These are people wey conspired against him: Zabad the son of Shimeath the Ammonitess and Jehozabad the son of Shimrith the Moabitess.

Now concerning his sons, the greatness of the burdens laid on him, and the rebuilding of God’s house, see am, Dem be written in the commentary of the book of the kings. Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jehoaddan, of Jerusalem.
He did that which was right in Baba God’s eyes, but not with a perfect heart.
Now when the kingdom was established to him, he killed his workers who had killed his father the king.

But he didn’t put dem pikin dem to death, but did according to that which is written in the law in the book of Moses, as Baba God commanded, saying, “The fathers no go die for the pikin dem, neither shall the pikin dem die for the fathers; but every man shall die for his own sin.”

Moreover Amaziah gathered Judah together, and ordered dem according to dem fathers’ houses, under captains of thousands and captains of hundreds, even all Judah and Benjamin. He counted dem from twenty years old and upward, and find that there were three hundred thousand chosen men, able to go out to war, who could handle spear and shield.
He also hired one hundred thousand mighty men of valor out of Israel for one hundred talents of silver.
A man of God come to him, saying, “O king, no let the army of Israel go with you, for Baba God No be with Israel, with all the pikin dem of Ephraim.
But if You go go, take action, and be strong for the battle. God will overthrow you before the enemy; for God has power to help, and to overthrow.”
Amaziah talk say to the man of God, “But what shall we do for the hundred talents which I have given to the army of Israel?” The man of God answer, “Baba God is able to give you much more than this.”
Then Amaziah separated dem, the army that had come to him out of Ephraim, to go home again. So dem anger was greatly kindled against Judah, and dem come back home in fierce anger.
Amaziah take courage, and led his people out, and go to the Valley of Salt, and struck ten thousand of the pikin dem of Seir.
The pikin dem of Judah carried away ten thousand alive, and bring dem to the top of the rock, and threw dem down from the top of the rock, so that dem all were broken in pieces.

But the men of the army whom Amaziah sent back, that dem no suppose go with him to battle, fell on the cities of Judah, from Samaria even to Beth Horon, and struck of dem three thousand, and take much plunder.
Now after Amaziah had come from the slaughter of the Edomites, he bring the gods of the pikin dem of Seir, and set dem up to be his gods, and bowed down imself before dem, and burned incense to dem.

So Baba God’s anger burned against Amaziah, and he sent to him a prophet, who talk say to him, “Why have you sought after the gods of the people, which have not delivered dem own people out of una hand?”

As he talked with him, the king talk say to him, “Have we made you one of the king’s counselors? Stop! Why should you be struck down?” Then the prophet stopped, and talk say, “I know that God has determined to destroy you, because you have done this, and have not listened to my counsel.”
Then Amaziah king of Judah consulted his advisers, and sent to Joash, the son of Jehoahaz the son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, “Come, Make we look each other in the face.”

Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, “The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give una daughter to my son as his wife. Then a wild animal that was in Lebanon passed by, and trampled down the thistle.
You say to yourself that you have struck Edom; and una heart lifts you up to boast. Now stay at home. Why should you meddle with trouble, that you should fall, even you, and Judah with you?’”
But Amaziah would not listen; for it was of God, that he might deliver dem into the hand of dem enemies, because dem had sought after the gods of Edom.
So Joash king of Israel go up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah looked each other in the face at Beth Shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
Judah was defeated by Israel; and dem every man fled to his tent.

Joash king of Israel take Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash the son of Jehoahaz, at Beth Shemesh, and bring him to Jerusalem, and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits.
He take all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that were find in God’s house with Obed-Edom, and the treasures of the king’s house, the hostages also, and come back to Samaria.
Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah lived for fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah, first and last, see am, no be dem written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel?
Now from the time that Amaziah turned away from following Baba God, dem made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem. He fled to Lachish, but dem sent after him to Lachish, and killed him there.
Dem bring him on horses, and buried him with his fathers in the City of Judah.
All the people of Judah take Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the place of his father Amaziah.
He built Eloth, and restored it to Judah, after that the king slept with his fathers.
Uzziah was sixteen years old when he began to reign; and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jechiliah, of Jerusalem.
He did that which was right in Baba God’s eyes, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
He set imself to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the vision of God; and as long as he sought Baba God, God made him prosper.
He go out and fought against the Philistines, and broke down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod; and he built cities in the country of Ashdod, and among the Philistines.
God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians who lived in Gur Baal, and the Meunim.
The Ammonites give tribute to Uzziah. His name spread abroad even to the entrance of Egypt; for he grew exceedingly strong.
Moreover Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the corner gate, at the valley gate, and at the turning of the wall, and fortified dem.

He built towers in the wilderness, and dug out many cisterns, for he had much livestock; in the lowland also, and in the plain. He had farmers and vineyard keepers in the mountains and in the fruitful fields, for he love farming.

Moreover Uzziah had an army of fighting men, who go out to war by bands, according to the number of dem reckoning made by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer, under the hand of Hananiah, one of the king’s captains.
The whole number of the heads of fathers’ households, even the mighty men of valor, was two thousand six hundred.
Under dem hand was an army, three hundred seven thousand five hundred, who made war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy.
Uzziah prepared for dem, even for all the army, shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and stones for slinging.

In Jerusalem, he made devices, invented by skillful men, to be on the towers and on the battlements, with which to shoot arrows and great stones. His name spread far abroad, because he was marvelously helped until he was strong.
But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up, so that he did corruptly, and he trespassed against Baba God his God; for he go into Baba God’s temple to burn incense on the altar of incense.
Azariah the priest go in after him, and with him eighty priests of Baba God, who were valiant men.

Dem resisted Uzziah the king, and talk say to him, “It no be for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to Baba God, but for the priests the sons of Aaron, Wey be consecrated to burn incense. Go out of the sanctuary, for you have trespassed. It No go be for una honor from Baba God.”

Then Uzziah was angry. He had a censer in his hand to burn incense, and while he was angry with the priests, the leprosy broke out on his forehead before the priests in Baba God’s house, beside the altar of incense.

Azariah the chief priest, and all the priests, looked at him, and see am, he was leprous in his forehead, and dem thrust him out sharp-sharp from there. Yes, he imself also hurried to go out, because Baba God had struck him.

Uzziah the king was a leper to the day of his death, and lived in a separate house, being a leper; for he was cut off from Baba God’s house. Jotham his son was over the king’s house, judging the people of the land.
Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, first and last, Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, wrote.
So Uzziah slept with his fathers; and dem buried him with his fathers in the field of burial which belonged to the kings, for dem talk say, “He is a leper.” Jotham his son reigned in his place.
Jotham was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jerushah the daughter of Zadok.
He did that which was right in Baba God’s eyes, according to all that his father Uzziah had done. However he didn’t enter into Baba God’s temple. The people still acted corruptly.
He built the upper gate of Baba God’s house, and he built much on the wall of Ophel.
Moreover he built cities in the hill country of Judah, and in the forests he built fortresses and towers.

He also fought with the king of the pikin dem of Ammon, and prevailed against dem. The pikin dem of Ammon give him the same year one hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat, and ten thousand cors of barley. The pikin dem of Ammon also give that much to him in the second year, and in the third.
So Jotham became mighty, because he ordered his ways before Baba God his God.
Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all his wars, and his ways, see am, Dem be written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
He was five and twenty years old when he began to reign, and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
Jotham slept with his fathers, and dem buried him in David’s city; and Ahaz his son reigned in his place.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He didn’t do that which was right in Baba God’s eyes, like David his father,
but he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and also made molten images for the Baals.

Moreover he burned incense in the valley of the son of Hinnom, and burned his pikin dem in the fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom Baba God throw out before the pikin dem of Israel.
He sacrificed and burned incense in the high places, and on the hills, and under every green tree.

So Baba God his God delivered him into the hand of the king of Syria. Dem struck him, and carried away from him Plenty people of captives, and bring dem to Damascus. He was also delivered into the hand of the king of Israel, who struck him with a great slaughter.
For Pekah the son of Remaliah killed in Judah one hundred twenty thousand in one day, all of dem valiant men, because dem had forsaken Baba God, the God of dem fathers.
Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king’s son, Azrikam the ruler of the house, and Elkanah who was next to the king.
The pikin dem of Israel carried away captive of dem brothers two hundred thousand, women, sons, and daughters, and take also away much plunder from dem, and bring the plunder to Samaria.

But a prophet of Baba God was there, whose name was Oded; and he go out to meet the army that come to Samaria, and talk say to dem, “See am, because Baba God, the God of una fathers, was angry with Judah, he has delivered dem into una hand, and you have slain dem in a rage which has reached up to heaven.
Now you intend to degrade the pikin dem of Judah and Jerusalem as male and female slaves for unaself. No be there even with you trespasses of una own against Baba God una God?
Now hear me so, and send back the captives that you have taken captive from una brothers, for the fierce serious anger of Baba God is on you.”

Then some of the heads of the pikin dem of Ephraim, Azariah the son of Johanan, Berechiah the son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah the son of Shallum, and Amasa the son of Hadlai, stood up against people wey come from the war,

and talk say to dem, “You must not bring in the captives here, for you intend that which will bring on us a trespass against Baba God, to add to our sins and to our guilt; for our gulit is great, and E get fierce serious anger against Israel.”
So the armed men left the captives and the plunder before the princes and all the assembly.

The men who Don dey mentioned by name rose up and take the captives, and with the plunder clothed all who were naked among dem, dressed dem, give dem sandals, and give dem something to eat and to drink, anointed dem, carried all the feeble of dem on donkeys, and bring dem to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to dem brothers. Then dem come back to Samaria.
At that time king Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria to help him.
For again the Edomites had come and struck Judah, and carried away captives.

The Philistines also had invaded the cities of the lowland, and of the South of Judah, and had taken Beth Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco with its villages, Timnah with its villages, and also Gimzo and its villages; and dem lived there.
For Baba God bring Judah low because of Ahaz king of Israel, because he acted without restraint in Judah and trespassed severely against Baba God.
Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria come to him, and give him trouble, but didn’t strengthen him.
For Ahaz take away a portion out of Baba God’s house, and out of the house of the king and of the princes, and give it to the king of Assyria; but it didn’t help him.
In the time of his distress, he trespassed yet more against Baba God, this same king Ahaz.

For he sacrificed to the gods of Damascus, which struck him. He talk say, “Because the gods of the kings of Syria helped dem, so I go sacrifice to dem, that dem may help me.” But dem were the ruin of him, and of all Israel.
Ahaz gathered together the vessels of God’s house, and cut the vessels of God’s house in pieces, and shut up the doors of Baba God’s house; and he made imself altars in every corner of Jerusalem.
In every city of Judah he made high places to burn incense to other gods, and provoked Baba God, the God of his fathers, to anger.
Now the rest of his acts, and all his ways, first and last, see am, Dem be written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
Ahaz slept with his fathers, and dem buried him in the city, even in Jerusalem, because dem didn’t bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel; and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.
Hezekiah began to reign when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Abijah, the daughter of Zechariah.
He did that which was right in Baba God’s eyes, according to all that David his father had done.
In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of Baba God’s house, and repaired dem.
He bring in the priests and the Levites, and gathered dem together into the wide place on the east,
and talk say to dem, “Listen to me, you Levites! Now sanctify unaself, and sanctify Baba God, the God of una fathers’ house, and carry the filthiness out of the holy place.

For our fathers were unfaithful, and have done that which was evil in Baba God our God’s sight, and have forsaken him, and have turned away dem faces from the habitation of Baba God, and turned dem backs.
Also dem have shut up the doors of the porch, and put out the lamps, and have not burned incense nor offered burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.
So Baba God’s serious anger was on Judah and Jerusalem, and he has delivered dem to be tossed back and forth, to be an astonishment, and a hissing, as you see with una eyes.
For, see am, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives are in captivity for this.
Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with Baba God, the God of Israel, that his fierce anger may turn away from us.
My sons, no be negligent now; for Baba God has chosen you to stand before him, to minister to him, and that you should be his ministers, and burn incense.”

Then the Levites arose, Mahath, the son of Amasai, and Joel the son of Azariah, of the sons of the Kohathites; and of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi, and Azariah the son of Jehallelel; and of the Gershonites, Joah the son of Zimmah, and Eden the son of Joah;
and of the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeuel; and of the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah;
and of the sons of Heman, Jehuel and Shimei; and of the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
Dem gathered dem brothers, sanctified themselves, and go in, according to the commandment of the king by Baba God’s words, to cleanse Baba God’s house.

The priests go into the inner part of Baba God’s house to cleanse it, and bring out all the uncleanness that dem find in Baba God’s temple into the court of Baba God’s house. The Levites take it from there to carry it out to the brook Kidron.

Now dem began on the first day of the first month to sanctify, and on the eighth day of the month dem come to Baba God’s porch. Dem sanctified Baba God’s house in eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month dem finished.

Then dem go in to Hezekiah the king within the palace, and talk say, “We have cleansed all Baba God’s house, including the altar of burnt offering with all its vessels, and the table of show bread with all its vessels.
Moreover all the vessels, which king Ahaz in his reign threw away when he was unfaithful, have we prepared and sanctified. See am, Dem be before Baba God’s altar.”
Then Hezekiah the king arose early, gathered the princes of the city, and go up to Baba God’s house.

Dem bring seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats, for a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah. He commanded the priests the sons of Aaron to offer dem on Baba God’s altar.

So dem killed the bulls, and the priests received the blood, and sprinkled it on the altar. Dem killed the rams, and sprinkled the blood on the altar. Dem also killed the lambs, and sprinkled the blood on the altar.
Dem bring near the male goats for the sin offering before the king and the assembly; and dem laid dem hands on dem.

Then the priests killed dem, and dem made a sin offering with dem blood on the altar, to make atonement for all Israel; for the king commanded that the burnt offering and the sin offering should be made for all Israel.

He set the Levites in Baba God’s house with cymbals, with stringed instruments, and with harps, according to the commandment of David, of Gad the king’s seer, and Nathan the prophet; for the commandment was from Baba God by his prophets.
The Levites stood with David’s instruments, and the priests with the trumpets.
Hezekiah commanded dem to offer the burnt offering on the altar. When the burnt offering began, Baba God’s song also began, along with the trumpets and David king of Israel’s instruments.
All the assembly worshiped, the singers sang, and the trumpeters sounded. All this continued until the burnt offering was finished.
When dem had finished offering, the king and all who were present with him bowed themselves and worshiped.

Moreover Hezekiah the king and the princes commanded the Levites to sing praises to Baba God with the words of David, and of Asaph the seer. Dem sang praises with gladness, and dem bowed dem heads and worshiped.

Then Hezekiah answer, “Now you have consecrated unaself to Baba God. Come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings into Baba God’s house.” The assembly bring in sacrifices and thank offerings, and as many as were of a willing heart bring burnt offerings.
The number of the burnt offerings which the assembly bring was seventy bulls, one hundred rams, and two hundred lambs. All these were for a burnt offering to Baba God.
The consecrated things were six hundred head of cattle and three thousand sheep.

But the priests were too few, so that dem could not flay all the burnt offerings. So dem brothers the Levites helped dem, until the work was ended, and until the priests had sanctified themselves; for the Levites were more upright in heart to sanctify themselves than the priests.
Also the burnt offerings were in abundance, with the fat of the peace offerings, and with the drink offerings for every burnt offering. So the service of Baba God’s house was set in order.
Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced, because of that which God had prepared for the people; for the thing was done suddenly.
Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and wrote letters also to Ephraim and Manasseh, that dem should come to Baba God’s house at Jerusalem, to keep the Passover to Baba God, the God of Israel.
For the king had taken counsel with his princes and all the assembly in Jerusalem to keep the Passover in the second month.
For dem could not keep it at that time, because the priests had not sanctified themselves in sufficient number, and the people had not gathered themselves together to Jerusalem.
The thing was right in the eyes of the king and of all the assembly.

So dem established a decree to make proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beersheba even to Dan, that dem should come to keep the Passover to Baba God, the God of Israel, at Jerusalem, for dem had not kept it in great numbers in the way it is written.

So the couriers go with the letters from the king and his princes throughout all Israel and Judah, and according to the commandment of the king, saying, “You pikin dem of Israel, turn again to Baba God, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, that he may return to the remnant of you that have escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria.
No be like una fathers and like una brothers, who trespassed against Baba God, the God of dem fathers, so that he give dem up to desolation, as you see.

Now no be stiff-necked, as una fathers were, but yield unaself to Baba God, and enter into his sanctuary, which he has sanctified forever, and serve Baba God una God, that his fierce anger may turn away from you.

For if you turn again to Baba God, una brothers and una pikin dem will find compassion before people wey led dem captive, and will come again into this land, because Baba God una God is gracious and merciful, and No go turn away his face from you, if you return to him.”
So the couriers passed from city to city through the country of Ephraim and Manasseh, even to Zebulun, but people ridiculed dem and mocked dem.
Nevertheless some men of Asher and Manasseh and of Zebulun humbled themselves, and come to Jerusalem.
Also the hand of God come on Judah to give dem one heart, to do the commandment of the king and of the princes by Baba God’s word.
Many people assembled at Jerusalem to keep the feast of unleavened bread in the second month, a plenty well-well assembly.
Dem arose and take away the altars that were in Jerusalem, and dem take away all the altars for incense and threw dem into the brook Kidron.
Then dem killed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and the Levites were ashamed, and sanctified themselves, and bring burnt offerings into Baba God’s house.
Dem stood in dem place after dem order, according to the law of Moses the man of God. The priests sprinkled the blood which dem received of the hand of the Levites.
For there were many in the assembly who had not sanctified themselves: so the Levites were in charge of killing the Passovers for Everybody wey No be clean, to sanctify dem to Baba God.

For a plenty people of the people, even many of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves, yet dem ate the Passover other than the way it is written. For Hezekiah had prayed for dem, saying, “May the good Baba God pardon everyone
who sets his heart to seek God, Baba God, the God of his fathers, even if dem no be clean according to the purification of the sanctuary.”
Baba God listened to Hezekiah, and healed the people.

The pikin dem of Israel who were present at Jerusalem kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great gladness. The Levites and the priests praised Baba God day by day, singing with loud instruments to Baba God.

Hezekiah spoke encouragingly to all the Levites who had good understanding in the service of Baba God. So dem ate throughout the feast for the seven days, offering sacrifices of peace offerings, and making confession to Baba God, the God of dem fathers.
The whole assembly take counsel to keep another seven days, and dem kept another seven days with gladness.

For Hezekiah king of Judah give to the assembly for offerings one thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep; and the princes give to the assembly a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep: and a great number of priests sanctified themselves.
All the assembly of Judah, with the priests and the Levites, and all the assembly who come out of Israel, and the foreigners who come out of the land of Israel, and who lived in Judah, rejoiced.
So there was great gladness in Jerusalem; for since the time of Solomon the son of David king of Israel there was nothing like this in Jerusalem.
Then the priests the Levites arose and blessed the people. Dem voice was heard, and dem prayer come up to his holy habitation, even to heaven.

Now when all this was finished, all Israel who were present go out to the cities of Judah, and broke the pillars in pieces, cut down the Asherah poles, and broke down the high places and the altars out of all Judah and Benjamin, also in Ephraim and Manasseh, until dem had destroyed dem all. Then all the pikin dem of Israel come back, every man to his possession, into dem own cities.

Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites after dem divisions, every man according to his service, both the priests and the Levites, for burnt offerings and for peace offerings, to minister, to Thank God, and to praise in the gates of Baba God’s camp.

He also appointed the king’s portion of his posessions for the burnt offerings, for the morning and evening burnt offerings, and the burnt offerings for the Sabbaths, for the new moons, and for the set feasts, as it is written in Baba God’s law.
Moreover he commanded the people who lived in Jerusalem to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, that dem might give themselves to Baba God’s law.

As soon as the commandment go out, the pikin dem of Israel give in abundance the first fruits of grain, new wine, oil, honey, and of all the increase of the field; and dem bring in the tithe of all things abundantly.

The pikin dem of Israel and Judah, who lived in the cities of Judah, also bring in the tithe of cattle and sheep, and the tithe of dedicated things which were consecrated to Baba God dem God, and laid dem in heaps.
In the third month dem began to lay the foundation of the heaps, and finished dem in the seventh month.
When Hezekiah and the princes come and see the heaps, dem blessed Baba God and his people Israel.
Then Hezekiah questioned the priests and the Levites about the heaps.

Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok, answer him and talk say, “Since people began to bring the offerings into Baba God’s house, we have eaten and had enough, and have plenty left over, for Baba God has blessed his people; and that which is left is this great store.”
Then Hezekiah commanded dem to prepare rooms in Baba God’s house, and dem prepared dem.
Dem bring in the offerings, the tithes, and the dedicated things faithfully. Conaniah the Levite was ruler over dem, and Shimei his brother was second.

Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah were overseers under the hand of Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by the appointment of Hezekiah the king and Azariah the ruler of God’s house.
Kore the son of Imnah the Levite, the porter at the east gate, was over the freewill offerings of God, to distribute Baba God’s offerings and the most holy things.

Under him were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah, in the cities of the priests, in dem office of trust, to give to dem brothers by divisions, to the great as well as to the small;

besides people wey were listed by genealogy of males, from three years old and upward, even Everybody wey entered into Baba God’s house, as the duty of every day required, for dem service in dem offices according to dem divisions;
and people wey were listed by genealogy of the priests by dem fathers’ houses, and the Levites from twenty years old and upward, in dem offices by dem divisions;
and people wey were listed by genealogy of all dem little ones, dem wives, dem sons, and dem daughters, through all the congregation; for in dem office of trust dem sanctified themselves in holiness.

Also for the sons of Aaron the priests, who were in the fields of the suburbs of dem cities, in every city, there were men who were mentioned by name, to give portions to all the males among the priests, and to all who were listed by genealogy among the Levites.
Hezekiah did so throughout all Judah; and he did that which was good, right, and faithful before Baba God his God.
In every work that he began in the service of God’s house, in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart, and prospered.
After these things and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria come, entered into Judah, and encamped against the fortified cities, and intended to win dem for imself.
When Hezekiah see that Sennacherib had come, and that he was planning to fight against Jerusalem,
he take counsel with his princes and his mighty men to stop the waters of the springs which were outside of the city, and dem helped him.
So, many people gathered together and dem stopped all the springs and the brook that flowed through the middle of the land, saying, “Why should the kings of Assyria come, and find abundant water?”

He take courage, built up all the wall that was broken down, and raised it up to the towers, with the other wall outside, and strengthened Millo in David’s city, and made weapons and shields in abundance.
He set captains of war over the people, and gathered dem together to him in the wide place at the gate of the city, and spoke encouragingly to dem, saying,
“Be strong and courageous. No fear or dismayed because of the king of Assyria, nor for all the plenty people Wey be with him; for E get a greater one with us than with him.
An arm of flesh is with him, but Baba God our God is with us to help us and to fight our battles.” The people rested themselves on the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.

After this, Sennacherib king of Assyria sent his workers to Jerusalem, (now he was before Lachish, and all his power with him), to Hezekiah king of Judah, and to all Judah who were at Jerusalem, saying,
Thus says Sennacherib king of Assyria, “In whom do you trust, that you remain under siege in Jerusalem?
No dey Hezekiah persuade you, to give you over to die by famine and by thirst, saying, ‘Baba God our God will deliver us out of the hand of the king of Assyria?’
Hasn’t the same Hezekiah taken away his high places and his altars, and commanded Judah and Jerusalem, saying, ‘You shall worship before one altar, and you shall burn incense on it?’
No you know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of the lands in any way able to deliver dem land out of my hand?
Who was there among all the gods of those nations which my fathers utterly destroyed, that could deliver his people out of my hand, that una God should be able to deliver you out of my hand?

Now so no let Hezekiah deceive you, nor persuade you in this way. No believe him, for no god of any nation or kingdom was able to deliver his people out of my hand, and out of the hand of my fathers. How much less will una God deliver you out of my hand?”
His workers spoke yet more against Baba God, and against his worker Hezekiah.

He also wrote letters insulting Baba God, the God of Israel, and speaking against him, saying, “As the gods of the nations of the lands, which have not delivered dem people out of my hand, so shall the God of Hezekiah not deliver his people out of my hand.”
Dem call out with a loud voice in the Jews’ language to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to frighten dem, and to trouble dem; that dem might take the city.
Dem spoke of the God of Jerusalem as of the gods of the peoples of the earth, which are the work of men’s hands.
Hezekiah the king and Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz, prayed because of this, and cried to heaven.

Baba God sent an angel, who cut off all the mighty men of valor, and the leaders and captains, in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he come back with shame of face to his own land. When he had come into the house of his god, people wey come out of his own bowels killed him there with the sword.
Thus Baba God saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib the king of Assyria and from the hand of all others, and guided dem on every side.
Many bring gifts to Baba God to Jerusalem, and precious things to Hezekiah king of Judah; so that he was exalted in the sight of people for everywhere from then on.
In those days Hezekiah was terminally ill, and he prayed to Baba God; and he spoke to him, and give him a sign.
But Hezekiah didn’t reciprocate appropriate to the benefit done for him, because his heart was lifted up. So there was serious anger on him, and on Judah and Jerusalem.
Notwithstanding Hezekiah humbled imself for the pride of his heart, both he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that Baba God’s serious anger didn’t come on dem in the days of Hezekiah.
Hezekiah had exceedingly much riches and honor. He provided imself with treasuries for silver, for gold, for precious stones, for spices, for shields, and for all kinds of valuable vessels;
also storehouses for the increase of grain, new wine, and oil; and stalls for all kinds of animals, and flocks in folds.
Moreover he provided for imself cities, and possessions of flocks and herds in abundance; for God had given him abundant posessions.
This same Hezekiah also stopped the upper spring of the waters of Gihon, and bring dem straight down on the west side of David’s city. Hezekiah prospered in all his works.

However concerning the ambassadors of the princes of Babylon, who sent to him to inquire of the wonder that was done in the land, God left him, to try him, that he might know all that was in his heart.
Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and his good deeds, see am, Dem be written in the vision of Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz, in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

Hezekiah slept with his fathers, and dem buried him in the ascent of the tombs of the sons of David. All Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem honored him at his death. Manasseh his son reigned in his place.
Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, after the abominations of the nations whom Baba God throw out before the pikin dem of Israel.
For he built again the high places which Hezekiah his father had broken down; and he raised up altars for the Baals, made Asheroth, and worshiped all the army of the sky, and served dem.
He built altars in Baba God’s house, of which Baba God talk say, “My name go be in Jerusalem forever.”
He built altars for all the army of the sky in the two courts of Baba God’s house.

He also made his pikin dem to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom. He practiced sorcery, divination, and witchcraft, and dealt with people wey had familiar spirits, and with wizards. He did much evil in Baba God’s sight, to provoke him to anger.

He set the engraved image of the idol, which he had made, in God’s house, of which God talk say to David and to Solomon his son, “In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, will I put my name forever.

I go not any more remove the foot of Israel from off the land which I have appointed for una fathers, if only Dem go observe to do all that I have commanded dem, even all the law, the statutes, and the ordinances given by Moses.”
Manasseh seduced Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that dem did more evil than the nations whom Baba God destroyed before the pikin dem of Israel did.
Baba God spoke to Manasseh, and to his people; but dem didn’t listen.
So Baba God bring on dem the captains of the army of the king of Assyria, who take Manasseh in chains, bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon.
When he was in distress, he begged Baba God his God, and humbled imself greatly before the God of his fathers.
He prayed to him; and he was entreated by him, and heard his supplication, and bring him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh know that Baba God was God.

Now after this, he built an outer wall to David’s city, on the west side of Gihon, in the valley, even to the entrance at the fish gate. He encircled Ophel with it, and raised it up to a plenty well-well height; and he put valiant captains in all the fortified cities of Judah.
He take away the foreign gods, and the idol out of Baba God’s house, and all the altars that he had built in the mountain of Baba God’s house, and in Jerusalem, and throw dem out of the city.
He built up Baba God’s altar, and offered sacrifices of peace offerings and of thanksgiving on it, and commanded Judah to serve Baba God, the God of Israel.
Nevertheless the people sacrificed still in the high places, but only to Baba God dem God.

Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of Baba God, the God of Israel, see am, Dem be written among the acts of the kings of Israel.

His prayer also, and how God was entreated of him, and all his sin and his trespass, and the places in which he built high places, and set up the Asherah poles and the engraved images, before he humbled imself: see am, Dem be written in the history of Hozai.
So Manasseh slept with his fathers, and dem buried him in his own house; and Amon his son reigned in his place.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he began to reign; and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, as did Manasseh his father; and Amon sacrificed to all the engraved images which Manasseh his father had made, and served dem.
He didn’t humble imself before Baba God, as Manasseh his father had humbled imself; but this same Amon trespassed more and more.
His workers conspired against him, and put him to death in his own house.
But the people of the land killed all people wey had conspired against king Amon; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.
Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
He did that which was right in Baba God’s eyes, and walked in the ways of David his father, and didn’t turn aside to the right hand or to the left.

For in the eighth year of his reign, while he was yet young, he began to seek after the God of David his father; and in the twelfth year he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, the Asherah poles, the engraved images, and the molten images.

Dem broke down the altars of the Baals in his presence; and he cut down the incense altars that were on high above dem. He broke the Asherah poles, the engraved images, and the molten images in pieces, made dust of dem, and scattered it on the graves of people wey had sacrificed to dem.
He burned the bones of the priests on dem altars, and purged Judah and Jerusalem.
He did this in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, even to Naphtali, around in dem ruins.
He broke down the altars, and beat the Asherah poles and the engraved images into powder, and cut down all the incense altars throughout all the land of Israel, then come back to Jerusalem.

Now in the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had purged the land and the house, he sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, and Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah the son of Joahaz the recorder, to repair Baba God his God’s house.

Dem come to Hilkiah the high priest, and delivered the money that was bring into God’s house, which the Levites, the keepers of the threshold, had gathered from the hands of Manasseh, Ephraim, of all the remnant of Israel, of all Judah and Benjamin, and of the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
Dem delivered it into the hands of the workmen who had the oversight of Baba God’s house; and the workmen who labored in Baba God’s house give it to mend and repair the house.
Dem give it to the carpenters and to the builders, to buy cut stone and timber for couplings, and to make beams for the houses which the kings of Judah had destroyed.

The men did the work faithfully. Dem overseers were Jahath and Obadiah, the Levites, of the sons of Merari; and Zechariah and Meshullam, of the sons of the Kohathites, to give direction; and others of the Levites, who were all skillful with musical instruments.
Also dem were over the bearers of burdens, and directed all who did the work in every kind of service. Of the Levites, there were scribes, officials, and porters.
When dem bring out the money that was bring into Baba God’s house, Hilkiah the priest find the book of Baba God’s law given by Moses.
Hilkiah answer Shaphan the scribe, “I have find the book of the law in Baba God’s house.” So Hilkiah delivered the book to Shaphan.
Shaphan carried the book to the king, and moreover bring back word to the king, saying, “All that was committed to una workers, Dem be doing.
Dem have emptied out the money that was find in Baba God’s house, and have delivered it into the hand of the overseers, and into the hand of the workmen.”
Shaphan the scribe told the king, saying, “Hilkiah the priest has delivered me a book.” Shaphan read from it to the king.
When the king had heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes.
The king commanded Hilkiah, Ahikam the son of Shaphan, Abdon the son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king’s worker, saying,

“Go inquire of Baba God for me, and for people Wey left in Israel and in Judah, concerning the words of the book that is find; for great is Baba God’s serious anger that is poured out on us, because our fathers have not kept Baba God’s word, to do according to all that is written in this book.”

So Hilkiah, and dem whom the king had commanded, go to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tokhath, the son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe (now she lived in Jerusalem in the second quarter), and dem spoke to her to that effect.
She tell dem say, “Baba God, the God of Israel says: ‘Tell the man who sent you to me,
“Baba God says, ‘See am, I go bring evil on this place, and on its inhabitants, even all the curses that are written in the book which dem have read before the king of Judah.

Because dem have forsaken me, and have burned incense to other gods, that dem might provoke me to anger with all the works of dem hands; so my serious anger is poured out on this place, and it No go be quenched.’”’
But to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of Baba God, you shall tell him this, ‘Baba God, the God of Israel says: “About the words which you have heard,

because una heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before God, when you heard his words against this place, and against its inhabitants, and have humbled yourself before me, and have torn una clothes, and wept before me, I also have heard you,” says Baba God.

“See am, I go gather you to una fathers, and You go be gathered to una grave in peace. Una eyes no go see all the evil that I go bring on this place and on its inhabitants.”’” Dem bring back word to the king.
Then the king sent and gathered together all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

The king go up to Baba God’s house, with all the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests, the Levites, and all the people, both great and small; and he read in dem hearing all the words of the book of the covenant that was find in Baba God’s house.

The king stood in his place, and made a covenant before Baba God, to walk after Baba God, and to keep his commandments, and his testimonies, and his statutes, with all his heart, and with all his soul, to perform the words of the covenant that were written in this book.
He caused all who were find in Jerusalem and Benjamin to stand. The inhabitants of Jerusalem did according to the covenant of God, the God of dem fathers.

Josiah take away all the abominations out of all the countries that belonged to the pikin dem of Israel, and made all who were find in Israel to serve, even to serve Baba God dem God. All his days dem didn’t depart from following Baba God, the God of dem fathers.
Josiah kept a Passover to Baba God in Jerusalem. Dem killed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
He set the priests in dem offices, and encouraged dem in the service of Baba God’s house.

He talk say to the Levites who taught all Israel, who were holy to Baba God, “Put the holy ark in the house which Solomon the son of David king of Israel built. It will no longer be a burden on una shoulders. Now serve Baba God una God, and his people Israel.
Prepare unaself after una fathers’ houses by una divisions, according to the writing of David king of Israel, and according to the writing of Solomon his son.
Stand in the holy place according to the divisions of the fathers’ houses of una brothers the pikin dem of the people, and let there be for each a portion of a fathers’ house of the Levites.
Kill the Passover, sanctify unaself, and prepare for una brothers, to do according to Baba God’s word by Moses.”

Josiah give to the pikin dem of the people, of the flock, lambs and young goats, all of dem for the Passover offerings, to all who were present, to the number of thirty thousand, and three thousand bulls. These were of the king’s substance.

His princes give for a freewill offering to the people, to the priests, and to the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, the rulers of God’s house, give to the priests for the Passover offerings two thousand six hundred small livestock, and three hundred head of cattle.

Conaniah also, and Shemaiah and Nethanel, his brothers, and Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, the chiefs of the Levites, give to the Levites for the Passover offerings five thousand small livestock and five hundred head of cattle.
So the service was prepared, and the priests stood in dem place, and the Levites by dem divisions, according to the king’s commandment.
Dem killed the Passover, and the priests sprinkled the blood which dem received of dem hand, and the Levites flayed dem.

Dem removed the burnt offerings, that dem might give dem according to the divisions of the fathers’ houses of the pikin dem of the people, to offer to Baba God, as it is written in the book of Moses. Dem did the same with the cattle.
Dem roasted the Passover with fire according to the ordinance. The boiled the holy offerings in pots, in cauldrons, and in pans, and carried dem sharp-sharp to all the pikin dem of the people.

Afterward dem prepared for themselves and for the priests, because the priests the sons of Aaron were busy with offering the burnt offerings and the fat until night. So the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests the sons of Aaron.

The singers the sons of Asaph were in dem place, according to the commandment of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king’s seer; and the porters were at every gate. Dem didn’t need to depart from dem service, because dem brothers the Levites prepared for dem.
So all the service of Baba God was prepared the same day, to keep the Passover, and to offer burnt offerings on Baba God’s altar, according to the commandment of king Josiah.
The pikin dem of Israel who were present kept the Passover at that time, and the feast of unleavened bread seven days.

There was no Passover like that kept in Israel from the days of Samuel the prophet, nor did any of the kings of Israel keep such a Passover as Josiah kept, with the priests, the Levites, and all Judah and Israel who were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
This passover was kept in the eighteenth year of the reign of Josiah.
After all this, when Josiah had prepared the temple, Neco king of Egypt go up to fight against Carchemish by the Euphrates, and Josiah go out against him.

But he sent ambassadors to him, saying, “What have I to do with you, you king of Judah? I come not against you today, but against the house with which I have war. God has commanded me to make haste. Beware that it is God Wey be with me, that he not destroy you.”

Nevertheless Josiah would not turn his face from him, but disguised imself, that he might fight with him, and didn’t listen to the words of Neco from the mouth of God, and come to fight in the valley of Megiddo.
The archers shot at king Josiah; and the king talk say to his workers, “Take me away, because I be seriously wounded!”

So his workers take him out of the chariot, and put him in the second chariot that he had, and bring him to Jerusalem; and he died, and was buried in the tombs of his fathers. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.

Jeremiah lamented for Josiah, and all the singing men and singing women spoke of Josiah in dem lamentations to this day; and dem made dem an ordinance in Israel. See am, Dem be written in the lamentations.
Now the rest of the acts of Josiah, and his good deeds, according to that which is written in Baba God’s law,
and his acts, first and last, see am, Dem be written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
Then the people of the land take Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and made him king in his father’s place in Jerusalem.
Joahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign; and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.
The king of Egypt removed him from office at Jerusalem, and fined the land one hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
The king of Egypt made Eliakim his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. Neco take Joahaz his brother, and carried him to Egypt.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. He did that which was evil in Baba God his God’s sight.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon come up against him, and bound him in fetters to carry him to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar also carried some of the vessels of Baba God’s house to Babylon, and put dem in his temple at Babylon.

Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and his abominations which he did, and that which was find in him, see am, Dem be written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah; and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.
Jehoiachin was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight.
At the return of the year, king Nebuchadnezzar sent and bring him to Babylon, with the valuable vessels of Baba God’s house, and made Zedekiah his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
He did that which was evil in Baba God his God’s sight. He didn’t humble imself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from Baba God’s mouth.
He also rebelled against king Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God; but he stiffened his neck, and hardened his heart against turning to Baba God, the God of Israel.
Moreover all the chiefs of the priests, and the people, trespassed very greatly after all the abominations of the nations; and dem polluted Baba God’s house which he had made holy in Jerusalem.
Baba God, the God of dem fathers, sent to dem by his messengers, rising up early and sending, because he had compassion on his people, and on his dwelling place;
but dem mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and scoffed at his prophets, until Baba God’s serious anger arose against his people, until there was no remedy.

So he bring on dem the king of the Chaldeans, who killed dem young men with the sword in the house of dem sanctuary, and had no compassion on young man or virgin, old man or gray-headed. He give dem all into his hand.
All the vessels of God’s house, great and small, and the treasures of Baba God’s house, and the treasures of the king, and of his princes, all these he bring to Babylon.
Dem burned God’s house, and broke down the wall of Jerusalem, and burned all its palaces with fire, and destroyed all of its valuable vessels.
He carried people wey had escaped from the sword away to Babylon, and dem were workers to him and his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia,
to fulfill Baba God’s word by Jeremiah’s mouth, until the land had enjoyed its Sabbaths. As long as it lay desolate, it kept Sabbath, to fulfill seventy years.

Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that Baba God’s word by the mouth of Jeremiah might be accomplished, Baba God stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and put it also in writing, saying,

“Thus says Cyrus king of Persia, ‘Baba God, the God of heaven, has given all the kingdoms of the earth to me; and he has commanded me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Anybody wey E get among you of all his people, Baba God his God be with him, and Make e go up.’”

Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that Baba God’s word by Jeremiah’s mouth might be accomplished, Baba God stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and put it also in writing, saying,
“Thus says Cyrus king of Persia, ‘Baba God, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he has commanded me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.

Anybody wey E get among you of all his people, may his God be with him, and Make e go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of Baba God, the God of Israel (he is God), which is in Jerusalem.

Anybody wey is left, in any place where he lives, let the men of his place help him with silver, with gold, with goods, and with animals, besides the freewill offering for God’s house which is in Jerusalem.’”
Then the heads of fathers’ households of Judah and Benjamin, the priests, and the Levites, all whose spirit God had stirred to go up rose up to build Baba God’s house which is in Jerusalem.
All people wey were around dem strengthened dem hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, with animals, and with precious things, besides all that was willingly offered.
Also Cyrus the king bring out the vessels of Baba God’s house, which Nebuchadnezzar had bring out of Jerusalem, and had put in the house of his gods;
even those, Cyrus king of Persia bring out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and counted dem out to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah.
This is the number of dem: thirty platters of gold, one thousand platters of silver, twenty-nine knives,
thirty bowls of gold, four hundred ten silver bowls of a second sort, and one thousand other vessels.
All the vessels of gold and of silver were five thousand four hundred. Sheshbazzar bring all these up when the captives were bring up from Babylon to Jerusalem.

Now these are the pikin dem of the province, who go up out of the captivity of people wey Bin dey carried away, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away to Babylon, and who come back to Jerusalem and Judah, everyone to his city;
who come with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
The pikin dem of Parosh, two thousand one hundred seventy-two.
The pikin dem of Shephatiah, three hundred seventy-two.
The pikin dem of Arah, seven hundred seventy-five.
The pikin dem of Pahathmoab, of the pikin dem of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred twelve.
The pikin dem of Elam, one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
The pikin dem of Zattu, nine hundred forty-five.
The pikin dem of Zaccai, seven hundred sixty.
The pikin dem of Bani, six hundred forty-two.
The pikin dem of Bebai, six hundred twenty-three.
The pikin dem of Azgad, one thousand two hundred twenty-two.
The pikin dem of Adonikam, six hundred sixty-six.
The pikin dem of Bigvai, two thousand fifty-six.
The pikin dem of Adin, four hundred fifty-four.
The pikin dem of Ater, of Hezekiah, ninety-eight.
The pikin dem of Bezai, three hundred twenty-three.
The pikin dem of Jorah, one hundred twelve.
The pikin dem of Hashum, two hundred twenty-three.
The pikin dem of Gibbar, ninety-five.
The pikin dem of Bethlehem, one hundred twenty-three.
The men of Netophah, fifty-six.
The men of Anathoth, one hundred twenty-eight.
The pikin dem of Azmaveth, forty-two.
The pikin dem of Kiriath Arim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred forty-three.
The pikin dem of Ramah and Geba, six hundred twenty-one.
The men of Michmas, one hundred twenty-two.
The men of Bethel and Ai, two hundred twenty-three.
The pikin dem of Nebo, fifty-two.
The pikin dem of Magbish, one hundred fifty-six.
The pikin dem of the other Elam, one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
The pikin dem of Harim, three hundred twenty.
The pikin dem of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, seven hundred twenty-five.
The pikin dem of Jericho, three hundred forty-five.
The pikin dem of Senaah, three thousand six hundred thirty.
The priests: the pikin dem of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred seventy-three.
The pikin dem of Immer, one thousand fifty-two.
The pikin dem of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred forty-seven.
The pikin dem of Harim, one thousand seventeen.
The Levites: the pikin dem of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the pikin dem of Hodaviah, seventy-four.
The singers: the pikin dem of Asaph, one hundred twenty-eight.

The pikin dem of the porters: the pikin dem of Shallum, the pikin dem of Ater, the pikin dem of Talmon, the pikin dem of Akkub, the pikin dem of Hatita, the pikin dem of Shobai, in all one hundred thirty-nine.
The temple workers: the pikin dem of Ziha, the pikin dem of Hasupha, the pikin dem of Tabbaoth,
the pikin dem of Keros, the pikin dem of Siaha, the pikin dem of Padon,
the pikin dem of Lebanah, the pikin dem of Hagabah, the pikin dem of Akkub,
the pikin dem of Hagab, the pikin dem of Shamlai, the pikin dem of Hanan,
the pikin dem of Giddel, the pikin dem of Gahar, the pikin dem of Reaiah,
the pikin dem of Rezin, the pikin dem of Nekoda, the pikin dem of Gazzam,
the pikin dem of Uzza, the pikin dem of Paseah, the pikin dem of Besai,
the pikin dem of Asnah, the pikin dem of Meunim, the pikin dem of Nephisim,
the pikin dem of Bakbuk, the pikin dem of Hakupha, the pikin dem of Harhur,
the pikin dem of Bazluth, the pikin dem of Mehida, the pikin dem of Harsha,
the pikin dem of Barkos, the pikin dem of Sisera, the pikin dem of Temah,
the pikin dem of Neziah, the pikin dem of Hatipha.
The pikin dem of Solomon’s workers: the pikin dem of Sotai, the pikin dem of Hassophereth, the pikin dem of Peruda,
the pikin dem of Jaalah, the pikin dem of Darkon, the pikin dem of Giddel,
the pikin dem of Shephatiah, the pikin dem of Hattil, the pikin dem of Pochereth Hazzebaim, the pikin dem of Ami.
All the temple workers, and the pikin dem of Solomon’s workers, were three hundred ninety-two.
These were people wey go up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer; but dem could not show dem fathers’ houses, and dem offspring, whether dem were of Israel:
the pikin dem of Delaiah, the pikin dem of Tobiah, the pikin dem of Nekoda, six hundred fifty-two.

Of the pikin dem of the priests: the pikin dem of Habaiah, the pikin dem of Hakkoz, and the pikin dem of Barzillai, who take a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was call after dem name.
These sought dem place among people wey were registered by genealogy, but dem No be find: so were dem deemed disqualified and removed from the priesthood.
The governor told dem that dem no suppose eat of the most holy things until a priest stood up to serve with Urim and with Thummim.
The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred sixty,
besides dem male workers and dem female workers, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven; and dem had two hundred singing men and singing women.
Dem horses were seven hundred thirty-six; dem mules, two hundred forty-five;
dem camels, four hundred thirty-five; dem donkeys, six thousand seven hundred twenty.
Some of the heads of fathers’ households, when dem come to Baba God’s house which is in Jerusalem, offered willingly for God’s house to set it up in its place.
Dem give according to dem ability into the treasury of the work sixty-one thousand darics of gold, and five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred priests’ garments.
So the priests, and the Levites, and some of the people, the singers, the porters, and the temple workers, lived in dem cities, and all Israel in dem cities.
When the seventh month had come, and the pikin dem of Israel were in the cities, the people gathered themselves together as one man to Jerusalem.

Then Jeshua the son of Jozadak stood up with his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and his brothers, and built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the law of Moses the man of God.
In spite of dem fear because of the peoples of the surrounding lands, dem set the altar on its base; and dem offered burnt offerings on it to Baba God, even burnt offerings morning and evening.
Dem kept the feast of tents, as it is written, and offered the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the ordinance, as the duty of every day required;

and afterward the continual burnt offering, the offerings of the new moons, of all the set feasts of Baba God that were consecrated, and of Everybody wey willingly offered a freewill offering to Baba God.
From the first day of the seventh month, dem began to offer burnt offerings to Baba God; but the foundation of Baba God’s temple No be yet laid.

Dem also give money to the masons, and to the carpenters. Dem also give chop, drink, and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre, to bring cedar trees from Lebanon to the sea, to Joppa, according to the grant that dem had from Cyrus King of Persia.

Now in the second year of dem coming to God’s house at Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and the rest of dem brothers the priests and the Levites, and all people wey had come out of the captivity to Jerusalem, began the work and appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, to have the oversight of the work of Baba God’s house.

Then Jeshua stood with his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, together, to have the oversight of the workmen in God’s house: the sons of Henadad, with dem sons and dem brothers the Levites.

When the builders laid the foundation of Baba God’s temple, dem set the priests in dem clothing with trumpets, with the Levites the sons of Asaph with cymbals, to praise Baba God, according to the directions of David king of Israel.

Dem sang to each other in praising and giving thanks to Baba God, “For he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever toward Israel.” All the people shouted with a great shout, when dem praised Baba God, because the foundation of Baba God’s house Bin dey laid.

But many of the priests and Levites and heads of fathers’ households, the old men who had seen the first house, when the foundation of this house was laid before dem eyes, wept with a loud voice. Many also shouted aloud for gladness,
so that the people could not discern the noise of the shout of gladness from the noise of the weeping of the people; for the people shouted with a loud shout, and the noise was heard far away.
Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the pikin dem of the captivity were building a temple to Baba God, the God of Israel;
