dem come near to Zerubbabel, and to the heads of fathers’ households, and talk say to dem, “Make we build with you; for we seek una God, as you do; and we Don dey sacrificing to him since the days of Esar Haddon king of Assyria, who bring us up here.”

But Zerubbabel, and Jeshua, and the rest of the heads of fathers’ households of Israel, talk say to dem, “You have nothing to do with us in building a house to our God; but we ourselves together will build to Baba God, the God of Israel, as king Cyrus the king of Persia has commanded us.”
Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled dem in building.
Dem hired counselors against dem, to frustrate dem purpose, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
In the reign of Ahasuerus, For the beginning of his reign, wrote dem an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.

In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of his companions, wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia; and the writing of the letter was written in Syrian, and delivered in the Syrian language.
Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king as follows,

then Rehum the chancellor, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of dem companions, the Dinaites, and the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Archevites, the Babylonians, the Shushanchites, the Dehaites, the Elamites,
and the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Osnappar bring over, and set in the city of Samaria, and in the rest of the country beyond the River, and so forth, wrote.
This is the copy of the letter that dem sent: To King Artaxerxes, From una workers the men beyond the River.
Be it known to the king that the Jews who come up from you have come to us to Jerusalem. Dem be building the rebellious and bad city, and have finished the walls, and repaired the foundations.
Be it known now to the king that if this city is built and the walls finished, Dem go not pay tribute, custom, or toll, and in the end it Go be hurtful to the kings.
Now because we eat the salt of the palace, and it No be appropriate for us to see the king’s dishonor, so we have sent and informed the king,

that search may be made in the book of the records of una fathers. You go see in the book of the records, and know that this city is a rebellious city, and hurtful to kings and provinces, and that dem have started rebellions within it in the past. That is why this city was destroyed.
We inform the king that, if this city is built and the walls finished, then You go have no possession beyond the River.
Then the king sent an answer to Rehum the chancellor, and to Shimshai the scribe, and to the rest of dem companions who live in Samaria, and in the rest of the country beyond the River: Peace.
The letter which you sent to us Don dey plainly read before me.
I decreed, and search Don dey made, and it was find that this city has made insurrection against kings in the past, and that rebellion and revolts Don dey made in it.
There have also been mighty kings over Jerusalem, who have ruled over all the country beyond the River; and tribute, custom, and toll, was paid to dem.
Make a decree now to cause these men to cease, and that this city not be built, until a decree is made by me.
Be careful that you not be slack doing so. Why should damage grow to the hurt of the kings?
Then when the copy of king Artaxerxes’ letter was read before Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and dem companions, dem go in haste to Jerusalem to the Jews, and made dem to cease by force of arms.
Then work stopped on God’s house which is at Jerusalem. It stopped until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
Now the prophets, Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo, prophesied to the Jews who were in Judah and Jerusalem. Dem prophesied to dem in the name of the God of Israel.
Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak rose up and began to build God’s house which is at Jerusalem; and with dem were the prophets of God, helping dem.
At the same time Tattenai, the governor beyond the River come to dem, with Shetharbozenai, and dem companions, and ask dem, “Who give you a decree to build this house, and to finish this wall?”
Dem also ask for the names of the men were who were making this building.
But the eye of dem God was on the elders of the Jews, and dem No make dem cease, until the matter should come to Darius, and an answer should be come back by letter concerning it.
The copy of the letter that Tattenai, the governor beyond the River, and Shetharbozenai, and his companions the Apharsachites, who were beyond the River, sent to Darius the king follows.
Dem sent a letter to him, in which was written: To Darius the king, all peace.

Be it known to the king that we go into the province of Judah, to the house of the great God, which is built with great stones, and timber is laid in the walls. This work goes on with diligence and prospers in dem hands.
Then we ask those elders, and talk say to dem thus, “Who give you a decree to build this house, and to finish this wall?”
We ask dem dem names also, to inform you that we might write the names of the men who were at dem head.

Thus dem come back us answer, saying, “We be the workers of the God of heaven and earth, and are building the house that was built these many years ago, which a great king of Israel built and finished.

But after that our fathers had provoked the God of heaven to serious anger, he give dem into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, who destroyed this house, and carried the people away into Babylon.
But in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, Cyrus the king made a decree to build this house of God.

The gold and silver vessels of God’s house, which Nebuchadnezzar take out of the temple that was in Jerusalem, and bring into the temple of Babylon, those Cyrus the king also take out of the temple of Babylon, and dem were delivered to one whose name was Sheshbazzar, whom he had made governor.
E tell am say, ‘Take these vessels, go, put dem in the temple that is in Jerusalem, and let God’s house be built in its place.’
Then the same Sheshbazzar come and laid the foundations of God’s house which is in Jerusalem. Since that time even until now has it been in building, and yet it No be completed.

Now so, if it seems good to the king, let a search be made in the king’s treasure house, which is there at Babylon, whether it is so, that a decree was made of Cyrus the king to build this house of God at Jerusalem; and let the king send his pleasure to us concerning this matter.”
Then Darius the king made a decree, and the house of the archives, where the treasures were laid up in Babylon, was searched.
A scroll was find at Achmetha, in the palace that is in the province of Media, and in it this was written for a record:

In the first year of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king made a decree: Concerning God’s house at Jerusalem, let the house be built, the place where dem offer sacrifices, and let its foundations be strongly laid; with its height sixty cubits, and its width sixty cubits;
with three courses of great stones and a course of new timber. Let the expenses be given out of the king’s house.

Also let the gold and silver vessels of God’s house, which Nebuchadnezzar take out of the temple which is at Jerusalem, and bring to Babylon, be restored and bring again to the temple which is at Jerusalem, everything to its place. You shall put dem in God’s house.
Now so, Tattenai, governor beyond the River, Shetharbozenai, and una companions the Apharsachites, Wey be beyond the River, you must stay far from there.
Leave the work of this house of God alone; let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build this house of God in its place.

Moreover I make a decree Wetin you shall do for these elders of the Jews for the building of this house of God: that of the king’s goods, even of the tribute beyond the River, expenses must be given with all diligence to these men, that dem not be hindered.

That which dem have need of, including young bulls, rams, and lambs, for burnt offerings to the God of heaven; also wheat, salt, wine, and oil, according to the word of the priests Wey be at Jerusalem, let it be given dem day by day without fail;
that dem may offer sacrifices of pleasant aroma to the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king, and of his sons.
I have also made a decree that Anybody wey alters this message, let a beam be pulled out from his house, and Make e be lifted up and fastened on it; and let his house be made a dunghill for this.

May the God who has caused his name to live there overthrow all kings and peoples who stretch out dem hand to alter the same, to destroy this house of God which is at Jerusalem. I Darius have made a decree. Let it be done with all diligence.
Then Tattenai, the governor beyond the River, Shetharbozenai, and dem companions did accordingly with all diligence, because Darius the king had sent a decree.

The elders of the Jews built and prospered, through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo. Dem built and finished it, according to the commandment of the God of Israel, and according to the decree of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
This house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.
The pikin dem of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the pikin dem of the captivity, kept the dedication of this house of God with gladness.

Dem offered at the dedication of this house of God one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; and for a sin offering for all Israel, twelve male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
Dem set the priests in dem divisions, and the Levites in dem courses, for the service of God, which is at Jerusalem, as it is written in the book of Moses.
The pikin dem of the captivity kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.

Because the priests and the Levites had purified themselves together, all of dem were pure. Dem killed the Passover for all the pikin dem of the captivity, for dem brothers the priests, and for themselves.
The pikin dem of Israel who had come back out of the captivity, and all who had separated themselves to dem from the filthiness of the nations of the land, to seek Baba God, the God of Israel, ate,

and kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with gladness; because Baba God had made dem joyful, and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria to dem, to strengthen dem hands in the work of God, the God of Israel’s house.
Now after these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra the son of Seraiah, the son of Azariah, the son of Hilkiah,
the son of Shallum, the son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub,
the son of Amariah, the son of Azariah, the son of Meraioth,
the son of Zerahiah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki,
the son of Abishua, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the chief priest —

this Ezra go up from Babylon. He was a skilled scribe in the law of Moses, which Baba God, the God of Israel, had given; and the king granted him all his request, according to Baba God his God’s hand on him.
Some of the pikin dem of Israel, including some of the priests, the Levites, the singers, the porters, and the temple workers go up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of Artaxerxes the king.
He come to Jerusalem in the fifth month, which was in the seventh year of the king.
For on the first day of the first month he began to go up from Babylon; and on the first day of the fifth month he come to Jerusalem, according to the good hand of his God on him.
For Ezra had set his heart to seek Baba God’s law, and to do it, and to teach statutes and ordinances in Israel.
Now this is the copy of the letter that the king Artaxerxes give to Ezra the priest, the scribe, even the scribe of the words of Baba God’s commandments, and of his statutes to Israel:
Artaxerxes, king of kings, To Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the perfect God of heaven. Now
I make a decree, that all those of the people of Israel, and dem priests and the Levites, in my realm, who intend of dem own free will to go to Jerusalem, go with you.
Because You be sent by the king and his seven counselors, to inquire concerning Judah and Jerusalem, according to the law of una God which is in una hand,
and to carry the silver and gold, which the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose habitation is in Jerusalem,

and all the silver and gold that You go find in all the province of Babylon, with the freewill offering of the people, and of the priests, offering willingly for the house of dem God which is in Jerusalem;

so you shall with all diligence buy with this money bulls, rams, lambs, with dem meal offerings and dem drink offerings, and shall offer dem on the altar of the house of una God which is in Jerusalem.
Anything wey seems good to you and to una brothers to do with the rest of the silver and the gold, do that according to the will of una God.
The vessels that are given to you for the service of the house of una God, deliver before the God of Jerusalem.
Anything wey more Go be needed for the house of una God, which you may have occasion to give, give it out of the king’s treasure house.

I, even I Artaxerxes the king, make a decree to all the treasurers Wey be beyond the River, that Anything wey Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven, requires of you, it go be done with all diligence,
up to one hundred talents of silver, and to one hundred cors of wheat, and to one hundred baths of wine, and to one hundred baths of oil, and salt without prescribing how much.
Anything wey is commanded by the God of heaven, let it be done exactly for the house of the God of heaven; for why should there be serious anger against the realm of the king and his sons?
Also we inform you that it no go be lawful to impose tribute, custom, or toll, on any of the priests, Levites, singers, porters, temple workers, or laborers of this house of God.

You, Ezra, according to the wisdom of una God that is in una hand, appoint magistrates and judges, who may judge all the people Wey be beyond the River, who all know the laws of una God; and teach him who no dey know dem.

Anybody wey No go do the law of una God and the law of the king, let judgment be executed on him with all diligence, whether it is to death, or to banishment, or to confiscation of goods, or to imprisonment.
Blessed be Baba God, the God of our fathers, who has put such a thing as this in the king’s heart, to beautify Baba God’s house which is in Jerusalem;

and has extended loving kindness to me before the king and his counselors, and before all the king’s mighty princes. I was strengthened according to Baba God my God’s hand on me, and I gathered together chief men out of Israel to go up with me.
Now these are the heads of dem fathers’ households, and this is the genealogy of people wey go up with me from Babylon, in the reign of Artaxerxes the king:
Of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom. Of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel. Of the sons of David, Hattush.
Of the sons of Shecaniah, of the sons of Parosh, Zechariah; and with him were listed by genealogy of the males one hundred fifty.
Of the sons of Pahathmoab, Eliehoenai the son of Zerahiah; and with him two hundred males.
Of the sons of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel; and with him three hundred males.
Of the sons of Adin, Ebed the son of Jonathan; and with him fifty males.
Of the sons of Elam, Jeshaiah the son of Athaliah; and with him seventy males.
Of the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah the son of Michael; and with him eighty males.
Of the sons of Joab, Obadiah the son of Jehiel; and with him two hundred eighteen males.
Of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah; and with him one hundred sixty males.
Of the sons of Bebai, Zechariah the son of Bebai; and with him twenty-eight males.
Of the sons of Azgad, Johanan the son of Hakkatan; and with him one hundred ten males.
Of the sons of Adonikam, who were the last; and these are dem names: Eliphelet, Jeuel, and Shemaiah; and with dem sixty males.
Of the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zabbud; and with dem seventy males.
I gathered dem together to the river that runs to Ahava; and there we encamped three days: and I looked around at the people the priests, and find there were none of the sons of Levi.
Then sent I for Eliezer, for Ariel, for Shemaiah, for Elnathan, for Jarib, for Elnathan, for Nathan, for Zechariah, and for Meshullam, chief men; also for Joiarib and for Elnathan, who were teachers.

I sent dem out to Iddo the chief at the place Casiphia; and I told dem Wetin dem should tell Iddo, and his brothers the temple workers, at the place Casiphia, that dem should bring to us ministers for the house of our God.
According to the good hand of our God on us dem bring us a man of discretion, of the sons of Mahli, the son of Levi, the son of Israel; and Sherebiah, with his sons and his brothers, eighteen;
and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari, his brothers and dem sons, twenty;
and of the temple workers, whom David and the princes had given for the service of the Levites, two hundred twenty temple workers. All of dem were mentioned by name.
Then I proclaimed a fast there, at the river Ahava, that we might humble ourselves before our God, to seek from him a straight way for us, and for our little ones, and for all our possessions.

For I was ashamed to ask of the king a band of soldiers and horsemen to help us against the enemy on the way, because we had spoken to the king, saying, “The hand of our God is on all people wey seek him, for good; but his power and his serious anger is against all people wey forsake him.”
So we fasted and begged our God for this: and he granted our request.
Then I set apart twelve of the chiefs of the priests, even Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of dem brothers with dem,
and weighed to dem the silver, the gold, and the vessels, even the offering for the house of our God, which the king, his counselors, his princes, and all Israel there present, had offered.
I weighed into dem hand six hundred fifty talents of silver, one hundred talents of silver vessels; one hundred talents of gold,
twenty bowls of gold weighing one thousand darics; and two vessels of fine bright brass, precious as gold.
I talk say to dem, “You be holy to Baba God, and the vessels are holy. The silver and the gold are a freewill offering to Baba God, the God of una fathers.
Watch and keep dem, until you weigh dem before the chiefs of the priests and the Levites, and the princes of the fathers’ households of Israel, at Jerusalem, in the rooms of Baba God’s house.”
So the priests and the Levites received the weight of the silver and the gold, and the vessels, to bring dem to Jerusalem to the house of our God.
Then we comot from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month, to go to Jerusalem. The hand of our God was on us, and he delivered us from the hand of the enemy and the bandit by the way.
We come to Jerusalem, and stayed there three days.

On the fourth day the silver and the gold and the vessels were weighed in the house of our God into the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest; and with him was Eleazar the son of Phinehas; and with dem was Jozabad the son of Jeshua, and Noadiah the son of Binnui, the Levite;
everything by number and by weight; and all the weight was written at that time.

The pikin dem of the captivity, who had come out of exile, offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel, twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats for a sin offering. All this was a burnt offering to Baba God.
Dem delivered the king’s commissions to the king’s satraps, and to the governors beyond the River. So dem supported the people and God’s house.

Now when these things were done, the princes come near to me, saying, “The people of Israel, the priests, and the Levites, have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands, following dem abominations, even those of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.

For dem have taken of dem daughters for themselves and for dem sons, so that the holy offspring have mixed themselves with the peoples of the lands. Yes, the hand of the princes and rulers Don dey chief in this trespass.”
When I heard this thing, I tore my garment and my robe, and pulled the hair out of my head and of my beard, and sat down confounded.
Then Everybody wey trembled at the words of the God of Israel were assembled to me, because of dem trespass of the captivity; and I sat confounded until the evening offering.
At the evening offering I arose up from my humiliation, even with my garment and my robe torn; and I fell on my knees, and spread out my hands to Baba God my God;
and I talk say, “My God, I be ashamed and blush to lift up my face to you, my God; for our iniquities have increased over our head, and our guiltiness has grown up to the heavens.

Since the days of our fathers we Don dey exceeding guilty to this day; and for our iniquities we, our kings, and our priests, Don dey delivered into the hand of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to confusion of face, as it is this day.

Now for a little moment grace Don dey shown from Baba God our God, to leave us a remnant to escape, and to give us a nail in his holy place, that our God may lighten our eyes, and revived us a little in our bondage.

For We be bondservants; yet our God has not forsaken us in our bondage, but has extended loving kindness to us in the sight of the kings of Persia, to revive us, to set up the house of our God, and to repair its ruins, and to give us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.
“Now, our God, what shall we say after this? For we have forsaken una commandments,

which you have commanded by una workers the prophets, saying, ‘The land, to which you go to possess it, is an unclean land through the uncleanness of the peoples of the lands, through dem abominations, which have filled it from one end to another with dem filthiness.

Now so no give una daughters to dem sons. No take dem daughters to una sons, nor seek dem peace or dem prosperity forever; that you may be strong, and eat the good of the land, and leave it for an inheritance to una pikin dem forever.’
“After all that has come on us for our evil deeds, and for our great guilt, since you, our God, have punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and have given us such a remnant,

shall we again break una commandments, and join in affinity with the peoples that do these abominations? Wouldn’t you be angry with us until you had consumed us, so that there would be no remnant, nor any to escape?
Baba God, the God of Israel, You be righteous; for We be left a remnant that has escaped, as it is today. See am, We be before you in our guiltiness; for Nobody can stand before you because of this.”

Now while Ezra prayed and made confession, weeping and casting imself down before God’s house, there was gathered together to him out of Israel a plenty well-well assembly of men and women and pikin dem; for the people wept very bitterly.

Shecaniah the son of Jehiel, one of the sons of Elam, answer Ezra, “We have trespassed against our God, and have married foreign women of the peoples of the land. Yet now E get hope for Israel concerning this thing.

Now so Make we make a covenant with our God to put away all the wives, and people wey as are born of dem, according to the counsel of my lord, and of people wey tremble at the commandment of our God. Let it be done according to the law.
Arise; for the matter belongs to you, and We be with you. Be courageous, and do it.”
Then Ezra arose, and made the chiefs of the priests, the Levites, and all Israel, to swear that dem would do according to this word. So dem swore.

Then Ezra rose up from before God’s house, and go into the room of Jehohanan the son of Eliashib. When he come there, he ate no bread, nor drank water; for he mourned because of dem trespass of the captivity.
Dem made a proclamation throughout Judah and Jerusalem to all the pikin dem of the captivity, that dem should gather themselves together to Jerusalem;

and that Anybody wey didn’t come within three days, according to the counsel of the princes and the elders, all his possessions should be forfeited, and imself separated from the assembly of the captivity.

Then all the men of Judah and Benjamin gathered themselves together to Jerusalem within the three days. It was the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month; and all the people sat in the wide place in front of God’s house, trembling because of this matter, and because of the great rain.
Ezra the priest stood up and talk say to dem, “You have trespassed, and have married foreign women, to increase the guilt of Israel.
Now so make confession to Baba God, the God of una fathers, and do his pleasure; and separate unaself from the peoples of the land, and from the foreign women.”
Then all the assembly answer with a loud voice, “As you have talk say concerning us, so must we do.
But the people are many, and it is a time of much rain, and we No be able to stand outside. This No be a work of one day or two, for we have greatly transgressed in this matter.

Now let our princes be appointed for all the assembly, and let all people Wey in our cities who have married foreign women come at appointed times, and with dem the elders of every city, and its judges, until the fierce serious anger of our God is turned from us, until this matter is resolved.”
Only Jonathan the son of Asahel and Jahzeiah the son of Tikvah stood up against this; and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped dem.

The pikin dem of the captivity did so. Ezra the priest, with certain heads of fathers’ households, after dem fathers’ houses, and all of dem by dem names, were set apart; and dem sat down in the first day of the tenth month to examine the matter.
Dem finished with all the men who had married foreign women by the first day of the first month.
Among the sons of the priests there were find who had married foreign women: of the sons of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and his brothers, Maaseiah, and Eliezer, and Jarib, and Gedaliah.
Dem give dem hand that dem would put away dem wives; and being guilty, dem offered a ram of the flock for dem guilt.
Of the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
Of the sons of Harim: Maaseiah, and Elijah, and Shemaiah, and Jehiel, and Uzziah.
Of the sons of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
Of the Levites: Jozabad, and Shimei, and Kelaiah (also call Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
Of the singers: Eliashib. Of the porters: Shallum, and Telem, and Uri.
Of Israel: Of the sons of Parosh: Ramiah, and Izziah, and Malchijah, and Mijamin, and Eleazar, and Malchijah, and Benaiah.
Of the sons of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, and Abdi, and Jeremoth, and Elijah.
Of the sons of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, and Jeremoth, and Zabad, and Aziza.
Of the sons of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, Athlai.
Of the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, and Adaiah, Jashub, and Sheal, Jeremoth.
Of the sons of Pahathmoab: Adna, and Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, and Binnui, and Manasseh.
Of the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,
Benjamin, Malluch, Shemariah.
Of the sons of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, Shimei.
Of the sons of Bani: Maadai, Amram, and Uel,
Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluhi,
Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,
Mattaniah, Mattenai, and Jaasu,
and Bani, and Binnui, Shimei,
and Shelemiah, and Nathan, and Adaiah,
Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,
Azarel, and Shelemiah, Shemariah,
Shallum, Amariah, Joseph.
Of the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Iddo, and Joel, Benaiah.
All these had taken foreign wives; and some of dem had wives by whom dem had pikin dem.
The words of Nehemiah the son of Hacaliah. Now in the month Chislev, in the twentieth year, as I was in Shushan the palace,
Hanani, one of my brothers, come, he and certain men out of Judah; and I ask dem about the Jews who had escaped, who were left of the captivity, and concerning Jerusalem.

Dem talk say to me, “The remnant Wey be left of the captivity there in the province are in great suffering and reproach. The wall of Jerusalem is also broken down, and its gates are burned with fire.”
When I heard these words, I sat down and wept, and mourned several days; and I fasted and prayed before the God of heaven,
and talk say, “I beg you, Baba God, the God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps covenant and loving kindness with people wey love him and keep his commandments:

Let una ear now be attentive, and una eyes open, that you may listen to the prayer of una worker, which I pray before you at this time, day and night, for the pikin dem of Israel una workers, while I confess the sins of the pikin dem of Israel, which we have sinned against you. Yes, I and my father’s house have sinned.
We have dealt very corruptly against you, and have not kept the commandments, nor the statutes, nor the ordinances, which you commanded una worker Moses.
“Remember, I beg you, the word that you commanded una worker Moses, saying, ‘If you trespass, I go scatter you among the peoples;

but if you return to me, and keep my commandments and do dem, though una outcasts were in the uttermost part of the heavens, yet I go gather dem from there, and will bring dem to the place that I have chosen, to cause my name to live there.’
“Now these are una workers and una people, whom you have redeemed by una great power, and by una strong hand.

Lord, I beg you, let una ear be attentive now to the prayer of una worker, and to the prayer of una workers, who delight to fear una name; and please prosper una worker today, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man.” Now I was cup bearer to the king.
In the month Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, when wine was before him, I picked up the wine, and give it to the king. Now I had not been sad before in his presence.
The king talk say to me, “Why is una face sad, since you No be sick? This is nothing else but sorrow of heart.” Then I was well-well afraid.
I talk say to the king, “Let the king live forever! Why shouldn’t my face be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers’ tombs, lies waste, and its gates Don dey consumed with fire?”
Then the king talk say to me, “Wetin be una request?” So I prayed to the God of heaven.
I talk say to the king, “If it pleases the king, and if una worker has find favor in una sight, that you would send me to Judah, to the city of my fathers’ tombs, that I may build it.”
The king talk say to me (the queen was also sitting by him), “How long will una journey be? When will you return?” So it pleased the king to send me, and I set a time for he.
Moreover I talk say to the king, “If it pleases the king, let letters be given me to the governors beyond the River, that dem may let me pass through until I come to Judah;

and a letter to Asaph the keeper of the king’s forest, that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel by the temple, for the wall of the city, and for the house that I go occupy.” The king granted my requests, because of the good hand of my God on me.
Then I come to the governors beyond the River, and give dem the king’s letters. Now the king had sent captains of the army and horsemen with me.
When Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the worker, the Ammonite, heard of it, it grieved dem exceedingly, because a man had come to seek the welfare of the pikin dem of Israel.
So I come to Jerusalem, and was there three days.
I arose in the night, I and a few men with me. I didn’t tell anyone what my God put into my heart to do for Jerusalem. There no be any animal with me, except the animal that I rode on.
I go out by night by the valley gate, even toward the jackal’s well, then to the dung gate, and inspected the walls of Jerusalem, which were broken down, and its gates were consumed with fire.
Then I go on to the spring gate and to the king’s pool, but there was no place for the animal that was under me to pass.
Then go I up in the night by the brook, and inspected the wall; and I turned back, and entered by the valley gate, and so come back.
The rulers didn’t know where I go, or what I did. I had No be like yet told it to the Jews, nor to the priests, nor to the nobles, nor to the rulers, nor to the rest who did the work.

Then I talk say to dem, “You see the bad situation that We be in, how Jerusalem lies waste, and its gates are burned with fire. Come, Make we build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we no go be disgraced.”
I told dem of the hand of my God which was good on me, as also of the king’s words that he had spoken to me. Dem talk say, “Let’s rise up and build.” So dem strengthened dem hands for the good work.

But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammontite worker, and Geshem the Arabian, heard it, dem ridiculed us, and despised us, and talk say, “Wetin be this thing that You be doing? Will you rebel against the king?”
Then I answer dem, and talk say to dem, “The God of heaven will prosper us. So we, his workers, will arise and build; but you have no portion, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.”

Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brothers the priests, and dem built the sheep gate. Dem sanctified it, and set up its doors. Dem sanctified it even to the tower of Hammeah, to the tower of Hananel.
Next to him the men of Jericho built. Next to dem Zaccur the son of Imri built.
The sons of Hassenaah built the fish gate. Dem laid its beams, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.

Next to dem, Meremoth the son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz made repairs. Next to dem, Meshullam the son of Berechiah, the son of Meshezabel made repairs. Next to dem, Zadok the son of Baana made repairs.
Next to dem, the Tekoites made repairs; but dem nobles didn’t put dem necks to the Lord’s work.
Joiada the son of Paseah and Meshullam the son of Besodeiah repaired the old gate. Dem laid its beams, and set up its doors, and its bolts, and its bars.
Next to dem, Melatiah the Gibeonite, and Jadon the Meronothite, the men of Gibeon and of Mizpah, repaired the residence of the governor beyond the River.
Next to him, Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, goldsmiths, made repairs. Next to him, Hananiah, one of the perfumers, made repairs, and dem fortified Jerusalem even to the wide wall.
Next to dem, Rephaiah the son of Hur, the ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs.
Next to dem, Jedaiah the son of Harumaph made repairs across from his house. Next to him, Hattush the son of Hashabneiah made repairs.
Malchijah the son of Harim, and Hasshub the son of Pahathmoab, repaired another portion, and the tower of the furnaces.
Next to him, Shallum the son of Hallohesh, the ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, he and his daughters, made repairs.
Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the valley gate. Dem built it, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars, and one thousand cubits of the wall to the dung gate.
Malchijah the son of Rechab, the ruler of the district of Beth Haccherem repaired the dung gate. He built it, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.

Shallun the son of Colhozeh, the ruler of the district of Mizpah repaired the spring gate. He built it, and covered it, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars, and the wall of the pool of Shelah by the king’s garden, even to the stairs that go down from David’s city.

After him, Nehemiah the son of Azbuk, the ruler of half the district of Beth Zur, made repairs to the place opposite the tombs of David, and to the pool that was made, and to the house of the mighty men.
After him, the Levites, Rehum the son of Bani made repairs. Next to him, Hashabiah, the ruler of half the district of Keilah, made repairs for his district.
After him, dem brothers, Bavvai the son of Henadad, the ruler of half the district of Keilah made repairs.
Next to him, Ezer the son of Jeshua, the ruler of Mizpah, repaired another portion, across from the ascent to the armory at the turning of the wall.
After him, Baruch the son of Zabbai earnestly repaired another portion, from the turning of the wall to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
After him, Meremoth the son of Uriah the son of Hakkoz repaired another portion, from the door of the house of Eliashib even to the end of the house of Eliashib.
After him, the priests, the men of the Plain made repairs.
After dem, Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs across from dem house. After dem, Azariah the son of Maaseiah the son of Ananiah made repairs beside his own house.
After him, Binnui the son of Henadad repaired another portion, from the house of Azariah to the turning of the wall, and to the corner.

Palal the son of Uzai made repairs opposite the turning of the wall, and the tower that stands out from the upper house of the king, which is by the court of the guard. After him Pedaiah the son of Parosh made repairs.
(Now the temple workers lived in Ophel, to the place over against the water gate toward the east, and the tower that stands out.)
After him the Tekoites repaired another portion, over against the great tower that stands out, and to the wall of Ophel.
Above the horse gate, the priests made repairs, everyone across from his own house.
After dem, Zadok the son of Immer made repairs across from his own house. After him, Shemaiah the son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the east gate made repairs.
After him, Hananiah the son of Shelemiah, and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another portion. After him, Meshullam the son of Berechiah made repairs across from his room.
After him, Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths to the house of the temple workers, and of the merchants, made repairs opposite the gate of Hammiphkad, and to the ascent of the corner.
Between the ascent of the corner and the sheep gate, the goldsmiths and the merchants made repairs.
But when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he was angry, and was very indignant, and mocked the Jews.

He spoke before his brothers and the army of Samaria, and talk say, “Wetin be these feeble Jews doing? Will dem fortify themselves? Will dem sacrifice? Will dem finish in a day? Will dem revive the stones out of the heaps of rubbish, since Dem be burned?”
Now Tobiah the Ammonite was by him, and he talk say, “Wetin dem are building, if a fox climbed up it, he would break down dem stone wall.”
“Hear, our God; for We be despised; and turn back dem reproach on dem own head, give dem up for a plunder in a land of captivity;
no cover dem wickedness, and no let dem sin be blotted out from before you; for dem have insulted the builders.”
So we built the wall; and all the wall was joined together to half its height: for the people had a mind to work.

But when Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabians, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that the repairing of the walls of Jerusalem go forward, and that the breaches began to be filled, dem were very angry;
and dem all conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem, and to cause confusion among us.
But we made our prayer to our God, and set a watch against dem day and night, because of dem.
Judah talk say, “The strength of the bearers of burdens is fading, and E get much rubble; so that we No be able to build the wall.”
Our adversaries talk say, “Dem go not know or see, until we come in among dem and kill dem, and cause the work to cease.”
When the Jews who lived by dem come, dem talk say to us ten times from all places, “Anywhere wey you turn, Dem go attack us.”
So I set guards in the lowest parts of the space behind the wall, in the open places. I set the people by family groups with dem swords, dem spears, and dem bows.

I looked, and rose up, and talk say to the nobles, to the rulers, and to the rest of the people, “No fear of dem! Remember the Lord, Wey be great and awesome, and fight for una brothers, una sons, una daughters, una wives, and una houses.”
When our enemies heard that it was known to us, and God had bring dem counsel to nothing, all of us come back to the wall, everyone to his work.
From that time forth, half of my workers did the work, and half of dem held the spears, the shields, the bows, and the coats of mail; and the rulers were behind all the house of Judah.
People wey built the wall, and people wey bore burdens loaded themselves; everyone with one of his hands did the work, and with the other held his weapon.
Among the builders, everyone wore his sword at his side, and so built. Person wey sounded the trumpet was by me.
I talk say to the nobles, and to the rulers and to the rest of the people, “The work is great and large, and We be separated on the wall, one far from each other.
Anywhere wey you hear the sound of the trumpet, rally there to us. Our God will fight for us.”
So we did the work. Half of the people held the spears from the rising of the morning until the stars appeared.
Likewise at the same time talk say I to the people, “Let everyone with his worker lodge within Jerusalem, that in the night dem may be a guard to us, and may labor in the day.”
So neither I, nor my brothers, nor my workers, nor the men of the guard who follow me, none of us take off our clothes. Everyone take his weapon to the water.
Then there arose a great cry of the people and of dem wives against dem brothers the Jews.
For there were that talk say, “We, our sons and our daughters, are many. Make we get grain, that we may eat and live.”
There were also some that talk say, “We be mortgaging our fields, and our vineyards, and our houses. Make we get grain, because of the famine.”
There were also some who talk say, “We have borrowed money for the king’s tribute using our fields and our vineyards as collateral.

Yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our brothers, our pikin dem as dem pikin dem. See am, we bring our sons and our daughters into bondage to be workers, and some of our daughters Don dey bring into bondage. It is also not in our power to help it, because other men have our fields and our vineyards.”
I was very angry when I heard dem cry and these words.
Then I consulted with myself, and contended with the nobles and the rulers, and talk say to dem, “You exact usury, everyone of his brother.” I held a great assembly against dem.

I talk say to dem, “We, after our ability, have redeemed our brothers the Jews that were sold to the nations; and would you even sell una brothers, and should dem be sold to us?” Then dem held dem peace, and find not a word to say.
Also I talk say, “The thing that you do No be good. Shouldn’t you walk in the fear of our God, because of the reproach of the nations our enemies?
I likewise, my brothers and my workers, lend dem money and grain. Please Make we stop this usury.

Please restore to dem, even today, dem fields, dem vineyards, dem olive groves, and dem houses, also the hundredth part of the money, and of the grain, the new wine, and the oil, that You be charging dem.”
Then dem talk say, “We go restore dem, and will require nothing of dem. We go do so, even as you say.” Then I call the priests, and take an oath of dem, that dem would do according to this promise.

Also I shook out my lap, and talk say, “So may God shake out every man from his house, and from his labor, that no dey perform this promise; even be he shaken out, and emptied like this.” All the assembly talk say, “Amen,” and praised Baba God. The people did according to this promise.

Moreover from the time that I was appointed to be dem governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year even to the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes the king, that is, twelve years, I and my brothers have not eaten the bread of the governor.

But the former governors who were before me were supported by the people, and take bread and wine from dem, plus forty shekels of silver; yes, even dem workers ruled over the people; but I didn’t do so, because of the fear of God.
Yes, I also continued in the work of this wall. We didn’t buy any land. All my workers were gathered there to the work.
Moreover there were at my table, of the Jews and the rulers, one hundred fifty men, besides people wey come to us from among the nations that were around us.

Now that which was prepared for one day was one ox and six choice sheep. Also fowls were prepared for me, and once in ten days a store of all sorts of wine. Yet for all this, I didn’t demand the governor’s pay, because the bondage was heavy on this people.
Remember to me, my God, for good, all that I have done for this people.

Now when it was reported to Sanballat, Tobiah, and to Geshem the Arabian, and to the rest of our enemies, that I had built the wall, and that there was no breach left in it (though even to that time I had not set up the doors in the gates)
Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, “Come, Make we meet together in the villages in the plain of Ono.” But dem intended to harm me.
I sent messengers to dem, saying, “I be doing a great work, so that I no fit come down. Why should the work cease, while I leave it, and come down to you?”
Dem sent to me four times like this; and I answer dem the same way.
Then Sanballat sent his worker to me the same way the fifth time with an open letter in his hand,

in which was written, “It is reported among the nations, and Gashmu says it, that you and the Jews intend to rebel. Because of that, You be building the wall. You would be dem king, according to these words.

You have also appointed prophets to proclaim of you at Jerusalem, saying, ‘E get a king in Judah!’ Now it Go be reported to the king according to these words. Come now so, and Make we take counsel together.”
Then I sent to him, saying, “E get no such things done as you say, but you imagine dem out of una own heart.”
For dem all would have made us afraid, saying, “Dem hands Go be weakened from the work, that it not be done.” But now, strengthen my hands.

I go to the house of Shemaiah the son of Delaiah the son of Mehetabel, who was shut in at his home; and he talk say, “Make we meet together in God’s house, within the temple, and Make we shut the doors of the temple; for Dem go come to kill you. Yes, in the night will dem come to kill you.”
I talk say, “Should a man like me flee? Wey be there that, being such as I, would go into the temple to save his life? I go not go in.”
I discerned, and see am, God had not sent him; but he pronounced this prophecy against me. Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
He hired so that I would be afraid, do so, and sin, and that dem might have material for an evil report, that dem might reproach me.
“Remember, my God, Tobiah and Sanballat according to these dem works, and also the prophetess Noadiah, and the rest of the prophets, that would have put me in fear.”
So the wall was finished in the twenty-fifth day of Elul, in fifty-two days.
When all our enemies heard of it, all the nations that were around us were afraid, and dem lost dem confidence; for dem perceived that this work was done by our God.
Moreover in those days the nobles of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah’s letters come to dem.
For there were many in Judah sworn to him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah the son of Arah; and his son Jehohanan had taken the daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechiah as wife.
Also dem spoke of his good deeds before me, and reported my words to him. Tobiah sent letters to put me in fear.
Now when the wall was built, and I had set up the doors, and the porters and the singers and the Levites were appointed,
I put my brother Hanani, and Hananiah the governor of the fortress, in charge of Jerusalem; for he was a faithful man, and feared God above many.

I talk say to dem, “No let the gates of Jerusalem be opened until the sun is hot; and while dem stand guard, Make dem shut the doors, and you bar dem: and appoint watches of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, everyone in his watch, with everyone near his house.”
Now the city was wide and large; but the people were few inside am, and the houses No be built.

My God put into my heart to gather together the nobles, and the rulers, and the people, that dem might be listed by genealogy. I find the book of the genealogy of people wey come up at the first, and I find this written in it:

These are the pikin dem of the province, who go up out of the captivity of people wey Bin dey carried away, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away, and who come back to Jerusalem and to Judah, everyone to his city;
who come with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
The pikin dem of Parosh, two thousand one hundred seventy-two.
The pikin dem of Shephatiah, three hundred seventy-two.
The pikin dem of Arah, six hundred fifty-two.
The pikin dem of Pahathmoab, of the pikin dem of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred eighteen.
The pikin dem of Elam, one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
The pikin dem of Zattu, eight hundred forty-five.
The pikin dem of Zaccai, seven hundred sixty.
The pikin dem of Binnui, six hundred forty-eight.
The pikin dem of Bebai, six hundred twenty-eight.
The pikin dem of Azgad, two thousand three hundred twenty-two.
The pikin dem of Adonikam, six hundred sixty-seven.
The pikin dem of Bigvai, two thousand sixty-seven.
The pikin dem of Adin, six hundred fifty-five.
The pikin dem of Ater, of Hezekiah, ninety-eight.
The pikin dem of Hashum, three hundred Twenty-eight.
The pikin dem of Bezai, three hundred twenty-four.
The pikin dem of Hariph, one hundred twelve.
The pikin dem of Gibeon, ninety-five.
The men of Bethlehem and Netophah, one hundred eighty-eight.
The men of Anathoth, one hundred twenty-eight.
The men of Beth Azmaveth, forty-two.
The men of Kiriath Jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred forty-three.
The men of Ramah and Geba, six hundred twenty-one.
The men of Michmas, one hundred twenty-two.
The men of Bethel and Ai, one hundred twenty-three.
The men of the other Nebo, fifty-two.
The pikin dem of the other Elam, one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
The pikin dem of Harim, three hundred twenty.
The pikin dem of Jericho, three hundred forty-five.
The pikin dem of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, seven hundred twenty-one.
The pikin dem of Senaah, three thousand nine hundred thirty.
The priests: The pikin dem of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred seventy-three.
The pikin dem of Immer, one thousand fifty-two.
The pikin dem of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred forty-seven.
The pikin dem of Harim, one thousand seventeen.
The Levites: the pikin dem of Jeshua, of Kadmiel, of the pikin dem of Hodevah, seventy-four.
The singers: the pikin dem of Asaph, one hundred forty-eight.
The porters: the pikin dem of Shallum, the pikin dem of Ater, the pikin dem of Talmon, the pikin dem of Akkub, the pikin dem of Hatita, the pikin dem of Shobai, one hundred thirty-eight.
The temple workers: the pikin dem of Ziha, the pikin dem of Hasupha, the pikin dem of Tabbaoth,
the pikin dem of Keros, the pikin dem of Sia, the pikin dem of Padon,
the pikin dem of Lebana, the pikin dem of Hagaba, the pikin dem of Salmai,
the pikin dem of Hanan, the pikin dem of Giddel, the pikin dem of Gahar,
the pikin dem of Reaiah, the pikin dem of Rezin, the pikin dem of Nekoda,
the pikin dem of Gazzam, the pikin dem of Uzza, the pikin dem of Paseah.
The pikin dem of Besai, the pikin dem of Meunim, the pikin dem of Nephushesim,
the pikin dem of Bakbuk, the pikin dem of Hakupha, the pikin dem of Harhur,
the pikin dem of Bazlith, the pikin dem of Mehida, the pikin dem of Harsha,
the pikin dem of Barkos, the pikin dem of Sisera, the pikin dem of Temah,
the pikin dem of Neziah, the pikin dem of Hatipha.
The pikin dem of Solomon’s workers: the pikin dem of Sotai, the pikin dem of Sophereth, the pikin dem of Perida,
the pikin dem of Jaala, the pikin dem of Darkon, the pikin dem of Giddel,
the pikin dem of Shephatiah, the pikin dem of Hattil, the pikin dem of Pochereth Hazzebaim, the pikin dem of Amon.
All the temple workers, and the pikin dem of Solomon’s workers, were three hundred ninety-two.
These were people wey go up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer; but dem could not show dem fathers’ houses, nor dem offspring, whether dem were of Israel:
The pikin dem of Delaiah, the pikin dem of Tobiah, the pikin dem of Nekoda, six hundred forty-two.
Of the priests: the pikin dem of Hobaiah, the pikin dem of Hakkoz, the pikin dem of Barzillai, who take a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was call after dem name.
These searched for dem genealogical records, but no fit find dem. So were dem deemed disqualified and removed from the priesthood.
The governor told that dem no suppose eat of the most holy things until a priest stood up to minister with Urim and Thummim.
The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred sixty,
besides dem male workers and dem female workers, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven; and dem had two hundred forty-five singing men and singing women.
Dem horses were seven hundred thirty-six; dem mules, two hundred forty-five;
dem camels, four hundred thirty-five; dem donkeys, six thousand seven hundred twenty.
Some from among the heads of fathers’ households give to the work. The governor give to the treasury one thousand darics of gold, fifty basins, and five hundred thirty priests’ garments.
Some of the heads of fathers’ households give into the treasury of the work twenty thousand darics of gold, and two thousand two hundred minas of silver.
That which the rest of the people give was twenty thousand darics of gold, plus two thousand minas of silver, and sixty-seven priests’ garments.

So the priests, the Levites, the porters, the singers, some of the people, the temple workers, and all Israel, lived in dem cities. When the seventh month had come, the pikin dem of Israel were in dem cities.

All the people gathered themselves together as one man into the wide place that was in front of the water gate; and dem spoke to Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which Baba God had commanded to Israel.
Ezra the priest bring the law before the assembly, both men and women, and all who could hear with understanding, on the first day of the seventh month.

He read from it before the wide place that was in front of the water gate from early morning until midday, in the presence of the men and the women, and of people wey could understand. The ears of all the people were attentive to the book of the law.

Ezra the scribe stood on a pulpit of wood, which dem had made for the purpose; and beside him stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, on his right hand; and on his left hand, Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people (for he was above all the people), and when he opened it, all the people stood up.
Then Ezra blessed Baba God, the great God. All the people answer, “Amen, Amen,” with the lifting up of dem hands. Dem bowed dem heads, and worshiped Baba God with dem faces to the ground.

Also Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites, caused the people to understand the law; and the people stayed in dem place.
Dem read in the book, in the law of God, distinctly; and dem give the sense, so that dem understand the reading.

Nehemiah, who was the governor, and Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who taught the people, talk say to all the people, “Today is holy to Baba God una God. No mourn, nor weep.” For all the people wept when dem heard the words of the law.

Then E tell dem say, “Go una way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for today is holy to our Lord. No be grieved, for the gladness of Baba God is una strength.”
So the Levites calmed all the people, saying, “Hold una peace, for the day is holy. No be grieved.”
All the people go dem way to eat, to drink, to send portions, and to celebrate, because dem had understand the words that were declared to dem.
On the second day, the heads of fathers’ households of all the people, the priests, and the Levites were gathered together to Ezra the scribe, to study the words of the law.
Dem find written in the law how Baba God had commanded by Moses that the pikin dem of Israel should live in booths in the feast of the seventh month;

and that dem should publish and proclaim in all dem cities, and in Jerusalem, saying, “Go out to the mountain, and get olive branches, branches of wild olive, myrtle branches, palm branches, and branches of thick trees, to make temporary shelters, as it is written.”

So the people go out, and bring dem, and made themselves temporary shelters, everyone on the roof of his house, in dem courts, in the courts of God’s house, in the wide place of the water gate, and in the wide place of Ephraim’s gate.

All the assembly of people wey had come back out of the captivity made temporary shelters, and lived in the booths; for since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun to that day the pikin dem of Israel had not done so. There was plenty well-well gladness.
Also day by day, from the first day to the last day, he read in the book of the law of God. Dem kept the feast seven days; and on the eighth day was a solemn assembly, according to the ordinance.
Now in the twenty-fourth day of this month the pikin dem of Israel were assembled with fasting, with sackcloth, and dirt on dem.
The offspring of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners, and stood and confessed dem sins, and the iniquities of dem fathers.
Dem stood up in dem place, and read in the book of the law of Baba God dem God a fourth part of the day; and a fourth part dem confessed, and worshiped Baba God dem God.
Then Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani of the Levites stood up on the stairs, and cried with a loud voice to Baba God dem God.

Then the Levites, Jeshua, and Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah, talk say, “Stand up and bless Baba God una God from everlasting to everlasting! Blessed be una glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise!

You be Baba God, even you alone. You have made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all dem army, the earth and all things that are on it, the seas and all that is in dem, and you preserve dem all. The army of heaven worships you.
You be Baba God, the God who chose Abram, bring him out of Ur of the Chaldees, give him the name of Abraham,

find his heart faithful before you, and made a covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite, and the Girgashite, to give it to his offspring, and have performed una words; for You be righteous.
“You see the suffering of our fathers in Egypt, and heard dem cry by the Red Sea,

and showed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, and against all his workers, and against all the people of his land; for you know that dem dealt proudly against dem, and made a name for yourself, as it is today.
You divided the sea before dem, so that dem go through the middle of the sea on the dry land; and you throw dem pursuers into the depths, as a stone into the mighty waters.
Moreover, in a pillar of cloud you led dem by day; and in a pillar of fire by night, to give dem light in the way in which dem should go.
“You also come down on Mount Sinai, and spoke with dem from heaven, and give dem right ordinances and true laws, good statutes and commandments,
and made known to dem una holy Sabbath, and commanded dem commandments, statutes, and a law, by Moses una worker,
and give dem bread from the sky for dem hunger, and bring water out of the rock for dem for dem thirst, and commanded dem that dem should go in to possess the land which you had sworn to give dem.
“But dem and our fathers behaved proudly, hardened dem neck, didn’t listen to una commandments,

and refused to obey. Dem no be mindful of una wonders that you did among dem, but hardened dem neck, and in dem rebellion appointed a captain to return to dem bondage. But You be a God ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and didn’t forsake dem.
Yes, when dem had made themselves a molten calf, and talk say, ‘This is una God who bring you up out of Egypt,’ and had committed awful blasphemies;

yet you in una manifold mercies didn’t forsake dem in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud didn’t depart from over dem by day, to lead dem in the way; neither did the pillar of fire by night, to show dem light, and the way in which dem should go.
You give also una good Spirit to instruct dem, and didn’t withhold una manna from dem mouth, and give dem water for dem thirst.
“Yes, forty years you sustained dem in the wilderness. Dem lacked nothing. Dem clothes didn’t grow old, and dem feet didn’t swell.
Moreover you give dem kingdoms and peoples, which you allotted according to dem portions. So dem possessed the land of Sihon, even the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.
You also multiplied dem pikin dem as the stars of the sky, and bring dem into the land concerning which you talk say to dem fathers, that dem should go in to possess it.

“So the pikin dem go in and possessed the land, and you subdued before dem the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and give dem into dem hands, with dem kings and the peoples of the land, that dem might do with dem as dem pleased.

Dem take fortified cities and a rich land, and possessed houses full of all good things, cisterns dug out, vineyards, and olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. So dem ate, were filled, became fat, and delighted themselves in una great goodness.

“Nevertheless dem were disobedient, and rebelled against you, throw una law behind dem back, killed una prophets that testified against dem to turn dem again to you, and dem committed awful blasphemies.

So you delivered dem into the hand of dem adversaries, who distressed dem. In the time of dem trouble, when dem cried to you, you heard from heaven; and according to una manifold mercies you give dem saviors who saved dem out of the hands of dem adversaries.

But after dem had rest, dem did evil again before you; so left you dem in the hands of dem enemies, so that dem had the dominion over dem; yet when dem come back, and cried to you, you heard from heaven; and many times you delivered dem according to una mercies,

and testified against dem, that you might bring dem again to una law. Yet dem were arrogant, and didn’t listen to una commandments, but sinned against una ordinances (which if a man does, he shall live in dem), turned dem backs, stiffened dem neck, and would not hear.
Yet many years you put up with dem, and testified against dem by una Spirit through una prophets. Yet would dem not give ear. So you give dem into the hand of the peoples of the lands.
“Nevertheless in una manifold mercies you No make a full end of dem, nor forsake dem; for You be a gracious and merciful God.

Now so, our God, the great, the mighty, and the awesome God, who keeps covenant and loving kindness, no let all the travail seem little before you, that has come on us, on our kings, on our princes, on our priests, on our prophets, on our fathers, and on all una people, since the time of the kings of Assyria to this day.
However You be just in all that has come on us; for you have dealt truly, but we have done wickedly.
Also our kings, our princes, our priests, and our fathers have not kept una law, nor listened to una commandments and una testimonies with which you testified against dem.
For dem have not served you in dem kingdom, and in una great goodness that you give dem, and in the large and rich land which you give before dem. Dem No turn from dem wicked works.
“See am, We be workers today, and as for the land that you give to our fathers to eat its fruit and its good, see am, We be workers in it.
It yields much increase to the kings whom you have set over us because of our sins. Also dem have power over our bodies and over our livestock, at dem pleasure, and We be in great distress.
Yet for all this, we make a sure covenant, and write it; and our princes, our Levites, and our priests, seal it.”
Now people wey sealed were: Nehemiah the governor, the son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah,
Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah,
Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah,
Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch,
Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah,
Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch,
Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin,
Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah. These were the priests.
The Levites: namely, Jeshua the son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel;
and dem brothers, Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah,
Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,
Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.
The chiefs of the people: Parosh, Pahathmoab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,
Bunni, Azgad, Bebai,
Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,
Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur,
Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai,
Hariph, Anathoth, Nobai,
Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,
Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua,
Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,
Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub,
Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek,
Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,
and Ahiah, Hanan, Anan,
Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.

The rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the porters, the singers, the temple workers, and all people wey had separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to the law of God, dem wives, dem sons, and dem daughters, Everybody wey had knowledge, and understanding —

dem joined with dem brothers, dem nobles, and entered into a curse, and into an oath, to walk in God’s law, which was given by Moses the worker of God, and to observe and do all the commandments of Baba God our Lord, and his ordinances and his statutes;
and that we would not give our daughters to the peoples of the land, nor take dem daughters for our sons;

and if the peoples of the land bring wares or any grain on the Sabbath day to sell, that we would not buy from dem on the Sabbath, or on a holy day; and that we would forego the seventh year, and the exaction of every debt.
Also we made ordinances for ourselves, to charge ourselves yearly with the third part of a shekel for the service of the house of our God;

for the show bread, for the continual meal offering, for the continual burnt offering, for the Sabbaths, for the new moons, for the set feasts, and for the holy things, and for the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.

We throw lots, the priests, the Levites, and the people, for the wood offering, to bring it into the house of our God, according to our fathers’ houses, at times appointed, year by year, to burn on Baba God our God’s altar, as it is written in the law;
and to bring the first fruits of our ground, and the first fruits of all fruit of all kinds of trees, year by year, to Baba God’s house;

also the firstborn of our sons, and of our livestock, as it is written in the law, and the firstborn of our herds and of our flocks, to bring to the house of our God, to the priests who minister in the house of our God;

and that we should bring the first fruits of our dough, our wave offerings, the fruit of all kinds of trees, and the new wine and the oil, to the priests, to the rooms of the house of our God; and the tithes of our ground to the Levites; for dem, the Levites, take the tithes in all the cities of our tillage.
The priest the son of Aaron go be with the Levites, when the Levites take tithes. The Levites shall bring up the tithe of the tithes to the house of our God, to the rooms, into the treasure house.

For the pikin dem of Israel and the pikin dem of Levi shall bring the wave offering of the grain, of the new wine, and of the oil, to the rooms, where the vessels of the sanctuary are, and the priests who minister, with the porters and the singers. We go not forsake the house of our God.
The princes of the people lived in Jerusalem. The rest of the people also throw lots, to bring one of ten to live in Jerusalem the holy city, and nine parts in the other cities.
The people blessed all the men who willingly offered themselves to live in Jerusalem.

Now these are the chiefs of the province who lived in Jerusalem; but in the cities of Judah everyone lived in his possession in dem cities: Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple workers, and the pikin dem of Solomon’s workers.

Some of the pikin dem of Judah and of the pikin dem of Benjamin lived in Jerusalem. Of the pikin dem of Judah: Athaiah the son of Uzziah, the son of Zechariah, the son of Amariah, the son of Shephatiah, the son of Mahalalel, of the pikin dem of Perez;
and Maaseiah the son of Baruch, the son of Colhozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, the son of the Shilonite.
All the sons of Perez who lived in Jerusalem were four hundred sixty-eight valiant men.
These are the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jeshaiah.
After him Gabbai, Sallai, nine hundred twenty-eight.
Joel the son of Zichri was dem overseer; and Judah the son of Hassenuah was second over the city.
Of the priests: Jedaiah the son of Joiarib, Jachin,
Seraiah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the ruler of God’s house,

and dem brothers who did the work of the house, eight hundred twenty-two; and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pelaliah, the son of Amzi, the son of Zechariah, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah,
and his brothers, chiefs of fathers’ households, two hundred forty-two; and Amashsai the son of Azarel, the son of Ahzai, the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer,
and dem brothers, mighty men of valor, one hundred twenty-eight; and dem overseer was Zabdiel, the son of Haggedolim.
Of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Bunni;
and Shabbethai and Jozabad, of the chiefs of the Levites, who had the oversight of the outward business of God’s house;

and Mattaniah the son of Mica, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph, who was the chief to begin the thanksgiving in prayer, and Bakbukiah, the second among his brothers; and Abda the son of Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun.
All the Levites in the holy city were two hundred eighty-four.
Moreover the porters, Akkub, Talmon, and dem brothers, who kept watch at the gates, were one hundred seventy-two.
The residue of Israel, of the priests, the Levites, were in all the cities of Judah, everyone in his inheritance.
But the temple workers lived in Ophel: and Ziha and Gishpa were over the temple workers.

The overseer also of the Levites at Jerusalem was Uzzi the son of Bani, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Mica, of the sons of Asaph, the singers, over the business of God’s house.
For there was a commandment from the king concerning dem, and a settled provision for the singers, as every day required.
Pethahiah the son of Meshezabel, of the pikin dem of Zerah the son of Judah, was at the king’s hand in all matters concerning the people.
As for the villages, with dem fields, some of the pikin dem of Judah lived in Kiriath Arba and its towns, in Dibon and its towns, in Jekabzeel and its villages,
in Jeshua, in Moladah, Beth Pelet,
in Hazar Shual, in Beersheba and its towns,
in Ziklag, in Meconah and in its towns,
in En Rimmon, in Zorah, in Jarmuth,
Zanoah, Adullam, and dem villages, Lachish and its fields, and Azekah and its towns. So dem encamped from Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom.
The pikin dem of Benjamin also lived from Geba onward, at Michmash and Aija, and at Bethel and its towns,
at Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
Lod, and Ono, the valley of craftsmen.
Of the Levites, certain divisions in Judah settled in Benjamin’s territory.
Now these are the priests and the Levites who go up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
Shemaiah, and Joiarib, Jedaiah.
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah. These were the chiefs of the priests and of dem brothers in the days of Jeshua.
Moreover the Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, who was over the thanksgiving, he and his brothers.
Also Bakbukiah and Unno, dem brothers, were close to dem according to dem offices.
Jeshua became the father of Joiakim, and Joiakim became the father of Eliashib, and Eliashib became the father of Joiada,
and Joiada became the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan became the father of Jaddua.
In the days of Joiakim were priests, heads of fathers’ households: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;
of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;
of Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph;
of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;
of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;
of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai;
of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan;
and of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;
of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;
of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel.
As for the Levites, in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, and Johanan, and Jaddua, there were recorded the heads of fathers’ households; also the priests, in the reign of Darius the Persian.
The sons of Levi, heads of fathers’ households, were written in the book of the chronicles, even until the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib.

The chiefs of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel, with dem brothers close to dem, to praise and Thank God, according to the commandment of David the man of God, watch next to watch.
Mattaniah, and Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, Akkub, were porters keeping the watch at the storehouses of the gates.
These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest and scribe.

At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, dem sought the Levites out of all dem places, to bring dem to Jerusalem, to keep the dedication with gladness, both with giving thanks, and with singing, with cymbals, stringed instruments, and with harps.
The sons of the singers gathered themselves together, both out of the plain around Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites;
also from Beth Gilgal, and out of the fields of Geba and Azmaveth: for the singers had built themselves villages around Jerusalem.
The priests and the Levites purified themselves; and dem purified the people, and the gates, and the wall.
Then I bring up the princes of Judah on the wall, and appointed two great companies who Thank God and go in procession. One go on the right hand on the wall toward the dung gate;
and after dem go Hoshaiah, with half of the princes of Judah,
and Azariah, Ezra, and Meshullam,
Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, Jeremiah,
and some of the priests’ sons with trumpets: Zechariah the son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Micaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph;
and his brothers, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God; and Ezra the scribe was before dem.
By the spring gate, and straight before dem, dem go up by the stairs of David’s city, at the ascent of the wall, above David’s house, even to the water gate eastward.
The other company of people wey Thank God go to meet dem, and I after dem, with the half of the people, on the wall, above the tower of the furnaces, even to the wide wall,
and above the gate of Ephraim, and by the old gate, and by the fish gate, and the tower of Hananel, and the tower of Hammeah, even to the sheep gate: and dem stood still in the gate of the guard.
So the two companies of people wey Thank God in God’s house stood, and I, and the half of the rulers with me;
and the priests, Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with trumpets;
and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. The singers sang loud, with Jezrahiah dem overseer.

Dem offered great sacrifices that day, and rejoiced; for God had made dem glad well-well with great gladness; and the women and the pikin dem also rejoiced; so that the gladness of Jerusalem was heard even far away.

On that day were men appointed over the rooms for the treasures, for the wave offerings, for the first fruits, and for the tithes, to gather into dem, according to the fields of the cities, the portions appointed by the law for the priests and Levites; for Judah rejoiced for the priests and for the Levites who waited.
Dem performed the duty of dem God, and the duty of the purification, and so did the singers and the porters, according to the commandment of David, and of Solomon his son.
For in the days of David and Asaph of old there was a chief of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.

All Israel in the days of Zerubbabel, and in the days of Nehemiah, give the portions of the singers and the porters, as every day required; and dem set apart that which was for the Levites; and the Levites set apart that which was for the sons of Aaron.
On that day dem read in the book of Moses in the hearing of the people; and it was find written in it that an Ammonite and a Moabite no suppose enter into the assembly of God forever,
because dem didn’t meet the pikin dem of Israel with bread and with water, but hired Balaam against dem, to curse dem; however our God turned the curse into a blessing.
E happen say, when dem had heard the law, that dem separated all the mixed plenty people from Israel.
Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the rooms of the house of our God, being allied to Tobiah,

had prepared for him a great room, where before dem laid the meal offerings, the frankincense, the vessels, and the tithes of the grain, the new wine, and the oil, which were given by commandment to the Levites, the singers, and the porters; and the wave offerings for the priests.
But in all this, I No be at Jerusalem; for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I go to the king; and after some days I ask leave of the king,
and I come to Jerusalem, and understand the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, in preparing him a room in the courts of God’s house.
It grieved me severely. So I threw all Tobiah’s household stuff out of the room.
Then I commanded, and dem cleansed the rooms. I bring into dem the vessels of God’s house, with the meal offerings and the frankincense again.
I perceived that the portions of the Levites had not been given dem; so that the Levites and the singers, who did the work, had each fled to his field.
Then I contended with the rulers, and talk say, “Why is God’s house forsaken?” I gathered dem together, and set dem in dem place.
Then all Judah bring the tithe of the grain, the new wine, and the oil to the treasuries.
