I made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah: and next to dem was Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah; for dem were counted faithful, and dem business was to distribute to dem brothers.
Remember me, my God, concerning this, and no wipe out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for its observances.

In those days see I in Judah some men treading wine presses on the Sabbath, bringing in sheaves, and loading donkeys; also with wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of burdens, which dem bring into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day; and I testified against dem in the day in which dem sold chop.
Some men of Tyre also lived there, who bring in fish and all kinds of wares, and sold on the Sabbath to the pikin dem of Judah, and in Jerusalem.
Then I contended with the nobles of Judah, and talk say to dem, “What evil thing is this that you do, and profane the Sabbath day?
Didn’t una fathers do thus, and didn’t our God bring all this evil on us, and on this city? Yet you bring more serious anger on Israel by profaning the Sabbath.”

E happen say that when the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the Sabbath, I commanded that the doors should be shut, and commanded that dem no suppose be opened until after the Sabbath. I set some of my workers over the gates, so that no burden should be bring in on the Sabbath day.
So the merchants and sellers of all kinds of wares camped outside of Jerusalem once or twice.
Then I testified against dem, and talk say to dem, “Why do you stay around the wall? If you do so again, I go lay hands on you.” From that time on, dem didn’t come on the Sabbath.

I commanded the Levites that dem should purify themselves, and that dem should come and keep the gates, to sanctify the Sabbath day. Remember to me, my God, this also, and spare me according to the greatness of una loving kindness.
In those days I also see the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab;
and dem pikin dem spoke half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language, but according to the language of each people.

I contended with dem, and cursed dem, and struck certain of dem, and plucked off dem hair, and made dem swear by God, “You no go give una daughters to dem sons, nor take dem daughters for una sons, or for unaself.

Didn’t Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? Yet among many nations was there no king like him, and he was beloved of his God, and God made him king over all Israel. Nevertheless foreign women caused even him to sin.
Shall we then listen to you to do all this great evil, to trespass against our God in marrying foreign women?”
One of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite; so I chased him from me.
Remember dem, my God, because dem have defiled the priesthood, and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.
Thus I cleansed dem from all foreigners, and appointed duties for the priests and for the Levites, everyone in his work;
and for the wood offering, at times appointed, and for the first fruits. Remember me, my God, for good.
Now in the days of Ahasuerus (this is Ahasuerus who reigned from India even to Ethiopia, over one hundred twenty-seven provinces),
in those days, when the King Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom, which was in Shushan the palace,
in the third year of his reign, he made a feast for all his princes and his workers; the power of Persia and Media, the nobles and princes of the provinces, being before him.
He displayed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the honor of his excellent majesty many days, even one hundred eighty days.
When these days were fulfilled, the king made a seven day feast for all the people who were present in Shushan the palace, both great and small, in the court of the garden of the king’s palace.

There were hangings of white, green, and blue material, fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings and marble pillars. The couches were of gold and silver, on a pavement of red, white, yellow, and black marble.
Dem give dem drinks in golden vessels of various kinds, including royal wine in abundance, according to the bounty of the king.
In accordance with the law, the drinking No be compulsory; for so the king had instructed all the officials of his house, that dem should do according to every man’s pleasure.
Also Vashti the queen made a feast for the women in the royal house which belonged to King Ahasuerus.

On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was merry with wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, and Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcass, the seven eunuchs who served in the presence of Ahasuerus the king,
to bring Vashti the queen before the king with the royal crown, to show the people and the princes her beauty; for she was beautiful.
But the queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s commandment by the eunuchs. So the king was very angry, and his anger burned in him.
Then the king talk say to the wise men, who know the times (for it was the king’s custom to consult people wey know law and judgment;
and the next to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media, who see the king’s face, and sat first in the kingdom),
“What shall we do to the queen Vashti according to law, because she has not done the bidding of the King Ahasuerus by the eunuchs?”

Memucan answer before the king and the princes, “Vashti the queen has not done wrong to just the king, but also to all the princes, and to all the people Wey be in all the provinces of the King Ahasuerus.

For this deed of the queen will become known to all women, causing dem to show contempt for dem husbands, when it is reported, ‘King Ahasuerus commanded Vashti the queen to be bring in before him, but she didn’t come.’
Today, the princesses of Persia and Media who have heard of the queen’s deed will tell all the king’s princes. This will cause much contempt and serious anger.

“If it please the king, let a royal commandment go from him, and let it be written among the laws of the Persians and the Medes, so that it cannot be altered, that Vashti may never again come before King Ahasuerus; and let the king give her royal estate to another Wey be better than she.
When the king’s decree which he shall make is published throughout all his kingdom (for it is great), all the wives will give dem husbands honor, both great and small.”
This advice pleased the king and the princes, and the king did according to the word of Memucan:

for he sent letters into all the king’s provinces, into every province according to its writing, and to every people in dem language, that every man should rule his own house, speaking in the language of his own people.
After these things, when the serious anger of King Ahasuerus was pacified, he remember Vashti, and what she had done, and what was decreed against her.
Then the king’s workers who served him talk say, “Let beautiful young virgins be sought for the king.

Let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that dem may gather together all the beautiful young virgins to the citadel of Susa, to the women’s house, to the custody of Hegai the king’s eunuch, keeper of the women. Let cosmetics be given dem;
and let the maiden who pleases the king be queen instead of Vashti.” The thing pleased the king, and he did so.
There was a certain Jew in the citadel of Susa, whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite,
who Bin dey carried away from Jerusalem with the captives who Bin dey carried away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away.

He bring up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle’s daughter; for she had neither father nor mother. The maiden was fair and beautiful; and when her father and mother were dead, Mordecai take her for his own daughter.

So, when the king’s commandment and his decree was heard, and when many maidens were gathered together to the citadel of Susa, to the custody of Hegai, Esther was taken into the king’s house, to the custody of Hegai, keeper of the women.

The maiden pleased him, and she obtained kindness from him. He sharp-sharp give her cosmetics and her portions of chop, and the seven choice maidens who were to be given her out of the king’s house. He moved her and her maidens to the best place in the women’s house.
Esther had not made known her people nor her relatives, because Mordecai had instructed her that she no suppose make it known.
Mordecai walked every day in front of the court of the women’s house, to find out how Esther was doing, and what would become of her.

Each young woman’s turn come to go in to King Ahasuerus after her purification for twelve months (for so were the days of dem purification accomplished, six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with sweet fragrances and with preparations for beautifying women).
The young woman then come to the king like this: Anything wey she desired was given her to go with her out of the women’s house to the king’s house.

In the evening she go, and on the next day she come back into the second women’s house, to the custody of Shaashgaz, the king’s eunuch, who kept the concubines. She come in to the king no more, unless the king delighted in her, and she was call by name.

Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter, come to go in to the king, she required nothing but what Hegai the king’s eunuch, the keeper of the women, advised. Esther obtained favor in the sight of all people wey looked at her.
So Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus into his royal house in the tenth month, which is the month Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.

The king love Esther more than all the women, and she obtained favor and kindness in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he set the royal crown on her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti.
Then the king made a great feast for all his princes and his workers, even Esther’s feast; and he proclaimed a holiday in the provinces, and give gifts according to the king’s bounty.
When the virgins were gathered together the second time, Mordecai was sitting in the king’s gate.
Esther had not yet made known her relatives nor her people, as Mordecai had commanded her; for Esther obeyed Mordecai, like she did when she was bring up by him.
In those days, while Mordecai was sitting in the king’s gate, two of the king’s eunuchs, Bigthan and Teresh, who were doorkeepers, were angry, and sought to lay hands on the King Ahasuerus.
This thing became known to Mordecai, who informed Esther the queen; and Esther informed the king in Mordecai’s name.
When this matter was investigated, and it was find to be so, dem were both hanged on a tree; and it was written in the book of the chronicles in the king’s presence.
After these things King Ahasuerus promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes who were with him.
All the king’s workers who were in the king’s gate bowed down, and paid homage to Haman; for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai didn’t bow down or pay him homage.
Then the king’s workers, who were in the king’s gate, talk say to Mordecai, “Why do you disobey the king’s commandment?”
Now E happen say, when dem spoke daily to him, and he didn’t listen to dem, that dem told Haman, to see whether Mordecai’s reason would stand; for he had told dem that he was a Jew.
When Haman see that Mordecai didn’t bow down, nor pay him homage, Haman was full of serious anger.

But he scorned the thought of laying hands on Mordecai alone, for dem had made known to him Mordecai’s people. So Haman sought to destroy all the Jews who were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, even Mordecai’s people.

In the first month, which is the month Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, dem throw Pur, that is, the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month, and chose the twelfth month, which is the month Adar.

Haman talk say to King Ahasuerus, “E get a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the peoples in all the provinces of una kingdom, and dem laws are different than other people’s. Dem no keep the king’s laws. So it No be for the king’s profit to allow dem to remain.

If it pleases the king, let it be written that dem be destroyed; and I go pay ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of people Wey in charge of the king’s business, to bring it into the king’s treasuries.”
The king take his ring from his hand, and give it to Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews’ enemy.
The king talk say to Haman, “The silver is given to you, the people also, to do with dem as it seems good to you.”

Then the king’s scribes were call in on the first month, on the thirteenth day of the month; and all that Haman commanded was written to the king’s satraps, and to the governors who were over every province, and to the princes of every people, to every province according to its writing, and to every people in dem language. It was written in the name of King Ahasuerus, and it was sealed with the king’s ring.

Letters were sent by couriers into all the king’s provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Jews, both young and old, little pikin dem and women, in one day, even on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, and to plunder dem possessions.
A copy of the letter, that the decree should be given out in every province, was published to all the peoples, that dem should be ready against that day.
The couriers go out in haste by the king’s commandment, and the decree was given out in the citadel of Susa. The king and Haman sat down to drink; but the city of Shushan was perplexed.
Now when Mordecai find out all that was done, Mordecai tore his clothes, and put on sackcloth with ashes, and go out into the middle of the city, and wailed loudly and a bitterly.
He come even before the king’s gate, for Nobody is allowed inside the king’s gate clothed with sackcloth.
In every province, Anywhere wey the king’s commandment and his decree come, there was great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
Esther’s maidens and her eunuchs come and told her this, and the queen was exceedingly grieved. She sent clothing to Mordecai, to replace his sackcloth; but he didn’t receive it.
Then Esther call for Hathach, one of the king’s eunuchs, whom he had appointed to attend her, and commanded him to go to Mordecai, to find out what this was, and why it was.
So Hathach go out to Mordecai, to city square which was before the king’s gate.
Mordecai told him of all that had happened to him, and the exact sum of the money that Haman had promised to pay to the king’s treasuries for the destruction of the Jews.

He also give him the copy of the writing of the decree that was given out in Shushan to destroy dem, to show it to Esther, and to declare it to her, and to urge her to go in to the king, to make supplication to him, and to make request before him, for her people.
Hathach come and told Esther the words of Mordecai.
Then Esther spoke to Hathach, and give him a message to Mordecai:

“All the king’s workers, and the people of the king’s provinces, know, that Anybody wey, whether man or woman, comes to the king into the inner court without being call, E get one law for him, that he be put to death, except those to whom the king might hold out the golden scepter, that he may live. I have not been call to come in to the king these thirty days.”
Dem told to Mordecai Esther’s words.
Then Mordecai ask dem return answer to Esther, “No think to yourself that You go escape in the king’s house any more than all the Jews.

For if you remain silent now, then relief and deliverance will come to the Jews from another place, but you and una father’s house will perish. Wey know if you haven’t come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”
Then Esther ask dem to answer Mordecai,

“Go, gather together all the Jews Wey be present in Shushan, and fast for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day. I and my maidens will also fast the same way. Then I go go in to the king, which is against the law; and if I perish, I perish.”
So Mordecai go his way, and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.

Now on the third day, Esther put on her royal clothing, and stood in the inner court of the king’s house, next to the king’s house. The king sat on his royal throne in the royal house, next to the entrance of the house.

When the king see Esther the queen standing in the court, she obtained favor in his sight; and the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand. So Esther come near, and touched the top of the scepter.
Then the king ask her, “What would you like, queen Esther? Wetin be una request? It go be given you even to the half of the kingdom.”
Esther talk say, “If it seems good to the king, let the king and Haman come today to the banquet that I have prepared for him.”
Then the king talk say, “Bring Haman sharp-sharp, so that it may be done as Esther has talk say.” So the king and Haman come to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
The king talk say to Esther at the banquet of wine, “Wetin be una petition? It go be granted you. Wetin be una request? Even to the half of the kingdom it go be performed.”
Then Esther answer and talk say, “My petition and my request is this.

If I have find favor in the sight of the king, and if it please the king to grant my petition and to perform my request, let the king and Haman come to the banquet that I go prepare for dem, and I go do tomorrow as the king has talk say.”
Then Haman go out that day joyful and glad of heart, but when Haman see Mordecai in the king’s gate, that he didn’t stand up nor move for him, he was filled with serious anger against Mordecai.
Nevertheless Haman restrained imself, and go home. There, he sent and call for his friends and Zeresh his wife.

Haman recounted to dem the glory of his riches, the plenty people of his pikin dem, all the things in which the king had promoted him, and how he had advanced him above the princes and workers of the king.
Haman also talk say, “Yes, Esther the queen let no man come in with the king to the banquet that she had prepared but myself; and tomorrow I be also invited by her together with the king.
Yet all this avails me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king’s gate.”

Then Zeresh his wife and all his friends talk say to him, “Let a gallows be made fifty cubits high, and in the morning speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on it. Then go in merrily with the king to the banquet.” This pleased Haman, so he had the gallows made.
On that night, the king no fit sleep. He commanded the book of records of the chronicles to be bring, and dem were read to the king.
It was find written that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs, who were doorkeepers, who had tried to lay hands on the King Ahasuerus.
The king talk say, “What honor and dignity Don dey given to Mordecai for this?” Then the king’s workers who attended him talk say, “Nothing Don dey done for him.”
The king talk say, “Wey be in the court?” Now Haman had come into the outer court of the king’s house, to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows that he had prepared for him.
The king’s workers talk say to him, “See am, Haman stands in the court.” The king talk say, “Make e come in.”
So Haman come in. The king talk say to him, “What go be done to the man whom the king delights to honor?” Now Haman talk say in his heart, “Who would the king delight to honor more than myself?”
Haman talk say to the king, “For the man whom the king delights to honor,
let royal clothing be bring which the king uses to wear, and the horse that the king rides on, and on the head of which a crown royal is set.

Let the clothing and the horse be delivered to the hand of one of the king’s most noble princes, that dem may array the man whom the king delights to honor with dem, and have him ride on horseback through the city square, and proclaim before him, ‘Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!’”

Then the king talk say to Haman, “Hurry and take the clothing and the horse, as you have talk say, and do this for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king’s gate. Let nothing fail of all that you have spoken.”

Then Haman take the clothing and the horse, and arrayed Mordecai, and had him ride through the city square, and proclaimed before him, “Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!”
Mordecai come back to the king’s gate, but Haman hurried to his house, mourning and having his head covered.

Haman recounted to Zeresh his wife and all his friends everything that had happened to him. Then his wise men and Zeresh his wife talk say to him, “If Mordecai, before whom you have begun to fall, is of Jewish descent, You go not prevail against him, but You go surely fall before him.”
While dem were yet talking with him, the king’s eunuchs come, and hurried to bring Haman to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
So the king and Haman come to banquet with Esther the queen.

The king talk say again to Esther on the second day at the banquet of wine, “Wetin be una petition, queen Esther? It go be granted you. Wetin be una request? Even to the half of the kingdom it go be performed.”
Then Esther the queen answer, “If I have find favor in una sight, O king, and if it please the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request.

For We be sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we Bin dey sold for male and female slaves, I would have held my peace, although the adversary could not have compensated for the king’s loss.”
Then King Ahasuerus talk say to Esther the queen, “Wey be he, and where is person wey dared presume in his heart to do so?”
Esther talk say, “An adversary and an enemy, even this wicked Haman!” Then Haman was afraid before the king and the queen.

The king arose in his serious anger from the banquet of wine and go into the palace garden. Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther the queen; for he see that there was evil determined against him by the king.

Then the king come back out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman had fallen on the couch where Esther was. Then the king talk say, “Will he even assault the queen in front of me in the house?” As the word go out of the king’s mouth, dem covered Haman’s face.

Then Harbonah, one of the eunuchs who were with the king talk say, “See am, the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman has made for Mordecai, who spoke good for the king, is standing at Haman’s house.” The king talk say, “Hang him on it!”
So dem hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king’s serious anger pacified.
On that day, King Ahasuerus give the house of Haman, the Jews’ enemy, to Esther the queen. Mordecai come before the king; for Esther had told what he was to her.
The king take off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and give it to Mordecai. Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.
Esther spoke yet again before the king, and fell down at his feet, and begged him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite, and his device that he had devised against the Jews.
Then the king held out to Esther the golden scepter. So Esther arose, and stood before the king.

She talk say, “If it pleases the king, and if I have find favor in his sight, and the thing seem right to the king, and I be pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews Wey be in all the king’s provinces.
For how can I endure to see the evil that would come to my people? How can I endure to see the destruction of my relatives?”
Then King Ahasuerus talk say to Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Jew, “See, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and him dem have hanged on the gallows, because he laid his hand on the Jews.

Write also to the Jews, as it pleases you, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s ring; for the writing which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring, may not be reversed by any man.”

Then the king’s scribes were call at that time, in the third month, which is the month Sivan, on the twenty-third day of the month; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded to the Jews, and to the satraps, and the governors and princes of the provinces which are from India to Ethiopia, one hundred twenty-seven provinces, to every province according to its writing, and to every people in dem language, and to the Jews in dem writing, and in dem language.
He wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, and sealed it with the king’s ring, and sent letters by courier on horseback, riding on royal horses that were bred from swift steeds.

In those letters, the king granted the Jews who were in every city to gather themselves together, and to defend dem life, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all the power of the people and province that would assault dem, dem little ones and women, and to plunder dem possessions,
on one day in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar.
A copy of the letter, that the decree should be given out in every province, was published to all the peoples, that the Jews should be ready for that day to avenge themselves on dem enemies.
So the couriers who rode on royal horses go out, hastened and pressed on by the king’s commandment. The decree was given out in the citadel of Susa.
Mordecai go out of the presence of the king in royal clothing of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a robe of fine linen and purple; and the city of Susa shouted and was glad.
The Jews had light, gladness, gladness, and honor.

In every province, and in every city, Anywhere wey the king’s commandment and his decree come, the Jews had gladness, gladness, a feast, and a good day. Many from among the peoples of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews was fallen on dem.

Now in the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the month, when the king’s commandment and his decree come near to be put in execution, on the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to conquer dem, (but it was turned out the opposite happened, that the Jews conquered people wey hated dem),

the Jews gathered themselves together in dem cities throughout all the provinces of the King Ahasuerus, to lay hands on people wey want to harm dem. Nobody could withstand dem, because the fear of dem had fallen on all the people.
All the princes of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and people wey did the king’s business helped the Jews, because the fear of Mordecai had fallen on dem.
For Mordecai was great in the king’s house, and his fame go out throughout all the provinces; for the man Mordecai grew greater and greater.
The Jews struck all dem enemies with the stroke of the sword, and with slaughter and destruction, and did Wetin dem want to people wey hated dem.
In the citadel of Susa, the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men.
Dem killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,
Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,
Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha,
the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Jews’ enemy, but dem didn’t lay dem hand on the plunder.
On that day, the number of people wey were slain in the citadel of Susa was bring before the king.

The king talk say to Esther the queen, “The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in the citadel of Susa, including the ten sons of Haman; what then have dem done in the rest of the king’s provinces! Now Wetin be una petition? It go be granted you. Wetin be una further request? It go be done.”
Then Esther talk say, “If it pleases the king, let it be granted to the Jews Wey be in Shushan to do tomorrow also according to today’s decree, and let Haman’s ten sons be hanged on the gallows.”
The king commanded this to be done. A decree was given out in Shushan; and dem hanged Haman’s ten sons.
The Jews who were in Shushan gathered themselves together on the fourteenth day also of the month Adar, and killed three hundred men in Shushan; but dem didn’t lay dem hand on the plunder.

The other Jews who were in the king’s provinces gathered themselves together, defended dem lives, had rest from dem enemies, and killed seventy-five thousand of people wey hated dem; but dem didn’t lay dem hand on the plunder.
This was done on the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and on the fourteenth day of that month dem rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

But the Jews who were in Shushan assembled together on the thirteenth and on the fourteenth days of the month; and on the fifteenth day of that month, dem rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
So the Jews of the villages, who live in the unwalled towns, make the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of gladness and feasting, a good day, and a day of sending presents of chop to each other.
Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters to all the Jews who were in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, both near and far,
to enjoin dem that dem should keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month Adar yearly,

as the days in which the Jews had rest from dem enemies, and the month which was turned to dem from sorrow to gladness, and from mourning into a good day; that dem should make dem days of feasting and gladness, and of sending presents of chop to each other, and gifts to the needy.
The Jews accepted the custom that dem had begun, as Mordecai had written to dem;
because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy dem, and had throw “Pur”, that is the lot, to consume dem, and to destroy dem;

but when this became known to the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he had devised against the Jews, should return on his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.
So dem call these days “Purim”, from the word “Pur.” So because of all the words of this letter, and of that which dem had seen concerning this matter, and that which had come to dem,

the Jews established, and imposed on themselves, and on dem descendants, and on all people wey joined themselves to dem, so that it no suppose fail, that dem would keep these two days according to what was written, and according to its appointed time, every year;

and that these days should be remember and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim no suppose fail from among the Jews, nor dem memory perish from dem offspring,
Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.
He sent letters to all the Jews, to the hundred twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, with words of peace and truth,

to confirm these days of Purim in dem appointed times, as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had decreed, and as dem had imposed upon themselves and dem descendants, in the matter of the fastings and dem cry.
The commandment of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim; and it was written in the book.
King Ahasuerus laid a tribute on the land, and on the islands of the sea.

All the acts of his power and of his might, and the full account of the greatness of Mordecai, to which the king advanced him, no be dem written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?

For Mordecai the Jew was next to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted by the plenty people of his brothers, seeking the good of his people, and speaking peace to all his descendants.
There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.
There were born to him seven sons and three daughters.

His possessions also were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and a plenty well-well household; so that this man was the greatest of all the pikin dem of the east.
His sons go and held a feast in the house of each one on his birthday; and dem sent and call for dem three sisters to eat and to drink with dem.

It was so, when the days of dem feasting had run dem course, that Job sent and sanctified dem, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of dem all. For Job talk say, “It may be that my sons have sinned, and renounced God in dem hearts.” Job did so continually.
Now on the day when God’s sons come to present themselves before Baba God, Satan also come among dem.
Baba God talk say to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Then Satan answer Baba God, and talk say, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”
Baba God talk say to Satan, “Have you considered my worker, Job? For E get Nobody like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil.”
Then Satan answer Baba God, and talk say, “Does Job fear God for nothing?
Haven’t you made a hedge around him, and around his house, and around all that he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.
But stretch out una hand now, and touch all that he has, and he will renounce you to una face.”
Baba God talk say to Satan, “See am, all that he has is in una power. Only on imself no stretch out una hand.” So Satan go out from the presence of Baba God.
It fell on a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in dem oldest brother’s house,
that there come a messenger to Job, and talk say, “The oxen were plowing, and the donkeys feeding beside dem,
and the Sabeans attacked, and take dem away. Yes, dem have killed the workers with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”

While he was still speaking, there also come another, and talk say, “The fire of God has fallen from the sky, and has burned up the sheep and the workers, and consumed dem, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”

While he was still speaking, there come also another, and talk say, “The Chaldeans made three bands, and swept down on the camels, and have taken dem away, yes, and killed the workers with the edge of the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
While he was still speaking, there come also another, and talk say, “Una sons and una daughters were eating and drinking wine in dem oldest brother’s house,
and see am, there come a great wind from the wilderness, and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young men, and Dem be dead. I alone have escaped to tell you.”
Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshiped.
He talk say, “Naked I come out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return there. Baba God give, and Baba God has taken away. Blessed be Baba God’s name.”
In all this, Job No sin, nor charge God with wrongdoing.
Again, on the day when the God’s sons come to present themselves before Baba God, Satan come also among dem to present imself before Baba God.
Baba God talk say to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answer Baba God, and talk say, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”

Baba God talk say to Satan, “Have you considered my worker Job? For E get Nobody like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil. He still maintains his integrity, although you incited me against him, to ruin him without cause.”
Satan answer Baba God, and talk say, “Skin for skin. Yes, all that a man has he will give for his life.
But stretch out una hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will renounce you to una face.”
Baba God talk say to Satan, “See am, he is in una hand. Only spare his life.”
So Satan go out from the presence of Baba God, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.
He take for imself a potsherd to scrape imself with, and he sat among the ashes.
Then his wife talk say to him, “Do you still maintain una integrity? Renounce God, and die.”
But E tell am say, “You speak as one of the foolish women would speak. What? Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” In all this Job didn’t sin with his lips.

Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, dem each come from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and dem made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him.
When dem lifted up dem eyes from a distance, and didn’t recognize him, dem raised dem voices, and wept; and dem each tore his robe, and sprinkled dust on dem heads toward the sky.
So dem sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and Nobody spoke a word to him, for dem see that his grief was plenty well-well.
After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed the day of his birth.
Job answer:
“Let the day perish in which I was born, the night which talk say, ‘E get a boy conceived.’
Let that day be darkness. No let God from above seek for it, neither let the light shine on it.
Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for dem own. Let a cloud live on it. Let all that makes black the day terrify it.
As for that night, let thick darkness seize on it. Let it not glad well-well among the days of the year. Let it not come into the number of the months.
See am, let that night be barren. Let no joyful voice come inside am.
Make dem curse it who curse the day, Wey be ready to rouse up leviathan.
Let the stars of its twilight be dark. Let it look for light, but have none, neither let it see the eyelids of the morning,
because it didn’t shut up the doors of my mother’s womb, nor did it hide trouble from my eyes.
“Why didn’t I die from the womb? Why didn’t I give up the spirit when my mother bore me?
Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breast, that I should nurse?
For now should I have lain down and been quiet. I should have slept, then I would Don dey at rest,
with kings and counselors of the earth, who built up waste places for themselves;
or with princes who had gold, who filled dem houses with silver:
or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, as infants who never see light.
There the wicked cease from troubling. There the weary are at rest.
There the prisoners are at ease together. Dem no hear the voice of the taskmaster.
The small and the great are there. The worker is free from his master.
“Why is light given to him Wey be in misery, life to the bitter in soul,
Who long for death, but it no dey come; and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,
who glad well-well exceedingly, and are glad, when dem can find the grave?
Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
For my sighing comes before I eat. My groanings are poured out like water.
For the thing which I fear comes on me, That which I be afraid of comes to me.
I be not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither have I rest; but trouble comes.”
Then Eliphaz the Temanite answer,
“If someone ventures to talk with you, will you be grieved? But who can withhold imself from speaking?
See am, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the weak hands.
Una words have supported him who was falling, You have made firm the feeble knees.
But now it has come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and You be troubled.
No be una piety una confidence? No be the integrity of una ways una hope?
“Remember, now, Anybody wey perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?
According to what I have seen, people wey plow wickedness, and sow trouble, reap the same.
By the breath of God dem perish. By the blast of his anger are dem consumed.
The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, the teeth of the young lions, are broken.
The old lion perishes for lack of prey. The cubs of the lioness are scattered abroad.
“Now a thing was secretly bring to me. My ear received a whisper of it.
In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men,
fear come on me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake.
Then a spirit passed before my face. The hair of my flesh stood up.
It stood still, but I no fit discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes. Silence, then I heard a voice, saying,
‘Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?
See am, he puts no trust in his workers. He charges his angels with error.
How much more, people wey live in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, Wey be crushed before the moth!
Between morning and evening Dem be destroyed. Dem perish forever without any regarding it.
No be dem tent cord plucked up within dem? Dem die, and that without wisdom.’
“Call now; is there any who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
For resentment kills the foolish man, and jealousy kills the simple.
I have seen the foolish taking root, but suddenly I cursed his habitation.
His pikin dem are far from safety. Dem be crushed in the gate. Neither is there any to deliver dem,
whose harvest the hungry eats up, and take it even out of the thorns. The snare gapes for dem substance.
For suffering no dey come out of the dust, neither does trouble spring out of the ground;
but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.
“But as for me, I would seek God. I would commit my cause to God,
wey do great things that no fit be fathomed, marvelous things without number;
wey dey give rain on the earth, and sends waters on the fields;
so that he sets up on high people Wey low, people wey mourn are exalted to safety.
He frustrates the devices of the crafty, So that dem hands no fit perform dem enterprise.
He takes the wise in dem own craftiness; the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.
Dem meet with darkness in the day time, and grope at noonday as in the night.
But he saves from the sword of dem mouth, even the needy from the hand of the mighty.
So the poor has hope, and injustice shuts her mouth.
“See am, happy is the man whom God corrects. So No despise the chastening of the Almighty.
For he wounds, and binds up. He injures, and his hands make whole.
He will deliver you in six troubles; yes, in seven no evil shall touch you.
In famine he will redeem you from death; in war, from the power of the sword.
You go be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, neither shall you be afraid of destruction when it comes.
At destruction and famine you shall laugh, neither shall you be afraid of the animals of the earth.
For you go be allied with the stones of the field. The animals of the field go be at peace with you.
You shall know that una tent is in peace. You shall visit una fold, and shall miss nothing.
You shall know also that una offspring go be great, Una offspring as the grass of the earth.
You shall come to una grave in a full age, like a shock of grain comes in its season.
Look this, we have searched it, so it is. Hear it, and know it for una good.”
Then Job answer,
“Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!
For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, so have my words been rash.
For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up dem poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.
Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?
Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
My soul refuses to touch dem. Dem be as loathsome chop to me.
“Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,
even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
Be it still my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that no dey spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
Wetin be my strength, that I should wait? Wetin be my end, that I should be patient?
Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass?
No be it that I have no help in me, That wisdom is driven quite from me?
“To him Wey be ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;
Which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.
In the dry season, dem vanish. When it is hot, Dem be consumed out of dem place.
The caravans that travel beside dem turn aside. Dem go up into the waste, and perish.
The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for dem.
Dem were distressed because dem were confident. Dem come there, and were confounded.
For now You be nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.
Did I say, ‘Give to me?’ or, ‘Offer a present for me from una substance?’
or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand?’ or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?’
“Teach me, and I go hold my peace. Cause me to understand where I have erred.
How forcible are words of uprightness! But una reproof, what does it reprove?
Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one Wey be desperate are as wind?
Yes, you would even throw lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of una friend.
Now so be pleased to look at me, for surely I no go lie to una face.
Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.
Is there injustice on my tongue? No fit my taste discern mischievous things?
“No be a man forced to labor on earth? No be his days like the days of a hired hand?
As a worker who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages,
so am I made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me.
When I lie down, I say, ‘When shall I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.
My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.
My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.
Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye shall no more see good.
The eye of him wey see me shall see me no more. Una eyes go be on me, but I no go be.
As the cloud is consumed and vanishes away, so person wey goes down to Sheol shall come up no more.
He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.
“So I go not keep silent. I go speak in the anguish of my spirit. I go complain in the bitterness of my soul.
Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?
When I say, ‘My bed shall comfort me. My couch shall ease my complaint;’
then you scare me with dreams, and terrify me through visions:
so that my soul chooses strangling, death rather than my bones.
I loathe my life. I no want to live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
Wetin be man, that you should magnify him, that you should set una mind on him,
that you should visit him every morning, and test him every moment?
How long will you not look away from me, nor leave me alone until I swallow down my spittle?
If I have sinned, what do I do to you, you watcher of men? Why have you set me as a mark for you, so that I be a burden to myself?
Why do you not pardon my disobedience, and take away my wickedness? For now shall I lie down in the dust. You go seek me diligently, but I no go be.”
Then Bildad the Shuhite answer,
“How long will you speak these things? Shall the words of una mouth be a mighty wind?
Does God pervert justice? Or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?
If una pikin dem have sinned against him, He has delivered dem into the hand of dem disobedience.
If you want to seek God diligently, make una supplication to the Almighty.
If you were pure and upright, surely now he would awaken for you, and make the habitation of una righteousness prosperous.
Though una beginning was small, yet una latter end would greatly increase.
“Please inquire of past generations. Find out about the learning of dem fathers.
(For We be but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days on earth are a shadow.)
Shall dem not teach you, tell you, and utter words out of dem heart?
“Can the papyrus grow up without mire? Can the rushes grow without water?
While it is yet in its greenness, not cut down, it withers before any other reed.
So are the paths of all who forget God. The hope of the godless man shall perish,
Whose confidence shall break apart, Whose trust is a spider’s web.
He shall lean on his house, but it no go stand. He shall cling to it, but it no go endure.
He is green before the sun. His shoots go out along his garden.
His roots are wrapped around the rock pile. He sees the place of stones.
If he is destroyed from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, ‘I have not seen you.’
See am, this is the gladness of his way: out of the earth, others shall spring.
“See am, God No go throw away a blameless man, neither will he uphold the evildoers.
He will still fill una mouth with laughter, una lips with shouting.
People wey hate you go be clothed with shame. The tent of the wicked go be no more.”
Then Job answer,
“Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?
If he is pleased to contend with him, he no fit answer him one time in a thousand.
God Wey be wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who has hardened imself against him, and prospered?
He removes the mountains, and dem no know it, when he overturns dem in his anger.
He shakes the earth out of its place. Its pillars tremble.
He commands the sun, and it no dey rise, and seals up the stars.
He alone stretches out the heavens, and treads on the waves of the sea.
He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the rooms of the south.
He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.
See am, he goes by me, and I no see him. He passes on also, but I no perceive him.
See am, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, ‘Wetin be you doing?’
“God No go withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.
How much less shall I answer him, And choose my words to argue with him?
Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn’t answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.
If I had call, and he had answer me, yet I wouldn’t believe that he listened to my voice.
For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.
He No go allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
If it is a matter of strength, see am, he is mighty! If of justice, ‘Who,’ says he, ‘will summon me?’
Though I be righteous, my own mouth shall condemn me. Though I be blameless, it shall prove me perverse.
I be blameless. I no respect myself. I despise my life.
“It is all the same. So I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.
If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.
The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then Wey be it?
“Now my days are swifter than a runner. Dem flee away, dem see no good.
Dem have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.
If I say, ‘I go forget my complaint, I go put off my sad face, and cheer up;’
I be afraid of all my sorrows, I know that You go not hold me innocent.
I go be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?
If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,
yet You go plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes shall abhor me.
For he No be a man, as I be, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.
E get no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.
Make e take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;
then I would speak, and not fear him, for I be not so in myself.
“My soul is weary of my life. I go give free course to my complaint. I go speak in the bitterness of my soul.
I go tell God, ‘No condemn me. Show me why you contend with me.
Is it good to you that you should oppress, that you should despise the work of una hands, and smile on the counsel of the wicked?
Do you have eyes of flesh? Or do you see as man sees?
Are una days as the days of mortals, or una years as man’s years,
that you inquire after my wickedness, and search after my sin?
Although you know that I be not wicked, E get Nobody who can deliver out of una hand.
“‘Una hands have framed me and fashioned me altogether, yet you destroy me.
Remember, I beg you, that you have fashioned me as clay. Will you bring me into dust again?
Haven’t you poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese?
You have clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.
You have granted me life and loving kindness. Una visitation has preserved my spirit.
Yet you hid these things in una heart. I know that this is with you:
if I sin, then you mark me. You go not acquit me from my wickedness.
If I be wicked, woe to me. If I be righteous, I still no go lift up my head, being filled with disgrace, and conscious of my suffering.
If my head is held high, you hunt me like a lion. Again you show yourself powerful to me.
You renew una witnesses against me, and increase una indignation on me. Changes and warfare are with me.
“‘Why, then, have you bring me out of the womb? I wish I had given up the spirit, and no eye had seen me.
I should Don dey as though I had not been. I should Don dey carried from the womb to the grave.
No be my days few? Cease then. Leave me alone, that I may find a little comfort,
before I go where I no go return from, to the land of darkness and of the shadow of death;
the land dark as midnight, of the shadow of death, without any order, where the light is as midnight.’”
Then Zophar, the Naamathite, answer,
“Shouldn’t the plenty people of words be answer? Should a man full of talk be justified?
Should una boastings make men hold dem peace? When you mock, shall no man make you ashamed?
For you say, ‘My doctrine is pure. I be clean in una eyes.’
But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against you,
that he would show you the secrets of wisdom! For true wisdom has two sides. Know so that God exacts of you less than una wickedness deserves.
“Can you fathom the mystery of God? Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?
Dem be high as heaven. What can you do? Dem be deeper than Sheol. What can you know?
Its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
If he passes by, or confines, or convenes a court, then who can oppose him?
For he knows false men. He sees wickedness also, even though he no dey consider it.
An empty-headed man becomes wise when a man is born as a wild donkey’s colt.
“If you set una heart aright, stretch out una hands toward him.
If wickedness is in una hand, put it far away. No let unrighteousness live in una tents.
Surely then you shall lift up una face without spot; Yes, you go be steadfast, and no go fear:
for you shall forget una misery. You shall remember it like waters that have passed away.
Life go be clearer than the noonday. Though E get darkness, it go be as the morning.
You go be secure, because E get hope. Yes, you shall search, and shall take una rest in safety.
Also you shall lie down, and Nobody shall make you afraid. Yes, many shall court una favor.
But the eyes of the wicked shall fail. Dem go get no way to flee. Dem hope go be the giving up of the spirit.”
Then Job answer,
“No doubt, but You be the people, and wisdom shall die with you.
But I have understanding as well as you; I be not inferior to you. Yes, who no dey know such things as these?
I be like one Wey be a joke to his neighbor, I, who call on God, and he answer. The just, the blameless man is a joke.
In the thought of him Wey be at ease E get contempt for misfortune. It is ready for dem whose foot slips.
The tents of robbers prosper. People wey provoke God are secure, who carry dem God in dem hands.
“But ask the animals, now, and dem shall teach you; the birds of the sky, and dem shall tell you.
Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach you. The fish of the sea shall declare to you.
Who no dey know that in all these, Baba God’s hand has done this,
in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind?
No dey the ear try words, even as the palate tastes its chop?
With aged men is wisdom, in length of days understanding.
“With God is wisdom and might. He has counsel and understanding.
See am, he breaks down, and it no fit be built again. He imprisons a man, and there can be no release.
See am, he withholds the waters, and dem dry up. Again, he sends dem out, and dem overturn the earth.
With him is strength and wisdom. The deceived and the deceiver are his.
He leads counselors away stripped. He makes judges fools.
He loosens the bond of kings. He binds dem waist with a belt.
He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty.
He removes the speech of people Wey trusted, and takes away the understanding of the elders.
He pours contempt on princes, and loosens the belt of the strong.
He uncovers deep things out of darkness, and brings out to light the shadow of death.
He increases the nations, and he destroys dem. He enlarges the nations, and he leads dem captive.
He takes away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth, and causes dem to wander in a wilderness where E get no way.
Dem grope in the dark without light. He makes dem stagger like a drunken man.
“See am, my eye has seen all this. My ear has heard and understand it.
Wetin you know, I know also. I be not inferior to you.
“Surely I would speak to the Almighty. I desire to reason with God.
But You be forgers of lies. You be all physicians of no value.
Oh that you would be completely silent! Then you would be wise.
Hear now my reasoning. Listen to the pleadings of my lips.
Will you speak unrighteously for God, and talk deceitfully for him?
Will you show partiality to him? Will you contend for God?
Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceives a man, will you deceive him?
He will surely reprove you, if you secretly show partiality.
No go his majesty make you afraid, And his dread fall on you?
Una memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, Una defenses are defenses of clay.
“Be silent, leave me alone, that I may speak. Let come on me what will.
Why should I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hand?
See am, he will kill me. I have no hope. Nevertheless, I go maintain my ways before him.
This also go be my salvation, that a godless man no go come before him.
Hear diligently my speech. Let my declaration be in una ears.
See now, I have set my cause in order. I know that I be righteous.
Wey be person wey will contend with me? For then would I hold my peace and give up the spirit.
“Only no do two things to me; then I go not hide myself from una face:
withdraw una hand far from me; and no let una terror make me afraid.
Then call, and I go answer; or let me speak, and you answer me.
How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my disobedience and my sin.
Why hide you una face, and hold me for una enemy?
Will you harass a driven leaf? Will you pursue the dry stubble?
For you write bitter things against me, and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth:
You also put my feet in the stocks, and mark all my paths. You set a bound to the soles of my feet,
though I be decaying like a rotten thing, like a garment that is moth-eaten.
“Man, Wey be born of a woman, is of few days, and full of trouble.
He grows up like a flower, and is cut down. He also flees like a shadow, and no dey continue.
Do you open una eyes on such a one, and bring me into judgment with you?
Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? Not one.
Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months is with you, and you have appointed his bounds that he no fit pass;
Look away from him, that he may rest, until he shall accomplish, as a hireling, his day.
“For E get hope for a tree, If it is cut down, that it will sprout again, that the tender branch of it No go cease.
Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stock dies in the ground,
yet through the scent of water it will bud, and sprout boughs like a plant.
But man dies, and is laid low. Yes, man gives up the spirit, and where is he?
As the waters fail from the sea, and the river wastes and dries up,
so man lies down and no dey rise. Until the heavens are no more, dem no go awake, nor be roused out of dem sleep.
“Oh that you would hide me in Sheol, that you would keep me secret, until una serious anger is past, that you would appoint me a set time, and remember me!
If a man dies, shall he live again? All the days of my warfare would I wait, until my release should come.
You would call, and I would answer you. You would have a desire to the work of una hands.
But now you count my steps. No you watch over my sin?
My disobedience is sealed up in a bag. You fasten up my wickedness.
“But the mountain falling comes to nothing. The rock is removed out of its place;
The waters wear the stones. The torrents of it wash away the dust of the earth. So you destroy the hope of man.
You forever prevail against him, and he departs. You change his face, and send him away.
His sons come to honor, and he no dey know it. Dem be bring low, but he no dey perceive it of dem.
But his flesh on him has pain, and his soul within him mourns.”
Then Eliphaz the Temanite answer,
“Should a wise man answer with vain knowledge, and fill imself with the east wind?
Should he reason with unprofitable talk, or with speeches with which he can do no good?
Yes, you do away with fear, and hinder devotion before God.
For una wickedness teaches una mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.
Una own mouth condemns you, and not I. Yes, una own lips testify against you.
“Are you the first man who was born? Or were you bring out before the hills?
Have you heard the secret counsel of God? Do you limit wisdom to yourself?
What do you know, that we no know? What do you understand, which No be in us?
With us are both the gray-headed and the very aged men, much elder than una father.
Are the consolations of God too small for you, even the word that is gentle toward you?
Why does una heart carry you away? Why do una eyes flash,
That you turn una spirit against God, and let such words go out of una mouth?
Wetin be man, that he should be clean? Wetin be person Wey born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
See am, he puts no trust in his holy ones. Yes, the heavens No be clean in his sight;
how much less one Wey be abominable and corrupt, a man who drinks wickedness like water!
“I go show you, listen to me; that which I have seen I go declare
(which wise men have told by dem fathers, and have not hidden it;
to whom alone the land was given, and no stranger passed among dem):
the wicked man writhes in pain all his days, even the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor.
A sound of terrors is in his ears. In prosperity the destroyer shall come on him.
He no dey believe that he shall return out of darkness. He is waited for by the sword.
He wanders abroad for bread, saying, ‘Where is it?’ He knows that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
Distress and anguish make him afraid. Dem prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.
Because he has stretched out his hand against God, and behaves imself proudly against the Almighty;
he runs at him with a stiff neck, with the thick shields of his bucklers;
because he has covered his face with his fatness, and gathered fat on his thighs.
He has lived in desolate cities, in houses which Nobody inhabited, which were ready to become heaps.
He no go be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall dem possessions be extended on the earth.
He no go depart out of darkness. The flame shall dry up his branches. By the breath of God’s mouth shall he go away.
Make e not trust in emptiness, deceiving imself; for emptiness go be his reward.
It go be accomplished before his time. His branch no go be green.
He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall throw off his flower as the olive tree.
For the company of the godless go be barren, and fire shall consume the tents of bribery.
Dem conceive mischief, and produce wickedness. Dem heart prepares deceit.”
Then Job answer,
“I have heard many such things. You be all miserable comforters!
Shall vain words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer?
I also could speak as you do. If una soul were in my soul’s place, I could join words together against you, and shake my head at you,
but I would strengthen you with my mouth. The solace of my lips would relieve you.
“Though I speak, my grief No be subsided. Though I forbear, what am I eased?
But now, God, you have surely worn me out. You have made desolate all my company.
You have shriveled me up. This is a witness against me. My leanness rises up against me. It testifies to my face.
He has torn me in his serious anger, and persecuted me. He has gnashed on me with his teeth. My adversary sharpens his eyes on me.
Dem have gaped on me with dem mouth. Dem have struck me on the cheek reproachfully. Dem gather themselves together against me.
God delivers me to the ungodly, and casts me into the hands of the wicked.
I was at ease, and he broke me apart. Yes, he has taken me by the neck, and dashed me to pieces. He has also set me up for his target.
His archers surround me. He splits my kidneys apart, and No dey spare. He pours out my gall on the ground.
He breaks me with breach on breach. He runs on me like a giant.
I have sewed sackcloth on my skin, and have thrust my horn in the dust.
My face is red with weeping. Deep darkness is on my eyelids.
Although E get no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.
“Earth, no cover my blood. Let my cry have no place to rest.
Even now, see am, my witness is in heaven. Person wey vouches for me is on high.
My friends scoff at me. My eyes pour out tears to God,
that he would maintain the right of a man with God, of a Son of Man with his neighbor!
For when a few years have come, I shall go the way of no return.
“My spirit is consumed. My days are extinct, And the grave is ready for me.
Surely E get mockers with me. My eye dwells on dem provocation.
“Now give a pledge, be collateral for me with yourself. Wey be there who will strike hands with me?
For you have hidden dem heart from understanding, So you no go exalt dem.
Person wey denounces his friends for plunder, Even the eyes of his pikin dem shall fail.
“But he has made me a byword of the people. Dem spit in my face.
My eye also is dim by reason of sorrow. All my members are as a shadow.
Upright men go be astonished at this. The innocent shall stir up imself against the godless.
Yet shall the righteous hold on his way. Person wey has clean hands shall grow stronger and stronger.
But as for you all, come on now again; I no go find a wise man among you.
My days are past, my plans are broken off, as are the thoughts of my heart.
Dem change the night into day, saying ‘The light is near’ in the presence of darkness.
If I look for Sheol as my house, if I have spread my couch in the darkness,
If I have talk say to corruption, ‘You be my father;’ to the worm, ‘My mother,’ and ‘my sister;’
where then is my hope? as for my hope, who shall see it?
Shall it go down with me to the gates of Sheol, or descend together into the dust?”
Then Bildad the Shuhite answer,
“How long will you hunt for words? Consider, and afterwards We go speak.
Why are we counted as animals, which have become unclean in una sight?
You who tear yourself in una anger, shall the earth be forsaken for you? Or shall the rock be removed out of its place?
“Yes, the light of the wicked go be put out, The spark of his fire no go shine.
The light go be dark in his tent. His lamp above him go be put out.
The steps of his strength go be shortened. His own counsel shall throw him down.
For he is throw into a net by his own feet, and he wanders into its mesh.
A snare will take him by the heel. A trap will catch him.
A noose is hidden for him in the ground, a trap for him on the path.
Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and shall chase him at his heels.
His strength go be famished. Calamity go be ready at his side.
The members of his body go be devoured. The firstborn of death shall devour his members.
He go be rooted out of the security of his tent. He go be bring to the king of terrors.
There shall live in his tent that which is none of his. Sulfur go be scattered on his habitation.
His roots go be dried up beneath. Above shall his branch be cut off.
His memory shall perish from the earth. He go get no name in the street.
He go be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.
He go get neither son nor grandson among his people, nor any remaining where he lived.
People wey come after go be astonished at his day, as people wey go before were frightened.
Surely such are the dwellings of the unrighteous. This is the place of him who no dey know God.”
Then Job answer,
“How long will you torment me, and crush me with words?
You have reproached me ten times. You no be ashamed that you attack me.
If it is true that I have erred, my error remains with myself.
If indeed You go magnify unaself against me, and plead against me my reproach;
know now that God has subverted me, and has surrounded me with his net.
“See am, I cry out of wrong, but I be not heard. I cry for help, but E get no justice.
He has walled up my way so that I no fit pass, and has set darkness in my paths.
He has stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head.
He has broken me down on every side, and I be gone. My hope he has plucked up like a tree.
He has also kindled his serious anger against me. He counts me among his adversaries.
His troops come on together, build a siege ramp against me, and encamp around my tent.
“He has put my brothers far from me. My acquaintances are wholly estranged from me.
My relatives have gone away. My familiar friends have forgotten me.
People wey live in my house and my maids consider me a stranger. I be an alien in dem sight.
I call to my worker, and he gives me no answer. I beg him with my mouth.
My breath is offensive to my wife. I be loathsome to the pikin dem of my own mother.
Even young pikin dem despise me. If I arise, dem speak against me.
All my familiar friends abhor me. Dem whom I love have turned against me.
My bones stick to my skin and to my flesh. I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
“Have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends; for the hand of God has touched me.
Why do you persecute me as God, and No be satisfied with my flesh?
“Oh that my words were now written! Oh that dem were inscribed in a book!
That with an iron pen and lead dem were engraved in the rock forever!
But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth.
After my skin is destroyed, then in my flesh shall I see God,
Whom I, even I, shall see on my side. My eyes shall see, and No be like a stranger. “My heart is consumed within me.
If you say, ‘How We go persecute him!’ because the root of the matter is find in me,
be afraid of the sword, for serious anger brings the punishments of the sword, that you may know E get a judgment.”
Then Zophar the Naamathite answer,
“So do my thoughts give answer to me, even by reason of my haste that is in me.
I have heard the reproof which puts me to shame. The spirit of my understanding answers me.
No you know this from old time, since man was placed on earth,
that the triumphing of the wicked is short, the gladness of the godless but for a moment?
Though his height mount up to the heavens, and his head reach to the clouds,
yet he shall perish forever like his own dung. People wey have seen him shall say, ‘Where is he?’
He shall fly away as a dream, and no go be find. Yes, he go be chased away like a vision of the night.
The eye which see him shall see him no more, neither shall his place any more see him.
His pikin dem shall seek the favor of the poor. His hands shall give back his wealth.
His bones are full of his youth, but youth shall lie down with him in the dust.
“Though wickedness is sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue,
though he spare it, and No go let it go, but keep it still within his mouth;
yet his chop in his bowels is turned. It is cobra venom within him.
He has swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit dem up again. God will throw dem out of his belly.
He shall suck cobra venom. The viper’s tongue shall kill him.
He no go look at the rivers, the flowing streams of honey and butter.
That for which he labored he shall restore, and no go swallow it down. According to the substance that he has gotten, he no go glad well-well.
For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor. He has violently taken away a house, and he no go build it up.
“Because he know no quietness within him, he no go save anything of that in which he delights.
There was nothing left that he didn’t devour, so his prosperity no go endure.
In the fullness of his sufficiency, distress shall overtake him. The hand of everyone Wey be in misery shall come on him.
When he is about to fill his belly, God will throw the fierceness of his serious anger on him. It will rain on him while he is eating.
He shall flee from the iron weapon. The bronze arrow shall strike him through.
He draws it out, and it comes out of his body. Yes, the glittering point comes out of his liver. Terrors are on him.
All darkness is laid up for his treasures. An unfanned fire shall devour him. It shall consume that which is left in his tent.
The heavens shall reveal his wickedness. The earth shall rise up against him.
The increase of his house shall depart. Dem shall rush away in the day of his serious anger.
This is the portion of a wicked man from God, the heritage appointed to him by God.”
Then Job answer,
“Listen diligently to my speech. Let this be una consolation.
Allow me, and I also will speak; After I have spoken, mock on.
As for me, is my complaint to man? Why shouldn’t I be impatient?
Look at me, and be astonished. Lay una hand on una mouth.
When I remember, I be troubled. Horror takes hold of my flesh.
“Why do the wicked live, become old, yes, and grow mighty in power?
Dem pikin is established with dem in dem sight, dem offspring before dem eyes.
Dem houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon dem.
Dem bulls breed without fail. Dem cows calve, and no miscarry.
Dem send out dem little ones like a flock. Dem pikin dem dance.
Dem sing to the tambourine and harp, and glad well-well at the sound of the pipe.
Dem spend dem days in prosperity. In an instant dem go down to Sheol.
Dem tell God, ‘Depart from us, for we no want to know about una ways.
Wetin be the Almighty, that we should serve him? What profit should we have, if we pray to him?’
See am, dem prosperity No be in dem hand. The counsel of the wicked is far from me.
“How often is it that the lamp of the wicked is put out, that dem calamity comes on dem, that God distributes sorrows in his anger?
How often is it that Dem be as stubble before the wind, as chaff that the storm carries away?
You say, ‘God lays up his wickedness for his pikin dem.’ Make e recompense it to imself, that he may know it.
Let his own eyes see his destruction. Make e drink of the serious anger of the Almighty.
For what does he care for his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off?
“Shall any teach God knowledge, since he judges people Wey high?
One dies in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.
His pails are full of milk. The marrow of his bones is moistened.
Another dies in bitterness of soul, and never tastes of good.
Dem lie down alike in the dust. The worm covers dem.
“See am, I know una thoughts, the devices with which you would wrong me.
For you say, ‘Where is the house of the prince? Where is the tent in which the wicked lived?’
Haven’t you ask wayfaring men? No you know dem evidences,
that the evil man is reserved to the day of calamity, That Dem be led out to the day of serious anger?
Who shall declare his way to his face? Who shall repay him what he has done?
Yet he Go be borne to the grave. Men shall Shine una eye over the tomb.
The clods of the valley go be sweet to him. All men shall draw after him, as there were innumerable before him.
So how can you comfort me with nonsense, because in una answers there remains only falsehood?”
Then Eliphaz the Temanite answer,
“Can a man be profitable to God? Surely person Wey wise is profitable to imself.
Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that You be righteous? Or does it benefit him, that you make una ways perfect?
Is it for una piety that he reproves you, that he enters with you into judgment?
No be una wickedness great? Neither is there any end to una iniquities.
For you have taken pledges from una brother for nothing, and stripped the naked of dem clothing.
You haven’t given water to the weary to drink, and you have withheld bread from the hungry.
But as for the mighty man, he had the earth. The honorable man, he lived in it.
You have sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless Don dey broken.
So snares are around you. Sudden fear troubles you,
or darkness, so that you can not see, and floods of waters cover you.
“No be God in the heights of heaven? See the height of the stars, how high Dem be!
You say, ‘What does God know? Can he judge through the thick darkness?
Thick clouds are a covering to him, so that he no dey see. He walks on the vault of the sky.’
Will you keep the old way, which wicked men have trodden,
who were snatched away before dem time, whose foundation was poured out as a stream,
who talk say to God, ‘Depart from us;’ and, ‘What can the Almighty do for us?’
Yet he filled dem houses with good things, but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
The righteous see it, and are glad. The innocent ridicule dem,
saying, ‘Surely people wey rose up against us are cut off. The fire has consumed dem remnant.’
“Acquaint yourself with him, now, and be at peace. Through am good shall come to you.
Please receive instruction from his mouth, and lay up his words in una heart.
If you return to the Almighty, you go be built up, if you put away unrighteousness far from una tents.
Lay una treasure in the dust, the gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks.
The Almighty Go be una treasure, and precious silver to you.
For then You go delight yourself in the Almighty, and shall lift up una face to God.
You shall make una prayer to him, and he will hear you. You shall pay una vows.
You shall also decree a thing, and it go be established to you. Light shall shine on una ways.
When dem throw down, you shall say, ‘be lifted up.’ He will save the humble person.
He will even deliver him Wey be not innocent. Yes, he go be delivered through the cleanness of una hands.”
Then Job answer,
“Even today my complaint is rebellious. His hand is heavy in spite of my groaning.
Oh that I know where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat!
I would set my cause in order before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.
I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would tell me.
Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power? No, but he would listen to me.
There the upright might reason with him, so I should be delivered forever from my judge.
