“If I go east, he No be there; if west, I no fit find him;
He works to the north, but I no fit see him. He turns south, but I no fit catch a glimpse of him.
But he knows the way that I take. When he has tried me, I shall come out like gold.
My foot has held fast to his steps. I have kept his way, and not turned aside.
I haven’t gone back from the commandment of his lips. I have treasured up the words of his mouth more than my necessary chop.
But he stands alone, and who can oppose him? What his soul desires, even that he does.
For he performs that which is appointed for me. Many such things are with him.
So I be terrified at his presence. When I consider, I be afraid of him.
For God has made my heart faint. The Almighty has terrified me.
Because I No be cut off before the darkness, neither did he cover the thick darkness from my face.
“Why no be times laid up by the Almighty? Why no people wey know him see his days?
E get people who remove the landmarks. Dem violently take away flocks, and feed dem.
Dem drive away the donkey of the fatherless, and dem take the widow’s ox for a pledge.
Dem turn the needy out of the way. The poor of the earth all hide themselves.
See am, as wild donkeys in the desert, dem go out to dem work, seeking diligently for chop. The wilderness yields dem bread for dem pikin dem.
Dem cut dem chop in the field. Dem glean the vineyard of the wicked.
Dem lie all night naked without clothing, and have no covering in the cold.
Dem be wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for lack of a shelter.
E get people wey pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor,
So that dem go around naked without clothing. Being hungry, dem carry the sheaves.
Dem make oil within the walls of these men. Dem tread wine presses, and suffer thirst.
From out of the populous city, men groan. The soul of the wounded cries out, yet God no dey regard the folly.
“These are of people wey rebel against the light. Dem no know its ways, nor stay in its paths.
The murderer rises with the light. He kills the poor and needy. In the night he is like a thief.
The eye also of the adulterer waits for the twilight, saying, ‘No eye shall see me.’ He disguises his face.
In the dark dem dig through houses. Dem shut themselves up in the daytime. Dem no know the light.
For the morning is to all of dem like thick darkness, for dem know the terrors of the thick darkness.
“Dem be foam on the surface of the waters. Dem portion is cursed in the earth. Dem no turn into the way of the vineyards.
Drought and heat consume the snow waters, so does Sheol people wey have sinned.
The womb shall forget him. The worm shall feed sweetly on him. He go be no more remember. Unrighteousness go be broken as a tree.
He devours the barren who no bear. He shows no kindness to the widow.
Yet God preserves the mighty by his power. He rises up who has no assurance of life.
God gives dem security, and dem rest in it. His eyes are on dem ways.
Dem be exalted; yet a little while, and Dem be gone. Yes, Dem be bring low, Dem be taken out of the way as all others, and are cut off as the tops of the ears of grain.
If it no be so now, who will prove me a liar, and make my speech worth nothing?”
Then Bildad the Shuhite answer,
“Dominion and fear are with him. He makes peace in his high places.
Can his armies be counted? On whom does his light not arise?
How then can man be just with God? Or how can person Wey born of a woman be clean?
See am, even the moon has no brightness, and the stars No be pure in his sight;
How much less man, Wey be a worm, the Son of Man, Wey be a worm!”
Then Job answer,
“How have you helped him Wey be without power! How have you saved the arm that has no strength!
How have you counseled him who has no wisdom, and plentifully declared sound knowledge!
To whom have you uttered words? Whose spirit come out of you?
“The comot spirits tremble, those beneath the waters and all that live in dem.
Sheol is naked before God, and Abaddon has no covering.
He stretches out the north over empty space, and hangs the earth on nothing.
He binds up the waters in his thick clouds, and the cloud No be burst under dem.
He encloses the face of his throne, and spreads his cloud on it.
He has described a boundary on the surface of the waters, and to the confines of light and darkness.
The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his rebuke.
He stirs up the sea with his power, and by his understanding he strikes through Rahab.
By his Spirit the heavens are garnished. His hand has pierced the swift serpent.
See am, these are but the outskirts of his ways. How small a whisper do we hear of him! But the thunder of his power who can understand?”
Job again take up his parable, and talk say,
“As God lives, who has taken away my right, the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter
(for the length of my life is still in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils);
surely my lips no go speak unrighteousness, neither shall my tongue utter deceit.
Far be it from me that I should justify you. Until I die I go not put away my integrity from me.
I Hold am tight to my righteousness, and No go let it go. My heart no go reproach me so long as I live.
“Let my enemy be as the wicked. Make e who rises up against me be as the unrighteous.
For Wetin be the hope of the godless, when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
Will God hear his cry when trouble comes on him?
Will he delight imself in the Almighty, and call on God at all times?
I go teach you about the hand of God. That which is with the Almighty will I not conceal.
See am, all of you have seen it unaself; why then have you become altogether vain?
“This is the portion of a wicked man with God, the heritage of oppressors, which dem receive from the Almighty.
If his pikin dem are multiplied, it is for the sword. His offspring no go be satisfied with bread.
People wey remain of him go be buried in death. His widows shall make no lamentation.
Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare clothing as the clay;
he may prepare it, but the just shall put it on, and the innocent shall divide the silver.
He builds his house as the moth, as a booth which the watchman makes.
He lies down rich, but he no go do so again. He opens his eyes, and he No be.
Terrors overtake him like waters. A storm steals him away in the night.
The east wind carries him away, and he departs. It sweeps him out of his place.
For it hurls at him, and No dey spare, as he flees away from his hand.
Men shall clap dem hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.
“Surely E get a mine for silver, and a place for gold which dem refine.
Iron is taken out of the earth, and copper is smelted out of the ore.
Man sets an end to darkness, and searches out, to the furthest bound, the stones of obscurity and of thick darkness.
He breaks open a shaft away from where people live. Dem be forgotten by the foot. Dem hang far from men, dem swing back and forth.
As for the earth, out of it comes bread; Underneath it is turned up as it were by fire.
Sapphires come from its rocks. It has dust of gold.
That path no bird of prey knows, neither has the falcon’s eye seen it.
The proud animals have not trodden it, nor has the fierce lion passed by there.
He puts his hand on the flinty rock, and he overturns the mountains by the roots.
He cuts out channels among the rocks. His eye sees every precious thing.
He binds the streams that dem no trickle. The thing that is hidden he brings out to light.
“But where shall wisdom be find? Where is the place of understanding?
Man no dey know its price; Neither is it find in the land of the living.
The deep says, ‘It no be in me.’ The sea says, ‘It no be with me.’
It no fit be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for its price.
It no fit be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.
Gold and glass no fit equal it, neither shall it be exchanged for jewels of fine gold.
No mention go be made of coral or of crystal. Yes, the price of wisdom is above rubies.
The topaz of Ethiopia no go equal it, Neither shall it be valued with pure gold.
Where then does wisdom come from? Where is the place of understanding?
Seeing it is hidden from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the birds of the sky.
Destruction and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor of it with our ears.’
“God understands its way, and he knows its place.
For he looks to every corner of the world, and sees under the whole sky.
He establishes the force of the wind. Yes, he measures out the waters by measure.
When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder;
then he see it, and declared it. He established it, yes, and searched it out.
To man he talk say, ‘See am, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom. To depart from evil is understanding.’”
Job again take up his parable, and talk say,
“Oh that I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me;
when his lamp shone on my head, and by his light I walked through darkness,
as I was in the ripeness of my days, when the friendship of God was in my tent,
when the Almighty was yet with me, and my pikin dem were around me,
when my steps were washed with butter, and the rock poured out streams of oil for me,
when I go out to the city gate, when I prepared my seat in the street.
The young men see me and hid themselves. The aged rose up and stood.
The princes refrained from talking, and laid dem hand on dem mouth.
The voice of the nobles was hushed, and dem tongue stuck to the roof of dem mouth.
For when the ear heard me, then it blessed me; and when the eye see me, it commended me:
Because I delivered the poor who cried, and the fatherless also, who had Nobody to help him,
the blessing of him who was ready to perish come on me, and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for gladness.
I put on righteousness, and it clothed me. My justice was as a robe and a diadem.
I was eyes to the blind, and feet to the lame.
I was a father to the needy. The cause of him who I didn’t know, I searched out.
I broke the jaws of the unrighteous, and plucked the prey out of his teeth.
Then I talk say, ‘I shall die in my own house, I shall count my days as the sand.
My root is spread out to the waters. The dew lies all night on my branch.
My glory is fresh in me. My bow is renewed in my hand.’
“Men listened to me, waited, and kept silence for my counsel.
After my words dem didn’t speak again. My speech fell on dem.
Dem waited for me as for the rain. Dem mouths drank as with the spring rain.
I smiled on dem when dem had no confidence. Dem didn’t reject the light of my face.
I chose out dem way, and sat as chief. I lived as a king in the army, as one who comforts the mourners.
“But now people Wey younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to put with my sheep dogs.
Of what use is the strength of dem hands to me, men in whom ripe age has perished?
Dem be gaunt from lack and famine. Dem gnaw the dry ground, in the gloom of waste and desolation.
Dem pluck salt herbs by the bushes. The roots of the broom are dem chop.
Dem be driven out from among men. Dem cry after dem as after a thief;
So that dem live in frightful valleys, and in holes of the earth and of the rocks.
Among the bushes dem bray; and under the nettles Dem be gathered together.
Dem be pikin dem of fools, yes, pikin dem of base men. Dem were flogged out of the land.
“Now I have become dem song. Yes, I be a byword to dem.
Dem abhor me, dem stand aloof from me, and no hesitate to spit in my face.
For he has untied his cord, and afflicted me; and dem have thrown off restraint before me.
On my right hand rise the rabble. Dem thrust aside my feet, Dem throw up against me dem ways of destruction.
Dem mar my path, Dem set forward my calamity, without anyone’s help.
As through a wide breach dem come, in the middle of the ruin dem roll themselves in.
Terrors have turned on me. Dem chase my honor as the wind. My welfare has passed away as a cloud.
“Now my soul is poured out within me. Days of suffering have taken hold on me.
In the night season my bones are pierced in me, and the pains that gnaw me take no rest.
By great force is my garment disfigured. It binds me about as the collar of my coat.
He has throw me into the mire. I have become like dust and ashes.
I cry to you, and you No answer me. I stand up, and you gaze at me.
You have turned to be cruel to me. With the might of una hand you persecute me.
You lift me up to the wind, and drive me with it. You dissolve me in the storm.
For I know that You go bring me to death, To the house appointed for all living.
“However no dey one stretch out a hand in his fall? Or in his calamity so cry for help?
Didn’t I weep for him who was in trouble? No be my soul grieved for the needy?
When I looked for good, then evil come; When I waited for light, there come darkness.
My heart is troubled, and no dey rest. Days of suffering have come on me.
I go mourning without the sun. I stand up in the assembly, and cry for help.
I be a brother to jackals, and a companion to ostriches.
My skin grows black and peels from me. My bones are burned with heat.
So my harp has turned to mourning, and my pipe into the voice of people wey weep.
“I made a covenant with my eyes, how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?
For Wetin be the portion from God above, and the heritage from the Almighty on high?
Is it not calamity to the unrighteous, and disaster to the workers of wickedness?
No dey he see my ways, and count all my steps?
“If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried to deceit
(let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know my integrity);
if my step has turned out of the way, if my heart walked after my eyes, if any defilement has stuck to my hands,
then let me sow, and let another eat. Yes, let the produce of my field be rooted out.
“If my heart Don dey enticed to a woman, and I have laid wait at my neighbor’s door,
then let my wife grind for another, and let others sleep with her.
For that would be a heinous crime. Yes, it would be an wickedness to be punished by the judges:
For it is a fire that consumes to destruction, and would root out all my increase.
“If I have despised the cause of my male worker or of my female worker, when dem contended with me;
What then shall I do when God rises up? When he visits, what shall I answer him?
Didn’t person wey made me in the womb make him? Didn’t one fashion us in the womb?
“If I have withheld the poor from dem desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
or have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten of it
(no, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, her I have guided from my mother’s womb);
if I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or that the needy had no covering;
if his heart hasn’t blessed me, if he hasn’t been warmed with my sheep’s fleece;
if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, because I see my help in the gate,
then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder blade, and my arm be broken from the bone.
For calamity from God is a terror to me. Because his majesty, I can do nothing.
“If I have made gold my hope, and have talk say to the fine gold, ‘You be my confidence;’
If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gotten much;
if I have seen the sun when it shined, or the moon moving in splendor,
and my heart Don dey secretly enticed, and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth,
this also would be an wickedness to be punished by the judges; for I should have denied the God Wey be above.
“If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, or lifted up myself when evil find him
(yes, I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking his life with a curse);
if the men of my tent have not talk say, ‘Who can find one who has not been filled with his meat?’
(the foreigner has not camped in the street, but I have opened my doors to the traveler);
if like Adam I have covered my wrongdoings, by hiding my wickedness in my heart,
because I feared the great plenty people, and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I kept silence, and didn’t go out of the door —
oh that I had one to hear me! See am, here is my signature! Let the Almighty answer me! Let the accuser write my indictment!
Surely I would carry it on my shoulder; and I would bind it to me as a crown.
I would declare to him the number of my steps. as a prince would I go near to him.
If my land cries out against me, and its furrows weep together;
if I have eaten its fruits without money, or have caused its owners to lose dem life,
let briers grow instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.
So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
Then the serious anger of Elihu the son of Barachel, the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was kindled against Job. His serious anger was kindled because he justified imself rather than God.
Also his serious anger was kindled against his three friends, because dem had find no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job, because dem were elder than he.
When Elihu see that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his serious anger was kindled.
Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answer, “I be young, and You be very old; So I held back, and didn’t dare show you my opinion.
I talk say, ‘Days should speak, and plenty people of years should teach wisdom.’
But E get a spirit in man, and the breath of the Almighty gives dem understanding.
It No be the great Wey be wise, nor the aged who understand justice.
So I talk say, ‘Listen to me; I also will show my opinion.’
“See am, I waited for una words, and I listened for una reasoning, while you searched out what to say.
Yes, I give you my full attention, but there was Nobody who convinced Job, or who answer his words, among you.
Beware lest you say, ‘We have find wisdom, God may refute him, not man;’
for he has not directed his words against me; neither will I answer him with una speeches.
“Dem be amazed. Dem answer no more. Dem no have a word to say.
Shall I wait, because dem no speak, because dem stand still, and answer no more?
I also will answer my part, and I also will show my opinion.
For I be full of words. The spirit within me constrains me.
See am, my breast is as wine which has no vent; like new wineskins it is ready to burst.
I go speak, that I may be refreshed. I go open my lips and answer.
Please no let me respect any man’s person, neither will I give flattering titles to any man.
For I no know how to give flattering titles; or else my Maker would soon take me away.
“However, Job, please hear my speech, and listen to all my words.
See now, I have opened my mouth. My tongue has spoken in my mouth.
My words shall utter the uprightness of my heart. That which my lips know dem shall speak sincerely.
The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
If you can, answer me. Set una words in order before me, and stand up.
See am, I be toward God even as You be. I be also formed out of the clay.
See am, my terror no go make you afraid, neither shall my pressure be heavy on you.
“Surely you have spoken in my hearing, I have heard the voice of una words, saying,
‘I be clean, without disobedience. I be innocent, neither is there wickedness in me.
See am, he finds occasions against me. He counts me for his enemy.
He puts my feet in the stocks. He marks all my paths.’
“See am, I go answer you. In this you No be just, for God is greater than man.
Why do you strive against him, because he no dey give account of any of his matters?
For God speaks once, yes twice, though man pays no attention.
In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on men, in slumbering on the bed;
Then he opens the ears of men, and seals dem instruction,
That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.
He keeps back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.
He is chastened also with pain on his bed, with continual strife in his bones;
So that his life abhors bread, and his soul dainty chop.
His flesh is so consumed away, that it no fit be seen. His bones that No be seen stick out.
Yes, his soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the destroyers.
“If E get beside him an angel, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to show to man Wetin be right for him;
then God is gracious to him, and says, ‘Deliver him from going down to the pit, I have find a ransom.’
His flesh go be fresher than a pikin’s. He returns to the days of his youth.
He prays to God, and he is favorable to him, so that he sees his face with gladness. He restores to man his righteousness.
He sings before men, and says, ‘I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it didn’t profit me.
He has redeemed my soul from going into the pit. My life shall see the light.’
“See am, God does all these things, twice, yes three times, with a man,
to bring back his soul from the pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of the living.
Mark well, Job, and listen to me. Hold una peace, and I go speak.
If you have anything to say, answer me. Speak, for I desire to justify you.
If not, listen to me. Hold una peace, and I go teach you wisdom.”
Moreover Elihu answer,
“Hear my words, you wise men. Give ear to me, you who have knowledge.
For the ear tries words, as the palate tastes chop.
Make we choose for us that which is right. Make we know among ourselves Wetin be good.
For Job has talk say, ‘I be righteous, God has taken away my right:
Notwithstanding my right I be considered a liar. My wound is incurable, though I be without disobedience.’
What man is like Job, who drinks scorn like water,
Who goes in company with the workers of wickedness, and walks with wicked men?
For he has talk say, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight imself with God.’
“So listen to me, you men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness, from the Almighty, that he should commit wickedness.
For the work of a man he will render to him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.
Yes surely, God No go do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert justice.
Who put him in charge of the earth? or who has appointed him over the whole world?
If he set his heart on imself, If he gathered to imself his spirit and his breath,
all flesh would perish together, and man would turn again to dust.
“If now you have understanding, hear this. Listen to the voice of my words.
Shall even one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn him Wey be righteous and mighty? —
Who says to a king, ‘Vile!’ or to nobles, ‘Wicked!’?
Who no dey respect the persons of princes, nor respects the rich more than the poor; for dem all are the work of his hands.
In a moment dem die, even at midnight. The people are shaken and pass away. The mighty are taken away without a hand.
“For his eyes are on the ways of a man. He sees all his goings.
E get no darkness, nor thick gloom, where the workers of wickedness may hide themselves.
For he no dey need to consider a man further, that he should go before God in judgment.
He breaks in pieces mighty men in ways past finding out, and sets others in dem place.
So he takes knowledge of dem works. He overturns dem in the night, so that Dem be destroyed.
He strikes dem as wicked men in the open sight of others;
because dem turned aside from following him, and wouldn’t pay attention to any of his ways,
so that dem caused the cry of the poor to come to him. He heard the cry of the afflicted.
When he gives quietness, who then can condemn? When he hides his face, who then can see him? Alike whether to a nation, or to a man,
that the godless man may not reign, that there be Nobody to ensnare the people.
“For has any talk say to God, ‘I be guilty, but I go not offend any more.
Teach me that which I no see. If I have done wickedness, I go do it no more’?
Shall his recompense be as you desire, that you refuse it? For you must choose, and not I. So speak Wetin you know.
Men of understanding will tell me, yes, every wise man wey hear me:
‘Job speaks without knowledge. His words are without wisdom.’
I wish that Job were tried to the end, because of his answering like wicked men.
For he adds rebellion to his sin. He claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against God.”
Moreover Elihu answer,
“Do you think this to be una right, or do you say, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s,’
That you ask, ‘What advantage will it be to you? What profit shall I have, more than if I had sinned?’
I go answer you, and una companions with you.
Look to the heavens, and see. See the skies, which are higher than you.
If you have sinned, what effect do you have against him? If una wrongdoings are multiplied, what do you do to him?
If You be righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from una hand?
Una wickedness may hurt a man as You be, and una righteousness may profit a Son of Man.
“By reason of the plenty people of oppressions dem cry out. Dem cry for help by reason of the arm of the mighty.
But Nobody says, ‘Where is God my Maker, wey dey give songs in the night,
who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?’
There dem cry, but Nobody gives answer, because of the pride of evil men.
Surely God No go hear an empty cry, neither will the Almighty regard it.
How much less when you say you no see him. The cause is before him, and you wait for him!
But now, because he has not visited in his anger, neither does he greatly regard arrogance.
So Job opens his mouth with empty talk, and he multiplies words without knowledge.”
Elihu also continued, and talk say,
“Bear with me a little, and I go show you; for I still have something to say on God’s behalf.
I go get my knowledge from far away, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
For truly my words No be false. One Wey be perfect in knowledge is with you.
“See am, God is mighty, and no dey despise anyone. He is mighty in strength of understanding.
He no dey preserve the life of the wicked, but gives to the afflicted dem right.
He no dey withdraw his eyes from the righteous, but with kings on the throne, he sets dem forever, and Dem be exalted.
If Dem be bound in fetters, and are taken in the cords of afflictions,
then he shows dem dem work, and dem wrongdoings, that dem have behaved themselves proudly.
He also opens dem ears to instruction, and commands that dem return from wickedness.
If dem listen and serve him, dem shall spend dem days in prosperity, and dem years in pleasures.
But if dem no listen, dem shall perish by the sword; dem shall die without knowledge.
“But people Wey godless in heart lay up anger. Dem no cry for help when he binds dem.
Dem die in youth. Dem life perishes among the unclean.
He delivers the afflicted by dem suffering, and opens dem ear in oppression.
Yes, he would have allured you out of distress, into a wide place, where E get no restriction. That which is set on una table would be full of fatness.
“But You be full of the judgment of the wicked. Judgment and justice take hold of you.
No let riches entice you to serious anger, neither let the great size of a bribe turn you aside.
Would una wealth sustain you in distress, or all the might of una strength?
No desire the night, when people are cut off in dem place.
Take heed, no regard wickedness; for you have chosen this rather than suffering.
See am, God is exalted in his power. Wey be a teacher like him?
Who has prescribed his way for him? Or who can say, ‘You have committed unrighteousness?’
“Remember that you magnify his work, wey men have sung.
All men have looked on it. Man sees it far away off.
See am, God is great, and we no know him. The number of his years is unsearchable.
For he draws up the drops of water, which distill in rain from his vapor,
Which the skies pour down and which drop on man abundantly.
Yes, can any understand the spreading of the clouds, and the thunderings of his pavilion?
See am, he spreads his light around him. He covers the bottom of the sea.
For by these he judges the people. He gives chop in abundance.
He covers his hands with the lightning, and commands it to strike the mark.
Its noise tells about him, and the livestock also concerning the storm that comes up.
“Yes, at this my heart trembles, and is moved out of its place.
Hear, oh, hear the noise of his voice, the sound that goes out of his mouth.
He sends it out under the whole sky, and his lightning to every corner of the world.
After it a voice roars. He thunders with the voice of his majesty. He no dey hold back anything when his voice is heard.
God thunders marvelously with his voice. He does great things, which we no fit comprehend.
For he says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth;’ likewise to the shower of rain, and to the showers of his mighty rain.
He seals up the hand of every man, that all men whom he has made may know it.
Then the animals take cover, and remain in dem dens.
Out of its room comes the storm, and cold out of the north.
By the breath of God, ice is given, and the width of the waters is frozen.
Yes, he loads the thick cloud with moisture. He spreads abroad the cloud of his lightning.
It is turned around by his guidance, that dem may do Anything wey he commands dem on the surface of the habitable world,
Whether it is for correction, or for his land, or for loving kindness, that he causes it to come.
“Listen to this, Job. Stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.
Do you know how God controls dem, and causes the lightning of his cloud to shine?
Do you know the workings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him Wey be perfect in knowledge?
You whose clothing is warm, when the earth is still by reason of the south wind?
Can you, with him, spread out the sky, which is strong as a throw metal mirror?
Teach us what we shall tell him, for we no fit make our case by reason of darkness.
Will it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man wish that he were swallowed up?
Now men no see the light which is bright in the skies, but the wind passes, and clears dem.
Out of the north comes golden splendor. With God is awesome majesty.
We no fit reach the Almighty. He is exalted in power. In justice and great righteousness, he No go oppress.
So men revere him. He no dey regard any Wey be wise of heart.”
Then Baba God answer Job out of the whirlwind,
“Wey be this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?
Brace yourself like a man, for I go question you, then you answer me!
“Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding.
Who determined its measures, if you know? Or who stretched the line on it?
Whereupon were its foundations fastened? Or who laid its cornerstone,
when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for gladness?
“Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke out of the womb,
when I made clouds its garment, and wrapped it in thick darkness,
marked out for it my bound, set bars and doors,
and talk say, ‘Here you may come, but no further. Here una proud waves go be stayed?’
“Have you commanded the morning in una days, and caused the dawn to know its place;
that it might take hold of every corner of the world, and shake the wicked out of it?
It is changed as clay under the seal, and presented as a garment.
From the wicked, dem light is withheld. The high arm is broken.
“Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?
Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Or have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
Have you comprehended the earth in its width? Declare, if you know it all.
“Wetin be the way to the dwelling of light? As for darkness, where is its place,
that you should take it to its bound, that you should discern the paths to its house?
Surely you know, for you were born then, and the number of una days is great!
Have you entered the treasuries of the snow, or have you seen the treasures of the hail,
which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?
By what way is the lightning distributed, or the east wind scattered on the earth?
Who has cut a channel for the flood water, or the path for the thunderstorm;
To cause it to rain on a land where no man is; on the wilderness, in which E get no man;
to satisfy the waste and desolate ground, to cause the tender grass to grow?
Does the rain have a father? Or who fathers the drops of dew?
Out of whose womb come the ice? The gray frost of the sky, who has given birth to it?
The waters become hard like stone, when the surface of the deep is frozen.
“Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?
Can you lead the constellations out in dem season? Or can you guide the Bear with her cubs?
Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you establish its dominion over the earth?
“Can you lift up una voice to the clouds, That abundance of waters may cover you?
Can you send out lightnings, that dem may go? Do dem report to you, ‘Here We be?’
Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who has given understanding to the mind?
Who can count the clouds by wisdom? Or who can pour out the bottles of the sky,
when the dust runs into a mass, and the clods of earth stick together?
“Can you hunt the prey for the lioness, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
when dem crouch in dem dens, and lie in wait in the thicket?
Who provides for the raven his prey, when his young ones cry to God, and wander for lack of chop?
“Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?
Can you count the months that dem fulfill? Or do you know the time when dem give birth?
Dem bow themselves, dem bear dem young. Dem end dem labor pains.
Dem young ones become strong. Dem grow up in the open field. Dem go out, and no return again.
“Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,
Whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?
He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.
The range of the mountains is his pasture, He searches after every green thing.
“Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by una feeding trough?
Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?
Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him una labor?
Will you confide in him, that he will bring home una seed, and gather the grain of una threshing floor?
“The wings of the ostrich wave proudly; but are dem the feathers and plumage of love?
For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms dem in the dust,
and forgets that the foot may crush dem, or that the wild animal may trample dem.
She deals harshly with her young ones, as if dem No be hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,
because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.
When she lifts up sheself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.
“Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?
Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.
He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.
He mocks at fear, and No be dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.
The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.
He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.
As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle far away off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
“Is it by una wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?
Is it at una command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?
On the cliff he dwells, and makes his home, on the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.
From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it far away off.
His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”
Moreover Baba God answer Job,
“Shall person wey argues contend with the Almighty? Person wey argues with God, Make e answer it.”
Then Job answer Baba God,
“See am, I be of small account. What shall I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.
I have spoken once, and I go not answer; Yes, twice, but I go proceed no further.”
Then Baba God answer Job out of the whirlwind,
“Now brace yourself like a man. I go question you, and You go answer me.
Will you even annul my judgment? Will you condemn me, that you may be justified?
Or do you have an arm like God? Can you thunder with a voice like him?
“Now deck yourself with excellency and dignity. Array yourself with honor and majesty.
Pour out the fury of una anger. Look at everyone Wey be proud, and bring him low.
Look at everyone Wey be proud, and humble him. Crush the wicked in dem place.
Hide dem in the dust together. Bind dem faces in the hidden place.
Then I go also admit to you that una own right hand can save you.
“See now, behemoth, which I made as well as you. He eats grass as an ox.
Look now, his strength is in his thighs. His force is in the muscles of his belly.
He moves his tail like a cedar. The sinews of his thighs are knit together.
His bones are like tubes of brass. His limbs are like bars of iron.
He is the chief of the ways of God. Person wey made him gives him his sword.
Surely the mountains produce chop for him, where all the animals of the field play.
He lies under the lotus trees, in the covert of the reed, and the marsh.
The lotuses cover him with dem shade. The willows of the brook surround him.
See am, if a river overflows, he no dey tremble. He is confident, though the Jordan swells even to his mouth.
Shall any take him when he is on the watch, or pierce through his nose with a snare?
“Can you draw out Leviathan with a fish hook, or press down his tongue with a cord?
Can you put a rope into his nose, or pierce his jaw through with a hook?
Will he make many petitions to you, or will he speak soft words to you?
Will he make a covenant with you, that you should take him for a worker forever?
Will you play with him as with a bird? Or will you bind him for una girls?
Will traders barter for him? Will dem part him among the merchants?
Can you fill his skin with barbed irons, or his head with fish spears?
Lay una hand on him. Remember the battle, and do so no more.
See am, the hope of him is in vain. No go one be throw down even at the sight of him?
None is so fierce that he dare stir him up. Who then is person wey can stand before me?
Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Everything under the heavens is mine.
“I go not keep silence concerning his limbs, nor his mighty strength, nor his goodly frame.
Who can strip off his outer garment? Who shall come within his jaws?
Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.
Strong scales are his pride, shut up together with a close seal.
One is so near to another, that no air can come between dem.
Dem be joined to each other. Dem stick together, so that dem no fit be pulled apart.
His sneezing flashes out light. His eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
Out of his mouth go burning torches. Sparks of fire leap out.
Out of his nostrils a smoke goes, as of a boiling pot over a fire of reeds.
His breath kindles coals. A flame goes out of his mouth.
E get strength in his neck. Terror dances before him.
The flakes of his flesh are joined together. Dem be firm on him. Dem no fit be moved.
His heart is as firm as a stone, yes, firm as the lower millstone.
When he raises imself up, the mighty are afraid. Dem retreat before his thrashing.
If one attacks him with the sword, it no fit prevail; nor the spear, the dart, nor the pointed shaft.
He counts iron as straw; and brass as rotten wood.
The arrow no fit make him flee. Sling stones are like chaff to him.
Clubs are counted as stubble. He laughs at the rushing of the javelin.
His undersides are like sharp potsherds, leaving a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.
He makes the deep to boil like a pot. He makes the sea like a pot of ointment.
He makes a path shine after him. One would think the deep had white hair.
On earth there No be his equal, that is made without fear.
He sees everything that is high. He is king over all the sons of pride.”
Then Job answer Baba God,
“I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.
You ask, ‘Wey be this who hides counsel without knowledge?’ so I have uttered that which I No understand, things too wonderful for me, which I didn’t know.
You talk say, ‘Listen, now, and I go speak; I go question you, and You go answer me.’
I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.
So I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.”

It was so, that after Baba God had spoken these words to Job, Baba God talk say to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My serious anger is kindled against you, and against una two friends; for you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my worker Job has.

Now so, take to unaself seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my worker Job, and offer up for unaself a burnt offering; and my worker Job shall pray for you, for I go accept him, that I not deal with you according to una folly. For you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my worker Job has.”
So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite go, and did what Baba God commanded dem, and Baba God accepted Job.
Baba God turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends. Baba God give Job twice as much as he had before.

Then come there to him all his brothers, and all his sisters, and all people wey Bin dey of his acquaintance before, and ate bread with him in his house. Dem comforted him, and consoled him concerning all the evil that Baba God had bring on him. Everyone also give him a piece of money, and everyone a ring of gold.
So Baba God blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.
He had also seven sons and three daughters.
He call the name of the first, Jemimah; and the name of the second, Keziah; and the name of the third, Keren Happuch.
In all the land were no women find so beautiful as the daughters of Job. Dem father give dem an inheritance among dem brothers.
After this Job lived one hundred forty years, and see his sons, and his sons’ sons, to four generations.
So Job died, being old and full of days.
Blessed is the man who no dey walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand on the path of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers;
but his delight is in Baba God’s law. On his law he meditates day and night.
He Go be like a tree planted by the streams of water, that produces its fruit in its season, whose leaf also No dey wither. Anything wey he does shall prosper.
The wicked No be so, but are like the chaff which the wind drives away.
So the wicked no go stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous.
For Baba God knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked shall perish.
Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot a vain thing?
The kings of the earth take a stand, and the rulers take counsel together, against Baba God, and against his Anointed, saying,
“Let’s break dem bonds apart, and throw dem cords from us.”
Person wey sits in the heavens will laugh. The Lord Go get dem in derision.
Then he will speak to dem in his anger, and terrify dem in his serious anger:
“Yet I have set my King on my holy hill of Zion.”
I go tell of the decree. Baba God talk say to me, “You be my son. Today I have become una father.
Ask of me, and I go give the nations for una inheritance, the uttermost parts of the earth for una possession.
You shall break dem with a rod of iron. You shall dash dem in pieces like a potter’s vessel.”
Now so be wise, you kings. Be instructed, you judges of the earth.
Serve Baba God with fear, and glad well-well with trembling.
Give sincere homage to the Son, lest he be angry, and you perish on the way, for his serious anger will soon be kindled. Blessed are all people wey take refuge in him.
A Psalm by David, when he fled from Absalom his son. Baba God, how my adversaries have increased! Many are people wey rise up against me.
Many E get who say of my soul, “E get no help for him in God.” Selah.
But you, Baba God, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.
I cry to Baba God with my voice, and he answers me out of his holy hill. Selah.
I laid myself down and slept. I awakened; for Baba God sustains me.
I go not be afraid of tens of thousands of people who have set themselves against me on every side.
Arise, Baba God! Save me, my God! For you have struck all of my enemies on the cheek bone. You have broken the teeth of the wicked.
Salvation belongs to Baba God. Una blessing be on una people. Selah.
For the Chief Musician; on stringed instruments. A Psalm by David. Answer me when I call, God of my righteousness. Give me relief from my distress. Have mercy on me, and hear my prayer.
You sons of men, how long shall my glory be turned into dishonor? Will you love vanity, and seek after falsehood? Selah.
But know that Baba God has set apart for imself him Wey be godly: Baba God will hear when I call to him.
Stand in awe, and no sin. Search una own heart on una bed, and be still. Selah.
Offer the sacrifices of righteousness. Put una trust in Baba God.
Many say, “Who will show us any good?” Baba God, let the light of una face shine on us.
You have put gladness in my heart, more than when dem grain and dem new wine are increased.
In peace I go both lay myself down and sleep, for you, Baba God alone, make me live in safety.
For the Chief Musician, with the flutes. A Psalm by David. Give ear to my words, Baba God. Consider my meditation.
Listen to the voice of my cry, my King and my God; for to you do I pray.
Baba God, in the morning you shall hear my voice. In the morning I go lay my requests before you, and will watch expectantly.
For you No be a God who has pleasure in wickedness. Evil no fit live with you.
The arrogant no go stand in una sight. You hate all workers of wickedness.
You go destroy people wey speak lies. Baba God abhors the bloodthirsty and deceitful man.
But as for me, in the abundance of una loving kindness I go come into una house. I go bow toward una holy temple in reverence of you.
Lead me, Baba God, in una righteousness because of my enemies. Make una way straight before my face.
For E get no faithfulness in dem mouth. Dem heart is destruction. Dem throat is an open tomb. Dem flatter with dem tongue.
Hold dem guilty, God. Make dem fall by dem own counsels; Thrust dem out in the plenty people of dem wrongdoings, for dem have rebelled against you.
But let all people wey take refuge in you glad well-well, Make dem always shout for gladness, because you defend dem. Make dem also who love una name be joyful in you.
For You go bless the righteous. Baba God, You go surround him with favor as with a shield.
For the Chief Musician; on stringed instruments, upon the eight-stringed lyre. A Psalm by David. Baba God, no rebuke me in una anger, neither discipline me in una serious anger.
Have mercy on me, Baba God, for I be faint. Baba God, heal me, for my bones are troubled.
My soul is also in great anguish. But you, Baba God — how long?
Return, Baba God. Deliver my soul, and save me for una loving kindness’ sake.
For in death E get no memory of you. In Sheol, who shall give you thanks?
I be weary with my groaning. Every night I flood my bed. I drench my couch with my tears.
My eye wastes away because of grief. It grows old because of all my adversaries.
Depart from me, all you workers of wickedness, for Baba God has heard the voice of my weeping.
Baba God has heard my supplication. Baba God accepts my prayer.
May all my enemies be ashamed and dismayed. Dem shall turn back, dem go be disgraced suddenly.
A meditation by David, which he sang to Baba God, concerning the words of Cush, the Benjamite. Baba God, my God, I take refuge in you. Save me from all people wey pursue me, and deliver me,
lest dem tear apart my soul like a lion, ripping it in pieces, while E get Nobody to deliver.
Baba God, my God, if I have done this, if E get wickedness in my hands,
if I have rewarded evil to him who was at peace with me (yes, if I have delivered him who without cause was my adversary),
let the enemy pursue my soul, and overtake it; yes, Make e tread my life down to the earth, and lay my glory in the dust. Selah.
Arise, Baba God, in una anger. Lift up yourself against the rage of my adversaries. Awake for me. You have commanded judgment.
Let the congregation of the peoples surround you. Rule over dem on high.
Baba God administers judgment to the peoples. Judge me, Baba God, according to my righteousness, and to my integrity that is in me.
Oh let the wickedness of the wicked come to an end, but establish the righteous; dem minds and hearts are searched by the righteous God.
My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart.
God is a righteous judge, yes, a God who has indignation every day.
If a man no dey relent, he will sharpen his sword; he has bent and strung his bow.
He has also prepared for imself the instruments of death. He makes ready his flaming arrows.
See am, he travails with wickedness. Yes, he has conceived mischief, and bring out falsehood.
He has dug a hole, and has fallen into the pit which he made.
The trouble he causes shall return to his own head. His violence shall come down on the crown of his own head.
I go Thank God to Baba God according to his righteousness, and will sing praise to the name of Baba God Most High.
For the Chief Musician; on an instrument of Gath. A Psalm by David. Baba God, our Lord, how majestic is una name in all the earth, who has set una glory above the heavens!
From the lips of babes and infants you have established strength, because of una adversaries, that you might silence the enemy and the avenger.
When I consider una heavens, the work of una fingers, the moon and the stars, which you have ordained;
Wetin be man, that you think of him? Wetin be the Son of Man, that you care for him?
For you have made him a little lower than God, and crowned him with glory and honor.
You make him ruler over the works of una hands. You have put all things under his feet:
All sheep and cattle, yes, and the animals of the field,
The birds of the sky, the fish of the sea, and Anything wey passes through the paths of the seas.
Baba God, our Lord, how majestic is una name in all the earth!
For the Chief Musician. Set to “The Death of the Son.” A Psalm by David. I go Thank God to Baba God with my whole heart. I go tell of all una marvelous works.
I go be glad and glad well-well in you. I go sing praise to una name, O Most High.
When my enemies turn back, dem stumble and perish in una presence.
For you have maintained my just cause. You sit on the throne judging righteously.
You have rebuked the nations. You have destroyed the wicked. You have blotted out dem name forever and ever.
The enemy is overtaken by endless ruin. The very memory of the cities which you have overthrown has perished.
But Baba God reigns forever. He has prepared his throne for judgment.
He will judge the world in righteousness. He will administer judgment to the peoples in uprightness.
Baba God will also be a high tower for the oppressed; a high tower in times of trouble.
People wey know una name will put dem trust in you, for you, Baba God, have not forsaken people wey seek you.
Sing praises to Baba God, who dwells in Zion, and declare among the people what he has done.
For person wey avenges blood remembers dem. He no dey forget the cry of the afflicted.
Have mercy on me, Baba God. See my suffering by people wey hate me, and lift me up from the gates of death;
that I may show all of una praise. In the gates of the daughter of Zion, I go glad well-well in una salvation.
The nations have sunk down in the pit that dem made. In the net which dem hid, dem own foot is taken.
Baba God has made imself known. He has executed judgment. The wicked is snared by the work of his own hands. Meditation. Selah.
The wicked go be turned back to Sheol, even all the nations that forget God.
For the needy no go always be forgotten, nor the hope of the poor perish forever.
Arise, Baba God! No let man prevail. Let the nations be judged in una sight.
Put dem in fear, Baba God. Let the nations know that Dem be only men. Selah.
Why do you stand far off, Baba God? Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble?
In arrogance, the wicked hunt down the weak. Dem be caught in the schemes that dem devise.
For the wicked boasts of his heart’s cravings. He blesses the greedy, and condemns Baba God.
The wicked, in the pride of his face, has no room in his thoughts for God.
His ways are prosperous at all times. He is haughty, and una laws are far from his sight. As for all his adversaries, he sneers at dem.
He says in his heart, “I no go be shaken. For generations I go get no trouble.”
His mouth is full of cursing, deceit, and oppression. Under his tongue is mischief and wickedness.
He lies in wait near the villages. From ambushes, he murders the innocent. His eyes are secretly set against the helpless.
He lurks in secret as a lion in his ambush. He lies in wait to catch the helpless. He catches the helpless, when he draws him in his net.
The helpless are crushed. Dem collapse. Dem fall under his strength.
He says in his heart, “God has forgotten. He hides his face. He will never see it.”
Arise, Baba God! God, lift up una hand! No forget the helpless.
Why does the wicked person condemn God, and say in his heart, “God no go call me into account?”
But you do see trouble and grief. You consider it to take it into una hand. You help the victim and the fatherless.
Break the arm of the wicked. As for the evil man, seek out his wickedness until you find none.
Baba God is King forever and ever! The nations will perish out of his land.
Baba God, you have heard the desire of the humble. You go prepare dem heart. You go cause una ear to hear,
to judge the fatherless and the oppressed, that man Wey be of the earth may terrify no more.
For the Chief Musician. By David. In Baba God, I take refuge. How can you say to my soul, “Flee as a bird to una mountain!”
For, see am, the wicked bend dem bows. Dem set dem arrows on the strings, that dem may shoot in darkness at the upright in heart.
If the foundations are destroyed, what can the righteous do?
Baba God is in his holy temple. Baba God is on his throne in heaven. His eyes observe. His eyes examine the pikin dem of men.
Baba God examines the righteous, but the wicked and him wey love violence his soul hates.
On the wicked he will rain blazing coals; fire, sulfur, and scorching wind go be the portion of dem cup.
For Baba God is righteous. He loves righteousness. The upright shall see his face.
For the Chief Musician; upon an eight-stringed lyre. A Psalm of David. Help, Baba God; for the godly man ceases. For the faithful fail from among the pikin dem of men.
Everyone lies to his neighbor. Dem speak with flattering lips, and with a double heart.
May Baba God cut off all flattering lips, and the tongue that boasts,
who have talk say, “With our tongue We go prevail. Our lips are our own. Wey be lord over us?”
“Because of the oppression of the weak and because of the groaning of the needy, I go now arise,” says Baba God; “I go set him in safety from people wey malign him.”
Baba God’s words are flawless words, as silver refined in a clay furnace, purified seven times.
You go keep dem, Baba God. You go preserve dem from this generation forever.
The wicked walk on every side, when Wetin be vile is exalted among the sons of men.
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David. How long, Baba God? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide una face from me?
How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having sorrow in my heart every day? How long shall my enemy triumph over me?
See am, and answer me, Baba God, my God. Give light to my eyes, lest I sleep in death;
Lest my enemy say, “I have prevailed against him”; Lest my adversaries glad well-well when I fall.
But I trust in una loving kindness. My heart rejoices in una salvation.
I go sing to Baba God, because he Don dey good to me.
For the Chief Musician. By David. The fool has talk say in his heart, “E get no God.” Dem be corrupt. Dem have done abominable deeds. E get Nobody wey do good.
Baba God looked down from heaven on the pikin dem of men, to see if there were any who understand, who sought after God.
Dem have all gone aside. Dem have together become corrupt. E get Nobody wey do good, no, not one.
Have all the workers of wickedness no knowledge, who eat up my people as dem eat bread, and no call on Baba God?
There dem were in great fear, for God is in the generation of the righteous.
You frustrate the plan of the poor, because Baba God is his refuge.
Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion! When Baba God restores the fortunes of his people, then Jacob shall glad well-well, and Israel go be glad.
A Psalm by David. Baba God, who shall live in una sanctuary? Who shall live on una holy hill?
Person wey walks blamelessly does Wetin be right, and speaks truth in his heart;
Person wey no dey slander with his tongue, nor does evil to his friend, nor casts slurs against his fellow man;
In whose eyes a vile man is despised, but who honors people wey fear Baba God; person wey keeps an oath even when it hurts, and no dey change;
person wey no dey lend out his money for usury, nor take a bribe against the innocent. Person wey does these things shall never be shaken.
A Poem by David. Preserve me, God, for in you do I take refuge.
My soul, you have talk say to Baba God, “You be my Lord. Apart from you I have no good thing.”
As for the saints Wey be in the earth, Dem be the excellent ones in whom is all my delight.
Dem sorrows go be multiplied who give gifts to another god. Dem drink offerings of blood I go not offer, nor take dem names on my lips.
Baba God assigned my portion and my cup. You made my lot secure.
The lines have fallen to me in pleasant places. Yes, I have a good inheritance.
I go bless Baba God, who has given me counsel. Yes, my heart instructs me in the night seasons.
I have set Baba God always before me. Because he is at my right hand, I no go be moved.
So my heart is glad, and my tongue rejoices. My body shall also live in safety.
For You go not leave my soul in Sheol, neither will you allow una holy one to see corruption.
You go show me the path of life. In una presence is fullness of gladness. In una right hand E get pleasures forever more.
A Prayer by David. Hear, Baba God, my righteous plea; Give ear to my prayer, that no dey go out of deceitful lips.
Let my sentence come out of una presence. Let una eyes look on equity.
You have proved my heart. You have visited me in the night. You have tried me, and find nothing. I have resolved that my mouth no go disobey.
As for the deeds of men, by the word of una lips, I have kept myself from the ways of the violent.
My steps have held fast to una paths. My feet have not slipped.
I have call on you, for You go answer me, God. Turn una ear to me. Hear my speech.
Show una marvelous loving kindness, you who save people wey take refuge by una right hand from dem enemies.
Keep me as the apple of una eye. Hide me under the shadow of una wings,
from the wicked who oppress me, my deadly enemies, who surround me.
Dem close up dem callous hearts. With dem mouth dem speak proudly.
Dem have now surrounded us in our steps. Dem set dem eyes to throw us down to the earth.
He is like a lion that is greedy of his prey, as it were a young lion lurking in secret places.
Arise, Baba God, confront him. Throw him down. Deliver my soul from the wicked by una sword;
from men by una hand, Baba God, from men of the world, whose portion is in this life. You fill the belly of una cherished ones. Una sons have plenty, and dem store up wealth for dem pikin dem.
As for me, I shall see una face in righteousness. I go be satisfied, when I awake, with seeing una form.

For the Chief Musician. By David the worker of Baba God, who spoke to Baba God the words of this song in the day that Baba God delivered him from the hand of all his enemies, and from the hand of Saul. He talk say, I love you, Baba God, my strength.
Baba God is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my rock, in whom I take refuge; my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower.
I call on Baba God, Wey be worthy to be praised; and I be saved from my enemies.
The cords of death surrounded me. The floods of ungodliness made me afraid.
The cords of Sheol were around me. The snares of death come on me.
In my distress I call on Baba God, and cried to my God. He heard my voice out of his temple. My cry before him come into his ears.
Then the earth shook and trembled. The foundations also of the mountains quaked and were shaken, because he was angry.
Smoke go out of his nostrils. Consuming fire come out of his mouth. Coals were kindled by it.
He bowed the heavens also, and come down. Thick darkness was under his feet.
He rode on a cherub, and flew. Yes, he soared on the wings of the wind.
He made darkness his hiding place, his pavilion around him, darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies.
At the brightness before him his thick clouds passed, hailstones and coals of fire.
Baba God also thundered in the sky. The Most High uttered his voice: hailstones and coals of fire.
He sent out his arrows, and scattered dem; Yes, great lightning bolts, and routed dem.
Then the channels of waters appeared. The foundations of the world were laid bare at una rebuke, Baba God, at the blast of the breath of una nostrils.
He sent from on high. He take me. He drew me out of many waters.
He delivered me from my strong enemy, from people wey hated me; for dem were too mighty for me.
Dem come on me in the day of my calamity, but Baba God was my support.
He bring me out also into a large place. He delivered me, because he delighted in me.
Baba God has rewarded me according to my righteousness. According to the cleanness of my hands has he recompensed me.
For I have kept the ways of Baba God, and have not wickedly comot from my God.
For all his ordinances were before me. I didn’t put away his statutes from me.
I was also blameless with him. I kept myself from my wickedness.
So Baba God has rewarded me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands in his eyesight.
With the merciful You go show yourself merciful. With the perfect man, You go show yourself perfect.
With the pure, You go show yourself pure. With the crooked You go show yourself shrewd.
For You go save the afflicted people, but the haughty eyes You go bring down.
For You go light my lamp, Baba God. My God will light up my darkness.
For by you, I advance through a troop. By my God, I leap over a wall.
As for God, his way is perfect. Baba God’s word is tried. He is a shield to all people wey take refuge in him.
For Wey be God, except Baba God? Wey be a rock, besides our God,
the God who arms me with strength, and makes my way perfect?
He makes my feet like deer’s feet, and sets me on my high places.
He teaches my hands to war, so that my arms bend a bow of bronze.
You have also given me the shield of una salvation. Una right hand sustains me. Una gentleness has made me great.
You have enlarged my steps under me, My feet have not slipped.
I go pursue my enemies, and overtake dem. Neither will I turn again until Dem be consumed.
I go strike dem through, so that Dem go not be able to rise. Dem shall fall under my feet.
For you have armed me with strength to the battle. You have subdued under me people wey rose up against me.
You have also made my enemies turn dem backs to me, that I might cut off people wey hate me.
Dem cried, but there was Nobody to save; even to Baba God, but he didn’t answer dem.
Then I beat dem small as the dust before the wind. I throw dem out as the mire of the streets.
You have delivered me from the strivings of the people. You have made me the head of the nations. A people whom I have not known shall serve me.
As soon as dem hear of me dem shall obey me. The foreigners shall submit themselves to me.
The foreigners shall fade away, and shall come trembling out of dem close places.
Baba God lives; and blessed be my rock. Exalted be the God of my salvation,
even the God who executes vengeance for me, and subdues peoples under me.
He rescues me from my enemies. Yes, you lift me up above people wey rise up against me. You deliver me from the violent man.
So I go Thank God to you, Baba God, among the nations, and will sing praises to una name.
He gives great deliverance to his king, and shows loving kindness to his anointed, to David and to his offspring, forever more.
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David. The heavens declare the glory of God. The expanse shows his handiwork.
Day after day dem pour out speech, and night after night dem display knowledge.
E get no speech nor language, where dem voice No be heard.
Dem voice has gone out through all the earth, dem words to the end of the world. In dem he has set a tent for the sun,
which is as a bridegroom coming out of his room, like a strong man rejoicing to run his course.
His going out is from the end of the heavens, his circuit to its ends; E get nothing hidden from its heat.
Baba God’s law is perfect, restoring the soul. Baba God’s testimony is sure, making wise the simple.
Baba God’s precepts are right, rejoicing the heart. Baba God’s commandment is pure, enlightening the eyes.
The fear of Baba God is clean, enduring forever. Baba God’s ordinances are true, and righteous altogether.
More to be desired are dem than gold, yes, than much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and the extract of the honeycomb.
Moreover by dem is una worker warned. In keeping dem E get great reward.
Who can discern his errors? Forgive me from hidden errors.
Keep back una worker also from presumptuous sins. Make dem not have dominion over me. Then I go be upright. I go be blameless and innocent of great wrongdoing.
Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in una sight, Baba God, my rock, and my redeemer.
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David. May Baba God answer you in the day of trouble. May the name of the God of Jacob set you up on high,
send you help from the sanctuary, grant you support from Zion,
remember all una offerings, and accept una burned sacrifice. Selah.
May He grant you una heart’s desire, and fulfill all una counsel.
We go triumph in una salvation. In the name of our God, We go set up our banners. May Baba God grant all una requests.
Now I know that Baba God saves his anointed. He will answer him from his holy heaven, with the saving strength of his right hand.
Some trust in chariots, and some in horses, but we trust the name of Baba God our God.
Dem be bowed down and fallen, but we rise up, and stand upright.
Save, Baba God! Let the King answer us when we call!
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David. The king rejoices in una strength, Baba God! How greatly he rejoices in una salvation!
You have given him his heart’s desire, and have not withheld the request of his lips. Selah.
For you meet him with the blessings of goodness. You set a crown of fine gold on his head.
He ask life of you, you give it to him, even length of days forever and ever.
His glory is great in una salvation. You lay honor and majesty on him.
For you make him most blessed forever. You make him glad with gladness in una presence.
For the king trusts in Baba God. Through the loving kindness of the Most High, he no go be moved.
Una hand will find out all of una enemies. Una right hand will find out people wey hate you.
You go make dem as a fiery furnace in the time of una anger. Baba God will swallow dem up in his serious anger. The fire shall devour dem.
You go destroy dem descendants from the earth, dem posterity from among the pikin dem of men.
For dem intended evil against you. Dem plotted evil against you which cannot succeed.
For You go make dem turn dem back, when you aim drawn bows at dem face.
Be exalted, Baba God, in una strength, so We go sing and praise una power.
For the Chief Musician; set to “The Doe of the Morning.” A Psalm by David. My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me, and from the words of my groaning?
My God, I cry in the daytime, but you no answer; in the night season, and am not silent.
But You be holy, you who inhabit the praises of Israel.
Our fathers trusted in you. Dem trusted, and you delivered dem.
Dem cried to you, and were delivered. Dem trusted in you, and No be disappointed.
But I be a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised by the people.
All people wey see me mock me. Dem insult me with dem lips. Dem shake dem heads, saying,
“He trusts in Baba God; Make e deliver him. Make e rescue him, since he delights in him.”
But you bring me out of the womb. You made me trust while at my mother’s breasts.
I was thrown on you from my mother’s womb. You be my God since my mother bore me.
No be far from me, for trouble is near. For E get Nobody to help.
Many bulls have surrounded me. Strong bulls of Bashan have encircled me.
Dem open dem mouths wide against me, lions tearing prey and roaring.
I be poured out like water. All my bones are out of joint. My heart is like wax; it is melted within me.
My strength is dried up like a potsherd. My tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth. You have bring me into the dust of death.
For dogs have surrounded me. A company of evildoers have enclosed me. Dem have pierced my hands and feet.
I can count all of my bones. Dem look and stare at me.
Dem divide my garments among dem. Dem throw lots for my clothing.
But no be far off, Baba God. You be my help: hurry to help me.
Deliver my soul from the sword, my precious life from the power of the dog.
Save me from the lion’s mouth! Yes, from the horns of the wild oxen, you have answer me.
I go declare una name to my brothers. Among the assembly, I go praise you.
You who fear Baba God, praise him! All you descendants of Jacob, glorify him! Stand in awe of him, all you descendants of Israel!
For he has not despised nor abhorred the suffering of the afflicted, Neither has he hidden his face from him; but when he cried to him, he heard.
Of you comes my praise in the great assembly. I go pay my vows before people wey fear him.
The humble shall eat and be satisfied. Dem shall praise Baba God who seek after him. Let una hearts live forever.
All every corner of the world shall remember and turn to Baba God. All the relatives of the nations shall worship before you.
For the kingdom is Baba God’s. He is the ruler over the nations.
All the rich ones of the earth shall eat and worship. All people wey go down to the dust shall bow before him, even person wey no fit keep his soul alive.
Posterity shall serve him. Future generations go be told about the Lord.
Dem shall come and shall declare his righteousness to a people that go be born, for he has done it.
A Psalm by David. Baba God na my shepherd; I no go lack anything.
He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters.
He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I go fear no evil, for You be with me. Una rod and una staff, dem comfort me.
You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil. My cup runs over.
Surely goodness and loving kindness shall follow me all the days of my life, and I go live in Baba God’s house forever.
A Psalm by David. The earth is Baba God’s, with its fullness; the world, and people wey live inside am.
For he has founded it on the seas, and established it on the floods.
Who may ascend to Baba God’s hill? Who may stand in his holy place?
Person wey has clean hands and a pure heart; who has not lifted up his soul to falsehood, and has not sworn deceitfully.
He shall receive a blessing from Baba God, righteousness from the God of his salvation.
This is the generation of people wey seek Him, who seek una face — even Jacob. Selah.
Lift up una heads, you gates! Be lifted up, you everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in.
Wey be the King of glory? Baba God strong and mighty, Baba God mighty in battle.
Lift up una heads, you gates; yes, lift dem up, you everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in.
Wey be this King of glory? Baba God of Armies is the King of glory! Selah.
By David. To you, Baba God, do I lift up my soul.
My God, I have trusted in you. No let me be shamed. No let my enemies triumph over me.
Yes, Nobody who waits for you go be shamed. Dem go be shamed who deal treacherously without cause.
Show me una ways, Baba God. Teach me una paths.
Guide me in una truth, and teach me, For You be the God of my salvation, I wait for you all day long.
Baba God, remember una tender mercies and una loving kindness, for Dem be from old times.
No remember the sins of my youth, nor my wrongdoings. Remember me according to una loving kindness, for una goodness’ sake, Baba God.
Good and upright is Baba God, so he will instruct sinners in the way.
He will guide the humble in justice. He will teach the humble his way.
All the paths of Baba God are loving kindness and truth to such as keep his covenant and his testimonies.
For una name’s sake, Baba God, pardon my wickedness, for it is great.
What man is person wey fears Baba God? He shall instruct him in the way that he shall choose.
His soul shall live at ease. His offspring shall inherit the land.
The friendship of Baba God is with people wey fear him. He will show dem his covenant.
My eyes are ever on Baba God, for he will pluck my feet out of the net.
Turn to me, and have mercy on me, for I be desolate and afflicted.
The troubles of my heart are enlarged. Oh bring me out of my distresses.
Consider my suffering and my travail. Forgive all my sins.
Consider my enemies, for Dem be many. Dem hate me with cruel hatred.
Oh keep my soul, and deliver me. Let me not be disappointed, for I take refuge in you.
Let integrity and uprightness preserve me, for I wait for you.
Redeem Israel, God, out all of his troubles.
By David. Judge me, Baba God, for I have walked in my integrity. I have trusted also in Baba God without wavering.
Examine me, Baba God, and prove me. Try my heart and my mind.
For una loving kindness is before my eyes. I have walked in una truth.
I have not sat with deceitful men, neither will I go in with fake people.
I hate the assembly of evildoers, and No go sit with the wicked.
I go wash my hands in innocence, so I go go about una altar, Baba God;
that I may make the voice of thanksgiving to be heard, and tell of all una wondrous deeds.
Baba God, I love the habitation of una house, the place where una glory dwells.
No gather my soul with sinners, nor my life with bloodthirsty men;
in whose hands is wickedness, dem right hand is full of bribes.
But as for me, I go walk in my integrity. Redeem me, and be merciful to me.
My foot stands in an even place. In the congregations I go bless Baba God.
By David. Baba God is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? Baba God is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?
When evildoers come at me to eat up my flesh, even my adversaries and my foes, dem stumbled and fell.
Though an army should encamp against me, my heart no go fear. Though war should rise against me, even then I go be confident.
One thing I have ask of Baba God, that I go seek after: that I may live in Baba God’s house all the days of my life, to see Baba God’s beauty, and to inquire in his temple.
For in the day of trouble he will keep me secretly in his pavilion. In the covert of his tabernacle he will hide me. He will lift me up on a rock.
Now my head Go be lifted up above my enemies around me; I go offer sacrifices of gladness in his tent. I go sing, yes, I go sing praises to Baba God.
Hear, Baba God, when I cry with my voice. Have mercy also on me, and answer me.
When you talk say, “Seek my face,” my heart talk say to you, “I go seek una face, Baba God.”
No hide una face from me. No put una worker away in anger. You Don dey my help. No abandon me, neither forsake me, God of my salvation.
When my father and my mother forsake me, then Baba God will take me up.
Teach me una way, Baba God. Lead me in a straight path, because of my enemies.
No deliver me over to the desire of my adversaries, for false witnesses have risen up against me, such as breathe out cruelty.
I be still confident of this: I go see the goodness of Baba God in the land of the living.
Wait for Baba God. Be strong, and let una heart take courage. Yes, wait for Baba God.
By David. To you, Baba God, I call. My rock, no be deaf to me; lest, if You be silent to me, I would become like people wey go down into the pit.
Hear the voice of my petitions, when I cry to you, when I lift up my hands toward una Most Holy Place.
No draw me away with the wicked, with the workers of wickedness who speak peace with dem neighbors, but mischief is in dem hearts.
Give dem according to dem work, and according to the wickedness of dem doings. Give dem according to the operation of dem hands. Bring back on dem Wetin dem deserve.
Because dem no respect the works of Baba God, nor the operation of his hands, he will break dem down and not build dem up.
Blessed be Baba God, because he has heard the voice of my petitions.
Baba God is my strength and my shield. My heart has trusted in him, and I be helped. So my heart greatly rejoices. With my song I go thank him.
Baba God is dem strength. He is a stronghold of salvation to his anointed.
Save una people, and bless una inheritance. Be dem shepherd also, and bear dem up forever.
A Psalm by David. Ascribe to Baba God, you sons of the mighty, ascribe to Baba God glory and strength.
Ascribe to Baba God the glory due to his name. Worship Baba God in holy array.
Baba God’s voice is on the waters. The God of glory thunders, even Baba God on many waters.
Baba God’s voice is powerful. Baba God’s voice is full of majesty.
Baba God’s voice breaks the cedars. Yes, Baba God breaks in pieces the cedars of Lebanon.
He makes dem also to skip like a calf; Lebanon and Sirion like a young, wild ox.
Baba God’s voice strikes with flashes of lightning.
Baba God’s voice shakes the wilderness. Baba God shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.
Baba God’s voice makes the deer calve, and strips the forests bare. In his temple everything says, “Glory!”
Baba God sat enthroned at the Flood. Yes, Baba God sits as King forever.
Baba God will give strength to his people. Baba God will bless his people with peace.
A Psalm. A Song for the Dedication of the Temple. By David. I go extol you, Baba God, for you have raised me up, and have not made my foes to glad well-well over me.
Baba God my God, I cried to you, and you have healed me.
Baba God, you have bring up my soul from Sheol. You have kept me alive, that I no suppose go down to the pit.
Sing praise to Baba God, you saints of his. Thank God to his holy name.
For his anger is but for a moment. His favor is for a lifetime. Weeping may stay for the night, but gladness comes in the morning.
As for me, I talk say in my prosperity, “I shall never be moved.”
You, Baba God, when you favored me, made my mountain stand strong; but when you hid una face, I was troubled.
I cried to you, Baba God. I made supplication to the Lord:
