“What profit is there in my destruction, if I go down to the pit? Shall the dust praise you? Shall it declare una truth?
Hear, Baba God, and have mercy on me. Baba God, be my helper.”
You have turned my mourning into dancing for me. You have removed my sackcloth, and clothed me with gladness,
To the end that my heart may sing praise to you, and not be silent. Baba God my God, I go Thank God to you forever!
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David. In you, Baba God, I take refuge. Let me never be disappointed. Deliver me in una righteousness.
Bow down una ear to me. Deliver me speedily. Be to me a strong rock, a house of defense to save me.
For You be my rock and my fortress, so for una name’s sake lead me and guide me.
Pluck me out of the net that dem have laid secretly for me, for You be my stronghold.
Into una hand I commend my spirit. You redeem me, Baba God, God of truth.
I hate people wey regard lying vanities, but I trust in Baba God.
I go be glad and glad well-well in una loving kindness, for you have seen my suffering. You have known my soul in adversities.
You have not shut me up into the hand of the enemy. You have set my feet in a large place.
Have mercy on me, Baba God, for I be in distress. My eye, my soul, and my body waste away with grief.
For my life is spent with sorrow, my years with sighing. My strength fails because of my wickedness. My bones are wasted away.
Because of all my adversaries I have become utterly contemptible to my neighbors, A fear to my acquaintances. People wey see me on the street fled from me.
I be forgotten from dem hearts like a dead man. I be like broken pottery.
For I have heard the slander of many, terror on every side, while dem conspire together against me, dem plot to take away my life.
But I trust in you, Baba God. I talk say, “You be my God.”
My times are in una hand. Deliver me from the hand of my enemies, and from people wey persecute me.
Make una face to shine on una worker. Save me in una loving kindness.
Let me not be disappointed, Baba God, for I have call on you. Let the wicked be disappointed. Make dem be silent in Sheol.
Let the lying lips be mute, which speak against the righteous insolently, with pride and contempt.
Oh how great is una goodness, which you have laid up for people wey fear you, which you have worked for people wey take refuge in you, before the sons of men!
In the shelter of una presence You go hide dem from the plotting of man. You go keep dem secretly in a dwelling away from the strife of tongues.
Praise be to Baba God, for he has shown me his marvelous loving kindness in a strong city.
As for me, I talk say in my haste, “I be cut off from before una eyes.” Nevertheless you heard the voice of my petitions when I cried to you.
Oh love Baba God, all you his saints! Baba God preserves the faithful, and fully recompenses him who behaves arrogantly.
Be strong, and let una heart take courage, all you who hope in Baba God.
By David. A contemplative psalm. Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven, whose sin is covered.
Blessed is the man to whom Baba God no dey impute wickedness, in whose spirit E get no deceit.
When I kept silence, my bones wasted away through my groaning all day long.
For day and night una hand was heavy on me. My strength was sapped in the heat of summer. Selah.
I acknowledged my sin to you. I didn’t hide my wickedness. I talk say, I go confess my wrongdoings to Baba God, and you forgave the wickedness of my sin. Selah.
For this, let everyone Wey be godly pray to you in a time when you may be find. Surely when the great waters overflow, dem no go reach to him.
You be my hiding place. You go preserve me from trouble. You go surround me with songs of deliverance. Selah.
I go instruct you and teach you in the way which you shall go. I go counsel you with my eye on you.
No be like the horse, or like the mule, which have no understanding, Wey be controlled by bit and bridle, or else Dem go not come near to you.
Many sorrows come to the wicked, but loving kindness shall surround him who trusts in Baba God.
Be glad in Baba God, and glad well-well, you righteous! Shout for gladness, all you Wey be upright in heart!
Glad well-well in Baba God, you righteous! Praise is fitting for the upright.
Thank God to Baba God with the lyre. Sing praises to him with the harp of ten strings.
Sing to him a new song. Play skillfully with a shout of gladness!
For Baba God’s word is right. All his work is done in faithfulness.
He loves righteousness and justice. The earth is full of the loving kindness of Baba God.
By Baba God’s word, the heavens were made; all dem army by the breath of his mouth.
He gathers the waters of the sea together as a heap. He lays up the deeps in storehouses.
Let all the earth fear Baba God. Let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of him.
For he spoke, and it was done. He commanded, and it stood firm.
Baba God brings the counsel of the nations to nothing. He makes the thoughts of the peoples to be of no effect.
The counsel of Baba God stands fast forever, the thoughts of his heart to all generations.
Blessed is the nation whose God is Baba God, the people whom he has chosen for his own inheritance.
Baba God looks from heaven. He sees all the sons of men.
From the place of his habitation he looks out on all the inhabitants of the earth,
person wey fashions all of dem hearts; and he considers all of dem works.
E get no king saved by the plenty people of an army. A mighty man No be delivered by great strength.
A horse is a vain thing for safety, neither does he deliver any by his great power.
See am, Baba God’s eye is on people wey fear him, on people wey hope in his loving kindness;
to deliver dem soul from death, to keep dem alive in famine.
Our soul has waited for Baba God. He is our help and our shield.
For our heart rejoices in him, because we have trusted in his holy name.
Let una loving kindness be on us, Baba God, since we have hoped in you.
By David; when he pretended to be insane before Abimelech, who drove him away, and he comot. I go bless Baba God at all times. His praise will always be in my mouth.
My soul shall boast in Baba God. The humble shall hear of it, and be glad.
Oh magnify Baba God with me. Make we exalt his name together.
I sought Baba God, and he answer me, and delivered me from all my fears.
Dem looked to him, and were radiant. Dem faces shall never be covered with shame.
This poor man cried, and Baba God heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles.
Baba God’s angel encamps around people wey fear him, and delivers dem.
Oh taste and see that Baba God is good. Blessed is the man who takes refuge in him.
Oh fear Baba God, you his saints, for E get no lack with people wey fear him.
The young lions do lack, and suffer hunger, but people wey seek Baba God no go lack any good thing.
Come, you pikin dem, listen to me. I go teach you the fear of Baba God.
Wey be someone who desires life, and loves many days, that he may see good?
Keep una tongue from evil, and una lips from speaking lies.
Depart from evil, and do good. seek peace, and pursue it.
Baba God’s eyes are toward the righteous. His ears listen to dem cry.
Baba God’s face is against people wey do evil, to cut off dem memory from the earth.
The righteous cry, and Baba God hears, and delivers dem out of all dem troubles.
Baba God is near to people wey have a broken heart, and saves people wey have a crushed spirit.
Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but Baba God delivers him out of dem all.
He protects all of his bones. Not one of dem is broken.
Evil shall kill the wicked. People wey hate the righteous go be condemned.
Baba God redeems the soul of his workers. None of people wey take refuge in him go be condemned.
By David. Contend, Baba God, with people wey contend with me. Fight against people wey fight against me.
Take hold of shield and buckler, and stand up for my help.
Brandish the spear and block people wey pursue me. Tell my soul, “I be una salvation.”
Let people wey seek after my soul be disappointed and bring to dishonor. Let people wey plot my ruin be turned back and confounded.
Make dem be as chaff before the wind, Baba God’s angel driving dem on.
Let dem way be dark and slippery, Baba God’s angel pursuing dem.
For without cause dem have hidden dem net in a pit for me. Without cause dem have dug a pit for my soul.
Let destruction come on him unawares. Let his net that he has hidden catch imself. Make e fall into that destruction.
My soul go be joyful in Baba God. It shall glad well-well in his salvation.
All my bones shall say, “Baba God, Wey be like you, who delivers the poor from him Wey be too strong for him; yes, the poor and the needy from him who robs him?”
Unrighteous witnesses rise up. Dem ask me about things that I no know about.
Dem reward me evil for good, to the bereaving of my soul.
But as for me, when dem were sick, my clothing was sackcloth. I afflicted my soul with fasting. My prayer come back into my own bosom.
I behaved myself as though it Bin dey my friend or my brother. I bowed down mourning, as one who mourns his mother.
But in my adversity, dem rejoiced, and gathered themselves together. The attackers gathered themselves together against me, and I didn’t know it. Dem tore at me, and didn’t cease.
Like the profane mockers in feasts, dem gnashed dem teeth at me.
Lord, how long will you look on? Rescue my soul from dem destruction, my precious life from the lions.
I go give you thanks in the great assembly. I go praise you among many people.
No let people Wey my enemies wrongfully glad well-well over me; neither let people wey hate me without a cause wink dem eyes.
For dem no speak peace, but dem devise deceitful words against people Wey quiet in the land.
Yes, dem opened dem mouth wide against me. Dem talk say, “Aha! Aha! Our eye has seen it!”
You have seen it, Baba God. No keep silent. Lord, no be far from me.
Wake up! Rise up to defend me, my God! My Lord, contend for me!
Vindicate me, Baba God my God, according to una righteousness. No Make dem gloat over me.
No Make dem say in dem heart, “Aha! That’s the way we want it!” No Make dem say, “We have swallowed him up!”
Make dem be disappointed and confounded together who glad well-well at my calamity. Make dem be clothed with shame and dishonor who magnify themselves against me.
Make dem shout for gladness and be glad, who favor my righteous cause. Yes, Make dem say continually, “Baba God be magnified, who has pleasure in the prosperity of his worker!”
My tongue shall talk about una righteousness and about una praise all day long.
For the Chief Musician. By David, the worker of Baba God. An inner sanctuary is within my heart about the disobedience of the wicked: “E get no fear of God before his eyes.”
For he flatters imself in his own eyes, too much to detect and hate his sin.
The words of his mouth are wickedness and deceit. He has ceased to be wise and to do good.
He plots wickedness on his bed. He sets imself in a way that No be good. He no dey abhor evil.
Una loving kindness, Baba God, is in the heavens. Una faithfulness reaches to the skies.
Una righteousness is like the mountains of God. Una judgments are like a great deep. Baba God, you preserve man and animal.
How precious is una loving kindness, God! The pikin dem of men take refuge under the shadow of una wings.
Dem go be abundantly satisfied with the abundance of una house. You go make dem drink of the river of una pleasures.
For with you is the spring of life. In una light shall we see light.
Oh continue una loving kindness to people wey know you, una righteousness to the upright in heart.
No let the foot of pride come against me. No let the hand of the wicked drive me away.
There the workers of wickedness are fallen. Dem be thrust down, and no go be able to rise.
By David. No fret because of evildoers, neither be envious against people wey work unrighteousness.
For dem shall soon be cut down like the grass, and wither like the green herb.
Trust in Baba God, and do good. Live in the land, and enjoy safe pasture.
Also delight yourself in Baba God, and he will give you the desires of una heart.
Commit una way to Baba God. Trust also in him, and he will do this:
he will make una righteousness go out as the light, and una justice as the noon day sun.
Rest in Baba God, and wait patiently for him. No fret because of him who prospers in his way, because of the man who makes wicked plots happen.
Cease from anger, and forsake serious anger. No fret, it leads only to evildoing.
For evildoers go be cut off, but people wey wait for Baba God shall inherit the land.
For yet a little while, and the wicked Go be no more. Yes, though you look for his place, he no be there.
But the humble shall inherit the land, and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.
The wicked plots against the just, and gnashes at him with his teeth.
The Lord will laugh at him, for he sees that his day is coming.
The wicked have drawn out the sword, and have bent dem bow, to throw down the poor and needy, to kill people Wey upright on the path.
Dem sword shall enter into dem own heart. Dem bows go be broken.
Better is a little that the righteous has, than the abundance of many wicked.
For the arms of the wicked go be broken, but Baba God upholds the righteous.
Baba God knows the days of the perfect. Dem inheritance go be forever.
Dem no go be disappointed in the time of evil. In the days of famine dem go be satisfied.
But the wicked shall perish. The enemies of Baba God go be like the beauty of the fields. Dem go vanish — vanish like smoke.
The wicked borrow, and no pay back, but the righteous give generously.
For such as are blessed by him shall inherit the land. People Wey cursed by him go be cut off.
A man’s goings are established by Baba God. He delights in his way.
Though he stumble, he no go fall, for Baba God holds him up with his hand.
I Don dey young, and now am old, yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his pikin dem begging for bread.
All day long he deals graciously, and lends. His offspring is blessed.
Depart from evil, and do good. Live securely forever.
For Baba God loves justice, and no dey forsake his saints. Dem be preserved forever, but the pikin dem of the wicked go be cut off.
The righteous shall inherit the land, and live in it forever.
The mouth of the righteous talks of wisdom. His tongue speaks justice.
The law of his God is in his heart. None of his steps shall slide.
The wicked watches the righteous, and seeks to kill him.
Baba God No go leave him in his hand, nor condemn him when he is judged.
Wait for Baba God, and keep his way, and he will exalt you to inherit the land. When the wicked are cut off, you shall see it.
I have seen the wicked in great power, spreading imself like a green tree in its native soil.
But he passed away, and see am, he No be. Yes, I sought him, but he could not be find.
Mark the perfect man, and see the upright, for E get a future for the man of peace.
As for transgressors, dem go be destroyed together. The future of the wicked go be cut off.
But the salvation of the righteous is from Baba God. He is dem stronghold in the time of trouble.
Baba God helps dem, and rescues dem. He rescues dem from the wicked, and saves dem, Because dem have taken refuge in him.
A Psalm by David, for a memorial. Baba God, no rebuke me in una serious anger, neither chasten me in una hot displeasure.
For una arrows have pierced me, una hand presses hard on me.
E get no soundness in my flesh because of una indignation, neither is there any health in my bones because of my sin.
For my iniquities have gone over my head. As a heavy burden, Dem be too heavy for me.
My wounds are loathsome and corrupt, because of my foolishness.
I be pained and bowed down greatly. I go mourning all day long.
For my waist is filled with burning. E get no soundness in my flesh.
I be faint and severely bruised. I have groaned by reason of the anguish of my heart.
Lord, all my desire is before you. My groaning No be hidden from you.
My heart throbs. My strength fails me. As for the light of my eyes, it has also left me.
My lovers and my friends stand aloof from my plague. My family people stand far away.
Dem also who seek after my life lay snares. People wey seek my hurt speak mischievous things, and meditate deceits all day long.
But I, as a deaf man, no hear. I be as a mute man who no dey open his mouth.
Yes, I be as a man who no dey hear, in whose mouth are no reproofs.
For in you, Baba God, do I hope. You go answer, Lord my God.
For I talk say, “No Make dem gloat over me, or exalt themselves over me when my foot slips.”
For I be ready to fall. My pain is continually before me.
For I go declare my wickedness. I go be sorry for my sin.
But my enemies are vigorous and many. People wey hate me without reason are numerous.
Dem who also render evil for good are adversaries to me, because I follow Wetin be good.
No forsake me, Baba God. My God, no be far from me.
Hurry to help me, Lord, my salvation.
For the Chief Musician. For Jeduthun. A Psalm by David. I talk say, “I go watch my ways, so that I no sin with my tongue. I go keep my mouth with a bridle while the wicked is before me.”
I was mute with silence. I held my peace, even from good. My sorrow was stirred.
My heart was hot within me. While I meditated, the fire burned. I spoke with my tongue:
“Baba God, show me my end, Wetin be the measure of my days. Let me know how frail I be.
See am, you have made my days hand widths. My lifetime is as nothing before you. Surely every man stands as a breath.” Selah.
“Surely every man walks like a shadow. Surely dem busy themselves in vain. He heaps up, and no dey know who shall gather.
Now, Lord, what do I wait for? My hope is in you.
Deliver me from all my wrongdoings. No make me the reproach of the foolish.
I was mute. I didn’t open my mouth, because you did it.
Remove una scourge away from me. I be overcome by the blow of una hand.
When you rebuke and correct man for wickedness, You consume his wealth like a moth. Surely every man is but a breath.” Selah.
“Hear my prayer, Baba God, and give ear to my cry. No be silent at my tears. For I be a stranger with you, a foreigner, as all my fathers were.
Oh spare me, that I may recover strength, before I go away, and exist no more.”
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David. I waited patiently for Baba God. He turned to me, and heard my cry.
He bring me up also out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay. He set my feet on a rock, and give me a firm place to stand.
He has put a new song in my mouth, even praise to our God. Many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in Baba God.
Blessed is the man who makes Baba God his trust, and no dey respect the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies.

Many, Baba God, my God, are the wonderful works which you have done, and una thoughts which are toward us. Dem no fit be declared back to you. If I would declare and speak of dem, Dem be more than can be counted.
Sacrifice and offering you didn’t desire. You have opened my ears. You have not required burnt offering and sin offering.
Then I talk say, “See am, I have come. It is written about me in the book in the scroll.
I delight to do una will, my God. Yes, una law is within my heart.”
I have proclaimed glad news of righteousness in the great assembly. See am, I go not seal my lips, Baba God, you know.
I have not hidden una righteousness within my heart. I have declared una faithfulness and una salvation. I have not concealed una loving kindness and una truth from the great assembly.
No withhold una tender mercies from me, Baba God. Let una loving kindness and una truth continually preserve me.
For innumerable evils have surrounded me. My iniquities have overtaken me, so that I be not able to look up. Dem be more than the hairs of my head. My heart has failed me.
Be pleased, Baba God, to deliver me. Hurry to help me, Baba God.
Make dem be disappointed and confounded together who seek after my soul to destroy it. Make dem be turned backward and bring to dishonor who delight in my hurt.
Make dem be desolate by reason of dem shame that tell me, “Aha! Aha!”
Let all people wey seek you glad well-well and be glad in you. Let such as love una salvation say continually, “Let Baba God be exalted!”
But I be poor and needy. May the Lord think about me. You be my help and my deliverer. No delay, my God.
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David. Blessed is person wey considers the poor. Baba God will deliver him in the day of evil.
Baba God will preserve him, and keep him alive. He go be blessed on the earth, and he No go surrender him to the will of his enemies.
Baba God will sustain him on his sickbed, and restore him from his bed of illness.
I talk say, “Baba God, have mercy on me! Heal me, for I have sinned against you.”
My enemies speak evil against me: “When will he die, and his name perish?”
If he comes to see me, he speaks falsehood. His heart gathers wickedness to itself. When he goes abroad, he tells it.
All who hate me whisper together against me. Dem imagine the worst for me.
“An evil disease”, dem say, “has afflicted him. Now that he lies he shall rise up no more.”
Yes, my own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, who ate bread with me, has lifted up his heel against me.
But you, Baba God, have mercy on me, and raise me up, that I may repay dem.
By this I know that you delight in me, because my enemy no dey triumph over me.
As for me, you uphold me in my integrity, and set me in una presence forever.
Blessed be Baba God, the God of Israel, from everlasting and to everlasting! Amen and amen.
For the Chief Musician. A contemplation by the sons of Korah. As the deer pants for the water brooks, so my soul pants after you, God.
My soul thirsts for God, for the living God. When shall I come and appear before God?
My tears Don dey my chop day and night, while dem continually ask me, “Where is una God?”
These things I remember, and pour out my soul within me, how I used to go with the crowd, and led dem to God’s house, with the voice of gladness and praise, a plenty people keeping a holy day.
Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him for the saving help of his presence.
My God, my soul is in despair within me. So I remember you from the land of the Jordan, the heights of Hermon, from the hill Mizar.
Deep calls to deep at the noise of una waterfalls. All una waves and una billows have swept over me.
Baba God will command his loving kindness in the daytime. In the night his song go be with me: a prayer to the God of my life.
I go ask God, my rock, “Why have you forgotten me? Why do I go mourning because of the oppression of the enemy?”
As with a sword in my bones, my adversaries reproach me, while dem continually ask me, “Where is una God?”
Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him, the saving help of my countenance, and my God.
Vindicate me, God, and plead my cause against an ungodly nation. Oh, deliver me from deceitful and wicked men.
For You be the God of my strength. Why have you rejected me? Why do I go mourning because of the oppression of the enemy?
Oh, send out una light and una truth. Make dem lead me. Make dem bring me to una holy hill, To una tents.
Then I go go to the altar of God, to God, my exceeding gladness. I go praise you on the harp, God, my God.
Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him: my Savior, my helper, and my God.
For the Chief Musician. By the sons of Korah. A contemplative psalm. We have heard with our ears, God; our fathers have told us, what work you did in dem days, in the days of old.
You drove out the nations with una hand, but you planted dem. You afflicted the peoples, but you spread dem abroad.
For dem didn’t get the land in possession by dem own sword, neither did dem own arm save dem; but una right hand, and una arm, and the light of una face, because you were favorable to dem.
You be my King, God. Command victories for Jacob!
Through you, will we push down our adversaries. Through una name, will we tread dem under who rise up against us.
For I go not trust in my bow, neither shall my sword save me.
But you have saved us from our adversaries, and have shamed people wey hate us.
In God we have made our boast all day long, We go Thank God to una name forever. Selah.
But now you rejected us, and bring us to dishonor, and no go out with our armies.
You make us turn back from the adversary. People wey hate us take plunder for themselves.
You have made us like sheep for chop, and have scattered us among the nations.
You sell una people for nothing, and have gained nothing from dem sale.
You make us a reproach to our neighbors, a scoffing and a derision to people Wey around us.
You make us a byword among the nations, a shaking of the head among the peoples.
All day long my dishonor is before me, and shame covers my face,
At the taunt of one who reproaches and verbally abuses, because of the enemy and the avenger.
All this has come on us, yet have we not forgotten you, Neither have we been false to una covenant.
Our heart has not turned back, neither have our steps strayed from una path,
Though you have crushed us in the haunt of jackals, and covered us with the shadow of death.
If we have forgotten the name of our God, or spread out our hands to a strange god;
no go God search this out? For he knows the secrets of the heart.
Yes, for una sake We be killed all day long. We be regarded as sheep for the slaughter.
Wake up! Why do you sleep, Lord? Arise! No reject us forever.
Why do you hide una face, and forget our suffering and our oppression?
For our soul is bowed down to the dust. Our body clings to the earth.
Rise up to help us. Redeem us for una loving kindness’ sake.

For the Chief Musician. Set to “The Lilies.” A contemplation by the sons of Korah. A wedding song. My heart overflows with a noble theme. I recite my verses for the king. My tongue is like the pen of a skillful writer.
You be the most excellent of the sons of men. Grace has anointed una lips, so God has blessed you forever.
Strap una sword on una thigh, mighty one: una splendor and una majesty.
In una majesty ride on victoriously on behalf of truth, humility, and righteousness. Let una right hand display awesome deeds.
Una arrows are sharp. The nations fall under you, with arrows in the heart of the king’s enemies.
Una throne, God, is forever and ever. A scepter of equity is the scepter of una kingdom.
You have love righteousness, and hated wickedness. So God, una God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above una fellows.
All una garments smell like myrrh, aloes, and cassia. Out of ivory palaces stringed instruments have made you glad.
Kings’ daughters are among una honorable women. At una right hand the queen stands in gold of Ophir.
Listen, daughter, consider, and turn una ear. Forget una own people, and also una father’s house.
So the king will desire una beauty, honor him, for he is una lord.
The daughter of Tyre comes with a gift. The rich among the people entreat una favor.
The princess inside is all glorious. Her clothing is interwoven with gold.
She go be led to the king in embroidered work. The virgins, her companions who follow her, go be bring to you.
With gladness and rejoicing dem go be led. Dem shall enter into the king’s palace.
Una sons will take the place of una fathers. You shall make dem princes in all the earth.
I go make una name to be remember in all generations. So the peoples shall give you thanks forever and ever.
For the Chief Musician. By the sons of Korah. According to Alamoth. God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
So we no go be afraid, though the earth changes, though the mountains are shaken into the heart of the seas;
though its waters roar and are troubled, though the mountains tremble with dem swelling. Selah.
E get a river, the streams of which make the city of God glad, the holy place of the tents of the Most High.
God is within her. She no go be moved. God will help her at dawn.
The nations raged. The kingdoms were moved. He lifted his voice, and the earth melted.
Baba God of Armies is with us. The God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.
Come, see Baba God’s works, what desolations he has made in the earth.
He makes wars cease to the end of the earth. He breaks the bow, and shatters the spear. He burns the chariots in the fire.
“Be still, and know that I be God. I go be exalted among the nations. I go be exalted in the earth.”
Baba God of Armies is with us. The God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by the sons of Korah. Oh clap una hands, all you nations. Shout to God with the voice of triumph!
For Baba God Most High is awesome. He is a great King over all the earth.
He subdues nations under us, and peoples under our feet.
He chooses our inheritance for us, the glory of Jacob whom he love. Selah.
God has gone up with a shout, Baba God with the sound of a trumpet.
Sing praises to God, sing praises. Sing praises to our King, sing praises.
For God is the King of all the earth. Sing praises with understanding.
God reigns over the nations. God sits on his holy throne.
The princes of the peoples are gathered together, the people of the God of Abraham. For the shields of the earth belong to God. He is greatly exalted!
A Song. A Psalm by the sons of Korah. Great is Baba God, and greatly to be praised, in the city of our God, in his holy mountain.
Beautiful in elevation, the gladness of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the north sides, the city of the great King.
God has shown imself in her citadels as a refuge.
For, see am, the kings assembled themselves, dem passed by together.
Dem see it, then dem were amazed. Dem were dismayed. Dem hurried away.
Trembling take hold of dem there, pain, as of a woman in travail.
With the east wind, you break the ships of Tarshish.
As we have heard, so we have seen, in the city of Baba God of Armies, in the city of our God. God will establish it forever. Selah.
We have thought about una loving kindness, God, in the middle of una temple.
As is una name, God, so is una praise to every corner of the world. Una right hand is full of righteousness.
Let Mount Zion be glad! Let the daughters of Judah glad well-well, Because of una judgments.
Walk about Zion, and go around her. Number its towers.
Mark well her bulwarks. Consider her palaces, that you may tell it to the next generation.
For this God is our God forever and ever. He Go be our guide even to death.
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by the sons of Korah. Hear this, all you peoples. Listen, all you inhabitants of the world,
both low and high, rich and poor together.
My mouth will speak words of wisdom. My heart shall utter understanding.
I go incline my ear to a proverb. I go open my riddle on the harp.
Why should I fear in the days of evil, when wickedness at my heels surrounds me?
People wey trust in dem wealth, and boast in the plenty people of dem riches —
none of dem can by any means redeem his brother, nor give God a ransom for him.
For the redemption of dem life is costly, no payment is ever enough,
that he should live on forever, that he no suppose see corruption.
For he sees that wise men die; likewise the fool and the senseless perish, and leave dem wealth to others.
Dem inward thought is that dem houses will endure forever, and dem dwelling places to all generations. Dem name dem lands after themselves.
But man, despite his riches, no dey endure. He is like the animals that perish.
This is the destiny of people Wey foolish, and of people wey approve dem sayings. Selah.
Dem be appointed as a flock for Sheol. Death go be dem shepherd. The upright go get dominion over dem in the morning. Dem beauty shall decay in Sheol, far from dem mansion.
But God will redeem my soul from the power of Sheol, for he will receive me. Selah.
No fear when a man is made rich, when the glory of his house is increased;
for when he dies he will carry nothing away. His glory no go descend after him.
Though while he lived he blessed his soul — and men praise you when you do well for yourself —
he shall go to the generation of his fathers. Dem shall never see the light.
A man who has riches without understanding, is like the animals that perish.
A Psalm by Asaph. The Mighty One, God, Baba God, speaks, and calls the earth from sunrise to sunset.
Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God shines out.
Our God comes, and No dey keep silent. A fire devours before him. It is very stormy around him.
He calls to the heavens above, to the earth, that he may judge his people:
“Gather my saints together to me, people wey have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.”
The heavens shall declare his righteousness, for God imself is judge. Selah.
“Hear, my people, and I go speak; Israel, and I go testify against you. I be God, una God.
I no rebuke you for una sacrifices. Una burnt offerings are continually before me.
I have no need for a bull from una stall, nor male goats from una pens.
For every animal of the forest is mine, and the livestock on a thousand hills.
I know all the birds of the mountains. The wild animals of the field are mine.
If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is mine, and all that is in it.
Will I eat the meat of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
Offer to God the sacrifice of thanksgiving. Pay una vows to the Most High.
Call on me in the day of trouble. I go deliver you, and You go honor me.”
But to the wicked God says, “What right do you have to declare my statutes, that you have taken my covenant on una lips,
since you hate instruction, and throw my words behind you?
When you see a thief, you consented with him, and have participated with adulterers.
“You give una mouth to evil. Una tongue frames deceit.
You sit and speak against una brother. You slander una own mother’s son.
You have done these things, and I kept silent. You thought that I was just like you. I go rebuke you, and accuse you in front of una eyes.
“Now consider this, you who forget God, lest I tear you into pieces, and there be Nobody to deliver.
Anybody wey offers the sacrifice of thanksgiving glorifies me, and prepares his way so that I go show God’s salvation to him.”

For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David, when Nathan the prophet come to him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba. Have mercy on me, God, according to una loving kindness. According to the plenty people of una tender mercies, blot out my wrongdoings.
Wash me thoroughly from my wickedness. Cleanse me from my sin.
For I know my wrongdoings. My sin is constantly before me.
Against you, and you only, I have sinned, and done that which is evil in una sight; that you may be proved right when you speak, and justified when you judge.
See am, I was born in wickedness. In sin my mother conceived me.
See am, you desire truth in the inward parts. You teach me wisdom in the inmost place.
Purify me with hyssop, and I go be clean. Wash me, and I go be whiter than snow.
Let me hear gladness and gladness, That the bones which you have broken may glad well-well.
Hide una face from my sins, and blot out all of my iniquities.
Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.
No throw me from una presence, and no take una holy Spirit from me.
Restore to me the gladness of una salvation. Uphold me with a willing spirit.
Then I go teach transgressors una ways. Sinners go be converted to you.
Deliver me from the guilt of bloodshed, O God, the God of my salvation. My tongue shall sing aloud of una righteousness.
Lord, open my lips. My mouth shall declare una praise.
For you no delight in sacrifice, or else I would give it. You have no pleasure in burnt offering.
The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit. A broken and contrite heart, O God, You go not despise.
Do well in una good pleasure to Zion. Build the walls of Jerusalem.
Then You go delight in the sacrifices of righteousness, in burnt offerings and in whole burnt offerings. Then Dem go offer bulls on una altar.

For the Chief Musician. A contemplation by David, when Doeg the Edomite come and told Saul, “David has come to Ahimelech’s house.” Why do you boast of mischief, mighty man? God’s loving kindness endures continually.
Una tongue plots destruction, like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.
You love evil more than good, lying rather than speaking the truth. Selah.
You love all devouring words, you deceitful tongue.
God will likewise destroy you forever. He will take you up, and pluck you out of una tent, and root you out of the land of the living. Selah.
The righteous also will see it, and fear, and laugh at him, saying,
“See am, this is the man who didn’t make God his strength, but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened imself in his wickedness.”
But as for me, I be like a green olive tree in God’s house. I trust in God’s loving kindness forever and ever.
I go give you thanks forever, because you have done it. I go hope in una name, for it is good, in the presence of una saints.

For the Chief Musician. To the tune of “Mahalath.” A contemplation by David. The fool has talk say in his heart, “E get no God.” Dem be corrupt, and have done abominable wickedness. E get Nobody wey do good.
God looks down from heaven on the pikin dem of men, to see if E get any who understand, who seek after God.
Every one of dem has gone back. Dem have become filthy together. E get Nobody wey do good, no, not one.
Have the workers of wickedness no knowledge, who eat up my people as dem eat bread, and no call on God?
There dem were in great fear, where no fear was, for God has scattered the bones of him who encamps against you. You have put dem to shame, because God has rejected dem.
Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion! When God brings back his people from captivity, then Jacob shall glad well-well, and Israel go be glad.

For the Chief Musician. On stringed instruments. A contemplation by David, when the Ziphites come and talk say to Saul, “No be David hiding imself among us?” Save me, God, by una name. Vindicate me in una might.
Hear my prayer, God. Listen to the words of my mouth.
For strangers have risen up against me. Violent men have sought after my soul. Dem haven’t set God before dem. Selah.
See am, God is my helper. The Lord is the one who sustains my soul.
He will repay the evil to my enemies. Destroy dem in una truth.
With a free will offering, I go sacrifice to you. I go Thank God to una name, Baba God, for it is good.
For he has delivered me out of all trouble. My eye has seen triumph over my enemies.
For the Chief Musician. On stringed instruments. A contemplation by David. Listen to my prayer, God. No hide yourself from my supplication.
Attend to me, and answer me. I be restless in my complaint, and moan,
Because of the voice of the enemy, Because of the oppression of the wicked. For dem bring suffering on me. In anger dem hold a grudge against me.
My heart is severely pained within me. The terrors of death have fallen on me.
Fearfulness and trembling have come on me. Horror has overwhelmed me.
I talk say, “Oh that I had wings like a dove! Then I would fly away, and be at rest.
See am, then I would wander far off. I would lodge in the wilderness.” Selah.
“I would hurry to a shelter from the stormy wind and storm.”
Confuse dem, Lord, and confound dem language, for I have seen violence and strife in the city.
Day and night dem prowl around on its walls. Malice and abuse are also within her.
Destructive forces are within her. Threats and lies no depart from her streets.
For it No be an enemy who insulted me, then I could have endured it. Neither was it person wey hated me who raised imself up against me, then I would have hidden myself from him.
But it was you, a man like me, my companion, and my familiar friend.
We take sweet fellowship together. We walked in God’s house with company.
Let death come suddenly on dem. Make dem go down alive into Sheol. For wickedness is among dem, in dem dwelling.
As for me, I go call on God. Baba God will save me.
Evening, morning, and at noon, I go cry out in distress. He will hear my voice.
He has redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me, although E get many who oppose me.
God, Wey be enthroned forever, will hear, and answer dem. Selah. Dem never change, who no fear God.
He raises his hands against his friends. He has violated his covenant.
His mouth was smooth as butter, but his heart was war. His words were softer than oil, yet dem were drawn swords.
Throw una burden on Baba God, and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved.
But you, God, will bring dem down into the pit of destruction. Bloodthirsty and deceitful men no go live out half dem days, but I go trust in you.

For the Chief Musician. To the tune of “Silent Dove in Distant Lands.” A poem by David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath. Be merciful to me, God, for man wants to swallow me up. All day long, he attacks and oppresses me.
My enemies want to swallow me up all day long, for Dem be many who fight proudly against me.
When I be afraid, I go put my trust in you.
In God, I praise his word. In God, I put my trust. I go not be afraid. What can flesh do to me?
All day long dem twist my words. All dem thoughts are against me for evil.
Dem conspire and lurk, watching my steps, Dem be eager to take my life.
Shall dem escape by wickedness? In anger throw down the peoples, God.
You count my wanderings. You put my tears into una bottle. No be dem in una book?
Then my enemies shall turn back in the day that I call. I know this, that God is for me.
In God, I go praise his word. In Baba God, I go praise his word.
I have put my trust in God. I go not be afraid. What can man do to me?
Una vows are on me, God. I go give thank offerings to you.
For you have delivered my soul from death, and prevented my feet from falling, that I may walk before God in the light of the living.

For the Chief Musician. To the tune of “No Destroy.” A poem by David, when he fled from Saul, in the cave. Be merciful to me, God, be merciful to me, for my soul takes refuge in you. Yes, in the shadow of una wings, I go take refuge, until disaster has passed.
I cry out to God Most High, to God who accomplishes my requests for me.
He will send from heaven, and save me, he rebukes the one Wey be pursuing me. Selah. God will send out his loving kindness and his truth.
My soul is among lions. I lie among people Wey set on fire, even the sons of men, whose teeth are spears and arrows, and dem tongue a sharp sword.
Be exalted, God, above the heavens! Let una glory be above all the earth!
Dem have prepared a net for my steps. My soul is bowed down. Dem dig a pit before me. Dem fall into the middle of it themselves. Selah.
My heart is steadfast, God, my heart is steadfast. I go sing, yes, I go sing praises.
Wake up, my glory! Wake up, lute and harp! I go wake up the dawn.
I go Thank God to you, Lord, among the peoples. I go sing praises to you among the nations.
For una great loving kindness reaches to the heavens, and una truth to the skies.
Be exalted, God, above the heavens. Let una glory be over all the earth.
For the Chief Musician. To the tune of “No Destroy.” A poem by David. Do you indeed speak righteousness, silent ones? Do you judge blamelessly, you sons of men?
No, in una heart you plot injustice. You measure out the violence of una hands in the earth.
The wicked go astray from the womb. Dem be wayward as soon as Dem be born, speaking lies.
Dem poison is like the poison of a snake; like a deaf cobra that stops its ear,
which no dey listen to the voice of charmers, no matter how skillful the charmer may be.
Break dem teeth, God, in dem mouth. Break out the great teeth of the young lions, Baba God.
Make dem vanish like water that flows away. When dem draw the bow, let dem arrows be made blunt.
Make dem be like a snail which melts and passes away, like the stillborn pikin, who has not seen the sun.
Before una pots can feel the heat of the thorns, he will sweep away the green and the burning alike.
The righteous shall glad well-well when he sees the vengeance. He shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked;
so that men shall say, “Most certainly E get a reward for the righteous. Most certainly E get a God who judges the earth.”

For the Chief Musician. To the tune of “No Destroy.” A poem by David, when Saul sent, and dem watched the house to kill him. Deliver me from my enemies, my God. Set me on high from people wey rise up against me.
Deliver me from the workers of wickedness. Save me from the bloodthirsty men.
For, see am, dem lie in wait for my soul. The mighty gather themselves together against me, not for my disobedience, nor for my sin, Baba God.
I have done no wrong, yet Dem be ready to attack me. Rise up, see am, and help me!
You, Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, rouse yourself to punish the nations. Show no mercy to the wicked traitors. Selah.
Dem return at evening, howling like dogs, and prowl around the city.
See am, dem spew with dem mouth. Swords are in dem lips, “For”, dem say, “wey hear us?”
But you, Baba God, laugh at dem. You scoff at all the nations.
Oh, my Strength, I watch for you, for God is my high tower.
My God will go before me with his loving kindness. God will let me look at my enemies in triumph.
No kill dem, or my people may forget. Scatter dem by una power, and bring dem down, Lord our shield.
For the sin of dem mouth, and the words of dem lips, Make dem be caught in dem pride, for the curses and lies which dem utter.
Consume dem in serious anger. Consume dem, and Dem go be no more. Make dem know that God rules in Jacob, to every corner of the world. Selah.
At evening Make dem return. Make dem howl like a dog, and go around the city.
Dem shall wander up and down for chop, and wait all night if dem no be satisfied.
But I go sing of una strength. Yes, I go sing aloud of una loving kindness in the morning. For you Don dey my high tower, a refuge in the day of my distress.
To you, my strength, I go sing praises. For God is my high tower, the God of my mercy.

For the Chief Musician. To the tune of “The Lily of the Covenant.” A teaching poem by David, when he fought with Aram Naharaim and with Aram Zobah, and Joab come back, and killed twelve thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt. God, you have rejected us. You have broken us down. You Don dey angry. Restore us, again.
You have made the land tremble. You have torn it. Mend its fractures, for it quakes.
You have shown una people hard things. You have made us drink the wine that makes us stagger.
You have given a banner to people wey fear you, that it may be displayed because of the truth. Selah.
So that una beloved may be delivered, save with una right hand, and answer us.
God has spoken from his sanctuary: “I go triumph. I go divide Shechem, and measure out the valley of Succoth.
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine. Ephraim also is the defense of my head. Judah is my scepter.
Moab is my wash basin. I go throw my shoe on Edom. I shout in triumph over Philistia.”
Who will bring me into the strong city? Who has led me to Edom?
Haven’t you, God, rejected us? You no go out with our armies, God.
Give us help against the adversary, for the help of man is vain.
Through God we shall do valiantly, for it is person wey will tread down our adversaries.
For the Chief Musician. For a stringed instrument. By David. Hear my cry, God. Listen to my prayer.
From the end of the earth, I go call to you, when my heart is overwhelmed. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
For you Don dey a refuge for me, a strong tower from the enemy.
I go live in una tent forever. I go take refuge in the shelter of una wings. Selah.
For you, God, have heard my vows. You have given me the heritage of people wey fear una name.
You go prolong the king’s life; his years go be for generations.
He go be enthroned in God’s presence forever. Appoint una loving kindness and truth, that dem may preserve him.
So I go sing praise to una name forever, that I may fulfill my vows daily.
For the Chief Musician. To Jeduthun. A Psalm by David. My soul rests in God alone. My salvation is from him.
He alone is my rock and my salvation, my fortress — I go never be greatly shaken.
How long will you assault a man, would all of you throw him down, Like a leaning wall, like a tottering fence?
Dem fully intend to throw him down from his lofty place. Dem delight in lies. Dem bless with dem mouth, but dem curse inwardly. Selah.
My soul, wait in silence for God alone, for my expectation is from him.
He alone is my rock and my salvation, my fortress. I go not be shaken.
With God is my salvation and my honor. The rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God.
Trust in him at all times, you people. Pour out una heart before him. God is a refuge for us. Selah.
Surely men of low degree are just a breath, and men of high degree are a lie. In the balances Dem go go up. Dem be together lighter than a breath.
No trust in oppression. No become vain in robbery. If riches increase, no set una heart on dem.
God has spoken once; twice I have heard this, that power belongs to God.
Also to you, Lord, belongs loving kindness, for you reward every man according to his work.
A Psalm by David, when he was in the desert of Judah. God, You be my God. I go earnestly seek you. My soul thirsts for you. My flesh longs for you, in a dry and weary land, where E get no water.
So I have seen you in the sanctuary, watching una power and una glory.
Because una loving kindness is better than life, my lips shall praise you.
So I go bless you while I live. I go lift up my hands in una name.
My soul go be satisfied as with the richest chop. My mouth shall praise you with joyful lips,
when I remember you on my bed, and think about you in the night watches.
For you Don dey my help. I go glad well-well in the shadow of una wings.
My soul stays close to you. Una right hand holds me up.
But people wey seek my soul, to destroy it, shall go into the lower parts of the earth.
Dem go be given over to the power of the sword. Dem go be jackal chop.
But the king shall glad well-well in God. Everybody wey swears by him will praise him, for the mouth of people wey speak lies go be silenced.
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David. Hear my voice, God, in my complaint. Preserve my life from fear of the enemy.
Hide me from the conspiracy of the wicked, from the noisy crowd of the ones doing evil;
who sharpen dem tongue like a sword, and aim dem arrows, deadly words,
to shoot innocent men from ambushes. Dem shoot at him suddenly and fearlessly.
Dem encourage themselves in evil plans. Dem talk about laying snares secretly. Dem say, “Who will see dem?”
Dem plot injustice, saying, “We have made a perfect plan!” Surely man’s mind and heart are cunning.
But God will shoot at dem. Dem go be suddenly struck down with an arrow.
Dem own tongues shall ruin dem. All who see dem will shake dem heads.
All mankind go be afraid. Dem shall declare the work of God, and shall wisely ponder what he has done.
The righteous go be glad in Baba God, and shall take refuge in him. All the upright in heart shall praise him!
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David. A song. Praise waits for you, God, in Zion. To you shall vows be performed.
You who hear prayer, to you all men will come.
Sins overwhelmed me, but you atoned for our wrongdoings.
Blessed is one whom you choose, and cause to come near, that he may live in una courts. We go be filled with the goodness of una house, una holy temple.
By awesome deeds of righteousness, you answer us, God of our salvation. You Wey be the hope of all every corner of the world, of people Wey far away on the sea;
Who by his power forms the mountains, having armed yourself with strength;
who stills the roaring of the seas, the roaring of dem waves, and the turmoil of the nations.
Dem also who live in faraway places are afraid at una wonders. You call the morning’s dawn and the evening with songs of gladness.
You visit the earth, and water it. You greatly enrich it. The river of God is full of water. You provide dem grain, for so you have ordained it.
You drench its furrows. You level its ridges. You soften it with showers. You bless it with a crop.
You crown the year with una bounty. Una carts overflow with abundance.
The wilderness grasslands overflow. The hills are clothed with gladness.
The pastures are covered with flocks. The valleys also are clothed with grain. Dem shout for gladness! Dem also sing.
For the Chief Musician. A song. A Psalm. Make a joyful shout to God, all the earth!
Sing to the glory of his name! Offer glory and praise!
Tell God, “How awesome are una deeds! Through the greatness of una power, una enemies submit themselves to you.
All the earth will worship you, and will sing to you; Dem go sing to una name.” Selah.
Come, and see God’s deeds — awesome work on behalf of the pikin dem of men.
He turned the sea into dry land. Dem go through the river on foot. There, we rejoiced in him.
He rules by his might forever. His eyes watch the nations. No let the rebellious rise up against him. Selah.
Praise our God, you peoples! Make the sound of his praise heard,
who preserves our life among the living, and no dey allow our feet to be moved.
For you, God, have tested us. You have refined us, as silver is refined.
You bring us into prison. You laid a burden on our backs.
You allowed men to ride over our heads. We go through fire and through water, but you bring us to the place of abundance.
I go come into una temple with burnt offerings. I go pay my vows to you,
which my lips promised, and my mouth spoke, when I was in distress.
I go offer to you burnt offerings of fat animals, with the offering of rams, I go offer bulls with goats. Selah.
Come, and hear, all you who fear God. I go declare what he has done for my soul.
I cried to him with my mouth. He was extolled with my tongue.
If I cherished sin in my heart, the Lord wouldn’t have listened.
But most certainly, God has listened. He has heard the voice of my prayer.
Blessed be God, who has not turned away my prayer, nor his loving kindness from me.
For the Chief Musician. With stringed instruments. A Psalm. A song. May God be merciful to us, bless us, and cause his face to shine on us. Selah.
That una way may be known on earth, and una salvation among people for everywhere,
let the peoples praise you, God. Let all the peoples praise you.
Oh let the nations be glad and sing for gladness, for You go judge the peoples with equity, and govern the nations on earth. Selah.
Let the peoples praise you, God. Let all the peoples praise you.
The earth has yielded its increase. God, even our own God, will bless us.
God will bless us. All every corner of the world shall fear him.
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David. A song. Let God arise! Let his enemies be scattered! Make dem who hate him also flee before him.
As smoke is driven away, so drive dem away. As wax melts before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.
But let the righteous be glad. Make dem glad well-well before God. Yes, Make dem glad well-well with gladness.
Sing to God! Sing praises to his name! Extol him who rides on the clouds: to Yah, his name! Glad well-well before him!
A father of the fatherless, and a defender of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.
God sets the lonely in families. He brings out the prisoners with singing, but the rebellious live in a sun-scorched land.
God, when you go out before una people, when you marched through the wilderness... Selah.
The earth trembled. The sky also poured down rain at the presence of the God of Sinai — at the presence of God, the God of Israel.
You, God, sent a plentiful rain. You confirmed una inheritance, when it was weary.
Una congregation lived inside am. You, God, prepared una goodness for the poor.
The Lord announced the word. The ones who proclaim it are a great company.
“Kings of armies flee! Dem flee!” Person wey waits at home divides the plunder,
while you sleep among the camp fires, the wings of a dove sheathed with silver, her feathers with shining gold.
When the Almighty scattered kings in her, it snowed on Zalmon.
The mountains of Bashan are majestic mountains. The mountains of Bashan are rugged.
Why do you look in envy, you rugged mountains, at the mountain where God chooses to reign? Yes, Baba God will live there forever.
The chariots of God are tens of thousands and thousands of thousands. The Lord is among dem, from Sinai, into the sanctuary.
You have ascended on high. You have led away captives. You have received gifts among men, yes, among the rebellious also, that Yah God might live there.
Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears our burdens, even the God Wey be our salvation. Selah.
God is to us a God of deliverance. To Baba God, the Lord, belongs escape from death.
But God will strike through the head of his enemies, the hairy scalp of such a one as still continues in his guiltiness.
The Lord talk say, “I go bring you again from Bashan, I go bring you again from the depths of the sea;
That you may crush dem, dipping una foot in blood, that the tongues of una dogs may have dem portion from una enemies.”
Dem have seen una processions, God, even the processions of my God, my King, into the sanctuary.
The singers go before, the minstrels follow after, among the ladies playing with tambourines,
“Bless God in the congregations, even the Lord in the assembly of Israel!”
E get little Benjamin, dem ruler, the princes of Judah, dem council, the princes of Zebulun, and the princes of Naphtali.
Una God has commanded una strength. Strengthen, God, that which you have done for us.
Because of una temple at Jerusalem, kings shall bring presents to you.
Rebuke the wild animal of the reeds, the plenty people of the bulls, with the calves of the peoples. Being humbled, may it bring bars of silver. Scatter the nations that delight in war.
Princes shall come out of Egypt. Ethiopia shall hurry to stretch out her hands to God.
Sing to God, you kingdoms of the earth! Sing praises to the Lord! Selah.
To him who rides on the heaven of heavens, which are of old; see am, he utters his voice, a mighty voice.
Ascribe strength to God! His excellency is over Israel, his strength is in the skies.
You be awesome, God, in una sanctuaries. The God of Israel gives strength and power to his people. Praise be to God!
For the Chief Musician. To the tune of “Lilies.” By David. Save me, God, for the waters have come up to my neck!
I sink in deep mire, where E get no foothold. I have come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.
I be weary with my crying. My throat is dry. My eyes fail, looking for my God.
People wey hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head. People wey want to cut me off, being my enemies wrongfully, are mighty. I have to restore what I didn’t take away.
God, you know my foolishness. My sins no be hidden from you.
No let people wey wait for you be shamed through me, Lord Baba God of Armies. No let people wey seek you be bring to dishonor through me, God of Israel.
Because for una sake, I have borne reproach. Shame has covered my face.
I have become a stranger to my brothers, an alien to my mother’s pikin dem.
For the zeal of una house consumes me. The reproaches of people wey reproach you have fallen on me.
When I wept and I fasted, that was to my reproach.
When I made sackcloth my clothing, I became a byword to dem.
People wey sit in the gate talk about me. I be the song of the drunkards.
But as for me, my prayer is to you, Baba God, in an acceptable time. God, in the abundance of una loving kindness, answer me in the truth of una salvation.
Deliver me out of the mire, and no let me sink. Let me be delivered from people wey hate me, and out of the deep waters.
No let the flood waters overwhelm me, neither let the deep swallow me up. No let the pit shut its mouth on me.
Answer me, Baba God, for una loving kindness is good. According to the plenty people of una tender mercies, turn to me.
No hide una face from una worker, for I be in distress. Answer me speedily!
Draw near to my soul, and redeem it. Ransom me because of my enemies.
You know my reproach, my shame, and my dishonor. My adversaries are all before you.
Reproach has broken my heart, and I be full of heaviness. I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; for comforters, but I find none.
Dem also give me gall for my chop. In my thirst, dem give me vinegar to drink.
Let dem table before dem become a snare. May it become a retribution and a trap.
Let dem eyes be darkened, so that dem no fit see. Let dem backs be continually bent.
Pour out una indignation on dem. Let the fierceness of una anger overtake dem.
Let dem habitation be desolate. Let Nobody live in dem tents.
For dem persecute him whom you have wounded. Dem tell of the sorrow of those whom you have hurt.
Charge dem with crime upon crime. No Make dem come into una righteousness.
Make dem be blotted out of the book of life, and not be written with the righteous.
But I be in pain and distress. Let una salvation, God, protect me.
I go praise the name of God with a song, and will magnify him with thanksgiving.
It will please Baba God better than an ox, or a bull that has horns and hoofs.
The humble have seen it, and are glad. You who seek after God, let una heart live.
For Baba God hears the needy, and no dey despise his captive people.
Let heaven and earth praise him; the seas, and everything that moves inside am!
For God will save Zion, and build the cities of Judah. Dem shall settle there, and own it.
The pikin dem also of his workers shall inherit it. People wey love his name shall live inside am.
For the Chief Musician. By David. A reminder. Hurry, God, to deliver me. Come sharp-sharp to help me, Baba God.
Make dem be disappointed and confounded who seek my soul. Let people wey desire my ruin be turned back in disgrace.
Make dem be turned because of dem shame Who say, “Aha! Aha!”
Let all people wey seek you glad well-well and be glad in you. Let people wey love una salvation continually say, “Let God be exalted!”
But I be poor and needy. Come to me sharp-sharp, God. You be my help and my deliverer. Baba God, no delay.
In you, Baba God, I take refuge. Never let me be disappointed.
Deliver me in una righteousness, and rescue me. Turn una ear to me, and save me.
Be to me a rock of refuge to which I may always go. Give the command to save me, for You be my rock and my fortress.
Rescue me, my God, from the hand of the wicked, from the hand of the unrighteous and cruel man.
For You be my hope, Lord Baba God; my confidence from my youth.
I have relied on you from the womb. You be person wey take me out of my mother’s womb. I go always praise you.
I be a marvel to many, but You be my strong refuge.
My mouth go be filled with una praise, with una honor all day long.
No reject me in my old age. No forsake me when my strength fails.
For my enemies talk about me. People wey watch for my soul conspire together,
saying, “God has forsaken him. Pursue and take him, for Nobody will rescue him.”
God, no be far from me. My God, hurry to help me.
Let my accusers be disappointed and consumed. Make dem be covered with disgrace and scorn who want to harm me.
But I go always hope, and will add to all of una praise.
My mouth will tell about una righteousness, and of una salvation all day, though I no know its full measure.
I go come with the mighty acts of the Lord Baba God. I go make mention of una righteousness, even of yours alone.
God, you have taught me from my youth. Until now, I have declared una wondrous works.
Yes, even when I be old and gray-haired, God, no forsake me, until I have declared una strength to the next generation, una might to everyone Wey be to come.
Una righteousness also, God, reaches to the heavens; you have done great things. God, Wey be like you?
You, who have shown us many and bitter troubles, You go let me live. You go bring us up again from the depths of the earth.
Increase my honor, and comfort me again.
I go also praise you with the harp for una faithfulness, my God. I sing praises to you with the lyre, Holy One of Israel.
My lips shall shout for gladness! My soul, which you have redeemed, sings praises to you!
My tongue will also talk about una righteousness all day long, for Dem be disappointed, and Dem be confounded, who want to harm me.
By Solomon. God, give the king una justice; una righteousness to the royal son.
He will judge una people with righteousness, and una poor with justice.
The mountains shall bring prosperity to the people. The hills bring the fruit of righteousness.
He will judge the poor of the people. He will save the pikin dem of the needy, and will break the oppressor in pieces.
Dem shall fear you while the sun endures; and as long as the moon, throughout all generations.
He will come down like rain on the mown grass, as showers that water the earth.
In his days, the righteous shall flourish, and abundance of peace, until the moon is no more.
He go get dominion also from sea to sea, from the River to every corner of the world.
People wey live in the wilderness shall bow before him. His enemies shall lick the dust.
The kings of Tarshish and of the islands will bring tribute. The kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts.
Yes, all kings shall fall down before him. People for everywhere shall serve him.
For he will deliver the needy when he cries; the poor, who has no helper.
He Go get pity on the poor and needy. He will save the souls of the needy.
He will redeem dem soul from oppression and violence. Dem blood Go be precious in his sight.
Dem shall live, and to him go be given of the gold of Sheba. Men shall pray for him continually. Dem shall bless him all day long.
Abundance of grain go be throughout the land. Its fruit sways like Lebanon. Let it flourish, thriving like the grass of the field.
His name endures forever. His name continues as long as the sun. Men go be blessed by him. People for everywhere will call him blessed.
Praise be to Baba God, the God of Israel, who alone does marvelous deeds.
Blessed be his glorious name forever! Let the whole earth be filled with his glory! Amen and amen.
This ends the prayers by David, the son of Jesse.
A Psalm by Asaph. Surely God is good to Israel, to people Wey pure in heart.
But as for me, my feet were almost gone. My steps had nearly slipped.
For I was envious of the arrogant, when I see the prosperity of the wicked.
For E get no struggles in dem death, but dem strength is firm.
Dem be free from burdens of men, neither are dem plagued like other men.
So pride is like a chain around dem neck. Violence covers dem like a garment.
Dem eyes bulge with fat. Dem minds pass the limits of conceit.
Dem scoff and speak with malice. In arrogance, dem threaten oppression.
Dem have set dem mouth in the heavens. Dem tongue walks through the earth.
So dem people return to dem, and dem drink up waters of abundance.
Dem say, “How does God know? Is there knowledge in the Most High?”
See am, these are the wicked. Being always at ease, dem increase in riches.
Surely I have cleansed my heart in vain, and washed my hands in innocence,
For all day long I Don dey plagued, and punished every morning.
If I had talk say, “I go speak thus”; see am, I would have betrayed the generation of una pikin dem.
When I tried to understand this, it was too painful for me;
Until I entered God’s sanctuary, and considered dem latter end.
Surely you set dem in slippery places. You throw dem down to destruction.
How Dem be suddenly destroyed! Dem be completely swept away with terrors.
As a dream when one wakes up, so, Lord, when you awake, You go despise dem fantasies.
For my soul was grieved. I was embittered in my heart.
I was so senseless and ignorant. I was a brute beast before you.
Nevertheless, I be continually with you. You have held my right hand.
You go guide me with una counsel, and afterward receive me to glory.
Whom do I have in heaven? E get Nobody on earth whom I desire besides you.
My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
For, see am, people Wey far from you shall perish. You have destroyed all people Wey unfaithful to you.
But it is good for me to come close to God. I have made the Lord Baba God my refuge, that I may tell of all una works.
A contemplation by Asaph. God, why have you rejected us forever? Why does una anger smolder against the sheep of una pasture?
Remember una congregation, which you purchased of old, which you have redeemed to be the tribe of una inheritance; Mount Zion, in which you have lived.
Lift up una feet to the perpetual ruins, all the evil that the enemy has done in the sanctuary.
Una adversaries have roared in the middle of una assembly. Dem have set up dem standards as signs.
Dem behaved like men wielding axes, cutting through a thicket of trees.
Now dem break all its carved work down with hatchet and hammers.
Dem have burned una sanctuary to the ground. Dem have profaned the dwelling place of una Name.
Dem talk say in dem heart, “We go crush dem completely.” Dem have burned up all the places in the land where God was worshiped.
We see no miraculous signs. E get no longer any prophet, neither is there among us anyone wey know how long.
How long, God, shall the adversary reproach? Shall the enemy blaspheme una name forever?
Why do you draw back una hand, even una right hand? Take it out of una pocket and consume dem!
Yet God is my King of old, working salvation throughout the earth.
You divided the sea by una strength. You broke the heads of the sea monsters in the waters.
You broke the heads of Leviathan in pieces. You give him as chop to people and desert creatures.
You opened up spring and stream. You dried up mighty rivers.
The day is yours, the night is also yours. You have prepared the light and the sun.
You have set all the boundaries of the earth. You have made summer and winter.
Remember this, that the enemy has mocked you, Baba God. Foolish people have blasphemed una name.
No deliver the soul of una dove to wild beasts. No forget the life of una poor forever.
Honor una covenant, for haunts of violence fill the dark places of the earth.
No let the oppressed return ashamed. Let the poor and needy praise una name.
Arise, God! Plead una own cause. Remember how the foolish man mocks you all day.
No forget the voice of una adversaries. The tumult of people wey rise up against you ascends continually.
For the Chief Musician. To the tune of “No Destroy.” A Psalm by Asaph. A song. We Thank God to you, God. We Thank God, for una Name is near. Men tell about una wondrous works.
When I choose the appointed time, I go judge blamelessly.
The earth and all its inhabitants quake. I firmly hold its pillars. Selah.
I talk say to the arrogant, “No boast!” I talk say to the wicked, “No lift up the horn.
No lift up una horn on high. No speak with a stiff neck.”
For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor yet from the south, comes exaltation.
But God is the judge. He puts down one, and lifts up another.
For in Baba God’s hand E get a cup, full of foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours it out. Indeed the wicked of the earth drink and drink it to its very dregs.
But I go declare this forever: I go sing praises to the God of Jacob.
I go cut off all the horns of the wicked, but the horns of the righteous go be lifted up.
For the Chief Musician. On stringed instruments. A Psalm by Asaph. A song. In Judah, God is known. His name is great in Israel.
His tabernacle is also in Salem; His dwelling place in Zion.
There he broke the flaming arrows of the bow, the shield, and the sword, and the weapons of war. Selah.
Glorious are you, and excellent, more than mountains of game.
Valiant men lie plundered, dem have slept dem last sleep. None of the men of war can lift dem hands.
At una rebuke, God of Jacob, both chariot and horse are throw into a dead sleep.
You, even you, are to be feared. Who can stand in una sight when You be angry?
You pronounced judgment from heaven. The earth feared, and was silent,
when God arose to judgment, to save all the afflicted ones of the earth. Selah.
Surely the serious anger of man praises you. The survivors of una serious anger are restrained.
Make vows to Baba God una God, and fulfill dem! Let all of his neighbors bring presents to him Wey be to be feared.
He will cut off the spirit of princes. He is feared by the kings of the earth.
For the Chief Musician. To Jeduthun. A Psalm by Asaph. My cry goes to God! Indeed, I cry to God for help, and for him to listen to me.
In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord. My hand was stretched out in the night, and didn’t get tired. My soul refused to be comforted.
I remember God, and I groan. I complain, and my spirit is overwhelmed. Selah.
You hold my eyelids open. I be so troubled that I no fit speak.
I have considered the days of old, the years of ancient times.
I remember my song in the night. I consider in my own heart; my spirit diligently inquires:
“Will the Lord reject us forever? Will he be favorable no more?
Has his loving kindness vanished forever? Does his promise fail for generations?
Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has he, in anger, withheld his compassion?” Selah.
Then I thought, “I go appeal to this: the years of the right hand of the Most High.”
I go remember Yah’s deeds; for I go remember una wonders of old.
I go also meditate on all una work, and consider una doings.
Una way, God, is in the sanctuary. What god is great like God?
You be the God wey do wonders. You have made una strength known among the peoples.
You have redeemed una people with una arm, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
The waters see you, God. The waters see you, and dem writhed. The depths also convulsed.
The clouds poured out water. The skies resounded with thunder. Una arrows also flashed around.
The voice of una thunder was in the whirlwind. The lightnings lit up the world. The earth trembled and shook.
Una way was through the sea; una paths through the great waters. Una footsteps No be known.
You led una people like a flock, by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
A contemplation by Asaph. Hear my teaching, my people. Turn una ears to the words of my mouth.
I go open my mouth in a parable. I go utter dark sayings of old,
Which we have heard and known, and our fathers have told us.
We go not hide dem from dem pikin dem, telling to the generation to come the praises of Baba God, his strength, and his wondrous deeds that he has done.
For he established a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a teaching in Israel, which he commanded our fathers, that dem should make dem known to dem pikin dem;
that the generation to come might know, even the pikin dem who should be born; who should arise and tell dem pikin dem,
that dem might set dem hope in God, and not forget God’s deeds, but keep his commandments,
and might not be as dem fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation, a generation that didn’t make dem hearts loyal, whose spirit No be steadfast with God.
The pikin dem of Ephraim, being armed and carrying bows, turned back in the day of battle.
Dem didn’t keep God’s covenant, and refused to walk in his law.
Dem forgot his doings, his wondrous deeds that he had shown dem.
He did marvelous things in the sight of dem fathers, in the land of Egypt, in the field of Zoan.
He split the sea, and caused dem to pass through. He made the waters stand as a heap.
In the daytime he also led dem with a cloud, and all night with a light of fire.
He split rocks in the wilderness, and give dem drink abundantly as out of the depths.
He bring streams also out of the rock, and caused waters to run down like rivers.
Yet dem still go on to sin against him, to rebel against the Most High in the desert.
Dem tempted God in dem heart by asking chop according to dem desire.
Yes, dem spoke against God. Dem talk say, “Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?
See am, he struck the rock, so that waters gushed out, and streams overflowed. Can he give bread also? Will he provide meat for his people?”
So Baba God heard, and was angry. A fire was kindled against Jacob, anger also go up against Israel,
because dem didn’t believe in God, and didn’t trust in his salvation.
Yet he commanded the skies above, and opened the doors of heaven.
He rained down manna on dem to eat, and give dem chop from the sky.
Man ate the bread of angels. He sent dem chop to the full.
He caused the east wind to blow in the sky. By his power he guided the south wind.
He rained also meat on dem as the dust; winged birds as the sand of the seas.
He Make dem fall in the middle of dem camp, around dem habitations.
So dem ate, and were well filled. He give dem dem own desire.
Dem didn’t turn from dem cravings. Dem chop was yet in dem mouths,
when the anger of God go up against dem, killed some of dem fattest, and struck down the young men of Israel.
For all this dem still sinned, and didn’t believe in his wondrous works.
So he consumed dem days in vanity, and dem years in terror.
When he killed dem, then dem inquired after him. Dem come back and sought God earnestly.
Dem remember that God was dem rock, the Most High God, dem redeemer.
But dem flattered him with dem mouth, and lied to him with dem tongue.
For dem heart No be right with him, neither were dem faithful in his covenant.
But he, being merciful, forgave wickedness, and didn’t destroy dem. Yes, many times he turned his anger away, and didn’t stir up all his serious anger.
He remember that dem were but flesh, a wind that passes away, and no dey come again.
How often dem rebelled against him in the wilderness, and grieved him in the desert!
Dem turned again and tempted God, and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
Dem didn’t remember his hand, nor the day when he redeemed dem from the adversary;
how he set his signs in Egypt, his wonders in the field of Zoan,
he turned dem rivers into blood, and dem streams, so that dem could not drink.
He sent among dem swarms of flies, which devoured dem; and frogs, which destroyed dem.
He give also dem increase to the caterpillar, and dem labor to the locust.
He destroyed dem vines with hail, dem sycamore fig trees with frost.
He give over dem livestock also to the hail, and dem flocks to hot thunderbolts.
He threw on dem the fierceness of his anger, serious anger, indignation, and trouble, and a band of angels of evil.
He made a path for his anger. He didn’t spare dem soul from death, but give dem life over to the pestilence,
and struck all the firstborn in Egypt, the chief of dem strength in the tents of Ham.
But he led out his own people like sheep, and guided dem in the wilderness like a flock.
He led dem safely, so that dem no be afraid, but the sea overwhelmed dem enemies.
He bring dem to the border of his sanctuary, to this mountain, which his right hand had taken.
He also drove out the nations before dem, allotted dem for an inheritance by line, and made the tribes of Israel to live in dem tents.
Yet dem tempted and rebelled against the Most High God, and didn’t keep his testimonies;
but turned back, and dealt treacherously like dem fathers. Dem were turned aside like a deceitful bow.
For dem provoked him to anger with dem high places, and moved him to jealousy with dem engraved images.
When God heard this, he was angry, and greatly abhorred Israel;
So that he abandoned the tent of Shiloh, the tent which he placed among men;
and delivered his strength into captivity, his glory into the adversary’s hand.
He also give his people over to the sword, and was angry with his inheritance.
Fire devoured dem young men. Dem virgins had no wedding song.
Dem priests fell by the sword, and dem widows no fit weep.
