Then the Lord awakened as one out of sleep, like a mighty man who shouts by reason of wine.
He struck his adversaries backward. He put dem to a perpetual reproach.
Moreover he rejected the tent of Joseph, and didn’t choose the tribe of Ephraim,
But chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion which he love.
He built his sanctuary like the heights, like the earth which he has established forever.
He also chose David his worker, and take him from the sheepfolds;
from following the ewes that have dem young, he bring him to be the shepherd of Jacob, his people, and Israel, his inheritance.
So he was dem shepherd according to the integrity of his heart, and guided dem by the skillfulness of his hands.
A Psalm by Asaph. God, the nations have come into una inheritance. Dem have defiled una holy temple. Dem have laid Jerusalem in heaps.
Dem have given the dead bodies of una workers to be chop for the birds of the sky, the flesh of una saints to the animals of the earth.
Dem blood dem have shed like water around Jerusalem. There was Nobody to bury dem.
We have become a reproach to our neighbors, a scoffing and derision to people Wey around us.
How long, Baba God? Will you be angry forever? Will una jealousy burn like fire?
Pour out una serious anger on the nations that no know you; on the kingdoms that no call on una name;
For dem have devoured Jacob, and destroyed his homeland.
No hold the iniquities of our forefathers against us. Let una tender mercies speedily meet us, for We be in desperate need.
Help us, God of our salvation, for the glory of una name. Deliver us, and forgive our sins, for una name’s sake.
Why should the nations say, “Where is dem God?” Let it be known among the nations, before our eyes, that vengeance for una workers’ blood is being poured out.
Let the sighing of the prisoner come before you. According to the greatness of una power, preserve people Wey sentenced to death.
Pay back to our neighbors seven times into dem bosom dem reproach with which dem have reproached you, Lord.
So we, una people and sheep of una pasture, will give you thanks forever. We go praise you forever, to all generations.
For the Chief Musician. To the tune of “The Lilies of the Covenant.” A Psalm by Asaph. Hear us, Shepherd of Israel, you who lead Joseph like a flock, you who sit above the cherubim, shine out.
Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh, stir up una might! Come to save us!
Turn us again, God. Cause una face to shine, and We go be saved.
Baba God of Armies, How long will you be angry against the prayer of una people?
You have fed dem with the bread of tears, and given dem tears to drink in large measure.
You make us a source of contention to our neighbors. Our enemies laugh among themselves.
Turn us again, God of Armies. Cause una face to shine, and We go be saved.
You bring a vine out of Egypt. You drove out the nations, and planted it.
You cleared the ground for it. It take deep root, and filled the land.
The mountains were covered with its shadow. Its boughs were like God’s cedars.
It sent out its branches to the sea, Its shoots to the River.
Why have you broken down its walls, so that all people wey pass by the way pluck it?
The boar out of the wood ravages it. The wild animals of the field feed on it.
Turn again, we beg you, God of Armies. Look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vine,
the stock which una right hand planted, the branch that you made strong for yourself.
It’s burned with fire. It’s cut down. Dem perish at una rebuke.
Let una hand be on the man of una right hand, on the Son of Man whom you made strong for yourself.
So We go not turn away from you. Revive us, and We go call on una name.
Turn us again, Baba God of Armies. Cause una face to shine, and We go be saved.
For the Chief Musician. On an instrument of Gath. By Asaph. Sing aloud to God, our strength! Make a joyful shout to the God of Jacob!
Raise a song, and bring here the tambourine, the pleasant lyre with the harp.
Blow the trumpet at the New Moon, at the full moon, on our feast day.
For it is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
He appointed it in Joseph for a testimony, when he go out over the land of Egypt, I heard a language that I didn’t know.
“I removed his shoulder from the burden. His hands were freed from the basket.
You call in trouble, and I delivered you. I answer you in the secret place of thunder. I tested you at the waters of Meribah.” Selah.
“Hear, my people, and I go testify to you, Israel, if you would listen to me!
There go be no strange god in you, neither shall you worship any foreign god.
I be Baba God, una God, who bring you up out of the land of Egypt. Open una mouth wide, and I go fill it.
But my people didn’t listen to my voice. Israel desired none of me.
So I Make dem go after the stubbornness of dem hearts, that dem might walk in dem own counsels.
Oh that my people would listen to me, that Israel would walk in my ways!
I would soon subdue dem enemies, and turn my hand against dem adversaries.
The haters of Baba God would cringe before him, and dem punishment would last forever.
But he would have also fed dem with the finest of the wheat. I go satisfy you with honey out of the rock.”
A Psalm by Asaph. God presides in the great assembly. He judges among the gods.
“How long will you judge unjustly, and show partiality to the wicked?” Selah.
“Defend the weak, the poor, and the fatherless. Maintain the rights of the poor and oppressed.
Rescue the weak and needy. Deliver dem out of the hand of the wicked.”
Dem no know, neither do dem understand. Dem walk back and forth in darkness. All the foundations of the earth are shaken.
I talk say, “You be gods, all of You be sons of the Most High.
Nevertheless you shall die like men, and fall like one of the rulers.”
Arise, God, judge the earth, for you inherit all of the nations.
A song. A Psalm by Asaph. God, no keep silent. No keep silent, and no be still, God.
For, see am, una enemies are stirred up. People wey hate you have lifted up dem heads.
Dem conspire with cunning against una people. Dem plot against una cherished ones.
“Come,” dem say, “let’s destroy dem as a nation, that the name of Israel may be remember no more.”
For dem have conspired together with one mind. Dem form an alliance against you.
The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites; Moab, and the Hagrites;
Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek; Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre;
Assyria also is joined with dem. Dem have helped the pikin dem of Lot. Selah.
Do to dem as you did to Midian, as to Sisera, as to Jabin, at the river Kishon;
who perished at Endor, who became as dung for the earth.
Make dem nobles like Oreb and Zeeb; yes, all dem princes like Zebah and Zalmunna;
who talk say, “Make we take possession of God’s pasture lands.”
My God, make dem like tumbleweed; like chaff before the wind.
As the fire that burns the forest, as the flame that sets the mountains on fire,
so pursue dem with una tempest, and terrify dem with una storm.
Fill dem faces with confusion, that dem may seek una name, Baba God.
Make dem be disappointed and dismayed forever. Yes, Make dem be confounded and perish;
that dem may know that you alone, whose name is Baba God, are the Most High over all the earth.
For the Chief Musician. On an instrument of Gath. A Psalm by the sons of Korah. How lovely are una dwellings, Baba God of Armies!
My soul longs, and even faints for the courts of Baba God. My heart and my flesh cry out for the living God.
Yes, the sparrow has find a home, and the swallow a nest for sheself, where she may have her young, near una altars, Baba God of Armies, my King, and my God.
Blessed are people wey live in una house. Dem be always praising you. Selah.
Blessed are those whose strength is in you; who have set dem hearts on a pilgrimage.
Passing through the valley of Weeping, dem make it a place of springs. Yes, the autumn rain covers it with blessings.
Dem go from strength to strength. Everyone of dem appears before God in Zion.
Baba God, God of Armies, hear my prayer. Listen, God of Jacob. Selah.
See am, God our shield, look at the face of una anointed.
For a day in una courts is better than a thousand. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to live in the tents of wickedness.
For Baba God is a sun and a shield. Baba God will give grace and glory. He withholds no good thing from people wey walk blamelessly.
Baba God of Armies, blessed is the man who trusts in you.
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by the sons of Korah. Baba God, you Don dey favorable to una land. You have restored the fortunes of Jacob.
You have forgiven the wickedness of una people. You have covered all dem sin. Selah.
You have taken away all una serious anger. You have turned from the fierceness of una anger.
Turn us, God of our salvation, and cause una indignation toward us to cease.
Will you be angry with us forever? Will you draw out una anger to all generations?
No go you revive us again, that una people may glad well-well in you?
Show us una loving kindness, Baba God. Grant us una salvation.
I go hear what God, Baba God, will speak, for he will speak peace to his people, his saints; but Make dem not turn again to folly.
Surely his salvation is near people wey fear him, that glory may live in our land.
Mercy and truth meet together. Righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
Truth springs out of the earth. Righteousness has looked down from heaven.
Yes, Baba God will give that which is good. Our land will yield its increase.
Righteousness goes before him, And prepares the way for his steps.
A Prayer by David. Hear, Baba God, and answer me, for I be poor and needy.
Preserve my soul, for I be godly. You, my God, save una worker who trusts in you.
Be merciful to me, Lord, for I call to you all day long.
Bring gladness to the soul of una worker, for to you, Lord, do I lift up my soul.
For you, Lord, are good, and ready to forgive; abundant in loving kindness to all people wey call on you.
Hear, Baba God, my prayer. Listen to the voice of my petitions.
In the day of my trouble I go call on you, for You go answer me.
E get Nobody like you among the gods, Lord, nor any deeds like una deeds.
People for everywhere you have made will come and worship before you, Lord. Dem shall glorify una name.
For You be great, and do wondrous things. You be God alone.
Teach me una way, Baba God. I go walk in una truth. Make my heart undivided to fear una name.
I go praise you, Lord my God, with my whole heart. I go glorify una name forever more.
For una loving kindness is great toward me. You have delivered my soul from the lowest Sheol.
God, the proud have risen up against me. A company of violent men have sought after my soul, and dem no hold regard for you before dem.
But you, Lord, are a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth.
Turn to me, and have mercy on me! Give una strength to una worker. Save the son of una worker.
Show me a sign of una goodness, that people wey hate me may see it, and be shamed, because you, Baba God, have helped me, and comforted me.
A Psalm by the sons of Korah; a Song. His foundation is in the holy mountains.
Baba God loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
Glorious things are spoken about you, city of God. Selah.
I go record Rahab and Babylon among people wey acknowledge me. See am, Philistia, Tyre, and also Ethiopia: “This one was born there.”
Yes, of Zion it Go be talk say, “This one and that one was born in her”; the Most High imself will establish her.
Baba God will count, when he writes up the peoples, “This one was born there.” Selah.
People wey sing as well as people wey dance say, “All my springs are in you.”

A Song. A Psalm by the sons of Korah. For the Chief Musician. To the tune of “The Suffering of Suffering.” A contemplation by Heman, the Ezrahite. Baba God, the God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before you.
Let my prayer enter into una presence. Turn una ear to my cry.
For my soul is full of troubles. My life draws near to Sheol.
I be counted among people wey go down into the pit. I be like a man who has no help,
set apart among the dead, like the slain who lie in the grave, whom you remember no more. Dem be cut off from una hand.
You have laid me in the lowest pit, in the darkest depths.
Una serious anger lies heavily on me. You have afflicted me with all una waves. Selah.
You have taken my friends from me. You have made me an abomination to dem. I be confined, and I no fit escape.
My eyes are dim from grief. I have call on you daily, Baba God. I have spread out my hands to you.
Do you show wonders to the dead? Do the comot spirits rise up and praise you? Selah.
Is una loving kindness declared in the grave? Or una faithfulness in Destruction?
Are una wonders made known in the dark? Or una righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?
But to you, Baba God, I have cried. In the morning, my prayer comes before you.
Baba God, why do you reject my soul? Why do you hide una face from me?
I be afflicted and ready to die from my youth up. While I suffer una terrors, I be distracted.
Una fierce serious anger has gone over me. Una terrors have cut me off.
Dem come around me like water all day long. Dem completely engulfed me.
You have put lover and friend far from me, and my friends into darkness.
A contemplation by Ethan, the Ezrahite. I go sing of the loving kindness of Baba God forever. With my mouth, I go make known una faithfulness to all generations.
I indeed declare, “Love stands firm forever. You established the heavens. Una faithfulness is in dem.”
“I have made a covenant with my chosen one, I have sworn to David, my worker,
‘I go establish una offspring forever, and build up una throne to all generations.’” Selah.
The heavens will praise una wonders, Baba God; una faithfulness also in the assembly of the holy ones.
For who in the skies can be compared to Baba God? Who among the sons of the heavenly beings is like Baba God,
a very awesome God in the council of the holy ones, to be feared above all people Wey around him?
Baba God, God of Armies, Wey be a mighty one, like you? Yah, una faithfulness is around you.
You rule the pride of the sea. When its waves rise up, you calm dem.
You have broken Rahab in pieces, like one of the slain. You have scattered una enemies with una mighty arm.
The heavens are yours. The earth also is yours; the world and its fullness. You have founded dem.
The north and the south, you have created dem. Tabor and Hermon glad well-well in una name.
You have a mighty arm. Una hand is strong, and una right hand is exalted.
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of una throne. Loving kindness and truth go before una face.
Blessed are the people who learn to acclaim you. Dem walk in the light of una presence, Baba God.
In una name dem glad well-well all day. In una righteousness, Dem be exalted.
For You be the glory of dem strength. In una favor, our horn Go be exalted.
For our shield belongs to Baba God; our king to the Holy One of Israel.
Then you spoke in vision to una saints, and talk say, “I have given strength to the warrior. I have exalted a young man from the people.
I have find David, my worker. I have anointed him with my holy oil,
with whom my hand go be established. My arm will also strengthen him.
No enemy will tax him. No wicked man will oppress him.
I go beat down his adversaries before him, and strike people wey hate him.
But my faithfulness and my loving kindness Go be with him. In my name, his horn Go be exalted.
I go set his hand also on the sea, and his right hand on the rivers.
He will call to me, ‘You be my Father, my God, and the rock of my salvation!’
I go also appoint him my firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.
I go keep my loving kindness for him forever more. My covenant will stand firm with him.
I go also make his offspring endure forever, and his throne as the days of heaven.
If his pikin dem forsake my law, and no walk in my ordinances;
if dem break my statutes, and no keep my commandments;
then I go punish dem sin with the rod, and dem wickedness with stripes.
But I go not completely take my loving kindness from him, nor allow my faithfulness to fail.
I go not break my covenant, nor alter what my lips have uttered.
Once I have sworn by my holiness, I go not lie to David.
His offspring will endure forever, his throne like the sun before me.
It Go be established forever like the moon, the faithful witness in the sky.” Selah.
But you have rejected and spurned. You Don dey angry with una anointed.
You have renounced the covenant of una worker. You have defiled his crown in the dust.
You have broken down all his hedges. You have bring his strongholds to ruin.
All who pass by the way rob him. He has become a reproach to his neighbors.
You have exalted the right hand of his adversaries. You have made all of his enemies glad well-well.
Yes, you turn back the edge of his sword, and haven’t supported him in battle.
You have ended his splendor, and thrown his throne down to the ground.
You have shortened the days of his youth. You have covered him with shame. Selah.
How long, Baba God? Will you hide yourself forever? Will una serious anger burn like fire?
Remember how short my time is! For what vanity have you created all the pikin dem of men!
What man is person wey shall live and not see death, who shall deliver his soul from the power of Sheol? Selah.
Lord, where are una former loving kindnesses, which you swore to David in una faithfulness?
Remember, Lord, the reproach of una workers, how I bear in my heart the taunts of all the mighty peoples,
With which una enemies have mocked, Baba God, with which dem have mocked the footsteps of una anointed one.
Blessed be Baba God forever more. Amen, and Amen.
A Prayer by Moses, the man of God. Lord, you Don dey our dwelling place for all generations.
Before the mountains were born, before you had formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, You be God.
You turn man to destruction, saying, “Return, you pikin dem of men.”
For a thousand years in una sight are just like yesterday when it is past, like a watch in the night.
You sweep dem away as dem sleep. In the morning dem sprout like new grass.
In the morning it sprouts and springs up. By evening, it is withered and dry.
For We be consumed in una anger. We be troubled in una serious anger.
You have set our iniquities before you, our secret sins in the light of una presence.
For all our days have passed away in una serious anger. We bring our years to an end as a sigh.
The days of our years are seventy, or even by reason of strength eighty years; yet dem pride is but labor and sorrow, for it passes sharp-sharp, and we fly away.
Wey know the power of una anger, una serious anger according to the fear that is due to you?
So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
Relent, Baba God! How long? Have compassion on una workers!
Satisfy us in the morning with una loving kindness, that we may glad well-well and be glad all our days.
Make us glad for as many days as you have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen evil.
Let una work appear to una workers; una glory to dem pikin dem.
Let the favor of the Lord our God be on us; establish the work of our hands for us; yes, establish the work of our hands.
Person wey dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.
I go say of Baba God, “He is my refuge and my fortress; my God, in whom I trust.”
For he will deliver you from the snare of the fowler, and from the deadly pestilence.
He will cover you with his feathers. Under his wings You go take refuge. His faithfulness is una shield and rampart.
You no go be afraid of the terror by night, nor of the arrow that flies by day;
nor of the pestilence that walks in darkness, nor of the destruction that wastes at noonday.
A thousand may fall at una side, and ten thousand at una right hand; but it No go come near you.
You go only look with una eyes, and see the recompense of the wicked.
Because you have made Baba God una refuge, and the Most High una dwelling place,
no evil shall happen to you, neither shall any plague come near una dwelling.
For he will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all una ways.
Dem go bear you up in dem hands, so that you no go dash una foot against a stone.
You go tread on the lion and cobra. You go trample the young lion and the serpent underfoot.
“Because he has set his love on me, so I go deliver him. I go set him on high, because he has known my name.
He will call on me, and I go answer him. I go be with him in trouble. I go deliver him, and honor him.
I go satisfy him with long life, and show him my salvation.”
A Psalm. A song for the Sabbath day. It is a good thing to Thank God to Baba God, to sing praises to una name, Most High;
to proclaim una loving kindness in the morning, and una faithfulness every night,
with the ten-stringed lute, with the harp, and with the melody of the lyre.
For you, Baba God, have made me glad through una work. I go triumph in the works of una hands.
How great are una works, Baba God! Una thoughts are very deep.
A senseless man no dey know, neither does a fool understand this:
though the wicked spring up as the grass, and all the evildoers flourish, Dem go be destroyed forever.
But you, Baba God, are on high forever more.
For, see am, una enemies, Baba God, for, see am, una enemies shall perish. All the evildoers Go be scattered.
But you have exalted my horn like that of the wild ox. I be anointed with fresh oil.
My eye has also seen my enemies. My ears have heard of the wicked enemies who rise up against me.
The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree. He will grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
Dem be planted in Baba God’s house. Dem go flourish in our God’s courts.
Dem go still produce fruit in old age. Dem go be full of sap and green,
to show that Baba God is upright. He is my rock, and E get no unrighteousness in him.
Baba God reigns! He is clothed with majesty! Baba God is armed with strength. The world also is established. It no fit be moved.
Una throne is established from long ago. You be from everlasting.
The floods have lifted up, Baba God, the floods have lifted up dem voice. The floods lift up dem waves.
Above the voices of many waters, the mighty breakers of the sea, Baba God on high is mighty.
Una statutes stand firm. Holiness adorns una house, Baba God, forever more.
Baba God, you God to whom vengeance belongs, you God to whom vengeance belongs, shine out.
Rise up, you judge of the earth. Pay back the proud Wetin dem deserve.
Baba God, how long will the wicked, how long will the wicked triumph?
Dem pour out arrogant words. All the evildoers boast.
Dem break una people in pieces, Baba God, and afflict una heritage.
Dem kill the widow and the alien, and murder the fatherless.
Dem say, “Yah No go see, neither will Jacob’s God consider.”
Consider, you senseless among the people; you fools, when will you be wise?
Person wey implanted the ear, no go he hear? Person wey formed the eye, no go he see?
Person wey disciplines the nations, no go he punish? Person wey teaches man knows.
Baba God knows the thoughts of man, that Dem be futile.
Blessed is the man whom you discipline, Yah, and teach out of una law;
that you may give him rest from the days of adversity, until the pit is dug for the wicked.
For Baba God no go reject his people, neither will he forsake his inheritance.
For judgment will return to righteousness. All the upright in heart shall follow it.
Who will rise up for me against the wicked? Who will stand up for me against the evildoers?
Unless Baba God Bin dey my help, my soul would have soon lived in silence.
When I talk say, “My foot is slipping!” Una loving kindness, Baba God, held me up.
In the plenty people of my thoughts within me, una comforts delight my soul.
Shall the throne of wickedness have fellowship with you, which brings about mischief by statute?
Dem gather themselves together against the soul of the righteous, and condemn the innocent blood.
But Baba God Don dey my high tower, my God, the rock of my refuge.
He has bring on dem dem own wickedness, and will cut dem off in dem own wickedness. Baba God, our God, will cut dem off.
Oh come, let’s sing to Baba God. Let’s shout aloud to the rock of our salvation!
Let’s come before his presence with thanksgiving. Let’s extol him with songs!
For Baba God is a great God, a great King above all gods.
In his hand are the deep places of the earth. The heights of the mountains are also his.
The sea is his, and he made it. His hands formed the dry land.
Oh come, let’s worship and bow down. Let’s kneel before Baba God, our Maker,
for he is our God. We be the people of his pasture, and the sheep in his care. Today, oh that you would hear his voice!
No harden una heart, as at Meribah, as in the day of Massah in the wilderness,
when una fathers tempted me, tested me, and see my work.
Forty long years I was grieved with that generation, and talk say, “It is a people that errs in dem heart. Dem have not known my ways.”
So I swore in my serious anger, “Dem no go enter into my rest.”
Sing to Baba God a new song! Sing to Baba God, all the earth.
Sing to Baba God! Bless his name! Proclaim his salvation from day to day!
Declare his glory among the nations, his marvelous works among all the peoples.
For great is Baba God, and greatly to be praised! He is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but Baba God made the heavens.
Honor and majesty are before him. Strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.
Ascribe to Baba God, you families of nations, ascribe to Baba God glory and strength.
Ascribe to Baba God the glory due to his name. Bring an offering, and come into his courts.
Worship Baba God in holy array. Tremble before him, all the earth.
Say among the nations, “Baba God reigns.” The world is also established. It no fit be moved. He will judge the peoples with equity.
Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth glad well-well. Let the sea roar, and its fullness!
Let the field and all that is in it exult! Then all the trees of the woods shall sing for gladness
before Baba God; for he comes, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness, the peoples with his truth.
Baba God reigns! Let the earth glad well-well! Let the plenty people of islands be glad!
Clouds and darkness are around him. Righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne.
A fire goes before him, and burns up his adversaries on every side.
His lightning lights up the world. The earth sees, and trembles.
The mountains melt like wax at the presence of Baba God, at the presence of the Lord of the whole earth.
The heavens declare his righteousness. All the peoples have seen his glory.
Let all dem be shamed who serve engraved images, who boast in dem idols. Worship him, all you gods!
Zion heard and was glad. The daughters of Judah rejoiced, because of una judgments, Baba God.
For you, Baba God, are most high above all the earth. You be exalted far above all gods.
You who love Baba God, hate evil. He preserves the souls of his saints. He delivers dem out of the hand of the wicked.
Light is sown for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart.
Be glad in Baba God, you righteous people! Thank God to his holy Name.
A Psalm. Sing to Baba God a new song, for he has done marvelous things! His right hand, and his holy arm, have worked salvation for him.
Baba God has made known his salvation. He has openly shown his righteousness in the sight of the nations.
He has remember his loving kindness and his faithfulness toward the house of Israel. All every corner of the world have seen the salvation of our God.
Make a joyful noise to Baba God, all the earth! Burst out and sing for gladness, yes, sing praises!
Sing praises to Baba God with the harp, with the harp and the voice of melody.
With trumpets and sound of the ram’s horn, make a joyful noise before the King, Baba God.
Let the sea roar with its fullness; the world, and people wey live inside am.
Let the rivers clap dem hands. Let the mountains sing for gladness together.
Make dem sing before Baba God, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness, and the peoples with equity.
Baba God reigns! Let the peoples tremble. He sits enthroned among the cherubim. Let the earth be moved.
Baba God is great in Zion. He is high above all the peoples.
Make dem praise una great and awesome name. He is Holy!
The King’s strength also loves justice. You do establish equity. You execute justice and righteousness in Jacob.
Exalt Baba God our God. Worship at his footstool. He is Holy!
Moses and Aaron were among his priests, Samuel among people wey call on his name; dem call on Baba God, and he answer dem.
He spoke to dem in the pillar of cloud. Dem kept his testimonies, the statute that he give dem.
You answer dem, Baba God our God. You be a God who forgave dem, although you take vengeance for dem doings.
Exalt Baba God, our God. Worship at his holy hill, for Baba God, our God, is holy!
A Psalm of thanksgiving. Shout for gladness to Baba God, all you lands!
Serve Baba God with gladness. Come before his presence with singing.
Know that Baba God, he is God. It is person wey has made us, and We be his. We be his people, and the sheep of his pasture.
Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, into his courts with praise. Thank God to him, and bless his name.
For Baba God is good. His loving kindness endures forever, his faithfulness to all generations.
A Psalm by David. I go sing of loving kindness and justice. To you, Baba God, I go sing praises.
I go be careful to live a blameless life. When will you come to me? I go walk within my house with a blameless heart.
I go set no vile thing before my eyes. I hate the deeds of faithless men. Dem go not cling to me.
A perverse heart Go be far from me. I go have nothing to do with evil.
I go silence Anybody wey secretly slanders his neighbor. I no go tolerate one Wey be haughty and conceited.
My eyes Go be on the faithful of the land, that dem may live with me. Person wey walks in a perfect way, he will serve me.
Person wey practices deceit no go live within my house. Person wey speaks falsehood no go be established before my eyes.
Morning by morning, I go destroy all the wicked of the land; to cut off all the workers of wickedness from Baba God’s city.
A Prayer of the afflicted, when he is overwhelmed and pours out his complaint before Baba God. Hear my prayer, Baba God! Let my cry come to you.
No hide una face from me in the day of my distress. Turn una ear to me. Answer me sharp-sharp in the day when I call.
For my days consume away like smoke. My bones are burned as a torch.
My heart is blighted like grass, and withered, for I forget to eat my bread.
By reason of the voice of my groaning, my bones stick to my skin.
I be like a pelican of the wilderness. I have become as an owl of the waste places.
I watch, and have become like a sparrow that is alone on the housetop.
My enemies reproach me all day. People Wey mad at me use my name as a curse.
For I have eaten ashes like bread, and mixed my drink with tears,
Because of una indignation and una serious anger, for you have taken me up, and thrown me away.
My days are like a long shadow. I have withered like grass.
But you, Baba God, will remain forever; una renown endures to all generations.
You go arise and have mercy on Zion; for it is time to have pity on her. Yes, the set time has come.
For una workers take pleasure in her stones, and have pity on her dust.
So the nations will fear Baba God’s name; all the kings of the earth una glory.
For Baba God has built up Zion. He has appeared in his glory.
He has responded to the prayer of the destitute, and has not despised dem prayer.
This Go be written for the generation to come. A people which Go be created will praise Yah.
For he has looked down from the height of his sanctuary. From heaven, Baba God see the earth;
to hear the groans of the prisoner; to free people Wey condemned to death;
that men may declare Baba God’s name in Zion, and his praise in Jerusalem;
when the peoples are gathered together, the kingdoms, to serve Baba God.
He weakened my strength along the course. He shortened my days.
I talk say, “My God, no take me away in the middle of my days. Una years are throughout all generations.
Of old, you laid the foundation of the earth. The heavens are the work of una hands.
Dem go perish, but You go endure. Yes, all of dem will wear out like a garment. You go change dem like a cloak, and Dem go be changed.
But You be the same. Una years Go get no end.
The pikin dem of una workers will continue. Dem offspring Go be established before you.”
By David. Praise Baba God, my soul! All that is within me, praise his holy name!
Praise Baba God, my soul, and no forget all his benefits;
who forgives all una sins; who heals all una diseases;
who redeems una life from destruction; who crowns you with loving kindness and tender mercies;
who satisfies una desire with good things, so that una youth is renewed like the eagle’s.
Baba God executes righteous acts, and justice for all Wey be oppressed.
He made known his ways to Moses, his deeds to the pikin dem of Israel.
Baba God is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness.
He No go always accuse; neither will he stay angry forever.
He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us for our iniquities.
For as the heavens are high above the earth, so great is his loving kindness toward people wey fear him.
As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our wrongdoings from us.
Like a father has compassion on his pikin dem, so Baba God has compassion on people wey fear him.
For he knows how We be made. He remembers that We be dust.
As for man, his days are like grass. As a flower of the field, so he flourishes.
For the wind passes over it, and it is gone. Its place remembers it no more.
But Baba God’s loving kindness is from everlasting to everlasting with people wey fear him, his righteousness to pikin dem’s pikin dem;
to people wey keep his covenant, to people wey remember to obey his precepts.
Baba God has established his throne in the heavens. His kingdom rules over all.
Praise Baba God, you angels of his, Wey be mighty in strength, who fulfill his word, obeying the voice of his word.
Praise Baba God, all you armies of his, you workers of his, who do his pleasure.
Praise Baba God, all you works of his, in all places of his dominion. Praise Baba God, my soul!
Bless Baba God, my soul. Baba God, my God, You be plenty well-well. You be clothed with honor and majesty.
He covers imself with light as with a garment. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain.
He lays the beams of his rooms in the waters. He makes the clouds his chariot. He walks on the wings of the wind.
He makes his messengers winds; his workers flames of fire.
He laid the foundations of the earth, that it no suppose be moved forever.
You covered it with the deep as with a cloak. The waters stood above the mountains.
At una rebuke dem fled. At the voice of una thunder dem hurried away.
The mountains rose, the valleys sank down, to the place which you had assigned to dem.
You have set a boundary that dem may not pass over; that dem no turn again to cover the earth.
He sends springs into the valleys. Dem run among the mountains.
Dem give drink to every animal of the field. The wild donkeys quench dem thirst.
The birds of the sky nest by dem. Dem sing among the branches.
He waters the mountains from his rooms. The earth is filled with the fruit of una works.
He causes the grass to grow for the livestock, and plants for man to cultivate, that he may produce chop out of the earth:
wine that makes glad the heart of man, oil to make his face to shine, and bread that dey give power man’s heart.
Baba God’s trees are well watered, the cedars of Lebanon, which he has planted;
where the birds make dem nests. The stork makes its home in the cypress trees.
The high mountains are for the wild goats. The rocks are a refuge for the rock badgers.
He appointed the moon for seasons. The sun knows when to set.
You make darkness, and it is night, in which all the animals of the forest prowl.
The young lions roar after dem prey, and seek dem chop from God.
The sun rises, and dem steal away, and lay down in dem dens.
Man goes out to his work, to his labor until the evening.
Baba God, how many are una works! In wisdom have you made dem all. The earth is full of una riches.
E get the sea, great and wide, in which are innumerable living things, both small and large animals.
There the ships go, and leviathan, whom you formed to play there.
These all wait for you, that you may give dem dem chop in due season.
You give to dem; dem gather. You open una hand; Dem be satisfied with good.
You hide una face: Dem be troubled; you take away dem breath: dem die, and return to the dust.
You send out una Spirit and Dem be created. You renew the face of the ground.
Let Baba God’s glory endure forever. Let Baba God glad well-well in his works.
He looks at the earth, and it trembles. He touches the mountains, and dem smoke.
I go sing to Baba God as long as I live. I go sing praise to my God while I have any being.
Let my meditation be sweet to him. I go glad well-well in Baba God.
Let sinners be consumed out of the earth. Let the wicked be no more. Bless Baba God, my soul. Praise Yah!
Thank God to Baba God! Call on his name! Make his doings known among the peoples.
Sing to him, sing praises to him! Tell of all his marvelous works.
Glory in his holy name. Let the heart of people wey seek Baba God glad well-well.
Seek Baba God and his strength. Seek his face forever more.
Remember his marvelous works that he has done; his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth,
you offspring of Abraham, his worker, you pikin dem of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He is Baba God, our God. His judgments are in all the earth.
He has remember his covenant forever, the word which he commanded to a thousand generations,
the covenant which he made with Abraham, his oath to Isaac,
and confirmed the same to Jacob for a statute; to Israel for an everlasting covenant,
saying, “To you I go give the land of Canaan, the lot of una inheritance”;
when dem were but a few men in number, yes, very few, and foreigners in it.
Dem go about from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
He allowed Nobody to do dem wrong. Yes, he reproved kings for dem sakes,
“No touch my anointed ones! Do my prophets no harm!”
He call for a famine on the land. He destroyed the chop supplies.
He sent a man before dem. Joseph was sold for a slave.
Dem bruised his feet with shackles. His neck was locked in irons,
until the time that his word happened, and Baba God’s word proved him true.
The king sent and freed him; even the ruler of peoples, and Make e go free.
He made him lord of his house, and ruler of all of his possessions;
to discipline his princes at his pleasure, and to teach his elders wisdom.
Israel also come into Egypt. Jacob lived in the land of Ham.
He increased his people greatly, and made dem stronger than dem adversaries.
He turned dem heart to hate his people, to conspire against his workers.
He sent Moses, his worker, and Aaron, whom he had chosen.
Dem performed miracles among dem, and wonders in the land of Ham.
He sent darkness, and made it dark. Dem didn’t rebel against his words.
He turned dem waters into blood, and killed dem fish.
Dem land swarmed with frogs, even in the rooms of dem kings.
He spoke, and swarms of flies come, and lice in all dem borders.
He give dem hail for rain, with lightning in dem land.
He struck dem vines and also dem fig trees, and shattered the trees of dem country.
He spoke, and the locusts come, and the grasshoppers, without number,
ate up every plant in dem land; and ate up the fruit of dem ground.
He struck also all the firstborn in dem land, the first fruits of all dem manhood.
He bring dem out with silver and gold. There No be one feeble person among his tribes.
Egypt was glad when dem comot, for the fear of dem had fallen on dem.
He spread a cloud for a covering, fire to give light in the night.
Dem ask, and he bring quails, and satisfied dem with the bread of the sky.
He opened the rock, and waters gushed out. Dem ran as a river in the dry places.
For he remember his holy word, and Abraham, his worker.
He bring his people out with gladness, his chosen with singing.
He give dem the lands of the nations. Dem take the labor of the peoples in possession,
that dem might keep his statutes, and observe his laws. Praise Yah!
Praise Baba God! Thank God to Baba God, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever.
Who can utter the mighty acts of Baba God, or fully declare all his praise?
Blessed are people wey keep justice. Blessed is one wey do Wetin be right at all times.
Remember me, Baba God, with the favor that you show to una people. Visit me with una salvation,
that I may see the prosperity of una chosen, that I may glad well-well in the gladness of una nation, that I may glory with una inheritance.
We have sinned with our fathers. We have committed wickedness. We have done wickedly.
Our fathers didn’t understand una wonders in Egypt. Dem didn’t remember the plenty people of una loving kindnesses, but were rebellious at the sea, even at the Red Sea.
Nevertheless he saved dem for his name’s sake, that he might make his mighty power known.
He rebuked the Red Sea also, and it was dried up; so he led dem through the depths, as through a desert.
He saved dem from the hand of him who hated dem, and redeemed dem from the hand of the enemy.
The waters covered dem adversaries. There No be one of dem left.
Then dem believe his words. Dem sang his praise.
Dem soon forgot his works. Dem didn’t wait for his counsel,
but give in to craving in the desert, and tested God in the wasteland.
He give dem dem request, but sent leanness into dem soul.
Dem envied Moses also in the camp, and Aaron, Baba God’s saint.
The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram.
A fire was kindled in dem company. The flame burned up the wicked.
Dem made a calf in Horeb, and worshiped a molten image.
Thus dem exchanged dem glory for an image of a bull that eats grass.
Dem forgot God, dem Savior, who had done great things in Egypt,
Wondrous works in the land of Ham, and awesome things by the Red Sea.
So he talk say that he would destroy dem, had Moses, his chosen, not stood before him in the breach, to turn away his serious anger, so that he wouldn’t destroy dem.
Yes, dem despised the pleasant land. Dem didn’t believe his word,
but murmured in dem tents, and didn’t listen to Baba God’s voice.
So he swore to dem that he would overthrow dem in the wilderness,
that he would overthrow dem offspring among the nations, and scatter dem in the lands.
Dem joined themselves also to Baal Peor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead.
Thus dem provoked him to anger with dem deeds. The plague broke in on dem.
Then Phinehas stood up, and executed judgment, so the plague was stopped.
That was credited to him for righteousness, for all generations to come.
Dem angered him also at the waters of Meribah, so that Moses was troubled for dem sakes;
because dem were rebellious against his spirit, he spoke rashly with his lips.
Dem didn’t destroy the peoples, as Baba God commanded dem,
but mixed themselves with the nations, and learned dem works.
Dem served dem idols, which became a snare to dem.
Yes, dem sacrificed dem sons and dem daughters to demons.
Dem shed innocent blood, even the blood of dem sons and of dem daughters, whom dem sacrificed to the idols of Canaan. The land was polluted with blood.
Thus were dem defiled with dem works, and prostituted themselves in dem deeds.
So Baba God burned with anger against his people. He abhorred his inheritance.
He give dem into the hand of the nations. People wey hated dem ruled over dem.
Dem enemies also oppressed dem. Dem were bring into subjection under dem hand.
He rescued dem many times, but dem were rebellious in dem counsel, and were bring low in dem wickedness.
Nevertheless he regarded dem distress, when he heard dem cry.
He remember for dem his covenant, and repented according to the plenty people of his loving kindnesses.
He made dem also to be pitied by all people wey carried dem captive.
Save us, Baba God, our God, gather us from among the nations, to Thank God to una holy name, to triumph in una praise!
Blessed be Baba God, the God of Israel, from everlasting even to everlasting! Let all the people say, “Amen.” Praise Yah!
Thank God to Baba God, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever.
Let the redeemed by Baba God say so, whom he has redeemed from the hand of the adversary,
And gathered out of the lands, from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south.
Dem wandered in the wilderness in a desert way. Dem find no city to live in.
Hungry and thirsty, dem soul fainted in dem.
Then dem cried to Baba God in dem trouble, and he delivered dem out of dem distresses,
he led dem also by a straight way, that dem might go to a city to live in.
Make dem praise Baba God for his loving kindness, for his wonderful deeds to the pikin dem of men!
For he satisfies the longing soul. He fills the hungry soul with good.
Some sat in darkness and in the shadow of death, being bound in suffering and iron,
because dem rebelled against the words of God, and condemned the counsel of the Most High.
So he bring down dem heart with labor. Dem fell down, and there was Nobody to help.
Then dem cried to Baba God in dem trouble, and he saved dem out of dem distresses.
He bring dem out of darkness and the shadow of death, and broke away dem chains.
Make dem praise Baba God for his loving kindness, for his wonderful deeds to the pikin dem of men!
For he has broken the gates of brass, and cut through bars of iron.
Fools are afflicted because of dem disobedience, and because of dem iniquities.
Dem soul abhors all kinds of chop. Dem draw near to the gates of death.
Then dem cry to Baba God in dem trouble, he saves dem out of dem distresses.
He sends his word, and heals dem, and delivers dem from dem graves.
Make dem praise Baba God for his loving kindness, for his wonderful deeds to the pikin dem of men!
Make dem offer the sacrifices of thanksgiving, and declare his deeds with singing.
People wey go down to the sea in ships, who do business in great waters;
These see Baba God’s deeds, and his wonders in the deep.
For he commands, and raises the stormy wind, which lifts up its waves.
Dem mount up to the sky; dem go down again to the depths. Dem soul melts away because of trouble.
Dem reel back and forth, and stagger like a drunken man, and are at dem wits’ end.
Then dem cry to Baba God in dem trouble, and he brings dem out of dem distress.
He makes the storm a calm, so that its waves are still.
Then Dem be glad because it is calm, so he brings dem to dem desired haven.
Make dem praise Baba God for his loving kindness, for his wonderful deeds for the pikin dem of men!
Make dem exalt him also in the assembly of the people, and praise him in the seat of the elders.
He turns rivers into a desert, water springs into a thirsty ground,
and a fruitful land into a salt waste, for the wickedness of people wey live in it.
He turns a desert into a pool of water, and a dry land into water springs.
There he makes the hungry live, that dem may prepare a city to live in,
sow fields, plant vineyards, and reap the fruits of increase.
He blesses dem also, so that Dem be multiplied greatly. He no dey allow dem livestock to decrease.
Again, Dem be diminished and bowed down through oppression, trouble, and sorrow.
He pours contempt on princes, and causes dem to wander in a trackless waste.
Yet he lifts the needy out of dem suffering, and increases dem families like a flock.
The upright will see it, and be glad. All the wicked will shut dem mouths.
Anybody wey is wise will pay attention to these things. Dem go consider the loving kindnesses of Baba God.
A Song. A Psalm by David. My heart is steadfast, God. I go sing and I go make music with my soul.
Wake up, harp and lyre! I go wake up the dawn.
I go Thank God to you, Baba God, among the nations. I go sing praises to you among the peoples.
For una loving kindness is great above the heavens. Una faithfulness reaches to the skies.
Be exalted, God, above the heavens! Let una glory be over all the earth.
That una beloved may be delivered, save with una right hand, and answer us.
God has spoken from his sanctuary: “In triumph, I go divide Shechem, and measure out the valley of Succoth.
Gilead is mine. Manasseh is mine. Ephraim also is my helmet. Judah is my scepter.
Moab is my wash pot. I go toss my sandal on Edom. I go shout over Philistia.”
Who will bring me into the fortified city? Who has led me to Edom?
Haven’t you rejected us, God? You no go out, God, with our armies.
Give us help against the enemy, for the help of man is vain.
Through God, We go do valiantly. For it is person wey will tread down our enemies.
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David. God of my praise, no remain silent,
for dem have opened the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of deceit against me. Dem have spoken to me with a lying tongue.
Dem have also surrounded me with words of hatred, and fought against me without a cause.
In return for my love, Dem be my adversaries; but I be in prayer.
Dem have rewarded me evil for good, and hatred for my love.
Set a wicked man over him. Let an adversary stand at his right hand.
When he is judged, Make e come out guilty. Let his prayer be turned into sin.
Let his days be few. Let another take his office.
Let his pikin dem be fatherless, and his wife a widow.
Let his pikin dem be wandering beggars. Make dem be sought from dem ruins.
Let the creditor seize all that he has. Let strangers plunder the fruit of his labor.
Let there be Nobody to extend kindness to him, neither let there be anyone to have pity on his fatherless pikin dem.
Let his posterity be cut off. In the generation following let dem name be blotted out.
Let the wickedness of his fathers be remember by Baba God. No let the sin of his mother be blotted out.
Make dem be before Baba God continually, that he may cut off dem memory from the earth;
because he didn’t remember to show kindness, but persecuted the poor and needy man, the broken in heart, to kill dem.
Yes, he love cursing, and it come to him. He didn’t delight in blessing, and it was far from him.
He clothed imself also with cursing as with his garment. It come into his inward parts like water, like oil into his bones.
Let it be to him as the clothing with which he covers imself, for the belt that is always around him.
This is the reward of my adversaries from Baba God, of people wey speak evil against my soul.
But deal with me, Baba God the Lord, for una name’s sake, because una loving kindness is good, deliver me;
for I be poor and needy. My heart is wounded within me.
I fade away like an evening shadow. I be shaken off like a locust.
My knees are weak through fasting. My body is thin and lacks fat.
I have also become a reproach to dem. When dem see me, dem shake dem head.
Help me, Baba God, my God. Save me according to una loving kindness;
that dem may know that this is una hand; that you, Baba God, have done it.
Dem may curse, but you bless. When dem arise, Dem go be shamed, but una worker shall glad well-well.
Let my adversaries be clothed with dishonor. Make dem cover themselves with dem own shame as with a robe.
I go give great thanks to Baba God with my mouth. Yes, I go praise him among the plenty people.
For he will stand at the right hand of the needy, to save him from people wey judge his soul.
A Psalm by David. Baba God says to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make una enemies una footstool for una feet.”
Baba God will send out the rod of una strength out of Zion. Rule among una enemies.
Una people offer themselves willingly in the day of una power, in holy array. Out of the womb of the morning, you have the dew of una youth.
Baba God has sworn, and No go change his mind: “You be a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”
The Lord is at una right hand. He will crush kings in the day of his serious anger.
He will judge among the nations. He will heap up dead bodies. He will crush the ruler of the whole earth.
He will drink of the brook on the way; so he will lift up his head.
Praise Yah! I go Thank God to Baba God with my whole heart, in the council of the upright, and in the congregation.
Baba God’s works are great, pondered by all people wey delight in dem.
His work is honor and majesty. His righteousness endures forever.
He has caused his wonderful works to be remember. Baba God is gracious and merciful.
He has given chop to people wey fear him. He always remembers his covenant.
He has shown his people the power of his works, in giving dem the heritage of the nations.
The works of his hands are truth and justice. All his precepts are sure.
Dem be established forever and ever. Dem be done in truth and uprightness.
He has sent redemption to his people. He has ordained his covenant forever. His name is holy and awesome!
The fear of Baba God is the beginning of wisdom. All people wey do his work have a good understanding. His praise endures forever!
Praise Yah! Blessed is the man who fears Baba God, who delights greatly in his commandments.
His offspring Go be mighty in the land. The generation of the upright Go be blessed.
Wealth and riches are in his house. His righteousness endures forever.
Light dawns in the darkness for the upright, gracious, merciful, and righteous.
It is well with the man who deals graciously and lends. He will maintain his cause in judgment.
For he will never be shaken. The righteous Go be remember forever.
He No go be afraid of evil news. His heart is steadfast, trusting in Baba God.
His heart is established. He No go be afraid in the end when he sees his adversaries.
He has dispersed, he has given to the poor. His righteousness endures forever. His horn Go be exalted with honor.
The wicked will see it, and be grieved. He shall gnash with his teeth, and melt away. The desire of the wicked will perish.
Praise Yah! Praise, you workers of Baba God, praise Baba God’s name.
Blessed be Baba God’s name, from this time forward and forever more.
From the rising of the sun to the going down of the same, Baba God’s name is to be praised.
Baba God is high above people for everywhere, his glory above the heavens.
Wey be like Baba God, our God, who has his seat on high,
Who stoops down to see in heaven and in the earth?
He raises up the poor out of the dust. Lifts up the needy from the ash heap;
that he may set him with princes, even with the princes of his people.
He settles the barren woman in her home, as a joyful mother of pikin dem. Praise Yah!
When Israel go out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of foreign language;
Judah became his sanctuary, Israel his dominion.
The sea see it, and fled. The Jordan was driven back.
The mountains skipped like rams, the little hills like lambs.
What was it, you sea, that you fled? You Jordan, that you turned back?
You mountains, that you skipped like rams; you little hills, like lambs?
Tremble, you earth, at the presence of the Lord, at the presence of the God of Jacob,
who turned the rock into a pool of water, the flint into a spring of waters.
Not to us, Baba God, not to us, but to una name give glory, for una loving kindness, and for una truth’s sake.
Why should the nations say, “Where is dem God, now?”
But our God is in the heavens. He does Anything wey he pleases.
Dem idols are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands.
Dem have mouths, but dem no speak. Dem have eyes, but dem no see.
Dem have ears, but dem no hear. Dem have noses, but dem no smell.
Dem have hands, but dem no feel. Dem have feet, but dem no walk, neither do dem speak through dem throat.
People wey make dem Go be like dem; yes, Everybody wey trusts in dem.
Israel, trust in Baba God! He is dem help and dem shield.
House of Aaron, trust in Baba God! He is dem help and dem shield.
You who fear Baba God, trust in Baba God! He is dem help and dem shield.
Baba God remembers us. He will bless us. He will bless the house of Israel. He will bless the house of Aaron.
He will bless people wey fear Baba God, both small and great.
May Baba God increase you more and more, you and una pikin dem.
Blessed are you by Baba God, who made heaven and earth.
The heavens are the heavens of Baba God; but the earth has he given to the pikin dem of men.
The dead no praise Yah, neither any who go down into silence;
But We go bless Yah, from this time forward and forever more. Praise Yah!
I love Baba God, because he listens to my voice, and my cries for mercy.
Because he has turned his ear to me, so I go call on him as long as I live.
The cords of death surrounded me, the pains of Sheol got a hold of me. I find trouble and sorrow.
Then I call on Baba God’s name: “Baba God, I beg you, deliver my soul.”
Baba God is Gracious and righteous. Yes, our God is merciful.
Baba God preserves the simple. I was bring low, and he saved me.
Return to una rest, my soul, for Baba God has dealt bountifully with you.
For you have delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from falling.
I go walk before Baba God in the land of the living.
I believe, so I talk say, “I was greatly afflicted.”
I talk say in my haste, “All men are liars.”
What will I give to Baba God for all his benefits toward me?
I go take the cup of salvation, and call on Baba God’s name.
I go pay my vows to Baba God, yes, in the presence of all his people.
Precious in Baba God’s sight is the death of his saints.
Baba God, truly I be una worker. I be una worker, the son of una worker. You have freed me from my chains.
I go offer to you the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call on Baba God’s name.
I go pay my vows to Baba God, yes, in the presence of all his people,
in the courts of Baba God’s house, in the middle of you, Jerusalem. Praise Yah!
Praise Baba God, all you nations! Extol him, all you peoples!
For his loving kindness is great toward us. Baba God’s faithfulness endures forever. Praise Yah!
Thank God to Baba God, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever.
Let Israel now say that his loving kindness endures forever.
Let the house of Aaron now say that his loving kindness endures forever.
Now let people wey fear Baba God say that his loving kindness endures forever.
Out of my distress, I call on Yah. Yah answer me with freedom.
Baba God is on my side. I go not be afraid. What can man do to me?
Baba God is on my side among people wey help me. So I go look in triumph at people wey hate me.
It is better to take refuge in Baba God, than to put confidence in man.
It is better to take refuge in Baba God, than to put confidence in princes.
All the nations surrounded me, but in Baba God’s name, I cut dem off.
Dem surrounded me, yes, dem surrounded me. In Baba God’s name I indeed cut dem off.
Dem surrounded me like bees. Dem be quenched like the burning thorns. In Baba God’s name I cut dem off.
You pushed me back hard, to make me fall, but Baba God helped me.
Yah is my strength and song. He has become my salvation.
The voice of rejoicing and salvation is in the tents of the righteous. “The right hand of Baba God does valiantly.
The right hand of Baba God is exalted! The right hand of Baba God does valiantly!”
I go not die, but live, and declare Yah’s works.
Yah has punished me severely, but he has not given me over to death.
Open to me the gates of righteousness. I go enter into dem. I go Thank God to Yah.
This is the gate of Baba God; the righteous will enter into it.
I go Thank God to you, for you have answer me, and have become my salvation.
The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
This is Baba God’s doing. It is marvelous in our eyes.
This is the day that Baba God has made. We go glad well-well and be glad in it!
Save us now, we beg you, Baba God! Baba God, we beg you, send prosperity now.
Blessed is person wey comes in Baba God’s name! We have blessed you out of Baba God’s house.
Baba God is God, and he has given us light. Bind the sacrifice with cords, even to the horns of the altar.
You be my God, and I go Thank God to you. You be my God, I go exalt you.
Oh Thank God to Baba God, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever.
ALEPH Blessed are those whose ways are blameless, who walk according to Baba God’s law.
Blessed are people wey keep his statutes, who seek him with dem whole heart.
Yes, dem do nothing wrong. Dem walk in his ways.
You have commanded una precepts, that we should fully obey dem.
Oh that my ways were steadfast to obey una statutes!
Then I wouldn’t be disappointed, when I consider all of una commandments.
I go Thank God to you with uprightness of heart, when I learn una righteous judgments.
I go observe una statutes. No utterly forsake me. BET
How can a young man keep his way pure? By living according to una word.
With my whole heart, I have sought you. No let me wander from una commandments.
I have hidden una word in my heart, that I might not sin against you.
Blessed are you, Baba God. Teach me una statutes.
With my lips, I have declared all the ordinances of una mouth.
I have rejoiced in the way of una testimonies, as much as in all riches.
I go meditate on una precepts, and consider una ways.
I go delight myself in una statutes. I go not forget una word. GIMEL
Do good to una worker. I go live and I go obey una word.
Open my eyes, that I may see wondrous things out of una law.
I be a stranger on the earth. No hide una commandments from me.
My soul is consumed with longing for una ordinances at all times.
You have rebuked the proud Wey be cursed, who wander from una commandments.
Take reproach and contempt away from me, for I have kept una statutes.
Though princes sit and slander me, una worker will meditate on una statutes.
Indeed una statutes are my delight, and my counselors. DALED
My soul is laid low in the dust. Revive me according to una word!
I declared my ways, and you answer me. Teach me una statutes.
Let me understand the teaching of una precepts! Then I go meditate on una wondrous works.
My soul is weary with sorrow: strengthen me according to una word.
Keep me from the way of deceit. Grant me una law graciously!
I have chosen the way of truth. I have set una ordinances before me.
I cling to una statutes, Baba God. No let me be disappointed.
I run in the path of una commandments, for you have set my heart free. HEY
Teach me, Baba God, the way of una statutes. I go keep dem to the end.
Give me understanding, and I go keep una law. Yes, I go obey it with my whole heart.
Direct me in the path of una commandments, for I delight in dem.
Turn my heart toward una statutes, not toward selfish gain.
Turn my eyes away from looking at worthless things. Revive me in una ways.
Fulfill una promise to una worker, that you may be feared.
Take away my disgrace that I dread, for una ordinances are good.
See am, I long for una precepts! Revive me in una righteousness. WAW
Let una loving kindness also come to me, Baba God, una salvation, according to una word.
So I go have an answer for him who reproaches me, for I trust in una word.
No snatch the word of truth out of my mouth, for I put my hope in una ordinances.
So I go obey una law continually, forever and ever.
I go walk in liberty, for I have sought una precepts.
I go also speak of una statutes before kings, and No go be disappointed.
I go delight myself in una commandments, because I love dem.
I reach out my hands for una commandments, which I love. I go meditate on una statutes. ZAYIN
Remember una word to una worker, because you give me hope.
This is my comfort in my suffering, for una word has revived me.
The arrogant mock me excessively, but I no swerve from una law.
I remember una ordinances of old, Baba God, and have comforted myself.
Indignation has taken hold on me, because of the wicked who forsake una law.
Una statutes Don dey my songs, in the house where I live.
I have remember una name, Baba God, in the night, and I obey una law.
This is my way, that I keep una precepts. CHET
Baba God is my portion. I promised to obey una words.
I sought una favor with my whole heart. Be merciful to me according to una word.
I considered my ways, and turned my steps to una statutes.
I go hurry, and not delay, to obey una commandments.
The ropes of the wicked bind me, but I no go forget una law.
At midnight I go rise to Thank God to you, because of una righteous ordinances.
I be a friend of all people wey fear you, of people wey observe una precepts.
The earth is full of una loving kindness, Baba God. Teach me una statutes. TET
Do good to una worker, according to una word, Baba God.
Teach me good judgment and knowledge, for I believe in una commandments.
Before I was afflicted, I go astray; but now I observe una word.
You be good, and do good. Teach me una statutes.
The proud have smeared a lie upon me. With my whole heart, I go keep una precepts.
Dem heart is as callous as the fat, but I delight in una law.
It is good for me that I Don dey afflicted, that I may learn una statutes.
The law of una mouth is better to me than thousands of pieces of gold and silver. YUD
Una hands have made me and formed me. Give me understanding, that I may learn una commandments.
People wey fear You go see me and be glad, because I have put my hope in una word.
Baba God, I know that una judgments are righteous, that in faithfulness you have afflicted me.
Please let una loving kindness be for my comfort, according to una word to una worker.
Let una tender mercies come to me, that I may live; for una law is my delight.
Let the proud be disappointed, for dem have overthrown me wrongfully. I go meditate on una precepts.
Let people wey fear you turn to me. Dem go know una statutes.
Let my heart be blameless toward una decrees, that I may not be disappointed. KAF
My soul faints for una salvation. I hope in una word.
My eyes fail for una word. I say, “When will you comfort me?”
For I have become like a wineskin in the smoke. I no forget una statutes.
How many are the days of una worker? When will you execute judgment on people wey persecute me?
The proud have dug pits for me, contrary to una law.
All of una commandments are faithful. Dem persecute me wrongfully. Help me!
Dem had almost wiped me from the earth, but I didn’t forsake una precepts.
Preserve my life according to una loving kindness, so I go obey the statutes of una mouth. LAMED
Baba God, una word is settled in heaven forever.
Una faithfulness is to all generations. You have established the earth, and it remains.
Una laws remain to this day, for all things serve you.
Unless una law Bin dey my delight, I would have perished in my suffering.
I go never forget una precepts, for with dem, you have revived me.
I be yours. Save me, for I have sought una precepts.
The wicked have waited for me, to destroy me. I go consider una statutes.
I have seen a limit to all perfection, but una commands are boundless. MEM
How I love una law! It is my meditation all day.
Una commandments make me wiser than my enemies, for una commandments are always with me.
I have more understanding than all my teachers, for una testimonies are my meditation.
I understand more than the aged, because I have kept una precepts.
I have kept my feet from every evil way, that I might observe una word.
I have not turned aside from una ordinances, for you have taught me.
How sweet are una promises to my taste, more than honey to my mouth!
Through una precepts, I get understanding; so I hate every false way. NUN
Una word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.
I have sworn, and have confirmed it, that I go obey una righteous ordinances.
I be afflicted well-well. Revive me, Baba God, according to una word.
Accept, I beg you, the willing offerings of my mouth. Baba God, teach me una ordinances.
My soul is continually in my hand, yet I no go forget una law.
The wicked have laid a snare for me, yet I haven’t gone astray from una precepts.
I have taken una testimonies as a heritage forever, for Dem be the gladness of my heart.
I have set my heart to perform una statutes forever, even to the end. SAMEKH
I hate double-minded men, but I love una law.
You be my hiding place and my shield. I hope in una word.
Depart from me, you evildoers, that I may keep the commandments of my God.
Uphold me according to una word, that I may live. Let me not be ashamed of my hope.
Hold me up, and I go be safe, and Go get respect for una statutes continually.
You reject all people wey stray from una statutes, for dem deceit is in vain.
You put away all the wicked of the earth like dross. So I love una testimonies.
My flesh trembles for fear of you. I be afraid of una judgments. AYIN
I have done Wetin be just and righteous. No leave me to my oppressors.
Ensure una worker’s well-being. No let the proud oppress me.
My eyes fail looking for una salvation, for una righteous word.
Deal with una worker according to una loving kindness. Teach me una statutes.
I be una worker. Give me understanding, that I may know una testimonies.
It is time to act, Baba God, for dem break una law.
So I love una commandments more than gold, yes, more than pure gold.
So I consider all of una precepts to be right. I hate every false way. PEY
Una testimonies are wonderful, so my soul keeps dem.
The entrance of una words gives light. It gives understanding to the simple.
I opened my mouth wide and panted, for I longed for una commandments.
Turn to me, and have mercy on me, as you always do to people wey love una name.
Establish my footsteps in una word. No let any wickedness have dominion over me.
Redeem me from the oppression of man, so I go observe una precepts.
Make una face shine on una worker. Teach me una statutes.
Streams of tears run down my eyes, because dem no observe una law. TZADI
You be righteous, Baba God. Una judgments are upright.
You have commanded una statutes in righteousness. Dem be fully trustworthy.
My zeal wears me out, because my enemies ignore una words.
Una promises Don dey thoroughly tested, and una worker loves dem.
I be small and despised. I no forget una precepts.
Una righteousness is an everlasting righteousness. Una law is truth.
Trouble and anguish have taken hold of me. Una commandments are my delight.
Una testimonies are righteous forever. Give me understanding, that I may live. KUF
I have call with my whole heart. Answer me, Baba God! I go keep una statutes.
I have call to you. Save me! I go obey una statutes.
I rise before dawn and cry for help. I put my hope in una words.
My eyes stay open through the night watches, that I might meditate on una word.
Hear my voice according to una loving kindness. Revive me, Baba God, according to una ordinances.
Dem draw near who follow after wickedness. Dem be far from una law.
You be near, Baba God. All una commandments are truth.
Of old I have known from una testimonies, that you have founded dem forever. RESH
Consider my suffering, and deliver me, for I no forget una law.
Plead my cause, and redeem me! Revive me according to una promise.
Salvation is far from the wicked, for dem no seek una statutes.
Great are una tender mercies, Baba God. Revive me according to una ordinances.
Many are my persecutors and my adversaries. I haven’t swerved from una testimonies.
I look at the faithless with loathing, because dem no observe una word.
Consider how I love una precepts. Revive me, Baba God, according to una loving kindness.
All of una words are truth. Every one of una righteous ordinances endures forever. SIN AND SHIN
Princes have persecuted me without a cause, but my heart stands in awe of una words.
I glad well-well at una word, as one who finds great plunder.
I hate and abhor falsehood. I love una law.
Seven times a day, I praise you, because of una righteous ordinances.
People wey love una law have great peace. Nothing causes dem to stumble.
I have hoped for una salvation, Baba God. I have done una commandments.
My soul has observed una testimonies. I love dem exceedingly.
I have obeyed una precepts and una testimonies, for all my ways are before you. TAV
Let my cry come before you, Baba God. Give me understanding according to una word.
Let my supplication come before you. Deliver me according to una word.
Let my lips utter praise, for you teach me una statutes.
Let my tongue sing of una word, for all una commandments are righteousness.
Let una hand be ready to help me, for I have chosen una precepts.
I have longed for una salvation, Baba God. Una law is my delight.
Let my soul live, that I may praise you. Let una ordinances help me.
I have gone astray like a lost sheep. Seek una worker, for I no forget una commandments.
A Song of Ascents. In my distress, I cried to Baba God. He answer me.
Deliver my soul, Baba God, from lying lips, from a deceitful tongue.
What Go be given to you, and what Go be done more to you, you deceitful tongue?
Sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals of juniper.
Woe is me, that I live in Meshech, that I live among the tents of Kedar!
My soul has had her dwelling too long with him who hates peace.
I be for peace, but when I speak, Dem be for war.
A Song of Ascents. I go lift up my eyes to the hills. Where does my help come from?
My help comes from Baba God, who made heaven and earth.
He No go allow una foot to be moved. Person wey keeps You go not slumber.
See am, person wey keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
Baba God is una keeper. Baba God is una shade on una right hand.
The sun No go harm you by day, nor the moon by night.
Baba God will keep you from all evil. He will keep una soul.
Baba God will keep una going out and una coming in, from this time forward, and forever more.
A Song of Ascents. By David. I was glad when dem talk say to me, “Let’s go to Baba God’s house!”
Our feet are standing within una gates, Jerusalem;
Jerusalem, that is built as a city that is compact together;
where the tribes go up, even Yah’s tribes, according to an ordinance for Israel, to Thank God to Baba God’s name.
For E get set thrones for judgment, the thrones of David’s house.
Pray for the peace of Jerusalem. People wey love You go prosper.
Peace be within una walls, and prosperity within una palaces.
For my brothers’ and companions’ sakes, I go now say, “Peace be within you.”
For the sake of the house of Baba God our God, I go seek una good.
A Song of Ascents. To you I do lift up my eyes, you who sit in the heavens.
See am, as the eyes of workers look to the hand of dem master, as the eyes of a maid to the hand of her mistress; so our eyes look to Baba God, our God, until he has mercy on us.
Have mercy on us, Baba God, have mercy on us, for we have endured much contempt.
Our soul is exceedingly filled with the scoffing of people Wey at ease, with the contempt of the proud.
A Song of Ascents. By David. If it had not been Baba God who was on our side, let Israel now say,
if it had not been Baba God who was on our side, when men rose up against us;
then dem would have swallowed us up alive, when dem serious anger was kindled against us;
then the waters would have overwhelmed us, the stream would have gone over our soul;
then the proud waters would have gone over our soul.
Blessed be Baba God, who has not given us as a prey to dem teeth.
Our soul has escaped like a bird out of the fowler’s snare. The snare is broken, and we have escaped.
Our help is in Baba God’s name, who made heaven and earth.
A Song of Ascents. People wey trust in Baba God are as Mount Zion, which no fit be moved, but remains forever.
As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so Baba God surrounds his people from this time forward and forever more.
For the scepter of wickedness no go remain over the allotment of the righteous; so that the righteous no go use dem hands to do evil.
Do good, Baba God, to people Wey good, to people Wey upright in dem hearts.
But as for people wey turn aside to dem crooked ways, Baba God will lead dem away with the workers of wickedness. Peace be on Israel.
A Song of Ascents. When Baba God bring back people wey come back to Zion, we were like people wey dream.
Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing. Then dem talk say among the nations, “Baba God has done great things for dem.”
Baba God has done great things for us, and We be glad.
Restore our fortunes again, Baba God, like the streams in the Negev.
People wey sow in tears will reap in gladness.
Person wey goes out weeping, carrying seed for sowing, will certainly come again with gladness, carrying his sheaves.
A Song of Ascents. By Solomon. Unless Baba God builds the house, dem labor in vain who build it. Unless Baba God watches over the city, the watchman guards it in vain.
It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil; for he gives sleep to his love ones.
See am, pikin dem are a heritage of Baba God. The fruit of the womb is his reward.
As arrows in the hand of a mighty man, so are the pikin dem of youth.
Happy is the man who has his quiver full of dem. Dem no go be disappointed when dem speak with dem enemies in the gate.
A Song of Ascents. Blessed is Everybody wey fears Baba God, who walks in his ways.
For You go eat the labor of una hands. You go be happy, and it Go be well with you.
Una wife Go be as a fruitful vine, in the innermost parts of una house; una pikin dem like olive plants, around una table.
See am, thus is the man blessed who fears Baba God.
May Baba God bless you out of Zion, and may you see the good of Jerusalem all the days of una life.
Yes, may you see una pikin dem’s pikin dem. Peace be upon Israel.
A Song of Ascents. Many times dem have afflicted me from my youth up. Let Israel now say,
many times dem have afflicted me from my youth up, yet dem have not prevailed against me.
The plowers plowed on my back. Dem made dem furrows long.
Baba God is righteous. He has cut apart the cords of the wicked.
Make dem be disappointed and turned backward, all people wey hate Zion.
Make dem be as the grass on the housetops, which withers before it grows up;
with which the reaper no dey fill his hand, nor person wey binds sheaves, his bosom.
Neither do people wey go by say, “The blessing of Baba God be on you. We bless you in Baba God’s name.”
A Song of Ascents. Out of the depths I have cried to you, Baba God.
Lord, hear my voice. Let una ears be attentive to the voice of my petitions.
If you, Yah, kept a record of sins, Lord, who could stand?
But E get forgiveness with you, so You be feared.
I wait for Baba God. My soul waits. I hope in his word.
My soul longs for the Lord more than watchmen long for the morning; more than watchmen for the morning.
Israel, hope in Baba God, for with Baba God E get loving kindness. With him is abundant redemption.
He will redeem Israel from all dem sins.
A Song of Ascents. By David. Baba God, my heart no be haughty, nor my eyes lofty; nor do I concern myself with great matters, or things too wonderful for me.
Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul, like a weaned pikin with his mother, like a weaned pikin is my soul within me.
Israel, hope in Baba God, from this time forward and forever more.
A Song of Ascents. Baba God, remember David and all his suffering,
how he swore to Baba God, and vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob:
“Surely I go not come into the structure of my house, nor go up into my bed;
I go not give sleep to my eyes, or slumber to my eyelids;
until I find out a place for Baba God, a dwelling for the Mighty One of Jacob.”
See am, we heard of it in Ephrathah. We find it in the field of Jaar:
