“We go go into his dwelling place. We go worship at his footstool.
Arise, Baba God, into una resting place; you, and the ark of una strength.
Let una priests be clothed with righteousness. Let una saints shout for gladness!”
For una worker David’s sake, no turn away the face of una anointed one.
Baba God has sworn to David in truth. He No go turn from it: “I go set the fruit of una body on una throne.
If una pikin dem will keep my covenant, my testimony that I go teach dem, dem pikin dem also will sit on una throne forever more.”
For Baba God has chosen Zion. He has desired it for his habitation.
“This is my resting place forever. Here I go live, for I have desired it.
I go abundantly bless her provision. I go satisfy her poor with bread.
Her priests I go also clothe with salvation. Her saints will shout aloud for gladness.
There I go make the horn of David to bud. I have ordained a lamp for my anointed.
I go clothe his enemies with shame, but on imself, his crown Go be resplendent.”
A Song of Ascents. By David. See how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together in unity!
It is like the precious oil on the head, that ran down on the beard, even Aaron’s beard; that come down on the edge of his robes;
like the dew of Hermon, that comes down on the hills of Zion: for there Baba God gives the blessing, even life forever more.
A Song of Ascents. Look! Praise Baba God, all you workers of Baba God, who stand by night in Baba God’s house!
Lift up una hands in the sanctuary. Praise Baba God!
May Baba God bless you from Zion; even person wey made heaven and earth.
Praise Yah! Praise Baba God’s name! Praise him, you workers of Baba God,
you who stand in Baba God’s house, in the courts of our God’s house.
Praise Yah, for Baba God is good. Sing praises to his name, for that is pleasant.
For Yah has chosen Jacob for imself; Israel for his own possession.
For I know that Baba God is great, that our Lord is above all gods.
Anything wey Baba God pleased, that he has done, in heaven and in earth, in the seas and in all deeps;
who causes the clouds to rise from every corner of the world; who makes lightnings with the rain; who brings the wind out of his treasuries;
Who struck the firstborn of Egypt, both of man and animal;
Who sent signs and wonders into the middle of you, Egypt, on Pharaoh, and on all his workers;
who struck many nations, and killed mighty kings,
Sihon king of the Amorites, Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan,
and give dem land for a heritage, a heritage to Israel, his people.
Una name, Baba God, endures forever; una renown, Baba God, throughout all generations.
For Baba God will judge his people, and have compassion on his workers.
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands.
Dem have mouths, but dem no fit speak. Dem have eyes, but dem no fit see.
Dem have ears, but dem no fit hear; neither is there any breath in dem mouths.
People wey make dem Go be like dem; yes, Everybody wey trusts in dem.
House of Israel, praise Baba God! House of Aaron, praise Baba God!
House of Levi, praise Baba God! You who fear Baba God, praise Baba God!
Blessed be Baba God from Zion, Who dwells at Jerusalem. Praise Yah!
Thank God to Baba God, for he is good; for his loving kindness endures forever.
Thank God to the God of gods; for his loving kindness endures forever.
Thank God to the Lord of lords; for his loving kindness endures forever:
To him who alone does great wonders; for his loving kindness endures forever:
To him who by understanding made the heavens; for his loving kindness endures forever:
To him who spread out the earth above the waters; for his loving kindness endures forever:
To him who made the great lights; for his loving kindness endures forever:
The sun to rule by day; for his loving kindness endures forever;
The moon and stars to rule by night; for his loving kindness endures forever:
To him who struck down the Egyptian firstborn; for his loving kindness endures forever;
And bring out Israel from among dem; for his loving kindness endures forever;
With a strong hand, and with an outstretched arm; for his loving kindness endures forever:
To him who divided the Red Sea apart; for his loving kindness endures forever;
And made Israel to pass through the middle of it; for his loving kindness endures forever;
But overthrew Pharaoh and his army in the Red Sea; for his loving kindness endures forever:
To him who led his people through the wilderness; for his loving kindness endures forever:
To him who struck great kings; for his loving kindness endures forever;
And killed mighty kings; for his loving kindness endures forever:
Sihon king of the Amorites; for his loving kindness endures forever;
Og king of Bashan; for his loving kindness endures forever;
And give dem land as an inheritance; for his loving kindness endures forever;
Even a heritage to Israel his worker; for his loving kindness endures forever:
Who remember us in our low estate; for his loving kindness endures forever;
And has delivered us from our adversaries; for his loving kindness endures forever:
Wey dey give chop to every creature; for his loving kindness endures forever.
Oh Thank God to the God of heaven; for his loving kindness endures forever.
By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down. Yes, we wept, when we remember Zion.
On the willows in that land, we hung up our harps.
For there, people wey led us captive ask us for songs. People wey tormented us demanded songs of gladness: “Sing us one of the songs of Zion!”
How can we sing Baba God’s song in a foreign land?
If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand forget its skill.
Let my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth if I no remember you; if I no prefer Jerusalem above my chief gladness.
Remember, Baba God, against the pikin dem of Edom, the day of Jerusalem; who talk say, “Raze it! Raze it even to its foundation!”
Daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction, he Go be happy who rewards you, as you have served us.
Happy shall he be, who takes and dashes una little ones against the rock.
By David. I go give you thanks with my whole heart. Before the gods, I go sing praises to you.
I go bow down toward una holy temple, and Thank God to una Name for una loving kindness and for una truth; for you have exalted una Name and una Word above all.
In the day that I call, you answer me. You encouraged me with strength in my soul.
All the kings of the earth will give you thanks, Baba God, for dem have heard the words of una mouth.
Yes, Dem go sing of the ways of Baba God; for great is Baba God’s glory.
For though Baba God is high, yet he looks after the lowly; but the proud, he knows from far away.
Though I walk in the middle of trouble, You go revive me. You go stretch out una hand against the serious anger of my enemies. Una right hand will save me.
Baba God will fulfill that which concerns me; una loving kindness, Baba God, endures forever. No forsake the works of una own hands.
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David. Baba God, you have searched me, and you know me.
You know my sitting down and my rising up. You perceive my thoughts from far away.
You search out my path and my lying down, and are acquainted with all my ways.
For there No be a word on my tongue, but, see am, Baba God, you know it altogether.
You hem me in behind and before. You laid una hand on me.
This knowledge is beyond me. It’s lofty. I no fit attain it.
Where could I go from una Spirit? Or where could I flee from una presence?
If I ascend up into heaven, You be there. If I make my bed in Sheol, see am, You be there!
If I take the wings of the dawn, and settle in the uttermost parts of the sea;
Even there una hand will lead me, and una right hand will hold me.
If I say, “Surely the darkness will overwhelm me; the light around me Go be night”;
even the darkness no dey hide from you, but the night shines as the day. The darkness is like light to you.
For you formed my inmost being. You knit me together in my mother’s womb.
I go Thank God to you, for I be fearfully and wonderfully made. Una works are wonderful. My soul knows that very well.
My frame no be hidden from you, when I was made in secret, woven together in the depths of the earth.
Una eyes see my body. In una book dem were all written, the days that were ordained for me, when as yet there were none of dem.
How precious to me are una thoughts, God! How vast is dem sum!
If I would count dem, Dem be more in number than the sand. When I wake up, I be still with you.
If only you, God, would kill the wicked. Get away from me, you bloodthirsty men!
For dem speak against you wickedly. Una enemies take una name in vain.
Baba God, no I hate people wey hate you? Am I not grieved with people wey rise up against you?
I hate dem with perfect hatred. Dem have become my enemies.
Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts.
See if E get any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David. Deliver me, Baba God, from the evil man. Preserve me from the violent man;
people wey devise mischief in dem hearts. Dem continually gather themselves together for war.
Dem have sharpened dem tongues like a serpent. Viper’s poison is under dem lips. Selah.
Baba God, keep me from the hands of the wicked. Preserve me from the violent men who have determined to trip my feet.
The proud have hidden a snare for me, dem have spread the cords of a net by the path. Dem have set traps for me. Selah.
I talk say to Baba God, “You be my God.” Listen to the cry of my petitions, Baba God.
Baba God, the Lord, the strength of my salvation, you have covered my head in the day of battle.
Baba God, no grant the desires of the wicked. No let dem evil plans succeed, or Dem go become proud. Selah.
As for the head of people wey surround me, let the mischief of dem own lips cover dem.
Let burning coals fall on dem. Make dem be thrown into the fire, into miry pits, from where dem never rise.
An evil speaker no go be established in the earth. Evil will hunt the violent man to overthrow him.
I know that Baba God will maintain the cause of the afflicted, and justice for the needy.
Surely the righteous will Thank God to una name. The upright will live in una presence.
A Psalm by David. Baba God, I have call on you. Come to me sharp-sharp! Listen to my voice when I call to you.
Let my prayer be set before you like incense; the lifting up of my hands like the evening sacrifice.
Set a watch, Baba God, before my mouth. Keep the door of my lips.
No incline my heart to any evil thing, to practice deeds of wickedness with men who work wickedness. No let me eat of dem delicacies.
Let the righteous strike me, it is kindness; Make e reprove me, it is like oil on the head; no let my head refuse it; Yet my prayer is always against evil deeds.
Dem judges are thrown down by the sides of the rock. Dem go hear my words, for Dem be well spoken.
“As when one plows and breaks up the earth, our bones are scattered at the mouth of Sheol.”
For my eyes are on you, Baba God, the Lord. In you, I take refuge. No leave my soul destitute.
Keep me from the snare which dem have laid for me, from the traps of the workers of wickedness.
Let the wicked fall together into dem own nets, while I pass by.
A contemplation by David, when he was in the cave. A Prayer. I cry with my voice to Baba God. With my voice, I ask Baba God for mercy.
I pour out my complaint before him. I tell him my troubles.
When my spirit was overwhelmed within me, you know my route. On the path in which I walk, dem have hidden a snare for me.
Look on my right, and see; for E get Nobody Wey be concerned for me. Refuge has fled from me. Nobody cares for my soul.
I cried to you, Baba God. I talk say, “You be my refuge, my portion in the land of the living.”
Listen to my cry, for I be in desperate need. deliver me from my persecutors, For Dem be stronger than me.
Bring my soul out of prison, that I may Thank God to una name. The righteous will surround me, for You go be good to me.
A Psalm by David. Hear my prayer, Baba God. Listen to my petitions. In una faithfulness and righteousness, relieve me.
No enter into judgment with una worker, for in una sight no man living is righteous.
For the enemy pursues my soul. He has struck my life down to the ground. He has made me live in dark places, as people wey Don dey long dead.
So my spirit is overwhelmed within me. My heart within me is desolate.
I remember the days of old. I meditate on all una doings. I contemplate the work of una hands.
I spread out my hands to you. My soul thirsts for you, like a parched land. Selah.
Hurry to answer me, Baba God. My spirit fails. No hide una face from me, so that I no become like people wey go down into the pit.
Cause me to hear una loving kindness in the morning, for I trust in you. Cause me to know the way in which I should walk, for I lift up my soul to you.
Deliver me, Baba God, from my enemies. I flee to you to hide me.
Teach me to do una will, for You be my God. Una Spirit is good. Lead me in the land of uprightness.
Revive me, Baba God, for una name’s sake. In una righteousness, bring my soul out of trouble.
In una loving kindness, cut off my enemies, and destroy all people wey afflict my soul, For I be una worker.
By David. Blessed be Baba God, my rock, who teaches my hands to war, and my fingers to battle:
my loving kindness, my fortress, my high tower, my deliverer, my shield, and he in whom I take refuge; who subdues my people under me.
Baba God, Wetin be man, that you care for him? Or the Son of Man, that you think of him?
Man is like a breath. His days are like a shadow that passes away.
Part una heavens, Baba God, and come down. Touch the mountains, and Dem go smoke.
Throw out lightning, and scatter dem. Send out una arrows, and rout dem.
Stretch out una hand from above, rescue me, and deliver me out of great waters, out of the hands of foreigners;
whose mouths speak deceit, Whose right hand is a right hand of falsehood.
I go sing a new song to you, God. On a ten-stringed lyre, I go sing praises to you.
You be person wey gives salvation to kings, who rescues David, his worker, from the deadly sword.
Rescue me, and deliver me out of the hands of foreigners, whose mouths speak deceit, whose right hand is a right hand of falsehood.
Then our sons Go be like well-nurtured plants, our daughters like pillars carved to adorn a palace.
Our barns are full, filled with all kinds of provision. Our sheep produce thousands and ten thousands in our fields.
Our oxen will pull heavy loads. E get no breaking in, and no going away, and no outcry in our streets.
Happy are the people Wey be in such a situation. Happy are the people whose God is Baba God.
A praise psalm by David. I go exalt you, my God, the King. I go praise una name forever and ever.
Every day I go praise you. I go extol una name forever and ever.
Great is Baba God, and greatly to be praised! His greatness is unsearchable.
One generation will commend una works to another, and will declare una mighty acts.
Of the glorious majesty of una honor, of una wondrous works, I go meditate.
Men will speak of the might of una awesome acts. I go declare una greatness.
Dem go utter the memory of una great goodness, and will sing of una righteousness.
Baba God is gracious, merciful, slow to anger, and of great loving kindness.
Baba God is good to all. His tender mercies are over all his works.
All una works will Thank God to you, Baba God. Una saints will extol you.
Dem go speak of the glory of una kingdom, and talk about una power;
to make known to the sons of men his mighty acts, the glory of the majesty of his kingdom.
Una kingdom is an everlasting kingdom. Una dominion endures throughout all generations. Baba God is faithful in all his words, and loving in all his deeds.
Baba God upholds all who fall, and raises up all people Wey bowed down.
The eyes of all wait for you. You give dem dem chop in due season.
You open una hand, and satisfy the desire of every living thing.
Baba God is righteous in all his ways, and gracious in all his works.
Baba God is near to all people wey call on him, to all who call on him in truth.
He will fulfill the desire of people wey fear him. He also will hear dem cry, and will save dem.
Baba God preserves all people wey love him, but all the wicked he will destroy.
My mouth will speak the praise of Baba God. Let all flesh bless his holy name forever and ever.
Praise Yah! Praise Baba God, my soul.
While I live, I go praise Baba God. I go sing praises to my God as long as I exist.
No put una trust in princes, each a Son of Man in whom E get no help.
His spirit departs, and he returns to the earth. In that very day, his thoughts perish.
Happy is person wey has the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in Baba God, his God:
who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in dem; who keeps truth forever;
who executes justice for the oppressed; wey dey give chop to the hungry. Baba God frees the prisoners.
Baba God opens the eyes of the blind. Baba God raises up people Wey bowed down. Baba God loves the righteous.
Baba God preserves the foreigners. He upholds the fatherless and widow, but the way of the wicked he turns upside down.
Baba God will reign forever; una God, O Zion, to all generations. Praise Yah!
Praise Yah, for it is good to sing praises to our God; for it is pleasant and fitting to praise him.
Baba God builds up Jerusalem. He gathers together the outcasts of Israel.
He heals the broken in heart, and binds up dem wounds.
He counts the number of the stars. He calls dem all by dem names.
Great is our Lord, and mighty in power. His understanding is infinite.
Baba God upholds the humble. He brings the wicked down to the ground.
Sing to Baba God with thanksgiving. Sing praises on the harp to our God,
who covers the sky with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass grow on the mountains.
He provides chop for the livestock, and for the young ravens when dem call.
He no dey delight in the strength of the horse. He takes no pleasure in the legs of a man.
Baba God takes pleasure in people wey fear him, in people wey hope in his loving kindness.
Praise Baba God, Jerusalem! Praise una God, Zion!
For he has strengthened the bars of una gates. He has blessed una pikin dem within you.
He makes peace in una borders. He fills you with the finest of the wheat.
He sends out his commandment to the earth. His word runs very swiftly.
He gives snow like wool, and scatters frost like ashes.
He hurls down his hail like pebbles. Who can stand before his cold?
He sends out his word, and melts dem. He causes his wind to blow, and the waters flow.
He shows his word to Jacob; his statutes and his ordinances to Israel.
He has not done this for just any nation. Dem no know his ordinances. Praise Yah!
Praise Yah! Praise Baba God from the heavens! Praise him in the heights!
Praise him, all his angels! Praise him, all his army!
Praise him, sun and moon! Praise him, all you shining stars!
Praise him, you heavens of heavens, You waters that are above the heavens.
Make dem praise Baba God’s name, For he commanded, and dem were created.
He has also established dem forever and ever. He has made a decree which No go pass away.
Praise Baba God from the earth, you great sea creatures, and all depths;
lightning and hail, snow and clouds; stormy wind, fulfilling his word;
mountains and all hills; fruit trees and all cedars;
wild animals and all livestock; small creatures and flying birds;
kings of the earth and all peoples; princes and all judges of the earth;
both young men and maidens; old men and pikin dem:
Make dem praise Baba God’s name, for his name alone is exalted. His glory is above the earth and the heavens.
He has lifted up the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the pikin dem of Israel, a people near to him. Praise Yah!
Praise Baba God! Sing to Baba God a new song, his praise in the assembly of the saints.
Let Israel glad well-well in him who made dem. Let the pikin dem of Zion be joyful in dem King.
Make dem praise his name in the dance! Make dem sing praises to him with tambourine and harp!
For Baba God takes pleasure in his people. He crowns the humble with salvation.
Let the saints glad well-well in honor. Make dem sing for gladness on dem beds.
May the high praises of God be in dem mouths, and a two-edged sword in dem hand;
To execute vengeance on the nations, and punishments on the peoples;
To bind dem kings with chains, and dem nobles with fetters of iron;
to execute on dem the written judgment. All his saints have this honor. Praise Yah!
Praise Yah! Praise God in his sanctuary! Praise him in his heavens for his acts of power!
Praise him for his mighty acts! Praise him according to his excellent greatness!
Praise him with the sounding of the trumpet! Praise him with harp and lyre!
Praise him with tambourine and dancing! Praise him with stringed instruments and flute!
Praise him with loud cymbals! Praise him with resounding cymbals!
Let everything that has breath praise Yah! Praise Yah!

This Psalm is a genuine one of David, though extra, composed when he fought in single combat with Goliath. I was small among my brothers, and youngest in my father’s house. I tended my father’s sheep.
My hands formed a musical instrument, and my fingers tuned a lute.
Who shall tell my Lord? The Lord imself, he imself hears.
He sent forth his angel and take me from my father’s sheep, and he anointed me with his anointing oil.
My brothers were handsome and tall; but the Lord No take pleasure in dem.
I go out to meet the Philistine, and he cursed me by his idols.
But I drew his own sword and beheaded him, and removed reproach from the pikin dem of Israel.
The proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel:
to know wisdom and instruction; to discern the words of understanding;
to receive instruction in wise dealing, in righteousness, justice, and equity;
to give prudence to the simple, knowledge and discretion to the young man:
that the wise man may hear, and increase in learning; that the man of understanding may attain to sound counsel:
to understand a proverb, and parables, the words and riddles of the wise.
The fear of Baba God is the beginning of knowledge; but the foolish despise wisdom and instruction.
My son, listen to una father’s instruction, and no forsake una mother’s teaching:
for Dem go be a garland to grace una head, and chains around una neck.
My son, if sinners entice you, no consent.
If dem say, “Come with us. Let’s lay in wait for blood. Let’s lurk secretly for the innocent without cause.
Let’s swallow dem up alive like Sheol, and whole, like people wey go down into the pit.
We’ll find all valuable wealth. We’ll fill our houses with plunder.
You shall throw una lot among us. We’ll all have one purse.”
My son, no walk on the path with dem. Keep una foot from dem path,
for dem feet run to evil. Dem hurry to shed blood.
For in vain is the net spread in the sight of any bird:
but these lay wait for dem own blood. Dem lurk secretly for dem own lives.
So are the ways of everyone Wey be greedy for gain. It takes away the life of its owners.
Wisdom calls aloud in the street. She utters her voice in the public squares.
She calls at the head of noisy places. At the entrance of the city gates, she utters her words:
“How long, you simple ones, will you love simplicity? How long will mockers delight themselves in mockery, and fools hate knowledge?
Turn at my reproof. See am, I go pour out my spirit on you. I go make known my words to you.
Because I have call, and you have refused; I have stretched out my hand, and Nobody has paid attention;
but you have ignored all my counsel, and want none of my reproof;
I also will laugh at una disaster. I go mock when calamity overtakes you;
when calamity overtakes you like a storm, when una disaster comes on like a whirlwind; when distress and anguish come on you.
Then will dem call on me, but I go not answer. Dem go seek me diligently, but Dem go not find me;
because dem hated knowledge, and didn’t choose the fear of Baba God.
Dem want none of my counsel. Dem despised all my reproof.
So Dem go eat of the fruit of dem own way, and be filled with dem own schemes.
For the backsliding of the simple will kill dem. The careless ease of fools will destroy dem.
But Anybody wey listens to me will live securely, and Go be at ease, without fear of harm.”
My son, if You go receive my words, and store up my commandments within you;
So as to turn una ear to wisdom, and apply una heart to understanding;
Yes, if you call out for discernment, and lift up una voice for understanding;
If you seek her as silver, and search for her as for hidden treasures:
then You go understand the fear of Baba God, and find the knowledge of God.
For Baba God gives wisdom. Out of his mouth comes knowledge and understanding.
He lays up sound wisdom for the upright. He is a shield to people wey walk in integrity;
that he may guard the paths of justice, and preserve the way of his saints.
Then You go understand righteousness and justice, equity and every good path.
For wisdom will enter into una heart. Knowledge Go be pleasant to una soul.
Discretion will watch over you. Understanding will keep you,
to deliver you from the way of evil, from the men who speak perverse things;
who forsake the paths of uprightness, to walk in the ways of darkness;
who glad well-well to do evil, and delight in the perverseness of evil;
Wey be crooked in dem ways, and wayward in dem paths:
To deliver you from the strange woman, even from the foreigner who flatters with her words;
who forsakes the friend of her youth, and forgets the covenant of her God:
for her house leads down to death, her paths to the comot spirits.
None who go to her return again, neither do dem attain to the paths of life:
that you may walk in the way of good men, and keep the paths of the righteous.
For the upright will live in the land. The perfect will remain in it.
But the wicked Go be cut off from the land. The treacherous Go be rooted out of it.
My son, no forget my teaching; but let una heart keep my commandments:
for length of days, and years of life, and peace, will dem add to you.
No let kindness and truth forsake you. Bind dem around una neck. Write dem on the tablet of una heart.
So You go find favor, and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
Trust in Baba God with all una heart, and no lean on una own understanding.
In all una ways acknowledge him, and he will make una paths straight.
No be wise in una own eyes. Fear Baba God, and depart from evil.
It Go be health to una body, and nourishment to una bones.
Honor Baba God with una substance, with the first fruits of all una increase:
so una barns Go be filled with plenty, and una vats will overflow with new wine.
My son, no despise Baba God’s discipline, neither be weary of his reproof:
for whom Baba God loves, he reproves; even as a father reproves the son in whom he delights.
Happy is the man who finds wisdom, the man who gets understanding.
For her good profit is better than getting silver, and her return is better than fine gold.
She is more precious than rubies. None of the things you can desire are to be compared to her.
Length of days is in her right hand. In her left hand are riches and honor.
Her ways are ways of pleasantness. All her paths are peace.
She is a tree of life to people wey lay hold of her. Happy is Everybody wey retains her.
By wisdom Baba God founded the earth. By understanding, he established the heavens.
By his knowledge, the depths were broken up, and the skies drop down the dew.
My son, Make dem not depart from una eyes. Keep sound wisdom and discretion:
so Dem go be life to una soul, and grace for una neck.
Then you shall walk in una way securely. Una foot no go stumble.
When you lie down, You go not be afraid. Yes, You go lie down, and una sleep Go be sweet.
No fear of sudden fear, neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it comes:
for Baba God Go be una confidence, and will keep una foot from being taken.
No withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in the power of una hand to do it.
No say to una neighbor, “Go, and come again; tomorrow I go give it to you,” when you have it by you.
No devise evil against una neighbor, since he dwells securely by you.
No strive with a man without cause, if he has done you no harm.
No envy the man of violence. Choose none of his ways.
For the perverse is an abomination to Baba God, but his friendship is with the upright.
Baba God’s curse is in the house of the wicked, but he blesses the habitation of the righteous.
Surely he mocks the mockers, but he gives grace to the humble.
The wise will inherit glory, but shame Go be the promotion of fools.
Listen, sons, to a father’s instruction. Pay attention and know understanding;
for I give you sound learning. No forsake my law.
For I was a son to my father, tender and an only pikin in the sight of my mother.
He taught me, and talk say to me: “Let una heart retain my words. Keep my commandments, and live.
Get wisdom. Get understanding. No forget, neither swerve from the words of my mouth.
No forsake her, and she will preserve you. Love her, and she will keep you.
Wisdom is supreme. Get wisdom. Yes, though it costs all una possessions, get understanding.
Esteem her, and she will exalt you. She will bring you to honor, when you embrace her.
She will give to una head a garland of grace. She will deliver a crown of splendor to you.”
Listen, my son, and receive my sayings. The years of una life Go be many.
I have taught you in the way of wisdom. I have led you in straight paths.
When you go, una steps No go be hampered. When you run, You go not stumble.
Take firm hold of instruction. No Make she go. Keep her, for she is una life.
No enter into the path of the wicked. No walk in the way of evil men.
Avoid it, and no pass by it. Turn from it, and pass on.
For dem no sleep, unless dem do evil. Dem sleep is taken away, unless dem make someone fall.
For dem eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of violence.
But the path of the righteous is like the dawning light, that shines more and more until the perfect day.
The way of the wicked is like darkness. Dem no know Wetin dem stumble over.
My son, attend to my words. Turn una ear to my sayings.
Make dem not depart from una eyes. Keep dem in the center of una heart.
For Dem be life to people wey find dem, and health to dem whole body.
Keep una heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
Put away from yourself a perverse mouth. Put corrupt lips far from you.
Let una eyes look straight ahead. Fix una gaze directly before you.
Make the path of una feet level. Let all of una ways be established.
No turn to the right hand nor to the left. Remove una foot from evil.
My son, pay attention to my wisdom. Turn una ear to my understanding:
that you may maintain discretion, that una lips may preserve knowledge.
For the lips of an adulteress drip honey. Her mouth is smoother than oil,
but in the end she is as bitter as wormwood, and as sharp as a two-edged sword.
Her feet go down to death. Her steps lead straight to Sheol.
She gives no thought to the way of life. Her ways are crooked, and she no dey know it.
Now so, my sons, listen to me. No depart from the words of my mouth.
Remove una way far from her. No come near the door of her house,
lest you give una honor to others, and una years to the cruel one;
lest strangers feast on una wealth, and una labors enrich another man’s house.
You go groan at una latter end, when una flesh and una body are consumed,
and say, “How I have hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof;
neither have I obeyed the voice of my teachers, nor turned my ear to people wey instructed me!
I have come to the brink of utter ruin, among the gathered assembly.”
Drink water out of una own cistern, running water out of una own well.
Should una springs overflow in the streets, streams of water in the public squares?
Make dem be for yourself alone, not for strangers with you.
Let una spring be blessed. Glad well-well in the wife of una youth.
A loving doe and a graceful deer — Make she breasts satisfy you at all times. Be captivated always with her love.
For why should you, my son, be captivated with an adulteress? Why embrace the bosom of another?
For the ways of man are before Baba God’s eyes. He examines all his paths.
The evil deeds of the wicked ensnare him. The cords of his sin hold him firmly.
He will die for lack of instruction. In the greatness of his folly, he will go astray.
My son, if you have become collateral for una neighbor, if you have struck una hands in pledge for a stranger;
You be trapped by the words of una mouth. You be ensnared with the words of una mouth.
Do this now, my son, and deliver yourself, since you have come into the hand of una neighbor. Go, humble yourself. Press una plea with una neighbor.
Give no sleep to una eyes, nor slumber to una eyelids.
Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the snare of the fowler.
Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise;
which having no chief, overseer, or ruler,
provides her bread in the summer, and gathers her chop in the harvest.
How long will you sleep, sluggard? When will you arise out of una sleep?
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:
so una poverty will come as a robber, and una scarcity as an armed man.
A worthless person, a man of wickedness, is person wey walks with a perverse mouth;
who winks with his eyes, who signals with his feet, who motions with his fingers;
in whose heart is perverseness, who devises evil continually, who always sows discord.
So his calamity will come suddenly. He Go be broken suddenly, and that without remedy.
E get six things which Baba God hates; yes, seven which are an abomination to him:
haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood;
a heart that devises wicked schemes, feet that are swift in running to mischief,
a false witness who utters lies, and person wey sows discord among brothers.
My son, keep una father’s commandment, and no forsake una mother’s teaching.
Bind dem continually on una heart. Tie dem around una neck.
When you walk, it will lead you. When you sleep, it will watch over you. When you awake, it will talk with you.
For the commandment is a lamp, and the law is light. Reproofs of instruction are the way of life,
to keep you from the immoral woman, from the flattery of the wayward wife’s tongue.
No lust after her beauty in una heart, neither Make she captivate you with her eyelids.
For a prostitute reduces you to a piece of bread. The adulteress hunts for una precious life.
Can a man scoop fire into his lap, and his clothes not be burned?
Or can one walk on hot coals, and his feet not be scorched?
So is person wey goes in to his neighbor’s wife. Anybody wey touches her No go be unpunished.
Men no despise a thief, if he steals to satisfy imself when he is hungry:
but if he is find, he shall restore seven times. He shall give all the wealth of his house.
Person wey commits adultery with a woman is void of understanding. Person wey does it destroys his own soul.
He will get wounds and dishonor. His reproach No go be wiped away.
For jealousy arouses the fury of the husband. He no go spare in the day of vengeance.
He no go regard any ransom, neither will he rest content, though you give many gifts.
My son, keep my words. Lay up my commandments within you.
Keep my commandments and live! Guard my teaching as the apple of una eye.
Bind dem on una fingers. Write dem on the tablet of una heart.
Tell wisdom, “You be my sister.” Call understanding una relative,
that dem may keep you from the strange woman, from the foreigner who flatters with her words.
For at the window of my house, I looked out through my lattice.
I see among the simple ones. I discerned among the youths a young man void of understanding,
passing through the street near her corner, he go the way to her house,
in the twilight, in the evening of the day, in the middle of the night and in the darkness.
See am, there a woman met him with the attire of a prostitute, and with crafty intent.
She is loud and defiant. Her feet no stay in her house.
Now she is in the streets, now in the squares, and lurking at every corner.
So she caught him, and kissed him. With an impudent face she talk say to him:
“Sacrifices of peace offerings are with me. Today I have paid my vows.
So I come out to meet you, to diligently seek una face, and I have find you.
I have spread my couch with carpets of tapestry, with striped cloths of the yarn of Egypt.
I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
Come, let’s take our fill of loving until the morning. Let’s solace ourselves with loving.
For my husband no be at home. He has gone on a long journey.
He has taken a bag of money with him. He will come home at the full moon.”
With persuasive words, she led him astray. With the flattering of her lips, she seduced him.
He follow her sharp-sharp, as an ox goes to the slaughter, as a fool stepping into a noose.
Until an arrow strikes through his liver, as a bird hurries to the snare, and no dey know that it will cost his life.
Now so, sons, listen to me. Pay attention to the words of my mouth.
No let una heart turn to her ways. No go astray in her paths,
for she has thrown down many wounded. Yes, all her slain are a mighty army.
Her house is the way to Sheol, going down to the rooms of death.
No dey wisdom cry out? No dey understanding raise her voice?
On the top of high places by the way, where the paths meet, she stands.
Beside the gates, at the entry of the city, at the entry doors, she cries aloud:
“To you men, I call! I send my voice to the sons of mankind.
You simple, understand prudence. You fools, be of an understanding heart.
Hear, for I go speak excellent things. The opening of my lips is for right things.
For my mouth speaks truth. Wickedness is an abomination to my lips.
All the words of my mouth are in righteousness. E get nothing crooked or perverse in dem.
Dem be all plain to him who understands, right to people wey find knowledge.
Receive my instruction rather than silver; knowledge rather than choice gold.
For wisdom is better than rubies. All the things that may be desired no fit be compared to it.
“I, wisdom, have made prudence my dwelling. Find out knowledge and discretion.
The fear of Baba God is to hate evil. I hate pride, arrogance, the evil way, and the perverse mouth.
Counsel and sound knowledge are mine. I have understanding and power.
By me kings reign, and princes decree justice.
By me princes rule; nobles, and all the righteous rulers of the earth.
I love people wey love me. People wey seek me diligently will find me.
With me are riches, honor, enduring wealth, and prosperity.
My fruit is better than gold, yes, than fine gold; my yield than choice silver.
I walk in the way of righteousness, in the middle of the paths of justice;
That I may give wealth to people wey love me. I fill dem treasuries.
“Baba God possessed me For the beginning of his work, before his deeds of old.
I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, before the earth existed.
When there were no depths, I was born, when there were no springs abounding with water.
Before the mountains were settled in place, before the hills, I was born;
while as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the beginning of the dust of the world.
When he established the heavens, I was there; when he set a circle on the surface of the deep,
when he established the clouds above, when the springs of the deep became strong,
when he give to the sea its boundary, that the waters no suppose violate his commandment, when he marked out the foundations of the earth;
then I was the craftsman by his side. I was a delight day by day, always rejoicing before him,
Rejoicing in his whole world. My delight was with the sons of men.
“Now so, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are people wey keep my ways.
Hear instruction, and be wise. No refuse it.
Blessed is the man wey hear me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at my door posts.
For Anybody wey finds me, finds life, and will obtain favor from Baba God.
But person wey sins against me wrongs his own soul. All people wey hate me love death.”
Wisdom has built her house. She has carved out her seven pillars.
She has prepared her meat. She has mixed her wine. She has also set her table.
She has sent out her maidens. She cries from the highest places of the city:
“Anybody wey is simple, Make e turn in here!” As for him Wey be void of understanding, she says to him,
“Come, eat some of my bread, Drink some of the wine which I have mixed!
Leave una simple ways, and live. Walk in the way of understanding.”
Person wey corrects a mocker invites insult. Person wey reproves a wicked man invites abuse.
No reprove a scoffer, lest he hate you. Reprove a wise man, and he will love you.
Instruct a wise man, and he Go be still wiser. Teach a righteous man, and he will increase in learning.
The fear of Baba God is the beginning of wisdom. The knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
For by me una days Go be multiplied. The years of una life Go be increased.
If You be wise, You be wise for yourself. If you mock, you alone will bear it.
The foolish woman is loud, undisciplined, and knows nothing.
She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,
To call to people wey pass by, who go straight on dem ways,
“Anybody wey is simple, Make e turn in here.” as for him Wey be void of understanding, she says to him,
“Stolen water is sweet. Chop eaten in secret is pleasant.”
But he no dey know that the comot spirits are there, that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.
The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes a glad father; but a foolish son brings grief to his mother.
Treasures of wickedness profit nothing, but righteousness delivers from death.
Baba God No go allow the soul of the righteous to go hungry, but he thrusts away the desire of the wicked.
He becomes poor who works with a lazy hand, but the hand of the diligent brings wealth.
Person wey gathers in summer is a wise son, but person wey sleeps during the harvest is a son who causes shame.
Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.
The memory of the righteous is blessed, but the name of the wicked will rot.
The wise in heart accept commandments, but a chattering fool will fall.
Person wey walks blamelessly walks surely, but person wey perverts his ways Go be find out.
One winking with the eye causes sorrow, but a chattering fool will fall.
The mouth of the righteous is a spring of life, but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.
Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.
Wisdom is find on the lips of him who has discernment, but a rod is for the back of him Wey be void of understanding.
Wise men lay up knowledge, but the mouth of the foolish is near ruin.
The rich man’s wealth is his strong city. The destruction of the poor is dem poverty.
The labor of the righteous leads to life. The increase of the wicked leads to sin.
He is in the way of life who heeds correction, but person wey forsakes reproof leads others astray.
Person wey hides hatred has lying lips. Person wey utters a slander is a fool.
In the plenty people of words E get no lack of disobedience, but person wey restrains his lips does wisely.
The tongue of the righteous is like choice silver. The heart of the wicked is of little worth.
The lips of the righteous feed many, but the foolish die for lack of understanding.
Baba God’s blessing brings wealth, and he adds no trouble to it.
It is a fool’s pleasure to do wickedness, but wisdom is a man of understanding’s pleasure.
What the wicked fear, will overtake dem, but the desire of the righteous Go be granted.
When the whirlwind passes, the wicked is no more; but the righteous stand firm forever.
As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to people wey send him.
The fear of Baba God prolongs days, but the years of the wicked go be shortened.
The prospect of the righteous is gladness, but the hope of the wicked will perish.
The way of Baba God is a stronghold to the upright, but it is a destruction to the workers of wickedness.
The righteous will never be removed, but the wicked No go live in the land.
The mouth of the righteous produces wisdom, but the perverse tongue Go be cut off.
The lips of the righteous know Wetin be acceptable, but the mouth of the wicked is perverse.
A false balance is an abomination to Baba God, but accurate weights are his delight.
When pride comes, then comes shame, but with humility comes wisdom.
The integrity of the upright shall guide dem, but the perverseness of the treacherous shall destroy dem.
Riches no profit in the day of serious anger, but righteousness delivers from death.
The righteousness of the blameless will direct his way, but the wicked shall fall by his own wickedness.
The righteousness of the upright shall deliver dem, but the unfaithful Go be trapped by evil desires.
When a wicked man dies, hope perishes, and expectation of power comes to nothing.
A righteous person is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked takes his place.
With his mouth the godless man destroys his neighbor, but the righteous Go be delivered through knowledge.
When it goes well with the righteous, the city rejoices. When the wicked perish, E get shouting.
By the blessing of the upright, the city is exalted, but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
One who despises his neighbor is void of wisdom, but a man of understanding holds his peace.
One who brings gossip betrays a confidence, but one Wey be of a trustworthy spirit is one who keeps a secret.
Where E get no wise guidance, the nation falls, but in the plenty people of counselors E get victory.
Person Wey collateral for a stranger will suffer for it, but person wey refuses pledges of collateral is secure.
A gracious woman obtains honor, but violent men obtain riches.
The merciful man does good to his own soul, but person Wey cruel troubles his own flesh.
Wicked people earn deceitful wages, but one who sows righteousness reaps a sure reward.
Person Wey truly righteous gets life. Person wey pursues evil gets death.
People Wey perverse in heart are an abomination to Baba God, but those whose ways are blameless are his delight.
Most certainly, the evil man No go be unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous Go be delivered.
Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout, is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.
The desire of the righteous is only good. The expectation of the wicked is serious anger.
E get one who scatters, and increases yet more. E get one who withholds more than is appropriate, but gains poverty.
The liberal soul go be made fat. Person wey waters go be watered also imself.
People curse someone who withholds grain, but blessing Go be on the head of him who sells it.
Person wey diligently seeks good seeks favor, but person wey searches after evil, it shall come to him.
Person wey trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous shall flourish as the green leaf.
Person wey troubles his own house shall inherit the wind. The foolish go be worker to the wise of heart.
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life. Person Wey wise wins souls.
See am, the righteous go be repaid in the earth; how much more the wicked and the sinner!
Anybody wey loves correction loves knowledge, but person wey hates reproof is stupid.
A good man shall obtain favor from Baba God, but he will condemn a man of wicked devices.
A man no go be established by wickedness, but the root of the righteous no go be moved.
A worthy woman is the crown of her husband, but a disgraceful wife is as rottenness in his bones.
The thoughts of the righteous are just, but the advice of the wicked is deceitful.
The words of the wicked are about lying in wait for blood, but the speech of the upright rescues dem.
The wicked are overthrown, and are no more, but the house of the righteous shall stand.
A man go be commended according to his wisdom, but person wey has a warped mind go be despised.
Better is person Wey lightly esteemed, and has a worker, than person wey honors imself, and lacks bread.
A righteous man respects the life of his animal, but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.
Person wey tills his land go get plenty of bread, but person wey chases fantasies is void of understanding.
The wicked desires the plunder of evil men, but the root of the righteous flourishes.
An evil man is trapped by sinfulness of lips, but the righteous shall come out of trouble.
A man go be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth. The work of a man’s hands go be rewarded to him.
The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but person Wey wise listens to counsel.
A fool shows his annoyance the same day, but one who overlooks an insult is prudent.
Person Wey truthful testifies honestly, but a false witness lies.
E get one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.
Truth’s lips Go be established forever, but a lying tongue is only momentary.
Deceit is in the heart of people wey plot evil, but gladness comes to the promoters of peace.
No mischief shall happen to the righteous, but the wicked go be filled with evil.
Lying lips are an abomination to Baba God, but people wey do the truth are his delight.
A prudent man keeps his knowledge, but the hearts of fools proclaim foolishness.
The hands of the diligent ones shall rule, but laziness ends in slave labor.
Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
A righteous person is cautious in friendship, but the way of the wicked leads dem astray.
The slothful man no dey roast his game, but the possessions of diligent men are prized.
In the way of righteousness is life; in its path E get no death.
A wise son listens to his father’s instruction, but a scoffer no dey listen to rebuke.
By the fruit of his lips, a man enjoys good things; but the unfaithful crave violence.
Person wey guards his mouth guards his soul. One who opens wide his lips comes to ruin.
The soul of the sluggard desires, and has nothing, but the desire of the diligent go be fully satisfied.
A righteous man hates lies, but a wicked man brings shame and disgrace.
Righteousness guards the way of integrity, but wickedness overthrows the sinner.
E get some who pretend to be rich, yet have nothing. E get some who pretend to be poor, yet have great wealth.
The ransom of a man’s life is his riches, but the poor hear no threats.
The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is snuffed out.
Pride only breeds quarrels, but with ones who take advice is wisdom.
Wealth gained dishonestly dwindles away, but person wey gathers by hand makes it grow.
Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when longing is fulfilled, it is a tree of life.
Anybody wey despises instruction will pay for it, but person wey respects a command Go be rewarded.
The teaching of the wise is a spring of life, to turn from the snares of death.
Good understanding wins favor; but the way of the unfaithful is hard.
Every prudent man acts from knowledge, but a fool exposes folly.
A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a trustworthy envoy gains healing.
Poverty and shame come to him who refuses discipline, but person wey heeds correction go be honored.
Longing fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but fools detest turning from evil.
One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.
Misfortune pursues sinners, but prosperity rewards the righteous.
A good man leaves an inheritance to his pikin dem’s pikin dem, but the wealth of the sinner is stored for the righteous.
An abundance of chop is in poor people’s fields, but injustice sweeps it away.
One who spares the rod hates his son, but one wey love him is careful to discipline him.
The righteous one eats to the satisfying of his soul, but the belly of the wicked goes hungry.
Every wise woman builds her house, but the foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
Person wey walks in his uprightness fears Baba God, but person Wey perverse in his ways despises him.
The fool’s talk brings a rod to his back, but the lips of the wise protect dem.
Where no oxen are, the crib is clean, but much increase is by the strength of the ox.
A truthful witness No go lie, but a false witness pours out lies.
A scoffer seeks wisdom, and no dey find it, but knowledge comes easily to a discerning person.
Stay away from a foolish man, for you no go find knowledge on his lips.
The wisdom of the prudent is to think about his way, but the folly of fools is deceit.
Fools mock at making atonement for sins, but among the upright E get good will.
The heart knows its own bitterness and gladness; he No go share these with a stranger.
The house of the wicked Go be overthrown, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
E get a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.
Even in laughter the heart may be sorrowful, and mirth may end in heaviness.
The unfaithful Go be repaid for his own ways; likewise a good man Go be rewarded for his ways.
A simple man believe everything, but the prudent man carefully considers his ways.
A wise man fears and shuns evil, but the fool is hot headed and reckless.
Person Wey quick to become angry will commit folly, and a crafty man is hated.
The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
The evil bow down before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
The poor person is shunned even by his own neighbor, but the rich person has many friends.
Person wey despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is person wey has pity on the poor.
No dem go astray who plot evil? But love and faithfulness belong to people wey plan good.
In all hard work E get profit, but the talk of the lips leads only to poverty.
The crown of the wise is dem riches, but the folly of fools crowns dem with folly.
A truthful witness saves souls, but a false witness is deceitful.
In the fear of Baba God is a secure fortress, and he Go be a refuge for his pikin dem.
The fear of Baba God is a fountain of life, turning people from the snares of death.
In the plenty people of people is the king’s glory, but in the lack of people is the destruction of the prince.
Person Wey slow to anger has great understanding, but person wey has a quick temper displays folly.
The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.
Person wey oppresses the poor shows contempt for his Maker, but person Wey kind to the needy honors him.
The wicked is bring down in his calamity, but in death, the righteous has a refuge.
Wisdom rests in the heart of one who has understanding, and is even made known in the inward part of fools.
Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
The king’s favor is toward a worker who deals wisely, but his serious anger is toward one who causes shame.
A gentle answer turns away serious anger, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouth of fools gush out folly.
Baba God’s eyes are everywhere, keeping watch on the evil and the good.
A gentle tongue is a tree of life, but deceit in it crushes the spirit.
A fool despises his father’s correction, but person wey heeds reproof shows prudence.
In the house of the righteous is much treasure, but the income of the wicked brings trouble.
The lips of the wise spread knowledge; not so with the heart of fools.
The sacrifice made by the wicked is an abomination to Baba God, but the prayer of the upright is his delight.
The way of the wicked is an abomination to Baba God, but he loves him who follows after righteousness.
E get stern discipline for one who forsakes the way: Anybody wey hates reproof shall die.
Sheol and Abaddon are before Baba God — how much more then the hearts of the pikin dem of men!
A scoffer no dey love to be reproved; he No go go to the wise.
A glad heart makes a cheerful face; but an aching heart breaks the spirit.
The heart of one who has understanding seeks knowledge, but the mouths of fools feed on folly.
All the days of the afflicted are wretched, but one who has a cheerful heart enjoys a continual feast.
Better is little, with the fear of Baba God, than great treasure with trouble.
Better is a dinner of herbs, where love is, than a fattened calf with hatred.
A wrathful man stirs up contention, but one Wey be slow to anger appeases strife.
The way of the sluggard is like a thorn patch, but the path of the upright is a highway.
A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish man despises his mother.
Folly is gladness to one Wey be void of wisdom, but a man of understanding keeps his way straight.
Where E get no counsel, plans fail; but in a plenty people of counselors Dem be established.
Gladness comes to a man with the reply of his mouth. How good is a word at the right time!
The path of life leads upward for the wise, to keep him from going downward to Sheol.
Baba God will uproot the house of the proud, but he will keep the widow’s borders intact.
Baba God detests the thoughts of the wicked, but the thoughts of the pure are pleasing.
Person Wey greedy for gain troubles his own house, but person wey hates bribes will live.
The heart of the righteous weighs answers, but the mouth of the wicked gushes out evil.
Baba God is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous.
The light of the eyes rejoices the heart. Better news gives health to the bones.
The ear that listens to reproof lives, and Go be at home among the wise.
Person wey refuses correction despises his own soul, but person wey listens to reproof gets understanding.
The fear of Baba God teaches wisdom. Before honor is humility.
The plans of the heart belong to man, but the answer of the tongue is from Baba God.
All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes; but Baba God weighs the motives.
Commit una deeds to Baba God, and una plans shall succeed.
Baba God has made everything for its own end — yes, even the wicked for the day of evil.
Everyone Wey be proud in heart is an abomination to Baba God: dem shall certainly not be unpunished.
By mercy and truth wickedness is atoned for. By the fear of Baba God men depart from evil.
When a man’s ways please Baba God, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him.
Better is a little with righteousness, than great revenues with injustice.
A man’s heart plans his course, but Baba God directs his steps.
Inspired judgments are on the lips of the king. He no go betray his mouth.
Honest balances and scales are Baba God’s; all the weights in the bag are his work.
It is an abomination for kings to do wrong, for the throne is established by righteousness.
Righteous lips are the delight of kings. Dem value one who speaks the truth.
The king’s serious anger is a messenger of death, but a wise man will pacify it.
In the light of the king’s face is life. His favor is like a cloud of the spring rain.
How much better it is to get wisdom than gold! Yes, to get understanding is to be chosen rather than silver.
The highway of the upright is to depart from evil. Person wey keeps his way preserves his soul.
Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
It is better to be of a lowly spirit with the poor, than to divide the plunder with the proud.
Person wey heeds the Word finds prosperity. Anybody wey trusts in Baba God is blessed.
The wise in heart go be call prudent. Pleasantness of the lips promotes instruction.
Understanding is a fountain of life to one who has it, but the punishment of fools is dem folly.
The heart of the wise instructs his mouth, and adds learning to his lips.
Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
E get a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.
The appetite of the laboring man labors for him; for his mouth urges him on.
A worthless man devises mischief. His speech is like a scorching fire.
A perverse man stirs up strife. A whisperer separates close friends.
A man of violence entices his neighbor, and leads him in a way that No be good.
One who winks his eyes to plot perversities, one who compresses his lips, is bent on evil.
Gray hair is a crown of glory. It is attained by a life of righteousness.
One Wey be slow to anger is better than the mighty; one who rules his spirit, than person wey takes a city.
The lot is throw into the lap, but its every decision is from Baba God.
Better is a dry morsel with quietness, than a house full of feasting with strife.
A worker who deals wisely will rule over a son who causes shame, and go get a part in the inheritance among the brothers.
The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold, but Baba God tests the hearts.
An evildoer heeds wicked lips. A liar gives ear to a mischievous tongue.
Anybody wey mocks the poor reproaches his Maker. Person Wey glad at calamity no go be unpunished.
Pikin dem’s pikin dem are the crown of old men; the glory of pikin dem are dem parents.
Arrogant speech no be fitting for a fool, much less do lying lips fit a prince.
A bribe is a precious stone in the eyes of him wey dey give it; Anywhere wey he turns, he prospers.
Person wey covers an offense promotes love; but person wey repeats a matter separates best friends.
A rebuke enters deeper into one who has understanding than a hundred lashes into a fool.
An evil man seeks only rebellion; so a cruel messenger go be sent against him.
Let a bear robbed of her cubs meet a man, rather than a fool in his folly.
Anybody wey rewards evil for good, evil no go depart from his house.
The beginning of strife is like breaching a dam, so stop contention before quarreling breaks out.
Person wey justifies the wicked, and person wey condemns the righteous, both of dem alike are an abomination to Baba God.
Why is there money in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, since he has no understanding?
A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.
A man void of understanding strikes hands, and becomes collateral in the presence of his neighbor.
Person wey loves disobedience loves strife. One who builds a high gate seeks destruction.
One who has a perverse heart no dey find prosperity, and one who has a deceitful tongue falls into trouble.
Person wey becomes the father of a fool grieves. The father of a fool has no gladness.
A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
A wicked man receives a bribe in secret, to pervert the ways of justice.
Wisdom is before the face of one who has understanding, but the eyes of a fool wander to every corner of the world.
A foolish son brings grief to his father, and bitterness to her who bore him.
Also to punish the righteous No be good, nor to flog officials for dem integrity.
Person wey spares his words has knowledge. Person Wey even tempered is a man of understanding.
Even a fool, when he keeps silent, is counted wise. When he shuts his lips, he is thought to be discerning.
An unfriendly man pursues selfishness, and defies all sound judgment.
A fool has no delight in understanding, but only in revealing his own opinion.
When wickedness comes, contempt also comes, and with shame comes disgrace.
The words of a man’s mouth are like deep waters. The fountain of wisdom is like a flowing brook.
To be partial to the faces of the wicked No be good, nor to deprive the innocent of justice.
A fool’s lips come into strife, and his mouth invites beatings.
A fool’s mouth is his destruction, and his lips are a snare to his soul.
The words of a gossip are like dainty morsels: dem go down into a person’s innermost parts.
One Wey be slack in his work is brother to him Wey be a master of destruction.
Baba God’s name is a strong tower: the righteous run to him, and are safe.
The rich man’s wealth is his strong city, like an unscalable wall in his own imagination.
Before destruction the heart of man is proud, but before honor is humility.
Person wey gives answer before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
A man’s spirit will sustain him in sickness, but a crushed spirit, who can bear?
The heart of the discerning gets knowledge. The ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
A man’s gift makes room for him, and brings him before great men.
Person wey pleads his cause first seems right; until another comes and questions him.
The lot settles disputes, and keeps strong ones apart.
A brother offended is more difficult than a fortified city; and disputes are like the bars of a fortress.
A man’s stomach is filled with the fruit of his mouth. With the harvest of his lips he is satisfied.
Death and life are in the power of the tongue; people wey love it will eat its fruit.
Anybody wey finds a wife finds a good thing, and obtains favor of Baba God.
The poor plead for mercy, but the rich answer harshly.
A man of many companions may be ruined, but E get a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
Better is the poor who walks in his integrity than person Wey perverse in his lips and is a fool.
It no be good to have zeal without knowledge; nor being hasty with one’s feet and missing the way.
The foolishness of man subverts his way; his heart rages against Baba God.
Wealth adds many friends, but the poor is separated from his friend.
A false witness no go be unpunished. Person wey pours out lies no go go free.
Many will entreat the favor of a ruler, and everyone is a friend to a man wey dey give gifts.
All the relatives of the poor shun him: how much more do his friends avoid him! He pursues dem with pleas, but Dem be gone.
Person wey gets wisdom loves his own soul. Person wey keeps understanding shall find good.
A false witness no go be unpunished. Person wey utters lies shall perish.
Delicate living No be appropriate for a fool, much less for a worker to have rule over princes.
The discretion of a man makes him slow to anger. It is his glory to overlook an offense.
The king’s serious anger is like the roaring of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
A foolish son is the calamity of his father. A wife’s quarrels are a continual dripping.
House and riches are an inheritance from fathers, but a prudent wife is from Baba God.
Slothfulness casts into a deep sleep. The idle soul shall suffer hunger.
Person wey keeps the commandment keeps his soul, but person Wey contemptuous in his ways shall die.
Person wey has pity on the poor lends to Baba God; he will reward him.
Discipline una son, for E get hope; no be a willing party to his death.
A hot-tempered man must pay the penalty, for if you rescue him, you must do it again.
Listen to counsel and receive instruction, that you may be wise in una latter end.
E get many plans in a man’s heart, but Baba God’s counsel will prevail.
That which makes a man to be desired is his kindness. A poor man is better than a liar.
The fear of Baba God leads to life, then contentment; he rests and No go be touched by trouble.
The sluggard buries his hand in the dish; he No go so much as bring it to his mouth again.
Flog a scoffer, and the simple will learn prudence; rebuke one who has understanding, and he will gain knowledge.
Person wey robs his father and drives away his mother, is a son who causes shame and brings reproach.
If you stop listening to instruction, my son, You go stray from the words of knowledge.
A corrupt witness mocks justice, and the mouth of the wicked gulps down wickedness.
Penalties are prepared for scoffers, and beatings for the backs of fools.
Wine is a mocker, and beer is a brawler. Anybody wey is led astray by dem No be wise.
The terror of a king is like the roaring of a lion. Person wey provokes him to anger forfeits his own life.
It is an honor for a man to keep aloof from strife; but every fool Go be quarreling.
The sluggard No go plow by reason of the winter; so he shall beg in harvest, and have nothing.
Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water; but a man of understanding will draw it out.
Many men claim to be men of unfailing love, but who can find a faithful man?
A righteous man walks in integrity. Blessed are his pikin dem after him.
A king who sits on the throne of judgment scatters away all evil with his eyes.
Who can say, “I have made my heart pure. I be clean and without sin?”
Differing weights and differing measures, both of dem alike are an abomination to Baba God.
Even a pikin makes imself known by his doings, whether his work is pure, and whether it is right.
The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, Baba God has made even both of dem.
No love sleep, lest you come to poverty. Open una eyes, and you go be satisfied with bread.
“It’s no good, it’s no good,” says the buyer; but when he is gone his way, then he boasts.
E get gold and abundance of rubies; but the lips of knowledge are a rare jewel.
Take the garment of one who puts up collateral for a stranger; and hold him in pledge for a wayward woman.
Fraudulent chop is sweet to a man, but afterwards his mouth is filled with gravel.
Plans are established by advice; by wise guidance you wage war!
Person wey goes about as a tale-bearer reveals secrets; so no keep company with him who opens wide his lips.
Anybody wey curses his father or his mother, his lamp go be put out in blackness of darkness.
An inheritance sharp-sharp gained at the beginning, no go be blessed in the end.
No say, “I go pay back evil.” Wait for Baba God, and he will save you.
Baba God detests differing weights, and dishonest scales No be pleasing.
A man’s steps are from Baba God; how then can man understand his way?
It is a snare to a man to make a rash dedication, then later to consider his vows.
A wise king winnows out the wicked, and drives the threshing wheel over dem.
The spirit of man is Baba God’s lamp, searching all his innermost parts.
Love and faithfulness keep the king safe. His throne is sustained by love.
The glory of young men is dem strength. The splendor of old men is dem gray hair.
Wounding blows cleanse away evil, and beatings purge the innermost parts.
The king’s heart is in Baba God’s hand like the watercourses. He turns it Anywhere wey he desires.
Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but Baba God weighs the hearts.
To do righteousness and justice is more acceptable to Baba God than sacrifice.
A high look, and a proud heart, the lamp of the wicked, is sin.
The plans of the diligent surely lead to profit; and everyone Wey be hasty surely rushes to poverty.
Getting treasures by a lying tongue is a fleeting vapor for people wey seek death.
The violence of the wicked will drive dem away, because dem refuse to do Wetin be right.
The way of the guilty is devious, but the conduct of the innocent is upright.
It is better to live in the corner of the housetop, than to share a house with a contentious woman.
The soul of the wicked desires evil; his neighbor finds no mercy in his eyes.
When the mocker is punished, the simple gains wisdom. When the wise is instructed, he receives knowledge.
The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked, and brings the wicked to ruin.
Anybody wey stops his ears at the cry of the poor, he will also cry out, but no go be heard.
A gift in secret pacifies anger; and a bribe in the cloak, strong serious anger.
It is gladness to the righteous to do justice; but it is a destruction to the workers of wickedness.
The man who wanders out of the way of understanding shall rest in the assembly of the comot spirits.
Person wey loves pleasure go be a poor man. Person wey loves wine and oil no go be rich.
The wicked is a ransom for the righteous; the treacherous for the upright.
It is better to live in a desert land, than with a contentious and fretful woman.
E get precious treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man swallows it up.
Person wey follows after righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness, and honor.
A wise man scales the city of the mighty, and brings down the strength of its confidence.
Anybody wey guards his mouth and his tongue keeps his soul from troubles.
The proud and haughty man, “scoffer” is his name; he works in the arrogance of pride.
The desire of the sluggard kills him, for his hands refuse to labor.
E get people wey covet greedily all day long; but the righteous give and no withhold.
The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination; how much more, when he brings it with a wicked mind!
A false witness will perish, and a man who listens speaks to eternity.
A wicked man hardens his face; but as for the upright, he establishes his ways.
E get no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against Baba God.
The horse is prepared for the day of battle; but victory is with Baba God.
A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favor is better than silver and gold.
The rich and the poor have this in common: Baba God is the maker of dem all.
A prudent man sees danger, and hides imself; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
The result of humility and the fear of Baba God is wealth, honor, and life.
Thorns and snares are in the path of the wicked: Anybody wey guards his soul stays from dem.
Train up a pikin in the way he should go, and when he is old he No go depart from it.
The rich rule over the poor. The borrower is worker to the lender.
Person wey sows wickedness reaps trouble, and the rod of his fury Go be destroyed.
Person wey has a generous eye Go be blessed; for he shares his chop with the poor.
Drive out the mocker, and strife will go out; yes, quarrels and insults will stop.
Person wey loves purity of heart and speaks gracefully is the king’s friend.
Baba God’s eyes watch over knowledge; but he frustrates the words of the unfaithful.
The sluggard says, “E get a lion outside! I go be killed in the streets!”
The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit. Person Wey under Baba God’s serious anger will fall into it.
Folly is bound up in the heart of a pikin: the rod of discipline drives it far from him.
Anybody wey oppresses the poor for his own increase and Anybody wey gives to the rich, both come to poverty.
Turn una ear, and listen to the words of the wise. Apply una heart to my teaching.
For it is a pleasant thing if you keep dem within you, if all of dem are ready on una lips.
That una trust may be in Baba God, I teach you today, even you.
Haven’t I written to you thirty excellent things of counsel and knowledge,
To teach you truth, reliable words, to give sound answers to the ones who sent you?
No exploit the poor, because he is poor; and no crush the needy in court;
for Baba God will plead dem case, and plunder the life of people wey plunder dem.
No befriend a hot-tempered man, and no associate with one who harbors anger:
lest you learn his ways, and ensnare una soul.
No you be one of people wey strike hands, of people Wey collateral for debts.
If you no have means to pay, why should he take away una bed from under you?
No move the ancient boundary stone, which una fathers have set up.
Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve kings. He no go serve obscure men.
When you sit to eat with a ruler, consider diligently Wetin be before you;
put a knife to una throat, if You be a man given to appetite.
No be desirous of his dainties, since Dem be deceitful chop.
No weary yourself to be rich. In una wisdom, show restraint.
Why do you set una eyes on that which No be? For it certainly sprouts wings like an eagle and flies in the sky.
No eat the chop of him who has a stingy eye, and no crave his delicacies:
for as he thinks about the cost, so he is. “Eat and drink!” he says to you, but his heart No be with you.
The morsel which you have eaten you shall vomit up, and lose una good words.
No speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of una words.
No move the ancient boundary stone. No encroach on the fields of the fatherless:
for dem Defender is strong. He will plead dem case against you.
Apply una heart to instruction, and una ears to the words of knowledge.
No withhold correction from a pikin. If you punish him with the rod, he No go die.
Punish him with the rod, and save his soul from Sheol.
My son, if una heart is wise, then my heart Go be glad, even mine:
yes, my heart will glad well-well, when una lips speak Wetin be right.
No let una heart envy sinners; but rather fear Baba God all day long.
Indeed surely E get a future hope, and una hope No go be cut off.
Listen, my son, and be wise, and keep una heart on the right path!
No be among ones drinking too much wine, or people wey gorge themselves on meat:
for the drunkard and the glutton shall become poor; and drowsiness clothes dem in rags.
Listen to una father who give you life, and no despise una mother when she is old.
Buy the truth, and no sell it. Get wisdom, discipline, and understanding.
The father of the righteous has great gladness. Anybody wey fathers a wise pikin delights in him.
Let una father and una mother be glad! Make she who bore you glad well-well!
My son, give me una heart; and let una eyes keep in my ways.
For a prostitute is a deep pit; and a wayward wife is a narrow well.
Yes, she lies in wait like a robber, and increases the unfaithful among men.
Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has strife? Who has complaints? Who has needless bruises? Who has bloodshot eyes?
People wey stay long at the wine; people wey go to seek out mixed wine.
No look at the wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly.
In the end, it bites like a snake, and poisons like a viper.
Una eyes will see strange things, and una mind will imagine confusing things.
Yes, You go be as person wey lies down in the middle of the sea, or as person wey lies on top of the rigging:
“Dem hit me, and I No be hurt! Dem beat me, and I no feel it! When will I wake up? I can do it again. I can find another.”
No be envious of evil men; neither desire to be with dem:
for dem hearts plot violence, and dem lips talk about mischief.
Through wisdom a house is built; by understanding it is established;
by knowledge the rooms are filled with all rare and beautiful treasure.
A wise man has great power; and a knowledgeable man increases strength;
for by wise guidance you wage una war; and victory is in many advisors.
Wisdom is too high for a fool: he no dey open his mouth in the gate.
One who plots to do evil Go be call a schemer.
The schemes of folly are sin. The mocker is detested by men.
If you falter in the time of trouble, una strength is small.
Rescue people Wey being led away to death! Indeed, hold back people Wey staggering to the slaughter!
If you say, “See am, we didn’t know this”; no dey person wey weighs the hearts consider it? Person wey keeps una soul, no dey he know it? Shall he not render to every man according to his work?
My son, eat honey, for it is good; the droppings of the honeycomb, which are sweet to una taste:
so you shall know wisdom to be to una soul; if you have find it, then there Go be a reward, una hope No go be cut off.
No lay in wait, wicked man, against the habitation of the righteous. No destroy his resting place:
for a righteous man falls seven times, and rises up again; but the wicked are overthrown by calamity.
No glad well-well when una enemy falls. No let una heart be glad when he is overthrown;
lest Baba God see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his serious anger from him.
No fret yourself because of evildoers; neither be envious of the wicked:
for there Go be no reward to the evil man; and the lamp of the wicked go be snuffed out.
My son, fear Baba God and the king. No join people Wey rebellious:
for dem calamity will rise suddenly; the destruction from dem both — wey know?
These also are sayings of the wise. To show partiality in judgment No be good.
Person wey says to the wicked, “You be righteous”; peoples will curse him, and nations will abhor him —
