but it will go well with people wey convict the guilty, and a rich blessing will come on dem.
An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.
Prepare una work outside, and get una fields ready. Afterwards, build una house.
No be a witness against una neighbor without cause. No deceive with una lips.
No say, “I go do to him as he has done to me; I go render to the man according to his work.”
I go by the field of the sluggard, by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;
See am, it was all grown over with thorns. Its surface was covered with nettles, and its stone wall was broken down.
Then I see, and considered well. I see, and received instruction:
a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep;
so una poverty will come as a robber, and una want as an armed man.
These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
It is the glory of God to conceal a thing, but the glory of kings is to search out a matter.
As the heavens for height, and the earth for depth, so the hearts of kings are unsearchable.
Take away the dross from the silver, and material comes out for the refiner;
Take away the wicked from the king’s presence, and his throne Go be established in righteousness.
No exalt yourself in the presence of the king, or claim a place among great men;
for it is better that it be talk say to you, “Come up here,” than that you should be put lower in the presence of the prince, whom una eyes have seen.
No be hasty in bringing charges to court. What will you do in the end when una neighbor shames you?
Debate una case with una neighbor, and no betray the confidence of another;
lest one wey hear it put you to shame, and una bad reputation never depart.
A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover to an obedient ear.
As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to people wey send him; for he refreshes the soul of his masters.
As clouds and wind without rain, so is person wey boasts of gifts deceptively.
By patience a ruler is persuaded. A soft tongue breaks the bone.
Have you find honey? Eat as much as is sufficient for you, lest you eat too much, and vomit it.
Let una foot be seldom in una neighbor’s house, lest he be weary of you, and hate you.
A man wey dey give false testimony against his neighbor is like a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.
Confidence in someone unfaithful in time of trouble is like a bad tooth, or a lame foot.
As one who takes away a garment in cold weather, or vinegar on soda, so is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
If una enemy is hungry, give him chop to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink:
for You go heap coals of fire on his head, and Baba God will reward you.
The north wind produces rain; so a backbiting tongue brings an angry face.
It is better to live in the corner of the housetop, than to share a house with a contentious woman.
Like cold water to a thirsty soul, so is better news from a far country.
Like a muddied spring, and a polluted well, so is a righteous man wey dey give way before the wicked.
It No be good to eat much honey; nor is it honorable to seek one’s own honor.
Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.
Like snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honor No be fitting for a fool.
Like a fluttering sparrow, like a darting swallow, so the undeserved curse no dey come to rest.
A whip is for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of fools!
No answer a fool according to his folly, lest you also be like him.
Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own eyes.
One who sends a message by the hand of a fool is cutting off feet and drinking violence.
Like the legs of the lame that hang loose, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
As one who binds a stone in a sling, so is person wey gives honor to a fool.
Like a thorn bush that goes into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
As an archer who wounds all, so is person wey hires a fool or person wey hires people wey pass by.
As a dog that returns to his vomit, so is a fool who repeats his folly.
Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? E get more hope for a fool than for him.
The sluggard says, “E get a lion in the road! A fierce lion roams the streets!”
As the door turns on its hinges, so does the sluggard on his bed.
The sluggard buries his hand in the dish. He is too lazy to bring it back to his mouth.
The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer with discretion.
Like one who grabs a dog’s ears is one who passes by and meddles in a quarrel not his own.
Like a madman who shoots torches, arrows, and death,
is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “Am I not joking?”
For lack of wood a fire goes out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.
As coals are to hot embers, and wood to fire, so is a contentious man to kindling strife.
The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, dem go down into the innermost parts.
Like silver dross on an earthen vessel are the lips of a fervent one with an evil heart.
A malicious man disguises imself with his lips, but he harbors evil in his heart.
When his speech is charming, no believe him; for E get seven abominations in his heart.
His malice may be concealed by deception, but his wickedness Go be exposed in the assembly.
Anybody wey digs a pit shall fall into it. Anybody wey rolls a stone, it will come back on him.
A lying tongue hates those it hurts; and a flattering mouth works ruin.
No boast about tomorrow; for you no know what a day may bring.
Let another man praise you, and not una own mouth; a stranger, and not una own lips.
A stone is heavy, and sand is a burden; but a fool’s provocation is heavier than both.
Serious anger is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; but Wey be able to stand before jealousy?
Better is open rebuke than hidden love.
Faithful are the wounds of a friend; although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
A full soul loathes a honeycomb; but to a hungry soul, every bitter thing is sweet.
As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his home.
Perfume and incense bring gladness to the heart; so does earnest counsel from a man’s friend.
No forsake una friend and una father’s friend. No go to una brother’s house in the day of una disaster: better is a neighbor Wey be near than a distant brother.
Be wise, my son, and bring gladness to my heart, then I can answer my tormentor.
A prudent man sees danger and takes refuge; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
Take his garment when he puts up collateral for a stranger. Hold it for a wayward woman!
Person wey blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it Go be taken as a curse by him.
A continual dropping on a rainy day and a contentious wife are alike:
restraining her is like restraining the wind, or like grasping oil in his right hand.
Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
Anybody wey tends the fig tree shall eat its fruit. Person wey looks after his master go be honored.
Like water reflects a face, so a man’s heart reflects the man.
Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; and a man’s eyes are never satisfied.
The crucible is for silver, and the furnace for gold; but man is refined by his praise.
Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, yet his foolishness No go be removed from him.
Know well the state of una flocks, and pay attention to una herds:
for riches No be forever, nor does the crown endure to all generations.
The hay is removed, and the new growth appears, the grasses of the hills are gathered in.
The lambs are for una clothing, and the goats are the price of a field.
There Go be plenty of goats’ milk for una chop, for una family’s chop, and for the nourishment of una worker girls.
The wicked flee when Nobody pursues; but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
In rebellion, a land has many rulers, but order is maintained by a man of understanding and knowledge.
A needy man who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain which leaves no crops.
People wey forsake the law praise the wicked; but people wey keep the law contend with dem.
Evil men no understand justice; but people wey seek Baba God understand it fully.
Better is the poor who walks in his integrity, than person Wey perverse in his ways, and he is rich.
Anybody wey keeps the law is a wise son; but person Wey a companion of gluttons shames his father.
Person wey increases his wealth by excessive interest gathers it for one who has pity on the poor.
Person wey turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer is an abomination.
Anybody wey causes the upright to go astray in an evil way, he will fall into his own trap; but the blameless will inherit good.
The rich man is wise in his own eyes; but the poor who has understanding sees through him.
When the righteous triumph, E get great glory; but when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.
Person wey conceals his sins no dey prosper, but Anybody wey confesses and renounces dem finds mercy.
Blessed is the man who always fears; but one who hardens his heart falls into trouble.
As a roaring lion or a charging bear, so is a wicked ruler over helpless people.
A tyrannical ruler lacks judgment. One who hates ill-gotten gain Go get long days.
A man Wey be tormented by life blood Go be a fugitive until death; Nobody will support him.
Anybody wey walks blamelessly is kept safe; but one with perverse ways will fall suddenly.
One who works his land Go get an abundance of chop; but one who chases fantasies Go get his fill of poverty.
A faithful man is rich with blessings; but one Wey be eager to be rich No go go unpunished.
To show partiality No be good; yet a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.
A stingy man hurries after riches, and no dey know that poverty waits for him.
One who rebukes a man will afterward find more favor than one who flatters with the tongue.
Anybody wey robs his father or his mother, and says, “It’s not wrong.” He is a partner with a destroyer.
One Wey be greedy stirs up strife; but one who trusts in Baba God will prosper.
One who trusts in imself is a fool; but one who walks in wisdom is kept safe.
One wey dey give to the poor has no lack; but one who closes his eyes Go get many curses.
When the wicked rise, men hide themselves; but when dem perish, the righteous thrive.
Person Wey often rebuked and stiffens his neck Go be destroyed suddenly, with no remedy.
When the righteous thrive, the people glad well-well; but when the wicked rule, the people groan.
Anybody wey loves wisdom brings gladness to his father; but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.
The king by justice makes the land stable, but person wey takes bribes tears it down.
A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.
An evil man is snared by his sin, but the righteous can sing and be glad.
The righteous care about justice for the poor. The wicked no be concerned about knowledge.
Mockers stir up a city, but wise men turn away anger.
If a wise man goes to court with a foolish man, the fool rages or scoffs, and E get no peace.
The bloodthirsty hate a man of integrity; and dem seek the life of the upright.
A fool vents all of his anger, but a wise man brings imself under control.
If a ruler listens to lies, all of his officials are wicked.
The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: Baba God gives sight to the eyes of both.
The king who fairly judges the poor, his throne go be established forever.
The rod of correction gives wisdom, but a pikin left to imself causes shame to his mother.
When the wicked increase, sin increases; but the righteous will see dem downfall.
Correct una son, and he will give you peace; yes, he will bring delight to una soul.
Where E get no revelation, the people throw off restraint; but one who keeps the law is blessed.
A worker no fit be corrected by words. Though he understands, yet he No go respond.
Do you see a man Wey be hasty in his words? E get more hope for a fool than for him.
Person wey pampers his worker from youth Go get him become a son in the end.
An angry man stirs up strife, and a wrathful man abounds in sin.
A man’s pride brings him low, but one of lowly spirit gains honor.
Anybody wey is an accomplice of a thief is an enemy of his own soul. He takes an oath, but dares not testify.
The fear of man proves to be a snare, but Anybody wey puts his trust in Baba God is kept safe.
Many seek the ruler’s favor, but a man’s justice comes from Baba God.
A dishonest man detests the righteous, and the upright in dem ways detest the wicked.
The words of Agur the son of Jakeh; the revelation: the man says to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
“Surely I be the most ignorant man, and no have a man’s understanding.
I have not learned wisdom, neither do I have the knowledge of the Holy One.

Who has ascended up into heaven, and descended? Who has gathered the wind in his fists? Who has bound the waters in his garment? Who has established all every corner of the world? Wetin be his name, and Wetin be his son’s name, if you know?
“Every word of God is flawless. He is a shield to people wey take refuge in him.
No you add to his words, lest he reprove you, and you be find a liar.
“Two things I have ask of you; no deny me before I die:
Remove far from me falsehood and lies. Give me neither poverty nor riches. Feed me with the chop that is needful for me;
lest I be full, deny you, and say, ‘Wey be Baba God?’ or lest I be poor, and steal, and so dishonor the name of my God.
“No slander a worker to his master, lest he curse you, and you be held guilty.
E get a generation that curses dem father, and no dey bless dem mother.
E get a generation that is pure in dem own eyes, yet No be washed from dem filthiness.
E get a generation, oh how lofty are dem eyes! Dem eyelids are lifted up.
E get a generation whose teeth are like swords, and dem jaws like knives, to devour the poor from the earth, and the needy from among men.
“The leach has two daughters: ‘Give, give.’ “E get three things that are never satisfied; four that no say, ‘Enough:’
Sheol, the barren womb; the earth that No be satisfied with water; and the fire that no dey say, ‘Enough.’
“The eye that mocks at his father, and scorns obedience to his mother: the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, the young eagles shall eat it.
“E get three things which are too amazing for me, four which I no understand:
The way of an eagle in the air; the way of a serpent on a rock; the way of a ship in the middle of the sea; and the way of a man with a maiden.
“So is the way of an adulterous woman: she eats and wipes her mouth, and says, ‘I have done nothing wrong.’
“For three things the earth tremble, and under four, it no fit bear up:
For a worker when he is king; a fool when he is filled with chop;
for an unloved woman when she is married; and a worker Wey be heir to her mistress.
“E get four things which are little on the earth, but Dem be exceedingly wise:
the ants No be a strong people, yet dem provide dem chop in the summer.
The conies are but a feeble folk, yet make dem dem houses in the rocks.
The locusts have no king, yet dem advance in ranks.
You can catch a lizard with una hands, yet it is in kings’ palaces.
“E get three things which are stately in dem march, four which are stately in going:
The lion, which is mightiest among animals, and no dey turn away for any;
the greyhound, the male goat also; and the king against whom E get no rising up.
“If you have done foolishly in lifting up yourself, or if you have thought evil, put una hand over una mouth.
For as the churning of milk produces butter, and the wringing of the nose produces blood; so the forcing of serious anger produces strife.”
The words of king Lemuel; the revelation which his mother taught him.
“Oh, my son! Oh, son of my womb! Oh, son of my vows!
No give una strength to women, nor una ways to that which destroys kings.
It No be for kings, Lemuel; it No be for kings to drink wine; nor for princes to say, ‘Where is strong drink?’
lest dem drink, and forget the law, and pervert the justice due to anyone Wey be afflicted.
Give strong drink to him Wey be ready to perish; and wine to the bitter in soul:
Make e drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
Open una mouth for the mute, in the cause of all Wey be left desolate.
Open una mouth, judge righteously, and serve justice to the poor and needy.”
Who can find a worthy woman? For her price is far above rubies.
The heart of her husband trusts in her. He go get no lack of gain.
She does him good, and not harm, all the days of her life.
She seeks wool and flax, and works eagerly with her hands.
She is like the merchant ships. She brings her bread from far away.
She rises also while it is yet night, gives chop to her household, and portions for her worker girls.
She considers a field, and buys it. With the fruit of her hands, she plants a vineyard.
She arms her waist with strength, and makes her arms strong.
She perceives that her merchandise is profitable. Her lamp no dey go out by night.
She lays her hands to the distaff, and her hands hold the spindle.
She opens her arms to the poor; yes, she extends her hands to the needy.
She No be afraid of the snow for her household; for all her household are clothed with scarlet.
She makes for sheself carpets of tapestry. Her clothing is fine linen and purple.
Her husband is respected in the gates, when he sits among the elders of the land.
She makes linen garments and sells dem, and delivers sashes to the merchant.
Strength and dignity are her clothing. She laughs at the time to come.
She opens her mouth with wisdom. Faithful instruction is on her tongue.
She looks well to the ways of her household, and no dey eat the bread of idleness.
Her pikin dem rise up and call her blessed. Her husband also praises her:
“Many women do noble things, but you excel dem all.”
Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain; but a woman who fears Baba God, she go be praised.
Give her of the fruit of her hands! Make she works praise her in the gates!
The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:
“Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher; “Vanity of vanities, all is vanity.”
What does man gain from all his labor in which he labors under the sun?
One generation goes, and another generation comes; but the earth remains forever.
The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, and hurries to its place where it rises.
The wind goes toward the south, and turns around to the north. It turns around continually as it goes, and the wind returns again to its courses.
All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea No be full. To the place where the rivers flow, there dem flow again.
All things are full of weariness beyond uttering. The eye No be satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
That which Don dey is that which go be; and that which Don dey done is that which go be done: and E get no new thing under the sun.
Is there a thing of which it may be talk say, “See am, this is new?” It Don dey long ago, in the ages which were before us.
E get no memory of the former; neither shall there be any memory of the latter that are to come, among those that shall come after.
I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under the sky. It is a heavy burden that God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with.
I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and see am, all is vanity and a chasing after wind.
That which is crooked no fit be made straight; and that which is lacking no fit be counted.
I talk say to myself, “See am, I have obtained for myself great wisdom above all who were before me in Jerusalem. Yes, my heart has had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.”
I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also was a chasing after wind.
For in much wisdom is much grief; and person wey increases knowledge increases sorrow.
I talk say in my heart, “Come now, I go test you with mirth: so enjoy pleasure”; and see am, this also was vanity.
I talk say of laughter, “It is foolishness”; and of mirth, “What does it accomplish?”

I searched in my heart how to cheer my flesh with wine, my heart yet guiding me with wisdom, and how to lay hold of folly, until I might see what it was good for the sons of men that dem should do under heaven all the days of dem lives.
I made myself great works. I built myself houses. I planted myself vineyards.
I made myself gardens and parks, and I planted trees in dem of all kinds of fruit.
I made myself pools of water, to water from it the forest where trees were reared.
I bought male workers and female workers, and had workers born in my house. I also had great possessions of herds and flocks, above all who were before me in Jerusalem;

I also gathered silver and gold for myself, and the treasure of kings and of the provinces. I got myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men — musical instruments, and that of all sorts.
So I was great, and increased more than all who were before me in Jerusalem. My wisdom also remain with me.
Anything wey my eyes desired, I didn’t keep from dem. I didn’t withhold my heart from any gladness, for my heart rejoiced because of all my labor, and this was my portion from all my labor.
Then I looked at all the works that my hands had worked, and at the labor that I had labored to do; and see am, all was vanity and a chasing after wind, and there was no profit under the sun.
I turned myself to consider wisdom, madness, and folly: for what can the king’s successor do? Just that which Don dey done long ago.
Then I see that wisdom excels folly, as far as light excels darkness.
The wise man’s eyes are in his head, and the fool walks in darkness — and yet I perceived that one event happens to dem all.
Then I talk say in my heart, “As it happens to the fool, so will it happen even to me; and why was I then more wise?” Then I talk say in my heart that this also is vanity.
For of the wise man, even as of the fool, E get no memory for ever, since in the days to come all Go get been long forgotten. Indeed, the wise man must die just like the fool!
So I hated life, because the work that is worked under the sun was grievous to me; for all is vanity and a chasing after wind.
I hated all my labor in which I labored under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.
Wey know whether he Go be a wise man or a fool? Yet he Go get rule over all of my labor in which I have labored, and in which I have shown myself wise under the sun. This also is vanity.
So I began to cause my heart to despair concerning all the labor in which I had labored under the sun.
For E get a man whose labor is with wisdom, with knowledge, and with skillfulness; yet he shall leave it for his portion to a man who has not labored for it. This also is vanity and a great evil.
For what has a man of all his labor, and of the striving of his heart, in which he labors under the sun?
For all his days are sorrows, and his travail is grief; yes, even in the night his heart takes no rest. This also is vanity.
E get nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and make his soul enjoy good in his labor. This also I see, that it is from the hand of God.
For who can eat, or who can have enjoyment, more than I?

For to the man who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge, and gladness; but to the sinner he gives travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him who pleases God. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
For everything E get a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:
a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;
a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
a time to throw away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to throw away;
a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.
What profit has person wey works in that in which he labors?
I have seen the burden which God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with.
He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in dem hearts, yet so that man no fit find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.
I know that E get nothing better for dem than to glad well-well, and to do good as long as dem live.
Also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy good in all his labor, is the gift of God.
I know that Anything wey God does, it go be forever. Nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it; and God has done it, that men should fear before him.
That which is Don dey long ago, and that which is to be Don dey long ago: and God seeks again that which is passed away.
Moreover I see under the sun, in the place of justice, that wickedness was there; and in the place of righteousness, that wickedness was there.
I talk say in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked; for E get a time there for every purpose and for every work.”
I talk say in my heart, “As for the sons of men, God tests dem, so that dem may see that dem themselves are like animals.

For that which happens to the sons of men happens to animals. Even one thing happens to dem. As the one dies, so the other dies. Yes, dem have all one breath; and man has no advantage over the animals: for all is vanity.
All go to one place. All are from the dust, and all turn to dust again.
Wey know the spirit of man, whether it goes upward, and the spirit of the animal, whether it goes downward to the earth?”
So I see that E get nothing better, than that a man should glad well-well in his works; for that is his portion: for who can bring him to see what Go be after him?

Then I come back and see all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and see am, the tears of people wey were oppressed, and dem had no comforter; and on the side of dem oppressors there was power; but dem had no comforter.
So I praised the dead who Don dey long dead more than the living Wey be yet alive.
Yes, better than dem both is him who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
Then I see all the labor and achievement that is the envy of a man’s neighbor. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.
The fool folds his hands together and ruins imself.
Better is a handful, with quietness, than two handfuls with labor and chasing after wind.
Then I come back and see vanity under the sun.

E get one Wey be alone, and he has neither son nor brother. E get no end to all of his labor, neither are his eyes satisfied with wealth. “For whom then, do I labor, and deprive my soul of enjoyment?” This also is vanity. Yes, it is a miserable business.
Two are better than one, because dem have a good reward for dem labor.
For if dem fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him Wey be alone when he falls, and no dey have another to lift him up.
Again, if two lie together, then dem have warmth; but how can one keep warm alone?
If a man prevails against one Wey be alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord No be sharp-sharp broken.
Better is a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king who no dey know how to receive admonition any more.
For out of prison he come out to be king; yes, even in his kingdom he was born poor.
I see all the living who walk under the sun, that dem were with the youth, the other, who succeeded him.
There was no end of all the people, even of all dem over whom he was — yet people wey come after no go glad well-well in him. Surely this also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
Guard una steps when you go to God’s house; for to draw near to listen is better than to give the sacrifice of fools, for dem no know that dem do evil.
No be rash with una mouth, and no let una heart be hasty to utter anything before God; for God is in heaven, and you on earth. So let una words be few.
For as a dream comes with a plenty people of cares, so a fool’s speech with a plenty people of words.
When you vow a vow to God, no defer to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools. Pay that which you vow.
It is better that you no suppose vow, than that you should vow and not pay.
No allow una mouth to lead you into sin. No protest before the messenger that this was a mistake. Why should God be angry at una voice, and destroy the work of una hands?
For in the plenty people of dreams E get vanities, as well as in many words: but you must fear God.

If you see the oppression of the poor, and the violent taking away of justice and righteousness in a district, no marvel at the matter: for one official is eyed by a higher one; and E get officials over dem.
Moreover the profit of the earth is for all. The king profits from the field.
Person wey loves silver no go be satisfied with silver; nor person wey loves abundance, with increase: this also is vanity.
When goods increase, people wey eat dem are increased; and what advantage is there to its owner, except to feast on dem with his eyes?
The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the rich No go allow him to sleep.
E get a grievous evil which I have seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to his harm.
Those riches perish by misfortune, and if he has fathered a son, E get nothing in his hand.
As he come out of his mother’s womb, naked shall he go again as he come, and shall take nothing for his labor, which he may carry away in his hand.
This also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he come, so shall he go. And what profit does he have who labors for the wind?
All his days he also eats in darkness, he is frustrated, and has sickness and serious anger.

See am, that which I have seen to be good and proper is for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his labor, in which he labors under the sun, all the days of his life which God has given him; for this is his portion.
Every man also to whom God has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to glad well-well in his labor — this is the gift of God.
For he no go often reflect on the days of his life; because God occupies him with the gladness of his heart.
E get an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is heavy on men:

a man to whom God gives riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet God gives him no power to eat of it, but an alien eats it. This is vanity, and it is an evil disease.

If a man fathers a hundred pikin dem, and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul No be filled with good, and moreover he has no burial; I say, that a stillborn pikin is better than he:
for it comes in vanity, and departs in darkness, and its name is covered with darkness.
Moreover it has not seen the sun nor known it. This has rest rather than the other.
Yes, though he live a thousand years twice told, and yet fails to enjoy good, no all go to one place?
All the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite No be filled.
For what advantage has the wise more than the fool? What has the poor man, that knows how to walk before the living?
Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
Anything wey Don dey, its name was given long ago; and it is known what man is; neither can he contend with him Wey be mightier than he.
For E get many words that create vanity. What does that profit man?
For wey know Wetin be good for man in life, all the days of his vain life which he spends like a shadow? For who can tell a man what Go be after him under the sun?
A good name is better than fine perfume; and the day of death better than the day of one’s birth.
It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men, and the living should take this to heart.
Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made good.
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.
Surely extortion makes the wise man foolish; and a bribe destroys the understanding.
Better is the end of a thing than its beginning. The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
No be hasty in una spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.
No say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For you No ask wisely about this.
Wisdom is as good as an inheritance. Yes, it is more excellent for people wey see the sun.
For wisdom is a defense, even as money is a defense; but the excellency of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of him who has it.
Consider the work of God, for who can make that straight, which he has made crooked?
In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider; yes, God has made the one side by side with the other, to the end that man no suppose find out anything after him.
All this I have seen in my days of vanity: E get a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness, and E get a wicked man who lives long in his evildoing.
No be overly righteous, neither make yourself overly wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
No be too wicked, neither be foolish. Why should you die before una time?
It is good that you should take hold of this. Yes, also from that no withdraw una hand; for person wey fears God will come out of dem all.
Wisdom is a strength to the wise man more than ten rulers Wey be in a city.
Surely there No be a righteous man on earth, wey do good and no dey sin.
Also no take heed to all words that are spoken, lest you hear una worker curse you;
for often una own heart knows that you yourself have likewise cursed others.
All this I have proved in wisdom. I talk say, “I go be wise”; but it was far from me.
That which is, is far off and exceedingly deep. Who can find it out?
I turned around, and my heart sought to know and to search out, and to seek wisdom and the scheme of things, and to know that wickedness is stupidity, and that foolishness is madness.
I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and traps, whose hands are chains. Anybody wey pleases God shall escape from her; but the sinner Go be ensnared by her.
“See am, I have find this,” says the Preacher, “to each other, to find out the scheme;
which my soul still seeks; but I have not find. I have find one man among a thousand; but I have not find a woman among all those.
See am, I have only find this: that God made man upright; but dem search for many schemes.”
Wey be like the wise man? And wey know the interpretation of a thing? A man’s wisdom makes his face shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.
I say, “Keep the king’s command!” because of the oath to God.
No be hasty to go out of his presence. No persist in an evil thing, for he does Anything wey pleases him,
for the king’s word is supreme. Who can say to him, “Wetin be you doing?”
Anybody wey keeps the commandment no go come to harm, and his wise heart will know the time and procedure.
For E get a time and procedure for every purpose, although the misery of man is heavy on him.
For he no dey know that which Go be; for who can tell him how it Go be?
E get no man who has power over the spirit to contain the spirit; neither does he have power over the day of death. E get no discharge in war; neither shall wickedness deliver people wey practice it.
All this I have seen, and applied my mind to every work that is done under the sun. E get a time in which one man has power over another to his hurt.
So I see the wicked buried. Indeed dem come also from holiness. Dem go and were forgotten in the city where dem did this. This also is vanity.
Because sentence against an evil work No be executed speedily, so the heart of the sons of men is fully set in dem to do evil.
Though a sinner commits crimes a hundred times, and lives long, yet surely I know that it Go be better with people wey fear God, Wey be reverent before him.
But it no go be well with the wicked, neither shall he lengthen days like a shadow; because he no dey fear God.

E get a vanity which is done on the earth, that E get righteous men to whom it happens according to the work of the wicked. Again, E get wicked men to whom it happens according to the work of the righteous. I talk say that this also is vanity.

Then I commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be joyful: for that will accompany him in his labor all the days of his life which God has given him under the sun.
When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done on the earth (for also E get that neither day nor night sees sleep with his eyes),

then I see all the work of God, that man no fit find out the work that is done under the sun, because however much a man labors to seek it out, yet he no go find it. Yes even though a wise man thinks he can comprehend it, he no go be able to find it.

For all this I laid to my heart, even to explore all this: that the righteous, and the wise, and dem works, are in the hand of God; whether it is love or hatred, man no dey know it; all is before dem.

All things come alike to all. E get one event to the righteous and to the wicked; to the good, to the clean, to the unclean, to him who sacrifices, and to him who no dey sacrifice. As is the good, so is the sinner; person wey takes an oath, as person wey fears an oath.

This is an evil in all that is done under the sun, that E get one event to all: yes also, the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in dem heart while dem live, and after that dem go to the dead.
For to him Wey be joined with all the living E get hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
For the living know that Dem go die, but the dead no know anything, neither do dem have any more a reward; for dem memory is forgotten.
Also dem love, dem hatred, and dem envy has perished long ago; neither have dem any more a portion forever in anything that is done under the sun.
Go una way — eat una bread with gladness, and drink una wine with a merry heart; for God has already accepted una works.
Let una garments be always white, and no let una head lack oil.

Live joyfully with the wife whom you love all the days of una life of vanity, which he has given you under the sun, all una days of vanity: for that is una portion in life, and in una labor in which you labor under the sun.
Anything wey una hand finds to do, do it with una might; for E get no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, where You be going.

I come back, and see under the sun, that the race No be to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happen to dem all.

For man also no dey know his time. As the fish that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare, even so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falls suddenly on dem.
I have also seen wisdom under the sun in this way, and it seemed great to me.
There was a little city, and few men within it; and a great king come against it, besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it.
Now a poor wise man was find in it, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remember that same poor man.
Then I talk say, “Wisdom is better than strength.” Nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words No be heard.
The words of the wise heard in quiet are better than the cry of him who rules among fools.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war; but one sinner destroys much good.
Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to produce an evil odor; so does a little folly outweigh wisdom and honor.
A wise man’s heart is at his right hand, but a fool’s heart at his left.
Yes also, when the fool walks by the way, his understanding fails him, and he says to everyone that he is a fool.
If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, no leave una place; for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.
E get an evil which I have seen under the sun, the sort of error which proceeds from the ruler.
Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.
I have seen workers on horses, and princes walking like workers on the earth.
Person wey digs a pit may fall into it; and Anybody wey breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
Anybody wey carves out stones may be injured by dem. Anybody wey splits wood may be endangered through am.
If the ax is blunt, and one no dey sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.
If the snake bites before it is charmed, then is there no profit for the charmer’s tongue.
The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but a fool is swallowed by his own lips.
The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
A fool also multiplies words. Man no dey know what Go be; and that which Go be after him, who can tell him?
The labor of fools wearies every one of dem; for he no dey know how to go to the city.
Woe to you, land, when una king is a pikin, and una princes eat in the morning!
Happy are you, land, when una king is the son of nobles, and una princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
By slothfulness the roof sinks in; and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.
A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes the life glad; and money is the answer for all things.
No curse the king, no, not in una thoughts; and no curse the rich in una bedroom: for a bird of the sky may carry una voice, and that which has wings may tell the matter.
Throw una bread on the waters; for you shall find it after many days.
Give a portion to seven, yes, even to eight; for you no know what evil Go be on the earth.
If the clouds are full of rain, dem empty themselves on the earth; and if a tree falls toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falls, there shall it be.
Person wey observes the wind no go sow; and person wey regards the clouds no go reap.
As you no know Wetin be the way of the wind, nor how the bones grow in the womb of her Wey be with pikin; even so you no know the work of God wey do all.
In the morning sow una seed, and in the evening no withhold una hand; for you no know which will prosper, whether this or that, or whether dem both Go be equally good.
Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to see the sun.
Yes, if a man lives many years, Make e glad well-well in dem all; but Make e remember the days of darkness, for dem go be many. All that comes is vanity.

Glad well-well, young man, in una youth, and let una heart cheer you in the days of una youth, and walk in the ways of una heart, and in the sight of una eyes; but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
So remove sorrow from una heart, and put away evil from una flesh; for youth and the dawn of life are vanity.
Remember also una Creator in the days of una youth, before the evil days come, and the years draw near, when You go say, “I have no pleasure in dem”;
Before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain;
in the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because Dem be few, and people wey look out of the windows are darkened,
and the doors go be shut in the street; when the sound of the grinding is low, and one shall rise up at the voice of a bird, and all the daughters of music go be bring low;

yes, dem go be afraid of heights, and terrors Go be on the way; and the almond tree shall blossom, and the grasshopper go be a burden, and desire shall fail; because man goes to his everlasting home, and the mourners go about the streets:
before the silver cord is severed, or the golden bowl is broken, or the pitcher is broken at the spring, or the wheel broken at the cistern,
and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who give it.
“Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher. “All is vanity!”
Further, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge. Yes, he pondered, sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
The Preacher sought to find out acceptable words, and that which was written blamelessly, words of truth.
The words of the wise are like goads; and like nails well fastened are words from the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
Furthermore, my son, be admonished: of making many books E get no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
This is the end of the matter. All Don dey heard. Fear God, and keep his commandments; for this is the whole duty of man.
For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it is good, or whether it is evil.
The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s.
Make e kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; for una love is better than wine.
Una oils have a pleasing fragrance. Una name is oil poured out, so the virgins love you.
Take me away with you. Make we hurry. The king has bring me into his rooms. We go be glad and glad well-well in you. We go praise una love more than wine! Dem be right to love you.
I be dark, but lovely, you daughters of Jerusalem, like Kedar’s tents, like Solomon’s curtains.
No stare at me because I be dark, because the sun has scorched me. My mother’s sons were angry with me. Dem made me keeper of the vineyards. I haven’t kept my own vineyard.
Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you graze una flock, where you rest dem at noon; For why should I be as one Wey be veiled beside the flocks of una companions?
If you no know, most beautiful among women, follow the tracks of the sheep. Graze una young goats beside the shepherds’ tents.
I have compared you, my love, to a steed in Pharaoh’s chariots.
Una cheeks are beautiful with earrings, una neck with strings of jewels.
We go make you earrings of gold, with studs of silver.
While the king sat at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.
My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh, that lies between my breasts.
My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi.
See am, You be beautiful, my love. See am, You be beautiful. Una eyes are doves.
See am, You be beautiful, my beloved, yes, pleasant; and our couch is verdant.
The beams of our house are cedars. Our rafters are firs.
I be a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
As a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, his fruit was sweet to my taste.
He bring me to the banquet hall. His banner over me is love.
Strengthen me with raisins, refresh me with apples; For I be faint with love.
His left hand is under my head. His right hand embraces me.
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.
The voice of my beloved! See am, he comes, leaping on the mountains, skipping on the hills.
My beloved is like a roe or a young deer. See am, he stands behind our wall! He looks in at the windows. He glances through the lattice.
My beloved spoke, and talk say to me, “Rise up, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.
For, see am, the winter is past. The rain is over and gone.
The flowers appear on the earth. The time of the singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
The fig tree ripens her green figs. The vines are in blossom. Dem give out dem fragrance. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.”
My dove in the clefts of the rock, In the hiding places of the mountainside, Let me see una face. Let me hear una voice; for una voice is sweet, and una face is lovely.
Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that plunder the vineyards; for our vineyards are in blossom.
My beloved is mine, and I be his. He browses among the lilies.
Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be like a roe or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.
By night on my bed, I sought him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
I go get up now, and go about the city; in the streets and in the squares I go seek him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
The watchmen who go about the city find me; “Have you seen him whom my soul loves?”
I had scarcely passed from dem, when I find him whom my soul loves. I held him, and would not Make e go, until I had bring him into my mother’s house, into the room of her who conceived me.
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.
Wey be this who comes up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all spices of the merchant?
See am, it is Solomon’s carriage! Sixty mighty men are around it, of the mighty men of Israel.
Dem all handle the sword, and are expert in war. Every man has his sword on his thigh, because of fear in the night.
King Solomon made imself a carriage of the wood of Lebanon.
He made its pillars of silver, its bottom of gold, its seat of purple, the middle of it being paved with love, from the daughters of Jerusalem.
Go out, you daughters of Zion, and see king Solomon, with the crown with which his mother has crowned him, in the day of his weddings, in the day of the gladness of his heart.
See am, You be beautiful, my love. See am, You be beautiful. Una eyes are doves behind una veil. Una hair is as a flock of goats, that descend from Mount Gilead.
Una teeth are like a newly shorn flock, which have come up from the washing, where every one of dem has twins. None is bereaved among dem.
Una lips are like scarlet thread. Una mouth is lovely. Una temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind una veil.
Una neck is like David’s tower built for an armory, whereon a thousand shields hang, all the shields of the mighty men.
Una two breasts are like two fawns that are twins of a roe, which feed among the lilies.
Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, I go go to the mountain of myrrh, to the hill of frankincense.
You be all beautiful, my love. E get no spot in you.
Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon. Look from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
You have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride. You have ravished my heart with one of una eyes, with one chain of una neck.
How beautiful is una love, my sister, my bride! How much better is una love than wine! The fragrance of una perfumes than all kinds of spices!
Una lips, my bride, drip like the honeycomb. Honey and milk are under una tongue. The smell of una garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
A locked up garden is my sister, my bride; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.
Una shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits: henna with spikenard plants,
spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree; myrrh and aloes, with all the best spices,
a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, flowing streams from Lebanon.
Awake, north wind; and come, you south! Blow on my garden, that its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and taste his precious fruits.

I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved.

I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It is the voice of my beloved who knocks: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night.”
I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? I have washed my feet. Indeed, must I soil dem?
My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening. My heart pounded for him.
I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock.
I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left; and had gone away. My heart go out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I call him, but he didn’t answer.
The watchmen who go about the city find me. Dem beat me. Dem bruised me. The keepers of the walls take my cloak away from me.
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, that you tell him that I be faint with love.
How is una beloved better than another beloved, you fairest among women? How is una beloved better than another beloved, that you do so adjure us?
My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among ten thousand.
His head is like the purest gold. His hair is bushy, black as a raven.
His eyes are like doves beside the water brooks, washed with milk, mounted like jewels.
His cheeks are like a bed of spices with towers of perfumes. His lips are like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.
His hands are like rings of gold set with beryl. His body is like ivory work overlaid with sapphires.
His legs are like pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
His mouth is sweetness; yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.
Where has una beloved gone, you fairest among women? Where has una beloved turned, that we may seek him with you?
My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
I be my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine. He browses among the lilies,
You be beautiful, my love, as Tirzah, lovely as Jerusalem, awesome as an army with banners.
Turn away una eyes from me, for dem have overcome me. Una hair is like a flock of goats, that lie along the side of Gilead.
Una teeth are like a flock of ewes, which have come up from the washing; of which every one has twins; Nobody is bereaved among dem.
Una temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind una veil.
E get sixty queens, eighty concubines, and virgins without number.

My dove, my perfect one, is unique. She is her mother’s only daughter. She is the favorite one of her who bore her. The daughters see her, and call her blessed; the queens and the concubines, and dem praised her.
Wey be person wey looks out as the morning, beautiful as the moon, clear as the sun, and awesome as an army with banners?
I go down into the nut tree grove, to see the green plants of the valley, to see whether the vine budded, and the pomegranates were in flower.
Without realizing it, my desire set me with my royal people’s chariots.
Return, return, Shulammite! Return, return, that we may gaze at you. Why do you desire to gaze at the Shulammite, as at the dance of Mahanaim?
How beautiful are una feet in sandals, prince’s daughter! Una rounded thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a skillful workman.
Una body is like a round goblet, no mixed wine is wanting. Una waist is like a heap of wheat, set about with lilies.
Una two breasts are like two fawns, that are twins of a roe.
Una neck is like an ivory tower. Una eyes are like the pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bathrabbim. Una nose is like the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.
Una head on you is like Carmel. The hair of una head like purple. The king is held captive in its tresses.
How beautiful and how pleasant You be, love, for delights!
This, una stature, is like a palm tree, una breasts like its fruit.
I talk say, “I go climb up into the palm tree. I go take hold of its fruit.” Let una breasts be like clusters of the vine, the smell of una breath like apples,
Una mouth like the best wine, that goes down smoothly for my beloved, gliding through the lips of people Wey asleep.
I be my beloved’s. His desire is toward me.
Come, my beloved, Make we go out into the field. Make we lodge in the villages.
Let’s go early up to the vineyards. Let’s see whether the vine has budded, its blossom is open, and the pomegranates are in flower. There I go give you my love.
The mandrakes produce fragrance. At our doors are all kinds of precious fruits, new and old, which I have stored up for you, my beloved.
Oh that you were like my brother, who nursed from the breasts of my mother! If I find you outside, I would kiss you; yes, and Nobody would despise me.
I would lead you, bringing you into my mother’s house, who would instruct me. I would have you drink spiced wine, of the juice of my pomegranate.
His left hand would be under my head. His right hand would embrace me.
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.
Wey be this who comes up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? Under the apple tree I aroused you. There una mother conceived you. There she was in labor and bore you.
Set me as a seal on una heart, as a seal on una arm; for love is strong as death. Jealousy is as cruel as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a very flame of Baba God.
Many waters no fit quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned.
We have a little sister. She has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister in the day when she is to be spoken for?
If she is a wall, We go build on her a turret of silver. if she is a door, We go enclose her with boards of cedar.
I be a wall, and my breasts like towers, then I was in his eyes like one who find peace.
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal Hamon. He leased out the vineyard to keepers. Each was to bring a thousand shekels of silver for its fruit.
My own vineyard is before me. The thousand are for you, Solomon; two hundred for people wey tend its fruit.
You who live in the gardens, with friends in attendance, let me hear una voice!
Come away, my beloved! Be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices!
The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he see concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Hear, heavens, and listen, earth; for Baba God has spoken: “I have nourished and bring up pikin dem, and dem have rebelled against me.
The ox knows his owner, and the donkey his master’s crib; but Israel no dey know, my people no consider.”

Ah sinful nation, a people loaded with wickedness, offspring of evildoers, pikin dem who deal corruptly! Dem have forsaken Baba God. Dem have despised the Holy One of Israel. Dem be estranged and backward.
Why should you be beaten more, that you revolt more and more? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.
From the sole of the foot even to the head E get no soundness in it: wounds, welts, and open sores. Dem haven’t been closed, neither bandaged, neither soothed with oil.
Una country is desolate. Una cities are burned with fire. Strangers devour una land in una presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.
The daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a field of melons, like a besieged city.
Unless Baba God of Armies had left to us a very small remnant, we would Don dey as Sodom; we would Don dey like Gomorrah.
Hear Baba God’s word, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah!

“Wetin be the plenty people of una sacrifices to me?”, says Baba God. “I have had enough of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed animals. I no delight in the blood of bulls, or of lambs, or of male goats.
When you come to appear before me, who has required this at una hand, to trample my courts?
Bring no more vain offerings. Incense is an abomination to me; new moons, Sabbaths, and convocations: I no fit bear with evil assemblies.
My soul hates una New Moons and una appointed feasts. Dem be a burden to me. I be weary of bearing dem.
When you spread out una hands, I go hide my eyes from you. Yes, when you make many prayers, I go not hear. Una hands are full of blood.
Wash unaself, make yourself clean. Put away the evil of una doings from before my eyes. Cease to do evil.
Learn to do well. Seek justice. Relieve the oppressed. Judge the fatherless. Plead for the widow.”
“Come now, and Make we reason together,” says Baba God: “Though una sins be as scarlet, dem go be as white as snow. Though dem be red like crimson, dem go be as wool.
If You be willing and obedient, you shall eat the good of the land;
but if you refuse and rebel, you go be devoured with the sword; for the mouth of Baba God has spoken it.”
How the faithful city has become a prostitute! She was full of justice; righteousness lodged in her, but now murderers.
Una silver has become dross, una wine mixed with water.
Una princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves. Everyone loves bribes, and follows after rewards. Dem no judge the fatherless, neither does the cause of the widow come to dem.
So the Lord, Baba God of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says: “Ah, I go get relief from my adversaries, and avenge myself on my enemies;
and I go turn my hand on you, thoroughly purge away una dross, and will take away all una tin.
I go restore una judges as at the first, and una counselors as at the beginning. Afterward you go be call ‘The city of righteousness, a faithful town.’
Zion go be redeemed with justice, and her converts with righteousness.
But the destruction of transgressors and sinners go be together, and people wey forsake Baba God go be consumed.
For dem go be ashamed of the oaks which you have desired, and you go be confounded for the gardens that you have chosen.
For you go be as an oak whose leaf fades, and as a garden that has no water.
The strong Go be like tinder, and his work like a spark. Dem go both burn together, and Nobody will quench dem.”
This is what Isaiah the son of Amoz see concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
It shall happen in the latter days, that the mountain of Baba God’s house go be established on the top of the mountains, and go be raised above the hills; and people for everywhere shall flow to it.

Many peoples shall go and say, “Come, let’s go up to the mountain of Baba God, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and We go walk in his paths.” For out of Zion the law shall go out, and Baba God’s word from Jerusalem.

He will judge between the nations, and will decide concerning many peoples; and dem shall beat dem swords into plowshares, and dem spears into pruning hooks. Nation no go lift up sword against nation, neither shall dem learn war any more.
House of Jacob, come, and Make we walk in the light of Baba God.

For you have forsaken una people, the house of Jacob, because Dem be filled from the east, with people wey practice divination like the Philistines, and dem clasp hands with the pikin dem of foreigners.
Dem land is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of dem treasures. Dem land also is full of horses, neither is there any end of dem chariots.
Dem land also is full of idols. Dem worship the work of dem own hands, that which dem own fingers have made.
Man is bring low, and mankind is humbled; so no forgive dem.
Enter into the rock, and hide in the dust, from before the terror of Baba God, and from the glory of his majesty.
The lofty looks of man Go be bring low, the haughtiness of men Go be bowed down, and Baba God alone Go be exalted in that day.
For there Go be a day of Baba God of Armies for all that is proud and haughty, and for all that is lifted up; and it go be bring low:
For all the cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, for all the oaks of Bashan,
For all the high mountains, for all the hills that are lifted up,
For every lofty tower, for every fortified wall,
For all the ships of Tarshish, and for all pleasant imagery.
The loftiness of man go be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men go be bring low; and Baba God alone go be exalted in that day.
The idols shall utterly pass away.
Men shall go into the caves of the rocks, and into the holes of the earth, from before the terror of Baba God, and from the glory of his majesty, when he arises to shake the earth mightily.
In that day, men shall throw away dem idols of silver, and dem idols of gold, which Don dey made for themselves to worship, to the moles and to the bats;
To go into the caverns of the rocks, and into the clefts of the ragged rocks, from before the terror of Baba God, and from the glory of his majesty, when he arises to shake the earth mightily.
Stop trusting in man, whose breath is in his nostrils; for of what account is he?
For, see am, the Lord, Baba God of Armies, takes away from Jerusalem and from Judah supply and support, the whole supply of bread, and the whole supply of water;
the mighty man, the man of war, the judge, the prophet, the diviner, the elder,
the captain of fifty, the honorable man, the counselor, the skilled craftsman, and the clever enchanter.
I go give boys to be dem princes, and pikin dem shall rule over dem.
The people Go be oppressed, everyone by another, and everyone by his neighbor. The pikin will behave imself proudly against the old man, and the base against the honorable.
Indeed a man shall take hold of his brother in the house of his father, saying, “You have clothing, you be our ruler, and let this ruin be under una hand.”
In that day he will cry out, saying, “I go not be a healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing. You no go make me ruler of the people.”
For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen; because dem tongue and dem doings are against Baba God, to provoke the eyes of his glory.
The look of dem faces testify against dem. Dem parade dem sin like Sodom. Dem no hide it. Woe to dem soul! For dem have bring disaster upon themselves.
Tell the righteous “Good!” For dem shall eat the fruit of dem deeds.
Woe to the wicked! Disaster is upon dem; for the deeds of his hands Go be paid back to him.
As for my people, pikin dem are dem oppressors, and women rule over dem. My people, people wey lead you cause you to err, and destroy the way of una paths.
Baba God stands up to contend, and stands to judge the peoples.
Baba God will enter into judgment with the elders of his people, and dem leaders: “It is you who have eaten up the vineyard. The plunder of the poor is in una houses.
What do you mean that you crush my people, and grind the face of the poor?” says the Lord, Baba God of Armies.
Moreover Baba God talk say, “Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with outstretched necks and flirting eyes, walking to trip as dem go, jingling ornaments on dem feet;
so the Lord brings sores on the crown of the head of the women of Zion, and Baba God will make dem scalps bald.”
In that day the Lord will take away the beauty of dem anklets, the headbands, the crescent necklaces,
the earrings, the bracelets, the veils,
the headdresses, the ankle chains, the sashes, the perfume bottles, the charms,
the signet rings, the nose rings,
the fine robes, the capes, the cloaks, the purses,
the hand mirrors, the fine linen garments, the tiaras, and the shawls.

It shall happen that instead of sweet spices, there go be rottenness; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of well set hair, baldness; instead of a robe, a wearing of sackcloth; and branding instead of beauty.
Una men shall fall by the sword, and una mighty in the war.
Her gates shall lament and mourn; and she go be desolate and sit on the ground.
Seven women shall take hold of one man in that day, saying, “We go eat our own bread, and wear our own clothing: only Make we be call by una name. Take away our reproach.”
In that day, Baba God’s branch Go be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land Go be the beauty and glory of the survivors of Israel.
It will happen, that person Wey left in Zion, and person wey remains in Jerusalem, go be call holy, even everyone Wey be written among the living in Jerusalem;
when the Lord go get washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and go get purged the blood of Jerusalem from within it, by the spirit of justice, and by the spirit of burning.
Baba God will create over the whole habitation of Mount Zion, and over her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory Go be a canopy.
There Go be a pavilion for a shade in the daytime from the heat, and for a refuge and for a shelter from storm and from rain.
Let me sing for my well beloved a song of my beloved about his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a very fruitful hill.

He dug it up, gathered out its stones, planted it with the choicest vine, built a tower in the middle of it, and also cut out a wine press inside am. He looked for it to yield grapes, but it yielded wild grapes.
“Now, inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, please judge between me and my vineyard.
What could Don dey done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it? Why, when I looked for it to yield grapes, did it yield wild grapes?
Now I go tell you what I go do to my vineyard. I go take away its hedge, and it Go be eaten up. I go break down its wall, and it Go be trampled down.
I go lay it a wasteland. It no go be pruned nor hoed, but it will grow briers and thorns. I go also command the clouds that dem rain no rain on it.”

For the vineyard of Baba God of Armies is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant: and he looked for justice, but, see am, oppression; for righteousness, but, see am, a cry of distress.
Woe to people wey join house to house, who lay field to field, until E get no room, and You be made to live alone in the middle of the land!
In my ears, Baba God of Armies says: “Surely many houses Go be desolate, even great and beautiful, unoccupied.
For ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and a homer of seed shall yield an ephah.”
Woe to people wey rise up early in the morning, that dem may follow strong drink; who stay late into the night, until wine inflames dem!
The harp, lyre, tambourine, and flute, with wine, are at dem feasts; but dem no respect the work of Baba God, neither have dem considered the operation of his hands.
So my people go into captivity for lack of knowledge. Dem honorable men are famished, and dem plenty people are parched with thirst.
So Sheol has enlarged its desire, and opened its mouth without measure; and dem glory, dem plenty people, dem pomp, and person wey rejoices among dem, descend into it.
So man is bring low, mankind is humbled, and the eyes of the arrogant ones are humbled;
but Baba God of Armies is exalted in justice, and God the Holy One is sanctified in righteousness.
Then the lambs will graze as in dem pasture, and strangers will eat the ruins of the rich.
Woe to people wey draw wickedness with cords of falsehood, and wickedness as with cart rope;
Who say, “Make e make speed, Make e hasten his work, that we may see it; and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, that we may know it!”
Woe to people wey call evil good, and good evil; who put darkness for light, and light for darkness; who put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!
Woe to people Wey wise in dem own eyes, and prudent in dem own sight!
Woe to people Wey mighty to drink wine, and champions at mixing strong drink;
who acquit the guilty for a bribe, but deny justice for the innocent!

So as the tongue of fire devours the stubble, and as the dry grass sinks down in the flame, so dem root go be as rottenness, and dem blossom shall go up as dust; because dem have rejected the law of Baba God of Armies, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

So Baba God’s anger burns against his people, and he has stretched out his hand against dem, and has struck dem. The mountains tremble, and dem dead bodies are as refuse in the middle of the streets. For all this, his anger No be turned away, but his hand is still stretched out.
He will lift up a banner to the nations from far, and he will whistle for dem from the end of the earth. See am, Dem go come speedily and swiftly.
Nobody go be weary nor stumble among dem; Nobody shall slumber nor sleep; neither shall the belt of dem waist be untied, nor the strap of dem sandals be broken:
whose arrows are sharp, and all dem bows bent. Dem horses’ hoofs Go be like flint, and dem wheels like a whirlwind.
Dem roaring Go be like a lioness. Dem go roar like young lions. Yes, dem shall roar, and seize dem prey and carry it off, and there Go be Nobody to deliver.
Dem go roar against dem in that day like the roaring of the sea. If one looks to the land see am, darkness and distress. The light is darkened in its clouds.
In the year that king Uzziah died, I see the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.
Above him stood the seraphim. Each one had six wings. With two he covered his face. With two he covered his feet. With two he flew.
One call to another, and talk say, “Holy, holy, holy, is Baba God of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!”
The foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of him who call, and the house was filled with smoke.
Then I talk say, “Woe is me! For I be undone, because I be a man of unclean lips, and I live among a people of unclean lips: for my eyes have seen the King, Baba God of Armies!”
Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar.
He touched my mouth with it, and talk say, “See am, this has touched una lips; and una wickedness is taken away, and una sin forgiven.”
I heard the Lord’s voice, saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Then I talk say, “Here I be. Send me!”
He talk say, “Go, and tell this people, ‘You hear indeed, but no understand; and you see indeed, but no perceive.’
Make the heart of this people fat. Make dem ears heavy, and shut dem eyes; lest dem see with dem eyes, and hear with dem ears, and understand with dem heart, and turn again, and be healed.”
Then I talk say, “Lord, how long?” He answer, “Until cities are waste without inhabitant, and houses without man, and the land becomes utterly waste,
And Baba God has removed men far away, and the forsaken places are many within the land.
If E get a tenth left in it, that also will in turn be consumed: as a terebinth, and as an oak, whose stock remains when Dem be felled; so the holy seed is its stock.”

In the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, go up to Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.
David’s house was told, “Syria is allied with Ephraim.” His heart trembled, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the forest tremble with the wind.
Then Baba God talk say to Isaiah, “Go out now to meet Ahaz, you, and Shearjashub una son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway of the fuller’s field.
Tell him, ‘Be careful, and keep calm. No fear, neither let una heart be faint because of these two tails of smoking torches, for the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.
Because Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, have plotted evil against you, saying,
“Let’s go up against Judah, and tear it apart, and let’s divide it among ourselves, and set up a king within it, even the son of Tabeel.”
This is what the Lord Baba God says: “It no go stand, neither shall it happen.”
For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within sixty-five years Ephraim go be broken in pieces, so that it no go be a people;
and the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If You go not believe, surely you no go be established.’”
Baba God spoke again to Ahaz, saying,
“Ask a sign of Baba God una God; ask it either in the depth, or in the height above.”
But Ahaz talk say, “I go not ask, neither will I tempt Baba God.”
He talk say, “Listen now, house of David. Is it not enough for you to try the patience of men, that You go try the patience of my God also?
So the Lord imself will give you a sign. See am, the virgin will conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
He shall eat butter and honey when he knows to refuse the evil, and choose the good.
For before the pikin knows to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land whose two kings you abhor go be forsaken.
Baba God will bring on you, on una people, and on una father’s house, days that have not come, from the day that Ephraim comot from Judah; even the king of Assyria.
It will happen in that day that Baba God will whistle for the fly that is in the uttermost part of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
Dem shall come, and shall all rest in the desolate valleys, in the clefts of the rocks, on all thorn hedges, and on all pastures.
In that day the Lord will shave with a razor that is hired in the parts beyond the River, even with the king of Assyria, the head and the hair of the feet; and it shall also consume the beard.
It shall happen in that day that a man shall keep alive a young cow, and two sheep;
and it shall happen, that because of the abundance of milk which dem shall give he shall eat butter: for everyone will eat butter and honey that is left within the land.
It will happen in that day that every place where there were a thousand vines at a thousand silver shekels, go be for briers and thorns.
People will go there with arrows and with bow, because all the land Go be briers and thorns.
All the hills that were cultivated with the hoe, you no go come there for fear of briers and thorns; but it go be for the sending out of oxen, and for the treading of sheep.”
Baba God talk say to me, “Take a large tablet, and write on it with a man’s pen, ‘For Maher Shalal Hash Baz’;
and I go take for myself faithful witnesses to testify: Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.”
I go to the prophetess, and she conceived, and bore a son. Then Baba God talk say to me, “Call his name ‘Maher Shalal Hash Baz.’
For before the pikin knows how to say, ‘My father,’ and, ‘My mother,’ the riches of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria Go be carried away by the king of Assyria.”
Baba God spoke to me yet again, saying,
“Because this people have refused the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and glad well-well in Rezin and Remaliah’s son;
now so, see am, the Lord brings upon dem the mighty flood waters of the River: the king of Assyria and all his glory. It will come up over all its channels, and go over all its banks.
It will sweep onward into Judah. It will overflow and pass through; it will reach even to the neck; and the stretching out of its wings will fill the width of una land, Immanuel.
Make an uproar, you peoples, and be broken in pieces! Listen, all you from far countries: dress for battle, and be shattered! Dress for battle, and be shattered!
Take counsel together, and it Go be bring to nothing; speak the word, and it No go stand: for God is with us.”
For Baba God spoke thus to me with a strong hand, and instructed me not to walk in the way of this people, saying,
