“No say, ‘A conspiracy!’ concerning all about which this people say, ‘A conspiracy!’ neither fear dem threats, nor be terrorized.
Baba God of Armies is who you must respect as holy. He is the one you must fear. He is the one you must dread.
He Go be a sanctuary, but for both houses of Israel, he Go be a trap and a snare for the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
Many will stumble over it, fall, be broken, be snared, and be captured.”
Wrap up the testimony. Seal the law among my disciples.
I go wait for Baba God, who hides his face from the house of Jacob, and I go look for him.
See am, I and the pikin dem whom Baba God has given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from Baba God of Armies, who dwells in Mount Zion.

When dem tell you, “Consult with people wey have familiar spirits and with the wizards, who chirp and who mutter:” shouldn’t a people consult with dem God? Should dem consult the dead on behalf of the living?
Turn to the law and to the testimony! If dem no speak according to this word, surely E get no morning for dem.
Dem go pass through it, very distressed and hungry; and it will happen that when Dem be hungry, Dem go worry, and curse by dem king and by dem God. Dem go turn dem faces upward,
and look to the earth, and see distress, darkness, and the gloom of anguish. Dem go be driven into thick darkness.

But there go be no more gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time, he bring into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time he has made it glorious, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. People wey lived in the land of the shadow of death, on dem the light has shined.
You have multiplied the nation. You have increased dem gladness. Dem glad well-well before you according to the gladness in harvest, as men glad well-well when dem divide the plunder.
For the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, you have broken as in the day of Midian.
For all the armor of the armed man in the noisy battle, and the garments rolled in blood, Go be for burning, fuel for the fire.
For to us a pikin is born. To us a son is given; and the government Go be on his shoulders. His name Go be call Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

Of the increase of his government and of peace there go be no end, on David’s throne, and on his kingdom, to establish it, and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness from that time on, even forever. The zeal of Baba God of Armies will perform this.
The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it falls on Israel.
All the people will know, including Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria, who say in pride and in arrogance of heart,
“The bricks have fallen, but We go build with cut stone. The sycamore fig trees Don dey cut down, but We go put cedars in dem place.”
So Baba God will set up on high against him the adversaries of Rezin, and will stir up his enemies,
The Syrians in front, and the Philistines behind; and Dem go devour Israel with open mouth. For all this, his anger No be turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
Yet the people have not turned to him who struck dem, neither have dem sought Baba God of Armies.
So Baba God will cut off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed, in one day.
The elder and the honorable man is the head, and the prophet who teaches lies is the tail.
For people wey lead this people lead dem astray; and people Wey led by dem are destroyed.

So the Lord No go glad well-well over dem young men, neither will he have compassion on dem fatherless and widows; for everyone is profane and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks folly. For all this his anger No be turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
For wickedness burns like a fire. It devours the briers and thorns; yes, it kindles in the thickets of the forest, and dem roll upward in a column of smoke.
Through Baba God of Armies’ serious anger, the land is burned up; and the people are the fuel for the fire. Nobody spares his brother.
One will devour on the right hand, and be hungry; and he will eat on the left hand, and Dem go not be satisfied. Everyone will eat the flesh of his own arm:
Manasseh, Ephraim; and Ephraim, Manasseh; and dem together go be against Judah. For all this his anger No be turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
Woe to people wey decree unrighteous decrees, and to the writers who write oppressive decrees;
to deprive the needy from justice, and to rob the poor among my people of dem rights, that widows may be dem plunder, and that dem may make the fatherless dem prey!
What will you do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation which will come from far away? To whom will you flee for help? Where will you leave una wealth?
Dem go only bow down under the prisoners, and will fall under the slain. For all this his anger No be turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
Alas Assyrian, the rod of my anger, the staff in whose hand is my indignation!
I go send him against a profane nation, and against the people who anger me will I give him a command to take the plunder and to take the prey, and to tread dem down like the mire of the streets.
However he no dey mean so, neither does his heart think so; but it is in his heart to destroy, and to cut off not a few nations.
For he says, “No be all of my princes kings?
No be Calno like Carchemish? No be Hamath like Arpad? No be Samaria like Damascus?”
As my hand has find the kingdoms of the idols, whose engraved images exceeded those of Jerusalem and of Samaria;
shall I not, as I have done to Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?

So it will happen that, when the Lord has performed his whole work on Mount Zion and on Jerusalem, I go punish the fruit of the willful proud heart of the king of Assyria, and the insolence of his haughty looks.

For he has talk say, “By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; for I have understanding: and I have removed the boundaries of the peoples, and have robbed dem treasures. Like a valiant man I have bring down dem rulers.

My hand has find the riches of the peoples like a nest, and like one gathers eggs that are abandoned, I have gathered all the earth. There was Nobody who moved dem wing, or that opened dem mouth, or chirped.”

Should an ax brag against him who chops with it? Should a see exalt itself above him who saws with it? As if a rod should lift people wey lift it up, or as if a staff should lift up someone Wey be not wood.
So the Lord, Baba God of Armies, will send among his fat ones leanness; and under his glory a burning Go be kindled like the burning of fire.
The light of Israel Go be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame; and it will burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day.
He will consume the glory of his forest, and of his fruitful field, both soul and body. It Go be as when a standard bearer faints.
The remnant of the trees of his forest go be few, so that a pikin could write dem number.

It will come to pass in that day that the remnant of Israel, and people wey have escaped from the house of Jacob will no more again lean on him who struck dem, but shall lean on Baba God, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.
A remnant will return, even the remnant of Jacob, to the mighty God.
For though una people, Israel, are like the sand of the sea, only a remnant of dem will return. A destruction is determined, overflowing with righteousness.
For the Lord, Baba God of Armies, will make a full end, and that determined, throughout all the earth.
So the Lord, Baba God of Armies, says “My people who live in Zion, No fear of the Assyrian, though he strike you with the rod, and lift up his staff against you, as Egypt did.
For yet a very little while, and the indignation against You go be accomplished, and my anger Go be directed to his destruction.”
Baba God of Armies will stir up a scourge against him, as in the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb. His rod Go be over the sea, and he will lift it up like he did against Egypt.
It will happen in that day, that his burden will depart from off una shoulder, and his yoke from off una neck, and the yoke go be destroyed because of the anointing oil.
He has come to Aiath. He has passed through Migron. At Michmash he stores his baggage.
Dem have gone over the pass. Dem have taken up dem lodging at Geba. Ramah trembles. Gibeah of Saul has fled.
Cry aloud with una voice, daughter of Gallim! Listen, Laishah! You poor Anathoth!
Madmenah is a fugitive. The inhabitants of Gebim flee for safety.
This very day he will halt at Nob. He shakes his hand at the mountain of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
See am, the Lord, Baba God of Armies, will lop the boughs with terror. The tall Go be cut down, and the lofty Go be bring low.
He will cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall by the Mighty One.
A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.
Baba God’s Spirit will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Baba God.
His delight Go be in the fear of Baba God. He No go judge by the sight of his eyes, neither decide by the hearing of his ears;

but with righteousness he will judge the poor, and decide with equity for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked.
Righteousness Go be the belt of his waist, and faithfulness the belt of his waist.
The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat; The calf, the young lion, and the fattened calf together; and a little pikin will lead dem.
The cow and the bear will graze. Dem young ones will lie down together. The lion will eat straw like the ox.
The nursing pikin will play near a cobra’s hole, and the weaned pikin will put his hand on the viper’s den.
Dem go not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain; for the earth Go be full of the knowledge of Baba God, as the waters cover the sea.
It will happen in that day that the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner of the peoples; and his resting place Go be glorious.

It will happen in that day that the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.
He will set up a banner for the nations, and will assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
The envy also of Ephraim will depart, and people wey persecute Judah Go be cut off. Ephraim no go envy Judah, and Judah no go persecute Ephraim.

Dem go fly down on the shoulders of the Philistines on the west. Together Dem go plunder the pikin dem of the east. Dem go extend dem power over Edom and Moab, and the pikin dem of Ammon will obey dem.

Baba God will utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea; and with his scorching wind he will wave his hand over the River, and will split it into seven streams, and cause men to march over in sandals.
There Go be a highway for the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, like there was for Israel in the day that he come up out of the land of Egypt.
In that day You go say, “I go Thank God to you, Baba God; for though you were angry with me, una anger has turned away and you comfort me.
See am, God is my salvation. I go trust, and No go be afraid; for Yah, Baba God, is my strength and song; and he has become my salvation.”
So with gladness You go draw water out of the wells of salvation.
In that day You go say, “Thank God to Baba God! Call on his name. Declare his doings among the peoples. Proclaim that his name is exalted!
Sing to Baba God, for he has done excellent things! Let this be known in all the earth!
Cry aloud and shout, you inhabitant of Zion; for the Holy One of Israel is great among you!”
The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz see:
Set up a banner on the bare mountain! Lift up una voice to dem! Wave una hand, that dem may go into the gates of the nobles.
I have commanded my consecrated ones; yes, I have call my mighty men for my anger, even my proudly exulting ones.

The noise of a plenty people is in the mountains, as of a great people; the noise of an uproar of the kingdoms of the nations gathered together! Baba God of Armies is mustering the army for the battle.
Dem come from a far country, from the uttermost part of heaven, even Baba God, and the weapons of his indignation, to destroy the whole land.
Wail; for the day of Baba God is at hand! It will come as destruction from the Almighty.
So all hands Go be feeble, and everyone’s heart will melt.
Dem go be dismayed. Pangs and sorrows will seize dem. Dem go be in pain like a woman in labor. Dem go look in amazement one at another. Dem faces Go be faces of flame.
See am, the day of Baba God comes, cruel, with serious anger and fierce anger; to make the land a desolation, and to destroy its sinners out of it.
For the stars of the sky and its constellations No go give dem light. The sun Go be darkened in its going out, and the moon No go cause its light to shine.
I go punish the world for dem evil, and the wicked for dem wickedness. I go cause the arrogance of the proud to cease, and will humble the haughtiness of the terrible.
I go make people more rare than fine gold, even a person than the pure gold of Ophir.
So I go make the heavens tremble, and the earth Go be shaken out of its place in Baba God of Armies’ serious anger, and in the day of his fierce anger.
It will happen that like a hunted gazelle, and like sheep that Nobody gathers, Dem go each turn to dem own people, and will each flee to dem own land.
Everyone Wey be find Go be thrust through. Everyone Wey be captured will fall by the sword.
Dem infants also Go be dashed in pieces before dem eyes. Dem houses Go be ransacked, and dem wives raped.
See am, I go stir up the Medes against dem, who No go value silver, and as for gold, Dem go not delight in it.
Dem bows will dash the young men in pieces; and dem go get no pity on the fruit of the womb. Dem eyes No go spare pikin dem.
Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldeans’ pride, Go be like when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.
It will never be inhabited, neither will it be lived in from generation to generation. The Arabian No go pitch a tent there, neither will shepherds make dem flocks lie down there.
But wild animals of the desert will lie there, and dem houses Go be full of jackals. Ostriches will live there, and wild goats will frolic there.
Wolves will cry in dem fortresses, and jackals in the pleasant palaces. Her time is near to come, and her days No go be prolonged.
For Baba God Go get compassion on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set dem in dem own land. The foreigner will join imself with dem, and Dem go unite with the house of Jacob.

The peoples will take dem, and bring dem to dem place. The house of Israel will possess dem in Baba God’s land for workers and for handmaids. Dem go take as captives those whose captives dem were; and dem shall rule over dem oppressors.
It will happen in the day that Baba God will give you rest from una sorrow, from una trouble, and from the hard service in which you were made to serve,
that You go take up this parable against the king of Babylon, and say, “How the oppressor has ceased! The golden city has ceased!”
Baba God has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of the rulers,
who struck the peoples in serious anger with a continual stroke, who ruled the nations in anger, with a persecution that Nobody restrained.
The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet. Dem break out song.
Yes, the cypress trees glad well-well with you, with the cedars of Lebanon, saying, “Since You be humbled, no lumberjack has come up against us.”

Sheol from beneath has moved for you to meet you at una coming. It stirs up the comot spirits for you, even all the rulers of the earth. It has raised up from dem thrones all the kings of the nations.
Dem all will answer and ask you, “Have you also become as weak as We be? Have you become like us?”
Una pomp is bring down to Sheol, with the sound of una stringed instruments. Maggots are spread out under you, and worms cover you.
How you have fallen from heaven, morning star, son of the dawn! How You be cut down to the ground, who laid the nations low!
You talk say in una heart, “I go ascend into heaven! I go exalt my throne above the stars of God! I go sit on the mountain of assembly, in the far north!
I go ascend above the heights of the clouds! I go make myself like the Most High!”
Yet you go be bring down to Sheol, to the depths of the pit.
People wey see You go stare at you. Dem go ponder you, saying, “Is this the man who made the earth to tremble, who shook kingdoms;
who made the world like a wilderness, and overthrew its cities; who didn’t release his prisoners to dem home?”
All the kings of the nations, sleep in glory, everyone in his own house.
But You be throw away from una tomb like an abominable branch, clothed with the slain, Wey be thrust through with the sword, who go down to the stones of the pit; like a dead body trodden under foot.
You go not join dem in burial, because you have destroyed una land. You have killed una people. The offspring of evildoers No go be named forever.
Prepare for slaughter of his pikin dem because of the wickedness of dem fathers, that dem not rise up and possess the earth, and fill the surface of the world with cities.
“I go rise up against dem,” says Baba God of Armies, “and cut off from Babylon name and remnant, and son and son’s son,” says Baba God.
“I go also make it a possession for the porcupine, and pools of water. I go sweep it with the broom of destruction,” says Baba God of Armies.
Baba God of Armies has sworn, saying, “Surely, as I have thought, so shall it happen; and as I have purposed, so shall it stand:
that I go break the Assyrian in my land, and tread him under foot on my mountains. Then his yoke will leave dem, and his burden leave dem shoulders.
This is the plan that is determined for the whole earth. This is the hand that is stretched out over all the nations.
For Baba God of Armies has planned, and who can stop it? His hand is stretched out, and who can turn it back?”
This burden was in the year that king Ahaz died.
No glad well-well, O Philistia, all of you, because the rod that struck you is broken; for out of the serpent’s root an adder will emerge, and his fruit Go be a fiery flying serpent.
The firstborn of the poor will eat, and the needy will lie down in safety; and I go kill una root with famine, and una remnant Go be killed.
Howl, gate! Cry, city! You be melted away, Philistia, all of you; for smoke comes out of the north, and E get no straggler in his ranks.
What will dem answer the messengers of the nation? That Baba God has founded Zion, and in her the afflicted of his people will take refuge.
The burden of Moab: for in a night, Ar of Moab is laid waste, and bring to nothing; for in a night Kir of Moab is laid waste, and bring to nothing.
Dem have gone up to Bayith, and to Dibon, to the high places, to weep. Moab wails over Nebo and over Medeba. Baldness is on all of dem heads. Every beard is cut off.
In dem streets, dem clothe themselves in sackcloth. In dem streets and on dem housetops, everyone wails, weeping abundantly.
Heshbon cries out with Elealeh. Dem voice is heard even to Jahaz. So the armed men of Moab cry aloud. Dem souls tremble within dem.
My heart cries out for Moab! Her nobles flee to Zoar, to Eglath Shelishiyah; for dem go up by the ascent of Luhith with weeping; for on the way to Horonaim, dem raise up a cry of destruction.
For the waters of Nimrim Go be desolate; for the grass has withered away, the tender grass fails, E get no green thing.
So Dem go carry away the abundance dem have gotten, and that which dem have stored up, over the brook of the willows.
For the cry has gone around the borders of Moab; its wailing to Eglaim, and its wailing to Beer Elim.
For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; for I go bring yet more on Dimon, a lion on those of Moab who escape, and on the remnant of the land.
Send the lambs for the ruler of the land from Selah to the wilderness, to the mountain of the daughter of Zion.
For it Go be that as wandering birds, as a scattered nest, so will the daughters of Moab be at the fords of the Arnon.
Give counsel! Execute justice! Make una shade like the night in the middle of the noonday! Hide the outcasts! No betray the fugitive!

Let my outcasts live with you! As for Moab, be a hiding place for him from the face of the destroyer. For the extortionist is bring to nothing. Destruction ceases. The oppressors are consumed out of the land.
A throne Go be established in loving kindness. One will sit on it in truth, in the tent of David, judging, seeking justice, and swift to do righteousness.
We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is very proud; even of his arrogance, his pride, and his serious anger. His boastings are nothing.
So Moab will wail for Moab. Everyone will wail. You go mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth, utterly stricken.

For the fields of Heshbon languish with the vine of Sibmah. The lords of the nations have broken down its choice branches, which reached even to Jazer, which wandered into the wilderness. Its shoots were spread abroad. Dem passed over the sea.
So I go weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah. I go water you with my tears, Heshbon, and Elealeh: for on una summer fruits and on una harvest the battle shout has fallen.

Gladness is taken away, and gladness out of the fruitful field; and in the vineyards there Go be no singing, neither joyful noise. Nobody will tread out wine in the presses. I have made the shouting stop.
So my heart sounds like a harp for Moab, and my inward parts for Kir Heres.
It will happen that when Moab presents imself, when he wearies imself on the high place, and comes to his sanctuary to pray, that he No go prevail.
This is the word that Baba God spoke concerning Moab in time past.

But now Baba God has spoken, saying, “Within three years, as a worker bound by contract would count dem, the glory of Moab go be bring into contempt, with all his great plenty people; and the remnant Go be very small and feeble.”
The burden of Damascus: “See am, Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it Go be a ruinous heap.
The cities of Aroer are forsaken. Dem go be for flocks, which shall lie down, and Nobody shall make dem afraid.
The fortress shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Syria. Dem go be as the glory of the pikin dem of Israel,” says Baba God of Armies.
“It will happen in that day that the glory of Jacob Go be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh will become lean.
It Go be like when the harvester gathers the wheat, and his arm reaps the grain. Yes, it Go be like when one gleans grain in the valley of Rephaim.

Yet gleanings Go be left there, like the shaking of an olive tree, two or three olives in the top of the uppermost bough, four or five in the outermost branches of a fruitful tree,” says Baba God, the God of Israel.
In that day, people will look to dem Maker, and dem eyes Go get respect for the Holy One of Israel.
Dem go not look to the altars, the work of dem hands; neither shall dem respect that which dem fingers have made, either the Asherah poles, or the incense altars.
In that day, dem strong cities Go be like the forsaken places in the woods and on the mountain top, which were forsaken from before the pikin dem of Israel; and it Go be a desolation.
For you have forgotten the God of una salvation, and have not remember the rock of una strength. So you plant pleasant plants, and set out foreign seedlings.
In the day of una planting, you hedge it in. In the morning, you make una seed blossom, but the harvest flees away in the day of grief and of desperate sorrow.
Ah, the uproar of many peoples, who roar like the roaring of the seas; and the rushing of nations, that rush like the rushing of mighty waters!

The nations will rush like the rushing of many waters: but he will rebuke dem, and Dem go flee far off, and Go be chased like the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like the whirling dust before the storm.
At evening, see am, terror! Before the morning, Dem be no more. This is the portion of people wey plunder us, and the lot of people wey rob us.
Ah, the land of the rustling of wings, which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia;

that sends ambassadors by the sea, even in vessels of papyrus on the waters, saying, “Go, you swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth, to a people awesome from dem beginning onward, a nation that measures out and treads down, whose land the rivers divide!”
All you inhabitants of the world, and you dwellers on the earth, when a banner is lifted up on the mountains, look! When the trumpet is blown, listen!
For Baba God talk say to me, “I go be still, and I go see in my dwelling place, like clear heat in sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.”
For before the harvest, when the blossom is over, and the flower becomes a ripening grape, he will cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks, and he will cut down and take away the spreading branches.
Dem go be left together for the ravenous birds of the mountains, and for the animals of the earth. The ravenous birds will summer on dem, and all the animals of the earth will winter on dem.

In that time, a present Go be bring to Baba God of Armies from a people tall and smooth, even from a people awesome from dem beginning onward, a nation that measures out and treads down, whose land the rivers divide, to the place of the name of Baba God of Armies, Mount Zion.
The burden of Egypt: “See am, Baba God rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt. The idols of Egypt will tremble at his presence; and the heart of Egypt will melt within it.
I go stir up the Egyptians against the Egyptians, and Dem go fight everyone against his brother, and everyone against his neighbor; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.
The spirit of Egypt will fail within it. I go destroy its counsel. Dem go seek the idols, the charmers, people wey have familiar spirits, and the wizards.
I go give over the Egyptians into the hand of a cruel lord. A fierce king will rule over dem,” says the Lord, Baba God of Armies.
The waters will fail from the sea, and the river Go be wasted and become dry.
The rivers will become foul. The streams of Egypt Go be diminished and dried up. The reeds and flags will wither away.
The meadows by the Nile, by the brink of the Nile, and all the sown fields of the Nile, will become dry, be driven away, and be no more.
The fishermen will lament, and all people wey fish in the Nile will mourn, and people wey spread nets on the waters will languish.
Moreover people wey work in combed flax, and people wey weave white cloth, Go be confounded.
The pillars Go be broken in pieces. All people wey work for hire Go be grieved in soul.
The princes of Zoan are utterly foolish. The counsel of the wisest counselors of Pharaoh has become stupid. How do you say to Pharaoh, “I be the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings?”
Where then are una wise men? Make dem tell you now; and Make dem know what Baba God of Armies has purposed concerning Egypt.
The princes of Zoan have become fools. The princes of Memphis are deceived. Dem have caused Egypt to go astray, Wey be the cornerstone of her tribes.
Baba God has mixed a spirit of perverseness in the middle of her; and dem have caused Egypt to go astray in all of its works, like a drunken man staggers in his vomit.
Neither shall there be any work for Egypt, which head or tail, palm branch or rush, may do.
In that day the Egyptians Go be like women. Dem go tremble and fear because of the shaking of Baba God of Armies’s hand, which he shakes over dem.
The land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt. Everyone to whom mention is made of it Go be afraid, because of the plans of Baba God of Armies, which he determines against it.
In that day, there Go be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan, and swear to Baba God of Armies. One Go be call “The city of destruction.”
In that day, there Go be an altar to Baba God in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to Baba God at its border.

It Go be for a sign and for a witness to Baba God of Armies in the land of Egypt; for Dem go cry to Baba God because of oppressors, and he will send dem a savior and a defender, and he will deliver dem.
Baba God Go be known to Egypt, and the Egyptians will know Baba God in that day. Yes, Dem go worship with sacrifice and offering, and will vow a vow to Baba God, and will perform it.
Baba God will strike Egypt, striking and healing. Dem go return to Baba God, and he Go be entreated by dem, and will heal dem.
In that day there Go be a highway out of Egypt to Assyria, and the Assyrian shall come into Egypt, and the Egyptian into Assyria; and the Egyptians will worship with the Assyrians.
In that day, Israel Go be the third with Egypt and with Assyria, a blessing within the earth;
because Baba God of Armies has blessed dem, saying, “Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance.”
In the year that Tartan come to Ashdod, when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him, and he fought against Ashdod and take it;
at that time Baba God spoke by Isaiah the son of Amoz, saying, “Go, and loosen the sackcloth from off una waist, and take una shoes from off una feet.” He did so, walking naked and barefoot.
Baba God talk say, “As my worker Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot three years for a sign and a wonder concerning Egypt and concerning Ethiopia,
so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Ethiopia, young and old, naked and barefoot, and with buttocks uncovered, to the shame of Egypt.
Dem go be dismayed and confounded, because of Ethiopia dem expectation, and of Egypt dem glory.
The inhabitants of this coast land will say in that day, ‘See am, this is our expectation, where we fled for help to be delivered from the king of Assyria. And we, how will we escape?’”
The burden of the wilderness of the sea. As whirlwinds in the South sweep through, it comes from the wilderness, from an awesome land.
A grievous vision is declared to me. The treacherous man deals treacherously, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam; attack! I have stopped all of Media’s sighing.
So my thighs are filled with anguish. Pains have taken hold on me, like the pains of a woman in labor. I be in so much pain that I no fit hear. I so am dismayed that I no fit see.
My heart flutters. Horror has frightened me. The twilight that I desired Don dey turned into trembling for me.
Dem prepare the table. Dem set the watch. Dem eat. Dem drink. Rise up, you princes, oil the shield!
For the Lord talk say to me, “Go, set a watchman. Make e declare what he sees.
When he sees a troop, horsemen in pairs, a troop of donkeys, a troop of camels, he shall listen diligently with great attentiveness.”
He cried like a lion: “Lord, I stand continually on the watchtower in the daytime, and every night I stay at my post.
See am, here comes a troop of men, horsemen in pairs.” He answer, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon; and all the engraved images of her gods are broken to the ground.
You be my threshing, and the grain of my floor!” That which I have heard from Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, I have declared to you.
The burden of Dumah. One calls to me out of Seir, “Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?”
The watchman talk say, “The morning comes, and also the night. If You go inquire, inquire. Come back again.”
The burden on Arabia. In the forest in Arabia You go lodge, you caravans of Dedanites.
Dem bring water to him who was thirsty. The inhabitants of the land of Tema met the fugitives with dem bread.
For dem fled away from the swords, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the heat of battle.
For the Lord talk say to me, “Within a year, as a worker bound by contract would count it, all the glory of Kedar will fail,
and the residue of the number of the archers, the mighty men of the pikin dem of Kedar, Go be few; for Baba God, the God of Israel, has spoken it.”
The burden of the valley of vision. What ails you now, that you have all gone up to the housetops?
You that are full of shouting, a tumultuous city, a joyous town; una slain No be slain with the sword, neither are dem dead in battle.
All una rulers fled away together. Dem were bound by the archers. All who were find by you were bound together. Dem fled far away.
So I talk say, “Look away from me. I go weep bitterly. No labor to comfort me for the destruction of the daughter of my people.
For it is a day of confusion, and of treading down, and of perplexity, from the Lord, Baba God of Armies, in the valley of vision; a breaking down of the walls, and a crying to the mountains.”
Elam carried his quiver, with chariots of men and horsemen; and Kir uncovered the shield.
Una choicest valleys were full of chariots, and the horsemen set themselves in array at the gate.
He take away the covering of Judah; and you looked in that day to the armor in the house of the forest.
You see the breaches of David’s city, that dem were many; and you gathered together the waters of the lower pool.
You counted the houses of Jerusalem, and you broke down the houses to fortify the wall.
You also made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool. But you didn’t look to him who had done this, neither did you have respect for him who purposed it long ago.
In that day, the Lord, Baba God of Armies, call to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to dressing in sackcloth:
and see am, gladness and gladness, killing cattle and killing sheep, eating meat and drinking wine: “Make we eat and drink, for tomorrow We go die.”
Baba God of Armies revealed imself in my ears, “Surely this wickedness No go be forgiven you until you die,” says the Lord, Baba God of Armies.
Thus says the Lord, Baba God of Armies, “Go, get yourself to this treasurer, even to Shebna, Wey be over the house, and say,
‘Wetin be you doing here? Who has you here, that you have dug out a tomb here?’ Cutting imself out a tomb on high, chiseling a habitation for imself in the rock!”
See am, Baba God will overcome you and hurl you away violently. Yes, he will grasp you firmly.
He will surely wind you around and around, and throw you like a ball into a large country. There You go die, and there the chariots of una glory Go be, you shame of una lord’s house.
I go thrust you from una office. You go be pulled down from una station.
It will happen in that day that I go call my worker Eliakim the son of Hilkiah,
and I go clothe him with una robe, and strengthen him with una belt. I go commit una government into his hand; and he Go be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah.
I go lay the key of David’s house on his shoulder. He will open, and Nobody will shut. He will shut, and Nobody will open.
I go fasten him like a nail in a sure place. He Go be for a throne of glory to his father’s house.
Dem go hang on him all the glory of his father’s house, the offspring and the issue, every small vessel, from the cups even to all the pitchers.
“In that day,” says Baba God of Armies, “the nail that was fastened in a sure place will give way. It Go be cut down, and fall. The burden that was on it Go be cut off, for Baba God has spoken it.”
The burden of Tyre. Howl, you ships of Tarshish! For it is laid waste, so that E get no house, no entering in. From the land of Kittim it is revealed to dem.
Be still, you inhabitants of the coast, you whom the merchants of Sidon, that pass over the sea, have replenished.
On great waters, the seed of the Shihor, the harvest of the Nile, was her revenue. She was the market of nations.
Be ashamed, Sidon; for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the sea, saying, “I have not travailed, nor given birth, neither have I nourished young men, nor bring up virgins.”
When the report comes to Egypt, Dem go be in anguish at the report of Tyre.
Pass over to Tarshish! Wail, you inhabitants of the coast!
Is this una joyous city, whose antiquity is of ancient days, whose feet carried her far away to travel?
Who has planned this against Tyre, the giver of crowns, whose merchants are princes, whose traffickers are the honorable of the earth?
Baba God of Armies has planned it, to stain the pride of all glory, to bring into contempt all the honorable of the earth.
Pass through una land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish. E get no restraint any more.
He has stretched out his hand over the sea. He has shaken the kingdoms. Baba God has ordered the destruction of Canaan’s strongholds.
He talk say, “You shall glad well-well no more, you oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon. Arise, pass over to Kittim. Even there You go have no rest.”
See am, the land of the Chaldeans. This people No be. The Assyrians founded it for people wey live in the wilderness. Dem set up dem towers. Dem overthrew its palaces. Dem made it a ruin.
Howl, you ships of Tarshish, for una stronghold is laid waste!
It will come to pass in that day that Tyre Go be forgotten seventy years, according to the days of one king. After the end of seventy years it Go be to Tyre like in the song of the prostitute.
Take a harp; go about the city, you prostitute that Don dey forgotten. Make sweet melody. Sing many songs, that you may be remember.

It will happen after the end of seventy years that Baba God will visit Tyre, and she shall return to her wages, and will play the prostitute with all the kingdoms of the world on the surface of the earth.

Her merchandise and her wages Go be holiness to Baba God. It No go be treasured nor laid up; for her merchandise Go be for people wey live before Baba God, to eat sufficiently, and for durable clothing.
See am, Baba God makes the earth empty, makes it waste, turns it upside down, and scatters its inhabitants.

It Go be as with the people, so with the priest; as with the worker, so with his master; as with the maid, so with her mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the creditor, so with the debtor; as with the taker of interest, so with the giver of interest.
The earth Go be utterly emptied and utterly laid waste; for Baba God has spoken this word.
The earth mourns and fades away. The world languishes and fades away. The lofty people of the earth languish.
The earth also is polluted under its inhabitants, because dem have transgressed the laws, violated the statutes, and broken the everlasting covenant.
So the curse has devoured the earth, and people wey live inside am are find guilty. So the inhabitants of the earth are burned, and few men left.
The new wine mourns. The vine languishes. All the merry-hearted sigh.
The mirth of tambourines ceases. The sound of people wey glad well-well ends. The gladness of the harp ceases.
Dem go not drink wine with a song. Strong drink Go be bitter to people wey drink it.
The confused city is broken down. Every house is shut up, that no man may come in.
E get a crying in the streets because of the wine. All gladness is darkened. The mirth of the land is gone.
The city is left in desolation, and the gate is struck with destruction.
For it Go be so within the earth among the peoples, as the shaking of an olive tree, as the gleanings when the vintage is done.
These shall lift up dem voice. Dem go shout for the majesty of Baba God. Dem cry aloud from the sea.
So glorify Baba God in the east, even the name of Baba God, the God of Israel, in the islands of the sea!

From the uttermost part of the earth have we heard songs. Glory to the righteous! But I talk say, “I pine away! I pine away! woe is me!” The treacherous have dealt treacherously. Yes, the treacherous have dealt very treacherously.
Fear, the pit, and the snare, are on you who inhabitant the earth.

It will happen that person wey flees from the noise of the fear will fall into the pit; and person wey comes up out of the middle of the pit Go be taken in the snare; for the windows on high are opened, and the foundations of the earth tremble.
The earth is utterly broken. The earth is torn apart. The earth is shaken violently.
The earth will stagger like a drunken man, and will sway back and forth like a hammock. Its disobedience Go be heavy on it, and it will fall and not rise again.
It shall happen in that day that Baba God will punish the army of the high ones on high, and the kings of the earth on the earth.
Dem go be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and go be shut up in the prison; and after many days shall dem be visited.
Then the moon go be confounded, and the sun ashamed; for Baba God of Armies will reign on Mount Zion, and in Jerusalem; and before his elders Go be glory.
Baba God, You be my God. I go exalt you! I go praise una name, for you have done wonderful things, things planned long ago, in complete faithfulness and truth.
For you have made a city into a heap, a fortified city into a ruin, a palace of strangers to be no city. It will never be built.
So a strong people will glorify you. A city of awesome nations will fear you.

For you Don dey a stronghold to the poor, a stronghold to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shade from the heat, when the blast of the dreaded ones is like a storm against the wall.
As the heat in a dry place will you bring down the noise of strangers; as the heat by the shade of a cloud, the song of the dreaded ones Go be bring low.
In this mountain, Baba God of Armies will make all peoples a feast of choice meat, a feast of choice wines, of choice meat full of marrow, of well refined choice wines.
He will destroy in this mountain the surface of the covering that covers all peoples, and the veil that is spread over people for everywhere.
He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord Baba God will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for Baba God has spoken it.
It go be talk say in that day, “See am, this is our God! We have waited for him, and he will save us! This is Baba God! We have waited for him. We go be glad and glad well-well in his salvation!”
For in this mountain Baba God’s hand will rest. Moab Go be trodden down in his place, even like straw is trodden down in the water of the dunghill.
He will spread out his hands in the middle of it, like one who swims spreads out hands to swim, but his pride Go be humbled together with the craft of his hands.
He has bring the high fortress of una walls down, laid low, and bring to the ground, even to the dust.
In that day, this song Go be sung in the land of Judah: “We have a strong city. God appoints salvation for walls and bulwarks.
Open the gates, that the righteous nation may enter: the one which keeps faith.
You go keep Anybody wey’s mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you.
Trust in Baba God forever; for in Yah, Baba God, is an everlasting Rock.
For he has bring down people wey live on high, the lofty city. He lays it low. He lays it low even to the ground. He brings it even to the dust.
The foot shall tread it down; Even the feet of the poor, and the steps of the needy.”
The way of the just is uprightness. You Wey be upright make the path of the righteous level.
Yes, in the way of una judgments, Baba God, have we waited for you. Una name and una renown are the desire of our soul.
With my soul I have desired you in the night. Yes, with my spirit within me will I seek you earnestly; for when una judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
Let favor be shown to the wicked, yet he No go learn righteousness. In the land of uprightness he will deal wrongfully, and No go see Baba God’s majesty.
Baba God, una hand is lifted up, yet dem no see; but Dem go see una zeal for the people, and be disappointed. Yes, fire will consume una adversaries.
Baba God, You go ordain peace for us, for you have also done all our work for us.
Baba God our God, other lords besides you have had dominion over us, but by you only will we make mention of una name.
The dead no go live. The comot spirits no go rise. So you have visited and destroyed dem, and caused all memory of dem to perish.
You have increased the nation, O Baba God. You have increased the nation! You be glorified! You have enlarged all the borders of the land.
Baba God, in trouble dem have visited you. Dem poured out a prayer when una chastening was on dem.
Like as a woman with pikin, who draws near the time of her delivery, is in pain and cries out in her pangs; so we Don dey before you, Baba God.
We Don dey with pikin. We Don dey in pain. We give birth, it seems, only to wind. We have not worked any deliverance in the earth; neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen.
Una dead shall live. My dead bodies shall arise. Awake and sing, you who live in the dust; for una dew is like the dew of herbs, and the earth will throw out the comot spirits.
Come, my people, enter into una rooms, and shut una doors behind you. Hide yourself for a little moment, until the indignation is past.
For, see am, Baba God comes out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for dem wickedness. The earth also will disclose her blood, and will no longer cover her slain.
In that day, Baba God with his hard and great and strong sword will punish leviathan, the fleeing serpent, and leviathan the twisted serpent; and he will kill the dragon that is in the sea.
In that day, sing to her, “A pleasant vineyard!
I, Baba God, am its keeper. I go water it every moment. Lest anyone damage it, I go keep it night and day.
Serious anger No be in me, but if I should find briers and thorns, I would do battle! I would march on dem and I would burn dem together.
Or else Make e take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me. Make e make peace with me.”
In days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will blossom and bud. Dem go fill the surface of the world with fruit.
Has he struck dem as he struck people wey struck dem? Or are dem killed like people wey killed dem were killed?
In measure, when you send dem away, you contend with dem. He has removed dem with his rough blast in the day of the east wind.

So by this the wickedness of Jacob Go be forgiven, and this is all the fruit of taking away his sin: that he makes all the stones of the altar as chalk stones that are beaten in pieces, so that the Asherah poles and the incense altars shall rise no more.
For the fortified city is solitary, a habitation deserted and forsaken, like the wilderness. The calf will feed there, and there he will lie down, and consume its branches.

When its boughs are withered, Dem go be broken off. The women will come and set dem on fire, for Dem be a people of no understanding. So person wey made dem No go have compassion on dem, and person wey formed dem will show dem no favor.
It will happen in that day, that Baba God will thresh from the flowing stream of the Euphrates to the brook of Egypt; and You go be gathered one by one, pikin dem of Israel.

It will happen in that day that a great trumpet Go be blown; and people wey were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and people wey were outcasts in the land of Egypt, shall come; and Dem go worship Baba God in the holy mountain at Jerusalem.
Woe to the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim, and to the fading flower of his glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fertile valley of people Wey overcome with wine!
See am, the Lord has a mighty and strong one. Like a storm of hail, a destroying storm, and like a storm of mighty waters overflowing, he will throw dem down to the earth with his hand.
The crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim Go be trodden under foot.
The fading flower of his glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fertile valley, go be like the first-ripe fig before the summer; which someone picks and eats as soon as he sees it.
In that day, Baba God of Armies will become a crown of glory, and a diadem of beauty, to the residue of his people;
and a spirit of justice to him who sits in judgment, and strength to people wey turn back the battle at the gate.

Dem also reel with wine, and stagger with strong drink. The priest and the prophet reel with strong drink. Dem be swallowed up by wine. Dem stagger with strong drink. Dem err in vision. Dem stumble in judgment.
For all tables are completely full of filthy vomit and filthiness.
Whom will he teach knowledge? To whom will he explain the message? People Wey weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts?
For it is precept on precept, precept on precept; line on line, line on line; here a little, there a little.
But he will speak to this nation with stammering lips and in another language;
to whom he talk say, “This is the resting place. Give rest to weary”; and “This is the refreshing”; yet dem would not hear.
So Baba God’s word Go be to dem precept on precept, precept on precept; line on line, line on line; here a little, there a little; that dem may go, fall backward, be broken, be snared, and be taken.
So hear Baba God’s word, you scoffers, that rule this people in Jerusalem:

“Because you have talk say, ‘We have made a covenant with death, and with Sheol are we in agreement. When the overflowing scourge passes through, it no go come to us; for we have made lies our refuge, and we have hidden ourselves under falsehood.’”
So thus says the Lord Baba God, “See am, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a sure foundation. Person wey believe no go act hastily.
I go make justice the measuring line, and righteousness the plumb line. The hail will sweep away the refuge of lies, and the waters will overflow the hiding place.
Una covenant with death go be annulled, and una agreement with Sheol no go stand. When the overflowing scourge passes through, then You go be trampled down by it.
As often as it passes through, it will seize you; for morning by morning it will pass through, by day and by night; and it Go be nothing but terror to understand the message.”
For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket is too narrow to wrap oneself in.
For Baba God will rise up as on Mount Perazim. He Go be angry as in the valley of Gibeon; that he may do his work, his unusual work, and bring to pass his act, his extraordinary act.
Now so no be scoffers, lest una bonds be made strong; for I have heard a decree of destruction from the Lord, Baba God of Armies, on the whole earth.
Give ear, and hear my voice! Listen, and hear my speech!
Does person wey plows to sow plow continually? Does he keep turning the soil and breaking the clods?
When he has leveled its surface, no dey he plant the dill, and scatter the cumin seed, and put in the wheat in rows, the barley in the appointed place, and the spelt in its place?
For his God instructs him in right judgment, and teaches him.
For the dill No be threshed with a sharp instrument, neither is a cart wheel turned over the cumin; but the dill is beaten out with a stick, and the cumin with a rod.
Bread flour must be ground; so he No go always be threshing it. Although he drives the wheel of his threshing cart over it, his horses no grind it.
This also comes out from Baba God of Armies, Wey be wonderful in counsel, and excellent in wisdom.
Woe to Ariel! Ariel, the city where David encamped! Add year to year; let the feasts come around;
then I go distress Ariel, and there Go be mourning and lamentation. She go be to me as an altar hearth.
I go encamp against you all around you, and will lay siege against you with posted troops. I go raise siege works against you.

You go be bring down, and will speak out of the ground. Una speech will mumble out of the dust. Una voice Go be as of one who has a familiar spirit, out of the ground, and una speech will whisper out of the dust.
But the plenty people of una foes Go be like fine dust, and the plenty people of the ruthless ones like chaff that blows away. Yes, it Go be in an instant, suddenly.
She Go be visited by Baba God of Armies with thunder, with earthquake, with great noise, with whirlwind and storm, and with the flame of a devouring fire.
The plenty people of all the nations that fight against Ariel, even all who fight against her and her stronghold, and who distress her, Go be like a dream, a vision of the night.

It Go be like when a hungry man dreams, and see am, he eats; but he awakes, and his hunger no be satisfied; or like when a thirsty man dreams, and see am, he drinks; but he awakes, and see am, he is faint, and he is still thirsty. The plenty people of all the nations that fight against Mount Zion Go be like that.
Pause and wonder! Blind unaself and be blind! Dem be drunken, but not with wine; dem stagger, but not with strong drink.
For Baba God has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep, and has closed una eyes, the prophets; and he has covered una heads, the seers.
All vision has become to you like the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one Wey be educated, saying, “Read this, please”; and he says, “I no fit, for it is sealed:”
and the book is delivered to one Wey be not educated, saying, “Read this, please”; and he says, “I no fit read.”

The Lord talk say, “Because this people draws near with dem mouth and with dem lips to honor me, but dem have removed dem heart far from me, and dem fear of me is a commandment of men which Don dey taught;

so, see am, I go proceed to do a marvelous work among this people, even a marvelous work and a wonder; and the wisdom of dem wise men will perish, and the understanding of dem prudent men Go be hidden.”
Woe to people wey deeply hide dem counsel from Baba God, and whose deeds are in the dark, and who say, “Wey see us?” and “Wey know us?”

You turn things upside down! Should the potter be thought to be like clay; that the thing made should say about him who made it, “He didn’t make me”; or the thing formed say of him who formed it, “He has no understanding?”
No be it yet a very little while, and Lebanon Go be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field Go be regarded as a forest?
In that day, the deaf will hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind will see out of obscurity and out of darkness.
The humble also will increase dem gladness in Baba God, and the poor among men will glad well-well in the Holy One of Israel.
For the ruthless is bring to nothing, and the scoffer ceases, and all people Wey alert to do evil are cut off —
who cause a person to be indicted by a word, and lay a snare for the arbiter in the gate, and who deprive the innocent of justice with false testimony.
So Baba God, who redeemed Abraham, says concerning the house of Jacob: “Jacob shall no longer be ashamed, neither shall his face grow pale.
But when he sees his pikin dem, the work of my hands, in the middle of him, Dem go sanctify my name. Yes, Dem go sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and will stand in awe of the God of Israel.
Dem also who err in spirit will come to understanding, and people wey grumble will receive instruction.”
“Woe to the rebellious pikin dem”, says Baba God, “who take counsel, but not from me; and who make an alliance, but not with my Spirit, that dem may add sin to sin,
who set out to go down into Egypt, and have not ask my advice; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to take refuge in the shadow of Egypt!
So the strength of Pharaoh Go be una shame, and the refuge in the shadow of Egypt una confusion.
For dem princes are at Zoan, and dem ambassadors have come to Hanes.
Dem shall all be ashamed because of a people that no fit profit dem, that No be a help nor profit, but a shame, and also a reproach.”

The burden of the animals of the South. Through the land of trouble and anguish, of the lioness and the lion, the viper and fiery flying serpent, dem carry dem riches on the shoulders of young donkeys, and dem treasures on the humps of camels, to an unprofitable people.
For Egypt helps in vain, and to no purpose; so I have call her Rahab who sits still.
Now go, write it before dem on a tablet, and inscribe it in a book, that it may be for the time to come forever and ever.
For it is a rebellious people, lying pikin dem, pikin dem who No go hear Baba God’s law;
who tell the seers, “No see!” and to the prophets, “No prophesy to us right things. Tell us pleasant things. Prophesy deceits.
Get out of the way. Turn aside from the path. Cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us.”
So thus says the Holy One of Israel, “Because you despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and rely on it;
so this wickedness go be to you like a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking comes suddenly in an instant.

He will break it as a potter’s vessel is broken, breaking it in pieces without sparing, so that there no go be find among the broken piece a piece good enough to take fire from the hearth, or to dip up water out of the cistern.”
For thus talk say the Lord Baba God, the Holy One of Israel, “You go be saved in returning and rest. Una strength Go be in quietness and in confidence.” You refused,
but you talk say, “No, for We go flee on horses”; so You go flee; and, “We go ride on the swift”; so people wey pursue You go be swift.
One thousand will flee at the threat of one. At the threat of five, You go flee until You be left like a beacon on the top of a mountain, and like a banner on a hill.
So Baba God will wait, that he may be gracious to you; and so he Go be exalted, that he may have mercy on you, for Baba God is a God of justice. Blessed are all people wey wait for him.
For the people will live in Zion at Jerusalem. You go weep no more. He will surely be gracious to you at the voice of una cry. When he hears you, he will answer you.
Though the Lord may give you the bread of adversity and the water of suffering, yet una teachers no go be hidden any more, but una eyes will see una teachers;
and when you turn to the right hand, and when you turn to the left, una ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, “This is the way. Walk in it.”
You shall defile the overlaying of una engraved images of silver, and the plating of una molten images of gold. You shall throw dem away as an unclean thing. You shall tell it, “Go away!”
He will give the rain for una seed, with which You go sow the ground; and bread of the increase of the ground Go be rich and plentiful. In that day, una livestock will feed in large pastures.
The oxen likewise and the young donkeys that till the ground will eat savory feed, which Don dey winnowed with the shovel and with the fork.
There go be brooks and streams of water on every lofty mountain and on every high hill in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.

Moreover the light of the moon Go be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun Go be seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, in the day that Baba God binds up the fracture of his people, and heals the wound dem were struck with.
See am, Baba God’s name comes from far away, burning with his anger, and in thick rising smoke. His lips are full of indignation, and his tongue is as a devouring fire.
His breath is as an overflowing stream that reaches even to the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of destruction; and a bridle that leads to ruin Go be in the jaws of the peoples.
You go have a song, as in the night when a holy feast is kept; and gladness of heart, as when one goes with a flute to come to Baba God’s mountain, to Israel’s Rock.
Baba God will cause his glorious voice to be heard, and will show the descent of his arm, with the indignation of his anger, and the flame of a devouring fire, with a blast, storm, and hailstones.
For through Baba God’s voice the Assyrian Go be dismayed. He will strike him with his rod.
Every stroke of the rod of punishment, which Baba God will lay on him, Go be with the sound of tambourines and harps. He will fight with dem in battles, brandishing weapons.
For his burning place has long been ready. Yes, for the king it is prepared. He has made its pyre deep and large with fire and much wood. Baba God’s breath, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.

Woe to people wey go down to Egypt for help, and rely on horses, and trust in chariots because Dem be many, and in horsemen because Dem be very strong, but dem no look to the Holy One of Israel, and dem no seek Baba God!
Yet he also is wise, and will bring disaster, and No go call back his words, but will arise against the house of the evildoers, and against the help of people wey work wickedness.

Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and dem horses flesh, and not spirit. When Baba God stretches out his hand, both person wey helps shall stumble, and person Wey helped shall fall, and dem all go be consumed together.

For Baba God says to me, “As the lion and the young lion growling over his prey, if a plenty people of shepherds is call together against him, No go be dismayed at dem voice, nor abase imself for dem noise, so Baba God of Armies will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its heights.
As birds hovering, so Baba God of Armies will protect Jerusalem. He will protect and deliver it. He will pass over and preserve it.”
Return to him from whom you have deeply revolted, pikin dem of Israel.
For in that day everyone shall throw away his idols of silver and his idols of gold — sin which una own hands have made for you.
“The Assyrian will fall by the sword, not of man; and the sword, not of mankind, shall devour him. He will flee from the sword, and his young men will become subject to forced labor.
His rock will pass away by reason of terror, and his princes Go be afraid of the banner,” says Baba God, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem.
See am, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in justice.
A man go be as a hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the storm, as streams of water in a dry place, as the shade of a large rock in a weary land.
The eyes of people wey see No go be dim, and the ears of people wey hear will listen.
The heart of the rash will understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers Go be ready to speak plainly.
The fool will no longer be call noble, nor the scoundrel be highly respected.

For the fool will speak folly, and his heart will work wickedness, to practice profanity, and to utter error against Baba God, To make empty the soul of the hungry, and to cause the drink of the thirsty to fail.
The ways of the scoundrel are evil. He devises wicked devices to destroy the humble with lying words, even when the needy speaks right.
But the noble devises noble things; and he will continue in noble things.
Rise up, you women Wey be at ease! Hear my voice! You careless daughters, give ear to my speech!
For days beyond a year You go be troubled, you careless women; for the vintage shall fail. The harvest no go come.
Tremble, you women Wey be at ease! Be troubled, you careless ones! Strip unaself, make unaself naked, and put sackcloth on una waist.
Beat una breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine.
Thorns and briers will come up on my people’s land; yes, on all the houses of gladness in the joyous city.
For the palace Go be forsaken. The populous city Go be deserted. The hill and the watchtower Go be for dens forever, a delight for wild donkeys, a pasture of flocks;
Until the Spirit is poured on us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is considered a forest.
Then justice will live in the wilderness; and righteousness will remain in the fruitful field.
The work of righteousness Go be peace; and the effect of righteousness, quietness and confidence forever.
My people will live in a peaceful habitation, in safe dwellings, and in quiet resting places.
Though hail flattens the forest, and the city is leveled completely.
Blessed are you who sow beside all waters, who send out the feet of the ox and the donkey.

Woe to you who destroy, but you no be destroyed; and who betray, but nobody betrayed you! When you have finished destroying, You go be destroyed; and when you have finished betrayal, You go be betrayed.
Baba God, be gracious to us. We have waited for you. Be our strength every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.
At the noise of the thunder, the peoples have fled. When you lift yourself up, the nations are scattered.
Una plunder Go be gathered as the caterpillar gathers. Men will leap on it as locusts leap.
Baba God is exalted, for he dwells on high. He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
There Go be stability in una times, abundance of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of Baba God is una treasure.
See am, dem valiant ones cry outside; the ambassadors of peace weep bitterly.
The highways are desolate. The traveling man ceases. The covenant is broken. He has despised the cities. He no dey respect man.
The land mourns and languishes. Lebanon is confounded and withers away. Sharon is like a desert, and Bashan and Carmel are stripped bare.
“Now I go arise,” says Baba God; “Now I go lift myself up. Now I go be exalted.
You go conceive chaff. You go give birth to stubble. Una breath is a fire that will devour you.
The peoples Go be like the burning of lime, like thorns that are cut down and burned in the fire.
Hear, you Wey be far off, what I have done; and, you Wey be near, acknowledge my might.”
The sinners in Zion are afraid. Trembling has seized the godless ones. Who among us can live with the devouring fire? Who among us can live with everlasting burning?

Person wey walks righteously, and speaks blamelessly; Person wey despises the gain of oppressions, who gestures with his hands, refusing to take a bribe, who stops his ears from hearing of blood, and shuts his eyes from looking at evil —
he will live on high. His place of defense Go be the fortress of rocks. His bread Go be supplied. His waters Go be sure.
Una eyes will see the king in his beauty. Dem go see a distant land.
Una heart will meditate on the terror. Where is person wey counted? Where is person wey weighed? Where is person wey counted the towers?
You go no longer see the fierce people, a people of a deep speech that you no fit comprehend, with a strange language that you no fit understand.

Look at Zion, the city of our appointed festivals. Una eyes will see Jerusalem, a quiet habitation, a tent that no go be removed. Its stakes will never be plucked up, nor will any of its cords be broken.
But there Baba God Go be with us in majesty, a place of wide rivers and streams, in which no galley with oars will go, neither will any gallant ship pass by there.
For Baba God is our judge. Baba God is our lawgiver. Baba God is our king. He will save us.
Una rigging is untied. Dem no fit strengthen the foot of dem mast. Dem no fit spread the sail. Then the prey of a great plunder was divided. The lame take the prey.
The inhabitant no go say, “I be sick.” The people who live inside am Go be forgiven dem wickedness.
Come near, you nations, to hear! Listen, you peoples. Let the earth and all it contains hear; the world, and everything that comes from it.
For Baba God is enraged against all the nations, and angry with all dem armies. He has utterly destroyed dem. He has given dem over for slaughter.
Dem slain will also be throw out, and the stench of dem dead bodies will come up; and the mountains will melt in dem blood.
All of the army of the sky Go be dissolved. The sky Go be rolled up like a scroll, and all its armies will fade away, as a leaf fades from off a vine or a fig tree.
For my sword has drunk its fill in the sky. See am, it will come down on Edom, and on the people of my curse, for judgment.

Baba God’s sword is filled with blood. It is covered with fat, with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams; for Baba God has a sacrifice in Bozrah, And a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
The wild oxen will come down with dem, and the young bulls with the mighty bulls; and dem land Go be drunken with blood, and dem dust made greasy with fat.
For Baba God has a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.
Its streams Go be turned into pitch, its dust into sulfur, And its land will become burning pitch.
It no go be quenched night nor day. Its smoke will go up forever. From generation to generation, it will lie waste. Nobody will pass through it forever and ever.
But the pelican and the porcupine will possess it. The owl and the raven will live in it. He will stretch the line of confusion over it, and the plumb line of emptiness.
Dem shall call its nobles to the kingdom, but none go be there; and all its princes go be nothing.
Thorns will come up in its palaces, nettles and thistles in its fortresses; and it Go be a habitation of jackals, a court for ostriches.
The wild animals of the desert will meet with the wolves, and the wild goat will cry to his fellow. Yes, the night creature shall settle there, and shall find sheself a place of rest.
The arrow snake will make her nest there, and lay, hatch, and gather under her shade. Yes, the kites Go be gathered there, every one with her mate.
Search in the book of Baba God, and read: not one of these Go be missing. none will lack her mate. For my mouth has commanded, and his Spirit has gathered dem.
He has throw the lot for dem, and his hand has divided it to dem with a measuring line. Dem shall possess it forever. From generation to generation Dem go live in it.
The wilderness and the dry land Go be glad. The desert will glad well-well and blossom like a rose.

It will blossom abundantly, and glad well-well even with gladness and singing. Lebanon’s glory Go be given to it, the excellence of Carmel and Sharon. Dem go see Baba God’s glory, the excellence of our God.
Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees.
Tell people wey have a fearful heart, “Be strong. No fear. See am, una God will come with vengeance, God’s retribution. He will come and save you.
Then the eyes of the blind Go be opened, and the ears of the deaf Go be unstopped.
Then the lame man will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will sing; for waters will break out in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.
The burning sand will become a pool, and the thirsty ground springs of water. Grass with reeds and rushes Go be in the habitation of jackals, where dem lay.
A highway Go be there, a road, and it Go be call The Holy Way. The unclean no go pass over it, but it Go be for people wey walk in the Way. Wicked fools No go go there.
No lion Go be there, nor will any ravenous animal go up on it. Dem go not be find there; but the redeemed will walk there.
The Baba God’s ransomed ones will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting gladness Go be on dem heads. Dem go obtain gladness and gladness, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.”
Now in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all of the fortified cities of Judah, and captured dem.
The king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem to king Hezekiah with a large army. He stood by the aqueduct from the upper pool in the fuller’s field highway.
Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder come out to him.
Rabshakeh talk say to dem, “Now tell Hezekiah, ‘Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria, “What confidence is this in which you trust?
I say that una counsel and strength for the war are only vain words. Now in whom do you trust, that you have rebelled against me?
See am, you trust in the staff of this bruised reed, even in Egypt, which if a man leans on it, it will go into his hand and pierce it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.

But if you tell me, ‘We trust in Baba God our God,’ no be that he whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah has taken away, and has talk say to Judah and to Jerusalem, ‘You shall worship before this altar?’”
Now so, please make a pledge to my master the king of Assyria, and I go give you two thousand horses, if You be able on una part to set riders on dem.
How then can you turn away the face of one captain of the least of my master’s workers, and put una trust on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?
Have I come up now without Baba God against this land to destroy it? Baba God talk say to me, “Go up against this land, and destroy it.”’”

Then Eliakim, Shebna and Joah talk say to Rabshakeh, “Please speak to una workers in Aramaic, for we understand it; and no speak to us in the Jews’ language in the hearing of the people Wey be on the wall.”

But Rabshakeh talk say, “Has my master sent me only to una master and to you, to speak these words, and not to the men who sit on the wall, who will eat dem own dung and drink dem own urine with you?”
Then Rabshakeh stood, and call out with a loud voice in the Jews’ language, and talk say, “Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
Thus says the king, ‘No let Hezekiah deceive you; for he No go be able to deliver you.
No let Hezekiah make you trust in Baba God, saying, “Baba God will surely deliver us. This city no go be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.”’

No listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of Assyria, ‘Make una peace with me, and come out to me; and each of you eat from his vine, and each one from his fig tree, and each one of you drink the waters of his own cistern;
until I come and take you away to a land like una own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
Beware lest Hezekiah persuade you, saying, “Baba God will deliver us.” Have any of the gods of the nations delivered dem lands from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Have dem delivered Samaria from my hand?
Wey be dem among all the gods of these countries that have delivered dem country out of my hand, that Baba God should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?’”
But dem remain silent, and talk say nothing in reply, for the king’s commandment was, “No answer him.”

Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder, come to Hezekiah with dem clothes torn, and told him the words of Rabshakeh.
When king Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, covered imself with sackcloth, and go into Baba God’s house.
He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
Dem tell am say, “Thus says Hezekiah, ‘Today is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and of rejection; for the pikin dem have come to the birth, and E get no strength to give birth.

It may be Baba God una God will hear the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master has sent to defy the living God, and will rebuke the words which Baba God una God has heard. So lift up una prayer for the remnant that is left.’”
So the workers of king Hezekiah come to Isaiah.
Isaiah talk say to dem, “Tell una master, ‘Baba God says, “No fear of the words that you have heard, with which the workers of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
See am, I go put a spirit in him and he will hear news, and will return to his own land. I go cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.”’”
So Rabshakeh come back, and find the king of Assyria warring against Libnah, for he had heard that he was comot from Lachish.
He heard news concerning Tirhakah king of Ethiopia, “He has come out to fight against you.” When he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
“Thus you shall speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying, ‘No let una God in whom you trust deceive you, saying, “Jerusalem no go be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.”
See am, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, by destroying dem utterly. Shall you be delivered?
Have the gods of the nations delivered dem, which my fathers have destroyed, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the pikin dem of Eden who were in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah?’”
Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it. Then Hezekiah go up to Baba God’s house, and spread it before Baba God.
Hezekiah prayed to Baba God, saying,
“Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, Wey be enthroned among the cherubim, You be the God, even you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth.
Turn una ear, Baba God, and hear. Open una eyes, Baba God, and see am. Hear all of the words of Sennacherib, who has sent to defy the living God.
Truly, Baba God, the kings of Assyria have destroyed all the countries and dem land,
and have throw dem gods into the fire; for dem were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone; so dem have destroyed dem.
Now so, Baba God our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You be Baba God, even you only.”
Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, “Baba God, the God of Israel says, ‘Because you have prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria,
this is the word which Baba God has spoken concerning him. The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and ridiculed you. The daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you.
Whom have you defied and blasphemed? Against whom have you exalted una voice and lifted up una eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel.

By una workers, have you defied the Lord, and have talk say, “With the plenty people of my chariots I have come up to the height of the mountains, to the innermost parts of Lebanon. I go cut down its tall cedars and its choice cypress trees. I go enter into its farthest height, the forest of its fruitful field.
I have dug and drunk water, and with the sole of my feet I go dry up all the rivers of Egypt.”
Have you not heard how I have done it long ago, and formed it in ancient times? Now I have bring it to pass, that it should be yours to destroy fortified cities, turning dem into ruinous heaps.

So dem inhabitants had little power. Dem were dismayed and confounded. Dem were like the grass of the field, and like the green herb, like the grass on the housetops, and like a field before its crop has grown.
But I know una sitting down, una going out, una coming in, and una raging against me.
Because of una raging against me, and because una arrogance has come up into my ears, so will I put my hook in una nose and my bridle in una lips, and I go turn you back by the way by which you come.

This go be the sign to you. You go eat this year that which grows of itself, and in the second year that which springs from the same; and in the third year sow and reap and plant vineyards, and eat dem fruit.
The remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah will again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.
For out of Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and survivors will escape from Mount Zion. The zeal of Baba God of Armies will perform this.’
So Baba God says concerning the king of Assyria, ‘He No go come to this city, nor shoot an arrow there, neither will he come before it with shield, nor throw up a mound against it.
