By the way that he come, by the same he shall return, and he no go come to this city,’ says Baba God.
‘For I go defend this city to save it, for my own sake, and for my worker David’s sake.’”
Baba God’s angel go out and struck one hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the camp of the Assyrians. When men arose early in the morning, see am, these were all dead bodies.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria comot, go away, come back to Nineveh, and stayed there.
As he was worshiping in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him with the sword; and dem escaped into the land of Ararat. Esar Haddon his son reigned in his place.
In those days was Hezekiah sick and near death. Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, come to him, and talk say to him, “Baba God says, ‘Set una house in order, for You go die, and not live.’”
Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to Baba God,
and talk say, “Remember now, Baba God, I beg you, how I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in una sight.” Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Then Baba God’s word come to Isaiah, saying,
“Go, and tell Hezekiah, ‘Baba God says, the God of David una father, “I have heard una prayer. I have seen una tears. See am, I go add fifteen years to una life.
I go deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and I go defend this city.
This go be the sign to you from Baba God, that Baba God will do this thing that he has spoken.

See am, I go cause the shadow on the sundial, which has gone down on the sundial of Ahaz with the sun, to return backward ten steps. So the sun come back ten steps on the sundial on which it had gone down.”’”
The writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he Bin dey sick, and had recovered of his sickness.
I talk say, “In the middle of my life I go into the gates of Sheol. I be deprived of the residue of my years.”
I talk say, “I no go see Yah, Yah in the land of the living. I go see man no more with the inhabitants of the world.

My dwelling is removed, and is carried away from me like a shepherd’s tent. I have rolled up, like a weaver, my life. He will cut me off from the loom. From day even to night You go make an end of me.
I waited patiently until morning. He breaks all my bones like a lion. From day even to night You go make an end of me.
I chattered like a swallow or a crane. I moaned like a dove. My eyes weaken looking upward. Lord, I be oppressed. Be my security.”
What will I say? He has both spoken to me, and imself has done it. I go walk carefully all my years because of the anguish of my soul.
Lord, men live by these things; and my spirit finds life in all of dem: you restore me, and cause me to live.
See am, for peace I had great anguish, but you have in love for my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption; for you have throw all my sins behind una back.
For Sheol no fit praise you. Death no fit celebrate you. People wey go down into the pit no fit hope for una truth.
The living, the living, he shall praise you, as I do today. The father shall make known una truth to the pikin dem.
Baba God will save me. So We go sing my songs with stringed instruments all the days of our life in Baba God’s house.
Now Isaiah had talk say, “Make dem take a cake of figs, and lay it for a poultice on the boil, and he shall recover.”
Hezekiah also had talk say, “Wetin be the sign that I go go up to Baba God’s house?”
At that time, Merodach Baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah; for he heard that he Bin dey sick, and had recovered.

Hezekiah was pleased with dem, and showed dem the house of his precious things, the silver, and the gold, the spices, and the precious oil, and all the house of his armor, and all that was find in his treasures. There was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah didn’t show dem.
Then Isaiah the prophet come to king Hezekiah, and ask him, “What did these men say? Where did dem come from to you?” Hezekiah talk say, “Dem have come from a country far from me, even from Babylon.”
Then he ask, “What have dem seen in una house?” Hezekiah answer, “Dem have seen all that is in my house. E get nothing among my treasures that I have not shown dem.”
Then Isaiah talk say to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of Baba God of Armies:
‘See am, the days are coming when all that is in una house, and that which una fathers have stored up until today, Go be carried to Babylon. Nothing Go be left,’ says Baba God.
‘Dem go take away una sons who will issue from you, whom you shall father, and Dem go be eunuchs in the king of Babylon’s palace.’”
Then Hezekiah talk say to Isaiah, “Baba God’s word which you have spoken is good.” He talk say moreover, “For there Go be peace and truth in my days.”
“Comfort, comfort my people,” says una God.
“Speak comfortably to Jerusalem; and call out to her that her warfare is accomplished, that her wickedness is pardoned, that she has received of Baba God’s hand double for all her sins.”
The voice of one who calls out, “Prepare the way of Baba God in the wilderness! Make a level highway in the desert for our God.
Every valley go be exalted, and every mountain and hill go be made low. The uneven go be made level, and the rough places a plain.
Baba God’s glory go be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together; for the mouth of Baba God has spoken it.”
The voice of one saying, “Cry!” One talk say, “What shall I cry?” “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the field.
The grass withers, the flower fades, because Baba God’s breath blows on it. Surely the people are like grass.
The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.”
You who tell better news to Zion, go up on a high mountain. You who tell better news to Jerusalem, lift up una voice with strength. Lift it up. No fear. Say to the cities of Judah, “See am, una God!”
See am, the Lord Baba God will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him. See am, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.
He will feed his flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry dem in his bosom. He will gently lead people wey have dem young.

Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and marked off the sky with his span, and calculated the dust of the earth in a measuring basket, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?
Who has directed Baba God’s Spirit, or has taught him as his counselor?
Who did he take counsel with, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of justice, and taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?
See am, the nations are like a drop in a bucket, and are regarded as a speck of dust on a balance. See am, he lifts up the islands like a very little thing.
Lebanon No be sufficient to burn, nor its animals sufficient for a burnt offering.
All the nations are like nothing before him. Dem be regarded by him as less than nothing, and vanity.
To whom then will you liken God? Or what likeness will you compare to him?
A workman has throw an image, and the goldsmith overlays it with gold, and casts silver chains for it.
Person Wey too impoverished for such an offering chooses a tree that No go rot. He seeks a skillful workman to set up an engraved image for him that No go be moved.
Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard, yet? Haven’t you been told from the beginning? Haven’t you understand from the foundations of the earth?
It is person wey sits above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads dem out like a tent to live in;
who brings princes to nothing; who makes the judges of the earth like meaningless.
Dem be planted scarcely. Dem be sown scarcely. Dem stock has scarcely taken root in the ground. He merely blows on dem, and dem wither, and the whirlwind takes dem away as stubble.
“To whom then will you liken me? Wey be my equal?” says the Holy One.

Lift up una eyes on high, and see who has created these, who brings out dem army by number. He calls dem all by name. by the greatness of his might, and because he is strong in power, Not one is lacking.
Why do you say, Jacob, and speak, Israel, “My way is hidden from Baba God, and the justice due me is disregarded by my God?”
Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard? The everlasting God, Baba God, The Creator of every corner of the world, no dey faint. He no be weary. His understanding is unsearchable.
He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might.
Even the youths faint and get weary, and the young men utterly fall;
But people wey wait for Baba God will renew dem strength. Dem go mount up with wings like eagles. Dem go run, and not be weary. Dem go walk, and not faint.
“Keep silent before me, islands, and let the peoples renew dem strength. Make dem come near, then Make dem speak. Let’s meet together for judgment.

Who has raised up one from the east? Who call him to his foot in righteousness? He hands over nations to him, and makes him rule over kings. He gives dem like the dust to his sword, like the driven stubble to his bow.
He pursues dem, and passes by safely, Even by a way that he had not gone with his feet.
Who has worked and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, Baba God, the first, and with the last, I be he.”
The islands have seen, and fear. Every corner of the world tremble. Dem approach, and come.
Everyone helps his neighbor. Dem say to dem brothers, “Be strong!”

So the carpenter encourages the goldsmith. Person wey smoothes with the hammer encourages him who strikes the anvil, saying of the soldering, “It is good”; and he fastens it with nails, that it might not totter.
“But you, Israel, my worker, Jacob whom I have chosen, the offspring of Abraham my friend,
You whom I have taken hold of from every corner of the world, and call from its corners, and talk say to you, ‘You be my worker, I have chosen you and not throw you away;’
No you be afraid, for I be with you. No be dismayed, for I be una God. I go strengthen you. Yes, I go help you. Yes, I go uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
See am, all people Wey incensed against You go be disappointed and confounded. People wey strive with You go be like nothing, and shall perish.
You go seek dem, and no go find dem, even people wey contend with you. People wey war against You go be as nothing, as a non-existent thing.
For I, Baba God una God, will hold una right hand, saying to you, ‘No fear. I go help you.’
No fear, you worm Jacob, and you men of Israel. I go help you,” says Baba God, “and una Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
See am, I have made you into a new sharp threshing instrument with teeth. You go thresh the mountains, and beat dem small, and will make the hills like chaff.
You go winnow dem, and the wind will carry dem away, and the whirlwind will scatter dem. You go glad well-well in Baba God. You go glory in the Holy One of Israel.
The poor and needy seek water, and E get none. Dem tongue fails for thirst. I, Baba God, will answer dem. I, the God of Israel, No go forsake dem.
I go open rivers on the bare heights, and springs in the middle of the valleys. I go make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.
I go put cedar, acacia, myrtle, and oil trees in the wilderness. I go set cypress trees, pine, and box trees together in the desert;
that dem may see, know, consider, and understand together, that Baba God’s hand has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it.
Produce una cause,” says Baba God. “Bring out una strong reasons,” says the King of Jacob.
“Make dem announce, and declare to us what shall happen. Declare the former things, Wetin dem are, that we may consider dem, and know the latter end of dem; or show us things to come.
Declare the things that are to come hereafter, that we may know that You be gods. Yes, do good, or do evil, that we may be dismayed, and see it together.
See am, You be of nothing, and una work is of nothing. Person wey chooses you is an abomination.
“I have raised up one from the north, and he has come; from the rising of the sun, one who calls on my name; and he shall come on rulers as on mortar, and as the potter treads clay.

Who has declared it from the beginning, that we may know? And before, that we may say, ‘He is right?’ Surely, E get Nobody who declares. Surely, E get Nobody who shows. Surely, E get Nobody wey hear una words.
I be the first to say to Zion, ‘See am, look at dem;’ and I go give one who brings better news to Jerusalem.
When I look, E get no man; even among dem E get no counselor who, when I ask of dem, can answer a word.
See am, all of dem, dem deeds are vanity and nothing. Dem molten images are wind and confusion.
“See am, my worker, whom I uphold; my chosen, in whom my soul delights — I have put my Spirit on him. He will bring justice to the nations.
He No go shout, nor raise his voice, nor cause it to be heard in the street.
He no go break a bruised reed. He no go quench a dimly burning wick. He will faithfully bring justice.
He No go fail nor be discouraged, until he has set justice in the earth, and the islands will wait for his law.”

Thus says Baba God, person wey created the heavens and stretched dem out, person wey spread out the earth and that which comes out of it, person wey gives breath to its people and spirit to people wey walk in it.
“I, Baba God, have call you in righteousness, and will hold una hand, and will keep you, and make you a covenant for the people, as a light for the nations;
to open the blind eyes, to bring the prisoners out of the dungeon, and people wey sit in darkness out of the prison.
“I be Baba God. That is my name. I go not give my glory to another, nor my praise to engraved images.
See am, the former things have happened, and I declare new things. I tell una about dem before dem come up.”
Sing to Baba God a new song, and his praise from the end of the earth, you who go down to the sea, and all that is inside am, the islands and dem inhabitants.
Let the wilderness and its cities raise dem voices, with the villages that Kedar inhabits. Let the inhabitants of Sela sing. Make dem shout from the top of the mountains!
Make dem give glory to Baba God, and declare his praise in the islands.
Baba God will go out like a mighty man. He will stir up zeal like a man of war. He will raise a war cry. Yes, he will shout aloud. He will triumph over his enemies.
“I Don dey silent a long time. I Don dey quiet and restrained myself. Now I go cry out like a travailing woman. I go both gasp and pant.
I go destroy mountains and hills, and dry up all dem herbs. I go make the rivers islands, and will dry up the pools.

I go bring the blind by a way that dem no know. I go lead dem in paths that dem no know. I go make darkness light before dem, and crooked places straight. I go do these things, and I go not forsake dem.
“People wey trust in engraved images, who tell molten images, ‘You be our gods’ Go be turned back. Dem go be utterly disappointed.
“Hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see.
Wey be blind, but my worker? Or Wey be as deaf as my messenger whom I send? Wey be as blind as person Wey at peace, and as blind as Baba God’s worker?
You see many things, but no observe. His ears are open, but he no dey listen.
It pleased Baba God, for his righteousness’ sake, to magnify the law, and make it honorable.
But this is a robbed and plundered people. All of dem are snared in holes, and Dem be hidden in prisons. Dem have become captives, and Nobody delivers; and a plunder, and Nobody says, ‘Restore dem!’
Wey be there among you who will give ear to this? Who will listen and hear for the time to come?
Who give Jacob as plunder, and Israel to the robbers? Didn’t Baba God, he against whom we have sinned? For dem would not walk in his ways, and dem disobeyed his law.
So he poured the fierceness of his anger on him, and the strength of battle; and it set him on fire all around, but he didn’t know; and it burned him, but he didn’t take it to heart.”
But now Baba God who created you, Jacob, and person wey formed you, Israel says: “No fear, for I have redeemed you. I have call you by una name. You be mine.
When you pass through the waters, I go be with you; and through the rivers, Dem go not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, You go not be burned, and flame No go scorch you.
For I be Baba God una God, the Holy One of Israel, una Savior. I have given Egypt as una ransom, Ethiopia and Seba in una place.
Since you Don dey precious and honored in my sight, and I have love you; so I go give people in una place, and nations instead of una life.
No fear; for I be with you. I go bring una offspring from the east, and gather you from the west.
I go tell the north, ‘Give dem up!’ and tell the south, ‘No hold dem back! Bring my sons from far, and my daughters from every corner of the world —
everyone Wey be call by my name, and whom I have created for my glory, whom I have formed, yes, whom I have made.’”
Bring out the blind people who have eyes, and the deaf who have ears.

Let all the nations be gathered together, and let the peoples be assembled. Who among dem can declare this, and show us former things? Make dem bring dem witnesses, that dem may be justified; or Make dem hear, and say, “That is true.”

“You be my witnesses,” says Baba God, “With my worker whom I have chosen; that you may know and believe me, and understand that I be he. Before me there was no God formed, neither will there be after me.
I myself am Baba God; and besides me E get no savior.
I have declared, I have saved, and I have shown; and there was no strange god among you. So You be my witnesses”, says Baba God, “and I be God.
Yes, since the day was I be he; and E get Nobody who can deliver out of my hand. I go work, and who can hinder it?”
Baba God, una Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel says: “For una sake, I have sent to Babylon, and I go bring all of dem down as fugitives, even the Chaldeans, in the ships of dem rejoicing.
I be Baba God, una Holy One, the Creator of Israel, una King.”
Baba God, who makes a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters says:
who brings out the chariot and horse, the army and the mighty man (dem lie down together, dem no go rise; Dem be extinct, Dem be quenched like a wick):
“No remember the former things, and no consider the things of old.
See am, I go do a new thing. It springs out now. No you know it? I go even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.
The animals of the field shall honor me, the jackals and the ostriches; because I give water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen,
the people which I formed for myself, that dem might declare my praise.
Yet you have not call on me, Jacob; but you Don dey weary of me, Israel.
You have not bring me of una sheep for burnt offerings; neither have you honored me with una sacrifices. I have not burdened you with offerings, nor wearied you with frankincense.
You have bought me no sweet cane with money, nor have you filled me with the fat of una sacrifices; but you have burdened me with una sins. You have wearied me with una iniquities.
I, even I, am person wey blots out una wrongdoings for my own sake; and I go not remember una sins.
Put me in remembrance. Make we plead together. Declare una case, that you may be justified.
Una first father sinned, and una teachers have transgressed against me.
So I go profane the princes of the sanctuary; and I go make Jacob a curse, and Israel an insult.”
Yet listen now, Jacob my worker, and Israel, whom I have chosen.
This is what Baba God who made you, and formed you from the womb, who will help you says: “No fear, Jacob my worker; and you, Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.
For I go pour water on him Wey be thirsty, and streams on the dry ground. I go pour my Spirit on una descendants, and my blessing on una offspring:
and Dem go spring up among the grass, as willows by the watercourses.
One will say, ‘I be Baba God’s;’ and another Go be call by the name of Jacob; and another will write with his hand ‘to Baba God,’ and honor the name of Israel.”
This is what Baba God, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, Baba God of Armies, says: “I be the first, and I be the last; and besides me E get no God.
Wey be like me? Who will call, and will declare it, and set it in order for me, since I established the ancient people? Make dem declare the things that are coming, and that will happen.
No fear, neither be afraid. Haven’t I declared it to you long ago, and shown it? You be my witnesses. Is there a God besides me? Indeed, there No be. I no know any other Rock.”
Everybody wey makes an engraved image is vain. The things that dem delight in No go profit. Dem own witnesses no see, nor know, that dem may be disappointed.
Who has fashioned a god, or molds an image that is profitable for nothing?
See am, all his fellows Go be disappointed; and the workmen are mere men. Make dem all be gathered together. Make dem stand up. Dem go fear. Dem go be put to shame together.
The blacksmith takes an ax, works in the coals, fashions it with hammers, and works it with his strong arm. He is hungry, and his strength fails; he drinks no water, and is faint.

The carpenter stretches out a line. He marks it out with a pencil. He shapes it with planes. He marks it out with compasses, and shapes it like the figure of a man, with the beauty of a man, to reside in a house.
He cuts down cedars for imself, and takes the cypress and the oak, and dey give power for imself one among the trees of the forest. He plants a cypress tree, and the rain nourishes it.

Then it Go be for a man to burn; and he takes some of it, and warms imself. Yes, he burns it, and bakes bread. Yes, he makes a god, and worships it; he makes it an engraved image, and falls down to it.
He burns part of it in the fire. With part of it, he eats meat. He roasts a roast, and is satisfied. Yes, he warms imself, and says, “Aha! I be warm. I have seen the fire.”
The rest of it he makes into a god, even his engraved image. He bows down to it and worships, and prays to it, and says, “Deliver me; for You be my god!”
Dem no know, neither do dem consider: for he has shut dem eyes, that dem no fit see; and dem hearts, that dem no fit understand.

Nobody thinks, neither is there knowledge nor understanding to say, “I have burned part of it in the fire. Yes, I have also baked bread on its coals. I have roasted meat and eaten it. Shall I make the rest of it into an abomination? Shall I bow down to a tree trunk?”
He feeds on ashes. A deceived heart has turned him aside; and he no fit deliver his soul, nor say, “No be there a lie in my right hand?”
Remember these things, Jacob and Israel; for You be my worker. I have formed you. You be my worker. Israel, You go not be forgotten by me.
I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, una wrongdoings, and, as a cloud, una sins. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.

Sing, you heavens, for Baba God has done it! Shout, you lower parts of the earth! Break out into singing, you mountains, O forest, all of una trees, for Baba God has redeemed Jacob, and will glorify imself in Israel.
Baba God, una Redeemer, and person wey formed you from the womb says: “I be Baba God, who makes all things; who alone stretches out the heavens; who spreads out the earth by myself;
who frustrates the signs of the liars, and makes diviners mad; who turns wise men backward, and makes dem knowledge foolish;

who confirms the word of his worker, and performs the counsel of his messengers; who says of Jerusalem, ‘She Go be inhabited;’ and of the cities of Judah, ‘Dem go be built,’ and ‘I go raise up its waste places;’
who says to the deep, ‘Be dry,’ and ‘I go dry up una rivers;’
Who says of Cyrus, ‘He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure,’ even saying of Jerusalem, ‘She Go be built;’ and of the temple, ‘Una foundation Go be laid.’”
Baba God says to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have held, to subdue nations before him, and strip kings of dem armor; to open the doors before him, and the gates no go be shut:
“I go go before you, and make the rough places smooth. I go break the doors of brass in pieces, and cut apart the bars of iron.
I go give you the treasures of darkness, and hidden riches of secret places, that you may know that it is I, Baba God, who call you by una name, even the God of Israel.
For Jacob my worker’s sake, and Israel my chosen, I have call you by una name. I have given you a title, though you have not known me.
I be Baba God, and E get Nobody else. Besides me, E get no God. I go strengthen you, though you have not known me;
that dem may know from the rising of the sun, and from the west, that E get Nobody besides me. I be Baba God, and E get Nobody else.
I form the light, and create darkness. I make peace, and create calamity. I be Baba God, wey do all these things.

Rain, you heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness. Let the earth open, that it may produce salvation, and let it cause righteousness to spring up with it. I, Baba God, have created it.
Woe to him who strives with his Maker — a clay pot among the clay pots of the earth! Shall the clay ask him who fashions it, ‘Wetin be you making?’ or una work, ‘He has no hands?’
Woe to him who says to a father, ‘What have you become the father of?’ or to a mother, ‘To what have you given birth?’”
Baba God, the Holy One of Israel, and his Maker says: “You ask me about the things that are to come, concerning my sons, and you command me concerning the work of my hands!
I have made the earth, and created man on it. I, even my hands, have stretched out the heavens; and I have commanded all dem army.
I have raised him up in righteousness, and I go make straight all his ways. He shall build my city, and he shall let my exiles go free, not for price nor reward,” says Baba God of Armies.

Baba God says: “The labor of Egypt, and the merchandise of Ethiopia, and the Sabeans, men of stature, shall come over to you, and dem go be yours. Dem go go after you. Dem shall come over in chains; and Dem go bow down to you. Dem go make supplication to you: ‘Surely God is in you; and E get Nobody else. E get no other god.
Most certainly You be a God who has hidden yourself, God of Israel, the Savior.’”
Dem go be disappointed, yes, confounded, all of dem. People Wey makers of idols will go into confusion together.
Israel Go be saved by Baba God with an everlasting salvation. You go not be disappointed nor confounded to ages everlasting.

For Baba God who created the heavens, the God who formed the earth and made it, who established it and didn’t create it a waste, who formed it to be inhabited says: “I be Baba God; and E get no other.
I have not spoken in secret, in a place of the land of darkness. I didn’t say to the offspring of Jacob, ‘Seek me in vain.’ I, Baba God, speak righteousness. I declare things that are right.
“Assemble unaself and come. Draw near together, you who have escaped from the nations. Those have no knowledge who carry the wood of dem engraved image, and pray to a god that no fit save.

Declare and present it. Yes, Make dem take counsel together. Who has shown this from ancient time? Who has declared it of old? Haven’t I, Baba God? E get no other God besides me, a just God and a Savior; E get Nobody besides me.
“Look to me, and be saved, all every corner of the world; for I be God, and E get no other.
I have sworn by myself. The word has gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and No go be revoked, that to me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall take an oath.
Dem go say of me, ‘E get righteousness and strength only in Baba God.’” Even to him shall men come; and all people wey raged against him go be disappointed.
All the offspring of Israel Go be justified in Baba God, and will glad well-well!
Bel bows down. Nebo stoops. Dem idols are carried by animals, and on the livestock. The things that you carried around are heavy loads, a burden for the weary.
Dem stoop and dem bow down together. Dem could not deliver the burden, but dem have gone into captivity.
“Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, that Don dey carried from dem birth, that Don dey carried from the womb.
Even to old age I be he, and even to gray hairs I go carry you. I have made, and I go bear. Yes, I go carry, and will deliver.
“To whom will you liken me, and consider my equal, and compare me, that we may be equal?
Some pour out gold from the bag, and weigh silver in the balance. Dem hire a goldsmith, and he makes it a god. Dem fall down — yes, dem worship.

Dem bear it on dem shoulder. Dem carry it, and set it in its place, and it stands there. It cannot move from its place. Yes, one may cry to it, yet it can not answer. It cannot save him out of his trouble.
“Remember this, and show unaself men. Bring it to mind again, you transgressors.
Remember the former things of old: for I be God, and E get no other. I be God, and E get none like me.
I declare the end from the beginning, and from ancient times things that No be yet done. I say: My counsel will stand, and I go do all that I please.
I call a ravenous bird from the east, the man of my counsel from a far country. Yes, I have spoken. I go also bring it to pass. I have planned. I go also do it.
Listen to me, you stubborn-hearted, Wey be far from righteousness!
I bring my righteousness near. It No be far off, and my salvation No go wait. I go grant salvation to Zion, my glory to Israel.
“Come down, and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground without a throne, daughter of the Chaldeans. For You go no longer be call tender and delicate.
Take the millstones, and grind flour. Remove una veil, lift up una skirt, uncover una legs, and wade through the rivers.
Una nakedness Go be uncovered. Yes, una shame Go be seen. I go take vengeance, and will spare Nobody.”
Our Redeemer, Baba God of Armies is his name, is the Holy One of Israel.
“Sit in silence, and go into darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. For you shall no longer be call the mistress of kingdoms.
I was angry with my people. I profaned my inheritance, and give dem into una hand. You showed dem no mercy. You laid a very heavy yoke on the aged.
You talk say, ‘I go be a princess forever;’ so that you No lay these things to una heart, nor did you remember the results.
“Now so hear this, you Wey be given to pleasures, who sit securely, who say in una heart, ‘I be, and E get Nobody else besides me. I no go sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of pikin dem.’

But these two things shall come to you in a moment in one day, the loss of pikin dem and widowhood. Dem go come on you in dem full measure, in the plenty people of una sorceries, and the great abundance of una enchantments.
For you have trusted in una wickedness. You have talk say, ‘Nobody sees me.’ Una wisdom and una knowledge has perverted you. You have talk say in una heart, ‘I be, and E get Nobody else besides me.’
So disaster will come on you. You no go know when it dawns. Mischief will fall on you. You no go be able to put it away. Desolation will come on you suddenly, which you no understand.
“Stand now with una enchantments, and with the plenty people of una sorceries, in which you have labored from una youth; as if you might profit; as if you might prevail.
You be wearied in the plenty people of una counsels. Now let the astrologers, the stargazers, and the monthly prognosticators, stand up and save you from the things that will come on you.
See am, Dem be like stubble. The fire will burn dem. Dem no go deliver themselves from the power of the flame. It no go be a coal to warm at or a fire to sit by.
The things that you labored in Go be like this: people wey have trafficked with you from una youth will each wander in his own way. There Go be Nobody to save you.

“Hear this, house of Jacob, you Wey be call by the name of Israel, and have come out of the waters of Judah. You swear by Baba God’s name, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in righteousness
(for dem call themselves citizens of the holy city, and rely on the God of Israel; Baba God of Armies is his name):
I have declared the former things from of old; yes, dem go out of my mouth, and I revealed dem. I did dem suddenly, and dem happened.
Because I know that You be obstinate, and una neck is an iron sinew, and una brow brass;
so I have declared it to you from of old; before E happen say I showed it to you; lest you should say, ‘My idol has done dem, and my engraved image, and my molten image, has commanded dem.’
You have heard it; see all this. And you, no go you declare it? “I have shown you new things from this time, even hidden things, which you have not known.
Dem be created now, and not from of old; and before today you didn’t hear dem; lest you should say, ‘See am, I know dem.’
Yes, you didn’t hear; yes, you didn’t know; yes, from of old una ear No be opened: for I know that you dealt very treacherously, and were call a transgressor from the womb.
For my name’s sake, I go defer my anger, and for my praise I hold it back for you, so that I no cut you off.
See am, I have refined you, but No be like silver. I have chosen you in the furnace of suffering.
For my own sake, for my own sake, I go do it; for how would my name be profaned? I go not give my glory to another.
“Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel my call: I be he; I be the first, I be also the last.
Yes, my hand has laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand has spread out the heavens. when I call to dem, dem stand up together.
“Assemble unaself, all of you, and hear; who among dem has declared these things? He whom Baba God loves will do what he likes to Babylon, and his arm Go be against the Chaldeans.
I, even I, have spoken; yes, I have call him. I have bring him, and he shall make his way prosperous.
“Come near to me and hear this: “From the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time that it happened, I was there.” Now the Lord Baba God has sent me, with his Spirit.
Baba God, una Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel says: “I be Baba God una God, who teaches you to profit, who leads you by the way that you should go.
Oh that you had listened to my commandments! Then una peace would Don dey like a river, and una righteousness like the waves of the sea.
Una offspring also would Don dey as the sand, and the descendants of una body like its grains. His name would not be cut off nor destroyed from before me.”
Leave Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! With a voice of singing announce this, tell it even to the end of the earth: say, “Baba God has redeemed his worker Jacob!”
Dem didn’t thirst when he led dem through the deserts. He caused the waters to flow out of the rock for dem. He split the rock also, and the waters gushed out.
“E get no peace”, says Baba God, “for the wicked.”
Listen, islands, to me. Listen, you peoples, from far away: Baba God has call me from the womb; from the inside of my mother he has mentioned my name.
He has made my mouth like a sharp sword. He has hidden me in the shadow of his hand. He has made me a polished shaft. He has kept me close in his quiver.
He talk say to me, “You be my worker; Israel, in whom I go be glorified.”
But I talk say, “I have labored in vain. I have spent my strength in vain for nothing; yet surely the justice due to me is with Baba God, and my reward with my God.”

Now Baba God says, person wey formed me from the womb to be his worker, to bring Jacob again to him, and to gather Israel to him, for I be honorable in Baba God’s eyes, and my God has become my strength.

Indeed, he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my worker to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel? I go also give you as a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.”

Baba God, the Redeemer of Israel, and his Holy One, says to him whom man despises, to him whom the nation abhors, to a worker of rulers: “Kings shall see and rise up; princes, and dem shall worship; because of Baba God Wey be faithful, even the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you.”

Baba God says, “In an acceptable time I have answer you, and in a day of salvation I have helped you. I go preserve you, and give you for a covenant of the people, to raise up the land, to make dem inherit the desolate heritage:
saying to people Wey bound, ‘Come out!’; to people Wey in darkness, ‘Show unaself!’ “Dem shall feed along the paths, and dem pasture go be on all treeless heights.
Dem no go hunger nor thirst; neither shall the heat nor sun strike dem: for person wey has mercy on dem will lead dem. He will guide dem by springs of water.
I go make all my mountains a road, and my highways go be exalted.
See am, these shall come from far away; and see am, these from the north and from the west; and these from the land of Sinim.”
Sing, heavens; and be joyful, earth; and break out into singing, mountains: for Baba God has comforted his people, and Go get compassion on his afflicted.
But Zion talk say, “Baba God has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me.”
“Can a woman forget her nursing pikin, that she no suppose have compassion on the son of her womb? Yes, these may forget, yet I go not forget you!
See am, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands. una walls are continually before me.
Una pikin dem hurry. Una destroyers and people wey devastated You go leave you.

Lift up una eyes all around, and see: all these gather themselves together, and come to you. As I live,” says Baba God, “you shall surely clothe yourself with dem all as with an ornament, and dress yourself with dem, like a bride.
“For, as for una waste and una desolate places, and una land that Don dey destroyed, surely now that land Go be too small for the inhabitants, and people wey swallowed you up Go be far away.
The pikin dem of una bereavement will say in una ears, ‘This place is too small for me. Give me a place to live in.’

Then You go say in una heart, ‘Who has conceived these for me, since I Don dey bereaved of my pikin dem, and am solitary, an exile, and wandering back and forth? Who has bring these up? See am, I was left alone. Where were these?’”

Thus says the Lord Baba God, “See am, I go lift up my hand to the nations, and lift up my banner to the peoples; and dem shall bring una sons in dem bosom, and una daughters go be carried on dem shoulders.

Kings go be una foster fathers, and dem queens una nursing mothers. Dem go bow down to you with dem faces to the earth, and lick the dust of una feet; Then You go know that I be Baba God; and people wey wait for me no go be disappointed.”
Shall the plunder be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captives be delivered?
But Baba God says, “Even the captives of the mighty go be taken away, and the plunder retrieved from the fierce; for I go contend with him who contends with you, and I go save una pikin dem.

I go feed people wey oppress you with dem own flesh; and Dem go be drunk on dem own blood, as with sweet wine. Then all flesh shall know that I, Baba God, am una Savior, and una Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.”

Baba God says, “Where is the bill of una mother’s divorce, with which I have put her away? or to which of my creditors have I sold you? See am, you were sold for una iniquities, and una mother was put away for una wrongdoings.

Why, when I come, was there Nobody? when I call, why was there Nobody to answer? Is my hand shortened at all, that it no fit redeem? or have I no power to deliver? See am, at my rebuke I dry up the sea. I make the rivers a wilderness: dem fish stink, because E get no water, and die for thirst.
I clothe the heavens with blackness, and I make sackcloth dem covering.”

The Lord Baba God has given me the tongue of people Wey taught, that I may know how to sustain with words him Wey be weary. He wakens morning by morning, he wakens my ear to hear as people Wey taught.
The Lord Baba God has opened my ear, and I No be rebellious. I have not turned back.
I give my back to people wey beat me, and my cheeks to people wey plucked off the hair. I didn’t hide my face from shame and spitting.
For the Lord Baba God will help me. So I have not been confounded. So I have set my face like a flint, and I know that I no go be disappointed.
Person wey justifies me is near. Who will bring charges against me? Make we stand up together. Wey be my adversary? Make e come near to me.
See am, the Lord Baba God will help me! Wey be person wey will condemn me? See am, Dem go all grow old like a garment. The moths will eat dem up.
Who among you fears Baba God, and obeys the voice of his worker? Person wey walks in darkness, and has no light, Make e trust in Baba God’s name, and rely on his God.

See am, all you who kindle a fire, who adorn unaself with torches around unaself; walk in the flame of una fire, and among the torches that you have kindled. You go have this from my hand: You go lie down in sorrow.
“Listen to me, you who follow after righteousness, you who seek Baba God: look to the rock you were cut from, and to the quarry you were dug from.
Look to Abraham una father, and to Sarah who bore you; for when he was but one I call him, and I blessed him, and made him many.

For Baba God has comforted Zion. He has comforted all her waste places, and has made her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of Baba God. Gladness and gladness Go be find inside am, thanksgiving, and the voice of melody.
“Listen to me, my people; and hear me, my nation: for a law will go out from me, and I go establish my justice for a light to the peoples.
My righteousness is near. My salvation has gone out, and my arms will judge the peoples. The islands will wait for me, and Dem go trust my arm.

Lift up una eyes to the heavens, and look on the earth beneath; for the heavens will vanish away like smoke, and the earth will wear out like a garment; and its inhabitants will die in the same way: but my salvation Go be forever, and my righteousness No go be abolished.
“Listen to me, you who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law: No fear the reproach of men, and no be dismayed at dem insults.
For the moth will eat dem up like a garment, and the worm will eat dem like wool; but my righteousness Go be forever, and my salvation to all generations.”
Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of Baba God! Awake, as in the days of old, the generations of ancient times. No be it you who cut Rahab in pieces, who pierced the monster?
No be it you who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep; who made the depths of the sea a way for the redeemed to pass over?
Those ransomed by Baba God will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting gladness go be on dem heads. Dem go obtain gladness and gladness. Sorrow and sighing shall flee away.
“I, even I, am person wey comforts you. Wey be you, that You be afraid of man who shall die, and of the Son of Man who Go be made as grass?

Have you forgotten Baba God una Maker, who stretched out the heavens, and laid the foundations of the earth? Do you live in fear continually all day because of the fury of the oppressor, when he prepares to destroy? Where is the fury of the oppressor?
The captive exile will speedily be freed; and he No go die and go down into the pit, and his bread No go fail.
For I be Baba God una God, who stirs up the sea, so that its waves roar: Baba God of Armies is his name.
I have put my words in una mouth, and have covered you in the shadow of my hand, that I may plant the heavens, and lay the foundations of the earth, and tell Zion, ‘You be my people.’”
Awake, awake! Stand up, Jerusalem, you who have drunk from Baba God’s hand the cup of his serious anger. You have drunken the bowl of the cup of staggering, and drained it.
E get Nobody to guide her among all the sons to whom she has given birth; and E get Nobody who takes her by the hand among all the sons who she has bring up.
These two things have happened to you — who will grieve with you? — desolation and destruction, and famine and the sword. How can I comfort you?
Una sons have fainted. Dem lie at the head of all the streets, like an antelope in a net. Dem be full of the Baba God’s serious anger, the rebuke of una God.
So now hear this, you afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine:

Thus says una Lord Baba God, una God who pleads the cause of his people, “See am, I have taken out of una hand the cup of staggering, even the bowl of the cup of my serious anger. You go not drink it any more:

and I go put it into the hand of people wey afflict you, who have talk say to una soul, ‘Bow down, that we may walk over you;’ and you have laid una back as the ground, like a street to people wey walk over.”
Awake, awake! Put on una strength, Zion. Put on una beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city: for from now on the uncircumcised and the unclean will no more come into you.
Shake yourself from the dust! Arise, sit up, Jerusalem! Release yourself from the bonds of una neck, captive daughter of Zion!
For Baba God says, “You were sold for nothing; and You go be redeemed without money.”
For thus says the Lord Baba God: “My people go down at the first into Egypt to live there: and the Assyrian has oppressed dem without cause.
“Now so, what do I do here,” says Baba God, “seeing that my people are taken away for nothing? People wey rule over dem mock,” says Baba God, “and my name is blasphemed continually all day long.
So my people shall know my name. So dem shall know in that day that I be person wey speaks. See am, it is I.”
How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings better news, who publishes peace, who brings better news, who proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, “Una God reigns!”
Una watchmen lift up dem voice, together dem sing; for dem shall see eye to eye, when Baba God returns to Zion.
Break out into gladness, sing together, you waste places of Jerusalem; for Baba God has comforted his people. He has redeemed Jerusalem.
Baba God has made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations; and all every corner of the world have seen the salvation of our God.
Depart, depart, go out from there; touch no unclean thing! Go out from among her! Cleanse unaself, you who carry Baba God’s vessels.
For you no go go out in haste, neither shall you go by flight: for Baba God will go before you; and the God of Israel Go be una rear guard.
See am, my worker will deal wisely. He Go be exalted and lifted up, and Go be very high.
Just as many were astonished at you (his appearance was marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men),
so he will cleanse many nations. Kings will shut dem mouths at him: for Dem go see that which had not been told dem; and Dem go understand that which dem had not heard.
Who has believe our message? To whom has the arm of Baba God been revealed?
For he grew up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of dry ground. He has no good looks or majesty. When we see him, E get no beauty that we should desire him.
He was despised, and rejected by men; a man of suffering, and acquainted with disease. He was despised as one from whom men hide dem face; and we didn’t respect him.
Surely he has borne our sickness, and carried our suffering; yet we considered him plagued, struck by God, and afflicted.
But he was pierced for our wrongdoings. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that bring our peace was on him; and by his wounds We be healed.
All we like sheep have gone astray. Everyone has turned to his own way; and Baba God has laid on him the wickedness of us all.
He was oppressed, yet when he was afflicted he didn’t open his mouth. As a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and as a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he didn’t open his mouth.
He was taken away by oppression and judgment; and as for his generation, who considered that he was cut off out of the land of the living and stricken for the disobedience of my people?
Dem made his grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in his death; although he had done no violence, nor was any deceit in his mouth.

Yet it pleased Baba God to bruise him. He has caused him to suffer. When you make his soul an offering for sin, he will see his offspring. He will prolong his days, and Baba God’s pleasure will prosper in his hand.
After the suffering of his soul, he will see the light and be satisfied. My righteous worker will justify many by the knowledge of imself; and he will bear dem iniquities.

So will I give him a portion with the great, and he will divide the plunder with the strong; because he poured out his soul to death, and was counted with the transgressors; yet he bore the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.

“Sing, barren, you who didn’t give birth; break out into singing, and cry aloud, you who No travail with pikin: for more are the pikin dem of the desolate than the pikin dem of the married wife,” says Baba God.
“Enlarge the place of una tent, and Make dem stretch out the curtains of una habitations; no spare: lengthen una cords, and strengthen una stakes.
For You go spread out on the right hand and on the left; and una offspring will possess the nations, and settle in desolate cities.
“No fear; for You go not be ashamed. No be confounded; for You go not be disappointed. For You go forget the shame of una youth; and the reproach of una widowhood you shall remember no more.
For una Maker is una husband; Baba God of Armies is his name. The Holy One of Israel is una Redeemer. He Go be call the God of the whole earth.
For Baba God has call you as a wife forsaken and grieved in spirit, even a wife of youth, when she is throw off,” says una God.
“For a small moment I have forsaken you; but with great mercies will I gather you.
In overflowing serious anger I hid my face from you for a moment; but with everlasting loving kindness I go have mercy on you,” says Baba God una Redeemer.
“For this is like the waters of Noah to me; for as I have sworn that the waters of Noah will no more go over the earth, so I have sworn that I go not be angry with you, nor rebuke you.
For the mountains may depart, and the hills be removed; but my loving kindness No go depart from you, and my covenant of peace No go be removed,” says Baba God who has mercy on you.
“You afflicted, tossed with storms, and not comforted, see am, I go set una stones in beautiful colors, and lay una foundations with sapphires.
I go make una pinnacles of rubies, una gates of sparkling jewels, and all una walls of precious stones.
All una pikin dem Go be taught by Baba God; and una pikin dem’s peace Go be great.
In righteousness You go be established. You go be far from oppression, for You go not be afraid; and far from terror, for it no go come near you.
See am, dem may gather together, but not by me. Anybody wey gathers together against You go fall because of you.
“See am, I have created the blacksmith who fans the coals into flame, and forges a weapon for his work; and I have created the destroyer to destroy.

No weapon that is formed against You go prevail; and You go condemn every tongue that rises against you in judgment. This is the heritage of Baba God’s workers, and dem righteousness is of me,” says Baba God.
“Hey! Come, Everybody wey thirsts, to the waters! Come, person wey has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
Why do you spend money for that which No be bread, and una labor for that which no dey satisfy? Listen diligently to me, and eat that which is good, and let una soul delight itself in richness.
Turn una ear, and come to me. Hear, and una soul will live: and I go make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David.
See am, I have given him for a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander to the peoples.
See am, you shall call a nation that you no know; and a nation that didn’t know you shall run to you, because of Baba God una God, and for the Holy One of Israel; for he has glorified you.”
Seek Baba God while he may be find. Call on him while he is near.
Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts. Make e return to Baba God, and he Go get mercy on him; and to our God, for he will freely pardon.
“For my thoughts No be una thoughts, and una ways No be my ways,” says Baba God.
“For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than una ways, and my thoughts than una thoughts.
For as the rain comes down and the snow from the sky, and no dey return there, but waters the earth, and makes it grow and bud, and gives seed to the sower and bread to the eater;
so is my word that goes out of my mouth: it No go return to me void, but it will accomplish that which I please, and it will prosper in the thing I sent it to do.
For you shall go out with gladness, and be led out with peace. The mountains and the hills will break out before you into singing; and all the trees of the fields will clap dem hands.
Instead of the thorn the cypress tree will come up; and instead of the brier the myrtle tree will come up: and it will make a name for Baba God, for an everlasting sign that No go be cut off.”
Baba God says, “Maintain justice, and do Wetin be right; for my salvation is near, and my righteousness will soon be revealed.
Blessed is the man wey do this, and the Son of Man who holds it fast; who keeps the Sabbath without profaning it, and keeps his hand from doing any evil.”
Let no foreigner, who has joined imself to Baba God, speak, saying, “Baba God will surely separate me from his people.” No let the eunuch say, “See am, I be a dry tree.”
For Baba God says, “To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, and choose the things that please me, and Hold am tight to my covenant:
I go give dem in my house and within my walls a memorial and a name better than of sons and of daughters. I go give dem an everlasting name, that No go be cut off.
Also the foreigners who join themselves to Baba God, to serve him, and to love Baba God’s name, to be his workers, Everybody wey keeps the Sabbath from profaning it, and holds fast my covenant;

I go bring these to my holy mountain, and make dem joyful in my house of prayer. Dem burnt offerings and dem sacrifices Go be accepted on my altar; for my house Go be call a house of prayer for all peoples.”
The Lord Baba God, who gathers the outcasts of Israel, says, “I go yet gather others to him, besides his own Wey be gathered.”
All you animals of the field, come to devour, all you animals in the forest.
His watchmen are blind. Dem be all without knowledge. Dem be all mute dogs. Dem no fit bark; dreaming, lying down, loving to slumber.
Yes, the dogs are greedy. Dem can never have enough. Dem be shepherds who no fit understand. Dem have all turned to dem own way, each one to his gain, from every quarter.
“Come,” say dem, “I go get wine, and We go fill ourselves with strong drink; and tomorrow Go be as today, great beyond measure.”
The righteous perish, and Nobody lays it to heart. Merciful men are taken away, and Nobody considers that the righteous is taken away from the evil.
He enters into peace. Dem rest in dem beds, each one who walks in his uprightness.
“But draw near here, you sons of a sorceress, you offspring of adulterers and prostitutes.
Whom do you mock? Against whom do you make a wide mouth, and stick out una tongue? No be you pikin dem of disobedience, and offspring of falsehood,
you who inflame unaself among the oaks, under every green tree; who kill the pikin dem in the valleys, under the clefts of the rocks?
Among the smooth stones of the valley is una portion; dem, Dem be una lot. You have even poured a drink offering to dem. You have offered an offering. Shall I be appeased for these things?
On a high and lofty mountain you have set una bed. You also go up there to offer sacrifice.

You have set up una memorial behind the doors and the posts; for you have exposed yourself to someone besides me, and have gone up; you have enlarged una bed, and made you a covenant with dem. You love Wetin you see on dem bed.
You go to the king with oil, and increased una perfumes, and sent una ambassadors far off, and degraded yourself even to Sheol.
You were wearied with the length of una ways; yet you didn’t say, ‘It is in vain.’ You find a reviving of una strength; so you no be faint.
“Whom have you dreaded and feared, so that you lie, and have not remember me, nor laid it to una heart? Haven’t I held my peace for a long time, and you no fear me?
I go declare una righteousness; and as for una works, Dem go not benefit you.

When you cry, let those whom you have gathered deliver you; but the wind will take dem. a breath will carry dem all away: but person wey takes refuge in me will possess the land, and will inherit my holy mountain.”
He will say, “Build up, build up, prepare the way! Remove the stumbling-block out of the way of my people.”

For thus says the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I live in the high and holy place, with him also Wey be of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.
For I go not contend forever, neither will I be always angry; for the spirit would faint before me, and the souls whom I have made.
I was angry because of the wickedness of his covetousness, and struck him; I hid myself and was angry; and he go on backsliding in the way of his heart.
I have seen his ways, and will heal him: I go lead him also, and restore comforts to him and to his mourners.
I create the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace, to him Wey be far off and to him Wey be near,” says Baba God; “and I go heal dem.”
But the wicked are like the troubled sea; for it no fit rest, and its waters throw up mire and mud.
“E get no peace”, says my God, “for the wicked.”
“Cry aloud, no spare. Lift up una voice like a trumpet. Declare to my people dem disobedience, and to the house of Jacob dem sins.

Yet dem seek me daily, and delight to know my ways. As a nation that did righteousness, and didn’t forsake the ordinance of dem God, dem ask of me righteous judgments. Dem delight to draw near to God.
‘Why have we fasted,’ say dem, ‘and you no see? Why have we afflicted our soul, and you no notice?’ “See am, in the day of una fast you find pleasure, and oppress all una laborers.
See am, you fast for strife and contention, and to strike with the fist of wickedness. You no fast today so as to make una voice to be heard on high.

Is this the fast that I have chosen? A day for a man to humble his soul? Is it to bow down his head like a reed, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under imself? Will you call this a fast, and an acceptable day to Baba God?
“No be this the fast that I have chosen: to release the bonds of wickedness, to undo the straps of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free, and that you break every yoke?

No be it to distribute una bread to the hungry, and that you bring the poor Wey be throw out to una house? When you see the naked, that you cover him; and that you not hide yourself from una own flesh?
Then una light will break out as the morning, and una healing will appear sharp-sharp; then una righteousness shall go before you; and Baba God’s glory Go be una rear guard.
Then You go call, and Baba God will answer; You go cry for help, and he will say, ‘Here I be.’ “If you take away from among you the yoke, finger pointing, and speaking wickedly;
and if you pour out una soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul: then una light will rise in darkness, and una obscurity Go be as the noonday;
and Baba God will guide you continually, and satisfy una soul in dry places, and make una bones strong; and you go be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters no fail.
People wey go be of you shall build the old waste places; you shall raise up the foundations of many generations; and you go be call Repairer of the Breach, Restorer of Paths with Dwellings.

“If you turn away una foot from the Sabbath, from doing una pleasure on my holy day; and call the Sabbath a delight, and the holy of Baba God honorable; and shall honor it, not doing una own ways, nor finding una own pleasure, nor speaking una own words:
then you shall delight yourself in Baba God; and I go make you to ride on the high places of the earth; and I go feed you with the heritage of Jacob una father:” for Baba God’s mouth has spoken it.
See am, Baba God’s hand No be shortened, that it no fit save; nor his ear dull, that it no fit hear.
But una iniquities have separated you and una God, and una sins have hidden his face from you, so that he No go hear.
For una hands are defiled with blood, and una fingers with wickedness. Una lips have spoken lies. Una tongue mutters wickedness.
Nobody sues in righteousness, and Nobody pleads in truth. Dem trust in vanity, and speak lies. Dem conceive mischief, and give birth to wickedness.
Dem hatch adders’ eggs, and weave the spider’s web. Person wey eats of dem eggs dies; and that which is crushed breaks out into a viper.
Dem webs no go become garments. Dem no go cover themselves with dem works. Dem works are works of wickedness, and acts of violence are in dem hands.
Dem feet run to evil, and dem hurry to shed innocent blood. Dem thoughts are thoughts of wickedness. desolation and destruction are in dem paths.
Dem no know the way of peace; and E get no justice in dem ways. Dem have made crooked paths for themselves; Anybody wey goes in dem no dey know peace.
So is justice far from us, and righteousness no dey overtake us. We look for light, but see darkness; for brightness, but we walk in obscurity.
We grope for the wall like the blind. Yes, we grope as people wey have no eyes. We stumble at noon as if it were twilight. Among people Wey strong, We be like dead men.
We all roar like bears, and moan bitterly like doves. We look for justice, but E get none; for salvation, but it is far off from us.
For our wrongdoings are multiplied before you, and our sins testify against us; for our wrongdoings are with us, and as for our iniquities, we know dem:
transgressing and denying Baba God, and turning away from following our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood.
Justice is turned away backward, and righteousness stands far away; for truth has fallen in the street, and uprightness no fit enter.
Yes, truth is lacking; and person wey departs from evil makes imself a prey. Baba God see it, and it displeased him that there was no justice.
He see that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor. So his own arm bring salvation to him; and his righteousness sustained him.
He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation on his head. He put on garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a mantle.
According to dem deeds, he will repay as appropriate, serious anger to his adversaries, recompense to his enemies; he will repay the islands dem due.
So shall dem fear Baba God’s name from the west, and his glory from the rising of the sun; for he will come as a rushing stream, which Baba God’s breath drives.
“A Redeemer will come to Zion, and to people wey turn from disobedience in Jacob,” says Baba God.

“As for me, this is my covenant with dem,” says Baba God. “My Spirit Wey be on you, and my words which I have put in una mouth, no go depart out of una mouth, nor out of the mouth of una offspring, nor out of the mouth of una offspring’s offspring,” says Baba God, “from from now and forever.”
“Arise, shine; for una light has come, and Baba God’s glory has risen on you.
For, see am, darkness will cover the earth, and thick darkness the peoples; but Baba God will arise on you, and his glory go be seen on you.
Nations will come to una light, and kings to the brightness of una rising.
“Lift up una eyes all around, and see: dem all gather themselves together. Dem come to you. Una sons will come from far away, and una daughters Go be carried in arms.
Then you shall see and be radiant, and una heart will thrill and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea Go be turned to you. The wealth of the nations will come to you.
A plenty people of camels will cover you, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah. All from Sheba will come. Dem go bring gold and frankincense, and will proclaim the praises of Baba God.
All the flocks of Kedar Go be gathered together to you. The rams of Nebaioth will serve you. Dem go be accepted as offerings on my altar; and I go beautify my glorious house.
“Wey be these who fly as a cloud, and as the doves to dem windows?

Surely the islands will wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring una sons from far, dem silver and dem gold with dem, for the name of Baba God una God, and for the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you.
“Foreigners will build up una walls, and dem kings will serve you: for in my serious anger I struck you, but in my favor I have had mercy on you.
Una gates also go be open continually; dem no go be shut day nor night; that men may bring to you the wealth of the nations, and dem kings led captive.
For that nation and kingdom that No go serve you shall perish; yes, those nations go be utterly wasted.
“The glory of Lebanon shall come to you, the cypress tree, the pine, and the box tree together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I go make the place of my feet glorious.

The sons of people wey afflicted You go come bowing to you; and all people wey despised You go bow themselves down at the soles of una feet. Dem go call you Baba God’s City, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
“Whereas you Don dey forsaken and hated, so that Nobody passed through you, I go make you an eternal excellency, a gladness of many generations.
You go also drink the milk of the nations, and will nurse from royal breasts. Then You go know that I, Baba God, am una Savior, una Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
For brass I go bring gold; for iron I go bring silver; for wood, brass, and for stones, iron. I go also make peace una governor, and righteousness una ruler.
Violence shall no more be heard in una land, nor desolation or destruction within una borders; but You go call una walls Salvation, and una gates Praise.
The sun Go be no more una light by day; nor will the brightness of the moon give light to you, but Baba God Go be una everlasting light, and una God Go be una glory.
Una sun No go go down any more, nor will una moon withdraw itself; for Baba God Go be una everlasting light, and the days of una mourning will end.
Then una people will all be righteous. Dem go inherit the land forever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.
The little one will become a thousand, and the small one a strong nation. I, Baba God, will do this sharp-sharp in its time.”

The Lord Baba God’s Spirit is on me; because Baba God has anointed me to preach better news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to people Wey bound;
to proclaim the year of Baba God’s favor, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all who mourn;

to provide for people wey mourn in Zion, to give to dem a garland for ashes, the oil of gladness for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that dem may be call trees of righteousness, the planting of Baba God, that he may be glorified.
Dem go rebuild the old ruins. Dem go raise up the places long devastated. Dem go repair the ruined cities, that Don dey devastated for many generations.
Strangers will stand and feed una flocks, and foreigners will work una fields and una vineyards.
But You go be call Baba God’s priests. Men will call you the workers of our God. You go eat the wealth of the nations, and You go boast in dem glory.
Instead of una shame You go have double. Instead of dishonor, Dem go glad well-well in dem portion. So in dem land, Dem go possess double. Everlasting gladness Go be to dem.
“For I, Baba God, love justice. I hate robbery and wickedness. I go give dem dem reward in truth, and I go make an everlasting covenant with dem.
Dem offspring Go be known among the nations, and dem offspring among the peoples. All who see dem will acknowledge dem, that Dem be the offspring which Baba God has blessed.”

I go greatly glad well-well in Baba God! My soul Go be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation. He has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks imself with a garland, and as a bride adorns sheself with her jewels.
For as the earth produces its bud, and as the garden causes the things that are sown in it to spring up; so the Lord Baba God will cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations.
For Zion’s sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem’s sake I go not rest, until her righteousness shines out like the dawn, and her salvation like a burning lamp.
The nations will see una righteousness, and all kings una glory, and You go be call by a new name, which Baba God‘s mouth will name.
You go also be a crown of beauty in Baba God‘s hand, and a royal diadem in una God‘s hand.
You go not be call Forsaken any more; nor will una land be call Desolate any more: but You go be call Hephzibah, and una land Beulah; for Baba God delights in you, and una land Go be married.
For as a young man marries a virgin, so una sons will marry you. As a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so una God will glad well-well over you.
I have set watchmen on una walls, Jerusalem. Dem go never be silent day nor night. You who call on Baba God, take no rest,
and give him no rest, until he establishes, and until he makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.

Baba God has sworn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength, “Surely I go no more give una grain to be chop for una enemies; and foreigners No go drink una new wine, for which you have labored;
but people wey have harvested it will eat it, and praise Baba God; and people wey have gathered it will drink it in the courts of my sanctuary.”
Go through, go through the gates! Prepare the way of the people! Build up, build up the highway! Gather out the stones! Lift up a banner for the peoples.
See am, Baba God has proclaimed to the end of the earth, “Say to the daughter of Zion, ‘See am, una salvation comes. See am, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.’”
Dem go call dem The holy people, Baba God’s redeemed. You go be call Sought out, A city not forsaken.

Wey be this who comes from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? Who this Wey be glorious in his clothing, marching in the greatness of his strength? “It is I who speak in righteousness, mighty to save.”
Why is una clothing red, and una garments like him who treads in the wine vat?

“I have trodden the wine press alone; and of the peoples, Nobody was with me: Yes, I trod dem in my anger, and trampled dem in my serious anger. Dem lifeblood is sprinkled on my garments, and I have stained all my clothing.
For the day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redeemed has come.
I looked, and there was Nobody to help; and I wondered that there was Nobody to uphold: so my own arm bring salvation to me; and my own serious anger upheld me.
I trod down the peoples in my anger, and made dem drunk in my serious anger, and I poured out dem lifeblood on the earth.”

I go tell of the loving kindnesses of Baba God and the praises of Baba God, according to all that Baba God has given to us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel, which he has given to dem according to his mercies, and according to the plenty people of his loving kindnesses.
For he talk say, “Surely, Dem be my people, pikin dem who No go deal falsely;” so he became dem Savior.
In all dem suffering he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved dem. In his love and in his pity he redeemed dem. He bore dem, and carried dem all the days of old.
But dem rebelled, and grieved his holy Spirit. So he turned and became dem enemy, and he imself fought against dem.
Then he remember the days of old, Moses and his people, saying, “Where is person wey bring dem up out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? Where is person wey put his Holy Spirit among dem?”
Who caused his glorious arm to be at Moses’ right hand? Who divided the waters before dem, to make imself an everlasting name?
Who led dem through the depths, like a horse in the wilderness, so that dem didn’t stumble?
As the livestock that go down into the valley, Baba God’s Spirit caused dem to rest. So you led una people, to make yourself a glorious name.
Look down from heaven, and see from the habitation of una holiness and of una glory. Where are una zeal and una mighty acts? The yearning of una heart and una compassion is restrained toward me.
For You be our Father, though Abraham no dey know us, and Israel No dey acknowledge us. You, Baba God, are our Father. Our Redeemer from everlasting is una name.
O Baba God, why do you make us wander from una ways, and harden our heart from una fear? Return for una workers’ sake, the tribes of una inheritance.
Una holy people possessed it but a little while. Our adversaries have trodden down una sanctuary.
We have become like those over whom you never ruled, like people wey No be call by una name.
Oh that you would tear the heavens, that you would come down, that the mountains might quake at una presence.
As when fire kindles the brushwood, and the fire causes the water to boil; Make una name known to una adversaries, that the nations may tremble at una presence!
When you did awesome things which we didn’t look for, you come down, and the mountains quaked at una presence.
For from of old men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, nor has the eye seen a God besides you, who works for him who waits for him.
You meet him who rejoices and does righteousness, people wey remember you in una ways. See am, you were angry, and we sinned. We Don dey in sin for a long time. Shall we be saved?
For we have all become like one Wey be unclean, and all our righteousness is like a polluted garment. We all fade like a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, take us away.
E get Nobody who calls on una name, who stirs imself up to take hold of you; for you have hidden una face from us, and have consumed us by means of our iniquities.
But now, Baba God, You be our Father. We be the clay, and you our potter. We all are the work of una hand.
No be furious, Baba God, and no remember wickedness forever. Look and see, we beg you, We be all una people.
Una holy cities have become a wilderness. Zion has become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.
Our holy and our beautiful house, where our fathers praised you, is burned with fire; and all our pleasant places are laid waste.
Will you hold yourself back for these things, Baba God? Will you keep silent, and punish us very severely?
“I be inquired of by people wey didn’t ask. I be find by people wey didn’t seek me. I talk say, ‘See me, see me,’ to a nation that No be call by my name.
I have spread out my hands all day to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that No be good, after dem own thoughts;
a people who provoke me to my face continually, sacrificing in gardens, and burning incense on bricks;
who sit among the graves, and spend nights in secret places; who eat pig’s meat, and broth of abominable things is in dem vessels;
who say, ‘Stay by yourself, no come near to me, for I be holier than you.’ These are smoke in my nose, a fire that burns all day.
“See am, it is written before me: I go not keep silence, but will repay, yes, I go repay into dem bosom,

una own iniquities, and the iniquities of una fathers together”, says Baba God, “who have burned incense on the mountains, and blasphemed me on the hills. So I go first measure dem work into dem bosom.”
Baba God says, “As the new wine is find in the cluster, and one says, ‘No destroy it, for a blessing is in it:’ so will I do for my workers’ sake, that I may not destroy dem all.
I go bring offspring out of Jacob, and out of Judah an inheritor of my mountains. My chosen will inherit it, and my workers will live there.
Sharon Go be a fold of flocks, and the valley of Achor a place for herds to lie down in, for my people who have sought me.
“But you who forsake Baba God, who forget my holy mountain, who prepare a table for Fortune, and who fill up mixed wine to Destiny;

I go destine you to the sword, and You go all bow down to the slaughter; because when I call, you didn’t answer. When I spoke, you didn’t listen; but you did that which was evil in my eyes, and chose that in which I didn’t delight.”

So thus says the Lord Baba God, “See am, my workers will eat, but You go be hungry; see am, my workers will drink, but You go be thirsty. See am, my workers will glad well-well, but You go be disappointed;
See am, my workers will sing for gladness of heart, but You go cry for sorrow of heart, and will wail for anguish of spirit.
You go leave una name for a curse to my chosen; and the Lord Baba God will kill you. He will call his workers by another name,

so that person wey blesses imself in the earth will bless imself in the God of truth; and person wey swears in the earth will swear by the God of truth; because the former troubles are forgotten, and because Dem be hidden from my eyes.
“For, see am, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things No go be remember, nor come into mind.
But be glad and glad well-well forever in that which I create; for, see am, I create Jerusalem to be a delight, and her people a gladness.
I go glad well-well in Jerusalem, and delight in my people; and the voice of weeping and the voice of crying Go be heard in her no more.

“No more will there be an infant who only lives a few days, nor an old man who has not filled his days; for the pikin will die one hundred years old, and the sinner being one hundred years old Go be accursed.
Dem go build houses, and inhabit dem. Dem go plant vineyards, and eat dem fruit.
Dem go not build, and another inhabit. Dem go not plant, and another eat: for the days of my people Go be like the days of a tree, and my chosen will long enjoy the work of dem hands.
Dem go not labor in vain, nor give birth for calamity; for Dem be the offspring of Baba God’s blessed, and dem descendants with dem.
It will happen that, before dem call, I go answer; and while Dem be yet speaking, I go hear.
The wolf and the lamb will feed together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox. Dust Go be the serpent’s chop. Dem go not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain,” says Baba God.
Baba God says, “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build to me? Where will I rest?
For my hand has made all these things, and so all these things come to be,” says Baba God: “but to this man will I look, even to person Wey poor and of a contrite spirit, and who trembles at my word.

Person wey kills an ox is as person wey kills a man; person wey sacrifices a lamb, as person wey breaks a dog’s neck; person wey offers an offering, as person wey offers pig’s blood; person wey burns frankincense, as person wey blesses an idol. Yes, dem have chosen dem own ways, and dem soul delights in dem abominations:

I also will choose dem delusions, and will bring dem fears on dem; because when I call, Nobody answer; when I spoke, dem didn’t listen; but dem did that which was evil in my eyes, and chose that in which I didn’t delight.”
