Hear Baba God’s word, you who tremble at his word: “Una brothers who hate you, who throw you out for my name’s sake, have talk say, ‘Let Baba God be glorified, that we may see una gladness;’ but it is people wey go be disappointed.
A voice of tumult from the city, a voice from the temple, a voice of Baba God that repays his enemies Wetin dem deserve.
“Before she travailed, she give birth. Before her pain come, she delivered a son.
Who has heard of such a thing? Who has seen such things? Shall a land be born in one day? Shall a nation be born at once? For as soon as Zion travailed, she give birth to her pikin dem.
Shall I bring to the birth, and not cause to be delivered?” says Baba God. “Shall I who cause to give birth shut the womb?” says una God.
“Glad well-well with Jerusalem, and be glad for her, all you who love her. Glad well-well for gladness with her, all you who mourn over her;
that you may nurse and be satisfied at the comforting breasts; that you may drink deeply, and be delighted with the abundance of her glory.”

For Baba God says, “See am, I go extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the nations like an overflowing stream; and You go nurse. You go be carried on her side, and Go be dandled on her knees.
As one whom his mother comforts, so will I comfort you. You go be comforted in Jerusalem.”
You go see it, and una heart shall glad well-well, and una bones will flourish like the tender grass. Baba God’s hand Go be known among his workers; and he Go get indignation against his enemies.
For, see am, Baba God will come with fire, and his chariots Go be like the whirlwind; to render his anger with fierceness, and his rebuke with flames of fire.
For Baba God will execute judgment by fire and by his sword on all flesh; and those slain by Baba God Go be many.

“People wey sanctify themselves and purify themselves to go to the gardens, behind one in the middle, eating pig’s meat, abominable things, and the mouse, dem shall come to an end together,” says Baba God.
“For I know dem works and dem thoughts. The time comes that I go gather people for everywhere and languages, and Dem go come, and will see my glory.

“I go set a sign among dem, and I go send people wey escape of dem to the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, who draw the bow, to Tubal and Javan, to far-away islands, who have not heard my fame, nor have seen my glory; and dem shall declare my glory among the nations.

Dem shall bring all una brothers out of all the nations for an offering to Baba God, on horses, in chariots, in litters, on mules, and on camels, to my holy mountain Jerusalem, says Baba God, as the pikin dem of Israel bring dem offering in a clean vessel into Baba God’s house.
Of dem I go also select priests and Levites,” says Baba God.
“For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I go make, shall remain before me,” says Baba God, “so una offspring and una name shall remain.
It shall happen that from one new moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh will come to worship before me,” says Baba God.
“Dem go go out, and look at the dead bodies of the men who have transgressed against me; for dem worm No go die, nor will dem fire be quenched, and Dem go be loathsome to all mankind.”
The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
Baba God’s word come to him in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.

It come also in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, to the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah, the son of Josiah, king of Judah, to the carrying away of Jerusalem captive in the fifth month.
Now Baba God’s word come to me, saying,
“Before I formed you in the womb, I know you. Before you were born, I sanctified you. I have appointed you a prophet to the nations.”
Then I talk say, “Ah, Lord Baba God! See am, I no know how to speak; for I be a pikin.”
But Baba God talk say to me, “No say, ‘I be a pikin;’ for you must go to whomever I send you, and you must say Anything wey I command you.
No fear because of dem, for I be with you to rescue you,” says Baba God.
Then Baba God stretched out his hand, and touched my mouth. Then Baba God talk say to me, “See am, I have put my words in una mouth.
See am, I have today set you over the nations and over the kingdoms, to uproot and to tear down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant.”
Moreover Baba God’s word come to me, saying, “Jeremiah, what do you see?” I talk say, “I see a branch of an almond tree.”
Then Baba God talk say to me, “You have seen well; for I watch over my word to perform it.”
Baba God’s word come to me the second time, saying, “What do you see?” I talk say, “I see a boiling cauldron; and it is tipping away from the north.”
Then Baba God talk say to me, “Out of the north, evil will break out on all the inhabitants of the land.

For, see am, I go call all the families of the kingdoms of the north,” says Baba God. “Dem go come, and Dem go each set his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem, and against all its walls all around, and against all the cities of Judah.
I go utter my judgments against dem concerning all dem wickedness, in that dem have forsaken me, and have burned incense to other gods, and worshiped the works of dem own hands.
“You so put una belt on una waist, arise, and say to dem all that I command you. No be dismayed at dem, lest I dismay you before dem.

For, see am, I have made you today a fortified city, an iron pillar, and bronze walls, against the whole land, against the kings of Judah, against its princes, against its priests, and against the people of the land.
Dem go fight against you, but Dem go not prevail against you; for I be with you”, says Baba God, “to rescue you.”
Baba God’s word come to me, saying,

“Go, and proclaim in the ears of Jerusalem, saying, ‘Baba God says, “I remember for you the kindness of una youth, the love of una weddings; how you go after me in the wilderness, in a land that No be sown.
Israel was holiness to Baba God, the first fruits of his increase. All who devour him go be held guilty. Evil shall come on dem,”’ says Baba God.”
Hear Baba God’s word, O house of Jacob, and all the families of the house of Israel!
Baba God says, “What unrighteousness have una fathers find in me, that dem have gone far from me, and have walked after worthless vanity, and have become worthless?

Dem didn’t say, ‘Where is Baba God who bring us up out of the land of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness, through a land of deserts and of pits, through a land of drought and of the shadow of death, through a land that Nobody passed through, and where no man lived?’
I bring you into a plentiful land, to eat its fruit and its goodness; but when you entered, you defiled my land, and made my heritage an abomination.

The priests didn’t say, ‘Where is Baba God?’ and people wey handle the law didn’t know me. The rulers also transgressed against me, and the prophets prophesied by Baal, and follow things that No profit.
“So I go yet contend with you,” says Baba God, “and I go contend with una pikin dem’s pikin dem.
For pass over to the islands of Kittim, and see; and send to Kedar, and consider diligently; and see if there Don dey such a thing.
Has a nation changed its gods, which really are no gods? But my people have changed dem glory for that which No dey profit.
“Be astonished, you heavens, at this, and be horribly afraid. Be very desolate,” says Baba God.
“For my people have committed two evils: dem have forsaken me, the spring of living waters, and cut dem out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.
Is Israel a slave? Is he born into slavery? Why has he become a captive?
The young lions have roared at him, and yelled. Dem have made his land waste. His cities are burned up, without inhabitant.
The pikin dem also of Memphis and Tahpanhes have broken the crown of una head.
“Haven’t you bring this on yourself, in that you have forsaken Baba God una God, when he led you by the way?
Now what do you gain by going to Egypt, to drink the waters of the Shihor? Or why do you to go on the way to Assyria, to drink the waters of the River?

“Una own wickedness will correct you, and una backsliding will rebuke you. Know so and see that it is an evil and bitter thing, that you have forsaken Baba God una God, and that my fear No be in you,” says the Lord, Baba God of Armies.
“For long ago I broke off una yoke, and burst una bonds. You talk say, ‘I go not serve;’ for on every high hill and under every green tree you bowed yourself, playing the prostitute.
Yet I had planted you a noble vine, a pure and faithful seed. How then have you turned into the degenerate branches of a foreign vine to me?
For though you wash yourself with lye, and use much soap, yet una wickedness is marked before me,” says the Lord Baba God.
“How can you say, ‘I be not defiled. I have not gone after the Baals’? See una way in the valley. Know Wetin you have done. You be a swift dromedary traversing her ways;
a wild donkey used to the wilderness, that sniffs the wind in her craving. When she is in heat, who can turn her away? All people wey seek her No go weary themselves. In her month, Dem go find her.
“Keep una feet from being bare, and una throat from thirst. But you talk say, ‘It is in vain. No, for I have love strangers, and I go go after dem.’
As the thief is ashamed when he is find, so is the house of Israel ashamed; dem, dem kings, dem princes, and dem priests, and dem prophets;
who tell wood, ‘You be my father;’ and a stone, ‘You have given birth to me:’ for dem have turned dem back to me, and not dem face; but in the time of dem trouble Dem go say, ‘Arise, and save us.’
“But where are una gods that you have made for unaself? Make dem arise, if dem can save you in the time of una trouble: for you have as many gods as you have towns, O Judah.
“Why will you contend with me? You all have transgressed against me,” says Baba God.
“I have struck una pikin dem in vain. Dem received no correction. Una own sword has devoured una prophets, like a destroying lion.
Generation, consider Baba God’s word. Have I been a wilderness to Israel? Or a land of thick darkness? Why do my people say, ‘We have broken loose. We go come to you no more?’
“Can a virgin forget her ornaments, or a bride her attire? Yet my people have forgotten me for days without number.
How well you prepare una way to seek love! So you have even taught the wicked women una ways.
Also the blood of the souls of the innocent poor is find in una skirts. You No find dem breaking in; but it is because of all these things.
“Yet you talk say, ‘I be innocent. Surely his anger has turned away from me.’ “See am, I go judge you, because you say, ‘I have not sinned.’
Why do you go about so much to change una ways? You go be ashamed of Egypt also, as you were ashamed of Assyria.
You go also leave that place with una hands on una head; for Baba God has rejected those in whom you trust, and you no go prosper with dem.

“Dem say, ‘If a man puts away his wife, and she goes from him, and becomes another man’s, should he return to her again?’ Wouldn’t that land be greatly polluted? But you have played the prostitute with many lovers; yet return again to me,” says Baba God.

“Lift up una eyes to the bare heights, and see! Where have you not been lain with? You have sat waiting for dem by the road, as an Arabian in the wilderness. You have polluted the land with una prostitution and with una wickedness.
So the showers Don dey withheld, and there Don dey no latter rain; yet you have a prostitute’s forehead. You refused to be ashamed.
Will you not from this time cry to me, ‘My Father, You be the guide of my youth?’
“‘Will he retain his anger forever? Will he keep it to the end?’ See am, you have spoken and have done evil things, and have had una way.”

Moreover, Baba God talk say to me in the days of Josiah the king, “Have you seen that which backsliding Israel has done? She has gone up on every high mountain and under every green tree, and has played the prostitute there.
I talk say after she had done all these things, ‘She will return to me;’ but she didn’t return; and her treacherous sister Judah see it.

I see when, for this very cause, that backsliding Israel had committed adultery, I had put her away and given her a bill of divorce, yet treacherous Judah, her sister, had no fear; but she also go and played the prostitute.
Because she take her prostitution lightly, the land was polluted, and she committed adultery with stones and with wood.
Yet for all this her treacherous sister, Judah, has not come back to me with her whole heart, but only in pretense,” says Baba God.
Baba God talk say to me, “Backsliding Israel has shown sheself more righteous than treacherous Judah.

Go, and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, ‘Return, you backsliding Israel,’ says Baba God; ‘I go not look in anger on you; for I be merciful,’ says Baba God. ‘I go not keep anger forever.

Only acknowledge una wickedness, that you have transgressed against Baba God una God, and have scattered una ways to the strangers under every green tree, and you have not obeyed my voice,’ says Baba God.”
“Return, backsliding pikin dem,” says Baba God; “for I be a husband to you. I go take one of you from a city, and two from a family, and I go bring you to Zion.
I go give you shepherds according to my heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.

It will come to pass, when You be multiplied and increased in the land, in those days,” says Baba God, “Dem go no longer say, ‘the ark of Baba God’s covenant!’ It No go come to mind. Dem no go remember it. Dem no go miss it, nor will another be made.
At that time Dem go call Jerusalem ‘Baba God’s Throne;’ and all the nations Go be gathered to it, to Baba God’s name, to Jerusalem. Dem go no longer walk after the stubbornness of dem evil heart.
In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and Dem go come together out of the land of the north to the land that I give for an inheritance to una fathers.

“But I talk say, ‘How I desire to put you among the pikin dem, and give you a pleasant land, a goodly heritage of the armies of the nations!’ and I talk say, ‘You shall call me “My Father”, and no go turn away from following me.’
“Surely as a wife treacherously departs from her husband, so you have dealt treacherously with me, house of Israel,” says Baba God.
A voice is heard on the bare heights, the weeping and the petitions of the pikin dem of Israel; because dem have perverted dem way, dem have forgotten Baba God dem God.
Return, you backsliding pikin dem, and I go heal una backsliding. “See am, we have come to you; for You be Baba God our God.
Truly in vain is help from the hills, the tumult on the mountains. Truly the salvation of Israel is in Baba God our God.
But the shameful thing has devoured the labor of our fathers from our youth, dem flocks and dem herds, dem sons and dem daughters.

Make we lie down in our shame, and let our confusion cover us; for we have sinned against Baba God our God, we and our fathers, from our youth even to this day. We have not obeyed Baba God our God’s voice.”
“If You go return, Israel,” says Baba God, “if You go return to me, and if You go put away una abominations out of my sight; then you no go be removed;
and you shall swear, ‘As Baba God lives,’ in truth, in justice, and in righteousness. The nations shall bless themselves in him, and in him shall dem glory.”
For Baba God says to the men of Judah and to Jerusalem, “Break up una fallow ground, and no sow among thorns.

Circumcise unaself to Baba God, and take away the foreskins of una heart, you men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem; lest my serious anger go out like fire, and burn so that Nobody can quench it, because of the evil of una doings.
Declare in Judah, and publish in Jerusalem; and say, ‘Blow the trumpet in the land!’ Cry aloud and say, ‘Assemble unaself! Make we go into the fortified cities!’
Set up a standard toward Zion. Flee for safety! No wait; for I go bring evil from the north, and a great destruction.”
A lion has gone up from his thicket, and a destroyer of nations; he is on his way, he has gone out from his place, to make una land desolate, that una cities be laid waste, without inhabitant.
For this clothe yourself with sackcloth, lament and wail; for the fierce anger of Baba God hasn’t turned back from us.
“It shall happen at that day,” says Baba God, “that the heart of the king shall perish, and the heart of the princes; and the priests go be astonished, and the prophets shall wonder.”
Then I talk say, “Ah, Lord Baba God! Surely you have greatly deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, ‘You go get peace;’ whereas the sword reaches to the heart.”
At that time it Go be talk say to this people and to Jerusalem, “A hot wind from the bare heights in the wilderness toward the daughter of my people, not to winnow, nor to cleanse;
a full wind from these shall come for me. Now I go also utter judgments against dem.”
See am, he shall come up as clouds, and his chariots go be as the whirlwind: his horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us! For We be ruined.
Jerusalem, wash una heart from wickedness, that you may be saved. How long shall una evil thoughts lodge within you?
For a voice declares from Dan, and publishes evil from the hills of Ephraim:
“Tell the nations; see am, publish against Jerusalem, ‘Watchers come from a far country, and raise dem voice against the cities of Judah.
As keepers of a field, Dem be against her all around, because she Don dey rebellious against me,’” says Baba God.
“Una way and una doings have bring these things to you. This is una wickedness; for it is bitter, for it reaches to una heart.”
My anguish, my anguish! I be pained at my very heart; my heart is disquieted in me; I no fit hold my peace; because you have heard, O my soul, the sound of the trumpet, the alarm of war.
Destruction on destruction is cried; for the whole land is laid waste: suddenly are my tents destroyed, and my curtains in a moment.
How long shall I see the standard, and hear the sound of the trumpet?
“For my people are foolish, dem no know me. Dem be foolish pikin dem, and dem have no understanding. Dem be skillful in doing evil, but to do good dem have no knowledge.”
I see the earth, and, see am, it was waste and void; and the heavens, and dem had no light.
I see the mountains, and see am, dem trembled, and all the hills moved back and forth.
I see, and see am, there was no man, and all the birds of the sky had fled.
I see, and see am, the fruitful field was a wilderness, and all its cities were broken down at the presence of Baba God, before his fierce anger.
For Baba God says, “The whole land go be a desolation; yet will I not make a full end.
For this the earth will mourn, and the heavens above be black; because I have spoken it, I have purposed it, and I have not repented, neither will I turn back from it.”
Every city flees for the noise of the horsemen and archers; dem go into the thickets, and climb up on the rocks: every city is forsaken, and not a man dwells inside am.

You, when You be made desolate, what will you do? Though you clothe yourself with scarlet, though you deck yourself with ornaments of gold, though you enlarge una eyes with makeup, you make yourself beautiful in vain. Una lovers despise you. Dem seek una life.

For I have heard a voice as of a woman in travail, the anguish as of her wey dey give birth to her first pikin, the voice of the daughter of Zion, who gasps for breath, who spreads her hands, saying, “Woe is me now! For my soul faints before the murderers.”
“Run back and forth through the streets of Jerusalem, and see now, and know, and seek in its wide places, if you can find a man, if E get any wey do justly, who seeks truth; and I go pardon her.
Though dem say, ‘As Baba God lives;’ surely dem swear falsely.”

O Baba God, no una eyes look on truth? You have stricken dem, but dem No be grieved. You have consumed dem, but dem have refused to receive correction. Dem have made dem faces harder than a rock. Dem have refused to return.
Then I talk say, “Surely these are poor. Dem be foolish; for dem no know the way of Baba God, nor the law of dem God.
I go go to the great men, and will speak to dem; for dem know the way of Baba God, and the law of dem God.” But these with one accord have broken the yoke, and burst the bonds.

So a lion out of the forest shall kill dem, a wolf of the evenings shall destroy dem, a leopard shall watch against dem cities; Everybody wey goes out there go be torn in pieces; because dem wrongdoings are many, and dem backsliding is increased.

“How can I pardon you? Una pikin dem have forsaken me, and sworn by Wetin be no gods. When I had fed dem to the full, dem committed adultery, and assembled themselves in troops at the prostitutes’ houses.
Dem were as fed horses roaming at large: everyone neighed after his neighbor’s wife.
Shouldn’t I punish dem for these things?” says Baba God; “and shouldn’t my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?
“Go up on her walls, and destroy; but no make a full end. Take away her branches; for dem No be Baba God’s.
For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me,” says Baba God.
Dem have denied Baba God, and talk say, “It No be he; neither shall evil come on us; neither shall we see sword nor famine.
The prophets shall become wind, and the word No be in dem. Thus shall it be done to dem.”
So Baba God, the God of Armies says, “Because you speak this word, see am, I go make my words in una mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour dem.
See am, I go bring a nation on you from far, house of Israel,” says Baba God. “It is a mighty nation. It is an ancient nation, a nation whose language you no know, neither understand Wetin dem say.
Dem quiver is an open tomb, Dem be all mighty men.

Dem shall eat up una harvest, and una bread, which una sons and una daughters should eat. Dem shall eat up una flocks and una herds. Dem shall eat up una vines and una fig trees. Dem shall beat down una fortified cities, in which you trust, with the sword.
“But even in those days,” says Baba God, “I go not make a full end with you.

It will happen, when you say, ‘Why has Baba God our God done all these things to us?’ Then you shall say to dem, ‘Just like you have forsaken me, and served foreign gods in una land, so you shall serve strangers in a land that No be yours.’
“Declare this in the house of Jacob, and publish it in Judah, saying,
‘Hear now this, foolish people, and without understanding; who have eyes, and no see; who have ears, and no hear:

No you fear me?’ says Baba God ‘No go you tremble at my presence, who have placed the sand for the bound of the sea, by a perpetual decree, that it no fit pass it? and though its waves toss themselves, yet dem no fit prevail; though dem roar, yet dem no fit pass over it.’
“But this people has a revolting and a rebellious heart; dem have revolted and gone.
Neither do dem say in dem heart, ‘Make we now fear Baba God our God, wey dey give rain, both the former and the latter, in its season; who preserves to us the appointed weeks of the harvest.’
“Una iniquities have turned away these things, and una sins have withheld good from you.
For among my people are find wicked men. Dem watch, as fowlers lie in wait. Dem set a trap. Dem catch men.
As a cage is full of birds, so are dem houses full of deceit. So dem have become great, and grew rich.
Dem have grown fat. Dem shine; yes, dem excel in deeds of wickedness. Dem no plead the cause, the cause of the fatherless, that dem may prosper; and dem no judge the right of the needy.
“Shall I not punish for these things?” says Baba God. “No go my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?
“An astonishing and horrible thing has happened in the land.
The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests rule by dem own authority; and my people love to have it so. What will you do in the end of it?

“Flee for safety, you pikin dem of Benjamin, out of the middle of Jerusalem, and blow the trumpet in Tekoa, and raise up a signal on Beth Haccherem; for evil looks out from the north, and a great destruction.
I go cut off the comely and delicate one, the daughter of Zion.
Shepherds with dem flocks shall come to her; dem shall pitch dem tents against her all around; dem shall feed everyone in his place.”
“Prepare war against her; arise, and Make we go up at noon. Woe to us! For the day declines, for the shadows of the evening are stretched out.
Arise, and Make we go up by night, and Make we destroy her palaces.”
For Baba God of Armies talk say, “Cut down trees, and throw up a mound against Jerusalem: this is the city to be visited; she is wholly oppression within her.
As a well produces its waters, so she produces her wickedness: violence and destruction is heard in her; before me continually is sickness and wounds.
Be instructed, Jerusalem, lest my soul be alienated from you; lest I make you a desolation, a land not inhabited.”
Baba God of Armies says, “Dem shall thoroughly glean the remnant of Israel like a vine. Turn again una hand as a grape gatherer into the baskets.”
To whom shall I speak and testify, that dem may hear? See am, dem ear is uncircumcised, and dem no fit listen. See am, Baba God’s word has become a reproach to dem. Dem have no delight in it.

So I be full of Baba God’s serious anger. I be weary with holding in. “Pour it out on the pikin dem in the street, and on the assembly of young men together; for even the husband with the wife go be taken, the aged with him Wey be full of days.
Dem houses go be turned to others, dem fields and dem wives together; for I go stretch out my hand on the inhabitants of the land, says Baba God.”
“For from dem least even to dem greatest, everyone is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even to the priest, everyone deals falsely.
Dem have healed also the hurt of my people superficially, saying, ‘Peace, peace!’ when E get no peace.

Were dem ashamed when dem had committed abomination? No, dem No be at all ashamed, neither could dem blush. So dem shall fall among people wey fall; at the time that I visit dem, dem go be throw down,” says Baba God.
Baba God says, “Stand in the ways and see, and ask for the old paths, ‘Where is the good way?’ and walk in it, and You go find rest for una souls. But dem talk say, ‘We go not walk in it.’
I set watchmen over you, saying, ‘Listen to the sound of the trumpet!’ But dem talk say, ‘We go not listen!’
So hear, you nations, and know, congregation, Wetin be among dem.
Hear, earth! See am, I go bring evil on this people, even the fruit of dem thoughts, because dem have not listened to my words; and as for my law, dem have rejected it.
To what purpose comes there to me frankincense from Sheba, and the sweet cane from a far country? una burnt offerings No be acceptable, nor una sacrifices pleasing to me.”
So Baba God says, “See am, I go lay stumbling blocks before this people. The fathers and the sons together shall stumble against dem. The neighbor and his friend shall perish.”
Baba God says, “See am, a people comes from the north country. A great nation go be stirred up from the uttermost parts of the earth.
Dem take hold of bow and spear. Dem be cruel, and have no mercy. Dem voice roars like the sea, and dem ride on horses, everyone set in array, as a man to the battle, against you, daughter of Zion.”
We have heard its report; our hands become feeble: anguish has taken hold of us, and pains as of a woman in labor.
No go out into the field, nor walk by the way; for the sword of the enemy and terror, are on every side.
Daughter of my people, clothe yourself with sackcloth, and wallow in ashes! Mourn, as for an only son, most bitter lamentation; for the destroyer shall suddenly come on us.
“I have made you a tester of metals and a fortress among my people; that you may know and try dem way.
Dem be all grievous rebels, going about with slanders; Dem be brass and iron: dem all of dem deal corruptly.
The bellows blow fiercely; the lead is consumed of the fire: in vain do dem go on refining; for the wicked No be plucked away.
Men will call dem rejected silver, because Baba God has rejected dem.”
The word that come to Jeremiah from Baba God, saying,
“Stand in the gate of Baba God’s house, and proclaim there this word, and say, ‘Hear Baba God’s word, all you of Judah, who enter in at these gates to worship Baba God.’”
Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel says, “Amend una ways and una doings, and I go cause you to live in this place.
No trust in lying words, saying, ‘Baba God’s temple, Baba God’s temple, Baba God’s temple, are these.’
For if you thoroughly amend una ways and una doings; if you thoroughly execute justice between a man and his neighbor;
if you no oppress the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, and no shed innocent blood in this place, neither walk after other gods to una own hurt:
then I go cause you to live in this place, in the land that I give to una fathers, from of old even forever more.
See am, you trust in lying words, that no fit profit.
Will you steal, murder, and commit adultery, and swear falsely, and burn incense to Baal, and walk after other gods that you have not known,
and come and stand before me in this house, which is call by my name, and say, ‘We be delivered;’ that you may do all these abominations?
Has this house, which is call by my name, become a den of robbers in una eyes? See am, I, even I, have seen it,” says Baba God.
“But go now to my place which was in Shiloh, where I caused my name to live at the first, and see what I did to it for the wickedness of my people Israel.
Now, because you have done all these works,” says Baba God, “and I spoke to you, rising up early and speaking, but you didn’t hear; and I call you, but you didn’t answer:
so will I do to the house which is call by my name, in which you trust, and to the place which I give to you and to una fathers, as I did to Shiloh.
I go throw you out of my sight, as I have throw out all una brothers, even the whole offspring of Ephraim.
“So no pray for this people, neither lift up a cry nor prayer for dem, neither make intercession to me; for I go not hear you.
No you see Wetin dem do in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?

The pikin dem gather wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead the dough, to make cakes to the queen of the sky, and to pour out drink offerings to other gods, that dem may provoke me to anger.
Do dem provoke me to anger? says Baba God. “No dem provoke themselves, to the confusion of dem own faces?”

So thus says the Lord Baba God: “See am, my anger and my serious anger go be poured out on this place, on man, and on animal, and on the trees of the field, and on the fruit of the ground; and it shall burn, and no go be quenched.”
Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel says: “Add una burnt offerings to una sacrifices, and eat meat.
For I didn’t speak to una fathers, nor command dem in the day that I bring dem out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices:
but this thing I commanded dem, saying, ‘Listen to my voice, and I go be una God, and you go be my people; and walk in all the way that I command you, that it may be well with you.’
But dem didn’t listen nor turn dem ear, but walked in dem own counsels and in the stubbornness of dem evil heart, and go backward, and not forward.
Since the day that una fathers come out of the land of Egypt to this day, I have sent to you all my workers the prophets, daily rising up early and sending dem:
yet dem didn’t listen to me, nor did dem incline dem ear, but made dem neck stiff. Dem did worse than dem fathers.
“You shall speak all these words to dem; but Dem go not listen to you: you shall also call to dem; but Dem go not answer you.
You shall tell dem, ‘This is the nation that has not listened to Baba God dem God’s voice, nor received instruction. Truth has perished, and is cut off from dem mouth.’
Cut off una hair, and throw it away, and take up a lamentation on the bare heights; for Baba God has rejected and forsaken the generation of his serious anger.
“For the pikin dem of Judah have done that which is evil in my sight,” says Baba God. “Dem have set dem abominations in the house which is call by my name, to defile it.
Dem have built the high places of Topheth, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn dem sons and dem daughters in the fire; which I didn’t command, nor did it come into my mind.

So see am, the days come”, says Baba God, “that it shall no more be call Topheth, nor The valley of the son of Hinnom, but The valley of Slaughter; for dem shall bury in Topheth, until E get no place to bury.
The dead bodies of this people go be chop for the birds of the sky, and for the animals of the earth; and Nobody shall frighten dem away.

Then I go cause to cease from the cities of Judah, and from the streets of Jerusalem, the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride; for the land shall become a waste.”

“At that time,” says Baba God, “dem shall bring out the bones of the kings of Judah, and the bones of his princes, and the bones of the priests, and the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, out of dem graves;

and dem shall spread dem before the sun, and the moon, and all the army of the sky, which dem have love, and which dem have served, and after which dem have walked, and which dem have sought, and which dem have worshiped: dem no go be gathered, nor be buried, dem go be for dung on the surface of the earth.
Death go be chosen rather than life by all the residue that remain of this evil family, that remain in all the places where I have driven dem,” says Baba God of Armies.
“Moreover you shall tell dem, ‘Baba God says: “‘Shall men fall, and not rise up again? Shall one turn away, and not return?
Why then have the people of Jerusalem fallen back by a perpetual backsliding? Dem cling to deceit, dem refuse to return.
I listened and heard, but dem didn’t say Wetin be right. Nobody repents of his wickedness, saying, “What have I done?” Everyone turns to his course, as a horse that rushes headlong in the battle.
Yes, the stork in the sky knows her appointed times; and the turtledove, the swallow, and the crane observe the time of dem coming; but my people no know Baba God’s law.
“‘How do you say, “We be wise, and Baba God’s law is with us?” But, see am, the false pen of the scribes has worked falsely.
The wise men are disappointed. Dem be dismayed and trapped. See am, dem have rejected Baba God’s word. What kind of wisdom is in dem?

So will I give dem wives to others, and dem fields to people wey shall possess dem. For everyone from the least even to the greatest is given to covetousness; from the prophet even to the priest everyone deals falsely.
Dem have healed the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, “Peace, peace,” when E get no peace.

Were dem ashamed when dem had committed abomination? No, dem No be at all ashamed, neither could dem blush: so dem shall fall among people wey fall; in the time of dem visitation dem go be throw down, says Baba God.
“‘I go utterly consume dem, says Baba God: no grapes go be on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree, and the leaf shall fade; and the things that I have given dem shall pass away from dem.’”

“Why do we sit still? Assemble unaself, and Make we enter into the fortified cities, and Make we be silent there; for Baba God our God has put us to silence, and given us water of gall to drink, because we have sinned against Baba God.
We looked for peace, but no good come; and for a time of healing, and see am, dismay!

The snorting of his horses is heard from Dan: at the sound of the neighing of his strong ones the whole land trembles; for dem have come, and have devoured the land and all that is in it; the city and people wey live inside am.”
“For, see am, I go send serpents, adders among you, which No go be charmed; and dem shall bite you,” says Baba God.
Oh that I could comfort myself against sorrow! My heart is faint within me.

See am, the voice of the cry of the daughter of my people from a land that is very far off: “No be Baba God in Zion? No be her King in her?” “Why have dem provoked me to anger with dem engraved images, and with foreign vanities?”
“The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we No be saved.”
For the hurt of the daughter of my people am I hurt: I mourn; dismay has taken hold on me.
Is there no balm in Gilead? is there no physician there? Why then no be the health of the daughter of my people recovered?
Oh that my head were waters, and my eyes a spring of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!
Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from dem! For Dem be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.
“Dem bend dem tongue, as dem bow, for falsehood; and dem have grown strong in the land, but not for truth: for dem proceed from evil to evil, and dem no know me,” says Baba God.
“Everyone beware of his neighbor, and no trust in any brother; for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbor will go about with slanders.
Everyone will deceive dem neighbors, and No go speak the truth. Dem have taught dem tongue to speak lies. Dem weary themselves commiting wickedness.
Una habitation is in the middle of deceit; through deceit dem refuse to know me,” says Baba God.
So Baba God of Armies says, “See am, I go melt dem, and try dem; for how should I deal with the daughter of my people?
Dem tongue is a deadly arrow. It speaks deceit. One speaks peaceably to his neighbor with his mouth, but in his heart, he lays wait for him.
Shall I not punish dem for these things?” says Baba God. “Shouldn’t my soul be avenged on a nation such as this?

I go weep and wail for the mountains, and lament for the pastures of the wilderness, because Dem be burned up, so that Nobody passes through; neither can men hear the voice of the livestock. Both the birds of the sky and the animals have fled. Dem be gone.
“I go make Jerusalem heaps, a dwelling place of jackals. I go make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant.”

Wey be wise enough to understand this? Wey be he to whom the mouth of Baba God has spoken, that he may declare it? Why is the land perished and burned up like a wilderness, so that Nobody passes through?
Baba God says, “Because dem have forsaken my law which I set before dem, and have not obeyed my voice, neither walked inside am,
but have walked after the stubbornness of dem own heart, and after the Baals, which dem fathers taught dem.”
so Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says, “See am, I go feed dem, even this people, with wormwood, and give dem water of gall to drink.
I go scatter dem also among the nations, whom neither dem nor dem fathers have known; and I go send the sword after dem, until I have consumed dem.”
Baba God of Armies says, “Consider, and call for the mourning women, that dem may come; and send for the skillful women, that dem may come.
Make dem make haste, and take up a wailing for us, that our eyes may run down with tears, and our eyelids gush out with waters.
For a voice of wailing is heard out of Zion, ‘How are we ruined! We be greatly confounded, because we have forsaken the land, because dem have throw down our dwellings.’”
Yet hear Baba God’s word, you women, and let una ear receive the word of his mouth. Teach una daughters wailing, and everyone her neighbor lamentation.
For death has come up into our windows. It has entered into our palaces; to cut off the pikin dem from outside, and the young men from the streets.
Speak, “Baba God says, “‘The dead bodies of men will fall as dung on the open field, and as the handful after the harvester; and Nobody will gather dem.’”
Baba God says, “No let the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might. No let the rich man glory in his riches.

But Make e who glories glory in this, that he has understanding, and knows me, that I be Baba God who exercises loving kindness, justice, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight,” says Baba God.
“See am, the days come,” says Baba God, “that I go punish all people Wey circumcised only in dem flesh:

Egypt, and Judah, and Edom, and the pikin dem of Ammon, and Moab, and all that have the corners of dem hair cut off, who live in the wilderness; for all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in heart.”
Hear the word which Baba God speaks to you, house of Israel!
Baba God says, “No learn the way of the nations, and no be dismayed at the signs of the sky; for the nations are dismayed at dem.
For the customs of the peoples are vanity; for one cuts a tree out of the forest, the work of the hands of the workman with the ax.
Dem deck it with silver and with gold; dem fasten it with nails and with hammers, that it not move.
Dem be like a palm tree, of turned work, and no speak: dem must be carried, because dem no fit move. No fear of dem; for dem no fit do evil, neither is it in dem to do good.”
E get Nobody like you, Baba God. You be great, and una name is great in might.
Who no suppose fear you, King of the nations? For it belongs to you. Because among all the wise men of the nations, and in all dem royal estate, E get Nobody like you.
But Dem be together brutish and foolish, instructed by idols! It is just wood.

E get silver beaten into plates, which is bring from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the work of the artificer and of the hands of the goldsmith; Blue and purple are dem clothing; Dem be all the work of skillful men.
But Baba God is the true God; he is the living God, and an everlasting King. At his serious anger, the earth trembles, and the nations No be able to withstand his indignation.
“You shall say this to dem: ‘The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth, these shall perish from the earth, and from under the heavens.’”
He has made the earth by his power. he has established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding has he stretched out the heavens.

when he utters his voice, E get a tumult of waters in the heavens, and he causes the vapors to ascend from every corner of the world. He makes lightnings for the rain, and brings the wind out of his treasuries.
Every man has become brutish and without knowledge; every goldsmith is disappointed by his engraved image; for his molten image is falsehood, and E get no breath in dem.
Dem be vanity, a work of delusion. In the time of dem visitation Dem go perish.
The portion of Jacob No be like these; for he is the former of all things; and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance: Baba God of Armies is his name.
Gather up una wares out of the land, you who live under siege.
For Baba God says, “See am, I go sling out the inhabitants of the land at this time, and will distress dem, that dem may feel it.”
Woe is me because of my injury! My wound is serious: but I talk say, “Truly this is my grief, and I must bear it.”
My tent is destroyed, and all my cords are broken. My pikin dem have gone away from me, and Dem be no more. E get Nobody to spread my tent any more, and to set up my curtains.
For the shepherds have become brutish, and have not inquired of Baba God. So dem have not prospered, and all dem flocks are scattered.
The voice of news, see am, it comes, and a great commotion out of the north country, to make the cities of Judah a desolation, a dwelling place of jackals.
Baba God, I know that the way of man No be in imself: it No be in man who walks to direct his steps.
Baba God, correct me, but in measure: not in una anger, lest you bring me to nothing.

Pour out una serious anger on the nations that no know you, and on the families that no call on una name: for dem have devoured Jacob. Yes, dem have devoured him and consumed him, and have laid waste his habitation.
The word that come to Jeremiah from Baba God, saying,
“Hear the words of this covenant, and speak to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem;
and say to dem, Baba God, the God of Israel says: ‘Cursed is the man who no dey hear the words of this covenant,

which I commanded una fathers in the day that I bring dem out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace,’ saying, ‘Obey my voice, and do dem, according to all which I command you: so you go be my people, and I go be una God;
that I may establish the oath which I swore to una fathers, to give dem a land flowing with milk and honey,’ as it is today.” Then answer I, and talk say, “Amen, Baba God.”
Baba God talk say to me, “Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, saying, ‘Hear the words of this covenant, and do dem.
For I earnestly protested to una fathers in the day that I bring dem up out of the land of Egypt, even to this day, rising early and protesting, saying, “Obey my voice.”

Yet dem didn’t obey, nor turn dem ear, but walked everyone in the stubbornness of dem evil heart: so I bring on dem all the words of this covenant, which I commanded dem to do, but dem didn’t do dem.’”
Baba God talk say to me, “A conspiracy is find among the men of Judah, and among the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

Dem be turned back to the iniquities of dem forefathers, who refused to hear my words; and Dem be gone after other gods to serve dem: the house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken my covenant which I made with dem fathers.
So Baba God says, ‘See am, I go bring evil on dem, which dem no go be able to escape; and dem shall cry to me, but I go not listen to dem.
Then shall the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem go and cry to the gods to which dem offer incense: but Dem go not save dem at all in the time of dem trouble.

For according to the number of una cities are una gods, Judah; and according to the number of the streets of Jerusalem have you set up altars to the shameful thing, even altars to burn incense to Baal.’
“So no pray for this people, neither lift up cry nor prayer for dem; for I go not hear dem in the time that dem cry to me because of dem trouble.
What has my beloved to do in my house, since she has worked lewdness with many, and the holy flesh is passed from you? When you do evil, then you glad well-well.”
Baba God call una name, “A green olive tree, beautiful with goodly fruit.” With the noise of a great tumult he has kindled fire on it, and its branches are broken.

For Baba God of Armies, who planted you, has pronounced evil against you, because of the evil of the house of Israel and of the house of Judah, which dem have worked for themselves in provoking me to anger by offering incense to Baal.
Baba God give me knowledge of it, and I know it: then you showed me dem doings.

But I was like a gentle lamb that is led to the slaughter; and I didn’t know that dem had devised devices against me, saying, “Make we destroy the tree with its fruit, and Make we cut him off from the land of the living, that his name may be no more remember.”
But, Baba God of Armies, who judges righteously, who tests the heart and the mind, I shall see una vengeance on dem; for to you I have revealed my cause.
“So Baba God says concerning the men of Anathoth, who seek una life, saying, ‘You no go prophesy in Baba God’s name, that you not die by our hand;’
so Baba God of Armies says, ‘See am, I go punish dem: the young men shall die by the sword; dem sons and dem daughters shall die by famine;
and there go be no remnant to dem: for I go bring evil on the men of Anathoth, even the year of dem visitation.’”
You be righteous, Baba God, when I contend with you; yet I would reason the cause with you: why does the way of the wicked prosper? why are all dem at ease who deal very treacherously?
You have planted dem, yes, dem have taken root; dem grow, yes, dem produce fruit. You be near in dem mouth, and far from dem heart.
But you, Baba God, know me; you see me, and try my heart toward you. Pull dem out like sheep for the slaughter, and prepare dem for the day of slaughter.

How long shall the land mourn, and the herbs of the whole country wither? For the wickedness of people wey live inside am, the animals are consumed, and the birds; because dem talk say, “He no go see our latter end.”
“If you have run with the footmen, and dem have wearied you, then how can you contend with horses? Though in a land of peace You be secure, yet how will you do in the pride of the Jordan?
For even una brothers, and the house of una father, even dem have dealt treacherously with you; even dem have cried aloud after you! No believe dem, though dem speak beautiful words to you.
“I have forsaken my house. I have throw off my heritage. I have given the dearly beloved of my soul into the hand of her enemies.
My heritage has become to me as a lion in the forest. She has uttered her voice against me; so I have hated her.
Is my heritage to me as a speckled bird of prey? Are the birds of prey against her all around? Go, assemble all the animals of the field, bring dem to devour.
Many shepherds have destroyed my vineyard. Dem have trodden my portion under foot. Dem have made my pleasant portion a desolate wilderness.
Dem have made it a desolation. It mourns to me, being desolate. The whole land is made desolate, because no man lays it to heart.
Destroyers have come on all the bare heights in the wilderness; for the sword of Baba God devours from the one end of the land even to the other end of the land. No flesh has peace.
Dem have sown wheat, and have reaped thorns. Dem have put themselves to pain, and profit nothing. You go be ashamed of una fruits, because of the fierce anger of Baba God.”

Baba God says, “Concerning all my evil neighbors, who touch the inheritance which I have caused my people Israel to inherit: see am, I go pluck dem up from off dem land, and will pluck up the house of Judah from among dem.
It shall happen, after that I have plucked dem up, I go return and have compassion on dem; and I go bring dem again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.

It shall happen, if Dem go diligently learn the ways of my people, to swear by my name, ‘As Baba God lives;’ even as dem taught my people to swear by Baal; then shall dem be built up in the middle of my people.
But if Dem go not hear, then I go pluck up that nation, plucking up and destroying it,” says Baba God.
Baba God says to me, “Go, and buy yourself a linen belt, and put it on una waist, and no put it in water.”
So I bought a belt according to Baba God’s word, and put it on my waist.
Baba God’s word come to me the second time, saying,
“Take the belt that you have bought, which is on una waist, and arise, go to the Euphrates, and hide it there in a cleft of the rock.”
So I go, and hid it by the Euphrates, as Baba God commanded me.
After many days, Baba God talk say to me, “Arise, go to the Euphrates, and take the belt from there, which I commanded you to hide there.”
Then I go to the Euphrates, and dug, and take the belt from the place where I had hidden it; and see am, the belt was ruined. It was profitable for nothing.
Then Baba God’s word come to me, saying,
“Baba God says, ‘In this way I, will ruin the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.

This evil people, who refuse to hear my words, who walk in the stubbornness of dem heart, and are gone after other gods to serve dem, and to worship dem, shall even be as this belt, which is profitable for nothing.

For as the belt clings to the waist of a man, so I have caused to cling to me the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah,’ says Baba God; ‘that dem may be to me for a people, and for a name, and for a praise, and for a glory: but dem would not hear.’
“So you shall speak to dem this word: ‘Baba God, the God of Israel says, “Every bottle go be filled with wine.”’ Dem go tell you, ‘Do we not certainly know that every bottle go be filled with wine?’

Then tell dem, ‘Baba God says, “See am, I go fill all the inhabitants of this land, even the kings who sit on David’s throne, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, with drunkenness.
I go dash dem one against another, even the fathers and the sons together,” says Baba God: “I go not pity, nor spare, nor have compassion, that I no suppose destroy dem.”’”
Hear, and give ear. No be proud; for Baba God has spoken.

Give glory to Baba God una God, before he causes darkness, and before una feet stumble on the dark mountains, and, while you look for light, he turns it into the shadow of death, and makes it gross darkness.
But if You go not hear it, my soul shall weep in secret for una pride; and my eye shall weep bitterly, and run down with tears, because Baba God’s flock is taken captive.
Say to the king and to the queen mother, “Humble unaself, sit down; for una headdresses have come down, even the crown of una glory.
The cities of the South are shut up, and E get Nobody to open dem. Judah is carried away captive, all of it; it is wholly carried away captive.
Lift up una eyes, and see people wey come from the north. where is the flock that was given you, una beautiful flock?
What will you say, when he shall set over you as head those whom you have yourself taught to be friends to you? No go sorrows take hold of you, as of a woman in travail?
If you say in una heart, “Why are these things come on me?” For the greatness of una wickedness una skirts are uncovered, and una heels suffer violence.
Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? Then may you also do good, Wey be accustomed to do evil.
“So I go scatter dem, as the stubble that passes away, by the wind of the wilderness.
This is una lot, the portion measured to you from me,” says Baba God; “because you have forgotten me, and trusted in falsehood.”
So will I also uncover una skirts on una face, and una shame shall appear.

I have seen una abominations, even una adulteries, and una neighing, the lewdness of una prostitution, on the hills in the field. Woe to you, Jerusalem! You go not be made clean; how long shall it yet be?”
This is Baba God’s word that come to Jeremiah concerning the drought.
“Judah mourns, and its gates languish, dem sit in black on the ground; and the cry of Jerusalem goes up.
Dem nobles send dem little ones to the waters. Dem come to the cisterns, and find no water. Dem return with dem vessels empty. Dem be disappointed and confounded, and cover dem heads.
Because of the ground which is cracked, because no rain Don dey in the land. The plowmen are disappointed. Dem cover dem heads.
Yes, the hind also in the field calves, and forsakes her young, because E get no grass.
The wild donkeys stand on the bare heights. Dem pant for air like jackals. Dem eyes fail, because E get no vegetation.
Though our iniquities testify against us, work for una name’s sake, Baba God; for our rebellions are many. We have sinned against you.
You hope of Israel, its Savior in the time of trouble, why should you be as a foreigner in the land, and as a wayfaring man who turns aside to stay for a night?
Why should you be like a scared man, as a mighty man who no fit save? Yet you, Baba God, are in the middle of us, and We be call by una name. No leave us.
Baba God says to this people, “Even so dem have love to wander. Dem have not restrained dem feet. So Baba God No dey accept dem. Now he will remember dem wickedness, and punish dem for dem sins.”
Baba God talk say to me, “No pray for this people for dem good.
When dem fast, I go not hear dem cry; and when dem offer burnt offering and meal offering, I go not accept dem; but I go consume dem by the sword, and by the famine, and by the pestilence.”
Then I talk say, “Ah, Lord Baba God! See am, the prophets tell dem, ‘You go not see the sword, neither shall you have famine; but I go give you assured peace in this place.’”

Then Baba God talk say to me, “The prophets prophesy lies in my name. I didn’t send dem, neither have I commanded dem, neither did I speak to dem. Dem prophesy to you a lying vision, divination, and a thing of nothing, and the deceit of dem own heart.
So Baba God says concerning the prophets who prophesy in my name, and I didn’t send dem, yet dem say, ‘Sword and famine No go be in this land.’ Those prophets Go be consumed by sword and famine.

The people to whom dem prophesy go be throw out in the streets of Jerusalem because of the famine and the sword. Dem go get Nobody to bury dem — dem, dem wives, nor dem sons, nor dem daughters: for I go pour dem wickedness on dem.

“You shall say this word to dem, “‘Let my eyes run down with tears night and day, and Make dem not cease; for the virgin daughter of my people is broken with a great breach, with a very grievous wound.

If I go out into the field, then, see am, the slain with the sword! If I enter into the city, then, see am, people Wey sick with famine! For both the prophet and the priest go about in the land, and have no knowledge.’”
Have you utterly rejected Judah? Has una soul loathed Zion? Why have you struck us, and E get no healing for us? We looked for peace, but no good come; and for a time of healing, and see am, dismay!
We acknowledge, Baba God, our wickedness, and the wickedness of our fathers; for we have sinned against you.
No abhor us, for una name’s sake. No disgrace the throne of una glory. Remember, and no break una covenant with us.
Are there any among the vanities of the nations that can cause rain? Or can the sky give showers? No be you he, Baba God our God? So We go wait for you; for you have made all these things.
Then Baba God talk say to me, “Though Moses and Samuel stood before me, yet my mind would not be toward this people. Throw dem out of my sight, and Make dem go out!

It shall happen, when dem tell you, ‘Where shall we go out?’ Then you shall tell dem, ‘Baba God says: “Such as are for death, to death; and such as are for the sword, to the sword; and such as are for the famine, to the famine; and such as are for captivity, to captivity.”’
“I go appoint over dem four kinds,” says Baba God: “the sword to kill, and the dogs to tear, and the birds of the sky, and the animals of the earth, to devour and to destroy.
I go cause dem to be tossed back and forth among all the kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasseh, the son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, for that which he did in Jerusalem.
For who Go get pity on you, Jerusalem? or who will bemoan you? or who will turn aside to ask of una welfare?
You have rejected me,” says Baba God. “You have gone backward: so I have stretched out my hand against you, and destroyed you; I be weary with repenting.
I have winnowed dem with a fan in the gates of the land; I have bereaved dem of pikin dem. I have destroyed my people. Dem didn’t return from dem ways.
Dem widows are increased to me above the sand of the seas; I have bring on dem against the mother of the young men a destroyer at noonday. I have caused anguish and terrors to fall on her suddenly.

Person wey has borne seven languishes; she has given up the spirit. Her sun has gone down while it was yet day. She Don dey disappointed and confounded: and dem residue will I deliver to the sword before dem enemies,” says Baba God.
Woe is me, my mother, that you have borne me a man of strife and a man of contention to the whole earth! I have not lent, neither have men lent to me; yet everyone of dem curses me.
Baba God talk say, “Most certainly I go strengthen you for good. Most certainly I go cause the enemy to make supplication to you in the time of evil and in the time of suffering.
Can one break iron, even iron from the north, and brass?
Una substance and una treasures will I give for a plunder without price, and that for all una sins, even in all una borders.
I go make dem to pass with una enemies into a land which you no know; for a fire is kindled in my anger, which shall burn on you.”
Baba God, you know; remember me, and visit me, and avenge me of my persecutors. You be patient, so no take me away. Know that for una sake I have suffered reproach.
Una words were find, and I ate dem. Una words were to me a gladness and the rejoicing of my heart, for I be call by una name, Baba God, God of Armies.
I didn’t sit in the assembly of people wey make merry, nor rejoiced; I sat alone because of una hand; for you have filled me with indignation.
Why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable, which refuses to be healed? Will you indeed be to me as a deceitful brook, like waters that fail?

So Baba God says, “If you return, then I go bring you again, that you may stand before me; and if you take out the precious from the vile, you go be as my mouth. Dem shall return to you, but you no go return to dem.
I go make you to this people a fortified bronze wall; and dem shall fight against you, but dem no go prevail against you; for I be with you to save you and to deliver you,” says Baba God.
“I go deliver you out of the hand of the wicked, and I go redeem you out of the hand of the terrible.”
Baba God’s word come also to me, saying,
“You no go take a wife, neither shall you have sons or daughters, in this place.”
For Baba God says concerning the sons and concerning the daughters Wey be born in this place, and concerning dem mothers who bore dem, and concerning dem fathers who became dem father in this land:

“Dem shall die grievous deaths: dem no go be lamented, neither shall dem be buried; dem go be as dung on the surface of the ground; and dem go be consumed by the sword, and by famine; and dem dead bodies go be chop for the birds of the sky, and for the animals of the earth.”

For Baba God says, “No enter into the house of mourning, neither go to lament, neither bemoan dem; for I have taken away my peace from this people,” says Baba God, “even loving kindness and tender mercies.
Both great and small shall die in this land; dem no go be buried, neither shall men lament for dem, nor cut themselves, nor make themselves bald for dem;
neither shall men break bread for dem in mourning, to comfort dem for the dead; neither shall men give dem the cup of consolation to drink for dem father or for dem mother.
“You no go go into the house of feasting to sit with dem, to eat and to drink.”

For Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel says: “See am, I go cause to cease out of this place, before una eyes and in una days, the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride.

It shall happen, when you shall show this people all these words, and dem ask you, ‘Why has Baba God pronounced all this great evil against us?’ or ‘Wetin be our wickedness? or ‘Wetin be our sin that we have committed against Baba God our God?’

Then you shall tell dem, ‘Because una fathers have forsaken me,’ says Baba God, ‘and have walked after other gods, and have served dem, and have worshiped dem, and have forsaken me, and have not kept my law;
and you have done evil more than una fathers; for, see am, you walk every one after the stubbornness of his evil heart, so that you no listen to me.
So will I throw you out of this land into the land that you have not known, neither you nor una fathers; and there you shall serve other gods day and night; for I go show you no favor.’
“So see am, the days come,” says Baba God, “that it shall no more be talk say, ‘As Baba God lives, who bring up the pikin dem of Israel out of the land of Egypt;’

but, ‘As Baba God lives, who bring up the pikin dem of Israel from the land of the north, and from all the countries where he had driven dem.’ I go bring dem again into dem land that I give to dem fathers.

“See am, I go send for many fishermen,” says Baba God, “and dem shall fish dem up; and afterward I go send for many hunters, and dem shall hunt dem from every mountain, and from every hill, and out of the clefts of the rocks.
For my eyes are on all dem ways; dem No be hidden from my face, neither is dem wickedness concealed from my eyes.
First I go recompense dem wickedness and dem sin double, because dem have polluted my land with the carcasses of dem detestable things, and have filled my inheritance with dem abominations.”

Baba God, my strength, and my stronghold, and my refuge in the day of suffering, to you shall the nations come from every corner of the world, and shall say, “Our fathers have inherited nothing but lies, vanity and things in which E get no profit.
Shall a man make to imself gods, which yet are no gods?”
“So see am, I go cause dem to know, this once will I cause dem to know my hand and my might; and dem shall know that my name is Baba God.”
“The sin of Judah is written with a pen of iron, and with the point of a diamond. It is engraved on the tablet of dem heart, and on the horns of una altars.
Even dem pikin dem remember dem altars and dem Asherah poles by the green trees on the high hills.
My mountain in the field, I go give una substance and all una treasures for a plunder, and una high places, because of sin, throughout all una borders.

You, even of yourself, shall discontinue from una heritage that I give you. I go cause you to serve una enemies in the land which you no know, for you have kindled a fire in my anger which shall burn forever.”
Baba God says: “Cursed is the man who trusts in man, and makes flesh his arm, and whose heart departs from Baba God.
For he go be like a bush in the desert, and no go see when good comes, but shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, a salt land and not inhabited.
“Blessed is the man who trusts in Baba God, and whose confidence is in Baba God.

For he go be as a tree planted by the waters, who spreads out its roots by the river, and no go fear when heat comes, but its leaf go be green; and no go be careful in the year of drought, neither shall cease from yielding fruit.
The heart is deceitful above all things, and it is exceedingly corrupt. Who can know it?
“I, Baba God, search the mind, I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.”
As the partridge that sits on eggs which she has not laid, so is person wey gets riches, and not by right; in the middle of his days dem shall leave him, and at his end he go be a fool.
A glorious throne, set on high from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary.
Baba God, the hope of Israel, all who forsake you go be disappointed. People wey depart from me go be written in the earth, because dem have forsaken Baba God, the spring of living waters.
Heal me, O Baba God, and I go be healed; save me, and I go be saved: for You be my praise.
See am, dem tell me, “Where is Baba God’s word? Let it be fulfilled now.”
As for me, I have not hurried from being a shepherd after you; neither have I desired the woeful day; you know. That which come out of my lips was before una face.
No be a terror to me: You be my refuge in the day of evil.
Make dem be disappointed who persecute me, but let not me be disappointed; Make dem be dismayed, but no let me be dismayed; bring on dem the day of evil, and destroy dem with double destruction.
Thus talk say Baba God to me: “Go, and stand in the gate of the pikin dem of the people, through which the kings of Judah come in, and by which dem go out, and in all the gates of Jerusalem;
and tell dem, ‘Hear Baba God’s word, you kings of Judah, and all Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, that enter in by these gates:
Baba God says, “Be careful, and bear no burden on the Sabbath day, nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem;
neither carry a burden out of una houses on the Sabbath day, neither do any work: but make the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded una fathers.
But dem didn’t listen, neither turn dem ear, but made dem neck stiff, that dem might not hear, and might not receive instruction.
It shall happen, if you diligently listen to me,” says Baba God, “to bring in no burden through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, but to make the Sabbath day holy, to do no work inside am;

then shall there enter in by the gates of this city kings and princes sitting on David’s throne, riding in chariots and on horses, dem, and dem princes, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and this city shall remain forever.

Dem shall come from the cities of Judah, and from the places around Jerusalem, and from the land of Benjamin, and from the lowland, and from the hill country, and from the South, bringing burnt offerings, and sacrifices, and meal offerings, and frankincense, and bringing sacrifices of thanksgiving, to Baba God’s house.

But if You go not listen to me to make the Sabbath day holy, and not to bear a burden and enter in at the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day; then I go kindle a fire in its gates, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem, and it no go be quenched.”’”
The word which come to Jeremiah from Baba God, saying,
“Arise, and go down to the potter’s house, and there I go cause you to hear my words.”
Then I go down to the potter’s house, and see am, he was making a work on the wheels.
When the vessel that he made of the clay was marred in the hand of the potter, he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.
Then Baba God’s word come to me, saying,
“House of Israel, no fit I do with you as this potter?” says Baba God. “See am, as the clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, house of Israel.
At what instant I shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up and to break down and to destroy it;
if that nation, concerning which I have spoken, turn from dem evil, I go repent of the evil that I thought to do to dem.
At what instant I shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to build and to plant it;
if dem do that which is evil in my sight, that dem not obey my voice, then I go repent of the good, with which I talk say I would benefit dem.

“Now so, speak to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying, ‘Baba God says: “See am, I frame evil against you, and devise a device against you. Everyone return from his evil way now, and amend una ways and una doings.”’
But dem say, ‘It is in vain; for We go walk after our own devices, and We go do everyone after the stubbornness of his evil heart.’”
So Baba God says: “Ask now among the nations, who has heard such things. The virgin of Israel has done a very horrible thing.
Shall the snow of Lebanon fail from the rock of the field? Shall the cold waters that flow down from far away be dried up?
For my people have forgotten me. Dem have burned incense to false gods. Dem Don dey made to stumble in dem ways, in the ancient paths, to walk in byways, in a way not built up;
to make dem land an astonishment, and a perpetual hissing. Everybody wey passes through am go be astonished, and shake his head.
I go scatter dem as with an east wind before the enemy. I go show dem the back, and not the face, in the day of dem calamity.

Then dem talk say, “Come, and Make we devise devices against Jeremiah; for the law no go perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come, and Make we strike him with the tongue, and Make we not give heed to any of his words.”
Give heed to me, Baba God, and listen to the voice of people wey contend with me.
Shall evil be recompensed for good? For dem have dug a pit for my soul. Remember how I stood before you to speak good for dem, to turn away una serious anger from dem.

So deliver up dem pikin dem to the famine, and give dem over to the power of the sword. Let dem wives become childless, and widows; and let dem men be slain of death, and dem young men struck by the sword in battle.
Let a cry be heard from dem houses, when you shall bring a troop suddenly on dem; for dem have dug a pit to take me, and hidden snares for my feet.

Yet, Baba God, you know all dem counsel against me to kill me. No forgive dem wickedness, neither blot out dem sin from una sight; but Make dem be overthrown before you. Deal you with dem in the time of una anger.
Thus talk say Baba God, “Go, and buy a potter’s earthen bottle, and take some of the elders of the people, and of the elders of the priests;
and go out to the valley of the son of Hinnom, which is by the entry of the gate Harsith, and proclaim there the words that I shall tell you;

and say, ‘Hear Baba God’s word, kings of Judah, and inhabitants of Jerusalem: Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel says, “See am, I go bring evil on this place, which Anybody wey hears, his ears shall tingle.

Because dem have forsaken me, and have estranged this place, and have burned incense in it to other gods, that dem didn’t know, dem and dem fathers and the kings of Judah; and have filled this place with the blood of innocents,
and have built the high places of Baal, to burn dem sons in the fire for burnt offerings to Baal; which I didn’t command, nor spoke it, neither come it into my mind:
so, see am, the days come,” says Baba God, “that this place shall no more be call Topheth, nor The valley of the son of Hinnom, but The valley of Slaughter.

“‘“I go make void the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem in this place; and I go cause dem to fall by the sword before dem enemies, and by the hand of people wey seek dem life: and dem dead bodies will I give to be chop for the birds of the sky, and for the animals of the earth.
I go make this city an astonishment, and a hissing; Everybody wey passes through am go be astonished and hiss because of all its plagues.

I go cause dem to eat the flesh of dem sons and the flesh of dem daughters; and dem shall eat everyone the flesh of his friend, in the siege and in the distress, with which dem enemies, and people wey seek dem life, shall distress dem.”’
“Then you shall break the bottle in the sight of the men who go with you,

and shall tell dem, ‘Baba God of Armies says: “Even so will I break this people and this city, as one breaks a potter’s vessel, that no fit be made whole again; and dem shall bury in Topheth, until E get no place to bury.
Thus will I do to this place,” says Baba God, “and to its inhabitants, even making this city as Topheth:

and the houses of Jerusalem, and the houses of the kings of Judah, which are defiled, go be as the place of Topheth, even all the houses on whose roofs dem have burned incense to all the army of the sky, and have poured out drink offerings to other gods.”’”
Then Jeremiah come from Topheth, where Baba God had sent him to prophesy; and he stood in the court of Baba God’s house, and talk say to all the people:

“Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel says, ‘See am, I go bring on this city and on all its towns all the evil that I have pronounced against it; because dem have made dem neck stiff, that dem may not hear my words.’”
Now Pashhur, the son of Immer the priest, who was chief officer in Baba God’s house, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things.
Then Pashhur struck Jeremiah the prophet, and put him in the stocks that were in the upper gate of Benjamin, which was in Baba God’s house.
On the next day, Pashhur released Jeremiah out of the stocks. Then Jeremiah talk say to him, “Baba God has not call una name Pashhur, but Magormissabib.

For Baba God says, ‘See am, I go make you a terror to yourself, and to all una friends; and dem shall fall by the sword of dem enemies, and una eyes shall see it; and I go give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall carry dem captive to Babylon, and shall kill dem with the sword.

Moreover I go give all the riches of this city, and all its gains, and all the precious things of it, yes, all the treasures of the kings of Judah will I give into the hand of dem enemies; and dem shall make dem captives, and take dem, and carry dem to Babylon.

You, Pashhur, and all who live in una house shall go into captivity; and you shall come to Babylon, and there you shall die, and there you go be buried, you, and all una friends, to whom you have prophesied falsely.’”
Baba God, you have persuaded me, and I was persuaded; You be stronger than I, and have prevailed. I have become a laughing-stock all day. Every one mocks me.
For as often as I speak, I cry out; I cry, Violence and destruction! because Baba God’s word Don dey made a reproach to me, and a derision, all day.
If I say, I go not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name, then E get in my heart as it were a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I be weary with holding it in, and I no fit.

For I have heard the defaming of many, “Terror on every side! Denounce, and We go denounce him!” say all my familiar friends, people wey watch for my fall. “Perhaps he Go be persuaded, and we shall prevail against him, and we shall take our revenge on him.”

But Baba God is with me as an awesome mighty one. So my persecutors shall stumble, and dem no go prevail. Dem go be utterly disappointed, because dem have not dealt wisely, even with an everlasting dishonor which shall never be forgotten.
But, Baba God of Armies, who tests the righteous, wey see the heart and the mind, let me see una vengeance on dem; for to you I have revealed my cause.
Sing to Baba God, praise Baba God; for he has delivered the soul of the needy from the hand of evildoers.
Cursed is the day in which I was born. No let the day in which my mother bore me be blessed.
Cursed is the man who bring news to my father, saying, “A boy is born to you,” making him very glad.
Let that man be as the cities which Baba God overthrew, and didn’t repent. Make e hear a cry in the morning, and shouting at noontime;
because he didn’t kill me from the womb; and so my mother would Don dey my grave, and her womb always great.
Why did I come out of the womb to see labor and sorrow, that my days should be consumed with shame?
The word which come to Jeremiah from Baba God, when king Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur the son of Malchijah, and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah, the priest, saying,
“Please inquire of Baba God for us; for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon makes war against us. Perhaps Baba God will deal with us according to all his wondrous works, that he may withdraw from us.”
Then Jeremiah talk say to dem, “Tell Zedekiah:

‘Baba God, the God of Israel says, “See am, I go turn back the weapons of war that are in una hands, with which you fight against the king of Babylon, and against the Chaldeans who besiege you, without the walls; and I go gather dem into the middle of this city.
I myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand and with a strong arm, even in anger, and in serious anger, and in great indignation.
I go strike the inhabitants of this city, both man and animal. Dem go die of a great pestilence.

Afterward,” says Baba God, “I go deliver Zedekiah king of Judah, and his workers, and the people, even people Wey left in this city from the pestilence, from the sword, and from the famine, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of dem enemies, and into the hand of people wey seek dem life. He will strike dem with the edge of the sword. He No go spare dem, neither have pity, nor have mercy.”’
“To this people you shall say, ‘Baba God says: “See am, I set before you the way of life and the way of death.

Person wey remains in this city will die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence; but person wey goes out, and passes over to the Chaldeans who besiege you, he shall live, and he will escape with his life.
For I have set my face on this city for evil, and not for good,” says Baba God. “It Go be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall burn it with fire.”’
“Concerning the house of the king of Judah, hear Baba God’s word.
