House of David, Baba God says, ‘Execute justice in the morning, and deliver him Wey be robbed out of the hand of the oppressor, lest my serious anger go out like fire, and burn so that Nobody can quench it, because of the evil of una doings.
See am, I be against you, O inhabitant of the valley, and of the rock of the plain,’ says Baba God. ‘You that say, “Who would come down against us?” or “Who would enter into our homes?”
I go punish you according to the fruit of una doings, says Baba God; and I go kindle a fire in her forest, and it shall devour all that is around her.’”
Thus talk say Baba God: “Go down to the house of the king of Judah, and speak there this word,
‘Hear Baba God’s word, king of Judah, who sits on David’s throne, you, and una workers, and una people who enter in by these gates.

Baba God says: “Execute justice and righteousness, and deliver him Wey be robbed out of the hand of the oppressor. Do no wrong. Do no violence, to the foreigner, the fatherless, nor the widow; neither shed innocent blood in this place.
For if you do this thing indeed, then shall there enter in by the gates of this house kings sitting on David’s throne, riding in chariots and on horses, he, and his workers, and his people.
But if You go not hear these words, I swear by myself,” says Baba God, “that this house shall become a desolation.”’”
For Baba God says concerning the house of the king of Judah: “You be Gilead to me, the head of Lebanon. Yet surely I go make you a wilderness, cities which No be inhabited.
I go prepare destroyers against you, everyone with his weapons, and Dem go cut down una choice cedars, and throw dem into the fire.
“Many nations will pass by this city, and Dem go each ask his neighbor, ‘Why has Baba God done this to this great city?’
Then dem shall answer, ‘Because dem abandoned the covenant of Baba God dem God, and worshiped other gods, and served dem.’”
No weep for the dead, neither bemoan him; but weep bitterly for him who goes away; for he shall return no more, nor see his native country.
For Baba God says touching Shallum the son of Josiah, king of Judah, who reigned instead of Josiah his father, and who go out of this place: “He no go return there any more.
But in the place where dem have led him captive, there shall he die, and he shall see this land no more.”
“Woe to him who builds his house by unrighteousness, and his rooms by injustice; who uses his neighbor’s service without wages, and no dey give him his hire;
who says, ‘I go build me a wide house and spacious rooms,’ and cuts out windows for imself; and it is ceiling with cedar, and painted with vermilion.
“Shall you reign, because you strive to excel in cedar? Didn’t una father eat and drink, and do justice and righteousness? Then it was well with him.
He judged the cause of the poor and needy; then it was well. No be this to know me?” says Baba God.
But una eyes and una heart No be but for una covetousness, and for shedding innocent blood, for oppression, and for doing violence.”

So Baba God says concerning Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah: “Dem no go lament for him, saying, ‘Ah my brother!’ or, ‘Ah sister!’ Dem no go lament for him, saying ‘Ah lord!’ or, ‘Ah his glory!’
He go be buried with the burial of a donkey, drawn and throw out beyond the gates of Jerusalem.”
“Go up to Lebanon, and cry; and lift up una voice in Bashan, and cry from Abarim; for all una lovers are destroyed.
I spoke to you in una prosperity; but you talk say, ‘I go not listen.’ This Don dey una way from una youth, that you didn’t obey my voice.
The wind shall feed all una shepherds, and una lovers shall go into captivity. Surely then You go be ashamed and confounded for all una wickedness.
Inhabitant of Lebanon, who makes una nest in the cedars, how greatly to be pitied You go be when pangs come on you, the pain as of a woman in travail!
“As I live,” says Baba God, “though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet on my right hand, yet would I pluck you from there;

and I would give you into the hand of people wey seek una life, and into the hand of dem of whom You be afraid, even into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of the Chaldeans.
I go throw you out with una mother who bore you, into another country, where you No be born; and there You go die.
But to the land to which dem soul longs to return, there shall dem not return.”
Is this man Coniah a despised broken vessel? Is he a vessel in which Nobody delights? Why are dem throw out, he and his offspring, and throw into a land which dem no know?
O earth, earth, earth, hear Baba God’s word!
Baba God says, “Record this man as childless, a man who No go prosper in his days; for no more shall a man of his offspring prosper, sitting on David’s throne, and ruling in Judah.”
“Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture!” says Baba God.

So Baba God, the God of Israel, says against the shepherds who feed my people: “You have scattered my flock, and driven dem away, and have not visited dem; see am, I go visit on you the evil of una doings,” says Baba God.
“I go gather the remnant of my flock out of all the countries where I have driven dem, and will bring dem again to dem folds; and dem go be fruitful and multiply.
I go set up shepherds over dem, who shall feed dem; and dem shall fear no more, nor be dismayed, neither shall any be lacking,” says Baba God.
“See am, the days come,” says Baba God, “that I go raise to David a righteous Branch, and he shall reign as king and deal wisely, and shall execute justice and righteousness in the land.
In his days Judah go be saved, and Israel shall live safely. This is his name by which he go be call: Baba God our righteousness.
“So see am, the days come,” says Baba God, “that dem shall no more say, ‘As Baba God lives, who bring up the pikin dem of Israel out of the land of Egypt;’
but, ‘As Baba God lives, who bring up and who led the offspring of the house of Israel out of the north country, and from all the countries where I had driven dem.’ Then Dem go live in dem own land.”
Concerning the prophets: My heart within me is broken. All my bones shake. I be like a drunken man, and like a man whom wine has overcome, because of Baba God, and because of his holy words.
For the land is full of adulterers; for because of the curse the land mourns. The pastures of the wilderness are dried up. Dem course is evil, and dem might No be right;
for both prophet and priest are profane; yes, in my house I have find dem wickedness,” says Baba God.
So dem way go be to dem as slippery places in the darkness. Dem go be driven on, and fall inside am; for I go bring evil on dem, even the year of dem visitation,” says Baba God.
“I have seen folly in the prophets of Samaria. Dem prophesied by Baal, and caused my people Israel to err.

In the prophets of Jerusalem also I have seen a horrible thing: dem commit adultery, and walk in lies. Dem strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that Nobody returns from his wickedness. Dem have all become to me as Sodom, and its inhabitants as Gomorrah.”

So Baba God of Armies says concerning the prophets: “See am, I go feed dem with wormwood, and make dem drink the water of gall; for from the prophets of Jerusalem ungodliness has gone out into all the land.”
Baba God of Armies says, “No listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you. Dem teach you vanity. Dem speak a vision of dem own heart, and not out of the mouth of Baba God.
Dem say continually to people wey despise me, ‘Baba God has talk say, “You go get peace;”’ and to Everybody wey walks in the stubbornness of his own heart dem say, ‘No evil shall come on you.’
For who has stood in the council of Baba God, that he should perceive and hear his word? Who has listend to my word, and heard it?
See am, Baba God’s storm, his serious anger, has gone out. Yes, a whirling storm. It shall burst on the head of the wicked.
Baba God’s anger no go return, until he has executed, and until he has performed the intents of his heart. In the latter days, You go understand it perfectly.
I didn’t send these prophets, yet dem ran. I didn’t speak to dem, yet dem prophesied.
But if dem had stood in my council, then dem would have caused my people to hear my words, and would have turned dem from dem evil way, and from the evil of dem doings.
“Am I a God at hand,” says Baba God, “and not a God far away off?
Can anyone hide imself in secret places so that I no fit see him?” says Baba God. “No I fill heaven and earth?” says Baba God.
“I have heard what the prophets have talk say, who prophesy lies in my name, saying, ‘I had a dream! I had a dream!’
How long shall this be in the heart of the prophets who prophesy lies, even the prophets of the deceit of dem own heart?
Dem intend to cause my people to forget my name by dem dreams which dem each tell his neighbor, as dem fathers forgot my name because of Baal.
The prophet who has a dream, Make e tell a dream; and person wey has my word, Make e speak my word faithfully. Wetin be the straw to the wheat?” says Baba God.
“No be my word like fire?” says Baba God; “and like a hammer that breaks the rock in pieces?
“So see am, I be against the prophets,” says Baba God, “who each steal my words from his neighbor.
See am, I be against the prophets,” says Baba God, “who use dem tongues, and say, ‘He says.’

See am, I be against people wey prophesy lying dreams,” says Baba God, “who tell dem, and cause my people to err by dem lies, and by dem vain boasting; yet I didn’t send dem, nor command dem; neither do dem profit this people at all,” says Baba God.
“When this people, or the prophet, or a priest, shall ask you, saying, ‘Wetin be the message from Baba God?’ Then you shall tell dem, ‘“What message? I go throw you off,” says Baba God.’
As for the prophet, and the priest, and the people, who say, ‘The message from Baba God,’ I go even punish that man and his household.
You shall say everyone to his neighbor, and everyone to his brother, ‘What has Baba God answer?’ and, ‘What has Baba God spoken?’
You shall mention the message from Baba God no more: for every man’s own word has become his message; for you have perverted the words of the living God, of Baba God of Armies, our God.
You shall say to the prophet, ‘What has Baba God answer you?’ and, ‘What has Baba God spoken?’
Although you say, ‘The message from Baba God;’ so Baba God says: ‘Because you say this word, “The message from Baba God,” and I have sent to you, telling you not to say, “The message from Baba God;”
so, see am, I go utterly forget you, and I go throw you off, and the city that I give to you and to una fathers, away from my presence.
I go bring an everlasting reproach on you, and a perpetual shame, which no go be forgotten.’”

Baba God showed me, and see am, two baskets of figs set before Baba God’s temple, after that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away captive Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and the princes of Judah, with the craftsmen and smiths, from Jerusalem, and had bring dem to Babylon.
One basket had very good figs, like the figs that are first-ripe; and the other basket had very bad figs, which could not be eaten, dem were so bad.
Then Baba God ask me, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” I talk say, “Figs. The good figs are very good, and the bad are very bad, so bad that no fit be eaten.”
Baba God’s word come to me, saying,
“Baba God, the God of Israel says: ‘Like these good figs, so will I regard the captives of Judah, whom I have sent out of this place into the land of the Chaldeans, for good.
For I go set my eyes on dem for good, and I go bring dem again to this land. I go build dem, and not pull dem down. I go plant dem, and not pluck dem up.
I go give dem a heart to know me, that I be Baba God: and dem go be my people, and I go be dem God; for dem shall return to me with dem whole heart.

“‘As the bad figs, which no fit be eaten, Dem be so bad,’ surely Baba God says, ‘So I go give up Zedekiah the king of Judah, and his princes, and the remnant of Jerusalem, who remain in this land, and people wey live in the land of Egypt.
I go even give dem up to be tossed back and forth among all the kingdoms of the earth for evil; to be a reproach and a proverb, a taunt and a curse, in all places where I shall drive dem.
I go send the sword, the famine, and the pestilence, among dem, until dem be consumed from off the land that I give to dem and to dem fathers.’”
The word that come to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah (the same was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon),
which Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all the people of Judah, and to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying:

From the thirteenth year of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah, even to this day, these twenty-three years, Baba God’s word has come to me, and I have spoken to you, rising up early and speaking; but you have not listened.
Baba God has sent to you all his workers the prophets, rising up early and sending dem (but you have not listened, nor inclined una ear to hear)
saying, “Return now everyone from his evil way, and from the evil of una doings, and live in the land that Baba God has given to you and to una fathers, from of old and even forever more.
No go after other gods to serve dem or worship dem, and no provoke me to anger with the work of una hands; and I go do you no harm.”
“Yet you have not listened to me,” says Baba God; “that you may provoke me to anger with the work of una hands to una own hurt.”
So Baba God of Armies says: “Because you have not heard my words,

see am, I go send and take all the families of the north,” says Baba God, “and I go send to Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my worker, and will bring dem against this land, and against its inhabitants, and against all these nations around. I go utterly destroy dem, and make dem an astonishment, and a hissing, and perpetual desolations.
Moreover I go take from dem the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the lamp.
This whole land go be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.

“It shall happen, when seventy years are accomplished, that I go punish the king of Babylon, and that nation,” says Baba God, “for dem wickedness, and the land of the Chaldeans; and I go make it desolate forever.
I go bring on that land all my words which I have pronounced against it, even all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah has prophesied against all the nations.
For many nations and great kings shall make bondservants of dem, even of dem; and I go recompense dem according to dem deeds, and according to the work of dem hands.”
For Baba God, the God of Israel, says to me: “take this cup of the wine of serious anger at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send you, to drink it.
Dem shall drink, and reel back and forth, and be mad, because of the sword that I go send among dem.”
Then take I the cup at Baba God’s hand, and made all the nations to drink, to whom Baba God had sent me:
Jerusalem, and the cities of Judah, and its kings, and its princes, to make dem a desolation, an astonishment, a hissing, and a curse, as it is today;
Pharaoh king of Egypt, and his workers, and his princes, and all his people;
and all the mixed people, and all the kings of the land of the Uz, and all the kings of the Philistines, and Ashkelon, and Gaza, and Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;
Edom, and Moab, and the pikin dem of Ammon;
and all the kings of Tyre, and all the kings of Sidon, and the kings of the isle which is beyond the sea;
Dedan, and Tema, and Buz, and all who have the corners of dem beard cut off;
and all the kings of Arabia, and all the kings of the mixed people who live in the wilderness;
and all the kings of Zimri, and all the kings of Elam, and all the kings of the Medes;
and all the kings of the north, far and near, one with another; and all the kingdoms of the world, which are on the surface of the earth: and the king of Sheshach shall drink after dem.
“You shall tell dem, ‘Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel says: “Drink, and be drunk, vomit, fall, and rise no more, because of the sword which I go send among you.”’
It go be, if dem refuse to take the cup at una hand to drink, then you shall tell dem, ‘Baba God of Armies says: “You shall surely drink.

For, see am, I begin to work evil at the city which is call by my name; and should you be utterly unpunished? You no go be unpunished; for I go call for a sword on all the inhabitants of the earth, says Baba God of Armies.”’

“So prophesy you against dem all these words, and tell dem, “‘Baba God will roar from on high, and utter his voice from his holy habitation; he will mightily roar against his fold. He will give a shout, as people wey tread grapes, against all the inhabitants of the earth.

A noise shall come even to the end of the earth; for Baba God has a controversy with the nations; he will enter into judgment with all flesh: as for the wicked, he will give dem to the sword,”’ says Baba God.”
Baba God of Armies says, “See am, evil shall go out from nation to nation, and a great storm go be raised up from the uttermost parts of the earth.”
The slain of Baba God go be at that day from one end of the earth even to the other end of the earth: dem no go be lamented, neither gathered, nor buried; dem go be dung on the surface of the ground.
Wail, you shepherds, and cry; and wallow in dust, you leader of the flock; for the days of una slaughter and of una dispersions are fully come, and you shall fall like a goodly vessel.
The shepherds go get no way to flee, nor the leader of the flock to escape.
A voice of the cry of the shepherds, and the wailing of the leader of the flock, for Baba God lays waste dem pasture.
The peaceable folds are bring to silence because of the fierce anger of Baba God.
He has left his covert, as the lion; for dem land has become an astonishment because of the fierceness of the oppression, and because of his fierce anger.
For the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word come from Baba God:

“Baba God says: ‘Stand in the court of Baba God’s house, and speak to all the cities of Judah, which come to worship in Baba God’s house, all the words that I command you to speak to dem. No omit a word.
It may be Dem go listen, and turn every man from his evil way; that I may relent from the evil which I intend to do to dem because of the evil of dem doings.’
You shall tell dem, “Baba God says: ‘If You go not listen to me, to walk in my law, which I have set before you,
to listen to the words of my workers the prophets, whom I send to you, even rising up early and sending dem, but you have not listened;
then I go make this house like Shiloh, and will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.”’”
The priests and the prophets and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in Baba God’s house.
When Jeremiah had finished speaking all that Baba God had commanded him to speak to all the people, the priests and the prophets and all the people seized him, saying, “You shall surely die!
Why have you prophesied in Baba God’s name, saying, ‘This house go be like Shiloh, and this city go be desolate, without inhabitant?’” All the people were crowded around Jeremiah in Baba God’s house.
When the princes of Judah heard these things, dem come up from the king’s house to Baba God’s house; and dem sat in the entry of the new gate of Baba God’s house.
Then spoke the priests and the prophets to the princes and to all the people, saying, “This man is worthy of death; for he has prophesied against this city, as you have heard with una ears.”
Then Jeremiah spoke to all the princes and to all the people, saying, “Baba God sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city all the words that you have heard.
Now so amend una ways and una doings, and obey Baba God una God’s voice; and Baba God will relent from the evil that he has pronounced against you.
But as for me, see am, I be in una hand. Do with me Wetin be good and right in una eyes.

Only know for certain that, if you put me to death, You go bring innocent blood on unaself, and on this city, and on its inhabitants; for in truth Baba God has sent me to you to speak all these words in una ears.”
Then the princes and all the people talk say to the priests and to the prophets: “This man No be worthy of death; for he has spoken to us in the name of Baba God our God.”
Then certain of the elders of the land rose up, and spoke to all the assembly of the people, saying,

“Micah the Morashtite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah; and he spoke to all the people of Judah, saying, ‘Baba God of Armies says: “‘Zion Go be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of a forest.’

Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Didn’t he fear Baba God, and entreat the favor of Baba God, and Baba God relented of the disaster which he had pronounced against dem? We would commit great evil against our own souls that way!”
There was also a man who prophesied in Baba God’s name, Uriah the son of Shemaiah of Kiriath Jearim; and he prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of Jeremiah.
When Jehoiakim the king, with all his mighty men, and all the princes, heard his words, the king sought to put him to death; but when Uriah heard it, he was afraid, and fled, and go into Egypt:
and Jehoiakim the king sent men into Egypt, Elnathan the son of Achbor, and certain men with him, into Egypt;
and dem fetched Uriah out of Egypt, and bring him to Jehoiakim the king, who killed him with the sword, and throw his dead body into the graves of the common people.
But the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah, that dem no suppose give him into the hand of the people to put him to death.
For the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, come this word to Jeremiah from Baba God, saying,
Baba God says to me: “Make bonds and bars, and put dem on una neck.

Then send dem to the king of Edom, and to the king of Moab, and to the king of the pikin dem of Ammon, and to the king of Tyre, and to the king of Sidon, by the hand of the messengers who come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah.
Give dem a command to dem masters, saying, ‘Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel says, “You shall tell una masters:
‘I have made the earth, the men and the animals that are on the surface of the earth, by my great power and by my outstretched arm; and I give it to whom it seems right to me.
Now I have given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my worker; and I have also given the animals of the field to him to serve him.
All the nations will serve him, and his son, and his son’s son, until the time of his own land comes. Then many nations and great kings will make him dem bondservant.

“‘“‘It will happen that the nation and the kingdom which No go serve the same Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and that No go put dem neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, that nation will I punish,’ says Baba God, ‘with the sword, and with the famine, and with the pestilence, until I have consumed dem by his hand.
But as for you, no you listen to una prophets, nor to una diviners, nor to una dreams, nor to una soothsayers, nor to una sorcerers, who speak to you, saying, “You no go serve the king of Babylon;”
for dem prophesy a lie to you, to remove you far from una land, and that I should drive you out, and you should perish.

But the nation that shall bring dem neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him, that nation will I let remain in dem own land,’ says Baba God; ‘and dem shall till it, and live inside am.’”’”
I spoke to Zedekiah king of Judah according to all these words, saying, “Bring una necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live.
Why will you die, you and una people, by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence, as Baba God has spoken concerning the nation that No go serve the king of Babylon?
No listen to the words of the prophets who speak to you, saying, ‘You no go serve the king of Babylon;’ for dem prophesy a lie to you.
For I have not sent dem,” says Baba God, “but dem prophesy falsely in my name; that I may drive you out, and that you may perish, you, and the prophets who prophesy to you.”

Also I spoke to the priests and to all this people, saying, Baba God says, “No listen to the words of una prophets who prophesy to you, saying, ‘See am, the vessels of Baba God’s house shall now shortly be bring again from Babylon;’ for dem prophesy a lie to you.
No listen to dem. Serve the king of Babylon, and live. Why should this city become a desolation?

But if Dem be prophets, and if Baba God’s word is with dem, Make dem now make intercession to Baba God of Armies, that the vessels which are left in Baba God’s house, and in the house of the king of Judah, and at Jerusalem, no go to Babylon.
For Baba God of Armies says concerning the pillars, and concerning the sea, and concerning the bases, and concerning the residue of the vessels that are left in this city,
which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon didn’t take, when he carried away captive Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, from Jerusalem to Babylon, and all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem;
yes, Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says concerning the vessels that are left in Baba God’s house, and in the house of the king of Judah, and at Jerusalem:
‘Dem go be carried to Babylon, and there shall dem be, until the day that I visit dem,’ says Baba God; ‘then I go bring dem up, and restore dem to this place.’”

That same year, For the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month, Hananiah the son of Azzur, the prophet, who was of Gibeon, spoke to me in Baba God’s house, in the presence of the priests and of all the people, saying,
“Thus speaks Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, saying, ‘I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Within two full years will I bring again into this place all the vessels of Baba God’s house, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon take away from this place, and carried to Babylon.
I go bring again to this place Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, with all the captives of Judah, who go to Babylon,’ says Baba God; ‘for I go break the yoke of the king of Babylon.’”
Then the prophet Jeremiah talk say to the prophet Hananiah in the presence of the priests, and in the presence of all the people who stood in Baba God’s house,

even the prophet Jeremiah talk say, “Amen! May Baba God do so. May Baba God perform una words which you have prophesied, to bring again the vessels of Baba God’s house, and all dem of the captivity, from Babylon to this place.
Nevertheless listen now to this word that I speak in una ears, and in the ears of all the people:
The prophets who Don dey before me and before you of old prophesied against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.
The prophet who prophesies of peace, when the word of the prophet shall happen, then shall the prophet be known, that Baba God has truly sent him.”
Then Hananiah the prophet take the bar from off the prophet Jeremiah’s neck, and broke it.

Hananiah spoke in the presence of all the people, saying, “Baba God says: ‘Even so I go break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon within two full years from off the neck of all the nations.’” Then the prophet Jeremiah go his way.
Then Baba God’s word come to Jeremiah, after that Hananiah the prophet had broken the bar from off the neck of the prophet Jeremiah, saying,
“Go, and tell Hananiah, saying, ‘Baba God says, “You have broken the bars of wood, but you have made in dem place bars of iron.”

For Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel says, “I have put a yoke of iron on the neck of all these nations, that dem may serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; and Dem go serve him. I have also given him the animals of the field.”’”
Then the prophet Jeremiah talk say to Hananiah the prophet, “Listen, Hananiah! Baba God has not sent you, but you make this people trust in a lie.
So Baba God says, ‘See am, I go send you away from off the surface of the earth. This year You go die, because you have spoken rebellion against Baba God.’”
So Hananiah the prophet died the same year in the seventh month.

Now these are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the residue of the elders of the captivity, and to the priests, to the prophets, and to all the people, whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away captive from Jerusalem to Babylon,
(after that Jeconiah the king, the queen mother, the eunuchs, the princes of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen, and the smiths, had comot from Jerusalem),
by the hand of Elasah the son of Shaphan, and Gemariah the son of Hilkiah, (whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Babylon to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon), saying,
Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says to all the captivity, whom I have caused to be carried away captive from Jerusalem to Babylon:
“Build houses, and live in dem; and plant gardens, and eat dem fruit.
Take wives, and father sons and daughters; and take wives for una sons, and give una daughters to husbands, that dem may bear sons and daughters; and multiply there, and no be diminished.
Seek the peace of the city where I have caused you to be carried away captive, and pray to Baba God for it; for in its peace you go get peace.”
For Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel says: “No let una prophets Wey be among you, and una diviners, deceive you; neither listen to una dreams which you cause to be dreamed.
For dem prophesy falsely to you in my name. I have not sent dem,” says Baba God.
For Baba God says, “After seventy years are accomplished for Babylon, I go visit you, and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place.
For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says Baba God, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.
You shall call on me, and you shall go and pray to me, and I go listen to you.
You shall seek me, and find me, when you shall search for me with all una heart.

I go be find by you,” says Baba God, “and I go turn again una captivity, and I go gather you from all the nations, and from all the places where I have driven you, says Baba God; and I go bring you again to the place from where I caused you to be carried away captive.”
Because you have talk say, “Baba God has raised us up prophets in Babylon;”
Baba God says concerning the king who sits on David’s throne, and concerning all the people who live in this city, una brothers who haven’t gone with you into captivity;
Baba God of Armies says: “See am, I go send on dem the sword, the famine, and the pestilence, and will make dem like vile figs, that no fit be eaten, Dem be so bad.

I go pursue after dem with the sword, with the famine, and with the pestilence, and will deliver dem to be tossed back and forth among all the kingdoms of the earth, to be an object of horror, and an astonishment, and a hissing, and a reproach, among all the nations where I have driven dem;
because dem have not listened to my words,” says Baba God, “with which I sent to dem my workers the prophets, rising up early and sending dem; but you would not hear,” says Baba God.
Hear so Baba God’s word, all you of the captivity, whom I have sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon.

Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says concerning Ahab the son of Kolaiah, and concerning Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, who prophesy a lie to you in my name: “See am, I go deliver dem into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; and he shall kill dem before una eyes.
A curse go be taken up about dem by all the captives of Judah Wey be in Babylon, saying, ‘Baba God make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire;’

because dem have done foolish things in Israel, and have committed adultery with dem neighbors’ wives, and have spoken words in my name falsely, which I didn’t command dem. I be person wey knows, and am witness,” says Baba God.
Concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite you shall speak, saying,

“Thus speaks Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, saying, ‘Because you have sent letters in una own name to all the people Wey be at Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah, the priest, and to all the priests, saying,

“Baba God has made you priest in the place of Jehoiada the priest, that there may be officers in Baba God’s house, for every man Wey be mad, and makes imself a prophet, that you should put him in the stocks and in shackles.
Now so, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who makes imself a prophet to you,
because he has sent to us in Babylon, saying, The captivity is long: build houses, and live in dem; and plant gardens, and eat dem fruit?”’”
Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the ears of Jeremiah the prophet.
Then Baba God’s word come to Jeremiah, saying,
“Send to all dem of the captivity, saying, ‘Baba God says concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite: “Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you, and I didn’t send him, and he has caused you to trust in a lie;”

so Baba God says, “See am, I go punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite, and his offspring. He no go have a man to live among this people, neither shall he see the good that I go do to my people,” says Baba God, “because he has spoken rebellion against Baba God.”’”
The word that come to Jeremiah from Baba God, saying,
“Baba God, the God of Israel, says, ‘Write all the words that I have spoken to you in a book.

For, see am, the days come,’ says Baba God, ‘that I go turn again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah,’ says Baba God. ‘I go cause dem to return to the land that I give to dem fathers, and dem shall possess it.’”
These are the words that Baba God spoke concerning Israel and concerning Judah.
For Baba God says: “We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace.
Ask now, and see whether a man travails with pikin. Why do I see every man with his hands on his waist, as a woman in travail, and all faces are turned pale?
Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it. It is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he go be saved out of it.
It shall come to pass in that day, says Baba God of Armies, that I go break his yoke from off una neck, and will burst una bonds; and strangers shall no more make dem dem bondservants;
but Dem go serve Baba God dem God, and David dem king, whom I go raise up to dem.

So no you be afraid, O Jacob my worker, says Baba God; neither be dismayed, Israel: for, see am, I go save you from far away, and una offspring from the land of dem captivity. Jacob shall return, and go be quiet and at ease, and Nobody shall make him afraid.

For I be with you, says Baba God, to save you; for I go make a full end of all the nations where I have scattered you, but I go not make a full end of you; but I go correct you in measure, and will in no way leave you unpunished.”
For Baba God says, “Una hurt is incurable, and una wound grievous.
E get Nobody to plead una cause, that you may be bound up. You have no healing medicines.

All una lovers have forgotten you. Dem no seek you: for I have wounded you with the wound of an enemy, with the chastisement of a cruel one, for the greatness of una wickedness, because una sins were increased.
Why do you cry for una hurt? Una pain is incurable: for the greatness of una wickedness, because una sins were increased, I have done these things to you.
So all people wey devour you go be devoured; and all una adversaries, everyone of dem, shall go into captivity; and people wey plunder you go be plunder, and all who prey on You go I give for a prey.
For I go restore health to you, and I go heal you of una wounds,” says Baba God; “because dem have call you an outcast, saying, ‘It is Zion, whom no man seeks after.’”

Baba God says: “See am, I go turn again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have compassion on his dwelling places. The city go be built on its own hill, and the palace go be inhabited in its own place.
Out of dem shall proceed thanksgiving and the voice of people wey make merry. I go multiply dem, and dem no go be few; I go also glorify dem, and Dem go not be small.
Dem pikin dem also go be as before, and dem congregation go be established before me. I go punish all who oppress dem.

Dem prince go be of themselves, and dem ruler shall proceed from among dem. I go cause him to draw near, and he shall approach to me; for Wey be person wey has had boldness to approach to me?” says Baba God.
“You go be my people, and I go be una God.
See am, Baba God’s storm, his serious anger, has gone out, a sweeping storm: it shall burst on the head of the wicked.
The fierce anger of Baba God No go return, until he has executed, and until he has performed the intentions of his heart. In the latter days You go understand it.”
“At that time,” says Baba God, “I go be the God of all the families of Israel, and Dem go be my people.”
Baba God says, “The people who survive the sword find favor in the wilderness; even Israel, when I go to cause him to rest.”
Baba God appeared of old to me, saying, “Yes, I have love you with an everlasting love. So I have drawn you with loving kindness.
I go build you again, and You go be built, O virgin of Israel. You go again be adorned with una tambourines, and will go out in the dances of people wey make merry.
Again You go plant vineyards on the mountains of Samaria. The planters will plant, and will enjoy its fruit.
For there Go be a day that the watchmen on the hills of Ephraim cry, ‘Arise, and Make we go up to Zion to Baba God our God.’”
For Baba God says, “Sing with gladness for Jacob, and shout for the chief of the nations. Publish, praise, and say, ‘Baba God, save una people, the remnant of Israel!’

See am, I go bring dem from the north country, and gather dem from the uttermost parts of the earth, along with the blind and the lame, the woman with pikin and her who travails with pikin together. Dem go return as a great company.

Dem shall come with weeping; and with petitions will I lead dem: I go cause dem to walk by rivers of waters, in a straight way in which dem no go stumble; for I be a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
“Hear Baba God’s word, you nations, and declare it in the islands far away off; and say, ‘Person wey scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd does his flock.’
For Baba God has ransomed Jacob, and redeemed him from the hand of him who was stronger than he.

Dem shall come and sing in the height of Zion, and shall flow to the goodness of Baba God, to the grain, and to the new wine, and to the oil, and to the young of the flock and of the herd: and dem soul go be as a watered garden; and dem no go sorrow any more at all.
Then the virgin will glad well-well in the dance, and the young men and the old together; for I go turn dem mourning into gladness, and will comfort dem, and make dem glad well-well from dem sorrow.
I go satiate the soul of the priests with fatness, and my people go be satisfied with my goodness,” says Baba God.
Baba God says: “A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation, and bitter weeping, Rachel weeping for her pikin dem; she refuses to be comforted for her pikin dem, because Dem be no more.”
Baba God says: “Refrain una voice from weeping, and una eyes from tears; for una work go be rewarded,” says Baba God; “and dem shall come again from the land of the enemy.
E get hope for una latter end,” says Baba God; “and una pikin dem shall come again to dem own border.
“I have surely heard Ephraim bemoaning imself thus, ‘You have chastised me, and I was chastised, as an untrained calf: turn me, and I go be turned; for You be Baba God my God.
Surely after that I was turned, I repented; and after that I was instructed, I struck on my thigh: I was ashamed, yes, even confounded, because I bore the reproach of my youth.’
Is Ephraim my dear son? is he a darling pikin? for as often as I speak against him, I do earnestly remember him still: so my heart yearns for him; I go surely have mercy on him,” says Baba God.
“Set up road signs, make guideposts; set una heart toward the highway, even the way by which you go: turn again, virgin of Israel, turn again to these una cities.
How long will you go here and there, you backsliding daughter? for Baba God has created a new thing in the earth: a woman shall encompass a man.”

Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: “Yet again shall dem use this speech in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I shall bring again dem captivity: ‘Baba God bless you, habitation of righteousness, mountain of holiness.’
Judah and all its cities shall live inside am together, the farmers, and people wey go about with flocks.
For I have satiated the weary soul, and every sorrowful soul I have replenished.”
On this I awakened, and see; and my sleep was sweet to me.
“See am, the days come,” says Baba God, “that I go sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man, and with the seed of animal.
It shall happen that, like as I have watched over dem to pluck up and to break down and to overthrow and to destroy and to afflict, so will I watch over dem to build and to plant,” says Baba God.
“In those days dem shall say no more, “‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the pikin dem’s teeth are set on edge.’
But everyone shall die for his own wickedness: every man who eats the sour grapes, his teeth go be set on edge.
“See am, the days come,” says Baba God, “that I go make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah:

not according to the covenant that I made with dem fathers in the day that I take dem by the hand to bring dem out of the land of Egypt; which my covenant dem broke, although I was a husband to dem,” says Baba God.

“But this is the covenant that I go make with the house of Israel after those days,” says Baba God: I go put my law in dem inward parts, and in dem heart will I write it; and I go be dem God, and dem go be my people:

and dem shall teach no more every man his neighbor, and every man his brother, saying, ‘Know Baba God;’ for dem shall all know me, from dem least to dem greatest,” says Baba God: “for I go forgive dem wickedness, and dem sin will I remember no more.”

Baba God, wey dey give the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, who stirs up the sea, so that its waves roar; Baba God of Armies is his name, says:
“If these ordinances depart from before me,” says Baba God, “then the offspring of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me forever.”

Baba God says: “If heaven above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath, then I go also throw off all the offspring of Israel for all that dem have done,” says Baba God.
“See am, the days come,” says Baba God, “that the city go be built to Baba God from the tower of Hananel to the gate of the corner.
The measuring line shall go out further straight onward to the hill Gareb, and shall turn about to Goah.

The whole valley of the dead bodies and of the ashes, and all the fields to the brook Kidron, to the corner of the horse gate toward the east, go be holy to Baba God; it no go be plucked up, nor thrown down any more forever.”
The word that come to Jeremiah from Baba God in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
Now at that time the king of Babylon’s army was besieging Jerusalem; and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the guard, which was in the king of Judah’s house.
For Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying, “Why do you prophesy, and say, ‘Baba God says, “See am, I go give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall take it;

and Zedekiah king of Judah no go escape out of the hand of the Chaldeans, but shall surely be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon, and shall speak with him mouth to mouth, and his eyes shall see his eyes;
and he shall bring Zedekiah to Babylon, and he go be there until I visit him,” says Baba God: “though you fight with the Chaldeans, you no go prosper?”’”
Jeremiah talk say, “Baba God’s word come to me, saying,
‘See am, Hanamel the son of Shallum una uncle shall come to you, saying, “Buy my field that is in Anathoth; for the right of redemption is yours to buy it.”’”

“So Hanamel my uncle’s son come to me in the court of the guard according to Baba God’s word, and talk say to me, ‘Please buy my field that is in Anathoth, which is in the land of Benjamin; for the right of inheritance is yours, and the redemption is yours; buy it for yourself.’ “Then I know that this was Baba God’s word.
I bought the field that was in Anathoth of Hanamel my uncle’s son, and weighed him the money, even seventeen shekels of silver.
I signed the deed, sealed it, call witnesses, and weighed the money in the balances to him.
So I take the deed of the purchase, both that which was sealed, containing the terms and conditions, and that which was open;

and I delivered the deed of the purchase to Baruch the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, in the presence of Hanamel my uncle’s son, and in the presence of the witnesses who subscribed the deed of the purchase, before all the Jews who sat in the court of the guard.
“I commanded Baruch before dem, saying,

Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel says: ‘Take these deeds, this deed of the purchase which is sealed, and this deed which is open, and put dem in an earthen vessel; that dem may continue many days.’
For Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel says: ‘Houses and fields and vineyards shall yet again be bought in this land.’
Now after I had delivered the deed of the purchase to Baruch the son of Neriah, I prayed to Baba God, saying,
“Ah Lord Baba God! See am, you have made the heavens and the earth by una great power and by una outstretched arm; E get nothing too hard for you,
who show loving kindness to thousands, and recompense the wickedness of the fathers into the bosom of dem pikin dem after dem; the great, the mighty God, Baba God of Armies is his name;
great in counsel, and mighty in work; whose eyes are open to all the ways of the sons of men, to give everyone according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings:
who performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, even to this day, both in Israel and among other men; and made yourself a name, as it is today;
and bring una people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs, and with wonders, and with a strong hand, and with an outstretched arm, and with great terror;
and give dem this land, which you swore to dem fathers to give dem, a land flowing with milk and honey;

and dem come in, and possessed it, but dem didn’t obey una voice, neither walked in una law; dem have done nothing of all that you commanded dem to do: so you have caused all this evil to come upon dem.

“See am, the mounds, dem have come to the city to take it; and the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans who fight against it, because of the sword, and of the famine, and of the pestilence; and Wetin you have spoken has happened; and see am, you see it.
You have talk say to me, Lord Baba God, ‘Buy the field for money, and call witnesses;’ whereas the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.”
Then Baba God’s word come to Jeremiah, saying,
“See am, I be Baba God, the God of all flesh: is there anything too hard for me?
So Baba God says: See am, I go give this city into the hand of the Chaldeans, and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he shall take it:

and the Chaldeans, who fight against this city, shall come and set this city on fire, and burn it, with the houses, on whose roofs dem have offered incense to Baal, and poured out drink offerings to other gods, to provoke me to anger.

“For the pikin dem of Israel and the pikin dem of Judah have done only that which was evil in my sight from dem youth; for the pikin dem of Israel have only provoked me to anger with the work of dem hands, says Baba God.
For this city Don dey to me a provocation of my anger and of my serious anger from the day that dem built it even to this day; that I should remove it from before my face,

because of all the evil of the pikin dem of Israel and of the pikin dem of Judah, which dem have done to provoke me to anger, dem, dem kings, dem princes, dem priests, and dem prophets, and the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
Dem have turned to me the back, and not the face: and though I taught dem, rising up early and teaching dem, yet dem have not listened to receive instruction.
But dem set dem abominations in the house which is call by my name, to defile it.

Dem built the high places of Baal, which are in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to cause dem sons and dem daughters to pass through fire to Molech; which I didn’t command dem, neither did it come into my mind, that dem should do this abomination, to cause Judah to sin.”
Now so Baba God, the God of Israel, says concerning this city, about which you say, “It is given into the hand of the king of Babylon by the sword, and by the famine, and by the pestilence:”

“See am, I go gather dem out of all the countries, where I have driven dem in my anger, and in my serious anger, and in great indignation; and I go bring dem again to this place, and I go cause dem to live safely:
and dem go be my people, and I go be dem God:
and I go give dem one heart and one way, that dem may fear me forever, for dem good, and of dem pikin dem after dem:
and I go make an everlasting covenant with dem, that I go not turn away from following dem, to do dem good; and I go put my fear in dem hearts, that dem may not depart from me.
Yes, I go glad well-well over dem to do dem good, and I go plant dem in this land assuredly with my whole heart and with my whole soul.”
For Baba God says: “Like as I have bring all this great evil on this people, so will I bring on dem all the good that I have promised dem.
Fields go be bought in this land, about which you say, It is desolate, without man or animal; it is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.

Men shall buy fields for money, and subscribe the deeds, and seal dem, and call witnesses, in the land of Benjamin, and in the places about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, and in the cities of the hill country, and in the cities of the lowland, and in the cities of the South: for I go cause dem captivity to return,” says Baba God.
Moreover Baba God’s word come to Jeremiah the second time, while he was yet shut up in the court of the guard, saying,
“Baba God wey do it, Baba God who forms it to establish it; Baba God is his name, says:
‘Call to me, and I go answer you, and will show you great things, and difficult, which you no know.’

For Baba God, the God of Israel, says concerning the houses of this city, and concerning the houses of the kings of Judah, which are broken down to make a defense against the mounds and against the sword;

while men come to fight with the Chaldeans, and to fill dem with the dead bodies of men, whom I have killed in my anger and in my serious anger, and for all whose wickedness I have hidden my face from this city:
‘See am, I go bring it health and cure, and I go cure dem; and I go reveal to dem abundance of peace and truth.
I go cause the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Israel to return, and will build dem, as at the first.
I go cleanse dem from all dem wickedness, by which dem have sinned against me; and I go pardon all dem iniquities, by which dem have sinned against me, and by which dem have transgressed against me.

This city go be to me for a name of gladness, for a praise and for a glory, before all the nations of the earth, which shall hear all the good that I do to dem, and shall fear and tremble for all the good and for all the peace that I procure to it.’”

Baba God says: “Yet again there go be heard in this place, about which you say, ‘It is waste, without man and without animal, even in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, that are desolate, without man and without inhabitant and without animal,’

the voice of gladness and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of people wey say, ‘Thank God to Baba God of Armies, for Baba God is good, for his loving kindness endures forever;’ who bring thanksgiving into Baba God’s house. For I go cause the captivity of the land to return as at the first,” says Baba God.
Baba God of Armies says: “Yet again shall there be in this place, which is waste, without man and without animal, and in all its cities, a habitation of shepherds causing dem flocks to lie down.

In the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the lowland, and in the cities of the South, and in the land of Benjamin, and in the places about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, shall the flocks again pass under the hands of him who counts dem,” says Baba God.
“See am, the days come,” says Baba God, “that I go perform that good word which I have spoken concerning the house of Israel and concerning the house of Judah.
“In those days, and at that time, I go cause a Branch of righteousness to grow up to David; and he will execute justice and righteousness in the land.
In those days Judah Go be saved, and Jerusalem will live safely; and this is the name by which she go be call: Baba God our righteousness.”
For Baba God says: “David shall never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel;
neither shall the priests the Levites want a man before me to offer burnt offerings, and to burn meal offerings, and to do sacrifice continually.”
Baba God’s word come to Jeremiah, saying,
“Baba God says: ‘If you can break my covenant of the day, and my covenant of the night, so that there no go be day and night in dem season;
then may also my covenant be broken with David my worker, that he no go have a son to reign on his throne; and with the Levites the priests, my ministers.
As the army of the sky no fit be counted, neither the sand of the sea measured; so I go multiply the offspring of David my worker, and the Levites who minister to me.’”
Baba God’s word come to Jeremiah, saying,
“No consider what this people has spoken, saying, ‘The two families which Baba God chose, he has throw dem off?’ Thus dem despise my people, that dem should be no more a nation before dem.”
Baba God says: “If my covenant of day and night fails, if I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth;

then I go also throw away the offspring of Jacob, and of David my worker, so that I go not take of his offspring to be rulers over the offspring of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: for I go cause dem captivity to return, and Go get mercy on dem.”

The word which come to Jeremiah from Baba God, when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and all his army, and all the kingdoms of the earth that were under his dominion, and all the peoples, were fighting against Jerusalem, and against all the cities of it, saying:

“Baba God, the God of Israel, says, ‘Go, and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah, and tell him, Baba God says, “See am, I go give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.

You no go escape out of his hand, but will surely be taken, and delivered into his hand. Una eyes will see the eyes of the king of Babylon, and he will speak with you mouth to mouth. You go go to Babylon.”’
“Yet hear Baba God’s word, O Zedekiah king of Judah: Baba God says concerning you, ‘You no go die by the sword.

You go die in peace; and with the burnings of una fathers, the former kings who were before you, so Dem go make a burning for you. Dem shall lament you, saying, “Ah Lord!” for I have spoken the word,’ says Baba God.”
Then Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem,

when the king of Babylon’s army was fighting against Jerusalem, and against all the cities of Judah that were left, against Lachish and against Azekah; for these alone remain of the cities of Judah as fortified cities.
The word come to Jeremiah from Baba God, after king Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people who were at Jerusalem, to proclaim liberty to dem;
that every man should let his male worker, and every man his female worker, Wey be a Hebrew or a Hebrewess, go free; that Nobody should make bondservants of dem, of a Jew his brother.

All the princes and all the people obeyed, who had entered into the covenant, that everyone should let his male worker, and everyone his female worker, go free, that Nobody should make bondservants of dem any more; dem obeyed, and Make dem go:
but afterwards dem turned, and caused the workers and the handmaids, whom dem had let go free, to return, and bring dem into subjection for workers and for handmaids.
So Baba God’s word come to Jeremiah from Baba God, saying,
“Baba God, the God of Israel, says: ‘I made a covenant with una fathers in the day that I bring dem out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, saying,

At the end of seven years, every man of you shall release his brother Wey be a Hebrew, who Don dey sold to you, and has served you six years. You shall Make e go free from you; but una fathers didn’t listen to me, and didn’t incline dem ear.
You had now turned, and had done that which is right in my eyes, in every man proclaiming liberty to his neighbor; and you had made a covenant before me in the house which is call by my name;

but you turned and profaned my name, and every man caused his worker, and every man his female worker, whom you had let go free at dem pleasure, to return; and you bring dem into subjection, to be to you for workers and for handmaids.’”

So Baba God says: “You have not listened to me, to proclaim liberty, every man to his brother, and every man to his neighbor. See am, I proclaim to you a liberty,” says Baba God, “to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine. I go make you be tossed back and forth among all the kingdoms of the earth.
I go give the men who have transgressed my covenant, who have not performed the words of the covenant which dem made before me, when dem cut the calf in two and passed between its parts:
the princes of Judah, the princes of Jerusalem, the eunuchs, the priests, and all the people of the land, who passed between the parts of the calf;
I go even give dem into the hand of dem enemies, and into the hand of people wey seek dem life. Dem dead bodies Go be chop for the birds of the sky, and for the animals of the earth.

“I go give Zedekiah king of Judah and his princes into the hands of dem enemies, into the hands of people wey seek dem life, and into the hands of the king of Babylon’s army, who has gone away from you.

See am, I go command,” says Baba God, “and cause dem to return to this city; and dem shall fight against it, take it, and burn it with fire. I go make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant.”
The word which come to Jeremiah from Baba God in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying,
“Go to the house of the Rechabites, and speak to dem, and bring dem into Baba God’s house, into one of the rooms, and give dem wine to drink.”
Then I take Jaazaniah the son of Jeremiah, the son of Habazziniah, and his brothers, and all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites;

and I bring dem into Baba God’s house, into the room of the sons of Hanan the son of Igdaliah, the man of God, which was by the room of the princes, which was above the room of Maaseiah the son of Shallum, the keeper of the threshold.
I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites bowls full of wine, and cups; and I talk say to dem, “Drink wine!”
But dem talk say, “We go drink no wine; for Jonadab the son of Rechab, our father, commanded us, saying, ‘You shall drink no wine, neither you, nor una sons, forever.
You no go build a house, sow seed, plant a vineyard, or have any; but all una days you shall live in tents; that you may live many days in the land in which you live.’
We have obeyed the voice of Jonadab the son of Rechab, our father, in all that he commanded us, to drink no wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons, or our daughters;
and not to build houses for ourselves to live in. We have no vineyard, field, or seed;
but we have lived in tents, and have obeyed, and done according to all that Jonadab our father commanded us.

But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon come up into the land, we talk say, ‘Come, and Make we go to Jerusalem for fear of the army of the Chaldeans, and for fear of the army of the Syrians; so We go live at Jerusalem.’”
Then Baba God’s word come to Jeremiah, saying,
“Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘Go, and tell the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, “Will you not receive instruction to listen to my words?” says Baba God.

“The words of Jonadab the son of Rechab, that he commanded his sons, not to drink wine, are performed; and to this day dem drink none, for dem obey dem father’s commandment: but I have spoken to you, rising up early and speaking; and you have not listened to me.

I have sent also to you all my workers the prophets, rising up early and sending dem, saying, ‘Return now every man from his evil way, and amend una doings, and no go after other gods to serve dem, and You go live in the land which I have given to you and to una fathers:’ but you have not inclined una ear, nor listened to me.
The sons of Jonadab the son of Rechab have performed the commandment of dem father which he commanded dem, but this people has not listened to me.”’

“So Baba God, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘See am, I go bring on Judah and on all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the evil that I have pronounced against dem; because I have spoken to dem, but dem have not heard; and I have call to dem, but dem have not answer.’”

Jeremiah talk say to the house of the Rechabites, “Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘Because you have obeyed the commandment of Jonadab una father, and kept all his precepts, and done according to all that he commanded you;’
so Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘Jonadab the son of Rechab no go lack a man to stand before me forever.’”
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word come to Jeremiah from Baba God, saying,

“Take a scroll of a book, and write in it all the words that I have spoken to you against Israel, and against Judah, and against all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah, even to this day.
It may be that the house of Judah will hear all the evil which I purpose to do to dem; that dem may each return from his evil way; that I may forgive dem wickedness and dem sin.”
Then Jeremiah call Baruch the son of Neriah; and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all Baba God’s words, which he had spoken to him, on a scroll of a book.
Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, “I be restricted. I no fit go into Baba God’s house.

So you go, and read from the scroll, which you have written from my mouth, Baba God’s words in the ears of the people in Baba God’s house on the fast day. Also you shall read dem in the ears of all Judah who come out of dem cities.
It may be Dem go present dem supplication before Baba God, and will each return from his evil way; for Baba God has pronounced great anger and serious anger against this people.”
Baruch the son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading in the book Baba God’s words in Baba God’s house.

Now in the fifth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, all the people in Jerusalem, and all the people who come from the cities of Judah to Jerusalem, proclaimed a fast before Baba God.

Then Baruch read the words of Jeremiah from the book in Baba God’s house, in the room of Gemariah the son of Shaphan, the scribe, in the upper court, at the entry of the new gate of Baba God’s house, in the ears of all the people.
When Micaiah the son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, had heard out of the book all Baba God’s words,

he go down into the king’s house, into the scribe’s room: and see am, all the princes were sitting there, Elishama the scribe, Delaiah the son of Shemaiah, Elnathan the son of Achbor, Gemariah the son of Shaphan, Zedekiah the son of Hananiah, and all the princes.
Then Micaiah declared to dem all the words that he had heard, when Baruch read the book in the ears of the people.

So all the princes sent Jehudi the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, to Baruch, saying, “Take in una hand the scroll in which you have read in the ears of the people, and come.” So Baruch the son of Neriah take the scroll in his hand, and come to dem.
Dem tell am say, “Sit down now, and read it in our hearing.” So Baruch read it in dem hearing.
Now when dem had heard all the words, dem turned in fear one toward another, and talk say to Baruch, “We go surely tell the king of all these words.”
Dem ask Baruch, saying, “Tell us now, How did you write all these words at his mouth?”
Then Baruch answer dem, “He dictated all these words to me with his mouth, and I wrote dem with ink in the book.”
Then the princes talk say to Baruch, “You and Jeremiah go hide. No let anyone know where You be.”
Dem go in to the king into the court; but dem had laid up the scroll in the room of Elishama the scribe; and dem told all the words in the ears of the king.
So the king sent Jehudi to get the scroll; and he take it out of the room of Elishama the scribe. Jehudi read it in the ears of the king, and in the ears of all the princes who stood beside the king.
Now the king was sitting in the winter house in the ninth month: and there was a fire in the brazier burning before him.

When Jehudi had read three or four leaves, the king cut it with the penknife, and throw it into the fire that was in the brazier, until all the scroll was consumed in the fire that was in the brazier.
The king and his workers who heard all these words No be afraid, and didn’t tear dem garments.
Moreover Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah had made intercession to the king that he would not burn the scroll; but he would not listen to dem.
The king commanded Jerahmeel the king’s son, and Seraiah the son of Azriel, and Shelemiah the son of Abdeel, to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet; but Baba God hid dem.
Then Baba God’s word come to Jeremiah, after the king had burned the scroll, and the words which Baruch wrote at the mouth of Jeremiah, saying,
“Take again another scroll, and write in it all the former words that were in the first scroll, which Jehoiakim the king of Judah has burned.

Concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say, ‘Baba God says: “You have burned this scroll, saying, “Why have you written inside am, saying, ‘The king of Babylon shall certainly come and destroy this land, and shall cause to cease from there man and animal?’”’
So Baba God says concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: “He Go get Nobody to sit on David’s throne. His dead body Go be throw out in the day to the heat, and in the night to the frost.

I go punish him and his offspring and his workers for dem wickedness; and I go bring on dem, on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and on the men of Judah, all the evil that I have pronounced against dem, but dem didn’t listen.”’”

Then take Jeremiah another scroll, and give it to Baruch the scribe, the son of Neriah, who wrote inside am from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book which Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire; and many similar words were added to dem.
Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned as king, instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.
But neither he, nor his workers, nor the people of the land, listened to Baba God’s words, which he spoke by the prophet Jeremiah.
Zedekiah the king sent Jehucal the son of Shelemiah, and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah, the priest, to the prophet Jeremiah, saying, “Pray now to Baba God our God for us.”
Now Jeremiah come in and go out among the people; for dem had not put him into prison.
Pharaoh’s army had come out of Egypt; and when the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard news of dem, dem broke up from Jerusalem.
Then come Baba God’s word to the prophet Jeremiah, saying,

“Baba God, the God of Israel, says, ‘You shall tell the king of Judah, who sent you to me to inquire of me: “See am, Pharaoh’s army, which has come out to help you, shall return to Egypt into dem own land.
The Chaldeans shall come again, and fight against this city; and dem shall take it, and burn it with fire.”’
“Baba God says, ‘No deceive unaself, saying, “The Chaldeans shall surely depart from us;” for dem no go depart.
For though you had struck the whole army of the Chaldeans who fight against you, and there remain but wounded men among dem, yes dem would each rise up in his tent and burn this city with fire.’”
When the army of the Chaldeans had broken up from Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh’s army,
then Jeremiah go out of Jerusalem to go into the land of Benjamin, to receive his portion there, in the middle of the people.

When he was in the gate of Benjamin, a captain of the guard was there, whose name was Irijah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah; and he laid hold on Jeremiah the prophet, saying, “You be defecting to the Chaldeans!”
Then Jeremiah talk say, “That is false! I be not falling away to the Chaldeans.” But he didn’t listen to him; so Irijah siezed Jeremiah, and bring him to the princes.
The princes were angry with Jeremiah, and struck him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe; for dem had made that the prison.
When Jeremiah had come into the dungeon house, and into the cells, and Jeremiah had remain there many days,

then Zedekiah the king sent, and fetched him. The king ask him secretly in his house, and talk say, “Is there any word from Baba God?” Jeremiah talk say, “E get.” He talk say also, “You go be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon.”
Moreover Jeremiah talk say to king Zedekiah, “How have I sinned against you, against una workers, or against this people, that you have put me in prison?
Now where are una prophets who prophesied to you, saying, ‘The king of Babylon No go come against you, nor against this land?’
Now please hear, my lord the king: please let my supplication be presented before you, that you not cause me to return to the house of Jonathan the scribe, lest I die there.”

Then Zedekiah the king commanded, and dem committed Jeremiah into the court of the guard. Dem give him daily a loaf of bread out of the bakers’ street, until all the bread in the city was gone. Thus Jeremiah remain in the court of the guard.
Shephatiah the son of Mattan, and Gedaliah the son of Pashhur, and Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur the son of Malchijah, heard the words that Jeremiah spoke to all the people, saying,

“Baba God says, ‘Person wey remains in this city shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence; but person wey goes out to the Chaldeans shall live, and his life go be to him for a prey, and he shall live.’
Baba God says, ‘This city will surely be given into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, and he will take it.’”

Then the princes talk say to the king, “Please let this man be put to death; because he weakens the hands of the men of war who remain in this city, and the hands of all the people, in speaking such words to dem: for this man no dey seek the welfare of this people, but harm.”
Zedekiah the king talk say, “See am, he is in una hand; for the king no fit do anything to oppose you.”

Then take dem Jeremiah, and throw him into the dungeon of Malchijah the king’s son, that was in the court of the guard. Dem let down Jeremiah with cords. In the dungeon there was no water, but mire; and Jeremiah sank in the mire.
Now when Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, a eunuch, who was in the king’s house, heard that dem had put Jeremiah in the dungeon (the king was then sitting in the gate of Benjamin),
Ebedmelech go out of the king’s house, and spoke to the king, saying,

“My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that dem have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom dem have throw into the dungeon. He is likely to die in the place where he is, because of the famine; for E get no more bread in the city.”
Then the king commanded Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, saying, “Take from here thirty men with you, and take up Jeremiah the prophet out of the dungeon, before he dies.”
So Ebedmelech take the men with him, and go into the house of the king under the treasury, and take there rags and worn-out garments, and Make dem down by cords into the dungeon to Jeremiah.
Ebedmelech the Ethiopian talk say to Jeremiah, “Now put these rags and worn-out garments under una armpits under the cords.” Jeremiah did so.
So dem drew up Jeremiah with the cords, and take him up out of the dungeon; and Jeremiah remain in the court of the guard.

Then Zedekiah the king sent, and take Jeremiah the prophet to imself into the third entry that is in Baba God’s house. Then the king talk say to Jeremiah, “I go ask you something. Hide nothing from me.”
Then Jeremiah talk say to Zedekiah, “If I declare it to you, will you not surely put me to death? If I give you counsel, You go not listen to me.”
So Zedekiah the king swore secretly to Jeremiah, saying, “As Baba God lives, who made us this soul, I go not put you to death, neither will I give you into the hand of these men who seek una life.”

Then Jeremiah talk say to Zedekiah, “Baba God, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘If You go go out to the king of Babylon’s princes, then una soul will live, and this city No go be burned with fire. You go live, along with una house.
But if You go not go out to the king of Babylon’s princes, then this city Go be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and Dem go burn it with fire, and you no go escape out of dem hand.’”
Zedekiah the king talk say to Jeremiah, “I be afraid of the Jews who have defected to the Chaldeans, lest dem deliver me into dem hand, and dem mock me.”
But Jeremiah talk say, “Dem no go deliver you. Obey, I beg you, Baba God’s voice, in that which I speak to you; so it Go be well with you, and una soul shall live.
But if you refuse to go out, this is the word that Baba God has shown me:

‘See am, all the women Wey be left in the king of Judah’s house Go be bring out to the king of Babylon’s princes, and those women will say, “Una familiar friends have turned on you, and have prevailed over you. Una feet are sunk in the mire, dem have turned away from you.”

Dem go bring out all una wives and una pikin dem to the Chaldeans. You no go escape out of dem hand, but Go be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon. You go cause this city to be burned with fire.’”
Then Zedekiah talk say to Jeremiah, “Let no man know of these words, and you no go die.

But if the princes hear that I have talked with you, and dem come to you, and tell you, ‘Declare to us now Wetin you have talk say to the king; no hide it from us, and We go not put you to death; also what the king talk say to you;’
then you shall tell dem, ‘I presented my supplication before the king, that he would not cause me to return to Jonathan’s house, to die there.’”
Then come all the princes to Jeremiah, and ask him; and he told dem according to all these words that the king had commanded. So dem stopped speaking with him; for the matter No be perceived.
So Jeremiah stayed in the court of the guard until the day that Jerusalem was taken.
When Jerusalem was taken, (in the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army come against Jerusalem, and besieged it.
In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, the ninth day of the month, a breach was made in the city),

all the princes of the king of Babylon come in, and sat in the middle gate, Nergal Sharezer, Samgarnebo, Sarsechim, Rabsaris, Nergal Sharezer, Rabmag, with all the rest of the princes of the king of Babylon.

When Zedekiah the king of Judah and all the men of war see dem, then dem fled, and go out of the city by night, by the way of the king’s garden, through the gate between the two walls; and he go out toward the Arabah.

But the army of the Chaldeans pursued dem, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho: and when dem had taken him, dem bring him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath; and he give judgment on him.
Then the king of Babylon killed the sons of Zedekiah in Riblah before his eyes. The king of Babylon also killed all the nobles of Judah.
Moreover he put out Zedekiah’s eyes, and bound him in fetters, to carry him to Babylon.
The Chaldeans burned the king’s house, and the houses of the people, with fire, and broke down the walls of Jerusalem.

Then Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive into Babylon the residue of the people who remain in the city, the deserters also who fell away to him, and the residue of the people who remain.
But Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left of the poor of the people, who had nothing, in the land of Judah, and give dem vineyards and fields at the same time.
Now Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon commanded Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard concerning Jeremiah, saying,
“Take him, and look well to him, and do him no harm; but do to him even as he shall tell you.”
So Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard sent, and Nebushazban, Rabsaris, and Nergal Sharezer, Rabmag, and all the chief officers of the king of Babylon;
dem sent, and take Jeremiah out of the court of the guard, and committed him to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, that he should carry him home: so he lived among the people.
Now Baba God’s word come to Jeremiah, while he was shut up in the court of the guard, saying,

“Go, and speak to Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, saying, Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘See am, I go bring my words on this city for evil, and not for good; and dem go be accomplished before you in that day.
But I go deliver you in that day,’ says Baba God; ‘and You go not be given into the hand of the men of whom You be afraid.
For I go surely save you, and you no go fall by the sword, but una life go be for a prey to you; because you have put una trust in me,’ says Baba God.”

The word which come to Jeremiah from Baba God, after Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had Make e go from Ramah, when he had taken him being bound in chains among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah, who were carried away captive to Babylon.
The captain of the guard take Jeremiah, and talk say to him, “Baba God una God pronounced this evil on this place;
and Baba God has bring it, and done according as he spoke: because you have sinned against Baba God, and have not obeyed his voice, so this thing has come on you.

Now, see am, I release you today from the chains which are on una hand. If it seems good to you to come with me into Babylon, come, and I go take care of you; but if it seems bad to you to come with me into Babylon, no. See am, all the land is before you. Where it seems good and right to you to go, there go.”
