Now while he had not yet gone back, “Go back then,” he talk say, “to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has made governor over the cities of Judah, and live with him among the people; or go Anywhere wey it seems right to you to go.” So the captain of the guard give him chop and a present, and Make e go.
Then Jeremiah go to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah, and lived with him among the people who were left in the land.

Now when all the captains of the forces who were in the fields, even dem and dem men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam governor in the land, and had committed to him men, women, pikin dem, and of the poorest of the land, of people wey No be carried away captive to Babylon;

then dem come to Gedaliah to Mizpah, Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah the son of the Maacathite, dem and dem men.
Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan swore to dem and to dem men, saying, “No fear to serve the Chaldeans. Live in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and it go be well with you.

As for me, see am, I go live at Mizpah, to stand before the Chaldeans who will come to us; but you, gather wine and summer fruits and oil, and put dem in una vessels, and live in una cities that you have taken.”

Likewise when all the Jews who were in Moab, and among the pikin dem of Ammon, and in Edom, and who were in all the countries, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah, and that he had set over dem Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan;
then all the Jews come back out of all places where dem were driven, and come to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah, to Mizpah, and gathered wine and summer fruits well-well.
Moreover Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces who were in the fields, come to Gedaliah to Mizpah,
and talk say to him, “Do you know that Baalis the king of the pikin dem of Ammon has sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to take una life?” But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam didn’t believe dem.

Then Johanan the son of Kareah spoke to Gedaliah in Mizpah secretly, saying, “Please let me go, and I go kill Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and no man shall know it. Why should he take una life, that all the Jews Wey be gathered to you should be scattered, and the remnant of Judah perish?”
But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam talk say to Johanan the son of Kareah, “You no go do this thing; for you speak falsely of Ishmael.”

Now in the seventh month, Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the royal offspring and one of the chief officers of the king, and ten men with him, come to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah; and there dem ate bread together in Mizpah.

Then Ishmael the son of Nethaniah arose, and the ten men who were with him, and struck Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan with the sword, and killed him, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land.
Ishmael also killed all the Jews who were with him, with Gedaliah, at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans who were find there, the men of war.
The second day after he had killed Gedaliah, and no man know it,

men come from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria, even eighty men, having dem beards shaved and dem clothes torn, and having cut themselves, with meal offerings and frankincense in dem hand, to bring dem to Baba God’s house.
Ishmael the son of Nethaniah go out from Mizpah to meet dem, weeping all along as he go: and as he met dem, E tell dem say, “Come to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam.”
It was so, when dem come into the middle of the city, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah killed dem, and throw dem into the middle of the pit, he, and the men who were with him.

But ten men were find among people wey talk say to Ishmael, “No kill us; for we have stores hidden in the field, of wheat, and of barley, and of oil, and of honey.” So he stopped, and didn’t kill dem among dem brothers.

Now the pit in which Ishmael throw all the dead bodies of the men whom he had killed, by the side of Gedaliah (the same was who which Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel), Ishmael the son of Nethaniah filled it with people wey were killed.

Then Ishmael carried away captive all the of the people who were left in Mizpah, even the king’s daughters, and all the people who remain in Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had committed to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam. Ishmael the son of Nethaniah carried dem away captive, and comot to go over to the pikin dem of Ammon.
But when Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces who were with him, heard of all the evil that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had done,
then dem take all the men, and go to fight with Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and find him by the great waters that are in Gibeon.
Now when all the people who were with Ishmael see Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces who were with him, then dem were glad.
So all the people who Ishmael had carried away captive from Mizpah turned about and come back, and go to Johanan the son of Kareah.
But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men, and go to the pikin dem of Ammon.

Then Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces who were with him, take all the remnant of the people whom he had recovered from Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah, after that he had killed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the men of war, and the women, and the pikin dem, and the eunuchs, whom he had bring back from Gibeon.
Dem comot, and lived in Geruth Chimham, which is by Bethlehem, to go to enter into Egypt,
because of the Chaldeans; for dem were afraid of dem, because Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon made governor over the land.
Then all the captains of the forces, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least even to the greatest, come near,

and talk say to Jeremiah the prophet, “Please let our supplication be presented before you, and pray for us to Baba God una God, even for all this remnant; for We be left but a few of many, as una eyes do see us;
that Baba God una God may show us the way in which we should walk, and the thing that we should do.”

Then Jeremiah the prophet talk say to dem, “I have heard you; see am, I go pray to Baba God una God according to una words; and it shall happen that Anything wey thing Baba God shall answer you, I go declare it to you; I go keep nothing back from you.”
Then dem talk say to Jeremiah, “May Baba God be a true and faithful witness among us, if we no do according to all the word with which Baba God una God shall send you to us.
Whether it is good, or whether it is bad, We go obey the voice of Baba God our God, to whom we send you; that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of Baba God our God.”
After ten days, Baba God’s word come to Jeremiah.
Then he call Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces who were with him, and all the people from the least even to the greatest,
and talk say to dem, “Baba God, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to present una supplication before him, says:
‘If You go still live in this land, then I go build you, and not pull you down, and I go plant you, and not pluck you up; for I grieve over the distress that I have bring on you.
No fear of the king of Babylon, of whom You be afraid. No fear of him,’ says Baba God: ‘for I be with you to save you, and to deliver you from his hand.
I go grant you mercy, that he may have mercy on you, and cause you to return to una own land.
“‘But if you say, “We go not live in this land;” so that you no obey Baba God una God’s voice,
saying, “No; but We go go into the land of Egypt, where we shall see no war, nor hear the sound of the trumpet, nor have hunger of bread; and there will we live:”’
now so hear Baba God’s word, O remnant of Judah: Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says, ‘If you indeed set una faces to enter into Egypt, and go to live there;

then it shall happen, that the sword, which you fear, shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt; and the famine, about which You be afraid, shall follow close behind you there in Egypt; and you shall die there.

So shall it be with all the men who set dem faces to go into Egypt to live there: dem shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence; and none of dem shall remain or escape from the evil that I go bring on dem.’

For Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘As my anger and my serious anger Don dey poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so shall my serious anger be poured out on you, when you shall enter into Egypt; and you go be an object of horror, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach; and you shall see this place no more.’
“Baba God has spoken concerning you, remnant of Judah, No you go into Egypt: know certainly that I have testified to you today.

For you have dealt deceitfully against una own souls; for you sent me to Baba God una God, saying, ‘Pray for us to Baba God our God; and according to all that Baba God our God shall say, so declare to us, and We go do it:’
and I have declared it to you today; but you have not obeyed Baba God una God’s voice in anything for which he has sent me to you.
Now so know certainly that you shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence, in the place where you desire to go to live there.”
When Jeremiah had finished speaking to all the people all the words of Baba God dem God, with which Baba God dem God had sent him to dem, even all these words,

then Azariah the son of Hoshaiah, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the proud men spoke, saying to Jeremiah, “You speak falsely. Baba God our God has not sent you to say, ‘You no go go into Egypt to live there;’
but Baruch the son of Neriah has turned you against us, to deliver us into the hand of the Chaldeans, that dem may put us to death, and carry us away captive to Babylon.”
So Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces, and all the people, didn’t obey Baba God’s voice, to live in the land of Judah.
But Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces, take all the remnant of Judah, who had come back from all the nations where dem Bin dey driven, to live in the land of Judah;

the men, and the women, and the pikin dem, and the king’s daughters, and every person who Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan; and Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch the son of Neriah;
and dem come into the land of Egypt; for dem didn’t obey Baba God’s voice: and dem come to Tahpanhes.
Then Baba God’s word come to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,
“Take great stones in una hand, and hide dem in mortar in the brick work, which is at the entry of Pharaoh’s house in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah;

and tell dem, Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘See am, I go send and take Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my worker, and will set his throne on these stones that I have hidden; and he shall spread his royal pavilion over dem.
He will come, and will strike the land of Egypt; such as are for death go be put to death, and such as are for captivity to captivity, and such as are for the sword to the sword.

I go kindle a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt; and he shall burn dem, and carry dem away captive: and he shall array imself with the land of Egypt, as a shepherd puts on his garment; and he shall go out from there in peace.
He shall also break the pillars of Beth Shemesh, that is in the land of Egypt; and he shall burn the houses of the gods of Egypt with fire.’”
The word that come to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews who lived in the land of Egypt, who lived at Migdol, and at Tahpanhes, and at Memphis, and in the country of Pathros, saying,

“Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘You have seen all the evil that I have bring on Jerusalem, and on all the cities of Judah. See am, today Dem be a desolation, and no man dwells inside am,
because of dem wickedness which dem have committed to provoke me to anger, in that dem go to burn incense, to serve other gods, that dem didn’t know, neither dem, nor you, nor una fathers.
However I sent to you all my workers the prophets, rising up early and sending dem, saying, “Oh, no do this abominable thing that I hate.”
But dem didn’t listen and didn’t incline dem ear. Dem didn’t turn from dem wickedness, to stop burning incense to other gods.
So my serious anger and my anger was poured out, and was kindled in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem; and Dem be wasted and desolate, as it is today.’

“So now Baba God, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘Why do you commit great evil against una own souls, to cut off from unaself man and woman, infant and nursing pikin out of the middle of Judah, to leave unaself Nobody remaining;

in that you provoke me to anger with the works of una hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt, where you have gone to live; that you may be cut off, and that you may be a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?

Have you forgotten the wickedness of una fathers, and the wickedness of the kings of Judah, and the wickedness of dem wives, and una own wickedness, and the wickedness of una wives which dem committed in the land of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem?
Dem No be humbled even to this day, neither have dem feared, nor walked in my law, nor in my statutes, that I set before you and before una fathers.’
“So Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘See am, I go set my face against you for evil, even to cut off all Judah.

I go take the remnant of Judah, that have set dem faces to go into the land of Egypt to live there, and Dem go all be consumed. Dem go fall in the land of Egypt. Dem go be consumed by the sword and by the famine. Dem go die, from the least even to the greatest, by the sword and by the famine. Dem go be an object of horror, an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach.
For I go punish people wey live in the land of Egypt, as I have punished Jerusalem, by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence;

so that none of the remnant of Judah, who have gone into the land of Egypt to live there, shall escape or be left, to return into the land of Judah, to which dem have a desire to return to live there; for Nobody will return except people wey will escape.’”

Then all the men who know that dem wives burned incense to other gods, and all the women who stood by, a great assembly, even all the people who lived in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answer Jeremiah, saying,
“As for the word that you have spoken to us in Baba God’s name, We go not listen to you.

But We go certainly perform every word that has gone out of our mouth, to burn incense to the queen of the sky, and to pour out drink offerings to her, as we have done, we and our fathers, our kings and our princes, in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem; for then had we plenty of chop, and were well, and see no evil.
But since we stopped burning incense to the queen of the sky, and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked all things, and Don dey consumed by the sword and by the famine.
“When we burned incense to the queen of the sky, and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make her cakes to worship her, and pour out drink offerings to her, without our husbands?”
Then Jeremiah talk say to all the people, to the men, and to the women, even to all the people who had given him an answer, saying,

“The incense that you burned in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, you and una fathers, una kings and una princes, and the people of the land, didn’t Baba God remember dem, and didn’t it come into his mind?

Thus Baba God could no longer bear, because of the evil of una doings, and because of the abominations which you have committed; so una land has become a desolation, and an astonishment, and a curse, without inhabitant, as it is today.

Because you have burned incense, and because you have sinned against Baba God, and have not obeyed Baba God’s voice, nor walked in his law, nor in his statutes, nor in his testimonies; so this evil has happened to you, as it is today.”
Moreover Jeremiah talk say to all the people, and to all the women, “Hear Baba God’s word, all Judah Wey be in the land of Egypt!

Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says, ‘You and una wives have both spoken with una mouths, and with una hands have fulfilled it, saying, “We go surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of the sky, and to pour out drink offerings to her.” “‘Establish then una vows, and perform una vows.’

“So hear Baba God’s word, all Judah who live in the land of Egypt: ‘See am, I have sworn by my great name,’ says Baba God, ‘that my name shall no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, “As the Lord Baba God lives.”
See am, I watch over dem for evil, and not for good; and all the men of Judah Wey be in the land of Egypt go be consumed by the sword and by the famine, until Dem be all gone.

People wey escape the sword shall return out of the land of Egypt into the land of Judah, few in number; and all the remnant of Judah, who have gone into the land of Egypt to live there, shall know whose word shall stand, mine, or dem own.
“‘This go be the sign to you,’ says Baba God, ‘that I go punish you in this place, that you may know that my words shall surely stand against you for evil.’

Baba God says, ‘See am, I go give Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of people wey seek his life; as I give Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who was his enemy, and sought his life.’”

The message that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch the son of Neriah, when he wrote these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying,
“Baba God, the God of Israel, says to you, Baruch:
‘You talk say, “Woe is me now! For Baba God has added sorrow to my pain! I be weary with my groaning, and I find no rest.”’
“You shall tell him, Baba God says: ‘See am, that which I have built, I go break down, and that which I have planted I go pluck up; and this in the whole land.
Do you seek great things for yourself? No seek dem; for, see am, I go bring evil on all flesh,’ says Baba God; ‘but una life will I give to you for a prey in all places where you go.’”
Baba God’s word which come to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.

Of Egypt: concerning the army of Pharaoh Necoh king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah.
“Prepare the buckler and shield, and draw near to battle!
Harness the horses, and get up, you horsemen, and stand up with una helmets. Polish the spears, put on the coats of mail.
Why have I seen it? Dem be dismayed and are turned backward. Dem mighty ones are beaten down, have fled in haste, and no look back. Terror is on every side,” says Baba God.
“No let the swift flee away, nor the mighty man escape. In the north by the river Euphrates dem have stumbled and fallen.
“Wey be this who rises up like the Nile, whose waters toss themselves like the rivers?
Egypt rises up like the Nile, and his waters toss themselves like the rivers: and he says, ‘I go rise up, I go cover the earth. I go destroy cities and its inhabitants.’
Go up, you horses; and rage, you chariots! Let the mighty men go out: Cush and Put, who handle the shield; and the Ludim, who handle and bend the bow.

For that day is of the Lord, Baba God of Armies, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge imself of his adversaries. The sword will devour and be satiated, and will drink its fill of dem blood; for the Lord, Baba God of Armies, has a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates.
Go up into Gilead, and take balm, virgin daughter of Egypt. In vain do you use many medicines. E get no healing for you.
The nations have heard of una shame, and the earth is full of una cry; for the mighty man has stumbled against the mighty, dem both fall together.”
The word that Baba God spoke to Jeremiah the prophet, how that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon should come and strike the land of Egypt.
“Declare in Egypt, publish in Migdol, and publish in Memphis and in Tahpanhes: say, ‘Stand up, and prepare; for the sword has devoured around you.’
Why are una strong ones swept away? dem didn’t stand, because Baba God pushed dem.
He made many to stumble, yes, dem fell on each other: and dem talk say, ‘Arise, and Make we go again to our own people, and to the land of our birth, from the oppressing sword.’
Dem cried there, ‘Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he has let the appointed time pass by.’
“As I live,” says the King, whose name is Baba God of Armies, “surely like Tabor among the mountains, and like Carmel by the sea, so shall he come.
You daughter who dwells in Egypt, furnish yourself to go into captivity; for Memphis shall become a desolation, and go be burned up, without inhabitant.
“Egypt is a very beautiful heifer; but destruction out of the north has come. It has come.

Also her hired men in the middle of her are like calves of the stall; for dem also are turned back. Dem have fled away together. Dem didn’t stand, for the day of dem calamity has come on dem, the time of dem visitation.
It’s sound will go like the serpent; for dem shall march with an army, and come against her with axes, as wood cutters.
Dem shall cut down her forest,” says Baba God, “though it no fit be searched; because Dem be more than the locusts, and are innumerable.
The daughter of Egypt go be disappointed; she go be delivered into the hand of the people of the north.”
Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: “See am, I go punish Amon of No, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, with her gods, and her kings; even Pharaoh, and people wey trust in him.

I go deliver dem into the hand of people wey seek dem lives, and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of his workers. Afterwards it go be inhabited, as in the days of old,” says Baba God.

“But no you be afraid, Jacob my worker, neither be dismayed, Israel; for, see am, I go save you from far away, and una offspring from the land of dem captivity. Jacob will return, and Go be quiet and at ease. Nobody will make him afraid.

No fear, O Jacob my worker,” says Baba God; “for I be with you; for I go make a full end of all the nations where I have driven you; but I go not make a full end of you, but I go correct you in measure, and will in no way leave you unpunished.”
Baba God’s word that come to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before that Pharaoh struck Gaza.

Baba God says: “See am, waters rise up out of the north, and will become an overflowing stream, and will overflow the land and all that is inside am, the city and people wey live inside am. The men will cry, and all the inhabitants of the land shall wail.
At the noise of the stamping of the hoofs of his strong ones, at the rushing of his chariots, at the rumbling of his wheels, the fathers no look back to dem pikin dem for feebleness of hands;
because of the day that comes to destroy all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every helper who remains; for Baba God will destroy the Philistines, the remnant of the isle of Caphtor.
Baldness has come on Gaza; Ashkelon is bring to nothing, the remnant of dem valley: how long will you cut yourself?
“‘You sword of Baba God, how long will it be before You be quiet? Put yourself back into una scabbard; rest, and be still.’
“How can you be quiet, since Baba God has given you a command? Against Ashkelon, and against the seashore, there has he appointed it.”
Of Moab. Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: “Woe to Nebo! for it is laid waste; Kiriathaim is disappointed, it is taken; Misgab is put to shame and broken down.
The praise of Moab is no more; in Heshbon dem have devised evil against her: ‘Come, and Make we cut her off from being a nation.’ You also, Madmen, Go be bring to silence. The sword will pursue you.
The sound of a cry from Horonaim, desolation and great destruction!
Moab is destroyed. Her little ones have caused a cry to be heard.
For dem shall go up by the ascent of Luhith with continual weeping. For at the descent of Horonaim dem have heard the distress of the cry of destruction.
Flee! Save una lives! Be like the juniper bush in the wilderness.
For, because you have trusted in una works and in una treasures, you also go be taken. Chemosh will go out into captivity, his priests and his princes together.
The destroyer will come on every city, and no city will escape; the valley also will perish, and the plain Go be destroyed; as Baba God has spoken.
Give wings to Moab, that she may fly and get sheself away: and her cities will become a desolation, without anyone to live in dem.
“Cursed is person wey does the work of Baba God negligently; and cursed is person wey keeps back his sword from blood.

“Moab Don dey at ease from his youth, and he has settled on his lees, and has not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither has he gone into captivity: so his taste remains in him, and his scent No be changed.
So see am, the days come,” says Baba God, “that I go send to him people wey pour off, and dem shall pour him off; and dem shall empty his vessels, and break dem bottles in pieces.
Moab go be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel dem confidence.
“How do you say, ‘We be mighty men, and valiant men for the war?’
Moab is laid waste, and dem have gone up into his cities, and his chosen young men have gone down to the slaughter,” says the King, whose name is Baba God of Armies.
“The calamity of Moab is near to come, and his suffering hurries fast.
All you Wey be around him, bemoan him, and all you who know his name; say, ‘How is the strong staff broken, the beautiful rod!’
“You daughter who dwells in Dibon, come down from una glory, and sit in thirst; for the destroyer of Moab has come up against you, he has destroyed una strongholds.
Inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the way, and watch: ask him who flees, and her who escapes; say, ‘What Don dey done?’
Moab is disappointed; for it is broken down. Wail and cry! Tell it by the Arnon, that Moab is laid waste.
Judgment has come on the plain country, on Holon, and on Jahzah, and on Mephaath,
and on Dibon, and on Nebo, and on Beth Diblathaim,
and on Kiriathaim, and on Beth Gamul, and on Beth Meon,
and on Kerioth, and on Bozrah, and on all the cities of the land of Moab, far or near.
The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken,” says Baba God.
“Make him drunken; for he magnified imself against Baba God: and Moab shall wallow in his vomit, and he also go be in derision.
For no be Israel a derision to you? was he find among thieves? for as often as you speak of him, you shake una head.
You inhabitants of Moab, leave the cities, and live in the rock; and be like the dove that makes her nest over the mouth of the abyss.
“We have heard of the pride of Moab. He is very proud; his loftiness, and his pride, and his arrogance, and the haughtiness of his heart.
I know his serious anger,” says Baba God, “that it is nothing; his boastings have worked nothing.
So I go wail for Moab. Yes, I go cry out for all Moab. Dem shall mourn for the men of Kir Heres.

With more than the weeping of Jazer will I weep for you, vine of Sibmah. Una branches passed over the sea. Dem reached even to the sea of Jazer. The destroyer has fallen on una summer fruits and on una vintage.

Gladness and gladness is taken away from the fruitful field and from the land of Moab. I have caused wine to cease from the wine presses. Nobody will tread with shouting. The shouting Go be no shouting.
From the cry of Heshbon even to Elealeh, even to Jahaz have dem uttered dem voice, from Zoar even to Horonaim, to Eglath Shelishiyah: for the waters of Nimrim also will become desolate.
Moreover I go cause to cease in Moab,” says Baba God, “him who offers in the high place, and him who burns incense to his gods.
So my heart sounds for Moab like pipes, and my heart sounds like pipes for the men of Kir Heres. So the abundance that he has gotten has perished.
For every head is bald, and every beard clipped. E get cuttings on all the hands, and sackcloth on the waist.
On all the housetops of Moab, and in its streets, E get lamentation everywhere; for I have broken Moab like a vessel in which Nobody delights,” says Baba God.
“How it is broken down! How dem wail! How Moab has turned the back with shame! So shall Moab become a derision and a terror to all Wey be around him.”
For Baba God says: “See am, he shall fly as an eagle, and shall spread out his wings against Moab.
Kerioth is taken, and the strongholds are seized. The heart of the mighty men of Moab at that day go be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.
Moab go be destroyed from being a people, because he has magnified imself against Baba God.
Terror, the pit, and the snare are on you, inhabitant of Moab,” says Baba God.

“Person wey flees from the terror will fall into the pit; and person wey gets up out of the pit Go be taken in the snare: for I go bring on him, even on Moab, the year of dem visitation,” says Baba God.

“People wey fled stand without strength under the shadow of Heshbon; for a fire has gone out of Heshbon, and a flame from the middle of Sihon, and has devoured the corner of Moab, and the crown of the head of the tumultuous ones.
Woe to you, O Moab! The people of Chemosh are undone; for una sons are taken away captive, and una daughters into captivity.
“Yet I go bring back the captivity of Moab in the latter days,” says Baba God. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.
Of the pikin dem of Ammon. Baba God says: “Has Israel no sons? has he no heir? Why then does Malcam possess Gad, and his people live in its cities?

So see am, the days come,” says Baba God, “that I go cause an alarm of war to be heard against Rabbah of the pikin dem of Ammon; and it shall become a desolate heap, and her daughters Go be burned with fire: then Israel will possess people wey possessed him,” says Baba God.

“Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is laid waste! Cry, you daughters of Rabbah! Clothe yourself in sackcloth. Lament, and run back and forth among the fences; for Malcam will go into captivity, his priests and his princes together.
Why do you boast in the valleys, una flowing valley, backsliding daughter? You trusted in her treasures, saying, ‘Who will come to me?’
See am, I go bring a terror on you,” says the Lord, Baba God of Armies, “from all Wey be around you. All of You go be driven completely out, and there Go be Nobody to gather together the fugitives.
“But afterward I go bring back the captivity of the pikin dem of Ammon,” says Baba God.
Of Edom. Baba God of Armies says: “Is wisdom no more in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has dem wisdom vanished?
Flee! Turn back! Live in the depths, inhabitants of Dedan; for I go bring the calamity of Esau on him when I visit him.
If grape gatherers come to you, would dem not leave some gleaning grapes? If thieves come by night, wouldn’t dem steal until dem had enough?
But I have made Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places, and he No go be able to hide imself. His offspring is destroyed, with his brothers and his neighbors; and he is no more.
Leave una fatherless pikin dem. I go preserve dem alive. Let una widows trust in me.”

For Baba God says: “See am, dem to whom it didn’t pertain to drink of the cup shall certainly drink; and are you person wey shall altogether go unpunished? You no go go unpunished, but you shall surely drink.
For I have sworn by myself,” says Baba God, “that Bozrah will become an astonishment, a reproach, a waste, and a curse. All its cities Go be perpetual wastes.”
I have heard news from Baba God, and an ambassador is sent among the nations, saying, “Gather unaself together! Come against her! Rise up to the battle!”
“For, see am, I have made you small among the nations, and despised among men.

As for una terror, the pride of una heart has deceived you, O you who live in the clefts of the rock, who hold the height of the hill, though you should make una nest as high as the eagle, I go bring you down from there,” says Baba God.
“Edom will become an astonishment. Everybody wey passes by it Go be astonished, and will hiss at all its plagues.
As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and its neighbor cities,” says Baba God, “no man will live there, neither will any Son of Man live inside am.

“See am, he will come up like a lion from the pride of the Jordan against the strong habitation: for I go suddenly make dem run away from it; and Anybody wey is chosen, I go appoint him over it. For Wey be like me? Who will appoint me a time? Wey be the shepherd who will stand before me?”

So hear the counsel of Baba God, that he has taken against Edom; and his purposes, that he has purposed against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely Dem go drag dem away, the little ones of the flock. Surely he will make dem habitation desolate over dem.
The earth trembles at the noise of dem fall; E get a cry, the noise which is heard in the Red Sea.
See am, he will come up and fly as the eagle, and spread out his wings against Bozrah. The heart of the mighty men of Edom at that day Go be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.
Of Damascus: “Hamath is confounded, and Arpad; for dem have heard evil news, Dem be melted away: E get sorrow on the sea; it no fit be quiet.
Damascus has grown feeble, she turns sheself to flee, and trembling has seized on her: anguish and sorrows have taken hold of her, as of a woman in travail.
How is the city of praise not forsaken, the city of my gladness?
So her young men shall fall in her streets, and all the men of war go be bring to silence in that day,” says Baba God of Armies.
“I go kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it shall devour the palaces of Ben Hadad.”
Of Kedar, and of the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck. Baba God says: “Arise, go up to Kedar, and destroy the pikin dem of the east.
Dem go take dem tents and dem flocks. Dem go carry away for themselves dem curtains, all dem vessels, and dem camels; and Dem go cry to dem, Terror on every side!
Flee! Wander far off! Live in the depths, you inhabitants of Hazor,” says Baba God; “for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has taken counsel against you, and has conceived a purpose against you.
Arise! Go up to a nation that is at ease, that dwells without care,” says Baba God; “that has neither gates nor bars, that dwells alone.

Dem camels Go be a booty, and the plenty people of dem livestock a plunder. I go scatter to all winds people wey have the corners of dem beards cut off; and I go bring dem calamity from every side of dem,” says Baba God.
Hazor Go be a dwelling place of jackals, a desolation forever. No man shall live there, neither shall any Son of Man live inside am.”
Baba God’s word that come to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, For the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying,
“Baba God of Armies says: ‘See am, I go break the bow of Elam, the chief of dem might.
On Elam will I bring the four winds from the four quarters of the sky, and will scatter dem toward all those winds. There Go be no nation where the outcasts of Elam No go come.

I go cause Elam to be dismayed before dem enemies, and before people wey seek dem life; and I go bring evil on dem, even my fierce anger,’ says Baba God; ‘and I go send the sword after dem, until I have consumed dem;
and I go set my throne in Elam, and will destroy from there king and princes,’ says Baba God.
‘But it shall happen in the latter days, that I go bring back the captivity of Elam,’ says Baba God.”
The word that Baba God spoke concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, by Jeremiah the prophet.

“Declare among the nations and publish, and set up a standard; publish, and no conceal: say, ‘Babylon Don dey taken, Bel is disappointed, Merodach is dismayed! Her images are disappointed. Her idols are dismayed.’
For a nation comes up out of the north against her, which shall make her land desolate, and Nobody shall live inside am. Dem have fled. Dem be gone, both man and animal.
“In those days, and in that time,” says Baba God, “the pikin dem of Israel will come, dem and the pikin dem of Judah together; Dem go go on dem way weeping, and will seek Baba God dem God.
Dem go inquire concerning Zion with dem faces turned toward it, saying, ‘Come, and join unaself to Baba God in an everlasting covenant that no go be forgotten.’
My people Don dey lost sheep: dem shepherds have caused dem to go astray; dem have turned dem away on the mountains; dem have gone from mountain to hill; dem have forgotten dem resting place.
All who find dem have devoured dem; and dem adversaries talk say, ‘We No be guilty, because dem have sinned against Baba God, the habitation of righteousness, even Baba God, the hope of dem fathers.’
“Flee out of the middle of Babylon! Go out of the land of the Chaldeans, and be as the male goats before the flocks.

For, see am, I go stir up and cause to come up against Babylon a company of great nations from the north country; and Dem go set themselves in array against her. She Go be taken from there. Dem arrows Go be as of an expert mighty man. None of dem will return in vain.
Chaldea go be a prey. All who prey on her go be satisfied,” says Baba God.
“Because You be glad, because you glad well-well, O you who plunder my heritage, because You be wanton as a heifer that treads out the grain, and neigh as strong horses;
una mother Go be utterly disappointed. Person wey bore You go be confounded. See am, she go be the least of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert.
Because of Baba God’s serious anger she no go be inhabited, but she Go be wholly desolate. Everybody wey goes by Babylon Go be astonished, and hiss at all her plagues.
Set unaself in array against Babylon all around, all you who bend the bow; shoot at her, spare no arrows: for she has sinned against Baba God.

Shout against her all around. She has submitted sheself. Her bulwarks have fallen. Her walls Don dey thrown down, for it is the vengeance of Baba God. Take vengeance on her. As she has done, do to her.
Cut off the sower from Babylon, and him who handles the sickle in the time of harvest. For fear of the oppressing sword, Dem go each return to dem own people, and Dem go each flee to dem own land.
“Israel is a hunted sheep. The lions have driven him away. First, the king of Assyria devoured him, and now at last Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has broken his bones.”
So Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: “See am, I go punish the king of Babylon and his land, as I have punished the king of Assyria.
I go bring Israel again to his pasture, and he will feed on Carmel and Bashan. His soul Go be satisfied on the hills of Ephraim and in Gilead.

In those days, and in that time,” says Baba God, “the wickedness of Israel go be sought for, and there Go be none; also the sins of Judah, and dem no go be find; for I go pardon dem whom I leave as a remnant.
“Go up against the land of Merathaim, even against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod. Kill and utterly destroy after dem,” says Baba God, “and do according to all that I have commanded you.
A sound of battle is in the land, and of great destruction.
How the hammer of the whole earth is cut apart and broken! How Babylon has become a desolation among the nations!
I have laid a snare for you, and You be also taken, Babylon, and you no be aware. You be find, and also caught, because you have fought against Baba God.
Baba God has opened his armory, and has bring out the weapons of his indignation; for the Lord, Baba God of Armies, has a work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.
Come against her from the farthest border. Open her storehouses. Throw her up as heaps. Destroy her utterly. Let nothing of her be left.
Kill all her bulls. Make dem go down to the slaughter. Woe to dem! For dem day has come, the time of dem visitation.
Listen to people wey flee and escape out of the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of Baba God our God, the vengeance of his temple.

“Call together the archers against Babylon, all people wey bend the bow. Encamp against her all around. Let none of it escape. Recompense her according to her work. According to all that she has done, do to her; for she Don dey proud against Baba God, against the Holy One of Israel.
So her young men will fall in her streets, and all her men of war Go be bring to silence in that day,” says Baba God.
“See am, I be against you, you proud one,” says the Lord, Baba God of Armies; “for una day has come, the time that I go visit you.
The proud one will stumble and fall, and Nobody will raise him up. I go kindle a fire in his cities, and it shall devour all Wey be around him.”
Baba God of Armies says: “The pikin dem of Israel and the pikin dem of Judah are oppressed together. All who take dem captive hold dem fast. Dem refuse to Make dem go.
Dem Redeemer is strong: Baba God of Armies is his name. He will thoroughly plead dem cause, that he may give rest to the earth, and disquiet the inhabitants of Babylon.
“A sword is on the Chaldeans,” says Baba God, “and on the inhabitants of Babylon, on her princes, and on her wise men.
A sword is on the boasters, and Dem go become fools. A sword is on her mighty men, and Dem go be dismayed.
A sword is on dem horses, on dem chariots, and on all the mixed people Wey be in the middle of her; and Dem go become as women. A sword is on her treasures, and Dem go be robbed.
A drought is on her waters, and dem go be dried up; for it is a land of engraved images, and Dem be mad over idols.

So the wild animals of the desert with the wolves will live there. The ostriches will live inside am; and it Go be inhabited no more forever; neither will it be lived in from generation to generation.
As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and its neighbor cities,” says Baba God, “so no man will live there, neither will any Son of Man live inside am.
“See am, a people comes from the north; and a great nation and many kings go be stirred up from the uttermost parts of the earth.
Dem take up bow and spear. Dem be cruel, and have no mercy. Dem voice roars like the sea. Dem ride on horses, everyone set in array, as a man to the battle, against you, daughter of Babylon.
The king of Babylon has heard the news of dem, and his hands become feeble: anguish has taken hold of him, pains as of a woman in labor.

See am, the enemy will come up like a lion from the pride of the Jordan against the strong habitation; for I go suddenly make dem run away from it. Anybody wey is chosen, I go appoint him over it; for Wey be like me? Who will appoint me a time? Wey be the shepherd who can stand before me?”

So hear the counsel of Baba God, that he has taken against Babylon; and his purposes, that he has purposed against the land of the Chaldeans: Surely dem shall drag dem away, even the little ones of the flock. Surely he shall make dem habitation desolate over dem.
At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth trembles; and the cry is heard among the nations.
Baba God says: “See am, I go raise up against Babylon, and against people wey live in Lebkamai, a destroying wind.
I go send to Babylon strangers, who will winnow her. Dem go empty her land; for in the day of trouble Dem go be against her all around.
Against him who bends, let the archer bend his bow, also against him who lifts imself up in his coat of mail. No spare her young men! Utterly destroy all her army!
Dem go fall down slain in the land of the Chaldeans, and thrust through in her streets.
For Israel No be forsaken, nor Judah, by his God, by Baba God of Armies; though dem land is full of guilt against the Holy One of Israel.
“Flee out of the middle of Babylon! Everyone save his own life! No be cut off in her wickedness; for it is the time of Baba God’s vengeance. He will render to her a recompense.
Babylon Don dey a golden cup in Baba God’s hand, who made all the earth drunk. The nations have drunk of her wine; so the nations have gone mad.
Babylon has suddenly fallen and been destroyed! Wail for her! Take balm for her pain. Perhaps she may be healed.
“We would have healed Babylon, but she No be healed. Forsake her, and Make we each go into his own country; for her judgment reaches to heaven, and is lifted up even to the skies.
‘Baba God has produced our righteousness: come, and Make we declare in Zion the work of Baba God our God.’

“Make the arrows sharp! Hold the shields firmly! Baba God has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, because his purpose is against Babylon, to destroy it; for it is the vengeance of Baba God, the vengeance of his temple.

Set up a standard against the walls of Babylon! Make the watch strong! Set the watchmen, and prepare the ambushes; for Baba God has both purposed and done that which he spoke concerning the inhabitants of Babylon.
You who live on many waters, abundant in treasures, una end has come, the measure of una covetousness.
Baba God of Armies has sworn by imself, saying, ‘Surely I go fill you with men, as with the canker worm; and Dem go lift up a shout against you.’
“He has made the earth by his power. He has established the world by his wisdom. By his understanding he has stretched out the heavens.

When he utters his voice, E get a roar of waters in the heavens, and he causes the vapors to ascend from every corner of the world. He makes lightning for the rain, and brings the wind out of his treasuries.
“Every man has become brutish without knowledge. Every goldsmith is disappointed by his image; for his molten image is falsehood, and E get no breath in dem.
Dem be vanity, a work of delusion. In the time of dem visitation, Dem go perish.
The portion of Jacob No be like these, for he is the former of all things; including the tribe of his inheritance: Baba God of Armies is his name.
“You be my battle ax and weapons of war. With you I go break the nations into pieces. With you I go destroy kingdoms.
With you I go break in pieces the horse and his rider.

With you I go break in pieces the chariot and him who rides inside am. With you I go break in pieces man and woman. With you I go break in pieces the old man and the youth. With you I go break in pieces the young man and the virgin.
With you I go break in pieces the shepherd and his flock. With you I go break in pieces the farmer and his yoke. With You go I break in pieces governors and deputies.
“I go render to Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all dem evil that dem have done in Zion in una sight,” says Baba God.
“See am, I be against you, destroying mountain,” says Baba God, “which destroys all the earth. I go stretch out my hand on you, roll you down from the rocks, and will make you a burned mountain.
Dem no go take cornerstone from you, nor a stone for foundations; but You go be desolate for ever,” says Baba God.

“Set up a standard in the land! Blow the trumpet among the nations! Prepare the nations against her! Call together against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz! Appoint a marshal against her! Cause the horses to come up as the rough canker worm!
Prepare against her the nations, the kings of the Medes, its governors, and all its deputies, and all the land of dem dominion!
The land trembles and is in pain; for the purposes of Baba God against Babylon stand, to make the land of Babylon a desolation, without inhabitant.
The mighty men of Babylon have stopped fighting, dem remain in dem strongholds. Dem might has failed. Dem have become as women. Her dwelling places are set on fire. Her bars are broken.
One runner will run to meet another, and one messenger to meet another, to show the king of Babylon that his city is taken on every quarter.
So the passages are seized. Dem have burned the reeds with fire. The men of war are frightened.”
For Baba God of Armies, the God of Israel says: “The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time when it is trodden. Yet a little while, and the time of harvest shall come for her.”

“Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon has devoured me. He has crushed me. He has made me an empty vessel. He has, like a monster, swallowed me up. He has filled his mouth with my delicacies. He has throw me out.
May the violence done to me and to my flesh be on Babylon!” the inhabitant of Zion will say; and, “May my blood be on the inhabitants of Chaldea!” will Jerusalem say.
So Baba God says: “See am, I go plead una cause, and take vengeance for you. I go dry up her sea, and make her fountain dry.
Babylon will become heaps, a dwelling place for jackals, an astonishment, and a hissing, without inhabitant.
Dem go roar together like young lions. Dem go growl as lions’ cubs.
When Dem be heated, I go make dem feast, and I go make dem drunk, that dem may glad well-well, and sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake up,” says Baba God.
“I go bring dem down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with male goats.
“How Sheshach is taken! and the praise of the whole earth seized! How Babylon has become a desolation among the nations!
The sea has come up on Babylon. She is covered with the plenty people of its waves.
Her cities have become a desolation, a dry land, and a desert, a land in which no man dwells, neither does any Son of Man pass by it.
I go execute judgment on Bel in Babylon, and I go bring out of his mouth that which he has swallowed up. The nations no go flow any more to him. Yes, the wall of Babylon will fall.
“My people, go away from the middle of her, and each of you save unaself from Baba God’s fierce anger.
No let una heart faint. No fear for the news that Go be heard in the land. For news will come one year, and after that in another year news will come, and violence in the land, ruler against ruler.
So see am, the days come that I go execute judgment on the engraved images of Babylon; and her whole land Go be confounded. All her slain will fall in the middle of her.
Then the heavens and the earth, and all that is inside am, will sing for gladness over Babylon; for the destroyers will come to her from the north,” says Baba God.
“As Babylon has caused the slain of Israel to fall, so the slain of all the land will fall at Babylon.
You who have escaped the sword, go! No stand still! Remember Baba God from far away, and let Jerusalem come into una mind.”
“We be confounded, because we have heard reproach. Confusion has covered our faces, for strangers have come into the sanctuaries of Baba God’s house.”
“So see am, the days come,” says Baba God, “that I go execute judgment on her engraved images; and through all her land the wounded will groan.
Though Babylon should mount up to the sky, and though she should fortify the height of her strength, yet destroyers will come to her from me,” says Baba God.
“The sound of a cry comes from Babylon, and of great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans!
For Baba God lays Babylon waste, and destroys out of her the great voice! Dem waves roar like many waters. The noise of dem voice is uttered.
For the destroyer has come on her, even on Babylon. Her mighty men are taken. Dem bows are broken in pieces, for Baba God is a God of recompenses. He will surely repay.
I go make her princes, her wise men, her governors, her deputies, and her mighty men drunk. Dem go sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake up,” says the King, whose name is Baba God of Armies.

Baba God of Armies says: “The wide walls of Babylon Go be utterly overthrown. Her high gates Go be burned with fire. The peoples will labor for vanity, and the nations for the fire; and Dem go be weary.”

The word which Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, when he go with Zedekiah the king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Now Seraiah was chief quartermaster.
Jeremiah wrote in a book all the evil that should come on Babylon, even all these words that are written concerning Babylon.
Jeremiah talk say to Seraiah, “When you come to Babylon, then see that you read all these words,
and say, ‘Baba God, you have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, that Nobody will live in it, neither man nor animal, but that it Go be desolate forever.’
It go be, when you have finished reading this book, that you shall bind a stone to it, and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates.
Then you shall say, ‘Thus will Babylon sink, and No go rise again because of the evil that I go bring on her; and dem go be weary.’” Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign. He reigned eleven years in Jerusalem: and his mother’s name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He did that which was evil in Baba God’s sight, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
For through Baba God’s anger this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until he had throw dem out from his presence. Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon come, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and encamped against it; and dem built forts against it round about.
So the city was besieged to the eleventh year of king Zedekiah.
In the fourth month, in the ninth day of the month, the famine was severe in the city, so that there was no bread for the people of the land.

Then a breach was made in the city, and all the men of war fled, and go out of the city by night by the way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king’s garden. Now the Chaldeans were against the city all around. The men of war go toward the Arabah,
but the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.
Then dem take the king, and carried him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath; and he give judgment on him.
The king of Babylon killed the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes: he killed also all the princes of Judah in Riblah.
He put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in fetters, and carried him to Babylon, and put him in prison until the day of his death.

Now in the fifth month, in the tenth day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, who stood before the king of Babylon, come into Jerusalem.
He burned Baba God’s house, and the king’s house; and all the houses of Jerusalem, even every great house, he burned with fire.
All the army of the Chaldeans, who were with the captain of the guard, broke down all the walls of Jerusalem all around.

Then Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive of the poorest of the people, and the residue of the people who were left in the city, and people wey fell away, who fell to the king of Babylon, and the residue of the plenty people.
But Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left of the poorest of the land to be vineyard keepers and farmers.
The Chaldeans broke the pillars of brass that were in Baba God’s house, and the bases and the bronze sea that were in Baba God’s house in pieces, and carried all of dem brass to Babylon.
Dem also take away the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the basins, the spoons, and all the vessels of brass with which dem ministered.
The captain of the guard take away the cups, the fire pans, the basins, the pots, the lamp stands, the spoons, and the bowls; that which was of gold, in gold, and that which was of silver, in silver.
Dem take the two pillars, the one sea, and the twelve bronze bulls that were under the bases, which king Solomon had made for Baba God’s house. The brass of all these vessels was without weight.
As for the pillars, the height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits; and a line of twelve cubits encircled it; and its thickness was four fingers. It was hollow.

A capital of brass was on it; and the height of the one capital was five cubits, with network and pomegranates on the capital all around, all of brass: and the second pillar also had like these, and pomegranates.
There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides; all the pomegranates were one hundred on the network all around.
The captain of the guard take Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold:

and out of the city he take an officer who was set over the men of war; and seven men of people wey see the king’s face, who were find in the city; and the scribe of the captain of the army, who mustered the people of the land; and sixty men of the people of the land, who were find in the middle of the city.
Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard take dem, and bring dem to the king of Babylon to Riblah.
The king of Babylon struck dem, and put dem to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was carried away captive out of his land.
This is the people whom Nebuchadnezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year three thousand twenty-three Jews;
in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar he carried away captive from Jerusalem eight hundred thirty-two persons;
in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive of the Jews seven hundred forty-five persons: all the persons were four thousand and six hundred.

In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, in the twenty-fifth day of the month, Evilmerodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and released him from prison;
and he spoke kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings who were with him in Babylon,
and changed his prison garments. Jehoiachin ate bread before him continually all the days of his life:
and for his allowance, there was a continual allowance given him by the king of Babylon, every day a portion until the day of his death, all the days of his life.
How the city sits solitary, that was full of people! She has become as a widow, who was great among the nations! Person wey was a princess among the provinces has become tributary!
She weeps bitterly in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks; among all her lovers she has Nobody to comfort her: All her friends have dealt treacherously with her; dem have become her enemies.
Judah has gone into captivity because of suffering, and because of great servitude; she dwells among the nations, she finds no rest: all her persecutors overtook her within the straits.
The ways of Zion mourn, because Nobody come to the solemn assembly; all her gates are desolate, her priests sigh: her virgins are afflicted, and she sheself is in bitterness.
Her adversaries have become the head, her enemies prosper; for Baba God has afflicted her for the plenty people of her wrongdoings: her young pikin dem have gone into captivity before the adversary.
All majesty has comot from the daughter of Zion: her princes have become like deer that find no pasture, dem have gone without strength before the pursuer.

Jerusalem remembers in the days of her suffering and of her miseries all her pleasant things that were from the days of old: when her people fell into the hand of the adversary, and Nobody helped her, The adversaries see her, dem mocked at her desolations.
Jerusalem has grievously sinned; so she has become as an unclean thing; all who honored her despise her, because dem have seen her nakedness: yes, she sighs, and turns backward.
Her filthiness was in her skirts; she didn’t remember her latter end; so she has come down astoundingly; she has no comforter: “See, Baba God, my suffering; for the enemy has magnified imself.”

The adversary has spread out his hand on all her pleasant things: for she has seen that the nations are entered into her sanctuary, concerning whom you commanded that dem no suppose enter into una assembly.
All her people sigh, dem seek bread; dem have given dem pleasant things for chop to refresh the soul: “Look, Baba God, and see; for I have become abject.”
“Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by? Look, and see if E get any sorrow like my sorrow, which is bring on me, with which Baba God has afflicted me in the day of his fierce anger.
“From on high has he sent fire into my bones, and it prevails against dem; He has spread a net for my feet. He has turned me back. He has made me desolate and faint all day long.

“The yoke of my wrongdoings is bound by his hand; Dem be knit together. Dem have come up on my neck. He has made my strength to fail. The Lord has delivered me into dem hands, against whom I be not able to stand.
“The Lord has set at nothing all my mighty men within me. He has call a solemn assembly against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trodden as in a wine press the virgin daughter of Judah.
“For these things I weep. My eye, my eye runs down with water, because the comforter who should refresh my soul is far from me. My pikin dem are desolate, because the enemy has prevailed.”
Zion spreads out her hands. E get Nobody to comfort her; Baba God has commanded concerning Jacob, that people Wey around him should be his adversaries. Jerusalem is among dem as an unclean thing.
“Baba God is righteous; for I have rebelled against his commandment. Please hear all you peoples, and see my sorrow. My virgins and my young men have gone into captivity.
“I call for my lovers, but dem deceived me. My priests and my elders give up the spirit in the city, while dem sought chop for themselves to refresh dem souls.
“See, Baba God; for I be in distress. My heart is troubled. My heart is turned within me, for I have grievously rebelled. Abroad the sword bereaves. At home it is like death.

“Dem have heard that I sigh. E get Nobody to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my trouble. Dem be glad that you have done it: You go bring the day that you have proclaimed, and Dem go be like me.
“Let all dem wickedness come before you; Do to dem as you have done to me for all my wrongdoings. For my sighs are many, and my heart is faint.
How has the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger! He has throw down from heaven to the earth the beauty of Israel, And hasn’t remember his footstool in the day of his anger.

The Lord has swallowed up all the habitations of Jacob, and has not pitied: He has thrown down in his serious anger the strongholds of the daughter of Judah; He has bring dem down to the ground; he has profaned the kingdom and its princes.
He has cut off in fierce anger all the horn of Israel; He has drawn back his right hand from before the enemy: He has burned up Jacob like a flaming fire, which devours all around.

He has bent his bow like an enemy, he has stood with his right hand as an adversary, Has killed all that were pleasant to the eye: In the tent of the daughter of Zion he has poured out his serious anger like fire.

The Lord has become as an enemy, he has swallowed up Israel; He has swallowed up all her palaces, he has destroyed his strongholds; He has multiplied in the daughter of Judah mourning and lamentation.

He has violently taken away his tabernacle, as if it were of a garden; he has destroyed his place of assembly: Baba God has caused solemn assembly and Sabbath to be forgotten in Zion, Has despised in the indignation of his anger the king and the priest.

The Lord has throw off his altar, he has abhorred his sanctuary; He has given up into the hand of the enemy the walls of her palaces: Dem have made a noise in Baba God’s house, as in the day of a solemn assembly.

Baba God has purposed to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion; He has stretched out the line, he has not withdrawn his hand from destroying; He has made the rampart and wall to lament; dem languish together.
Her gates are sunk into the ground; he has destroyed and broken her bars: Her king and her princes are among the nations where the law No be; Yes, her prophets find no vision from Baba God.

The elders of the daughter of Zion sit on the ground, dem keep silence; Dem have throw up dust on dem heads; dem have clothed themselves with sackcloth: The virgins of Jerusalem hang down dem heads to the ground.

My eyes fail with tears, my heart is troubled; My liver is poured on the earth, because of the destruction of the daughter of my people, Because the young pikin dem and the infants swoon in the streets of the city.
Dem ask dem mothers, “Where is grain and wine?” when dem swoon as the wounded in the streets of the city, when dem soul is poured out into dem mothers’ bosom.

What shall I testify to you? what shall I liken to you, daughter of Jerusalem? What shall I compare to you, that I may comfort you, virgin daughter of Zion? For una breach is great like the sea: who can heal you?
Una prophets have seen for you false and foolish visions; Dem have not uncovered una wickedness, to bring back una captivity, but have seen for you false revelations and causes of banishment.
All that pass by clap dem hands at you. Dem hiss and wag dem head at the daughter of Jerusalem, saying, “Is this the city that men call ‘The perfection of beauty, the gladness of the whole earth’?”

All una enemies have opened dem mouth wide against you. Dem hiss and gnash the teeth. Dem say, “We have swallowed her up. Certainly this is the day that we looked for. We have find it. We have seen it.”

Baba God has done that which he purposed; he has fulfilled his word that he commanded in the days of old; He has thrown down, and has not pitied: He has caused the enemy to glad well-well over you; he has exalted the horn of una adversaries.
Dem heart cried to the Lord: wall of the daughter of Zion, let tears run down like a river day and night; Give yourself no respite; no let the apple of una eye cease.

Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the watches; Pour out una heart like water before the face of the Lord: Lift up una hands toward him for the life of una young pikin dem, that faint for hunger at the head of every street.

“Look, Baba God, and see to whom you have done thus! Shall the women eat dem offspring, the pikin dem that are dandled in the hands? Shall the priest and the prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?
“The youth and the old man lie on the ground in the streets. My virgins and my young men have fallen by the sword. You have killed dem in the day of una anger. You have slaughtered, and not pitied.

“You have call, as in the day of a solemn assembly, my terrors on every side. There was Nobody that escaped or remain in the day of Baba God’s anger. My enemy has consumed those whom I have dandled and bring up.
I be the man that has seen suffering by the rod of his serious anger.
He has led me and caused me to walk in darkness, and not in light.
Surely against me he turns his hand again and again all day long.
He has made my flesh and my skin old; he has broken my bones.
He has built against me, and surrounded me with gall and travail.
He has made me to live in dark places, as those that Don dey long dead.
He has walled me about, that I no fit go out; he has made my chain heavy.
Yes, when I cry, and call for help, he shuts out my prayer.
He has walled up my ways with cut stone; he has made my paths crooked.
He is to me as a bear lying in wait, as a lion in secret places.
He has turned aside my ways, and pulled me in pieces; he has made me desolate.
He has bent his bow, and set me as a mark for the arrow.
He has caused the shafts of his quiver to enter into my kidneys.
I have become a derision to all my people, and dem song all day long.
He has filled me with bitterness. He has sated me with wormwood.
He has also broken my teeth with gravel stones; he has covered me with ashes.
You have removed my soul far off from peace; I forgot prosperity.
I talk say, “My strength has perished, along with my expectation from Baba God.”
Remember my suffering and my misery, the wormwood and the gall.
My soul still remembers dem, and is bowed down within me.
This I recall to my mind; so I have hope.
It is because of Baba God’s loving kindnesses that we No be consumed, because his compassion no dey fail.
Dem be new every morning; great is una faithfulness.
“Baba God is my portion,” says my soul. “So I go hope in him.”
Baba God is good to people wey wait for him, to the soul who seeks him.
It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of Baba God.
It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth.
Make e sit alone and keep silence, because he has laid it on him.
Make e put his mouth in the dust, if so be there may be hope.
Make e give his cheek to him who strikes him; Make e be filled full with reproach.
For the Lord No go throw off forever.
For though he cause grief, yet he Go get compassion according to the plenty people of his loving kindnesses.
For he No dey afflict willingly, nor grieve the pikin dem of men.
To crush under foot all the prisoners of the earth,
To turn aside the right of a man before the face of the Most High,
To subvert a man in his cause, the Lord no dey approve.
Wey be person wey says, and it comes to pass, when the Lord no dey command it?
No dey evil and good come out of the mouth of the Most High?
Why does a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?
Make we search and try our ways, and turn again to Baba God.
Make we lift up our heart with our hands to God in the heavens.
“We have transgressed and have rebelled. You have not pardoned.
“You have covered us with anger and pursued us. You have killed. You have not pitied.
You have covered yourself with a cloud, so that no prayer can pass through.
You have made us an off-scouring and refuse in the middle of the peoples.
“All our enemies have opened dem mouth wide against us.
Terror and the pit have come on us, devastation and destruction.”
My eye runs down with streams of water, for the destruction of the daughter of my people.
My eye pours down, and no dey cease, without any intermission,
until Baba God looks down, and sees from heaven.
My eye affects my soul, because of all the daughters of my city.
Dem have chased me relentlessly like a bird, people Wey my enemies without cause.
Dem have cut off my life in the dungeon, and have throw a stone on me.
Waters flowed over my head; I talk say, I be cut off.
I call on una name, Baba God, out of the lowest dungeon.
You heard my voice: “No hide una ear from my sighing, and my cry.”
You come near in the day that I call on you; you talk say, “No fear.”
Lord, you have pleaded the causes of my soul; you have redeemed my life.
Baba God, you have seen my wrong. Judge my cause.
You have seen all dem vengeance and all dem devices against me.
You have heard dem reproach, Baba God, and all dem devices against me,
The lips of those that rose up against me, and dem device against me all day long.
You see dem sitting down and dem rising up; I be dem song.
You go render to dem a recompense, Baba God, according to the work of dem hands.
You go give dem hardness of heart, una curse to dem.
You go pursue dem in anger, and destroy dem from under the heavens of Baba God.
How the gold has become dim! The most pure gold has changed! The stones of the sanctuary are poured out at the head of every street.
The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold, How are dem esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the hands of the potter!
Even the jackals draw out the breast, dem nurse dem young ones: But the daughter of my people has become cruel, like the ostriches in the wilderness.
The tongue of the nursing pikin clings to the roof of his mouth for thirst: The young pikin dem ask bread, and no man breaks it to dem.
People wey fed delicately are desolate in the streets: People wey were bring up in scarlet embrace dunghills.
For the wickedness of the daughter of my people is greater than the sin of Sodom, That was overthrown as in a moment, and no hands were laid on her.
Her nobles were purer than snow, dem were whiter than milk; Dem were more ruddy in body than rubies, dem polishing was as of sapphire.
Dem appearance is blacker than a coal; dem No be known in the streets: Dem skin clings to dem bones; it is withered, it has become like a stick.
People Wey killed with the sword are better than people Wey killed with hunger; For these pine away, stricken through, for want of the fruits of the field.
The hands of the pitiful women have boiled dem own pikin dem; Dem were dem chop in the destruction of the daughter of my people.
Baba God has accomplished his serious anger, he has poured out his fierce anger; He has kindled a fire in Zion, which has devoured its foundations.
The kings of the earth didn’t believe, neither did all the inhabitants of the world, That the adversary and the enemy would enter into the gates of Jerusalem.
It is because of the sins of her prophets, and the iniquities of her priests, That have shed the blood of the just in the middle of her.
Dem wander as blind men in the streets. Dem be polluted with blood, So that men no fit touch dem garments.
“Go away!” dem cried to dem, “Unclean! Go away! Go away! No touch! When dem fled away and wandered, men talk say among the nations, “Dem no fit live here any more.”
Baba God’s anger has scattered dem; he will no more regard dem: Dem didn’t respect the persons of the priests, dem didn’t favor the elders.
Our eyes still fail, looking in vain for our help: In our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save.
Dem hunt our steps, so that we no fit go in our streets: Our end is near, our days are fulfilled; for our end has come.
Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of the sky: Dem chased us on the mountains, dem laid wait for us in the wilderness.
The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of Baba God, was taken in dem pits; Of whom we talk say, Under his shadow we shall live among the nations.
Glad well-well and be glad, daughter of Edom, that live in the land of Uz: The cup shall pass through to you also; you go be drunken, and shall make yourself naked.
The punishment of una wickedness is accomplished, daughter of Zion; he will no more carry you away into captivity: He will visit una wickedness, daughter of Edom; he will uncover una sins.
Remember, Baba God, what has come on us: Look, and see our reproach.
Our inheritance is turned to strangers, Our houses to aliens.
We be orphans and fatherless; Our mothers are as widows.
We have drunken our water for money; Our wood is sold to us.
Our pursuers are on our necks: We be weary, and have no rest.
We have given the hand to the Egyptians, To the Assyrians, to be satisfied with bread.
Our fathers sinned, and are no more; We have borne dem iniquities.
Workers rule over us: E get Nobody to deliver us out of dem hand.
We get our bread at the peril of our lives, Because of the sword of the wilderness.
Our skin is black like an oven, Because of the burning heat of famine.
Dem ravished the women in Zion, The virgins in the cities of Judah.
Princes were hanged up by dem hand: The faces of elders No be honored.
The young men bare the mill; The pikin dem stumbled under the wood.
The elders have ceased from the gate, The young men from dem music.
The gladness of our heart is ceased; Our dance is turned into mourning.
The crown is fallen from our head: Woe to us! for we have sinned.
For this our heart is faint; For these things our eyes are dim;
For the mountain of Zion, which is desolate: The foxes walk on it.
You, Baba God, remain forever; Una throne is from generation to generation.
Why do you forget us forever, And forsake us so long time?
Turn us to yourself, Baba God, and we go be turned. Renew our days as of old.
But you have utterly rejected us; You be very angry against us.
Now in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, in the fifth of the month, as I was among the captives by the river Chebar, the heavens were opened, and I see visions of God.
In the fifth of the month, which was the fifth year of king Jehoiachin’s captivity,
Baba God’s word come expressly to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and Baba God’s hand was there on him.

I looked, and see am, a stormy wind come out of the north, a great cloud, with flashing lightning, and a brightness around it, and out of the middle of it as it were glowing metal, out of the middle of the fire.
Out of its center come the likeness of four living creatures. This was dem appearance: dem had the likeness of a man.
Everyone had four faces, and each one of dem had four wings.
Dem feet were straight feet; and the sole of dem feet was like the sole of a calf’s foot; and dem sparkled like burnished brass.
Dem had the hands of a man under dem wings on dem four sides; and the four of dem had dem faces and dem wings thus:
dem wings were joined to each other; dem didn’t turn when dem go; each one go straight forward.

As for the likeness of dem faces, dem had the face of a man; and the four of dem had the face of a lion on the right side; and the four of dem had the face of an ox on the left side; the four of dem also had the face of an eagle.
Such were dem faces. Dem wings were spread out above. Two wings of each one touched another, and two covered dem bodies.
Each one go straight forward: where the spirit was to go, dem go; dem didn’t turn when dem go.

As for the likeness of the living creatures, dem appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches: the fire go up and down among the living creatures; and the fire was bright, and lightning go out of the fire.
The living creatures ran and come back as the appearance of a flash of lightning.
Now as I see the living creatures, see am, one wheel on the earth beside the living creatures, for each of the four faces of it.
The appearance of the wheels and dem work was like a beryl: and the four of dem had one likeness; and dem appearance and dem work was as it were a wheel within a wheel.
When dem go, dem go in dem four directions: dem didn’t turn when dem go.
As for dem rims, dem were high and dreadful; and the four of dem had dem rims full of eyes all around.
When the living creatures go, the wheels go beside dem; and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up.
Anywhere wey the spirit was to go, dem go; there was the spirit to go: and the wheels were lifted up beside dem; for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.

When those go, these go; and when those stood, these stood; and when those were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up beside dem: for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.
Over the head of the living creature there was the likeness of an expanse, like the awesome crystal to look on, stretched out over dem heads above.
Under the expanse were dem wings straight, the one toward the other: each one had two which covered on this side, and every one had two which covered on that side, dem bodies.
When dem go, I heard the noise of dem wings like the noise of great waters, like the voice of the Almighty, a noise of tumult like the noise of an army: when dem stood, dem let down dem wings.
There was a voice above the expanse that was over dem heads: when dem stood, dem let down dem wings.
