So he measured the house, one hundred cubits long; and the separate place, and the building, with its walls, one hundred cubits long;
also the width of the face of the house, and of the separate place toward the east, one hundred cubits.

He measured the length of the building before the separate place which was at its back, and its galleries on the one side and on the other side, one hundred cubits; and the inner temple, and the porches of the court;

the thresholds, and the closed windows, and the galleries around on dem three stories, over against the threshold, with wood ceilings all around, and from the ground up to the windows, (now the windows were covered),
to the space above the door, even to the inner house, and outside, and by all the wall all around inside and outside, by measure.
It was made with cherubim and palm trees; and a palm tree was between cherub and cherub, and every cherub had two faces;
so that there was the face of a man toward the palm tree on the one side, and the face of a young lion toward the palm tree on the other side. It was made like this through all the house all around:
from the ground to above the door were cherubim and palm trees made: thus was the wall of the temple.
As for the temple, the door posts were squared; and as for the face of the sanctuary, its appearance was as the appearance of the temple.
The altar was of wood, three cubits high, and its length two cubits; and its corners, and its length, and its walls, were of wood: and he talk say to me, This is the table that is before Baba God.
The temple and the sanctuary had two doors.
The doors had two leaves each, two turning leaves: two for the one door, and two leaves for the other.
There were made on dem, on the doors of the temple, cherubim and palm trees, like as were made on the walls; and there was a threshold of wood on the face of the porch outside.
There were closed windows and palm trees on the one side and on the other side, on the sides of the porch: thus were the side rooms of the house, and the thresholds.
Then he bring me out into the outer court, the way toward the north: and he bring me into the room that was over against the separate place, and which was over against the building toward the north.
Before the length of one hundred cubits was the north door, and the width was fifty cubits.
Over against the twenty cubits which belonged to the inner court, and over against the pavement which belonged to the outer court, was gallery against gallery in the third floor.
Before the rooms was a walk of ten cubits’ width inward, a way of one cubit; and dem doors were toward the north.
Now the upper rooms were shorter; for the galleries take away from these, more than from the lower and the middle, in the building.
For dem were in three stories, and dem didn’t have pillars as the pillars of the courts: so the uppermost was set back more than the lowest and the middle from the ground.
The wall that was outside by the side of the rooms, toward the outer court before the rooms, its length was fifty cubits.
For the length of the rooms that were in the outer court was fifty cubits: and see am, before the temple were one hundred cubits.
From under these rooms was the entry on the east side, as one goes into dem from the outer court.
In the thickness of the wall of the court toward the east, before the separate place, and before the building, there were rooms.

The way before dem was like the appearance of the rooms which were toward the north; according to dem length so was dem width: and all dem exits were both according to dem fashions, and according to dem doors.
According to the doors of the rooms that were toward the south was a door at the head of the way, even the way directly before the wall toward the east, as one enters into dem.

Then he talk say to me, The north rooms and the south rooms, which are before the separate place, Dem be the holy rooms, where the priests Wey be near to Baba God shall eat the most holy things: there shall dem lay the most holy things, and the meal offering, and the sin offering, and the trespass offering; for the place is holy.

When the priests enter in, then shall dem not go out of the holy place into the outer court, but there dem shall lay dem garments in which dem minister; for Dem be holy: and dem shall put on other garments, and shall approach to that which is for the people.
Now when he had finished measuring the inner house, he bring me out by the way of the gate whose prospect is toward the east, and measured it all around.
He measured on the east side with the measuring reed five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed all around.
He measured on the north side five hundred reeds with the measuring reed all around.
He measured on the south side five hundred reeds with the measuring reed.
He turned about to the west side, and measured five hundred reeds with the measuring reed.
He measured it on the four sides: it had a wall around it, the length five hundred, and the width five hundred, to make a separation between that which was holy and that which was common.
Afterward he bring me to the gate, even the gate that looks toward the east.
See am, the glory of the God of Israel come from the way of the east: and his voice was like the sound of many waters; and the earth shined with his glory.

It was according to the appearance of the vision which I see, even according to the vision that I see when I come to destroy the city; and the visions were like the vision that I see by the river Chebar; and I fell on my face.
Baba God’s glory come into the house by the way of the gate whose prospect is toward the east.
The Spirit take me up, and bring me into the inner court; and see am, Baba God’s glory filled the house.
I heard one speaking to me out of the house; and a man stood by me.

He talk say to me, Son of Man, this is the place of my throne, and the place of the soles of my feet, where I go live among the pikin dem of Israel forever. The house of Israel shall no more defile my holy name, neither dem, nor dem kings, by dem prostitution, and by the dead bodies of dem kings in dem high places;

in dem setting of dem threshold by my threshold, and dem door post beside my door post, and there was a wall between me and dem; and dem have defiled my holy name by dem abominations which dem have committed: so I have consumed dem in my anger.
Now Make dem put away dem prostitution, and the dead bodies of dem kings, far from me; and I go live among dem forever.
You, Son of Man, show the house to the house of Israel, that dem may be ashamed of dem iniquities; and Make dem measure the pattern.

If dem be ashamed of all that dem have done, make known to dem the form of the house, and its fashion, and its exits, and its entrances, and all its forms, and all its ordinances, and all its forms, and all its laws; and write it in dem sight; that dem may keep the whole form of it, and all its ordinances, and do dem.
This is the law of the house: on the top of the mountain the whole limit around it go be most holy. See am, this is the law of the house.

These are the measurements of the altar by cubits (the cubit is a cubit and a hand width): the bottom go be a cubit, and the width a cubit, and its border around its edge a span; and this go be the base of the altar.
From the bottom on the ground to the lower ledge go be two cubits, and the width one cubit; and from the lesser ledge to the greater ledge go be four cubits, and the width a cubit.
The upper altar go be four cubits; and from the altar hearth and upward there go be four horns.
The altar hearth go be twelve cubits long by twelve wide, square in its four sides.
The ledge go be fourteen cubits long by fourteen wide in its four sides; and the border about it go be half a cubit; and its bottom go be a cubit around; and its steps shall look toward the east.
He talk say to me, Son of Man, thus says the Lord Baba God: These are the ordinances of the altar in the day when dem shall make it, to offer burnt offerings on it, and to sprinkle blood on it.
You shall give to the priests the Levites Wey be of the offspring of Zadok, Wey be near to me, to minister to me, says the Lord Baba God, a young bull for a sin offering.
You shall take of its blood, and put it on the four horns of it, and on the four corners of the ledge, and on the border all around: thus you shall cleanse it and make atonement for it.
You shall also take the bull of the sin offering, and it go be burned in the appointed place of the house, outside of the sanctuary.
On the second day you shall offer a male goat without defect for a sin offering; and dem shall cleanse the altar, as dem cleansed it with the bull.
When you have finished cleansing it, you shall offer a young bull without defect, and a ram out of the flock without defect.
You shall bring dem near to Baba God, and the priests shall throw salt on dem, and dem shall offer dem up for a burnt offering to Baba God.
Seven days you shall prepare every day a goat for a sin offering: dem shall also prepare a young bull, and a ram out of the flock, without defect.
Seven days shall dem make atonement for the altar and purify it; so shall dem consecrate it.

When dem have accomplished the days, it go be that on the eighth day, and forward, the priests shall make una burnt offerings on the altar, and una peace offerings; and I go accept you, says the Lord Baba God.
Then he bring me back by the way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, which looks toward the east; and it was shut.
Baba God talk say to me, This gate go be shut; it no go be opened, neither shall any man enter in by it; for Baba God, the God of Israel, has entered in by it; so it go be shut.
As for the prince, he shall sit inside am as prince to eat bread before Baba God; he shall enter by the way of the porch of the gate, and shall go out by the way of the same.
Then he bring me by the way of the north gate before the house; and I looked, and see am, Baba God’s glory filled Baba God’s house: and I fell on my face.

Baba God talk say to me, Son of Man, mark well, and see with una eyes, and hear with una ears all that I tell una concerning all the ordinances of Baba God’s house, and all its laws; and mark well the entrance of the house, with every exit of the sanctuary.
You shall tell the rebellious, even to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord Baba God: you house of Israel, let it suffice you of all una abominations,

in that you have bring in foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in my sanctuary, to profane it, even my house, when you offer my bread, the fat and the blood, and dem have broken my covenant, to add to all una abominations.
You have not performed the duty of my holy things; but you have set performers of my duty in my sanctuary for unaself.
Thus says the Lord Baba God, No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter into my sanctuary, of any foreigners Wey be among the pikin dem of Israel.
But the Levites who go far from me, when Israel go astray, who go astray from me after dem idols, dem shall bear dem wickedness.

Yet dem go be ministers in my sanctuary, having oversight at the gates of the house, and ministering in the house: dem shall kill the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and dem shall stand before dem to minister to dem.

Because dem ministered to dem before dem idols, and became a stumbling block of wickedness to the house of Israel; so I have lifted up my hand against dem, says the Lord Baba God, and dem shall bear dem wickedness.

Dem no go come near to me, to execute the office of priest to me, nor to come near to any of my holy things, to the things that are most holy; but dem shall bear dem shame, and dem abominations which dem have committed.
Yet will I make dem performers of the duty of the house, for all its service, and for all that go be done inside am.

But the priests the Levites, the sons of Zadok, who performed the duty of my sanctuary when the pikin dem of Israel go astray from me, dem shall come near to me to minister to me; and dem shall stand before me to offer to me the fat and the blood, says the Lord Baba God:
dem shall enter into my sanctuary, and dem shall come near to my table, to minister to me, and dem shall keep my instruction.
It go be that, when dem enter in at the gates of the inner court, dem go be clothed with linen garments; and no wool shall come on dem, while dem minister in the gates of the inner court, and within.
Dem go get linen tires on dem heads, and go get linen breeches on dem waists; dem no go clothe themselves with anything that makes dem sweat.

When dem go out into the outer court, even into the outer court to the people, dem shall put off dem garments in which dem minister, and lay dem in the holy rooms; and dem shall put on other garments, that dem not sanctify the people with dem garments.
Neither shall dem shave dem heads, nor allow dem locks to grow long; dem shall only cut off the hair of dem heads.
Neither shall any of the priests drink wine, when dem enter into the inner court.
Neither shall dem take for dem wives a widow, nor her Wey be put away; but dem shall take virgins of the offspring of the house of Israel, or a widow Wey be the widow of a priest.
Dem shall teach my people the difference between the holy and the common, and cause dem to discern between the unclean and the clean.
In a controversy dem shall stand to judge; according to my ordinances shall dem judge it: and dem shall keep my laws and my statutes in all my appointed feasts; and dem shall make my Sabbaths holy.
Dem shall go in to no dead person to defile themselves; but for father, or for mother, or for son, or for daughter, for brother, or for sister who has had no husband, dem may defile themselves.
After he is cleansed, dem shall reckon to him seven days.
In the day that he goes into the sanctuary, into the inner court, to minister in the sanctuary, he shall offer his sin offering, says the Lord Baba God.
Dem go get an inheritance: I be dem inheritance; and you shall give dem no possession in Israel; I be dem possession.
Dem shall eat the meal offering, and the sin offering, and the trespass offering; and every devoted thing in Israel go be dem own.

The first of all the first fruits of every thing, and every offering of everything, of all una offerings, go be for the priest: you shall also give to the priests the first of una dough, to cause a blessing to rest on una house.
The priests no go eat of anything that dies of itself, or is torn, whether it is bird or animal.

Moreover, when you shall divide by lot the land for inheritance, you shall offer an offering to Baba God, a holy portion of the land; the length go be the length of twenty-five thousand reeds, and the width go be ten thousand: it go be holy in all its border all around.
Of this there go be a five hundred by five hundred square for the holy place; and fifty cubits for its suburbs all around.
Of this measure you shall measure a length of twenty-five thousand, and a width of ten thousand: and in it go be the sanctuary, which is most holy.

It is a holy portion of the land; it go be for the priests, the ministers of the sanctuary, who come near to minister to Baba God; and it go be a place for dem houses, and a holy place for the sanctuary.
Twenty-five thousand in length, and ten thousand in width, go be to the Levites, the ministers of the house, for a possession to themselves, for twenty rooms.
You shall appoint the possession of the city five thousand wide, and twenty-five thousand long, side by side with the offering of the holy portion: it go be for the whole house of Israel.

Wetin be for the prince go be on the one side and on the other side of the holy offering and of the possession of the city, in front of the holy offering and in front of the possession of the city, on the west side westward, and on the east side eastward; and in length answerable to one of the portions, from the west border to the east border.
In the land it go be to him for a possession in Israel: and my princes shall no more oppress my people; but dem shall give the land to the house of Israel according to dem tribes.
Thus says the Lord Baba God: Let it suffice you, princes of Israel: remove violence and plunder, and execute justice and righteousness; dispossessing my people, says the Lord Baba God.
You go get just balances, and a just ephah, and a just bath.
The ephah and the bath go be of one measure, that the bath may contain one tenth of a homer, and the ephah one tenth of a homer: its measure go be after the homer.
The shekel go be twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels plus twenty-five shekels plus fifteen shekels go be una mina.
This is the offering that you shall offer: the sixth part of an ephah from a homer of wheat; and you shall give the sixth part of an ephah from a homer of barley;
and the set portion of oil, of the bath of oil, one tenth of a bath out of the cor, which is ten baths, even a homer; (for ten baths are a homer;)

and one lamb of the flock, out of two hundred, from the well-watered pastures of Israel — for a meal offering, and for a burnt offering, and for peace offerings, to make atonement for dem, says the Lord Baba God.
All the people of the land shall give to this offering for the prince in Israel.

It go be the prince’s part to give the burnt offerings, and the meal offerings, and the drink offerings, in the feasts, and on the new moons, and on the Sabbaths, in all the appointed feasts of the house of Israel: he shall prepare the sin offering, and the meal offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make atonement for the house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord Baba God: In the first month, in the first day of the month, you shall take a young bull without defect; and you shall cleanse the sanctuary.
The priest shall take of the blood of the sin offering, and put it on the door posts of the house, and on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the posts of the gate of the inner court.
So you shall do on the seventh day of the month for Everybody wey errs, and for him Wey be simple: so you shall make atonement for the house.
In the first month, in the fourteenth day of the month, you go get the Passover, a feast of seven days; unleavened bread go be eaten.
On that day shall the prince prepare for imself and for all the people of the land a bull for a sin offering.
The seven days of the feast he shall prepare a burnt offering to Baba God, seven bulls and seven rams without defect daily the seven days; and a male goat daily for a sin offering.
He shall prepare a meal offering, an ephah for a bull, and an ephah for a ram, and a hin of oil to an ephah.

In the seventh month, in the fifteenth day of the month, in the feast, shall he do the like the seven days; according to the sin offering, according to the burnt offering, and according to the meal offering, and according to the oil.

Thus says the Lord Baba God: The gate of the inner court that looks toward the east go be shut the six working days; but on the Sabbath day it go be opened, and on the day of the new moon it go be opened.

The prince shall enter by the way of the porch of the gate outside, and shall stand by the post of the gate; and the priests shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he shall worship at the threshold of the gate: then he shall go out; but the gate no go be shut until the evening.
The people of the land shall worship at the door of that gate before Baba God on the Sabbaths and on the new moons.
The burnt offering that the prince shall offer to Baba God go be on the Sabbath day six lambs without defect and a ram without defect;
and the meal offering go be an ephah for the ram, and the meal offering for the lambs as he is able to give, and a hin of oil to an ephah.
On the day of the new moon it go be a young bull without defect, and six lambs, and a ram; dem go be without defect:
and he shall prepare a meal offering, an ephah for the bull, and an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs according as he is able, and a hin of oil to an ephah.
When the prince shall enter, he shall go in by the way of the porch of the gate, and he shall go out by its way.

But when the people of the land shall come before Baba God in the appointed feasts, person wey enters by the way of the north gate to worship shall go out by the way of the south gate; and person wey enters by the way of the south gate shall go out by the way of the north gate: he no go return by the way of the gate by which he come in, but shall go out straight before him.
The prince shall go in with dem when dem go in; and when dem go out, he shall go out.
In the feasts and in the solemnities the meal offering go be an ephah for a bull, and an ephah for a ram, and for the lambs as he is able to give, and a hin of oil to an ephah.

When the prince shall prepare a freewill offering, a burnt offering or peace offerings as a freewill offering to Baba God, one shall open for him the gate that looks toward the east; and he shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings, as he does on the Sabbath day: then he shall go out; and after his going out one shall shut the gate.
You shall prepare a lamb a year old without defect for a burnt offering to Baba God daily: morning by morning you shall prepare it.

You shall prepare a meal offering with it morning by morning, the sixth part of an ephah, and the third part of a hin of oil, to moisten the fine flour; a meal offering to Baba God continually by a perpetual ordinance.
Thus shall dem prepare the lamb, and the meal offering, and the oil, morning by morning, for a continual burnt offering.
Thus says the Lord Baba God: If the prince give a gift to any of his sons, it is his inheritance, it shall belong to his sons; it is dem possession by inheritance.
But if he give of his inheritance a gift to one of his workers, it go be his to the year of liberty; then it shall return to the prince; but as for his inheritance, it go be for his sons.

Moreover the prince no go take of the people’s inheritance, to thrust dem out of dem possession; he shall give inheritance to his sons out of his own possession, that my people not be scattered every man from his possession.
Then he bring me through the entry, which was at the side of the gate, into the holy rooms for the priests, which looked toward the north: and see am, there was a place on the hinder part westward.

He talk say to me, This is the place where the priests shall boil the trespass offering and the sin offering, and where dem shall bake the meal offering; that dem not bring dem out into the outer court, to sanctify the people.
Then he bring me out into the outer court, and caused me to pass by the four corners of the court; and see am, in every corner of the court there was a court.
In the four corners of the court there were courts enclosed, forty cubits long and thirty wide: these four in the corners were of one measure.
There was a wall around in dem, around the four, and boiling places were made under the walls all around.
Then he talk say to me, These are the boiling houses, where the ministers of the house shall boil the sacrifice of the people.

He bring me back to the door of the house; and see am, waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward; (for the forefront of the house was toward the east;) and the waters come down from under, from the right side of the house, on the south of the altar.

Then he bring me out by the way of the gate northward, and led me round by the way outside to the outer gate, by the way of the gate that looks toward the east; and see am, there ran out waters on the right side.
When the man go out eastward with the line in his hand, he measured one thousand cubits, and he caused me to pass through the waters, waters that were to the ankles.
Again he measured one thousand, and caused me to pass through the waters, waters that were to the knees. Again he measured one thousand, and caused me to pass through waters that were to the waist.
Afterward he measured one thousand; and it was a river that I could not pass through; for the waters were risen, waters to swim in, a river that could not be passed through.
He talk say to me, Son of Man, have you seen? Then he bring me, and caused me to return to the bank of the river.
Now when I had come back, see am, on the bank of the river were very many trees on the one side and on the other.

Then he talk say to me, These waters flow out toward the eastern region, and will go down into the Arabah; and Dem go go toward the sea; and flow into the sea which Go be made to flow out; and the waters Go be healed.

It shall happen, that every living creature which swarms, in every place where the rivers come, shall live; and there go be a plenty well-well plenty people of fish; for these waters have come there, and the waters of the sea go be healed, and everything shall live Anywhere wey the river comes.

It shall happen, that fishermen shall stand by it: from En Gedi even to En Eglaim go be a place for the spreading of nets; dem fish go be after dem kinds, as the fish of the great sea, exceeding many.
But the miry places of it, and its marshes, no go be healed; dem go be given up to salt.

By the river on its bank, on this side and on that side, shall grow every tree for chop, whose leaf no go wither, neither shall its fruit fail: it shall produce new fruit every month, because its waters issue out of the sanctuary; and its fruit go be for chop, and its leaf for healing.
Thus says the Lord Baba God: This go be the border, by which you shall divide the land for inheritance according to the twelve tribes of Israel: Joseph go get two portions.
You shall inherit it, one as well as another; for I swore to give it to una fathers: and this land shall fall to you for inheritance.
This go be the border of the land: On the north side, from the great sea, by the way of Hethlon, to the entrance of Zedad;
Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, which is between the border of Damascus and the border of Hamath; Hazer Hatticon, which is by the border of Hauran.
The border from the sea, go be Hazar Enon at the border of Damascus; and on the north northward is the border of Hamath. This is the north side.
The east side, between Hauran and Damascus and Gilead, and the land of Israel, go be the Jordan; from the north border to the east sea you shall measure. This is the east side.
The south side southward go be from Tamar as far as the waters of Meriboth Kadesh, to the brook, to the great sea. This is the south side southward.
The west side go be the great sea, from the south border as far as over against the entrance of Hamath. This is the west side.
So you shall divide this land to you according to the tribes of Israel.

It shall happen, that you shall divide it by lot for an inheritance to you and to the aliens who live among you, who shall father pikin dem among you; and dem go be to you as the native-born among the pikin dem of Israel; dem go get inheritance with you among the tribes of Israel.
It shall happen, that in what tribe the stranger lives, there you shall give him his inheritance, says the Lord Baba God.

Now these are the names of the tribes: From the north end, beside the way of Hethlon to the entrance of Hamath, Hazar Enan at the border of Damascus, northward beside Hamath, (and dem go get dem sides east and west), Dan, one portion.
By the border of Dan, from the east side to the west side, Asher, one portion.
By the border of Asher, from the east side even to the west side, Naphtali, one portion.
By the border of Naphtali, from the east side to the west side, Manasseh, one portion.
By the border of Manasseh, from the east side to the west side, Ephraim, one portion.
By the border of Ephraim, from the east side even to the west side, Reuben, one portion.
By the border of Reuben, from the east side to the west side, Judah, one portion.

By the border of Judah, from the east side to the west side, go be the offering which you shall offer, twenty-five thousand reeds in width, and in length as one of the portions, from the east side to the west side: and the sanctuary go be in the middle of it.
The offering that you shall offer to Baba God go be twenty-five thousand reeds in length, and ten thousand in width.

For these, even for the priests, go be the holy offering: toward the north twenty-five thousand in length, and toward the west ten thousand in width, and toward the east ten thousand in width, and toward the south twenty-five thousand in length: and the sanctuary of Baba God go be in the middle of it.
It go be for the priests Wey be sanctified of the sons of Zadok, who have kept my instruction, who didn’t go astray when the pikin dem of Israel go astray, as the Levites go astray.
It go be to dem an offering from the offering of the land, a thing most holy, by the border of the Levites.
Answerable to the border of the priests, the Levites go get twenty-five thousand in length, and ten thousand in width: all the length go be twenty-five thousand, and the width ten thousand.
Dem shall sell none of it, nor exchange it, nor shall the first fruits of the land be alienated; for it is holy to Baba God.
The five thousand that are left in the width, in front of the twenty-five thousand, go be for common use, for the city, for dwelling and for suburbs; and the city go be in the middle of it.

These go be its measurements: the north side four thousand and five hundred, and the south side four thousand and five hundred, and on the east side four thousand and five hundred, and the west side four thousand and five hundred.
The city go get suburbs: toward the north two hundred fifty, and toward the south two hundred fifty, and toward the east two hundred fifty, and toward the west two hundred fifty.

The remainder in the length, answerable to the holy offering, go be ten thousand eastward, and ten thousand westward; and it go be answerable to the holy offering; and its increase go be for chop to people wey labor in the city.
People wey labor in the city, out of all the tribes of Israel, shall cultivate it.
All the offering go be a square of twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand: you shall offer it as a holy offering, with the possession of the city.

The remainder go be for the prince, on the one side and on the other of the holy offering and of the possession of the city; in front of the twenty-five thousand of the offering toward the east border, and westward in front of the twenty-five thousand toward the west border, answerable to the portions, it go be for the prince: and the holy offering and the sanctuary of the house go be in the middle of it.

Moreover from the possession of the Levites, and from the possession of the city, being in the middle of that which is the prince’s, between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin, it go be for the prince.
As for the rest of the tribes: from the east side to the west side, Benjamin, one portion.
By the border of Benjamin, from the east side to the west side, Simeon, one portion.
By the border of Simeon, from the east side to the west side, Issachar, one portion.
By the border of Issachar, from the east side to the west side, Zebulun, one portion.
By the border of Zebulun, from the east side to the west side, Gad, one portion.
By the border of Gad, at the south side southward, the border go be even from Tamar to the waters of Meribath Kadesh, to the brook, to the great sea.
This is the land which you shall divide by lot to the tribes of Israel for inheritance, and these are dem several portions, says the Lord Baba God.
These are the exits of the city: On the north side four thousand and five hundred reeds by measure;
and the gates of the city go be after the names of the tribes of Israel, three gates northward: the gate of Reuben, one; the gate of Judah, one; the gate of Levi, one.
At the east side four thousand and five hundred reeds, and three gates: even the gate of Joseph, one; the gate of Benjamin, one; the gate of Dan, one.
At the south side four thousand and five hundred reeds by measure, and three gates: the gate of Simeon, one; the gate of Issachar, one; the gate of Zebulun, one.
At the west side four thousand and five hundred reeds, with dem three gates: the gate of Gad, one; the gate of Asher, one; the gate of Naphtali, one.
It go be eighteen thousand reeds around: and the name of the city from that day go be, Baba God is there.
In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah come Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to Jerusalem, and besieged it.

The Lord give Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, with part of the vessels of the house of God; and he carried dem into the land of Shinar to the house of his god: and he bring the vessels into the treasure house of his god.
The king spoke to Ashpenaz the master of his eunuchs, that he should bring in some of the pikin dem of Israel, even of the royal offspring and of the nobles;

youths in whom was no defect, but well-favored, and skillful in all wisdom, and endowed with knowledge, and understanding science, and such as had ability to stand in the king’s palace; and that he should teach dem the learning and the language of the Chaldeans.
The king appointed for dem a daily portion of the king’s dainties, and of the wine which he drank, and that dem should be nourished three years; that at its end dem should stand before the king.
Now among these were, of the pikin dem of Judah, Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
The prince of the eunuchs give names to dem: to Daniel he give the name Belteshazzar; and to Hananiah, Shadrach; and to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.

But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile imself with the king’s dainties, nor with the wine which he drank: so he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile imself.
Now God made Daniel to find kindness and compassion in the sight of the prince of the eunuchs.

The prince of the eunuchs talk say to Daniel, I fear my lord the king, who has appointed una chop and una drink: for why should he see una faces worse looking than the youths Wey be of una own age? so would you endanger my head with the king.
Then Daniel talk say to the steward whom the prince of the eunuchs had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah:
Test una workers, I beg you, ten days; and Make dem give us vegetables to eat, and water to drink.
Then let our faces be looked on before you, and the face of the youths who eat of the king’s dainties; and as you see, deal with una workers.
So he listened to dem in this matter, and proved dem ten days.
At the end of ten days dem faces appeared fairer, and dem were fatter in flesh, than all the youths who ate of the king’s dainties.
So the steward take away dem dainties, and the wine that dem should drink, and give dem pulse.
Now as for these four youths, God give dem knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom: and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.
At the end of the days which the king had appointed for bringing dem in, the prince of the eunuchs bring dem in before Nebuchadnezzar.
The king talked with dem; and among dem all was find Nobody like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah: so stood dem before the king.
In every matter of wisdom and understanding, concerning which the king inquired of dem, he find dem ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters who were in all his realm.
Daniel continued even to the first year of king Cyrus.
In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams; and his spirit was troubled, and his sleep go from him.
Then the king commanded to call the magicians, and the enchanters, and the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans, to tell the king his dreams. So dem come in and stood before the king.
The king talk say to dem, I have dreamed a dream, and my spirit is troubled to know the dream.
Then spoke the Chaldeans to the king in the Syrian language, O king, live forever: tell una workers the dream, and We go show the interpretation.
The king answer the Chaldeans, The thing is gone from me: if you no make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you go be cut in pieces, and una houses go be made a dunghill.
But if you show the dream and its interpretation, you shall receive of me gifts and rewards and great honor: so show me the dream and its interpretation.
Dem answer the second time and talk say, Let the king tell his workers the dream, and We go show the interpretation.
The king answer, I know of a certainty that you would gain time, because you see the thing is gone from me.

But if you no make known to me the dream, E get but one law for you; for you have prepared lying and corrupt words to speak before me, until the time be changed: so tell me the dream, and I shall know that you can show me its interpretation.

The Chaldeans answer before the king, and talk say, There No be a man on the earth who can show the king’s matter, because no king, lord, or ruler, has ask such a thing of any magician, or enchanter, or Chaldean.
It is a rare thing that the king requires, and E get no other who can show it before the king, except the gods, whose dwelling No be with flesh.
For this cause the king was angry and very furious, and commanded to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
So the decree go out, and the wise men were to be slain; and dem sought Daniel and his companions to be slain.
Then Daniel come back answer with counsel and prudence to Arioch the captain of the king’s guard, who was gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon;
he answer Arioch the king’s captain, Why is the decree so urgent from the king? Then Arioch made the thing known to Daniel.
Daniel go in, and desired of the king that he would appoint him a time, and he would show the king the interpretation.
Then Daniel go to his house, and made the thing known to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions:
that dem would desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret; that Daniel and his companions no suppose perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
Then was the secret revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
Daniel answer, Blessed be the name of God forever and ever; for wisdom and might are his.
He changes the times and the seasons; he removes kings, and sets up kings; he gives wisdom to the wise, and knowledge to people wey have understanding;
he reveals the deep and secret things; he knows Wetin be in the darkness, and the light dwells with him.
I thank you, and praise you, you God of my fathers, who have given me wisdom and might, and have now made known to me what we desired of you; for you have made known to us the king’s matter.

So Daniel go in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon; he go and talk say thus to him: No destroy the wise men of Babylon; bring me in before the king, and I go show to the king the interpretation.
Then Arioch bring in Daniel before the king in haste, and talk say thus to him, I have find a man of the pikin dem of the captivity of Judah, who will make known to the king the interpretation.
The king answer Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, Are you able to make known to me the dream which I have seen, and its interpretation?
Daniel answer before the king, and talk say, The secret which the king has demanded can neither wise men, enchanters, magicians, nor soothsayers, show to the king;
but E get a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what go be in the latter days. Una dream, and the visions of una head on una bed, are these:
as for you, O king, una thoughts come on una bed, what should happen hereafter; and person wey reveals secrets has made known to you what shall happen.

But as for me, this secret No be revealed to me for any wisdom that I have more than any living, but to the intent that the interpretation may be made known to the king, and that you may know the thoughts of una heart.
You, O king, see, and see am, a great image. This image, which was mighty, and whose brightness was excellent, stood before you; and its aspect was awesome.
As for this image, its head was of fine gold, its breast and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of brass,
its legs of iron, its feet part of iron, and part of clay.
You see until a stone was cut out without hands, which struck the image on its feet that were of iron and clay, and broke dem in pieces.

Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken in pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshing floors; and the wind carried dem away, so that no place was find for dem: and the stone that struck the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.
This is the dream; and We go tell its interpretation before the king.
You, O king, are king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, the power, and the strength, and the glory;
and Anywhere wey the pikin dem of men live, the animals of the field and the birds of the sky has he given into una hand, and has made you to rule over dem all: You be the head of gold.
After you shall arise another kingdom inferior to you; and another third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth.
The fourth kingdom go be strong as iron, because iron breaks in pieces and subdues all things; and as iron that crushes all these, shall it break in pieces and crush.

Whereas you see the feet and toes, part of potters’ clay, and part of iron, it go be a divided kingdom; but there go be in it of the strength of the iron, because you see the iron mixed with miry clay.
As the toes of the feet were part of iron, and part of clay, so the kingdom go be partly strong, and partly broken.
Whereas you see the iron mixed with miry clay, dem shall mingle themselves with the seed of men; but dem no go cling to each other, even as iron No dey mingle with clay.

In the days of those kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed, nor shall its sovereignty be left to another people; but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand forever.

Because you see that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it broke in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God has made known to the king what shall happen hereafter: and the dream is certain, and its interpretation sure.
Then the king Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face, and worshiped Daniel, and commanded that dem should offer an offering and sweet odors to him.
The king answer to Daniel, and talk say, Of a truth una God is the God of gods, and the Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, since you Don dey able to reveal this secret.
Then the king made Daniel great, and give him many great gifts, and made him to rule over the whole province of Babylon, and to be chief governor over all the wise men of Babylon.
Daniel requested of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, over the affairs of the province of Babylon: but Daniel was in the gate of the king.
Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, whose height was sixty cubits, and its width six cubits: he set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon.

Then Nebuchadnezzar the king sent to gather together the satraps, the deputies, and the governors, the judges, the treasurers, the counselors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image which Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.

Then the satraps, the deputies, and the governors, the judges, the treasurers, the counselors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, were gathered together to the dedication of the image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up; and dem stood before the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
Then the herald cried aloud, To you it is commanded, peoples, nations, and languages,
that whenever you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, you fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king has set up;
and Anybody wey no dey fall down and worship shall the same hour be throw into the middle of a burning fiery furnace.

So at that time, when all the peoples heard the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, all the peoples, the nations, and the languages, fell down and worshiped the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.
So at that time certain Chaldeans come near, and bring accusation against the Jews.
Dem answer Nebuchadnezzar the king, O king, live for ever.
You, O king, have made a decree, that every man that shall hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, shall fall down and worship the golden image;
and Anybody wey no dey fall down and worship go be throw into the middle of a burning fiery furnace.

E get certain Jews whom you have appointed over the affairs of the province of Babylon: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego; these men, O king, have not respected you. Dem no serve una gods, nor worship the golden image which you have set up.
Then Nebuchadnezzar in rage and fury commanded to bring Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. Then dem bring these men before the king.
Nebuchadnezzar answer dem, Is it on purpose, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you no serve my god, nor worship the golden image which I have set up?

Now if You be ready whenever you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music to fall down and worship the image which I have made, good: but if you no worship, you go be throw the same hour into the middle of a burning fiery furnace; and Wey be that god that shall deliver you out of my hands?
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answer the king, Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer you in this matter.
If it happens, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace; and he will deliver us out of una hand, O king.
But if not, let it be known to you, O king, that We go not serve una gods, nor worship the golden image which you have set up.

Then was Nebuchadnezzar full of fury, and the form of his appearance was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He spoke, and commanded that dem should heat the furnace seven times more than it was usually heated.
He commanded certain mighty men who were in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, and to throw dem into the burning fiery furnace.
Then these men were bound in dem pants, dem tunics, and dem mantles, and dem other clothes, and were throw into the middle of the burning fiery furnace.
So because the king’s commandment was urgent, and the furnace exceeding hot, the flame of the fire killed those men who take up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
These three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell down bound into the middle of the burning fiery furnace.

Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonished, and rose up in haste: he spoke and talk say to his counselors, Didn’t we throw three men bound into the middle of the fire? Dem answer the king, True, O king.
He answer, Look, I see four men loose, walking in the middle of the fire, and Dem be unharmed; and the aspect of the fourth is like a son of the gods.

Then Nebuchadnezzar come near to the mouth of the burning fiery furnace: he spoke and talk say, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, you workers of the Most High God, come out, and come here. Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego come out of the middle of the fire.

The satraps, the deputies, and the governors, and the king’s counselors, being gathered together, see these men, that the fire had no power on dem bodies, nor was the hair of dem head singed, neither were dem pants changed, nor had the smell of fire passed on dem.

Nebuchadnezzar spoke and talk say, Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who has sent his angel, and delivered his workers who trusted in him, and have changed the king’s word, and have yielded dem bodies, that dem might not serve nor worship any god, except dem own God.

So I make a decree, that every people, nation, and language, which speak anything evil against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, go be cut in pieces, and dem houses go be made a dunghill; because E get no other god Wey be able to deliver after this sort.
Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar the king, to all the peoples, nations, and languages, who live in all the earth: Peace be multiplied to you.
It has seemed good to me to show the signs and wonders that the Most High God has worked toward me.
How great are his signs! and how mighty are his wonders! his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his dominion is from generation to generation.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at rest in my house, and flourishing in my palace.
I see a dream which made me afraid; and the thoughts on my bed and the visions of my head troubled me.
So made I a decree to bring in all the wise men of Babylon before me, that dem might make known to me the interpretation of the dream.
Then come in the magicians, the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers; and I told the dream before dem; but dem No make known to me its interpretation.
But at the last Daniel come in before me, whose name was Belteshazzar, according to the name of my god, and in whom is the spirit of the holy gods: and I told the dream before him, saying,
Belteshazzar, master of the magicians, because I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you, and no secret troubles you, tell me the visions of my dream that I have seen, and its interpretation.
Thus were the visions of my head on my bed: I see, and see am, a tree in the middle of the earth; and its height was great.
The tree grew, and was strong, and its height reached to the sky, and its sight to the end of all the earth.

The leaves of it were beautiful, and its fruit much, and in it was chop for all: the animals of the field had shadow under it, and the birds of the sky lived in its branches, and all flesh was fed from it.
I see in the visions of my head on my bed, and see am, a watcher and a holy one come down from the sky.
He cried aloud, and talk say thus, Cut down the tree, and cut off its branches, shake off its leaves, and scatter its fruit: let the animals get away from under it, and the fowls from its branches.

Nevertheless leave the stump of its roots in the earth, even with a band of iron and brass, in the tender grass of the field; and let it be wet with the dew of the sky: and let his portion be with the animals in the grass of the earth:
let his heart be changed from man’s, and let an animal’s heart be given to him; and let seven times pass over him.

The sentence is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones; to the intent that the living may know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he will, and sets up over it the lowest of men.

This dream I, king Nebuchadnezzar, have seen; and you, Belteshazzar, declare the interpretation, because all the wise men of my kingdom No be able to make known to me the interpretation; but You be able; for the spirit of the holy gods is in you.

Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was stricken mute for a while, and his thoughts troubled him. The king answer, Belteshazzar, no let the dream, or the interpretation, trouble you. Belteshazzar answer, My lord, the dream be to people wey hate you, and its interpretation to una adversaries.
The tree that you see, which grew, and was strong, whose height reached to the sky, and its sight to all the earth;
whose leaves were beautiful, and its fruit much, and in it was chop for all; under which the animals of the field lived, and on whose branches the birds of the sky had dem habitation:
it is you, O king, that are grown and become strong; for una greatness is grown, and reaches to the sky, and una dominion to the end of the earth.

Whereas the king see a watcher and a holy one coming down from the sky, and saying, Cut down the tree, and destroy it; nevertheless leave the stump of its roots in the earth, even with a band of iron and brass, in the tender grass of the field, and let it be wet with the dew of the sky: and let his portion be with the animals of the field, until seven times pass over him;
this is the interpretation, O king, and it is the decree of the Most High, which has come on my lord the king:

that you go be driven from men, and una dwelling go be with the animals of the field, and you go be made to eat grass as oxen, and go be wet with the dew of the sky, and seven times shall pass over you; until you know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he will.
Whereas dem commanded to leave the stump of the roots of the tree; una kingdom go be sure to you, after that you go get known that the heavens do rule.
So, O king, let my counsel be acceptable to you, and break off una sins by righteousness, and una iniquities by showing mercy to the poor; if there may be a lengthening of una tranquility.
All this come on the king Nebuchadnezzar.
At the end of twelve months he was walking in the royal palace of Babylon.
The king spoke and talk say, No be this great Babylon, which I have built for the royal dwelling place, by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?
While the word was in the king’s mouth, a voice come from the sky, saying, “O king Nebuchadnezzar, to you it is spoken: The kingdom has comot from you.

You go be driven from men; and una dwelling go be with the animals of the field. You go be made to eat grass as oxen. Seven times shall pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he will.”

This was fulfilled the same hour on Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven from men, and ate grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the sky, until his hair had grown like eagles’ feathers, and his nails like birds’ claws.

At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding come back to me, and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and honored him who lives forever; for his dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom from generation to generation.

All the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing; and he does according to his will in the army of heaven, and among the inhabitants of the earth; and Nobody can stop his hand, or ask him, Wetin be you doing?

At the same time my understanding come back to me; and for the glory of my kingdom, my majesty and brightness come back to me; and my counselors and my lords sought to me; and I was established in my kingdom, and excellent greatness was added to me.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and extol and honor the King of heaven; for all his works are truth, and his ways justice; and people wey walk in pride he is able to abase.
Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords, and drank wine before the thousand.

Belshazzar, while he tasted the wine, commanded to bring the golden and silver vessels which Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem; that the king and his lords, his wives and his concubines, might drink from dem.
Then dem bring the golden vessels that were taken out of the temple of God’s house which was at Jerusalem; and the king and his lords, his wives and his concubines, drank from dem.
Dem drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone.
In the same hour, the fingers of a man’s hand come out and wrote near the lamp stand on the plaster of the wall of the king’s palace. The king see the part of the hand that wrote.
Then the king’s face was changed in him, and his thoughts troubled him; and the joints of his thighs were loosened, and his knees struck one against another.

The king cried aloud to bring in the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers. The king spoke and talk say to the wise men of Babylon, Anybody wey shall read this writing, and show me its interpretation, go be clothed with purple, and have a chain of gold about his neck, and go be the third ruler in the kingdom.
Then come in all the king’s wise men; but dem could not read the writing, nor make known to the king the interpretation.
Then was king Belshazzar greatly troubled, and his face was changed in him, and his lords were perplexed.

The queen by reason of the words of the king and his lords come into the banquet house: the queen spoke and talk say, O king, live forever; no let una thoughts trouble you, nor let una face be changed.

E get a man in una kingdom, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods; and in the days of una father light and understanding and wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods, were find in him; and the king Nebuchadnezzar una father, the king, una father, made him master of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and soothsayers;

because an excellent spirit, and knowledge, and understanding, interpreting of dreams, and showing of dark sentences, and dissolving of doubts, were find in the same Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be call, and he will show the interpretation.
Then was Daniel bring in before the king. The king spoke and talk say to Daniel, Are you that Daniel, Wey be of the pikin dem of the captivity of Judah, whom the king my father bring out of Judah?
I have heard of you, that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that light and understanding and excellent wisdom are find in you.
Now the wise men, the enchanters, Don dey bring in before me, that dem should read this writing, and make known to me its interpretation; but dem could not show the interpretation of the thing.

But I have heard of you, that you can give interpretations, and dissolve doubts; now if you can read the writing, and make known to me its interpretation, you go be clothed with purple, and have a chain of gold about una neck, and go be the third ruler in the kingdom.
Then Daniel answer before the king, Let una gifts be to yourself, and give una rewards to another; nevertheless I go read the writing to the king, and make known to him the interpretation.
You, king, the Most High God give Nebuchadnezzar una father the kingdom, and greatness, and glory, and majesty:

and because of the greatness that he give him, all the peoples, nations, and languages trembled and feared before him: whom he would he killed, and whom he would he kept alive; and whom he would he raised up, and whom he would he put down.
But when his heart was lifted up, and his spirit was hardened so that he dealt proudly, he was deposed from his kingly throne, and dem take his glory from him:

and he was driven from the sons of men, and his heart was made like the animals’, and his dwelling was with the wild donkeys; he was fed with grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the sky; until he know that the Most High God rules in the kingdom of men, and that he sets up over it whomever he will.
You, his son, Belshazzar, have not humbled una heart, though you know all this,

but have lifted up yourself against the Lord of heaven; and dem have bring the vessels of his house before you, and you and una lords, una wives and una concubines, have drunk wine from dem; and you have praised the gods of silver and gold, of brass, iron, wood, and stone, which no see, nor hear, nor know; and the God in whose hand una breath is, and whose are all una ways, you have not glorified.
Then was the part of the hand sent from before him, and this writing was inscribed.
This is the writing that was inscribed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.
This is the interpretation of the thing: MENE; God has counted una kingdom, and bring it to an end;
TEKEL; You be weighed in the balances, and are find wanting.
PERES; una kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians.
Then commanded Belshazzar, and dem clothed Daniel with purple, and put a chain of gold about his neck, and made proclamation concerning him, that he should be the third ruler in the kingdom.
In that night Belshazzar the Chaldean King was slain.
Darius the Mede received the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old.
It pleased Darius to set over the kingdom one hundred twenty satraps, who should be throughout the whole kingdom;
and over dem three presidents, of whom Daniel was one; that these satraps might give account to dem, and that the king should have no damage.
Then this Daniel was distinguished above the presidents and the satraps, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the king thought to set him over the whole realm.

Then the presidents and the satraps sought to find occasion against Daniel as touching the kingdom; but dem could find no occasion nor fault, because he was faithful, neither was there any error or fault find in him.
Then these men talk say, We no go find any occasion against this Daniel, except we find it against him concerning the law of his God.
Then these presidents and satraps assembled together to the king, and talk say thus to him, King Darius, live forever.

All the presidents of the kingdom, the deputies and the satraps, the counselors and the governors, have consulted together to establish a royal statute, and to make a strong decree, that Anybody wey shall ask a petition of any god or man for thirty days, except of you, O king, he go be throw into the den of lions.
Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it not be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which no dey alter.
So king Darius signed the writing and the decree.

When Daniel know that the writing was signed, he go into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem) and he kneeled on his knees three times a day, and prayed, and Thank God before his God, as he did before.
Then these men assembled together, and find Daniel making petition and supplication before his God.

Then dem come near, and spoke before the king concerning the king’s decree: Haven’t you signed a decree that every man who makes a petition to any god or man within thirty days, except to you, O king, go be throw into the den of lions? The king answer, The thing is true, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which no dey alter.

Then answer dem and talk say before the king, That Daniel, Wey be of the pikin dem of the captivity of Judah, no dey respect you, O king, nor the decree that you have signed, but makes his petition three times a day.
Then the king, when he heard these words, was very displeased, and set his heart on Daniel to deliver him; and he labored until the going down of the sun to rescue him.

Then these men assembled together to the king, and talk say to the king, Know, O king, that it is a law of the Medes and Persians, that no decree nor statute which the king establishes may be changed.
Then the king commanded, and dem bring Daniel, and throw him into the den of lions. The king spoke and talk say to Daniel, Una God whom you serve continually, he will deliver you.
A stone was bring, and laid on the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel.
Then the king go to his palace, and passed the night fasting; neither were instruments of music bring before him: and his sleep fled from him.
Then the king arose very early in the morning, and go in haste to the den of lions.

When he come near to the den to Daniel, he cried with a lamentable voice; the king spoke and talk say to Daniel, Daniel, worker of the living God, is una God, whom you serve continually, able to deliver you from the lions?
Then Daniel talk say to the king, O king, live forever.
My God has sent his angel, and has shut the lions’ mouths, and dem have not hurt me; because as before him innocence was find in me; and also before you, O king, I have done no hurt.

Then was the king exceeding glad, and commanded that dem should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no kind of harm was find on him, because he had trusted in his God.

The king commanded, and dem bring those men who had accused Daniel, and dem throw dem into the den of lions, dem, dem pikin dem, and dem wives; and the lions mauled dem, and broke all dem bones in pieces, before dem come to the bottom of the den.
Then king Darius wrote to all the peoples, nations, and languages, who live in all the earth: Peace be multiplied to you.

I make a decree, that in all the dominion of my kingdom men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel; for he is the living God, and steadfast forever, His kingdom that which no go be destroyed; and his dominion go be even to the end.
He delivers and rescues, and he works signs and wonders in heaven and in earth, who has delivered Daniel from the power of the lions.
So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon Daniel had a dream and visions of his head on his bed: then he wrote the dream and told the sum of the matters.
Daniel spoke and talk say, I see in my vision by night, and, see am, the four winds of the sky broke out on the great sea.
Four great animals come up from the sea, diverse one from another.
The first was like a lion, and had eagle’s wings: I see until its wings were plucked, and it was lifted up from the earth, and made to stand on two feet as a man; and a man’s heart was given to it.
See am, another animal, a second, like a bear; and it was raised up on one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth: and dem talk say thus to it, Arise, devour much flesh.
After this I see, and see am, another, like a leopard, which had on its back four wings of a bird; the animal had also four heads; and dominion was given to it.

After this I see in the night visions, and, see am, a fourth animal, awesome and powerful, and strong exceedingly; and it had great iron teeth; it devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet: and it was diverse from all the animals that were before it; and it had ten horns.

I considered the horns, and see am, there come up among dem another horn, a little one, before which three of the first horns were plucked up by the roots: and see am, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a man, and a mouth speaking great things.

I see until thrones were placed, and one who was ancient of days sat: his clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire.
A fiery stream issued and come out from before him: thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.
I see at that time because of the voice of the great words which the horn spoke; I see even until the animal was slain, and its body destroyed, and it was given to be burned with fire.
As for the rest of the animals, dem dominion was taken away: yet dem lives were prolonged for a season and a time.
I see in the night visions, and see am, there come with the clouds of the sky one like a Son of Man, and he come even to the ancient of days, and dem bring him near before him.

There was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which no go pass away, and his kingdom that which no go be destroyed.
As for me, Daniel, my spirit was grieved within my body, and the visions of my head troubled me.
I come near to one of people wey stood by, and ask him the truth concerning all this. So he told me, and made me know the interpretation of the things.
These great animals, which are four, are four kings, who shall arise out of the earth.
But the saints of the Most High shall receive the kingdom, and possess the kingdom forever, even forever and ever.

Then I desired to know the truth concerning the fourth animal, which was diverse from all of dem, exceedingly terrible, whose teeth were of iron, and its nails of brass; which devoured, broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet;

and concerning the ten horns that were on its head, and the other horn which come up, and before which three fell, even that horn that had eyes, and a mouth that spoke great things, whose look was more stout than its fellows.
I see, and the same horn made war with the saints, and prevailed against dem;
until the ancient of days come, and judgment was given to the saints of the Most High, and the time come that the saints possessed the kingdom.
Thus he talk say, The fourth animal go be a fourth kingdom on earth, which go be diverse from all the kingdoms, and shall devour the whole earth, and shall tread it down, and break it in pieces.
As for the ten horns, out of this kingdom shall ten kings arise: and another shall arise after dem; and he go be diverse from the former, and he shall put down three kings.

He shall speak words against the Most High, and shall wear out the saints of the Most High; and he shall think to change the times and the law; and dem go be given into his hand until a time and times and half a time.
But the judgment go be set, and dem shall take away his dominion, to consume and to destroy it to the end.

The kingdom and the dominion, and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole sky, go be given to the people of the saints of the Most High: his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.
Here is the end of the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts much troubled me, and my face was changed in me: but I kept the matter in my heart.
In the third year of the reign of king Belshazzar a vision appeared to me, even to me, Daniel, after that which appeared to me at the first.
I see in the vision; now it was so, that when I see, I was in the citadel of Susa, which is in the province of Elam; and I see in the vision, and I was by the river Ulai.
Then I lifted up my eyes, and see, and see am, there stood before the river a ram which had two horns: and the two horns were high; but one was higher than the other, and the higher come up last.

I see the ram pushing westward, and northward, and southward; and no animals could stand before him, neither was there any who could deliver out of his hand; but he did according to his will, and magnified imself.
As I was considering, see am, a male goat come from the west over the surface of the whole earth, and didn’t touch the ground: and the goat had a notable horn between his eyes.
He come to the ram that had the two horns, which I see standing before the river, and ran on him in the fury of his power.

I see him come close to the ram, and he was moved with anger against him, and struck the ram, and broke his two horns; and there was no power in the ram to stand before him; but he throw him down to the ground, and trampled on him; and there was Nobody who could deliver the ram out of his hand.
The male goat magnified imself exceedingly: and when he was strong, the great horn was broken; and instead of it there come up four notable horns toward the four winds of the sky.
Out of one of dem come out a little horn, which grew exceeding great, toward the south, and toward the east, and toward the glorious land.
It grew great, even to the army of the sky; and some of the army and of the stars it throw down to the ground, and trampled on dem.
Yes, it magnified itself, even to the prince of the army; and it take away from him the continual burnt offering, and the place of his sanctuary was throw down.
The army was given over to it together with the continual burnt offering through disobedience; and it throw down truth to the ground, and it did its pleasure and prospered.

Then I heard a holy one speaking; and another holy one talk say to that certain one who spoke, How long go be the vision about the continual burnt offering, and the disobedience that makes desolate, to give both the sanctuary and the army to be trodden under foot?
He talk say to me, To two thousand and three hundred evenings and mornings; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed.
When I, even I Daniel, had seen the vision, I sought to understand it; and see am, there stood before me as the appearance of a man.
I heard a man’s voice between the banks of the Ulai, which call, and talk say, Gabriel, make this man to understand the vision.
So he come near where I stood; and when he come, I was frightened, and fell on my face: but he talk say to me, Understand, Son of Man; for the vision belongs to the time of the end.
Now as he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep with my face toward the ground; but he touched me, and set me upright.
He talk say, See am, I go make you know what go be in the latter time of the indignation; for it belongs to the appointed time of the end.
The ram which you see, that had the two horns, Dem be the kings of Media and Persia.
The rough male goat is the king of Greece: and the great horn that is between his eyes is the first king.
As for that which was broken, in the place where four stood up, four kingdoms shall stand up out of the nation, but not with his power.
In the latter time of dem kingdom, when the transgressors have come to the full, a king of fierce face, and understanding dark sentences, shall stand up.
His power go be mighty, but not by his own power; and he shall destroy wonderfully, and shall prosper in what he does; and he shall destroy the mighty ones and the holy people.

Through his policy he shall cause craft to prosper in his hand; and he shall magnify imself in his heart, and he shall destroy many in dem security. He shall also stand up against the prince of princes; but he go be broken without hand.
The vision of the evenings and mornings which Don dey told is true: but seal up the vision; for it belongs to many days to come.
I, Daniel, fainted, and was sick certain days; then I rose up, and did the king’s business: and I wondered at the vision, but Nobody understand it.
In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the offspring of the Medes, who was made king over the realm of the Chaldeans,

in the first year of his reign I, Daniel, understand by the books the number of the years about which Baba God’s word come to Jeremiah the prophet, for the accomplishing of the desolations of Jerusalem, even seventy years.
I set my face to the Lord God, to seek by prayer and petitions, with fasting and sackcloth and ashes.
I prayed to Baba God my God, and made confession, and talk say, Oh, Lord, the great and dreadful God, who keeps covenant and loving kindness with people wey love him and keep his commandments,
we have sinned, and have dealt perversely, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even turning aside from una precepts and from una ordinances;
neither have we listened to una workers the prophets, who spoke in una name to our kings, our princes, and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.

Lord, righteousness belongs to you, but to us confusion of face, as it is today; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to all Israel, Wey be near, and Wey be far off, through all the countries where you have driven dem, because of dem trespass that dem have trespassed against you.
Lord, to us belongs confusion of face, to our kings, to our princes, and to our fathers, because we have sinned against you.
To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgiveness; for we have rebelled against him;
neither have we obeyed Baba God our God’s voice, to walk in his laws, which he set before us by his workers the prophets.

Yes, all Israel have transgressed una law, turning aside, that dem no suppose obey una voice: so the curse and the oath written in the law of Moses the worker of God Don dey poured out on us; for we have sinned against him.

He has confirmed his words, which he spoke against us, and against our judges who judged us, by bringing on us a great evil; for under the whole sky, such has not been done as Don dey done to Jerusalem.

As it is written in the law of Moses, all this evil has come on us: yet have we not entreated the favor of Baba God our God, that we should turn from our iniquities, and have discernment in una truth.
So has Baba God watched over the evil, and bring it on us; for Baba God our God is righteous in all his works which he does, and we have not obeyed his voice.
Now, Lord our God, who has bring una people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and have gotten yourself renown, as it is today; we have sinned, we have done wickedly.

Lord, according to all una righteousness, let una anger and please let una serious anger be turned away from una city Jerusalem, una holy mountain; because for our sins, and for the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and una people have become a reproach to all Wey be around us.
Now so, our God, listen to the prayer of una worker, and to his petitions, and cause una face to shine on una sanctuary that is desolate, for the Lord’s sake.

My God, turn una ear, and hear; open una eyes, and see our desolations, and the city which is call by una name: for we No present our petitions before you for our righteousness, but for una great mercies’ sake.
Lord, hear; Lord, forgive; Lord, listen and do; no defer, for una own sake, my God, because una city and una people are call by una name.
While I was speaking, and praying, and confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and presenting my supplication before Baba God my God for the holy mountain of my God;
yes, while I was speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening offering.
He instructed me, and talked with me, and talk say, Daniel, I have now come to give you wisdom and understanding.
At the beginning of una petitions the commandment go out, and I have come to tell you; for You be greatly beloved: so consider the matter, and understand the vision.

Seventy weeks are decreed on una people and on una holy city, to finish disobedience, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for wickedness, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most holy.

Know so and discern, that from the going out of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem to the Anointed One, the prince, go be seven weeks, and sixty-two weeks: it go be built again, with street and moat, even in troubled times.

After the sixty-two weeks the Anointed One go be cut off, and go get nothing: and the people of the prince who shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and its end go be with a flood, and even to the end go be war; desolations are determined.

He shall make a firm covenant with many for one week: and in the middle of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the offering to cease; and on the wing of abominations shall come one who makes desolate; and even to the full end, and that determined, shall serious anger be poured out on the desolate.

In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia a thing was revealed to Daniel, whose name was call Belteshazzar; and the thing was true, even a great warfare: and he understand the thing, and had understanding of the vision.
In those days I, Daniel, was mourning three whole weeks.
I ate no pleasant bread, neither come meat nor wine into my mouth, neither did I anoint myself at all, until three whole weeks were fulfilled.
