In the four and twentieth day of the first month, as I was by the side of the great river, which is Hiddekel,
I lifted up my eyes, and looked, and see am, a man clothed in linen, whose thighs were adorned with pure gold of Uphaz:

his body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as flaming torches, and his arms and his feet like burnished brass, and the voice of his words like the voice of a plenty people.
I, Daniel, alone see the vision; for the men who were with me didn’t see the vision; but a great quaking fell on dem, and dem fled to hide themselves.
So I was left alone, and see this great vision, and there remain no strength in me; for my comeliness was turned in me into corruption, and I retained no strength.
Yet heard I the voice of his words; and when I heard the voice of his words, then was I fallen into a deep sleep on my face, with my face toward the ground.
See am, a hand touched me, which set me on my knees and on the palms of my hands.
He talk say to me, Daniel, you man greatly beloved, understand the words that I speak to you, and stand upright; for am I now sent to you. When he had spoken this word to me, I stood trembling.
Then he talk say to me, No fear, Daniel; for from the first day that you set una heart to understand, and to humble yourself before una God, una words were heard: and I have come for una words’ sake.
But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me twenty-one days; but, see am, Michael, one of the chief princes, come to help me: and I remain there with the kings of Persia.
Now I have come to make you understand what shall happen to una people in the latter days; for the vision is yet for many days:
and when he had spoken to me according to these words, I set my face toward the ground, and was mute.

See am, one in the likeness of the sons of men touched my lips: then I opened my mouth, and spoke and talk say to him who stood before me, my lord, by reason of the vision my sorrows are turned on me, and I retain no strength.
For how can the worker of this my lord talk with this my lord? for as for me, sharp-sharp there remain no strength in me, neither was there breath left in me.
Then there touched me again one like the appearance of a man, and he strengthened me.
He talk say, “Greatly beloved man, No fear: peace be to you, be strong, yes, be strong.” When he spoke to me, I was strengthened, and talk say, “Let my lord speak; for you have strengthened me.”
Then he talk say, “Do you know why I have come to you? Now I go return to fight with the prince of Persia. When I go out, see am, the prince of Greece shall come.
But I go tell you that which is inscribed in the writing of truth: and E get Nobody who holds with me against these, but Michael una prince.”
“As for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood up to confirm and strengthen him.

Now will I show you the truth. See am, there shall stand up yet three kings in Persia; and the fourth go be far richer than dem all: and when he has grown strong through his riches, he shall stir up all against the realm of Greece.
A mighty king shall stand up, who shall rule with great dominion, and do according to his will.

When he shall stand up, his kingdom go be broken, and go be divided toward the four winds of the sky, but not to his posterity, nor according to his dominion with which he ruled; for his kingdom go be plucked up, even for others besides these.
The king of the south go be strong, and one of his princes; and he go be strong above him, and have dominion; his dominion go be a great dominion.

At the end of years dem shall join themselves together; and the daughter of the king of the south shall come to the king of the north to make an agreement: but she no go retain the strength of her arm; neither shall he stand, nor his arm; but she go be given up, and people wey bring her, and person wey became the father of her, and person wey strengthened her in those times.

But out of a shoot from her roots shall one stand up in his place, who shall come to the army, and shall enter into the fortress of the king of the north, and shall deal against dem, and shall prevail.
Also dem gods, with dem molten images, and with dem goodly vessels of silver and of gold, shall he carry captive into Egypt; and he shall refrain some years from the king of the north.
He shall come into the realm of the king of the south, but he shall return into his own land.
His sons shall war, and shall assemble a plenty people of great forces, which shall come on, and overflow, and pass through; and dem shall return and war, even to his fortress.

The king of the south go be moved with anger, and shall come out and fight with him, even with the king of the north; and he shall send out Plenty people, and the plenty people go be given into his hand.
The plenty people go be lifted up, and his heart go be exalted; and he shall throw down tens of thousands, but he no go prevail.
The king of the north shall return, and shall send out a plenty people greater than the former; and he shall come on at the end of the times, even of years, with a great army and with much substance.
In those times there shall many stand up against the king of the south: also the pikin dem of the violent among una people shall lift themselves up to establish the vision; but dem shall fall.

So the king of the north shall come, and throw up a mound, and take a well-fortified city: and the forces of the south no go stand, neither his chosen people, neither shall there be any strength to stand.
But person wey comes against him shall do according to his own will, and Nobody shall stand before him; and he shall stand in the glorious land, and in his hand go be destruction.

He shall set his face to come with the strength of his whole kingdom, and with him equitable conditions; and he shall perform dem: and he shall give him the daughter of women, to corrupt her; but she no go stand, neither be for him.
After this shall he turn his face to the islands, and shall take many: but a prince shall cause the reproach offered by him to cease; yes, moreover, he shall cause his reproach to turn on him.
Then he shall turn his face toward the fortresses of his own land; but he shall stumble and fall, and no go be find.
Then shall stand up in his place one who shall cause a tax collector to pass through the kingdom to maintain its glory; but within few days he go be destroyed, neither in anger, nor in battle.
In his place shall stand up a contemptible person, to whom dem had not given the honor of the kingdom: but he shall come in time of security, and shall obtain the kingdom by flatteries.
The overwhelming forces go be overwhelmed from before him, and go be broken; yes, also the prince of the covenant.
After the treaty made with him he shall work deceitfully; for he shall come up, and shall become strong, with a small people.

In time of security shall he come even on the fattest places of the province; and he shall do that which his fathers have not done, nor his fathers’ fathers; he shall scatter among dem prey, and plunder, and substance: yes, he shall devise his devices against the strongholds, even for a time.

He shall stir up his power and his courage against the king of the south with a great army; and the king of the south shall war in battle with an exceeding great and mighty army; but he no go stand; for dem shall devise devices against him.
Yes, dem who eat of his dainties shall destroy him, and his army shall overflow; and many shall fall down slain.
As for both these kings, dem hearts go be to do mischief, and dem shall speak lies at one table: but it no go prosper; for yet the end go be at the time appointed.
Then he will return into his land with great substance; and his heart Go be against the holy covenant; and he will take action, and return to his own land.
At the time appointed he shall return, and come into the south; but it no go be in the latter time as it was in the former.

For ships of Kittim shall come against him; so he go be grieved, and shall return, and have indignation against the holy covenant, and shall take action: he shall even return, and have regard to people wey forsake the holy covenant.
Forces shall stand on his part, and dem shall profane the sanctuary, even the fortress, and shall take away the continual burnt offering, and dem shall set up the abomination that makes desolate.
Such as do wickedly against the covenant shall he pervert by flatteries; but the people who know dem God go be strong, and take action.
People Wey wise among the people shall instruct many; yet dem shall fall by the sword and by flame, by captivity and by plunder, many days.
Now when dem shall fall, dem go be helped with a little help; but many shall join themselves to dem with flatteries.
Some of people Wey wise shall fall, to refine dem, and to purify, and to make dem white, even to the time of the end; because it is yet for the time appointed.

The king shall do according to his will; and he shall exalt imself, and magnify imself above every god, and shall speak marvelous things against the God of gods; and he shall prosper until the indignation be accomplished; for that which is determined go be done.
Neither shall he regard the gods of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor regard any god; for he shall magnify imself above all.
But in his place shall he honor the god of fortresses; and a god whom his fathers didn’t know shall he honor with gold, and silver, and with precious stones, and pleasant things.

He shall deal with the strongest fortresses by the help of a foreign god: Anybody wey acknowledges him he will increase with glory; and he shall cause dem to rule over many, and shall divide the land for a price.

At the time of the end shall the king of the south contend with him; and the king of the north shall come against him like a whirlwind, with chariots, and with horsemen, and with many ships; and he shall enter into the countries, and shall overflow and pass through.
He shall enter also into the glorious land, and many countries go be overthrown; but these go be delivered out of his hand: Edom, and Moab, and the chief of the pikin dem of Ammon.
He shall stretch out his hand also on the countries; and the land of Egypt no go escape.
But he go get power over the treasures of gold and of silver, and over all the precious things of Egypt; and the Libyans and the Ethiopians go be at his steps.
But news out of the east and out of the north shall trouble him; and he shall go out with great fury to destroy and utterly to sweep away many.
He shall plant the tents of his palace between the sea and the glorious holy mountain; yet he shall come to his end, and Nobody shall help him.

“At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the pikin dem of una people; and there go be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time una people go be delivered, Everybody wey go be find written in the book.
Many of people wey sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to life wey no dey end, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
People Wey wise shall shine as the brightness of the expanse; and people wey turn many to righteousness as the stars forever and ever.
But you, Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run back and forth, and knowledge go be increased.”
Then I, Daniel, looked, and see am, two others stood, one on the river bank on this side, and the other on the river bank on that side.
One talk say to the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?

I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand to heaven, and swore by him who lives forever that it go be for a time, times, and a half; and when dem have finished breaking in pieces the power of the holy people, all these things go be finished.
I heard, but I didn’t understand: then I talk say, my lord, what go be the issue of these things?
He talk say, Go una way, Daniel; for the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end.
Many shall purify themselves, and make themselves white, and be refined; but the wicked shall do wickedly; and none of the wicked shall understand; but people Wey wise shall understand.
From the time that the continual burnt offering go be taken away, and the abomination that makes desolate set up, there go be one thousand two hundred ninety days.
Blessed is person wey waits, and comes to the one thousand three hundred thirty-five days.
But go you una way until the end; for you shall rest, and shall stand in una lot, at the end of the days.
Baba God’s word that come to Hosea the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.

When Baba God spoke at first by Hosea, Baba God talk say to Hosea, “Go, take for yourself a wife of prostitution and pikin dem of unfaithfulness; for the land commits great adultery, forsaking Baba God.”
So he go and take Gomer the daughter of Diblaim; and she conceived, and bore him a son.
Baba God talk say to him, “Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I go avenge the blood of Jezreel on the house of Jehu, and will cause the kingdom of the house of Israel to cease.
It will happen in that day that I go break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel.”
She conceived again, and bore a daughter. Then E tell am say, “Call her name Lo-Ruhamah; for I go no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, that I should in any way pardon dem.
But I go have mercy on the house of Judah, and will save dem by Baba God dem God, and No go save dem by bow, sword, battle, horses, or horsemen.”
Now when she had weaned Lo-Ruhamah, she conceived, and bore a son.
He talk say, “Call his name Lo-Ammi; for you No be my people, and I go not be yours.

Yet the number of the pikin dem of Israel Go be as the sand of the sea, which no fit be measured or counted; and it will come to pass that, in the place where it was talk say to dem, ‘You No be my people,’ Dem go be call ‘sons of the living God.’
The pikin dem of Judah and the pikin dem of Israel Go be gathered together, and Dem go appoint themselves one head, and will go up from the land; for great Go be the day of Jezreel.
“Say to una brothers, ‘My people!’ and to una sisters, ‘My love one!’
Contend with una mother! Contend, for she No be my wife, neither am I her husband; and Make she put away her prostitution from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts;
Lest I strip her naked, and make her bare as in the day that she was born, and make her like a wilderness, and set her like a dry land, and kill her with thirst.
Indeed, on her pikin dem I go have no mercy; for Dem be pikin dem of unfaithfulness;

For dem mother has played the prostitute. Person wey conceived dem has done shamefully; for she talk say, ‘I go go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink.’
So see am, I go hedge up una way with thorns, and I go build a wall against her, that she no fit find her way.

She will follow after her lovers, but she no go overtake dem; and she will seek dem, but no go find dem. Then she will say, ‘I go go and return to my first husband; for then was it better with me than now.’
For she No know that I give her the grain, the new wine, and the oil, and multiplied to her silver and gold, which dem used for Baal.
So I go take back my grain in its time, and my new wine in its season, and will pluck away my wool and my flax which should have covered her nakedness.
Now I go uncover her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and Nobody will deliver her out of my hand.
I go also cause all her celebrations to cease: her feasts, her new moons, her Sabbaths, and all her solemn assemblies.
I go lay waste her vines and her fig trees, about which she has talk say, ‘These are my wages that my lovers have given me; and I go make dem a forest,’ and the animals of the field shall eat dem.
I go visit on her the days of the Baals, to which she burned incense, when she decked sheself with her earrings and her jewels, and go after her lovers, and forgot me,” says Baba God.
“So see am, I go allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak tenderly to her.
I go give her vineyards from there, and the valley of Achor for a door of hope; and she will respond there, as in the days of her youth, and as in the day when she come up out of the land of Egypt.
It Go be in that day,” says Baba God, “that You go call me ‘my husband,’ and no longer call me ‘my master.’
For I go take away the names of the Baals out of her mouth, and Dem go no longer be mentioned by name.

In that day I go make a covenant for dem with the animals of the field, and with the birds of the sky, and with the creeping things of the ground. I go break the bow, the sword, and the battle out of the land, and will make dem lie down safely.
I go betroth you to me forever. Yes, I go betroth you to me in righteousness, in justice, in loving kindness, and in compassion.
I go even betroth you to me in faithfulness; and you shall know Baba God.
It will happen in that day, I go respond,” says Baba God, “I go respond to the heavens, and Dem go respond to the earth;
and the earth will respond to the grain, and the new wine, and the oil; and Dem go respond to Jezreel.
I go sow her to me in the earth; and I go have mercy on her who had not obtained mercy; and I go tell people wey No be my people, ‘You be my people;’ and Dem go say, ‘My God!’”
Baba God talk say to me, “Go again, love a woman love by another, and an adulteress, even as Baba God loves the pikin dem of Israel, though dem turn to other gods, and love cakes of raisins.”
So I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver and a homer and a half of barley.
I talk say to her, “You shall stay with me many days. You no go play the prostitute, and you no go be with any other man. I go also be so toward you.”
For the pikin dem of Israel shall live many days without king, and without prince, and without sacrifice, and without sacred stone, and without ephod or idols.
Afterward the pikin dem of Israel shall return, and seek Baba God dem God, and David dem king, and shall come with trembling to Baba God and to his blessings in the last days.
Hear Baba God’s word, you pikin dem of Israel; for Baba God has a charge against the inhabitants of the land: “Indeed E get no truth, nor goodness, nor knowledge of God in the land.
E get cursing, lying, murder, stealing, and committing adultery; dem break boundaries, and bloodshed causes bloodshed.
So the land will mourn, and Everybody wey dwells inside am will waste away. all living things in her, even the animals of the field and the birds of the sky; yes, the fish of the sea also die.
“Yet let no man bring a charge, neither let any man accuse; For una people are like people wey bring charges against a priest.
You go stumble in the day, and the prophet will also stumble with you in the night; and I go destroy una mother.

My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I go also reject you, that you may be no priest to me. Because you have forgotten una God’s law, I go also forget una pikin dem.
As dem were multiplied, so dem sinned against me. I go change dem glory into shame.
Dem feed on the sin of my people, and set dem heart on dem wickedness.
It Go be, like people, like priest; and I go punish dem for dem ways, and will repay dem for dem deeds.
Dem go eat, and not have enough. Dem go play the prostitute, and No go increase; because dem have abandoned giving to Baba God.
Prostitution, wine, and new wine take away understanding.
My people consult with dem wooden idol, and answer to a stick of wood. Indeed the spirit of prostitution has led dem astray, and dem Don dey unfaithful to dem God.

Dem sacrifice on the tops of the mountains, and burn incense on the hills, under oaks and poplars and terebinths, because its shade is good. So una daughters play the prostitute, and una brides commit adultery.

I go not punish una daughters when dem play the prostitute, nor una brides when dem commit adultery; because the men consort with prostitutes, and dem sacrifice with the shrine prostitutes; so the people without understanding will come to ruin.
“Though you, Israel, play the prostitute, yet no let Judah offend; and no come to Gilgal, neither go up to Beth Aven, nor swear, ‘As Baba God lives.’
For Israel has behaved extremely stubbornly, like a stubborn heifer. Then how will Baba God feed dem like a lamb in a meadow.
Ephraim is joined to idols. Leave him alone!
Dem drink has become sour. Dem play the prostitute continually. Her rulers dearly love dem shameful way.
The wind has wrapped her up in its wings; and dem go be disappointed because of dem sacrifices.
“Listen to this, you priests! Listen, house of Israel, and give ear, house of the king! For the judgment is against you; for you Don dey a snare at Mizpah, and a net spread on Tabor.
The rebels are deep in slaughter; but I discipline all of dem.
I know Ephraim, and Israel No be hidden from me; for now, Ephraim, you have played the prostitute. Israel is defiled.
Dem deeds no go allow dem to turn to dem God; for the spirit of prostitution is within dem, and dem no know Baba God.
The pride of Israel testifies to his face. So Israel and Ephraim will stumble in dem wickedness. Judah also will stumble with dem.
Dem go go with dem flocks and with dem herds to seek Baba God; but dem no go find him. He has withdrawn imself from dem.
Dem be unfaithful to Baba God; for dem have borne illegitimate pikin dem. Now the new moon will devour dem with dem fields.
“Blow the cornet in Gibeah, and the trumpet in Ramah! Sound a battle cry at Beth Aven, behind you, Benjamin!
Ephraim will become a desolation in the day of rebuke. Among the tribes of Israel, I have made known that which will surely be.
The princes of Judah are like people wey remove a landmark. I go pour out my serious anger on dem like water.
Ephraim is oppressed, he is crushed in judgment; Because he is intent in his pursuit of idols.
So I be to Ephraim like a moth, and to the house of Judah like rottenness.
“When Ephraim see his sickness, and Judah his wound, Then Ephraim go to Assyria, and sent to king Jareb: but he No be able to heal you, neither will he cure you of una wound.
For I go be to Ephraim like a lion, and like a young lion to the house of Judah. I myself will tear in pieces and go away. I go carry off, and there Go be Nobody to deliver.
I go go and return to my place, until dem acknowledge dem offense, and seek my face. In dem suffering Dem go seek me earnestly.”
“Come, and Make we return to Baba God; for he has torn us to pieces, and he will heal us; he has injured us, and he will bind up our wounds.
After two days he will revive us. On the third day he will raise us up, and We go live before him.
Make we acknowledge Baba God. Make we press on to know Baba God. As surely as the sun rises, Baba God will appear. He will come to us like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth.”
“Ephraim, what shall I do to you? Judah, what shall I do to you? For una love is like a morning cloud, and like the dew that disappears early.
So I have cut dem to pieces with the prophets; I killed dem with the words of my mouth. Una judgments are like a flash of lightning.
For I desire mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
But dem, like Adam, have broken the covenant. Dem were unfaithful to me, there.
Gilead is a city of people wey work wickedness; it is stained with blood.
As gangs of robbers wait to ambush a man, so the company of priests murder on the path toward Shechem, committing shameful crimes.
In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing. E get prostitution in Ephraim. Israel is defiled.
“Also, Judah, E get a harvest appointed for you, when I restore the fortunes of my people.
When I would heal Israel, then the wickedness of Ephraim is uncovered, also the wickedness of Samaria; for dem commit falsehood, and the thief enters in, and the gang of robbers ravages outside.
Dem no consider in dem hearts that I remember all dem wickedness. Now dem own deeds have engulfed dem. Dem be before my face.
Dem make the king glad with dem wickedness, and the princes with dem lies.
Dem be all adulterers. Dem be burning like an oven that the baker stops stirring, from the kneading of the dough, until it is leavened.
On the day of our king, the princes made themselves sick with the heat of wine. He joined his hand with mockers.
For dem have prepared dem heart like an oven, while dem lie in wait. Dem baker sleeps all the night. In the morning it burns as a flaming fire.
Dem be all hot as an oven, and devour dem judges. All dem kings have fallen. E get Nobody among dem who calls to me.
Ephraim, he mixes imself among the nations. Ephraim is a pancake not turned over.
Strangers have devoured his strength, and he no dey realize it. Indeed, gray hairs are here and there on him, and he no dey realize it.
The pride of Israel testifies to his face; yet dem haven’t come back to Baba God dem God, nor sought him, for all this.
“Ephraim is like an easily deceived dove, without understanding. Dem call to Egypt. Dem go to Assyria.
When dem go, I go spread my net on dem. I go bring dem down like the birds of the sky. I go chastise dem, as dem congregation has heard.
Woe to dem! For dem have wandered from me. Destruction to dem! For dem have trespassed against me. Though I would redeem dem, yet dem have spoken lies against me.
Dem haven’t cried to me with dem heart, but dem howl on dem beds. Dem assemble themselves for grain and new wine. Dem turn away from me.
Though I have taught and strengthened dem arms, yet dem plot evil against me.
Dem return, but not to the Most High. Dem be like a faulty bow. Dem princes will fall by the sword for the rage of dem tongue. This Go be dem derision in the land of Egypt.
“Put the trumpet to una lips! Something like an eagle is over Baba God’s house, because dem have broken my covenant, and rebelled against my law.
Dem cry to me, ‘My God, we Israel acknowledge you!’
Israel has throw off that which is good. The enemy will pursue him.
Dem have set up kings, but not by me. Dem have made princes, and I didn’t approve. Of dem silver and dem gold dem have made themselves idols, that dem may be cut off.
Let Samaria throw out his calf idol! My anger burns against dem! How long will it be until Dem be capable of purity?
For this is even from Israel! The workman made it, and it is no God; indeed, the calf of Samaria go be broken in pieces.
For dem sow the wind, and Dem go reap the whirlwind. He has no standing grain. The stalk will yield no head. If it does yield, strangers will swallow it up.
Israel is swallowed up. Now Dem be among the nations like a worthless thing.
For dem have gone up to Assyria, like a wild donkey wandering alone. Ephraim has hired lovers for imself.
But although dem sold themselves among the nations, I go now gather dem; and dem begin to waste away because of the oppression of the king of mighty ones.
Because Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning, dem became for him altars for sinning.
I wrote for him the many things of my law; but dem were regarded as a strange thing.
As for the sacrifices of my offerings, dem sacrifice meat and eat it; But Baba God no dey accept dem. Now he will remember dem wickedness, and punish dem sins. Dem go return to Egypt.
For Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces; and Judah has multiplied fortified cities; but I go send a fire on his cities, and it will devour its fortresses.”
No glad well-well, Israel, to jubilation like the nations; for you were unfaithful to una God. You love the wages of a prostitute at every grain threshing floor.
The threshing floor and the wine press no go feed dem, and the new wine will fail her.
Dem no go live in Baba God’s land; but Ephraim will return to Egypt, and Dem go eat unclean chop in Assyria.

Dem no go pour out wine offerings to Baba God, neither will dem be pleasing to him. Dem sacrifices Go be to dem like the bread of mourners; all who eat of it Go be polluted; for dem bread Go be for dem appetite. It No go come into Baba God’s house.
What will you do in the day of solemn assembly, and in the day of the feast of Baba God?
For, see am, dem have gone away from destruction. Egypt will gather dem up. Memphis will bury dem. Nettles will possess dem pleasant things of silver. Thorns Go be in dem tents.

The days of visitation have come. The days of reckoning have come. Israel will consider the prophet to be a fool, and the man Wey be inspired to be insane, because of the abundance of una sins, and because una hostility is great.
A prophet watches over Ephraim with my God. A fowler’s snare is on all of his paths, and hostility in the house of his God.
Dem have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah. He will remember dem wickedness. He will punish dem for dem sins.

I find Israel like grapes in the wilderness. I see una fathers as the first ripe in the fig tree at its first season; but dem come to Baal Peor, and consecrated themselves to the shameful thing, and became abominable like that which dem love.
As for Ephraim, dem glory will fly away like a bird. There Go be no birth, Nobody with pikin, and no conception.
Though dem bring up dem pikin dem, yet I go bereave dem, so that not a man go be left. Indeed, woe also to dem when I depart from dem!
I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre, planted in a pleasant place; but Ephraim will bring out his pikin dem to the murderer.
Give dem — Baba God what will you give? Give dem a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.
“All dem wickedness is in Gilgal; for there I hated dem. Because of the wickedness of dem deeds I go drive dem out of my house! I go love dem no more. All dem princes are rebels.
Ephraim is struck. Dem root has dried up. Dem go bear no fruit. Even though dem give birth, yet I go kill the beloved ones of dem womb.”
My God will throw dem away, because dem No listen to him; and Dem go be wanderers among the nations.
Israel is a luxuriant vine that produces his fruit. According to the abundance of his fruit he has multiplied his altars. As dem land has prospered, dem have adorned dem sacred stones.
Dem heart is divided. Now Dem go be find guilty. He will demolish dem altars. He will destroy dem sacred stones.
Surely now Dem go say, “We have no king; for we no fear Baba God; and the king, what can he do for us?”
Dem make promises, swearing falsely in making covenants. So judgment springs up like poisonous weeds in the furrows of the field.
The inhabitants of Samaria Go be in terror for the calves of Beth Aven; for its people will mourn over it, Along with its priests who rejoiced over it, for its glory, because it has comot from it.
It also Go be carried to Assyria for a present to a great king. Ephraim will receive shame, and Israel Go be ashamed of his own counsel.
Samaria and her king float away, like a twig on the water.
The high places also of Aven, the sin of Israel, Go be destroyed. The thorn and the thistle will come up on dem altars. Dem go tell the mountains, “Cover us!” and the hills, “Fall on us!”
“Israel, you have sinned from the days of Gibeah. There dem remain. The battle against the pikin dem of wickedness no dey overtake dem in Gibeah.
When it is my desire, I go chastise dem; and the nations Go be gathered against dem, when Dem be bound to dem two wrongdoings.
Ephraim is a trained heifer that loves to thresh; so I go put a yoke on her beautiful neck. I go set a rider on Ephraim. Judah will plow. Jacob will break his clods.
Sow to unaself in righteousness, reap according to kindness. Break up una fallow ground; for it is time to seek Baba God, until he comes and rains righteousness on you.
You have plowed wickedness. You have reaped wickedness. You have eaten the fruit of lies, for you trusted in una way, in the plenty people of una mighty men.
So a battle roar will arise among una people, and all una fortresses Go be destroyed, as Shalman destroyed Beth Arbel in the day of battle. The mother was dashed in pieces with her pikin dem.
So Bethel will do to you because of una great wickedness. At daybreak the king of Israel Go be destroyed.
“When Israel was a pikin, then I love him, and call my son out of Egypt.
Dem call to dem, so dem go from dem. Dem sacrificed to the Baals, and burned incense to engraved images.
Yet I taught Ephraim to walk. I take dem by his arms; but dem didn’t know that I healed dem.
I drew dem with cords of a man, with ties of love; and I was to dem like people wey lift up the yoke on dem necks; and I bent down to him and I fed him.
“Dem no go return into the land of Egypt; but the Assyrian Go be dem king, because dem refused to repent.
The sword will fall on dem cities, and will destroy the bars of dem gates, and will put an end to dem plans.
My people are determined to turn from me. Though dem call to the Most High, he certainly no go exalt dem.
“How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I make you like Zeboiim? My heart is turned within me, my compassion is aroused.
I go not execute the fierceness of my anger. I go not return to destroy Ephraim: for I be God, and not man; the Holy One among you; and I go not come in serious anger.
Dem go walk after Baba God, who will roar like a lion; for he will roar, and the pikin dem will come trembling from the west.
Dem go come trembling like a bird out of Egypt, and like a dove out of the land of Assyria; and I go settle dem in dem houses,” says Baba God.
Ephraim surrounds me with falsehood, and the house of Israel with deceit. Judah still strays from God, and is unfaithful to the Holy One.
Ephraim feeds on wind, and chases the east wind. He continually multiplies lies and desolation. Dem make a covenant with Assyria, and oil is carried into Egypt.
Baba God also has a controversy with Judah, and will punish Jacob according to his ways; according to his deeds he will repay him.
In the womb he take his brother by the heel; and in his manhood he contended with God.
Indeed, he struggled with the angel, and prevailed; he wept, and made supplication to him. He find him at Bethel, and there he spoke with us,
even Baba God, the God of Armies; Baba God is his name of renown!
So turn to una God. Keep kindness and justice, and wait continually for una God.
A merchant has dishonest scales in his hand. He loves to defraud.
Ephraim talk say, “Surely I have become rich, I have find myself wealth. In all my wealth dem no go find in me any wickedness that is sin.”
“But I be Baba God una God from the land of Egypt. I go yet again make you live in tents, as in the days of the solemn feast.
I have also spoken to the prophets, and I have multiplied visions; and by the ministry of the prophets I have used parables.
If Gilead is wicked, surely Dem be worthless. In Gilgal dem sacrifice bulls. Indeed, dem altars are like heaps in the furrows of the field.
Jacob fled into the country of Aram, and Israel served to get a wife, and for a wife he tended flocks and herds.
By a prophet Baba God bring Israel up out of Egypt, and by a prophet he was preserved.
Ephraim has bitterly provoked anger. So his blood Go be left on him, and his Lord will repay his contempt.
When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling. He exalted imself in Israel, but when he became guilty in Baal, he died.

Now dem sin more and more, and have made themselves molten images of dem silver, even idols according to dem own understanding, all of dem the work of the craftsmen. Dem say of dem, ‘Dem offer human sacrifice and kiss the calves.’
So Dem go be like the morning mist, and like the dew that passes away early, like the chaff that is driven with the whirlwind out of the threshing floor, and like the smoke out of the chimney.
“Yet I be Baba God una God from the land of Egypt; and you shall acknowledge no god but me, and besides me E get no savior.
I know you in the wilderness, in the land of great drought.
According to dem pasture, so were dem filled; dem were filled, and dem heart was exalted. So dem have forgotten me.
So I be like a lion to dem. Like a leopard, I go lurk by the path.
I go meet dem like a bear that is bereaved of her cubs, and will tear the covering of dem heart. There I go devour dem like a lioness. The wild animal will tear dem.
You be destroyed, Israel, because You be against me, against una help.
Where is una king now, that he may save you in all una cities? And una judges, of whom you talk say, ‘Give me a king and princes?’
I have given you a king in my anger, and have taken him away in my serious anger.
The guilt of Ephraim is stored up. His sin is stored up.
The sorrows of a travailing woman will come on him. He is an unwise son; for when it is time, he no dey come to the opening of the womb.
I go ransom dem from the power of Sheol. I go redeem dem from death! Death, where are una plagues? Sheol, where is una destruction? “Compassion Go be hidden from my eyes.

Though he is fruitful among his brothers, an east wind will come, the breath of Baba God coming up from the wilderness; and his spring will become dry, and his fountain Go be dried up. He will plunder the storehouse of treasure.
Samaria will bear her guilt; for she has rebelled against her God. Dem go fall by the sword. Dem infants Go be dashed in pieces, and dem pregnant women Go be ripped open.”
Israel, return to Baba God una God; for you have fallen because of una sin.
Take words with you, and return to Baba God. Tell him, “Forgive all our sins, and accept that which is good: so we offer our lips like bulls.
Assyria no fit save us. We no go ride on horses; neither will we say any more to the work of our hands, ‘Our gods!’ for in you the fatherless finds mercy.”
“I go heal dem waywardness. I go love dem freely; for my anger is turned away from him.
I go be like the dew to Israel. He will blossom like the lily, and send down his roots like Lebanon.
His branches will spread, and his beauty Go be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like Lebanon.
Men will live in his shade. Dem go revive like the grain, and blossom like the vine. Dem fragrance Go be like the wine of Lebanon.
Ephraim, what have I to do any more with idols? I answer, and will take care of him. I be like a green cypress tree; from me una fruit is find.”
Wey be wise, that he may understand these things? Wey be prudent, that he may know dem? For the ways of Baba God are right, and the righteous walk in dem; But the rebellious stumble in dem.
Baba God’s word that come to Joel, the son of Pethuel.
Hear this, you elders, And listen, all you inhabitants of the land. Has this ever happened in una days, or in the days of una fathers?
Tell una pikin dem about it, and have una pikin dem tell dem pikin dem, and dem pikin dem, another generation.
What the swarming locust has left, the great locust has eaten. What the great locust has left, the grasshopper has eaten. What the grasshopper has left, the caterpillar has eaten.
Wake up, you drunkards, and weep! Wail, all you drinkers of wine, because of the sweet wine; for it is cut off from una mouth.
For a nation has come up on my land, strong, and without number. His teeth are the teeth of a lion, and he has the fangs of a lioness.
He has laid my vine waste, and stripped my fig tree. He has stripped its bark, and thrown it away. Its branches are made white.
Mourn like a virgin dressed in sackcloth for the husband of her youth!
The meal offering and the drink offering are cut off from Baba God’s house. The priests, Baba God’s ministers, mourn.
The field is laid waste. The land mourns, for the grain is destroyed, The new wine has dried up, and the oil languishes.
Be confounded, you farmers! Wail, you vineyard keepers; for the wheat and for the barley; for the harvest of the field has perished.

The vine has dried up, and the fig tree withered; the pomegranate tree, the palm tree also, and the apple tree, even all of the trees of the field are withered; for gladness has withered away from the sons of men.

Put on sackcloth and mourn, you priests! Wail, you ministers of the altar. Come, lie all night in sackcloth, you ministers of my God, for the meal offering and the drink offering are withheld from una God’s house.
Sanctify a fast. Call a solemn assembly. Gather the elders, and all the inhabitants of the land, to the house of Baba God, una God, and cry to Baba God.
Alas for the day! For the day of Baba God is at hand, and it will come as destruction from the Almighty.
No be the chop cut off before our eyes; gladness and gladness from the house of our God?
The seeds rot under dem clods. The granaries are laid desolate. The barns are broken down, for the grain has withered.
How the animals groan! The herds of livestock are perplexed, because dem have no pasture. Yes, the flocks of sheep are made desolate.
Baba God, I cry to you, For the fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and the flame has burned all the trees of the field.
Yes, the animals of the field pant to you, for the water brooks have dried up, And the fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness.
Blow the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain! Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of Baba God comes, for it is close at hand:

A day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness. As the dawn spreading on the mountains, a great and strong people; there has never been the like, neither will there be any more after dem, even to the years of many generations.
A fire devours before dem, and behind dem, a flame burns. The land is as the garden of Eden before dem, and behind dem, a desolate wilderness. Yes, and Nobody has escaped dem.
Dem appearance is as the appearance of horses, and as horsemen, so do dem run.
Like the noise of chariots on the tops of the mountains do dem leap, like the noise of a flame of fire that devours the stubble, as a strong people set in battle array.
At dem presence the peoples are in anguish. All faces have grown pale.
Dem run like mighty men. Dem climb the wall like warriors. Dem each march in his line, and dem no swerve off course.
Neither does one jostle another; dem march everyone in his path, and dem burst through the defenses, and no break ranks.
Dem rush on the city. Dem run on the wall. Dem climb up into the houses. Dem enter in at the windows like thieves.
The earth quakes before dem. The heavens tremble. The sun and the moon are darkened, and the stars withdraw dem shining.
Baba God thunders his voice before his army; for his forces are plenty well-well; for he is strong who obeys his command; for the day of Baba God is great and very awesome, and who can endure it?
“Yet even now,” says Baba God, “turn to me with all una heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning.”
Tear una heart, and not una garments, and turn to Baba God, una God; for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and relents from sending calamity.
Wey know? He may turn and relent, and leave a blessing behind him, even a meal offering and a drink offering to Baba God, una God.
Blow the trumpet in Zion! Sanctify a fast. Call a solemn assembly.
Gather the people. Sanctify the assembly. Assemble the elders. Gather the pikin dem, and people wey nurse from breasts. Let the bridegroom go out of his room, and the bride out of her room.

Let the priests, the ministers of Baba God, weep between the porch and the altar, and Make dem say, “Spare una people, Baba God, and no give una heritage to reproach, that the nations should rule over dem. Why should dem say among the peoples, ‘Where is dem God?’”
Then Baba God was jealous for his land, And had pity on his people.
Baba God answer his people, “See am, I go send you grain, new wine, and oil, and You go be satisfied with dem; and I go no more make you a reproach among the nations.

But I go remove the northern army far away from you, and will drive it into a barren and desolate land, its front into the eastern sea, and its back into the western sea; and its stench will come up, and its bad smell will rise.” Surely he has done great things.
Land, No fear. Be glad and glad well-well, for Baba God has done great things.
No fear, you animals of the field; for the pastures of the wilderness spring up, for the tree bears its fruit. The fig tree and the vine yield dem strength.

“Be glad then, you pikin dem of Zion, and glad well-well in Baba God, una God; for he gives you the former rain in just measure, and he causes the rain to come down for you, the former rain and the latter rain, as before.
The threshing floors Go be full of wheat, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.
I go restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten, the great locust, the grasshopper, and the caterpillar, my great army, which I sent among you.
You go have plenty to eat, and be satisfied, and will praise the name of Baba God, una God, who has dealt wondrously with you; and my people will never again be disappointed.
You go know that I be among Israel, and that I be Baba God, una God, and E get Nobody else; and my people will never again be disappointed.
“It will happen afterward, that I go pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and una sons and una daughters will prophesy. Una old men will dream dreams. Una young men will see visions.
And also on the workers and on the handmaids in those days, I go pour out my Spirit.
I go show wonders in the heavens and in the earth: blood, fire, and pillars of smoke.
The sun Go be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of Baba God comes.

It will happen that Anybody wey will call on Baba God’s name go be saved; for in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there Go be people wey escape, as Baba God has talk say, and among the remnant, those whom Baba God calls.
“For, see am, in those days, and in that time, when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,

I go gather people for everywhere, and will bring dem down into the valley of Jehoshaphat; and I go execute judgment on dem there for my people, and for my heritage, Israel, whom dem have scattered among the nations. Dem have divided my land,
and have throw lots for my people, and have given a boy for a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine, that dem may drink.
“Yes, and Wetin be you to me, Tyre, and Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia? Will you repay me? And if you repay me, I go swiftly and speedily return una repayment on una own head.
Because you have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried my finest treasures into una temples,
and have sold the pikin dem of Judah and the pikin dem of Jerusalem to the sons of the Greeks, that you may remove dem far from dem border.
See am, I go stir dem up out of the place where you have sold dem, and will return una repayment on una own head;
and I go sell una sons and una daughters into the hands of the pikin dem of Judah, and Dem go sell dem to the men of Sheba, to a faraway nation, for Baba God has spoken it.”
Proclaim this among the nations: “Prepare for war! Stir up the mighty men. Let all the warriors draw near. Make dem come up.
Beat una plowshares into swords, and una pruning hooks into spears. Let the weak say, ‘I be strong.’
Hurry and come, all you surrounding nations, and gather unaself together.” Cause una mighty ones to come down there, Baba God.
“Let the nations arouse themselves, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat; for there will I sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
Put in the sickle; for the harvest is ripe. Come, tread, for the wine press is full, the vats overflow, for dem wickedness is great.”
Plenty people, plenty people in the valley of decision! For the day of Baba God is near, in the valley of decision.
The sun and the moon are darkened, and the stars withdraw dem shining.
Baba God will roar from Zion, and thunder from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth will shake; but Baba God Go be a refuge to his people, and a stronghold to the pikin dem of Israel.
“So You go know that I be Baba God, una God, dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain. Then Jerusalem Go be holy, and no strangers will pass through her any more.

It will happen in that day, that the mountains will drop down sweet wine, the hills will flow with milk, all the brooks of Judah will flow with waters, and a fountain will flow out from Baba God’s house, and will water the valley of Shittim.
Egypt Go be a desolation, and Edom Go be a desolate wilderness, for the violence done to the pikin dem of Judah, because dem have shed innocent blood in dem land.
But Judah Go be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
I go cleanse dem blood, that I have not cleansed: for Baba God dwells in Zion.”

The words of Amos, who was among the herdsmen of Tekoa, which he see concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
He talk say: “Baba God will roar from Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the pastures of the shepherds will mourn, and the top of Carmel will wither.”
Baba God says: “For three wrongdoings of Damascus, yes, for four, I go not turn away its punishment; because dem have threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron;
but I go send a fire into the house of Hazael, and it will devour the palaces of Ben Hadad.

I go break the bar of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitant from the valley of Aven, and him who holds the scepter from the house of Eden; and the people of Syria shall go into captivity to Kir,” says Baba God.
Baba God says: “For three wrongdoings of Gaza, yes, for four, I go not turn away its punishment; because dem carried away captive the whole community, to deliver dem up to Edom;
but I go send a fire on the wall of Gaza, and it will devour its palaces.
I go cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod, and him who holds the scepter from Ashkelon; and I go turn my hand against Ekron; and the remnant of the Philistines will perish,” says the Lord Baba God.
Baba God says: “For three wrongdoings of Tyre, yes, for four, I go not turn away its punishment; because dem delivered up the whole community to Edom, and didn’t remember the brotherly covenant;
but I go send a fire on the wall of Tyre, and it will devour its palaces.”

Baba God says: “For three wrongdoings of Edom, yes, for four, I go not turn away its punishment; because he pursued his brother with the sword, and throw off all pity, and his anger raged continually, and he kept his serious anger forever;
but I go send a fire on Teman, and it will devour the palaces of Bozrah.”

Baba God says: “For three wrongdoings of the pikin dem of Ammon, yes, for four, I go not turn away its punishment; because dem have ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead, that dem may enlarge dem border.
But I go kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it will devour its palaces, with shouting in the day of battle, with a storm in the day of the whirlwind;
and dem king will go into captivity, he and his princes together,” says Baba God.
Baba God says: “For three wrongdoings of Moab, yes, for four, I go not turn away its punishment; because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime;
but I go send a fire on Moab, and it will devour the palaces of Kerioth; and Moab will die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet;
and I go cut off the judge from among dem, and will kill all its princes with him,” says Baba God.

Baba God says: “For three wrongdoings of Judah, yes, for four, I go not turn away its punishment; because dem have rejected Baba God’s law, and have not kept his statutes, and dem lies have led dem astray, after which dem fathers walked;
But I go send a fire on Judah, and it will devour the palaces of Jerusalem.”
Baba God says: “For three wrongdoings of Israel, yes, for four, I go not turn away its punishment; because dem have sold the righteous for silver, and the needy for a pair of shoes;
Dem trample on the dust of the earth on the head of the poor, and deny justice to the oppressed; and a man and his father use the same maiden, to profane my holy name;
and dem lay themselves down beside every altar on clothes taken in pledge; and in the house of dem God dem drink the wine of people wey Don dey fined.
Yet I destroyed the Amorite before dem, whose height was like the height of the cedars, and he was strong as the oaks; yet I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots from beneath.
Also I bring you up out of the land of Egypt, and led you forty years in the wilderness, to possess the land of the Amorite.
I raised up some of una sons for prophets, and some of una young men for Nazirites. No be this true, you pikin dem of Israel?” says Baba God.
“But you give the Nazirites wine to drink, and commanded the prophets, saying, ‘No prophesy!’
See am, I go crush you in una place, as a cart crushes that is full of grain.
Flight will perish from the swift; and the strong no go strengthen his force; neither shall the mighty deliver imself;
neither shall he stand who handles the bow; and person Wey swift of foot no go escape; neither shall person wey rides the horse deliver imself;
and person Wey courageous among the mighty will flee away naked on that day,” says Baba God.
Hear this word that Baba God has spoken against you, pikin dem of Israel, against the whole family which I bring up out of the land of Egypt, saying:
“I have only chosen you of all the families of the earth. So I go punish you for all of una sins.”
Do two walk together, unless dem have agreed?
Will a lion roar in the thicket, when he has no prey? Does a young lion cry out of his den, if he has caught nothing?
Can a bird fall in a trap on the earth, where no snare is set for him? Does a snare spring up from the ground, when E get nothing to catch?
Does the trumpet alarm sound in a city, without the people being afraid? Does evil happen to a city, and Baba God hasn’t done it?
Surely the Lord Baba God will do nothing, unless he reveals his secret to his workers the prophets.
The lion has roared. Who No go fear? The Lord Baba God has spoken. Who can but prophesy?
Proclaim in the palaces at Ashdod, and in the palaces in the land of Egypt, and say, “Assemble unaself on the mountains of Samaria, and see what unrest is in her, and what oppression is among dem.”
“Indeed dem no know to do right,” says Baba God, “Who hoard plunder and loot in dem palaces.”
So thus says the Lord Baba God: “An adversary will overrun the land; and he will pull down una strongholds, and una fortresses Go be plundered.”

Baba God says: “As the shepherd rescues out of the mouth of the lion two legs, or a piece of an ear, so shall the pikin dem of Israel be rescued who sit in Samaria on the corner of a couch, and on the silken cushions of a bed.”
“Listen, and testify against the house of Jacob,” says the Lord Baba God, the God of Armies.
“For in the day that I visit the wrongdoings of Israel on him, I go also visit the altars of Bethel; and the horns of the altar Go be cut off, and fall to the ground.
I go strike the winter house with the summer house; and the houses of ivory will perish, and the great houses Go get an end,” says Baba God.
Listen to this word, you cows of Bashan, Wey be on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor, who crush the needy, who tell dem husbands, “Bring us drinks!”
The Lord Baba God has sworn by his holiness that see am, “The days shall come on you that Dem go take you away with hooks, and the last of you with fish hooks.
You go go out at the breaks in the wall, everyone straight before her; and You go throw unaself into Harmon,” says Baba God.
“Go to Bethel, and sin; to Gilgal, and sin more. Bring una sacrifices every morning, una tithes every three days,
offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving of that which is leavened, and proclaim free will offerings and brag about dem: for this pleases you, you pikin dem of Israel,” says the Lord Baba God.
“I also have given you cleanness of teeth in all una cities, and lack of bread in every town; yet you haven’t come back to me,” says Baba God.

“I also have withheld the rain from you, when there were yet three months to the harvest; and I caused it to rain on one city, and caused it not to rain on another city. One place was rained on, and the piece where it didn’t rain withered.
So two or three cities staggered to one city to drink water, and No be satisfied: yet you haven’t come back to me,” says Baba God.

“I struck you with blight and mildew many times in una gardens and una vineyards; and una fig trees and una olive trees have the swarming locust devoured: yet you haven’t come back to me,” says Baba God.

“I sent plagues among you like I did Egypt. I have slain una young men with the sword, and have carried away una horses; and I filled una nostrils with the stench of una camp, yet you haven’t come back to me,” says Baba God.
“I have overthrown some of you, as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a burning stick plucked out of the fire; yet you haven’t come back to me,” says Baba God.
“So thus will I do to you, Israel; because I go do this to you, prepare to meet una God, Israel.

For, see am, person wey forms the mountains, and creates the wind, and declares to man Wetin be his thought; who makes the morning darkness, and treads on the high places of the earth: Baba God, the God of Armies, is his name.”
Listen to this word which I take up for a lamentation over you, O house of Israel.
“The virgin of Israel has fallen; She shall rise no more. She is throw down on her land; E get Nobody to raise her up.”
For thus says the Lord Baba God: “The city that go out a thousand go get a hundred left, and that which go out one hundred go get ten left to the house of Israel.”
For Baba God says to the house of Israel: “Seek me, and You go live;
but no seek Bethel, nor enter into Gilgal, and no pass to Beersheba: for Gilgal shall surely go into captivity, and Bethel shall come to nothing.
Seek Baba God, and You go live; lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph, and it devour, and there be Nobody to quench it in Bethel.
You who turn justice to wormwood, and throw down righteousness to the earth:

seek him who made the Pleiades and Orion, and turns the shadow of death into the morning, and makes the day dark with night; who calls for the waters of the sea, and pours dem out on the surface of the earth, Baba God is his name,
who brings sudden destruction on the strong, so that destruction comes on the fortress.
Dem hate him who reproves in the gate, and dem abhor him who speaks blamelessly.

So, because you trample on the poor, and take taxes from him of wheat: You have built houses of cut stone, but You go not live in dem. You have planted pleasant vineyards, but you no go drink dem wine.
For I know how many una offenses, and how great are una sins — you who afflict the just, who take a bribe, and who turn aside the needy in the courts.
So a prudent person keeps silent in such a time, for it is an evil time.
Seek good, and not evil, that you may live; and so Baba God, the God of Armies, Go be with you, as you say.
Hate evil, love good, and establish justice in the courts. It may be that Baba God, the God of Armies, Go be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.”

So Baba God, the God of Armies, the Lord, says: “Wailing Go be in all the wide ways; and Dem go say in all the streets, ‘Alas! Alas!’ and Dem go call the farmer to mourning, and people Wey skillful in lamentation to wailing.
In all vineyards there Go be wailing; for I go pass through the middle of you,” says Baba God.
“Woe to you who desire the day of Baba God! Why do you long for the day of Baba God? It is darkness, and not light.
As if a man fled from a lion, and a bear met him; Or he go into the house and leaned his hand on the wall, and a snake bit him.
No go the day of Baba God be darkness, and not light? Even very dark, and no brightness in it?
I hate, I despise una feasts, and I no fit stand una solemn assemblies.
Yes, though you offer me una burnt offerings and meal offerings, I go not accept dem; neither will I regard the peace offerings of una fat animals.
Take away from me the noise of una songs! I go not listen to the music of una harps.
But let justice roll on like rivers, and righteousness like a mighty stream.
“Did you bring to me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness forty years, house of Israel?
You also carried the tent of una king and the shrine of una images, the star of una god, which you made for unaself.
So will I cause you to go into captivity beyond Damascus,” says Baba God, whose name is the God of Armies.
Woe to people Wey at ease in Zion, and to people Wey secure on the mountain of Samaria, the notable men of the chief of the nations, to whom the house of Israel come!
Go to Calneh, and see; and from there go to Hamath the great; then go down to Gath of the Philistines. are dem better than these kingdoms? or is dem border greater than una border?
People wey put far away the evil day, and cause the seat of violence to come near;
Who lie on beds of ivory, and stretch themselves on dem couches, and eat the lambs out of the flock, and the calves out of the middle of the stall;
who strum on the strings of a harp; who invent for themselves instruments of music, like David;
who drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the best oils; but dem No be grieved for the suffering of Joseph.
So Dem go now go captive with the first who go captive; and the feasting and lounging will end.
“The Lord Baba God has sworn by imself,” says Baba God, the God of Armies: “I abhor the pride of Jacob, and detest his fortresses. So I go deliver up the city with all that is in it.
It will happen, if there remain ten men in one house, that dem shall die.

“When a man’s relative carries him, even person wey burns him, to bring bodies out of the house, and asks him Wey be in the innermost parts of the house, ‘Is there yet any with you?’ And he says, ‘No;’ then he will say, ‘Hush! Indeed we must not mention Baba God’s name.’
“For, see am, Baba God commands, and the great house Go be smashed to pieces, and the little house into bits.
Do horses run on the rocky crags? Does one plow there with oxen? But you have turned justice into poison, and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness;
you who glad well-well in a thing of nothing, who say, ‘Haven’t we taken for ourselves horns by our own strength?’
For, see am, I go raise up against you a nation, house of Israel,” says Baba God, the God of Armies; “and Dem go afflict you from the entrance of Hamath to the brook of the Arabah.”
Thus the Lord Baba God showed me: and see am, he formed locusts For the beginning of the shooting up of the latter growth; and see am, it was the latter growth after the king’s harvest.
When dem finished eating the grass of the land, then I talk say, “Lord Baba God, forgive, I beg you! How could Jacob stand? For he is small.”
Baba God relented concerning this. “It no go be,” says Baba God.
Thus the Lord Baba God showed me and see am, the Lord Baba God call for judgment by fire; and it dried up the great deep, and would have devoured the land.
Then I talk say, “Lord Baba God, stop, I beg you! How could Jacob stand? For he is small.”
Baba God relented concerning this. “This also no go be,” says the Lord Baba God.
Thus he showed me and see am, the Lord stood beside a wall made by a plumb line, with a plumb line in his hand.

Baba God talk say to me, “Amos, what do you see?” I talk say, “A plumb line.” Then the Lord talk say, “See am, I go set a plumb line in the middle of my people Israel. I go not again pass by dem any more.
The high places of Isaac Go be desolate, the sanctuaries of Israel Go be laid waste; and I go rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.”
Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, “Amos has conspired against you in the middle of the house of Israel. The land No be able to bear all his words.
For Amos says, ‘Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of his land.’”
Amaziah also talk say to Amos, “You seer, go, flee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there:
but no prophesy again any more at Bethel; for it is the king’s sanctuary, and it is a royal house!”
Then Amos answer Amaziah, “I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son; but I was a herdsman, and a farmer of sycamore figs;
and Baba God take me from following the flock, and Baba God talk say to me, ‘Go, prophesy to my people Israel.’
Now so listen to Baba God’s word: ‘You say, No prophesy against Israel, and no preach against the house of Isaac.’

So Baba God says: ‘Una wife go be a prostitute in the city, and una sons and una daughters shall fall by the sword, and una land go be divided by line; and you yourself shall die in a land that is unclean, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of his land.’”
Thus the Lord Baba God showed me: see am, a basket of summer fruit.
He talk say, “Amos, what do you see?” I talk say, “A basket of summer fruit.” Then Baba God talk say to me, “The end has come on my people Israel. I go not again pass by dem any more.
The songs of the temple Go be wailings in that day,” says the Lord Baba God. “The dead bodies Go be many. In every place Dem go throw dem out with silence.
Hear this, you who desire to swallow up the needy, and cause the poor of the land to fail,
Saying, ‘When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell grain? And the Sabbath, that we may market wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel large, and dealing falsely with balances of deceit;
that we may buy the poor for silver, and the needy for a pair of shoes, and sell the sweepings with the wheat?’”
Baba God has sworn by the pride of Jacob, “Surely I go never forget any of dem works.
No go the land tremble for this, and everyone mourn who dwells in it? Yes, it will rise up wholly like the River; and it Go be stirred up and sink again, like the River of Egypt.
It will happen in that day,” says the Lord Baba God, “that I go cause the sun to go down at noon, and I go darken the earth in the clear day.

I go turn una feasts into mourning, and all una songs into lamentation; and I go make you wear sackcloth on all una bodies, and baldness on every head. I go make it like the mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.
See am, the days come,” says the Lord Baba God, “that I go send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing Baba God’s words.
Dem go wander from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east; Dem go run back and forth to seek Baba God’s word, and No go find it.
In that day the beautiful virgins and the young men will faint for thirst.
People wey swear by the sin of Samaria, and say, ‘As una god, Dan, lives;’ and, ‘As the way of Beersheba lives;’ Dem go fall, and never rise up again.”

I see the Lord standing beside the altar, and he talk say, “Strike the tops of the pillars, that the thresholds may shake; and break dem in pieces on the head of all of dem; and I go kill the last of dem with the sword: there no go one of dem flee away, and there no go one of dem escape.
Though dem dig into Sheol, there my hand will take dem; and though dem climb up to heaven, there I go bring dem down.

Though dem hide themselves in the top of Carmel, I go search and take dem out there; and though dem be hidden from my sight in the bottom of the sea, there I go command the serpent, and it will bite dem.
Though dem go into captivity before dem enemies, there I go command the sword, and it will kill dem. I go set my eyes on dem for evil, and not for good.

For the Lord, Baba God of Armies, is person wey touches the land and it melts, and all who live in it will mourn; and it will rise up wholly like the River, and will sink again, like the River of Egypt.

It is person wey builds his rooms in the heavens, and has founded his vault on the earth; person wey calls for the waters of the sea, and pours dem out on the surface of the earth; Baba God is his name.

Are you not like the pikin dem of the Ethiopians to me, pikin dem of Israel?” says Baba God. “Haven’t I bring up Israel out of the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Syrians from Kir?
See am, the eyes of the Lord Baba God are on the sinful kingdom, and I go destroy it from off the surface of the earth; except that I go not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,” says Baba God.
“For, see am, I go command, and I go sift the house of Israel among all the nations, as grain is sifted in a sieve, yet not the least kernel will fall on the earth.
All the sinners of my people will die by the sword, who say, ‘Evil no go overtake nor meet us.’
In that day I go raise up the tent of David Wey be fallen, and close up its breaches, and I go raise up its ruins, and I go build it as in the days of old;
that dem may possess the remnant of Edom, and all the nations Wey be call by my name,” says Baba God wey do this.

“See am, the days come,” says Baba God, “that the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the one treading grapes him who sows seed; and sweet wine will drip from the mountains, and flow from the hills.

I go bring my people Israel back from captivity, and Dem go rebuild the ruined cities, and inhabit dem; and Dem go plant vineyards, and drink wine from dem. Dem shall also make gardens, and eat dem fruit.
I go plant dem on dem land, and Dem go no more be plucked up out of dem land which I have given dem,” says Baba God una God.

The vision of Obadiah. This is what the Lord Baba God says about Edom. We have heard news from Baba God, and an ambassador is sent among the nations, saying, “Arise, and let’s rise up against her in battle.
See am, I have made you small among the nations. You be greatly despised.
The pride of una heart has deceived you, you who live in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high, who says in his heart, ‘Who will bring me down to the ground?’
Though you mount on high as the eagle, and though una nest is set among the stars, I go bring you down from there,” says Baba God.
“If thieves come to you, if robbers by night — oh, what disaster awaits you — wouldn’t dem only steal until dem had enough? If grape pickers come to you, wouldn’t dem leave some gleaning grapes?
How Esau Go be ransacked! How his hidden treasures are sought out!

All the men of una alliance have bring you on una way, even to the border. The men who were at peace with you have deceived you, and prevailed against you. Friends who eat una bread lay a snare under you. E get no understanding in him.”
“No go I in that day”, says Baba God, “destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mountain of Esau?
Una mighty men, Teman, Go be dismayed, to the end that everyone may be cut off from the mountain of Esau by slaughter.
For the violence done to una brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and You go be cut off forever.
In the day that you stood on the other side, in the day that strangers carried away his substance, and foreigners entered into his gates, and throw lots for Jerusalem, even you were like one of dem.
But no look down on una brother in the day of his disaster, and no glad well-well over the pikin dem of Judah in the day of dem destruction. No speak proudly in the day of distress.
No enter into the gate of my people in the day of dem calamity. No look down on dem suffering in the day of dem calamity, neither seize dem wealth on the day of dem calamity.
No stand in the crossroads to cut off those of his who escape. No deliver up those of his who remain in the day of distress.
For the day of Baba God is near all the nations! As you have done, it Go be done to you. Una deeds will return upon una own head.
For as you have drunk on my holy mountain, so will all the nations drink continually. Yes, Dem go drink, swallow down, and Go be as though dem had not been.
But in Mount Zion, there Go be people wey escape, and it Go be holy. The house of Jacob will possess dem possessions.

The house of Jacob Go be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble. Dem go burn among dem, and devour dem. There No go be any remaining to the house of Esau.” Indeed, Baba God has spoken.
Those of the South will possess the mountain of Esau, and those of the lowland, the Philistines. Dem go possess the field of Ephraim, and the field of Samaria. Benjamin will possess Gilead.

The captives of this army of the pikin dem of Israel, Wey be among the Canaanites, will possess even to Zarephath; and the captives of Jerusalem, Wey be in Sepharad, will possess the cities of the Negev.
Saviors will go up on Mount Zion to judge the mountains of Esau, and the kingdom Go be Baba God’s.
Now Baba God’s word come to Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,
“Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and preach against it, for dem wickedness has come up before me.”

But Jonah rose up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of Baba God. He go down to Joppa, and find a ship going to Tarshish; so he paid its fare, and go down into it, to go with dem to Tarshish from the presence of Baba God.
But Baba God sent out a great wind on the sea, and there was a mighty storm on the sea, so that the ship was likely to break up.

Then the mariners were afraid, and every man cried to his god. Dem threw the cargo that was in the ship into the sea to lighten the ship. But Jonah had gone down into the innermost parts of the ship, and he was laying down, and was fast asleep.
So the ship master come to him, and talk say to him, “What do you mean, sleeper? Arise, call on una God! Maybe una God will notice us, so that we no go perish.”
Dem all talk say to each other, “Come, Make we throw lots, that we may know Wey be responsible for this evil that is on us.” So dem throw lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
Then dem ask him, “Tell us, please, for whose cause this evil is on us. Wetin be una occupation? Where do you come from? Wetin be una country? Of what people are you?”
E tell dem say, “I be a Hebrew, and I fear Baba God, the God of heaven, who has made the sea and the dry land.”
Then were the men exceedingly afraid, and talk say to him, “Wetin be this that you have done?” For the men know that he was fleeing from the presence of Baba God, because he had told dem.
Then Dem tell am say, “What shall we do to you, that the sea may be calm to us?” For the sea grew more and more stormy.
E tell dem say, “Take me up, and throw me into the sea. Then the sea Go be calm for you; for I know that because of me this great storm is on you.”
Nevertheless the men rowed hard to get dem back to the land; but dem could not, for the sea grew more and more stormy against dem.
So dem cried to Baba God, and talk say, “We beg you, Baba God, we beg you, no Make we die for this man’s life, and no lay on us innocent blood; for you, Baba God, have done as it pleased you.”
So dem take up Jonah, and threw him into the sea; and the sea ceased its raging.
Then the men feared Baba God exceedingly; and dem offered a sacrifice to Baba God, and made vows.
Baba God prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
Then Jonah prayed to Baba God, his God, out of the fish’s belly.
He talk say, “I call because of my suffering to Baba God. He answer me. Out of the belly of Sheol I cried. You heard my voice.
For you threw me into the depths, in the heart of the seas. The flood was all around me. All una waves and una billows passed over me.
I talk say, ‘I Don dey banished from una sight; yet I go look again toward una holy temple.’
The waters surrounded me, even to the soul. The deep was around me. The weeds were wrapped around my head.
I go down to the bottoms of the mountains. The earth barred me in forever: yet have you bring up my life from the pit, Baba God my God.
“When my soul fainted within me, I remember Baba God. My prayer come in to you, into una holy temple.
People wey regard lying vanities forsake dem own mercy.
But I go sacrifice to you with the voice of thanksgiving. I go pay that which I have vowed. Salvation belongs to Baba God.”
Baba God spoke to the fish, and it vomited out Jonah on the dry land.
Baba God’s word come to Jonah the second time, saying,
“Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and preach to it the message that I give you.”
So Jonah arose, and go to Nineveh, according to Baba God’s word. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, three days’ journey across.
Jonah began to enter into the city a day’s journey, and he cried out, and talk say, “In forty days, Nineveh Go be overthrown!”
The people of Nineveh believe God; and dem proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from dem greatest even to dem least.
The news reached the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and take off his royal robe, covered imself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
He made a proclamation and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, “Let neither man nor animal, herd nor flock, taste anything; Make dem not feed, nor drink water;
but Make dem be covered with sackcloth, both man and animal, and Make dem cry mightily to God. Yes, Make dem turn everyone from his evil way, and from the violence that is in his hands.
Wey know whether God No go turn and relent, and turn away from his fierce anger, so that we might not perish?”
God see dem works, that dem turned from dem evil way. God relented of the disaster which he talk say he would do to dem, and he didn’t do it.
But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was angry.

He prayed to Baba God, and talk say, “Please, Baba God, no be this what I talk say when I was still in my own country? So I hurried to flee to Tarshish, for I know that You be a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and you relent of doing harm.
So now, Baba God, take, I beg you, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live.”
Baba God talk say, “Is it right for you to be angry?”
Then Jonah go out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and there made imself a booth, and sat under it in the shade, until he might see what would become of the city.
Baba God prepared a vine, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shade over his head, to deliver him from his discomfort. So Jonah was exceedingly glad because of the vine.
But God prepared a worm at dawn the next day, and it chewed on the vine, so that it withered.

When the sun arose, God prepared a sultry east wind; and the sun beat on Jonah’s head, so that he fainted, and requested for imself that he might die, and talk say, “It is better for me to die than to live.”
God talk say to Jonah, “Is it right for you to be angry about the vine?” He talk say, “I be right to be angry, even to death.”
Baba God talk say, “You Don dey concerned for the vine, for which you have not labored, neither made it grow; which come up in a night, and perished in a night.

Shouldn’t I be concerned for Nineveh, that great city, in which are more than one hundred twenty thousand persons who no fit discern between dem right hand and dem left hand; and also much livestock?”
Baba God’s word that come to Micah the Morashtite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he see concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
Hear, you peoples, all of you. Listen, O earth, and all that is inside am: and let the Lord Baba God be witness against you, the Lord from his holy temple.
