Will a man rob God? Yet you rob me! But you say, ‘How have we robbed you?’ In tithes and offerings.
You be cursed with the curse; for you rob me, even this whole nation.

Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, that there may be chop in my house, and test me now in this,” says Baba God of Armies, “if I go not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there No go be room enough for.
I go rebuke the devourer for una sakes, and he no go destroy the fruits of una ground; neither shall una vine throw its fruit before its time in the field,” says Baba God of Armies.
“People for everywhere shall call you blessed, for You go be a delightful land,” says Baba God of Armies.
“Una words Don dey stout against me,” says Baba God. “Yet you say, ‘What have we spoken against you?’
You have talk say, ‘It is vain to serve God;’ and ‘What profit is it that we have follow his instructions, and that we have walked mournfully before Baba God of Armies?
Now we call the proud happy; yes, people wey work wickedness are built up; yes, dem tempt God, and escape.’
Then people wey feared Baba God spoke one with another; and Baba God listened, and heard, and a book of memory was written before him, for people wey feared Baba God, and who honored his name.
Dem go be mine,” says Baba God of Armies, “my own possession in the day that I make, and I go spare dem, as a man spares his own son who serves him.
Then you shall return and discern between the righteous and the wicked, between him who serves God and him who no dey serve him.

“For, see am, the day comes, it burns as a furnace; and all the proud, and all who work wickedness, Go be stubble; and the day that comes will burn dem up,” says Baba God of Armies, “that it shall leave dem neither root nor branch.
But to you who fear my name shall the sun of righteousness arise with healing in its wings. You go go out, and leap like calves of the stall.
You shall tread down the wicked; for Dem go be ashes under the soles of una feet in the day that I make,” says Baba God of Armies.
“Remember the law of Moses my worker, which I commanded to him in Horeb for all Israel, even statutes and ordinances.
See am, I go send you Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of Baba God comes.
He will turn the hearts of the fathers to the pikin dem, and the hearts of the pikin dem to dem fathers, lest I come and strike the earth with a curse.”
The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
Abraham became the father of Isaac. Isaac became the father of Jacob. Jacob became the father of Judah and his brothers.
Judah became the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Perez became the father of Hezron. Hezron became the father of Ram.
Ram became the father of Amminadab. Amminadab became the father of Nahshon. Nahshon became the father of Salmon.
Salmon became the father of Boaz by Rahab. Boaz became the father of Obed by Ruth. Obed became the father of Jesse.
Jesse became the father of King David. David became the father of Solomon by her who Bin dey Uriah’s wife.
Solomon became the father of Rehoboam. Rehoboam became the father of Abijah. Abijah became the father of Asa.
Asa became the father of Jehoshaphat. Jehoshaphat became the father of Joram. Joram became the father of Uzziah.
Uzziah became the father of Jotham. Jotham became the father of Ahaz. Ahaz became the father of Hezekiah.
Hezekiah became the father of Manasseh. Manasseh became the father of Amon. Amon became the father of Josiah.
Josiah became the father of Jechoniah and his brothers, at the time of the exile to Babylon.
After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah became the father of Shealtiel. Shealtiel became the father of Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel became the father of Abiud. Abiud became the father of Eliakim. Eliakim became the father of Azor.
Azor became the father of Zadok. Zadok became the father of Achim. Achim became the father of Eliud.
Eliud became the father of Eleazar. Eleazar became the father of Matthan. Matthan became the father of Jacob.
Jacob became the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom was born Jesus, Wey be call Christ.

So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; from David to the exile to Babylon fourteen generations; and from the carrying away to Babylon to the Christ, fourteen generations.
Now the birth of Jesus Christ was like this; for after his mother, Mary, was engaged to Joseph, before dem come together, she was find pregnant by the Holy Spirit.
Joseph, her husband, being a righteous man, and not willing to make her a public example, intended to put her away secretly.

But when he thought about these things, see am, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, No fear to take to yourself Mary, una wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.
She shall give birth to a son. You shall call his name Jesus, for it is person wey shall save his people from dem sins.”
Now all this has happened, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying,
“See am, the virgin go be with pikin, and shall give birth to a son. Dem shall call his name Immanuel”; which is, being interpreted, “God with us.”
Joseph arose from his sleep, and did as the angel of the Lord commanded him, and take his wife to imself;
and didn’t know her sexually until she had given birth to her firstborn son. He named him Jesus.
Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of King Herod, see am, wise men from the east come to Jerusalem, saying,
“Where is person Wey born King of the Jews? For we see his star in the east, and have come to worship him.”
When King Herod heard it, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
Gathering together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he ask dem where the Christ would be born.
Dem tell am say, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for this is written through the prophet,
‘You Bethlehem, land of Judah, are in no way least among the princes of Judah: for out of you shall come a governor, who shall shepherd my people, Israel.’”
Then Herod secretly call the wise men, and learned from dem exactly what time the star appeared.
He sent dem to Bethlehem, and talk say, “Go and search diligently for the young pikin. When you have find him, bring me word, so that I also may come and worship him.”
Dem, having heard the king, go dem way; and see am, the star, which dem see in the east, go before dem, until it come and stood over where the young pikin was.
When dem see the star, dem rejoiced with exceedingly great gladness.
Dem come into the house and see the young pikin with Mary, his mother, and dem fell down and worshiped him. Opening dem treasures, dem offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Being warned in a dream that dem shouldn’t return to Herod, dem go back to dem own country another way.

Now when dem had comot, see am, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, “Arise and take the young pikin and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and stay there until I tell una, for Herod will seek the young pikin to destroy him.”
He arose and take the young pikin and his mother by night, and comot into Egypt,
and was there until the death of Herod; that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying, “Out of Egypt I call my son.”

Then Herod, when he see that he was mocked by the wise men, was exceedingly angry, and sent out, and killed all the male pikin dem who were in Bethlehem and in all the surrounding countryside, from two years old and under, according to the exact time which he had learned from the wise men.
Then that which was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying,
“A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her pikin dem; she wouldn’t be comforted, because Dem be no more.”
But when Herod was dead, see am, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, saying,
“Arise and take the young pikin and his mother, and go into the land of Israel, for people wey sought the young pikin’s life are dead.”
He arose and take the young pikin and his mother, and come into the land of Israel.
But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in the place of his father, Herod, he was afraid to go there. Being warned in a dream, he withdrew into the region of Galilee,
and come and lived in a city call Nazareth; that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophets: “He Go be call a Nazarene.”
In those days, John the Baptizer come, preaching in the wilderness of Judea, saying,
“Repent, for God kingdom for heaven is at hand!”
For this is person wey was spoken of by Isaiah the prophet, saying, “The voice of one crying in the wilderness, make ready the way of the Lord. Make his paths straight.”
Now John imself wore clothing made of camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist. His chop was locusts and wild honey.
Then people from Jerusalem, all of Judea, and all the region around the Jordan go out to him.
Dem were baptized by him in the Jordan, confessing dem sins.
But when he see many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming for his baptism, E tell dem say, “You offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the serious anger to come?
So produce fruit worthy of repentance!
No think to unaself, ‘We have Abraham for our father,’ for I tell una that God is able to raise up pikin dem to Abraham from these stones.
“Even now the ax lies at the root of the trees. So every tree that no dey produce good fruit is cut down, and throw into the fire.
I indeed baptize you in water for repentance, but person wey comes after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I be not worthy to carry. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.
His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor. He will gather his wheat into the barn, but the chaff he will burn up with unquenchable fire.”
Then Jesus come from Galilee to the Jordan to John, to be baptized by him.
But John would have hindered him, saying, “I need to be baptized by you, and you come to me?”
But Jesus, answering, talk say to him, “Allow it now, for this is the fitting way for us to fulfill all righteousness.” Then he allowed him.
Jesus, when he was baptized, go up directly from the water: and see am, the heavens were opened to him. He see the Spirit of God descending as a dove, and coming on him.
See am, a voice out of the heavens talk say, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I be well pleased.”
Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
When he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was hungry afterward.
The tempter come and talk say to him, “If You be the Son of God, command that these stones become bread.”
But he answer, “It is written, ‘Man no go live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.’”
Then the devil take him into the holy city. He set him on the pinnacle of the temple,

and talk say to him, “If You be the Son of God, throw yourself down, for it is written, ‘He will put his angels in charge of you.’ and, ‘On dem hands Dem go bear you up, so that you no dash una foot against a stone.’”
Jesus tell am say, “Again, it is written, ‘You no go test the Lord, una God.’”
Again, the devil take him to an exceedingly high mountain, and showed him all the kingdoms of the world, and dem glory.
E tell am say, “I go give you all of these things, if You go fall down and worship me.”
Then Jesus tell am say, “Get behind me, Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord una God, and you shall serve him only.’”
Then the devil left him, and see am, angels come and served him.
Now when Jesus heard that John was delivered up, he withdrew into Galilee.
Leaving Nazareth, he come and lived in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali,
that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,
“The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, toward the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles,
the people who sat in darkness see a great light, to people wey sat in the region and shadow of death, to dem light has dawned.”
From that time, Jesus began to preach, and to say, “Repent! For God kingdom for heaven is at hand.”
Walking by the sea of Galilee, he see two brothers: Simon, Wey be call Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for dem were fishermen.
E tell dem say, “Come after me, and I go make you fishers for men.”
Dem sharp-sharp left dem nets and follow him.
Going on from there, he see two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee dem father, mending dem nets. He call dem.
Dem sharp-sharp left the boat and dem father, and follow him.
Jesus go about in all Galilee, teaching in dem synagogues, preaching the Better news of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.
The report about him go out into all Syria. Dem bring to him all who were sick, afflicted with various diseases and torments, possessed with demons, epileptics, and paralytics; and he healed dem.
Plenty people from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea and from beyond the Jordan follow him.
Seeing the plenty people, he go up onto the mountain. When he had sat down, his disciples come to him.
He opened his mouth and taught dem, saying,
“God blessing dey for people wey humble for spirit, because God kingdom na dem own.
Blessed are people wey mourn, for dem go be comforted.
Blessed are the gentle, for dem shall inherit the earth.
Blessed are people wey hunger and thirst after righteousness, for dem go be filled.
Blessed are the merciful, for dem shall obtain mercy.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for dem shall see God.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for dem go be call pikin dem of God.
Blessed are people wey Don dey persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for dem own is God kingdom for heaven.
“Blessed are you when people reproach you, persecute you, and say all kinds of evil against you falsely, for my sake.
Glad well-well, and be exceedingly glad, for great is una reward in heaven. For that is how dem persecuted the prophets who were before you.
“You be the salt of the earth, but if the salt has lost its flavor, with what will it be salted? It is then good for nothing, but to be throw out and trodden under the feet of men.
You be the light of the world. A city located on a hill no fit be hidden.
Neither do you light a lamp, and put it under a measuring basket, but on a stand; and it shines to all Wey be in the house.
Even so, let una light shine before men; that dem may see una good works, and glorify una Father Wey be in heaven.
“No think that I come to destroy the law or the prophets. I didn’t come to destroy, but to fulfill.
For most certainly, I tell una, until heaven and earth pass away, not even one smallest letter or one tiny pen stroke shall in any way pass away from the law, until all things are accomplished.

Anybody wey, so, shall break one of these least commandments, and teach others to do so, go be call least in God kingdom for heaven; but Anybody wey shall do and teach dem go be call great in God kingdom for heaven.
For I tell una that unless una righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, E get no way You go enter into God kingdom for heaven.
“You have heard that it was talk say to the ancient ones, ‘You no go murder;’ and ‘Anybody wey murders Go be in danger of the judgment.’

But I tell una, that everyone Wey be angry with his brother without a cause Go be in danger of the judgment; and Anybody wey says to his brother, ‘Raca!’ Go be in danger of the council; and Anybody wey says, ‘You fool!’ Go be in danger of the fire of Gehenna.
“If so You be offering una gift at the altar, and there remember that una brother has anything against you,
leave una gift there before the altar, and go una way. First be reconciled to una brother, and then come and offer una gift.
Agree with una adversary sharp-sharp, while You be with him on the way; lest perhaps the prosecutor deliver you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and you be throw into prison.
True true, I tell una, you shall by no means get out of there, until you have paid the last penny.
“You have heard that it was talk say, ‘You no go commit adultery;’
but I tell una that Everybody wey gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart.

If una right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of una members should perish, than for una whole body to be throw into Gehenna.

If una right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off, and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of una members should perish, than for una whole body to be throw into Gehenna.
“It was also talk say, ‘Anybody wey shall put away his wife, Make e give her a writing of divorce,’
but I tell una that Anybody wey puts away his wife, except for the cause of sexual immorality, makes her an adulteress; and Anybody wey marries her when she is put away commits adultery.
“Again you have heard that it was talk say to dem of old time, ‘You no go make false vows, but shall perform to the Lord una vows,’
but I tell una, no swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God;
nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
Neither shall you swear by una head, for you no fit make one hair white or black.
But let una ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and una ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Anything wey is more than these is of the evil one.
“You have heard that it was talk say, ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’
But I tell una, no resist him Wey be evil; but Anybody wey strikes you on una right cheek, turn to him the other also.
If anyone sues you to take away una coat, Make e have una cloak also.
Anybody wey compels you to go one mile, go with him two.
Give to him who asks you, and no turn away him who desires to borrow from you.
“You have heard that it was talk say, ‘You shall love una neighbor and hate una enemy.’
But I tell una, love una enemies, bless people wey curse you, do good to people wey hate you, and pray for people wey mistreat you and persecute you,
that you may be pikin dem of una Father Wey be in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.
For if you love people wey love you, what reward do you have? No even the tax collectors do the same?
If you only greet una friends, what more do you do than others? No even the tax collectors do the same?
So you go be perfect, just as una Father in heaven is perfect.
“Be careful that you no do una charitable giving before men, to be seen by dem, or else you have no reward from una Father Wey be in heaven.

So when you do merciful deeds, no sound a trumpet before yourself, as the fake people do in the synagogues and in the streets, that dem may get glory from men. True true, I tell una, dem have received dem reward.
But when you do merciful deeds, no let una left hand know what una right hand does,
so that una merciful deeds may be in secret, then una Father wey see in secret will reward you openly.

“When you pray, you no go be as the fake people, for dem love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that dem may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell una, dem have received dem reward.
But you, when you pray, enter into una inner room, and having shut una door, pray to una Father Wey be in secret, and una Father wey see in secret will reward you openly.
In praying, no use vain repetitions, as the Gentiles do; for dem think that Dem go be heard for dem much speaking.
So no be like dem, for una Father knows what things you need, before you ask him.
Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may una name be kept holy.
Let una Kingdom come. Let una Go be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
Give us today our daily bread.
Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’
“For if you forgive men dem trespasses, una heavenly Father will also forgive you.
But if you no forgive men dem trespasses, neither will una Father forgive una trespasses.
“Moreover when you fast, no be like the fake people, with sad faces. For dem disfigure dem faces, that dem may be seen by men to be fasting. True true, I tell una, dem have received dem reward.
But you, when you fast, anoint una head, and wash una face;
so that you No be seen by men to be fasting, but by una Father Wey be in secret, and una Father, wey see in secret, will reward you.
“No lay up treasures for unaself on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal;
but lay up for unaself treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves no break through and steal;
for where una treasure is, there una heart Go be also.
“The lamp of the body is the eye. If so una eye is sound, una whole body Go be full of light.
But if una eye is evil, una whole body Go be full of darkness. If so the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness!
“Nobody can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he Go be devoted to one and despise the other. You no fit serve both God and Mammon.
So I tell una, No worry about una life: Wetin you go eat, or Wetin you go drink; nor yet for una body, Wetin you go wear. No be life more than chop, and the body more than clothing?
See the birds of the sky, that dem no sow, neither do dem reap, nor gather into barns. Una heavenly Father feeds dem. No be you of much more value than dem?
“Which of you, by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?
Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how dem grow. Dem no toil, neither do dem spin,
yet I tell una that even Solomon in all his glory No be dressed like one of these.
But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today exists, and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, no go he much more clothe you, you of little faith?
“So No worry about, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’
For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for una heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things Go be given to you as well.
So No worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow Go be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.
“No judge, so that you no go be judged.
For with Anything wey judgment you judge, You go be judged; and with Anything wey measure you measure, it Go be measured to you.
Why do you see the speck that is in una brother’s eye, but no consider the beam that is in una own eye?
Or how will you tell una brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from una eye;’ and see am, the beam is in una own eye?
You fake person! First remove the beam out of una own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of una brother’s eye.
“No give that which is holy to the dogs, neither throw una pearls before the pigs, lest perhaps dem trample dem under dem feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.
“Ask, and it Go be given you. Seek, and You go find. Knock, and it Go be opened for you.
For Everybody wey asks receives. Person wey seeks finds. To him who knocks it Go be opened.
Or Wey be there among you, who, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone?
Or if he asks for a fish, who will give him a serpent?
If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to una pikin dem, how much more will una Father Wey be in heaven give good things to people wey ask him!
So Anything wey you desire for men to do to you, you shall also do to dem; for this is the law and the prophets.
“Enter in by the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many are people wey enter in by it.
How narrow is the gate, and restricted is the way that leads to life! Few are people wey find it.
“Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.
By dem fruits You go know dem. Do you gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?
Even so, every good tree produces good fruit; but the corrupt tree produces evil fruit.
A good tree no fit produce evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree produce good fruit.
Every tree that no dey grow good fruit is cut down, and thrown into the fire.
So by dem fruits You go know dem.
Not Everybody wey says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter into God kingdom for heaven; but person wey does the will of my Father Wey be in heaven.
Many will tell me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, didn’t we prophesy in una name, in una name throw out demons, and in una name do many mighty works?’
Then I go tell dem, ‘I never know you. Depart from me, you who work wickedness.’
“Everyone so wey hear these words of mine, and does dem, I go liken him to a wise man, who built his house on a rock.
The rain come down, the floods come, and the winds blew, and beat on that house; and it didn’t fall, for it was founded on the rock.
Everyone wey hear these words of mine, and no dey do dem Go be like a foolish man, who built his house on the sand.
The rain come down, the floods come, and the winds blew, and beat on that house; and it fell — and great was its fall.”
When Jesus had finished saying these things, the plenty people were astonished at his teaching,
for he taught dem with authority, and not like the scribes.
When he come down from the mountain, Plenty people follow him.
See am, a leper come to him and worshiped him, saying, “Lord, if you want to, you can make me clean.”
Jesus stretched out his hand, and touched him, saying, “I want to. Be made clean.” Sharp-sharp his leprosy was cleansed.
Jesus tell am say, “See that you tell nobody, but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to dem.”
When he come into Capernaum, a centurion come to him, asking him,
and saying, “Lord, my worker lies in the house paralyzed, grievously tormented.”
Jesus tell am say, “I go come and heal him.”
The centurion answer, “Lord, I’m not worthy for you to come under my roof. Just say the word, and my worker Go be healed.
For I be also a man under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and tell another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and tell my worker, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
When Jesus heard it, he surprise well-well, and talk say to people wey follow, “True true, I tell una, I haven’t find so great a faith, not even in Israel.
I tell una that many will come from the east and the west, and will sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in God kingdom for heaven,
but the pikin dem of the Kingdom Go be thrown out into the outer darkness. There Go be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”
Jesus talk say to the centurion, “Go una way. Let it be done for you as you have believe.” His worker was healed in that hour.
When Jesus come into Peter’s house, he see his wife’s mother lying sick with a fever.
He touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and served him.
When evening come, dem bring to him many possessed with demons. He throw out the spirits with a word, and healed all who were sick;
that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying, “He take our infirmities, and bore our diseases.”
Now when Jesus see Plenty people around him, he give the order to depart to the other side.
A scribe come, and talk say to him, “Teacher, I go follow you Anywhere wey you go.”
Jesus tell am say, “The foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
Another of his disciples talk say to him, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”
But Jesus tell am say, “Follow me, and leave the dead to bury dem own dead.”
When he got into a boat, his disciples follow him.
See am, a violent storm come up on the sea, so much that the boat was covered with the waves, but he was asleep.
Dem come to him, and woke him up, saying, “Save us, Lord! We be dying!”
E tell dem say, “Why are you fearful, O you of little faith?” Then he got up, rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm.
The men surprise well-well, saying, “What kind of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
When he come to the other side, into the country of the Gergesenes, two people possessed by demons met him there, coming out of the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that nobody could pass that way.
See am, dem cried out, saying, “What do we have to do with you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?”
Now there was a herd of many pigs feeding far away from dem.
The demons begged him, saying, “If you throw us out, permit us to go away into the herd of pigs.”
E tell dem say, “Go!” Dem come out, and go into the herd of pigs: and see am, the whole herd of pigs rushed down the cliff into the sea, and died in the water.
People wey fed dem fled, and go away into the city, and told everything, including what happened to people wey were possessed with demons.
See am, all the city come out to meet Jesus. When dem see him, dem begged that he would depart from dem borders.
He entered into a boat, and crossed over, and come into his own city.
See am, dem bring to him a man who was paralyzed, lying on a bed. Jesus, seeing dem faith, talk say to the paralytic, “Son, cheer up! Una sins are forgiven you.”
See am, some of the scribes talk say to themselves, “This man blasphemes.”
Jesus, knowing dem thoughts, talk say, “Why do you think evil in una hearts?
For which is easier, to say, ‘Una sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Get up, and walk?’
But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” (then he talk say to the paralytic), “Get up, and take up una mat, and go to una house.”
He arose and comot to his house.
But when the plenty people see it, dem surprise well-well and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.
As Jesus passed by from there, he see a man call Matthew sitting at the tax collection office. E tell am say, “Follow me.” He got up and follow him.
As he sat in the house, see am, many tax collectors and sinners come and sat down with Jesus and his disciples.
When the Pharisees see it, dem talk say to his disciples, “Why does una teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
When Jesus heard it, E tell dem say, “People Wey healthy have no need for a physician, but people Wey sick do.
But you go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ for I come not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
Then John’s disciples come to him, saying, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but una disciples no fast?”
Jesus tell dem say, “Can the friends of the bridegroom mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with dem? But the days will come when the bridegroom Go be taken away from dem, and then Dem go fast.
Nobody puts a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; for the patch would tear away from the garment, and a worse hole is made.
Neither do people put new wine into old wine skins, or else the skins would burst, and the wine be spilled, and the skins ruined. No, dem put new wine into fresh wine skins, and both are preserved.”
While he told these things to dem, see am, a ruler come and worshiped him, saying, “My daughter has just died, but come and lay una hand on her, and she will live.”
Jesus got up and follow him, as did his disciples.
See am, a woman who had an issue of blood for twelve years come behind him, and touched the fringe of his garment;
for she talk say within sheself, “If I just touch his garment, I go be made well.”
But Jesus, turning around and seeing her, talk say, “Daughter, cheer up! Una faith has made you well.” And the woman was made well from that hour.
When Jesus come into the ruler’s house, and see the flute players, and the crowd in noisy disorder,
E tell dem say, “Make room, because the girl no be dead, but sleeping.” Dem were ridiculing him.
But when the crowd was put out, he entered in, take her by the hand, and the girl arose.
The report of this go out into all that land.
As Jesus passed by from there, two blind men follow him, calling out and saying, “Have mercy on us, son of David!”
When he had come into the house, the blind men come to him. Jesus tell dem say, “Do you believe that I be able to do this?” Dem told him, “Yes, Lord.”
Then he touched dem eyes, saying, “According to una faith be it done to you.”
Dem eyes were opened. Jesus strictly commanded dem, saying, “See that Nobody knows about this.”
But dem go out and spread abroad his fame in all that land.
As dem go out, see am, a mute man who was demon possessed was bring to him.
When the demon was throw out, the mute man spoke. The plenty people surprise well-well, saying, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!”
But the Pharisees talk say, “By the prince of the demons, he casts out demons.”
Jesus go about all the cities and the villages, teaching in dem synagogues, and preaching the Better news of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.
But when he see the plenty people, he was moved with compassion for dem, because dem were harassed and scattered, like sheep without a shepherd.
Then he talk say to his disciples, “The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the laborers are few.
Pray so that the Lord of the harvest will send out laborers into his harvest.”
He call to imself his twelve disciples, and give dem authority over unclean spirits, to throw dem out, and to heal every disease and every sickness.
Now the names of the twelve apostles are these. The first, Simon, Wey be call Peter; Andrew, his brother; James the son of Zebedee; John, his brother;
Philip; Bartholomew; Thomas; Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus; Lebbaeus, who was also call Thaddaeus;
Simon the Canaanite; and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
Jesus sent these twelve out, and commanded dem, saying, “No go among the Gentiles, and no enter into any city of the Samaritans.
Rather, go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
As you go, preach, saying, ‘God kingdom for heaven is at hand!’
Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, and throw out demons. Freely you received, so freely give.
No take any gold, silver, or brass in una money belts.
Take no bag for una journey, neither two coats, nor shoes, nor staff: for the laborer is worthy of his chop.
Into Anything wey city or village you enter, find out who in it is worthy; and stay there until you go on.
As you enter into the household, greet it.
If the household is worthy, let una peace come on it, but if it no be worthy, let una peace return to you.
Anybody wey no dey receive you, nor hear una words, as you go out of that house or that city, shake off the dust from una feet.
True true, I tell una, it Go be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city.
“See am, I send you out as sheep among wolves. So be wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.
But beware of men: for Dem go deliver you up to councils, and in dem synagogues Dem go scourge you.
Yes, and You go be bring before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony to dem and to the nations.
But when dem deliver you up, No worry about how or Wetin you go say, for it Go be given you in that hour Wetin you go say.
For it No be you who speak, but the Spirit of una Father who speaks in you.
“Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his pikin. Pikin dem will rise up against parents, and cause dem to be put to death.
You go be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but person wey endures to the end Go be saved.
But when dem persecute you in this city, flee into the next, for True true, I tell una, You go not have gone through the cities of Israel, until the Son of Man has come.
“A disciple No be above his teacher, nor a worker above his lord.
It is enough for the disciple that he be like his teacher, and the worker like his lord. If dem have call the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more those of his household!
So No fear of dem, for E get nothing covered that No go be revealed; and hidden that No go be known.
What I tell una in the darkness, speak in the light; and Wetin you hear whispered in the ear, proclaim on the housetops.
No fear of people wey kill the body, but No be able to kill the soul. Rather, fear him Wey be able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
“No be two sparrows sold for an assarion coin? Not one of dem falls on the ground apart from una Father’s will,
but the very hairs of una head are all numbered.
So No fear. You be of more value than many sparrows.
Everyone so who confesses me before men, him I go also confess before my Father Wey be in heaven.
But Anybody wey denies me before men, him I go also deny before my Father Wey be in heaven.
“No think that I come to send peace on the earth. I didn’t come to send peace, but a sword.
For I come to set a man at odds against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
A man’s foes Go be those of his own household.
Person wey loves father or mother more than me No be worthy of me; and person wey loves son or daughter more than me no be worthy of me.
Person wey no dey take his cross and follow after me, no be worthy of me.
Person wey seeks his life will lose it; and person wey loses his life for my sake will find it.
Person wey receives you receives me, and person wey receives me receives him who sent me.
Person wey receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward. Person wey receives a righteous man in the name of a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.
Anybody wey gives one of these little ones just a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, True true, I tell una he will in no way lose his reward.”
When Jesus had finished directing his twelve disciples, he comot from there to teach and preach in dem cities.
Now when John heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples
and talk say to him, “Are you person wey comes, or should we look for another?”
Jesus answer dem, “Go and tell John the things which you hear and see:
the blind receive dem sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have better news preached to dem.
Blessed is person wey finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”
As these go dem way, Jesus began to say to the plenty people concerning John, “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
But what did you go out to see? A man in soft clothing? See am, people wey wear soft clothing are in kings’ houses.
But why did you go out? To see a prophet? Yes, I tell una, and much more than a prophet.
For this is he, of whom it is written, ‘See am, I send my messenger before una face, who will prepare una way before you.’
True true, I tell una, among people Wey born of women there has not arisen anyone greater than John the Baptizer; yet person Wey least in God kingdom for heaven is greater than he.
From the days of John the Baptizer until now, God kingdom for heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force.
For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.
If You be willing to receive it, this is Elijah, Wey be to come.
Person wey has ears to hear, Make e hear.
“But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like pikin dem sitting in the marketplaces, who call to dem companions
and say, ‘We played the flute for you, and you didn’t dance. We mourned for you, and you didn’t lament.’
For John come neither eating nor drinking, and dem say, ‘He has a demon.’
The Son of Man come eating and drinking, and dem say, ‘See am, a gluttonous man and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is justified by her pikin dem.”
Then he began to denounce the cities in which most of his mighty works Bin dey done, because dem didn’t repent.
“Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works Bin dey done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, dem would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
But I tell una, it Go be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.
You, Capernaum, Wey be exalted to heaven, You go go down to Hades. For if the mighty works Bin dey done in Sodom which were done in you, it would have remain until today.
But I tell una that it Go be more tolerable for the land of Sodom, on the day of judgment, than for you.”
At that time, Jesus answer, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you hid these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed dem to infants.
Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in una sight.
All things Don dey delivered to me by my Father. Nobody knows the Son, except the Father; neither does anyone know the Father, except the Son, and he to whom the Son desires to reveal him.
“Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I go give you rest.
Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I be gentle and humble in heart; and You go find rest for una souls.
For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”
At that time, Jesus go on the Sabbath day through the grain fields. His disciples were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and to eat.
But the Pharisees, when dem see it, talk say to him, “See am, una disciples do Wetin be not lawful to do on the Sabbath.”
But E tell dem say, “Haven’t you read what David did, when he was hungry, and people wey were with him;
how he entered into God’s house, and ate the show bread, which No be lawful for him to eat, neither for people wey were with him, but only for the priests?
Or have you not read in the law, that on the Sabbath day, the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath, and are guiltless?
But I tell una that one greater than the temple is here.
But if you had known what this means, ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the guiltless.
For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
He comot there, and go into dem synagogue.
And see am there was a man with a withered hand. Dem ask him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath day?” that dem might accuse him.
E tell dem say, “What man is there among you, who has one sheep, and if this one falls into a pit on the Sabbath day, no go he grab on to it, and lift it out?
Of how much more value then is a man than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath day.”
Then he told the man, “Stretch out una hand.” He stretched it out; and it was restored whole, just like the other.
But the Pharisees go out, and conspired against him, how dem might destroy him.
Jesus, perceiving that, withdrew from there. Plenty people follow him; and he healed dem all,
and commanded dem that dem no suppose make him known:
that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,
“See am, my worker whom I have chosen; my beloved in whom my soul is well pleased: I go put my Spirit on him. He will proclaim justice to the nations.
He No go strive, nor shout; neither will anyone hear his voice in the streets.
He no go break a bruised reed. He no go quench a smoking flax, until he leads justice to victory.
In his name, the nations will hope.”
Then one possessed by a demon, blind and mute, was bring to him and he healed him, so that the blind and mute man both spoke and see.
All the plenty people were amazed, and talk say, “Can this be the son of David?”
But when the Pharisees heard it, dem talk say, “This man No dey throw out demons, except by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons.”
Knowing dem thoughts, Jesus tell dem say, “Every kingdom divided against itself is bring to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself No go stand.
If Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against imself. How then will his kingdom stand?
If I by Beelzebul throw out demons, by whom do una pikin dem throw dem out? So Dem go be una judges.
But if I by the Spirit of God throw out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come upon you.
Or how can one enter into the house of the strong man, and plunder his goods, unless he first bind the strong man? Then he will plunder his house.
“Person Wey not with me is against me, and person wey no dey gather with me, scatters.
So I tell una, every sin and blasphemy Go be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit No go be forgiven men.
Anybody wey speaks a word against the Son of Man, it Go be forgiven him; but Anybody wey speaks against the Holy Spirit, it No go be forgiven him, neither in this age, nor in that which is to come.
“Either make the tree good, and its fruit good, or make the tree corrupt, and its fruit corrupt; for the tree is known by its fruit.
You offspring of vipers, how can you, being evil, speak good things? For out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaks.
The good man out of his good treasure brings out good things, and the evil man out of his evil treasure brings out evil things.
I tell una that every idle word that men speak, Dem go give account of it in the day of judgment.
For by una words You go be justified, and by una words You go be condemned.”
Then certain of the scribes and Pharisees answer, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.”
But he answer dem, “An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, but no sign Go be given to it but the sign of Jonah the prophet.
For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the whale, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it, for dem repented at the preaching of Jonah; and see am, someone greater than Jonah is here.

The queen of the south will rise up in the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it, for she come from every corner of the world to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and see am, someone greater than Solomon is here.
When an unclean spirit has gone out of a man, he passes through waterless places, seeking rest, and no dey find it.
Then he says, ‘I go return into my house from which I come out,’ and when he has come back, he finds it empty, swept, and put in order.

Then he goes, and takes with imself seven other spirits more evil than he is, and dem enter in and live there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first. Even so will it be also to this evil generation.”
While he was yet speaking to the plenty people, see am, his mother and his brothers stood outside, seeking to speak to him.
One talk say to him, “See am, una mother and una brothers stand outside, seeking to speak to you.”
But he answer him who spoke to him, “Wey be my mother? Wey be my brothers?”
He stretched out his hand towards his disciples, and talk say, “See am, my mother and my brothers!
For Anybody wey does the will of my Father Wey be in heaven, he is my brother, and sister, and mother.”
On that day Jesus go out of the house, and sat by the seaside.
Plenty people gathered to him, so that he entered into a boat, and sat, and all the plenty people stood on the beach.
He spoke to dem many things in parables, saying, “See am, a farmer go out to sow.
As he sowed, some seeds fell by the roadside, and the birds come and devoured dem.
Others fell on rocky ground, where dem didn’t have much soil, and sharp-sharp dem sprang up, because dem had no depth of earth.
When the sun had risen, dem were scorched. Because dem had no root, dem withered away.
Others fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked dem.
Others fell on good soil, and yielded fruit: some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.
Person wey has ears to hear, Make e hear.”
The disciples come, and talk say to him, “Why do you speak to dem in parables?”
He answer dem, “To you it is given to know the mysteries of God kingdom for heaven, but it No be given to dem.
For Anybody wey has, to him Go be given, and he Go get abundance, but Anybody wey no dey have, from him Go be taken away even that which he has.
So I speak to dem in parables, because seeing dem no see, and hearing, dem no hear, neither do dem understand.
In dem the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says, ‘By hearing You go hear, and will in no way understand; Seeing You go see, and will in no way perceive:

for this people’s heart has grown callous, dem ears are dull of hearing, dem have closed dem eyes; or else perhaps dem might perceive with dem eyes, hear with dem ears, understand with dem heart, and would turn again; and I would heal dem.’
“But blessed are una eyes, for dem see; and una ears, for dem hear.
For True true, I tell una that many prophets and righteous men desired to see the things which you see, and didn’t see dem; and to hear the things which you hear, and didn’t hear dem.
“Hear, then, the parable of the farmer.
When anyone hears the word of the Kingdom, and no dey understand it, the evil one comes, and snatches away that which Don dey sown in his heart. This is what was sown by the roadside.
What was sown on the rocky places, this is person wey hears the word, and sharp-sharp with gladness receives it;
yet he has no root in imself, but endures for a while. When oppression or persecution arises because of the word, sharp-sharp he stumbles.
What was sown among the thorns, this is person wey hears the word, but the cares of this age and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and he becomes unfruitful.
What was sown on the good ground, this is person wey hears the word, and understands it, who most certainly bears fruit, and produces, some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.”
He set another parable before dem, saying, “God kingdom for heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field,
but while people slept, his enemy come and sowed darnel weeds also among the wheat, and go away.
But when the blade sprang up and produced fruit, then the darnel weeds appeared also.
The workers of the householder come and talk say to him, ‘Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in una field? Where did these darnel weeds come from?’
“E tell dem say, ‘An enemy has done this.’ “The workers ask him, ‘Do you want us to go and gather dem up?’
“But he talk say, ‘No, lest perhaps while you gather up the darnel weeds, you root up the wheat with dem.
Let both grow together until the harvest, and in the harvest time I go tell the reapers, “First, gather up the darnel weeds, and bind dem in bundles to burn dem; but gather the wheat into my barn.”’”
He set another parable before dem, saying, “God kingdom for heaven is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man take, and sowed in his field;
which indeed is smaller than all seeds. But when it is grown, it is greater than the herbs, and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches.”
He spoke another parable to dem. “God kingdom for heaven is like yeast, which a woman take, and hid in three measures of meal, until it was all leavened.”
Jesus spoke all these things in parables to the plenty people; and without a parable, he didn’t speak to dem,
that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying, “I go open my mouth in parables; I go utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.”
Then Jesus sent the plenty people away, and go into the house. His disciples come to him, saying, “Explain to us the parable of the darnel weeds of the field.”
He answer dem, “Person wey sows the good seed is the Son of Man,
the field is the world; and the good seed, these are the pikin dem of the Kingdom; and the darnel weeds are the pikin dem of the evil one.
The enemy who sowed dem is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.
As so the darnel weeds are gathered up and burned with fire; so will it be at the end of this age.
The Son of Man will send out his angels, and Dem go gather out of his Kingdom all things that cause stumbling, and people wey do wickedness,
and will throw dem into the furnace of fire. There Go be weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the Kingdom of dem Father. Person wey has ears to hear, Make e hear.
“Again, God kingdom for heaven is like a treasure hidden in the field, which a man find, and hid. In his gladness, he goes and sells all that he has, and buys that field.
“Again, God kingdom for heaven is like a man Wey be a merchant seeking fine pearls,
who having find one pearl of great price, he go and sold all that he had, and bought it.
“Again, God kingdom for heaven is like a dragnet, that was throw into the sea, and gathered some fish of every kind,
which, when it was filled, dem drew up on the beach. Dem sat down, and gathered the good into containers, but the bad dem threw away.
So will it be in the end of the world. The angels will come and separate the wicked from among the righteous,
and will throw dem into the furnace of fire. There Go be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.”
Jesus tell dem say, “Have you understand all these things?” Dem answer him, “Yes, Lord.”
E tell dem say, “So every scribe who Don dey made a disciple in God kingdom for heaven is like a man Wey be a householder, who brings out of his treasure new and old things.”
When Jesus had finished these parables, he comot from there.
Coming into his own country, he taught dem in dem synagogue, so that dem were astonished, and talk say, “Where did this man get this wisdom, and these mighty works?
No be this the carpenter’s son? No be his mother call Mary, and his brothers, James, Joses, Simon, and Judas?
No be all of his sisters with us? Where then did this man get all of these things?”
Dem were offended by him. But Jesus tell dem say, “A prophet No be without honor, except in his own country, and in his own house.”
He didn’t do many mighty works there because of dem unbelief.
At that time, Herod the tetrarch heard the report concerning Jesus,
and talk say to his workers, “This is John the Baptizer. He is risen from the dead. That is why these powers work in him.”
For Herod had laid hold of John, and bound him, and put him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife.
For John talk say to him, “It No be lawful for you to have her.”
When he would have put him to death, he feared the plenty people, because dem counted him as a prophet.
But when Herod’s birthday come, the daughter of Herodias danced among dem and pleased Herod.
Whereupon he promised with an oath to give her Anything wey she should ask.
She, being prompted by her mother, talk say, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptizer.”
The king was grieved, but for the sake of his oaths, and of people wey sat at the table with him, he commanded it to be given,
and he sent and beheaded John in the prison.
His head was bring on a platter, and given to the young lady: and she bring it to her mother.
His disciples come, and take the body, and buried it; and dem go and told Jesus.
Now when Jesus heard this, he withdrew from there in a boat, to a deserted place apart. When the plenty people heard it, dem follow him on foot from the cities.
Jesus go out, and he see Plenty people. He had compassion on dem, and healed dem sick.

When evening had come, his disciples come to him, saying, “This place is deserted, and the hour is already late. Send the plenty people away, that dem may go into the villages, and buy themselves chop.”
But Jesus tell dem say, “Dem no need to go away. You give dem something to eat.”
Dem told him, “We only have here five loaves and two fish.”
He talk say, “Bring dem here to me.”

He commanded the plenty people to sit down on the grass; and he take the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, broke and give the loaves to the disciples, and the disciples give to the plenty people.
Dem all ate, and were filled. Dem take up twelve baskets full of that which remain left over from the broken pieces.
People wey ate were about five thousand men, besides women and pikin dem.
Sharp-sharp Jesus made the disciples get into the boat, and to go ahead of him to the other side, while he sent the plenty people away.
After he had sent the plenty people away, he go up into the mountain by imself to pray. When evening had come, he was there alone.
But the boat was now in the middle of the sea, distressed by the waves, for the wind was contrary.
In the fourth watch of the night, Jesus come to dem, walking on the sea.
When the disciples see him walking on the sea, dem were troubled, saying, “It’s a ghost!” and dem cried out for fear.
But sharp-sharp Jesus spoke to dem, saying, “Cheer up! It is I! No fear.”
Peter answer him and talk say, “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the waters.”
He talk say, “Come!” Peter stepped down from the boat, and walked on the waters to come to Jesus.
But when he see that the wind was strong, he was afraid, and beginning to sink, he cried out, saying, “Lord, save me!”
Sharp-sharp Jesus stretched out his hand, take hold of him, and talk say to him, “You of little faith, why did you doubt?”
When dem got up into the boat, the wind ceased.
People wey were in the boat come and worshiped him, saying, “You be truly the Son of God!”
When dem had crossed over, dem come to the land of Gennesaret.
When the people of that place recognized him, dem sent into all that surrounding region, and bring to him all who were sick;
and dem begged him that dem might just touch the fringe of his garment. As many as touched it were made whole.
Then Pharisees and scribes come to Jesus from Jerusalem, saying,
“Why do una disciples disobey the tradition of the elders? For dem no wash dem hands when dem eat bread.”
He answer dem, “Why do you also disobey the commandment of God because of una tradition?
For God commanded, ‘Honor una father and una mother,’ and, ‘Person wey speaks evil of father or mother, Make e be put to death.’
But you say, ‘Anybody wey may tell his father or his mother, “Anything wey help you might otherwise have gotten from me is a gift devoted to God,”
he no go honor his father or mother.’ You have made the commandment of God void because of una tradition.
You fake people! Well did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying,
‘These people draw near to me with dem mouth, and honor me with dem lips; but dem heart is far from me.
And in vain do dem worship me, teaching as doctrine rules made by men.’”
He summoned the plenty people, and talk say to dem, “Hear, and understand.
That which enters into the mouth no dey defile the man; but that which proceeds out of the mouth, this defiles the man.”
Then the disciples come, and talk say to him, “Do you know that the Pharisees were offended, when dem heard this saying?”
But he answer, “Every plant which my heavenly Father didn’t plant Go be uprooted.
Leave dem alone. Dem be blind guides of the blind. If the blind guide the blind, both will fall into a pit.”
Peter answer him, “Explain the parable to us.”
So Jesus talk say, “Do you also still not understand?
No you understand that Anything wey goes into the mouth passes into the belly, and then out of the body?
But the things which proceed out of the mouth come out of the heart, and dem defile the man.
For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual sins, thefts, false testimony, and blasphemies.
These are the things which defile the man; but to eat with unwashed hands no dey defile the man.”
Jesus go out from there, and withdrew into the region of Tyre and Sidon.
See am, a Canaanite woman come out from those borders, and cried, saying, “Have mercy on me, Lord, you son of David! My daughter is severely possessed by a demon!”
But he answer her not a word. His disciples come and begged him, saying, “Send her away; for she cries after us.”
But he answer, “I no be sent to anyone but the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
But she come and worshiped him, saying, “Lord, help me.”
But he answer, “It No be appropriate to take the pikin dem’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
But she talk say, “Yes, Lord, but even the dogs eat the crumbs which fall from dem masters’ table.”
Then Jesus answer her, “Woman, great is una faith! Be it done to you even as you desire.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.
Jesus comot there, and come near to the sea of Galilee; and he go up into the mountain, and sat there.
Plenty people come to him, having with dem the lame, blind, mute, maimed, and many others, and dem put dem down at his feet. He healed dem,
so that the plenty people wondered when dem see the mute speaking, the injured healed, the lame walking, and the blind seeing — and dem glorified the God of Israel.

Jesus summoned his disciples and talk say, “I have compassion on the plenty people, because dem continue with me now three days and have nothing to eat. I no want to send dem away fasting, or dem might faint on the way.”
The disciples talk say to him, “Where should we get so many loaves in a deserted place as to satisfy so great a plenty people?”
Jesus tell dem say, “How many loaves do you have?” Dem talk say, “Seven, and a few small fish.”
He commanded the plenty people to sit down on the ground;
and he take the seven loaves and the fish. He Thank God and broke dem, and give to the disciples, and the disciples to the plenty people.
Dem all ate, and were filled. Dem take up seven baskets full of the broken pieces that were left over.
People wey ate were four thousand men, besides women and pikin dem.
Then he sent away the plenty people, got into the boat, and come into the borders of Magdala.
The Pharisees and Sadducees come, and testing him, ask him to show dem a sign from heaven.
But he answer dem, “When it is evening, you say, ‘It Go be fair weather, for the sky is red.’
In the morning, ‘It Go be foul weather today, for the sky is red and threatening.’ Fake people! You know how to discern the appearance of the sky, but you no fit discern the signs of the times!
An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, and there Go be no sign given to it, except the sign of the prophet Jonah.” He left dem, and comot.
The disciples come to the other side and had forgotten to take bread.
Jesus tell dem say, “Take heed and beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
Dem reasoned among themselves, saying, “We bring no bread.”
Jesus, perceiving it, talk say, “Why do you reason among unaself, you of little faith, ‘because you have bring no bread?’
No you yet perceive, neither remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you take up?
Nor the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many baskets you take up?
How is it that you no perceive that I didn’t speak to you concerning bread? But beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
Then dem understand that he didn’t tell dem to beware of the yeast of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
Now when Jesus come into the parts of Caesarea Philippi, he ask his disciples, saying, “Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?”
Dem talk say, “Some say John the Baptizer, some, Elijah, and others, Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.”
E tell dem say, “But who do you say that I be?”
Simon Peter answer, “You be the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
Jesus answer him, “Blessed are you, Simon Bar Jonah, for flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father Wey be in heaven.
I also tell you that You be Peter, and on this rock I go build my assembly, and the gates of Hades No go prevail against it.
I go give to you the keys of God kingdom for heaven, and Anything wey you bind on earth Go get been bound in heaven; and Anything wey you release on earth Go get been released in heaven.”
Then he commanded the disciples that dem should tell Nobody that he was Jesus the Christ.
From that time, Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.
Peter take him aside, and began to rebuke him, saying, “Far be it from you, Lord! This will never be done to you.”
But he turned, and talk say to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan! You be a stumbling block to me, for you No be setting una mind on the things of God, but on the things of men.”
Then Jesus talk say to his disciples, “If anyone desires to come after me, Make e deny imself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
For Anybody wey desires to save his life will lose it, and Anybody wey will lose his life for my sake will find it.
For what will it profit a man, if he gains the whole world, and forfeits his life? Or what will a man give in exchange for his life?
For the Son of Man will come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will render to everyone according to his deeds.
True true, I tell una, E get some standing here who will in no way taste of death, until dem see the Son of Man coming in his Kingdom.”
After six days, Jesus take with him Peter, James, and John his brother, and bring dem up into a high mountain by themselves.
He was transfigured before dem. His face shone like the sun, and his garments became as white as the light.
See am, Moses and Elijah appeared to dem talking with him.
Peter answer, and talk say to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you want, let’s make three tents here: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
While he was still speaking, see am, a bright cloud overshadowed dem. See am, a voice come out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I be well pleased. Listen to him.”
When the disciples heard it, dem fell on dem faces, and were very afraid.
Jesus come and touched dem and talk say, “Get up, and No fear.”
Lifting up dem eyes, dem see Nobody, except Jesus alone.
As dem were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded dem, saying, “No tell anyone Wetin you see, until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.”
His disciples ask him, saying, “Then why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
Jesus answer dem, “Elijah indeed comes first, and will restore all things,
but I tell una that Elijah has come already, and dem didn’t recognize him, but did to him Anything wey dem want to. Even so the Son of Man will also suffer by dem.”
Then the disciples understand that he spoke to dem of John the Baptizer.
When dem come to the plenty people, a man come to him, kneeling down to him, and saying,
“Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is epileptic, and suffers grievously; for he often falls into the fire, and often into the water.
So I bring him to una disciples, and dem could not cure him.”
Jesus answer, “Faithless and perverse generation! How long will I be with you? How long will I bear with you? Bring him here to me.”
Jesus rebuked him, the demon go out of him, and the boy was cured from that hour.
Then the disciples come to Jesus privately, and talk say, “Why no be we able to throw it out?”

E tell dem say, “Because of una unbelief. For True true, I tell una, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, You go tell this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing Go be impossible for you.
But this kind no dey go out except by prayer and fasting.”
While dem were staying in Galilee, Jesus tell dem say, “The Son of Man is about to be delivered up into the hands of men,
and Dem go kill him, and the third day he Go be raised up.” Dem were exceedingly sorry.
When dem had come to Capernaum, people wey collected the didrachma coins come to Peter, and talk say, “No dey una teacher pay the didrachma?”

He talk say, “Yes.” When he come into the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth receive toll or tribute? From dem pikin dem, or from strangers?”
Peter talk say to him, “From strangers.” Jesus tell am say, “So the pikin dem are exempt.

But, lest we cause dem to stumble, go to the sea, throw a hook, and take up the first fish that comes up. When you have opened its mouth, You go find a stater coin. Take that, and give it to dem for me and you.”
In that hour the disciples come to Jesus, saying, “Who then is greatest in God kingdom for heaven?”
Jesus call a little pikin to imself, and set him in the middle of dem,
and talk say, “True true, I tell una, unless you turn, and become as little pikin dem, You go in no way enter into God kingdom for heaven.
Anybody wey so humbles imself as this little pikin, the same is the greatest in God kingdom for heaven.
Anybody wey receives one such little pikin in my name receives me,

but Anybody wey causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him that a huge millstone should be hung around his neck, and that he should be sunk in the depths of the sea.
“Woe to the world because of occasions of stumbling! For it must be that the occasions come, but woe to that person through whom the occasion comes!

If una hand or una foot causes you to stumble, cut it off, and throw it from you. It is better for you to enter into life maimed or crippled, rather than having two hands or two feet to be throw into the eternal fire.
If una eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out, and throw it from you. It is better for you to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be throw into the Gehenna of fire.
See that you no despise one of these little ones, for I tell una that in heaven dem angels always see the face of my Father Wey be in heaven.
For the Son of Man come to save that which was lost.
“What do you think? If a man has one hundred sheep, and one of dem goes astray, no dey he leave the ninety-nine, go to the mountains, and seek that which has gone astray?
If he finds it, True true, I tell una, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine which have not gone astray.
Even so it No be the will of una Father Wey be in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.
“If una brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back una brother.
But if he no dey listen, take one or two more with you, that at the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.
If he refuses to listen to dem, tell it to the assembly. If he refuses to hear the assembly also, Make e be to you as a Gentile or a tax collector.
True true, I tell una, Anything wey things you bind on earth Go get been bound in heaven, and Anything wey things you release on earth Go get been released in heaven.
Again, assuredly I tell una, that if two of You go agree on earth concerning anything that Dem go ask, it Go be done for dem by my Father Wey be in heaven.
For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I be in the middle of dem.”
Then Peter come and talk say to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?”
Jesus tell am say, “I no tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.
So God kingdom for heaven is like a certain king, who want to reconcile accounts with his workers.
When he had begun to reconcile, one was bring to him who owed him ten thousand talents.
But because he no fit pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, with his wife, his pikin dem, and all that he had, and payment to be made.
The worker so fell down and knelt before him, saying, ‘Lord, have patience with me, and I go repay you all!’
The lord of that worker, being moved with compassion, released him, and forgave him the debt.
“But that worker go out, and find one of his fellow workers, who owed him one hundred denarii, and he grabbed him, and take him by the throat, saying, ‘Pay me Wetin you owe!’
“So his fellow worker fell down at his feet and begged him, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and I go repay you!’
He would not, but go and throw him into prison, until he should pay back that which was due.
So when his fellow workers see what was done, dem were exceedingly sorry, and come and told to dem lord all that was done.
Then his lord call him in, and talk say to him, ‘You wicked worker! I forgave you all that debt, because you begged me.
Shouldn’t you also have had mercy on una fellow worker, even as I had mercy on you?’
His lord was angry, and delivered him to the tormentors, until he should pay all that was due to him.
So my heavenly Father will also do to you, if you no each forgive una brother from una hearts for his misdeeds.”
When Jesus had finished these words, he comot from Galilee, and come into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan.
Plenty people follow him, and he healed dem there.
Pharisees come to him, testing him, and saying, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?”
He answer, “Haven’t you read that person wey made dem from the beginning made dem male and female,
and talk say, ‘For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall join to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh?’
So that Dem be no more two, but one flesh. What so God has joined together, no let man tear apart.”
Dem ask him, “Why then did Moses command us to give her a bill of divorce, and divorce her?”
E tell dem say, “Moses, because of the hardness of una hearts, allowed you to divorce una wives, but from the beginning it has not been so.
I tell una that Anybody wey divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery; and person wey marries her when she is divorced commits adultery.”
His disciples talk say to him, “If this is the case of the man with his wife, it No be expedient to marry.”
But E tell dem say, “Not all men can receive this saying, but those to whom it is given.

For E get eunuchs who were born that way from dem mother’s womb, and E get eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men; and E get eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for God kingdom for heaven’s sake. Person Wey able to receive it, Make e receive it.”
Then little pikin dem were bring to him, that he should lay his hands on dem and pray; and the disciples rebuked dem.
But Jesus talk say, “Allow the little pikin dem, and no forbid dem to come to me; for God kingdom for heaven belongs to ones like these.”
He laid his hands on dem, and comot from there.
See am, one come to him and talk say, “Good teacher, what good thing shall I do, that I may have life wey no dey end?”
E tell am say, “Why do you call me good? Nobody is good but one, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.”
E tell am say, “Which ones?” Jesus talk say, “‘You no go murder.’ ‘You no go commit adultery.’ ‘You no go steal.’ ‘You no go offer false testimony.’
‘Honor una father and una mother.’ And, ‘You shall love una neighbor as yourself.’”
The young man talk say to him, “All these things I have observed from my youth. What do I still lack?”
Jesus tell am say, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell Wetin you have, and give to the poor, and You go have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”
But when the young man heard the saying, he go away sad, for he was one who had great possessions.
Jesus talk say to his disciples, “Most certainly I say to you, a rich man will enter into God kingdom for heaven with difficulty.
Again I tell una, it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye, than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”
When the disciples heard it, dem were exceedingly astonished, saying, “Who then can be saved?”
Looking at dem, Jesus talk say, “With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”
Then Peter answer, “See am, we have left everything, and follow you. What then will we have?”

Jesus tell dem say, “True true, I tell una that you who have follow me, in the regeneration when the Son of Man will sit on the throne of his glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

Everybody wey has left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or pikin dem, or lands, for my name’s sake, will receive one hundred times, and will inherit life wey no dey end.
But many Go be last Wey be first; and first Wey be last.
“For God kingdom for heaven is like a man who was the master of a household, who go out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard.
When he had agreed with the laborers for a denarius a day, he sent dem into his vineyard.
He go out about the third hour, and see others standing idle in the marketplace.
E tell dem say, ‘You also go into the vineyard, and Anything wey is right I go give you.’ So dem go dem way.
Again he go out about the sixth and the ninth hour, and did likewise.
About the eleventh hour he go out, and find others standing idle. E tell dem say, ‘Why do you stand here all day idle?’
“Dem tell am say, ‘Because Nobody has hired us.’ “E tell dem say, ‘You also go into the vineyard, and You go receive Anything wey is right.’
When evening had come, the lord of the vineyard talk say to his manager, ‘Call the laborers and pay dem dem wages, beginning from the last to the first.’
“When people wey were hired at about the eleventh hour come, dem each received a denarius.
When the first come, dem supposed that dem would receive more; and dem likewise each received a denarius.
When dem received it, dem murmured against the master of the household,
saying, ‘These last have spent one hour, and you have made dem equal to us, who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat!’
“But he answer one of dem, ‘Friend, I be doing you no wrong. Didn’t you agree with me for a denarius?
Take that which is yours, and go una way. It is my desire to give to this last just as much as to you.
No be it lawful for me to do what I want to with what I own? Or is una eye evil, because I be good?’
So the last Go be first, and the first last. For many are call, but few are chosen.”
As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he take the twelve disciples aside, and on the way E tell dem say,
“See am, We be going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man Go be delivered to the chief priests and scribes, and Dem go condemn him to death,
and will hand him over to the Gentiles to mock, to scourge, and to crucify; and the third day he Go be raised up.”
Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee come to him with her sons, kneeling and asking a certain thing of him.
E tell am say, “What do you want?” She talk say to him, “Command that these, my two sons, may sit, one on una right hand, and one on una left hand, in una Kingdom.”
But Jesus answer, “You no know Wetin You be asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I be about to drink, and be baptized with the baptism that I be baptized with?” Dem tell am say, “We be able.”

E tell dem say, “You go indeed drink my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I be baptized with, but to sit on my right hand and on my left hand No be mine to give; but it is for whom it Don dey prepared by my Father.”
When the ten heard it, dem were indignant with the two brothers.
But Jesus summoned dem, and talk say, “You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over dem, and dem great ones exercise authority over dem.
It no go be so among you, but Anybody wey desires to become great among you go be una worker.
Anybody wey desires to be first among you go be una bondservant,
even as the Son of Man come not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
As dem go out from Jericho, Plenty people follow him.
See am, two blind men sitting by the road, when dem heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out, “Lord, have mercy on us, you son of David!”
The plenty people rebuked dem, telling dem that dem should be quiet, but dem cried out even more, “Lord, have mercy on us, you son of David!”
Jesus stood still, and call dem, and ask, “What do you want me to do for you?”
Dem told him, “Lord, that our eyes may be opened.”
