Jesus, being moved with compassion, touched dem eyes; and sharp-sharp dem eyes received dem sight, and dem follow him.
When dem come near to Jerusalem, and come to Bethsphage, to the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,
saying to dem, “Go into the village that is opposite you, and sharp-sharp You go find a donkey tied, and a colt with her. Untie dem, and bring dem to me.
If anyone says anything to you, you shall say, ‘The Lord needs dem,’ and sharp-sharp he will send dem.”
All this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying,
“Tell the daughter of Zion, see am, una King comes to you, humble, and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.”
The disciples go, and did just as Jesus commanded dem,
and bring the donkey and the colt, and laid dem clothes on dem; and he sat on dem.
A plenty well-well plenty people spread dem clothes on the road. Others cut branches from the trees, and spread dem on the road.
The plenty people who go in front of him, and people wey follow, kept shouting, “Hosanna to the son of David! Blessed is person wey comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”
When he had come into Jerusalem, all the city was stirred up, saying, “Wey be this?”
The plenty people talk say, “This is the prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.”
Jesus entered into the temple of God, and drove out all of people wey sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the money changers’ tables and the seats of people wey sold the doves.
E tell dem say, “It is written, ‘My house go be call a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a den of robbers!”
The blind and the lame come to him in the temple, and he healed dem.
But when the chief priests and the scribes see the wonderful things that he did, and the pikin dem who were crying in the temple and saying, “Hosanna to the son of David!” dem were indignant,
and talk say to him, “Do you hear what these are saying?” Jesus tell dem say, “Yes. Did you never read, ‘Out of the mouth of babes and nursing babies you have perfected praise?’”
He left dem, and go out of the city to Bethany, and camped there.
Now in the morning, as he come back to the city, he was hungry.
Seeing a fig tree by the road, he come to it, and find nothing on it but leaves. He talk say to it, “Let there be no fruit from you forever!” Sharp-sharp the fig tree withered away.
When the disciples see it, dem surprise well-well, saying, “How did the fig tree sharp-sharp wither away?”

Jesus answer dem, “True true, I tell una, if you have faith, and no doubt, You go not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you told this mountain, ‘Be taken up and throw into the sea,’ it would be done.
All things, Anything wey you ask in prayer, believing, You go receive.”
When he had come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people come to him as he was teaching, and talk say, “By what authority do you do these things? Who give you this authority?”
Jesus answer dem, “I also will ask you one question, which if you tell me, I likewise will tell you by what authority I do these things.
The baptism of John, where was it from? From heaven or from men?” Dem reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will ask us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
But if we say, ‘From men,’ we fear the plenty people, for all hold John as a prophet.”
Dem answer Jesus, and talk say, “We no know.” He also talk say to dem, “Neither will I tell una by what authority I do these things.
But what do you think? A man had two sons, and he come to the first, and talk say, ‘Son, go work today in my vineyard.’
He answer, ‘I go not,’ but afterward he changed his mind, and go.
He come to the second, and talk say the same thing. He answer, ‘I go, sir,’ but he didn’t go.

Which of the two did the will of his father?” Dem tell am say, “The first.” Jesus tell dem say, “True true, I tell una that the tax collectors and the prostitutes are entering into God’s Kingdom before you.

For John come to you in the way of righteousness, and you didn’t believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believe him. When you see it, you didn’t even repent afterward, that you might believe him.

“Hear another parable. There was a man who was a master of a household, who planted a vineyard, set a hedge about it, dug a wine press in it, built a tower, leased it out to farmers, and go into another country.
When the season for the fruit come near, he sent his workers to the farmers, to receive his fruit.
The farmers take his workers, beat one, killed another, and stoned another.
Again, he sent other workers more than the first: and dem treated dem the same way.
But afterward he sent to dem his son, saying, ‘Dem go respect my son.’
But the farmers, when dem see the son, talk say among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, and seize his inheritance.’
So dem take him, and threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him.
When so the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?”
Dem told him, “He will miserably destroy those miserable men, and will lease out the vineyard to other farmers, who will give him the fruit in its season.”
Jesus tell dem say, “Did you never read in the Scriptures, ‘The stone which the builders rejected, the same was made the head of the corner. This was from the Lord. It is marvelous in our eyes?’
“So I tell una, God’s Kingdom Go be taken away from you, and Go be given to a nation producing its fruit.
Person wey falls on this stone Go be broken to pieces, but on whomever it will fall, it will scatter him as dust.”
When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, dem perceived that he spoke about dem.
When dem sought to seize him, dem feared the plenty people, because dem considered him to be a prophet.
Jesus answer and spoke again in parables to dem, saying,
“God kingdom for heaven is like a certain king, who made a marriage feast for his son,
and sent out his workers to call people wey were invited to the marriage feast, but dem would not come.
Again he sent out other workers, saying, ‘Tell people Wey invited, “See am, I have prepared my dinner. My cattle and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready. Come to the marriage feast!”’
But dem made light of it, and go dem ways, one to his own farm, another to his merchandise,
and the rest grabbed his workers, and treated dem shamefully, and killed dem.
When the king heard that, he was angry, and sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned dem city.
“Then he talk say to his workers, ‘The wedding is ready, but people wey were invited no be worthy.
Go so to the intersections of the highways, and as many as you may find, invite to the marriage feast.’
Those workers go out into the highways, and gathered together as many as dem find, both bad and good. The wedding was filled with guests.
But when the king come in to see the guests, he see there a man who didn’t have on wedding clothing,
and E tell am say, ‘Friend, how did you come in here not wearing wedding clothing?’ He was speechless.
Then the king talk say to the workers, ‘Bind him hand and foot, take him away, and throw him into the outer darkness; E get where the weeping and grinding of teeth Go be.’
For many are call, but few chosen.”
Then the Pharisees go and take counsel how dem might entrap him in his talk.
Dem sent dem disciples to him, along with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that You be honest, and teach the way of God in truth, no matter whom you teach, for you no be partial to anyone.
Tell us so, what do you think? Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”
But Jesus perceived dem wickedness, and talk say, “Why do you test me, you fake people?
Show me the tax money.” Dem bring to him a denarius.
He ask dem, “Whose is this image and inscription?”
Dem tell am say, “Caesar’s.” Then E tell dem say, “Give so to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
When dem heard it, dem surprise well-well, and left him, and go away.
On that day Sadducees (people wey say that E get no resurrection) come to him. Dem ask him,
saying, “Teacher, Moses talk say, ‘If a man dies, having no pikin dem, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up offspring for his brother.’
Now there were with us seven brothers. The first married and died, and having no offspring left his wife to his brother.
In the same way, the second also, and the third, to the seventh.
After dem all, the woman died.
In the resurrection so, whose wife will she be of the seven? For dem all had her.”
But Jesus answer dem, “You be mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God.
For in the resurrection dem neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are like God’s angels in heaven.
But concerning the resurrection of the dead, haven’t you read that which was spoken to you by God, saying,
‘I be the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?’ God No be the God of the dead, but of the living.”
When the plenty people heard it, dem were astonished at his teaching.
But the Pharisees, when dem heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, gathered themselves together.
One of dem, a lawyer, ask him a question, testing him.
“Teacher, which is the greatest commandment in the law?”
Jesus tell am say, “‘You shall love the Lord una God with all una heart, with all una soul, and with all una mind.’
This is the first and great commandment.
A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love una neighbor as yourself.’
The whole law and the prophets depend on these two commandments.”
Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus ask dem a question,
saying, “What do you think of the Christ? Whose son is he?” Dem tell am say, “Of David.”
E tell dem say, “How then does David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying,
‘The Lord talk say to my Lord, sit on my right hand, until I make una enemies a footstool for una feet?’
“If then David calls him Lord, how is he his son?”
Nobody was able to answer him a word, neither did any man dare ask him any more questions from that day forward.
Then Jesus spoke to the plenty people and to his disciples,
saying, “The scribes and the Pharisees sat on Moses’ seat.
All things so Anything wey dem tell you to observe, observe and do, but no do dem works; for dem say, and no do.
For dem bind heavy burdens that are grievous to be borne, and lay dem on men’s shoulders; but dem themselves No go lift a finger to help dem.
But all dem works dem do to be seen by men. Dem make dem phylacteries broad, enlarge the fringes of dem garments,
and love the place of honor at feasts, the best seats in the synagogues,
the salutations in the marketplaces, and to be call ‘Rabbi, Rabbi’ by men.
But no you be call ‘Rabbi,’ for one is una teacher, the Christ, and all of You be brothers.
Call no man on the earth una father, for one is una Father, person Wey in heaven.
Neither be call masters, for one is una master, the Christ.
But person Wey greatest among You go be una worker.
Anybody wey exalts imself Go be humbled, and Anybody wey humbles imself Go be exalted.
“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, fake people! For you devour widows’ houses, and as a pretense you make long prayers. So You go receive greater condemnation.
“But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, fake people! Because you shut up God kingdom for heaven against men; for you no enter in unaself, neither do you allow people Wey entering in to enter.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, fake people! For you travel around by sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much of a son of Gehenna as unaself.
“Woe to you, you blind guides, who say, ‘Anybody wey swears by the temple, it is nothing; but Anybody wey swears by the gold of the temple, he is obligated.’
You blind fools! For which is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifies the gold?
‘Anybody wey swears by the altar, it is nothing; but Anybody wey swears by the gift that is on it, he is obligated?’
You blind fools! For which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifies the gift?
He so who swears by the altar, swears by it, and by everything on it.
Person wey swears by the temple, swears by it, and by him who was living in it.
Person wey swears by heaven, swears by the throne of God, and by him who sits on it.

“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, fake people! For you tithe mint, dill, and cumin, and have left undone the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faith. But you ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.
You blind guides, who strain out a gnat, and swallow a camel!
“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, fake people! For you clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within Dem be full of extortion and unrighteousness.
You blind Pharisee, first clean the inside of the cup and of the platter, that its outside may become clean also.
“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, fake people! For You be like whitened tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.
Even so you also outwardly appear righteous to men, but inwardly You be full of hypocrisy and wickedness.
“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, fake people! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and decorate the tombs of the righteous,
and say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we wouldn’t Don dey partakers with dem in the blood of the prophets.’
So you testify to unaself that You be pikin dem of people wey killed the prophets.
Fill up, then, the measure of una fathers.
You serpents, you offspring of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of Gehenna?
So see am, I send to you prophets, wise men, and scribes. Some of dem You go kill and crucify; and some of dem You go scourge in una synagogues, and persecute from city to city;
that on you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zachariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the sanctuary and the altar.
True true, I tell una, all these things will come upon this generation.

“Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets, and stones people Wey sent to her! How often I would have gathered una pikin dem together, even as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not!
See am, una house is left to you desolate.
For I tell una, You go not see me from now on, until you say, ‘Blessed is person wey comes in the name of the Lord!’”
Jesus go out from the temple, and was going on his way. His disciples come to him to show him the buildings of the temple.
But he answer dem, “You see all of these things, no you? True true, I tell una, there No go be left here one stone on another, that No go be thrown down.”
As he sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples come to him privately, saying, “Tell us, when will these things be? Wetin be the sign of una coming, and of the end of the age?”
Jesus answer dem, “Be careful that Nobody leads you astray.
For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I be the Christ,’ and will lead many astray.
You go hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you no be troubled, for all this must happen, but the end No be yet.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; and there Go be famines, plagues, and earthquakes in various places.
But all these things are the beginning of birth pains.
Then Dem go deliver you up to oppression, and will kill you. You go be hated by all of the nations for my name’s sake.
Then many will stumble, and will deliver up each other, and will hate each other.
Many false prophets will arise, and will lead many astray.
Because wickedness Go be multiplied, the love of many will grow cold.
But person wey endures to the end, the same Go be saved.
This Better news of the Kingdom Go be preached in the whole world for a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.
“When, so, you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place (let the reader understand),
then let people Wey in Judea flee to the mountains.
Make e Wey be on the housetop not go down to take out the things that are in his house.
Make e Wey be in the field not return back to get his clothes.
But woe to people Wey with pikin and to nursing mothers in those days!
Pray that una flight No go be in the winter, nor on a Sabbath,
for then there Go be great oppression, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, no, nor ever Go be.
Unless those days Bin dey shortened, no flesh would Don dey saved. But for the sake of the chosen ones, those days Go be shortened.
“Then if any man tells you, ‘See am, here is the Christ,’ or, ‘There,’ no believe it.
For there will arise false christs, and false prophets, and Dem go show great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
“See am, I have told you beforehand.
If so dem tell you, ‘See am, he is in the wilderness,’ no go out; ‘See am, he is in the inner rooms,’ no believe it.
For as the lightning flashes from the east, and is seen even to the west, so Go be the coming of the Son of Man.
For Anywhere wey the carcass is, E get where the vultures gather together.
But sharp-sharp after the oppression of those days, the sun Go be darkened, the moon No go give its light, the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens Go be shaken;
and then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. Then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and Dem go see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky with power and great glory.
He will send out his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and Dem go gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the sky to the other.
“Now from the fig tree learn this parable. When its branch has now become tender, and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near.
Even so you also, when you see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.
True true, I tell una, this generation No go pass away, until all these things are accomplished.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words No go pass away.
But Nobody knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, but my Father only.
“As the days of Noah were, so Go be the coming of the Son of Man.
For as in those days which were before the flood dem were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ship,
and dem didn’t know until the flood come, and take dem all away, so Go be the coming of the Son of Man.
Then two men Go be in the field: one Go be taken and one Go be left;
two women grinding at the mill, one Go be taken and one Go be left.
Watch so, for you no know in what hour una Lord comes.
But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have watched, and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
So also be ready, for in an hour that you no expect, the Son of Man will come.
“Who then is the faithful and wise worker, whom his lord has set over his household, to give dem dem chop in due season?
Blessed is that worker whom his lord finds doing so when he comes.
True true, I tell una that he will set him over all that he has.
But if that evil worker should say in his heart, ‘My lord is delaying his coming,’
and begins to beat his fellow workers, and eat and drink with the drunkards,
the lord of that worker will come in a day when he no dey expect it, and in an hour when he no dey know it,
and will cut him in pieces, and appoint his portion with the fake people. E get where the weeping and grinding of teeth Go be.
“Then God kingdom for heaven Go be like ten virgins, who take dem lamps, and go out to meet the bridegroom.
Five of dem were foolish, and five were wise.
People wey were foolish, when dem take dem lamps, take no oil with dem,
but the wise take oil in dem vessels with dem lamps.
Now while the bridegroom delayed, dem all slumbered and slept.
But at midnight there was a cry, ‘See am! The bridegroom is coming! Come out to meet him!’
Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed dem lamps.
The foolish talk say to the wise, ‘Give us some of una oil, for our lamps are going out.’
But the wise answer, saying, ‘What if there no be enough for us and you? You go rather to people wey sell, and buy for unaself.’
While dem go away to buy, the bridegroom come, and people wey were ready go in with him to the marriage feast, and the door was shut.
Afterward the other virgins also come, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us.’
But he answer, ‘True true, I tell una, I no know you.’
Watch so, for you no know the day nor the hour in which the Son of Man is coming.
“For it is like a man, going into another country, who call his own workers, and entrusted his goods to dem.
To one he give five talents, to another two, to another one; to each according to his own ability. Then he go on his journey.
Sharp-sharp person wey received the five talents go and traded with dem, and made another five talents.
In the same way, he also who got the two gained another two.
But person wey received the one talent go away and dug in the earth, and hid his lord’s money.
“Now after a long time the lord of those workers come, and reconciled accounts with dem.
Person wey received the five talents come and bring another five talents, saying, ‘Lord, you delivered to me five talents. See am, I have gained another five talents besides dem.’
“His lord talk say to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful worker. You Don dey faithful over a few things, I go set you over many things. Enter into the gladness of una lord.’
“He also who got the two talents come and talk say, ‘Lord, you delivered to me two talents. See am, I have gained another two talents besides dem.’
“His lord talk say to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful worker. You Don dey faithful over a few things, I go set you over many things. Enter into the gladness of una lord.’
“He also who had received the one talent come and talk say, ‘Lord, I know you that You be a hard man, reaping where you No sow, and gathering where you No scatter.
I was afraid, and go away and hid una talent in the earth. See am, you have Wetin be yours.’
“But his lord answer him, ‘You wicked and slothful worker. You know that I reap where I didn’t sow, and gather where I didn’t scatter.
You ought so to have deposited my money with the bankers, and at my coming I should have received back my own with interest.
Take away so the talent from him, and give it to him who has the ten talents.
For to Everybody wey has Go be given, and he Go get abundance, but from him who no dey have, even that which he has Go be taken away.
Throw out the unprofitable worker into the outer darkness, where there Go be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’
“But when the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.
Before him all the nations Go be gathered, and he will separate dem one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
He will set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.
Then the King will tell those on his right hand, ‘Come, blessed of my Father, inherit the Kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world;
for I was hungry, and you give me chop to eat. I was thirsty, and you give me drink. I was a stranger, and you take me in.
I was naked, and you clothed me. I was sick, and you visited me. I was in prison, and you come to me.’
“Then the righteous will answer him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, and feed you; or thirsty, and give you a drink?
When did we see you as a stranger, and take you in; or naked, and clothe you?
When did we see you sick, or in prison, and come to you?’
“The King will answer dem, ‘True true, I tell una, because you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.’
Then he will say also to those on the left hand, ‘Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire which is prepared for the devil and his angels;
for I was hungry, and you didn’t give me chop to eat; I was thirsty, and you give me no drink;
I was a stranger, and you didn’t take me in; naked, and you didn’t clothe me; sick, and in prison, and you didn’t visit me.’
“Then Dem go also answer, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and didn’t help you?’
“Then he will answer dem, saying, ‘True true, I tell una, because you didn’t do it to one of the least of these, you didn’t do it to me.’
These will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into life wey no dey end.”
When Jesus had finished all these words, he talk say to his disciples,
“You know that after two days the Passover is coming, and the Son of Man Go be delivered up to be crucified.”
Then the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders of the people were gathered together in the court of the high priest, who was call Caiaphas.
Dem take counsel together that dem might take Jesus by deceit, and kill him.
But dem talk say, “Not during the feast, lest a riot occur among the people.”
Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
a woman come to him having an alabaster jar of very expensive ointment, and she poured it on his head as he sat at the table.
But when his disciples see this, dem were indignant, saying, “Why this waste?
For this ointment might Don dey sold for much, and given to the poor.”
However, knowing this, Jesus tell dem say, “Why do you trouble the woman? Because she has done a good work for me.
For you always have the poor with you; but you no always have me.
For in pouring this ointment on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.
True true, I tell una, Anywhere wey this Better news is preached in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be spoken of as a memorial of her.”
Then one of the twelve, who was call Judas Iscariot, go to the chief priests,
and talk say, “Wetin be you willing to give me, that I should deliver him to you?” Dem weighed out for him thirty pieces of silver.
From that time he sought opportunity to betray him.
Now on the first day of unleavened bread, the disciples come to Jesus, saying to him, “Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?”
He talk say, “Go into the city to a certain person, and tell him, ‘The Teacher says, “My time is at hand. I go keep the Passover at una house with my disciples.”’”
The disciples did as Jesus commanded dem, and dem prepared the Passover.
Now when evening had come, he was reclining at the table with the twelve disciples.
As dem were eating, he talk say, “True true, I tell una that one of You go betray me.”
Dem were exceedingly sorrowful, and each began to ask him, “It no be me, is it, Lord?”
He answer, “Person wey dipped his hand with me in the dish, the same will betray me.
The Son of Man goes, even as it is written of him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.”
Judas, who betrayed him, answer, “It no be me, is it, Rabbi?” E tell am say, “You talk say it.”
As dem were eating, Jesus take bread, Thank God for it, and broke it. He give to the disciples, and talk say, “Take, eat; this is my body.”
He take the cup, Thank God, and give to dem, saying, “All of you drink it,
for this is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the remission of sins.
But I tell una that I go not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on, until that day when I drink it anew with you in my Father’s Kingdom.”
When dem had sung a hymn, dem go out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus tell dem say, “All of You go be made to stumble because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I go strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock Go be scattered.’
But after I be raised up, I go go before you into Galilee.”
But Peter answer him, “Even if all Go be made to stumble because of you, I go never be made to stumble.”
Jesus tell am say, “True true, I tell una that tonight, before the rooster crows, You go deny me three times.”
Peter talk say to him, “Even if I must die with you, I go not deny you.” All of the disciples also talk say likewise.
Then Jesus come with dem to a place call Gethsemane, and talk say to his disciples, “Sit here, while I go there and pray.”
He take with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and severely troubled.
Then E tell dem say, “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here, and watch with me.”
He go forward a little, fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me; nevertheless, not what I desire, but Wetin you desire.”
He come to the disciples, and find dem sleeping, and talk say to Peter, “What, no fit you watch with me for one hour?
Watch and pray, that you no enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
Again, a second time he go away, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if this cup no fit pass away from me unless I drink it, una desire be done.”
He come again and find dem sleeping, for dem eyes were heavy.
He left dem again, go away, and prayed a third time, saying the same words.
Then he come to his disciples, and talk say to dem, “Sleep on now, and take una rest. See am, the hour is at hand, and the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
Arise, let’s be going. See am, person wey betrays me is at hand.”
While he was still speaking, see am, Judas, one of the twelve, come, and with him Plenty people with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
Now person wey betrayed him give dem a sign, saying, “Anybody wey I kiss, he is the one. Seize him.”
Sharp-sharp he come to Jesus, and talk say, “Hail, Rabbi!” and kissed him.
Jesus tell am say, “Friend, why are you here?” Then dem come and laid hands on Jesus, and take him.
See am, one of people wey were with Jesus stretched out his hand, and drew his sword, and struck the worker of the high priest, and struck off his ear.
Then Jesus tell am say, “Put una sword back into its place, for all people wey take the sword will die by the sword.
Or do you think that I no fit ask my Father, and he would even now send me more than twelve legions of angels?
How then would the Scriptures be fulfilled that it must be so?”
In that hour Jesus talk say to the plenty people, “Have you come out as against a robber with swords and clubs to seize me? I sat daily in the temple teaching, and you didn’t arrest me.
But all this has happened, that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples left him, and fled.
People wey had taken Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were gathered together.
But Peter follow him from a distance, to the court of the high priest, and entered in and sat with the officers, to see the end.
Now the chief priests, the elders, and the whole council sought false testimony against Jesus, that dem might put him to death;
and dem find none. Even though many false witnesses come forward, dem find none. But at last two false witnesses come forward,
and talk say, “This man talk say, ‘I be able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days.’”
The high priest stood up, and talk say to him, “Have you no answer? Wetin be this that these testify against you?”
But Jesus held his peace. The high priest answer him, “I adjure you by the living God, that you tell us whether You be the Christ, the Son of God.”
Jesus tell am say, “You have talk say it. Nevertheless, I tell una, after this You go see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power, and coming on the clouds of the sky.”
Then the high priest tore his clothing, saying, “He has spoken blasphemy! Why do we need any more witnesses? See am, now you have heard his blasphemy.
What do you think?” Dem answer, “He is worthy of death!”
Then dem spit in his face and beat him with dem fists, and some slapped him,
saying, “Prophesy to us, you Christ! Who hit you?”
Now Peter was sitting outside in the court, and a maid come to him, saying, “You were also with Jesus, the Galilean!”
But he denied it before dem all, saying, “I no know Wetin You be talking about.”
When he had gone out onto the porch, someone else see him, and talk say to people wey were there, “This man also was with Jesus of Nazareth.”
Again he denied it with an oath, “I no know the man.”
After a little while people wey stood by come and talk say to Peter, “Surely You be also one of dem, for una speech makes you known.”
Then he began to curse and to swear, “I no know the man!” Sharp-sharp the rooster crowed.
Peter remember the word which Jesus had talk say to him, “Before the rooster crows, You go deny me three times.” He go out and wept bitterly.
Now when morning had come, all the chief priests and the elders of the people take counsel against Jesus to put him to death:
and dem bound him, and led him away, and delivered him up to Pontius Pilate, the governor.
Then Judas, who betrayed him, when he see that Jesus was condemned, felt remorse, and bring back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,
saying, “I have sinned in that I betrayed innocent blood.” But dem talk say, “Wetin be that to us? You see to it.”
He threw down the pieces of silver in the sanctuary, and comot. He go away and hanged imself.
The chief priests take the pieces of silver, and talk say, “It’s not lawful to put dem into the treasury, since it is the price of blood.”
Dem take counsel, and bought the potter’s field with dem, to bury strangers in.
So that field was call “The Field of Blood” to this day.

Then that which was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying, “Dem take the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him upon whom a price Bin dey set, whom some of the pikin dem of Israel priced,
and dem give dem for the potter’s field, as the Lord commanded me.”
Now Jesus stood before the governor: and the governor ask him, saying, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus tell am say, “So you say.”
When he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he answer nothing.
Then Pilate talk say to him, “No you hear how many things dem testify against you?”
He give him no answer, not even one word, so that the governor surprise well-well greatly.
Now at the feast the governor was accustomed to release to the plenty people one prisoner, whom dem desired.
Dem had then a notable prisoner, call Barabbas.
When so dem were gathered together, Pilate talk say to dem, “Whom do you want me to release to you? Barabbas, or Jesus, Wey be call Christ?”
For he know that because of envy dem had delivered him up.
While he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him, saying, “Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for I have suffered many things today in a dream because of him.”
Now the chief priests and the elders persuaded the plenty people to ask for Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.
But the governor answer dem, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” Dem talk say, “Barabbas!”
Pilate talk say to dem, “What then shall I do to Jesus, Wey be call Christ?” Dem all talk say to him, “Make e be crucified!”
But the governor talk say, “Why? What evil has he done?” But dem cried out exceedingly, saying, “Make e be crucified!”

So when Pilate see that nothing was being gained, but rather that a disturbance was starting, he take water, and washed his hands before the plenty people, saying, “I be innocent of the blood of this righteous person. You see to it.”
All the people answer, “May his blood be on us, and on our pikin dem!”
Then he released to dem Barabbas, but Jesus he flogged and delivered to be crucified.
Then the governor’s soldiers take Jesus into the Praetorium, and gathered the whole garrison together against him.
Dem stripped him, and put a scarlet robe on him.
Dem braided a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand; and dem kneeled down before him, and mocked him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
Dem spat on him, and take the reed and struck him on the head.
When dem had mocked him, dem take the robe off of him, and put his clothes on him, and led him away to crucify him.
As dem come out, dem find a man of Cyrene, Simon by name, and dem compelled him to go with dem, that he might carry his cross.
When dem come to a place call “Golgotha”, that is to say, “The place of a skull,”
dem give him sour wine to drink mixed with gall. When he had tasted it, he would not drink.
When dem had crucified him, dem divided his clothing among dem, casting lots,
and dem sat and watched him there.
Dem set up over his head the accusation against him written, “THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
Then there were two robbers crucified with him, one on his right hand and one on the left.
People wey passed by blasphemed him, wagging dem heads,
and saying, “You who destroy the temple, and build it in three days, save yourself! If You be the Son of God, come down from the cross!”
Likewise the chief priests also mocking, with the scribes, the Pharisees, and the elders, talk say,
“He saved others, but he no fit save imself. If he is the King of Israel, Make e come down from the cross now, and We go believe in him.
He trusts in God. Let God deliver him now, if he wants him; for he talk say, ‘I be the Son of God.’”
The robbers also who were crucified with him throw on him the same reproach.
Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.
About the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lima sabachthani?” That is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
Some of dem who stood there, when dem heard it, talk say, “This man is calling Elijah.”
Sharp-sharp one of dem ran, and take a sponge, and filled it with vinegar, and put it on a reed, and give him a drink.
The rest talk say, “Make e be. Let’s see whether Elijah comes to save him.”
Jesus cried again with a loud voice, and yielded up his spirit.
See am, the veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom. The earth quaked and the rocks were split.
The tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised;
and coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, dem entered into the holy city and appeared to many.
Now the centurion, and people wey were with him watching Jesus, when dem see the earthquake, and the things that were done, feared exceedingly, saying, “Truly this was the Son of God.”
Many women were there watching from far away, who had follow Jesus from Galilee, serving him.
Among dem were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
When evening had come, a rich man from Arimathaea, named Joseph, who imself was also Jesus’ disciple come.
This man go to Pilate, and ask for Jesus’ body. Then Pilate commanded the body to be given up.
Joseph take the body, and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut out in the rock, and he rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb, and comot.
Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the tomb.
Now on the next day, which was the day after the Preparation Day, the chief priests and the Pharisees were gathered together to Pilate,
saying, “Sir, we remember what that deceiver talk say while he was still alive: ‘After three days I go rise again.’

Command so that the tomb be made secure until the third day, lest perhaps his disciples come at night and steal him away, and tell the people, ‘He is risen from the dead;’ and the last deception Go be worse than the first.”
Pilate talk say to dem, “You have a guard. Go, make it as secure as you can.”
So dem go with the guard and made the tomb secure, sealing the stone.
Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary come to see the tomb.
See am, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from the sky, and come and rolled away the stone from the door, and sat on it.
His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing white as snow.
For fear of him, the guards shook, and became like dead men.
The angel answer the women, “No fear, for I know that you seek Jesus, who Don dey crucified.
He No be here, for he has risen, just like he talk say. Come, see the place where the Lord was lying.
Go sharp-sharp and tell his disciples, ‘He has risen from the dead, and see am, he goes before you into Galilee; there You go see him.’ See am, I have told you.”
Dem comot sharp-sharp from the tomb with fear and great gladness, and ran to bring his disciples word.
As dem go to tell his disciples, see am, Jesus met dem, saying, “Glad well-well!” Dem come and take hold of his feet, and worshiped him.
Then Jesus tell dem say, “No fear. Go tell my brothers that dem should go into Galilee, and there Dem go see me.”
Now while dem were going, see am, some of the guards come into the city, and told the chief priests all the things that had happened.
When dem were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel, dem give a large amount of silver to the soldiers,
saying, “Say that his disciples come by night, and stole him away while we slept.
If this comes to the governor’s ears, We go persuade him and make you free of worry.”
So dem take the money and did as dem were told. This saying was spread abroad among the Jews, and continues until today.
But the eleven disciples go into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent dem.
When dem see him, dem bowed down to him, but some doubted.
Jesus come to dem and spoke to dem, saying, “All authority Don dey given to me in heaven and on earth.
Go, and make disciples of people for everywhere, baptizing dem in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
teaching dem to observe all things that I commanded you. See am, I be with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
The beginning of the Better news of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
As it is written in the prophets, “See am, I send my messenger before una face, who will prepare una way before you:
the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make ready the way of the Lord! Make his paths straight!’”
John come baptizing in the wilderness and preaching the baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.
All the country of Judea and all those of Jerusalem go out to him. Dem were baptized by him in the Jordan river, confessing dem sins.
John was clothed with camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts and wild honey.
He preached, saying, “After me comes person Wey mightier than I, the thong of whose sandals I be not worthy to stoop down and loosen.
I baptized you in water, but he will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.”
In those days, Jesus come from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
Sharp-sharp coming up from the water, he see the heavens parting, and the Spirit descending on him like a dove.
A voice come out of the sky, “You be my beloved Son, in whom I be well pleased.”
Sharp-sharp the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness.
He was there in the wilderness forty days tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals; and the angels were serving him.
Now after John was taken into custody, Jesus come into Galilee, preaching the Better news of God’s Kingdom,
and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Better news.”
Passing along by the sea of Galilee, he see Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting a net into the sea, for dem were fishermen.
Jesus tell dem say, “Come after me, and I go make you into fishers for men.”
Sharp-sharp dem left dem nets, and follow him.
Going on a little further from there, he see James the son of Zebedee, and John, his brother, who were also in the boat mending the nets.
Sharp-sharp he call dem, and dem left dem father, Zebedee, in the boat with the hired workers, and go after him.
Dem go into Capernaum, and sharp-sharp on the Sabbath day he entered into the synagogue and taught.
Dem were astonished at his teaching, for he taught dem as having authority, and No be like the scribes.
Sharp-sharp there was in dem synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
saying, “Ha! What do we have to do with you, Jesus, you Nazarene? Have you come to destroy us? I know you who You be: the Holy One of God!”
Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be quiet, and come out of him!”
The unclean spirit, convulsing him and crying with a loud voice, come out of him.
Dem were all amazed, so that dem questioned among themselves, saying, “Wetin be this? A new teaching? For with authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and dem obey him!”
The report of him go out sharp-sharp everywhere into all the region of Galilee and its surrounding area.
Sharp-sharp, when dem had come out of the synagogue, dem come into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
Now Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick with a fever, and sharp-sharp dem told him about her.
He come and take her by the hand, and raised her up. The fever left her, and she served dem.
At evening, when the sun had set, dem bring to him all who were sick, and people wey were possessed by demons.
All the city was gathered together at the door.
He healed many who were sick with various diseases, and throw out many demons. He didn’t allow the demons to speak, because dem know him.
Early in the morning, while it was still dark, he rose up and go out, and comot into a deserted place, and prayed there.
Simon and people wey were with him follow after him;
and dem find him, and told him, “Everyone is looking for you.”
E tell dem say, “Let’s go elsewhere into the next towns, that I may preach there also, because I come out for this reason.”
He go into dem synagogues throughout all Galilee, preaching and casting out demons.
A leper come to him, begging him, kneeling down to him, and saying to him, “If you want to, you can make me clean.”
Being moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand, and touched him, and talk say to him, “I want to. Be made clean.”
When he had talk say this, sharp-sharp the leprosy comot from him, and he was made clean.
He strictly warned him, and sharp-sharp sent him out,
and talk say to him, “See you say nothing to anybody, but go show yourself to the priest, and offer for una cleansing the things which Moses commanded, for a testimony to dem.”

But he go out, and began to proclaim it much, and to spread about the matter, so that Jesus could no more openly enter into a city, but was outside in desert places: and dem come to him from everywhere.
When he entered again into Capernaum after some days, it was heard that he was in the house.
Sharp-sharp many were gathered together, so that there was no more room, not even around the door; and he spoke the word to dem.
Four people come, carrying a paralytic to him.
When dem could not come near to him for the crowd, dem removed the roof where he was. When dem had broken it up, dem let down the mat that the paralytic was lying on.
Jesus, seeing dem faith, talk say to the paralytic, “Son, una sins are forgiven you.”
But there were some of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in dem hearts,
“Why does this man speak blasphemies like that? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
Sharp-sharp Jesus, perceiving in his spirit that dem so reasoned within themselves, talk say to dem, “Why do you reason these things in una hearts?
Which is easier, to tell the paralytic, ‘Una sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Arise, and take up una bed, and walk?’
But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins” — he talk say to the paralytic —
“I tell una, arise, take up una mat, and go to una house.”
He arose, and sharp-sharp take up the mat, and go out in front of dem all; so that dem were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, “We never see anything like this!”
He go out again by the seaside. All the plenty people come to him, and he taught dem.
As he passed by, he see Levi, the son of Alphaeus, sitting at the tax office, and E tell am say, “Follow me.” And he arose and follow him.
He was reclining at the table in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners sat down with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many, and dem follow him.
The scribes and the Pharisees, when dem see that he was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, talk say to his disciples, “Why is it that he eats and drinks with tax collectors and sinners?”
When Jesus heard it, E tell dem say, “People Wey healthy have no need for a physician, but people Wey sick. I come not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting, and dem come and ask him, “Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but una disciples no fast?”
Jesus tell dem say, “Can the groomsmen fast while the bridegroom is with dem? As long as dem have the bridegroom with dem, dem no fit fast.
But the days will come when the bridegroom Go be taken away from dem, and then will dem fast in that day.
Nobody sews a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, or else the patch shrinks and the new tears away from the old, and a worse hole is made.
Nobody puts new wine into old wineskins, or else the new wine will burst the skins, and the wine pours out, and the skins Go be destroyed; but dem put new wine into fresh wineskins.”
He was going on the Sabbath day through the grain fields, and his disciples began, as dem go, to pluck the ears of grain.
The Pharisees talk say to him, “See am, why do dem do that which No be lawful on the Sabbath day?”
E tell dem say, “Did you never read what David did, when he had need, and was hungry — he, and people wey were with him?
How he entered into God’s house when Abiathar was high priest, and ate the show bread, which No be lawful to eat except for the priests, and give also to people wey were with him?”
E tell dem say, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
So the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”
He entered again into the synagogue, and there was a man there who had his hand withered.
Dem watched him, whether he would heal him on the Sabbath day, that dem might accuse him.
He talk say to the man who had his hand withered, “Stand up.”
E tell dem say, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath day to do good, or to do harm? To save a life, or to kill?” But dem were silent.

When he had looked around at dem with anger, being grieved at the hardening of dem hearts, he talk say to the man, “Stretch out una hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored as healthy as the other.
The Pharisees go out, and sharp-sharp conspired with the Herodians against him, how dem might destroy him.
Jesus withdrew to the sea with his disciples, and Plenty people follow him from Galilee, from Judea,
from Jerusalem, from Idumaea, beyond the Jordan, and those from around Tyre and Sidon. Plenty people, hearing what great things he did, come to him.
He spoke to his disciples that a little boat should stay near him because of the crowd, so that dem wouldn’t press on him.
For he had healed many, so that as many as had diseases pressed on him that dem might touch him.
The unclean spirits, whenever dem see him, fell down before him, and cried, “You be the Son of God!”
He sternly warned dem that dem no suppose make him known.
He go up into the mountain, and call to imself those whom he want, and dem go to him.
He appointed twelve, that dem might be with him, and that he might send dem out to preach,
and to have authority to heal sicknesses and to throw out demons:
Simon, to whom he give the name Peter;
James the son of Zebedee; John, the brother of James, and he call dem Boanerges, which means, Sons of Thunder;
Andrew; Philip; Bartholomew; Matthew; Thomas; James, the son of Alphaeus; Thaddaeus; Simon the Zealot;
and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him. He come into a house.
The plenty people come together again, so that dem could not so much as eat bread.
When his friends heard it, dem go out to seize him: for dem talk say, “He is insane.”
The scribes who come down from Jerusalem talk say, “He has Beelzebul,” and, “By the prince of the demons he casts out the demons.”
He summoned dem, and talk say to dem in parables, “How can Satan throw out Satan?
If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
If a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
If Satan has risen up against imself, and is divided, he no fit stand, but has an end.
But Nobody can enter into the house of the strong man to plunder, unless he first binds the strong man; and then he will plunder his house.
True true, I tell una, all sins of the descendants of man Go be forgiven, including dem blasphemies with which dem may blaspheme;
but Anybody wey may blaspheme against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is subject to eternal condemnation.”
— because dem talk say, “He has an unclean spirit.”
His mother and his brothers come, and standing outside, dem sent to him, calling him.
A plenty people was sitting around him, and dem told him, “See am, una mother, una brothers, and una sisters are outside looking for you.”
He answer dem, “Wey be my mother and my brothers?”
Looking around at people wey sat around him, he talk say, “See am, my mother and my brothers!
For Anybody wey does the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.”
Again he began to teach by the seaside. Plenty people was gathered to him, so that he entered into a boat in the sea, and sat down. All the plenty people were on the land by the sea.
He taught dem many things in parables, and told dem in his teaching,
“Listen! See am, the farmer go out to sow,
and as he sowed, some seed fell by the road, and the birds come and devoured it.
Others fell on the rocky ground, where it had little soil, and sharp-sharp it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil.
When the sun had risen, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.
Others fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
Others fell into the good ground, and yielded fruit, growing up and increasing. Some produced thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times as much.”
He talk say, “Anybody wey has ears to hear, Make e hear.”
When he was alone, people wey were around him with the twelve ask him about the parables.
E tell dem say, “To you is given the mystery of God’s Kingdom, but to people Wey outside, all things are done in parables,
that ‘seeing dem may see, and not perceive; and hearing dem may hear, and not understand; lest perhaps dem should turn again, and dem sins should be forgiven dem.’”
E tell dem say, “No you understand this parable? How will you understand all of the parables?
The farmer sows the word.
The ones by the road are the ones where the word is sown; and when dem have heard, sharp-sharp Satan comes, and takes away the word which Don dey sown in dem.
These in the same way are people Wey sown on the rocky places, who, when dem have heard the word, sharp-sharp receive it with gladness.
Dem have no root in themselves, but are short-lived. When oppression or persecution arises because of the word, sharp-sharp dem stumble.
Others are people Wey sown among the thorns. These are people wey have heard the word,
and the cares of this age, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
Those which were sown on the good ground are people wey hear the word, and accept it, and bear fruit, some thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times.”
E tell dem say, “Is the lamp bring to be put under a basket or under a bed? No be it put on a stand?
For E get nothing hidden, except that it should be made known; neither was anything made secret, but that it should come to light.
If any man has ears to hear, Make e hear.”
E tell dem say, “Take heed Wetin you hear. With Anything wey measure you measure, it Go be measured to you, and more Go be given to you who hear.
For Anybody wey has, to him will more be given, and person wey no dey have, even that which he has Go be taken away from him.”
He talk say, “God’s Kingdom is as if a man should throw seed on the earth,
and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and grow, he no dey know how.
For the earth bears fruit: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
But when the fruit is ripe, sharp-sharp he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come.”
He talk say, “How will we liken God’s Kingdom? Or with what parable will we illustrate it?
It’s like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, though it is less than all the seeds that are on the earth,
yet when it is sown, grows up, and becomes greater than all the herbs, and puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can lodge under its shadow.”
With many such parables he spoke the word to dem, as dem were able to hear it.
Without a parable he didn’t speak to dem; but privately to his own disciples he explained everything.
On that day, when evening had come, E tell dem say, “Let’s go over to the other side.”
Leaving the plenty people, dem take him with dem, even as he was, in the boat. Other small boats were also with him.
A big wind storm arose, and the waves beat into the boat, so much that the boat was already filled.
He imself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion, and dem woke him up, and told him, “Teacher, no you care that We be dying?”
He awoke, and rebuked the wind, and talk say to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
E tell dem say, “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?”
Dem were greatly afraid, and talk say to each other, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
Dem come to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.
When he had come out of the boat, sharp-sharp a man with an unclean spirit met him out of the tombs.
He lived in the tombs. Nobody could bind him any more, not even with chains,
because he Bin dey often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains Bin dey torn apart by him, and the fetters broken in pieces. Nobody had the strength to tame him.
Always, night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying out, and cutting imself with stones.
When he see Jesus from far away, he ran and bowed down to him,
and crying out with a loud voice, he talk say, “What have I to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, no torment me.”
For E tell am say, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!”
He ask him, “Wetin be una name?” E tell am say, “My name is Legion, for We be many.”
He begged him much that he would not send dem away out of the country.
Now on the mountainside there was a great herd of pigs feeding.
All the demons begged him, saying, “Send us into the pigs, that we may enter into dem.”
At once Jesus give dem permission. The unclean spirits come out and entered into the pigs. The herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea, and dem were drowned in the sea.
People wey fed dem fled, and told it in the city and in the country. The people come to see what it was that had happened.
Dem come to Jesus, and see him who Bin dey possessed by demons sitting, clothed, and in his right mind, even him who had the legion; and dem were afraid.
People wey see it declared to dem what happened to him who was possessed by demons, and about the pigs.
Dem began to beg him to depart from dem region.
As he was entering into the boat, person wey Bin dey possessed by demons begged him that he might be with him.
He didn’t allow him, but talk say to him, “Go to una house, to una friends, and tell dem what great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you.”
He go his way, and began to proclaim in Decapolis how Jesus had done great things for him, and everyone surprise well-well.
When Jesus had crossed back over in the boat to the other side, Plenty people was gathered to him; and he was by the sea.
See am, one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name, come; and seeing him, he fell at his feet,
and begged him much, saying, “My little daughter is at the point of death. Please come and lay una hands on her, that she may be made healthy, and live.”
He go with him, and Plenty people follow him, and dem pressed upon him on all sides.
A certain woman, who had an issue of blood for twelve years,
and had suffered many things by many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was no better, but rather grew worse,
having heard the things concerning Jesus, come up behind him in the crowd, and touched his clothes.
For she talk say, “If I just touch his clothes, I go be made well.”
Sharp-sharp the flow of her blood was dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of her suffering.
Sharp-sharp Jesus, perceiving in imself that the power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd, and ask, “Who touched my clothes?”
His disciples talk say to him, “You see the plenty people pressing against you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
He looked around to see her who had done this thing.
But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what Bin dey done to her, come and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.
E tell am say, “Daughter, una faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of una disease.”
While he was still speaking, people come from the synagogue ruler’s house saying, “Una daughter is dead. Why bother the Teacher any more?”
But Jesus, when he heard the message spoken, sharp-sharp talk say to the ruler of the synagogue, “No fear, only believe.”
He allowed Nobody to follow him, except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.
He come to the synagogue ruler’s house, and he see an uproar, weeping, and great wailing.
When he had entered in, E tell dem say, “Why do you make an uproar and weep? The pikin No be dead, but is asleep.”
Dem ridiculed him. But he, having put dem all out, take the father of the pikin, her mother, and people wey were with him, and go in where the pikin was lying.
Taking the pikin by the hand, E tell am say, “Talitha cumi!” which means, being interpreted, “Girl, I tell una, get up!”
Sharp-sharp the girl rose up and walked, for she was twelve years old. Dem were amazed with great amazement.
He strictly ordered dem that Nobody should know this, and commanded that something should be given to her to eat.
He go out from there. He come into his own country, and his disciples follow him.

When the Sabbath had come, he began to teach in the synagogue, and many hearing him were astonished, saying, “Where did this man get these things?” and, “Wetin be the wisdom that is given to this man, that such mighty works come about by his hands?
No be this the carpenter, the son of Mary, and brother of James, Joses, Judah, and Simon? No be his sisters here with us?” Dem were offended at him.
Jesus tell dem say, “A prophet No be without honor, except in his own country, and among his own relatives, and in his own house.”
He could do no mighty work there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people, and healed dem.
He surprise well-well because of dem unbelief. He go around the villages teaching.
He call to imself the twelve, and began to send dem out two by two; and he give dem authority over the unclean spirits.
He commanded dem that dem should take nothing for dem journey, except a staff only: no bread, no wallet, no money in dem purse,
but to wear sandals, and not put on two tunics.
E tell dem say, “Anywhere wey you enter into a house, stay there until you depart from there.

Anybody wey No go receive you nor hear you, as you depart from there, shake off the dust that is under una feet for a testimony against dem. Assuredly, I tell una, it Go be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city!”
Dem go out and preached that people should repent.
Dem throw out many demons, and anointed many with oil who were sick, and healed dem.
King Herod heard this, for his name had become known, and he talk say, “John the Baptizer has risen from the dead, and so these powers are at work in him.”
But others talk say, “He is Elijah.” Others talk say, “He is a prophet, or like one of the prophets.”
But Herod, when he heard this, talk say, “This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.”
For Herod imself had sent out and arrested John, and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, for he had married her.
For John talk say to Herod, “It No be lawful for you to have una brother’s wife.”
Herodias set sheself against him, and desired to kill him, but she no fit,
for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. When he heard him, he did many things, and he heard him gladly.
Then a convenient day come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper for his nobles, the high officers, and the chief men of Galilee.
When the daughter of Herodias sheself come in and danced, she pleased Herod and those sitting with him. The king talk say to the young lady, “Ask me Anything wey you want, and I go give it to you.”
He swore to her, “Anything wey you shall ask of me, I go give you, up to half of my kingdom.”
She go out, and talk say to her mother, “What shall I ask?” She talk say, “The head of John the Baptizer.”
She come in sharp-sharp with haste to the king, and ask, “I want you to give me right now the head of John the Baptizer on a platter.”
The king was exceedingly sorry, but for the sake of his oaths, and of his dinner guests, he didn’t wish to refuse her.
Sharp-sharp the king sent out a soldier of his guard, and commanded to bring John’s head, and he go and beheaded him in the prison,
and bring his head on a platter, and give it to the young lady; and the young lady give it to her mother.
When his disciples heard this, dem come and take up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.
The apostles gathered themselves together to Jesus, and dem told him all things, Anything wey dem had done, and Anything wey dem had taught.
E tell dem say, “You come apart into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and dem had no leisure so much as to eat.
Dem go away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.
Dem see dem going, and many recognized him and ran there on foot from all the cities. Dem arrived before dem and come together to him.
Jesus come out, see Plenty people, and he had compassion on dem, because dem were like sheep without a shepherd, and he began to teach dem many things.
When it was late in the day, his disciples come to him, and talk say, “This place is deserted, and it is late in the day.
Send dem away, that dem may go into the surrounding country and villages, and buy themselves bread, for dem have nothing to eat.”
But he answer dem, “You give dem something to eat.” Dem ask him, “Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread, and give dem something to eat?”
E tell dem say, “How many loaves do you have? Go see.” When dem know, dem talk say, “Five, and two fish.”
He commanded dem that everyone should sit down in groups on the green grass.
Dem sat down in ranks, by hundreds and by fifties.
He take the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to heaven, he blessed and broke the loaves, and he give to his disciples to set before dem, and he divided the two fish among dem all.
Dem all ate, and were filled.
Dem take up twelve baskets full of broken pieces and also of the fish.
People wey ate the loaves were five thousand men.
Sharp-sharp he made his disciples get into the boat, and to go ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he imself sent the plenty people away.
After he had taken leave of dem, he go up the mountain to pray.
When evening had come, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on the land.
Seeing dem distressed in rowing, for the wind was contrary to dem, about the fourth watch of the night he come to dem, walking on the sea, and he would have passed by dem,
but dem, when dem see him walking on the sea, supposed that it was a ghost, and cried out;
for dem all see him, and were troubled. But he sharp-sharp spoke with dem, and talk say to dem, “Cheer up! It is I! No fear.”
He got into the boat with dem; and the wind ceased, and dem were very amazed among themselves, and surprise well-well;
for dem hadn’t understand about the loaves, but dem hearts were hardened.
When dem had crossed over, dem come to land at Gennesaret, and moored to the shore.
When dem had come out of the boat, sharp-sharp the people recognized him,
and ran around that whole region, and began to bring people wey were sick, on dem mats, to where dem heard he was.

Anywhere wey he entered, into villages, or into cities, or into the country, dem laid the sick in the marketplaces, and begged him that dem might touch just the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched him were made well.
Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes gathered together to him, having come from Jerusalem.
Now when dem see some of his disciples eating bread with defiled, that is unwashed, hands, dem find fault.
(For the Pharisees and all the Jews, no eat unless dem wash dem hands and forearms, holding to the tradition of the elders.
Dem no eat when dem come from the marketplace unless dem bathe themselves, and E get many other things, which dem have received to hold to: washings of cups, pitchers, bronze vessels, and couches.)
The Pharisees and the scribes ask him, “Why no una disciples walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat dem bread with unwashed hands?”
He answer dem, “Well did Isaiah prophesy of you fake people, as it is written, ‘This people honors me with dem lips, but dem heart is far from me.
But dem worship me in vain, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.’
“For you set aside the commandment of God, and hold tightly to the tradition of men — the washing of pitchers and cups, and you do many other such things.”
E tell dem say, “Full well do you reject the commandment of God, that you may keep una tradition.
For Moses talk say, ‘Honor una father and una mother;’ and, ‘Person wey speaks evil of father or mother, Make e be put to death.’
But you say, ‘If a man tells his father or his mother, “Anything wey profit you might have received from me is Corban, that is to say, given to God”;’
then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or his mother,
making void the word of God by una tradition, which you have handed down. You do many things like this.”
He call all the plenty people to imself, and talk say to dem, “Hear me, all of you, and understand.
E get nothing from outside of the man, that going into him can defile him; but the things which proceed out of the man are those that defile the man.
If anyone has ears to hear, Make e hear!”
When he had entered into a house away from the plenty people, his disciples ask him about the parable.
E tell dem say, “Are you also without understanding? No you perceive that Anything wey goes into the man from outside no fit defile him,
because it no dey go into his heart, but into his stomach, then into the latrine, thus purifying all foods?”
He talk say, “That which proceeds out of the man, that defiles the man.
For from within, out of the hearts of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, sexual sins, murders, thefts,
covetings, wickedness, deceit, lustful desires, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, and foolishness.
All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.”
From there he arose, and go away into the borders of Tyre and Sidon. He entered into a house, and didn’t want anyone to know it, but he no fit escape notice.
For a woman, whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having heard of him, come and fell down at his feet.
Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by race. She begged him that he would throw the demon out of her daughter.
But Jesus tell am say, “Let the pikin dem be filled first, for it No be appropriate to take the pikin dem’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
But she answer him, “Yes, Lord. Yet even the dogs under the table eat the pikin dem’s crumbs.”
E tell am say, “For this saying, go una way. The demon has gone out of una daughter.”
She go away to her house, and find the pikin having been laid on the bed, with the demon gone out.
Again he comot from the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and come to the sea of Galilee, through the middle of the region of Decapolis.
Dem bring to him one who was deaf and had an impediment in his speech. Dem begged him to lay his hand on him.
He take him aside from the plenty people, privately, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spat, and touched his tongue.
Looking up to heaven, he sighed, and talk say to him, “Ephphatha!” that is, “Be opened!”
Sharp-sharp his ears were opened, and the impediment of his tongue was released, and he spoke clearly.
He commanded dem that dem should tell Nobody, but the more he commanded dem, so much the more widely dem proclaimed it.
Dem were astonished beyond measure, saying, “He has done all things well. He makes even the deaf hear, and the mute speak!”
In those days, when there was a plenty well-well plenty people, and dem had nothing to eat, Jesus call his disciples to imself, and talk say to dem,
“I have compassion on the plenty people, because dem have stayed with me now three days, and have nothing to eat.
If I send dem away fasting to dem home, Dem go faint on the way, for some of dem have come a long way.”
His disciples answer him, “From where could one satisfy these people with bread here in a deserted place?”
He ask dem, “How many loaves do you have?” Dem talk say, “Seven.”
He commanded the plenty people to sit down on the ground, and he take the seven loaves. Having given thanks, he broke dem, and give dem to his disciples to serve, and dem served the plenty people.
Dem had a few small fish. Having blessed dem, he talk say to serve these also.
Dem ate, and were filled. Dem take up seven baskets of broken pieces that were left over.
People wey had eaten were about four thousand. Then he sent dem away.
Sharp-sharp he entered into the boat with his disciples, and come into the region of Dalmanutha.
The Pharisees come out and began to question him, seeking from him a sign from heaven, and testing him.
He sighed deeply in his spirit, and talk say, “Why does this generation seek a sign? True true, I tell una, no sign Go be given to this generation.”
He left dem, and again entering into the boat, comot to the other side.
Dem forgot to take bread; and dem didn’t have more than one loaf in the boat with dem.
He warned dem, saying, “Take heed: beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod.”
Dem reasoned with each other, saying, “It’s because we have no bread.”
Jesus, perceiving it, talk say to dem, “Why do you reason that it’s because you have no bread? No you perceive yet, neither understand? Is una heart still hardened?
Having eyes, no you see? Having ears, no you hear? No you remember?
When I broke the five loaves among the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?” Dem told him, “Twelve.”
“When the seven loaves fed the four thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?” Dem told him, “Seven.”
He ask dem, “No you understand, yet?”
He come to Bethsaida. Dem bring a blind man to him, and begged him to touch him.
He take hold of the blind man by the hand, and bring him out of the village. When he had spit on his eyes, and laid his hands on him, he ask him if he see anything.
He looked up, and talk say, “I see men; for I see dem like trees walking.”
Then again he laid his hands on his eyes. He looked intently, and was restored, and see everyone clearly.
He sent him away to his house, saying, “No enter into the village, nor tell anyone in the village.”
Jesus go out, with his disciples, into the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way he ask his disciples, “Who do men say that I be?”
Dem told him, “John the Baptizer, and others say Elijah, but others: one of the prophets.”
E tell dem say, “But who do you say that I be?” Peter answer, “You be the Christ.”
He commanded dem that dem should tell Nobody about him.
He began to teach dem that the Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.
He spoke to dem openly. Peter take him, and began to rebuke him.
But he, turning around, and seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter, and talk say, “Get behind me, Satan! For you have in mind not the things of God, but the things of men.”
He call the plenty people to imself with his disciples, and talk say to dem, “Anybody wey wants to come after me, Make e deny imself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
For Anybody wey wants to save his life will lose it; and Anybody wey will lose his life for my sake and the sake of the Better news will save it.
For what does it profit a man, to gain the whole world, and forfeit his life?
For what will a man give in exchange for his life?
For Anybody wey Go be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man also Go be ashamed of him, when he comes in his Father’s glory, with the holy angels.”
E tell dem say, “True true, I tell una, E get some standing here who will in no way taste death until dem see God’s Kingdom come with power.”
After six days Jesus take with him Peter, James, and John, and bring dem up onto a high mountain privately by themselves, and he was changed into another form in front of dem.
His clothing became glistening, exceedingly white, like snow, such as no launderer on earth can whiten dem.
Elijah and Moses appeared to dem, and dem were talking with Jesus.
Peter answer Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let’s make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
For he didn’t know what to say, for dem were very afraid.
A cloud come, overshadowing dem, and a voice come out of the cloud, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.”
Suddenly looking around, dem see Nobody with dem any more, except Jesus only.
As dem were coming down from the mountain, he commanded dem that dem should tell Nobody what things dem had seen, until after the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
Dem kept this saying to themselves, questioning what the “rising from the dead” meant.
Dem ask him, saying, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
E tell dem say, “Elijah indeed comes first, and restores all things. How is it written about the Son of Man, that he should suffer many things and be despised?
But I tell una that Elijah has come, and dem have also done to him Anything wey dem want to, even as it is written about him.”
Coming to the disciples, he see Plenty people around dem, and scribes questioning dem.
Sharp-sharp all the plenty people, when dem see him, were greatly amazed, and running to him greeted him.
He ask the scribes, “Wetin be you asking dem?”
One of the plenty people answer, “Teacher, I bring to you my son, who has a mute spirit;
and Anywhere wey it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams at the mouth, and grinds his teeth, and wastes away. I ask una disciples to throw it out, and dem no be able.”
He answer him, “Unbelieving generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him to me.”
Dem bring him to him, and when he see him, sharp-sharp the spirit convulsed him, and he fell on the ground, wallowing and foaming at the mouth.
He ask his father, “How long has it been since this has come to him?” He talk say, “From childhood.
Often it has throw him both into the fire and into the water, to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us, and help us.”
