Jesus tell am say, “If you can believe, all things are possible to him wey believe.”
Sharp-sharp the father of the pikin cried out with tears, “I believe. Help my unbelief!”
When Jesus see that a plenty people come running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to him, “You mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him, and never enter him again!”
Having cried out, and convulsed greatly, it come out of him. The boy became like one dead; so much that most of dem talk say, “He is dead.”
But Jesus take him by the hand, and raised him up; and he arose.
When he had come into the house, his disciples ask him privately, “Why no fit we throw it out?”
E tell dem say, “This kind can come out by nothing, except by prayer and fasting.”
Dem go out from there, and passed through Galilee. He didn’t want anyone to know it.
For he was teaching his disciples, and talk say to dem, “The Son of Man is being handed over to the hands of men, and Dem go kill him; and when he is killed, on the third day he will rise again.”
But dem didn’t understand the saying, and were afraid to ask him.
He come to Capernaum, and when he was in the house he ask dem, “What were you arguing among unaself on the way?”
But dem were silent, for dem had disputed one with another on the way about who was the greatest.
He sat down, and call the twelve; and E tell dem say, “If any man wants to be first, he go be last of all, and worker of all.”
He take a little pikin, and set him in the middle of dem. Taking him in his arms, E tell dem say,
“Anybody wey receives one such little pikin in my name, receives me, and Anybody wey receives me, no dey receive me, but him who sent me.”
John talk say to him, “Teacher, we see someone who no dey follow us casting out demons in una name; and we forbade him, because he no dey follow us.”
But Jesus talk say, “No forbid him, for E get Nobody who will do a mighty work in my name, and be able sharp-sharp to speak evil of me.
For Anybody wey No be against us is on our side.
For Anybody wey will give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because You be Christ’s, True true, I tell una, he will in no way lose his reward.
Anybody wey will cause one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if he were thrown into the sea with a millstone hung around his neck.
If una hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life maimed, rather than having una two hands to go into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire,
‘where dem worm no dey die, and the fire No be quenched.’
If una foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life lame, rather than having una two feet to be throw into Gehenna, into the fire that will never be quenched —
‘where dem worm no dey die, and the fire No be quenched.’
If una eye causes you to stumble, throw it out. It is better for you to enter into God’s Kingdom with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be throw into the Gehenna of fire,
‘where dem worm no dey die, and the fire No be quenched.’
For everyone Go be salted with fire, and every sacrifice Go be seasoned with salt.
Salt is good, but if the salt has lost its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt in unaself, and be at peace with each other.”
He arose from there and come into the borders of Judea and beyond the Jordan. Plenty people come together to him again. As he usually did, he was again teaching dem.
Pharisees come to him testing him, and ask him, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?”
He answer, “What did Moses command you?”
Dem talk say, “Moses allowed a certificate of divorce to be written, and to divorce her.”
But Jesus tell dem say, “For una hardness of heart, he wrote you this commandment.
But from the beginning of the creation, God made dem male and female.
For this cause a man will leave his father and mother, and will join to his wife,
and the two will become one flesh, so that Dem be no longer two, but one flesh.
What so God has joined together, let no man separate.”
In the house, his disciples ask him again about the same matter.
E tell dem say, “Anybody wey divorces his wife, and marries another, commits adultery against her.
If a woman sheself divorces her husband, and marries another, she commits adultery.”
Dem were bringing to him little pikin dem, that he should touch dem, but the disciples rebuked people wey were bringing dem.
But when Jesus see it, he was moved with indignation, and talk say to dem, “Allow the little pikin dem to come to me! No forbid dem, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
True true, I tell una, Anybody wey No go receive God’s Kingdom like a little pikin, he will in no way enter into it.”
He take dem in his arms, and blessed dem, laying his hands on dem.
As he was going out into the way, one ran to him, knelt before him, and ask him, “Good Teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit life wey no dey end?”
Jesus tell am say, “Why do you call me good? Nobody is good except one — God.
You know the commandments: ‘No murder,’ ‘No commit adultery,’ ‘No steal,’ ‘No give false testimony,’ ‘No defraud,’ ‘Honor una father and mother.’”
E tell am say, “Teacher, I have observed all these things from my youth.”

Jesus looking at him love him, and talk say to him, “One thing you lack. Go, sell Anything wey you have, and give to the poor, and You go have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me, taking up the cross.”
But his face fell at that saying, and he go away sorrowful, for he was one who had great possessions.
Jesus looked around, and talk say to his disciples, “How difficult it is for people wey have riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!”
The disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus answer again, “Pikin dem, how hard is it for people wey trust in riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!
It is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”
Dem were exceedingly astonished, saying to him, “Then who can be saved?”
Jesus, looking at dem, talk say, “With men it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God.”
Peter began to tell him, “See am, we have left all, and have follow you.”

Jesus talk say, “True true, I tell una, E get Nobody who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or pikin dem, or land, for my sake, and for the sake of the Better news,
but he will receive one hundred times more now in this time, houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, pikin dem, and land, with persecutions; and in the age to come life wey no dey end.
But many Wey be first Go be last; and the last first.”

Dem were on the way, going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus was going in front of dem, and dem were amazed; and people wey follow were afraid. He again take the twelve, and began to tell dem the things that were going to happen to him.
“See am, We be going up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man Go be delivered to the chief priests and the scribes. Dem go condemn him to death, and will deliver him to the Gentiles.
Dem go mock him, spit on him, scourge him, and kill him. On the third day he will rise again.”
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come near to him, saying, “Teacher, we want you to do for us Anything wey We go ask.”
E tell dem say, “What do you want me to do for you?”
Dem tell am say, “Grant to us that we may sit, one at una right hand, and one at una left hand, in una glory.”
But Jesus tell dem say, “You no know Wetin You be asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, and to be baptized with the baptism that I be baptized with?”
Dem tell am say, “We be able.” Jesus tell dem say, “You shall indeed drink the cup that I drink, and you go be baptized with the baptism that I be baptized with;
but to sit at my right hand and at my left hand No be mine to give, but for whom it Don dey prepared.”
When the ten heard it, dem began to be indignant towards James and John.
Jesus summoned dem, and talk say to dem, “You know that dem Wey be recognized as rulers over the nations lord it over dem, and dem great ones exercise authority over dem.
But it no go be so among you, but Anybody wey wants to become great among you go be una worker.
Anybody wey of you wants to become first among you, go be bondservant of all.
For the Son of Man also come not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
Dem come to Jericho. As he go out from Jericho, with his disciples and Plenty people, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting by the road.
When he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out, and say, “Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!”
Many rebuked him, that he should be quiet, but he cried out much more, “You son of David, have mercy on me!”
Jesus stood still, and talk say, “Call him.” Dem call the blind man, saying to him, “Cheer up! Get up. He is calling you!”
He, casting away his cloak, sprang up, and come to Jesus.
Jesus ask him, “What do you want me to do for you?” The blind man talk say to him, “Rabboni, that I may see again.”
Jesus tell am say, “Go una way. Una faith has made you well.” Sharp-sharp he received his sight, and follow Jesus on the way.
When dem come near to Jerusalem, to Bethsphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples,
and talk say to dem, “Go una way into the village that is opposite you. Sharp-sharp as you enter into it, You go find a young donkey tied, on which Nobody has sat. Untie him, and bring him.
If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say, ‘The Lord needs him;’ and sharp-sharp he will send him back here.”
Dem go away, and find a young donkey tied at the door outside in the open street, and dem untied him.
Some of people wey stood there ask dem, “Wetin be you doing, untying the young donkey?”
Dem tell dem say just as Jesus had talk say, and dem Make dem go.
Dem bring the young donkey to Jesus, and threw dem garments on it, and Jesus sat on it.
Many spread dem garments on the way, and others were cutting down branches from the trees, and spreading dem on the road.
People wey go in front, and people wey follow, cried out, “Hosanna! Blessed is person wey comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the kingdom of our father David that is coming in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”
Jesus entered into the temple in Jerusalem. When he had looked around at everything, it being now evening, he go out to Bethany with the twelve.
The next day, when dem had come out from Bethany, he was hungry.
Seeing a fig tree far away off having leaves, he come to see if perhaps he might find anything on it. When he come to it, he find nothing but leaves, for it No be the season for figs.
Jesus told it, “May Nobody ever eat fruit from you again!” and his disciples heard it.

Dem come to Jerusalem, and Jesus entered into the temple, and began to throw out people wey sold and people wey bought in the temple, and overthrew the money changers’ tables, and the seats of people wey sold the doves.
He would not allow anyone to carry a container through the temple.
He taught, saying to dem, “No be it written, ‘My house Go be call a house of prayer for all the nations?’ But you have made it a den of robbers!”
The chief priests and the scribes heard it, and sought how dem might destroy him. For dem feared him, because all the plenty people was astonished at his teaching.
When evening come, he go out of the city.
As dem passed by in the morning, dem see the fig tree withered away from the roots.
Peter, remembering, talk say to him, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree which you cursed has withered away.”
Jesus answer dem, “Have faith in God.

For True true, I tell una, Anybody wey may tell this mountain, ‘Be taken up and throw into the sea,’ and no dey doubt in his heart, but believe that what he says is happening; he go get Anything wey he says.
So I tell una, all things Anything wey you pray and ask for, believe that you have received dem, and you go get dem.
Whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone; so that una Father, Wey be in heaven, may also forgive you una wrongdoings.
But if you No forgive, neither will una Father in heaven forgive una wrongdoings.”
Dem come again to Jerusalem, and as he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders come to him,
and dem began saying to him, “By what authority do you do these things? Or who give you this authority to do these things?”
Jesus tell dem say, “I go ask you one question. Answer me, and I go tell you by what authority I do these things.
The baptism of John — was it from heaven, or from men? Answer me.”
Dem reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we should say, ‘From heaven;’ he will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
If we should say, ‘From men’” — dem feared the people, for all held John to really be a prophet.
Dem answer Jesus, “We no know.” Jesus tell dem say, “Neither do I tell una by what authority I do these things.”
He began to speak to dem in parables. “A man planted a vineyard, put a hedge around it, dug a pit for the wine press, built a tower, rented it out to a farmer, and go into another country.
When it was time, he sent a worker to the farmer to get from the farmer his share of the fruit of the vineyard.
Dem take him, beat him, and sent him away empty.
Again, he sent another worker to dem; and dem threw stones at him, wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully treated.
Again he sent another; and dem killed him; and many others, beating some, and killing some.
So still having one, his beloved son, he sent him last to dem, saying, ‘Dem go respect my son.’
But those farmers talk say among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, and the inheritance Go be ours.’
Dem take him, killed him, and throw him out of the vineyard.
What so will the lord of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.
Haven’t you even read this Scripture: ‘The stone which the builders rejected, the same was made the head of the corner.
This was from the Lord, it is marvelous in our eyes’?”
Dem tried to seize him, but dem feared the plenty people; for dem perceived that he spoke the parable against dem. Dem left him, and go away.
Dem sent some of the Pharisees and of the Herodians to him, that dem might trap him with words.

When dem had come, dem ask him, “Teacher, we know that You be honest, and no defer to anyone; for you no be partial to anyone, but truly teach the way of God. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?
Shall we give, or shall we not give?” But he, knowing dem hypocrisy, talk say to dem, “Why do you test me? Bring me a denarius, that I may see it.”
Dem bring it. E tell dem say, “Whose is this image and inscription?” Dem tell am say, “Caesar’s.”
Jesus answer dem, “Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.” Dem surprise well-well greatly at him.
There come to him Sadducees, who say that E get no resurrection. Dem ask him, saying,
“Teacher, Moses wrote to us, ‘If a man’s brother dies, and leaves a wife behind him, and leaves no pikin dem, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up offspring for his brother.’
There were seven brothers. The first take a wife, and dying left no offspring.
The second take her, and died, leaving no pikin dem behind him. The third likewise;
and the seven take her and left no pikin dem. Last of all the woman also died.
In the resurrection, when dem rise, whose wife will she be of dem? For the seven had her as a wife.”
Jesus answer dem, “No be this because You be mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God?
For when Dem go rise from the dead, dem neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.
But about the dead, that Dem be raised; haven’t you read in the book of Moses, about the Bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I be the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?
He No be the God of the dead, but of the living. You be so badly mistaken.”
One of the scribes come, and heard dem questioning together. Knowing that he had answer dem well, ask him, “Which commandment is the greatest of all?”
Jesus answer, “The greatest is, ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one:
you shall love the Lord una God with all una heart, and with all una soul, and with all una mind, and with all una strength.’ This is the first commandment.
The second is like this, ‘You shall love una neighbor as yourself.’ E get no other commandment greater than these.”
The scribe talk say to him, “Truly, teacher, you have talk say well that he is one, and E get none other but he,

and to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as imself, is more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
When Jesus see that he answer wisely, E tell am say, “You No be far from God’s Kingdom.” Nobody dared ask him any question after that.
Jesus responded, as he taught in the temple, “How is it that the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
For David imself talk say in the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord talk say to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make una enemies the footstool of una feet.”’
So David imself calls him Lord, so how can he be his son?” The common people heard him gladly.
In his teaching E tell dem say, “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk in long robes, and to get greetings in the marketplaces,
and the best seats in the synagogues, and the best places at feasts:
people wey devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive greater condemnation.”
Jesus sat down opposite the treasury, and see how the plenty people throw money into the treasury. Many who were rich throw in much.
A poor widow come, and she throw in two small brass coins, which equal a quadrans coin.
He call his disciples to imself, and talk say to dem, “True true, I tell una, this poor widow give more than all people Wey giving into the treasury,
for dem all give out of dem abundance, but she, out of her poverty, give all that she had to live on.”
As he go out of the temple, one of his disciples talk say to him, “Teacher, see what kind of stones and what kind of buildings!”
Jesus tell am say, “Do you see these great buildings? There No go be left here one stone on another, which No go be thrown down.”
As he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew ask him privately,
“Tell us, when will these things be? Wetin be the sign that these things are all about to be fulfilled?”
Jesus, answering, began to tell dem, “Be careful that Nobody leads you astray.
For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I be he!’ and will lead many astray.
“When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, no be troubled. For those must happen, but the end No be yet.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There Go be earthquakes in various places. There Go be famines and troubles. These things are the beginning of birth pains.
But watch unaself, for Dem go deliver you up to councils. You go be beaten in synagogues. You go stand before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony to dem.
The Better news must first be preached to all the nations.

When dem lead you away and deliver you up, No worry about beforehand, or premeditate Wetin you go say, but say Anything wey Go be given you in that hour. For it No be you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
“Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his pikin. Pikin dem will rise up against parents, and cause dem to be put to death.
You go be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but person wey endures to the end, the same Go be saved.
But when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not (let the reader understand), then let people Wey in Judea flee to the mountains,
and Make e Wey be on the housetop not go down, nor enter in, to take anything out of his house.
Make e Wey be in the field not return back to take his cloak.
But woe to people Wey with pikin and to people wey nurse babies in those days!
Pray that una flight no go be in the winter.
For in those days there Go be oppression, such as there has not been the like from the beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never Go be.
Unless the Lord had shortened the days, no flesh would Don dey saved; but for the sake of the chosen ones, whom he picked out, he shortened the days.
Then if anyone tells you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ no believe it.
For there will arise false christs and false prophets, and will show signs and wonders, that dem may lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
But you watch. “See am, I have told you all things beforehand.
But in those days, after that oppression, the sun Go be darkened, the moon No go give its light,
the stars Go be falling from the sky, and the powers that are in the heavens Go be shaken.
Then Dem go see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
Then he will send out his angels, and will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from every corner of the world to the ends of the sky.
“Now from the fig tree, learn this parable. When the branch has now become tender, and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near;
even so you also, when you see these things coming to pass, know that it is near, at the doors.
Most certainly I say to you, this generation No go pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words No go pass away.
But of that day or that hour Nobody knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
Watch, keep alert, and pray; for you no know when the time is.
“It is like a man, traveling to another country, having left his house, and given authority to his workers, and to each one his work, and also commanded the doorkeeper to Shine una eye.
Watch so, for you no know when the lord of the house is coming, whether at evening, or at midnight, or when the rooster crows, or in the morning;
lest coming suddenly he might find you sleeping.
What I tell una, I tell all: Watch.”
It was now two days before the feast of the Passover and the unleavened bread, and the chief priests and the scribes sought how dem might seize him by deception, and kill him.
For dem talk say, “Not during the feast, because there might be a riot of the people.”

While he was at Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at the table, a woman come having an alabaster jar of ointment of pure nard — very costly. She broke the jar, and poured it over his head.
But there were some who were indignant among themselves, saying, “Why has this ointment been wasted?
For this might Don dey sold for more than three hundred denarii, and given to the poor.” Dem grumbled against her.
But Jesus talk say, “Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a good work for me.
For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want to, you can do dem good; but You go not always have me.
She has done what she could. She has anointed my body beforehand for the burying.
True true, I tell una, Anywhere wey this Better news may be preached throughout the whole world, that which this woman has done will also be spoken of for a memorial of her.”
Judas Iscariot, who was one of the twelve, go away to the chief priests, that he might deliver him to dem.
Dem, when dem heard it, were glad, and promised to give him money. He sought how he might conveniently deliver him.
On the first day of unleavened bread, when dem sacrificed the Passover, his disciples ask him, “Where do you want us to go and prepare that you may eat the Passover?”
He sent two of his disciples, and talk say to dem, “Go into the city, and there You go meet a man carrying a pitcher of water. Follow him,
and Anywhere wey he enters in, tell the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says, “Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’
He will imself show you a large upper room furnished and ready. Get ready for us there.”
His disciples go out, and come into the city, and find things as he had talk say to dem, and dem prepared the Passover.
When it was evening he come with the twelve.
As dem sat and were eating, Jesus talk say, “True true, I tell una, one of You go betray me — person wey eats with me.”
Dem began to be sorrowful, and to ask him one by one, “Surely not I?” And another talk say, “Surely not I?”
He answer dem, “It is one of the twelve, person wey dips with me in the dish.
For the Son of Man goes, even as it is written about him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.”
As dem were eating, Jesus take bread, and when he had blessed, he broke it, and give to dem, and talk say, “Take, eat. This is my body.”
He take the cup, and when he had given thanks, he give to dem. Dem all drank of it.
E tell dem say, “This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many.
True true, I tell una, I go no more drink of the fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it anew in God’s Kingdom.”
When dem had sung a hymn, dem go out to the Mount of Olives.
Jesus tell dem say, “All of You go be made to stumble because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I go strike the shepherd, and the sheep Go be scattered.’
However, after I be raised up, I go go before you into Galilee.”
But Peter talk say to him, “Although all Go be offended, yet I go not.”
Jesus tell am say, “True true, I tell una, that you today, even this night, before the rooster crows twice, You go deny me three times.”
But he spoke all the more, “If I must die with you, I go not deny you.” Dem all talk say the same thing.
Dem come to a place which was named Gethsemane. He talk say to his disciples, “Sit here, while I pray.”
He take with him Peter, James, and John, and began to be greatly troubled and distressed.
E tell dem say, “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here, and watch.”
He go forward a little, and fell on the ground, and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass away from him.
He talk say, “Abba, Father, all things are possible to you. Please remove this cup from me. However, not what I desire, but Wetin you desire.”
He come and find dem sleeping, and talk say to Peter, “Simon, are you sleeping? No fit you watch one hour?
Watch and pray, that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
Again he go away, and prayed, saying the same words.
Again he come back, and find dem sleeping, for dem eyes were very heavy, and dem didn’t know what to answer him.
He come the third time, and talk say to dem, “Sleep on now, and take una rest. It is enough. The hour has come. See am, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
Arise, Make we be going. See am, person wey betrays me is at hand.”
Sharp-sharp, while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, come — and with him a plenty people with swords and clubs, from the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders.
Now person wey betrayed him had given dem a sign, saying, “Whomever I go kiss, that is he. Seize him, and lead him away safely.”
When he had come, sharp-sharp he come to him, and talk say, “Rabbi! Rabbi!” and kissed him.
Dem laid dem hands on him, and seized him.
But a certain one of people wey stood by drew his sword, and struck the worker of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
Jesus answer dem, “Have you come out, as against a robber, with swords and clubs to seize me?
I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and you didn’t arrest me. But this is so that the Scriptures might be fulfilled.”
Dem all left him, and fled.
A certain young man follow him, having a linen cloth thrown around imself, over his naked body. The young men grabbed him,
but he left the linen cloth, and fled from dem naked.
Dem led Jesus away to the high priest. All the chief priests, the elders, and the scribes come together with him.
Peter had follow him from a distance, until he come into the court of the high priest. He was sitting with the officers, and warming imself in the light of the fire.
Now the chief priests and the whole council sought witnesses against Jesus to put him to death, and find none.
For many give false testimony against him, and dem testimony didn’t agree with each other.
Some stood up, and give false testimony against him, saying,
“We heard him say, ‘I go destroy this temple that is made with hands, and in three days I go build another made without hands.’”
Even so, dem testimony No agree.
The high priest stood up in the middle, and ask Jesus, “Have you no answer? Wetin be it which these testify against you?”
But he stayed quiet, and answer nothing. Again the high priest ask him, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?”
Jesus talk say, “I be. You go see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power, and coming with the clouds of the sky.”
The high priest tore his clothes, and talk say, “What further need have we of witnesses?
You have heard the blasphemy! What do you think?” Dem all condemned him to be worthy of death.
Some began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to beat him with fists, and to tell him, “Prophesy!” The officers struck him with the palms of dem hands.
As Peter was in the courtyard below, one of the maids of the high priest come,
and seeing Peter warming imself, she looked at him, and talk say, “You were also with the Nazarene, Jesus!”
But he denied it, saying, “I neither know, nor understand Wetin You be saying.” He go out on the porch, and the rooster crowed.
The maid see him, and began again to tell people wey stood by, “This is one of dem.”
But he again denied it. After a little while again people wey stood by talk say to Peter, “You truly are one of dem, for You be a Galilean, and una speech shows it.”
But he began to curse, and to swear, “I no know this man of whom you speak!”
The rooster crowed the second time. Peter remember the word, how that Jesus tell am say, “Before the rooster crows twice, You go deny me three times.” When he thought about that, he wept.
Sharp-sharp in the morning the chief priests, with the elders and scribes, and the whole council, held a consultation, and bound Jesus, and carried him away, and delivered him up to Pilate.
Pilate ask him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” He answer, “So you say.”
The chief priests accused him of many things.
Pilate again ask him, “Have you no answer? See how many things dem testify against you!”
But Jesus made no further answer, so that Pilate surprise well-well.
Now at the feast he used to release to dem one prisoner, whom dem ask of him.
There was one call Barabbas, bound with his fellow insurgents, men who in the insurrection had committed murder.
The plenty people, crying aloud, began to ask him to do as he always did for dem.
Pilate answer dem, saying, “Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”
For he perceived that for envy the chief priests had delivered him up.
But the chief priests stirred up the plenty people, that he should release Barabbas to dem instead.
Pilate again ask dem, “What then should I do to him whom you call the King of the Jews?”
Dem cried out again, “Crucify him!”
Pilate talk say to dem, “Why, what evil has he done?” But dem cried out exceedingly, “Crucify him!”
Pilate, wishing to please the plenty people, released Barabbas to dem, and handed over Jesus, when he had flogged him, to be crucified.
The soldiers led him away within the court, which is the Praetorium; and dem call together the whole cohort.
Dem clothed him with purple, and weaving a crown of thorns, dem put it on him.
Dem began to salute him, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
Dem struck his head with a reed, and spat on him, and bowing dem knees, did homage to him.
When dem had mocked him, dem take the purple off of him, and put his own garments on him. Dem led him out to crucify him.
Dem compelled one passing by, coming from the country, Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to go with dem, that he might bear his cross.
Dem bring him to the place call Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, “The place of a skull.”
Dem offered him wine mixed with myrrh to drink, but he didn’t take it.
Crucifying him, dem parted his garments among dem, casting lots on dem, what each should take.
It was the third hour, and dem crucified him.
The superscription of his accusation was written over him, “THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
With him dem crucified two robbers; one on his right hand, and one on his left.
The Scripture was fulfilled, which says, “He was counted with transgressors.”
People wey passed by blasphemed him, wagging dem heads, and saying, “Ha! You who destroy the temple, and build it in three days,
save yourself, and come down from the cross!”
Likewise, also the chief priests mocking among themselves with the scribes talk say, “He saved others. He no fit save imself.
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, now come down from the cross, that we may see and believe him.” People wey were crucified with him also insulted him.
When the sixth hour had come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.
At the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?” which is, being interpreted, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
Some of people wey stood by, when dem heard it, talk say, “See am, he is calling Elijah.”
One ran, and filling a sponge full of vinegar, put it on a reed, and give it to him to drink, saying, “Make e be. Let’s see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”
Jesus cried out with a loud voice, and give up the spirit.
The veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom.
When the centurion, who stood by opposite him, see that he cried out like this and breathed his last, he talk say, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”
There were also women watching from far away, among whom were both Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome;
who, when he was in Galilee, follow him, and served him; and many other women who come up with him to Jerusalem.
When evening had now come, because it was the Preparation Day, that is, the day before the Sabbath,
Joseph of Arimathaea, a prominent council member who also imself was looking for God’s Kingdom, come. He boldly go in to Pilate, and ask for Jesus’ body.
Pilate surprise well-well if he were already dead; and summoning the centurion, he ask him whether he Bin dey dead long.
When he find out from the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
He bought a linen cloth, and taking him down, wound him in the linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb which Bin dey cut out of a rock. He rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
Mary Magdalene and Mary, the mother of Joses, see where he was laid.
When the Sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome, bought spices, that dem might come and anoint him.
Very early on the first day of the week, dem come to the tomb when the sun had risen.
Dem were saying among themselves, “Who will roll away the stone from the door of the tomb for us?”
for it was very big. Looking up, dem see that the stone was rolled back.
Entering into the tomb, dem see a young man sitting on the right side, dressed in a white robe, and dem were amazed.
E tell dem say, “No be amazed. You seek Jesus, the Nazarene, who Don dey crucified. He has risen. He No be here. See am, the place where dem laid him!
But go, tell his disciples and Peter, ‘He goes before you into Galilee. There You go see him, as he talk say to you.’”
Dem go out, and fled from the tomb, for trembling and astonishment had come on dem. Dem talk say nothing to anyone; for dem were afraid.
Now when he had risen early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had throw out seven demons.
She go and told people wey Bin dey with him, as dem mourned and wept.
When dem heard that he was alive, and Bin dey seen by her, dem disbelieved.
After these things he was revealed in another form to two of dem, as dem walked, on dem way into the country.
Dem go away and told it to the rest. Dem didn’t believe dem, either.

Afterward he was revealed to the eleven themselves as dem sat at the table, and he rebuked dem for dem unbelief and hardness of heart, because dem didn’t believe people wey had seen him after he had risen.
E tell dem say, “Go into all the world, and preach the Better news to the whole creation.
Person wey believe and is baptized Go be saved; but person wey disbelieves Go be condemned.
These signs will accompany people wey believe: in my name Dem go throw out demons; Dem go speak with new languages;
Dem go take up serpents; and if dem drink any deadly thing, it will in no way hurt dem; Dem go lay hands on the sick, and Dem go recover.”
So then the Lord, after he had spoken to dem, was received up into heaven, and sat down at the right hand of God.
Dem go out, and preached everywhere, the Lord working with dem, and confirming the word by the signs that follow. Amen.
Since many have undertaken to set in order a narrative concerning those matters which Don dey fulfilled among us,
even as people wey from the beginning were eyewitnesses and workers of the word delivered dem to us,
it seemed good to me also, having traced the course of all things accurately from the first, to write to you in order, most excellent Theophilus;
that you might know the certainty concerning the things in which you were instructed.
There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the priestly division of Abijah. He had a wife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
Dem were both righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord.
But dem had no pikin, because Elizabeth was barren, and dem both were well advanced in years.
Now while he executed the priest’s office before God in the order of his division,
according to the custom of the priest’s office, his lot was to enter into the temple of the Lord and burn incense.
The whole plenty people of the people were praying outside at the hour of incense.
An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
Zacharias was troubled when he see him, and fear fell upon him.
But the angel talk say to him, “No fear, Zacharias, because una request Don dey heard, and una wife, Elizabeth, will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.
You go have gladness and gladness; and many will glad well-well at his birth.
For he Go be great in the sight of the Lord, and he will drink no wine nor strong drink. He Go be filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother’s womb.
He will turn many of the pikin dem of Israel to the Lord, dem God.

He will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, ‘to turn the hearts of the fathers to the pikin dem,’ and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just; to prepare a people prepared for the Lord.”
Zacharias talk say to the angel, “How can I be sure of this? For I be an old man, and my wife is well advanced in years.”
The angel answer him, “I be Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God. I was sent to speak to you, and to bring you this better news.
See am, You go be silent and not able to speak, until the day that these things will happen, because you didn’t believe my words, which Go be fulfilled in dem proper time.”
The people were waiting for Zacharias, and dem surprise well-well that he delayed in the temple.
When he come out, he could not speak to dem, and dem perceived that he had seen a vision in the temple. He continued making signs to dem, and remain mute.
When the days of his service were fulfilled, he comot to his house.
After these days Elizabeth, his wife, conceived, and she hid sheself five months, saying,
“Thus has the Lord done to me in the days in which he looked at me, to take away my reproach among men.”
Now in the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee, named Nazareth,
to a virgin pledged to be married to a man whose name was Joseph, of David’s house. The virgin’s name was Mary.
Having come in, the angel talk say to her, “Glad well-well, you highly favored one! The Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women!”
But when she see him, she was greatly troubled at the saying, and considered what kind of salutation this might be.
The angel talk say to her, “No fear, Mary, for you have find favor with God.
See am, You go conceive in una womb, and give birth to a son, and will call his name ‘Jesus.’
He Go be great, and Go be call the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father, David,
and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever. There Go be no end to his Kingdom.”
Mary talk say to the angel, “How can this be, seeing I be a virgin?”
The angel answer her, “The Holy Spirit will come on you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. So also the holy one Wey be born from You go be call the Son of God.
See am, Elizabeth, una relative, also has conceived a son in her old age; and this is the sixth month with her who was call barren.
For nothing spoken by God is impossible.”
Mary talk say, “See am, the worker of the Lord; let it be done to me according to una word.” The angel comot from her.
Mary arose in those days and go into the hill country with haste, into a city of Judah,
and entered into the house of Zacharias and greeted Elizabeth.
When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
She call out with a loud voice, and talk say, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of una womb!
Why am I so favored, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
For see am, when the voice of una greeting come into my ears, the baby leaped in my womb for gladness!
Blessed is person wey believe, for there Go be a fulfillment of the things which Don dey spoken to her from the Lord!”
Mary talk say, “My soul magnifies the Lord.
My spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,
for he has looked at the humble state of his worker. For see am, from now on, all generations will call me blessed.
For person Wey mighty has done great things for me. Holy is his name.
His mercy is for generations of generations on people wey fear him.
He has shown strength with his arm. He has scattered the proud in the imagination of dem hearts.
He has put down princes from dem thrones. And has exalted the lowly.
He has filled the hungry with good things. He has sent the rich away empty.
He has given help to Israel, his worker, that he might remember mercy,
As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his offspring forever.”
Mary stayed with her about three months, and then come back to her house.
Now the time that Elizabeth should give birth was fulfilled, and she give birth to a son.
Her neighbors and her relatives heard that the Lord had magnified his mercy towards her, and dem rejoiced with her.
On the eighth day, dem come to circumcise the pikin; and dem would have call him Zacharias, after the name of his father.
His mother answer, “Not so; but he Go be call John.”
Dem talk say to her, “E get Nobody among una relatives Wey be call by this name.”
Dem made signs to his father, what he would have him call.
He ask for a writing tablet, and wrote, “His name is John.” Dem all surprise well-well.
His mouth was opened sharp-sharp, and his tongue freed, and he spoke, blessing God.
Fear come on all who lived around dem, and all these sayings were talked about throughout all the hill country of Judea.
All who heard dem laid dem up in dem heart, saying, “What then will this pikin be?” The hand of the Lord was with him.
His father, Zacharias, was filled with the Holy Spirit, and prophesied, saying,
“Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, for he has visited and redeemed his people;
and has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of his worker David
(as he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets who Don dey from of old),
salvation from our enemies, and from the hand of all who hate us;
to show mercy towards our fathers, to remember his holy covenant,
the oath which he swore to Abraham, our father,
to grant to us that we, being delivered out of the hand of our enemies, should serve him without fear,
In holiness and righteousness before him all the days of our life.
And you, pikin, Go be call a prophet of the Most High, for You go go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways,
to give knowledge of salvation to his people by the remission of dem sins,
because of the tender mercy of our God, wey make the dawn from on high will visit us,
to shine on people wey sit in darkness and the shadow of death; to guide our feet into the way of peace.”
The pikin was growing, and becoming strong in spirit, and was in the desert until the day of his public appearance to Israel.
Now in those days, a decree go out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be enrolled.
This was the first enrollment made when Quirinius was governor of Syria.
All go to enroll themselves, everyone to his own city.
Joseph also go up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to David’s city, which is call Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David;
to enroll imself with Mary, who was pledged to be married to him as wife, being pregnant.
While dem were there, the day had come for her to give birth.
She give birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth, and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for dem in the inn.
There were shepherds in the same country staying in the field, and keeping watch by night over dem flock.
See am, an angel of the Lord stood by dem, and the glory of the Lord shone around dem, and dem were terrified.
The angel talk say to dem, “No fear, for see am, I bring you better news of great gladness which Go be to all the people.
For E get born to you today, in David’s city, a Savior, Wey be Christ the Lord.
This is the sign to you: You go find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth, lying in a feeding trough.”
Suddenly, there was with the angel a plenty people of the heavenly army praising God, and saying,
“Glory to God in the highest, on earth peace, good will toward men.”
When the angels go away from dem into the sky, the shepherds talk say to each other, “Let’s go to Bethlehem, now, and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
Dem come with haste, and find both Mary and Joseph, and the baby was lying in the feeding trough.
When dem see it, dem publicized widely the saying which was spoken to dem about this pikin.
All who heard it wondered at the things which were spoken to dem by the shepherds.
But Mary kept all these sayings, pondering dem in her heart.
The shepherds come back, glorifying and praising God for all the things that dem had heard and seen, just as it was told dem.
When eight days were fulfilled for the circumcision of the pikin, his name was call Jesus, which was given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
When the days of dem purification according to the law of Moses were fulfilled, dem bring him up to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord
(as it is written in the law of the Lord, “Every male who opens the womb go be call holy to the Lord”),
and to offer a sacrifice according to that which is talk say in the law of the Lord, “A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.”
See am, there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon. This man was righteous and devout, looking for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was on him.
It Bin dey revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he no suppose see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
He come in the Spirit into the temple. When the parents bring in the pikin, Jesus, that dem might do concerning him according to the custom of the law,
then he received him into his arms, and blessed God, and talk say,
“Now You be releasing una worker, Master, according to una word, in peace;
for my eyes have seen una salvation,
which you have prepared before the face of all peoples;
a light for revelation to the nations, and the glory of una people Israel.”
Joseph and his mother were marveling at the things which were spoken concerning him,
and Simeon blessed dem, and talk say to Mary, his mother, “See am, this pikin is set for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and for a sign which is spoken against.
Yes, a sword will pierce through una own soul, that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”
There was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher (she was of a great age, having lived with a husband seven years from her virginity,
and she Bin dey a widow for about eighty-four years), who didn’t depart from the temple, worshiping with fastings and petitions night and day.
Coming up at that very hour, she Thank God to the Lord, and spoke of him to all people wey were looking for redemption in Jerusalem.
When dem had accomplished all things that were according to the law of the Lord, dem come back into Galilee, to dem own city, Nazareth.
The pikin was growing, and was becoming strong in spirit, being filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.
His parents go every year to Jerusalem at the feast of the Passover.
When he was twelve years old, dem go up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast,
and when dem had fulfilled the days, as dem were returning, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. Joseph and his mother didn’t know it,
but supposing him to be in the company, dem go a day’s journey, and dem looked for him among dem relatives and acquaintances.
When dem didn’t find him, dem come back to Jerusalem, looking for him.
After three days dem find him in the temple, sitting in the middle of the teachers, both listening to dem, and asking dem questions.
All who heard him were amazed at his understanding and his answers.
When dem see him, dem were astonished, and his mother talk say to him, “Son, why have you treated us this way? See am, una father and I were anxiously looking for you.”
E tell dem say, “Why were you looking for me? Didn’t you know that I must be in my Father’s house?”
Dem didn’t understand the saying which he spoke to dem.
And he go down with dem, and come to Nazareth. He was subject to dem, and his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.
And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men.

Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,
in the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God come to John, the son of Zacharias, in the wilderness.
He come into all the region around the Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for remission of sins.
As it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet, “The voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make ready the way of the Lord. Make his paths straight.
Every valley Go be filled. Every mountain and hill Go be bring low. The crooked will become straight, and the rough ways smooth.
All flesh will see God’s salvation.’”
He talk say so to the plenty people who go out to be baptized by him, “You offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the serious anger to come?
So produce fruits worthy of repentance, and no begin to say among unaself, ‘We have Abraham for our father;’ for I tell una that God is able to raise up pikin dem to Abraham from these stones!
Even now the ax also lies at the root of the trees. Every tree so that no dey produce good fruit is cut down, and thrown into the fire.”
The plenty people ask him, “What then must we do?”
He answer dem, “Person wey has two coats, Make e give to him who has none. Person wey has chop, Make e do likewise.”
Tax collectors also come to be baptized, and Dem tell am say, “Teacher, what must we do?”
E tell dem say, “Collect no more than that which is appointed to you.”
Soldiers also ask him, saying, “What about us? What must we do?” E tell dem say, “Extort from Nobody by violence, neither accuse anyone wrongfully. Be content with una wages.”
As the people were in expectation, and all men reasoned in dem hearts concerning John, whether perhaps he was the Christ,
John answer dem all, “I indeed baptize you with water, but he comes Wey be mightier than I, the strap of whose sandals I be not worthy to loosen. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire,
whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor, and will gather the wheat into his barn; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”
Then with many other exhortations he preached better news to the people,
but Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him for Herodias, his brother’s wife, and for all the evil things which Herod had done,
added this also to dem all, that he shut up John in prison.
Now when all the people were baptized, Jesus also Bin dey baptized, and was praying. The sky was opened,
and the Holy Spirit descended in a bodily form like a dove on him; and a voice come out of the sky, saying “You be my beloved Son. In you I be well pleased.”
Jesus imself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,
the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,
the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai,
the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Joseph, the son of Judah,
the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri,
the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmodam, the son of Er,
the son of Jose, the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi,
the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonan, the son of Eliakim,
the son of Melea, the son of Menan, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David,
the son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Salmon, the son of Nahshon,
the son of Amminadab, the son of Aram, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,
the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor,
the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,
the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech,
the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalaleel, the son of Cainan,
the son of Enos, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.
Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, come back from the Jordan, and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness
for forty days, being tempted by the devil. He ate nothing in those days. Afterward, when dem were completed, he was hungry.
The devil talk say to him, “If You be the Son of God, command this stone to become bread.”
Jesus answer him, saying, “It is written, ‘Man no go live by bread alone, but by every word of God.’”
The devil, leading him up on a high mountain, showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
The devil talk say to him, “I go give you all this authority, and dem glory, for it Don dey delivered to me; and I give it to whomever I want.
If you so will worship before me, it will all be yours.”
Jesus answer him, “Get behind me Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord una God, and you shall serve him only.’”
He led him to Jerusalem, and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and talk say to him, “If You be the Son of God, throw yourself down from here,
for it is written, ‘He will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you;’
and, ‘On dem hands Dem go bear you up, lest perhaps you dash una foot against a stone.’”
Jesus answering, talk say to him, “It Don dey talk say, ‘You no go tempt the Lord una God.’”
When the devil had completed every temptation, he comot from him until another time.
Jesus come back in the power of the Spirit into Galilee, and news about him spread through all the surrounding area.
He taught in dem synagogues, being glorified by all.
He come to Nazareth, where he Bin dey bring up. He entered, as was his custom, into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and stood up to read.
The book of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. He opened the book, and find the place where it was written,

“The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to preach better news to the poor. He has sent me to heal the broken hearted, to proclaim release to the captives, recovering of sight to the blind, to deliver people Wey crushed,
and to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.”
He closed the book, give it back to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of all in the synagogue were fastened on him.
He began to tell dem, “Today, this Scripture Don dey fulfilled in una hearing.”
All testified about him, and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth, and dem talk say, “No be this Joseph’s son?”
E tell dem say, “Doubtless You go tell me this parable, ‘Physician, heal yourself! Anything wey we have heard done at Capernaum, do also here in una hometown.’”
He talk say, “True true, I tell una, no prophet is acceptable in his hometown.
But True true, I tell una, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut up three years and six months, when a great famine come over all the land.
Elijah was sent to none of dem, except to Zarephath, in the land of Sidon, to a woman who was a widow.
There were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, yet not one of dem was cleansed, except Naaman, the Syrian.”
Dem were all filled with serious anger in the synagogue, as dem heard these things.
Dem rose up, threw him out of the city, and led him to the brow of the hill that dem city was built on, that dem might throw him off the cliff.
But he, passing through the middle of dem, go his way.
He come down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee. He was teaching dem on the Sabbath day,
and dem were astonished at his teaching, for his word was with authority.
In the synagogue there was a man who had a spirit of an unclean demon, and he cried out with a loud voice,
saying, “Ah! what have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know you who You be: the Holy One of God!”
Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent, and come out of him!” When the demon had thrown him down in the middle of dem, he come out of him, having done him no harm.
Amazement come on all, and dem spoke together, one with another, saying, “Wetin be this word? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and dem come out!”
News about him go out into every place of the surrounding region.
He rose up from the synagogue, and entered into Simon’s house. Simon’s mother-in-law was afflicted with a great fever, and dem begged him for her.
He stood over her, and rebuked the fever; and it left her. Sharp-sharp she rose up and served dem.
When the sun was setting, all people wey had any sick with various diseases bring dem to him; and he laid his hands on every one of dem, and healed dem.
Demons also come out of many, crying out, and saying, “You be the Christ, the Son of God!” Rebuking dem, he didn’t allow dem to speak, because dem know that he was the Christ.
When it was day, he comot and go into an uninhabited place, and the plenty people looked for him, and come to him, and held on to him, so that he wouldn’t go away from dem.
But E tell dem say, “I must preach the better news of God’s Kingdom to the other cities also. For this reason I Don dey sent.”
He was preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.
Now while the plenty people pressed on him and heard the word of God, he was standing by the lake of Gennesaret.
He see two boats standing by the lake, but the fishermen had gone out of dem, and were washing dem nets.
He entered into one of the boats, which was Simon’s, and ask him to put out a little from the land. He sat down and taught the plenty people from the boat.
When he had finished speaking, he talk say to Simon, “Put out into the deep, and let down una nets for a catch.”
Simon answer him, “Master, we worked all night, and take nothing; but at una word I go let down the net.”
When dem had done this, dem caught Plenty people of fish, and dem net was breaking.
Dem beckoned to dem partners in the other boat, that dem should come and help dem. Dem come, and filled both boats, so that dem began to sink.
But Simon Peter, when he see it, fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, “Depart from me, for I be a sinful man, Lord.”
For he was amazed, and all who were with him, at the catch of fish which dem had caught;
and so also were James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. Jesus talk say to Simon, “No fear. From now on You go be catching people alive.”
When dem had bring dem boats to land, dem left everything, and follow him.
While he was in one of the cities, see am, there was a man full of leprosy. When he see Jesus, he fell on his face, and begged him, saying, “Lord, if you want to, you can make me clean.”
He stretched out his hand, and touched him, saying, “I want to. Be made clean.” Sharp-sharp the leprosy left him.
He commanded him to tell Nobody, “But go una way, and show yourself to the priest, and offer for una cleansing according to what Moses commanded, for a testimony to dem.”
But the report concerning him spread much more, and Plenty people come together to hear, and to be healed by him of dem infirmities.
But he withdrew imself into the desert, and prayed.

On one of those days, he was teaching; and there were Pharisees and teachers of the law sitting by, who had come out of every village of Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem. The power of the Lord was with him to heal dem.
See am, men bring a paralyzed man on a cot, and dem sought to bring him in to lay before Jesus.
Not finding a way to bring him in because of the plenty people, dem go up to the housetop, and Make e down through the tiles with his cot into the middle before Jesus.
Seeing dem faith, E tell am say, “Man, una sins are forgiven you.”
The scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, “Wey be this that speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?”
But Jesus, perceiving dem thoughts, answer dem, “Why are you reasoning so in una hearts?
Which is easier to say, ‘Una sins are forgiven you;’ or to say, ‘Arise and walk?’
But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins” (he talk say to the paralyzed man), “I tell una, arise, and take up una cot, and go to una house.”
Sharp-sharp he rose up before dem, and take up that which he was laying on, and comot to his house, glorifying God.
Amazement take hold on all, and dem glorified God. Dem were filled with fear, saying, “We have seen strange things today.”
After these things he go out, and see a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office, and talk say to him, “Follow me!”
He left everything, and rose up and follow him.
Levi made a great feast for him in his house. There was a great crowd of tax collectors and others who were reclining with dem.
Dem scribes and the Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with the tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus answer dem, “People Wey healthy have no need for a physician, but people Wey sick do.
I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
Dem tell am say, “Why do John’s disciples often fast and pray, likewise also the disciples of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink?”
E tell dem say, “Can you make the friends of the bridegroom fast, while the bridegroom is with dem?
But the days will come when the bridegroom Go be taken away from dem. Then Dem go fast in those days.”
He also told a parable to dem. “Nobody puts a piece from a new garment on an old garment, or else he will tear the new, and also the piece from the new No go match the old.
Nobody puts new wine into old wine skins, or else the new wine will burst the skins, and it Go be spilled, and the skins Go be destroyed.
But new wine must be put into fresh wine skins, and both are preserved.
No man having drunk old wine sharp-sharp desires new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’”
Now on the second Sabbath after the first, he was going through the grain fields. His disciples plucked the heads of grain and ate, rubbing dem in dem hands.
But some of the Pharisees talk say to dem, “Why do you do that which No be lawful to do on the Sabbath day?”
Jesus, answering dem, talk say, “Haven’t you read what David did when he was hungry, he, and people wey were with him;
how he entered into God’s house, and take and ate the show bread, and give also to people wey were with him, which No be lawful to eat except for the priests alone?”
E tell dem say, “The Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.”
It also happened on another Sabbath that he entered into the synagogue and taught. There was a man there, and his right hand was withered.
The scribes and the Pharisees watched him, to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, that dem might find an accusation against him.
But he know dem thoughts; and he talk say to the man who had the withered hand, “Rise up, and stand in the middle.” He arose and stood.
Then Jesus tell dem say, “I go ask you something: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good, or to do harm? To save a life, or to kill?”
He looked around at dem all, and talk say to the man, “Stretch out una hand.” He did, and his hand was restored as sound as the other.
But dem were filled with rage, and talked with each other about Wetin dem might do to Jesus.
In these days, he go out to the mountain to pray, and he continued all night in prayer to God.
When it was day, he call his disciples, and from dem he chose twelve, whom he also named apostles:
Simon, whom he also named Peter; Andrew, his brother; James; John; Philip; Bartholomew;
Matthew; Thomas; James, the son of Alphaeus; Simon, who was call the Zealot;
Judas the son of James; and Judas Iscariot, who also became a traitor.

He come down with dem, and stood on a level place, with a crowd of his disciples, and a great number of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem, and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, who come to hear him and to be healed of dem diseases;
as well as people wey were troubled by unclean spirits, and dem were being healed.
All the plenty people sought to touch him, for power come out of him and healed dem all.
He lifted up his eyes to his disciples, and talk say, “Blessed are you Wey be poor, God’s Kingdom is yours.
Blessed are you who hunger now, for You go be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for You go laugh.
Blessed are you when men shall hate you, and when dem shall exclude and mock you, and throw out una name as evil, for the Son of Man’s sake.
Glad well-well in that day, and leap for gladness, for see am, una reward is great in heaven, for dem fathers did the same thing to the prophets.
“But woe to you Wey be rich! For you have received una consolation.
Woe to you, you Wey be full now, for You go be hungry. Woe to you who laugh now, for You go mourn and weep.
Woe, when men speak well of you, for dem fathers did the same thing to the false prophets.
“But I tell una who hear: love una enemies, do good to people wey hate you,
bless people wey curse you, and pray for people wey mistreat you.
To him who strikes you on the cheek, offer also the other; and from him who takes away una cloak, no withhold una coat also.
Give to Everybody wey asks you, and no ask him who takes away una goods to give dem back again.
“As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to dem.
If you love people wey love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love people wey love dem.
If you do good to people wey do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do the same.
If you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, to receive back as much.
But love una enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting nothing back; and una reward Go be great, and You go be pikin dem of the Most High; for he is kind toward the unthankful and evil.
“So be merciful, even as una Father is also merciful.
No judge, and you no go be judged. No condemn, and you no go be condemned. Set free, and You go be set free.
“Give, and it Go be given to you: good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, Go be given to you. For with the same measure you measure it Go be measured back to you.”
He spoke a parable to dem. “Can the blind guide the blind? No go dem both fall into a pit?
A disciple No be above his teacher, but everyone when he is fully trained Go be like his teacher.
Why do you see the speck of chaff that is in una brother’s eye, but no consider the beam that is in una own eye?

Or how can you tell una brother, ‘Brother, let me remove the speck of chaff that is in una eye,’ when you yourself no see the beam that is in una own eye? You fake person! First remove the beam from una own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck of chaff that is in una brother’s eye.
For E get no good tree that produces rotten fruit; nor again a rotten tree that produces good fruit.
For each tree is known by its own fruit. For people no gather figs from thorns, nor do dem gather grapes from a bramble bush.

The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings out that which is good, and the evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart brings out that which is evil, for out of the abundance of the heart, his mouth speaks.
“Why do you call me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and no do the things which I say?
Everybody wey comes to me, and hears my words, and does dem, I go show you who he is like.

He is like a man building a house, who dug and go deep, and laid a foundation on the rock. When a flood arose, the stream broke against that house, and could not shake it, because it was founded on the rock.
But person wey hears, and no dey do, is like a man who built a house on the earth without a foundation, against which the stream broke, and sharp-sharp it fell, and the ruin of that house was great.”
After he had finished speaking in the hearing of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
A certain centurion’s worker, who was dear to him, was sick and at the point of death.
When he heard about Jesus, he sent to him elders of the Jews, asking him to come and save his worker.
When dem come to Jesus, dem begged him earnestly, saying, “He is worthy for you to do this for him,
for he loves our nation, and he built our synagogue for us.”
Jesus go with dem. When he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying to him, “Lord, no trouble yourself, for I be not worthy for you to come under my roof.
So I didn’t even think myself worthy to come to you; but say the word, and my worker Go be healed.
For I also am a man placed under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘Go!’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come!’ and he comes; and to my worker, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
When Jesus heard these things, he surprise well-well at him, and turned and talk say to the plenty people who follow him, “I tell una, I have not find such great faith, no, not in Israel.”
People wey were sent, returning to the house, find that the worker who Bin dey sick was well.
Soon afterwards, he go to a city call Nain. Many of his disciples, along with Plenty people, go with him.
Now when he come near to the gate of the city, see am, one who was dead was carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. Many people of the city were with her.
When the Lord see her, he had compassion on her, and talk say to her, “No cry.”
He come near and touched the coffin, and the bearers stood still. He talk say, “Young man, I tell una, arise!”
Person wey was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he give him to his mother.
Fear take hold of all, and dem glorified God, saying, “A great prophet has arisen among us!” and, “God has visited his people!”
This report go out concerning him in the whole of Judea, and in all the surrounding region.
The disciples of John told him about all these things.
John, calling to imself two of his disciples, sent dem to Jesus, saying, “Are you the one Wey be coming, or should we look for another?”
When the men had come to him, dem talk say, “John the Baptizer has sent us to you, saying, ‘Are you person wey comes, or should we look for another?’”
In that hour he cured many of diseases and plagues and evil spirits; and to many who were blind he give sight.

Jesus answer dem, “Go and tell John the things which you have seen and heard: that the blind receive dem sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have better news preached to dem.
Blessed is person wey finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”
When John’s messengers had comot, he began to tell the plenty people about John, “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft clothing? See am, people Wey gorgeously dressed, and live delicately, are in kings’ courts.
But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell una, and much more than a prophet.
This is he of whom it is written, ‘See am, I send my messenger before una face, who will prepare una way before you.’
“For I tell una, among people Wey born of women there No be a greater prophet than John the Baptizer, yet person Wey least in God’s Kingdom is greater than he.”
When all the people and the tax collectors heard this, dem declared God to be just, having been baptized with John’s baptism.
But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected the counsel of God, not being baptized by him themselves.
“To what then will I liken the people of this generation? Wetin be dem like?
Dem be like pikin dem who sit in the marketplace, and call to each other, saying, ‘We piped to you, and you didn’t dance. We mourned, and you didn’t weep.’
For John the Baptizer come neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon.’
The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, ‘See am, a gluttonous man, and a drunkard; a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
Wisdom is justified by all her pikin dem.”
One of the Pharisees invited him to eat with him. He entered into the Pharisee’s house, and sat at the table.
See am, a woman in the city who was a sinner, when she know that he was reclining in the Pharisee’s house, she bring an alabaster jar of ointment.
Standing behind at his feet weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears, and she wiped dem with the hair of her head, kissed his feet, and anointed dem with the ointment.

Now when the Pharisee who had invited him see it, he talk say to imself, “This man, if he were a prophet, would have perceived who and what kind of woman this is who touches him, that she is a sinner.”
Jesus answer him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” He talk say, “Teacher, say on.”
“A certain lender had two debtors. The one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
When dem no fit pay, he forgave dem both. Which of dem so will love him most?”
Simon answer, “He, I suppose, to whom he forgave the most.” E tell am say, “You have judged correctly.”

Turning to the woman, he talk say to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered into una house, and you give me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears, and wiped dem with the hair of her head.
You give me no kiss, but she, since the time I come in, has not ceased to kiss my feet.
You didn’t anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment.
So I tell una, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she love much. But to whom little is forgiven, the same loves little.”
E tell am say, “Una sins are forgiven.”
People wey sat at the table with him began to say to themselves, “Wey be this who even forgives sins?”
He talk say to the woman, “Una faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
Soon afterwards, he go about through cities and villages, preaching and bringing the better news of God’s Kingdom. With him were the twelve,
and certain women who Bin dey healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary who was call Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out;
and Joanna, the wife of Chuzas, Herod’s steward; Susanna; and many others; who served dem from dem possessions.
When Plenty people come together, and people from every city were coming to him, he spoke by a parable.
“The farmer go out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell along the road, and it was trampled under foot, and the birds of the sky devoured it.
Other seed fell on the rock, and as soon as it grew, it withered away, because it had no moisture.
Other fell amid the thorns, and the thorns grew with it, and choked it.
Other fell into the good ground, and grew, and produced one hundred times as much fruit.” As he talk say these things, he call out, “Person wey has ears to hear, Make e hear!”
Then his disciples ask him, “What does this parable mean?”
He talk say, “To you it is given to know the mysteries of God’s Kingdom, but to the rest in parables; that ‘seeing dem may not see, and hearing dem may not understand.’
Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.
Those along the road are people wey hear, then the devil comes, and takes away the word from dem heart, that dem may not believe and be saved.
Those on the rock are dem who, when dem hear, receive the word with gladness; but these have no root, who believe for a while, then fall away in time of temptation.
That which fell among the thorns, these are people wey have heard, and as dem go on dem way Dem be choked with cares, riches, and pleasures of life, and bring no fruit to maturity.
That in the good ground, these are such as in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, hold it tightly, and produces fruit with patience.
“Nobody, when he has lit a lamp, covers it with a container, or puts it under a bed; but puts it on a stand, that people wey enter in may see the light.
For nothing is hidden, that No go be revealed; nor anything secret, that No go be known and come to light.
Be careful so how you hear. For Anybody wey has, to him Go be given; and Anybody wey no dey have, from him Go be taken away even that which he thinks he has.”
His mother and brothers come to him, and dem could not come near him for the crowd.
Some people told him, “Una mother and una brothers stand outside, desiring to see you.”
But he answer dem, “My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God, and do it.”
Now on one of those days, he entered into a boat, imself and his disciples, and E tell dem say, “Let’s go over to the other side of the lake.” So dem launched out.
But as dem sailed, he fell asleep. A wind storm come down on the lake, and dem were taking on dangerous amounts of water.
Dem come to him, and awoke him, saying, “Master, master, We be dying!” He awoke, and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water, and dem ceased, and it was calm.
E tell dem say, “Where is una faith?” Being afraid dem surprise well-well, saying to each other, “Wey be this, then, that he commands even the winds and the water, and dem obey him?”
Dem arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is opposite Galilee.
When Jesus stepped ashore, a certain man out of the city who had demons for a long time met him. He wore no clothes, and didn’t live in a house, but in the tombs.
When he see Jesus, he cried out, and fell down before him, and with a loud voice talk say, “What do I have to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I beg you, no torment me!”
