For Jesus was commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For the unclean spirit had often seized the man. He was kept under guard, and bound with chains and fetters. Breaking the bands apart, he was driven by the demon into the desert.
Jesus ask him, “Wetin be una name?” He talk say, “Legion,” for many demons had entered into him.
Dem begged him that he would not command dem to go into the abyss.
Now there was there a herd of many pigs feeding on the mountain, and dem begged him that he would allow dem to enter into those. He allowed dem.
The demons come out of the man, and entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake, and were drowned.
When people wey fed dem see what had happened, dem fled, and told it in the city and in the country.
People go out to see what had happened. Dem come to Jesus, and find the man from whom the demons had gone out, sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind; and dem were afraid.
People wey see it told dem how person wey Bin dey possessed by demons was healed.
All the people of the surrounding country of the Gadarenes ask him to depart from dem, for dem were well-well afraid. He entered into the boat, and come back.
But the man from whom the demons had gone out begged him that he might go with him, but Jesus sent him away, saying,
“Return to una house, and declare what great things God has done for you.” He go his way, proclaiming throughout the whole city what great things Jesus had done for him.
When Jesus come back, the plenty people welcomed him, for dem were all waiting for him.
See am, there come a man named Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue. He fell down at Jesus’ feet, and begged him to come into his house,
for he had an only daughter, about twelve years of age, and she was dying. But as he go, the plenty people pressed against him.
A woman who had a flow of blood for twelve years, who had spent all her living on physicians, and could not be healed by any,
come behind him, and touched the fringe of his cloak, and sharp-sharp the flow of her blood stopped.
Jesus talk say, “Who touched me?” When all denied it, Peter and those with him talk say, “Master, the plenty people press and jostle you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
But Jesus talk say, “Someone did touch me, for I perceived that power has gone out of me.”

When the woman see that she No be hidden, she come trembling, and falling down before him declared to him in the presence of all the people the reason why she had touched him, and how she was healed sharp-sharp.
E tell am say, “Daughter, cheer up. Una faith has made you well. Go in peace.”
While he still spoke, one from the ruler of the synagogue’s house come, saying to him, “Una daughter is dead. No trouble the Teacher.”
But Jesus hearing it, answer him, “No fear. Only believe, and she Go be healed.”
When he come to the house, he didn’t allow anyone to enter in, except Peter, John, James, the father of the pikin, and her mother.
All were weeping and mourning her, but he talk say, “No weep. She no be dead, but sleeping.”
Dem were ridiculing him, knowing that she was dead.
But he put dem all outside, and taking her by the hand, he call, saying, “Pikin, arise!”
Her spirit come back, and she rose up sharp-sharp. He commanded that something be given to her to eat.
Her parents were amazed, but he commanded dem to tell Nobody what Bin dey done.
He call the twelve together, and give dem power and authority over all demons, and to cure diseases.
He sent dem out to preach God’s Kingdom and to heal the sick.
E tell dem say, “Take nothing for una journey — neither staffs, nor wallet, nor bread, nor money; neither have two coats apiece.
Into Anything wey house you enter, stay there, and depart from there.
As many as no receive you, when you depart from that city, shake off even the dust from una feet for a testimony against dem.”
Dem comot, and go throughout the villages, preaching the Better news, and healing everywhere.
Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was done by him; and he was very perplexed, because it was talk say by some that John had risen from the dead,
and by some that Elijah had appeared, and by others that one of the old prophets had risen again.
Herod talk say, “John I beheaded, but Wey be this, about whom I hear such things?” He sought to see him.
The apostles, when dem had come back, told him what things dem had done. He take dem, and withdrew apart to a deserted place of a city call Bethsaida.
But the plenty people, perceiving it, follow him. He welcomed dem, and spoke to dem of God’s Kingdom, and he cured people wey needed healing.

The day began to wear away; and the twelve come, and talk say to him, “Send the plenty people away, that dem may go into the surrounding villages and farms, and lodge, and get chop, for We be here in a deserted place.”
But E tell dem say, “You give dem something to eat.” Dem talk say, “We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we should go and buy chop for all these people.”
For dem were about five thousand men. He talk say to his disciples, “Make dem sit down in groups of about fifty each.”
Dem did so, and made dem all sit down.
He take the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to the sky, he blessed dem, and broke dem, and give dem to the disciples to set before the plenty people.
Dem ate, and were all filled. Dem gathered up twelve baskets of broken pieces that were left over.
As he was praying alone, the disciples were with him, and he ask dem, “Who do the plenty people say that I be?”
Dem answer, “‘John the Baptizer,’ but others say, ‘Elijah,’ and others, that one of the old prophets is risen again.”
E tell dem say, “But who do you say that I be?” Peter answer, “The Christ of God.”
But he warned dem, and commanded dem to tell this to Nobody,
saying, “The Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.”
He talk say to all, “If anyone desires to come after me, Make e deny imself, take up his cross, and follow me.
For Anybody wey desires to save his life will lose it, but Anybody wey will lose his life for my sake, the same will save it.
For what does it profit a man if he gains the whole world, and loses or forfeits his own self?
For Anybody wey Go be ashamed of me and of my words, of him will the Son of Man be ashamed, when he comes in his glory, and the glory of the Father, and of the holy angels.
But I tell una the truth: E get some of people wey stand here, who will in no way taste of death, until dem see God’s Kingdom.”
About eight days after these sayings, he take with him Peter, John, and James, and go up onto the mountain to pray.
As he was praying, the appearance of his face was altered, and his clothing became white and dazzling.
See am, two men were talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah,
who appeared in glory, and spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.
Now Peter and people wey were with him were heavy with sleep, but when dem were fully awake, dem see his glory, and the two men who stood with him.

As dem were parting from him, Peter talk say to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let’s make three tents: one for you, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah,” not knowing what he talk say.
While he talk say these things, a cloud come and overshadowed dem, and dem were afraid as dem entered into the cloud.
A voice come out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!”
When the voice come, Jesus was find alone. Dem were silent, and told Nobody in those days any of the things which dem had seen.
On the next day, when dem had come down from the mountain, Plenty people met him.
See am, a man from the crowd call out, saying, “Teacher, I beg you to look at my son, for he is my only pikin.
See am, a spirit takes him, he suddenly cries out, and it convulses him so that he foams, and it hardly departs from him, bruising him severely.
I begged una disciples to throw it out, and dem no fit.”
Jesus answer, “Faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring una son here.”
While he was still coming, the demon threw him down and convulsed him violently. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the boy, and give him back to his father.
Dem were all astonished at the majesty of God. But while all were marveling at all the things which Jesus did, he talk say to his disciples,
“Let these words sink into una ears, for the Son of Man Go be delivered up into the hands of men.”
But dem didn’t understand this saying. It was concealed from dem, that dem no suppose perceive it, and dem were afraid to ask him about this saying.
There arose an argument among dem about which of dem was the greatest.
Jesus, perceiving the reasoning of dem hearts, take a little pikin, and set him by his side,
and talk say to dem, “Anybody wey receives this little pikin in my name receives me. Anybody wey receives me receives him who sent me. For Anybody wey is least among you all, this one Go be great.”
John answer, “Master, we see someone casting out demons in una name, and we forbade him, because he no dey follow with us.”
Jesus tell am say, “No forbid him, for person Wey not against us is for us.”
E happen say, when the days were near that he should be taken up, he intently set his face to go to Jerusalem,
and sent messengers before his face. Dem go, and entered into a village of the Samaritans, so as to prepare for him.
Dem didn’t receive him, because he was traveling with his face set towards Jerusalem.
When his disciples, James and John, see this, dem talk say, “Lord, do you want us to command fire to come down from the sky, and destroy dem, just as Elijah did?”
But he turned and rebuked dem, “You no know of what kind of spirit You be.
For the Son of Man didn’t come to destroy men’s lives, but to save dem.” Dem go to another village.
As dem go on the way, a certain man talk say to him, “I want to follow you Anywhere wey you go, Lord.”
Jesus tell am say, “The foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay his head.”
He talk say to another, “Follow me!” But he talk say, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”
But Jesus tell am say, “Leave the dead to bury dem own dead, but you go and announce God’s Kingdom.”
Another also talk say, “I want to follow you, Lord, but first allow me to say good-bye to people Wey at my house.”
But Jesus tell am say, “Nobody, having put his hand to the plow, and looking back, is fit for God’s Kingdom.”
Now after these things, the Lord also appointed seventy others, and sent dem two by two ahead of him into every city and place, where he was about to come.
Then E tell dem say, “The harvest is indeed plentiful, but the laborers are few. Pray so to the Lord of the harvest, that he may send out laborers into his harvest.
Go una ways. See am, I send you out as lambs among wolves.
Carry no purse, nor wallet, nor sandals. Greet Nobody on the way.
Into Anything wey house you enter, first say, ‘Peace be to this house.’
If a son of peace is there, una peace will rest on him; but if not, it will return to you.
Remain in that same house, eating and drinking the things dem give, for the laborer is worthy of his wages. No go from house to house.
Into Anything wey city you enter, and dem receive you, eat the things that are set before you.
Heal the sick Wey be inside am, and tell dem, ‘God’s Kingdom has come near to you.’
But into Anything wey city you enter, and dem no receive you, go out into its streets and say,
‘Even the dust from una city that clings to us, we wipe off against you. Nevertheless know this, that God’s Kingdom has come near to you.’
I tell una, it Go be more tolerable in that day for Sodom than for that city.
“Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works Bin dey done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, dem would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
But it Go be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the judgment than for you.
You, Capernaum, Wey be exalted to heaven, Go be bring down to Hades.
Anybody wey listens to you listens to me, and Anybody wey rejects you rejects me. Anybody wey rejects me rejects him who sent me.”
The seventy come back with gladness, saying, “Lord, even the demons are subject to us in una name!”
E tell dem say, “I see Satan having fallen like lightning from heaven.
See am, I give you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will in any way hurt you.
Nevertheless, no glad well-well in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but glad well-well that una names are written in heaven.”

In that same hour Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit, and talk say, “I thank you, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed dem to little pikin dem. Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in una sight.”

Turning to the disciples, he talk say, “All things Don dey delivered to me by my Father. Nobody knows who the Son is, except the Father, and who the Father is, except the Son, and he to whomever the Son desires to reveal him.”
Turning to the disciples, he talk say privately, “Blessed are the eyes which see the things that you see,
for I tell una that many prophets and kings desired to see the things which you see, and didn’t see dem, and to hear the things which you hear, and didn’t hear dem.”
See am, a certain lawyer stood up and tested him, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit life wey no dey end?”
E tell am say, “Wetin be written in the law? How do you read it?”
He answer, “You shall love the Lord una God with all una heart, with all una soul, with all una strength, and with all una mind; and una neighbor as yourself.”
E tell am say, “You have answer correctly. Do this, and You go live.”
But he, desiring to justify imself, ask Jesus, “Wey be my neighbor?”
Jesus answer, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and comot, leaving him half dead.
By chance a certain priest was going down that way. When he see him, he passed by on the other side.
In the same way a Levite also, when he come to the place, and see him, passed by on the other side.
But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, come where he was. When he see him, he was moved with compassion,
come to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own animal, and bring him to an inn, and take care of him.
On the next day, when he comot, he take out two denarii, and give dem to the host, and talk say to him, ‘Take care of him. Anything wey you spend beyond that, I go repay you when I return.’
Now which of these three do you think seemed to be a neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?”
He talk say, “Person wey showed mercy on him.” Then Jesus tell am say, “Go and do likewise.”
As dem go on dem way, he entered into a certain village, and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.
She had a sister call Mary, who also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word.
But Martha was distracted with much serving, and she come up to him, and talk say, “Lord, no you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Ask her so to help me.”
Jesus answer her, “Martha, Martha, You be anxious and troubled about many things,
but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which No go be taken away from her.”
When he finished praying in a certain place, one of his disciples talk say to him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”
E tell dem say, “When you pray, say, ‘Our Father in heaven, may una name be kept holy. May una Kingdom come. May una Go be done on earth, as it is in heaven.
Give us day by day our daily bread.
Forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone Wey be indebted to us. Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’”
E tell dem say, “Which of you, if you go to a friend at midnight, and tell him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
for a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him,’
and he from within will answer and say, ‘No bother me. The door is now shut, and my pikin dem are with me in bed. I no fit get up and give it to you’?
I tell una, although he No go rise and give it to him because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence, he will get up and give him as many as he needs.
“I tell una, keep asking, and it Go be given you. Keep seeking, and You go find. Keep knocking, and it Go be opened to you.
For Everybody wey asks receives. Person wey seeks finds. To him who knocks it Go be opened.
“Which of you fathers, if una son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, he no go give him a snake instead of a fish, will he?
Or if he asks for an egg, he no go give him a scorpion, will he?
If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to una pikin dem, how much more will una heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to people wey ask him?”
He was casting out a demon, and it was mute. When the demon had gone out, the mute man spoke; and the plenty people surprise well-well.
But some of dem talk say, “He casts out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons.”
Others, testing him, sought from him a sign from heaven.
But he, knowing dem thoughts, talk say to dem, “Every kingdom divided against itself is bring to desolation. A house divided against itself falls.
If Satan also is divided against imself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I throw out demons by Beelzebul.
But if I throw out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do una pikin dem throw dem out? So will dem be una judges.
But if I by God’s finger throw out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come to you.
“When the strong man, fully armed, guards his own dwelling, his goods are safe.
But when someone stronger attacks him and overcomes him, he takes from him his whole armor in which he trusted, and divides his plunder.
“He that No be with me is against me. Person wey no dey gather with me scatters.
The unclean spirit, when he has gone out of the man, passes through dry places, seeking rest, and finding none, he says, ‘I go turn back to my house from which I come out.’
When he returns, he finds it swept and put in order.
Then he goes, and takes seven other spirits more evil than imself, and dem enter in and live there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first.”
E happen say, as he talk say these things, a certain woman out of the plenty people lifted up her voice, and talk say to him, “Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts which nursed you!”
But he talk say, “On the contrary, blessed are people wey hear the word of God, and keep it.”
When the plenty people were gathering together to him, he began to say, “This is an evil generation. It seeks after a sign. No sign Go be given to it but the sign of Jonah, the prophet.
For even as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so will also the Son of Man be to this generation.

The Queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and will condemn dem: for she come from every corner of the world to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and see am, one greater than Solomon is here.
The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it: for dem repented at the preaching of Jonah, and see am, one greater than Jonah is here.
“Nobody, when he has lit a lamp, puts it in a cellar or under a basket, but on a stand, that people wey come in may see the light.
The lamp of the body is the eye. So when una eye is good, una whole body is also full of light; but when it is evil, una body also is full of darkness.
So see whether the light that is in you no be darkness.
If so una whole body is full of light, having no part dark, it Go be wholly full of light, as when the lamp with its bright shining gives you light.”
Now as he spoke, a certain Pharisee ask him to dine with him. He go in, and sat at the table.
When the Pharisee see it, he surprise well-well that he had not first washed imself before dinner.
The Lord talk say to him, “Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but una inward part is full of extortion and wickedness.
You foolish ones, didn’t person wey made the outside make the inside also?
But give for gifts to the needy those things which are within, and see am, all things Go be clean to you.
But woe to you Pharisees! For you tithe mint and rue and every herb, but you bypass justice and God’s love. You ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.
Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the best seats in the synagogues, and the greetings in the marketplaces.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, fake people! For You be like hidden graves, and the men who walk over dem no know it.”
One of the lawyers answer him, “Teacher, in saying this you insult us also.”
He talk say, “Woe to you lawyers also! For you load men with burdens that are difficult to carry, and you unaself no go even lift one finger to help carry those burdens.
Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and una fathers killed dem.
So you testify and consent to the works of una fathers. For dem killed dem, and you build dem tombs.
So also the wisdom of God talk say, ‘I go send to dem prophets and apostles; and some of dem Dem go kill and persecute,
that the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zachariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary.’ Yes, I tell una, it Go be required of this generation.
Woe to you lawyers! For you take away the key of knowledge. You didn’t enter in unaself, and people wey were entering in, you hindered.”
As he talk say these things to dem, the scribes and the Pharisees began to be terribly angry, and to draw many things out of him;
lying in wait for him, and seeking to catch him in something he might say, that dem might accuse him.

Meanwhile, when a plenty people of many thousands had gathered together, so much so that dem trampled on each other, he began to tell his disciples first of all, “Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
But E get nothing covered up, that No go be revealed, nor hidden, that No go be known.
So Anything wey you have talk say in the darkness Go be heard in the light. Wetin you have spoken in the ear in the inner rooms Go be proclaimed on the housetops.
“I tell una, my friends, No fear of people wey kill the body, and after that have no more that dem can do.
But I go warn you whom you should fear. Fear him, who after he has killed, has power to throw into Gehenna. Yes, I tell una, fear him.
“No be five sparrows sold for two assaria coins? Not one of dem is forgotten by God.
But the very hairs of una head are all counted. So No fear. You be of more value than many sparrows.
“I tell una, Everybody wey confesses me before men, him will the Son of Man also confess before the angels of God;
but person wey denies me in the presence of men Go be denied in the presence of the angels of God.
Everybody wey speaks a word against the Son of Man Go be forgiven, but people wey blaspheme against the Holy Spirit No go be forgiven.
When dem bring you before the synagogues, the rulers, and the authorities, No worry about how or Wetin you go answer, or Wetin you go say;
for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that same hour Wetin you must say.”
One of the plenty people talk say to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
But E tell am say, “Man, who made me a judge or an arbitrator over you?”
E tell dem say, “Beware! Keep unaself from covetousness, for a man’s life no dey consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.”
He spoke a parable to dem, saying, “The ground of a certain rich man produced abundantly.
He reasoned within imself, saying, ‘What will I do, because I no have room to store my crops?’
He talk say, ‘This is what I go do. I go pull down my barns, and build bigger ones, and there I go store all my grain and my goods.
I go tell my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take una ease, eat, drink, be merry.”’
“But God talk say to him, ‘You foolish one, tonight una soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared — whose will dem be?’
So is person wey lays up treasure for imself, and No be rich toward God.”
He talk say to his disciples, “So I tell una, No worry about una life, Wetin you go eat, nor yet for una body, Wetin you go wear.
Life is more than chop, and the body is more than clothing.
Consider the ravens: dem no sow, dem no reap, dem have no warehouse or barn, and God feeds dem. How much more valuable are you than birds!
Which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his height?
If then you no be able to do even the least things, why are you anxious about the rest?
Consider the lilies, how dem grow. Dem no toil, neither do dem spin; yet I tell una, even Solomon in all his glory No be arrayed like one of these.
But if this is how God clothes the grass in the field, which today exists, and tomorrow is throw into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O you of little faith?
No seek Wetin you go eat or Wetin you go drink; neither be anxious.
For the nations of the world seek after all of these things, but una Father knows that you need these things.
But seek God’s Kingdom, and all these things Go be added to you.
No fear, little flock, for it is una Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.
Sell that which you have, and give gifts to the needy. Make for unaself purses which no grow old, a treasure in the heavens that no dey fail, where no thief approaches, neither moth destroys.
For where una treasure is, there will una heart be also.
“Let una waist be dressed and una lamps burning.
Be like men watching for dem lord, when he returns from the marriage feast; that, when he comes and knocks, dem may sharp-sharp open to him.
Blessed are those workers, whom the lord will find watching when he comes. True true, I tell una, that he will dress imself, and make dem recline, and will come and serve dem.
Dem go be blessed if he comes in the second or third watch, and finds dem so.
But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what hour the thief was coming, he would have watched, and not allowed his house to be broken into.
So be ready also, for the Son of Man is coming in an hour that you no expect him.”
Peter talk say to him, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everybody?”
The Lord talk say, “Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his lord will set over his household, to give dem dem portion of chop at the right times?
Blessed is that worker whom his lord will find doing so when he comes.
True true, I tell una, that he will set him over all that he has.
But if that worker says in his heart, ‘My lord delays his coming,’ and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken,
then the lord of that worker will come in a day when he no be expecting him, and in an hour that he no dey know, and will cut him in two, and place his portion with the unfaithful.
That worker, who know his lord’s will, and didn’t prepare, nor do what he want, Go be beaten with many stripes,

but person wey didn’t know, and did things worthy of stripes, Go be beaten with few stripes. To whomever much is given, of him will much be required; and to whom much was entrusted, of him more Go be ask.
“I come to throw fire on the earth. I wish it were already kindled.
But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I be until it is accomplished!
Do you think that I have come to give peace in the earth? I tell una, no, but rather division.
For from now on, there Go be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.

Dem go be divided, father against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against her mother; mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”
He talk say to the plenty people also, “When you see a cloud rising from the west, sharp-sharp you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and so it happens.
When a south wind blows, you say, ‘There Go be a scorching heat,’ and it happens.
You fake people! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you no interpret this time?
Why no you judge for unaself Wetin be right?

For when You be going with una adversary before the magistrate, try diligently on the way to be released from him, lest perhaps he drag you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
I tell una, You go by no means get out of there, until you have paid the very last penny. ”
Now there were some present at the same time who told him about the Galileans, whose blood Pilate had mixed with dem sacrifices.
Jesus answer dem, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because dem suffered such things?
I tell una, no, but unless you repent, You go all perish in the same way.
Or those eighteen, on whom the tower in Siloam fell, and killed dem; do you think that dem were worse offenders than all the men who live in Jerusalem?
I tell una, no, but, unless you repent, You go all perish in the same way.”
He spoke this parable. “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he come seeking fruit on it, and find none.
He talk say to the vine dresser, ‘See am, these three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, and find none. Cut it down. Why does it waste the soil?’
He answer, ‘Lord, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it, and fertilize it.
If it bears fruit, fine; but if not, after that, you can cut it down.’”
He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath day.
See am, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and she was bent over, and could in no way straighten sheself up.
When Jesus see her, he call her, and talk say to her, “Woman, You be freed from una infirmity.”
He laid his hands on her, and sharp-sharp she stood up straight, and glorified God.

The ruler of the synagogue, being indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, talk say to the plenty people, “E get six days in which men ought to work. So come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day!”
So the Lord answer him, “You fake people! No dey each one of you free his ox or his donkey from the stall on the Sabbath, and lead him away to water?
Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan had bound eighteen long years, be freed from this bondage on the Sabbath day?”
As he talk say these things, all his adversaries were disappointed, and all the plenty people rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.
He talk say, “Wetin be God’s Kingdom like? To what shall I compare it?
It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man take, and put in his own garden. It grew, and became a large tree, and the birds of the sky live in its branches.”
Again he talk say, “To what shall I compare God’s Kingdom?
It is like yeast, which a woman take and hid in three measures of flour, until it was all leavened.”
He go on his way through cities and villages, teaching, and traveling on to Jerusalem.
One talk say to him, “Lord, are dem few Wey be saved?” E tell dem say,
“Strive to enter in by the narrow door, for many, I tell una, will seek to enter in, and No go be able.

When once the master of the house has risen up, and has shut the door, and you begin to stand outside, and to knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us!’ then he will answer and tell you, ‘I no know you or where you come from.’
Then You go begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in una presence, and you taught in our streets.’
He will say, ‘I tell una, I no know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of wickedness.’
There Go be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets, in God’s Kingdom, and unaself being thrown outside.
Dem go come from the east, west, north, and south, and will sit down in God’s Kingdom.
See am, E get some Wey be last who Go be first, and E get some Wey be first who Go be last.”
On that same day, some Pharisees come, saying to him, “Get out of here, and go away, for Herod wants to kill you.”
E tell dem say, “Go and tell that fox, ‘See am, I throw out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I complete my mission.
Nevertheless I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the next day, for it no fit be that a prophet perish outside of Jerusalem.’

“Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that kills the prophets, and stones people Wey sent to her! How often I want to gather una pikin dem together, like a hen gathers her own brood under her wings, and you refused!
See am, una house is left to you desolate. I tell una, You go not see me, until you say, ‘Blessed is person wey comes in the name of the Lord!’”
When he go into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, dem were watching him.
See am, a certain man who had dropsy was in front of him.
Jesus, answering, spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”
But dem were silent. He take him, and healed him, and Make e go.
He answer dem, “Which of you, if una son or an ox fell into a well, wouldn’t sharp-sharp pull him out on a Sabbath day?”
Dem no fit answer him regarding these things.
He spoke a parable to people wey were invited, when he noticed how dem chose the best seats, and talk say to dem,
“When You be invited by anyone to a marriage feast, no sit in the best seat, since perhaps someone more honorable than you might be invited by him,
and person wey invited both of you would come and tell you, ‘Make room for this person.’ Then you would begin, with shame, to take the lowest place.

But when You be invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when person wey invited you comes, he may tell you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then You go be honored in the presence of all who sit at the table with you.
For Everybody wey exalts imself Go be humbled, and Anybody wey humbles imself Go be exalted.”

He also talk say to the one who had invited him, “When you make a dinner or a supper, no call una friends, nor una brothers, nor una family people, nor rich neighbors, or perhaps dem might also return the favor, and pay you back.
But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind;
and You go be blessed, because dem no have the resources to repay you. For You go be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous.”
When one of people wey sat at the table with him heard these things, E tell am say, “Blessed is person wey will feast in God’s Kingdom!”
But E tell am say, “A certain man made a great supper, and he invited many people.
He sent out his worker at supper time to tell people wey were invited, ‘Come, for everything is ready now.’
Dem all as one began to make excuses. “The first talk say to him, ‘I have bought a field, and I must go and see it. Please have me excused.’
“Another talk say, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I must go try dem out. Please have me excused.’
“Another talk say, ‘I have married a wife, and so I no fit come.’

“That worker come, and told his lord these things. Then the master of the house, being angry, talk say to his worker, ‘Go out sharp-sharp into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in the poor, maimed, blind, and lame.’
“The worker talk say, ‘Lord, it is done as you commanded, and E get still room.’
“The lord talk say to the worker, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel dem to come in, that my house may be filled.
For I tell una that none of those men who were invited will taste of my supper.’”
Now Plenty people were going with him. He turned and talk say to dem,
“If anyone comes to me, and no dey disregard his own father, mother, wife, pikin dem, brothers, and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he no fit be my disciple.
Anybody wey no dey bear his own cross, and come after me, no fit be my disciple.
For which of you, desiring to build a tower, no dey first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?
Or perhaps, when he has laid a foundation, and No be able to finish, everyone wey see begins to mock him,
saying, ‘This man began to build, and no be able to finish.’
Or what king, as he goes to encounter another king in war, No go sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand?
Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends an envoy, and asks for conditions of peace.
So so Anybody wey of you who no dey renounce all that he has, he no fit be my disciple.
Salt is good, but if the salt becomes flat and tasteless, with what do you season it?
It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile. It is thrown out. Person wey has ears to hear, Make e hear.”
Now all the tax collectors and sinners were coming close to him to hear him.
The Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with dem.”
He told dem this parable.
“Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep, and lost one of dem, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness, and go after the one that was lost, until he find it?
When he has find it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
When he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to dem, ‘Glad well-well with me, for I have find my sheep which was lost!’
I tell una that even so there Go be more gladness in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.
Or what woman, if she had ten drachma coins, if she lost one drachma coin, wouldn’t light a lamp, sweep the house, and seek diligently until she find it?
When she has find it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Glad well-well with me, for I have find the drachma which I had lost.’
Even so, I tell una, E get gladness in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”
He talk say, “A certain man had two sons.
The younger of dem talk say to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of una property.’ He divided his livelihood between dem.
Not many days after, the younger son gathered all of this together and traveled into a far country. There he wasted his property with riotous living.
When he had spent all of it, there arose a severe famine in that country, and he began to be in need.
He go and joined imself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
He want to fill his belly with the husks that the pigs ate, but Nobody give him any.
But when he come to imself he talk say, ‘How many hired workers of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!
I go get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in una sight.
I be no more worthy to be call una son. Make me as one of una hired workers.”’
“He arose, and come to his father. But while he was still far off, his father see him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
The son talk say to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in una sight. I be no longer worthy to be call una son.’
“But the father talk say to his workers, ‘Bring out the best robe, and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet.
Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and Make we eat, and celebrate;
for this, my son, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is find.’ Dem began to celebrate.
“Now his elder son was in the field. As he come near to the house, he heard music and dancing.
He call one of the workers to him, and ask what was going on.
E tell am say, ‘Una brother has come, and una father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and healthy.’
But he was angry, and would not go in. So his father come out, and begged him.
But he answer his father, ‘See am, these many years I have served you, and I never disobeyed a commandment of yours, but you never give me a goat, that I might celebrate with my friends.
But when this, una son, come, who has devoured una living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him.’
“E tell am say, ‘Son, You be always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
But it was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for this, una brother, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is find.’”
He also talk say to his disciples, “There was a certain rich man who had a manager. An accusation was made to him that this man was wasting his possessions.
He call him, and talk say to him, ‘Wetin be this that I hear about you? Give an accounting of una management, for you can no longer be manager.’
“The manager talk say within imself, ‘What will I do, seeing that my lord is taking away the management position from me? I no have strength to dig. I be ashamed to beg.
I know what I go do, so that when I be removed from management, dem may receive me into dem houses.’
Calling each one of his lord’s debtors to him, he talk say to the first, ‘How much do you owe to my lord?’
He talk say, ‘A hundred batos of oil.’ E tell am say, ‘Take una bill, and sit down sharp-sharp and write fifty.’
Then he talk say to another, ‘How much do you owe?’ He talk say, ‘A hundred cors of wheat.’ E tell am say, ‘Take una bill, and write eighty.’
“His lord commended the dishonest manager because he had done wisely, for the pikin dem of this world are, in dem own generation, wiser than the pikin dem of the light.
I tell una, make for unaself friends by means of unrighteous mammon, so that when you fail, dem may receive you into the eternal tents.
Person Wey faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. Person Wey dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
If so you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to una trust the true riches?
If you have not been faithful in that which is another’s, who will give you that which is una own?
No worker can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to one, and despise the other. You no be able to serve God and Mammon.”
The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, also heard all these things, and dem scoffed at him.
E tell dem say, “You be people wey justify unaself in the sight of men, but God knows una hearts. For that which is exalted among men is an abomination in the sight of God.
The law and the prophets were until John. From that time the Better news of God’s Kingdom is preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away, than for one tiny stroke of a pen in the law to fall.
Everybody wey divorces his wife, and marries another, commits adultery. Person wey marries one Wey be divorced from a husband commits adultery.
“Now there was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, living in luxury every day.
A certain beggar, named Lazarus, was laid at his gate, full of sores,
and desiring to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Yes, even the dogs come and licked his sores.
The beggar died, and he was carried away by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died, and was buried.
In Hades, he lifted up his eyes, being in torment, and see Abraham far off, and Lazarus at his bosom.
He cried and talk say, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue! For I be in anguish in this flame.’
“But Abraham talk say, ‘Son, remember that you, in una lifetime, received una good things, and Lazarus, in the same way, bad things. But now here he is comforted and You be in anguish.
Besides all this, between us and you E get a great gulf fixed, that people wey want to pass from here to you No be able, and that Nobody may cross over from there to us.’
“He talk say, ‘I ask you so, father, that you would send him to my father’s house;
for I have five brothers, that he may testify to dem, so dem no go also come into this place of torment.’
“But Abraham talk say to him, ‘Dem have Moses and the prophets. Make dem listen to dem.’
“He talk say, ‘No, father Abraham, but if one goes to dem from the dead, Dem go repent.’
“E tell am say, ‘If dem no listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will dem be persuaded if one rises from the dead.’”
He talk say to the disciples, “It is impossible that no occasions of stumbling should come, but woe to him through whom dem come!
It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, rather than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
Be careful. If una brother sins against you, rebuke him. If he repents, forgive him.
If he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”
The apostles talk say to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”
The Lord talk say, “If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would tell this sycamore tree, ‘Be uprooted, and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.
But Wey be there among you, having a worker plowing or keeping sheep, that will say, when he comes in from the field, ‘Come sharp-sharp and sit down at the table,’
and No go rather tell him, ‘Prepare my supper, clothe yourself properly, and serve me, while I eat and drink. Afterward you shall eat and drink’?
Does he thank that worker because he did the things that were commanded? I think not.
Even so you also, when you have done all the things that are commanded you, say, ‘We be unworthy workers. We have done our duty.’”
As he was on his way to Jerusalem, he was passing along the borders of Samaria and Galilee.
As he entered into a certain village, ten men who were lepers met him, who stood at a distance.
Dem lifted up dem voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
When he see dem, E tell dem say, “Go and show unaself to the priests.” As dem go, dem were cleansed.
One of dem, when he see that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.
He fell on his face at Jesus’ feet, giving him thanks; and he was a Samaritan.
Jesus answer, “No be the ten cleansed? But where are the nine?
Were there none find who come back to give glory to God, except this stranger?”
Then E tell am say, “Get up, and go una way. Una faith has healed you.”
Being ask by the Pharisees when God’s Kingdom would come, he answer dem, “God’s Kingdom no dey come with observation;
neither will dem say, ‘Look, here!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ for see am, God’s Kingdom is within you.”
He talk say to the disciples, “The days will come, when You go desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and You go not see it.
Dem go tell you, ‘Look, here!’ or ‘Look, there!’ No go away, nor follow after dem,
for as the lightning, when it flashes out of the one part under the sky, shines to the other part under the sky; so will the Son of Man be in his day.
But first, he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
As it was in the days of Noah, even so will it be also in the days of the Son of Man.
Dem ate, dem drank, dem married, dem were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ship, and the flood come, and destroyed dem all.
Likewise, even as it was in the days of Lot: dem ate, dem drank, dem bought, dem sold, dem planted, dem built;
but in the day that Lot go out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from the sky, and destroyed dem all.
It Go be the same way in the day that the Son of Man is revealed.
In that day, person wey Go be on the housetop, and his goods in the house, Make e not go down to take dem away. Make e Wey be in the field likewise not turn back.
Remember Lot’s wife!
Anybody wey seeks to save his life loses it, but Anybody wey loses his life preserves it.
I tell una, in that night there Go be two people in one bed. The one Go be taken, and the other Go be left.
There Go be two grinding grain together. One Go be taken, and the other Go be left.”
Dem, answering, ask him, “Where, Lord?” E tell dem say, “Where the body is, there will the vultures also be gathered together.”
He also spoke a parable to dem that dem must always pray, and not give up,
saying, “There was a judge in a certain city who didn’t fear God, and didn’t respect man.
A widow was in that city, and she often come to him, saying, ‘Defend me from my adversary!’
He wouldn’t for a while, but afterward he talk say to imself, ‘Though I neither fear God, nor respect man,
yet because this widow bothers me, I go defend her, or else she will wear me out by her continual coming.’”
The Lord talk say, “Listen to what the unrighteous judge says.
No go God avenge his chosen ones, Wey be crying out to him day and night, and yet he exercises patience with dem?
I tell una that he will avenge dem sharp-sharp. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”
He spoke also this parable to certain people who were convinced of dem own righteousness, and who despised all others.
“Two men go up into the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood and prayed to imself like this: ‘God, I thank you, that I be not like the rest of men, extortionists, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week. I give tithes of all that I get.’
But the tax collector, standing far away, wouldn’t even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’
I tell una, this man go down to his house justified rather than the other; for Everybody wey exalts imself Go be humbled, but person wey humbles imself Go be exalted.”
Dem were also bringing dem babies to him, that he might touch dem. But when the disciples see it, dem rebuked dem.
Jesus summoned dem, saying, “Allow the little pikin dem to come to me, and no hinder dem, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
Most certainly, I tell una, Anybody wey no dey receive God’s Kingdom like a little pikin, he will in no way enter into it.”
A certain ruler ask him, saying, “Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit life wey no dey end?”
Jesus ask him, “Why do you call me good? Nobody is good, except one — God.
You know the commandments: ‘No commit adultery,’ ‘No murder,’ ‘No steal,’ ‘No give false testimony,’ ‘Honor una father and una mother.’”
He talk say, “I have observed all these things from my youth up.”
When Jesus heard these things, E tell am say, “You still lack one thing. Sell all that you have, and distribute it to the poor. You go have treasure in heaven. Come, follow me.”
But when he heard these things, he became very sad, for he was very rich.
Jesus, seeing that he became very sad, talk say, “How hard it is for people wey have riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!
For it is easier for a camel to enter in through a needle’s eye, than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”
People wey heard it talk say, “Then who can be saved?”
But he talk say, “The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.”
Peter talk say, “Look, we have left everything, and follow you.”
E tell dem say, “True true, I tell una, E get Nobody who has left house, or wife, or brothers, or parents, or pikin dem, for God’s Kingdom’s sake,
who No go receive many times more in this time, and in the world to come, life wey no dey end.”
He take the twelve aside, and talk say to dem, “See am, We be going up to Jerusalem, and all the things that are written through the prophets concerning the Son of Man Go be completed.
For he Go be delivered up to the Gentiles, Go be mocked, treated shamefully, and spit on.
Dem go scourge and kill him. On the third day, he will rise again.”
Dem understand none of these things. This saying was hidden from dem, and dem didn’t understand the things that were talk say.
As he come near Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the road, begging.
Hearing a plenty people going by, he ask what this meant.
Dem told him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.
He cried out, “Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!”
People wey led the way rebuked him, that he should be quiet; but he cried out all the more, “You son of David, have mercy on me!”
Standing still, Jesus commanded him to be bring to him. When he had come near, he ask him,
“What do you want me to do?” He talk say, “Lord, that I may see again.”
Jesus tell am say, “Receive una sight. Una faith has healed you.”
Sharp-sharp he received his sight, and follow him, glorifying God. All the people, when dem see it, praised God.
He entered and was passing through Jericho.
There was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
He was trying to see who Jesus was, and no fit because of the crowd, because he was short.
He ran on ahead, and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was going to pass that way.
When Jesus come to the place, he looked up and see him, and talk say to him, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at una house.”
He hurried, come down, and received him joyfully.
When dem see it, dem all murmured, saying, “He has gone in to lodge with a man Wey be a sinner.”
Zacchaeus stood and talk say to the Lord, “See am, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor. If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much.”
Jesus tell am say, “Today, salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of Man come to seek and to save that which was lost.”
As dem heard these things, he go on and told a parable, because he was near Jerusalem, and dem supposed that God’s Kingdom would be revealed sharp-sharp.
He talk say so, “A certain nobleman go into a far country to receive for imself a kingdom, and to return.
He call ten workers of his, and give dem ten mina coins, and told dem, ‘Conduct business until I come.’
But his citizens hated him, and sent an envoy after him, saying, ‘We no want this man to reign over us.’

“When he had come back again, having received the kingdom, he commanded these workers, to whom he had given the money, to be call to him, that he might know Wetin dem had gained by conducting business.
The first come before him, saying, ‘Lord, una mina has made ten more minas.’
“E tell am say, ‘Well done, you good worker! Because you were find faithful with very little, you go get authority over ten cities.’
“The second come, saying, ‘Una mina, Lord, has made five minas.’
“So E tell am say, ‘And You be to be over five cities.’
Another come, saying, ‘Lord, see am, una mina, which I kept laid away in a handkerchief,
for I feared you, because You be an exacting man. You take up that which you didn’t lay down, and reap that which you didn’t sow.’
“E tell am say, ‘Out of una own mouth will I judge you, you wicked worker! You know that I be an exacting man, taking up that which I didn’t lay down, and reaping that which I didn’t sow.
Then why didn’t you deposit my money in the bank, and at my coming, I might have earned interest on it?’
He talk say to people wey stood by, ‘Take the mina away from him, and give it to him who has the ten minas.’
“Dem tell am say, ‘Lord, he has ten minas!’
‘For I tell una that to Everybody wey has, will more be given; but from him who no dey have, even that which he has Go be taken away from him.
But bring those enemies of mine who didn’t want me to reign over dem here, and kill dem before me.’”
Having talk say these things, he go on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
When he come near to Bethsphage and Bethany, at the mountain that is call Olivet, he sent two of his disciples,
saying, “Go una way into the village on the other side, in which, as you enter, You go find a colt tied, whereon no man ever yet sat. Untie it, and bring it.
If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ say to him: ‘The Lord needs it.’”
People wey were sent go away, and find things just as he had told dem.
As dem were untying the colt, its owners talk say to dem, “Why are you untying the colt?”
Dem talk say, “The Lord needs it.”
Dem bring it to Jesus. Dem threw dem cloaks on the colt, and set Jesus on dem.
As he go, dem spread dem cloaks on the road.

As he was now getting near, at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole plenty people of the disciples began to glad well-well and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works which dem had seen,
saying, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!”
Some of the Pharisees from the plenty people talk say to him, “Teacher, rebuke una disciples!”
He answer dem, “I tell una that if these were silent, the stones would cry out.”
When he come near, he see the city and wept over it,
saying, “If you, even you, had known today the things which belong to una peace! But now, Dem be hidden from una eyes.
For the days will come on you, when una enemies will throw up a barricade against you, surround you, hem you in on every side,
and will dash you and una pikin dem within you to the ground. Dem go not leave in you one stone on another, because you didn’t know the time of una visitation.”
He entered into the temple, and began to drive out people wey bought and sold in it,
saying to dem, “It is written, ‘My house is a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a ‘den of robbers’!”
He was teaching daily in the temple, but the chief priests and the scribes and the leading men among the people sought to destroy him.
Dem no fit find Wetin dem might do, for all the people hung on to every word that he talk say.
On one of those days, as he was teaching the people in the temple and preaching the Better news, the priests and scribes come to him with the elders.
Dem ask him, “Tell us: by what authority do you do these things? Or Wey be giving you this authority?”
He answer dem, “I also will ask you one question. Tell me:
the baptism of John, was it from heaven, or from men?”
Dem reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why didn’t you believe him?’
But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for Dem be persuaded that John was a prophet.”
Dem answer that dem didn’t know where it was from.
Jesus tell dem say, “Neither will I tell una by what authority I do these things.”
He began to tell the people this parable. “A man planted a vineyard, and rented it out to some farmers, and go into another country for a long time.
At the proper season, he sent a worker to the farmers to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard. But the farmers beat him, and sent him away empty.
He sent yet another worker, and dem also beat him, and treated him shamefully, and sent him away empty.
He sent yet a third, and dem also wounded him, and threw him out.
The lord of the vineyard talk say, ‘What shall I do? I go send my beloved son. It may be that seeing him, Dem go respect him.’
“But when the farmers see him, dem reasoned among themselves, saying, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.’
Dem threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him. What so will the lord of the vineyard do to dem?
He will come and destroy these farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.” When dem heard it, dem talk say, “May it never be!”
But he looked at dem, and talk say, “Then Wetin be this that is written, ‘The stone which the builders rejected, the same was made the chief cornerstone?’
Everybody wey falls on that stone Go be broken to pieces, but it will crush whomever it falls on to dust.”
The chief priests and the scribes sought to lay hands on him that very hour, but dem feared the people — for dem know he had spoken this parable against dem.
Dem watched him, and sent out spies, who pretended to be righteous, that dem might trap him in something he talk say, so as to deliver him up to the power and authority of the governor.
Dem ask him, “Teacher, we know that you say and teach Wetin be right, and no be partial to anyone, but truly teach the way of God.
Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”
But he perceived dem craftiness, and talk say to dem, “Why do you test me?
Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription are on it?” Dem answer, “Caesar’s.”
E tell dem say, “Then give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
Dem no be able to trap him in his words before the people. Dem surprise well-well at his answer, and were silent.
Some of the Sadducees come to him, people wey deny that E get a resurrection.
Dem ask him, “Teacher, Moses wrote to us that if a man’s brother dies having a wife, and he is childless, his brother should take the wife, and raise up pikin dem for his brother.
There were so seven brothers. The first take a wife, and died childless.
The second take her as wife, and he died childless.
The third take her, and likewise the seven all left no pikin dem, and died.
Afterward the woman also died.
So in the resurrection whose wife of dem will she be? For the seven had her as a wife.”
Jesus tell dem say, “The pikin dem of this age marry, and are given in marriage.
But people Wey considered worthy to attain to that age and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage.
For dem no fit die any more, for Dem be like the angels, and are pikin dem of God, being pikin dem of the resurrection.
But that the dead are raised, even Moses showed at the bush, when he call the Lord ‘The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’
Now he No be the God of the dead, but of the living, for all are alive to him.”
Some of the scribes answer, “Teacher, you speak well.”
Dem didn’t dare to ask him any more questions.
E tell dem say, “Why do dem say that the Christ is David’s son?
David imself says in the book of Psalms, ‘The Lord talk say to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand,
until I make una enemies the footstool of una feet.”’
“David so calls him Lord, so how is he his son?”
In the hearing of all the people, he talk say to his disciples,
“Beware of the scribes, who like to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the marketplaces, the best seats in the synagogues, and the best places at feasts;
who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers: these will receive greater condemnation.”
He looked up, and see the rich people who were putting dem gifts into the treasury.
He see a certain poor widow casting in two small brass coins.
He talk say, “True true, I tell una, this poor widow put in more than all of dem,
for all these put in gifts for God from dem abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in all that she had to live on.”
As some were talking about the temple and how it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts, he talk say,
“As for these things which you see, the days will come, in which there No go be left here one stone on another that No go be thrown down.”
Dem ask him, “Teacher, so when will these things be? Wetin be the sign that these things are about to happen?”
He talk say, “Watch out that you no get led astray, for many will come in my name, saying, ‘I be he,’ and, ‘The time is at hand.’ So no follow dem.
When you hear of wars and disturbances, no be terrified, for these things must happen first, but the end no go come sharp-sharp.”
Then E tell dem say, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
There Go be great earthquakes, famines, and plagues in various places. There Go be terrors and great signs from heaven.
But before all these things, Dem go lay dem hands on you and will persecute you, delivering you up to synagogues and prisons, bringing you before kings and governors for my name’s sake.
It will turn out as a testimony for you.
Settle it so in una hearts not to meditate beforehand how to answer,
for I go give you a mouth and wisdom which all una adversaries No go be able to withstand or to contradict.
You go be handed over even by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends. Dem go cause some of you to be put to death.
You go be hated by all men for my name’s sake.
And not a hair of una head will perish.
“By una endurance You go win una lives.
“But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation is at hand.
Then let people Wey in Judea flee to the mountains. Let people Wey in the middle of her depart. Let people Wey in the country not enter inside am.
For these are days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.
Woe to people Wey pregnant and to people wey nurse infants in those days! For there Go be great distress in the land, and serious anger to this people.
Dem go fall by the edge of the sword, and Go be led captive into all the nations. Jerusalem Go be trampled down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
There Go be signs in the sun, moon, and stars; and on the earth anxiety of nations, in perplexity for the roaring of the sea and the waves;
men fainting for fear, and for expectation of the things which are coming on the world: for the powers of the heavens Go be shaken.
Then Dem go see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
But when these things begin to happen, look up, and lift up una heads, because una redemption is near.”
He told dem a parable. “See the fig tree, and all the trees.
When Dem be already budding, you see it and know by una own selves that the summer is already near.
Even so you also, when you see these things happening, know that God’s Kingdom is near.
True true, I tell una, this generation No go pass away until all things are accomplished.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will by no means pass away.
“So be careful, or una hearts Go be loaded down with carousing, drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that day will come on you suddenly.
For it will come like a snare on all people wey live on the surface of all the earth.
So Shine una eye all the time, praying that you may be counted worthy to escape all these things that will happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.”
Every day Jesus was teaching in the temple, and every night he would go out and spend the night on the mountain that is call Olivet.
All the people come early in the morning to him in the temple to hear him.
Now the feast of unleavened bread, which is call the Passover, was approaching.
The chief priests and the scribes sought how dem might put him to death, for dem feared the people.
Satan entered into Judas, who was also call Iscariot, who was counted with the twelve.
He go away, and talked with the chief priests and captains about how he might deliver him to dem.
Dem were glad, and agreed to give him money.
He consented, and sought an opportunity to deliver him to dem in the absence of the plenty people.
The day of unleavened bread come, on which the Passover must be sacrificed.
He sent Peter and John, saying, “Go and prepare the Passover for us, that we may eat.”
Dem tell am say, “Where do you want us to prepare?”
E tell dem say, “See am, when you have entered into the city, a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you. Follow him into the house which he enters.
Tell the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you, “Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’
He will show you a large, furnished upper room. Make preparations there.”
Dem go, find things as he had told dem, and dem prepared the Passover.
When the hour had come, he sat down with the twelve apostles.
E tell dem say, “I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer,
for I tell una, I go no longer by any means eat of it until it is fulfilled in God’s Kingdom.”
He received a cup, and when he had given thanks, he talk say, “Take this, and share it among unaself,
for I tell una, I go not drink at all again from the fruit of the vine, until God’s Kingdom comes.”
He take bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it, and give to dem, saying, “This is my body which is given for you. Do this in memory of me.”
Likewise, he take the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.
But see am, the hand of him who betrays me is with me on the table.
The Son of Man indeed goes, as it Don dey determined, but woe to that man through whom he is betrayed!”
Dem began to question among themselves, which of dem it was who would do this thing.
There arose also a contention among dem, which of dem was considered to be greatest.
E tell dem say, “The kings of the nations lord it over dem, and people wey have authority over dem are call ‘benefactors.’
But not so with you. But one Wey be the greater among you, Make e become as the younger, and one Wey be governing, as one who serves.
For Wey be greater, one who sits at the table, or one who serves? No be it person wey sits at the table? But I be among you as one who serves.
But You be people wey have continued with me in my trials.
I confer on you a kingdom, even as my Father conferred on me,
that you may eat and drink at my table in my Kingdom. You go sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”
The Lord talk say, “Simon, Simon, see am, Satan ask to have you, that he might sift you as wheat,
but I prayed for you, that una faith wouldn’t fail. You, when once you have turned again, establish una brothers.”
E tell am say, “Lord, I be ready to go with you both to prison and to death!”
He talk say, “I tell una, Peter, the rooster will by no means crow today until you deny that you know me three times.”
E tell dem say, “When I sent you out without purse, and wallet, and shoes, did you lack anything?” Dem talk say, “Nothing.”
Then E tell dem say, “But now, Anybody wey has a purse, Make e take it, and likewise a wallet. Anybody wey has none, Make e sell his cloak, and buy a sword.
For I tell una that this which is written must still be fulfilled in me: ‘He was counted with transgressors.’ For that which concerns me has an end.”
Dem talk say, “Lord, see am, here are two swords.” E tell dem say, “That is enough.”
He come out, and go, as his custom was, to the Mount of Olives. His disciples also follow him.
When he was at the place, E tell dem say, “Pray that you no enter into temptation.”
He was withdrawn from dem about a stone’s throw, and he knelt down and prayed,
saying, “Father, if You be willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.”
An angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.
Being in agony he prayed more earnestly. His sweat became like great drops of blood falling down on the ground.
When he rose up from his prayer, he come to the disciples, and find dem sleeping because of grief,
and talk say to dem, “Why do you sleep? Rise and pray that you may not enter into temptation.”
While he was still speaking, see am, a plenty people, and person wey was call Judas, one of the twelve, was leading dem. He come near to Jesus to kiss him.
But Jesus tell am say, “Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?”
When people wey were around him see what was about to happen, Dem tell am say, “Lord, shall we strike with the sword?”
A certain one of dem struck the worker of the high priest, and cut off his right ear.
But Jesus answer, “Let me at least do this” — and he touched his ear, and healed him.
Jesus talk say to the chief priests, captains of the temple, and elders, who had come against him, “Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?
When I was with you in the temple daily, you didn’t stretch out una hands against me. But this is una hour, and the power of darkness.”
Dem seized him, and led him away, and bring him into the high priest’s house. But Peter follow from a distance.
When dem had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard, and had sat down together, Peter sat among dem.
A certain worker girl see him as he sat in the light, and looking intently at him, talk say, “This man also was with him.”
He denied Jesus, saying, “Woman, I no know him.”
After a little while someone else see him, and talk say, “You also are one of dem!” But Peter answer, “Man, I be not!”
After about one hour passed, another confidently affirmed, saying, “Truly this man also was with him, for he is a Galilean!”
But Peter talk say, “Man, I no know Wetin You be talking about!” Sharp-sharp, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
The Lord turned, and looked at Peter. Then Peter remember the Lord’s word, how E tell am say, “Before the rooster crows You go deny me three times.”
He go out, and wept bitterly.
The men who held Jesus mocked him and beat him.
Having blindfolded him, dem struck him on the face and ask him, “Prophesy! Wey be the one who struck you?”
Dem spoke many other things against him, insulting him.
As soon as it was day, the assembly of the elders of the people was gathered together, both chief priests and scribes, and dem led him away into dem council, saying,
“If You be the Christ, tell us.” But E tell dem say, “If I tell una, you no go believe,
and if I ask, You go in no way answer me or let me go.
From now on, the Son of Man Go be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
Dem all talk say, “Are you then the Son of God?” E tell dem say, “You say it, because I be.”
Dem talk say, “Why do we need any more witness? For we ourselves have heard from his own mouth!”
The whole company of dem rose up and bring him before Pilate.
Dem began to accuse him, saying, “We find this man perverting the nation, forbidding paying taxes to Caesar, and saying that he imself is Christ, a king.”
Pilate ask him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” He answer him, “So you say.”
Pilate talk say to the chief priests and the plenty people, “I find no basis for a charge against this man.”
But dem insisted, saying, “He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee even to this place.”
But when Pilate heard Galilee mentioned, he ask if the man was a Galilean.
When he find out that he was in Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem during those days.
Now when Herod see Jesus, he was exceedingly glad, for he had want to see him for a long time, because he had heard many things about him. He hoped to see some miracle done by him.
He questioned him with many words, but he give no answers.
The chief priests and the scribes stood, vehemently accusing him.
Herod with his soldiers humiliated him and mocked him. Dressing him in luxurious clothing, dem sent him back to Pilate.
Herod and Pilate became friends with each other that very day, for before that dem were enemies with each other.
Pilate call together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,

and talk say to dem, “You bring this man to me as one that perverts the people, and see, I have examined him before you, and find no basis for a charge against this man concerning those things of which you accuse him.
Neither has Herod, for I sent you to him, and see, nothing worthy of death Don dey done by him.
I go so chastise him and release him.”
Now he had to release one prisoner to dem at the feast.
But dem all cried out together, saying, “Away with this man! Release to us Barabbas!” —
one who was thrown into prison for a certain revolt in the city, and for murder.
Then Pilate spoke to dem again, wanting to release Jesus,
but dem shouted, saying, “Crucify! Crucify him!”
E tell dem say the third time, “Why? What evil has this man done? I have find no capital crime in him. I go so chastise him and release him.”
But dem were urgent with loud voices, asking that he might be crucified. Dem voices and the voices of the chief priests prevailed.
Pilate decreed that Wetin dem ask for should be done.
He released him who Bin dey thrown into prison for insurrection and murder, for whom dem ask, but he delivered Jesus up to dem will.
When dem led him away, dem grabbed one Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, and laid on him the cross, to carry it after Jesus.
Plenty people of the people follow him, including women who also mourned and lamented him.
But Jesus, turning to dem, talk say, “Daughters of Jerusalem, no weep for me, but weep for unaself and for una pikin dem.
For see am, the days are coming in which Dem go say, ‘Blessed are the barren, the wombs that never bore, and the breasts that never nursed.’
Then Dem go begin to tell the mountains, ‘Fall on us!’ and tell the hills, ‘Cover us.’
For if dem do these things in the green tree, what Go be done in the dry?”
There were also others, two criminals, led with him to be put to death.
When dem come to the place that is call The Skull, dem crucified him there with the criminals, one on the right and the other on the left.
Jesus talk say, “Father, forgive dem, for dem no know Wetin dem are doing.” Dividing his garments among dem, dem throw lots.
The people stood watching. The rulers with dem also scoffed at him, saying, “He saved others. Make e save imself, if this is the Christ of God, his chosen one!”
The soldiers also mocked him, coming to him and offering him vinegar,
and saying, “If You be the King of the Jews, save yourself!”
An inscription was also written over him in letters of Greek, Latin, and Hebrew: “THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
One of the criminals who was hanged insulted him, saying, “If You be the Christ, save yourself and us!”
But the other answer, and rebuking him talk say, “No you even fear God, seeing You be under the same condemnation?
And we indeed justly, for we receive the due reward for our deeds, but this man has done nothing wrong.”
He talk say to Jesus, “Lord, remember me when you come into una Kingdom.”
Jesus tell am say, “Assuredly I tell una, today You go be with me in Paradise.”
It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness come over the whole land until the ninth hour.
The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn in two.
Jesus, crying with a loud voice, talk say, “Father, into una hands I commit my spirit!” Having talk say this, he breathed his last.
When the centurion see what was done, he glorified God, saying, “Certainly this was a righteous man.”
All the plenty people that come together to see this, when dem see the things that were done, come back home beating dem breasts.
All his acquaintances, and the women who follow with him from Galilee, stood at a distance, watching these things.
See am, a man named Joseph, who was a member of the council, a good and righteous man
(he had not consented to dem counsel and deed), from Arimathaea, a city of the Jews, who was also waiting for God’s Kingdom:
this man go to Pilate, and ask for Jesus’ body.
He take it down, and wrapped it in a linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb that was cut in stone, where Nobody had ever been laid.
It was the day of the Preparation, and the Sabbath was drawing near.
The women, who had come with him out of Galilee, follow after, and see the tomb, and how his body was laid.
Dem come back, and prepared spices and ointments. On the Sabbath dem rested according to the commandment.
But on the first day of the week, at early dawn, dem and some others come to the tomb, bringing the spices which dem had prepared.
Dem find the stone rolled away from the tomb.
Dem entered in, and didn’t find the Lord Jesus’ body.
While dem were greatly perplexed about this, see am, two men stood by dem in dazzling clothing.
Becoming terrified, dem bowed dem faces down to the earth. Dem tell dem say, “Why do you seek the living among the dead?
He no be here, but is risen. Remember what he told you when he was still in Galilee,
saying that the Son of Man must be delivered up into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again?”
Dem remember his words,
