I glorified you on the earth. I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do.
Now, Father, glorify me with una own self with the glory which I had with you before the world existed.
I revealed una name to the people whom you have given me out of the world. Dem were yours, and you have given dem to me. Dem have kept una word.
Now dem have known that all things Anything wey you have given me are from you,
for the words which you have given me I have given to dem, and dem received dem, and know for sure that I come from you, and dem have believe that you sent me.
I pray for dem. I no pray for the world, but for those whom you have given me, for Dem be yours.
All things that are mine are yours, and yours are mine, and I be glorified in dem.
I be no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I be coming to you. Holy Father, keep dem through una name which you have given me, that dem may be one, even as We be.
While I was with dem in the world, I kept dem in una name. Those whom you have given me I have kept. None of dem is lost, except the son of destruction, that the Scripture might be fulfilled.
But now I come to you, and I say these things in the world, that dem may have my gladness made full in themselves.
I have given dem una word. The world hated dem, because dem No be of the world, even as I be not of the world.
I pray not that you would take dem from the world, but that you would keep dem from the evil one.
Dem No be of the world even as I be not of the world.
Sanctify dem in una truth. Una word is truth.
As you sent me into the world, even so I have sent dem into the world.
For dem sakes I sanctify myself, that dem themselves also may be sanctified in truth.
Not for these only do I pray, but for those also who believe in me through dem word,
that dem may all be one; even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that dem also may be one in us; that the world may believe that you sent me.
The glory which you have given me, I have given to dem; that dem may be one, even as We be one;
I in dem, and you in me, that dem may be perfected into one; that the world may know that you sent me, and love dem, even as you love me.
Father, I desire that dem also whom you have given me be with me where I be, that dem may see my glory, which you have given me, for you love me before the foundation of the world.
Righteous Father, the world hasn’t known you, but I know you; and these know that you sent me.
I made known to dem una name, and will make it known; that the love with which you love me may be in dem, and I in dem.”
When Jesus had spoken these words, he go out with his disciples over the brook Kidron, where there was a garden, into which he and his disciples entered.
Now Judas, who betrayed him, also know the place, for Jesus often met there with his disciples.
Judas then, having taken a detachment of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, come there with lanterns, torches, and weapons.
Jesus so, knowing all the things that were happening to him, go out, and talk say to dem, “Wey be you looking for?”
Dem answer him, “Jesus of Nazareth.” Jesus tell dem say, “I be he.” Judas also, who betrayed him, was standing with dem.
When so E tell dem say, “I be he,” dem go backward, and fell to the ground.
Again so he ask dem, “Wey be you looking for?” Dem talk say, “Jesus of Nazareth.”
Jesus answer, “I told you that I be he. If so you seek me, let these go dem way,”
that the word might be fulfilled which he spoke, “Of those whom you have given me, I have lost none.”
Simon Peter so, having a sword, drew it, and struck the high priest’s worker, and cut off his right ear. The worker’s name was Malchus.
Jesus so talk say to Peter, “Put the sword into its sheath. The cup which the Father has given me, shall I not surely drink it?”
So the detachment, the commanding officer, and the officers of the Jews, seized Jesus and bound him,
and led him to Annas first, for he was father-in-law to Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
Now it was Caiaphas who advised the Jews that it was expedient that one man should perish for the people.
Simon Peter follow Jesus, as did another disciple. Now that disciple was known to the high priest, and entered in with Jesus into the court of the high priest;
but Peter was standing at the door outside. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, go out and spoke to her who kept the door, and bring in Peter.
Then the maid who kept the door talk say to Peter, “Are you also one of this man’s disciples?” He talk say, “I be not.”
Now the workers and the officers were standing there, having made a fire of coals, for it was cold. Dem were warming themselves. Peter was with dem, standing and warming imself.
The high priest so ask Jesus about his disciples, and about his teaching.
Jesus answer him, “I spoke openly to the world. I always taught in synagogues, and in the temple, where the Jews always meet. I talk say nothing in secret.
Why do you ask me? Ask people wey have heard me what I talk say to dem. See am, these know the things which I talk say.”
When he had talk say this, one of the officers standing by slapped Jesus with his hand, saying, “Do you answer the high priest like that?”
Jesus answer him, “If I have spoken evil, testify of the evil; but if well, why do you beat me?”
Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas, the high priest.
Now Simon Peter was standing and warming imself. Dem talk say so to him, “You no be also one of his disciples, are you?” He denied it, and talk say, “I be not.”
One of the workers of the high priest, being a relative of him whose ear Peter had cut off, talk say, “Didn’t I see you in the garden with him?”
Peter so denied it again, and sharp-sharp the rooster crowed.
Dem led Jesus so from Caiaphas into the Praetorium. It was early, and dem themselves didn’t enter into the Praetorium, that dem might not be defiled, but might eat the Passover.
Pilate so go out to dem, and talk say, “What accusation do you bring against this man?”
Dem answer him, “If this man no be an evildoer, we wouldn’t have delivered him up to you.”
Pilate so talk say to dem, “Take him unaself, and judge him according to una law.” So the Jews talk say to him, “It No be lawful for us to put anyone to death,”
that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spoke, signifying by what kind of death he should die.
Pilate so entered again into the Praetorium, call Jesus, and talk say to him, “Are you the King of the Jews?”
Jesus answer him, “Do you say this by yourself, or did others tell you about me?”
Pilate answer, “I’m not a Jew, am I? Una own nation and the chief priests delivered you to me. What have you done?”
Jesus answer, “My Kingdom No be of this world. If my Kingdom were of this world, then my workers would fight, that I wouldn’t be delivered to the Jews. But now my Kingdom No be from here.”

Pilate so talk say to him, “Are you a king then?” Jesus answer, “You say that I be a king. For this reason I Don dey born, and for this reason I have come into the world, that I should testify to the truth. Everyone Wey be of the truth listens to my voice.”
Pilate talk say to him, “Wetin be truth?” When he had talk say this, he go out again to the Jews, and talk say to dem, “I find no basis for a charge against him.
But you have a custom, that I should release someone to you at the Passover. So do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”
Then dem all shouted again, saying, “Not this man, but Barabbas!” Now Barabbas was a robber.
So Pilate then take Jesus, and flogged him.
The soldiers twisted thorns into a crown, and put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple garment.
Dem kept saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and dem kept slapping him.
Then Pilate go out again, and talk say to dem, “See am, I bring him out to you, that you may know that I find no basis for a charge against him.”
Jesus so come out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment. Pilate talk say to dem, “See am, the man!”
When so the chief priests and the officers see him, dem shouted, saying, “Crucify! Crucify!” Pilate talk say to dem, “Take him unaself, and crucify him, for I find no basis for a charge against him.”
The Jews answer him, “We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made imself the Son of God.”
When so Pilate heard this saying, he was more afraid.
He entered into the Praetorium again, and talk say to Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus give him no answer.
Pilate so talk say to him, “No be you speaking to me? No you know that I have power to release you, and have power to crucify you?”
Jesus answer, “You would have no power at all against me, unless it were given to you from above. So person wey delivered me to you has greater sin.”
At this, Pilate was seeking to release him, but the Jews cried out, saying, “If you release this man, you no be Caesar’s friend! Everybody wey makes imself a king speaks against Caesar!”
When Pilate so heard these words, he bring Jesus out, and sat down on the judgment seat at a place call “The Pavement”, but in Hebrew, “Gabbatha.”
Now it was the Preparation Day of the Passover, at about the sixth hour. He talk say to the Jews, “See am, una King!”
Dem cried out, “Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!” Pilate talk say to dem, “Shall I crucify una King?” The chief priests answer, “We have no king but Caesar!”
So then he delivered him to dem to be crucified. So dem take Jesus and led him away.
He go out, bearing his cross, to the place call “The Place of a Skull”, which is call in Hebrew, “Golgotha”,
where dem crucified him, and with him two others, on either side one, and Jesus in the middle.
Pilate wrote a title also, and put it on the cross. There was written, “JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
So many of the Jews read this title, for the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek.
The chief priests of the Jews so talk say to Pilate, “No write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but, ‘he talk say, “I be King of the Jews.”’”
Pilate answer, “What I have written, I have written.”
Then the soldiers, when dem had crucified Jesus, take his garments and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also the coat. Now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

Then dem talk say to each other, “Let’s not tear it, but throw lots for it to decide whose it Go be,” that the Scripture might be fulfilled, which says, “Dem parted my garments among dem. For my cloak dem throw lots.” So the soldiers did these things.
But there were standing by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
So when Jesus see his mother, and the disciple whom he love standing there, he talk say to his mother, “Woman, see am, una son!”
Then he talk say to the disciple, “See am, una mother!” From that hour, the disciple take her to his own home.
After this, Jesus, seeing that all things were now finished, that the Scripture might be fulfilled, talk say, “I be thirsty.”
Now a vessel full of vinegar was set there; so dem put a sponge full of the vinegar on hyssop, and held it at his mouth.
When Jesus so had received the vinegar, he talk say, “It is finished.” He bowed his head, and give up his spirit.

So the Jews, because it was the Preparation Day, so that the bodies wouldn’t remain on the cross on the Sabbath (for that Sabbath was a special one), ask of Pilate that dem legs might be broken, and that dem might be taken away.
So the soldiers come, and broke the legs of the first, and of the other who was crucified with him;
but when dem come to Jesus, and see that he was already dead, dem didn’t break his legs.
However one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and sharp-sharp blood and water come out.
Person wey has seen has testified, and his testimony is true. He knows that he tells the truth, that you may believe.
For these things happened, that the Scripture might be fulfilled, “A bone of him No go be broken.”
Again another Scripture says, “Dem go look on him whom dem pierced.”

After these things, Joseph of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, ask of Pilate that he might take away Jesus’ body. Pilate give him permission. He come so and take away his body.
Nicodemus, who at first come to Jesus by night, also come bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred Roman pounds.
So dem take Jesus’ body, and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as the custom of the Jews is to bury.
Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden. In the garden was a new tomb in which no man had ever yet been laid.
Then because of the Jews’ Preparation Day (for the tomb was near at hand) dem laid Jesus there.
Now on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene go early, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and see the stone taken away from the tomb.
So she ran and come to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple whom Jesus love, and talk say to dem, “Dem have taken away the Lord out of the tomb, and we no know where dem have laid him!”
So Peter and the other disciple go out, and dem go toward the tomb.
Dem both ran together. The other disciple outran Peter, and come to the tomb first.
Stooping and looking in, he see the linen cloths lying, yet he didn’t enter in.
Then Simon Peter come, following him, and entered into the tomb. He see the linen cloths lying,
and the cloth that Bin dey on his head, not lying with the linen cloths, but rolled up in a place by itself.
So then the other disciple who come first to the tomb also entered in, and he see and believe.
For as yet dem didn’t know the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead.
So the disciples go away again to dem own homes.
But Mary was standing outside at the tomb weeping. So, as she wept, she stooped and looked into the tomb,
and she see two angels in white sitting, one at the head, and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.
Dem told her, “Woman, why are you weeping?” She tell dem say, “Because dem have taken away my Lord, and I no know where dem have laid him.”
When she had talk say this, she turned around and see Jesus standing, and didn’t know that it was Jesus.

Jesus tell am say, “Woman, why are you weeping? Wey be you looking for?” She, supposing him to be the gardener, talk say to him, “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I go take him away.”
Jesus tell am say, “Mary.” She turned and talk say to him, “Rabboni!” which is to say, “Teacher!”
Jesus tell am say, “No hold me, for I haven’t yet ascended to my Father; but go to my brothers, and tell dem, ‘I be ascending to my Father and una Father, to my God and una God.’”
Mary Magdalene come and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord, and that he had talk say these things to her.

When so it was evening, on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were locked where the disciples were assembled, for fear of the Jews, Jesus come and stood in the middle, and talk say to dem, “Peace be to you.”
When he had talk say this, he showed dem his hands and his side. The disciples so were glad when dem see the Lord.
Jesus so talk say to dem again, “Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.”
When he had talk say this, he breathed on dem, and talk say to dem, “Receive the Holy Spirit!
If you forgive anyone’s sins, dem Don dey forgiven dem. If you retain anyone’s sins, dem Don dey retained.”
But Thomas, one of the twelve, call Didymus, no be with dem when Jesus come.

The other disciples so talk say to him, “We have seen the Lord!” But E tell dem say, “Unless I see in his hands the print of the nails, put my finger into the print of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I go not believe.”
After eight days again his disciples were inside, and Thomas was with dem. Jesus come, the doors being locked, and stood in the middle, and talk say, “Peace be to you.”
Then he talk say to Thomas, “Reach here una finger, and see my hands. Reach here una hand, and put it into my side. No be unbelieving, but believing.”
Thomas answer him, “My Lord and my God!”
Jesus tell am say, “Because you have seen me, you have believe. Blessed are people wey have not seen, and have believe.”
So Jesus did many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which No be written in this book;
but these are written, that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in his name.
After these things, Jesus revealed imself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias. He revealed imself this way.
Simon Peter, Thomas call Didymus, Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together.
Simon Peter talk say to dem, “I’m going fishing.” Dem told him, “We be also coming with you.” Dem sharp-sharp go out, and entered into the boat. That night, dem caught nothing.
But when day had already come, Jesus stood on the beach, yet the disciples didn’t know that it was Jesus.
Jesus so talk say to dem, “Pikin dem, have you anything to eat?” Dem answer him, “No.”
E tell dem say, “Throw the net on the right side of the boat, and You go find some.” Dem throw it so, and now dem no be able to draw it in for the plenty people of fish.
That disciple so whom Jesus love talk say to Peter, “It’s the Lord!” So when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he wrapped his coat around him (for he was naked), and threw imself into the sea.
But the other disciples come in the little boat (for dem No be far from the land, but about two hundred cubits away), dragging the net full of fish.
So when dem got out on the land, dem see a fire of coals there, and fish laid on it, and bread.
Jesus tell dem say, “Bring some of the fish which you have just caught.”
Simon Peter go up, and drew the net to land, full of great fish, one hundred fifty-three; and even though there were so many, the net no be torn.
Jesus tell dem say, “Come and eat breakfast.” None of the disciples dared inquire of him, “Wey be you?” knowing that it was the Lord.
Then Jesus come and take the bread, give it to dem, and the fish likewise.
This is now the third time that Jesus was revealed to his disciples, after he had risen from the dead.

So when dem had eaten dem breakfast, Jesus talk say to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these?” E tell am say, “Yes, Lord; you know that I have affection for you.” E tell am say, “Feed my lambs.”
E tell am say again a second time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?” E tell am say, “Yes, Lord; you know that I have affection for you.” E tell am say, “Tend my sheep.”

E tell am say the third time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you have affection for me?” Peter was grieved because he ask him the third time, “Do you have affection for me?” E tell am say, “Lord, you know everything. You know that I have affection for you.” Jesus tell am say, “Feed my sheep.

True true, I tell una, when you were young, you dressed yourself, and walked where you want to. But when You be old, You go stretch out una hands, and another will dress you, and carry you where you no want to go.”
Now he talk say this, signifying by what kind of death he would glorify God. When he had talk say this, E tell am say, “Follow me.”
Then Peter, turning around, see a disciple following. This was the disciple whom Jesus love, the one who had also leaned on Jesus’ breast at the supper and ask, “Lord, Wey be going to betray You?”
Peter seeing him, talk say to Jesus, “Lord, what about this man?”
Jesus tell am say, “If I desire that he stay until I come, Wetin be that to you? You follow me.”
This saying so go out among the brothers, that this disciple wouldn’t die. Yet Jesus didn’t say to him that he wouldn’t die, but, “If I desire that he stay until I come, Wetin be that to you?”
This is the disciple who testifies about these things, and wrote these things. We know that his witness is true.
E get also many other things which Jesus did, which if dem would all be written, I suppose that even the world itself wouldn’t have room for the books that would be written.
The first book I wrote, Theophilus, concerned all that Jesus began both to do and to teach,
until the day in which he was received up, after he had given commandment through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom he had chosen.
To these he also showed imself alive after he suffered, by many proofs, appearing to dem over a period of forty days, and speaking about God’s Kingdom.
Being assembled together with dem, he commanded dem, “No depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father, which you heard from me.
For John indeed baptized in water, but You go be baptized in the Holy Spirit not many days from now.”
So when dem had come together, dem ask him, “Lord, are you now restoring the kingdom to Israel?”
E tell dem say, “It no be for you to know times or seasons which the Father has set within his own authority.
But You go receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You go be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.”
When he had talk say these things, as dem were looking, he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of dem sight.
While dem were looking steadfastly into the sky as he go, see am, two men stood by dem in white clothing,

who also talk say, “You men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into the sky? This Jesus, who was received up from you into the sky, will come back in the same way as you see him going into the sky.”
Then dem come back to Jerusalem from the mountain call Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath day’s journey away.

When dem had come in, dem go up into the upper room, where dem were staying; that is Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas the son of James.
All these with one accord continued steadfastly in prayer and supplication, along with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brothers.
In these days, Peter stood up in the middle of the disciples (and the number of names was about one hundred twenty), and talk say,
“Brothers, it was necessary that this Scripture should be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit spoke before by the mouth of David concerning Judas, who was guide to people wey take Jesus.
For he was counted with us, and received his portion in this ministry.
Now this man obtained a field with the reward for his wickedness, and falling headlong, his body burst open, and all his intestines gushed out.
It became known to Everybody wey lived in Jerusalem that in dem language that field was call ‘Akeldama,’ that is, ‘The field of blood.’
For it is written in the book of Psalms, ‘Let his habitation be made desolate. Let Nobody live inside am;’ and, ‘Let another take his office.’
“Of the men so who have accompanied us all the time that the Lord Jesus go in and out among us,
beginning from the baptism of John, to the day that he was received up from us, of these one must become a witness with us of his resurrection.”
Dem put forward two, Joseph call Barsabbas, who was also call Justus, and Matthias.
Dem prayed, and talk say, “You, Lord, who know the hearts of all men, show which one of these two you have chosen
to take part in this ministry and apostleship from which Judas fell away, that he might go to his own place.”
Dem drew lots for dem, and the lot fell on Matthias, and he was counted with the eleven apostles.
Now when the day of Pentecost had come, dem were all with one accord in one place.
Suddenly there come from the sky a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind, and it filled all the house where dem were sitting.
Tongues like fire appeared and were distributed to dem, and one sat on each of dem.
Dem were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak with other languages, as the Spirit give dem the ability to speak.
Now there were dwelling in Jerusalem Jews, devout men, from every nation under the sky.
When this sound was heard, the plenty people come together, and were bewildered, because everyone heard dem speaking in his own language.
Dem were all amazed and surprise well-well, saying to each other, “See am, no be all these who speak Galileans?
How do we hear, everyone in our own native language?
Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and people from Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, Asia,
Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, the parts of Libya around Cyrene, visitors from Rome, both Jews and proselytes,
Cretans and Arabians: we hear dem speaking in our languages the mighty works of God!”
Dem were all amazed, and were perplexed, saying to each other, “What does this mean?”
Others, mocking, talk say, “Dem be filled with new wine.”
But Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and spoke out to dem, “You men of Judea, and all you who live at Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and listen to my words.
For these no be drunken, as you suppose, seeing it is only the third hour of the day.
But this is what Don dey spoken through the prophet Joel:
‘It Go be in the last days, says God, that I go pour out my Spirit on all flesh. Una sons and una daughters will prophesy. Una young men will see visions. Una old men will dream dreams.
Yes, and on my workers and on my handmaidens in those days, I go pour out my Spirit, and Dem go prophesy.
I go show wonders in the sky above, and signs on the earth beneath; blood, and fire, and billows of smoke.
The sun Go be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and glorious day of the Lord comes.
It Go be that Anybody wey will call on the name of the Lord Go be saved.’
“Men of Israel, hear these words! Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved by God to you by mighty works and wonders and signs which God did by him among you, even as you unaself know,
him, being delivered up by the determined counsel and foreknowledge of God, you have taken by the hand of lawless men, crucified and killed;
whom God raised up, having freed him from the agony of death, because it No be possible that he should be held by it.
For David says concerning him, ‘I see the Lord always before my face, For he is on my right hand, that I no suppose be moved.
So my heart was glad, and my tongue rejoiced. Moreover my flesh also will live in hope;
because You go not leave my soul in Hades, neither will you allow una Holy One to see decay.
You made known to me the ways of life. You go make me full of gladness with una presence.’
“Brothers, I may tell you freely of the patriarch David, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day.
So, being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him that of the fruit of his body, according to the flesh, he would raise up the Christ to sit on his throne,
he foreseeing this spoke about the resurrection of the Christ, that neither was his soul left in Hades, nor did his flesh see decay.
This Jesus God raised up, to which we all are witnesses.
Being so exalted by the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, he has poured out this, which you now see and hear.
For David didn’t ascend into the heavens, but he says imself, ‘The Lord talk say to my Lord, “Sit by my right hand,
until I make una enemies a footstool for una feet.”’
“Let all the house of Israel so know certainly that God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified.”
Now when dem heard this, dem were cut to the heart, and talk say to Peter and the rest of the apostles, “Brothers, what shall we do?”
Peter talk say to dem, “Repent, and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and You go receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
For the promise is to you, and to una pikin dem, and to all Wey be far off, even as many as the Lord our God will call to imself.”
With many other words he testified, and exhorted dem, saying, “Save unaself from this crooked generation!”
Then people wey gladly received his word were baptized. There were added that day about three thousand souls.
Dem continued steadfastly in the apostles’ teaching and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and prayer.
Fear come on every soul, and many wonders and signs were done through the apostles.
All who believe were together, and had all things in common.
Dem sold dem possessions and goods, and distributed dem to all, according as anyone had need.
Day by day, continuing steadfastly with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread at home, dem take dem chop with gladness and singleness of heart,
praising God, and having favor with all the people. The Lord added to the assembly day by day people wey were being saved.
Peter and John were going up into the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.

A certain man who was lame from his mother’s womb was being carried, whom dem laid daily at the door of the temple which is call Beautiful, to ask gifts for the needy of people wey entered into the temple.
Seeing Peter and John about to go into the temple, he ask to receive gifts for the needy.
Peter, fastening his eyes on him, with John, talk say, “Look at us.”
He listened to dem, expecting to receive something from dem.
But Peter talk say, “I have no silver or gold, but what I have, that I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!”
He take him by the right hand, and raised him up. Sharp-sharp his feet and his ankle bones received strength.
Leaping up, he stood, and began to walk. He entered with dem into the temple, walking, leaping, and praising God.
All the people see him walking and praising God.
Dem recognized him, that it was person wey used to sit begging for gifts for the needy at the Beautiful Gate of the temple. Dem were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
As the lame man who was healed held on to Peter and John, all the people ran together to dem in the porch that is call Solomon’s, greatly wondering.
When Peter see it, he responded to the people, “You men of Israel, why do you marvel at this man? Why do you fasten una eyes on us, as though by our own power or godliness we had made him walk?
The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified his Worker Jesus, whom you delivered up, and denied in the presence of Pilate, when he had determined to release him.
But you denied the Holy and Righteous One, and ask for a murderer to be granted to you,
and killed the Prince of life, whom God raised from the dead, to which We be witnesses.
By faith in his name, his name has made this man strong, whom you see and know. Yes, the faith which is through him has given him this perfect soundness in the presence of you all.
“Now, brothers, I know that you did this in ignorance, as did also una rulers.
But the things which God announced by the mouth of all his prophets, that Christ should suffer, he thus fulfilled.
“Repent so, and turn again, that una sins may be blotted out, so that there may come times of refreshing from the presence of the Lord,
and that he may send Christ Jesus, who was ordained for you before,
whom heaven must receive until the times of restoration of all things, which God spoke long ago by the mouth of his holy prophets.
For Moses indeed talk say to the fathers, ‘The Lord God will raise up a prophet for you from among una brothers, like me. You shall listen to him in all things Anything wey he says to you.
It Go be that every soul that No go listen to that prophet Go be utterly destroyed from among the people.’
Yes, and all the prophets from Samuel and people wey follow after, as many as have spoken, dem also told of these days.
You be the pikin dem of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying to Abraham, ‘In una offspring will all the families of the earth be blessed.’
God, having raised up his worker Jesus, sent him to you first to bless you, in turning away every one of you from una wickedness.”
As dem spoke to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees come to dem,
being upset because dem taught the people and proclaimed in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.
Dem laid hands on dem, and put dem in custody until the next day, for it was now evening.
But many of people wey heard the word believe, and the number of the men come to be about five thousand.
In the morning, dem rulers, elders, and scribes were gathered together in Jerusalem.
Annas the high priest was there, with Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and as many as were relatives of the high priest.
When dem had stood dem in the middle of dem, dem inquired, “By what power, or in what name, have you done this?”
Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, talk say to dem, “You rulers of the people, and elders of Israel,
if We be examined today concerning a good deed done to a crippled man, by what means this man Don dey healed,

be it known to you all, and to all the people of Israel, that in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead, in him does this man stand here before you whole.
He is ‘the stone which was regarded as worthless by you, the builders, which has become the head of the corner.’
E get salvation in none other, for neither is there any other name under heaven, that is given among men, by which we must be saved!”
Now when dem see the boldness of Peter and John, and had perceived that dem were unlearned and ignorant men, dem surprise well-well. Dem recognized that dem Bin dey with Jesus.
Seeing the man who was healed standing with dem, dem could say nothing against it.
But when dem had commanded dem to go aside out of the council, dem conferred among themselves,
saying, “What shall we do to these men? Because indeed a notable miracle Don dey done through dem, as can be plainly seen by all who live in Jerusalem, and we no fit deny it.
But so that this spreads no further among the people, let’s threaten dem, that from now on dem no speak to anyone in this name.”
Dem call dem, and commanded dem not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Jesus.
But Peter and John answer dem, “Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God, judge for unaself,
for we no fit help telling the things which we see and heard.”
When dem had further threatened dem, dem Make dem go, finding no way to punish dem, because of the people; for everyone glorified God for that which was done.
For the man on whom this miracle of healing was performed was more than forty years old.
Being let go, dem come to dem own company, and reported all that the chief priests and the elders had talk say to dem.
When dem heard it, dem lifted up dem voice to God with one accord, and talk say, “O Lord, You be God, who made the heaven, the earth, the sea, and all that is in dem;
who by the mouth of una worker, David, talk say, ‘Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot a vain thing?
The kings of the earth take a stand, and the rulers take council together, against the Lord, and against his Christ.’
“For truly, in this city against una holy worker, Jesus, whom you anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles and the people of Israel, were gathered together
to do Anything wey una hand and una council foreordained to happen.
Now, Lord, look at dem threats, and grant to una workers to speak una word with all boldness,
while you stretch out una hand to heal; and that signs and wonders may be done through the name of una holy Worker Jesus.”
When dem had prayed, the place was shaken where dem were gathered together. Dem were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and dem spoke the word of God with boldness.
The plenty people of people wey believe were of one heart and soul. Not one of dem claimed that anything of the things which he possessed was his own, but dem had all things in common.
With great power, the apostles give dem testimony of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. Great grace was on dem all.
For neither was there among dem any who lacked, for as many as were owners of lands or houses sold dem, and bring the proceeds of the things that were sold,
and laid dem at the apostles’ feet, and distribution was made to each, according as anyone had need.
Joses, who by the apostles was also call Barnabas (which is, being interpreted, Son of Encouragement), a Levite, a man of Cyprus by race,
having a field, sold it, and bring the money and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira, his wife, sold a possession,
and kept back part of the price, his wife also being aware of it, and bring a certain part, and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
But Peter talk say, “Ananias, why has Satan filled una heart to lie to the Holy Spirit, and to keep back part of the price of the land?
While you kept it, didn’t it remain una own? After it was sold, no be it in una power? How is it that you have conceived this thing in una heart? You haven’t lied to men, but to God.”
Ananias, hearing these words, fell down and died. Great fear come on all who heard these things.
The young men arose and wrapped him up, and dem carried him out and buried him.
About three hours later, his wife, not knowing what had happened, come in.
Peter answer her, “Tell me whether you sold the land for so much.” She talk say, “Yes, for so much.”
But Peter ask her, “How is it that you have agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? See am, the feet of people wey have buried una husband are at the door, and Dem go carry you out.”
She fell down sharp-sharp at his feet, and died. The young men come in and find her dead, and dem carried her out and buried her by her husband.
Great fear come on the whole assembly, and on all who heard these things.
By the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were done among the people. Dem were all with one accord in Solomon’s porch.
None of the rest dared to join dem, however the people honored dem.
More believers were added to the Lord, plenty people of both men and women.
Dem even carried out the sick into the streets, and laid dem on cots and mattresses, so that as Peter come by, at the least his shadow might overshadow some of dem.
The plenty people also come together from the cities around Jerusalem, bringing sick people, and people wey were tormented by unclean spirits: and dem were all healed.
But the high priest rose up, and all people wey were with him (which is the sect of the Sadducees), and dem were filled with jealousy,
and laid hands on the apostles, and put dem in public custody.
But an angel of the Lord opened the prison doors by night, and bring dem out, and talk say,
“Go stand and speak in the temple to the people all the words of this life.”

When dem heard this, dem entered into the temple about daybreak, and taught. But the high priest come, and people wey were with him, and call the council together, and all the senate of the pikin dem of Israel, and sent to the prison to have dem bring.
But the officers who come didn’t find dem in the prison. Dem come back and reported,
“We find the prison shut and locked, and the guards standing before the doors, but when we opened dem, we find Nobody inside!”
Now when the high priest, the captain of the temple, and the chief priests heard these words, dem were very perplexed about dem and what might become of this.
One come and told dem, “See am, the men whom you put in prison are in the temple, standing and teaching the people.”
Then the captain go with the officers, and bring dem without violence, for dem were afraid that the people might stone dem.
When dem had bring dem, dem set dem before the council. The high priest questioned dem,
saying, “Didn’t we strictly command you not to teach in this name? See am, you have filled Jerusalem with una teaching, and intend to bring this man’s blood on us.”
But Peter and the apostles answer, “We must obey God rather than men.
The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you killed, hanging him on a tree.
God exalted him with his right hand to be a Prince and a Savior, to give repentance to Israel, and remission of sins.
We be His witnesses of these things; and so also is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to people wey obey him.”
But dem, when dem heard this, were cut to the heart, and were determined to kill dem.
But one stood up in the council, a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law, honored by all the people, and commanded to put the apostles out for a little while.
E tell dem say, “You men of Israel, be careful concerning these men, Wetin You be about to do.

For before these days Theudas rose up, making imself out to be somebody; to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves: who was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were dispersed, and come to nothing.
After this man, Judas of Galilee rose up in the days of the enrollment, and drew away some people after him. He also perished, and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered abroad.
Now I tell una, withdraw from these men, and leave dem alone. For if this counsel or this work is of men, it Go be overthrown.
But if it is of God, You go not be able to overthrow it, and you would be find even to be fighting against God!”
Dem agreed with him. Summoning the apostles, dem beat dem and commanded dem not to speak in the name of Jesus, and Make dem go.
Dem so comot from the presence of the council, rejoicing that dem were counted worthy to suffer dishonor for Jesus’ name.
Every day, in the temple and at home, dem never stopped teaching and preaching Jesus, the Christ.
Now in those days, when the number of the disciples was multiplying, a complaint arose from the Hellenists against the Hebrews, because dem widows were neglected in the daily service.
The twelve summoned the plenty people of the disciples and talk say, “It No be appropriate for us to forsake the word of God and serve tables.
So select from among you, brothers, seven men of good report, full of the Holy Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.
But We go continue steadfastly in prayer and in the ministry of the word.”
These words pleased the whole plenty people. Dem chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch;
whom dem set before the apostles. When dem had prayed, dem laid dem hands on dem.
The word of God increased and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem exceedingly. A great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.
Stephen, full of faith and power, performed great wonders and signs among the people.
But some of people wey were of the synagogue call “The Libertines”, and of the Cyrenians, of the Alexandrians, and of those of Cilicia and Asia arose, disputing with Stephen.
Dem no be able to withstand the wisdom and the Spirit by which he spoke.
Then dem secretly induced men to say, “We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses and God.”
Dem stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes, and come against him and seized him, and bring him in to the council,
and set up false witnesses who talk say, “This man never stops speaking blasphemous words against this holy place and the law.
For we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place, and will change the customs which Moses delivered to us.”
All who sat in the council, fastening dem eyes on him, see his face like it was the face of an angel.
The high priest talk say, “Are these things so?”
He talk say, “Brothers and fathers, listen. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran,
and talk say to him, ‘Get out of una land, and from una relatives, and come into a land which I go show you.’
Then he come out of the land of the Chaldaeans, and lived in Haran. From there, when his father was dead, God moved him into this land, where You be now living.
He give him no inheritance in it, no, not so much as to set his foot on. He promised that he would give it to him for a possession, and to his offspring after him, when he still had no pikin.
God spoke in this way: that his offspring would live as aliens in a strange land, and that dem would be enslaved and mistreated for four hundred years.
‘I go judge the nation to which Dem go be in bondage,’ talk say God, ‘and after that will dem come out, and serve me in this place.’

He give him the covenant of circumcision. So Abraham became the father of Isaac, and circumcised him the eighth day. Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob became the father of the twelve patriarchs.
“The patriarchs, moved with jealousy against Joseph, sold him into Egypt. God was with him,
and delivered him out of all his afflictions, and give him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh, king of Egypt. He made him governor over Egypt and all his house.
Now a famine come over all the land of Egypt and Canaan, and great suffering. Our fathers find no chop.
But when Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent out our fathers the first time.
On the second time Joseph was made known to his brothers, and Joseph’s race was revealed to Pharaoh.
Joseph sent, and summoned Jacob, his father, and all his relatives, seventy-five souls.
Jacob go down into Egypt, and he died, imself and our fathers,
and dem were bring back to Shechem, and laid in the tomb that Abraham bought for a price in silver from the pikin dem of Hamor of Shechem.
“But as the time of the promise come close which God had sworn to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,
until there arose a different king, who didn’t know Joseph.
The same take advantage of our race, and mistreated our fathers, and forced dem to throw out dem babies, so that dem wouldn’t stay alive.
At that time Moses was born, and was exceedingly handsome. He was nourished three months in his father’s house.
When he was thrown out, Pharaoh’s daughter take him up, and reared him as her own son.
Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians. He was mighty in his words and works.
But when he was forty years old, it come into his heart to visit his brothers, the pikin dem of Israel.
Seeing one of dem suffer wrong, he defended him, and avenged him who was oppressed, striking the Egyptian.
He supposed that his brothers understand that God, by his hand, was giving dem deliverance; but dem didn’t understand.
“The day following, he appeared to dem as dem fought, and urged dem to be at peace again, saying, ‘Sirs, You be brothers. Why do you wrong each other?’
But person wey did his neighbor wrong pushed him away, saying, ‘Who made you a ruler and a judge over us?
Do you want to kill me, as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?’
Moses fled at this saying, and became a stranger in the land of Midian, where he became the father of two sons.
“When forty years were fulfilled, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai, in a flame of fire in a bush.
When Moses see it, he wondered at the sight. As he come close to see, a voice of the Lord come to him,
‘I be the God of una fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’ Moses trembled, and dared not look.
The Lord talk say to him, ‘Take una sandals off of una feet, for the place where you stand is holy ground.
I have surely seen the suffering of my people that is in Egypt, and have heard dem groaning. I have come down to deliver dem. Now come, I go send you into Egypt.’
“This Moses, whom dem refused, saying, ‘Who made you a ruler and a judge?’ — God has sent him as both a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
This man led dem out, having worked wonders and signs in Egypt, in the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.
This is that Moses, who talk say to the pikin dem of Israel, ‘The Lord our God will raise up a prophet for you from among una brothers, like me.’
This is person wey was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel that spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers, who received living revelations to give to us,
to whom our fathers wouldn’t be obedient, but rejected him, and turned back in dem hearts to Egypt,
saying to Aaron, ‘Make us gods that will go before us, for as for this Moses, who led us out of the land of Egypt, we no know what has become of him.’
Dem made a calf in those days, and bring a sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of dem hands.

But God turned, and give dem up to serve the army of the sky, as it is written in the book of the prophets, ‘Did you offer to me slain animals and sacrifices forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
You take up the tabernacle of Moloch, the star of una god Rephan, the figures which you made to worship. I go carry you away beyond Babylon.’
“Our fathers had the tabernacle of the testimony in the wilderness, even as person wey spoke to Moses commanded him to make it according to the pattern that he had seen;
which also our fathers, in dem turn, bring in with Joshua when dem entered into the possession of the nations, whom God drove out before the face of our fathers, to the days of David,
who find favor in the sight of God, and ask to find a habitation for the God of Jacob.
But Solomon built him a house.
However, the Most High no dey live in temples made with hands, as the prophet says,
‘heaven is my throne, and the earth a footstool for my feet. What kind of house will you build me?’ says the Lord; ‘or Wetin be the place of my rest?
Didn’t my hand make all these things?’
“You stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit! As una fathers did, so you do.
Which of the prophets didn’t una fathers persecute? Dem killed people wey foretold the coming of the Righteous One, of whom you have now become betrayers and murderers.
You received the law as it was ordained by angels, and didn’t keep it!”
Now when dem heard these things, dem were cut to the heart, and dem gnashed at him with dem teeth.
But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, looked up steadfastly into heaven, and see the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God,
and talk say, “See am, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God!”
But dem cried out with a loud voice, and stopped dem ears, and rushed at him with one accord.
Dem threw him out of the city, and stoned him. The witnesses placed dem garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
Dem stoned Stephen as he call out, saying, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit!”
He kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, “Lord, no hold this sin against dem!” When he had talk say this, he fell asleep.

Saul was consenting to his death. A great persecution arose against the assembly which was in Jerusalem in that day. Dem were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except for the apostles.
Devout men buried Stephen, and lamented greatly over him.
But Saul ravaged the assembly, entering into every house, and dragged both men and women off to prison.
So people wey were scattered abroad go around preaching the word.
Philip go down to the city of Samaria, and proclaimed to dem the Christ.
The plenty people listened with one accord to the things that were spoken by Philip, when dem heard and see the signs which he did.
For unclean spirits come out of many of people wey had dem. Dem come out, crying with a loud voice. Many who Bin dey paralyzed and lame were healed.
There was great gladness in that city.
But there was a certain man, Simon by name, who used to practice sorcery in the city, and amazed the people of Samaria, making imself out to be some great one,
to whom dem all listened, from the least to the greatest, saying, “This man is that great power of God.”
Dem listened to him, because for a long time he had amazed dem with his sorceries.
But when dem believe Philip preaching better news concerning God’s Kingdom and the name of Jesus Christ, dem were baptized, both men and women.
Simon imself also believe. Being baptized, he continued with Philip. Seeing signs and great miracles occurring, he was amazed.
Now when the apostles who were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, dem sent Peter and John to dem,
who, when dem had come down, prayed for dem, that dem might receive the Holy Spirit;
for as yet he had fallen on none of dem. Dem had only been baptized in the name of Christ Jesus.
Then dem laid dem hands on dem, and dem received the Holy Spirit.
Now when Simon see that the Holy Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered dem money,
saying, “Give me also this power, that whomever I lay my hands on may receive the Holy Spirit.”
But Peter talk say to him, “May una silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money!
You have neither part nor lot in this matter, for una heart no be right before God.
Repent so of this, una wickedness, and ask God if perhaps the thought of una heart may be forgiven you.
For I see that You be in the poison of bitterness and in the bondage of wickedness.”
Simon answer, “Pray for me to the Lord, that none of the things which you have spoken happen to me.”
Dem so, when dem had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, come back to Jerusalem, and preached the Better news to many villages of the Samaritans.
But an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, “Arise, and go toward the south to the way that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza. This is a desert.”
He arose and go; and see am, there was a man of Ethiopia, a eunuch of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasure, who had come to Jerusalem to worship.
He was returning and sitting in his chariot, and was reading the prophet Isaiah.
The Spirit talk say to Philip, “Go near, and join yourself to this chariot.”
Philip ran to him, and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and talk say, “Do you understand Wetin You be reading?”
He talk say, “How can I, unless someone explains it to me?” He begged Philip to come up and sit with him.
Now the passage of the Scripture which he was reading was this, “He was led as a sheep to the slaughter. As a lamb before his shearer is silent, so he no dey open his mouth.
In his humiliation, his judgment was taken away. Who will declare His generation? For his life is taken from the earth.”
The eunuch answer Philip, “Wey be the prophet talking about? About imself, or about someone else?”
Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this Scripture, preached to him about Jesus.
As dem go on the way, dem come to some water, and the eunuch talk say, “See am, here is water. Wetin be keeping me from being baptized?”
He commanded the chariot to stand still, and dem both go down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.
When dem come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away, and the eunuch didn’t see him any more, for he go on his way rejoicing.
But Philip was find at Azotus. Passing through, he preached the Better news to all the cities, until he come to Caesarea.
But Saul, still breathing threats and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, go to the high priest,
and ask for letters from him to the synagogues of Damascus, that if he find any who were of the Way, whether men or women, he might bring dem bound to Jerusalem.
As he traveled, he got close to Damascus, and suddenly a light from the sky shone around him.
He fell on the earth, and heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?”
He talk say, “Wey be you, Lord?” The Lord talk say, “I be Jesus, whom You be persecuting.
But rise up, and enter into the city, and You go be told Wetin you must do.”
The men who traveled with him stood speechless, hearing the sound, but seeing Nobody.
Saul arose from the ground, and when his eyes were opened, he see Nobody. Dem led him by the hand, and bring him into Damascus.
He was without sight for three days, and neither ate nor drank.
Now there was a certain disciple at Damascus named Ananias. The Lord talk say to him in a vision, “Ananias!” He talk say, “See am, it’s me, Lord.”
The Lord talk say to him, “Arise, and go to the street which is call Straight, and inquire in the house of Judah for one named Saul, a man of Tarsus. For see am, he is praying,
and in a vision he has seen a man named Ananias coming in, and laying his hands on him, that he might receive his sight.”
But Ananias answer, “Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he did to una saints at Jerusalem.
Here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on una name.”
But the Lord talk say to him, “Go una way, for he is my chosen vessel to bear my name before the nations and kings, and the pikin dem of Israel.
For I go show him how many things he must suffer for my name’s sake.”

Ananias comot, and entered into the house. Laying his hands on him, he talk say, “Brother Saul, the Lord, who appeared to you on the road by which you come, has sent me, that you may receive una sight, and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
Sharp-sharp something like scales fell from his eyes, and he received his sight. He arose and was baptized.
He take chop and was strengthened. Saul stayed several days with the disciples who were at Damascus.
Sharp-sharp in the synagogues he proclaimed the Christ, that he is the Son of God.

All who heard him were amazed, and talk say, “No be this person wey in Jerusalem made havoc of people wey call on this name? And he had come here intending to bring dem bound before the chief priests!”
But Saul increased more in strength, and confounded the Jews who lived at Damascus, proving that this is the Christ.
When many days were fulfilled, the Jews conspired together to kill him,
but dem plot became known to Saul. Dem watched the gates both day and night that dem might kill him,
but his disciples take him by night, and Make e down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.
When Saul had come to Jerusalem, he tried to join imself to the disciples; but dem were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

But Barnabas take him, and bring him to the apostles, and declared to dem how he had seen the Lord on the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how at Damascus he had preached boldly in the name of Jesus.
He was with dem entering into Jerusalem,
preaching boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus. He spoke and disputed against the Hellenists, but dem were seeking to kill him.
When the brothers know it, dem bring him down to Caesarea, and sent him off to Tarsus.
So the assemblies throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, and were built up. Dem were multiplied, walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit.
As Peter go throughout all those parts, he come down also to the saints who lived at Lydda.
There he find a certain man named Aeneas, who Bin dey bedridden for eight years, because he was paralyzed.
Peter talk say to him, “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make una bed!” Sharp-sharp he arose.
All who lived at Lydda and in Sharon see him, and dem turned to the Lord.
Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which when translated, means Dorcas. This woman was full of good works and acts of mercy which she did.
In those days, she became sick, and died. When dem had washed her, dem laid her in an upper room.
As Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, imploring him not to delay in coming to dem.

Peter got up and go with dem. When he had come, dem bring him into the upper room. All the widows stood by him weeping, and showing the coats and garments which Dorcas had made while she was with dem.
Peter sent dem all out, and knelt down and prayed. Turning to the body, he talk say, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, and when she see Peter, she sat up.
He give her his hand, and raised her up. Calling the saints and widows, he presented her alive.
And it became known throughout all Joppa, and many believe in the Lord.
He stayed many days in Joppa with a tanner named Simon.
Now there was a certain man in Caesarea, Cornelius by name, a centurion of what was call the Italian Regiment,
a devout man, and one who feared God with all his house, who give gifts for the needy generously to the people, and always prayed to God.
At about the ninth hour of the day, he clearly see in a vision an angel of God coming to him, and saying to him, “Cornelius!”
He, fastening his eyes on him, and being frightened, talk say, “Wetin be it, Lord?” E tell am say, “Una prayers and una gifts to the needy have gone up for a memorial before God.
Now send men to Joppa, and get Simon, Wey be also call Peter.
He lodges with a tanner named Simon, whose house is by the seaside.
When the angel who spoke to him had comot, Cornelius call two of his household workers and a devout soldier of people wey waited on him continually.
Having explained everything to dem, he sent dem to Joppa.
Now on the next day as dem were on dem journey, and got close to the city, Peter go up on the housetop to pray at about noon.
He became hungry and desired to eat, but while dem were preparing, he fell into a trance.
He see heaven opened and a certain container descending to him, like a great sheet let down by four corners on the earth,
in which were all kinds of four-footed animals of the earth, wild animals, reptiles, and birds of the sky.
A voice come to him, “Rise, Peter, kill and eat!”
But Peter talk say, “Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten anything that is common or unclean.”
A voice come to him again the second time, “What God has cleansed, you must not call unclean.”
This was done three times, and sharp-sharp the vessel was received up into heaven.
Now while Peter was very perplexed in imself what the vision which he had seen might mean, see am, the men who were sent by Cornelius, having made inquiry for Simon’s house, stood before the gate,
and call and ask whether Simon, who was also call Peter, was lodging there.
While Peter was pondering the vision, the Spirit talk say to him, “See am, three men seek you.
But arise, get down, and go with dem, doubting nothing; for I have sent dem.”
Peter go down to the men, and talk say, “See am, I be he whom you seek. Why have you come?”

Dem talk say, “Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man and one who fears God, and well spoken of by all the nation of the Jews, was directed by a holy angel to invite you to his house, and to listen to Wetin you say.”
So he call dem in and provided a place to stay. On the next day Peter arose and go out with dem, and some of the brothers from Joppa accompanied him.
On the next day dem entered into Caesarea. Cornelius was waiting for dem, having call together his relatives and his near friends.
When Peter entered, Cornelius met him, fell down at his feet, and worshiped him.
But Peter raised him up, saying, “Stand up! I myself am also a man.”
As he talked with him, he go in and find many gathered together.

E tell dem say, “You unaself know how it is an unlawful thing for a man Wey be a Jew to join imself or come to one of another nation, but God has shown me that I shouldn’t call any man unholy or unclean.
So also I come without complaint when I was sent for. I ask so, why did you send for me?”
Cornelius talk say, “Four days ago, I was fasting until this hour, and at the ninth hour, I prayed in my house, and see am, a man stood before me in bright clothing,
and talk say, ‘Cornelius, una prayer is heard, and una gifts to the needy are remember in the sight of God.
Send so to Joppa, and summon Simon, Wey be also call Peter. He lodges in the house of a tanner named Simon, by the seaside. When he comes, he will speak to you.’
So I sent to you at once, and it was good of you to come. Now so We be all here present in the sight of God to hear all things that Don dey commanded you by God.”
Peter opened his mouth and talk say, “Truly I perceive that God no dey show favoritism;
but in every nation person wey fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him.
The word which he sent to the pikin dem of Israel, preaching better news of peace by Jesus Christ — he is Lord of all —
you unaself know what happened, which was proclaimed throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached;
even Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power, who go about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with him.
We be witnesses of everything he did both in the country of the Jews, and in Jerusalem; whom dem also killed, hanging him on a tree.
God raised him up the third day, and give him to be revealed,
not to all the people, but to witnesses who were chosen before by God, to us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.
He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that this is person Wey appointed by God as the Judge of the living and the dead.
All the prophets testify about him, that through his name everyone wey believe in him will receive remission of sins.”
While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all people wey heard the word.
Dem of the circumcision who believe were amazed, as many as come with Peter, because the gift of the Holy Spirit was also poured out on the Gentiles.
For dem heard dem speaking in other languages and magnifying God. Then Peter answer,
“Can anyone forbid these people from being baptized with water? Dem have received the Holy Spirit just like us.”
He commanded dem to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then dem ask him to stay some days.
Now the apostles and the brothers who were in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.
When Peter had come up to Jerusalem, people wey were of the circumcision contended with him,
saying, “You go in to uncircumcised men, and ate with dem!”
But Peter began, and explained to dem in order, saying,
“I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I see a vision: a certain container descending, like it was a great sheet let down from heaven by four corners. It come as far as me.
When I had looked intently at it, I considered, and see the four-footed animals of the earth, wild animals, creeping things, and birds of the sky.
I also heard a voice saying to me, ‘Rise, Peter, kill and eat!’
But I talk say, ‘Not so, Lord, for nothing unholy or unclean has ever entered into my mouth.’
But a voice answer me the second time out of heaven, ‘What God has cleansed, no you call unclean.’
This was done three times, and all were drawn up again into heaven.
See am, sharp-sharp three men stood before the house where I was, having been sent from Caesarea to me.
The Spirit told me to go with dem, without discriminating. These six brothers also accompanied me, and we entered into the man’s house.
He told us how he had seen the angel standing in his house, and saying to him, ‘Send to Joppa, and get Simon, Wey be call Peter,
who will speak to you words by which You go be saved, you and all una house.’
As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on dem, even as on us at the beginning.
I remember the word of the Lord, how he talk say, ‘John indeed baptized in water, but You go be baptized in the Holy Spirit.’
If then God give to dem the same gift as us, when we believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I, that I could withstand God?”
When dem heard these things, dem held dem peace, and glorified God, saying, “Then God has also granted to the Gentiles repentance to life!”
Dem so who were scattered abroad by the oppression that arose about Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to Nobody except to Jews only.
But there were some of dem, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when dem had come to Antioch, spoke to the Hellenists, preaching the Lord Jesus.
The hand of the Lord was with dem, and a great number believe and turned to the Lord.
The report concerning dem come to the ears of the assembly which was in Jerusalem. Dem sent out Barnabas to go as far as Antioch,
who, when he had come, and had seen the grace of God, was glad. He exhorted dem all, that with purpose of heart dem should remain near to the Lord.
For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith, and many people were added to the Lord.
Barnabas go out to Tarsus to look for Saul.
When he had find him, he bring him to Antioch. For a whole year dem were gathered together with the assembly, and taught many people. The disciples were first call Christians in Antioch.
Now in these days, prophets come down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of dem named Agabus stood up, and indicated by the Spirit that there should be a great famine all over the world, which also happened in the days of Claudius.
As any of the disciples had plenty, each determined to send relief to the brothers who lived in Judea;
which dem also did, sending it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul.
Now about that time, King Herod stretched out his hands to oppress some of the assembly.
He killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.
When he see that it pleased the Jews, he proceeded to seize Peter also. This was during the days of unleavened bread.
When he had arrested him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four squads of four soldiers each to guard him, intending to bring him out to the people after the Passover.
Peter so was kept in the prison, but constant prayer was made by the assembly to God for him.
The same night when Herod was about to bring him out, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains. Guards in front of the door kept the prison.
And see am, an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on the side, and woke him up, saying, “Stand up sharp-sharp!” His chains fell off from his hands.
The angel talk say to him, “Get dressed and put on una sandals.” He did so. E tell am say, “Put on una cloak, and follow me.”
And he go out and follow him. He didn’t know that what was being done by the angel was real, but thought he see a vision.

When dem were past the first and the second guard, dem come to the iron gate that leads into the city, which opened to dem by itself. Dem go out, and go down one street, and sharp-sharp the angel comot from him.
When Peter had come to imself, he talk say, “Now I truly know that the Lord has sent out his angel and delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from everything the Jewish people were expecting.”
Thinking about that, he come to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was call Mark, where many were gathered together and were praying.
When Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a maid named Rhoda come to answer.
When she recognized Peter’s voice, she didn’t open the gate for gladness, but ran in, and reported that Peter was standing in front of the gate.
Dem talk say to her, “You be crazy!” But she insisted that it was so. Dem talk say, “It is his angel.”
But Peter continued knocking. When dem had opened, dem see him, and were amazed.

But he, beckoning to dem with his hand to be silent, declared to dem how the Lord had bring him out of the prison. He talk say, “Tell these things to James, and to the brothers.” Then he comot, and go to another place.
Now as soon as it was day, there was no small stir among the soldiers about what had become of Peter.
When Herod had sought for him, and didn’t find him, he examined the guards, and commanded that dem should be put to death. He go down from Judea to Caesarea, and stayed there.

Now Herod was very angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon. Dem come with one accord to him, and, having made Blastus, the king’s personal aide, dem friend, dem ask for peace, because dem country depended on the king’s country for chop.
On an appointed day, Herod dressed imself in royal clothing, sat on the throne, and give a speech to dem.
The people shouted, “The voice of a god, and not of a man!”
Sharp-sharp an angel of the Lord struck him, because he didn’t give God the glory, and he was eaten by worms and died.
But the word of God grew and multiplied.
Barnabas and Saul come back to Jerusalem, when dem had fulfilled dem service, also taking with dem John who was call Mark.
Now in the assembly that was at Antioch there were some prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was call Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen the foster brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
As dem served the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit talk say, “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have call dem.”
Then, when dem had fasted and prayed and laid dem hands on dem, dem sent dem away.
So, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, dem go down to Seleucia. From there dem sailed to Cyprus.
When dem were at Salamis, dem proclaimed the word of God in the Jewish synagogues. Dem had also John as dem attendant.
When dem had gone through the island to Paphos, dem find a certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar Jesus,
who was with the proconsul, Sergius Paulus, a man of understanding. This man summoned Barnabas and Saul, and sought to hear the word of God.
But Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation) withstood dem, seeking to turn aside the proconsul from the faith.
But Saul, Wey be also call Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, fastened his eyes on him,
and talk say, “Full of all deceit and all cunning, you son of the devil, you enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord?
Now, see am, the hand of the Lord is on you, and You go be blind, not seeing the sun for a season!” Sharp-sharp a mist and darkness fell on him. He go around seeking someone to lead him by the hand.
Then the proconsul, when he see what was done, believe, being astonished at the teaching of the Lord.
Now Paul and his company set sail from Paphos, and come to Perga in Pamphylia. John comot from dem and come back to Jerusalem.
But dem, passing on from Perga, come to Antioch of Pisidia. Dem go into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and sat down.
After the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to dem, saying, “Brothers, if you have any word of exhortation for the people, speak.”
Paul stood up, and beckoning with his hand talk say, “Men of Israel, and you who fear God, listen.
The God of this people chose our fathers, and exalted the people when dem stayed as aliens in the land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm, he led dem out of it.
For a period of about forty years he put up with dem in the wilderness.
When he had destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, he give dem dem land for an inheritance, for about four hundred fifty years.
After these things he give dem judges until Samuel the prophet.
Afterward dem ask for a king, and God give to dem Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.
When he had removed him, he raised up David to be dem king, to whom he also testified, ‘I have find David the son of Jesse, a man after my heart, who will do all my will.’
From this man’s offspring, God has bring salvation to Israel according to his promise,
before his coming, when John had first preached the baptism of repentance to Israel.
As John was fulfilling his course, he talk say, ‘What do you suppose that I be? I be not he. But see am, one comes after me the sandals of whose feet I be not worthy to untie.’
Brothers, pikin dem of the stock of Abraham, and those among you who fear God, the word of this salvation is sent out to you.
For people wey live in Jerusalem, and dem rulers, because dem didn’t know him, nor the voices of the prophets which are read every Sabbath, fulfilled dem by condemning him.
Though dem find no cause for death, dem still ask Pilate to have him killed.
When dem had fulfilled all things that were written about him, dem take him down from the tree, and laid him in a tomb.
But God raised him from the dead,
and he was seen for many days by people wey come up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, Wey be his witnesses to the people.
We bring you better news of the promise made to the fathers,
that God has fulfilled the same to us, dem pikin dem, in that he raised up Jesus. As it is also written in the second psalm, ‘You be my Son. Today I have become una father.’
“Concerning that he raised him up from the dead, now no more to return to corruption, he has spoken thus: ‘I go give you the holy and sure blessings of David.’
So he says also in another psalm, ‘You go not allow una Holy One to see decay.’
For David, after he had in his own generation served the counsel of God, fell asleep, and was laid with his fathers, and see decay.
But he whom God raised up see no decay.
Be it known to you so, brothers, that through this man is proclaimed to you remission of sins,
and by him everyone wey believe is justified from all things, from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.
Beware so, lest that come on you which is spoken in the prophets:
‘See am, you scoffers, and wonder, and perish; for I work a work in una days, a work which You go in no way believe, if one declares it to you.’”
So when the Jews go out of the synagogue, the Gentiles begged that these words might be preached to dem the next Sabbath.
Now when the synagogue broke up, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes follow Paul and Barnabas; who, speaking to dem, urged dem to continue in the grace of God.
The next Sabbath almost the whole city was gathered together to hear the word of God.
But when the Jews see the plenty people, dem were filled with jealousy, and contradicted the things which were spoken by Paul, and blasphemed.

Paul and Barnabas spoke out boldly, and talk say, “It was necessary that God’s word should be spoken to you first. Since indeed you thrust it from you, and judge unaself unworthy of life wey no dey end, see am, we turn to the Gentiles.
For so has the Lord commanded us, saying, ‘I have set you as a light for the Gentiles, that you should bring salvation to the uttermost parts of the earth.’”
As the Gentiles heard this, dem were glad, and glorified the word of God. As many as were appointed to life wey no dey end believe.
The Lord’s word was spread abroad throughout all the region.
But the Jews stirred up the devout and prominent women and the chief men of the city, and stirred up a persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and threw dem out of dem borders.
But dem shook off the dust of dem feet against dem, and come to Iconium.
The disciples were filled with gladness and with the Holy Spirit.
In Iconium, dem entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spoke that Plenty people both of Jews and of Greeks believe.
But the disbelieving Jews stirred up and embittered the souls of the Gentiles against the brothers.
So dem stayed there a long time, speaking boldly in the Lord, who testified to the word of his grace, granting signs and wonders to be done by dem hands.
But the plenty people of the city was divided. Part sided with the Jews, and part with the apostles.
When some of both the Gentiles and the Jews, with dem rulers, made a violent attempt to mistreat and stone dem,
dem became aware of it, and fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra, Derbe, and the surrounding region.
There dem preached the Better news.
At Lystra a certain man sat, impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked.
He was listening to Paul speaking, who, fastening eyes on him, and seeing that he had faith to be made whole,
talk say with a loud voice, “Stand upright on una feet!” He leaped up and walked.
When the plenty people see what Paul had done, dem lifted up dem voice, saying in the language of Lycaonia, “The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men!”
Dem call Barnabas “Jupiter”, and Paul “Mercury”, because he was the chief speaker.
