May it never be! We who died to sin, how could we live in it any longer?
Or no you know that all we who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?
We were buried so with him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.
For if we have become united with him in the likeness of his death, We go also be part of his resurrection;
knowing this, that our old man was crucified with him, that the body of sin might be done away with, so that we would no longer be in bondage to sin.
For person wey has died Don dey freed from sin.
But if we died with Christ, we believe that We go also live with him;
knowing that Christ, being raised from the dead, dies no more. Death no more has dominion over him!
For the death that he died, he died to sin one time; but the life that he lives, he lives to God.
Thus consider unaself also to be dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
So no let sin reign in una mortal body, that you should obey it in its lusts.
Also, No present una members to sin as instruments of unrighteousness, but present unaself to God, as alive from the dead, and una members as instruments of righteousness to God.
For sin No go have dominion over you. For you No be under law, but under grace.
What then? Shall we sin, because we No be under law, but under grace? May it never be!
No you know that when you present unaself as workers and obey someone, You be the workers of whomever you obey; whether of sin to death, or of obedience to righteousness?
But thanks be to God, that, whereas you were bondservants of sin, you became obedient from the heart to that form of teaching to which you were delivered.
Being made free from sin, you became bondservants of righteousness.

I speak in human terms because of the weakness of una flesh, for as you presented una members as workers to uncleanness and to wickedness upon wickedness, even so now present una members as workers to righteousness for sanctification.
For when you were workers of sin, you were free in regard to righteousness.
What fruit then did you have at that time in the things of which You be now ashamed? For the end of those things is death.
But now, being made free from sin, and having become workers of God, you have una fruit of sanctification, and the result of life wey no dey end.
For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is life wey no dey end in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Or no you know, brothers (for I speak to men who know the law), that the law has dominion over a man for as long as he lives?
For the woman that has a husband is bound by law to the husband while he lives, but if the husband dies, she is discharged from the law of the husband.

So then if, while the husband lives, she is joined to another man, she would be call an adulteress. But if the husband dies, she is free from the law, so that she is no adulteress, though she is joined to another man.
So, my brothers, you also were made dead to the law through the body of Christ, that you would be joined to another, to him who was raised from the dead, that we might produce fruit to God.
For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions which were through the law, worked in our members to bring out fruit to death.
But now we Don dey discharged from the law, having died to that in which we were held; so that we serve in newness of the spirit, and not in oldness of the letter.

What shall we say then? Is the law sin? May it never be! However, I wouldn’t have known sin, except through the law. For I wouldn’t have known coveting, unless the law had talk say, “You no go covet.”
But sin, finding occasion through the commandment, produced in me all kinds of coveting. For apart from the law, sin is dead.
I was alive apart from the law once, but when the commandment come, sin revived, and I died.
The commandment, which was for life, this I find to be for death;
for sin, finding occasion through the commandment, deceived me, and through it killed me.
So the law indeed is holy, and the commandment holy, and righteous, and good.

Did then that which is good become death to me? May it never be! But sin, that it might be shown to be sin, by producing death in me through that which is good; that through the commandment sin might become exceedingly sinful.
For we know that the law is spiritual, but I be fleshly, sold under sin.
For I no know what I be doing. For I no practice what I desire to do; but what I hate, that I do.
But if what I no desire, that I do, I consent to the law that it is good.
So now it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwells in me.
For I know that in me, that is, in my flesh, dwells no good thing. For desire is present with me, but I no find it doing that which is good.
For the good which I desire, I no do; but the evil which I no desire, that I practice.
But if what I no desire, that I do, it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwells in me.
I find then the law, that, to me, while I desire to do good, evil is present.
For I delight in God’s law after the inward man,
but I see a different law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity under the law of sin which is in my members.
What a wretched man I be! Who will deliver me out of the body of this death?
I thank God through Jesus Christ, our Lord! So then with the mind, I myself serve God’s law, but with the flesh, the sin’s law.
E get so now no condemnation to people Wey in Christ Jesus, who no walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.
For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made me free from the law of sin and of death.
For what the law no fit do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God did, sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, he condemned sin in the flesh;
that the ordinance of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.
For people wey live according to the flesh set dem minds on the things of the flesh, but people wey live according to the Spirit, the things of the Spirit.
For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace;
because the mind of the flesh is hostile towards God; for it No be subject to God’s law, neither indeed can it be.
People Wey in the flesh no fit please God.
But you No be in the flesh but in the Spirit, if it is so that the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if any man no dey have the Spirit of Christ, he No be his.
If Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the spirit is alive because of righteousness.

But if the Spirit of him who raised up Jesus from the dead dwells in you, person wey raised up Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to una mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you.
So then, brothers, We be debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh.
For if you live after the flesh, you must die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, You go live.
For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are pikin dem of God.
For you didn’t receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”
The Spirit imself testifies with our spirit that We be pikin dem of God;
and if pikin dem, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint heirs with Christ; if indeed we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified with him.
For I consider that the sufferings of this present time No be worthy to be compared with the glory which Go be revealed toward us.
For the creation waits with eager expectation for the pikin dem of God to be revealed.
For the creation was subjected to vanity, not of its own will, but because of him who subjected it, in hope
that the creation itself also Go be delivered from the bondage of decay into the liberty of the glory of the pikin dem of God.
For we know that the whole creation groans and travails in pain together until now.
Not only so, but ourselves also, who have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for adoption, the redemption of our body.
For we were saved in hope, but hope that is seen No be hope. For who hopes for that which he sees?
But if we hope for that which we no see, we wait for it with patience.
In the same way, the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we no know how to pray as we ought. But the Spirit imself makes intercession for us with groanings which no fit be uttered.
Person wey searches the hearts knows Wetin be on the Spirit’s mind, because he makes intercession for the saints according to God.
We know that everything dey work together for good for people wey love God, to people Wey call according to his purpose.
For whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brothers.
Whom he predestined, those he also call. Whom he call, those he also justified. Whom he justified, those he also glorified.
What then shall we say about these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
Person wey didn’t spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how would he not also with him freely give us all things?
Who could bring a charge against God’s chosen ones? It is God who justifies.
Wey be person wey condemns? It is Christ who died, yes rather, who was raised from the dead, Wey be at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession for us.
Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Could oppression, or anguish, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?
Even as it is written, “For una sake We be killed all day long. We were accounted as sheep for the slaughter.”
No, in all these things, We be more than conquerors through him who love us.
For I be persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,
nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing, Go be able to separate us from God’s love, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
I tell the truth in Christ. I be not lying, my conscience testifying with me in the Holy Spirit,
that I have great sorrow and unceasing pain in my heart.
For I could wish that I myself were accursed from Christ for my brothers’ sake, my relatives according to the flesh,
Wey be Israelites; whose is the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the service, and the promises;
of whom are the fathers, and from whom is Christ as concerning the flesh, Wey be over all, God, blessed forever. Amen.
But it is No be like though the word of God has come to nothing. For dem No be all Israel, that are of Israel.
Neither, because Dem be Abraham’s offspring, are dem all pikin dem. But, “una offspring Go be accounted as from Isaac.”
That is, it No be the pikin dem of the flesh Wey be pikin dem of God, but the pikin dem of the promise are counted as heirs.
For this is a word of promise, “At the appointed time I go come, and Sarah Go get a son.”
Not only so, but Rebekah also conceived by one, by our father Isaac.
For being not yet born, neither having done anything good or bad, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him who calls,
it was talk say to her, “The elder will serve the younger.”
Even as it is written, “Jacob I love, but Esau I hated.”
What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? May it never be!
For he talk say to Moses, “I go have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I go have compassion on whom I have compassion.”
So then it No be of him who wills, nor of him who runs, but of God who has mercy.
For the Scripture says to Pharaoh, “For this very purpose I caused you to be raised up, that I might show in you my power, and that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”
So then, he has mercy on whom he desires, and he hardens whom he desires.
You go say then to me, “Why does he still find fault? For who withstands his will?”
But indeed, O man, Wey be you to reply against God? Will the thing formed ask him who formed it, “Why did you make me like this?”
Or hasn’t the potter a right over the clay, from the same lump to make one part a vessel for honor, and another for dishonor?
What if God, willing to show his serious anger, and to make his power known, endured with much patience vessels of serious anger made for destruction,
and that he might make known the riches of his glory on vessels of mercy, which he prepared beforehand for glory,
us, whom he also call, not from the Jews only, but also from the Gentiles?
As he says also in Hosea, “I go call dem ‘my people,’ which No be my people; and her ‘beloved,’ who No be beloved.”
“It Go be that in the place where it was talk say to dem, ‘You No be my people,’ There Dem go be call ‘pikin dem of the living God.’”
Isaiah cries concerning Israel, “If the number of the pikin dem of Israel are as the sand of the sea, it is the remnant who Go be saved;
for He will finish the work and cut it short in righteousness, because the LORD will make a short work upon the earth.”
As Isaiah has talk say before, “Unless the Lord of Armies had left us a seed, we would have become like Sodom, and would Don dey made like Gomorrah.”
What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, who didn’t follow after righteousness, attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith;
but Israel, following after a law of righteousness, didn’t arrive at the law of righteousness.
Why? Because dem didn’t seek it by faith, but as it were by works of the law. Dem stumbled over the stumbling stone;
even as it is written, “See am, I lay in Zion a stumbling stone and a rock of offense; and Nobody wey believe in him Go be disappointed.”
Brothers, my heart’s desire and my prayer to God is for Israel, that dem may be saved.
For I testify about dem that dem have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.
For being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and seeking to establish dem own righteousness, dem didn’t subject themselves to the righteousness of God.
For Christ is the fulfillment of the law for righteousness to everyone wey believe.
For Moses writes about the righteousness of the law, “The one wey do dem will live by dem.”
But the righteousness which is of faith says this, “No say in una heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’ (that is, to bring Christ down);
or, ‘Who will descend into the abyss?’ (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.)”
But what does it say? “The word is near you, in una mouth, and in una heart”; that is, the word of faith, which we preach:
that if You go confess with una mouth that Jesus is Lord, and believe in una heart that God raised him from the dead, You go be saved.
For with the heart, one believe to righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made to salvation.
For the Scripture says, “Anybody wey believe in him No go be disappointed.”
For E get no distinction between Jew and Greek; for the same Lord is Lord of all, and is rich to all who call on him.
For, “Anybody wey will call on the name of the Lord Go be saved.”
How then will dem call on him in whom dem have not believe? How will dem believe in him whom dem have not heard? How will dem hear without a preacher?
And how will dem preach unless Dem be sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of people wey preach the Better news of peace, who bring glad tidings of good things!”
But dem didn’t all listen to the glad news. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believe our report?”
So faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.
But I say, didn’t dem hear? Yes, most certainly, “Dem sound go out into all the earth, dem words to the ends of the world.”
But I ask, didn’t Israel know? First Moses says, “I go provoke you to jealousy with that which is no nation, with a nation void of understanding I go make you angry.”
Isaiah is very bold, and says, “I was find by people wey didn’t seek me. I was revealed to people wey didn’t ask for me.”
But as to Israel he says, “All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people.”
I ask then, did God reject his people? May it never be! For I also am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
God didn’t reject his people, which he foreknew. Or no you know what the Scripture says about Elijah? How he pleads with God against Israel:
“Lord, dem have killed una prophets, dem have broken down una altars; and I be left alone, and dem seek my life.”
But how does God answer him? “I have reserved for myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”
Even so then at this present time also E get a remnant according to the election of grace.
And if by grace, then it is no longer of works; otherwise grace is no longer grace. But if it is of works, it is no longer grace; otherwise work is no longer work.
What then? That which Israel seeks for, that he didn’t obtain, but the chosen ones obtained it, and the rest were hardened.
According as it is written, “God give dem a spirit of stupor, eyes that dem no suppose see, and ears that dem no suppose hear, to this very day.”
David says, “Let dem table be made a snare, and a trap, a stumbling block, and a retribution to dem.
Let dem eyes be darkened, that dem may not see. Bow down dem back always.”
I ask then, did dem stumble that dem might fall? May it never be! But by dem fall salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke dem to jealousy.
Now if dem fall is the riches of the world, and dem loss the riches of the Gentiles; how much more dem fullness?
For I speak to you Wey be Gentiles. Since then as I be an apostle to Gentiles, I glorify my ministry;
if by any means I may provoke to jealousy people Wey my flesh, and may save some of dem.
For if the rejection of dem is the reconciling of the world, what would dem acceptance be, but life from the dead?
If the first fruit is holy, so is the lump. If the root is holy, so are the branches.
But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among dem, and became partaker with dem of the root and of the richness of the olive tree;
no boast over the branches. But if you boast, it No be you who support the root, but the root supports you.
You go say then, “Branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in.”
True; by dem unbelief dem were broken off, and you stand by una faith. No be conceited, but fear;
for if God didn’t spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.
See then the goodness and severity of God. Toward people wey fell, severity; but toward you, goodness, if you continue in his goodness; otherwise you also Go be cut off.
Dem also, if dem no continue in dem unbelief, Go be grafted in, for God is able to graft dem in again.

For if you were cut out of that which is by nature a wild olive tree, and were grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree, how much more will these, which are the natural branches, be grafted into dem own olive tree?

For I no desire you to be ignorant, brothers, of this mystery, so that you no go be wise in una own conceits, that a partial hardening has happened to Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in,
and so all Israel Go be saved. Even as it is written, “There will come out of Zion the Deliverer, and he will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.
This is my covenant to dem, when I go take away dem sins.”
Concerning the Better news, Dem be enemies for una sake. But concerning the election, Dem be beloved for the fathers’ sake.
For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
For as you in time past were disobedient to God, but now have obtained mercy by dem disobedience,
even so these also have now been disobedient, that by the mercy shown to you dem may also obtain mercy.
For God has shut up all to disobedience, that he might have mercy on all.
Oh the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and the knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past tracing out!
“For who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who Don dey his counselor?”
“Or who has first given to him, and it Go be repaid to him again?”
For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things. To him be the glory for ever! Amen.
So I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present una bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is una spiritual service.
No be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of una mind, so that you may prove Wetin be the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.

For I say, through the grace that was given me, to every man Wey be among you, not to think of imself more highly than he ought to think; but to think reasonably, as God has apportioned to each person a measure of faith.
For even as we have many members in one body, and all the members no have the same function,
so we, Wey be many, are one body in Christ, and individually members one of another.
Having gifts differing according to the grace that was given to us, if prophecy, Make we prophesy according to the proportion of our faith;
or service, Make we give ourselves to service; or person wey teaches, to his teaching;
or person wey exhorts, to his exhorting: person wey gives, Make e do it with liberality; person wey rules, with diligence; person wey shows mercy, with cheerfulness.
Let love be without hypocrisy. Abhor that which is evil. Cling to that which is good.
In love of the brothers be tenderly affectionate to each other; in honor preferring each other;
not lagging in diligence; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord;
rejoicing in hope; enduring in troubles; continuing steadfastly in prayer;
contributing to the needs of the saints; given to hospitality.
Bless people wey persecute you; bless, and no curse.
Glad well-well with people wey glad well-well. Weep with people wey weep.
Be of the same mind one toward another. No set una mind on high things, but associate with the humble. No be wise in una own conceits.
Repay Nobody evil for evil. Respect Wetin be honorable in the sight of all men.
If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.
No seek revenge unaself, beloved, but give place to God’s serious anger. For it is written, “Vengeance belongs to me; I go repay, says the Lord.”
So “If una enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him a drink; for in doing so, You go heap coals of fire on his head.”
No be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
Let every soul be in subjection to the higher authorities, for E get no authority except from God, and people wey exist are ordained by God.
So person wey resists the authority, withstands the ordinance of God; and people wey withstand will receive to themselves judgment.
For rulers No be a terror to the good work, but to the evil. Do you desire to have no fear of the authority? Do that which is good, and You go have praise from the same,

for he is a worker of God to you for good. But if you do that which is evil, be afraid, for he no dey bear the sword in vain; for he is a worker of God, an avenger for serious anger to him wey do evil.
So you need to be in subjection, not only because of the serious anger, but also for conscience’ sake.
For this reason you also pay taxes, for Dem be workers of God’s service, attending continually on this very thing.
So give everyone Wetin you owe: if you owe taxes, pay taxes; if customs, then customs; if respect, then respect; if honor, then honor.
Owe Nobody anything, except to love each other; for person wey loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.

For the commandments, “You no go commit adultery,” “You no go murder,” “You no go steal,” “You no go covet,” and Anything wey other commandments E get, are all summed up in this saying, namely, “You shall love una neighbor as yourself.”
Love no dey harm a neighbor. Love so is the fulfillment of the law.
Do this, knowing the time, that it is already time for you to awaken out of sleep, for salvation is now nearer to us than when we first believe.
The night is far gone, and the day is near. Let’s so throw off the deeds of darkness, and let’s put on the armor of light.
Make we walk properly, as in the day; not in reveling and drunkenness, not in sexual promiscuity and lustful acts, and not in strife and jealousy.
But put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh, for its lusts.
Now accept one Wey be weak in faith, but not for disputes over opinions.
One man has faith to eat all things, but person Wey weak eats only vegetables.
No Make e who eats despise him who no dey eat. No Make e who no dey eat judge him who eats, for God has accepted him.
Wey be you who judge another’s worker? To his own lord he stands or falls. Yes, he Go be made to stand, for God has power to make him stand.
One man esteems one day as more important. Another esteems every day alike. Let each man be fully assured in his own mind.

Person wey observes the day, observes it to the Lord; and person wey No dey observe the day, to the Lord he No dey observe it. Person wey eats, eats to the Lord, for he gives God thanks. Person wey no dey eat, to the Lord he no dey eat, and gives God thanks.
For none of us lives to imself, and none dies to imself.
For if we live, we live to the Lord. Or if we die, we die to the Lord. If so we live or die, We be the Lord’s.
For to this end Christ died, rose, and lived again, that he might be Lord of both the dead and the living.
But you, why do you judge una brother? Or you again, why do you despise una brother? For We go all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.
For it is written, “‘As I live,’ says the Lord, ‘to me every knee will bow. Every tongue will confess to God.’”
So then each one of us will give account of imself to God.
So let’s not judge each other any more, but judge this rather, that no man put a stumbling block in his brother’s way, or an occasion for falling.
I know, and am persuaded in the Lord Jesus, that nothing is unclean of itself; except that to him who considers anything to be unclean, to him it is unclean.
Yet if because of chop una brother is grieved, you walk no longer in love. No destroy with una chop him for whom Christ died.
Then no let una good be slandered,
for God’s Kingdom No be eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and gladness in the Holy Spirit.
For person wey serves Christ in these things is acceptable to God and approved by men.
So then, Make we follow after things which make for peace, and things by which we may build each other up.
No overthrow God’s work for chop’s sake. All things indeed are clean, however it is evil for that man who creates a stumbling block by eating.
It is good to not eat meat, drink wine, nor do anything by which una brother stumbles, is offended, or is made weak.
Do you have faith? Have it to yourself before God. Happy is person wey no dey judge imself in that which he approves.
But person wey doubts is condemned if he eats, because it no be of faith; and Anything wey No be of faith is sin.
Now to him Wey be able to establish you according to my Better news and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery which Don dey kept secret through long ages,
but now is revealed, and by the Scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the eternal God, is made known for obedience of faith to all the nations;
to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory forever! Amen.
Now we Wey be strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak, and not to please ourselves.
Let each one of us please his neighbor for that which is good, to be building him up.
For even Christ didn’t please imself. But, as it is written, “The reproaches of people wey reproached you fell on me.”
For Anything wey things were written before were written for our learning, that through perseverance and through encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.
Now the God of perseverance and of encouragement grant you to be of the same mind one with another according to Christ Jesus,
that with one accord you may with one mouth glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So accept each other, even as Christ also accepted you, to the glory of God.
Now I say that Christ Don dey made a worker of the circumcision for the truth of God, that he might confirm the promises given to the fathers,
and that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy. As it is written, “So will I give praise to you among the Gentiles, and sing to una name.”
Again he says, “Glad well-well, you Gentiles, with his people.”
Again, “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles! Let all the peoples praise him.”
Again, Isaiah says, “There Go be the root of Jesse, person wey arises to rule over the Gentiles; in him the Gentiles will hope.”
Now may the God of hope fill you with all gladness and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope, in the power of the Holy Spirit.
I myself am also persuaded about you, my brothers, that you unaself are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish others.
But I write the more boldly to you in part, as reminding you, because of the grace that was given to me by God,
that I should be a worker of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, serving as a priest of the Better news of God, that the offering up of the Gentiles might be made acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
I have so my boasting in Christ Jesus in things pertaining to God.
For I go not dare to speak of any things except those which Christ worked through me, for the obedience of the Gentiles, by word and deed,
in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of God’s Spirit; so that from Jerusalem, and around as far as to Illyricum, I have fully preached the Better news of Christ;
yes, making it my aim to preach the Better news, not where Christ was already named, that I might not build on another’s foundation.
But, as it is written, “Dem go see, to whom no news of him come. Dem who haven’t heard will understand.”
So also I was hindered these many times from coming to you,
but now, no longer having any place in these regions, and having these many years a longing to come to you,
whenever I travel to Spain, I go come to you. For I hope to see you on my journey, and to be helped on my way there by you, if first I may enjoy una company for a while.
But now, I say, I be going to Jerusalem, serving the saints.
For it Don dey the good pleasure of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor among the saints Wey be at Jerusalem.
Yes, it Don dey dem good pleasure, and Dem be dem debtors. For if the Gentiles Don dey made partakers of dem spiritual things, dem owe it to dem also to serve dem in fleshly things.
When so I have accomplished this, and have sealed to dem this fruit, I go go on by way of you to Spain.
I know that, when I come to you, I go come in the fullness of the blessing of the Better news of Christ.
Now I beg you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ, and by the love of the Spirit, that you strive together with me in una prayers to God for me,
that I may be delivered from people Wey disobedient in Judea, and that my service which I have for Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints;
that I may come to you in gladness through the will of God, and together with you, find rest.
Now the God of Make peace dey with una all. Amen.
I commend to you Phoebe, our sister, Wey be a worker of the assembly that is at Cenchreae,

that you receive her in the Lord, in a way worthy of the saints, and that you assist her in Anything wey matter she may need from you, for she sheself also Don dey a helper of many, and of my own self.
Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
who for my life, laid down dem own necks; to whom not only I Thank God, but also all the assemblies of the Gentiles.
Greet the assembly that is in dem house. Greet Epaenetus, my beloved, Wey be the first fruits of Achaia to Christ.
Greet Mary, who labored much for us.
Greet Andronicus and Junia, my relatives and my fellow prisoners, Wey be notable among the apostles, who were also in Christ before me.
Greet Amplias, my beloved in the Lord.
Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and Stachys, my beloved.
Greet Apelles, the approved in Christ. Greet people Wey of the household of Aristobulus.
Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet dem of the household of Narcissus, Wey be in the Lord.
Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Greet Persis, the beloved, who labored much in the Lord.
Greet Rufus, the chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers Wey be with dem.
Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints Wey be with dem.
Greet each other with a holy kiss. The assemblies of Christ greet you.
Now I beg you, brothers, look out for people Wey causing the divisions and occasions of stumbling, contrary to the doctrine which you learned, and turn away from dem.
For people Wey such no serve our Lord, Jesus Christ, but dem own belly; and by dem smooth and flattering speech, dem deceive the hearts of the innocent.
For una obedience has become known to all. I glad well-well so over you. But I desire to have you wise in that which is good, but innocent in that which is evil.
And the God of peace will sharp-sharp crush Satan under una feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
Timothy, my fellow worker, greets you, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my relatives.
I, Tertius, who write the letter, greet you in the Lord.
Gaius, my host and host of the whole assembly, greets you. Erastus, the treasurer of the city, greets you, as does Quartus, the brother.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all! Amen.
Paul, call to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,
to the assembly of God which is at Corinth; people Wey sanctified in Christ Jesus, call to be saints, with all who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, both dem own and ours:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I always thank my God concerning you, for the grace of God which was given you in Christ Jesus;
that in everything you were enriched in him, in all speech and all knowledge;
even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you:
so that you come behind in no gift; waiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ;
who will also confirm you until the end, blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is faithful, through whom you were call into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ, our Lord.

Now I beg you, brothers, through the name of our Lord, Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfected together in the same mind and in the same judgment.
For it Don dey reported to me concerning you, my brothers, by people Wey from Chloe’s household, that E get contentions among you.
Now I mean this, that each one of you says, “I follow Paul,” “I follow Apollos,” “I follow Cephas,” and, “I follow Christ.”
Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized into the name of Paul?
I thank God that I baptized none of you, except Crispus and Gaius,
so that Nobody should say that I had baptized you into my own name.
(I also baptized the household of Stephanas; besides dem, I no know whether I baptized any other.)
For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the Better news — not in wisdom of words, so that the cross of Christ wouldn’t be made void.
For the word of the cross is foolishness to people Wey dying, but to us Wey be saved it is the power of God.
For it is written, “I go destroy the wisdom of the wise, I go bring the discernment of the discerning to nothing.”
Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the lawyer of this world? Hasn’t God made foolish the wisdom of this world?
For seeing that in the wisdom of God, the world through its wisdom didn’t know God, it was God’s good pleasure through the foolishness of the preaching to save people wey believe.
For Jews ask for signs, Greeks seek after wisdom,
but we preach Christ crucified; a stumbling block to Jews, and foolishness to Greeks,
but to people Wey call, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God.
Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men.
For you see una calling, brothers, that not many are wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, and not many noble;
but God chose the foolish things of the world that he might put to shame people Wey wise. God chose the weak things of the world, that he might put to shame the things that are strong;
and God chose the lowly things of the world, and the things that are despised, and the things that No be, that he might bring to nothing the things that are:
that no flesh should boast before God.
Because of him, You be in Christ Jesus, who was made to us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification, and redemption:
that, according as it is written, “Person wey boasts, Make e boast in the Lord.”
When I come to you, brothers, I didn’t come with excellence of speech or of wisdom, proclaiming to you the testimony of God.
For I determined not to know anything among you, except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
I was with you in weakness, in fear, and in much trembling.
My speech and my preaching No be in persuasive words of human wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power,
that una faith wouldn’t stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.
We speak wisdom, however, among people Wey full grown; yet a wisdom not of this world, nor of the rulers of this world, Wey be coming to nothing.
But we speak God’s wisdom in a mystery, the wisdom that Don dey hidden, which God foreordained before the worlds for our glory,
which none of the rulers of this world has known. For had dem known it, dem wouldn’t have crucified the Lord of glory.
But as it is written, “Things which an eye didn’t see, and an ear didn’t hear, which didn’t enter into the heart of man, these God has prepared for people wey love him.”
But to us, God revealed dem through the Spirit. For the Spirit searches all things, yes, the deep things of God.
For who among men knows the things of a man, except the spirit of the man, which is in him? Even so, Nobody knows the things of God, except God’s Spirit.
But we received, not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit which is from God, that we might know the things that were freely given to us by God.
Which things also we speak, not in words which man’s wisdom teaches, but which the Holy Spirit teaches, comparing spiritual things with spiritual things.
Now the natural man no dey receive the things of God’s Spirit, for Dem be foolishness to him, and he no fit know dem, because Dem be spiritually discerned.
But person Wey spiritual discerns all things, and he imself is judged by Nobody.
“For who has known the mind of the Lord, that he should instruct him?” But we have Christ’s mind.
Brothers, I no fit speak to you as to spiritual, but as to fleshly, as to babies in Christ.
I fed you with milk, not with meat; for you no be yet ready. Indeed, not even now are you ready,
for You be still fleshly. For insofar as E get jealousy, strife, and factions among you, no be you fleshly, and no you walk in the ways of men?
For when one says, “I follow Paul,” and another, “I follow Apollos,” no be you fleshly?
Who then is Apollos, and Wey be Paul, but workers through whom you believe; and each as the Lord give to him?
I planted. Apollos watered. But God give the increase.
So then neither person wey plants is anything, nor person wey waters, but God wey dey give the increase.
Now person wey plants and person wey waters are the same, but each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.
For We be God’s fellow workers. You be God’s farming, God’s building.
According to the grace of God which was given to me, as a wise master builder I laid a foundation, and another builds on it. But let each man be careful how he builds on it.
For Nobody can lay any other foundation than that which Don dey laid, which is Jesus Christ.
But if anyone builds on the foundation with gold, silver, costly stones, wood, hay, or stubble;
each man’s work Go be revealed. For the Day will declare it, because it is revealed in fire; and the fire itself will test what sort of work each man’s work is.
If any man’s work remains which he built on it, he will receive a reward.
If any man’s work is burned, he will suffer loss, but he imself Go be saved, but as through fire.
No you know that You be a temple of God, and that God’s Spirit lives in you?
If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for God’s temple is holy, which You be.
Let Nobody deceive imself. If anyone thinks that he is wise among you in this world, Make e become a fool, that he may become wise.
For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, “He has taken the wise in dem craftiness.”
And again, “The Lord knows the reasoning of the wise, that it is worthless.”
So let Nobody boast in men. For all things are yours,
whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come. All are yours,
and You be Christ’s, and Christ is God’s.
So let a man think of us as Christ’s workers, and stewards of God’s mysteries.
Here, moreover, it is required of stewards, that dem be find faithful.
But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged by you, or by man’s judgment. Yes, I no judge my own self.
For I know nothing against myself. Yet I be not justified by this, but person wey judges me is the Lord.
So judge nothing before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and reveal the counsels of the hearts. Then each man will get his praise from God.

Now these things, brothers, I have in a figure transferred to myself and Apollos for una sakes, that in us you might learn not to think beyond the things which are written, that none of you be puffed up against each other.
For who makes you different? And what do you have that you didn’t receive? But if you did receive it, why do you boast as if you had not received it?
You be already filled. You have already become rich. You have come to reign without us. Yes, and I wish that you did reign, that we also might reign with you.
For, I think that God has displayed us, the apostles, last of all, like men sentenced to death. For We be made a spectacle to the world, both to angels and men.
We be fools for Christ’s sake, but You be wise in Christ. We be weak, but You be strong. You have honor, but we have dishonor.
Even to this present hour we hunger, thirst, are naked, are beaten, and have no certain dwelling place.
We toil, working with our own hands. When people curse us, we bless. Being persecuted, we endure.
Being defamed, we entreat. We be made as the filth of the world, the dirt wiped off by all, even until now.
I no write these things to shame you, but to admonish you as my beloved pikin dem.
For though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, yet not many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, I became una father through the Better news.
I beg you so, be imitators of me.
Because of this I have sent Timothy to you, Wey be my beloved and faithful pikin in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways which are in Christ, even as I teach everywhere in every assembly.
Now some are puffed up, as though I No be coming to you.
But I go come to you shortly, if the Lord is willing. And I go know, not the word of people Wey puffed up, but the power.
For God’s Kingdom No be in word, but in power.
What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness?
It is actually reported that E get sexual immorality among you, and such sexual immorality as No be even named among the Gentiles, that one has his father’s wife.
You be puffed up, and didn’t rather mourn, that person wey had done this deed might be removed from among you.
For I most certainly, as being absent in body but present in spirit, have already, as though I were present, judged him who has done this thing.
In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, you being gathered together, and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,
are to deliver such a one to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.
Una boasting No be good. No you know that a little yeast leavens the whole lump?
Purge out the old yeast, that you may be a new lump, even as You be unleavened. For indeed Christ, our Passover, Don dey sacrificed in our place.
So Make we keep the feast, not with old yeast, neither with the yeast of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
I wrote to you in my letter to have no company with sexual sinners;
yet not at all meaning with the sexual sinners of this world, or with the covetous and extortionists, or with idolaters; for then you would have to leave the world.

But as it is, I wrote to you not to associate with anyone Wey be call a brother Wey be a sexual sinner, or covetous, or an idolater, or a slanderer, or a drunkard, or an extortionist. No even eat with such a person.
For what do I have to do with also judging people Wey outside? No you judge people Wey within?
But people Wey outside, God judges. “Put away the wicked man from among unaself.”
Dare any of you, having a matter against his neighbor, go to law before the unrighteous, and not before the saints?
No you know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?
No you know that We go judge angels? How much more, things that pertain to this life?
If then, you have to judge things pertaining to this life, do you set dem to judge Wey be of no account in the assembly?
I say this to move you to shame. No be there even one wise man among you who would be able to decide between his brothers?
But brother goes to law with brother, and that before unbelievers!
So it is already altogether a defect in you, that you have lawsuits one with another. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded?
No, but you unaself do wrong, and defraud, and that against una brothers.
Or no you know that the unrighteous No go inherit God’s Kingdom? No be deceived. Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor male prostitutes, nor homosexuals,
nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor slanderers, nor extortionists, will inherit God’s Kingdom.
Such were some of you, but you were washed. But you were sanctified. But you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and in the Spirit of our God.
“All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are expedient. “All things are lawful for me,” but I go not be bring under the power of anything.
“Foods for the belly, and the belly for foods,” but God will bring to nothing both it and dem. But the body No be for sexual immorality, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body.
Now God raised up the Lord, and will also raise us up by his power.
No you know that una bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ, and make dem members of a prostitute? May it never be!
Or no you know that person Wey joined to a prostitute is one body? For, “The two”, he says, “will become one flesh.”
But person Wey joined to the Lord is one spirit.
Flee sexual immorality! “Every sin that a man does is outside the body,” but person wey commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.
Or no you know that una body is a temple of the Holy Spirit Wey be in you, whom you have from God? You No be una own,
for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in una body and in una spirit, which are God’s.
Now concerning the things about which you wrote to me: it is good for a man not to touch a woman.
But, because of sexual immoralities, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.
Let the husband give his wife the affection owed her, and likewise also the wife her husband.
The wife no dey have authority over her own body, but the husband. Likewise also the husband no dey have authority over his own body, but the wife.

No deprive each other, unless it is by consent for a season, that you may give unaself to fasting and prayer, and may be together again, that Satan no dey tempt you because of una lack of self-control.
But this I say by way of concession, not of commandment.
Yet I wish that all men were like me. However each man has his own gift from God, one of this kind, and another of that kind.
But I say to the unmarried and to widows, it is good for dem if dem remain even as I be.
But if dem no have self-control, Make dem marry. For it’s better to marry than to burn.
But to the married I command — not I, but the Lord — that the wife not leave her husband
(but if she departs, Make she remain unmarried, or else be reconciled to her husband), and that the husband not leave his wife.
But to the rest I — not the Lord — say, if any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she is content to live with him, Make e not leave her.
The woman who has an unbelieving husband, and he is content to live with her, Make she not leave her husband.
For the unbelieving husband is sanctified in the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified in the husband. Otherwise una pikin dem would be unclean, but now Dem be holy.
Yet if the unbeliever departs, let there be separation. The brother or the sister No be under bondage in such cases, but God has call us in peace.
For how do you know, wife, whether You go save una husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether You go save una wife?
Only, as the Lord has distributed to each man, as God has call each, so Make e walk. So I command in all the assemblies.
Was anyone call having been circumcised? Make e not become uncircumcised. Has anyone been call in uncircumcision? Make e not be circumcised.
Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of the commandments of God.
Let each man stay in that calling in which he was call.
Were you call being a bondservant? No let that bother you, but if you get an opportunity to become free, use it.
For person wey was call in the Lord being a bondservant is the Lord’s free man. Likewise person wey was call being free is Christ’s bondservant.
You were bought with a price. No become bondservants of men.
Brothers, let each man, in Anything wey condition he was call, stay in that condition with God.
Now concerning virgins, I have no commandment from the Lord, but I give my judgment as one who has obtained mercy from the Lord to be trustworthy.
I think that it is good so, because of the distress that is on us, that it is good for a man to be as he is.
Are you bound to a wife? No seek to be freed. Are you free from a wife? No seek a wife.
But if you marry, you have not sinned. If a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet such Go get oppression in the flesh, and I want to spare you.
But I say this, brothers: the time is short, that from now on, both people wey have wives may be as though dem had none;
and people wey weep, as though dem didn’t weep; and people wey glad well-well, as though dem didn’t glad well-well; and people wey buy, as though dem didn’t possess;
and people wey use the world, as not using it to the fullest. For the mode of this world passes away.
But I desire to have you to be free from cares. Person Wey unmarried is concerned for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord;
but person Wey married is concerned about the things of the world, how he may please his wife.

E get also a difference between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman cares about the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But person Wey married cares about the things of the world — how she may please her husband.
This I say for una own profit; not that I may ensnare you, but for that which is appropriate, and that you may attend to the Lord without distraction.
But if any man thinks that he is behaving inappropriately toward his virgin, if she is past the flower of her age, and if need so requires, Make e do what he desires. He no dey sin. Make dem marry.
But person wey stands steadfast in his heart, having no urgency, but has power over his own will, and has determined in his own heart to keep his own virgin, does well.
So then both person wey gives his own virgin in marriage does well, and person wey no dey give her in marriage does better.
A wife is bound by law for as long as her husband lives; but if the husband is dead, she is free to be married to whomever she desires, only in the Lord.
But she is happier if she stays as she is, in my judgment, and I think that I also have God’s Spirit.
Now concerning things sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
But if anyone thinks that he knows anything, he no dey yet know as he ought to know.
But if anyone loves God, the same is known by him.
So concerning the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that no idol is anything in the world, and that E get no other God but one.
For though E get things that are call “gods”, whether in the heavens or on earth; as E get many “gods” and many “lords”;
yet to us E get one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we for him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we live through him.
However, that knowledge no be in all men. But some, with consciousness of the idol until now, eat as of a thing sacrificed to an idol, and dem conscience, being weak, is defiled.
But chop No go commend us to God. For neither, if we no eat, are we the worse; nor, if we eat, are we the better.
But be careful that by no means does this liberty of yours become a stumbling block to the weak.
For if a man sees you who have knowledge sitting in an idol’s temple, no go his conscience, if he is weak, be emboldened to eat things sacrificed to idols?
And through una knowledge, person Wey weak perishes, the brother for whose sake Christ died.
Thus, sinning against the brothers, and wounding dem conscience when it is weak, you sin against Christ.
So if chop causes my brother to stumble, I go eat no meat forever more, that I no cause my brother to stumble.
Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Haven’t I seen Jesus Christ, our Lord? No be you my work in the Lord?
If to others I be not an apostle, yet at least I be to you; for You be the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
My defense to people wey examine me is this.
Have we no right to eat and to drink?
Have we no right to take along a wife Wey be a believer, even as the rest of the apostles, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?
Or have only Barnabas and I no right to not work?
What soldier ever serves at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard, and no dey eat of its fruit? Or who feeds a flock, and no dey drink from the flock’s milk?
Do I speak these things according to the ways of men? Or no dey the law also say the same thing?
For it is written in the law of Moses, “You no go muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain.” Is it for the oxen that God cares,
or does he say it assuredly for our sake? Yes, it was written for our sake, because person wey plows ought to plow in hope, and person wey threshes in hope should partake of his hope.
If we sowed to you spiritual things, is it a great thing if we reap una fleshly things?
If others partake of this right over you, no we yet more? Nevertheless we No use this right, but we bear all things, that we may cause no hindrance to the Better news of Christ.
No you know that people wey serve around sacred things eat from the things of the temple, and people wey wait on the altar have dem portion with the altar?
Even so the Lord ordained that people wey proclaim the Better news should live from the Better news.
But I have used none of these things, and I no write these things that it may be done so in my case; for I would rather die, than that anyone should make my boasting void.
For if I preach the Better news, I have nothing to boast about; for necessity is laid on me; but woe is to me, if I no preach the Better news.
For if I do this of my own will, I have a reward. But if not of my own will, I have a stewardship entrusted to me.
What then is my reward? That, when I preach the Better news, I may present the Better news of Christ without charge, so as not to abuse my authority in the Better news.
For though I was free from all, I bring myself under bondage to all, that I might gain the more.
To the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain Jews; to people Wey under the law, as under the law, that I might gain people Wey under the law;
to people Wey without law, as without law (not being without law toward God, but under law toward Christ), that I might win people Wey without law.
To the weak I became as weak, that I might gain the weak. I have become all things to all men, that I may by all means save some.
Now I do this for the sake of the Better news, that I may be a joint partaker of it.
No you know that people wey run in a race all run, but one receives the prize? Run like that, that you may win.
Every man who strives in the games exercises self-control in all things. Now dem do it to receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible.
I so run like that, not aimlessly. I fight like that, not beating the air,
but I beat my body and bring it into submission, lest by any means, after I have preached to others, I myself should be rejected.
Now I would not have you ignorant, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;
and were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea;
and all ate the same spiritual chop;
and all drank the same spiritual drink. For dem drank of a spiritual rock that follow dem, and the rock was Christ.
However with most of dem, God No be well pleased, for dem were overthrown in the wilderness.
Now these things were our examples, to the intent we no suppose lust after evil things, as dem also lusted.
No be idolaters, as some of dem were. As it is written, “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.”
Make we not commit sexual immorality, as some of dem committed, and in one day twenty-three thousand fell.
Make we not test Christ, as some of dem tested, and perished by the serpents.
No grumble, as some of dem also grumbled, and perished by the destroyer.
Now all these things happened to dem by way of example, and dem were written for our admonition, on whom the ends of the ages have come.
So Make e who thinks he stands be careful that he no dey fall.

No temptation has taken you except Wetin be common to man. God is faithful, who No go allow you to be tempted above Wetin You be able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.
So, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
I speak as to wise men. Judge what I say.
The cup of blessing which we bless, no be it a sharing of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, no be it a sharing of the body of Christ?
Because E get one loaf of bread, we, Wey be many, are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf of bread.
Consider Israel according to the flesh. No people wey eat the sacrifices participate in the altar?
What am I saying then? That a thing sacrificed to idols is anything, or that an idol is anything?
But I say that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, dem sacrifice to demons, and not to God, and I no desire that you would have fellowship with demons.
You no fit both drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You no fit both partake of the table of the Lord, and of the table of demons.
Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?
“All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are profitable. “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things build up.
Let Nobody seek his own, but each one his neighbor’s good.
Anything wey is sold in the butcher shop, eat, asking no question for the sake of conscience,
for “the earth is the Lord’s, and its fullness.”
But if one of people wey no believe invites you to a meal, and You be inclined to go, eat Anything wey is set before you, asking no questions for the sake of conscience.
But if anyone says to you, “This was offered to idols,” no eat it for the sake of the one who told you, and for the sake of conscience. For “the earth is the Lord’s, and all its fullness.”
Conscience, I say, not una own, but the other’s conscience. For why is my liberty judged by another conscience?
If I partake with thankfulness, why am I denounced for that for which I Thank God?
Whether so you eat, or drink, or Anything wey you do, do all to the glory of God.
Give no occasion for stumbling, either to Jews, or to Greeks, or to the assembly of God;
even as I also please all men in all things, not seeking my own profit, but the profit of the many, that dem may be saved.
Be imitators of me, even as I also am of Christ.
Now I praise you, brothers, that you remember me in all things, and hold firm the traditions, even as I delivered dem to you.
But I would have you know that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.
Every man praying or prophesying, having his head covered, dishonors his head.
But every woman praying or prophesying with her head uncovered dishonors her head. For it is one and the same thing as if she were shaved.
For if a woman No be covered, Make she hair also be cut off. But if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut off or be shaved, Make she be covered.
For a man indeed ought not to have his head covered, because he is the image and glory of God, but the woman is the glory of the man.
For man No be from woman, but woman from man;
for man no be created for the woman, but woman for the man.
For this cause the woman ought to have authority over her own head, because of the angels.
Nevertheless, neither is the woman independent of the man, nor the man independent of the woman, in the Lord.
For as woman come from man, so a man also comes through a woman; but all things are from God.
Judge for unaself. Is it appropriate that a woman pray to God unveiled?
No dey even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a dishonor to him?
But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her, for her hair is given to her for a covering.
But if any man seems to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither do God’s assemblies.
But in giving you this command, I no praise you, that you come together not for the better but for the worse.
For first of all, when you come together in the assembly, I hear that divisions exist among you, and I partly believe it.
For there also must be factions among you, that people Wey approved may be revealed among you.
When so you assemble unaself together, it No be the Lord’s supper that you eat.
For in una eating each one takes his own supper first. One is hungry, and another is drunken.
What, no you have houses to eat and to drink in? Or do you despise God’s assembly, and put dem to shame who no have? What shall I tell una? Shall I praise you? In this I no praise you.
For I received from the Lord that which also I delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night in which he was betrayed take bread.
When he had given thanks, he broke it, and talk say, “Take, eat. This is my body, which is broken for you. Do this in memory of me.”
In the same way he also take the cup, after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in memory of me.”
For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.
So Anybody wey eats this bread or drinks the Lord’s cup in a way unworthy of the Lord Go be guilty of the body and the blood of the Lord.
But let a man examine imself, and so Make e eat of the bread, and drink of the cup.
For person wey eats and drinks in an unworthy way eats and drinks judgment to imself, if he no dey discern the Lord’s body.
For this cause many among You be weak and sickly, and not a few sleep.
For if we discerned ourselves, we wouldn’t be judged.
But when We be judged, We be punished by the Lord, that we may not be condemned with the world.
So, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for each other.
But if anyone is hungry, Make e eat at home, lest una coming together be for judgment. The rest I go set in order whenever I come.
Now concerning spiritual things, brothers, I no want you to be ignorant.
You know that when you were heathen, you were led away to those mute idols, however you might be led.
So I make known to you that no man speaking by God’s Spirit says, “Jesus is accursed.” Nobody can say, “Jesus is Lord,” but by the Holy Spirit.
Now E get various kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit.
E get various kinds of service, and the same Lord.
E get various kinds of workings, but the same God, who works all things in all.
But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the profit of all.
For to one is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom, and to another the word of knowledge, according to the same Spirit;
to another faith, by the same Spirit; and to another gifts of healings, by the same Spirit;
and to another workings of miracles; and to another prophecy; and to another discerning of spirits; to another different kinds of languages; and to another the interpretation of languages.
But the one and the same Spirit produces all of these, distributing to each one separately as he desires.
For as the body is one, and has many members, and all the members of the body, being many, are one body; so also is Christ.
For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether bond or free; and were all given to drink into one Spirit.
For the body No be one member, but many.
If the foot would say, “Because I’m not the hand, I’m not part of the body,” it No be so not part of the body.
If the ear would say, “Because I’m not the eye, I’m not part of the body,” it’s not so not part of the body.
If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the smelling be?
But now God has set the members, each one of dem, in the body, just as he desired.
If dem were all one member, where would the body be?
But now Dem be many members, but one body.
The eye no fit tell the hand, “I have no need for you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need for you.”
No, much rather, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.
Those parts of the body which we think to be less honorable, on those we bestow more abundant honor; and our unpresentable parts have more abundant propriety;
whereas our presentable parts have no such need. But God composed the body together, giving more abundant honor to the inferior part,
that there should be no division in the body, but that the members should have the same care for each other.
When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. Or when one member is honored, all the members glad well-well with it.
Now You be the body of Christ, and members individually.
God has set some in the assembly: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracle workers, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, and various kinds of languages.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all miracle workers?
Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak with various languages? Do all interpret?
But earnestly desire the best gifts. Moreover, I show a most excellent way to you.
If I speak with the languages of men and of angels, but no have love, I have become sounding brass, or a clanging cymbal.
If I have the gift of prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge; and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but no have love, I be nothing.
If I dole out all my goods to feed the poor, and if I give my body to be burned, but no have love, it profits me nothing.
Love dey patient and e kind; love no dey envy. Love no dey brag, No be proud,
no dey behave itself inappropriately, no dey seek its own way, No be provoked, takes no account of evil;
no dey glad well-well in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth;
bears all things, believe all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
Love never fails. But where E get prophecies, Dem go be done away with. Where E get various languages, Dem go cease. Where E get knowledge, it Go be done away with.
For we know in part, and we prophesy in part;
but when that which is complete has come, then that which is partial Go be done away with.
When I was a pikin, I spoke as a pikin, I felt as a pikin, I thought as a pikin. Now that I have become a man, I have put away childish things.
For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I go know fully, even as I was also fully known.
But now faith, hope, and love remain — these three. The greatest of these is love.
Follow after love, and earnestly desire spiritual gifts, but especially that you may prophesy.
For person wey speaks in another language speaks not to men, but to God; for Nobody understands; but in the Spirit he speaks mysteries.
But person wey prophesies speaks to men for dem edification, exhortation, and consolation.
Person wey speaks in another language edifies imself, but person wey prophesies edifies the assembly.

Now I desire to have you all speak with other languages, but rather that you would prophesy. For he is greater who prophesies than person wey speaks with other languages, unless he interprets, that the assembly may be built up.
But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking with other languages, what would I profit you, unless I speak to you either by way of revelation, or of knowledge, or of prophesying, or of teaching?
Even things without life, giving a voice, whether pipe or harp, if dem didn’t give a distinction in the sounds, how would it be known Wetin be piped or harped?
For if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who would prepare imself for war?
So also you, unless you uttered by the tongue words easy to understand, how would it be known Wetin be spoken? For you would be speaking into the air.
E get, it may be, so many kinds of sounds in the world, and none of dem is without meaning.
If then I no know the meaning of the sound, I would be to him who speaks a foreigner, and person wey speaks would be a foreigner to me.
So also you, since You be zealous for spiritual gifts, seek that you may abound to the building up of the assembly.
So Make e who speaks in another language pray that he may interpret.
For if I pray in another language, my spirit prays, but my understanding is unfruitful.
Wetin be it then? I go pray with the spirit, and I go pray with the understanding also. I go sing with the spirit, and I go sing with the understanding also.
Otherwise if you bless with the spirit, how will person wey fills the place of the unlearned say the “Amen” at una giving of thanks, seeing he no dey know Wetin you say?
For you most certainly Thank God well, but the other person No be built up.
I thank my God, I speak with other languages more than you all.
However in the assembly I would rather speak five words with my understanding, that I might instruct others also, than ten thousand words in another language.
Brothers, no be pikin dem in thoughts, yet in malice be babies, but in thoughts be mature.
In the law it is written, “By men of strange languages and by the lips of strangers I go speak to this people. Not even thus will dem hear me, says the Lord.”
So other languages are for a sign, not to people wey believe, but to the unbelieving; but prophesying is for a sign, not to the unbelieving, but to people wey believe.
If so the whole assembly is assembled together and all speak with other languages, and unlearned or unbelieving people come in, no go dem say that You be crazy?
But if all prophesy, and someone unbelieving or unlearned comes in, he is reproved by all, and he is judged by all.
And thus the secrets of his heart are revealed. So he will fall down on his face and worship God, declaring that God is among you indeed.

Wetin be it then, brothers? When you come together, each one of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has another language, has an interpretation. Let all things be done to build each other up.
If any man speaks in another language, let it be two, or at the most three, and in turn; and let one interpret.
But if E get no interpreter, Make e keep silent in the assembly, and Make e speak to imself, and to God.
Let the prophets speak, two or three, and let the others discern.
But if a revelation is made to another sitting by, let the first keep silent.
For you all can prophesy one by one, that all may learn, and all may be exhorted.
The spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets,
for God No be a God of confusion, but of peace, as in all the assemblies of the saints.
Let the women be quiet in the assemblies, for it has not been permitted for dem to be talking except in submission, as the law also says,
if dem desire to learn anything. “Make dem ask dem own husbands at home, for it is shameful for a woman to be talking in the assembly.”
What!? Was it from you that the word of God go out? Or did it come to you alone?
If any man thinks imself to be a prophet, or spiritual, Make e recognize the things which I write to you, that Dem be the commandment of the Lord.
But if anyone is ignorant, Make e be ignorant.
So, brothers, desire earnestly to prophesy, and no forbid speaking with other languages.
Let all things be done decently and in order.
Now I declare to you, brothers, the Better news which I preached to you, which also you received, in which you also stand,
by which also You be saved, if you hold firmly the word which I preached to you — unless you believe in vain.
For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.
Then he appeared to over five hundred brothers at once, most of whom remain until now, but some have also fallen asleep.
Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles,
and last of all, as to the pikin born at the wrong time, he appeared to me also.
For I be the least of the apostles, Wey be not worthy to be call an apostle, because I persecuted the assembly of God.
But by the grace of God I be what I be. His grace which was given to me No be futile, but I worked more than all of dem; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.
Whether then it is I or dem, so we preach, and so you believe.
Now if Christ is preached, that he Don dey raised from the dead, how do some among you say that E get no resurrection of the dead?
But if E get no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ been raised.
If Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is in vain, and una faith also is in vain.
Yes, We be also find false witnesses of God, because we testified about God that he raised up Christ, whom he didn’t raise up, if it is so that the dead No be raised.
For if the dead no be raised, neither has Christ been raised.
If Christ has not been raised, una faith is vain; You be still in una sins.
Then dem also Wey be fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
If we have only hoped in Christ in this life, We be of all men most pitiable.
But now Christ Don dey raised from the dead. He became the first fruits of people Wey asleep.
For since death come by man, the resurrection of the dead also come by man.
For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all Go be made alive.
But each in his own order: Christ the first fruits, then people Wey Christ’s, at his coming.
Then the end comes, when he will deliver up the Kingdom to God, even the Father; when he Go get abolished all rule and all authority and power.
For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.
The last enemy that Go be abolished is death.
For, “He put all things in subjection under his feet.” But when he says, “All things are put in subjection”, it is evident that he is excepted who subjected all things to him.
When all things Don dey subjected to him, then the Son will also imself be subjected to him who subjected all things to him, that God may be all in all.
Or else what will dem do Wey be baptized for the dead? If the dead no be raised at all, why then are dem baptized for the dead?
Why do we also stand in jeopardy every hour?
I affirm, by the boasting in you which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.
If I fought with animals at Ephesus for human purposes, what does it profit me? If the dead No be raised, then “Make we eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
No be deceived! “Evil companionships corrupt good morals.”
Wake up righteously, and no sin, for some have no knowledge of God. I say this to una shame.
But someone will say, “How are the dead raised?” and, “With what kind of body do dem come?”
You foolish one, that which you yourself sow No be made alive unless it dies.
That which you sow, you no sow the body that Go be, but a bare grain, maybe of wheat, or of some other kind.
But God gives it a body even as it pleased him, and to each seed a body of its own.
All flesh No be the same flesh, but E get one flesh of men, another flesh of animals, another of fish, and another of birds.
E get also celestial bodies, and terrestrial bodies; but the glory of the celestial differs from that of the terrestrial.
E get one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differs from another star in glory.
So also is the resurrection of the dead. The body is sown perishable; it is raised imperishable.
It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. E get a natural body and E get also a spiritual body.
So also it is written, “The first man, Adam, became a living soul.” The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
However that which is spiritual no be first, but that which is natural, then that which is spiritual.
The first man is of the earth, made of dust. The second man is the Lord from heaven.
As is the one made of dust, such are people Wey also made of dust; and as is the heavenly, such are dem also that are heavenly.
As we have borne the image of those made of dust, let’s also bear the image of the heavenly.
Now I say this, brothers, that flesh and blood no fit inherit God’s Kingdom; neither does the perishable inherit imperishable.
See am, I tell una a mystery. We go not all sleep, but We go all be changed,
in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead Go be raised incorruptible, and We go be changed.
For this perishable body must become imperishable, and this mortal must put on immortality.
But when this perishable body Go get become imperishable, and this mortal Go get put on immortality, then Wetin be written will happen: “Death is swallowed up in victory.”
“Death, where is una sting? Hades, where is una victory?”
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God, wey dey give us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
So, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, because you know that una labor No be in vain in the Lord.
Now concerning the collection for the saints, as I commanded the assemblies of Galatia, you do likewise.
On the first day of the week, let each one of you save, as he may prosper, that no collections be made when I come.
When I arrive, I go send Anybody wey you approve with letters to carry una gracious gift to Jerusalem.
