If it is appropriate for me to go also, Dem go go with me.
But I go come to you when I have passed through Macedonia, for I be passing through Macedonia.
But with you it may be that I go stay, or even winter, that you may send me on my journey Anywhere wey I go.
For I No wish to see you now in passing, but I hope to stay a while with you, if the Lord permits.
But I go stay at Ephesus until Pentecost,
for a great and effective door has opened to me, and E get many adversaries.
Now if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without fear, for he does the work of the Lord, as I also do.
So let Nobody despise him. But set him forward on his journey in peace, that he may come to me; for I expect him with the brothers.
Now concerning Apollos, the brother, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers; and it No be at all his desire to come now; but he will come when he has an opportunity.
Watch! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong!
Let all that you do be done in love.
Now I beg you, brothers (you know the house of Stephanas, that it is the first fruits of Achaia, and that dem have set themselves to serve the saints),
that you also be in subjection to such, and to Everybody wey helps in the work and labors.
I glad well-well at the coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus; for that which was lacking on una part, dem supplied.
For dem refreshed my spirit and yours. So acknowledge people Wey like that.
The assemblies of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla greet you much in the Lord, together with the assembly that is in dem house.
All the brothers greet you. Greet each other with a holy kiss.
This greeting is by me, Paul, with my own hand.
If any man no dey love the Lord Jesus Christ, Make e be accursed. Come, Lord!
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
My love to all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother, to the assembly of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints Wey be in the whole of Achaia:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort;
who comforts us in all our suffering, that we may be able to comfort people Wey in any suffering, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
For as the sufferings of Christ abound to us, even so our comfort also abounds through Christ.
But if We be afflicted, it is for una comfort and salvation. If We be comforted, it is for una comfort, which produces in you the patient enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer.
Our hope for you is steadfast, knowing that, since You be partakers of the sufferings, so also are you of the comfort.

For we no desire to have you uninformed, brothers, concerning our suffering which happened to us in Asia, that we were weighed down exceedingly, beyond our power, so much that we despaired even of life.
Yes, we ourselves have had the sentence of death within ourselves, that we no suppose trust in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead,
who delivered us out of so great a death, and does deliver; on whom we have set our hope that he will also still deliver us;
you also helping together on our behalf by una supplication; that, for the gift given to us by means of many, thanks may be given by many persons on una behalf.

For our boasting is this: the testimony of our conscience, that in holiness and sincerity of God, not in fleshly wisdom but in the grace of God we behaved ourselves in the world, and more abundantly toward you.
For we write no other things to you, than Wetin you read or even acknowledge, and I hope You go acknowledge to the end;
as also you acknowledged us in part, that We be una boasting, even as you also are ours, in the day of our Lord Jesus.
In this confidence, I was determined to come first to you, that you might have a second benefit;
and by you to pass into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come to you, and to be sent forward by you on my journey to Judea.
When I so was thus determined, did I show fickleness? Or the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, that with me there should be the “Yes, yes” and the “No, no?”
But as God is faithful, our word toward you No be “Yes and no.”
For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, by me, Silvanus, and Timothy, No be “Yes and no,” but in him is “Yes.”
For however many are the promises of God, in him is the “Yes.” So also through him is the “Amen”, to the glory of God through us.
Now person wey establishes us with you in Christ, and anointed us, is God;
who also sealed us, and give us the down payment of the Spirit in our hearts.
But I call God for a witness to my soul, that I didn’t come to Corinth to spare you.
Not that we control una faith, but are fellow workers with you for una gladness. For you stand firm in faith.
But I determined this for myself, that I would not come to you again in sorrow.
For if I make you sorry, then who will make me glad but person Wey made sorry by me?

And I wrote this very thing to you, so that, when I come, I wouldn’t have sorrow from dem of whom I ought to glad well-well; having confidence in you all, that my gladness would be shared by all of you.
For out of much suffering and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears, not that you should be made sorry, but that you might know the love that I have so abundantly for you.
But if any has caused sorrow, he has caused sorrow, not to me, but in part (that I not press too heavily) to you all.
This punishment which was inflicted by the many is sufficient for such a one;
so that on the contrary you should rather forgive him and comfort him, lest by any means such a one should be swallowed up with his excessive sorrow.
So I beg you to confirm una love toward him.
For to this end I also wrote, that I might know the proof of you, whether You be obedient in all things.
Now I also forgive whomever you forgive anything. For if indeed I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven that one for una sakes in the presence of Christ,
that no advantage may be gained over us by Satan; for we No be ignorant of his schemes.
Now when I come to Troas for the Better news of Christ, and when a door was opened to me in the Lord,
I had no relief for my spirit, because I didn’t find Titus, my brother, but taking my leave of dem, I go out into Macedonia.
Now thanks be to God, who always leads us in triumph in Christ, and reveals through us the sweet aroma of his knowledge in every place.
For We be a sweet aroma of Christ to God, in people Wey saved, and in people wey perish;
to the one a stench from death to death; to the other a sweet aroma from life to life. Wey be sufficient for these things?
For We be No be like so many, peddling the word of God. But as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God, we speak in Christ.
Are we beginning again to commend ourselves? Or do we need, as do some, letters of commendation to you or from you?
You be our letter, written in our hearts, known and read by all men;
being revealed that You be a letter of Christ, served by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tablets of stone, but in tablets that are hearts of flesh.
Such confidence we have through Christ toward God;
not that We be sufficient of ourselves, to account anything as from ourselves; but our sufficiency is from God;
who also made us sufficient as workers of a new covenant; not of the letter, but of the Spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

But if the service of death, written engraved on stones, come with glory, so that the pikin dem of Israel could not look steadfastly on the face of Moses for the glory of his face; which was passing away:
no go service of the Spirit be with much more glory?
For if the service of condemnation has glory, the service of righteousness exceeds much more in glory.
For most certainly that which Don dey made glorious has not been made glorious in this respect, by reason of the glory that surpasses.
For if that which passes away was with glory, much more that which remains is in glory.
Having so such a hope, we use great boldness of speech,
and No be like Moses, who put a veil on his face, that the pikin dem of Israel wouldn’t look steadfastly on the end of that which was passing away.
But dem minds were hardened, for until this very day at the reading of the old covenant the same veil remains, because in Christ it passes away.
But to this day, when Moses is read, a veil lies on dem heart.
But whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
Now the Lord is the Spirit and where the Spirit of the Lord is, E get liberty.
But we all, with unveiled face seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord, the Spirit.
So seeing we have this ministry, even as we obtained mercy, we no faint.

But we have renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by the manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.
Even if our Better news is veiled, it is veiled in people wey perish;
in whom the god of this world has blinded the minds of the unbelieving, that the light of the Better news of the glory of Christ, Wey be the image of God, no suppose dawn on dem.
For we no preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as una workers for Jesus’ sake;
seeing it is God who talk say, “Light will shine out of darkness,” who has shone in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
But we have this treasure in clay vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God, and not from ourselves.
We be pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair;
pursued, yet not forsaken; struck down, yet not destroyed;
always carrying in the body the putting to death of the Lord Jesus, that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
For we who live are always delivered to death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus may be revealed in our mortal flesh.
So then death works in us, but life in you.
But having the same spirit of faith, according to that which is written, “I believe, and so I spoke.” We also believe, and so also we speak;
knowing that person wey raised the Lord Jesus will raise us also with Jesus, and will present us with you.
For all things are for una sakes, that the grace, being multiplied through the many, may cause the thanksgiving to abound to the glory of God.
So we no faint, but though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day.
For our light suffering, which is for the moment, works for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory;
while we no look at the things which are seen, but at the things which No be seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which No be seen are eternal.
For we know that if the earthly house of our tent is dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal, in the heavens.
For most certainly in this we groan, longing to be clothed with our habitation which is from heaven;
if so be that being clothed We go not be find naked.
For indeed we Wey be in this tent do groan, being burdened; not that we desire to be unclothed, but that we desire to be clothed, that Wetin be mortal may be swallowed up by life.
Now person wey made us for this very thing is God, who also give to us the down payment of the Spirit.
So We be always confident and know that while We be at home in the body, We be absent from the Lord;
for we walk by faith, not by sight.
We be courageous, I say, and are willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be at home with the Lord.
So also we make it our aim, whether at home or absent, to be well pleasing to him.
For we must all be revealed before the judgment seat of Christ; that each one may receive the things in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad.
Knowing so the fear of the Lord, we persuade men, but We be revealed to God; and I hope that We be revealed also in una consciences.
For we No be commending ourselves to you again, but speak as giving you occasion of boasting on our behalf, that you may have something to answer people wey boast in appearance, and not in heart.
For if We be beside ourselves, it is for God. Or if We be of sober mind, it is for you.
For the love of Christ constrains us; because we judge thus, that one died for all, so all died.
He died for all, that people wey live should no longer live to themselves, but to him who for dem sakes died and rose again.
So we know Nobody after the flesh from now on. Even though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now we know him so no more.
So if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. See am, all things have become new.
But all things are of God, who reconciled us to imself through Jesus Christ, and give to us the ministry of reconciliation;
namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to imself, not reckoning to dem dem trespasses, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.
We be so ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us: we beg you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.
For him who know no sin he made to be sin on our behalf; so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.
Working together, we entreat also that you not receive the grace of God in vain,
for he says, “At an acceptable time I listened to you, in a day of salvation I helped you.” See am, now is the acceptable time. See am, now is the day of salvation.
We give no occasion of stumbling in anything, that our service may not be blamed,
but in everything commending ourselves, as workers of God, in great endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in distresses,
in beatings, in imprisonments, in riots, in labors, in watchings, in fastings;
in pureness, in knowledge, in perseverance, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in sincere love,
in the word of truth, in the power of God; by the armor of righteousness on the right hand and on the left,
by glory and dishonor, by evil report and good report; as deceivers, and yet true;
as unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and see am, we live; as punished, and not killed;
as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things.
Our mouth is open to you, Corinthians. Our heart is enlarged.
You No be restricted by us, but You be restricted by una own affections.
Now in return, I speak as to my pikin dem, you also be open wide.
No be unequally yoked with unbelievers, for what fellowship have righteousness and wickedness? Or what fellowship has light with darkness?
What agreement has Christ with Belial? Or what portion has a believer with an unbeliever?
What agreement has a temple of God with idols? For You be a temple of the living God. Even as God talk say, “I go live in dem, and walk in dem; and I go be dem God, and Dem go be my people.”
So “‘Come out from among dem, and be separate,’ says the Lord. ‘Touch no unclean thing. I go receive you.
I go be to you a Father. You go be to me sons and daughters,’ says the Lord Almighty.”
Having so these promises, beloved, Make we cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
Open una hearts to us. We wronged Nobody. We corrupted Nobody. We take advantage of Nobody.
I say this not to condemn you, for I have talk say before, that You be in our hearts to die together and live together.
Great is my boldness of speech toward you. Great is my boasting on una behalf. I be filled with comfort. I overflow with gladness in all our suffering.
For even when we had come into Macedonia, our flesh had no relief, but we were afflicted on every side. Fightings were outside. Fear was inside.
Nevertheless, person wey comforts the lowly, God, comforted us by the coming of Titus;
and not by his coming only, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted in you, while he told us of una longing, una mourning, and una zeal for me; so that I rejoiced still more.
For though I made you sorry with my letter, I No regret it, though I did regret it. For I see that my letter made you sorry, though just for a while.
I now glad well-well, not that you were made sorry, but that you were made sorry to repentance. For you were made sorry in a godly way, that you might suffer loss by us in nothing.
For godly sorrow produces repentance to salvation, which brings no regret. But the sorrow of the world produces death.

For see am, this same thing, that you were made sorry in a godly way, what earnest care it worked in you. Yes, what defense, indignation, fear, longing, zeal, and vengeance! In everything you demonstrated unaself to be pure in the matter.
So although I wrote to you, I wrote not for his cause that did the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered the wrong, but that una earnest care for us might be revealed in you in the sight of God.
So we Don dey comforted. In our comfort we rejoiced the more exceedingly for the gladness of Titus, because his spirit Don dey refreshed by you all.
For if in anything I have boasted to him on una behalf, I No be disappointed. But as we spoke all things to you in truth, so our glorying also which I made before Titus was find to be truth.
His affection is more abundantly toward you, while he remembers all of una obedience, how with fear and trembling you received him.
I glad well-well that in everything I be confident concerning you.
Moreover, brothers, we make known to you the grace of God which Don dey given in the assemblies of Macedonia;
how that in much proof of suffering the abundance of dem gladness and dem deep poverty abounded to the riches of dem liberality.
For according to dem power, I testify, yes and beyond dem power, dem give of dem own accord,
begging us with much entreaty to receive this grace and the fellowship in the service to the saints.
This was No be like we had hoped, but first dem give dem own selves to the Lord, and to us through the will of God.
So we urged Titus, that as he had made a beginning before, so he would also complete in you this grace.
But as you abound in everything, in faith, utterance, knowledge, all earnestness, and in una love to us, see that you also abound in this grace.
I speak not by way of commandment, but as proving through the earnestness of others the sincerity also of una love.
For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for una sakes he became poor, that you through his poverty might become rich.
I give a judgment in this: for this is expedient for you, who were the first to start a year ago, not only to do, but also to be willing.
But now complete the doing also, that as there was the readiness to be willing, so there may be the completion also out of una ability.
For if the readiness is there, it is acceptable according to Wetin you have, not according to Wetin you no have.
For this No be that others may be eased and you distressed,
but for equality. Una abundance at this present time supplies dem lack, that dem abundance also may become a supply for una lack; that there may be equality.
As it is written, “Person wey gathered much had nothing left over, and person wey gathered little had no lack.”
But thanks be to God, who puts the same earnest care for you into the heart of Titus.
For he indeed accepted our exhortation, but being imself very earnest, he go out to you of his own accord.
We have sent together with him the brother whose praise in the Better news is known through all the assemblies.
Not only so, but who was also appointed by the assemblies to travel with us in this grace, which is served by us to the glory of the Lord imself, and to show our readiness.
We be avoiding this, that any man should blame us concerning this abundance which is administered by us.
Having regard for honorable things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.
We have sent with dem our brother, whom we have many times proved earnest in many things, but now much more earnest, by reason of the great confidence which he has in you.
As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker for you. As for our brothers, Dem be the apostles of the assemblies, the glory of Christ.
So show the proof of una love to dem in front of the assemblies, and of our boasting on una behalf.
It is indeed unnecessary for me to write to you concerning the service to the saints,
for I know una readiness, of which I boast on una behalf to dem of Macedonia, that Achaia Don dey prepared for a year past. Una zeal has stirred up very many of dem.
But I have sent the brothers that our boasting on una behalf may not be in vain in this respect, that, just as I talk say, you may be prepared,
so that I no go by any means, if anyone from Macedonia comes there with me and finds you unprepared, we (to say nothing of you) should be disappointed in this confident boasting.

I thought it necessary so to entreat the brothers that dem would go before to you, and arrange ahead of time the generous gift that you promised before, that the same might be ready as a matter of generosity, and not of greediness.
Remember this: person wey sows sparingly will also reap sparingly. Person wey sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.
Let each man give according as he has determined in his heart; not grudgingly, or under compulsion; for God loves a cheerful giver.
And God is able to make all grace abound to you, that you, always having all sufficiency in everything, may abound to every good work.
As it is written, “He has scattered abroad, he has given to the poor. His righteousness remains forever.”
Now may person wey supplies seed to the sower and bread for chop, supply and multiply una seed for sowing, and increase the fruits of una righteousness;
you being enriched in everything to all liberality, which produces through us thanksgiving to God.
For this service of giving that you perform not only makes up for lack among the saints, but abounds also through many givings of thanks to God;
seeing that through the proof given by this service, dem glorify God for the obedience of una confession to the Better news of Christ, and for the liberality of una contribution to dem and to all;
while dem themselves also, with supplication on una behalf, yearn for you by reason of the exceeding grace of God in you.
Now thanks be to God for his unspeakable gift!
Now I Paul, myself, entreat you by the humility and gentleness of Christ; I who in una presence am lowly among you, but being absent am bold toward you.
Yes, I beg you that I may not, when present, show courage with the confidence with which I intend to be bold against some, who consider us to be walking according to the flesh.
For though we walk in the flesh, we no wage war according to the flesh;
for the weapons of our warfare No be of the flesh, but mighty before God to the throwing down of strongholds,
throwing down imaginations and every high thing that is exalted against the knowledge of God, and bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ;
and being in readiness to avenge all disobedience, when una obedience Go be made full.

Do you look at things only as dem appear in front of una face? If anyone trusts in imself that he is Christ’s, Make e consider this again with imself, that, even as he is Christ’s, so also We be Christ’s.
For though I should boast somewhat abundantly concerning our authority, (which the Lord give for building you up, and not for casting you down) I go not be disappointed,
that I may not seem as if I desire to terrify you by my letters.
For, “His letters”, dem say, “are weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech is despised.”
Let such a person consider this, that what We be in word by letters when We be absent, such are we also in deed when We be present.

For we No be bold to number or compare ourselves with some of people wey commend themselves. But dem themselves, measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves with themselves, are without understanding.
But We go not boast beyond proper limits, but within the boundaries with which God appointed to us, which reach even to you.
For we no stretch ourselves too much, as though we didn’t reach to you. For we come even as far as to you with the Better news of Christ,
not boasting beyond proper limits in other men’s labors, but having hope that as una faith grows, We go be abundantly enlarged by you in our sphere of influence,
so as to preach the Better news even to the parts beyond you, not to boast in what someone else has already done.
But “person wey boasts, Make e boast in the Lord.”
For it no be person wey commends imself Wey be approved, but whom the Lord commends.
I wish that you would bear with me in a little foolishness, but indeed you do bear with me.
For I be jealous over you with a godly jealousy. For I married you to one husband, that I might present you as a pure virgin to Christ.
But I be afraid that somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve in his craftiness, so una minds might be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.

For if person wey comes preaches another Jesus, whom we No preach, or if you receive a different spirit, which you No receive, or a different “better news”, which you No accept, you put up with that well enough.
For I reckon that I be not at all behind the very best apostles.
But though I be unskilled in speech, yet I be not unskilled in knowledge. No, in every way we Don dey revealed to you in all things.
Or did I commit a sin in humbling myself that you might be exalted, because I preached to you God’s Better news free of charge?
I robbed other assemblies, taking wages from dem that I might serve you.

When I was present with you and was in need, I no be a burden on anyone, for the brothers, when dem come from Macedonia, supplied the measure of my need. In everything I kept myself from being burdensome to you, and I go continue to do so.
As the truth of Christ is in me, Nobody will stop me from this boasting in the regions of Achaia.
Why? Because I no love you? God knows.
But what I do, that I go do, that I may cut off occasion from dem that desire an occasion, that in which dem boast, dem may be find even as we.
For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as Christ’s apostles.
And no wonder, for even Satan masquerades as an angel of light.
It is no great thing so if his workers also masquerade as workers of righteousness, whose end Go be according to dem works.
I say again, let Nobody think me foolish. But if so, yet receive me as foolish, that I also may boast a little.
That which I speak, I no speak according to the Lord, but as in foolishness, in this confidence of boasting.
Seeing that many boast after the flesh, I go also boast.
For you bear with the foolish gladly, being wise.
For you bear with a man, if he brings you into bondage, if he devours you, if he takes you captive, if he exalts imself, if he strikes you on the face.
I speak by way of disparagement, as though we Bin dey weak. Yet in Anything wey way anyone is bold (I speak in foolishness), I be bold also.
Are dem Hebrews? So am I. Are dem Israelites? So am I. Are dem the offspring of Abraham? So am I.
Are dem workers of Christ? (I speak as one beside imself) I be more so; in labors more abundantly, in prisons more abundantly, in stripes above measure, in deaths often.
Five times from the Jews I received forty stripes minus one.
Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I suffered shipwreck. I Don dey a night and a day in the deep.

I Don dey in travels often, perils of rivers, perils of robbers, perils from my countrymen, perils from the Gentiles, perils in the city, perils in the wilderness, perils in the sea, perils among false brothers;
in labor and travail, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, and in cold and nakedness.
Besides those things that are outside, E get that which presses on me daily, anxiety for all the assemblies.
Wey be weak, and I be not weak? Wey be caused to stumble, and I no burn with indignation?
If I must boast, I go boast of the things that concern my weakness.
The God and Father of the Lord Jesus Christ, person Wey blessed forever more, knows that I no lie.
In Damascus the governor under King Aretas guarded the city of the Damascenes desiring to arrest me.
Through a window I was let down in a basket by the wall, and escaped his hands.
It is doubtless not profitable for me to boast. For I go come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
I know a man in Christ, fourteen years ago (whether in the body, I no know, or whether out of the body, I no know; God knows), such a one caught up into the third heaven.
I know such a man (whether in the body, or outside of the body, I no know; God knows),
how he was caught up into Paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it No be lawful for a man to utter.
On behalf of such a one I go boast, but on my own behalf I go not boast, except in my weaknesses.
For if I would desire to boast, I go not be foolish; for I go speak the truth. But I refrain, so that no man may think more of me than that which he sees in me, or hears from me.

By reason of the exceeding greatness of the revelations, that I no suppose be exalted excessively, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to torment me, that I no suppose be exalted excessively.
Concerning this thing, I begged the Lord three times that it might depart from me.
He has talk say to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly so I go rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.
So I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses, for Christ’s sake. For when I be weak, then am I strong.
I have become foolish in boasting. You compelled me, for I ought to Don dey commended by you, for in nothing was I inferior to the very best apostles, though I be nothing.
Truly the signs of an apostle were worked among you in all perseverance, in signs and wonders and mighty works.
For Wetin be there in which you were made inferior to the rest of the assemblies, unless it is that I myself No be a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong.

See am, this is the third time I be ready to come to you, and I go not be a burden to you; for I seek not una possessions, but you. For the pikin dem ought not to save up for the parents, but the parents for the pikin dem.
I go most gladly spend and be spent for una souls. If I love you more abundantly, am I love the less?
But be it so, I No myself burden you. But, being crafty, I caught you with deception.
Did I take advantage of you by anyone of dem whom I have sent to you?
I exhorted Titus, and I sent the brother with him. Did Titus take any advantage of you? Didn’t we walk in the same spirit? Didn’t we walk in the same steps?
Again, do you think that We be excusing ourselves to you? In the sight of God we speak in Christ. But all things, beloved, are for una edifying.

For I be afraid that by any means, when I come, I might find you not the way I want to, and that I might be find by you as you no desire; that by any means there would be strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, factions, slander, whisperings, proud thoughts, riots;

that again when I come my God would humble me before you, and I would mourn for many of people wey have sinned before now, and not repented of the uncleanness and sexual immorality and lustfulness which dem committed.
This is the third time I be coming to you. “At the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established.”

I have talk say beforehand, and I do say beforehand, as when I was present the second time, so now, being absent, I write to people wey have sinned before now, and to all the rest, that, if I come again, I go not spare;
seeing that you seek a proof of Christ who speaks in me; who toward you No be weak, but is powerful in you.
For he was crucified through weakness, yet he lives through the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but We go live with him through the power of God toward you.
Examine una own selves, whether You be in the faith. Test una own selves. Or no you know as to una own selves, that Jesus Christ is in you? — unless indeed You be disqualified.
But I hope that You go know that we no be disqualified.
Now I pray to God that you do no evil; not that we may appear approved, but that you may do that which is honorable, though We be as reprobate.
For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.
For we glad well-well when We be weak and You be strong. And this we also pray for, even una perfecting.
For this cause I write these things while absent, that I may not deal sharply when present, according to the authority which the Lord give me for building up, and not for tearing down.
Finally, brothers, glad well-well. Be perfected, be comforted, be of the same mind, live in peace, and the God of love and peace Go be with you.
Greet each other with a holy kiss.
All the saints greet you.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, God’s love, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit, be with you all. Amen.
Paul, an apostle (not from men, nor through man, but through Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead),
and all the brothers Wey be with me, to the assemblies of Galatia:
Grace to you and peace from God the Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ,
who give imself for our sins, that he might deliver us out of this present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father —
to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
I marvel that You be so sharp-sharp deserting him who call you in the grace of Christ to a different “better news”;
and there no be another “better news.” Only E get some who trouble you, and want to pervert the Better news of Christ.
But even though we, or an angel from heaven, should preach to you any “better news” other than that which we preached to you, Make e be cursed.
As we have talk say before, so I now say again: if any man preaches to you any “better news” other than that which you received, Make e be cursed.
For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? For if I were still pleasing men, I wouldn’t be a worker of Christ.
But I make known to you, brothers, concerning the Better news which was preached by me, that it No be according to man.
For neither did I receive it from man, nor was I taught it, but it come to me through revelation of Jesus Christ.
For you have heard of my way of living in time past in the Jews’ religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the assembly of God, and ravaged it.
I advanced in the Jews’ religion beyond many of my own age among my countrymen, being more exceedingly zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
But when it was the good pleasure of God, who separated me from my mother’s womb, and call me through his grace,
to reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the Gentiles, I didn’t sharp-sharp confer with flesh and blood,
nor did I go up to Jerusalem to people wey were apostles before me, but I go away into Arabia. Then I come back to Damascus.
Then after three years I go up to Jerusalem to visit Peter, and stayed with him fifteen days.
But of the other apostles I see Nobody, except James, the Lord’s brother.
Now about the things which I write to you, see am, before God, I’m not lying.
Then I come to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
I was still unknown by face to the assemblies of Judea which were in Christ,
but dem only heard: “Person wey once persecuted us now preaches the faith that he once tried to destroy.”
And dem glorified God in me.
Then after a period of fourteen years I go up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus also with me.
I go up by revelation, and I laid before dem the Better news which I preach among the Gentiles, but privately before people wey were respected, for fear that I might be running, or had run, in vain.
But not even Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised.
This was because of the false brothers secretly bring in, who stole in to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that dem might bring us into bondage;
to whom we give no place in the way of subjection, not for an hour, that the truth of the Better news might continue with you.
But from people wey were reputed to be important (Anything wey dem were, it makes no difference to me; God no dey show partiality to man) — dem, I say, who were respected imparted nothing to me,
but to the contrary, when dem see that I Bin dey entrusted with the Better news for the uncircumcision, even as Peter with the Better news for the circumcision
(for person wey appointed Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision appointed me also to the Gentiles);

and when dem perceived the grace that was given to me, James and Cephas and John, dem who were reputed to be pillars, give to me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, that we should go to the Gentiles, and dem to the circumcision.
Dem only ask us to remember the poor — which very thing I was also zealous to do.
But when Peter come to Antioch, I resisted him to his face, because he stood condemned.
For before some people come from James, he ate with the Gentiles. But when dem come, he drew back and separated imself, fearing people wey were of the circumcision.
And the rest of the Jews joined him in his hypocrisy; so that even Barnabas was carried away with dem hypocrisy.

But when I see that dem didn’t walk uprightly according to the truth of the Better news, I talk say to Peter before dem all, “If you, being a Jew, live as the Gentiles do, and No be like the Jews do, why do you compel the Gentiles to live as the Jews do?
“We, being Jews by nature, and not Gentile sinners,

yet knowing that a man No be justified by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ, even we believe in Christ Jesus, that we might be justified by faith in Christ, and not by the works of the law, because no flesh Go be justified by the works of the law.
But if, while we sought to be justified in Christ, we ourselves also were find sinners, is Christ a worker of sin? Certainly not!
For if I build up again those things which I destroyed, I prove myself a law-breaker.
For I, through the law, died to the law, that I might live to God.

I Don dey crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I that live, but Christ lives in me. That life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who love me, and give imself up for me.
I no reject the grace of God. For if righteousness is through the law, then Christ died for nothing!”
Foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you not to obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was openly portrayed among you as crucified?
I just want to learn this from you: Did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law, or by hearing of faith?
Are you so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are you now completed in the flesh?
Did you suffer so many things in vain, if it is indeed in vain?
He so who supplies the Spirit to you, and does miracles among you, does he do it by the works of the law, or by hearing of faith?
Even as Abraham “believe God, and it was counted to him for righteousness.”
Know so that people Wey of faith, the same are pikin dem of Abraham.
The Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, preached the Better news beforehand to Abraham, saying, “In you all the nations Go be blessed.”
So then, people Wey of faith are blessed with the faithful Abraham.
For as many as are of the works of the law are under a curse. For it is written, “Cursed is Everybody wey no dey continue in all things that are written in the book of the law, to do dem.”
Now that no man is justified by the law before God is evident, for, “The righteous will live by faith.”
The law No be of faith, but, “The man wey do dem will live by dem.”
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us. For it is written, “Cursed is Everybody wey hangs on a tree,”
that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Christ Jesus; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
Brothers, speaking of human terms, though it is only a man’s covenant, yet when it Don dey confirmed, Nobody makes it void, or adds to it.
Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his offspring. He no dey say, “To descendants ”, as of many, but as of one, “To una offspring ”, which is Christ.
Now I say this. A covenant confirmed beforehand by God in Christ, the law, which come four hundred thirty years after, No dey annul, so as to make the promise of no effect.
For if the inheritance is of the law, it is no more of promise; but God has granted it to Abraham by promise.
What then is the law? It was added because of wrongdoings, until the offspring should come to whom the promise Don dey made. It was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator.
Now a mediator No be between one, but God is one.
Is the law then against the promises of God? Certainly not! For if there Bin dey a law given which could make alive, most certainly righteousness would Don dey of the law.
But the Scriptures imprisoned all things under sin, that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to people wey believe.
But before faith come, we were kept in custody under the law, confined for the faith which should afterwards be revealed.
So that the law has become our tutor to bring us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.
But now that faith has come, We be no longer under a tutor.
For You be all pikin dem of God, through faith in Christ Jesus.
For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
E get neither Jew nor Greek, E get neither slave nor free man, E get neither male nor female; for You be all one in Christ Jesus.
If You be Christ’s, then You be Abraham’s offspring and heirs according to promise.
But I say that so long as the heir is a pikin, he is no different from a bondservant, though he is lord of all;
but is under guardians and stewards until the day appointed by the father.
So we also, when we were pikin dem, were held in bondage under the elemental principles of the world.
But when the fullness of the time come, God sent out his Son, born to a woman, born under the law,
that he might redeem people wey were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of pikin dem.
And because You be pikin dem, God sent out the Spirit of his Son into una hearts, crying, “Abba, Father!”
So You be no longer a bondservant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.
However at that time, not knowing God, you were in bondage to people wey by nature No be gods.
But now that you have come to know God, or rather to be known by God, why do you turn back again to the weak and miserable elemental principles, to which you desire to be in bondage all over again?
You observe days, months, seasons, and years.
I be afraid for you, that I might have wasted my labor for you.
I beg you, brothers, become as I be, for I also have become as You be. You did me no wrong,
but you know that because of weakness of the flesh I preached the Better news to you the first time.
That which was a temptation to you in my flesh, you didn’t despise nor reject; but you received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.
What was the blessing you enjoyed? For I testify to you that, if possible, you would have plucked out una eyes and given dem to me.
So then, have I become una enemy by telling you the truth?
Dem zealously seek you in no good way. No, dem desire to alienate you, that you may seek dem.
But it is always good to be zealous in a good cause, and not only when I be present with you.
My little pikin dem, of whom I be again in travail until Christ is formed in you —
but I could wish to be present with you now, and to change my tone, for I be perplexed about you.
Tell me, you that desire to be under the law, no you listen to the law?
For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the worker, and one by the free woman.
However, the son by the worker was born according to the flesh, but the son by the free woman was born through promise.
These things contain an allegory, for these are two covenants. One is from Mount Sinai, bearing pikin dem to bondage, which is Hagar.
For this Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and answers to the Jerusalem that exists now, for she is in bondage with her pikin dem.
But the Jerusalem that is above is free, which is the mother of us all.
For it is written, “Glad well-well, you barren who no bear. Break out and shout, you that no travail. For more are the pikin dem of the desolate than of her who has a husband.”
Now we, brothers, as Isaac was, are pikin dem of promise.
But as then, person wey was born according to the flesh persecuted him who was born according to the Spirit, so also it is now.
However what does the Scripture say? “Throw out the worker and her son, for the son of the worker No go inherit with the son of the free woman.”
So then, brothers, we No be pikin dem of a worker, but of the free woman.
Stand firm so in the liberty by which Christ has made us free, and no be entangled again with a yoke of bondage.
See am, I, Paul, tell you that if you receive circumcision, Christ will profit you nothing.
Yes, I testify again to every man who receives circumcision, that he is a debtor to do the whole law.
You be alienated from Christ, you who desire to be justified by the law. You have fallen away from grace.
For we, through the Spirit, by faith wait for the hope of righteousness.
For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision amounts to anything, nor uncircumcision, but faith working through love.
You were running well! Who interfered with you that you no suppose obey the truth?
This persuasion No be from him who calls you.
A little yeast grows through the whole lump.
I have confidence toward you in the Lord that You go think no other way. But person wey troubles You go bear his judgment, Anybody wey he is.
But I, brothers, if I still preach circumcision, why am I still persecuted? Then the stumbling block of the cross Don dey removed.
I wish that people wey disturb you would cut themselves off.
For you, brothers, were call for freedom. Only no use una freedom for gain to the flesh, but through love be workers to each other.
For the whole law is fulfilled in one word, in this: “You shall love una neighbor as yourself.”
But if you bite and devour each other, be careful that you no consume each other.
But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you no go fulfill the lust of the flesh.
For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; and these are contrary to each other, that you may not do the things that you desire.
But if You be led by the Spirit, you No be under the law.
Now the deeds of the flesh are obvious, which are: adultery, sexual immorality, uncleanness, lustfulness,
idolatry, sorcery, hatred, strife, jealousies, outbursts of anger, rivalries, divisions, heresies,
envy, murders, drunkenness, orgies, and things like these; of which I forewarn you, even as I also forewarned you, that people wey practice such things No go inherit God’s Kingdom.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, gladness, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
gentleness, and self-control. Against such things E get no law.
People wey belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its passions and lusts.
If we live by the Spirit, let’s also walk by the Spirit.
Let’s not become conceited, provoking each other, and envying each other.
Brothers, even if a man is caught in some fault, you Wey be spiritual must restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness; looking to yourself so that you also no be tempted.
Bear each other’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.
For if a man thinks imself to be something when he is nothing, he deceives imself.
But let each man examine his own work, and then he Go get reason to boast in imself, and not in someone else.
For each man will bear his own burden.
But Make e Wey be taught in the word share all good things with him who teaches.
No be deceived. God No be mocked, for Anything wey a man sows, that he will also reap.
For person wey sows to his own flesh will from the flesh reap corruption. But person wey sows to the Spirit will from the Spirit reap life wey no dey end.
Make we not be weary in doing good, for We go reap in due season, if we no give up.
So then, as we have opportunity, let’s do Wetin be good toward all men, and especially toward people Wey of the household of the faith.
See with what large letters I write to you with my own hand.
As many as desire to look good in the flesh, dem compel you to be circumcised; only that dem may not be persecuted for the cross of Christ.
For even dem who receive circumcision no keep the law themselves, but dem desire to have you circumcised, that dem may boast in una flesh.
But far be it from me to boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world Don dey crucified to me, and I to the world.
For in Christ Jesus neither is circumcision anything, nor uncircumcision, but a new creation.
As many as walk by this rule, peace and mercy be on dem, and on God’s Israel.
From now on, let Nobody cause me any trouble, for I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus branded on my body.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with una spirit, brothers. Amen.
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, to the saints Wey be at Ephesus, and the faithful in Christ Jesus:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ;
even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we would be holy and without defect before him in love;
having predestined us for adoption as pikin dem through Jesus Christ to imself, according to the good pleasure of his desire,
to the praise of the glory of his grace, by which he freely give us favor in the Beloved,
in whom we have our redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace,
which he made to abound toward us in all wisdom and prudence,
making known to us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure which he purposed in him
to an administration of the fullness of the times, to sum up all things in Christ, the things in the heavens, and the things on the earth, in him;
in whom also we were assigned an inheritance, having been foreordained according to the purpose of him wey do all things after the counsel of his will;
to the end that we should be to the praise of his glory, we who had before hoped in Christ:
in whom you also, having heard the word of the truth, the Better news of una salvation — in whom, having also believe, you were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit,
Wey be a pledge of our inheritance, to the redemption of God’s own possession, to the praise of his glory.
For this cause I also, having heard of the faith in the Lord Jesus which is among you, and the love which you have toward all the saints,
no cease to Thank God for you, making mention of you in my prayers,
that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give to you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him;
having the eyes of una hearts enlightened, that you may know Wetin be the hope of his calling, and Wetin be the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints,
and Wetin be the exceeding greatness of his power toward us who believe, according to that working of the strength of his might
which he worked in Christ, when he raised him from the dead, and made him to sit at his right hand in the heavenly places,
far above all rule, and authority, and power, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this age, but also in that which is to come.
He put all things in subjection under his feet, and give him to be head over all things for the assembly,
which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all in all.
You were made alive when you were dead in wrongdoings and sins,
in which you once walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit who now works in the pikin dem of disobedience;
among whom we also all once lived in the lusts of our flesh, doing the desires of the flesh and of the mind, and were by nature pikin dem of serious anger, even as the rest.
But God, being rich in mercy, for his great love with which he love us,
even when we were dead through our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ (by grace you Don dey saved),
and raised us up with him, and made us to sit with him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus,
that in the ages to come he might show the exceeding riches of his grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus;
for by grace you Don dey saved through faith, and that not of unaself; it is the gift of God,
not of works, that Nobody would boast.
For We be his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared before that we would walk in dem.
So remember that once you, the Gentiles in the flesh, Wey be call “uncircumcision” by that which is call “circumcision”, (in the flesh, made by hands);
that you were at that time separate from Christ, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of the promise, having no hope and without God in the world.
But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off are made near in the blood of Christ.
For he is our peace, who made both one, and broke down the middle wall of partition,
having abolished in his flesh the hostility, the law of commandments contained in ordinances, that he might create in imself one new man of the two, making peace;
and might reconcile dem both in one body to God through the cross, having killed the hostility through am.
He come and preached peace to you who were far off and to people wey were near.
For through him we both have our access in one Spirit to the Father.
So then You be no longer strangers and foreigners, but You be fellow citizens with the saints, and of the household of God,
being built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus imself being the chief cornerstone;
in whom the whole building, fitted together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord;
in whom you also are built together for a habitation of God in the Spirit.
For this cause I, Paul, am the prisoner of Christ Jesus on behalf of you Gentiles,
if it is so that you have heard of the administration of that grace of God which was given me toward you;
how that by revelation the mystery was made known to me, as I wrote before in few words,
by which, when you read, you can perceive my understanding in the mystery of Christ;
which in other generations No be made known to the pikin dem of men, as it has now been revealed to his holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit;
that the Gentiles are fellow heirs, and fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of his promise in Christ Jesus through the Better news,
of which I was made a worker, according to the gift of that grace of God which was given me according to the working of his power.
To me, the very least of all saints, was this grace given, to preach to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ,
and to make all men see Wetin be the administration of the mystery which for ages Don dey hidden in God, who created all things through Jesus Christ;
to the intent that now through the assembly the manifold wisdom of God might be made known to the principalities and the powers in the heavenly places,
according to the eternal purpose which he purposed in Christ Jesus our Lord;
in whom we have boldness and access in confidence through our faith in him.
So I ask that you may not lose heart at my troubles for you, which are una glory.
For this cause, I bow my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named,
that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, that you may be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inward man;
that Christ may live in una hearts through faith; to the end that you, being rooted and grounded in love,
may be strengthened to comprehend with all the saints Wetin be the width and length and height and depth,
and to know Christ’s love which surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
Now to him Wey be able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us,
to him be the glory in the assembly and in Christ Jesus to all generations forever and ever. Amen.
I so, the prisoner in the Lord, beg you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were call,
with all lowliness and humility, with patience, bearing with each other in love;
being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
E get one body, and one Spirit, even as you also were call in one hope of una calling;
one Lord, one faith, one baptism,
one God and Father of all, Wey be over all, and through all, and in us all.
But to each one of us was the grace given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
So he says, “When he ascended on high, he led captivity captive, and give gifts to men.”
Now this, “He ascended”, Wetin be it but that he also first descended into the lower parts of the earth?
Person wey descended is the one who also ascended far above all the heavens, that he might fill all things.
He give some to be apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, shepherds and teachers;
for the perfecting of the saints, to the work of serving, to the building up of the body of Christ;
until we all attain to the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a full grown man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ;
that we may no longer be pikin dem, tossed back and forth and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the trickery of men, in craftiness, after the wiles of error;
but speaking truth in love, we may grow up in all things into him, Wey be the head, Christ;

from whom all the body, being fitted and knit together through that which every joint supplies, according to the working in measure of each individual part, makes the body increase to the building up of itself in love.
This I say so, and testify in the Lord, that you no longer walk as the rest of the Gentiles also walk, in the futility of dem mind,
being darkened in dem understanding, alienated from the life of God, because of the ignorance that is in dem, because of the hardening of dem hearts;
who having become callous give themselves up to lust, to work all uncleanness with greediness.
But you No learn Christ that way;
if indeed you heard him, and were taught in him, even as truth is in Jesus:
that you put away, as concerning una former way of life, the old man, that grows corrupt after the lusts of deceit;
and that you be renewed in the spirit of una mind,
and put on the new man, who in the likeness of God Don dey created in righteousness and holiness of truth.
So putting away falsehood, speak truth each one with his neighbor. For We be members of each other.
“Be angry, and no sin.” No let the sun go down on una serious anger,
and no give place to the devil.
Make e who stole steal no more; but rather Make e labor, producing with his hands something that is good, that he may have something to give to him who has need.
Let no corrupt speech proceed out of una mouth, but only Wetin be good for building others up as the need may be, that it may give grace to people wey hear.
No grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
Let all bitterness, serious anger, anger, outcry, and slander, be put away from you, with all malice.
And be kind to each other, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.
Be so imitators of God, as beloved pikin dem.
Walk in love, even as Christ also love you, and give imself up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweet-smelling fragrance.
But sexual immorality, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not even be mentioned among you, as becomes saints;
nor filthiness, nor foolish talking, nor jesting, which No be appropriate; but rather giving of thanks.
Know this for sure, that no sexually immoral person, nor unclean person, nor covetous man, Wey be an idolater, has any inheritance in the Kingdom of Christ and God.
Let Nobody deceive you with empty words. For because of these things, the serious anger of God comes on the pikin dem of disobedience.
So no be partakers with dem.
For you were once darkness, but are now light in the Lord. Walk as pikin dem of light,
for the fruit of the Spirit is in all goodness and righteousness and truth,
proving Wetin be well pleasing to the Lord.
Have no fellowship with the unfruitful deeds of darkness, but rather even reprove dem.
For the things which are done by dem in secret, it is a shame even to speak of.
But all things, when Dem be reproved, are revealed by the light, for everything that reveals is light.
So he says, “Awake, you who sleep, and arise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.”
So watch carefully how you walk, No be like unwise, but as wise;
redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
So no be foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is.
No be drunken with wine, in which is dissipation, but be filled with the Spirit,
speaking to each other in psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs; singing, and making melody in una heart to the Lord;
giving thanks always concerning all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to God, even the Father;
subjecting unaself to each other in the fear of Christ.
Wives, be subject to una own husbands, as to the Lord.
For the husband is the head of the wife, as Christ also is the head of the assembly, being imself the savior of the body.
But as the assembly is subject to Christ, so let the wives also be to dem own husbands in everything.
Husbands, love una wives, even as Christ also love the assembly, and give imself up for it;
that he might sanctify it, having cleansed it by the washing of water with the word,
that he might present the assembly to imself gloriously, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without defect.
Even so husbands also ought to love dem own wives as dem own bodies. Person wey loves his own wife loves imself.
For no man ever hated his own flesh; but nourishes and cherishes it, even as the Lord also does the assembly;
because We be members of his body, of his flesh and bones.
“For this cause a man will leave his father and mother, and Go be joined to his wife. The two will become one flesh.”
This mystery is great, but I speak concerning Christ and of the assembly.
Nevertheless each of you must also love his own wife even as imself; and let the wife see that she respects her husband.
Pikin dem, obey una parents in the Lord, for this is right.
“Honor una father and mother,” which is the first commandment with a promise:
“that it may be well with you, and you may live long on the earth.”
You fathers, no provoke una pikin dem to serious anger, but nurture dem in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.
Workers, be obedient to people wey according to the flesh are una masters, with fear and trembling, in singleness of una heart, as to Christ;
not in the way of service only when eyes are on you, as men pleasers; but as workers of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart;
with good will doing service, as to the Lord, and not to men;
knowing that Anything wey good thing each one does, he will receive the same again from the Lord, whether he is bound or free.
You masters, do the same things to dem, and give up threatening, knowing that person Wey both dem Master and yours is in heaven, and E get no partiality with him.
Finally, be strong in the Lord, and in the strength of his might.
Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.

For our wrestling No be against flesh and blood, but against the principalities, against the powers, against the world’s rulers of the darkness of this age, and against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places.
So put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to withstand in the evil day, and, having done all, to stand.
Stand so, having the utility belt of truth buckled around una waist, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness,
and having fitted una feet with the preparation of the Better news of peace;
above all, taking up the shield of faith, with which You go be able to quench all the fiery darts of the evil one.
And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God;
with all prayer and requests, praying at all times in the Spirit, and being watchful to this end in all perseverance and requests for all the saints:
on my behalf, that utterance may be given to me in opening my mouth, to make known with boldness the mystery of the Better news,
for which I be an ambassador in chains; that in it I may speak boldly, as I ought to speak.
But that you also may know my affairs, how I be doing, Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful worker in the Lord, will make known to you all things;
whom I have sent to you for this very purpose, that you may know our state, and that he may comfort una hearts.
Peace be to the brothers, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Grace be with all people wey love our Lord Jesus Christ with incorruptible love. Amen.
Paul and Timothy, workers of Jesus Christ; To all the saints in Christ Jesus Wey be at Philippi, with the overseers and workers:
Grace to you, and peace from God, our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God whenever I remember you,
always in every request of mine on behalf of you all making my requests with gladness,
for una partnership in furtherance of the Better news from the first day until now;
being confident of this very thing, that person wey began a good work in You go complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.

It is even right for me to think this way on behalf of all of you, because I have you in my heart, because, both in my bonds and in the defense and confirmation of the Better news, you all are partakers with me of grace.
For God is my witness, how I long after all of you in the tender mercies of Christ Jesus.
This I pray, that una love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and all discernment;
so that you may approve the things that are excellent; that you may be sincere and without offense to the day of Christ;
being filled with the fruits of righteousness, which are through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
Now I desire to have you know, brothers, that the things which happened to me have turned out rather to the progress of the Better news;
so that it became evident to the whole palace guard, and to all the rest, that my bonds are in Christ;
and that most of the brothers in the Lord, being confident through my bonds, are more abundantly bold to speak the word of God without fear.
Some indeed preach Christ even out of envy and strife, and some also out of good will.
The former insincerely preach Christ from selfish ambition, thinking that dem add suffering to my chains;
but the latter out of love, knowing that I be appointed for the defense of the Better news.
What does it matter? Only that in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is proclaimed. I glad well-well in this, yes, and will glad well-well.
For I know that this will turn out to my salvation, through una supplication and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,
according to my earnest expectation and hope, that I go in no way be disappointed, but with all boldness, as always, now also Christ Go be magnified in my body, whether by life, or by death.
For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
But if I live on in the flesh, this will bring fruit from my work; yet I no know what I go choose.
But I be in a dilemma between the two, having the desire to depart and be with Christ, which is far better.
Yet, to remain in the flesh is more needful for una sake.
Having this confidence, I know that I go remain, yes, and remain with you all, for una progress and gladness in the faith,
that una rejoicing may abound in Christ Jesus in me through my presence with you again.

Only let una way of life be worthy of the Better news of Christ, that, whether I come and see you or am absent, I may hear of una state, that you stand firm in one spirit, with one soul striving for the faith of the Better news;
and in nothing frightened by the adversaries, which is for dem a proof of destruction, but to you of salvation, and that from God.
Because it Don dey granted to you on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in him, but also to suffer on his behalf,
having the same conflict which you see in me, and now hear is in me.
If E get so any exhortation in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any tender mercies and compassion,
make my gladness full, by being like-minded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind;
doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than imself;
each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.
Have this in una mind, which was also in Christ Jesus,
who, existing in the form of God, didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped,
but emptied imself, taking the form of a worker, being made in the likeness of men.
And being find in human form, he humbled imself, becoming obedient to death, yes, the death of the cross.
So God also highly exalted him, and give to him the name which is above every name;
that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, those on earth, and those under the earth,
and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
So then, my beloved, even as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now much more in my absence, work out una own salvation with fear and trembling.
For it is God who works in you both to will and to work, for his good pleasure.
Do all things without murmurings and disputes,
that you may become blameless and harmless, pikin dem of God without defect in the middle of a crooked and perverse generation, among whom You be seen as lights in the world,
holding up the word of life; that I may have something to boast in the day of Christ, that I didn’t run in vain nor labor in vain.
Yes, and if I be poured out on the sacrifice and service of una faith, I glad well-well, and glad well-well with you all.
In the same way, you also glad well-well, and glad well-well with me.
But I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, that I also may be cheered up when I know how You be doing.
For I have Nobody else like-minded, who will truly care about you.
For dem all seek dem own, not the things of Jesus Christ.
But you know the proof of him, that, as a pikin serves a father, so he served with me in furtherance of the Better news.
So I hope to send him at once, as soon as I see how it will go with me.
But I trust in the Lord that I myself also will come shortly.
But I counted it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother, fellow worker, fellow soldier, and una apostle and worker of my need;
since he longed for you all, and was very troubled, because you had heard that he was sick.
For indeed he was sick, nearly to death, but God had mercy on him; and not on him only, but on me also, that I might not have sorrow on sorrow.
I have sent him so the more diligently, that, when you see him again, you may glad well-well, and that I may be the less sorrowful.
Receive him so in the Lord with all gladness, and hold such in honor,
because for the work of Christ he come near to death, risking his life to supply that which was lacking in una service toward me.
Finally, my brothers, glad well-well in the Lord. To write the same things to you, to me indeed No be tiresome, but for you it is safe.
Beware of the dogs, beware of the evil workers, beware of the false circumcision.
For We be the circumcision, who worship God in the Spirit, and glad well-well in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh;
though I myself might have confidence even in the flesh. If any other man thinks that he has confidence in the flesh, I yet more:
circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; concerning the law, a Pharisee;
concerning zeal, persecuting the assembly; concerning the righteousness which is in the law, find blameless.
However, I consider those things that were gain to me as a loss for Christ.

Yes most certainly, and I count all things to be a loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus, my Lord, for whom I suffered the loss of all things, and count dem nothing but refuse, that I may gain Christ
and be find in him, not having a righteousness of my own, that which is of the law, but that which is through faith in Christ, the righteousness which is from God by faith;
that I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, becoming conformed to his death;
if by any means I may attain to the resurrection from the dead.
Not that I have already obtained, or am already made perfect; but I press on, if it is so that I may take hold of that for which also I was taken hold of by Christ Jesus.
Brothers, I no regard myself as yet having taken hold, but one thing I do. Forgetting the things which are behind, and stretching forward to the things which are before,
I press on toward the goal for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
Make we so, as many as are perfect, think this way. If in anything you think otherwise, God will also reveal that to you.
Nevertheless, to the extent that we have already attained, Make we walk by the same rule. Make we be of the same mind.
Brothers, be imitators together of me, and note people wey walk this way, even as you have us for an example.
For many walk, of whom I told you often, and now tell you even weeping, as the enemies of the cross of Christ,
whose end is destruction, whose god is the belly, and whose glory is in dem shame, who think about earthly things.
For our citizenship is in heaven, from where we also wait for a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ;
who will change the body of our humiliation to be conformed to the body of his glory, according to the working by which he is able even to subject all things to imself.
So, my brothers, beloved and longed for, my gladness and crown, so stand firm in the Lord, my beloved.
I exhort Euodia, and I exhort Syntyche, to think the same way in the Lord.
Yes, I beg you also, true partner, help these women, for dem labored with me in the Better news, with Clement also, and the rest of my fellow workers, whose names are in the book of life.
Glad well-well in the Lord always! Again I go say, “Glad well-well!”
Let una gentleness be known to all men. The Lord is at hand.
In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let una requests be made known to God.
And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard una hearts and una thoughts in Christ Jesus.

Finally, brothers, Anything wey things are true, Anything wey things are honorable, Anything wey things are just, Anything wey things are pure, Anything wey things are lovely, Anything wey things are of good report; if E get any virtue, and if E get any praise, think about these things.
The things which you learned, received, heard, and see in me: do these things, and the God of peace Go be with you.
But I glad well-well in the Lord greatly, that now at length you have revived una thought for me; in which you did indeed take thought, but you lacked opportunity.
Not that I speak in respect to lack, for I have learned in Anything wey state I be, to be content in it.
I know how to be humbled, and I know also how to abound. In everything and in all things I have learned the secret both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in need.
I fit face anything through Christ wey dey give me power.
However you did well that you shared in my suffering.
You unaself also know, you Philippians, that For the beginning of the Better news, when I comot from Macedonia, no assembly shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving but you only.
For even in Thessalonica you sent once and again to my need.
Not that I seek for the gift, but I seek for the fruit that increases to una account.
But I have all things, and abound. I be filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things that come from you, a sweet-smelling fragrance, an acceptable and well-pleasing sacrifice to God.
My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
Now to our God and Father be the glory forever and ever! Amen.
Greet every saint in Christ Jesus. The brothers Wey be with me greet you.
All the saints greet you, especially people Wey of Caesar’s household.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother,
to the saints and faithful brothers in Christ at Colossae: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We Thank God to God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you,
having heard of una faith in Christ Jesus, and of the love which you have toward all the saints,
because of the hope which is laid up for you in the heavens, of which you heard before in the word of the truth of the Better news,
which has come to you; even as it is in all the world and is bearing fruit and growing, as it does in you also, since the day you heard and know the grace of God in truth;
even as you learned of Epaphras our beloved fellow worker, Wey be a faithful worker of Christ on our behalf,
who also declared to us una love in the Spirit.
For this cause, we also, since the day we heard this, no cease praying and making requests for you, that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,
that you may walk worthily of the Lord, to please him in all respects, bearing fruit in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God;
strengthened with all power, according to the might of his glory, for all endurance and perseverance with gladness;
giving thanks to the Father, who made us fit to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light;
who delivered us out of the power of darkness, and translated us into the Kingdom of the Son of his love;
in whom we have our redemption, the forgiveness of our sins;
Wey be the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.

For by him all things were created, in the heavens and on the earth, things visible and things invisible, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers; all things Don dey created through him, and for him.
He is before all things, and in him all things are held together.
He is the head of the body, the assembly, Wey be the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.
For all the fullness was pleased to live in him;
