and through him to reconcile all things to imself, by him, whether things on the earth, or things in the heavens, having made peace through the blood of his cross.
You, being in past times alienated and enemies in una mind in una evil deeds,
yet now he has reconciled in the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and without defect and blameless before him,

if it is so that you continue in the faith, grounded and steadfast, and not moved away from the hope of the Better news which you heard, which is being proclaimed in all creation under heaven; of which I, Paul, was made a worker.
Now I glad well-well in my sufferings for una sake, and fill up on my part that which is lacking of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh for his body’s sake, which is the assembly;
of which I was made a worker, according to the stewardship of God which was given me toward you, to fulfill the word of God,
the mystery which Don dey hidden for ages and generations. But now it Don dey revealed to his saints,
to whom God was pleased to make known Wetin be the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory;
whom we proclaim, admonishing every man and teaching every man in all wisdom, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus;
for which I also labor, striving according to his working, which works in me mightily.
For I desire to have you know how greatly I struggle for you, and for those at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh;

that dem hearts may be comforted, dem being knit together in love, and gaining all riches of the full assurance of understanding, that dem may know the mystery of God, both of the Father and of Christ,
in whom are all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hidden.
Now this I say that Nobody may delude you with persuasiveness of speech.
For though I be absent in the flesh, yet am I with you in the spirit, rejoicing and seeing una order, and the steadfastness of una faith in Christ.
As so you received Christ Jesus, the Lord, walk in him,
rooted and built up in him, and established in the faith, even as you were taught, abounding in it in thanksgiving.
Be careful that you no let anyone rob you through his philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the elements of the world, and not after Christ.
For in him all the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily,
and in him You be made full, Wey be the head of all principality and power;
in whom you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, in the putting off of the body of the sins of the flesh, in the circumcision of Christ;
having been buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through faith in the working of God, who raised him from the dead.
You were dead through una trespasses and the uncircumcision of una flesh. He made you alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses,
wiping out the handwriting in ordinances which was against us; and he has taken it out of the way, nailing it to the cross;
having stripped the principalities and the powers, he made a show of dem openly, triumphing over dem in it.
Let Nobody so judge you in eating, or in drinking, or with respect to a feast day or a new moon or a Sabbath day,
which are a shadow of the things to come; but the body is Christ’s.
Let Nobody rob you of una prize by a voluntary humility and worshiping of the angels, dwelling in the things which he has not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,
and not holding firmly to the Head, from whom all the body, being supplied and knit together through the joints and ligaments, grows with God’s growth.
If you died with Christ from the elements of the world, why, as though living in the world, do you subject unaself to ordinances,
“No handle, nor taste, nor touch”
(all of which perish with use), according to the precepts and doctrines of men?
Which things indeed appear like wisdom in self-imposed worship, and humility, and severity to the body; but no be of any value against the indulgence of the flesh.
If then you were raised together with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated on the right hand of God.
Set una mind on the things that are above, not on the things that are on the earth.
For you died, and una life is hidden with Christ in God.
When Christ, our life, is revealed, then You go also be revealed with him in glory.
Put to death so una members which are on the earth: sexual immorality, uncleanness, depraved passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry;
for which things’ sake the serious anger of God comes on the pikin dem of disobedience.
You also once walked in those, when you lived in dem;
but now you also put dem all away: anger, serious anger, malice, slander, and shameful speaking out of una mouth.
No lie to each other, seeing that you have put off the old man with his doings,
and have put on the new man, Wey be being renewed in knowledge after the image of his Creator,
where there no fit be Greek and Jew, circumcision and uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, bondservant, freeman; but Christ is all, and in all.
Put on so, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility, and perseverance;
bearing with each other, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do.
Above all these things, walk in love, which is the bond of perfection.
And let the peace of God rule in una hearts, to which also you were call in one body; and be thankful.
Let the word of Christ live in you richly; in all wisdom teaching and admonishing each other with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in una heart to the Lord.
Anything wey you do, in word or in deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father, through him.
Wives, be in subjection to una husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.
Husbands, love una wives, and no be bitter against dem.
Pikin dem, obey una parents in all things, for this pleases the Lord.
Fathers, no provoke una pikin dem, so that dem no go be discouraged.
Workers, obey in all things people Wey una masters according to the flesh, not just when Dem be looking, as men pleasers, but in singleness of heart, fearing God.
And Anything wey you do, work heartily, as for the Lord, and not for men,
knowing that from the Lord You go receive the reward of the inheritance; for you serve the Lord Christ.
But person wey does wrong will receive again for the wrong that he has done, and E get no partiality.
Masters, give to una workers that which is just and equal, knowing that you also have a Master in heaven.
Continue steadfastly in prayer, watching inside am with thanksgiving;
praying together for us also, that God may open to us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I be also in bonds;
that I may reveal it as I ought to speak.
Walk in wisdom toward people Wey outside, redeeming the time.
Let una speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, that you may know how you ought to answer each one.
All my affairs Go be made known to you by Tychicus, the beloved brother, faithful worker, and fellow bondservant in the Lord.
I be sending him to you for this very purpose, that he may know una circumstances and comfort una hearts,
together with Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother, Wey be one of you. Dem go make known to you everything that is going on here.
Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you, and Mark, the cousin of Barnabas (concerning whom you received commandments, “if he comes to you, receive him”),
and Jesus Wey be call Justus. These are my only fellow workers for God’s Kingdom Wey be of the circumcision, men who Don dey a comfort to me.
Epaphras, Wey be one of you, a worker of Christ, salutes you, always striving for you in his prayers, that you may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God.
For I testify about him, that he has great zeal for you, and for those in Laodicea, and for those in Hierapolis.
Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas greet you.
Greet the brothers Wey be in Laodicea, and Nymphas, and the assembly that is in his house.
When this letter Don dey read among you, cause it to be read also in the assembly of the Laodiceans; and that you also read the letter from Laodicea.
Tell Archippus, “Take heed to the ministry which you have received in the Lord, that you fulfill it.”
The salutation of me, Paul, with my own hand: remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.
Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the assembly of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We always Thank God to God for all of you, mentioning you in our prayers,
remembering without stop una work of faith and labor of love and perseverance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, before our God and Father.
We know, brothers love by God, that You be chosen,
and that our Better news come to you not in word only, but also in power, and in the Holy Spirit, and with much assurance. You know what kind of men we showed ourselves to be among you for una sake.
You became imitators of us, and of the Lord, having received the word in much suffering, with gladness of the Holy Spirit,
so that you became an example to all who believe in Macedonia and in Achaia.
For from you the word of the Lord Don dey declared, not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but also in every place una faith toward God has gone out; so that we need not to say anything.
For dem themselves report concerning us what kind of a reception we had from you; and how you turned to God from idols, to serve a living and true God,
and to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead — Jesus, who delivers us from the serious anger to come.
For you unaself know, brothers, our visit to you no be in vain,
but having suffered before and been shamefully treated, as you know, at Philippi, we grew bold in our God to tell you the Better news of God in much conflict.
For our exhortation No be of error, nor of uncleanness, nor in deception.
But even as we Don dey approved by God to be entrusted with the Better news, so we speak; No be like pleasing men, but God, who tests our hearts.
For neither were we at any time find using words of flattery, as you know, nor a cloak of covetousness (God is witness),
nor seeking glory from men (neither from you nor from others), when we might have claimed authority as apostles of Christ.
But we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother cherishes her own pikin dem.
Even so, affectionately longing for you, we were well pleased to impart to you, not the Better news of God only, but also our own souls, because you had become very dear to us.
For you remember, brothers, our labor and travail; for working night and day, that we might not burden any of you, we preached to you the Better news of God.
You be witnesses with God, how holy, righteously, and blamelessly we behaved ourselves toward you who believe.
As you know, we exhorted, comforted, and implored every one of you, as a father does his own pikin dem,
to the end that you should walk worthily of God, who calls you into his own Kingdom and glory.

For this cause we also thank God without stop, that, when you received from us the word of the message of God, you accepted it No be like the word of men, but, as it is in truth, the word of God, which also works in you who believe.
For you, brothers, became imitators of the assemblies of God which are in Judea in Christ Jesus; for you also suffered the same things from una own countrymen, even as dem did from the Jews;
who killed both the Lord Jesus and dem own prophets, and drove us out, and didn’t please God, and are contrary to all men;
forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles that dem may be saved; to fill up dem sins always. But serious anger has come on dem to the uttermost.
But we, brothers, being bereaved of you for a short season, in presence, not in heart, tried even harder to see una face with great desire,
because we want to come to you — indeed, I, Paul, once and again — but Satan hindered us.
For Wetin be our hope, or gladness, or crown of rejoicing? No be it even you, before our Lord Jesus at his coming?
For You be our glory and our gladness.
So when we no fit stand it any longer, we thought it good to be left behind at Athens alone,
and sent Timothy, our brother and God’s worker in the Better news of Christ, to establish you, and to comfort you concerning una faith;
that Nobody be moved by these afflictions. For you know that We be appointed to this task.
For most certainly, when we were with you, we told you beforehand that We be to suffer suffering, even as it happened, and you know.
For this cause I also, when I no fit stand it any longer, sent that I might know una faith, for fear that by any means the tempter had tempted you, and our labor would Don dey in vain.
But when Timothy come just now to us from you, and bring us glad news of una faith and love, and that you have good memories of us always, longing to see us, even as we also long to see you;
for this cause, brothers, we were comforted over you in all our distress and suffering through una faith.
For now we live, if you stand fast in the Lord.
For what thanksgiving can we render again to God for you, for all the gladness with which we glad well-well for una sakes before our God;
night and day praying exceedingly that we may see una face, and may perfect that which is lacking in una faith?
Now may our God and Father imself, and our Lord Jesus Christ, direct our way to you;
and the Lord make you to increase and abound in love one toward another, and toward all men, even as we also do toward you,
to the end he may establish una hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all his saints.
Finally then, brothers, we beg and exhort you in the Lord Jesus, that as you received from us how you ought to walk and to please God, that you abound more and more.
For you know what instructions we give you through the Lord Jesus.
For this is the will of God: una sanctification, that you abstain from sexual immorality,
that each one of you know how to control his own body in sanctification and honor,
not in the passion of lust, even as the Gentiles who no know God;
that Nobody should take advantage of and wrong a brother or sister in this matter; because the Lord is an avenger in all these things, as also we forewarned you and testified.
For God call us not for uncleanness, but in sanctification.
So person wey rejects this no dey reject man, but God, who has also given his Holy Spirit to you.
But concerning brotherly love, you have no need that one write to you. For you unaself are taught by God to love each other,
for indeed you do it toward all the brothers Wey be in all Macedonia. But we exhort you, brothers, that you abound more and more;
and that you make it una ambition to lead a quiet life, and to do una own business, and to work with una own hands, even as we instructed you;
that you may walk properly toward people Wey outside, and may have need of nothing.
But we no want you to be ignorant, brothers, concerning people wey have fallen asleep, so that you no grieve like the rest, who have no hope.
For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so God will bring with him people wey have fallen asleep in Jesus.
For this we tell you by the word of the Lord, that we Wey be alive, Wey be left to the coming of the Lord, will in no way precede people wey have fallen asleep.
For the Lord imself will descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with God’s trumpet. The dead in Christ will rise first,
then we Wey be alive, Wey be left, Go be caught up together with dem in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air. So We go be with the Lord forever.
So comfort each other with these words.
But concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need that anything be written to you.
For you unaself know well that the day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night.
For when Dem be saying, “Peace and safety,” then sudden destruction will come on dem, like birth pains on a pregnant woman; and Dem go in no way escape.
But you, brothers, no be in darkness, that the day should overtake you like a thief.
You be all pikin dem of light, and pikin dem of the day. We no belong to the night, nor to darkness,
so then let’s not sleep, as the rest do, but let’s watch and be sober.
For people wey sleep, sleep in the night; and people Wey drunk are drunk in the night.
But Make we, since we belong to the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and, for a helmet, the hope of salvation.
For God didn’t appoint us to serious anger, but to the obtaining of salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,
who died for us, that, whether we wake or sleep, we should live together with him.
So exhort each other, and build each other up, even as you also do.
But we beg you, brothers, to know people wey labor among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you,
and to respect and honor dem in love for dem work’s sake. Be at peace among unaself.
We exhort you, brothers, admonish the disorderly, encourage the faint-hearted, support the weak, be patient toward all.
See that Nobody returns evil for evil to anyone, but always follow after that which is good, for each other, and for all.
Glad well-well always.
Pray without stop.
In everything Thank God, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus toward you.
No quench the Spirit.
No despise prophesies.
Test all things, and hold firmly that which is good.
Abstain from every form of evil.
May the God of peace imself sanctify you completely. May una whole spirit, soul, and body be preserved blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Person wey calls you is faithful, who will also do it.
Brothers, pray for us.
Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.
I solemnly command you by the Lord that this letter be read to all the holy brothers.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the assembly of the Thessalonians in God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We be bound to always Thank God to God for you, brothers, even as it is appropriate, because una faith grows exceedingly, and the love of each and every one of you towards each other abounds;
so that we ourselves boast about you in the assemblies of God for una perseverance and faith in all una persecutions and in the afflictions which you endure.
This is an obvious sign of the righteous judgment of God, to the end that you may be counted worthy of God’s Kingdom, for which you also suffer.
Since it is a righteous thing with God to repay suffering to people wey afflict you,
and to give relief to you Wey be afflicted with us, when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his mighty angels in flaming fire,
giving vengeance to people wey no know God, and to people wey no obey the Better news of our Lord Jesus,
who will pay the penalty: eternal destruction from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his might,
when he comes to be glorified in his saints, and to be admired among all people wey have believe (because our testimony to you was believe) in that day.
To this end we also pray always for you, that our God may count you worthy of una calling, and fulfill every desire of goodness and work of faith, with power;
that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Now, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and our gathering together to him, we ask you
not to be sharp-sharp shaken in una mind, nor yet be troubled, either by spirit, or by word, or by letter as from us, saying that the day of Christ had come.
Let Nobody deceive you in any way. For it No go be, unless the departure comes first, and the man of sin is revealed, the son of destruction,
person wey opposes and exalts imself against all that is call God or that is worshiped; so that he sits as God in the temple of God, setting imself up as God.
No you remember that, when I was still with you, I told you these things?
Now you know Wetin be restraining him, to the end that he may be revealed in his own season.
For the mystery of lawlessness already works. Only E get one who restrains now, until he is taken out of the way.
Then the lawless one Go be revealed, whom the Lord will kill with the breath of his mouth, and destroy by the manifestation of his coming;
even he whose coming is according to the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders,
and with all deception of wickedness for people Wey being lost, because dem didn’t receive the love of the truth, that dem might be saved.
Because of this, God sends dem a working of error, that dem should believe a lie;
that dem all might be judged who didn’t believe the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.
But We be bound to always Thank God to God for you, brothers love by the Lord, because God chose you from the beginning for salvation through sanctification of the Spirit and belief in the truth;
to which he call you through our Better news, for the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, brothers, stand firm, and hold the traditions which you were taught by us, whether by word, or by letter.
Now our Lord Jesus Christ imself, and God our Father, who love us and give us eternal comfort and good hope through grace,
comfort una hearts and establish you in every good work and word.
Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may spread rapidly and be glorified, even as also with you;
and that we may be delivered from unreasonable and evil men; for not all have faith.
But the Lord is faithful, who will establish you, and guard you from the evil one.
We have confidence in the Lord concerning you, that you both do and will do the things we command.
May the Lord direct una hearts into God’s love, and into the perseverance of Christ.
Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you withdraw unaself from every brother who walks in rebellion, and not after the tradition which dem received from us.
For you know how you ought to imitate us. For we didn’t behave ourselves rebelliously among you,
neither did we eat bread from anyone’s hand without paying for it, but in labor and travail worked night and day, that we might not burden any of you;
not because we no have the right, but to make ourselves an example to you, that you should imitate us.
For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: “If anyone No go work, no Make e eat.”
For we hear of some who walk among you in rebellion, who no work at all, but are busybodies.
Now people Wey that way, we command and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ, that with quietness dem work, and eat dem own bread.
But you, brothers, no be weary in doing well.
If any man no dey obey our word in this letter, note that man, that you have no company with him, to the end that he may be ashamed.
No count him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.
Now may the Lord of peace imself give you peace at all times in all ways. The Lord be with you all.
The greeting of me, Paul, with my own hand, which is the sign in every letter: this is how I write.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ according to the commandment of God our Savior and the Lord Jesus Christ our hope;
to Timothy, my true pikin in faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God our Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
As I urged you when I was going into Macedonia, stay at Ephesus that you might command certain men not to teach a different doctrine,
and not to pay attention to myths and endless genealogies, which cause disputes, rather than God’s stewardship, which is in faith —
but the goal of this command is love, out of a pure heart and a good conscience and sincere faith;
from which things some, having missed the mark, have turned aside to vain talking;
desiring to be teachers of the law, though dem understand neither Wetin dem say, nor about Wetin dem strongly affirm.
But we know that the law is good, if a person uses it lawfully,

as knowing this, that law No be made for a righteous person, but for the lawless and insubordinate, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,
for the sexually immoral, for homosexuals, for slave-traders, for liars, for perjurers, and for any other thing contrary to the sound doctrine;
according to the Better news of the glory of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.
And I thank him who enabled me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he counted me faithful, appointing me to service;
although I was before a blasphemer, a persecutor, and insolent. However, I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
The grace of our Lord abounded exceedingly with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
The saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus come into the world to save sinners; of whom I be chief.
However, for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first, Jesus Christ might display all his patience, for an example of people wey were going to believe in him for life wey no dey end.
Now to the King eternal, immortal, invisible, to God who alone is wise, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
This instruction I commit to you, my pikin Timothy, according to the prophecies which led the way to you, that by dem you may wage the good warfare;
holding faith and a good conscience; which some having thrust away made a shipwreck concerning the faith;
of whom is Hymenaeus and Alexander; whom I delivered to Satan, that dem might be taught not to blaspheme.
I exhort so, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and givings of thanks, be made for all men:
for kings and all Wey be in high places; that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and reverence.
For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior;
who desires all people to be saved and come to full knowledge of the truth.
For E get one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus,
who give imself as a ransom for all; the testimony in its own times;
to which I was appointed a preacher and an apostle (I be telling the truth in Christ, not lying), a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
I desire so that the men in every place pray, lifting up holy hands without anger and doubting.
In the same way, that women also adorn themselves in decent clothing, with modesty and propriety; not just with braided hair, gold, pearls, or expensive clothing;
but (which becomes women professing godliness) with good works.
Let a woman learn in quietness with full submission.
But I no permit a woman to teach, nor to exercise authority over a man, but to be in quietness.
For Adam was first formed, then Eve.
Adam no be deceived, but the woman, being deceived, has fallen into disobedience;
but she Go be saved through her childbearing, if dem continue in faith, love, and sanctification with sobriety.
This is a faithful saying: if a man seeks the office of an overseer, he desires a good work.
The overseer so must be without reproach, the husband of one wife, temperate, sensible, modest, hospitable, good at teaching;
not a drinker, not violent, not greedy for money, but gentle, not quarrelsome, not covetous;
one who rules his own house well, having pikin dem in subjection with all reverence;
(but if a man no dey know how to rule his own house, how will he take care of the assembly of God?)
not a new convert, lest being puffed up he fall into the same condemnation as the devil.
Moreover he must have good testimony from people Wey outside, to avoid falling into reproach and the snare of the devil.
Workers, in the same way, must be reverent, not double-tongued, not addicted to much wine, not greedy for money;
holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
Make dem also first be tested; then Make dem serve if Dem be blameless.
Dem wives in the same way must be reverent, not slanderers, temperate, faithful in all things.
Let workers be husbands of one wife, ruling dem pikin dem and dem own houses well.
For people wey have served well gain for themselves a good standing, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.
These things I write to you, hoping to come to you shortly;
but if I wait long, that you may know how men ought to behave themselves in God’s house, which is the assembly of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.

Without controversy, the mystery of godliness is great: God was revealed in the flesh, justified in the spirit, seen by angels, preached among the nations, believe on in the world, and received up in glory.
But the Spirit says expressly that in later times some will fall away from the faith, paying attention to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons,
through the hypocrisy of men who speak lies, branded in dem own conscience as with a hot iron;
forbidding marriage and commanding to abstain from foods which God created to be received with thanksgiving by people wey believe and know the truth.
For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected, if it is received with thanksgiving.
For it is sanctified through the word of God and prayer.
If you instruct the brothers of these things, You go be a good worker of Christ Jesus, nourished in the words of the faith, and of the good doctrine which you have follow.
But refuse profane and old wives’ fables. Exercise yourself toward godliness.
For bodily exercise has some value, but godliness has value in all things, having the promise of the life which is now, and of that which is to come.
This saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance.
For to this end we both labor and suffer reproach, because we have set our trust in the living God, Wey be the Savior of all men, especially of people wey believe.
Command and teach these things.
Let no man despise una youth; but be an example to people wey believe, in word, in una way of life, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity.
Until I come, pay attention to reading, to exhortation, and to teaching.
No neglect the gift that is in you, which was given to you by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the elders.
Be diligent in these things. Give yourself wholly to dem, that una progress may be revealed to all.
Pay attention to yourself, and to una teaching. Continue in these things, for in doing this You go save both yourself and people wey hear you.
No rebuke an older man, but exhort him as a father; the younger men as brothers;
the elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, in all purity.
Honor widows Wey be widows indeed.
But if any widow has pikin dem or grandchildren, Make dem learn first to show piety towards dem own family, and to repay dem parents, for this is acceptable in the sight of God.
Now person Wey a widow indeed, and desolate, has her hope set on God, and continues in petitions and prayers night and day.
But person wey gives sheself to pleasure is dead while she lives.
Also command these things, that dem may be without reproach.
But if anyone no dey provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith, and is worse than an unbeliever.
Let Nobody be enrolled as a widow under sixty years old, having been the wife of one man,

being approved by good works, if she has bring up pikin dem, if she Don dey hospitable to strangers, if she has washed the saints’ feet, if she has relieved the afflicted, and if she has diligently follow every good work.
But refuse younger widows, for when dem have grown wanton against Christ, dem desire to marry;
having condemnation, because dem have rejected dem first pledge.
Besides, dem also learn to be idle, going about from house to house. Not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, saying things which dem ought not.
I desire so that the younger widows marry, bear pikin dem, rule the household, and give no occasion to the adversary for insulting.
For already some have turned aside after Satan.
If any man or woman wey believe has widows, Make dem relieve dem, and no let the assembly be burdened; that it might relieve people Wey widows indeed.
Let the elders who rule well be counted worthy of double honor, especially people wey labor in the word and in teaching.
For the Scripture says, “You no go muzzle the ox when it treads out the grain.” And, “The laborer is worthy of his wages.”
No receive an accusation against an elder, except at the word of two or three witnesses.
People wey sin, reprove in the sight of all, that the rest also may be in fear.
I command you in the sight of God, and Christ Jesus, and the chosen angels, that you observe these things without prejudice, doing nothing by partiality.
Lay hands hastily on Nobody, neither be a participant in other men’s sins. Keep yourself pure.
Be no longer a drinker of water only, but use a little wine for una stomach’s sake and una frequent infirmities.
Some men’s sins are evident, preceding dem to judgment, and some also follow later.
In the same way also E get good works that are obvious, and those that are otherwise no fit be hidden.
Let as many as are bondservants under the yoke count dem own masters worthy of all honor, that the name of God and the doctrine not be blasphemed.

People wey have believing masters, Make dem not despise dem, because Dem be brothers, but rather Make dem serve dem, because people wey partake of the benefit are believing and beloved. Teach and exhort these things.
If anyone teaches a different doctrine, and no dey consent to sound words, the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness,
he is conceited, knowing nothing, but obsessed with arguments, disputes, and word battles, from which come envy, strife, insulting, evil suspicions,
constant friction of people of corrupt minds and destitute of the truth, who suppose that godliness is a means of gain. Withdraw yourself from such.
But godliness with contentment is great gain.
For we bring nothing into the world, and we certainly no fit carry anything out.
But having chop and clothing, We go be content with that.
But people Wey determined to be rich fall into a temptation and a snare and many foolish and harmful lusts, such as drown men in ruin and destruction.
For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some Don dey led astray from the faith in dem greed, and have pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
But you, man of God, flee these things, and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, and gentleness.
Fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of the life wey no dey end to which you were call, and you confessed the good confession in the sight of many witnesses.
I command you before God, wey dey give life to all things, and before Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate testified the good confession,
that you keep the commandment without spot, blameless, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ;
which in its own times he will show, Wey be the blessed and only Ruler, the King of kings, and Lord of lords;
who alone has immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light; whom no man has seen, nor can see: to whom be honor and eternal power. Amen.
Charge people Wey rich in this present world that dem not be haughty, nor have dem hope set on the uncertainty of riches, but on the living God, who richly provides us with everything to enjoy;
that dem do good, that dem be rich in good works, that dem be ready to distribute, willing to communicate;
laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that dem may lay hold of life wey no dey end.
Timothy, guard that which is committed to you, turning away from the empty chatter and oppositions of Wetin be falsely call knowledge;
which some profess, and thus have wandered from the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.
Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, according to the promise of the life which is in Christ Jesus,
to Timothy, my beloved pikin: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
I thank God, whom I serve as my forefathers did, with a pure conscience. How unceasing is my memory of you in my petitions, night and day
longing to see you, remembering una tears, that I may be filled with gladness;
having been reminded of the sincere faith that is in you; which lived first in una grandmother Lois, and una mother Eunice, and, I be persuaded, in you also.
For this cause, I remind you that you should stir up the gift of God which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
So no be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner; but endure hardship for the Better news according to the power of God,
who saved us and call us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before times eternal,
but has now been revealed by the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus, who abolished death, and bring life and immortality to light through the Better news.
For this, I was appointed as a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles.
For this cause I also suffer these things. Yet I be not ashamed, for I know him whom I have believe, and I be persuaded that he is able to guard that which I have committed to him against that day.
Hold the pattern of sound words which you have heard from me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
That good thing which was committed to you, guard through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
This you know, that all Wey be in Asia turned away from me; of whom are Phygelus and Hermogenes.
May the Lord grant mercy to the house of Onesiphorus, for he often refreshed me, and No be ashamed of my chain,
but when he was in Rome, he sought me diligently, and find me
(the Lord grant to him to find the Lord’s mercy in that day); and in how many things he served at Ephesus, you know very well.
You so, my pikin, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
The things which you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit the same to faithful men, who Go be able to teach others also.
You so must endure hardship, as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
No soldier on duty entangles imself in the affairs of life, that he may please him who enrolled him as a soldier.
Also, if anyone competes in athletics, he no be crowned unless he has competed by the rules.
The farmer who labors must be the first to get a share of the crops.
Consider what I say, and may the Lord give you understanding in all things.
Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, of the offspring of David, according to my Better news,
in which I suffer hardship to the point of chains as a criminal. But God’s word no be chained.
So I endure all things for the chosen ones’ sake, that dem also may obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory.
This saying is trustworthy: “For if we died with him, We go also live with him.
If we endure, We go also reign with him. If we deny him, he also will deny us.
If We be faithless, he remains faithful. For he no fit deny imself.”
Remind dem of these things, charging dem in the sight of the Lord, that dem no argue about words, to no profit, to the subverting of people wey hear.
Give diligence to present yourself approved by God, a workman who no dey need to be ashamed, properly handling the Word of Truth.
But shun empty chatter, for it will go further in ungodliness,
and those words will consume like gangrene, of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus;
men who have erred concerning the truth, saying that the resurrection is already past, and overthrowing the faith of some.
However God’s firm foundation stands, having this seal, “The Lord knows people Wey his,” and, “Let every one who names the name of the Lord depart from unrighteousness.”
Now in a large house there No be only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of clay. Some are for honor, and some for dishonor.
If anyone so purges imself from these, he Go be a vessel for honor, sanctified, and suitable for the master’s use, prepared for every good work.
Flee from youthful lusts; but pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace with people wey call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
But refuse foolish and ignorant questionings, knowing that dem generate strife.
The Lord’s worker must not quarrel, but be gentle towards all, able to teach, patient,
in gentleness correcting people wey oppose him: perhaps God may give dem repentance leading to a full knowledge of the truth,
and dem may recover themselves out of the devil’s snare, having been taken captive by him to his will.
But know this, that in the last days, grievous times will come.
For men Go be lovers of self, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy,
without natural affection, unforgiving, slanderers, without self-control, fierce, not lovers of good,
traitors, headstrong, conceited, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God;
holding a form of godliness, but having denied its power. Turn away from these, also.
For some of these are people who creep into houses, and take captive gullible women loaded down with sins, led away by various lusts,
always learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.
Even as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so do these also oppose the truth; men corrupted in mind, who concerning the faith, are rejected.
But Dem go proceed no further. For dem folly Go be evident to all men, as dem own also come to be.
But you did follow my teaching, conduct, purpose, faith, patience, love, steadfastness,
persecutions, and sufferings: those things that happened to me at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. I endured those persecutions. The Lord delivered me out of dem all.
Yes, and all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution.
But evil men and impostors will grow worse and worse, deceiving and being deceived.
But you remain in the things which you have learned and Don dey assured of, knowing from whom you have learned dem.
From infancy, you have known the holy Scriptures which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith, which is in Christ Jesus.
Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness,
that the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work.
I command you so before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, who will judge the living and the dead at his appearing and his Kingdom:
preach the word; be urgent in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, and exhort, with all patience and teaching.
For the time will come when Dem go not listen to the sound doctrine, but, having itching ears, will heap up for themselves teachers after dem own lusts;
and will turn away dem ears from the truth, and turn aside to fables.
But you be sober in all things, suffer hardship, do the work of an evangelist, and fulfill una ministry.
For I be already being offered, and the time of my departure has come.
I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.

From now on, E get stored up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give to me on that day; and not to me only, but also to all people wey have love his appearing.
Be diligent to come to me soon,
for Demas left me, having love this present world, and go to Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.
Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service.
But I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
Bring the cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus when you come, and the books, especially the parchments.
Alexander, the coppersmith, did much evil to me. The Lord will repay him according to his deeds,
of whom you also must beware; for he greatly opposed our words.
At my first defense, Nobody come to help me, but all left me. May it not be held against dem.
But the Lord stood by me, and strengthened me, that through me the message might be fully proclaimed, and that all the Gentiles might hear; and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.
And the Lord will deliver me from every evil work, and will preserve me for his heavenly Kingdom; to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
Greet Prisca and Aquila, and the house of Onesiphorus.
Erastus remain at Corinth, but I left Trophimus at Miletus sick.
Be diligent to come before winter. Eubulus salutes you, as do Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers.
The Lord Jesus Christ be with una spirit. Grace be with you. Amen.
Paul, a worker of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God’s chosen ones, and the knowledge of the truth which is according to godliness,
in hope of life wey no dey end, which God, who no fit lie, promised before time began;
but in his own time revealed his word in the message with which I was entrusted according to the commandment of God our Savior;
to Titus, my true pikin according to a common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Savior.
I left you in Crete for this reason, that you would set in order the things that were lacking, and appoint elders in every city, as I directed you;
if anyone is blameless, the husband of one wife, having pikin dem who believe, Wey be not accused of loose or unruly behavior.
For the overseer must be blameless, as God’s steward; not self-pleasing, not easily angered, not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for dishonest gain;
but given to hospitality, a lover of good, sober minded, fair, holy, self-controlled;
holding to the faithful word which is according to the teaching, that he may be able to exhort in the sound doctrine, and to convict people wey contradict him.
For E get also many unruly men, vain talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision,
whose mouths must be stopped; men who overthrow whole houses, teaching things which dem ought not, for dishonest gain’s sake.
One of dem, a prophet of dem own, talk say, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, and idle gluttons.”
This testimony is true. For this cause, reprove dem sharply, that dem may be sound in the faith,
not paying attention to Jewish fables and commandments of men who turn away from the truth.
To the pure, all things are pure; but to people Wey defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure; but both dem mind and dem conscience are defiled.
Dem profess that dem know God, but by dem deeds dem deny him, being abominable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.
But say the things which fit sound doctrine,
that older men should be temperate, sensible, sober minded, sound in faith, in love, and in perseverance:
and that older women likewise be reverent in behavior, not slanderers nor enslaved to much wine, teachers of that which is good;
that dem may train the young women to love dem husbands, to love dem pikin dem,
to be sober minded, chaste, workers at home, kind, being in subjection to dem own husbands, that God’s word may not be blasphemed.
Likewise, exhort the younger men to be sober minded;
in all things showing yourself an example of good works; in una teaching showing integrity, seriousness, incorruptibility,
and soundness of speech that no fit be condemned; that person wey opposes you may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say about us.
Exhort workers to be in subjection to dem own masters, and to be well-pleasing in all things; not contradicting;
not stealing, but showing all good fidelity; that dem may adorn the doctrine of God, our Savior, in all things.
For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all men,
instructing us to the intent that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we would live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present world;
looking for the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ;
who give imself for us, that he might redeem us from all wickedness, and purify for imself a people for his own possession, zealous for good works.
Say these things and exhort and reprove with all authority. Let no man despise you.
Remind dem to be in subjection to rulers and to authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work,
to speak evil of Nobody, not to be contentious, to be gentle, showing all humility toward all men.
For we were also once foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving various lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating each other.
But when the kindness of God our Savior and his love toward mankind appeared,
not by works of righteousness which we did ourselves, but according to his mercy, he saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewing by the Holy Spirit,
whom he poured out on us richly, through Jesus Christ our Savior;
that being justified by his grace, we might be made heirs according to the hope of life wey no dey end.

This saying is faithful, and concerning these things I desire that you affirm confidently, so that people wey have believe God may be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable to men;
but shun foolish questionings, genealogies, strife, and disputes about the law; for Dem be unprofitable and vain.
Avoid a factious man after a first and second warning,
knowing that such a one is perverted and sins, being self-condemned.
When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, be diligent to come to me to Nicopolis, for I have determined to winter there.
Send Zenas, the lawyer, and Apollos on dem journey speedily, that nothing may be lacking for dem.
Let our people also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that dem may not be unfruitful.
All Wey be with me greet you. Greet people wey love us in faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon, our beloved fellow worker,
to the beloved Apphia, to Archippus, our fellow soldier, and to the assembly in una house:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God always, making mention of you in my prayers,
hearing of una love, and of the faith which you have toward the Lord Jesus, and toward all the saints;
that the fellowship of una faith may become effective, in the knowledge of every good thing which is in us in Christ Jesus.
For we have much gladness and comfort in una love, because the hearts of the saints Don dey refreshed through you, brother.
So though I have all boldness in Christ to command you that which is appropriate,
yet for love’s sake I rather beg, being such a one as Paul, the aged, but also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
I beg you for my pikin, whom I have become the father of in my chains, Onesimus,
who once was useless to you, but now is useful to you and to me.
I be sending him back. So receive him, that is, my own heart,
whom I desired to keep with me, that on una behalf he might serve me in my chains for the Better news.
But I was willing to do nothing without una consent, that una goodness would not be as of necessity, but of free will.
For perhaps he was so separated from you for a while, that you would have him forever,
no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much rather to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
If then you count me a partner, receive him as you would receive me.
But if he has wronged you at all, or owes you anything, put that to my account.
I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I go repay it (not to mention to you that you owe to me even una own self besides).
Yes, brother, let me have gladness from you in the Lord. Refresh my heart in the Lord.
Having confidence in una obedience, I write to you, knowing that You go do even beyond what I say.
Also, prepare a guest room for me, for I hope that through una prayers I go be restored to you.
Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, greets you,
as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with una spirit. Amen.
God, having in the past spoken to the fathers through the prophets at many times and in various ways,
has at the end of these days spoken to us by his Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom also he made the worlds.

His Son is the radiance of his glory, the very image of his substance, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by imself purified us of our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;
having become so much better than the angels, as he has inherited a more excellent name than dem have.
For to which of the angels did he say at any time, “You be my Son. Today I have become una father?” and again, “I go be to him a Father, and he Go be to me a Son?”
When he again brings in the firstborn into the world he says, “Let all the angels of God worship him.”
Of the angels he says, “Who makes his angels winds, and his workers a flame of fire.”
But of the Son he says, “Una throne, O God, is forever and ever. The scepter of uprightness is the scepter of una Kingdom.
You have love righteousness, and hated wickedness; so God, una God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above una fellows.”
And, “You, Lord, For the beginning, laid the foundation of the earth. The heavens are the works of una hands.
Dem go perish, but you continue. Dem all will grow old like a garment does.
You go roll dem up like a mantle, and Dem go be changed; but You be the same. Una years No go fail.”
But which of the angels has he told at any time, “Sit at my right hand, until I make una enemies the footstool of una feet?”
No be dem all serving spirits, sent out to do service for the sake of people wey will inherit salvation?
So we ought to pay greater attention to the things that were heard, lest perhaps we drift away.
For if the word spoken through angels proved steadfast, and every wrongdoing and disobedience received a just recompense;
how will we escape if we neglect so great a salvation — which at the first having been spoken through the Lord, was confirmed to us by people wey heard;
God also testifying with dem, both by signs and wonders, by various works of power, and by gifts of the Holy Spirit, according to his own will?
For he didn’t subject the world to come, of which we speak, to angels.
But one has somewhere testified, saying, “Wetin be man, that you think of him? Or the Son of Man, that you care for him?
You made him a little lower than the angels. You crowned him with glory and honor.
You have put all things in subjection under his feet.” For in that he subjected all things to him, he left nothing that No be subject to him. But now we no see all things subjected to him, yet.
But we see him who Don dey made a little lower than the angels, Jesus, because of the suffering of death crowned with glory and honor, that by the grace of God he should taste of death for everyone.
For it became him, for whom are all things, and through whom are all things, in bringing many pikin dem to glory, to make the author of dem salvation perfect through sufferings.
For both person wey sanctifies and people Wey sanctified are all from one, for which cause he No be ashamed to call dem brothers,
saying, “I go declare una name to my brothers. Among of the congregation I go sing una praise.”
Again, “I go put my trust in him.” Again, “See am, here I be with the pikin dem whom God has given me.”

Since then the pikin dem have shared in flesh and blood, he also imself in the same way partook of the same, that through death he might bring to nothing him who had the power of death, that is, the devil,
and might deliver all of dem who through fear of death were all dem lifetime subject to bondage.
For most certainly, he no dey give help to angels, but he gives help to the offspring of Abraham.
So he was obligated in all things to be made like his brothers, that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.
For in that he imself has suffered being tempted, he is able to help people Wey tempted.
So, holy brothers, partakers of a heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our confession, Jesus;
who was faithful to him who appointed him, as also was Moses in all his house.
For he Don dey counted worthy of more glory than Moses, because person wey built the house has more honor than the house.
For every house is built by someone; but person wey built all things is God.
Moses indeed was faithful in all his house as a worker, for a testimony of those things which were afterward to be spoken,
but Christ is faithful as a Son over his house; whose house We be, if we Hold am tight our confidence and the glorying of our hope firm to the end.
So, even as the Holy Spirit says, “Today if You go hear his voice,
no harden una hearts, as in the rebellion, like as in the day of the trial in the wilderness,
where una fathers tested me by proving me, and see my deeds for forty years.
So I was displeased with that generation, and talk say, ‘Dem always err in dem heart, but dem didn’t know my ways;’
as I swore in my serious anger, ‘Dem go not enter into my rest.’”
Beware, brothers, lest perhaps there be in any one of you an evil heart of unbelief, in falling away from the living God;
but exhort each other day by day, so long as it is call “today”; lest any one of you be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
For we have become partakers of Christ, if we Hold am tight the beginning of our confidence firm to the end:
while it is talk say, “Today if You go hear his voice, no harden una hearts, as in the rebellion.”
For who, when dem heard, rebelled? No, didn’t all people wey come out of Egypt by Moses?
With whom was he displeased forty years? No be it with people wey sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
To whom did he swear that dem wouldn’t enter into his rest, but to people wey were disobedient?
We see that dem No be able to enter in because of unbelief.
Make we fear so, lest perhaps anyone of you should seem to have come short of a promise of entering into his rest.
For indeed we have had better news preached to us, even as dem also did, but the word dem heard didn’t profit dem, because it no be mixed with faith by people wey heard.

For we who have believe do enter into that rest, even as he has talk say, “As I swore in my serious anger, Dem go not enter into my rest”; although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.
For he has talk say this somewhere about the seventh day, “God rested on the seventh day from all his works”;
and in this place again, “Dem go not enter into my rest.”
Seeing so it remains that some should enter inside am, and dem to whom the better news was before preached failed to enter in because of disobedience,
he again defines a certain day, today, saying through David so long a time afterward (just as Don dey talk say), “Today if You go hear his voice, no harden una hearts.”
For if Joshua had given dem rest, he would not have spoken afterward of another day.
There remains so a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
For person wey has entered into his rest has imself also rested from his works, as God did from his.
Make we so give diligence to enter into that rest, lest anyone fall after the same example of disobedience.

For the word of God is living and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the dividing of soul and spirit, of both joints and marrow, and is able to discern the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
E get no creature that is hidden from his sight, but all things are naked and laid open before the eyes of him to whom we must give an account.
Having then a great high priest, who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, Make we hold tightly to our confession.
For we no have a high priest who no fit be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one who Don dey in all points tempted like We be, yet without sin.
Make we so draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy, and may find grace for help in time of need.
For every high priest, being taken from among men, is appointed for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.
The high priest can deal gently with people Wey ignorant and going astray, because he imself is also surrounded with weakness.
Because of this, he must offer sacrifices for sins for the people, as well as for imself.
Nobody takes this honor on imself, but he is call by God, just like Aaron was.
So also Christ didn’t glorify imself to be made a high priest, but it was person wey talk say to him, “You be my Son. Today I have become una father.”
As he says also in another place, “You be a priest forever, after the order of Melchizedek.”
He, in the days of his flesh, having offered up prayers and petitions with strong crying and tears to him who was able to save him from death, and having been heard for his godly fear,
though he was a Son, yet learned obedience by the things which he suffered.
Having been made perfect, he became to all of people wey obey him the author of eternal salvation,
named by God a high priest after the order of Melchizedek.
About him we have many words to say, and hard to interpret, seeing you have become dull of hearing.

For although by this time you should be teachers, you again need to have someone teach you the rudiments of the first principles of the revelations of God. You have come to need milk, and not solid chop.
For Everybody wey lives on milk No be experienced in the word of righteousness, for he is a baby.
But solid chop is for people Wey full grown, who by reason of use have dem senses exercised to discern good and evil.
So leaving the teaching of the first principles of Christ, Make we press on to perfection — not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works, of faith toward God,
of the teaching of baptisms, of laying on of hands, of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
This will we do, if God permits.
For concerning people wey were once enlightened and tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Spirit,
and tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the age to come,
and then fell away, it is impossible to renew dem again to repentance; seeing dem crucify the Son of God for themselves again, and put him to open shame.
For the land which has drunk the rain that comes often on it, and produces a crop suitable for dem for whose sake it is also tilled, receives blessing from God;
but if it bears thorns and thistles, it is rejected and near being cursed, whose end is to be burned.
But, beloved, We be persuaded of better things for you, and things that accompany salvation, even though we speak like this.
For God No be unrighteous, so as to forget una work and the labor of love which you showed toward his name, in that you served the saints, and still do serve dem.
We desire that each one of you may show the same diligence to the fullness of hope even to the end,
that you no go be sluggish, but imitators of people wey through faith and perseverance inherited the promises.
For when God made a promise to Abraham, since he could swear by Nobody greater, he swore by imself,
saying, “Surely blessing I go bless you, and multiplying I go multiply you.”
Thus, having patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
For men indeed swear by a greater one, and in every dispute of dem own the oath is final for confirmation.
In this way God, being determined to show more abundantly to the heirs of the promise the immutability of his counsel, interposed with an oath;
that by two immutable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have a strong encouragement, who have fled for refuge to take hold of the hope set before us.
This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, a hope both sure and steadfast and entering into that which is within the veil;
where as a forerunner Jesus entered for us, having become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.
For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,
to whom also Abraham divided a tenth part of all (being first, by interpretation, “king of righteousness”, and then also “king of Salem”, which means “king of peace”;
without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but made like the Son of God), remains a priest continually.
Now consider how great this man was, to whom even Abraham, the patriarch, give a tenth out of the best plunder.

Dem indeed of the sons of Levi who receive the priest’s office have a commandment to take tithes of the people according to the law, that is, of dem brothers, though these have come out of the body of Abraham,
but he whose genealogy No be counted from dem has accepted tithes from Abraham, and has blessed him who has the promises.
But without any dispute the lesser is blessed by the greater.
Here people who die receive tithes, but there one receives tithes of whom it is testified that he lives.
We can say that through Abraham even Levi, who receives tithes, has paid tithes,
for he was yet in the body of his father when Melchizedek met him.

Now if there were perfection through the Levitical priesthood (for under it the people have received the law), what further need was there for another priest to arise after the order of Melchizedek, and not be call after the order of Aaron?
For the priesthood being changed, E get of necessity a change made also in the law.
For he of whom these things are talk say belongs to another tribe, from which Nobody has officiated at the altar.
For it is evident that our Lord has sprung out of Judah, about which tribe Moses spoke nothing concerning priesthood.
This is yet more abundantly evident, if after the likeness of Melchizedek there arises another priest,
who Don dey made, not after the law of a fleshly commandment, but after the power of an endless life:
for it is testified, “You be a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For E get an annulling of a foregoing commandment because of its weakness and uselessness
(for the law made nothing perfect), and a bringing in of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
Inasmuch as he No be made priest without the taking of an oath

(for dem indeed Don dey made priests without an oath), but he with an oath by him that says of him, “The Lord swore and No go change his mind, ‘You be a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.’”
By so much, Jesus has become the collateral of a better covenant.
Many, indeed, Don dey made priests, because Dem be hindered from continuing by death.
But he, because he lives forever, has his priesthood unchangeable.
So he is also able to save to the uttermost people wey draw near to God through him, seeing that he lives forever to make intercession for dem.
For such a high priest was fitting for us: holy, guiltless, undefiled, separated from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;
who no dey need, like those high priests, to offer up sacrifices daily, first for his own sins, and then for the sins of the people. For he did this once for all, when he offered up imself.
For the law appoints men as high priests who have weakness, but the word of the oath which come after the law appoints a Son forever who Don dey perfected.
Now in the things which We be saying, the main point is this. We have such a high priest, who sat down on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
a worker of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, not man.
For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices. So it is necessary that this high priest also have something to offer.
For if he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, seeing E get priests who offer the gifts according to the law;

who serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, even as Moses was warned by God when he was about to make the tabernacle, for he talk say, “See, you shall make everything according to the pattern that was shown to you on the mountain.”
But now he has obtained a more excellent ministry, by so much as he is also the mediator of a better covenant, which on better promises Don dey given as law.
For if that first covenant Bin dey faultless, then no place would Don dey sought for a second.
For finding fault with dem, he talk say, “See am, the days come”, says the Lord, “that I go make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah;

not according to the covenant that I made with dem fathers, in the day that I take dem by the hand to lead dem out of the land of Egypt; for dem didn’t continue in my covenant, and I disregarded dem,” says the Lord.

“For this is the covenant that I go make with the house of Israel. After those days,” says the Lord; “I go put my laws into dem mind, I go also write dem on dem heart. I go be dem God, and Dem go be my people.
Dem go not teach every man his fellow citizen, and every man his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ for all will know me, from dem least to dem greatest.
For I go be merciful to dem unrighteousness. I go remember dem sins and lawless deeds no more.”
In that he says, “A new covenant”, he has made the first old. But that which is becoming old and grows aged is near to vanishing away.
Now indeed even the first covenant had ordinances of divine service, and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tabernacle was prepared. In the first part were the lamp stand, the table, and the show bread; which is call the Holy Place.
After the second veil was the tabernacle which is call the Holy of Holies,
having a golden altar of incense, and the ark of the covenant overlaid on all sides with gold, in which was a golden pot holding the manna, Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tablets of the covenant;
and above it cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat, of which things we no fit speak now in detail.
Now these things having been thus prepared, the priests go in continually into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the services,
but into the second the high priest alone, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for imself, and for the errors of the people.
The Holy Spirit is indicating this, that the way into the Holy Place no be yet revealed while the first tabernacle was still standing;
which is a symbol of the present age, where gifts and sacrifices are offered that are incapable, concerning the conscience, of making the worshiper perfect;
being only (with meats and drinks and various washings) fleshly ordinances, imposed until a time of reformation.
But Christ having come as a high priest of the coming good things, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this creation,
nor yet through the blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood, entered in once for all into the Holy Place, having obtained eternal redemption.
For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling people wey Don dey defiled, sanctify to the cleanness of the flesh:
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered imself without defect to God, cleanse una conscience from dead works to serve the living God?

For this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant, since a death has occurred for the redemption of the wrongdoings that were under the first covenant, that people wey Don dey call may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
For where a last will and testament is, there must of necessity be the death of him who made it.
For a will is in force where there Don dey death, for it is never in force while person wey made it lives.
So even the first covenant has not been dedicated without blood.

For when every commandment Bin dey spoken by Moses to all the people according to the law, he take the blood of the calves and the goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,
saying, “This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded you.”
Moreover he sprinkled the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry in the same way with the blood.
According to the law, nearly everything is cleansed with blood, and apart from shedding of blood E get no remission.
It was necessary so that the copies of the things in the heavens should be cleansed with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
For Christ hasn’t entered into holy places made with hands, which are representations of the true, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us;
nor yet that he should offer imself often, as the high priest enters into the holy place year by year with blood not his own,
or else he must have suffered often since the foundation of the world. But now once at the end of the ages, he Don dey revealed to put away sin by the sacrifice of imself.
Inasmuch as it is appointed for men to die once, and after this, judgment,
so Christ also, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, without sin, to people Wey eagerly waiting for him for salvation.
For the law, having a shadow of the good to come, not the very image of the things, can never with the same sacrifices year by year, which dem offer continually, make perfect people wey draw near.
Or else wouldn’t dem have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, having been once cleansed, would have had no more consciousness of sins?
But in those sacrifices E get a yearly reminder of sins.
For it is impossible that the blood of bulls and goats should take away sins.
So when he comes into the world, he says, “Sacrifice and offering you didn’t desire, but you prepared a body for me.
You had no pleasure in whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin.
Then I talk say, ‘See am, I have come (in the scroll of the book it is written of me) to do una will, O God.’”
Previously saying, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin you didn’t desire, neither had pleasure in dem” (those which are offered according to the law),
then he has talk say, “See am, I have come to do una will.” He takes away the first, that he may establish the second,
by which will we Don dey sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
Every priest indeed stands day by day serving and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins,
but he, when he had offered one sacrifice for sins forever, sat down on the right hand of God;
from that time waiting until his enemies are made the footstool of his feet.
For by one offering he has perfected forever people Wey being sanctified.
The Holy Spirit also testifies to us, for after saying,
“This is the covenant that I go make with dem: ‘After those days,’ says the Lord, ‘I go put my laws on dem heart, I go also write dem on dem mind;’” then he says,
“I go remember dem sins and dem iniquities no more.”
Now where remission of these is, E get no more offering for sin.
Having so, brothers, boldness to enter into the holy place by the blood of Jesus,
by the way which he dedicated for us, a new and living way, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;
and having a great priest over God’s house,
let’s draw near with a true heart in fullness of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and having our body washed with pure water,
Make we Hold am tight the confession of our hope without wavering; for person wey promised is faithful.
Make we consider how to provoke each other to love and good works,
not forsaking our own assembling together, as the custom of some is, but exhorting each other; and so much the more, as you see the Day approaching.
For if we sin willfully after we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remains no more a sacrifice for sins,
but a certain fearful expectation of judgment, and a fierceness of fire which will devour the adversaries.
A man who disregards Moses’ law dies without compassion on the word of two or three witnesses.

How much worse punishment do you think he Go be judged worthy of who has trodden under foot the Son of God, and has counted the blood of the covenant with which he was sanctified an unholy thing, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?
For we know him who talk say, “Vengeance belongs to me,” says the Lord, “I go repay.” Again, “The Lord will judge his people.”
It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
But remember the former days, in which, after you were enlightened, you endured a great struggle with sufferings;
partly, being exposed to both reproaches and oppressions; and partly, becoming partakers with people wey were treated so.
For you both had compassion on me in my chains, and joyfully accepted the plundering of una possessions, knowing that you have for unaself a better possession and an enduring one in the heavens.
So no throw away una boldness, which has a great reward.
For you need endurance so that, having done the will of God, you may receive the promise.
“In a very little while, person wey comes will come, and No go wait.
But the righteous will live by faith. If he shrinks back, my soul has no pleasure in him.”
But we No be of people wey shrink back to destruction, but of people wey have faith to the saving of the soul.
Now faith is assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen.
For by this, the elders obtained testimony.
By faith, we understand that the universe Don dey framed by the word of God, so that Wetin be seen has not been made out of things which are visible.

By faith, Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, through which he had testimony given to him that he was righteous, God testifying with respect to his gifts; and through it he, being dead, still speaks.

By faith, Enoch was taken away, so that he wouldn’t see death, and he No be find, because God translated him. For he has had testimony given to him that before his translation he Bin dey well pleasing to God.
Without faith it is impossible to be well pleasing to him, for person wey comes to God must believe that he exists, and that he is a rewarder of people wey seek him.

By faith, Noah, being warned about things not yet seen, moved with godly fear, prepared a ship for the saving of his house, through which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is according to faith.
By faith, Abraham, when he was call, obeyed to go out to the place which he was to receive for an inheritance. He go out, not knowing where he go.
By faith, he lived as an alien in the land of promise, as in a land not his own, dwelling in tents, with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise.
For he looked for the city which has the foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
By faith, even Sarah sheself received power to conceive, and she bore a pikin when she was past age, since she counted him faithful who had promised.
So as many as the stars of the sky in plenty people, and as innumerable as the sand which is by the sea shore, were fathered by one man, and him as good as dead.
These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen dem and embraced dem from far away, and having confessed that dem were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
For people wey say such things make it clear that Dem be seeking a country of dem own.
